## What does this PR do?

When the provider is unreachable, rate limited or overloaded, the backend backs off and retries. The auto-recovery ladder alone waits 15/30/60/60/60 s over up to five cycles. It sends a live line for each wait over `thinking.delta`, e.g.

```
⏳ Provider temporarily unavailable — retrying automatically in 18s (cycle 1/5); press Esc to stop
```

Desktop only shows `thinking.delta` frames in the status row when `providerWaitText()` accepts them, and its prefix regex didn't cover these frames. Desktop showed only a spinner and a timer for minutes, with no sign that anything had failed or that Esc would stop it. The docs (`website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md`, `agent.auto_recovery_cycles`) say Desktop shows this line.

This PR widens the accepted prefixes in `apps/desktop/src/store/provider-wait.ts` to cover the frames the backend sends:

- `⏳ rate limited — resets in …, retrying in Ns (attempt k/n)` (`agent/turn_recovery.py`)
- `⏳ provider overloaded — …` (same site, Z.ai coding overload)
- `⏳ Provider temporarily unavailable — retrying automatically in Ns (cycle k/5); …` (`agent/turn_recovery_autorecover.ladder_notice`)

Spinner noise stays filtered out.

## Related Issue

Fixes #124375

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

- `apps/desktop/src/store/provider-wait.ts`: `providerWaitText` accepts `rate limited` and `provider overloaded|temporarily unavailable` after the wait glyph.

## What does this PR do?

The backend classifier stamps `failure_reason="timeout"` for every transport failure on a known provider, not only for slow replies. That includes refused connections, DNS failures and unreachable networks (`_CONNECTION_MESSAGE_PATTERNS` and `_TRANSPORT_ERROR_TYPES` in `agent/error_classifier.py`). The Desktop card for that code said "The reply timed out — did not answer in time. Retry to send it again." I reproduced this with the provider's `base_url` pointed at a closed port. The connection was refused on every attempt, yet the card said the reply was slow and suggested retrying. It never pointed at the network.

This PR changes only the copy for the `timeout` code so it covers both cases and points at the likely fix:

- Title: **Could not reach the AI service**
- Body: **{provider} could not be reached or did not answer in time. Check your internet connection, then retry.**

The classification stays the same. Splitting `timeout` into separate codes would also change retry and compression behaviour in the backend, which is a bigger change than this.

raw.body:
## Problem

Part of #124545. A configured Desktop whose two readiness probes fail transiently keeps its configured state, but raises a permanent red `Runtime not ready` toast. A later successful round does not remove it.

## Root cause

`refreshOnboarding` correctly recognizes non-authoritative fallback, then sends `kind: 'error'`, whose shared notification lifetime is unlimited. The common successful completion path does not dismiss that notice.

## Change

- Make that fallback notice informational, using the existing automatic expiry instead of introducing another timer.
- Dismiss only `runtime-not-ready` when onboarding completes successfully.
- Exercise the real onboarding and notification stores: transport failure, automatic expiry, another failure, recovery, and preservation of an unrelated error.

## Verification

Base: `802ae8544b59f62c97468ed31b55f417ba12e9f2`.

- RED on base: onboarding suite **1 failed / 21 passed**, expected info versus actual error.
- GREEN with this change: **22 passed**.
- Native Windows, isolated HOME/USERPROFILE/HERMES_HOME/APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA and local RPC fixtures; no live gateway, provider, or production config used.
- Existing dependencies reused without installation. The normal Vitest project config cannot load the locally missing `@rolldown/plugin-babel`; tests ran with a temporary jsdom config retaining the repository setup file and source aliases, without the build-only compiler/CSS plugins. This is not a full production build claim.
- Post-publication regression coverage: **48 passed across 6 files** (onboarding store, notification store, runtime-readiness, onboarding gate, free-tier intro, onboarding flow).
- Mutation check: removing only clear-on-recovery makes the regression fail because the old notice remains; restoring the exact committed head passes.
- Codex CLI v0.153.4 (`gpt-5.6-sol`, bridge) exact-head static review: **STATIC PASS**.
- Claude Code native 2.1.280 / Opus 5.5: repeated HTTP 503, stopped at the 180-second review deadline; **review remains incomplete, not PASS**.
- Wider `use-desktop-integrations.test.tsx` coverage is blocked at import by missing local `blobatar/react` (0 tests executed); no dependency installed and no integration pass claimed.

## Scope / continuation

Delivered: temporary severity/lifetime for unknown startup readiness and clear-on-recovery. Existing configured-state preservation, explicit onboarding requests, and authoritative credential failures remain unchanged.

Remaining optional issue suggestions: special handling of RPC error 5097 and changes to backend cold-start probe budgets. These are not necessary to resolve the sticky-toast contract and are not claimed here. Continue on this PR for demonstrated same-contract gaps and review findings.

Overlap checked by actual diffs: #113988 changes cold unknown/skip state; #123843 changes preservation on authoritative-looking background negatives. Both retain the sticky error notification. This PR changes neither policy.

raw.body:
Fixes #124072
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/115193 (@certaindaniel — the fix is your commits, cherry-picked with authorship kept) and https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/124276 (@Finn763 — same fix against the #124072 incident; the warn-only test below follows your notice assertions).

## What changes

`_result_hash()` takes the tool name and, for `execute_code` only, drops the two per-call bookkeeping fields from the parsed result before hashing: top-level `duration_seconds` and `kernel.execution_count`. Nothing else in the result, and no other tool's result, is touched. Non-JSON results hash as before.

## Root cause

The identical-call streak and repeating-cycle detectors in `ToolCallGuardrailController.observe_call()` key on `(tool, args, result_hash)`. An `execute_code` result carries a monotonic kernel cell counter and a wall-clock duration, so byte-identical replays of the same no-op cell never hashed equal and the streak stayed at 1. Those two detectors are the only guard path that can fire for `execute_code` at all (`after_call()` returns early for MUTATING tools), so a model replaying `print("...")` to keep a turn open produced zero notices across 186 calls in the incident, and the hard stop never had a count to act on where it is enabled.

## What this does and does not cover (the issue lists four defects)

- **Defect 3 (volatile fields blind the replay detectors)** — fixed here. The notice now fires from the 3rd identical replay on every surface; with `hard_stop_enabled` (telegram/cron/gateway) the streak halts at `hard_stop_after.idempotent_no_progress` as it does for `terminal`.
- **Defect 2 (execute_code-only rounds refund the iteration budget without bound)** — verified as reported (`used=0 remaining=10` after 1000 consume/refund pairs) but **not load-bearing for termination, so deliberately not changed here**. `IterationBudget(max_iterations)` is created fresh per turn (`agent/turn_context.py`), the loop runs `while api_call_count < max_iterations and budget.remaining > 0`, and every site that decrements `api_call_count` also refunds the budget, while the execute_code refund only ever lowers `budget.used`. So `budget.used <= api_call_count` holds for the whole turn and `api_call_count` reaches `max_iterations` first — which is exactly how the incident's first turn ended (`max_iterations_reached(150/150) budget=55/150`). A refund cap would be dead code for liveness; the refund/limiter divergence itself is #75097.
- **Defect 4a (MUTATING tools skip the no-progress detector)** — #84646 / #92475. **Defect 4b (hard stops warn-only on interactive surfaces)** — #25823, needs-decision. Neither would have helped without Defect 3: there was no count to act on.
- **Defect 1 (prompt tension while waiting on background children)** — prompt guidance, evaluated separately in https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/124486; left open for a maintainer call on the prompt copy.

The issue's stated minimum ("the wait loop is detected and reported, not silently tolerated") is what this PR delivers.

## Why tool-scoped, not recursive

#124276 (and the first revision of #115193) stripped every `duration_seconds` / `execution_count` key recursively from every tool's result. For any other tool those names can be the actual answer (a job-status tool reporting how long a job ran), and two different answers would then count as a replay. #115193's reviewer raised this and the author scoped it to `execute_code`'s two known locations; that revision is what is cherry-picked here, with a negative-control test for another tool.

Side effect worth knowing: the duplicate-result reference stub (`IDENTICAL_RESULT_STUB_MIN_CHARS`) now also applies to `execute_code` replays whose only difference is the counter/duration. The stub still says which earlier `tool_call_id` it matches.

## Tests

`tests/agent/test_tool_guardrails.py`:
- `test_identical_streak_ignores_volatile_execution_metadata` — hard-stop path halts at the threshold (red on base: `assert None is not None`).
- `test_identical_streak_still_resets_when_real_output_changes` — over-match guard.
- `test_other_tools_keep_duration_and_execution_count_as_real_output` — negative control for non-`execute_code` tools.
- `test_execute_code_replay_streak_notice_fires_on_warn_only_desktop_config` — the incident surface: `platform="desktop"` config, issue snippet A.2 payloads, notice from the 3rd call, no halt (red on base).

```
cwd: worktree at 831c3d2441 (touched files byte-identical on current origin/main), PYTHONPATH unset
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_tool_guardrails.py tests/agent/test_tool_call_guardrail_runtime.py tests/agent/test_stall_guards.py -q
=== Summary: 3 files, 77 tests passed, 0 failed ===
# with agent/tool_guardrails.py reverted to base:
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_tool_guardrails.py -k "volatile or real_output_changes or other_tools_keep"
1 failed, 2 passed   (FAILED test_identical_streak_ignores_volatile_execution_metadata)
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_tool_guardrails.py -k warn_only_desktop
1 failed             (FAILED test_execute_code_replay_streak_notice_fires_on_warn_only_desktop_config)
```

Issue repro snippets A.1–A.4 were each re-run on base and reproduce as written.

## Risk / auto-merge

Agent core loop guard. The change only makes an existing detector see what it was already meant to see; thresholds, hard-stop defaults and the MUTATING classification are untouched. The credible downside is a legitimate programmatic-tool-calling workflow that re-runs the same cell with the same output ≥3 times in a turn: on interactive surfaces it now gets the existing advisory notice; on gateway/cron with hard stops on, it halts at the same threshold `terminal` already does. Because that is a behavior change on unattended surfaces, **auto-merge is not requested** — flagged for a human read on that trade-off. Reviewed head: `e63a85296a9cd83ce304089e999c20563122a622` on `origin/main` `a1d2a5bd571751ffea0968de149296cb231741eb`.

raw.body:
On Linux, `hermes desktop` now opens its window when `$HERMES_HOME` is long. Before this change, Electron hung forever in `requestSingleInstanceLock()`.

Salvages #124696 by @Wenfengcheng (commit cherry-picked, authorship kept). Part of #124688.

## Root cause
The CLI exports `TMPDIR=$HERMES_HOME/cache/scratch` at boot, and `_desktop_launch_env()` handed that value to Electron unchanged. Chromium's ProcessSingleton binds `$TMPDIR/scoped_dirXXXXXX/SingletonSocket`. Once that path passes the 107-byte `sun_path` limit, the bind fails and the lock call never returns: no window, no error, and SIGKILL is the only way out.

## Change
- `hermes_cli/main_desktop.py::_desktop_launch_env`: on Linux, Electron gets a short `TMPDIR` only when the caller's `TMPDIR` exceeds Chromium's real budget. The budget is `_ELECTRON_TMPDIR_MAX_BYTES = 107 - len("/scoped_dirXXXXXX/SingletonSocket")`, which is **74 bytes**. Scratch roots of 51–74 bytes keep their `TMPDIR`; the shared 50-byte `SOCKET_TMPDIR_MAX_LEN`, sized for code-kernel/Chrome sockets, no longer decides this. The short root still comes from `socket_safe_tmpdir()`. The original value travels to Electron in `HERMES_DESKTOP_TMPDIR`.
- `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts`: immediately after `app.requestSingleInstanceLock()`, main restores `process.env.TMPDIR` from `HERMES_DESKTOP_TMPDIR` and deletes the marker. Only Chromium's singleton socket uses the short root. The Python backend and every other Electron child get the profile scratch dir back, so `apply_scratch_tmp_env` recognises it (`TMPDIR == HERMES_SCRATCH_DIR`) and the agent subtree keeps writing to scratch instead of `/tmp`.
- `TMP`/`TEMP`/`HERMES_SCRATCH_DIR` and the parent CLI process are unchanged. macOS is left alone on purpose: launchd always sets a short per-user `TMPDIR`, and a user-set temp var is never overridden.
- Tests: 2 invariants (`tests/hermes_cli/test_desktop_socket_tmpdir.py`). The salvaged tests stubbed `_desktop_launch_options` with a 4-tuple, but main now returns 5 values, so they failed on both base and head. They now call the real function.

## Validation
**Budget, measured on the shipped Electron 40.10.2 (Chrome 144):** a bare `app.requestSingleInstanceLock()` with a 60-byte `TMPDIR` bound `…/scoped_dir1rs9LQ/SingletonSocket` (93 bytes, so the suffix is 33 bytes). A 74-byte `TMPDIR` locks, with a 107-byte socket path. A 75-byte `TMPDIR` hangs.

**Live repro:** a real `scripts/install.sh` install (the Desktop update E2E seed) inside a bwrap PID namespace, with `HERMES_HOME=…/install-e2e/desktop/u1/sb/home/.hermes`. It runs `hermes desktop --skip-build` from a shell with no `TMPDIR`, so the CLI exports an 88-byte scratch dir; `--remote-debugging-port=9555` comes from `desktop.electron_flags`. The backend env below is read from `/proc/<pid>/environ` of the spawned `hermes serve`.

| tree | Electron's `TMPDIR` | DevTools | backend `TMPDIR` |
|---|---|---|---|
| base `fc9349082fd` | 88-byte scratch | never up in 60 s (hang) | none spawned |
| previous head `e4e8e48` | `/tmp` | `DevTools listening on ws://127.0.0.1:9555/…` | **`/tmp`** (`TMP`/`TEMP`/`HERMES_SCRATCH_DIR` = scratch, so `apply_scratch_tmp_env` treated `/tmp` as user-set) |
| this head | `/tmp` (+ `HERMES_DESKTOP_TMPDIR`=scratch) | up after 10 s, `DevTools listening on ws://127.0.0.1:9555/…` | **`…/u1/sb/home/.hermes/cache/scratch`**, with no `HERMES_DESKTOP_TMPDIR` leaked |

The fixed Electron side was the installed `app.asar` with exactly the 4-line block esbuild emits for the new `main.ts`. I checked it against a full `bundleElectronMain` build of this branch, where the block is identical.

| test | origin/main | previous head | this head |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_long_scratch_tmpdir_hosts_the_singleton_socket_and_is_kept_for_children` | **FAIL** `AF_UNIX path too long` | **FAIL** (no `HERMES_DESKTOP_TMPDIR`) | pass |
| `test_tmpdir_that_fits_the_socket_budget_is_passed_through` (74-byte `TMPDIR`) | pass | **FAIL** (`/tmp` != 74-byte dir) | pass |

Also run: every `tests/hermes_cli/*desktop*.py` file plus `test_gui_command.py` (205 passed); `tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json`; eslint on `main.ts`; ruff; the Windows-footgun check; the `/tmp`-literal check.

CI never showed this failure because `smoke-env` forces `TMPDIR=/tmp` (b3588460338). The failure was the Linux `hermes-desktop-app-update` install-e2e red (`launch-from-spec.mjs` `_electron.launch` timeout). The Xlib.h lines in those logs also appear in green runs.

raw.body:
## Root cause

Desktop cron run entries list fine but clicking one never opens the transcript: the run row takes the selected highlight and the main area stays empty.

A cron run is an ordinary session (`source='cron'`, id `cron_{job}_{ts}`), so opening one must go through the same owner-aware door as every other session-list row. The clicked **row** — not its bare id — carries the owning `(connection, profile)`; an id-only resume resolves against whichever cached row turns up first, i.e. the ambient backend. Over SSH/remote that backend has never seen the run, so the transcript never loads (`#92454` is the same shape for two profiles holding twin ids).

Two halves were missing:

1. **The cron call sites dropped the row.** `cron-jobs-section.tsx` called `onOpenRun(run.id)` and the Cron page called `onOpenSession(run.id)`, while the sessions sidebar passes its row (`onResumeSession(session.id, session)`).
2. **The run rows had no owner to pass.** `getCronJobRuns` returned the backend page raw. Every other backend-returned session page is tagged with its serving registry connection (`stampRowsWithOwningConnection`, used by `/api/sessions` and the sidebar slices); cron runs were not, so `sessionOwnerRouteFromRow(row)` yielded `undefined` even once the row was threaded through.

## Behavior

- `getCronJobRuns` stamps each run row with the registry connection that served it (via the canonical `stampRowsWithOwningConnection`, preserving the backend's owning `profile`), exactly as the session lists do. Local single-source windows stay untagged — byte-identical.
- `SidebarCronJobsSection` forwards the clicked run **row**; the Cron page's run history does the same.
- `wiring.tsx` now has one `openStoredSession(sessionId, session?)` — the owner-aware path that pins the row's `(connection, profile)` before navigating — and the sessions sidebar, the Cron page overlay and the command center all use it. That is a pure extraction of the existing `onResumeSession` body; the sidebar path is unchanged in behavior.

Untagged rows (single-profile installs, legacy primary-SSH) keep the ambient/id-only path, as before.

The command center's session list is the same call shape (id-only open of a stored session), so it rides the same door.

## Acceptance coverage

New/updated tests:

- `src/hermes-cron-scope.test.ts` — run rows are stamped with the active registry connection; the backend's owning profile is preserved; local windows stay untagged; a row that already names an owner is never clobbered.
- `src/app/chat/sidebar/cron-jobs-section.test.tsx` (new) — clicking a run hands `onOpenRun` the run **ROW** (`(RUN.id, RUN)`), not a bare id.
- `src/app/command-center/open-session.test.tsx` (new) — the command center passes the clicked row to `onOpenSession`.

Each new test **fails before** the corresponding source change (probed by reverting the one-line change and re-running) and passes after.

## Validation

Worktree `bb/82527-cron-run-owner-route` off `origin/main` @ `28e6496a5e`, `npm ci` at the repo root first.

```
$ cd apps/desktop && unset PYTHONPATH && npm run typecheck
> hermes@0.0.0 typecheck
> tsc -p . --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.e2e.json --noEmit && ...
exit 0

$ npx vitest run src/app/chat/sidebar src/app/cron src/app/command-center src/app/contrib src/hermes-cron-scope.test.ts
 Test Files  72 passed (72)
      Tests  547 passed (547)

$ npx eslint <changed files>       # exit 0
$ npx prettier --check <changed files>
All matched files use Prettier code style!
```

Behavioral probes (failing-before / passing-after), run individually:

```
# with `onOpenRun(run.id)` restored:
× opens a run with the run ROW so the resume can pin its owning backend   Tests 1 failed (1)
# with `return runs ?? []` restored:
× stamps the active registry connection onto every run row                Tests 1 failed | 7 passed (8)
# with `onOpenSession(session.id)` restored:
× passes the clicked ROW to onOpenSession, not a bare id                  Tests 1 failed (1)
```

## Not covered

- I could not reproduce the reporter's SSH-remote desktop session end-to-end in this environment; the fix is validated at the seam (row carries the owner → the owner-aware door pins it) plus typecheck/unit tests, not against a live remote backend.
- The reporter's related papercut (sidebar search can't find cron sessions by job name when the name contains a hyphen — the FTS query parser reads `ci-triage` as `ci AND NOT triage`) is a separate defect and is **not** addressed here.
- Legacy primary-SSH windows with no registry connection id remain untagged by design (there is no connection id to name); they keep the ambient path.

No source PR's work or diagnosis was reused — no merged fix and no open PR referenced #82527.

Fixes #82527

raw.body:
## Root cause

The desktop's `hermes serve` backend holds a **live session record** for a session the messaging
gateway created, and the model-facing history comes from that record's in-memory
`session["history"]` (`tui_gateway/prompt_turn.py::_invoke_agent` feeds
`conversation_history=list(st.history)`). When the gateway keeps appending to the same session while
the desktop holds it, the UI repaints from `state.db` (full transcript) while the early in-memory
snapshot is what reaches the provider — the "UI shows full, request body truncated" divergence in
#81951.

`_adopt_out_of_band_turns` already reconciles a live record with the store before each turn
(#42962), **keyed on the highest `_row_id` stamped onto the in-memory messages**. A record that
carries no `_row_id` at all (the provider-format shape `methods_prompt.py::_resolve_truncate_row_id`
already heals for rewind, #82959) hit `seen is None` and returned early, so the gateway's rows were
silently dropped.

Since #95514 the agent's own flushes stamp `_row_id` onto the live dicts
(`agent/transcript_repair.py::sync_flushed_message_markers`) and resume/branch-seed hydration stamps
too, so a fully unstamped record is rare on current `main`; the one loader found that still omits ids
is `agent/conversation_compression.py::_adopt_live_compression_child` (child transcript loaded without
`include_row_ids`), which a turn failing before its first flush would hand back verbatim via
`_restore_agent_history_after_turn_error`. The desktop's provider request must not truncate in that
shape either.

## Behavior

`_adopt_out_of_band_turns` delegates to `_adopt_store_tail_without_row_ids` when the in-memory
history carries no durable row ids. With no row boundary to key on, adoption is gated on proof
instead:

- the durable lineage **below this turn's own user row** (the same ceiling the stamped path uses —
  `_persist_submit_user_row` has already written that row when adoption runs, and the turn appends
  it itself) must be **strictly longer** than the in-memory view, and
- its head must equal the in-memory view **entry for entry** (role + content).

Only then is the durable tail appended (canonicalized, carrying `_row_id` stamps so the row-id path
is authoritative again on the next turn). A locally diverged view (prefix mismatch — e.g. a rewind
the store has not caught up with), a store that is *not* ahead (an unflushed local tail is the
fresher record), and an empty in-memory history are left untouched — the same guards that keep the
stamped path safe.

## Not changed

- The row-id path (#42962) is unchanged and remains the precise mechanism whenever any stamp exists.
- `_adopt_live_compression_child` still loads without `include_row_ids`; stamping there is an
  `agent/` change outside this PR's scope.
- Display/rendering on warm-cache resume (the renderer-side half of #82222) is not in this PR; this
  change is backend-only, and the model-input path is what the issue's evidence indicts.
- No live two-process end-to-end run against a real messaging gateway was performed; the tests drive
  the real `prompt.submit` handler against a real `SessionDB` with rows written out-of-band between
  the snapshot and the turn.

## Acceptance coverage

`tests/tui_gateway/test_out_of_band_history_adoption.py`:

- `test_desktop_prompt_carries_gateway_rows_appended_after_hydration` — the reported shape end-to-end
  through `prompt.submit` on a stamped record (already green on `main` via #42962; kept as the
  regression guard for the reported behavior).
- `test_unstamped_live_record_is_caught_up_from_the_store` — **fails on `main`**
  (`['ask0', '', 'probe0', 'answer0']`), passes after; second pass is a no-op.
- `test_unstamped_desktop_prompt_does_not_adopt_its_own_user_row` — the unstamped shape through the
  real `prompt.submit` path: the model must see the new prompt once and the live history keep one
  copy. **Fails on `main`** and on the first revision of this branch.
- `test_unstamped_record_that_diverged_from_the_store_is_left_alone`
- `test_unstamped_record_is_untouched_when_the_store_is_not_ahead`
- `test_unstamped_history_equal_to_the_store_is_untouched`

## Validation (real output)

```
$ unset PYTHONPATH; uvx ruff check tui_gateway/prompt_turn.py tests/tui_gateway/test_out_of_band_history_adoption.py
All checks passed!

$ unset PYTHONPATH; scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_out_of_band_history_adoption.py -q
=== Summary: 1 files, 8 tests passed, 0 failed (100% complete) ===

$ unset PYTHONPATH; scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway -q
```

raw.body:
## Root cause

The desktop's transcript authority is a newest-first REST page
(`getLatestSessionMessages` → `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages?limit=120&order=latest&include_compacted=true`).
The `order` param is recent; a backend built before it drops the unknown query
param (FastAPI ignores it), pages from the **oldest** row, and — unlike the
much older "no pagination" generation — still answers with a `pagination`
object (`{limit, offset, returned}`), just without an order echo.

Nothing checked that echo, and the only legacy detection in the desktop keyed on
a *missing* `pagination`. So the oldest page was adopted as the tail:

- the transcript silently became the session's first N rows (the reported
  "stuck at the pre-restart state"; live WS rows still appended, so it read as a
  render bug, not as history loss);
- a full page set `possiblyTruncated`, so "Show earlier" →
  `getOlderSessionMessages(offset = N)` then fetched rows N..2N counted from the
  **oldest** end and prepended the wrong prefix.

The server already stamps the order it honoured (`hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py`:
`"order": order or ("latest" if limit is None else "oldest")`), so the client has
everything it needs to detect the skew.

## Behavior

A page may only be adopted as the tail when it **proves** it honoured the
request (`pagination.order === 'latest'`). A missing echo counts as "not
honoured": a page that merely omits the field is indistinguishable from the
legacy response, and the fallback is correct for either.

- `getLatestSessionMessages` (`apps/desktop/src/api/sessions.ts`): when the page
  does not honour `order=latest`, return the complete transcript with no
  `pagination`, the established "this is everything" signal. A page with no
  `pagination` at all (the pre-paging generation) or an orderless page that came
  back short already holds every row (served from the oldest row at offset 0)
  and is adopted as-is, so those cost no extra request. Only a FULL orderless
  page is re-read via the existing `getAllSessionMessages` loop
  (`order: 'oldest'` — the newer generation honours it explicitly, the older one
  drops the param and always paged from the start, so both return the same full
  history); that read inherits the caller's `passive` flag so a hidden tile's
  background refresh (#103375) never wakes or holds a backend through it.
- `tailStateFromPage` / `pageHonorsLatestOrder`
  (`apps/desktop/src/store/transcript-tail.ts`): an orderless (or explicitly
  `'oldest'`) page is never a truncated tail, closing the sibling paths that arm
  backfill from a refresh page (`olderPageReader` → `extendRefreshPageToOverlap`,
  `recordTranscriptBackfillPage`), so `getOlderSessionMessages` cannot prepend
  the wrong prefix.
- `SessionMessagesResponse['pagination']['order']` is now optional
  (`apps/desktop/src/types/hermes.ts`): backends predating the param omit it.

No restyle, no contract bump (a retroactive `DESKTOP_BACKEND_CONTRACT` bump only
affects already-updated backends and would not have caught this install).

## Acceptance coverage

- `src/api/session-transcript-paging.test.ts` — "reads the whole transcript
  instead of adopting the oldest page from a backend that ignores order": the
  legacy response (oldest 120 rows + `pagination` with no order echo) yields the
  full 400-row transcript, no `pagination`, and `transcriptBackfillAvailable`
  false. Plus: a short orderless page and a `pagination`-less page are adopted
  as the complete transcript with exactly one request, and a passive read stays
  passive on the fallback.
- `src/store/transcript-tail.test.ts` — order-echo guard: an orderless page and
  a page stamped `'oldest'` never arm a truncated tail; a `'latest'` page still
  does. Fixture updated to carry the echo, so the existing tail/rewind cases
  exercise the modern path.

Repro (unfixed sources, same tests):

```
 FAIL  src/store/transcript-tail.test.ts > order-echo guard (#92508) > never adopts an orderless page as a truncated tail
 FAIL  src/store/transcript-tail.test.ts > order-echo guard (#92508) > never adopts a page stamped with the order it really served ('oldest')
 FAIL  src/api/session-transcript-paging.test.ts > ... > reads the whole transcript instead of adopting the oldest page from a backend that ignores order
AssertionError: expected [ 1, 2, …, 120 ] to deeply equal [ 1, 2, …, 400 ]
 Test Files  2 failed (2) | Tests  3 failed | 16 passed (19)
```

## Validation (rebased on `main` @ c04e9a1d0d)

```
$ cd apps/desktop && unset PYTHONPATH && npx tsc --noEmit -p . && npx tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json --noEmit   → exit 0

$ ../../node_modules/.bin/eslint src/store/transcript-tail.ts src/api/sessions.ts src/types/hermes.ts src/store/transcript-tail.test.ts src/api/session-transcript-paging.test.ts   → exit 0
$ npx prettier --check src/api/sessions.ts src/api/session-transcript-paging.test.ts   → All matched files use Prettier code style!

$ npx vitest run src/store src/api src/app/chat src/hermes.test.ts src/app/contrib/hooks/use-background-sync.test.ts \
    src/components/assistant-ui/thread/use-timeline-history.test.tsx src/lib/stale-transcript-guard.test.ts src/app/session/hooks
 Test Files  1 failed | 414 passed (415) | Tests  2 failed | 4129 passed (4131)
   └─ the only failures are src/store/voice-prefs.test.ts (2 tests), which fail identically with this
      branch's changes stashed — pre-existing, unrelated.

Red proof (production files reverted to origin/main, PR tests): 3 failed — the three tests quoted above.
```

## Residual (not covered)

- On a legacy backend, a session longer than one page costs one extra paged
  read per refresh (bounded by `getAllSessionMessages`' existing 32 MB
  safe-load guard). It is a compatibility path, not the hot path; a backend
  that echoes `order: 'latest'` is unaffected.
- `getAllSessionMessages`' safe-load guard still rejects a >32 MB transcript with
  its existing "use the Web Dashboard export" error — now reachable for a huge
  legacy-hosted session that would previously have shown a truncated page.
- Verified by unit/behavioral tests against mocked REST shapes; no live
  pre-`order` backend was stood up to exercise the SSH path end to end.

Diagnosis credits the reporter's analysis in #92508 (@Etaing4).

Fixes #92508

raw.body:
## Root cause

`sendConnectionApplied()` (`apps/desktop/electron/main.ts`) notified the window with a bare `hermes:connection:applied` event — no route payload. The renderer's soft switch (`softSwitch()` in `apps/desktop/src/app/gateway/hooks/use-gateway-boot.ts`) then re-dials **profile-less** (`desktop.getConnection(undefined)`), and main answers that from the window's recorded route via `resolveDesktopConnectionRequest` (`electron/desktop-profile.ts`: "a profile-less boot/reconnect belongs to its sender").

That recorded route names the source the user just **left**. So after a Settings → Gateway apply:

- main correctly re-homes (`[attach] attached to the running Hermes backend …`), but
- the renderer's re-dial is answered with the old, registry-scoped route, so it keeps dialing the gateway it just left: the Sessions list never re-scopes, the status bar keeps the old backend's version, the old TCP socket stays `ESTAB`, and every later reconnect re-asks the same stale question. Only a full app restart clears the in-memory record — exactly the reporter's 2026-09-22 repro on `836b5f8253` (`remote -> local`, `#111811`/`#94886`/`#105139` all present).

The direction asymmetry in the report falls out of the same mechanism: a **locally** recorded route is unscoped (`registryScoped: false`), so `resolveDesktopWindowRoute` drops its `connectionId` and the dial follows the newly written v1 config — which is why `local -> remote` looked fine while `remote -> local` did not. It also needs a registry-scoped record (e.g. a default route set), which is why plain v1-remote retests couldn't reproduce it.

## Fix

Re-point the applied window's recorded route at the **newly applied primary** in the same step as the notify, so the profile-less apply re-dial resolves against the gateway just applied instead of the one left behind:

- `appliedPrimaryWindowRoute(registry, profile)` (`electron/window-connection-route.ts`, pure): an applied registry source (remote/cloud/ssh) stays registry-scoped to that exact identity; a This-device apply stays unscoped so the dial follows the freshly written v1 config. The profile the window was viewing is kept (falling back to the canonical `default`).
- `hermes:connection-config:apply` wraps its `sendApplied` / `notifyConnectionApplied` in one `applyPrimaryRoute()` that records the new route (from the `nextRegistry` snapshot just written) then sends the event. Both run only after the config/registry write has committed (inside `applyConnectionConfigAtomically`'s `apply()`), so a rolled-back apply can never leave a record naming a source that never landed. Only a **global** apply (`payload.profile` unset) re-points: a profile-scoped apply (the v1 per-profile remote override) never reconciles the registry primary, so it keeps the bare `sendConnectionApplied()` and cannot yank a window viewing another source onto an unchanged primary.

Fixing the **record** (not just the event payload) also covers the sibling paths that read it: a window opened from that route afterwards ("New window" inherits its IPC sender's route, `resolveDesktopWindowRoute`) now inherits the applied gateway, and the `hermes:skin:local` payload follows the same record. The profile-scoped recycle path (`hermes:backend:recycle` → `recycleOwnedBackend`) intentionally keeps calling `sendConnectionApplied()` unchanged: a primary-backend recycle must not move a window that is viewing another profile.

## Behavior

- `remote(registry-scoped) -> local` apply: the re-dial now resolves to `{connectionId: null, profile}` → `ensureBackend` → the freshly applied primary (local), so Sessions/status/cwd re-scope to This device without a restart.
- `local -> remote` and `remote -> remote` applies: the record is re-pointed to the applied registry source, so the dial targets the gateway just applied (previously a `remote -> remote` apply kept dialing the old gateway too).
- No restyling; no renderer changes.

## Acceptance coverage

`apps/desktop/electron/window-connection-route.test.ts`:

- a primary apply re-points the window route so its re-dial leaves the gateway it just left — asserts the **stale** record resolves to `{connectionId: 'macmini'}` (the pre-fix behavior) and the applied record resolves to `{connectionId: null, profile: 'default'}` (post-fix);
- a remote apply stays registry-scoped to the applied source and keeps the viewed profile;
- falls back to the canonical profile when the applied window had no route to keep.

## Validation (worktree from `origin/main` @ `28e6496a5e`, `npm ci` at repo root)

```
cd apps/desktop && unset PYTHONPATH && npm run typecheck
→ clean (tsc -p . / tsconfig.electron.json / tsconfig.e2e.json / electron-builder.config.cjs)

cd apps/desktop && npx eslint electron/window-connection-route.ts electron/window-connection-route.test.ts electron/main.ts
→ LINT CLEAN

cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run electron/window-connection-route.test.ts electron/desktop-profile.test.ts \
  electron/backend-dial-claim.test.ts electron/connection-apply.test.ts \
  electron/connection-config-apply.test.ts electron/first-run-setup-main-process.test.ts
→ Test Files 6 passed (6) | Tests 46 passed (46)

cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run electron/ src/app/gateway/hooks/use-gateway-boot.test.tsx
→ Test Files 7 failed | 265 passed | 3 skipped (275) | Tests 10 failed | 2690 passed
```

The 7 failing files are **pre-existing environment failures on clean main**, not from this change — the same 7 files / same 10 tests fail with this diff stashed (`git stash push` → rerun → identical list): `backend-probes-runtime` (real Python bootstrap), `desktop-uninstall`, `updater/state-db-preflight` (`sqlite3` has no `SQLITE_BUSY` in the sandbox), `updater/checkout-source`, `source-backend`, `channel-build-version` (real checkout/git state), `remote-lifecycle` (installer-wrapper PID probe).

Behavioral probe (throwaway vitest harness driving the real primitives — window route registry + the `hermes:connection` resolver + the applied route the fix records — not committed):

```
[probe] BEFORE fix, apply re-dial resolves to: {"connectionId":"macmini","profile":"default"}
[probe] AFTER fix,  apply re-dial resolves to: {"connectionId":null,"profile":"default"}
```

## Residual / not covered

- **Not reproduced against a live two-gateway rig here** (no registered remote gateway in this environment). The witness above is at the resolver contract level: it proves the recorded route that main answers the apply re-dial with, which is the exact defect. A live `remote -> local` + `local -> remote` retest on a build containing this commit is still worth doing before closing.
- Other **already-open** windows that were dialing the old primary keep their own recorded route until their next publish/reconnect — the applied event only reaches the main window, so only its record is re-pointed. They recover on the next successful dial.
- The idle `connections.json:lastUsed` / `active-profile.json:defaultRoute` flip-flop the reporter captured is a **separate** defect (route-store writers with no sender validation) and is not addressed here.
- The reported "authoritative empty remote profile must commit empty, not repaint local rows" edge is not exercised by this change; it belongs to the session-list publication path.

Diagnosis credit: the route trace in #92352 by @minutechreview and the instrumented live repro from @m0nty81 (main switched correctly, renderer did not follow; remote -> local asymmetry; "only a full restart recovered").

Fixes #92352

raw.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #124617: "Update all instances" (and the single-connection managed SSH
update) aborts with a generic, unhelpful error whenever the remote drain
probe reports anything other than success — including the deliberate,
security-motivated refusal on Darwin remotes, which fires on *every* managed
update against a macOS box.

## Root cause

`buildOwnedTerminationCommand()` builds a Python probe that signals its
outcome two ways at once: it prints a status word to stdout (`TERMINATED`,
`ALREADY_STOPPED`, `REFUSED`, `DARWIN_UNAVAILABLE`, `UNAVAILABLE`, `TIMEOUT`)
**and** exits with a matching non-zero code (2, 3, or 4) for every outcome
except the two exit-0 ones.

`SshConnection.exec()` (`ssh-connection.ts`) throws for *any* non-zero remote
exit code before the caller ever sees stdout. So `terminateOwnedDashboardForUpdate()`'s
own classification of the probe's stdout (`result === 'REFUSED'`,
`result === 'DARWIN_UNAVAILABLE'`, ...) is dead code for every one of those
outcomes: `ssh.exec()` throws first, and the generic catch-all fires instead:

```
Could not terminate the Desktop-owned remote serve for update.
```

That's exactly the message in the issue. On a Darwin remote this isn't
occasional — the script's Darwin branch unconditionally prints
`DARWIN_UNAVAILABLE` (by design, to avoid a PID-reuse race), which means the
generic error fires on every attempt, and the remote is never updated.

Every *other* status-reporting probe in this file (`buildOwnedStaleTerminationCommand`,
`pidIsOurDashboard`, `remoteProcessCreationTime`) already follows the
"always exit 0, let stdout carry the status" convention — this one script is
the outlier.

## Fix

Change the four non-zero `sys.exit()` calls in `buildOwnedTerminationCommand()`'s
probe to `sys.exit(0)`, matching the established convention. `ssh.exec()` now
returns the real stdout for every outcome, so the existing, previously-dead
classification logic in `terminateOwnedDashboardForUpdate()` runs as written
and reports the actual reason (e.g. "Darwin cannot atomically bind a signal
to the verified PID; refusing termination.") instead of the generic message.

No change to the ownership/security checks themselves — the Darwin refusal
is still a refusal, it's just reported correctly now instead of being
swallowed into an opaque transport error.

## Test

Added a regression test that proves the defect end-to-end: it drives the
*real* termination probe (real `python3` subprocess, not a canned mock)
against a live-but-unrelated local process, so the probe's actual exit code
— not a hand-written string — is what reaches `terminateOwnedDashboardForUpdate()`.
The existing test double in this file (`fakeSsh`) always resolves with a
canned string regardless of exit code, which is why this bug was never
caught by the existing suite.

```
apps/desktop/electron/remote-lifecycle.test.ts
  ✓ managed update drain reports the real POSIX refusal, not a generic transport error
```

Confirmed the test fails without the fix (reverted only `remote-lifecycle.ts`
to its pre-fix state, kept the new test, and reran):

```
AssertionError: The input did not match regular expression /identity changed at the signal boundary/. Input:
'Error: Could not terminate the Desktop-owned remote serve for update.'
```

With the fix restored, the same test passes and asserts the specific message.

## How to test

From `apps/desktop`:

```sh
npx eslint electron/remote-lifecycle.ts electron/remote-lifecycle.test.ts
npx tsc -p . --noEmit
npx vitest run --project electron electron/remote-lifecycle.test.ts
```

Full `--project electron` run: 312 test files passed / 4 pre-existing
failures unrelated to this change (missing `uv`, `ruamel`, and
`HERMES_PYTHON` in this sandbox's Python environment — confirmed identical
on unmodified `main`).

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contributing guide and searched open PRs for duplicates (none
  address this issue).
- [x] Limited the PR to this fix (+7/-7 in the source file).
- [x] Added a regression test and verified it fails before the fix and
  passes after.
- [x] Lint and typecheck clean.
- [ ] Full Python suite: not applicable (TypeScript/Electron-only change).

raw.body:
## What does this PR do?

Right after a new session is created, Desktop's transcript-timeline mount fetch
and its periodic active/tile transcript sync read that session's `timeline` and
`messages` REST endpoints — even though `session.create` is intentionally lazy
(`tui_gateway/methods_session.py::_create_session`): a brand-new session's
`state.db` row is only written on the first prompt. Opening a "New chat" tile
and not typing into it yet therefore produces a burst of `404 Session not
found` reads (`desktop.log`: two before the first send, 28s apart in the
report, plus the ones racing the send itself), with no gate that recognizes
"this session was just minted by this window and has nothing to fetch yet".

This matches the exact mechanism already named for the Bot Mode canonical-chat
path (`plugins/hermes-bots/canonical-chat.ts`: *"session.create is intentionally
lazy: its stored row does not exist until the first prompt. Mounting `sid`
immediately therefore emits a noisy REST 404"*) — Bot Mode works around it by
eagerly titling (and thereby persisting) its one canonical row. An ordinary new
chat can't do that (the backend deliberately does NOT persist an empty draft
row — see the long comment in `_create_session`, "drafts left 'Untitled'
litter"), so the fix here is on the read side: don't ask for a transcript we
already know cannot exist yet.

## Mechanism

Reused the existing `createdThisRun` bookkeeping in
`use-session-actions/index.ts` (already tracked so a flapping/respawning
backend's 404 on a *just-made* session isn't misread as "deleted" —
`goneSessionVerdict`), moved it into its own tiny module
(`use-session-actions/created-this-run.ts`) so a lean transcript-reading hook
doesn't have to pull in the whole session-actions import graph, and added one
guard at each of the three places that read a session's transcript before
anything was submitted:

- `components/assistant-ui/thread/use-timeline-history.ts` — the 200ms
  post-mount `loadMore()`.
- `app/contrib/hooks/use-background-sync.ts::reconcileActiveTranscript` — the
  reconnect backstop / `sessions.changed` background poll for the active pane.
- `app/contrib/hooks/use-background-sync.ts::reconcileTileTranscripts` — same
  poll, for an open workspace tile.

Each guard is the same shape: skip the read when `sessionCreatedThisRun(id)`
is true AND the local view still holds zero messages. Once the user sends
anything, the local view becomes non-empty and the guard falls away — the
backend row exists (or is about to) by then, so a normal read is correct.
`hydrateStoredSessionTranscript` (the post-turn "stream carried no answer"
fallback) is untouched: it always runs *after* a prompt has been submitted, so
the row already exists there.

## Related

Refs #123622. Prior PR #123830 tried to fix this by loosening the
stale-transcript guard's length comparison, but a maintainer closed it after
reproducing directly on `main`: the guard itself was not misfiring for this
case, and "its real ask (the pre-persist request noise) is separate from the
guard." This PR addresses that real ask directly — no request, no 404, no log
noise — without touching the guard.

```
npx vitest run --project ui \
```

raw.body:
Deleting a session from the sidebar could leave its turn running — and a blocked approval / clarify / sudo / secret prompt (plus its native notification) could surface for a conversation that no longer existed. This makes delete end the turn first, on every delete path, and makes the renderer refuse to park a blocking-input card for a runtime it has already stopped.

## Symptom → cause

`removeSession` (`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/index.ts`) gated runtime teardown on selection:

```ts
const closingRuntimeId = wasSelected ? activeSessionIdRef.current : null
```

A **non-selected** (background) session therefore never sent `session.close` at all. And even the selected path only sent `session.close`, which finalizes the runtime (joins the run thread for a bounded grace, releases the slot, interrupts delegations) but never walks the interrupt path: `tui_gateway/session_lifecycle.py::_interrupt_session_turn` is the only place that calls `request_hard_interrupt`, `_clear_pending` → `server_requests.cancel`, and `resolve_gateway_approval(..., "deny", resolve_all=True)`. A run blocked on an approval outlived its sidebar row.

On current `main` this also blocks the delete outright: `session.delete` now refuses a row whose turn still holds the write lease (4023, #123583), so a running background session could not be deleted without stopping it first.

## Fix

- `removeSession` resolves the doomed runtime from the selection **or** `runtimeIdByStoredSessionIdRef`, marks it interrupted locally (`interrupted: true`, `needsInput: false`), sends `session.interrupt`, flushes its approval/clarify prompt state, then `session.close`, then the row delete. RPCs route by the row's owner (`requestForSessionProfile`), matching the existing delete/close contract. A "session not found" from the interrupt is tolerated (`isSessionGoneError` — no turn left to stop); any other interrupt failure restores the live state and the delete rolls back, leaving the row in the sidebar.
- Blocking-input requests for an interrupted runtime are **answered, not parked**: `server-requests.ts` gains `declineIfSessionStopped` on approval / sudo / secret / vault.code / vault.save_login / vault.unlock_prompt, which fails the request with a JSON-RPC error. The channel contract treats an error reply as "unanswered" — the same result the backend's own `request.cancel` produces — so the blocked tool returns immediately instead of waiting out its deadline. The clarify handler's interrupted branch already answered; the family now matches. `connection.request` (an event, no reply channel) is dropped under the same flag in `input-requests.ts`.
- Not a UI change: no new strings, no locale updates.

All desktop delete entry points (sidebar row, session tile, command palette "delete selected") go through `removeSession`. The Settings › Sessions permanent delete of *archived* rows calls the REST delete directly; those rows have no live runtime in this window and the backend refuses a live one anyway, so it is unchanged.

## Tests

- `use-session-actions.test.tsx`: deleting a non-selected session resolved from the runtime map sends `session.interrupt` then `session.close` for that runtime only, and sets `interrupted: true` before the first RPC; an interrupt failure that is not "session gone" sends no close, no delete, restores the live state, and keeps the row.
- `server-requests.test.ts`: an approval for an interrupted session is failed (not parked, `respond` untouched); one for a live session still parks with `fail` untouched.

Both new-behavior tests fail against `origin/main`'s production files (`session.interrupt` never called; approval parked).

Credits [@jonpol01](https://github.com/jonpol01) PR #75616 (closed) for the interrupt-before-close approach and the interrupted-session guard idea; this ports it onto the current `gateway-event/` split plus the non-selected-runtime resolution.

Fixes #75587

raw.body:
## What

Adds `plugin-catalog/openltm.yaml` — OpenLTM as a Hermes memory provider.

OpenLTM gives a Hermes agent durable long-term memory in a local SQLite database:
FTS5 full-text search with optional sqlite-vec vector recall, importance-weighted
decay, a queryable memory graph, and automatic capture.

## Automatic capture

Capture is a declarative rule engine rather than ad-hoc keyword lists. One ordered
rule table classifies each turn as a correction, constraint, preference, decision,
or agent-discovered fact, and distils it into a single self-contained declarative
sentence (speech markers stripped, negations preserved). Constraints are evaluated
before preferences so a rule like "Always use Bun, never npm" is stored as a
constraint (importance 4), not downgraded to a soft preference.

Named guards keep noise out: `is_transient_operational()` rejects runtime
notifications, and `is_read_only_memory_request()` rejects messages that are only
read-only OpenLTM bookkeeping. A *mixed* message still passes, so a constraint
stated alongside "call openltm_context" is kept.

`eval` time aside, capture policy is verified by 33 stdlib `unittest` tests that
need no third-party package and no Hermes runtime.

## Security notes for the reviewer

- **Secret redaction on every write.** The write path scrubs API keys, tokens, JWTs,
  private keys and connection strings before any database insert or dedup check.
- **No self-updating code** (catalog rule 3). The plugin contains no fetch, no git
  operations, and no remote loader. The only network egress is the optional
  embedding providers (Gemini / OpenAI / Ollama), which are disabled by default and
  require the operator to configure them.
- **No required environment variables** — `requires_env` is empty; it runs with zero
  configuration.
- **All data stays local** in `~/.hermes/openltm.db`. No cloud, no telemetry.
- **Declared capabilities match the pinned commit** (catalog rule 6): 8
  `openltm_*` tools and 7 hooks, all cross-checked against the plugin source by an
  automated validator.

## Admission checklist

| Requirement | Status |
|---|---|
| Owner-submitted | this PR is from the plugin repo's owner |
| Public, cloneable repo | https://github.com/RohiRIK/OpenLtm |
| Released (real tags) | yes, `v2.14.2` and later |
| Exact 40-hex SHA pin | yes |
| Passing validation | entry validated against `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` rules |
| Not self-updating | yes |

## Install

```bash
hermes plugins install openltm
```

Docs: https://github.com/RohiRIK/OpenLtm/blob/main/docs/10-hermes-plugin.md

raw.body:
## What

`hermes update` restarted whatever systemd unit a hand-started dashboard happened to be launched under, instead of respawning the dashboard, and left the dashboard down. Tracked in #124938.

`_get_systemd_service_for_pid` returned the `.service` leaf of the PID's cgroup. A cgroup only says where a process was started: a dashboard started from a shell that runs under some unit (the GitHub runner agent `hosted-compute-agent.service`, `cron.service` for an `@reboot` crontab line, a tmux or IDE user service, the gateway's own terminal tool) sits in that unit's cgroup. The stop phase then skipped the argv capture, ran `systemctl restart <that unit>`, and never brought the dashboard back. Where the restart is permitted (root), it restarts the unrelated service: cron, the gateway, a tmux server with every shell in it, or the CI runner.

## Fix

The unit is claimed only when its live `MainPID` (read-only `systemctl show --property=MainPID`, scope taken from the cgroup path) **is** the dashboard PID. Otherwise the PID takes the manual path: argv captured before the kill, respawned after the update. That is also what the update's own plan already predicted for these rows (`manual-serve` / `respawn-argv`, from the spawn ledger), so the plan and the stop phase now agree.

Units that exec the backend (`ExecStart=… hermes dashboard|serve …`, including the PM shell shim, which `exec`s) keep MainPID == backend PID and are still restarted through systemd. A wrapper unit whose main process is NOT the backend (e.g. `uv run hermes dashboard`) now goes down the argv respawn path. This trade-off is deliberate: from the cgroup alone such a unit cannot be told apart from a foreign unit, and a respawn that fails is reported, where restarting an unrelated service is not recoverable.

## Tests (2 new cells, one parametrized test)

`tests/hermes_cli/test_update_stale_dashboard.py::TestSupervisedBackendRestart::test_only_the_unit_whose_main_process_is_the_backend_is_restarted`
- `[foreign-unit-cgroup]`: the dashboard's cgroup is `hosted-compute-agent.service` and the unit's MainPID is another process, so no `systemctl restart`, and the dashboard is respawned from its argv. **Red on origin/main**: `restarted a unit that does not supervise the dashboard: [['systemctl', 'restart', 'hosted-compute-agent.service']]`.
- `[unit-main-process]`: MainPID is the dashboard, so the unit is restarted and nothing is respawned (the supervised path is unchanged).

Only the systemctl edge (`_run_probe`) and the process table are faked.

## E2E proof

Suite PR #124876, cell `tests/e2e/core/upgrade/handoff/test_handoff_from_head.py::TestFromHead::test_dashboard_is_back_on_its_port`, run inside a transient systemd user service (`systemd-run --user --wait …`, which is how CI hosts every job):
- origin/main plus the suite: the update prints `⚠ handoff-svc-svc-base.service: systemctl restart returned non-zero` and the cell fails exactly as on CI (`.x.xFxx`). The suite gates it on #124938.
- the suite plus this fix, same transient unit: no unit restart, the dashboard is respawned on its port, and the cell **passes** (`3 passed, 4 xfailed`, the same as the suite run from a login session).

Once both land, the HEAD column's cell flips from xfail to pass, and the suite's `DASHBOARD_GATES["head"]` entry is deleted. The N-1 column keeps its #124938 gate until a release carrying this fix becomes N-1, because the updater under test there is the old release's.

`tests/hermes_cli/test_update_stale_dashboard.py`: 33 passed, 3 skipped. Two cells (`test_all_failed_stops_do_not_claim_the_dashboard_was_stopped`, `test_cleanup_failure_is_isolated_and_recorded`) fail on this dev box both with and without the fix. They trip `home_io_guard` because the worktree lives under `~/.hermes`, so the failure is the box, not this change.

Fixes #124938 (related: #121156 point 3, which reaches the same restart through an argv false positive).

raw.body:
## Root cause

A cron run is finalised by `cron/scheduler.py::_finalize_cron_session`, which calls `SessionDB.end_session(...)` inside a `try/except` that only `logger.debug`s on failure. When the run is killed by the inactivity watchdog (or crashes on a provider/connection error), no code runs at all — the session row keeps `ended_at` NULL while no agent owns it. The desktop's orphan reap stamps it later, sometimes hours after.

Both desktop Cron surfaces rendered every run row as a clickable tile that resumed it as a normal desktop chat:

- `src/app/chat/sidebar/cron-jobs-section.tsx` → `onOpenRun(run.id)` → `onResumeSession`
- `src/app/cron/index.tsx` (`CronJobRuns`) → `onOpenSession?.(run.id)`

Neither consulted liveness or `source`, so clicking (or auto-restoring) such a run resumed it as a writable chat and the composer routed the user's messages into a dead `source='cron'` session, where the cron agent executed unrelated desktop work under the cron identity.

## Behaviour

Opening a cron run is now gated on the run being **live** (`is_active` — the scheduler's agent is still executing it) or **properly closed** (`ended_at` set). This needs no backend change: the runs endpoint already computes `is_active` as `ended_at IS NULL` **and** `last_active` inside a 300 s window (`hermes_cli/web_routers/cron.py`), so a zombie (never closed, not running) is distinguishable from a live run — and a backend that omits the flag fails safe (read as zombie → view-only).

- **Zombie run** → still opens, so the failed run's output stays one click away, but it is latched read-only *before* the route flips. `use-prompt-actions/submit.ts` now refuses the send with the existing read-only explanation ("This chat is open as a read-only transcript — sending is disabled"), exactly as the #94724 no-owner path already does. No user message can be routed into the dead session, and starting a fresh chat is the way forward.
- **Live / closed run** → unchanged, fully writable.
- The latch lives in its own `$readOnlyCronRuns` set: the #94724 owner-recovery latch is cleared by a successful live resume, which would evaporate this guard the moment the transcript painted. `isStoredTranscriptReadOnly` reports both, so every write path gets one answer.
- One policy owner (`openCronRun` / `isResumableCronRun` in `src/app/cron/open-cron-run.ts`) serves both surfaces, so they cannot drift.
- The latch is honoured on every desktop write path, not only the primary chat: the tile delegate's `submitToSession` (open in split / new tab) previously refused sends only for synthetic `read-only:` runtime ids, so moving a latched run's transcript into a tile reopened the write path. It now reads `isStoredTranscriptReadOnly` too — the same answer `submit` gets.

Reuses the existing read-only stored-transcript machinery from #94724 rather than inventing a second "view-only" concept.

## Acceptance coverage

- `src/app/cron/open-cron-run.test.ts` — policy truth table (live, closed, zombie, older-backend fail-safe) and the latch-before-open ordering.
- `src/app/chat/sidebar/cron-jobs-section.test.tsx` — renders the real sidebar run peek: zombie click → `onOpenRun` called **and** session latched read-only; closed click → not latched; live click → not latched; rendering alone latches nothing; script-only output rows stay non-clickable.
- `src/store/read-only-transcript.test.ts` — the cron latch blocks `isStoredTranscriptReadOnly` and survives a live resume clearing the owner-recovery latch.
- `src/app/contrib/hooks/use-session-tile-delegate.test.ts` — a tile submit into a latched cron run is refused (no `prompt.submit` on any gateway, read-only notice shown).

## Validation (all run in a fresh worktree off `origin/main` @ ddb56d0)

```
$ cd apps/desktop && unset PYTHONPATH && npm run typecheck
typecheck exit=0

$ npx vitest run --project ui src/app/chat/sidebar/cron-jobs-section.test.tsx \
    src/app/cron/open-cron-run.test.ts src/store/read-only-transcript.test.ts
Test Files  3 passed (3)
     Tests  19 passed (19)

$ npx vitest run --project ui src/app/cron src/app/chat/sidebar \
    src/store/read-only-transcript.test.ts src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions
Test Files  58 passed (58)
     Tests  638 passed (638)

$ npx eslint <changed files>       # clean
$ npx prettier --check <changed files>   # all files use Prettier code style
```

Behavioural probe (repro before / pass after), by reverting only the click handler:

```
# onClick={() => onOpenRun(run.id)}   (pre-fix)
     × opens a never-closed run (ended_at NULL, not live) READ-ONLY
AssertionError: expected false to be true
 Test Files  1 failed (1)   Tests  1 failed | 4 passed (5)

# onClick={() => openCronRun(run, onOpenRun)}   (post-fix)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  5 passed (5)
```

## Issue reference

Refs #88443 — the desktop half (requirement 2: "the desktop sidebar should not allow resuming a cron session that was never properly closed … at minimum, clicking a cron run should open it read-only, not route new messages to it"). This does **not** claim the scheduler-side guarantee (requirement 1: booking `end_reason`/`ended_at` when the process is killed) — that close is inherently best-effort for a watchdog kill, so it is left to the cron owner's judgement instead of being closed by a `Fixes` keyword.

Not covered here (deliberately out of scope, say the word and I'll fold it in): the guard is client-side and in-memory, so a *restored* route/tab that already points at a zombie run is resumed writable again after an app restart. Closing that needs the gate at the resume boundary (resolve the row there and refuse a live resume of a never-closed cron run), which is a larger change to `use-session-actions`.

raw.body:
Follow-up to the catalogued plugin (owner-submitted pin bump, catalog rules 4 and 5).

Pin: 17734a4049d24f5f705b4451c57ae40cc3fb4d57 -> b7ab470b51a2915e19e4df52bb80cd5973c1b0ca
Version: 1.0.4 -> 1.0.5
Release: https://github.com/soyelmismo/hermes-antigravity-subscription/releases/tag/v1.0.5

Commits adopted in range (`v1.0.4..v1.0.5`):

• `b7ab470` release: v1.0.5
• `9bb0849` feat: increase default context length to 200,000 tokens with env override
• `f94b2bc` fix: prune historical tool outputs, bound context length, and classify pubsub stalls

### Root Cause

Sessions with 100+ turns failed with:
```text
Antigravity model error: the connection to the agent was interrupted before the response finished:
subscriber fell behind updates, stalled for 5s
```

`agy` runs an internal Go language server (`jetski/cortex`) that streams state to the CLI over gRPC (`StreamAgentStateUpdates`). On every token or step, the server serializes the cumulative trajectory to Protobuf and sends it over an in-memory channel (`third_party/jetski/cortex/agent_state_component/pubsub.go`).

When Hermes sent unpruned prompts exceeding 500 KB (~140k tokens):
1. Ingestion latency increased while `agy` ran internal trajectory checks.
2. Token generation re-serialized the 500 KB trajectory on each step, flooding the Go channel at 50+ MB/s.
3. The channel consumer failed to drain within the 5-second deadline in `pubsub.go:78`, and the publisher dropped the stream.
4. Hermes catalog metadata lists `gemini-3.8-flash` with a 1,048,576 token window. At 140k tokens, Hermes saw 13% context use and never ran `context_compressor`.

### Changes in v1.0.5

1. **Tool output pruning (`prompt.py`)**
   - In failed sessions, old tool outputs (test output, diffs, directory trees) accounted for 85% of character volume (375 KB of 600 KB).
   - The prompt builder keeps the last 8 tool results intact and caps older tool outputs at 300 characters with a truncation marker.
   - A 20k character limit with head and tail preservation guards individual tool calls.
   - This cuts wire payloads by 70% (600 KB down to 180 KB), keeping Go channel throughput within the 5-second drain window.

2. **Context window bound (`__init__.py`)**
   - `get_model_context_length` now returns 200,000 tokens (overridable via `ANTIGRAVITY_CONTEXT_LENGTH`).
   - This aligns the Hermes context compression threshold (80% = 160,000 tokens) with `agy` throughput limits.

3. **Error classification (`__init__.py`)**
   - `classify_api_error` matches `subscriber fell behind updates, stalled for 5s`, `context canceled`, and empty SUCCESS status.
   - Returns `{"reason": "context_overflow", "retryable": True, "should_compress": True}`.
   - If a pubsub stall occurs, Hermes compresses the session and retries instead of failing after 3 attempts.

### Validation

• Plugin repo CI: 185 passed, 1 skipped on Linux against `HERMES_REF v2026.9.21`.
• `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/antigravity-subscription-directsdk.yaml` passed (1 file valid).
• `hermes plugins validate /root/.hermes/plugins/antigravity-subscription-directsdk` passed (safe, declared capabilities match).
• Manifest version 1.0.5 matches git tag `v1.0.5` and catalog entry.

raw.body:
## Summary

Adds `hermes-routines` to the plugin catalog, pinned to
`aa055f5851a9e9cacd0e8516f56c58f62c639292` (tag `v0.1.0`).

**Hermes Routines** is a standalone Desktop plugin that puts a
plain-language Routines page in front of the host's five
`cron.manage` actions. A non-developer names a routine, picks a
schedule from a small set of options, writes the prompt, and pauses or
resumes it — no crontab syntax, no field ordering to remember, and no
timezone or interval grammar to get wrong. Routine data stays in the
Hermes host; the plugin ships no service, database, or updater.

This PR adds the entry and, below, the reasoning and evidence a reviewer
needs for it.

## What the plugin does

The host exposes exactly five `cron.manage` actions: list, add, remove,
pause, resume. Reaching them directly means hand-writing a schedule
string and knowing which field holds what. This plugin sits in front of
them and gives each concept one surface:

| Crontab concept | What the user does |
| --- | --- |
| schedule expression | picks **Weekdays**, **Daily**, an interval, or a one-time date |
| command / prompt | writes plain text |
| enabled flag | toggles Active, or uses pause / resume |
| job list | browses, searches, and filters a list of cards |

Each routine card shows its schedule, next run, last run, and last result.
Selecting a row opens a read-only inspector that mirrors the composer
without exposing technical fields.

Current limits, stated plainly: no delete, no edit mutation, and no
run-now action. The row Edit control opens the inspector only.

## Why it is shaped this way

**Minimalism is the product, not a skin.** The plugin contributes zero
tools and zero hooks. It registers a page, a sidebar row, and a composer.
There is nothing for the agent to call and nothing that can act without
the user. A scheduling surface that a model can quietly rewrite is a
different product than one the user owns.

**Fail-closed routing.** A request without a resolved profile route is
rejected rather than sent to an unintended gateway. There is no fallback
to the active gateway.

## Entry

```yaml
name: hermes-routines
repo: https://github.com/crdesign8/hermes-routines
sha: aa055f5851a9e9cacd0e8516f56c58f62c639292
tier: community
category: desktop
version: "0.1.0"
platforms: [linux]
capabilities:
  provides_tools: []
  provides_hooks: []
  provides_middleware: []
  requires_env: []
```

Decisions worth a reviewer's attention, each against the admission policy:

- **Rule 2 — exact SHA.** Pinned to the `v0.1.0` tag commit, not the
  annotated tag object (`539aa26…`). The loader checks out a commit.
- **Rule 3 — no self-updating code.** The artifact contains no `fetch`,
  no remote `import()`, and no update path; the only URLs in the source
  are inline `data:` URIs for CSS masks. Users move between versions only
  through a SHA-bump PR here, per rule 4.
- **Rule 6 — declared capabilities match reality.** Zero tools, hooks,
  middleware, and env vars. `plugin.yaml` declares the same.
- **Rule 7 — the install scanner runs at admission.** At the pinned
  commit, `hermes plugins validate` reports `security scan — safe`, not
  `caution`, so there are no warnings to review past. An earlier commit
  reported `caution` from three scoped uninstall commands in the docs
  (the `destructive_home_rm` rule matches `rmdir ... $HOME` regardless of
  path scope); those are prose now, which is why the verdict is `safe`.
- **Rule 8 — desktop surface.** `validate` passes its `desktop surface`
  check: the artifact imports only `@hermes/plugin-sdk` and React, with
  no prototype patching, no `eval` / `new Function`, and no dynamic
  `import()`.
- **Rule 5 — owner submission.** The author owns the plugin repository.

Two fields deliberately left out:

- **`requires_hermes` is omitted.** The plugin does not declare a
  minimum and none has been established, so any floor would be invented.
  Comparable tool-less desktop entries (`agent-analytics`, `agent-log`)
  omit it too. Happy to add one if a reviewer can point at the release
  that introduced the surface this plugin uses.
- **`screenshot 02` is not in the gallery.** It is a portrait capture
  (420×813) and reads badly in a landscape gallery. The two landscape
  captures are included; the full set stays in the README.

## Verification at the pinned commit

```
npm test    -> tests 226, pass 226, fail 0
npm run check -> allowlist ok / check-version ok 0.1.0 /
                 check-manifest ok / check-label-policy ok /
                 check-generated ok
npm run build -> desktop/plugin.js 123381 bytes, in sync
hermes plugins validate . -> Validation passed (security scan: safe)
```

`tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_catalog.py` (11),
`test_plugins_hub_live_catalog.py` (2), and
`test_web_plugins_catalog.py` (2) pass with this entry added. The entry
parses through `entry_from_mapping()` with no dropped fields and no
warnings, and all four image URLs return HTTP 200 at the pinned commit.

The repository is public: https://github.com/crdesign8/hermes-routines
Release: https://github.com/crdesign8/hermes-routines/releases/tag/v0.1.0

The author is on a solo-maintainer flow here and is happy to iterate on
naming, the description, or the platform declaration.

raw.body: Fixes the native About panel reporting Version 0.0.0. Closes #124581. Related reports cited in the issue (#39248, #123117) are not fixed here. Task slug mentions skill fan-out; the live issue 124581 is the About-version bug and that is what this fixes. Mechanism: desktop package.json carries a 0.0.0 placeholder on main; real versions come from channel builds and the live backend (/api/health). Two paths leaked the placeholder: (1) appVersionInfo fell back to packageVersion when no display version was baked, or returned empty for offline source installs, which macOS renders as the bundle 0.0.0; (2) the native panel was seeded with applicationVersion empty. The fix skips placeholder values (empty, 0.0.0, v0.0.0, unknown) across every version candidate in appVersionInfo, and routes both native-panel writes (startup seed and showAboutPanelFresh) through a new nativeAboutVersion helper that maps unknown to an explicit label (backend spelling git.<short> with .dirty suffix, else the word unknown). The renderer keeps its empty-means-unavailable contract. RED-to-GREEN: 3 new tests in electron/app-version.test.ts failed on origin/main fb2dded (got 0.0.0, want 1.2.3; nativeAboutVersion missing) and pass with the fix (8/8 in file). Neighbors: gateway-version, bootstrap-state, payload-backend, commit-stamp-identity pass (17 passed). channel-build-version.test.ts (3 tests) fails identically on pristine base and with the fix - environmental (bare python without HERMES_PYTHON venv; temp-dir fixture resolving ./node_modules/app-builder-lib), unrelated. tsc on the electron project reports no errors in the touched files (11 pre-existing errors in untouched files from missing optional-dep types). Risks: offline source builds now show git.<sha> in About instead of 0.0.0 - truthful by design. No i18n keys added; the native panel stays English like its existing hardcoded strings.

raw.body:
Chore: advance the `desensitize` catalog pin to `2dbf63d`, version `1.0.0` → `1.4.0`.

Five commits upstream (`yubingz/hermes-desensitize`), following the review of #122574.

### `acd1263` — English default for command output

Review asked for an English default on the `/desensitize` feedback, which was Chinese-only. Now bilingual, English first: the `on`/`off`/`model`/`timeout`/`chunk` confirmations, the `status` field labels (e.g. `Engine / 主引擎`), the error strings, and the `model` sub-command usage block.

### `6385779` — make the output language configurable

Hardcoding the bilingual form still left an international user with English interleaved with Chinese and no way to turn the Chinese off. It is now an option:

```yaml
ui:
  language: both   # both (default) | en | zh
```

or `DESENSITIZE_UI__LANGUAGE=en`.

| `ui.language` | `status` first line |
|---|---|
| `both` (default) | `Status / 脱敏状态: ...` |
| `en` | `Status: ...` |
| `zh` | `脱敏状态: ...` |

Default is `both` rather than `en`: the plugin targets Chinese-language conversation, so `both` drops no reader while `en` hides the Chinese from most of its actual users. `en` exists for someone who cannot read Chinese at all.

### `8dc7c75` — `/desensitize lang` and English help

An in-session switch:

```
/desensitize lang en|zh|both
```

It deliberately does not persist — language is a session preference, and writing it to disk leaves a surprise behind on the next terminal or locale.

Help now follows its own `ui.help_language` (default `en`) instead of `ui.language`. Help is what a user reads when they do not yet know the plugin, often before any language is configured, so its default is the one readable by everyone. See `2dbf63d` below for one refinement: an explicit choice in-session now also moves the help.

### `bea37d3` — install/upgrade docs

Warn that a backup directory placed **inside** `~/.hermes/plugins/` is loaded as a second plugin under the same name. In practice the loaded copy was the backup, so a newly added sub-command looked like it had no effect. The README now says to replace the plugin directory wholesale, to keep backups outside that path, and how to print the plugin key/version the process actually loaded:

```python
from hermes_cli.plugins import PluginManager
pm = PluginManager(); pm.discover_and_load()
print([(p['key'], p['version']) for p in pm.list_plugins() if 'desens' in p['key']])
```

### `2dbf63d` — help follows an explicit choice; unknown subcommands report themselves

Four fixes, each traced to a user reporting the command "did nothing":

- **help follows an explicit `/desensitize lang <x>`.** `ui.help_language` remains the default for a user who has not chosen yet, but once they pick a language in-session the help follows it. Previously setting `lang zh` left the help in English, which reads as "the command did not work".
- **`lang` accepts the natural spellings** — `cn` / `中文` → `zh`, `english` / `英文` → `en`, `双语` → `both`. Accepting only the three canonical literals turned the spelling a user would actually type into an error receipt, which looks the same as a broken command.
- **Unknown subcommands announce themselves.** A notice line in the session language, with a `difflib` suggestion (`Unknown subcommand 'sta' — did you mean 'status'?`), now precedes the usage block; the usage block still follows `help_language`. Previously an unknown sub-command silently printed the usage, so someone who typed `leng` saw a screen of English and no indication of the typo.
- **`lang <invalid>` keeps the current value** instead of dropping back to `both`; the old receipt also claimed "kept: both" while changing it. Receipt wording "this session" → "this run": the value is process-global, `/new` does not reset it, restarting Hermes does.

Consequence for the `ui.language: zh` note above: help is no longer unconditionally English under `ui.language: zh`. It stays English until the user explicitly picks a language, and follows the choice afterwards, so the "readable before any language is set" property is preserved.

### One string is deliberately not translated

`[xxx数量级N]` is the placeholder actually written into redacted text (`plugin.py`). It is a value, not a label; it must stay byte-identical in every language or the `transform_llm_output` restore fails to match. The test pins this.

### Verification

- `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/desensitize.yaml` → `OK: 1 file(s) valid`
- All 6 upstream test scripts pass against `2dbf63d` (`test_behavior_parity`, `test_config`, `test_desensitize`, `test_plugin_behavior`, `test_regex_regression`, `test_ui_language`) — exit 0 each
- `test_ui_language.py` asserts each mode changes the output, that `en`/`zh` carry no characters of the other language (placeholder excepted), that `lang` switches and keeps its value on a bad argument, that the aliases resolve, that an unknown sub-command emits the notice before the usage block, that help follows an explicit in-session choice, and that both settings are driven by the config layer via env var and file. The notice line and the usage block are asserted separately, because they follow different languages.
- `test_behavior_parity.py` now loads `tests/fixtures/original_desensitize_20260817.py`. It previously loaded the installed `~/.hermes/plugins/desensitize/__init__.py` as a top-level module; after that directory was reinstalled with the package layout the file became a package root (`from .plugin import ...`) and the test failed at import — red for a reason unrelated to behaviour, and dependent on one machine's install state. The original 39 KB single file is archived as a fixture, so the comparison is reproducible.
