Opt-in shared metrics grow from 8 to 61 bounded counters that answer product questions: why tasks, tools and model calls fail, which features people keep and which they turn off, where setup stops, how accurate the agent loop is, what a task costs, how updates and platforms behave, and what gets used in Desktop. Hermes Desktop also gets a first-run consent question.

## Changes

**Failure and usage (first slice)**
- **Model routes** (`hermes.model_route.count`) gain `call_role`, `outcome`, `error_class` (the classifier's own `FailoverReason`) and `ttft_bucket`.
- **Task runs** carry `platform`; `task_run.finished` carries `failure_class`. Raw exit reasons stay on the machine.
- **`hermes.tool.usage.count`**: per-tool outcome and error class. Only names in `toolsets.BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES` are exported; MCP tools report `mcp`, plugin/custom tools `plugin`.
- **`hermes.install.snapshot`**, once per 24 h: memory provider plus bucketed counts of MCP servers, plugins, skills, cron jobs and profiles, install age, UI language, gateway count. No names.

**Decision data (this round)**
| Metric | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| `hermes.session.count` (entrypoint, surface, platform, turn / failed-turn / duration buckets, last outcome) | How deep real usage is per surface; do sessions end right after a failure? |
| `hermes.install.milestone` (milestone, install-age bucket), once per install | Time from install to first success, first gateway message, first cron run, first delegation, first long session. |
| `hermes.setup.completed` (surface, provider) | Which providers people pick at setup, on which surface. |
| `hermes.model_tokens.sum` (role, model, provider, aux task, token type) | Token volume, prompt-cache share, and what auxiliary work costs. |
| `hermes.compression.count` (trigger, outcome, context-fill bucket) | How often compaction runs and fails, and how full contexts get. |
| `hermes.model_switch.count` / `hermes.fallback.count` | Which providers people leave, and how often fallback rescues a turn. |
| `hermes.slash_command.count` (command, surface) | Which built-in commands get used (`/retry`, `/undo`, `/new` as friction signals). |
| `hermes.extension.install.count` (kind, source, name, outcome) | Which catalog skills, MCP servers and plugins get installed. |

Every dimension is a closed enum, a bucket, a provider Hermes ships (with that provider's public model id), or a name Nous itself publishes (`shared_metrics_catalog.py`: bundled/optional skills, `optional-mcps/`, `plugin-catalog/`, the slash registry). Anything else collapses to `custom` / `unknown`.

**v4 + v5 additions (51 new metrics, 3 widened)**
| Area | Metrics | Question it answers |
|---|---|---|
| Model quality | `model_friction`, `model_tool_quality`, `context_peak`, `model_switch_after`, `model_reply_issue` | Which models stall, emit bad tool calls, run out of context or get abandoned mid-session |
| Updates and exits | `update.run`, `update.stage`, `process.exit`, `startup.latency` | How long updates take, where they fail, how often Hermes exits uncleanly, how fast it starts |
| Platforms | `platform.health`, `platform.delivery`, `gateway.reply_latency` | Which messaging adapters drop, fail delivery or answer slowly (relay replies labelled by the platform the message came from) |
| Agent machinery | `memory.op`, `delegation.run`, `curator.run`, `cron.run`, `execution_backend`, `terminal.outcome` | Whether memory, subagents, cron and terminal backends work in practice |
| Harness accuracy | `file_edit`, `loop_guard`, `tool_recovery`, `tool_unavailable` | Edit match rates, loop-guard trips, recovery after a failed tool call |
| Efficiency | `task_cost`, `wasted_tokens`, `cache_break`, `tool_overhead`, `tool_output_truncation`, `tool_enabled_unused` | Calls/tokens per task, tokens spent on failed work, prompt-cache breaks, schema overhead, toolsets enabled but never used |
| Engagement | `engagement.day`, `engagement.surface_day`, `feature_adoption`, `provider_setup` | Active days per install/surface (one session per conversation across compression), time to adopt features, where provider setup stops |
| Feature signals | `feature_disabled` | Defaults users turn off (skills, plugins, toolsets, settings), and removals |
| Desktop | `desktop.mode_use`, `desktop.action_use`, `desktop.feature_use`, `desktop.friction`, `desktop.dislike`, `desktop.onboarding` | Bot vs Sessions mode, closed-allowlist action counts, and objective dislike proxies: fast closes, cancelled flows, rage clicks, undos, settings changed away from default |

No new UI: dislike and friction come from behaviour Desktop already observes. Action ids are a closed code-defined allowlist, daily aggregates only. The daily snapshot keeps three coarse hardware fields (RAM range, GPU type, local model server yes/no). Azure deployment names leave only when they are a public model id (`gpt-4o`); anything else reads `custom`. Cron runs never count as user activity.

**Where each event is recorded**
- Slash commands: CLI `process_command`, messaging gateway `_handle_message` (once per event, queued replays marked), ACP, and the Desktop and Ink TUI dispatchers through a new fire-and-forget RPC `shared_metrics.slash_command`, so commands the clients handle locally (`/new`, `/branch`, `/skin`, `/resume`) count too. Alias re-dispatches and the TUI slash worker replay are not counted.
- Compression at `_emit_compression_attempt_telemetry`; fallback at `_try_activate_fallback`; `/model` switches at each surface's commit point (internal swaps pass `count_switch=False`).
- Extension installs in `skills_hub.do_install`, `mcp_catalog.install_entry`, the connectors catalog backend, custom `mcp add` (CLI, dashboard, TUI) and `plugins_cmd_install.recorded_install`. Reinstalls, updates and cancels are not counted.
- Setup completion from `hermes setup` (full, quick, portal) and the Desktop first-run answer.

**Consent**
- Desktop: an offer strip in the composer status stack (Send to Nous / Local only / No thanks / Details). It never blocks the composer or takes focus, waits for onboarding, and stays until answered. Settings › Safety › Privacy & network gets both toggles. New RPCs `shared_metrics.status` / `shared_metrics.set` use the same config keys and consent reconciler as `hermes setup`, so a profile answered in one place is never asked again.
- CLI consent copy and the developer docs list every new category.

**Row budget**: `task_run.finished` keeps outcome, end reason, termination, failure class, entrypoint, surface and platform; duration and retries move to `hermes.task_run.duration`, and per-task call counts live on `task_cost`. `tool_call.count` keeps category, outcome and approval; latency and retries move to `hermes.tool_call.latency`. Otherwise almost every task and every few tool calls became a row of their own.

**Local store**: outbox files are compact JSON, and once the ingest accepts or refuses a package the database drops its copy of the body (the file stays as the local history). Pending packages keep theirs for resends.

**Schema**: packages move to `hermes.shared_metrics.v3`; v2 field sets of model-route, tool-call and task counters still validate, so counters recorded before an upgrade drain.

## Data volume

Simulated days through the real store and package builder (`record_counter` -> `create_and_export_package`), bytes as the sender posts them (gzip over 4 KB). Skewed draws are realistic; uniform draws are the ceiling for that activity.

| Profile (per day) | Rows | On the wire | Local disk, 30 days |
|---|---|---|---|
| light: 1 session, 5 turns, 15 tool calls | 121 | 2.7 KB | 3 MB |
| typical: 4 sessions, 40 turns, 250 tool calls | 650 | 6.8 KB | 13 MB |
| heavy: 20 sessions, 300 turns, 3k tool calls | 2,347 (was 2,788) | 17.7 KB (was 21.0) | 44 MB (was 102) |
| extreme: 250 sessions, 13k tool calls | 5,047 (was 6,561) | 33.6 KB (was 46.0) | 102 MB (was 272) |
| peak: 750 sessions, 37k tool calls | 8,011 (was 11,566) | 51.2 KB (was 79.9) | 171 MB (was 522) |

Uniform ceiling: heavy 64 KB, peak 181 KB on the wire. The ingest treats payloads as opaque and the rollup is generic over dimensions, so the split counters need no server change.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Live: `scripts/smoke_nemo_relay_shared_metrics.py` (real `hermes chat`, real NeMo Relay binding, fake model server, packages checked against the v3 JSON schema, prompt/response/tool canaries absent) | pass; package carries `session.count{turn_count_bucket=1,last_outcome=success}`, `install.milestone{first_task_success, lt_1h}`, `model_tokens.sum{input=20,output=2}`, `model_route{ttft_bucket}` |
| Live: real `hermes chat` under tmux: `/help`, `/version`, `/exit`, then `hermes setup --quick` | `slash_command{help,cli}`, `{version,cli}`, `{quit,cli}`, `setup.completed{cli}` |
| Live: real `AIAgent._compress_context`, `_commit_model_switch`, `tui_gateway._apply_model_switch`, `_try_activate_fallback` | one row each; slash-worker replay and `count_switch=False` not counted |
| Live: local skill, MCP catalog, custom MCP and `file://` plugin installs, then reinstalls | one row each; reinstalls leave every count at 1; custom names read `custom` |
| Live: real `tui_gateway.entry` over stdio, Desktop + TUI slash RPC | `branch`, `skin`, `journey` (desktop), `resume`, `new` (tui); unknown aliases `unknown` |
| Live Desktop (Electron build, Playwright on Xvfb) | strip shows after onboarding, composer accepts typing while it is pending, Details closes without recording, "Local only" saves and retires the strip |
| New invariant tests (each red on the base it targets) | sessions/milestones, token sums, CLI + gateway slash once, compression once, fallback once, MCP + plugin install once, slash RPC once, Desktop local command once / alias never, Desktop consent strip |
| `tests/hermes_cli`, `tests/gateway`, `tests/tui_gateway`, `tests/agent`, `tests/acp_adapter` (fake HOME) | no new failures; the remaining failures (update, plugin install, home guard) fail identically on the base branch |
| Desktop `check:lint` / related vitest; ui-tui typecheck + vitest | 0 errors / 1059 passed; 1581 passed |
| ruff, windows footguns, compat pointers, no-`/tmp`, gateway contract staleness | clean |
| v5 head `a82134cbb62`: live relay smoke (real `hermes chat`, v3 schema, canaries absent) | pass; agent-created skill records no adoption row |
| v5 head: shared-metrics, relay, gateway platform, smoke, contract suites (fake HOME, -n 8) | 543 passed |
| v5 review fixes: each new invariant test red on its base | B1, B2, M6, M13, m12, m16, ARN/alias collapse |
| v5: Desktop `check:lint` / onboarding + settings vitest | 0 errors / 87 passed |
| Row budget + local store: live relay smoke on the rebased head (real `hermes chat`, v3 schema) | pass; store holds `task_run.finished` (7 fields), `task_run.duration`, `tool_call.count` (3 fields), `tool_call.latency`; outbox files compact |
| Row budget + local store: shared-metrics, relay, gateway platform, smoke suites (fake HOME, -n 8) | 525 passed; the two new invariant tests fail with their guarded code removed |
| Rebase over #126139 (intro cinematic removed): Desktop `check:lint` / metrics + consent + hooks vitest | 0 errors / 163 passed |

## Independent review

A read-only privacy review with probes found five issues, all fixed in `39513b5fd94`:
- **Custom provider names leaked** (`custom:<config key>` into six provider fields, including the model route already on main). Providers now pass only when Hermes ships them; custom, unknown and loopback providers read `custom`, and so does their model id. Path- or URL-shaped model ids read `custom`.
- **Milestones took the launch profile's install age** under multiplex; the subscriber now captures its own home.
- **Gateway session summaries** arrived only at shutdown for auto-reset sessions; route transitions now close them.
- The dashboard MCP add recorded inside the config lock; it now records after.
- Helpers moved out of `conversation_compression.py` / `run_inbound.py`.

Existing assertions changed (each asserted the old leak): `test_model_call_fields_report_terminal_model_and_shipped_provider` (unshipped provider now `custom`), `test_real_binding_drives_lifecycle_aggregation_export_and_snapshot` (custom endpoint model id now `custom` and prohibited in the output), and the smoke script's model counter.

## Second independent review (v4 + v5)

A read-only privacy and correctness review of the integrated v5 branch (with probes) found 2 blockers, 15 majors and 24 minors; five fixer lanes plus a finishing pass closed them:
- **B1, user provider plugin names leaked.** Provider plugins under `$HERMES_HOME/plugins/model-providers/` (and pip) registered into the live provider registry, so `acmecorp-internal` and its model ids left verbatim. The allowlist is now built from shipped providers only; those plugins read `custom`.
- **B2, sessions undercounted after compression.** Lineage joining followed `/new`, `/branch` and gateway-reset parent links, so distinct conversations merged into one session row. Only compression rotations join now.
- Majors: cron excluded from active time/profiles, midnight rollover idempotent, Desktop state per profile and deduplicated across windows, crash rows respect opt-out, provider-setup funnel transitions, terminal `timeout` only on Hermes' own deadline, delivery rows land in the profile that owns the chat under multiplex (M6), Desktop provider forms flag their key saves so Gemini/xAI/DeepInfra connections still count (M13).
- Minors of note: `host:port` / IP / `localhost` model ids, AWS ARNs and loopback-provider aliases (`lm-studio`) collapse to `custom`; an opt-out from the CLI drops Desktop onboarding latches; SQLite writes retry on a busy lock.

Left as-is (documented): a user plugin re-registering a shipped provider name (e.g. its own `openrouter` proxy) reports that public name with its model ids; a relay turn the connector did not stamp keeps task/session `platform=relay`.

## Server side

`NousResearch/telemetry#4` (regular PR, not merged) fixes the rollup job shrinking older days on each run, stamps `computed_at` on every row, and adds weekly retention cohorts (D1/D7/D14/D30) plus feature-segmented retention from a per-install first-seen index kept in S3. It needs an IAM grant on `state/v1/*` and one backfill run after deploy.

## Infographic

![Shared Metrics v3](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aac257e/xyuEex46UNqcaOny6gHEK_MriHd4C8.png)

raw.body:
Adds **agora** to the plugin catalog.

`repo: https://github.com/yzy806806/agora` (public, MIT) · `sha: 2f87b19c5d862201897aea6c0b212932ef3a4e49` (`v2.0.3`) · submitted by the repository owner.

## What it is

A self-driving multi-agent development team. Role-based workers (architect, developer, reviewer, tester, researcher, writer, devops) are each a **real Hermes profile** with its own SOUL.md and skills. They discuss and vote on decisions, and the adopted conclusion is executed by the same team. A `leader` profile chairs the discussions; a heartbeat cron wakes it to assess state, unblock workers and plan the next phase.

Discussion and execution share one board — deliberately no second storage system:

- A **motion** is a sub-task of a per-project *team channel* task (a persistent kanban task pinned in `scheduled` status, so the dispatcher never claims it).
- Speech and votes are `[agora:msg]` JSON **comments** on that task (same convention as upstream `[swarm:blackboard]`).
- The conclusion is written to `task.result`; an adopted conclusion becomes **execution tasks parented to the motion**, so context reaches workers through Hermes' own parent handoff rather than any leader transcription.
- Worker state is plain kanban status — the dispatcher schedules work exactly as it does for any other task.

Ships 20 tools, 3 kanban lifecycle hooks (`kanban_task_completed` / `_claimed` / `_blocked`), a dashboard tab + REST routes, and an `hermes agora` CLI.

## Admission checks

- **No self-updating code** — the plugin never fetches or replaces its own files, and does not read GitHub releases or shell out to `hermes plugins update`. Updates reach users only through a SHA-bump PR here.
- **No third-party dependencies** — no `pyproject.toml`, no `python_dependencies`; only stdlib plus packages Hermes already ships (`yaml`/`fastapi`/`pydantic`, imported lazily or under `try/except ImportError`). So there is no dependency-floor question to settle.
- **Capabilities match reality** — `provides_tools` lists all 20 registrations, `provides_hooks` all 3; `provides_middleware` and `requires_env` are empty (verified: the plugin registers no middleware and requires no environment variables of its own).
- **Security scan clean** — `hermes plugins validate` on a fresh clone at the pinned SHA: exit 0, 13/13 checks pass, `security scan — safe` with no `caution` findings.

## Disclosure — what the plugin reads and writes

- **Creates a Hermes profile per worker**, copying the global `config.yaml` into it and symlinking the global `.env` (so workers use the operator's model credentials).
- **Spawns `hermes -p <profile> chat` subprocesses** to speak in discussions and to run dispatched tasks. These run as full agents with that profile's toolset, meaning model calls under the operator's own provider credentials, and terminal/file writes **inside the configured project workdir** (which is how the team writes code).
- **Reads and writes the kanban database** — `tasks`, `task_comments`, `task_events`, `task_runs`, `task_links` — including the persistent team-channel task, and deletes a project's tasks when it is stopped or completes (deliberate clean-slate behaviour, documented in the README's *Stop & Cleanup*).
- **Registers one recurring cron job** and writes its runner script to `HERMES_HOME/scripts/leader_heartbeat.sh`.
- **Writes `AGENTS.md`** into the configured project workdir (regenerated on heartbeat, motion create/close and project updates).
- **Deploys three bundled skills** (`agora-setup`, `agora-awareness`, `agora-deliberation`) into `~/.hermes/skills/collaboration/`.
- **Serves a dashboard tab and REST routes** through the Hermes dashboard.
- **No network egress of its own** — all model traffic happens inside the spawned subprocesses under the operator's credentials. No telemetry, no author-hosted endpoints.

## Notes

- `requires_hermes: ">=0.20"` — 2.0 is developed and verified against v0.20.x (including the September 2026 module decomposition; `agora/kanban_compat.py` bridges both the old and new import layouts so a single build works on either).
- Dashboard UI is English-first; the repo README is bilingual (Chinese default, `README_EN.md` mirror), and `readme: true` renders it at the pinned SHA.
- Happy to adjust the `description`, `category`, or anything else in the entry — and to re-pin whenever a new release lands.

Re-pins `memory-rewind` from 1.0.0 (`130ec1f`) to **1.2.0**. The PR is three commits, and each one changes only `plugin-catalog/memory-rewind.yaml`:

| Commit | Pin | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `bump memory-rewind to 1.1.0` | `41bbdee` | provenance in `log`, lock-file fix |
| `bump memory-rewind to 1.2.0` | `bca0cef` | `/memory-history`, fix for lost same-second edits; one clause added to the description |
| `memory-rewind catalog card` | `b747327` | `image:`; the pin adds only `docs/card.png` to 1.2.0 |

Upstream range: https://github.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-memory-rewind/compare/130ec1f...b747327. Nothing else changes: disclosure, `category: general`, hooks and `requires_hermes`.

## 1.1.0

- **`hermes memory-rewind log` shows what produced each version.** Every version records the tool call behind it and the session and platform it came from:
  - the call is summarised as tool, actions, memory target or skill names, plus the outcome unless it is `ok`;
  - both `operations` and flat call shapes are read with each tool's precedence;
  - the platform is learned from `on_session_start` / `on_session_end` and never guessed;
  - model-supplied values are reduced to safe tokens, and message or file content is never recorded.
- **Fix: skill lock files are no longer recorded.**
  - **Before.** Every `skill_manage` call creates `skills/.locks/*.lock` and `skills/.usage.json.lock`, so 1.0.0 added a version holding only a lock file after each call.
  - **Now excluded:** those files, plus `skills/.curator_state` and `skills/.termux_bundled_sync_stamp`. `.locks` is one of the dirs Hermes' own `EXCLUDED_SKILL_DIRS` skips.

## 1.2.0

- **`/memory-history`, a read-only view from any chat.** It works on gateway platforms, Desktop, TUI and the CLI chat.

  ```text
  /memory-history                     the last 10 versions
  /memory-history user                versions of USER.md (also memory, soul, skills/<path>)
  /memory-history <version> [target]  what that version changed
  ```

  - **Profile.** `HERMES_HOME` resolves when the handler is called. The gateway runs each message under its routed profile's scope and runs sync handlers with `copy_context()`; the TUI/Desktop wraps `command.dispatch` in the session's home scope. So each profile sees only its own history. A test drives this through `get_plugin_command_handler`, and the real `command.dispatch` RPC was checked for sessions of two profiles on v0.21.5 and `main`.
  - **Read-only.** Viewing never records a version. Restore stays a host command, and the version view prints the exact `hermes memory-rewind restore <version>~1 <file>` line.
  - **Format.** Plain text, like the bundled `disk-cleanup` command. Replies are capped at 3,000 characters, the budget `/skills diff` uses in chat.
  - **Group chats.** A reply never includes host paths or raw git errors. The README notes that a reply is visible to the whole chat, as `/memory pending` already is.
  - **Name.** `/memory-history` does not collide with a built-in command on either release.
- **Fix: edits that kept a file's size could be lost.**
  - **Cause.** Snapshots copied the cached git index with a fresh mtime, which defeats git's racy-git check. So an edit made in the same second as the previous snapshot, keeping the file's size, looked unchanged. Its content was not recorded, and the newest version kept the old bytes.
  - **Measured.** In a stress loop of rapid same-size edits, 2/480 edits were missed on the current code and 5/480 on 1.1.0. With the fix: 0/1200.
  - **Fix.** Every copy now keeps the index file's mtime, with a deterministic regression test for each copy site.

## Catalog card

`image:` points at `docs/card.png` at the pinned commit. It is 1200×600, the 2:1 frame the Desktop catalog card uses, and shows real `/memory-history` output. The file sits outside the plugin directory, so installs do not carry it. The raw URL returns HTTP 200 `image/png`.

Footprint is unchanged:
- No new hooks, tools, dependencies or network access; the only addition is the read-only `/memory-history` command.
- Writes nothing outside `plugin-data/memory-rewind/`.
- No self-updater.
- The install-time scanner reports the same single finding at every pin: medium `python_subprocess` at `gitstore.py:102`, the local `git` call.

## Checked

- **Plugin CI 8/8 at 1.2.0** ([run](https://github.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-memory-rewind/actions/runs/36321828846)):
  - end-to-end against Hermes v0.21.5 and `main`: 159 passed each, security scan safe;
  - unit tests on Linux, macOS and Windows × Python 3.11 and 3.14.
- **`plugin-catalog-ci.yml` replayed locally at `b747327`:**
  - `validate_plugin_catalog.py` with `ruamel.yaml==0.18.17`: 334 files valid;
  - pinned-source validate: clone, pinned sha, `plugins validate --install-deps`, self-updater gate.
- **Install from this branch's catalog.** `hermes plugins install memory-rewind` installs revision `b747327` as 1.2.0. `/memory-history` registers and answers, and `hermes plugins info memory-rewind` shows the image.
- **A real turn (1.1.0).** One `AIAgent` turn against the scripted loopback provider on v0.21.5 and `main`, platform `telegram`, recorded the `via`/`from` lines.

raw.body:
## Symptom

Every conversation started by hand in Bot Mode disappears. Right-click a bot → **New chat with this bot** (or the Bot Mode tab-strip `+` / ⌘T), talk to it, close the tab — the chat is gone:

- no row in the Sessions sidebar, under the bot's profile or under **All profiles**
- not offered by `/resume`
- not reachable from the bot row (that opens the canonical Bot Chat) and not from **Open recent session** either, because that reads `last_session`, which never reports a hidden row

So there is no way to find, rename, or delete a bot conversation you started yourself. Reported on Discord ("Chats in Bot mode": *"I don't know how to remove a chat with a bot, and if I make a new chat with the bot, I will not see this chat in the future"*), and reproduced earlier in #91740 with a controlled experiment that isolated the Bots-tab creation path as the deciding variable.

## Root cause — one line

`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/index.ts`, in `openNewSessionTile`:

```ts
...(workspaceScope.workspaceMode === 'bots' ? { hidden: true } : {})
```

The flag is applied to the whole mode, but this path only ever mints **side chats**. Both callers prove it:

- `sdk/index.ts` → `newChat(route, { workspaceMode: 'bots' })` → `$newSessionTabAction` — the roster context menu's "New chat with this bot"
- `app/contrib/wiring.tsx` → `openNewSessionTab()` — the tab-strip `+` / ⌘T while Bot Mode owns the workspace

Bot Mode's **plumbing** sessions never come through here; each mints its own row and sets the flag itself — the canonical Bot Chat in `plugins/hermes-bots/canonical-chat.ts` (`title: 'Bot Chat', hidden: true`) and group member sessions in `plugins/hermes-bots/group-turns.ts`. So the blanket flag hid nothing that wasn't already hidden, and hid every side chat forever.

## Why this is a bug and not the design

Three places in the tree already say side chats stay listed:

- `apps/desktop/src/AGENTS.md`: side chats *"are not plumbing-titled, **stay visible in the sidebar**, and are never the row's target"*
- `plugins/hermes-bots/session-sweep.ts`: the hide sweep's title allow-list is exact on purpose — *"a user's real conversation inside a bot profile keeps whatever title the user gave it and is never touched"*. The birth flag defeated that care.
- the maintainer ruling closing #91740: *"Side chats started via 'New chat with this agent' are NOT hidden and remain reachable in the Sessions sidebar; only the canonical row is."*

The canonical Bot Chat's unconditional hiding is untouched, and so is every invariant around it: one bot = one forever-chat identified by the `Bot Chat` title, no session-id pin, recency never wins.

## The fix

Drop the blanket flag. Nothing replaces it, because the sidebar concern it was reaching for (#113273 — hidden rows resurrected by the refresh keep-list) is already handled where it belongs: `mergeSessionPage` and `sessionsToKeep` in `store/session.ts` drop `hidden === true` rows, so a canonical Bot Chat cannot re-enter the list no matter what holds it live.

`listTileSessionRow`'s Bot Mode guard (`app/chat/session-tile-actions.ts`) stays as-is — the canonical chat does reach it, and it must not seed an optimistic row for a hidden session. A side chat therefore surfaces on the next list refresh once its first turn persists, exactly like a Sessions-mode ⌘T tab created with `listed: false`.

## Result

A Bot Mode side chat behaves like any other conversation: it appears in the Sessions sidebar under the bot's profile (or All profiles), `/resume` lists it, and its row menu offers Rename / Archive / Delete. Deleting a bot's hand-started chats no longer needs `state.db` surgery.

## Test plan

- New invariant test in `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions.test.tsx`: drives `openNewSessionTile` with a bots workspace scope and the bot's own route (the exact shape both callers use) and asserts `session.create` carries no `hidden` param. **Red on the unfixed tree** (received `hidden: true`), green after.
- The neighbouring bot-workspace test lost its incidental `hidden: true` assertion; its actual subject (the ambient composer selection is not leaked into a bot tile) is unchanged.
- `npx vitest run src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions.test.tsx src/app/chat/session-tile-actions.test.ts src/plugins/hermes-bots/ src/store/session.test.ts` → 93 files, 984 tests passing, including every Bot Mode canonical-chat contract test (`canonical-chat-registry`, `canonical-chat-creation`, `canonical-chat-adopt-on-conflict`, `bot-row-opens-canonical-chat`, `hide-bot-chats`).
- `npm run typecheck` (renderer project), `npx eslint`, and `npx prettier --check` clean on both changed files.

Refs #91740.

Fixes #105162

## What does this PR do?

`hermes update` on a systemd host never restarted `hermes-dashboard*` units: the systemd fleet-restart pass listed and name-gated only `hermes-gateway*`/`hermes-serve*`, and the abort-recovery serve pass enumerated `hermes-serve*` only. A systemd-supervised dashboard (`hermes-dashboard-<profile>.service`) therefore stayed on pre-update code after every update — the receipt recorded `outcome: deferred`, nothing ever restarted it, and the update still exited 0 with `outcome: success` (5 of 5 updates in #125297's receipts). The Desktop app then hits the stale dashboard over SSH (`/api/profiles` failing) until someone restarts the unit by hand.

The runtime-outcome reconciliation already credits `hermes-dashboard{,-<profile>}` unit restarts via `_serve_unit_matches_profile` — the unit pass simply never produced one, so this wires the existing sanctioned vocabulary into the two restart channels:

- the in-process systemd unit pass (`_LIST_GATEWAY_UNITS` glob + `_is_hermes_gateway_unit` name gate), and
- the fresh-process abort-recovery serve pass (`_UNIT_RE` + the `list-units` patterns in `update_restart_recovery.py`).

SIGUSR1 drain eligibility is intentionally unchanged: dashboard units don't run `gateway/run.py`, so like `hermes-serve*` they go straight to the blunt `reset-failed` + `restart`, which is what the workaround in the issue (`systemctl --user restart hermes-dashboard-<profile>`) already proved correct.

This mirrors the #83438 fix, which added `hermes-serve*` to the same pass for exactly this class of stale backend.

raw.body:
## plugin-catalog: add memex8 memory provider

Adds Ex8-ca/memex8 to the Hermes plugin catalog as a community-tier memory provider.

### What it is

memex8 is a self-hosted vector memory backend (Qdrant + TurboQuant compression) that gives the agent deep semantic recall across all past conversations and ingested documents. It replaces Hermes's built-in flat-file memory (MEMORY.md / USER.md) with:

- **Unlimited capacity** — vector store vs. 2,200-char hard limit
- **Semantic search** — relevance-ranked retrieval, not linear scan
- **Auto-discovered knowledge realms** — content clusters itself by topic
- **Slumber pipeline** — periodic memory consolidation, dedup, and verification
- **Hook integration** — implements `on_session_end` and `on_pre_compress` for durable checkpoint storage before lossy context compression
- **Cross-platform** — Rust core with REST API; works from any Hermes surface (CLI, TUI, gateway)

### Repo

- **URL**: https://github.com/Ex8-ca/memex8
- **Pin SHA**: `b5e87b7b9a537ec663dd0c5d68a5ebf819976abc`
- **Subdir**: `plugins/memex8`
- **Maintainer**: @Ex8-ca

### Plugin contract compliance

The plugin source at `plugins/memex8/` ships:

- `plugin.yaml` — manifest with `name`, `version`, `description`, `requires_env`, `hooks`
- `__init__.py` — implements `MemoryProvider` ABC and exports `register(ctx)` entry point
- **`pre_compress_checkpoint_api_version = 2`** — opts into the fail-closed pre-compress
  checkpoint contract. `on_pre_compress(messages, *, require_checkpoint)` synchronously
  archives the transcript to memex8; when the operator enables `compression.checkpoint_required:
  true`, a failure raises `RuntimeError` and BLOCKS the lossy rewrite. With the default
  (`require_checkpoint=False`), failures are logged and compression proceeds — matching
  the documented best-effort default for non-archiving providers, while the archive is
  still attempted on every cycle.
- **All background threads use `spawn_context_thread`** — `queue_prefetch`, `sync_turn`,
  `on_session_end`, and the `initialize` health probe. Bare `threading.Thread` runs with
  empty contextvars and would silently write to the default profile under multiplex;
  the host's wrapper propagates the spawning context so per-profile writes (config,
  secrets, logging scope) bind correctly.
- `README.md` — setup, configuration, and operations guide
- `docs/banner.png` — 1200×630 catalog card image

### Install/UX after merge

Users on Hermes `>=0.21.4` can run:

```bash
hermes plugins install memex8
hermes memory setup        # pick "memex8", enter MEMEX8_API_KEY + URL
```

…or configure manually in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:

```yaml
memory:
  provider: memex8
plugins:
  - memex8
```

…with secrets in `~/.hermes/.env`:

```
MEMEX8_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080
MEMEX8_API_KEY=<token>
```

### What this PR does NOT include

- No bundled-tree changes — memex8 lives in its own repo per Hermes's
  third-party-product policy (observability/SaaS plugins ship standalone).
- No auto-migration wiring — users upgrading from `memex8` referenced
  pre-catalog can re-install with the command above.
- No `config_schema.py` or `cli.py` — those would add a Desktop dashboard
  config panel and `hermes memex8 <subcmd>` tree. Optional; can land in a
  follow-up.

### Validation

- [x] Local `hermes plugins validate memex8` passes against `HERMES_HOME=/tmp/hermes-test`
- [x] `MEMORY.md` and `USER.md` continue to mirror to memex8 alongside the built-in store
- [x] Both YAML files parse cleanly; all required catalog fields present
- [ ] Catalog CI clone-and-validate expected to pass (will report via PR check)

---

**Checklist for reviewer:**

- [ ] `sha:` in catalog matches `origin/main` HEAD of `Ex8-ca/memex8` (currently `b5e87b7b`)
- [ ] `image:` URL resolves (raw GitHub CDN)
- [ ] `subdir: plugins/memex8` matches the actual repo layout
- [ ] `tier: community` is appropriate (no NousResearch sponsorship claimed)
- [ ] `category: memory` matches the `kind` of the plugin (MemoryProvider ABC)

raw.body:
Cron Python scripts can now run under a user-managed venv: `hermes cron create/edit --interpreter ~/venvs/x/bin/python`. Before this, a `script` / `monitor_script` always ran on Hermes' own Python, so `import openpyxl` (or any package the user installed) failed with `ModuleNotFoundError`, and a package installed into Hermes' venv disappeared on the next rebuild.

Salvage of #70500 by @M1racleShih (co-author @MestreY0d4-Uninter), which revives #8741. Closes #8714. The PR was ~21k commits behind and conflicted in all 6 production files: script execution has since moved to `cron/scheduler_script.py`, and the CLI and tool are now table-driven. The feature commit keeps the contributor's authorship and was re-applied to that layout.

## What changed

1. **feat(cron): external interpreter** (@M1racleShih, ported)
   - `cron/jobs.py`: `interpreter` goes through the existing field-normalizer tables; `""` clears it on edit.
   - `cron/scheduler_script.py`: `_resolve_cron_interpreter()` checks the path at run time (absolute or `~` path, regular file, executable on POSIX). `_script_argv` then runs `[interpreter, script]` and skips the managed-install bootstrap and PYTHONPATH additions, which exist for Hermes' own venv. A straight port would have put Hermes' repo onto the user's venv path (POSIX) or silently ignored the interpreter (Windows managed installs). The field is passed through all four script entry points: no-agent, pre-run, heartbeat wrapper, monitor.
   - CLI: `--interpreter` on `cron create` / `cron edit`; shown in `cron list` and job details.
   - `cronjob()`: available to the CLI and direct callers only, the same as `model` and `reasoning_effort`. It is not in the model-facing schema, so the always-sent tool description gains 0 characters and the model cannot choose an interpreter for unattended jobs.
2. **fix(cron): only accept a Python executable** (ours). The lifecycle guard treats a `.py` script as Python and skips its shell-reference walk. At the PR head, `interpreter=/bin/bash` plus a `.py` whose body is `bash restart.sh` was accepted and then executed as shell. Now the interpreter's name, and its symlink target's name, must match the guard's own `_INTERPRETER_IMAGE_RE`.
3. **refactor(cron): simplify after review** (ours). `pythonw` is refused because it discards captured output, which would make an agent job go quiet with no error. A cleared value is stored as null, like `workdir`. Minor tidy-ups.

Tests: I kept 2 of the PR's 34 tests (the end-to-end no-agent and monitor tests, which run a real wrapper interpreter) and added one parametrized test covering the 7 refusal cases. The rest were signature-order checks, mock-argument-only tests, a faked `sys.platform`, and argparse checks.

## Verification

- `tests/cron` + `tests/hermes_cli/test_cron*.py` + `tests/tools/test_cronjob_tools.py`: 1483 passed, 11 skipped (clean env).
- Full `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/`: every file that failed locally was rerun on this head and on its base on main (`6f7a7991bb`), in clones outside the real Hermes home. The failures are identical on both, 236 tests in 62 files, none only on this branch; all are host-environment failures that also happen on main.
- Mutation checks:
  - Ignoring the interpreter in `_script_argv` turns all 8 interpreter tests red.
  - Removing the Python-name check turns the bash and symlink-to-bash cases red.
- Live, real CLI, throwaway venv, temp `HERMES_HOME`:
  - With `--interpreter ~/extvenv/bin/python` the script imports the venv-only module (`EXTMARK-42`, venv prefix).
  - After `edit --interpreter ''` it is back to `ModuleNotFoundError`.
  - `interpreter=/bin/bash` on the `.py` wrapper fails at run time with "Interpreter must be a Python executable".
  - The same content as a `.sh` is still blocked at create.
  - The model handler drops an `interpreter` argument.
- Probe with a simulated managed-store install: with an interpreter set, argv is `[interpreter, script]` and the environment overlay is empty.
- ruff, windows-footguns, compat pointers and subprocess-stdin checks are clean. `ty` on the 8 touched files: 22 diagnostics, the same as main.

## Known limits

- The check is name-based: a non-Python binary renamed `python3` passes. The field is user-owned (CLI only), so this closes the accidental and agent-driven paths, not a deliberate local user.
- Free-threaded and debug builds (`python3.13t`, `python3.12d`) and PyPy are refused; the error says why.
- `~` expands against the scheduler process's HOME, which can differ from the CLI user's in container setups; the failure is a clear "not found".

## What does this PR do?

`_check_gates()` called `run_gate(gate)` with no `cwd`, so gates ran in the backend process's directory. In Desktop that's the default project or `$HOME`, not the session's workspace. A relative gate (`scripts/run_tests.sh …`, as the docs show) checked a different project, and when that project passed, the judge ran and a failing goal was saved as **done**.

`_gate_workspace()` resolves the directory once per check:

- **Session workspace declared and present:** gates run there.
- **No session workspace:** the existing resolution applies (`TERMINAL_CWD`, else the launch directory), so the classic CLI started inside the project is unchanged.
- **Session workspace declared but not a directory on this host** (deleted project, remote or container path): the goal pauses on that check with a reason naming the workspace, and no gate runs in the backend's directory. No retry is charged, since another agent turn can't fix a missing workspace.

## How this differs from #125377

#125377 uses `resolve_agent_cwd()`, which falls through to `TERMINAL_CWD` and then `os.getcwd()` when the declared session workspace doesn't exist (its docstring says so). That's the same false pass in another form: the gate runs in the backend's directory and can pass for the wrong project. `test_missing_session_workspace_pauses_instead_of_running_elsewhere` fails on #125377's head and passes here. The other two tests pass on both.

Tradeoff: in a session whose workspace is remote/container-only, a gate that `cd`s to an absolute host path used to run and now pauses the goal with the workspace message. Gates run on the Hermes host, so such a session has no local project for a relative gate to check, and I preferred failing loudly over a silent false "done". Happy to narrow this if you'd rather keep those running.

## Related Issue

Fixes #125369

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## How to Test

1. The issue's `repro_goal_gate_cwd.py`: on `main` it prints `gate recorded exit: 0 ran in: …/project-passing` and `goal status: done`. On this branch it prints `gate recorded exit: 1 ran in: …/project-failing` and `goal status: active | ✗ Quality gate failed`.
2. `tests/hermes_cli/test_goal_gates.py`: 3 new tests (session workspace used; missing workspace pauses without running a gate; no workspace keeps the launch directory). On `main` the first two fail.
3. Every test file that references goals/gates (59 files): 848 passed, 0 failed, 38 skipped.

raw.body:
Fresh Windows and Linux installs download ffmpeg again, and `pm update ffmpeg` can no longer write a pin that expires two weeks later.

**Why it broke.** BtbN deletes its daily autobuild tags after 14 days. It keeps the last build of each month for two years (`util/prunetags.sh`, and the "Release Retention Policy" in its README). Our pin was the daily `autobuild-2026-09-10-15-31`, which is now deleted. Where the artifact mirror is also refused (the regional 403 in #125350 and #122240), the install stops with an HTTP 404. `btbn_index` always picked the newest daily, so every `pm update ffmpeg` wrote a pin that would expire the same way.

**Changes**
- `pm/update.py` `btbn_index`: only month-end tags count. The current month's newest tag is skipped because the next daily build replaces it. In each finished month only the last tag counts. `latest` stays excluded.
- `pm/lock.json`: the 4 BtbN rows (win32-x64, win32-arm64, linux-x64, linux-arm64) now point at `autobuild-2026-08-31-13-27`, snapshot `n9.0.1-11-ge47273f4d9`. That snapshot matches the locked `9.0.1` label, and it is exactly what the new resolver picks against the live API. The sha256 values are GitHub's release digests. The source, build config, native arm64, x11grab and ffprobe are unchanged, and macOS and Termux rows are untouched. BtbN keeps this tag until about Aug 2028.

**Validation**

| | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| win32-x64 install, mirror forced to 403 | HTTP 404 | 145 MB `ffmpeg.exe`, sha OK, 85 s; rerun 0 s |
| linux-arm64 install, mirror forced to 403 | (same row class) | 108 MB `ffmpeg`, sha OK, 71 s; rerun 0 s |
| live `resolve_package(Ffmpeg, BtbN targets, "9.0.1")` | newest daily | `autobuild-2026-08-31-13-27` for all 4 targets |

- `tests/pm/test_ffmpeg_resolution.py` adds one invariant test. It fails if either rule is removed (current month, or older daily in a finished month); both mutations were checked red.
- `tests/pm/`: 778 passed, 39 failed. Every failing file fails the same way on origin/main (this macOS baseline).

**Who / when:** the original re-pin in #125371 was by @dskwe (Yuan Li), who is credited as co-author on the lock commit. That version pinned another daily tag, so it would have expired around Oct 11; this PR replaces it with the retained month-end build and fixes the resolver behind it. It supersedes the local re-pin approach in #125510, which I'm closing. Before, bumps were forced every two weeks; now a bump is a deliberate choice, needed about once a year at most.

raw.body:
The email adapter no longer accepts unauthenticated `From:` addresses under open access. On main, anyone could forge a sender and land in that sender's conversation.

Salvages #123256 by @dborosev. The auth fix is kept with dborosev as author; the follow-ups narrow the logging.

## Problem

With `EMAIL_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true`, or `GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true` with no allowlist, `_sender_accepted` returned early through `_open_access()` and skipped the authenticated-`From:` check. Each conversation and every reply is keyed on `From:`. A forged `From:` therefore puts the attacker's text into that address's session, and the agent emails its answer to the victim.

## Changes

- `plugins/platforms/email/adapter.py`: removes the open-access bypass and `_open_access()`, which had no other callers. Open access still admits any sender, but mail now has to pass the same `Authentication-Results` check (DMARC, or aligned SPF/DKIM) as allowlisted mail.
- Drop logging, so operators see what they can fix and public inboxes aren't flooded:
  - A granted sender with no `Authentication-Results` header logs a WARNING naming the opt-out (`platforms.email.require_authenticated_sender: false` / `EMAIL_TRUST_FROM_HEADER=true`). The text is unchanged from main.
  - No stamp from the pinned `authserv_id` logs a WARNING pointing at `platforms.email.authserv_id` (`EMAIL_AUTHSERV_ID`).
  - A failing verdict from an address in `EMAIL_ALLOWED_USERS` / `GATEWAY_ALLOWED_USERS` logs a WARNING with the verdict and no opt-out hint (broken DKIM, a forwarder breaking alignment). Main gave the opt-out hint here, which is the wrong fix for a failing verdict.
  - Everything else, such as forged stranger mail under open access, logs at debug.
  - The two reason strings are module constants shared by the verifier and the gate.
- Tests: the open-access cases were folded into the existing `TestDispatchDefersToGatewayAuthorization` admit/drop tables, which use the real gateway auth check. One caplog test pins the four log cases. Three formatting tests that only passed through the bypass now set `sender_authenticated: True`.
- Docs: `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/email.md` describes the new behaviour and the log lines.

Left out of #123256: the message-id sidecar and the transport-metadata commit. Neither is needed for the auth fix, and the metadata commit takes the event timestamp from the sender-controlled `Date:` header, which needs a separate review.

## Behaviour change

A public inbox whose mail server doesn't add `Authentication-Results` now drops all mail until the operator sets `require_authenticated_sender: false` or `EMAIL_TRUST_FROM_HEADER=true`. Each drop logs a WARNING naming that setting.

## Verification

- `tests/gateway -k email`: 99 passed, 1 skipped. Also green with `EMAIL_TRUST_FROM_HEADER` or `EMAIL_AUTHSERV_ID` set in the environment.
- Against main's adapter, the new open-access drop cases and the log test fail.
- Mutations: each behaviour commit has a red test (removing the listed-sender warning, warning on open-access forgeries, dropping the authserv hint, restoring the bypass).
- Probe through the real parse → `_dispatch_message` path, 21 cases: forged `From:` under both open-access variables is dispatched on main and dropped here. `dmarc=pass`, `require_authenticated_sender: false` and `EMAIL_TRUST_FROM_HEADER` are dispatched on both.
- `ruff check` is clean on the changed files.

Not covered: failing mail from pairing-approved contacts still logs at debug. Telling them apart from open-access grants would need a pairing-store lookup.

raw.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes a permanently non-convergent "Chat out of date" refusal loop on long, tool-heavy desktop chats (#123909).

Two consumers of the same session store hold incompatible assumptions:

- `boundRetainedTranscript` (`app/chat/transcript-retention.ts`, #77311) intentionally releases the store's **head**, keeping the live window plus one weight-budget page of slack. A tool-heavy coordinator transcript burns that budget quickly, so the trimmed store holds far fewer rendered messages than the session has.
- `messagesIfTranscriptBehind` (`lib/stale-transcript-guard.ts`) compared **authored counts**: the latest 120-row page (`includeCompacted: true`) folded to e.g. 85 chat messages vs a trimmed store of fewer than that. `85 > trimmed` → refuse the send and install the refreshed page → the next window-anchor move re-trims → the next send is refused again. Non-convergent by construction, and it survives reload/relaunch because hydration re-trims once the window cut is established. Short chats never cross the budget, which is why this only bites long heavy chats (including the canonical Bot Chat, which is a forever-chat by design).

The fix compares **tips, not totals**: when the last durable `rowId` of the local view equals the page's own last durable `rowId`, the view is current however much head retention has paged out — retention only ever releases the head, so the last durable row is always the live tail. A peer window's newer row still changes the tip, so the #65047 second-window protection is intact. The count comparison remains as the fallback when tips cannot be established (views/pages with no durable ids), matching the pre-fix behavior exactly on that shape.

## Related Issue

Fixes #123909

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/lib/stale-transcript-guard.ts` — added `lastDurableRowId` (last persisted row of a view, skipping unpersisted tail rows such as live stream bubbles) and a tip-equality short-circuit ahead of the count comparison in `messagesIfTranscriptBehind`; updated the doc comment to describe tip-first semantics.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/transcript-backfill.test.ts` — new `messagesIfTranscriptBehind retention tips (#123909)` block: trimmed-store-with-matching-tip is current, unpersisted tail rows are skipped when establishing the tip, a peer's newer row still refuses (#65047), and counts remain the fallback without durable ids.

## How to Test

1. `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/app/chat/transcript-backfill.test.ts` — should pass (32 tests, including the 4 new ones).
2. Confirmed the two tip short-circuit tests **fail against the pre-fix code** (`git stash push -- apps/desktop/src/lib/stale-transcript-guard.ts` → `2 failed | 30 passed`; restored afterwards).
3. Regression sweep across the affected surfaces, all green: `npx vitest run src/app/session/ src/app/contrib/ src/store/transcript-sync.test.ts src/app/chat/` → 2454 passed (one pre-existing suite failure, `sessions-pane-tab-title.test.tsx`, fails identically on an unmodified checkout — missing optional `@novnc/novnc` dep locally, unrelated to this change).
4. `npx tsc -p . --noEmit` and `npx eslint src/lib/stale-transcript-guard.ts src/app/chat/transcript-backfill.test.ts` are clean.

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/124857

## Problem
Right-click → Rename on a Bot Chat tab showed a "Renamed" toast, but the tab caption never changed.

## Cause
A canonical Bot Chat's caption comes from the roster label (`workspaceOwnerTitle`), not from the stored row title. The title "Bot Chat" is the chat's identity: the backend guard from #95397 refuses a user rename of a hidden canonical row. The Rename verb could never work there.

## Change
- `workspaceSessionRenameable()` in `workspace-scope.ts` uses the same discriminator as `workspaceOwnerTitle`.
- `SessionActions` gains an optional `renameable` flag. When it's false, the Rename item and its dialog are omitted, the same way `onPin`/`onBranch` are gated.
- `SessionTabMenu` computes it for tile tabs and the main tab. Sidebar rows keep Rename, because canonical chats are hidden there.

## Tests

- `tsc` and `eslint` are clean.

raw.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the "first send after laptop sleep bounces once with *Chat out of date*" gap (#125532).

When the machine sleeps with a Desktop chat open, agent replies that complete during sleep leave the open transcript behind, and the first send after wake is refused once by the pre-send stale-transcript guard (#65047 — working as designed). The existing reconnect backstop (#94779) cannot cover this: a socket that zombie-survives sleep never transitions `gatewayState`, so it never fires; and even on a normal reconnect its refresh is async, so a quick submit can beat it.

The fix catches up on **return**: a `visibilitychange`→visible / `window focus` event with the window actively viewed (`windowIsActivelyViewed`, same semantics as the existing `visiblePoll` safety nets) triggers the existing signature-gated `requestActiveTranscriptRefresh(true)`. This covers both reported gaps — the zombie-socket edge (no state transition ever happens, but the user must focus the window to type) and the async-race edge (focus necessarily precedes the first keystroke). The downstream `reconcileActiveTranscript` is signature-gated, so an unchanged transcript costs one cheap tail read, exactly like the #94779 backstop.

A 5s floor (`TRANSCRIPT_RETURN_REFRESH_MIN_GAP_MS`) collapses the visibilitychange+focus pair of a single return and rapid cmd-tab switches into one read per return. Messaging transcripts are excluded — they keep their own visible poll (unchanged behavior, per the existing "Desktop sessions never enter this effect" contract).

## Related Issue

Fixes #125532

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/hooks/use-background-sync.ts` — added a wake/return backstop effect after the #94779 reconnect backstop: on `visibilitychange`/`focus` with the window actively viewed and the gateway open (desktop session, not messaging), fire `requestActiveTranscriptRefresh(true)` at most once per `TRANSCRIPT_RETURN_REFRESH_MIN_GAP_MS`; exported that constant for tests.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/hooks/use-background-sync.test.ts` — three regression tests: one return (visibilitychange + focus) refreshes exactly once; repeats inside the 5s gap add no read while the next return after the gap refreshes again; a closed gateway does not refresh on return.

## How to Test

1. `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/app/contrib/hooks/use-background-sync.test.ts` — Observed result: 49 passed (46 pre-existing + 3 new).
2. Pre-fix failure check: `git stash push -- apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/hooks/use-background-sync.ts`, re-run with `-t "#125532"` — Observed result: 2 failed / 1 passed (the two behavioral tests fail without the fix; the closed-gateway test is defensive and passes either way). Restored afterwards.
3. Regression sweep: `npx vitest run src/app/contrib/ src/store/transcript-sync.test.ts src/app/chat/` — Observed result: 1422 passed; the one suite-level failure (`sessions-pane-tab-title.test.tsx`, missing optional `@novnc/novnc` dep) fails identically on an unmodified checkout and is unrelated.
4. `npx tsc -p . --noEmit` and `npx eslint src/app/contrib/hooks/use-background-sync.ts src/app/contrib/hooks/use-background-sync.test.ts` are clean.

Manual check of the reported scenario: open a chat, sleep the machine while a turn completes writing replies, wake and focus the app — the transcript catches up on focus, so the first send no longer bounces.

raw.body:
## Summary

The desktop voice conversation hardcoded its silence hold at 1,250 ms and ignored the existing `voice.silence_duration` config key that the CLI, TUI, and gateway capture paths already honour, so:

- a mid-thought pause cut the turn off and submitted a partial recording, with no way to raise the threshold (`hermes config set voice.silence_duration 10` had no effect on desktop),
- fast local STT/TTS stacks sat through a rigid extra second of dead air on every turn.

The loop now reads a `$voiceSilenceMs` nanostore seeded from `/api/config` on every refresh (the same `useHermesConfig` path as `voice.stop_phrases` and barge-in sensitivity), so config edits apply live without a restart. Two guards keep current behaviour:

- **Only a user-set value overrides the 1.25 s desktop hold.** `/api/config` merges `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, so an untouched install reports the backend default (3.0) rather than omitting the key; reading it unconditionally would triple the hold for everyone. A value equal to the `/api/config/defaults` payload keeps the tuned desktop default.
- **Malformed values fall back like the gateway's shape-safe lookup** — non-numeric, non-positive, or boolean (`true` must not coerce to 1 s) keeps the default.

The barge-in utterance endpoint reads the same atom live per frame instead of its own matching constant, so barge-in capture and the voice loop stay matched across config refreshes.

**Supersedes** (both read the key unconditionally, raising the hold from 1.25 s to 3 s for untouched installs; #85772 additionally coerces `true` to 1 s):

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/83572 — credit @chelsealong for the live-atom shape and the barge-in live read, both kept here
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/85772 — credit @Natetgmaxwell for the same shape and its tests

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/83518
Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/124760

## Test plan

- [x] New `applyVoiceSilenceMsFromConfig` tests proven red on base (import fails — the seam didn't exist) and green with the fix: user-set override (0.7 s → 700 ms, `'2'` → 2000 ms), untouched install keeps 1,250 ms (config == defaults, defaults endpoint unavailable, key absent, null payload), malformed values keep the default
- [x] `vitest run --project ui` on voice-prefs, voice-barge-in, use-voice-conversation, thinking-sound, voice-stop-word: 47 passed
- [x] `tsc -p . --noEmit` clean; eslint/prettier clean on touched files

raw.body:
## Summary

Update the existing community catalog entry for **Secure ENV Ingress from 0.5.1 to 0.6.4**, following the previous catalog update in #122836. This PR changes **one catalog YAML file only**; it does not modify Hermes core or install/configure a consumer.

- Old pin: `8f42ca9a66a98a446c21e193605a8ee18d5ca417`
- New pin: `78737e35e68e2b2954083d773b3ee8bcf926e921`
- [Full plugin review range](https://github.com/web3blind/hermes-secure-env-plugin/compare/8f42ca9a66a98a446c21e193605a8ee18d5ca417...78737e35e68e2b2954083d773b3ee8bcf926e921)
- Add the actual new `secure_operation` tool to declared capabilities, retaining `browser_vault` and `pre_gateway_dispatch`.
- Expand the catalog disclosure to cover code-field filling and administrator-installed consumer execution, not just Vault writes.

## Changes since the last catalog submission

### ENV profile compatibility (0.6.4)
- Restore `/senv <profile> <FIELD,...>` when configured operation consumers are present. ENV setup no longer rejects the separate consumers section, preserves it unchanged and still rejects unknown ENV settings. Consumer loading/validation is unchanged.
- Regression test reproduces the failure and verifies consumer preservation and unknown-setting rejection. The original direct-field command was also confirmed working by the user after restart.

### HTTPS form accessibility
- Disable password-generation/autofill hints on one-use masked inputs (`autocomplete="off"`). Browsers may ignore this hint; it is not a security guarantee.
- Improve initial/result focus, accessible status messages, validation-error association, and field clearing.
- The ordinary form's Tab-navigation fix was confirmed by a user on Windows + Chrome + NVDA; automated Chromium coverage does not establish every assistive-device scenario.

### Browser Vault and one-time codes
- Optional authenticator setup key in the login form, validated with the native TOTP generator before saving into Hermes' native encrypted Vault. Invalid keys do not create an unusable login. Invalid authenticated submissions consume the one-use capability.
- Standalone `browser_vault` `mode: "code"`: enter an email/SMS/authenticator code without supplying a username/password or saving a login. The plugin fills the captured page through the supervisor CDP connection, without persisting the code to Vault or `.env` or returning it to the model.
- Code results distinguish `filled` from successful site verification; the plugin does not explicitly submit the site form, although a site may auto-submit on input.
- Support localized verification-field markup, with regressions for missing/ambiguous fields and page/origin changes.

### Generic ephemeral secret operations
- New `secure_operation` tool accepts only an operation identifier and nonsensitive parameters. A one-use HTTPS form shows the bound action summary before secret entry. The secret is passed in memory to the registered consumer; only fixed status metadata returns to the tool, not consumer return values or exception text.
- Administrator allowlist in `plugins.entries.secure-env-ingress.settings.consumers`: reviewed Python file path, factory name, and SHA-256. The programmatic registration API remains available. No consumers are shipped/enabled by default; tool arguments cannot register a consumer or specify an arbitrary executable/URL.
- Profile-scoped registration, checked source bytes/hash/ownership/permissions, duplicate-name rejection, captured execution context, replay prevention and bounded result waiting. Consumer execution does not hold the runtime lifecycle lock.
- 0.6.3 fixes premature `unknown` after a one-use link was consumed while its callback was still running. The original deadline remains enforced; cancellation/expiry of an already-running action reports uncertainty rather than claiming the action stopped.
- [Consumer configuration and trust contract at the pin](https://github.com/web3blind/hermes-secure-env-plugin/blob/78737e35e68e2b2954083d773b3ee8bcf926e921/secure_env_ingress/OPERATIONS.md).

## Security boundaries and admission disclosures

- **Browser Use is compatibility mode, not exact named-tab binding.** 0.6.0 temporarily refused it; 0.6.1 restored the existing task-supervisor/page/origin checks. The final pin cannot prove that the captured supervisor page is the most recent named `browser_exec` session/tab/CDP endpoint. Same-origin named sessions can be confused. This limitation is documented, not claimed fixed; users must verify the actual target.
- **Consumers are trusted code, not sandboxed.** Configured external Python executes with gateway privileges. Its imports are not pinned by the top-level source hash. Consumers must enforce target integrity, bounded execution, idempotency and secret handling. This is an explicit privileged extension boundary, not self-updating plugin code.
- **Bearer links are authorization, not proof of submitter identity.** Anyone possessing a link can submit it. Registrations requiring a verified principal currently fail closed instead of silently accepting bearer-only submission.
- Cancellation/deadline cannot forcibly terminate an in-process consumer. `unknown` requires external result verification before retrying; `completed` means the trusted synchronous callback returned, not independent verification of every possible external side effect.
- Existing disclosure retained: `/senv setup` supplies installation instructions involving `sudo`, host packages and TLS setup after approval; the listener binds all interfaces by default; `pre_gateway_dispatch` observes gateway messages to bind commands to senders.
- Admission scanner result: **caution**, not suppressed. Findings in the setup skill: `curl_pipe_shell` at line 35 and `sudo_usage` at lines 14, 16, 23, 32, 36, 38. These are setup instructions, not automatic execution on catalog load.
- No private configuration, credentials, account identifiers, operational artifacts or local filesystem paths are included in this PR. The plugin does not replace its own code outside the catalog pin.

## Verification

- 0.6.4 release: **420 tests passed, 0 failed**; Ruff, build and diff checks passed. Installed package and manifest versions matched 0.6.4, installed-wheel HTTPS discovery and configured-consumer checks passed. Catalog structural and plugin admission validation were rerun for this update and passed, with the same disclosed scanner cautions.
- The following records describe the earlier cumulative 0.6.3 verification, retained for context:

- Catalog structural validator: **passed** for the changed entry.

raw.body:
## Problem

Bot-Mode deliveries spawn each DM/relay turn through the console script beside the caller's interpreter, so a long-lived caller pinned to an old dependency generation keeps launching that generation even after a newer one is selected. Plugin dependencies installed after the pointer was recorded are then invisible to every Bot Chat (`No module named 'hindsight_client'`), while the same profile works from the CLI.

https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/124868

## Root cause

`tools.bot_relay._hermes_cli()` prefers `sys.executable`'s sibling console script. Every Bot delivery path (`local_delivery_command`, local/peer `message_agent`) reuses it, so the spawned child boots the recorded generation's entrypoint instead of the installation-bound launcher whose bootstrap leases the currently selected generation at child start.

## Change

- `_hermes_cli()` now prefers this install's already-published `.hermes/bin/hermes` launcher (`hermes.exe` on Windows) — the same installation-bound command `hermes_cli/_launchers.py::installation_command()` persists for the systemd unit. Bootstrap/PM dependency selection stays owned by the launcher; no new selector.
- Interpreter-sibling, `shutil.which` and bare-name fallbacks remain for external/developer installs without a published launcher (#93590, #108628).
- Batch `.cmd` shims are never selected: `cmd.exe` reinterprets otherwise literal argv (e.g. an ampersand in a query-file path) even with `shell=False`.
- Existing fallback-ladder tests now isolate `bot_relay.__file__` so the checkout's own published launcher does not shadow the fallback they probe — without this they fail on any source install that has run the launcher publication step (found while validating the superseded PR on a real checkout; that PR's head reds `test_delivery_pins_the_hermes_entrypoint_beside_this_interpreter` and `test_bot_relay_windows_paths` in that environment).

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/124913 — same fix, cherry-picked with authorship preserved (`fix(bot-mode): prefer installation-bound delivery launchers`, `fix(bot-mode): avoid selecting batch shims for literal delivery argv` by @Wenfengcheng). The fallback-ladder test isolation and the base-`origin/main` rebase are added on top.

Credit: @Wenfengcheng for the resolver fix, the batch-shim guard, and the launcher test suite.

## Verification

Base `9fa23760bc` (current `origin/main`).

- RED on base: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_bot_delivery_install_launcher.py -q` → 1 failed (`test_delivery_prefers_install_launcher_over_old_generation`: resolver picked the old-generation sibling over the published launcher); reverted fix → 5 passed.
- GREEN with fix: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_bot_delivery_install_launcher.py tests/tools/test_bot_mode_dm.py tests/tools/test_bot_relay_windows_paths.py tests/tools/test_bot_retry_policy.py -q` → **97 passed, 0 failed, 7 skipped** (skips are `platforms('windows')` probes; they run on the Windows CI lane).
- Windows real-PM generation-selection test and native Windows validation were performed by the contributor on Windows (see superseded PR); this host (macOS) covered the POSIX paths.

## Non-goals

Batch-only Windows installs, dashboard service launchers, and the #106742 unified-gateway architecture that retires this transport are unchanged.

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/124868

raw.body:
Hermes no longer picks up the user's own `node`/`npm`/`npx`/`uv` when its PM-managed copy is missing. It provisions its own copy instead, or reports a clear error.

Maintainer ruling: *"only hermes and only packaged package managers (uv/pip/node/npm) should ever be used."*

## Changes
- **`hermes_constants.find_node_executable`**: `node`/`npm`/`npx` now resolve to PM's installed copy or `None`, with no PATH fallback. Every production caller (WhatsApp, Photon, `hermes whatsapp`, dashboard pairing, tools setup) already runs `pm.ensure()` when it gets `None`, so a missing runtime now gets provisioned instead of borrowing the user's Node.
- **`agent/lsp/install._install_npm`**: runs `pm.ensure("npm")` when PM's npm is absent, instead of dying or using PATH npm. pnpm and yarn stay an explicit user choice via `lsp.package_manager`.
- **`hermes_cli/gateway._append_node_dir_for_service`**: generated systemd units and launchd plists no longer bake in the invoker's PATH node dir.
- **`hermes_cli/main_install_repair._resolve_node_runtime_npm`**: no longer re-scans PATH for another npm (the old updater keeps importing it).
- **`hermes_cli/source_build.source_product_current`**: the build-freshness reader runs only under PM's node. Before, `env_for("node")` fell back to the ambient PATH.
- **`hermes doctor`**: the Node row and `npm audit` use PM's node and npm, and the audit runs under `with_hermes_node_path()`. Termux keeps its system Node because the Termux APT distribution relies on `pkg install nodejs`.
- **`scripts/install.sh::ensure_uv` / `scripts/install.ps1::Get-Uv`**: the "uv on PATH if at least the pin" developer shortcut is deleted, so the installers always stage the pinned artifact. The dead `version_at_least` helper is removed too.
- **Docs**: `getting-started/installation.md` no longer says an existing uv can bootstrap PM.
- **Test stand-ins**: Photon, WhatsApp, and source-build tests used to pass by implicitly borrowing the CI host's PATH node. They now stub the adapter's `find_node_executable` or `pm.installed_package("node")` with an explicit stand-in (`use_host_node_as_pm_node` in `test_source_build.py`). Test intent is unchanged.
- Allowlists: removed the `_ALLOWED` rows for `gateway.py` node and `main_install_repair.py` npm, plus 3 `resolution_allowlist.json` rows. The `main_tui_launch` reasons are corrected: those lookups run against a PATH composed by `pm.ensure`, not the ambient one.

## Validation

**Live repro:** in a scratch `HERMES_HOME` with an empty PM store and a fake user `node`/`npm`/`npx` 99.0.0 first on PATH:

| | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `find_node_executable("node"/"npm"/"npx")` | the user's `…/usernode/{node,npm,npx}` | `None` (caller runs `pm.ensure`) |
| `_append_node_dir_for_service` (unit PATH) | `['…/usernode']` | `[]` |
| `install.sh ensure_uv` with a fake `uv 99.0.0` on PATH | `UV_CMD=…/fakeuv/uv` | downloads the pin: `UV_CMD=$HERMES_HOME/tools/uv-0.12.3-linux-x64/uv` |

**Tests:** each changed invariant test is red on origin/main and green here.

| Test | Base |
|---|---|
| `tests/pm/test_node_resolution.py::test_passive_discovery_never_installs_or_repairs_a_legacy_tree` | red |
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_service.py::…test_no_pm_node_never_bakes_the_invokers_path_node` | red |
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_service.py::…test_stale_pm_facts_without_dirs_contribute_nothing` | red |
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_node_runtime_npm_resolution.py::test_resolve_node_runtime_npm_never_rescans_path_past_a_windows_shim` | red |
| `tests/scripts/install/test_install_sh_repository_stage.py::test_path_uv_is_never_used_even_when_newer_than_the_pin` | red |

**Why existing tests changed:** each rewritten assertion pinned the fallback that the ruling bans.
- `test_node_resolution` asserted that "a user-owned PATH toolchain remains usable". It now asserts `None`.
- In `test_gateway_service`, the `*_ambient_fallback` tests now expect `[]`. `test_node_path_lookup_remains_fallback_without_managed_node` duplicated one of them and is deleted. The two #48700 symlink-leak tests are also deleted: they could only fire through the removed `which("node")` rung, so that leak can no longer happen.
- The WSL npm re-scan test is flipped to "no re-scan".
- The installer test that accepted a new-enough PATH uv is flipped.

## Not in this PR
Product calls and borderline items are listed in the audit on the parent task. They include Desktop's login-shell PATH merge, `pm.activate()` refusing to prepend the store on drift, the terminal subshell appending the managed dirs after the user's PATH, `pip install X` hint strings, Termux/Nix system toolchains, and the MCP stdio PATH (owned by another lane).

raw.body:
Fresh Windows 10 installs no longer fail at `prerequisites` with `tar.exe: ... unable to run program "bzip2 -d"`. Pinned Git is now staged from Git for Windows' PortableGit self-extractor, so tar and bzip2 aren't needed at all.

Salvage of #123094 by @Finn763. His two commits are cherry-picked unchanged with authorship kept, on top of current `origin/main`. Two follow-up commits from review sit on top (below).

Fixes #122512, fixes #122774. Covers the git part of #125350 (the ffmpeg and `-SkipSetup` parts of that issue are separate).

## Why

- Windows 10's `System32\tar.exe` is `bsdtar 3.5.2 - libarchive 3.5.2 zlib/1.2.5.f-ipp`. It has no built-in bzip2 filter, so it shells out to a `bzip2` that a stock machine doesn't have.
- Newer Windows 11 builds ship `bsdtar 3.7.x ... bz2lib/1.0.8`, which is why Windows 11 hosts and CI never hit this.
- Hermes staged Git from PortableGit before the pm store landed (3601e20f47c). The `.tar.bz2` pin came with the pm store foundation (3d12e86ef13).
- PortableGit is also what Scoop (`Main/bucket/git.json`) and Chocolatey (`git.portable`) pin.

## Changes (from #123094)

- `pm/lock.json` and the generated pin fragment in `scripts/install.ps1`: both win32 git targets now point at `PortableGit-2.53.0.3-{64-bit,arm64}.7z.exe`. Same Git version; the sha256s match GitHub's published asset digests.
- `scripts/install.ps1::Get-PinnedGit`: runs the self-extractor with `-o<dir> -y`, waits on it through `Process.WaitForExit` (the stub is a GUI-subsystem exe, so `&` wouldn't wait), stops after 600 s, and reports the exit code. The `System32\tar.exe` call and its MSYS exclude list are removed.
- `pm/packages.py::Git.unpack`: runs a scratch copy of the sha256-verified artifact, never the cached bytes. This fixes the WinError 32 the PR's first CI round hit. On a non-Windows host it refuses with a clear message.
- `pm/store.py`: removes `extract_tar(git_msys=...)`, which no longer has a caller.
- Tests and docs: pm invariants now check the subprocess argv, plus one real-download `Get-PinnedGit` test that uses a bzip2-less tar stub. The `pm install --target` doc row notes the Windows-host requirement.

## Review follow-ups (two commits on top)

- `066c425` pm: refusal, non-zero exit and timeout raise `InstallError` (`pm/client.py` only catches `InstallError`; `TimeoutExpired` escaped). The extractor's stdio is `DEVNULL`: with `capture_output` the `RunProgram` children inherit the pipes and can hold `run()` open after the stub exits. The dead output-tail branch is gone. The off-Windows refusal now gives a real remedy instead of "retry". Tests use `CompletedProcess`, drop `raising=False`, add a timeout case, and the pin-suffix change-detector test is removed.
- `5660a6f` install.ps1: on timeout, `taskkill /T /F` kills the whole extractor tree (PS 5.1 `Process.Kill()` only kills the stub, so its children kept `%TEMP%` held). The single-wrapper-dir flatten is removed: the sha-pinned archive roots `cmd\git.exe` directly.

## Self-extractor behaviour, checked against source

Checked against `git-for-windows/7-Zip` `v26.03-VS2022-sfx` `CPP/7zip/Bundles/SFXSetup/SfxSetup.cpp`:

- Only `-y` and `-o` (quoted or unquoted) are parsed. Any other switch is appended to the `RunProgram` command line. The `-gm2` switch on the gitforwindows.org "zip archives" page belongs to the old 7zsfx.info module and would be passed through to `post-install.bat`, so it is deliberately not used.
- The stub waits on `RunProgram` (`WaitForSingleObject(..., INFINITE)`) and then returns 0. So when the process exits, extraction and the vendor post-install have both finished.

## Trade-offs (from the maintainer round-2 review)

- A 58 MB sha256-pinned, `Unblock-File`d PE now runs during bootstrap. An "Extracting..." progress window shows even with `-y`.
- `Git.unpack` for the win32 target now needs a Windows host. Bundled win32 builds already run on native Windows runners (`windows-latest-32-core`, `windows-latest-32-arm-core`).
- **hermes-assets mirror:** the two new objects (`upstream/sha256/b365da79…`, `upstream/sha256/0db54010…`) return 404 until merge. No manual upload is needed: `archive-inputs.yml` runs on any push to main that touches `pm/lock.json`. It downloads each pin from upstream, checks its sha256 and uploads it to R2 under the release-signing environment, which is limited to main and tags. The ffmpeg re-pin (#125350, run 36344056098) went through that path, and its object now returns 200. GitHub stays the primary URL, so the ~1 minute gap after merge doesn't matter.

## Validation

- `scripts/gen-bootstrap-pins.py --check`: clean. `check-windows-footguns.py --all`: clean. Ruff: clean.
- `tests/pm` and `tests/scripts/install` on macOS: 846 passed, 39 failed, 68 skipped. The 39 failures are the same 10 files and counts as on the untouched merge-base (846 passed, 39 failed), all pre-existing macOS environment failures. `tests/pm/test_store_extract.py` passes.
- On #123094's head `adaf76a`: 57 check runs succeeded, 23 skipped, 0 failed. That includes the Windows-only lane and `Windows E2E (real processes)`, which ran `git: unpacking` for real.
- The real x64 pin (downloaded on macOS, sha256 matches the lock and install.ps1): the SFX config is `RunProgram="git-bash.exe --needs-console --hide --no-cd --command=post-install.bat"`. `7zz l` lists `cmd/git.exe`, `usr/bin/bash.exe`, `bin/bash.exe` and `post-install.bat` at the archive root, with no wrapper dir and no symlinks. So every path `Git.binary_rel`, `env()`, `pm/shell._staged_bash` and `Get-PinnedGit` expect is present.
- Real `pm install --target win32-x64 git` on macOS (isolated HOME and HERMES_HOME): refuses before running anything and leaves no store entry.
- Follow-up commits: mutation-checked. Piping stdio again, dropping the timeout handler, dropping the remedy, or executing the cached bytes each fail a test. Consumer tests outside `tests/pm` (16 files) show the same result as the merge-base. `install.ps1` parses with 0 errors.
- Still needs the Windows lane on this PR's head.
