raw.body:
Windows install wrappers that still pass `-SkipSetup` work again, instead of dying at parameter binding with `NamedParameterNotFound` before any stage runs (#125350 item 3).

**Why.** The staged-installer rework dropped `-SkipSetup` from `install.ps1`'s `param()` block. PowerShell refuses an undeclared switch outright, so an old spelling can't be ignored; it has to be declared. `install.sh` still accepts `--skip-setup` as an alias for `--non-interactive` (kept in f91bd82286), so Windows was the only installer without it. The most-used community wrapper, fathah/hermes-desktop, passes it in two places:
- `src/main/installer.ts`: `-SkipSetup -NonInteractive …`
- the copy-paste command in `src/renderer/src/constants.ts`: `-SkipSetup` **without** `-NonInteractive`, so the alias has to mean "skip the prompts", not just bind.

**Changes**
- `scripts/install.ps1`: declares `[switch]$SkipSetup` and folds it into `$NonInteractive` before anything reads the parameters. It is documented in the header as a deprecated alias.
- The docs (English + zh-Hans `windows-native.md`) list it as a deprecated alias. `-NoVenv` and `-Tag` stay rejected.
- `tests/scripts/install/test_install_ps1_skipsetup_alias.py` (Windows lane) has two tests:
  - `-SkipSetup` binds.
  - `-SkipSetup` alone, with `-Stage setup -Json`, emits the `skipped / needs user input` frame. Only the fold can produce that frame, so deleting the fold line makes the test fail.

**Behaviour note (from @teknium1's review):** the old `-SkipSetup` skipped only the setup wizard. The alias skips every stage that needs input, which includes the gateway stage. That is what an unattended wrapper needs, and hermes-desktop already passes `-NonInteractive` anyway.

**Who / when:** this is a salvage of #125371 by @dskwe (Yuan Li), with authorship kept on the cherry-picked commits. It also includes Teknium's review fix-up commit (the doc line and header comment). The PR's `pm/lock.json` re-pin and the since-deleted liveness test are dropped. Its ffmpeg hunk pinned the 2026-09-27 daily, which BtbN deletes around Oct 11, and #125468 supersedes it with the retained month-end build. Merging #125371 as it stood would have reverted that pin.

**Validation:** macOS has no PowerShell, so the two Windows tests run in the Windows CI lane. `tests/scripts/install/` passes on macOS (69 passed, 20 skipped). ruff, windows-footguns and `git diff --check` are clean.

raw.body:
## Problem

Two sidebar state bugs:

1. **Archiving a session resurrects it** (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/123685). Archiving or deleting a chat from the sidebar could make it reappear a moment later, on the same profile, without touching the backend row.
2. **Renaming leaves project-scoped and other-slice rows stale** (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/123337). Renaming a session updated the recents list, but project overview previews, entered-project lanes, and cron/messaging rows kept the old title until an unrelated refetch (e.g. a profile switch).

## Root cause

**123685:** `applyProjectTreePayload` in `apps/desktop/src/store/projects.ts` prunes an archive tombstone once the authoritative projects tree no longer lists the id — correct for the tree overlay, but it strips the removal guard while a sidebar page **read before the archive RPC committed** is still in flight. When that stale page lands, tombstone membership is already empty, so `dropTombstoned` / the `mergeSessionPage` survivor filter have nothing to veto and the row re-enters through the keep set (the 30s settle grace still names it). Tombstones also matched only the row's tip id + lineage root, so the same conversation could sneak back under an intermediate lineage segment id.

**123337:** the rename flow (`RenameSessionDialog` submit, `/title` slash, `session.title` gateway event) patched only `$sessions` by bare id. Compressed rows matched by lineage, project-scoped snapshot rows, cron rows, and messaging rows never saw the new title until a refetch overwrote them.

## Fix

- `store/session-removal.ts`: track the direction of the last removal edge per id. `sessionRemovalIntersected(snapshot, id)` answers "did this id's removal lifecycle move **toward removal** since this fetch started" — the generation counter and edge direction survive the tombstone prune. `tombstoneRowIds(session)` names every id a row answers to (tip, lineage root, and all intermediate segments), replacing the tip+root-only match in `dropTombstoned` and `mergeSessionPage`.
- `use-session-list-actions.ts`: every fetch (recents `refreshSessions`, messaging refresh, platform load-more, cron slice) captures a tombstone-generation snapshot **before** the first read and rejects rows raced toward removal, filtering after the merge so survivor-path rows are covered too.
- `store/projects.ts`: `fetchProjectSessions` (project drill-in) applies the same guard through the existing `excludeProjectSessions` helper, keeping the project reference when nothing matches so the drill-in memo stays stable.
- `store/session.ts`: new `applySessionTitle(id, title)` patches the title across **every** sidebar slice (`$sessions`, cron, messaging, unlisted owner rows), matching lineage-aware via the existing `sessionMatchesStoredId`, reference-stable per slice when nothing changes.
- `store/projects.ts`: new `applyRenamedSessionTitle(id, title)` mirrors the rename into the cached project tree (lane rows + overview previews, recomputing counts) and re-pulls the authoritative tree.
- The rename dialog, `/title` slash command, and `session.title` gateway event all route through the new helpers.

Release edges (failed archive RPC, explicit unarchive) still re-admit the row: only edges that moved **toward** removal are vetoed.

## Tests

6 new behavioral tests, proven red on base `9fa23760bc` and green with this patch:

- `use-session-list-actions.test.tsx`: a doomed row whose tombstone was pruned mid-flight is dropped instead of resurrected through the keep set; a rolled-back archive mid-flight is re-admitted; a pruned-tombstone row is matched by any lineage segment and the cron slice is filtered too.
- `session.test.ts`: `mergeSessionPage` matches a tombstone by intermediate lineage segment; `applySessionTitle` patches every slice lineage-aware and stays reference-stable on no-op.
- `projects.test.ts`: `applyRenamedSessionTitle` mirrors into cached tree rows + previews (matched by tip and by lineage root) and re-pulls the tree; keeps the tree reference on no-match.

Full local validation in the worktree (rebased on current main):

- `npx vitest run use-session-list-actions.test.tsx session.test.ts projects.test.ts session-removal.test.ts` → **217 passed** (4 files)
- `npm run typecheck` (apps/desktop, all 4 tsconfigs) → clean
- `npx eslint` on all 10 touched files → clean

Store/hook logic only, no visual or behavioral surface a user could see change beyond the two fixes.

raw.body:
`hermes update`, `hermes update --check` and installer re-runs now work on the tag-pinned `--depth 1 --single-branch` checkouts older installers made, instead of reporting an existing `main` as missing.

Fixes #125112. Salvages #125123 by @dskwe (the fix and the forced-refspec test) and the end-to-end check test from #125132 by @kokhlo; both are cherry-picked with authorship kept.

Root cause: on these checkouts `remote.origin.fetch` maps only the tag, so a by-name `git fetch origin main` writes `FETCH_HEAD` and never creates the `origin/main` that everything afterwards resolves.

## Changes

- **Updater fetches** (`--check`, the apply fetch, the fork upstream sync) use an explicit forced refspec, `+refs/heads/<b>:refs/remotes/<r>/<b>`, built in one place: `update_cmd_check.tracking_refspec`. The `+` matters: on a depth-1 clone the new tip is not a descendant of the old one. (@dskwe)
- **Update count on these checkouts.** They are always detached with no local `main`, so the updater lands them with `checkout -B main origin/main`, which puts HEAD on the target before `rev-list HEAD..origin/main` counts. With the fetch fixed alone, that count read 0: the update moved the code, printed "Already up to date!", and skipped dependency sync, config migration and restarts. HEAD is now captured before that checkout, the count starts from it, and it reaches the pull phase as `pre_sync_sha` (the channel the fork upstream sync already uses), so the did-HEAD-move guard and the syntax rollback compare against the code that was running.
- **Installer re-runs** (`install.sh`, `install.ps1`) fetch by the same refspec. When there is no local branch they create it at the fetched tip, because `git checkout main`'s branch guess ignores remote refs the configured refspec does not map. The remote's fetch config is never rewritten.
- **Tests.** One invariant per surface, each red on `origin/main`: the end-to-end `--check` test (@kokhlo), the forced-tip advance (@dskwe), and the count from the pre-checkout HEAD. The narrow-clone fixture now creates its origin on `main` explicitly; before, it only passed where `init.defaultBranch=main`.
- **Typing.** `SourceTarget` carries either a commit or a branch but types both as optional. The branch arm now asserts that invariant where it takes the branch, so the typed helper receives a `str`. `ty` against main: 9 vs 10 diagnostics, none new.
- Not carried over from #125132: the `ls-remote` probe and its new message. With an explicit refspec, a genuinely missing branch fails the fetch itself, which already names it: `✗ Failed to fetch updates from origin.` / `fatal: couldn't find remote ref refs/heads/<b>`, verified on both `--check` and apply. So the probe's branch was unreachable. It also duplicated `source_check._branch_tip` without the timeout.
- Side effect, accepted: a fetch with an explicit destination auto-follows tags that point into the fetched history, where a by-name fetch did not.

## Validation

Each surface was run against a real narrow clone of this repo: a local origin plus `git clone --depth 1 --single-branch --branch v2026.9.24`, 335 commits behind.

| Surface | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `hermes update --check` | `✗ Branch 'main' not found on origin.` | `Update available: 335 commits behind origin/main` |
| apply fetch + checkout | `✗ Branch 'main' does not exist locally or on origin.` | lands `main` |
| apply count (fetch fix only) | `commit_count=0` → "Already up to date!" | counted; applied d25bbd01 → 7d7f712a; post-pull phase runs |
| same, parked on a merged branch | same miscount | applied |
| fork upstream sync, tag-only `upstream` | `Could not compare branches` | up to date with upstream |
| `install.sh --stage repository` re-run | `pathspec 'main' did not match` → failed | `main` at the tip; idempotent re-run |
| normal / treeless clones | — | identical refs and result to `origin/main` |

The neighbouring update, shallow, gitlock, source_check and installer test files run one per process: 107 files pass. The 15 that fail locally fail the same way on the base commit: identical test IDs in the 4 files that exercise the changed checkout code, identical counts in the rest. The cause is a local guard that trips on this machine's checkout location. The windows-footguns lint and `ruff check` are clean.

`install.ps1` was not executed; no PowerShell runtime is available here, so Windows CI covers it.

Reverts #124792: MCP stdio children get the PATH order they were configured with again. That PR moved the resolved command's directory to PATH[0], which leaves the #82309 layout unchanged and puts a later directory's node/python3/git ahead of the Hermes-managed ones.

WHO/WHEN/WHY: follow-up to the post-merge review on #124792 by @andrexibiza (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/124792#pullrequestreview-5328958540). I reproduced its F1/F2 findings on macOS, found the default Hermes PATH is also affected, and am opening the revert rather than patching on top, because whether managed Node should be authoritative for MCP children is a policy question (#125589, #124304, #125318).

## Changes
- Revert 79dbb145: `_prepend_path` goes back to prepending only when the directory is absent. The four tests it added are removed along with it.
- One invariant test: when a bare command is found in a later PATH directory, the child's PATH comes back unchanged. It fails on 79dbb145 and passes after the revert.

## Root cause
`_resolve_stdio_command` passes `_prepend_path` the directory the **command** was found in, not the managed Node directory. After 79dbb145, a command found anywhere on PATH pulled its directory ahead of every earlier entry.

## Live repro (real spawned children, macOS)

| Layout | before #124792 | on main (79dbb145) | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| System Node + npx first, managed behind (the #82309 shape) | system | system (no change) | system |
| Managed first, absolute foreign `npx` later | managed | **system** | managed |
| Managed first, bare `uvx` in a later dir that also has `node` | managed | **later dir's node** | managed |
| Real Hermes PATH (store dirs first, as `pm.activate()` sets it), `command: gh` from `/opt/homebrew/bin` → child's `node` / `python3` / `git` | store / store / /usr/bin | **brew / brew / brew** | store / store / /usr/bin |
| Real MCP server (`mcp` client), env.PATH `A:/usr/bin:/bin:B`, launcher in B | PATH[0]=A | PATH[0]=B | PATH[0]=A |

## Validation
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_mcp*.py`: 824 passed, 2 failed. The same 2 fail on main and before #124792 (`test_mcp_shared_connection_resolved_identity.py`); they trip the home-I/O guard because my worktree lives under the real hermes home.
- The new test is red with main's `tools/mcp_tool_common.py` swapped in and green on this branch.
- ruff, `check-windows-footguns.py --all`, `check_compat_pointers.py`: clean.

#82309 stays closed: its desktop dependency-install surface was already fixed on main by the PM refactor (`with_hermes_node_path` → `pm.env_for("npm")`), which both #124792's own scope note and the post-merge review verified.

raw.body:
## What does this PR do?

The stable release's signed-candidate legs died before building anything: every job inside `desktop-bundled-release.yml`, `docker.yml` and `termux-verify.yml` that declares a protected environment attached its deployment and read the environment's `vars`, but resolved `secrets.*` to the empty string. This PR lets those secrets reach the three callees that need them, and nothing else.

Root cause: a called workflow receives no secrets by default. A job-level `environment:` inside it is required but not sufficient — and a caller job that `uses:` a reusable workflow cannot declare `environment:` at all, so `secrets: inherit` is the only mechanism that can carry them across the boundary ([actions/runner#1490](https://github.com/actions/runner/issues/1490)).

Precedent, deliberately checked: #69803 hit the same symptom on the CI → Docker publish path and fixed it by making that publish top-level, adding *no* `secrets: inherit`. This PR takes the other branch of that fork on purpose — the stable release's callees hand receipts and artifacts back through `needs.*.outputs`, so they cannot become top-level dispatches without re-architecting the handoff. If "trusted work runs top-level" is the preferred shape here too, the two `docker.yml` calls are the one place it could be hoisted instead; say the word and I'll move the docker publish out of the call.

## Related Issue

No tracking issue — caught live on the first full stable-release dispatch: run [#36194968007](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/36194968007), job `108268960023` (`Build signed release candidates (win32-arm64) / Pre-build setup`) failed with `missing env CLOUDFLARE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`.

Fixes # (none — the failing run above is the report)

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `.github/workflows/stable-release.yml` — `secrets: inherit` on the 7 `desktop-bundled-release.yml` calls, the 2 `docker.yml` calls, and the `termux-verify.yml` call, plus a header comment stating why those three need it.
- `.github/workflows/desktop-bundled-release.yml` — the header contract now says callers must pass `secrets: inherit`; the previous wording implied repo-level or environment secrets would arrive on their own.
- Not added where it buys nothing: `ci.yaml` (its header forbids it — it runs PR-controlled code), `nix`, `pm-bundle`, `windows-venv-e2e`, `install-e2e*` reference no secrets.
- Credential boundary unchanged: a secret still reaches only jobs that declare the environment *and* whose ref its deployment policy allows. `secrets: inherit` changes what the callee's own environment-gated jobs can read, not which refs may deploy.

## How to Test

1. **Before** — run [#36194968007](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/36194968007), job `108268960023`: the step env showed the R2 secrets empty while the `vars` value arrived, i.e. environment attached, secrets withheld:

   ```text
   CLOUDFLARE_R2_ACCOUNT_ID: (empty)
   CLOUDFLARE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID: (empty)
   CLOUDFLARE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: (empty)
   CLOUDFLARE_R2_BUCKET: hermes-agent-artifacts
   ```

2. **Control** — same three secrets, same `release-signing` environment, same tag ref, but in a *top-level* job: `archive-inputs.yml` run [#36205453828](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/36205453828) shows all three masked (`***`) and archived the pinned inputs to R2. The credentials are fine; the boundary is the `workflow_call` hop.
3. **After** — needs a claim dispatch (the next `rc.N` cut). Check the first `Pre-build setup` step env: the three values should read `***`, and `Archive every pinned input` should get past its first line. Note this PR's own CI cannot exercise it — dispatching `desktop-bundled-release.yml` directly runs it top-level, where the secrets resolve anyway, which proves nothing.

`nix run nixpkgs#actionlint -- -shellcheck= -pyflakes= .github/workflows/stable-release.yml` exits 0. The 10 `cache-mode` complaints in `desktop-bundled-release.yml` are pre-existing (identical set at `origin/main`; actionlint's bundled schema predates the key).

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(ci):`, `feat(ci):`, etc.)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

Before (run #36194968007, job `108268960023`) — the environment resolves, the secrets do not:

```text

CLOUDFLARE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID:                        <- secrets: empty
Error: missing env CLOUDFLARE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID
```

```text

CLOUDFLARE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ***
Archived pinned inputs to R2 -> upstream/sha256/...
```

raw.body:
When a stdio MCP server's native addon was built for a different Node.js, Hermes now shows the failure and gives the exact rebuild command with its own Node's paths. Before this, the server was parked silently behind "Connection closed".

Fixes #124264. The report and diagnosis came from @michael2608H, and @rodricksz4h5 did the analysis in #124304.

## Ruling applied
Maintainer ruling: *"only hermes and only packaged package managers (uv/pip/node/npm) should ever be used."* Managed Node stays first for MCP children. The user's Node never runs them, and nothing suggests pinning `command:` to it. #124304 (managed Node moved behind the user's for MCP) was closed under this ruling.

## Changes
- `tools/mcp_tool_config.py::_StderrTee`: the stdio child's stderr now goes through a pipe. Every byte is still copied into `logs/mcp-stderr.log`, and the last 16 KB stay readable.
- `tools/mcp_tool_node_abi.py` (new): when a failed session's stderr shows `NODE_MODULE_VERSION` / `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED`, it builds a `NodeAbiMismatchError`. The error names the addon, both ABI numbers and the fix, using PM's own node/npm paths:
  - addon in an `~/.npm/_npx/<hash>` entry: `rm -rf <entry>`, and Hermes's npx reinstalls it on the next start;
  - either way: `PATH=<managed node dir>:"$PATH" <managed npm> rebuild <pkg> --prefix <root>`. Managed Node has to be first on PATH because npm's shebang and its install scripts both run the first `node` they find.
  - On Windows the same commands are rendered in PowerShell syntax. If PM has no Node installed, the message says `hermes pm install npm`.
- `tools/mcp_tool_transport.py::_run_stdio`: raises that error, chained to the SDK's error.
- `tools/mcp_tool_errors.py`: the error is classified as permanent, so the server parks at once instead of retrying 3 times. It self-probes, so it comes back after the rebuild. `_format_connect_error` returns the error's message on its own.
- `hermes_cli/mcp_config.py`: after the error, `hermes mcp test` says "After rebuilding it under Hermes's Node as above, run: hermes mcp test <name>".

Every place MCP status already shows up reads the error through `_format_connect_error` / `str(exc)`, so the new message reaches all of them without further changes: the startup banner (whose first ~120 characters carry the diagnosis), `/mcp` status, `hermes mcp test`, the TUI `mcp.test` RPC, the Desktop probe and the dashboard `/test` route.

## Validation
| | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `hermes mcp test` on a server whose stderr is Node's real ABI error | `✗ Connection failed (8.3s): Connection closed` / "Check the server is running…" | `✗ Connection failed (2.9s): native addon built for a different Node.js (NODE_MODULE_VERSION 127; Hermes's Node 26.7.0 needs 147): …/_npx/abc123/node_modules/better-sqlite3/…node. Hermes runs MCP servers on its own Node; rebuild the server under it: rm -rf …/_npx/abc123 (Hermes reinstalls it on the next start), or PATH=~/.hermes/tools/node-26.7.0-linux-x64/bin:"$PATH" ~/.hermes/tools/npm-12.0.2-linux-x64/bin/npm rebuild better-sqlite3 --prefix …/_npx/abc123` |
| Spawns before parking | 4 (initial attempt + 3 retries) | 1 |
| `logs/mcp-stderr.log` | has the child's stderr | still has it |
| hosts E2E `test_path_shapes` MCP cell (real `install.sh`, a stand-in user Node v22.11.0 first on PATH) | **red** at the remedy assertion. Managed Node already ran the server; the output was just "Connection closed" | **green** |
| `tests/tools/test_mcp_node_abi.py` (2 tests) | real stdio-child test red (`'Connection closed'`, 3 attempts) | green |
| `tests/tools -k mcp` | — | 922 passed |
| `tests/hermes_cli tests/tui_gateway -k mcp` | 4 fake-HOME env failures | the same 4 fail identically on base |

**E2E cell rewritten:** `test_mcp_server_configured_with_the_users_node_runs_on_the_users_node` asserted the user's Node wins, which contradicts the ruling. It was gated with `known_failure` on #124264. It is now `test_mcp_server_runs_on_the_managed_node_and_an_abi_mismatch_names_the_rebuild`. It asserts that the user's Node never runs the server, that the marker shows Hermes's managed Node ran it, that `hermes mcp test` exits 1, and that the output carries `NODE_MODULE_VERSION 127`, `rm -rf <sandbox>/.npm/_npx/<entry>` and `PATH=<managed node dir>: … rebuild better-sqlite3 --prefix`.

raw.body:
## What

After the Linux launcher rename (`com.nousresearch.hermes.desktop`), `install_desktop_entry()` deleted the pre-rename `hermes.desktop`. Shells resolve a taskbar pin by the entry file name it was pinned against, so that deletion silently killed existing pins: GNOME drops the favourite, Plasma leaves an inert item, and the shell has no mechanism to re-point the association for the user.

Instead of deleting the legacy entry, rewrite it as a `NoDisplay=true` alias with the same `Exec`/`Icon`/`StartupWMClass` as the app-id entry — invisible in the app grid (no second Hermes), still launchable and window-matched for old pins. Only a file that still names this app is converted; foreign files stay untouched, and the launcher-management opt-out still protects it. `gui_uninstall` now removes the alias together with the real entry.

## On-disk effect (Linux install/uninstall)

Install writes $XDG_DATA_HOME/applications/com.nousresearch.hermes.desktop as before, and now also rewrites $XDG_DATA_HOME/applications/hermes.desktop (only if it is our own pre-rename entry) to the same entry text plus a `NoDisplay=true` key; GUI uninstall additionally removes that hermes.desktop alias.

## Verification

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_linux_desktop_entry.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gui_uninstall.py tests/hermes_cli/test_linux_launcher_management.py` (HERMES_TEST_FILE_RETRIES=0): 55 passed, 0 failed, 3 platform-skips that run on CI lanes.
- The new alias test fails against origin/main's product code (scratch copy via `git show`, no stash): the legacy entry is deleted instead of aliased.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/124567 — notification-only approach (prints re-pin guidance once a migration renames the entry); this PR fixes the root cause so no pin ever breaks and no user action is needed.

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/124492

raw.body:
## Summary

A finished assistant reply could render twice after settle, via two independent paths, each keying on stale identity instead of the durable one:

- **use-message-stream**: a rewritten final (`response_previewed` / `response_transformed`) shares no text prefix with the streamed interim, so the prefix heuristics missed — and the volatile boundary flag could no longer speak for the bubble once a chained `message.start` reset it. The terminal frame carries a `persisted_turn` receipt naming the stored row it settled (`final_assistant_row_id`); the fix settles onto the display-only interim keyed on that durable receipt instead of appending a second bubble for one stored row.
- **use-session-actions `overlayConcurrentMessageChanges`**: the committed row and the settled live row capture the same reply at two moments while it kept streaming, so the strict text-equality guard rejected their fold and kept both. The fix accepts either side as a forward text-extension of the other via the existing `isStrictAnswerTextExtension` helper — the same trade `removeRepresentedLocalLiveProjection` already made.

Four new tests pin the rewritten-previewed, rewritten-transformed, lagging-live-row, and ran-past-committed-row shapes; all four fail on main and pass with this change.

raw.body:
## What does this PR do?

Add owner-maintained Vault View to the Desktop catalog, pinned to the published [v0.4.8 release](https://github.com/ergocogn/hermes-desktop-plugin-vault-view/releases/tag/v0.4.8), commit `532c9b95f204cafb224e33c8075c4a774ad6f7eb`. Vault View provides visual Markdown editing, progressive reading, cached local image previews, shared tabs, tag search, links and a graph. This PR changes one catalog file only; no Hermes runtime changes.

## Catalog review corrections

- SDK SandboxedFrame replaces the raw webview; plugin and catalog require Hermes >=0.21.5.
- Agent navigation guidance has an independent localized opt-in, off by default. Opt-out removes stale plugin guidance while preserving user attachments and note source.
- Remote note images are blocked by default and require a separate persistent opt-in. Opt-out removes existing remote sources while preserving Markdown.
- Runtime controls, errors, prompts, confirmations, bridge messages, code-copy, callout, link, image and agent-context text use English/French locale bundles.
- `platforms: [linux, macos]`. Windows Desktop requires a WSL-hosted Unix backend; native Windows gateways are unsupported.
- Removed the document.body observer and all transcript DOM rewriting; the composer reference no longer emits `<ide_opened_file>`. The workspace anchor uses the public SDK and the plugin’s own previous tab only. Image preference updates are scoped to the plugin root.

The release includes metadata-only plugin.yaml and byte-identical root/desktop entry points. The root file remains for direct installation as documented by the SDK; desktop/plugin.js is the catalog entry. There is no Python module or Agent runtime capability. Banner and synthetic screenshots are pinned to the same public commit. Related to #107262.

## Validation

Plugin regression, package parity, catalog policy, Playwright editor/image/navigation/privacy and synthetic WSL gateway suites passed. The browser suite checks remote-image requests before opt-in and Markdown preservation. The official Desktop surface lint and catalog validator accepted the reviewed source and entry at Hermes commit `8b66a51036c1e20920a17cdd049fdf55c968d683`. The installed Hermes plugin validator passed; its Python capability probe was skipped as expected for a Desktop-only plugin. The running Hermes Desktop UI showed v0.4.8 and restored a Vault View note tab after hide/show.

Full Hermes tests, clean install, restart, native external-application launches and cross-platform UI checks were not run. Direct Obsidian opening stays hidden; ffmpeg thumbnails are optional. Some websites reject SDK iframe embedding; external opening remains available. No note bodies are shared automatically.

## Disclosure

I maintain the plugin through ergoCogn. Prepared with AI assistance; automated checks and manual limitations are distinguished in the public documentation. Only public source, synthetic examples and public contribution guidance are included.

raw.body:
Desktop's own children (the `hermes serve` backend, its probes, the update hand-offs and the bootstrap installer) now resolve the PM store's node/npm/uv ahead of the user's nvm/Homebrew/`~/.local/bin` copies, even after the login-shell PATH merge.

Maintainer ruling: "the principle is now that only hermes and only packaged package managers (uv/pip/node/npm) should ever be used."

**Root cause:** `shell-path.ts` writes the user's interactive login-shell PATH into `process.env` with login entries first and the inherited PATH appended. When Desktop is started by `hermes desktop`, the inherited PATH is exactly where the store dirs sit (`with_hermes_node_path` / `pm.activate`), so every child env built from `process.env` put the user's toolchain first, and the backend's `pm.activate()` left the already-present store dirs where they were.

## Changes
- `electron/backend-env.ts`: new `storeFirstPath()` moves PATH entries under the PM store root to the front and keeps every other entry in its existing order. The store root is resolved like `pm.environments.store_root`: `HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR`, else `<hermes home>/tools`. Ownership is decided by path containment, so a look-alike prefix such as `~/.hermes/tools-old` does not count.
- `buildDesktopBackendEnv()` applies it. That covers every backend spawn (bundled payload, source, `HERMES_DESKTOP_HERMES`, Windows venv unwrapping), the backend probes, and the source/POSIX/Windows update hand-offs, which build their env through `sourceUpdateEnvironment`.
- `electron/bootstrap-runner.ts`: the install.sh/install.ps1 child env goes through the same helper. `install.sh` takes a uv from PATH when it is new enough, so a store uv that is already on PATH now wins.
- `process.env` itself is **not** reordered, so the embedded terminal (`terminal-ipc.ts`) and external terminal keep the user's own PATH order. A test asserts this.
- In-process half: the sibling Python PR (`fix/toolchain-principle-2`) makes `pm.install.activate()` always move store dirs to the FRONT of `os.environ["PATH"]`. At the moment it only prepends dirs that are missing. This PR is the spawn-env half, so the order is right before Python starts and for children that never run `activate()`.

## Validation

| Check | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| New `backend-env.test.ts` "backend runs the store toolchain even after the login-shell PATH is merged in front of it" | ✗ red | ✓ |
| New `backend-env.test.ts` "HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR names the store; look-alike prefixes are not Hermes-owned" | ✗ red | ✓ |
| Live probe: real `applyLoginShellPath` (host's real `bash -il`), inherited PATH = `<home>/.hermes/tools/node-26.7.0-linux-x64/bin:/usr/bin:/bin`, then `command -v node` in a child spawned with the backend env | `~/.local/bin/node` (user's) | `…/.hermes/tools/node-26.7.0-linux-x64/bin/node` → `HERMES-STORE-NODE` |
| Same probe, `process.env` (terminal base) | `~/.local/bin/node` | `~/.local/bin/node` (unchanged) |
| `npm run check:lint` (apps/desktop) | n/a | 0 errors |
| `vitest` backend-env, shell-path, bootstrap-runner, bootstrap-runner-git-binary, backend-probes, windows-hermes-path | n/a | green |

Locally, `source-backend.test.ts` (PM source launcher) and `updater/checkout-source.test.ts` fail on this host both on origin/main and on this branch. The cause is the host environment: no prepared PM Python env, and `ruamel` is missing from the Python those tests pick up. They are not affected by this change; CI runs them in a prepared env.

## Deliberately unchanged
- `terminal-ipc.ts` / `external-terminal.ts`: the user's shell is the user's environment.
- `shell-path.ts` merge order into `process.env`: it feeds the terminal, so the fix lives in the Hermes-child env builders instead.
- The Windows staged-installer recovery hand-off (`main.ts`, `spawnUpdaterProcess` with `process.env`): Windows-only, and the login-shell merge never runs on win32, so the store order there is whatever was inherited.
- Desktop uninstall (`hermes_cli.main uninstall`): out of scope.
- No facts.json parsing in Electron. Every store tool dir lives under the store root, so a containment rule is enough.

raw.body:
`hermes update` no longer exits 1 when a dashboard it just stopped and respawned is a not-yet-reaped zombie, and the handoff E2E (`test_update_exit_status_matches_what_came_back`) stops failing on unrelated branches because of it.

This PR carries @kshitijk4poor's fix from #125682 unchanged (their commit, their authorship) and adds a deterministic reproduction of the CI failure plus the removal of the now-obsolete HEAD dashboard gate. If #125682 lands first, this PR shrinks to the gate commit.

## Root cause (product bug, not a harness race)
The update stops the manual dashboard (`dashboard_procs._wait_gone` → `gateway.status._pid_exists` counts a **zombie as gone**), respawns it with a non-waiting `Popen`, and runs the survivor probe (`_surviving_pre_update_serve_runtimes` → `ledger_entries()`) milliseconds later. The ledger's non-strict liveness check (`process_identity._pid_alive_matches` → `_same_incarnation`) compares only `create_time`, which a zombie keeps until its parent reaps it, so it reads the old dashboard as **alive**. The runtime is booked `unaccounted` and the update exits 1 while the new dashboard is serving. Users whose dashboard's parent reaps lazily or never (a container PID 1 without an init, a supervisor script that doesn't `wait()`) get that false failure on every update.

The handoff sandbox agent reaps its children every 0.1 s, so CI lost the race sometimes. The cgroup was a red herring: after #124940 the CI dashboard takes the respawn path, same as on a dev box.

CI evidence: job 108684143708 (fix/ffmpeg-btbn-repin) and job 108695482545 (#125589) both show `✓ stopped PID 14x` → `✓ restarted: … dashboard --port …` → `These serve/dashboard processes still run pre-update code: pid 14x` → `✗ dashboard [default] pid 14x — planned mechanism: respawn-argv`, rc=1, with the new dashboard up.

## Changes
- `hermes_cli/process_identity.py` (#125682, @kshitijk4poor): the non-strict `_pid_alive_matches` reports a zombie as dead, as the strict path and `_pid_exists` already do. Test: `ledger_entries()` excludes a real killed-but-unreaped child.
- `tests/e2e/core/upgrade/handoff/_scenario.py`: drop `DASHBOARD_GATES["head"]`. #124940 makes the HEAD update respawn a dashboard started inside `hosted-compute-agent.service` instead of restarting the unit. In the failing CI runs above, `test_dashboard_is_back_on_its_port` passed rather than xfailed. The N-1 column keeps the gate until a release carrying #124940 is N-1.

## Validation
Handoff HEAD column run inside a transient user unit (`systemd-run --user`, same shape as the CI job running inside a systemd service). The injection is a scratch copy of `tests/e2e/core/upgrade/handoff/_ns_agent.py` whose reaper runs every 3 s instead of every 0.1 s (a parent that reaps lazily); it is not committed.

| run | base (origin/main) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| clean, systemd-run --user | 7 passed (the race is intermittent) | 7 passed |
| lazy-reap injection | **1 failed**: `update exited 1 though the gateway and the dashboard came back`, `dashboard pid 147 — planned mechanism: respawn-argv` (exact CI signature) | **7 passed** |

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_process_identity.py::test_ledger_entries_excludes_a_killed_but_unreaped_process`: fails on base, passes here.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_process_identity.py` + `test_update_serve_generation_recovery.py`: 79 passed.
- ruff, `check_no_tmp_literals.py`, `check_compat_pointers.py`: clean.

raw.body:
## Summary

Plugin inventory can take 40–80 seconds on a treeless (`tree:0`) source checkout because the catalog's path-scoped `git log` lazily fetches missing historical trees. This can exceed the Desktop's 30-second gateway request timeout.

- Use the existing `bounded_git_probe()` helper for the catalog date. It scopes `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` to the child, disables interactive Git behavior, and bounds process-tree cleanup on timeout.
- When history is unavailable in a Git checkout, use the newest checked-out catalog file's mtime. This preserves the fresh checkout's pin over an older live document, including equal or absent version labels. Full clones retain the precise commit time; release installs and never-checked-out clones retain the `None` fallback.
- Resolve pins, versions, and titles from one `load_catalog_live()` pass per plugin listing instead of three.

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/125683

## Verification

On head `db6ec3aab608b9aada68d4190c1eb9c5dd04271e`, the canonical runner reports **50 passed, 0 failed across seven files**:

```sh
HERMES_TEST_FILE_RETRIES=0 scripts/run_tests.sh \
  tests/agent/test_subprocess_env_guard.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_catalog.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins_cmd_catalog.py \
  tests/tui_gateway/test_plugins_manage_install.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_git_probe_no_lazy_fetch.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_bounded_probe_run.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_git_probe_tree_kill.py
```

The subprocess environment guard was reproduced failing before the helper change and passes afterward. Coverage includes real `file:// --filter=tree:0` clones, fresh/stale checkout pin precedence, one catalog resolution per listing, and bounded process-tree cleanup.

An additional local run of `tests/test_windows_subprocess_no_window_flags.py` hit a home-I/O isolation assertion in the unrelated `shell.exec` test; it is not included in the passing count above. Hosted CI remains the cross-platform gate.

raw.body:
Remaining items from the packaged-toolchain-only audit: "only hermes and only packaged package managers (uv/pip/node/npm) should ever be used". The Electron half is #125681.

## What changes

- **Post-write lint** (`tools/file_operations_lint.py`). On the local backend, `.js`/`.ts` lint (`node --check`, `npx tsc --noEmit`) used to run through the terminal shell. That shell's PATH puts the user's dirs first, so on this machine it picked `~/.local/bin/node` v26.5.1. It now runs PM's node/npx directly with `with_hermes_node_path`. If PM has no Node, the lint is skipped; it never falls back to the user's copy. Remote backends (docker/ssh/modal) are unchanged because PM's Node isn't there. The user's interactive terminal PATH order is also unchanged.
- **`pm.activate()` / drift** (`pm/install.py`). Before, any drift made activate prepend nothing at all, and a store dir already on PATH was never moved forward. Now the store dirs always go to the front, including ones already on PATH behind a user dir. The drift case still returns the problems, and it keeps the property it protected (git log `3d12e86ef13e`, "fail fast rather than serving a partial PATH"), now enforced per package: `_store_path_dirs` drops any package whose dependency chain isn't fully installed, so store npm over a missing store node never reaches PATH. New `pm.store_first_path(path)` does the same for child PATHs that get dirs prepended after activate.
- **tui_gateway** `_prepend_tool_paths`. PM store dirs now go ahead of `~/.local/bin`, which is where a user-installed uv lives, and ahead of the venv/managed bin.
- **MCP stdio launchers** (`tools/mcp_tool_config.py`). A bare `npx`/`npm`/`node`/`uv`/`uvx` (including `.cmd`/`.exe` spellings) now resolves to PM's copy, with PM's toolchain dirs first on the child PATH (npx re-execs `env node`). The old system fallback table is gone: `uv_tool_dirs` (`~/.local/bin`, Homebrew) and `/usr/local/bin` + `~/.local/bin` for node. If a `command:` is an absolute path, the user's choice is kept. PM ships no build on Termux, so Termux keeps the platform copy. `pm.uv_launcher(name)` is a new read-only accessor for PM's installed uv/uvx. Hermes's own Python work still goes through PM operations.

## Tests
One or two per behavior, each red on `origin/main`:
- `tests/pm/test_startup_activation.py`: store dirs move ahead of a user dir; drift activates intact chains only.
- `tests/tools/test_file_operations_edge_cases.py::test_local_js_lint_runs_pm_node_never_the_users`
- `tests/gateway/test_tui_slash_worker_path.py::test_pm_store_dirs_go_ahead_of_user_local_bin`
- `tests/tools/test_mcp_tool_issue_948.py`: bare npx → PM npm/node first; bare uvx → PM uv; an absolute path is kept.

I deleted the tests that pinned the removed system fallbacks. Two unrelated cwd/malware tests that happened to use `npx` now stub the launcher.

## Live probe (real PM store, user stand-ins first on PATH), base → head
- activate with the store node dir behind a user dir: `which(node)` user stand-in → `~/.hermes/tools/node-26.7.0-linux-x64/bin/node`
- MCP `npx`: user stand-in → `~/.hermes/tools/npm-12.0.2-linux-x64/bin/npx`, with PATH[0] = store npm
- MCP `uvx`: user stand-in → `~/.hermes/tools/uv-0.12.3-linux-x64/uvx`. An absolute user uvx is unchanged.
- tui PATH[0]: `~/.hermes/bin` → store dir
- lint: terminal-shell `~/.local/bin/node` v26.5.1 → PM node v26.7.0

raw.body:
## What does this PR do?

The Docker build sets `HERMES_PYTHON=/usr/local/bin/python3` for build helpers and leaves that value in the final image. The TUI launcher accepts the executable and gives it to the JSON-RPC gateway child. That child then exits with `hermes: no dependency environment is committed for this install`, although the image has a sealed dependency environment at `/opt/hermes/.venv`.

Keep system Python for the build steps, then point `HERMES_PYTHON` at the packaged venv in the final image. This matches the interpreter used by the image's `hermes` launcher.

## Related Issue

No public issue. Reproduced from a fresh local Docker image launched with `--tui`.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `Dockerfile`: switch `HERMES_PYTHON` to `/opt/hermes/.venv/bin/python` after the image build has finished using system Python.
- `tests/docker/test_tui_prebuilt_bundle.py`: exercise the image's real TUI interpreter selection as the container user, then import the gateway in the selected child Python. The test avoids `su`, which would clear the image environment and hide the regression.

## How to Test

1. Build the image: `docker build -t hermes-agent-tui-runtime-python:local .`
2. Run the focused Docker regression with that image: `HERMES_TEST_IMAGE=hermes-agent-tui-runtime-python:local scripts/run_tests.sh tests/docker/test_tui_prebuilt_bundle.py -k tui_gateway_child -j 4`
3. Start the image with `--tui` and no `HERMES_PYTHON` override. The gateway child should use the packaged venv and stay up.

Local verification on Docker Desktop's Linux/amd64 builder: the image build completed, and the new test function passed against the built image. Forcing the old `HERMES_PYTHON=/usr/local/bin/python3` value on the same image reproduced exit 1 with the original dependency-environment error. The canonical targeted runner on this Windows host stopped in its global fixture before running the test because the host's Python test environment lacks `ruamel.yaml`. The Docker CI lane builds the image and runs `tests/docker/` with its prepared test environment.

### Code

- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)

raw.body:
Agent-run children (terminal, `execute_code`, background processes, helper tools) no longer receive platform adapter secrets such as `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `WEIXIN_TOKEN`, `FEISHU_ENCRYPT_KEY` or `PHOTON_SIDECAR_TOKEN`, or Hermes' own dashboard-auth secrets. Language servers and their installers, the raft bridge, the buzz CLI, openviking-server, the bot desktop and the Telegram gmail-triage scripts now start from the scrubbed environment instead of Hermes' full one. Variables that belong to the user, such as `SLACK_USER_TOKEN` or `LOCAL_LLM_API_KEY`, are left alone.

Salvage of #122751 and #125191 by @jonpol01. Those PRs also carry commits from @andrexibiza and @necoweb3. All 11 of their commits are kept with authorship. Twelve follow-up commits from review and CI sit on top.

## Why

The child-env scrub strips credentials Hermes knows about: provider keys, bot tokens, and `OPTIONAL_ENV_VARS` messaging entries. Adapters read more secrets than that list names. Webhook signing secrets, app secrets and sidecar tokens read straight from the environment therefore reached every terminal command the agent ran. Several spawn sites also either built the scrubbed env and then spread `os.environ` back over it, or skipped the builder altogether.

## What changed

From #122751 / #125191:
- Adapter secrets are always stripped (Tier 1), including from children started with `inherit_credentials=True`, and skill or config passthrough refuses them. OAuth provider-profile keys join the blocklist.
- A passthrough accepted before an adapter claimed the name stops forwarding it once the adapter registers.
- LSP servers, the npm and `go install` installers, the raft bridge, the buzz CLI and openviking-server spawn from the scrubbed env.
- The spawn-env guard test now also catches `**os.environ` spreads and scans `plugins/`.

Follow-ups from review:
1. **Adapter secrets are the declared ones.** The PR matched any `<platform>_…_TOKEN/_SECRET/_PASSWORD/_KEY` name. Its platform list includes plain words (LOCAL, GATEWAY, WEBHOOK, SLACK), so the rule also stripped user variables Hermes never reads, and `terminal.env_passthrough` could not restore them. The list also failed open: one unreadable plugins dir cached an empty set. The set now has three sources:
   - Core `password` messaging entries of `OPTIONAL_ENV_VARS`, plus the secret entries of the bundled platform plugin manifests (Tier 1).
   - The secret entries of the bound profile's own user-installed platform plugins (Tier 1). These are read per spawn, per profile, and refreshed when a manifest changes, so under multiplex one profile's plugin never strips a same-named variable from another profile's children.
   - Secret-named keys that the gateway env-override table reads (Tier 1).
   - Secret-named `required_env` of adapters registered in the current profile, read per spawn without loading deferred adapters. These are Tier 2 only, because `required_env` is an unchecked setup list and a plugin that lists `OPENAI_API_KEY` must not strip it from credentialed children.

   Five secrets that nothing declared got a manifest entry. Three names read only in code sit in a short list in the policy module. One suffix rule (`PLATFORM_SECRET_ENV_SUFFIXES`) decides what counts as secret-named everywhere.

   None of these sources fail open. An unreadable bundled or `plugins/platforms/` manifest, or a registry error, fails the spawn instead of dropping the declaration. A manifest that doesn't parse declares nothing, because its adapter can't load either. An unsearchable dir such as a root-owned `__pycache__`, or an unreadable flat `plugins/*` manifest, is skipped with a warning.
2. **The compute host keeps Hermes' full environment.** It runs dashboard agent turns, and its `os.environ` layer is deliberate (#65895). Without it, keys that exist only in the process env (Docker `-e`, systemd) disappeared from turns, for example `HASS_TOKEN`, `MODAL_TOKEN_ID` and `DAYTONA_API_KEY`. `.env` keys came back anyway because the host reloads `.env`.
3. **openviking, raft and buzz keep the user's HOME** (`HERMES_REAL_HOME`). Their config and logins live there, and the builder rewrites HOME to the profile home in containers, including the official image.
4. **Hermes' own secrets that no source covered are now blocked:** the dashboard basic-auth password and signing secret, the dashboard drain and OIDC client secrets, `HERMES_ANON_API_SECRET`, and the Google Meet realtime key. The dashboard ones are Tier 1, so credential-inheriting CLIs such as claude and codex don't get them either. The session token next to them was already stripped.
5. **openviking-server takes provider keys from the bound profile,** not the launch profile. It then gets a second Tier 1 scrub, because the profile overlay would otherwise re-add that profile's bot and dashboard tokens. With no profile bound under multiplex, it refuses to start.
6. **Two more full-env spawns are fixed.** The bot desktop launcher now builds from `served_profile_child_env()`, like the agent browser. The agent drives that desktop, and its dock opens a terminal. The Telegram gmail-triage buttons run a script under `HERMES_HOME` that the agent can write. It now uses `build_subprocess_env`, like cron and webhook-filter scripts. In containers, those scripts therefore see the profile HOME, as cron scripts already do.

## Behaviour to know

Declared adapter secrets are now also stripped from children that run Hermes itself with inherited credentials: the restart watcher, the launchd fallback, the slash worker and `cli.exec`. Main already did this for `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` and `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`. Values from `.env` are re-read by those children. A value supplied only through systemd `Environment=` or `docker -e` is not passed to them.

## Not changed (follow-ups)

- **`key_cmd` token helpers still receive the bound profile's full `.env`, bot tokens included.** They run the user's own command and use the same overlay openviking now scrubs a second time. They are left alone here, because a `gh auth token` helper may legitimately need `GH_TOKEN`. That needs its own decision.
- **A detached `/restart` whose watcher env fails to build still stops the gateway.** That's existing behaviour for any helper-launch failure, such as a missing binary. This PR adds one more way the env can fail: an unreadable platform manifest.
- **The spawn-env guard does not yet match `{k: v for k, v in os.environ.items()}` or `dict(os.environ)`.** That shape is how the bot desktop slipped past it. Widening the guard flags about ten more sites, which each need a judgement call.
- **The raft bridge uses the launch profile's scrubbed env, not `served_profile_child_env()`.** The raft CLI reads its own `RAFT_PROFILE`, and the routed builder can raise when no scope is bound at connect time.

## Verification

- Live check on the final tree, with the plugins-dir scan forced to raise:
  - Declared secrets reach no child: terminal, non-terminal, or inherit.
  - Five user variables reach all three.
  - Passthrough accepts the user names and refuses the secrets.
- A plugin whose `required_env` lists `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` and `SLACK_USER_TOKEN`: credentialed children keep all of them, and the terminal drops them.
- Full suite, run from a clean clone of this branch before the last two commits: 53,869 passed and 301 failed. Re-running each failure on its own against origin/main: 2 were caused by this branch, both in `test_modal_snapshot_isolation.py`, which stubbed `hermes_cli.config`. They are fixed. All the others fail on origin/main too, from the local Python version, a missing `tomli_w`, and a full disk partway through the run.
- Targeted suites on the final tree (env policy, spawn sites, passthrough, modal, provider import order, platform registry, plugin env injection, openviking, bot desktop, session API): 296 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `test_runtime_provenance_is_independent_of_aliases_and_virtual_env[True]`, which fails on origin/main too.
- New tests cover per-profile plugin secrets under multiplex, in-place manifest edits, unreadable manifests (strict vs skipped), openviking with a routed profile's `.env`, a bundled manifest read failing closed, manifest deletion, and a symlinked home alias. Mutation checks: removing the openviking fix, keying the cache by the raw path, re-raising on an unsearchable dir, and keeping a partial bundled set each make a test fail.
- The per-home manifest stamp is one `scandir` per root, taken once per scrub. With 60 user plugins, `hermes_subprocess_env()` takes about 1.6 ms.
- The spawn-site test runs in profile-home mode and checks HOME for each child. Removing the raft HOME line makes it fail. `ty` gives the same output on the changed files as on origin/main.
- The bot desktop launcher and the gmail-triage spawn have no test harness. A probe showed their env drops only the intended secrets (plus `PYTHONPATH`) and keeps `LANG`, proxies, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`.

## plugin-catalog: bump memex8 to v1.1.0

Bumps the pinned SHA from `b5e87b7b` (v1.0.0) to `47fbe5b8` (v1.1.0) so users running `hermes plugins install memex8` get the six new features in the v1.1.0 release.

### Six new features (all default-off)

| # | Feature | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Per-session injection dedup | Stops re-injecting the same memory across turns; char-budget gate drops low-priority memories |
| 2 | Decision/evaluation promotion | Promotes turns with `decided`, `shipped`, `learned`, etc. to slower-decay memory types |
| 3 | Prompt-injection sanitization | Neutralizes `{{template}}`, `${template}`, unbalanced triple-backticks, `javascript:`/`vbscript:`/`data:text/html` URLs on read |
| 4 | Configurable system-prompt template | User can override the default preamble with `{{version}}`, `{{tool_*}}`, `{{base_url}}` substitutions |
| 5 | Export/import memories as JSON | Round-trip the whole store through `GET /api/v1/memories` for backup/migration |
| 6 | `/memex8` slash command | `stats`, `status`, `search`, `recall`, `remember`, `forget`, `export`, `import`, `realms`, `help` |

### Why the SHA bump is a "minor" version, not "patch"

Six new behaviors, six new config keys (`dedup_injected_memories`, `recall_max_inject_chars`, `promote_decisions`, `promote_evaluations`, `sanitize_for_prompt`, `enable_export_import`, `system_prompt_template`), and a new slash command. All default-off — existing users on v1.0.0 see zero behavior change until they opt in.

### Spec changes

- `sha`: `b5e87b7b9a537ec663dd0c5d68a5ebf819976abc` → `47fbe5b8813e712c8f0a52c6d4e5ab37e09498f5`
- `version`: `1.0.0` → `1.1.0`
- `image`: pinned to new SHA so catalog preview renders
- `description`: extended with the six-feature summary (preserves the existing disclosure sentence)
- `provides_hooks`: restored to `[on_session_end, on_pre_compress]` (was `[]` in the prior entry — both hooks are still implemented and surfaced in `plugin.yaml`)

### Reference

- Plan: https://github.com/Ex8-ca/memex8/blob/main/PLAN-memex8-v1.1-features.md
- Plugin repo: https://github.com/Ex8-ca/memex8
- Prior catalog PR: #125315 (merged)

Closes: bumping the v1.0.0 catalog entry added by #125315.

raw.body:
A fresh install comes with computer use and the Browser Use CLI working again: cua-driver is a default PM package, and the installers and `hermes update` provision the Browser Use CLI.

## Root cause

The unified package manager (3d12e86ef13) and the MSIX installer rework (47f4ab3a178) removed the install-time cua-driver fetch (7060ac7bedd) and the Browser Use CLI install (baa6b2e34d8), and the only PM default left was `agent-browser`. On a fresh install the `computer_use` check_fn stays False, so the tool never reaches the model and `cua_backend.start()`'s lazy ensure never fires. `browser_exec` silently falls back to the built-in tools.

## Changes

- `pm/packages.py`: `CuaDriver.default = True`, so the installers' PM stage, a bare `hermes pm install` and `hermes update` install it on every target it builds for (macOS, Windows, glibc Linux). Adds the missing `linux-arm64-bionic` gap: the lock has no Android artifact, and without the gap a default would fail every Termux install.
- `hermes_cli/update_cmd_maint.py`: the default-tool step, which the installers (via source completion) and `hermes update` both run, now provisions the Browser Use CLI for the default and explicit `browser-use` backends, with a 180 s timeout. `--skip-browser` declines it together with agent-browser; `off` and Camofox never use it. The per-package message stops calling every default "browser tools".
- `scripts/install.sh` / `install.ps1`: bring back `--skip-computer-use` / `-SkipComputerUse`, recorded as `--without cua-driver`.
- Docs: installation, computer use, browser, package management.

Salvages #122428 by @whyyagswhy (its commit is kept as authored). This PR widens it to the installers, cua-driver and the opt-out, and trims its tests to one invariant.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Live, fresh isolated home + PM runtime (`HOME`, `HERMES_HOME`, `HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR` in scratch), origin/main | `computer_use check_fn: False`, `is_browser_use_cli_mode: False`, PM defaults `['agent-browser']` |
| Same probe, this branch, running the real default-tool step | 40 s. cua-driver 0.21.0 installed into the runtime, Browser Use CLI in `environments/browser-use`, `computer_use check_fn: True`, `is_browser_use_cli_mode: True` |
| Real `browser_exec` through the provisioned CLI + packaged Chromium | `success: true`, printed `Example Domain` |
| Negative: `agent-browser` + `cua-driver` declined, fresh runtime | nothing installed, runtime dir empty, CLI absent |
| `tests/pm/test_install_default_closure.py` new invariant | red on origin/main (cua-driver not in defaults), red without the bionic gap (default target with no artifact), green here |
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_browser_use_cli_provision.py` | red on origin/main, green here |
| tests/pm, installation, scripts, computer_use, update/install/tools_config | identical 81 host-environment failures on origin/main and this branch (worktree + fake-home git/runtime tests), 0 new |

## Not covered

- Desktop sealed bundles already ship cua-driver (every lock package), but not the Browser Use CLI: it is a per-home PM tool environment, not a store package, and sealed installs skip the maintenance step.
- PM tool environments are anchored to `get_hermes_home()`, so a non-default profile does not see the CLI installed in the root home.
- macOS and Windows were not live-run. The macOS LaunchServices registration still happens on the next `hermes update` or `hermes tools` enable, same as the existing lazy path.

raw.body:
`⌘1…⌘9` is one chord with two meanings: the Nth tab of the pane under the pointer (else the focused pane, else the workspace's) when that pane is a real tab strip, and the Nth profile otherwise. #92639 (for #92569) removed the tab half entirely — `profile.switch.N` became unconditional and `view.tabSlot.N` shipped unbound — so holding ⌘ still painted the tab-number hints while the chord switched profiles. The legitimate complaint in #92569 was narrower: the tab dispatch was hardcoded inside the profile handler, so rebinding the chord could not separate the two.

This restores the contextual behavior as two independent actions on the same chord.

- `KeybindActionMeta.passthrough`: the handler may return `false` to decline, handing the chord to the next action bound to it.
- `$comboIndex` keeps every action on a chord in registration order; the dispatcher walks it and stops at the first action that runs.
- `view.tabSlot.N` defaults to `mod+N` ahead of `profile.switch.N` and declines when no zone is a tab strip or the strip has no Nth tab. Rebind either and only that one moves.
- `conflictsFor` does not report a passthrough action layered over a later one, so the panel stops flagging the shipped pair; a non-passthrough action landing on someone else's chord is still a conflict.
- The held-⌘ tab hints key off `view.tabSlot.N`, the action they describe.
- Docs (`desktop.md`, `multi-connection-desktop.md`) describe the chord's two meanings.

Tests: a dispatch test drives real `keydown` events through `useKeybinds` for hover → tab, no strip → profile, and no Nth tab → profile; store tests pin combo-index order, per-action rebinding, and conflict reporting. Verified live in a dev instance: ⌘1/⌘2 switch the main strip's tabs with the pointer over it and the hints render on the tabs.

Fixes #92569 regression from #92639.

Large pastes lost their chip once a turn left the composer. The live bubble showed the caption with a chip under it. Checked in a worktree Desktop against real sessions: a captioned paste renders `/pr-triage` in the bubble with the chip under it, and a bare paste renders one bubble holding the chip. Tests cover hydration (captioned, bare, and mixed with an image) and the chip label.

raw.body:
Four commits, each one catalog change for `memory-rewind`:

1. **`fix(plugin-catalog)`: fit the card inside the plugin page header.** Re-pins `b747327` → `e5b139b`, which only redraws `docs/card.png`.
2. **`feat(plugin-catalog)`: bump to 1.3.0.** Re-pins → `5f935c2` ([range](https://github.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-memory-rewind/compare/e5b139b...5f935c2)), fixes wrong provenance, and adds `pre_llm_call` to `provides_hooks`.
3. **`feat(plugin-catalog)`: bump to 1.3.1.** Re-pins → `b9af50b` ([range](https://github.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-memory-rewind/compare/5f935c2...b9af50b)). Importing a Hermes backup no longer cuts off the history recorded after it.
4. **`feat(plugin-catalog)`: bump to 1.3.2.** Re-pins → `3549271` ([range](https://github.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-memory-rewind/compare/b9af50b...3549271)). `restore` no longer replaces a running agent's memory write, and its plan lists the memory entries it brings back and removes.

`image` stays at `e5b139b` throughout. Commits 3 and 4 change only `sha` and `version`, and each pinned sha passes the pinned-source validate on its own, so the branch can land commit by commit. The branch is rebased onto current `main`; the first two commits' content is unchanged.

## 1.3.1: `hermes import` cut off the history recorded after the backup

`hermes backup` archives `plugin-data/memory-rewind/history.git`. `hermes import` (the dashboard's import runs the same command) overwrites every file the archive holds and leaves the rest, so the history's ref went back to the backup's head. Every version recorded after the backup, the state right before the import included, dropped out of `log`, and `gc` later deletes it for good.

Real `hermes backup -o` → two more memory writes → `hermes import --force` → one more turn, on Hermes main:

| | 1.3.0 (`5f935c2`) | 1.3.1 (`b9af50b`) |
|---|---|---|
| `hermes memory-rewind log` after the import | 3 versions; both written after the backup are gone | 6 versions |
| Unreachable commits (`git fsck --unreachable`) | 2, pruned by `gc` later | 0 |
| The import itself | not visible | one version, `history restored from an older copy; later versions kept`, that `restore` can undo |

**Fix.**
- Each published head leaves an empty marker file under `plugin-data/memory-rewind/tips/`. A marker newer than the backup survives the import, and a marker the head does not contain names cut-off history.
- `log` includes such tips, and the next snapshot builds on the newest one, so the import is recorded as one change.
- A copy from an unrelated history (a backup from another machine) is joined as a second parent instead of dropped; `log` lists a join's changes against the first parent.
- The usual case (one marker, the head's own) costs a directory listing and no git call.
- It protects any import made after 1.3.1 has run once (a session start is enough), whichever version made the backup.

It also fixes the plugin page's link to the design notes. The page resolves relative links against `memory-rewind/`, so `docs/DESIGN.md` was a 404; the link is now absolute.

## 1.3.2: `restore` could replace a running agent's memory write

`restore` wrote `MEMORY.md`/`USER.md` without the memory tool's lock and never checked the file against the plan it had shown. Both cases on Hermes main, with the real `MemoryStore`:

| What happened | 1.3.1 | 1.3.2 |
|---|---|---|
| A memory write is in flight (`MemoryStore._mutate` holds the lock and has read the file) when the restore applies | prints `Done`; the agent's write then lands on top and the restored entry is gone | waits for the lock, sees the file changed since its plan, refuses; the agent's entry is kept |
| One entry is deleted (Star Map / `hermes journey delete`), the agent adds another, and the user restores the version before the delete | the plan says only `write memories/MEMORY.md`; the newer entry is removed without a word | the plan lists `brings back: Project Atlas uses Postgres 16` and `removes: Editor: Helix` |

**Fix.**
- Restore holds the memory tool's own lock while it checks and writes a memory file, waiting up to 10 s. The lock is `<file>.lock`: `flock` on POSIX, a one-byte `msvcrt` lock at offset 0 on Windows. It is the lock `MemoryStore._file_lock` takes on both v0.21.5 and main, and the one journey edits moved under for #119668.
- It refuses when any file the plan looked at changed since the plan was made.
- A lock error other than "held by someone else" fails at once instead of waiting.
- For `MEMORY.md`/`USER.md`, the plan lists the entries the restore brings back and the entries it removes, split the way the memory store splits them.

**Tests** (extending the existing files):
- Real `hermes backup` / `hermes import` end to end.
- Emulated imports: a backup made by 1.3.1 and by 1.3.0, unchanged files, an unrelated history, stale and foreign markers, and no git call in the usual case.
- A real in-flight `MemoryStore._mutate` during a restore.
- The lock held the way Hermes holds it: wait, give up, lock error.
- A memory file and a skill changed after the plan; the entry preview through the CLI.

**Verification.**
- **Old code:** on Hermes main the new end-to-end tests fail on the previous plugin code: `log` lacks the post-backup version, `DID NOT RAISE RestoreError`, and no preview lines.
- **Mutation** (Hermes main): 15/15 mutants killed for 1.3.1 and 14/15 for 1.3.2. The survivor drops the explicit unlock, which closing the descriptor also does on POSIX. It stays for Windows, where Hermes unlocks explicitly too.

**Scope note.**
- Skills are not locked during a restore: `skill_manage` keys its per-skill lock on an internal digest of the skill name, not a documented contract. The changed-after-plan check still covers them.
- Bringing back a single entry while keeping the rest is not in this PR. This PR makes the whole-file restore say what it removes.

## 1.3.0: changes made outside the agent's turns were credited to the next call or session

A version recorded after a tool call, or at turn end, took everything that had changed since the previous version and credited it to that call or session. Two cases, run end to end on Hermes main with real `AIAgent` turns (FakeLLMServer), `memory.write_approval: true`, and the functions the handlers themselves call. The output is `hermes memory-rewind log`:

| What happened | 1.2.0 (`e5b139b`) | 1.3.0 (`5f935c2`) |
|---|---|---|
| Turn 1 stages a memory `add`. `/memory approve` applies it (`handle_pending_subcommand`). Turn 2 stages a `remove`, which changes nothing | `after memory` · `via memory: remove (memory)` · `from telegram, session tg-session`, holding the approved **add** | `turn start`, with no `via` and no `from` |
| The curator archives a skill while no session runs (`_archive_as_curator`). A new session starts on Discord | `session start` · `from discord, session dc-session` | `session start`, with no `from` |

Same results on v0.21.5. The catalog's `memory-review` Desktop plugin exists to approve staged memory writes, so the first case is a real workflow.

**Fix.**
- Every turn now starts with a synchronous baseline on `pre_llm_call`, and the session-start baseline no longer names the session.
- Both baselines name no call and no session. They first let queued snapshots land, with a 5 s cap, so a queued version keeps its call's change.
- The `pre_llm_call` callback declares only `session_id` and `platform`. Hermes passes a narrow-signature callback only the fields it declares (`_hook_callback_kwargs`), so the plugin never receives the user message or the conversation. It returns `None`, so nothing is injected into the prompt.
- Cost is one no-change snapshot per turn: 43 ms median, 45 ms p90, on the 333-file default tree.

**Tests** (extending the existing files):
- The approve-between-turns and archive-between-sessions cases, through the real memory tool, the real approval flow and `skill_usage.archive_skill`.
- A queued version landing before the baseline.
- The narrow `pre_llm_call` signature.
- `pre_llm_call` running in a multiplexed profile's scope.

**Verification.**
- **Mutation:** 9/9 mutants killed on both v0.21.5 and main (dropping the flush, dropping the turn-start baseline, the session claim back, a wide or context-returning callback, and others).
- **Old code:** both new tests fail on the 1.2.0 plugin code, with `'after memory' == 'turn start'` and `[('s2', 'discord')] == []`.

**Scope note.**
- **Not `pre_tool_call`.** It would isolate each call exactly, but Hermes fails it closed: a slow or raising callback blocks the tool, and a history plugin must never block a memory write.
- **Not `on_skill_lifecycle`.** `archived` also fires inside a background-review `skill_manage` delete, with no session id, so a separate version there would take the change away from its call.
- **Known gap, documented in the README's Limits.** Snapshots after a call and at turn end still run in the background and land within a fraction of a second. A change something else makes in that window, or while a turn is running, still goes with that call or turn.
- **`requires_hermes` stays `>=0.21.5`.** A probe with a real `AIAgent` turn showed the same hook order and payloads on v0.21.5 and main: `on_session_start → pre_llm_call → pre_tool_call → post_tool_call → on_session_end`.

## Card: fit inside the plugin page header

The plugin page header renders `image` at full width with `max-height: 360px; object-fit: cover`. At viewports of 1200px and wider the header is 1134×360, so only rows 110–490 of a 1200×600 image are visible. On the `b747327` card, https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/memory-rewind cut off the title and clipped the last history line.

The redrawn card puts the title and tagline on one row and centres the content vertically, so every drawn pixel sits in rows 127–477. It is still 1200×600 and still the plugin's real `/memory-history` output. Same shape as #124991 / #124992.

Measured in Chrome on the live site, with the entry's image URL served from each file:

| Where | Viewport | Rows visible (of 600) | `b747327` | `e5b139b` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Plugin page header | 1200, 1280, 1440, 1920 | 110–490 | title and last line cut | all visible |
| Plugin page header | 1024 | 75–526 | all visible | all visible |
| Plugin page header | 768 | 6–594 | all visible | all visible |
| Plugin page header | 390 | all rows (3px off each side) | all visible | all visible |
| Catalog grid card (2:1 slot, #125538) | 1440, 390 | whole image | all visible | all visible |

The Desktop catalog card and detail view use a 2:1 frame (`aspect-[2/1]`), so they show the whole image either way.

## Checked

- `validate_plugin_catalog.py` with `ruamel.yaml==0.18.17`: 338 files valid at commits 3 and 4.
- Pinned-source validate at `b9af50b` and at `3549271`: `plugins validate --install-deps` passed, the security scan reported safe, and the self-updater gate is clean. Scanner findings are the same as at 1.3.0: one medium `python_subprocess` for the git call.
- Plugin CI 8/8 at both pins:
  - `b9af50b` ([run](https://github.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-memory-rewind/actions/runs/36380745016)): end to end 170 on v0.21.5 and on main; unit 155 on Linux and macOS, 150 on Windows.
  - `3549271` ([run](https://github.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-memory-rewind/actions/runs/36380961242)): end to end 182 on v0.21.5 and on main; unit 165 on Linux and macOS, 160 on Windows. The Windows skips are the existing six.
- Installing by name from this branch's catalog gives revision `3549271`, pinned, at 1.3.2. A real oneshot agent turn with the GitHub-pinned install records the memory write on v0.21.5 and on main.
- The README at both pins and the image URL return HTTP 200.
- No other open PR touches the `memory-rewind` entry.

![memory-rewind card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-memory-rewind/e5b139b1059a47df34002e76a7bfd84bc60d9f35/docs/card.png)

raw.body:
## Summary

Two Desktop/TUI session-management gaps, one small PR:

- **`session.archive` RPC** (#47168): the TUI gateway had no JSON-RPC equivalent of the Desktop `PATCH /api/sessions/{id}` archive flow, so TUI clients had to keep every session visible or delete it permanently. The new method sits next to `session.set_hidden` in `tui_gateway/methods_session.py` and mirrors its two-tier resolution: a live runtime id first (a not-yet-persisted draft defers via `pending_archived`, applied by `_ensure_session_db_row` exactly like `pending_hidden`), then a stored id/key resolved through the profile db — which covers the historical rows the `session.list` picker shows, the gap open PR #47184 was held open for. Wire contract declared in `tui_gateway/contracts/sessions.py` and rendered into the generated TS/OpenRPC catalog.
- **`inline_images=false` on history reads** (#116511): `_history_dict_text` has always had both image renderings, but `_coerce_message_text` hard-coded `image_urls=True` at both call sites, so a remote client re-read the sum of every attachment the conversation ever carried (26.30 MiB `session.resume` / 26.33 MiB per REST page read on the measured conversation, paid on every reconnect) with no way to ask for less. `session.resume` now accepts `inline_images` (default `true`) threaded through every path that carries messages — cold/lazy/eager resume and the live reattach via `_live_session_payload` — and `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages` accepts the same query param, routing content through the identical projection so both surfaces agree by construction. `false` renders `[image]` in place of the data URI; the default is byte-identical to before.

## Behaviour

- `session.archive {session_id | session_key, archived, profile?}` → `{archived, session_key}`; unknown id → 4001, missing id → 4006; archives the whole compression lineage (`SessionDB.set_session_archived`), messages kept.
- `session.resume {..., inline_images?: bool = true}` — `false` renders image parts as `[image]`; text/audio/other parts and non-image rows unchanged.
- `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages?inline_images=false` — same projection on the REST pages the Desktop hydrates over; default unchanged.

## Summary

Adds configurable **Reasoning level up / Reasoning level down** actions to Desktop's keyboard-shortcuts panel, stepping the active session's effort one notch through `off → minimal → low → medium → high → xhigh`.

- Two new Composer rows in the Ctrl+/ panel, shipped unbound (like dictation) so users pick their own chord — Alt+., Ctrl+Alt+↑/↓, Numpad +/-, etc.

## What does this PR do?

Desktop file attachments stage into `<profile home>/attachments`, which sits outside the session workspace. An agent with a restricted workspace can then be unable to read the very files the user attached to it, and per-profile agents each have to be granted access to the shared Hermes-managed dir (#110662).

This adds a top-level `attachments.storage` config key:

- `hermes-home` (default, current behaviour): keep `<profile home>/attachments` — the directory container backends bind-mount, so `@file:` refs resolve in the sandbox (#76577).
- `workspace` (opt-in): stage into `<session workspace>/.hermes/attachments` — inside the allowed ref root, so the `@file:` ref stays workspace-relative and the profile's agent can always read its own attachments back.

The key is read **per profile** from the session's own `config.yaml` (`file.attach` runs before `prompt.submit` installs the profile scope, so the process config still belongs to the launch profile — the same reason as `_profile_configured_cwd`): one serve process can host an opt-in profile and a default profile side by side, each session following its own profile's config. A remote (ssh) profile keeps the profile home dir either way — its workspace lives on the execution host, and the bind-mounted home attachments dir is what container/remote backends receive. Workspace-boundary and path-traversal protections are unchanged: only the staging root moves, inside the allowed root.

## Related Issue

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/110662

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py`: new top-level `attachments.storage` key (`"hermes-home"` default) with user-facing comment docs.
- `tui_gateway/prompt_attachments.py`: `_session_home_dir` honours the opt-in for `attachments` — `_profile_attachments_storage` reads the session profile's config, `_session_attachments_workspace` returns the workspace only when it's a local, existing directory (ssh/remote cwds fall back to the profile home dir). Staging name sanitization and traversal checks untouched.
- `cli-config.yaml.example`: documented the new key with the two modes and the remote caveat.

## How to Test

1. Create a profile whose `config.yaml` sets `attachments.storage: workspace` and whose `terminal.cwd` is a workspace directory.
2. From Desktop, attach a file that lives outside the workspace (e.g. something from `~/Downloads`).
3. The staged copy lands at `<workspace>/.hermes/attachments/...`, and the `@file:` ref is workspace-relative (`.hermes/attachments/...`), so the agent reads it back without any extra allowlist.
4. A profile without the opt-in keeps staging into `<profile home>/attachments`; a profile bound to an ssh workspace does too.
