`hermes update` now tells the truth about git state: no false "history diverged" or rescue ref when a fast-forward fails for another reason, no branch switch under a stopped rebase, no "Update complete!" while the user's patch sits parked in a stash, and no "Not a git repository, please reinstall" when it runs from a PM environment's venv.

| Issue | Root cause (origin/main) | Fix | From | E2E gate flipped |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #124642 | `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py::_pull_updates` sent every non-zero `merge --ff-only` to `_reconcile_diverged_checkout` (rescue ref + `reset --hard` advice), including an `index.lock` or a cut lazy fetch | Reconcile only when `merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD <target>` returns 1; otherwise print git's error and stop, no reset | #124665 (@JoaoMarcos44), cherry-picked | `git/test_foreign_state.py::test_live_index_lock_is_refused_truthfully`, `git/test_truthful_outcome.py::test_transport_failure_is_reported_as_failure` |
| #124644 | `update_cmd.py::_cmd_update_impl` never checked for a git operation in progress; the detached-HEAD branch switch ran under `.git/rebase-merge`, so a later `git rebase --abort` rolled the update back | Refuse up front with `git <op> --abort` advice, using the marker list already in `_early_recovery.py::_GIT_OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS` | #124660 (@JoaoMarcos44), cherry-picked | `git/test_foreign_state.py::test_abandoned_interactive_rebase_is_healed_or_refused` |
| #122557 | `update_cmd_stash.py::_apply_stash` parks a conflicting restore (`_record_stash_disposition("parked", …)`) and returns; `update_cmd_maint.py` then prints `✓ Update complete!` and exits 0 | The run's autostash stays unsettled until it is restored, discarded, or parked because the user asked (`--keep-stash`, a declined prompt). An unsettled stash becomes the completion line (a ⚠ line naming the stash and the `git apply --3way` re-apply command), so the update ends partial, exits 1 and writes a partial receipt. Failure verdicts name it too (the Windows ZIP fallback used to go on to report success) | #122828 (@Finn763), cherry-picked for the run-scoped stash state; our follow-up makes it change the outcome instead of only printing | `git/test_local_modifications.py::test_conflicting_patch_is_recoverable_and_never_reported_complete` |
| #122627 | A PM generation venv imports `hermes_cli` from `<installs>/<key>/environments/<gen>/workspace/`, which has no `.git`. `update_owning_install.py::owning_install_root` only recognized `<checkout>/venv`, so no retarget happened and the git gates refused | `owning_install_root` recognizes a PM generation venv and returns the checkout recorded in `<installs>/<key>/inputs/.project-root`, trusted only when its path hashes to `<key>`. The existing retarget then re-runs `update` / `update --check` on the checkout's code | Ours. #122640 (@liuhao1024) found the same root cause, but its fix still refuses, with better wording; `update --check` would still exit 1 | `pm/test_stamps_and_doctor.py::test_managed_env_hermes_can_check_for_updates` |

Fixes #124642
Fixes #124644
Fixes #122557
Fixes #122627

Salvages #124665 and #124660 (@JoaoMarcos44) and #122828 (@Finn763); their authorship is kept on the cherry-picked commits. The #122627 diagnosis is shared with #122640 (@liuhao1024).

## Left gated (not in this PR)
- `test_managed_env_hermes_reports_the_checkout_as_the_install` (`--version` from the managed venv reports the workspace path) stays gated on #122425. The venv really does run the workspace snapshot's code (#122425: the snapshot drifts and has no install metadata), so reporting the checkout there would be wrong. The fix needs a product decision: should the managed venv's CLI always re-exec onto the checkout, or should the snapshot get resynced plus stamped?
- `test_work_committed_on_a_detached_head_stays_reachable` stays gated on #124643 (a separate bug).

## Validation
- Each flipped E2E cell was run locally: red on origin/main plus the flipped tests, green on this head (numbers below).
- Unit tests: 2 from #124665, 2 from #124660, 1 each for #122557 and #122627. #122828's tests were dropped because they conflict with main and the E2E cell covers that behaviour.

raw.body:
`desktop.log` now stamps each line in local time, in the same format as `agent.log`, `gui.log` and `errors.log`, so all the files in `logs/` use one clock.

## What changed

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| desktop.log line | `[2026-09-28T07:48:19.466Z] [hermes] [boot] ...` (UTC) | `2026-09-28 13:18:19,466 [hermes] [boot] ...` (local) |
| agent.log line | `2026-09-28 13:18:46,062 INFO ...` (local) | unchanged |
| `hermes logs desktop --since 1h` | returns every line, however old | returns only the last hour |

Root cause: the desktop stamp (added for #84405) was UTC ISO-8601. The Python logs use Python's default `asctime` format, which is local time. The `hermes logs` timestamp regex expects that format at the start of a line, and a line it can't parse passes the `--since` filter. So every desktop line passed.

`formatLogStamp()` in `apps/desktop/electron/desktop-log-line.ts` builds the stamp. `rememberLog` in `main.ts` uses it, so `desktop.log`, the in-app RECENT LOGS view and crash forensics all get it.

## Verification

- `electron/desktop-log-line.test.ts`: the stamp names the same local moment as the `Date` it was built from, in the Python format. The test fails on `origin/main`.
- E2E: wrote two lines through the real formatter into a temp `HERMES_HOME/logs/desktop.log` (one two hours old, one current), then ran `hermes logs desktop --since 1h`. Only the current line came back, and its stamp is on the same clock as an `agent.log` line written a moment later. On `origin/main`, both lines come back.
- `npm run check:lint` (apps/desktop): 0 errors.
- anti-slop: no net-new findings (4 touched files).
- Not run: a live Electron boot. The change is the stamp string only; the write path is unchanged.

Found while collecting logs for a Windows bundle bug report: reading the report meant converting `desktop.log` from UTC by hand.


## Addendum: `hermes logs --since` for every log file (commit 07fa4b09cd)

`hermes logs --since`, `--level` and `--component` now give correct results for traceback frames and for `mcp-stderr.log`.

### What changed

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `hermes logs errors --since 1h` over a 3h-old `ERROR` with a traceback | The old record's frames print without its header | The old record is dropped with its frames |
| `hermes logs errors --since 1h --level ERROR` over a fresh `ERROR` traceback | Header and frames print, and so do the old record's frames | Header and frames of the fresh record only |
| `--component gateway` over a matching traceback | Header only; frames dropped (no logger name on them) | Header and frames |
| Unstamped lines at the top of the read window, before any stamp | Always pass `--since`/`--level` | Dropped when `--since` or `--level` is set; kept otherwise |
| `hermes logs mcp --since 1h` | Prints the whole file | Prints only banners and server lines from the last hour |
| `mcp-stderr.log` banner | `===== [2026-09-28 15:16:54] starting MCP server 'x' =====` | `2026-09-28 15:19:06,722 ===== starting MCP server 'x' =====` |
| `mcp-stderr.log` server output | Raw 64 KiB chunks | One line per write, each prefixed `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS,mmm ` (local) |
| Docs, `timezone` key | "Affects timestamps in logs" | Affects cron scheduling and system prompt time; log lines use the machine's local time |

- `hermes_cli/logs.py:94` `_LineFilter`: a line with no stamp takes the verdict of the last stamped line above it, for all filters. It is used by the tail read (`logs.py:192`) and by `-f` (`logs.py:234`). `/api/logs` goes through the same `_read_tail`, so the dashboard and desktop log views get the same result.
- `hermes_cli/stderr_timestamp.py:25,30`: `timestamp()` and `stamp_line()` are now public. The file stays stdlib-only (it is a launcher boot file). The gateway stderr wrapper uses `stamp_line` too, so its output is unchanged.
- `tools/mcp_tool_config.py:77-95`: `_StderrTee._pump` splits the decoded stream on `\n`, holds a partial line until its newline or EOF, and writes each line through `stamp_line`. The raw tail bytes kept for the MCP status surfaces (#124264) are unchanged. The banner (`mcp_tool_config.py:111`) starts with `timestamp()`. The stale comment that said per-line prefixes need a pipe and reader thread is replaced.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/capabilities/mcp/mcp-logs.tsx:12`: the per-server section splitter matches the new banner and the old one, so existing files still split.
- `website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md:2776` corrected. `website/docs/reference/cli-commands.md` gains the `mcp` row and one sentence on how unstamped lines are filtered.

Root cause: the filter judged each line on its own, and a line with no stamp or level token passed those filters by default; `mcp-stderr.log` had no line that `_TS_RE` (`logs.py:29`) could parse.

### Verification

- Red on the base commit `f5708eaedd` (`runs/A-red.txt`): `2 files, 15 tests passed, 3 failed`.
  - `test_logs.py::TestReadTail::test_unstamped_lines_share_the_verdict_of_the_record_above`: `assert 'orphan tail ...eError: new\n' == '2026-09-28 0...eError: new\n'` (old frames leaked).
  - `test_logs.py::test_every_log_file_writes_a_stamp_hermes_logs_since_can_read`: `AssertionError: ('mcp', 'server says hello\n')`.
  - `test_mcp_stderr_lifecycle.py::test_every_mcp_log_line_carries_a_stamp_hermes_logs_since_reads`: `assert ['', '', ''] == ['first half ...line at exit']`.
  - `mcp-logs.test.ts` failed: the `git` section's banner was kept in the `fs` section.
- Green (`runs/A-green.txt`): `8 files, 65 tests passed, 0 failed, 9 skipped` (the skips are Windows-only tests) over `test_logs.py`, `test_mcp_stderr_lifecycle.py`, `test_stderr_timestamp.py`, `test_mcp_node_abi.py`, `test_source_launcher_publication.py`, `test_mcp_config_change_rebind.py`, `test_mcp_config_whitespace_warning.py`, `test_web_logs_async.py`. `vitest run src/app/capabilities/mcp/mcp-logs.test.ts`: 1 passed.
- The guard test builds agent/errors/gateway/gui samples with `RedactingFormatter(hermes_logging._LOG_FORMAT)` and the mcp sample by writing through a real `_StderrTee`. The desktop sample is a literal, because its writer is TypeScript; `apps/desktop/electron/desktop-log-line.test.ts` pins the same shape. A new `LOG_FILES` key without a sample fails the test.
- E2E (`scripts/A_logs_since_e2e.py`, fresh `HERMES_HOME`; real `hermes_logging` writes, and a real Python child through the MCP tee):
  - Before (`runs/A_logs_since_e2e_before.txt`): `hermes logs errors --since 1h` printed `Traceback (most recent call last):` / `File "old.py"` / `ValueError: old failure` ahead of the fresh record. `hermes logs mcp --since 1h` printed the 3h-old `===== [2026-09-28 12:16:53] starting MCP server 'old' =====` and `old server output`.
  - After (`runs/A_logs_since_e2e_after.txt`): the errors output starts at `2026-09-28 15:19:06,719 ERROR gateway.run: fresh failure` with its frames. The mcp output is only `2026-09-28 15:19:06,722 ===== starting MCP server 'probe' =====`, `... probe line 1`, `... probe line 2`.
- Gates: `ruff check` on the touched .py files, `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all`, `git diff --check`: all clean.
- Not run: the full test suite, Windows, desktop eslint/typecheck, and a live `hermes logs -f` session.
- Known limits: a server line with no trailing newline is written only when the newline or EOF arrives. The MCP parent-death supervisor still writes raw to `mcp-stderr.log` (`tools/mcp_tool.py:550-553`); its lines take the verdict of the stamped line above them. `-f` starts a fresh filter at EOF, so a continuation line that arrives before any new stamped line is treated as the top of a window. `--session` also carries: a frame line that contains the session ID but sits under a non-matching header is now hidden.

raw.body:
Held POSIX locks no longer read as dropped when other processes churn the kernel lock table: the live-DB preview lock tests stop flaking on CI, and the "state.db write lock unavailable" warning names the real writer instead of "no write-class lock held".

## Root cause

`/proc/locks` is host-wide, and the kernel serves it over several `read()` calls, resuming each one by record index. When other processes add or drop locks between those reads, the table shifts and entries get skipped, so a lock that is still held can be missing from one pass. The live-DB preview guard (`fc53717f723`, `48196b0ceb4`) never dropped a lock. The flaky `test_preview_preserves_live_database_locks[file-main]` was reading the table while CI's parallel workers churned it.

## Changes

- `tests/posix_lock_probe.py`: `own_posix_locks(*paths)` reads this process's locks from `/proc/self/fdinfo`, which lists them per open file in a single read. It takes the union across every fd open on the file, so SQLite's locks and the test's own `lockf` both count.
- `tests/agent/test_live_db_preview_locks.py` and `tests/hermes_state/test_state_db_file_identity.py` use it in place of their inline `/proc/locks` readers.
- `hermes_state_lockowners.state_db_write_lock_holders()` reads other processes' locks, so fdinfo cannot help there. It now unions three `/proc/locks` passes; a random skip rarely repeats.
- One new invariant test: a holder missing from the first pass is still named. Red on base, green here.
- An unrelated `read_text(encoding="utf-8")` in `test_state_db_file_identity.py` became `utf-8-sig`; it was the only Windows-footgun hit left in that file.

## Validation

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_live_db_preview_locks.py`, quiet box | 1/12 runs failed (origin/main) | 5/5 pass |
| Same file, 6 processes churning locks | 9/12 runs failed | 0/12 |
| Raw reads that missed a held lock (6-process churn) | `/proc/locks`: 445/20,000 | fdinfo: 0/20,000 |
| `state_db_write_lock_holders` with a real writer, under churn | holder not named in 17/400 calls | 0/400 |
| Sabotage: preview guard disabled | n/a | 4/4 lock rows fail (all main-file locks gone), so detection is intact |
| `tests/hermes_state` + preview test | n/a | 1425 passed, 1 failed |

The one failure, `test_fts_runtime_rebuild.py::test_foreign_holder_detection_proc_readlink_deleted_wal`, fails identically on base in this local environment and passes on main's CI. It is a fake-`/proc` descriptor-scan test with no `/proc/locks` read.

**Live repro:** before, an instrumented copy of the preview test caught held locks missing from one `/proc/locks` read and present again on the next, with only the main thread alive and no Python open of `state.db`. After, the fdinfo helper and the 3-pass union show zero misses under the same churn.

raw.body:
`hermes update` and its host-side neighbours stop hurting unrelated processes and stale state: the dashboard/serve kill list matches entrypoint+subcommand tokens instead of argv substrings, an SHA-less restart obligation can discharge, a named-profile update migrates the default `config.yaml`, abandoned runtime leases are collected, agent-run `hermes` resolves to the checkout launcher, and Desktop's Windows SSH probe only trusts a `HERMES_HOME` that exists on the remote.

## Per issue

- **Fixes #121156** (P1) — salvages #121243 by @MohamadKanso (slim redo with credit; #121781 is a later duplicate of the scan hunk). `hermes_cli/dashboard_procs.py::_scan_dashboard_processes` and `hermes_cli/main_dashboard.py::_parse_dashboard_runtime` (used by `hermes update` cleanup, `hermes dashboard --stop/--status`, launchd inventory, uninstall) now defer to the canonical token matcher `update_cmd_windows._hermes_holder_subcommand` (entry token `hermes` / `-m hermes_cli.main` / `…/hermes_cli/main.py`, followed by exactly `dashboard`|`serve`); `_DASHBOARD_PATTERNS` substring tuple deleted. `herdr --session hermes server` is no longer a victim. Foreign-unit restart guard already landed in #124940 (5dc05faf799).
- **Fixes #125952** — salvages #125964 by @kokhlo. `update_cmd_fleet._marker_only_restart_obsolete` no longer fail-closes on an empty `expected_sha` when the record carries no inventory, so the live-fleet rule (every non-external row `current` on the checkout) can discharge it; `update_cmd._complete_source_update` arms with `_current_checkout_sha()` instead of `""` when the head capture was empty. Trim dropped the PR's pid-liveness plumbing.
- **Fixes #105013** — salvages #105014 by @Adolanium. `update_cmd_config._migrate_sibling_profile_configs` enumerates via `backup._sibling_profile_homes(active_home)` (default home outside `profiles/` included, active home excluded) instead of walking `_get_profiles_root()` alone.
- **Fixes #125609** — salvages #125632 by @Ahmett101 (earliest; #125655 by @liuhao1024 is a later duplicate). `runtime_state.lease_directory` / `leases_held` prune lease files whose lock is no longer held, so `os.execv` (bootstrap re-exec) and `os._exit` (watchdog, `main.py`) exits stop accumulating one file per launch on the selected generation. Reader-side fix covers every hard-exit path at once.
- **Fixes #124627** — salvages #124828 by @chelsealong (#125499 is a +290 duplicate; #125061 is a different mechanism). `pm/environments.py::activate_dependencies` prepends `<checkout>/.hermes/bin` ahead of the venv `bin`, so `shutil.which("hermes")` in the gateway and in terminal children (`tools/environments/local.py::_resolve_hermes_bin_dir`) resolves to the launcher, never the venv's editable console script bound to the PM build snapshot.
- **Fixes #118988** — salvages #119022 by @MohamadKanso (slim redo with credit). `apps/desktop/electron/windows-remote-lifecycle.ts::probeWindowsRemote` honours `$env:HERMES_HOME` only when `Test-Path -PathType Container` succeeds on the remote, else falls back to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`. The installer half (User-scope `HERMES_HOME` persisted by `install.ps1`) was already removed on main in 47f4ab3a178; #119076's ps1 CI test is over the bar.

Not in this PR: #123376 (launch/update completion race) — mechanism identified (profile-home `update_marker_path` vs root-home marker; `source_completion.py` takes no `UpdateLock`), but the source change was lost in the sub-lane before commit; re-dispatch input recorded in the lane report. #125525 (root-owned files after update) — needs-repro, no mechanism located in this lane's budget.

## WHEN × WHERE
Process identity (L3 supervisors / atexit, L5 children): T1 standalone, T4 user systemd, T6 launchd (kill list + kickstart inventory), T7 pooled `serve` backends. Config migration (L8): T3 multiplex hosted by a named profile — "default" is the launch home's sibling, enumerated like every other sibling. Restart obligation (L3): T2/T3 multiplex fleet with one live gateway. PATH (L5): terminal-tool children under T2/T4/T6.

## Validation

| Item | Test | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|---|
| #121156 | `tests/hermes_cli/test_process_identity_canonical_matchers.py -k "decoy or never_substrings"` | 2 failed (decoy `tool --name hermes server 30` selected) | 2 passed; live decoy repro (`exec -a`) absent from scan |
| #125952 | `test_update_fleet_restart_pending.py::test_startup_warn_discharged_when_sha_less_marker_fleet_current`, `::test_completion_arms_obligation_with_checkout_sha_when_head_capture_empty` | 2 failed | 2 passed |
| #105013 | `test_sibling_config_migration.py::test_named_active_migrates_default_outside_profiles` (tmp homes, `_get_profiles_root`/`_get_default_hermes_home` patched) | 1 failed | 8 passed |
| #125609 | `tests/pm/test_runtime_gc.py::test_next_reader_removes_lease_left_by_hard_exit` | 1 failed | 3 passed |
| #124627 | `tests/pm/test_runtime_selection.py::test_boot_puts_the_checkout_launcher_ahead_of_the_venvs_own_console_script` | 1 failed | 18 passed |
| #118988 | vitest `electron/windows-remote-lifecycle.test.ts` › "Windows probe validates Hermes and Python topology before selection" | 1 failed / 14 passed | 15 passed |

Pre-existing under-load reds observed in `test_update_fleet_restart_pending.py` (home-I/O guard tripping on `retarget_to_owning_install` stat of the real checkout) reproduce identically with base sources; not introduced here. `scripts/audit_pr_attribution.py --fix`: all contributor emails mapped. ruff, `check_no_tmp_literals`, `check_compat_pointers`, `git diff --check`: clean.

## Infographic
(omitted — lane hit its time budget before the style-picker/image step; parent may add.)



## Changed existing tests

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_scoped_reconciliation.py::test_scoped_reconciliation_matrix[marker-no-sha]`: expectation flipped `True` → `False`. It pinned the pre-#125952 fail-closed default ("a marker with no expected_sha — nothing to verify against", 8130274b377); #125952 deliberately holds an inventory-less, SHA-less record to the checkout, so with every live gateway `current` on it the record now settles exactly like `marker-external-restart`. New row `marker-no-sha-stale` keeps the boundary pinned: the same record stays pending while a live row is stale.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_completion_process.py::test_interrupt_after_child_success_demotes_gateway_marker_at_boundary`: harness only. The `Popen` hook wrapped the FIRST child; the armer now probes the checkout identity (`git rev-parse` via `_current_checkout_sha()`) before spawning the completion child, so the hook wrapped git and recorded `subprocess.run`'s own waits (`[2.99, 2.99, None]`). The hook now matches the completion child by argv; the asserted invariant (interrupt after published success kills, bounded-timeout waits, stdout closed) is unchanged.

- `tests/pm/test_runtime_gc.py::test_next_reader_removes_lease_left_by_hard_exit`: harness only — the hard-exited lease is aged past `LEASE_GRACE_SECONDS` (`os.utime`) before the next reader runs. The invariant (next reader removes a lease nobody holds a lock on) is unchanged; a just-created lease is now deliberately not a prune candidate (see Review fixes, major 2).

## Review fixes

- **MAJOR — `runtime_state._prune_unlocked_leases` aborts boot on an unopenable sibling lease** (root-owned 0o600 from `sudo hermes`, the #125525 class → `PermissionError` in `activate_dependencies` → `hermes_bootstrap` exit 1 on every launch): any `OSError` other than `FileNotFoundError` now counts the lease as HELD (fail-closed for GC, never a boot failure). Test: `tests/pm/test_runtime_gc.py::test_prune_keeps_unopenable_and_just_created_sibling_leases` (red on the PR head with `PermissionError`, green after).
- **MAJOR — reader-side prune races `lease_directory`'s create-then-flock** (unlocked callers: `pm/worker.py`, `pm/launch.py`, `pm/environments.py`; a peer's prune between `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` and `flock` unlinked the file, leaving the first process pinning an unlinked inode): a lease younger than `LEASE_GRACE_SECONDS` (60 s, judged by `fstat` mtime) is never a prune candidate and counts as held. Taken over the temp-name + `os.replace` direction: 3 LOC, a crash between create and flock still leaves a collectable file, and 60 s dwarfs a two-syscall window. Same test.
- **MINOR (a) — `_marker_only_restart_obsolete` cleared the marker on an all-EXTERNAL fleet**: for the SHA-less, inventory-less record an all-external fleet is now treated like an empty one (marker stays armed). Test: `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_fleet_restart_pending.py::test_startup_warn_kept_when_sha_less_marker_fleet_is_all_external`.
- **MINOR (b) — `_hermes_holder_subcommand` stripped only double quotes**, so a `shlex.join`ed `runtime_command` bootstrap (`python -I -c '<bootstrap>' dashboard`, the launchd `ProgramArguments` shape `main_dashboard._parse_dashboard_runtime` feeds it) was never inventoried: strips both quote kinds like `_is_entry`. Test: `tests/hermes_cli/test_venv_holder_classifier.py::TestHolderSubcommand::test_shlex_joined_store_launcher_bootstrap_is_inventoried`.



### Review-fix amendment: no grace window

The 60 s lease grace window made `tests/e2e/core/upgrade/pm/test_generation_gc.py::test_repeated_repairs_collect_superseded_generations` red: back-to-back `hermes pm repair` runs leave a just-abandoned lease in the generation the previous run execv'd out of, and a time-based grace kept it 'held'. Replaced by a writer-side check: after taking the flock, `lease_directory` verifies its lease path still exists and retakes when a peer's prune unlinked it in the create→flock window (the pruner only unlinks while holding the lock, so a visible path after the lock is always ours). Rename+`os.replace` was rejected because msvcrt byte locks refuse renames on Windows. Tests: `test_prune_keeps_unopenable_sibling_lease` (root-owned lease stays held) and `test_lease_taken_while_a_peer_pruned_it_is_retaken` (deterministic race via a patched `_lock`).

raw.body:
Desktop composer, tab and Bot Chat state now survives cold resumes, profile/connection switches and toolset edits, and the gateway restart path refuses before it stops anything.

## Per issue

- **Fixes #125336** — an abandoned cold resume no longer wipes the composer provider: `applyStoredSessionPreviewRuntimeInfo` paints the preview through the transient setters, so `session.create` never ships a model with an empty provider. Salvages #125356 by @kokhlo (layer 2, the `orphanedModelPick` reseed, dropped as defense-in-depth).
- **Fixes #125678** — a restored tab whose session is gone is retired once every profile answered an explicit `404 Session not found` in calm conditions (no profile/connection switch in flight, backend open, no draft text). 5xx / network / inconclusive misses keep the tile. Salvages #125706 by @Wenfengcheng (3 commits, trimmed +285/-18 → +213/-23, tests folded into `session-tile.test.ts` as 2 invariants).
- **Fixes #123805** — a create-time composer pick on a follow-profile (Bot Chat) session now records `composer_override_profile` under the OWNING profile's config, so `_stored_session_runtime_overrides` restores model AND provider on resume instead of falling back to the ambient default. `session.create` was the only writer without the marker (`model_switch.py`, the three `session.resume` paths and `_persist_live_session_runtime` already had it). Salvages #125911 by @Nagisa-3000.
- **Fixes #122190** — `session.set_hidden` requires an explicit `hidden` flag (4021 otherwise) and the contract marks it required; a flag-less call used to hide the whole compression lineage. Salvages #122568 by @Finn763. Remaining atoms are recorded below, not relabelled: the bots-workspace side-chat `hidden: true` at create (#105162, parked by Teknium on #107024/#116127; #125223 is the ready cherry-pick) and the all-profiles Home "Show all N" count vs list (needs an all-profiles `projects.project_sessions` aggregate).
- **Fixes #124211** — toolset changes reach the canonical Bot Chat: `capability_fingerprint` hashes `platform_toolsets` + `disabled_toolsets` (the keys `hermes tools enable/disable` write; the old `tools.enabled_toolsets` key was dead), and the stale-epoch branch rebuilds the tool schema through the SAME builder new desktop/TUI sessions use (`_load_enabled_toolsets(platform)` / `_load_disabled_toolsets()`), then re-pins. Salvages #124307 by @Finn763 with its delivery half rewritten (its `platform_toolsets.<surface>` lookup resolved to `hermes-desktop` = 0 tools; live probe: `desktop` 18 tools vs 0, `tui` 7 vs 0). The existing `test_fingerprint_changes_on_each_capability_axis` now writes `platform_toolsets` and a `disabled_toolsets` step because the key it wrote was dead.
- **Fixes #120106** — session tiles are keyed by `backendScopeKey(connectionId, profile)` instead of the bare profile, so local and remote `default` no longer share one bucket: switching connections swaps the visible tile set and restores it on return; legacy remote-owned tiles migrate by `ownerRoute.connectionId`. Salvages #121983 by @teo-nex (2 commits; the `$connectionContextRestore` latch and chat-view restore were dropped as separate scope). #124520 (different mechanism, same surface) needs re-review against this keying; #121949 is rejected on direction (per-profile secondary gateway).
- **Part of #125394** — `hermes gateway restart` now refuses (`_guard_named_profile_under_multiplexer`) BEFORE anything is stopped: the Desktop backend's `_spawn_gateway_restart` no longer runs `_reap_unsupervised_gateway_orphans()` up front; the #77276 reap moves into `_cmd_restart` after the guard (best-effort, on every restarting path: service manager, external-supervisor hand-back, manual fallback). The Windows CN-fork refusal text in the report does not exist upstream; the upstream class is this ordering. Atom (1) — the Desktop profile switch re-homing `hermes serve` per profile (`ipcMain.handle('hermes:profile:set')` → `teardownPrimaryBackendAndWait` → Windows tree-kill) — is the per-profile-process contract #106742 replaces and is recorded as remaining work, not fixed here.

Not fixed in this PR (recorded for re-dispatch): **#121865** — `gatewayForProfile` redials a secondary profile on every background poll with no ladder check (`store/gateway.ts`); #121904 by @rodricksz4h5 is the right base, unverified against the 1005-after-5-messages first read.

## WHEN × WHERE
- #123805: L (create-time pick, before any turn) × T (one multiplexed backend, launch profile A ≠ owning profile B); the marker is written from B's `config.yaml` under `_profile_build_scope(profile_home)`.
- #125394: L5 (Desktop backend spawning a lifecycle child) × T4 (backend re-homed under a named profile while that profile's gateway runs).
- #120106 / #125678: same profile name on two connections, A→B→A, null connection = reconnect blip (no swap).

## Validation

| Item | Red on base (origin/main source swapped in) | Green on head |
|---|---|---|
| #125336 | `utils.test.ts` "moves the visible model/provider without persisting them": expected 'user-pick', received 'claude-opus-5-5' | 131/131 |
| #125678 | `session-tile.test.ts` "drops a restored tile once every profile answered 404": 1 failed / 18 passed | 19/19 |
| #123805 | `test_create_time_composer_pick_on_bot_chat_records_owning_profile_marker`: KeyError `composer_override_profile` (7 passed / 1 failed) | 8/8 |
| #122190 | `test_set_hidden_without_flag_leaves_visible_session_alone`: 1 failed / 6 passed | 9/9 incl. `contracts/test_generated.py` |
| #124211 | `test_stale_epoch_rebuilds_tools_through_the_surface_builder` + fingerprint axis: 18 passed / 2 failed | 20/20 |
| #120106 | `session-tiles-connection-scope.test.ts`: 2/2 fail (expected [] got ['stored-local']) | 96/96 with `session-states.test.ts` |
| #125394 | `test_spawn_gateway_restart_reap.py`: 2 failed (backend reap called; CLI order lacks 'reap'); review fix `test_cli_restart_reap_failure_does_not_block_restart` red on the PR's own head (OSError propagated) | 22/22 across `test_spawn_gateway_restart_reap.py`, `test_spawn_gateway_restart_cooldown.py`, `test_gateway_restart_external_supervisor.py`, `test_gateway_host_verbs.py` |

Desktop: `npx vitest run` on the 4 touched test files → 246/246; eslint on the 6 touched TS files → 0 errors. `npm run check:lint` typecheck fails only in `src/themes/*` (`HermesSkin.customCSS`) through the symlinked runtime-checkout `node_modules`, files this PR does not touch. Python: `ruff` clean, `check_no_tmp_literals` clean, `check_compat_pointers` clean, `audit_pr_attribution.py --fix` all mapped. No live Desktop CDP pass (lane budget) — listed as an open validation gap.

## Reviewer follow-ups

- **#125394 atom (1)** — the Desktop profile switch re-homes `hermes serve` per profile (`ipcMain.handle('hermes:profile:set')` → `teardownPrimaryBackendAndWait` → Windows tree-kill) and kills the other profile's gateway; the real fix is the Desktop attaching to the ONE host backend (#106742). This is the primary ask of the issue, hence `Part of`, not `Fixes`.
- **#125394 unswept paths (intentional)** — the s6 dispatch (`_dispatch_via_service_manager_if_s6`) and the `profile_lifecycle('restart')` return in `_cmd_restart` do not run the orphan reap: s6 supervises the gateway slot (the reap is a no-op where a supervisor exists), and `profile_lifecycle` only handles a profile whose `find_gateway_pids()` is empty, so the scan has nothing to find.
- **#121865** — `gatewayForProfile` redials a secondary profile on every background poll with no ladder/cooldown check (`store/gateway.ts`); #121904 by @rodricksz4h5 (dial cooldown) is the right base, unverified against the 1005-after-5-messages first read.
- **#122190 atoms 1b / 2** — the bots-workspace side-chat `hidden: true` at create (#105162, parked by Teknium on #107024/#116127; #125223 is the ready cherry-pick) and the all-profiles Home "Show all N" count vs list (needs an all-profiles `projects.project_sessions` aggregate).
- **#120106 residual** — #124520 (different mechanism, same surface) needs re-review against the `backendScopeKey(connectionId, profile)` keying; #121949 is rejected on direction (per-profile secondary gateway). The `$connectionContextRestore` latch and chat-view restore from #121983 were dropped as separate scope.

## Review fixes

- **MAJOR — `_cmd_restart` bare reap aborts the restart on a reaper exception** → wrapped `_reap_unsupervised_gateway_orphans()` in `try/except Exception: logger.debug(...)` like the sibling in `stop_profile_gateway()`; restored the invariant as `tests/hermes_cli/test_spawn_gateway_restart_reap.py::test_cli_restart_reap_failure_does_not_block_restart` (reap raises `OSError` under `kind='launchd'`, `_service_call('restart')` still reached; red on the PR head, green after).
- **MINOR — external-supervisor and manual-fallback paths reached no reap** → moved the guarded reap to just after the refusal guards / `--all` branch, before the `kind` branching, so every restarting path sweeps; s6 / `profile_lifecycle` stay unswept (see follow-ups).
- **PR body — #125394 downgraded from `Fixes` to `Part of`** (atom 1 is the primary ask; recorded above), follow-ups #121865 / #122190 / #120106 collected under `## Reviewer follow-ups`.

raw.body:
`gateway migrate --multiplex`, `profile rename/delete`, `gateway start --all`, the s6 container boot and systemd unit resolution no longer leave a host without a boot-startable gateway or with a stray unit for a profile that no longer exists.

## Issues

- Fixes #124922 — the multiplex migration enables the surviving default unit **before** the first secondary is removed (`_enable_default_at_boot` ahead of `_remove_secondary_gateways`; `systemd_install`'s "already current" early return now honours `enable_on_startup`). Salvages #124943 by @dskwe (earliest); #124948 by @kokhlo is the same fix a few hours later and is superseded.
- Fixes #120524 — the s6 boot reconciler boots a `gateway.standalone` profile's own slot from its own intent instead of folding it into the root that refuses to serve it. Salvages #120525 by @jonpol01.
- Fixes #124401 — `profile rename` removes the old name's unit whether or not the gateway runs, unregisters the old s6 slot / registers the new one, and prints the reinstall hint. Salvages #124402 by @jonpol01.
- Fixes #97897 — the ambient-override half already landed on main in bd970b0588b (`_cleanup_gateway_service` binds `set_hermes_home_override(profile_dir)`), so #97903 by @liuhao1024 is superseded; the remaining class gap (system-scope systemd unit and Windows task never removed on delete/rename) is closed here in `hermes_cli/profiles_service_cleanup.py`.
- Fixes #124473 — every `--all` verb (`start`/`restart`/`stop`) runs as the host root when a named profile is active, so the Windows Desktop update hand-off's `gateway start --all` is no longer refused by the named-profile guard. Salvages #124482 by @JoaoMarcos44.
- Fixes #123386 — the migration preflight reads a parked profile's gateway config under `suppress_plugin_discovery()`, so the parked home stays in the inventory and the duplicate-credential guard (existing `test_parked_profile_remains_in_migration_inventory` untouched) but none of its plugins are imported. Slim redo credited to @JoaoMarcos44 (#123397 flipped the tested "parking must not hide a conflict" guarantee, so it is superseded).
- Fixes #98699 — `user_systemd_unit_dir` resolves from the account home (`get_real_home()`), not the active profile's isolated process `HOME`. Salvages #98715 by @liuhao1024.
- Fixes #109476 — an unprivileged process adopts its own bare legacy `hermes-gateway.service` when that unit pins this custom `HERMES_HOME`, so `restart`/`stop`/`status` drive the unit instead of falling through to a foreground run beside a `Restart=always` loop.

Root cause, in one sentence: unit/slot lifecycle code was written per operation (restart, remove, rename) with no ordering or identity invariant across operations, so each surface could destroy the enablement or identity another surface relied on.

## WHEN × WHERE (cross-cutting table)

| Item | Row | Topology |
|---|---|---|
| #124922 migrate enable-before-remove | L3 (supervisor/install) | T4/T5 (user + system systemd), T9 (migrate is transactional: enable first is safe to interrupt) |
| #120524 s6 standalone slot | L3 | T10 |
| #124401 / #97897 rename/delete cleanup | L6 (CLI under a named profile) | T3, T4/T5, T6, T10 (s6), Windows task |
| #124473 `--all` host-scoped | L5 | T2/T3, T10 (Desktop update hand-off) |
| #123386 parked preflight | L1 (boot probes / plugin discovery) | T2/T3 |
| #98699 unit dir | L5 | T4 |
| #109476 legacy bare unit | L5 | T1/T3, T4 |

## Validation

| Item | Red on base (origin/main 5912ed81ed9) | Green on head |
|---|---|---|
| #124922 `test_migrate_enables_the_survivor_before_it_removes_anything` (fake systemctl recorder: `enable` index < first `stop`/`uninstall`; only the survivor enabled after) | `ValueError: ('default', 'enable') is not in list` | passed (+ `apply_clears`, `interruption_after` unchanged and green) |
| #120524 `test_a_standalone_profile_boots_its_own_slot_instead_of_folding_into_root` | 1 failed (registered/folded) | passed |
| #124401 `test_rename_removes_the_old_names_service_while_the_gateway_is_stopped`, `test_rename_moves_the_s6_slot_to_the_new_name` | 2 failed | 3 passed |
| #97897 class `test_profile_service_cleanup_scopes.py` (system unit + Windows task) | 3 failed | 6 passed |
| #124473 `test_gateway_host_verbs.py -k start_all / restart_all_with_host_down` | 2 + 1 failed (guard pre-empted `start --all`; restart relaunched under `profiles/leinad`) | 9 passed |
| #123386 `test_preflight_never_imports_a_parked_profiles_plugins` (parked profile's `register()` writes a marker) | 1 failed | 3 passed (`-k parked`) |
| #98699 `test_user_unit_dir_follows_the_account_home_not_a_profile_pinned_process_home` | AssertionError (unit under `<active-profile>/home/.config/systemd/user`) | passed |
| #109476 `test_bare_user_unit_pinning_this_custom_home_is_adopted_by_lifecycle_commands` | `'hermes-gateway-3770ed74' == 'hermes-gateway'` | passed |

Receipts (exact swap commands + output) under the lane scratch `RECEIPT.md` files. Known host artifact, not this branch: a worktree under `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/.worktrees` trips `tests/home_io_guard.py` on `.worktrees/manifest.json` for any test importing `gateway.run`; the receipts run with a scratch `HOME` and the same failure set reproduces with pristine `origin/main` sources swapped in.

Contributor commits are cherry-picked with authorship intact; `scripts/audit_pr_attribution.py --fix` reports every author mapped. Existing tests changed: none deleted; `test_gateway_service.py` fixture pins the fake machine home through `HOME` as well as `Path.home` (assertions unchanged).

## Infographic

![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aac3674/qmC8g83-eQmgMdUAerGwp_xk8Zj2zb.png)


## Review fixes

| Finding | What changed |
|---|---|

raw.body:
Fixes #125686.

## What changes

On a tag-pinned narrow checkout (`git clone --depth 1 --single-branch --branch <tag>`, the shape older installers made, see #125112), three worktree paths now branch from the real remote tip. Before this change:
- the dashboard and desktop app's "new worktree from `origin/<branch>`" failed with `fatal: invalid reference: origin/main`;
- converting a remote branch (`origin/feature`) failed the same way, because the name was read as a local branch;
- `hermes -w` printed `origin/main (fetched)` for a ref that didn't exist.

The cause is the same in all three. That checkout's `remote.origin.fetch` maps only the tag, so `git fetch origin <branch>` writes `FETCH_HEAD` and never creates `origin/<branch>`. Each fetch now uses the explicit tracking refspec that `hermes update` already uses (`update_cmd_check.tracking_refspec`, from #125631).

## Who and whose work

- **@686f6c61 (#125699):** base arm, dashboard and desktop app. It claimed the issue first (20:50Z); cherry-picked as is.
- **@kokhlo (#125712):** existing-branch conversion in the dashboard; cherry-picked. Our follow-up reorders it (see below).
- **Our commits on top:**
  1. **Register a branch only after the fetch finds it.** #125712 ran `git remote set-branches --add` before fetching, on every clone shape. For a branch the remote doesn't have, such as a typo, that permanently added a refspec with a missing source, and every later plain `git fetch` in the repo failed with `couldn't find remote ref`. That was reproduced live on normal and narrow clones. Normal clones also gained a redundant fetch line per converted branch. The fix fetches first, tries `--track`, and registers the branch plus its upstream only when `--track` can't map the ref and the fetch proved the branch exists.
  2. **Electron twin.** `git-worktree-ops.ts` mirrors `web_git`, so the same conversion logic went into the desktop app, which had the same failure.
  3. **`hermes -w`.** `worktree_ops._resolve_worktree_base` uses the tracking refspec.
  4. **Local slash-named branches stay local.** A local branch like `origin/feature` was sent to the remote fallback, which meant a network fetch and a silent swap to a new `feature` branch tracking the remote one. Both twins now check `refs/heads/<name>` first.
  5. **Base names are validated by git.** A glob base such as `origin/*` isn't turned into a fetch of every branch. The check is `git check-ref-format --branch`, so valid names like `fix+1` are still refreshed, and both twins make the same call.

## Behaviour notes

- On a narrow clone, a converted branch is registered in `remote.origin.fetch` (`remote set-branches --add`). That is git's own way of giving a tag-only clone an upstream. If the branch is later deleted on the remote, plain `git fetch` in that repo reports the missing ref until the line is removed. `hermes update` passes an explicit refspec and isn't affected.
- Offline, a narrow clone with a stale tracking ref gets an untracked worktree from that ref, and nothing is registered.

## Verification

- **Live E2E** on real narrow clones of this repo, main vs this branch:
  - dashboard base: main fails with `invalid reference: origin/main`; this branch lands on the `origin/main` tip.
  - dashboard convert: main fails with `invalid reference: origin/feature`; this branch lands on the `feature` tip with upstream `origin/feature`.
  - `hermes -w`: main resolves nothing; this branch resolves to the tip.
  - a typo, on narrow and normal clones: refused, fetch config unchanged, later `git fetch` still works. Same on both trees.
- **Tests:** `test_web_server_git.py` 17 passed; `test_worktree_sync_base.py` 10 passed; `git-worktree-ops.test.ts` 28 passed.
  - Each new test fails on the commit before its fix.
  - kokhlo's fixture now puts `feature` past the tag, so "branched from the remote, not the tag" can fail.
- **Neighbouring suites:** 12 worktree and git test files pass on this branch and on main. The only count changes are the added tests.
- **Gates:** ruff clean; `check-windows-footguns --all` clean; `tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json` clean; eslint and prettier clean; `ty` diagnostics equal to main for both Python files.
- **Review:** a 10-scenario Python/TypeScript parity probe (normal, narrow, stale ref, offline, typo, local shadow, existing branch) gave identical results for both twins.

raw.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a catalog entry for `tam`, a memory provider backed by
[total-agent-memory (TAM)](https://github.com/vbcherepanov/total-agent-memory). I maintain both TAM
and the plugin repo, https://github.com/vbcherepanov/hermes-tam-memory. The plugin lives in the
`hermes_tam_memory/` subdirectory, pinned at `0adc0b966971df6be5118e8d64e450c80bb7abf3`.

What the provider does:
- `sync_turn`: saves the user message and final reply of each turn to TAM, on a background writer
  with a bounded retry queue. Trivial prompts, very short turns and injected `<memory-context>`
  blocks are filtered first. TAM's quality gate, when enabled, can still reject a record. No tool
  calls or tool output are sent. Subagent, cron and flush contexts do not auto-save.
- `prefetch`: recalls from TAM within a token budget, stays under the 8 s external prefetch
  deadline, and skips the current session's own turns.
- Tools `tam_recall` and `tam_save`; mirrors built-in memory `add` writes; `post_setup` for
  `hermes memory setup tam` with a live connection check; `get_status_config` for
  `hermes memory status`.
- Local mode starts the separately installed `tam` binary over MCP stdio, with a reduced child
  environment that carries no Hermes provider keys. Remote mode speaks MCP streamable HTTP to a
  TAM HTTP server or team server, with an optional `TAM_API_TOKEN`.
- No Python dependencies (stdlib only), no self-update, and no network calls in `is_available()`.
  If TAM is missing, slow or crashing, the provider degrades to an empty recall and queued writes;
  it never raises into Hermes.

## Related Issue

None. This is a catalog addition following CONTRIBUTING's standalone memory provider policy.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/tam.yaml`: new `category: memory` entry pinned to `0adc0b966971df6be5118e8d64e450c80bb7abf3`, with `subdir: hermes_tam_memory`.

## How to Test

1. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/tam.yaml`
2. `hermes plugins validate <clone>/hermes_tam_memory` at `0adc0b966971df6be5118e8d64e450c80bb7abf3`: all checks pass, and the security
   scan reports `safe`.
3. `pipx install total-agent-memory`, `hermes plugins install tam`, `hermes memory setup tam`,
   chat twice. The second session's prompt includes the first session's turn under
   `## Recalled from total-agent-memory (TAM)`.

The plugin repo's CI runs unit tests against a scripted fake TAM on Linux and macOS, and
integration tests against TAM 14.6.0. The integration tests cover local stdio, TAM's HTTP
transport, and the team server with a Bearer token. I also verified the end-to-end flow above
with Hermes' `FakeLLMServer`.

`capabilities.provides_tools` lists `tam_recall` and `tam_save` for transparency. They are
memory-provider tools exposed through `get_tool_schemas()`, not `ctx.register_tool()`, so the
`register()` probe does not record them.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this feature
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass (N/A: catalog YAML only; plugin tests run in the plugin repo)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS (Hermes CLI, Python 3.14); Linux via the plugin repo's CI

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] README at the pinned SHA documents install, setup, configuration and what data goes where
- [x] N/A: `cli-config.yaml.example`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `AGENTS.md`
- [x] Cross-platform: `platforms: [linux, macos]` (Windows not yet tested)

A single proc_pidfdinfo call can block uninterruptibly in the kernel when a process sits in uninterruptible I/O on a dead network share. The darwin holder scan ran synchronously on the SessionDB connect path, so one stuck unrelated process froze every Hermes start indefinitely (#113187).

The whole darwin pass now runs in a daemon thread with a 5s wall-clock deadline; on expiry it logs a warning and returns no holders (fail open per the guard contract). A per-iteration time check cannot bound this: the block happens inside one call, which is also why open #115589 (per-iteration 1s budget for the many-fd slow case #115583) does not cover this hang -- different trigger, same file.

RED: blocking-fake libproc hangs pristine scan 50s+ with no deadline; new test fails on unfixed code (worker still alive past 30s hang guard). GREEN: 2 new tests pass (~6s); neighbors tests/hermes_state/test_deleted_wal_generation_guard.py green (8 passed, 18 platform-skipped).

Closes #113187

raw.body:
Fixes #125685.

## What changes

`hermes update` from a detached checkout (for example after rolling back with `git checkout <tag>`) no longer reports "Already up to date!" while it moves the code. That happened when local `main` already pointed at `origin/main`. The updater switched HEAD to `main` first and then counted `HEAD..origin/main`, which gave 0. It printed "Already up to date!" and skipped dependency sync, config migration and gateway restarts, even though the running code had just changed. The count now starts from the commit that was actually running.

A syntax-error rollback now returns the install to where the update started. Before, it ran `git reset --hard` on the update branch: a detached user ended up on `main`, and a parked feature branch's commits were written onto `main`. Now:
- **Detached checkout:** `git checkout --detach <sha>` back to the running commit.
- **Parked branch:** `git checkout <branch>`, leaving `main` alone. If that branch can't be checked out, for example because another worktree holds it, its commit is restored detached. The install is never left on the broken code.

The "did HEAD move" guard stays strict. The baseline depends on whether the target is already contained in the pre-pull commit, so a `merge --ff-only` that returns 0 without moving a stale local `main` is still refused.

## Who and whose work

- **@Wenfengcheng (#125728, 4 commits):** the running-checkout capture, count and rollback, plus the baseline helper. This is the base. It opened at 21:23Z, before #125771, and it keeps the did-not-move guard.
- **@JoaoMarcos44 (#125771):** its fork round-trip test is ported with authorship kept. The production change isn't used: its `movement_already_applied` flag skipped the did-not-move check on every detached or parked update. In review, a merge that did nothing on a stale `main` was accepted as success, and #125728's `[reverted]` fork test fails on that PR.
- **Our commits on top:**
  - Tidied the rollback: the command is chosen in one if/elif, the restored branch is named, `rollback_branch` is passed directly instead of via a dict splat, and `_plan.rollback_branch` replaces a `getattr`.
  - Added the detached fallback for an unavailable parked branch.
  - An update that switches branches with nothing to count now prints "Switched the running checkout to main (no new commits to count)". It used to print the shallow-checkout text on normal clones.
  - `_pull_updates` returns the baseline it verified, so `_apply_pulled_update` no longer recomputes it against a hardcoded `origin/<branch>`, which a fork push in between could move.
  - An rc-128 `merge-base` result now keeps the strict baseline.
  - The `updating.md` rollback text is updated.

## Behaviour notes

- After a syntax rollback from a detached or parked checkout, local `main` stays at the broken commit, which is the same commit `origin/main` points at. HEAD isn't on it. The next `hermes update` checks it again and refuses again, loudly.
- The recovery hint quotes branch names with `shlex.join`, which leaves ordinary names bare. `subprocess.list2cmdline` was considered for Windows and rejected: it doesn't quote cmd metacharacters such as `&`, while single-quoting works in PowerShell.

## Verification

- **Live E2E** on a real checkout of this repo. Start: detached at an older commit, with local `main` = `origin/main`.
  - count: main gives `commit_count=0` ("Already up to date!"); this branch gives `335`, and the pull lands on the tip.
  - bad upstream commit, from detached: main rolls back onto `main`; this branch exits 1 back at the original detached commit, with a clean tree.
  - bad upstream commit, from a parked `feature`: main leaves you on `main`; this branch exits 1 back on `feature` at its own tip.
- **Tests:** `test_update_existing_branch_baseline.py`, 15 passed.
  - The contributor tests fail with main's `update_cmd.py`.
  - The silent no-op merge test fails when the baseline is reverted to main's.
  - The detached-fallback test fails without the fallback.
- **Neighbouring suites:** 35 test files that call the changed updater functions give identical failing test IDs on this branch and on main. Those failures already exist on main: the home-directory test guard trips in this environment.
- **Gates:** ruff clean; `check-windows-footguns --all` clean; compat pointers clean; updater surface test 16 passed; `ty` diagnostics equal to main (6 and 6).

raw.body:
Hermes now solves every task in a 16-task cross-agent bench and costs 29% less per Opus run: the browser works again on older installs, `execute_code` stops hiding failed writes, and every profile shares one cached prompt prefix.

## Changes
- **fix(pm)**: `_installed_location` gives the exec bit back to a store binary that lost it (it runs only for the entry's own target). 28edf7c75a0 made `stage()` set the bit, but agent-browser entries staged earlier stay at 0644 forever: every `browser_*` call fails with `[Errno 13] Permission denied`, and the store never restages them because the entry still verifies. Modes are not part of the pinned digest. If an entry can't be chmodded (sealed store), it counts as not installed, so `ensure()` restages it.
- **fix(execute_code)**: when the script ignores a helper's `{"error": ...}` return, that cell's result now includes `tool_errors: [{tool, error}]`. This applies to the local session kernel, the remote kernel and remote per-call runs. The in-script `write_file` doc also says that an existing file must be read first.
- **perf(prompt)**: the `Active Hermes profile …` line names the home path. It moves from the stable tier to the volatile tail. The stable prefix (tools + stable system) is then byte-identical across profiles and homes, so a multiplexed gateway serving N profiles shares one cache entry instead of paying a full write per profile.

## Why (bench evidence)
Hermes and two reference CLI agents ran 16 tasks: 9 standard + 7 hard, each with 2 models × 2 reps. Every request went through the same Nous inference endpoint via a run-attributing relay, and each task has a deterministic hidden grader. The tasks covered multi-file bugfix and feature work, a 45 MB log forensics job, git bisect-and-fix, local web crawling, a JS-rendered catalog, xlsx reconciliation, SQL analytics, docs QA, a concurrency bug, a perf rewrite, a mini-interpreter and an Excalidraw diagram.

| arm (n=32 each) | score | tokens/run | $/run | req/run |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| reference CLI agent A, opus-5.5 | 1.000 | 146k | 0.158 | 5.4 |
| **Hermes base, opus-5.5** | 0.969 | 155k | 0.245 | 6.8 |
| **Hermes this PR, opus-5.5** | **1.000** | 152k | **0.173** | 6.1 |
| reference CLI agent B, gpt-5.6-terra | 0.995 | 145k | 0.123 | 9.4 |
| **Hermes base, gpt-5.6-terra** | 0.968 | 121k | 0.110 | 7.5 |
| **Hermes this PR, gpt-5.6-terra** | **1.000** | 115k | 0.108 | 7.1 |

- **Browser**: all 6 of 6 base `browser_navigate` calls failed with `Permission denied` on the 0644 agent-browser binary. With no browser, `js_catalog` scored 0.50 on Opus and 0.48 on Terra: Terra rebuilt JS `Math.round` with Python banker's rounding and got 2 of 56 prices wrong. With this PR, the entry heals on first lookup and all 4 runs render the page and score 1.0.
- **execute_code**: in 3 of 18 base Opus runs, the model wrote files through `hermes_tools.write_file` after only `cat`-ing them. The read-before-write guard refused, the script never printed the returned dict, and the cell came back as `status: success`. The model then spent 4–6 turns probing and re-emitting whole files (`feature_cli` base: 291k tokens and $0.49 vs reference agent A's 126k and $0.19).
- **Cache prefix**: on base Opus, the first request of every run read 0 cached tokens and wrote about 20k. With this PR it reads 13.5k (reference agent A: 15.7k), and cache writes per run drop from 27.3k to 15.7k. Caveat: a single-profile install with a fixed home already reuses this prefix across sessions. The saving there applies to multi-profile and multiplexed hosts, and to benches like this one where every run gets a fresh home.

## Validation
| | base | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/pm/test_installed_package.py::test_entry_staged_without_exec_bit_is_usable_again` | red | green |
| `tests/tools/test_code_kernel.py::TestInScriptToolErrors` | red | green |
| `tests/agent/test_system_prompt.py::test_stable_tier_is_identical_across_homes` | red | green |
| `tests/pm` + `tests/tools/test_browser_tool_install.py`: failing set | 47 (worktree home-guard env) | the same 47 |

**Live repro:** before, base Hermes' `browser_navigate` returned `[Errno 13] Permission denied: …/agent-browser-0.26.0-linux-x64/bin/agent-browser-linux-x64`, and the store entry was `-rw-r--r--`. After, the first lookup set it to `-rwxr-xr-x`, and `browser_navigate` → `browser_console` rendered all 56 rows on both models.

raw.body:
## Summary

Adds **reaction-feedback** to the catalog. When a user reacts to one of the bot's Telegram messages, the agent's next turn in that private chat starts with a short note naming the reaction and the user message it followed. Today a 👍 or 👎 on a reply never reaches the agent (#18408, #34660, #27438, #13942).

It uses the plugin lane from #64176. `gateway_platform_event` supplies the reaction, `pre_gateway_dispatch` the user's message ids, and `pre_llm_call` the note. Telegram numbers a private chat as one sequence shared by both sides, so a reaction is attributed to the turn whose window contains the reacted message. The user's own messages, slash-command answers and messages older than the plugin has seen are ignored rather than guessed. The design and the Hermes facts it relies on, with file references, are in `docs/DESIGN.md` in the repo.

Four commits:
- `add reaction-feedback`, pinned to `a0fcc77`, version 1.0.0.
- `catalog card`, pinned to `14f339e`. That commit only adds `docs/card.png` and the plugin code is identical. The card is drawn inside the detail hero's visible band (rows 110–490).
- `bump reaction-feedback to 1.0.1`, pinned to `17e4156`: a reaction on the answer to a message with an `@file:`/`@url:` reference was dropped.
- `bump reaction-feedback to 1.0.2`, pinned to `50d8dbd`: in a private chat with topics, a reaction on one topic's answer could be noted in another topic's conversation.

Both fixes came from re-checking the plugin's Hermes assumptions against main after opening; see **Updates** below.

## Disclosure / footprint

- Three hooks. `register()` only registers them.
- The `pre_gateway_dispatch` callback always returns `None`, so dispatch is never changed.
- State is kept in memory, per profile and per private chat, and is bounded:
  - 200 message ids per chat, 20 pending reactions per chat, a 48 h TTL for pending reactions;
  - 256 chats per profile that have started a turn, and 32 that have not. `pre_gateway_dispatch` runs before auth, so messages from unauthorized users can only evict that second pool.
- Nothing is written to disk. No network requests, no subprocesses, no secrets read.
- The note goes into the user message. Hermes keeps the exact API string in the `api_content` sidecar and replays it byte for byte (tested, including a fresh agent rebuilt from `state.db`), so later turns keep the prompt cache.

## Verification

- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` (ruamel.yaml 0.18.17): OK at both commits.
- Replay of the catalog CI's pinned-source step at both pins (`a0fcc77`, `14f339e`):
  - clone and checkout OK, `plugin.yaml` found at the subdir;
  - `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` passes: declared hooks match registrations, security scan safe;
  - self-updater gate OK, and the subdir README is present and identical to the root one.
- The pinned `image` URL returns 200 `image/png`, and its bytes match the committed file (sha256).
- Install by name from this branch's catalog gives `pinned: true` at revision `14f339e`.
- Plugin repo CI, [run 36402983892](https://github.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-reaction-feedback/actions/runs/36402983892), 8/8:
  - unit jobs on Linux/macOS/Windows × py3.11/3.14: 70 passed each;
  - end-to-end on Hermes v2026.9.24 and main: 73 passed each, and `validate` passes.
- Tests:
  - 70 without Hermes and 73 with Hermes.
  - The end-to-end tests load the plugin through the real `PluginManager`, send real `MessageEvent`s through `pre_gateway_dispatch`, and replay reaction payloads captured from a live bot through `gateway_platform_event`.
  - Real `AIAgent` turns run against `FakeLLMServer`, which records exactly what reaches the model.
- Mutation: 34/34 mutants killed, one per attribution rule and filter.
- Live, in a private chat with a test bot on Hermes main:
  - Message ids are one shared sequence (user 12/14/16, bot 13/15/17).
  - Reactions on the bot's messages and on the user's own messages both arrive. ❤ arrives without U+FE0F.
  - With the plugin installed by name from this branch at `14f339e`, a 👎 on the reply to "bir" reached the next turn as `- 👎 on a message you sent after the user's "bir"`.

## Scope note

- Private chats only. Groups share one id sequence among many people, and Discord reactions are not delivered to plugins yet.
- The note says "a message you sent after …", because no documented hook reports the ids of messages Hermes sends. That window is usually the reply, but it can also hold a progress update or a cron delivery.
- Messages sent while a turn is running skip `pre_gateway_dispatch` (#121976). The README lists this.
- Private chats with topics (threaded mode, `/topic`): reactions are ignored while the chat's recent messages span more than one topic. Topics answer in parallel and share one id sequence, and the reaction payload carries no topic (`thread_id` is always `None`), so the reacted message's conversation can't be told. Exact attribution needs the ids of the messages Hermes sends (#95444 would provide them).

## Related

- Core PRs implement the same request in core: #23731 and #27451 (since May, keep_open, P3) and #81709 (August, opt-in inbound reactions plus a react tool). This entry adds no core code; if one of them lands, this plugin can be retired.
- Visiterius/hermes-telegram-reaction-commands (June) is a prototype for a different idea: reactions as commands. It was waiting for this hook and is not in the catalog.

## Updates

Two fixes found by re-checking each Hermes fact in `docs/DESIGN.md` against main `aa96575ed1` and v2026.9.24. Each is its own release with its own tests, so either pin can be taken alone.

| | Before (1.0.0) | After |

Reproduced through the gateway's real `_prepare_inbound_message_text` + `_hmwa_apply_message_timestamp` and a real `AIAgent` turn. A plain message was the control (delivered before and after).
- 1.0.2: private-chat topics keep `chat_type == "dm"` and carry `source.thread_id`; `_normalize_reaction_event` sets `thread_id: None` because `message_reaction` has no topic. `post_llm_call` fires before the reply is delivered and not at all for interrupted turns, so turn windows can't be closed precisely; the plugin declines instead of guessing. One topic keeps working as in a plain chat.

raw.body:
Editing a file in a cloned repository no longer runs that repository's own interpreter, TypeScript SDK, compiler plugins or build scripts. The user's own project, where Hermes was launched or where the session was opened, keeps full LSP diagnostics.

Fixes #125954. This salvages #125955 by @jonpol01: both of his commits (his own rebase onto main, `1f3b384906` and `482e5a1e54`) are kept unchanged with his authorship, and our follow-ups sit on top.

## What changes

From #125955 (@jonpol01):
- Language servers are denied by default in an untrusted workspace. Only servers that run no project code start there, with settings that keep them on Hermes's own tools:
  - pyright uses `VIRTUAL_ENV` or the Hermes-managed Python, never the checkout's `.venv`.
  - typescript-language-server's `tsserver.path` is pinned to Hermes's TypeScript.
  - svelte-language-server gets `isTrusted: false`.
  - bash, yaml, dockerfile, intelephense and clangd are unchanged.
- The `npx tsc` and `rustfmt` post-write lint fallbacks are skipped in an untrusted workspace, because they pick up the checkout's `node_modules/.bin/tsc` and `rust-toolchain.toml`.
- A new `lsp.trusted_workspaces` config key lists extra trusted directories. `hermes lsp status` marks the servers that only run in trusted workspaces.

Follow-ups (ours):
- **Trust follows the workspace the session was opened in**, not only the process cwd. The PR anchored on `os.getcwd()`. `hermes -w` sets `TERMINAL_CWD` without a `chdir`, the Desktop/TUI backend runs from the install tree or `$HOME` with the project bound as the session cwd, the gateway runs from `HERMES_HOME`, and cron binds a workdir per job. On all of these, the user's own repository lost pyright's venv, 19 other servers and the lint fallbacks. `operator_workspace_roots()` now also trusts the worktree of `resolve_agent_cwd()`. Only surfaces set that directory; the agent's `cd` does not move it.
- **Cron runs and Kanban workers get no automatic trust.** The `cronjob` tool lets the model choose a job's workdir, and `kanban_create` lets it choose a task's workspace. Both would otherwise anchor trust on a repo the agent cloned. These surfaces use `lsp.trusted_workspaces` only.
- **A repo at or above `$HOME` is never an anchor.** A dotfiles repository at home would otherwise trust every directory under it, including a tarball the agent extracts into `~/Downloads`.
- **Vue is removed from the allowlist.** `@vue/language-core` 2.2.x `require()`s the `vueCompilerOptions.plugins` listed in a project's tsconfig, resolved against the project root, so pinning `tsdk` was not enough.
- The lint gate checks only the linter's cwd, which is where `npx` and rustup resolve the toolchain. The `except Exception` wrapper is gone.
- Trust is computed once per spawn, and trust lookups take no lock. pyright shares one process only among trusted roots, so whichever root spawned first no longer decides the interpreter for the others. A client that started while its root was untrusted is still found and released after the root becomes trusted.
- Svelte goes back to the declarative registry form (`untrusted_init=`), the two path-list config keys share one parser, and the docs table is reworded ("run no project code").

## Validation

Real `pyright-langserver`. Each checkout ships a `.venv/bin/python` that records when it is executed. The "origin/main" column is the pre-PR behaviour: every repository's own interpreter runs.

| Scenario | origin/main | #125955 as submitted | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Agent edits a clone, CLI launched outside it | project python runs | not run | not run |
| `hermes -w` linked worktree (the user's own project) | runs | not run (lost venv) | runs |
| Desktop session opened in the project, backend cwd elsewhere | runs | not run (lost venv) | runs |
| `$HOME` is a dotfiles repo, agent-made dir below it | runs | **runs** | not run |
| Cron run whose workdir is a clone | runs | not run | not run |

- Tests: `tests/agent/lsp/` plus the file-operations, config, runtime-cwd, pm and Windows-subprocess test files: 35 files, 392 passed, 0 failed.
- The two trust tests were mutation-checked. Each of these changes turns them red: removing the session-cwd anchor, removing the `$HOME` exclusion, removing the cron gate, or removing the Kanban gate.
- ruff, the Windows footgun check and the compat-pointer check are clean.

raw.body:
Gateway startup and `hermes doctor` now tell users when their config still asks for idle or daily session resets. Core stopped applying those resets in 1d5d059410, and until now nothing said so.

WHO/WHEN/WHY: A community plugin author reported on 2026-09-27 that his family's gateway conversations stopped resetting after the upgrade. Nobody in the house types `/new`, so context grew without bound and so did the bill. The docs say legacy `session_reset` settings are ignored, but a user whose config still carries them got no signal at all. Reset policy stays out of core. This PR only points those users at the opt-in catalog plugin, `hermes-session-reset-policy`, which reads the same block unchanged.

Changes:
- `hermes_cli/session_reset_retirement.py`: a small detector for `session_reset.mode` set to idle, daily or both. It checks the top level and the `gateway:` form the old loader accepted. The same module holds the "is the plugin enabled" check and the notice text.
- `gateway/run_startup.py`: one WARNING per served profile (multiplex included) at startup. Silent while the plugin is enabled.
- `hermes doctor`: new "Session Reset" section. Warns and adds a manual issue, or reports the policy as applied when the plugin is enabled.
- Docs: `sessions.md` and `messaging/index.md` name the warning and the plugin.
- The key is reported, never rewritten or dropped, because the plugin consumes it.

Live repro (isolated HOME + HERMES_HOME, `gateway run --force`, `session_reset: {mode: both}`):

| | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| gateway log | no mention of session_reset | `WARNING gateway.run: Profile default: session_reset.mode: both is no longer applied ... hermes plugins install hermes-session-reset-policy.` |
| `hermes doctor` | nothing | ⚠ same notice |
| plugin installed + enabled | n/a | no warning; doctor `✓ session_reset.mode: both is applied by the session reset plugin`; plugin logs `armed (pre_gateway_dispatch)` |
| multiplex, secondary profile `work` with `gateway.session_reset.mode: daily` | nothing | `Profile work: gateway.session_reset.mode: daily ... (move the block to top-level session_reset first)` |

Tests: `tests/gateway/test_retired_session_reset_notice.py` has 2 tests (3 cases). The first checks that startup warns and that the plugin silences it; it fails when the plugin gate is inverted. The second checks that only timed modes count, in both locations. Locally, `test_doctor.py` and `test_doctor_exit_status.py` show the same 41 environment failures on origin/main and on this branch, because the worktree's git dir sits under the real hermes home and trips the home-I/O guard. The failure sets are identical, and CI is the authority there.

Merge order: the notice names `hermes-session-reset-policy`. That name installs once the catalog entry lands, which waits on fastfinge/hermes-session-reset-policy#1 (a manifest `provides_hooks` line so `hermes plugins validate` passes). This PR should merge after the catalog entry.

raw.body:
The usage analytics daily chart now counts each session on the local calendar day it started, the same day `/insights` uses.

## What changed

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `daily[].day` in `/api/analytics/usage` | UTC calendar day: `date(started_at, 'unixepoch')` | Machine-local calendar day: `date(started_at, 'unixepoch', 'localtime')` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/analytics.py:87`) |
| Session at 02:00 IST on 2026-09-26 | counted on `2026-09-25` | counted on `2026-09-26` |
| Agreement with CLI `/insights` (`agent/insights.py:419-422`, `datetime.fromtimestamp`) | differs for sessions started between 00:00 and 05:30 IST | same day |

SQLite applies `'localtime'` per row, so each session uses the UTC offset in force at its own start time. A range that crosses a DST change is bucketed correctly. A single fixed offset for the whole range would not be.

Root cause: the daily query converted the epoch start time to a date without a zone modifier, so SQLite returned the UTC date, while both clients show the value as a local calendar date and `/insights` buckets by local day.

Refs #23982. Two older open PRs address the same issue, #62317 and #76764. Both edit `hermes_cli/web_server.py`, where this query no longer lives, and both use the `hermes_time` configured zone instead of the zone `/insights` uses. #76764 applies one offset to the whole range.

## Verification

- New tests in `tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server.py` (`TestNewEndpoints`), with `TZ` switched through `os.environ` + `time.tzset()` as in `tests/gateway/test_active_turn_recovery.py:560-574`:
  - `test_analytics_daily_buckets_use_local_day`: a session at 02:00 `Asia/Kolkata` on day D is counted on D.
  - `test_analytics_daily_buckets_follow_dst_offset_per_session`: sessions at 23:30 `America/New_York` on a January (EST) and a July (EDT) day each stay on their own day.
- Red on base: `AssertionError: assert {'2026-09-26': 1} == {'2026-09-27': 1}` and `assert {'2026-02-01'...026-08-01': 1} == {'2026-01-31'...026-07-31': 1}`.

raw.body:
After a gateway restart, a session interrupted shortly before a DST spring-forward is now auto-resumed instead of being treated as stale.

## What changed

`GatewayRunner._schedule_resume_pending_sessions` (`gateway/run_startup.py:590-592`) now checks marker freshness with `_is_fresh_gateway_interruption` (`gateway/run.py:1029`), which compares epoch seconds. It no longer subtracts naive local datetimes.

| Case (window 60 min) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Marker 01:50 local, boot 03:10 local on 2026-03-08 in America/New_York (20 real minutes) | measured as 80 min, session skipped | measured as 20 min, session auto-resumed |
| Marker carries a UTC offset | `TypeError: can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes` | compared exactly, session auto-resumed |
| `HERMES_AUTO_CONTINUE_FRESHNESS` set to 0 or below | every session with a marker skipped | gate disabled, as the docstring at `gateway/run.py:948` says |

Root cause: `last_resume_marked_at` / `updated_at` are naive local stamps written by the previous process (`gateway/session_lifecycle.py:21-23,211`), and naive subtraction ignores the UTC offset change between the write and the read. The per-turn path already reads the same field through the epoch helper (`gateway/run_turn_runner.py:1642`).

I also grepped `gateway/` for other code that subtracts a stored naive stamp from `datetime.now()`. `gateway/session_lifecycle.py:164-174` already uses epoch math. I left two cutoff sites unchanged: `SessionStore.list_sessions(active_minutes=...)` (`gateway/session.py:1274`) has no caller that passes `active_minutes`, and `prune_old_entries` (`gateway/session_lifecycle.py:230`) works in days, so a DST shift moves its cutoff by at most one hour.

## Verification

- New test `tests/gateway/test_restart_resume_pending.py::test_startup_auto_resume_freshness_survives_spring_forward`, parametrized over a naive local marker and an aware UTC marker. TZ is set to America/New_York with `time.tzset()`, as the neighbouring tests do.
  - On base `35272ce28b`: both cases fail. The naive case fails with `assert 0 == 1` and the aware case with `TypeError: can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes`.
  - With the fix: `2 tests passed`.
- Ran `scripts/run_tests.sh` on `tests/gateway/test_restart_resume_pending.py`, `test_platform_reconnect.py`, `test_restart_notice_replay.py` and `test_planned_restart_notice_multiplex.py` (every file that calls `_schedule_resume_pending_sessions`): 76 passed, 0 failed.
- E2E (`timestamp-recon/scripts/B5_auto_resume_dst_e2e.py`): one process uses a real `SessionStore` to write `sessions.json` with the marker at 01:50 local. A second process loads that file and runs the real scheduler at 03:10 local, with a fresh scratch `HERMES_HOME` and only the wall clock frozen.
  - Before: `real age s: 1200.0 | naive age s: 4800.0` → `scheduled auto-resume: 0`
  - After: `scheduled auto-resume: 1 | handle_message awaited: 1`
- Gates: `ruff check` on both touched files, `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all` and `git diff --check`, all clean.
- Not run: the full test suite, the rest of `tests/gateway/`, and a live gateway restart across a real DST transition.
