raw.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds **favorite models** to the desktop model picker. Every row starts with a star: an outline when the model isn't a favorite, filled when it is. Clicking the star moves the model into a **Favorites** section at the top of the picker, in the order you starred them, with the provider named on the row so two labs serving the same model id stay distinct. With nothing starred the section doesn't render at all.

Starring never selects a model or closes the menu, so the same gesture undoes it. There are three ways to star a row:

- click the star;
- **shift-click** the row (the gesture that pins a chat in the Sessions sidebar);
- **Shift+Enter** from the search field, on the highlighted row. The highlight moves with the row to its new position.

A plain click on a row still selects the model.

The picker remembers your last pick, which only helps with one model. Switching between two or three models means scrolling back to them or retyping the same search several times a day (#49777, #23117).

Design choices:

- **The star is the only control.** Favoriting is not a row option, so the options submenu (thinking / fast / effort) is the same as on `main`. The empty star sits at a quiet contrast and gets brighter when you hover the row or the star. The filled star uses secondary text colour, so it reads as on without outweighing the model name. The star column lines up with the footer's + and gear icons, and the model names line up with the footer labels.
- **One stored preference owned by the catalog.** `ModelCatalogMenu` reads `$favoriteModels` itself (as it does `$visibleModels`), so the composer pill, session tiles and the kanban override all show the same Favorites section without any wiring in the hosts.
- **One row renderer.** `ModelFamilyRow` is shared by Favorites and the provider groups, so the two render and behave identically. The flat keyboard list follows render order (favorites first), and the highlight is tracked by row key rather than index.
- **No duplicates.** A favorite is removed from its provider group, so an open menu never lists a model twice.
- **Search is exempt.** While typing, the section is hidden and each match appears under its own provider, still starred.
- **Favorites ignore the Edit Models shortlist** on purpose: starring a model means "always show me this one".
- **Favorites survive a disconnected provider.** A key with no matching model in the current catalog renders nothing but stays stored, so the row comes back when the provider reconnects.
- Stored per device under `hermes.desktop.favorite-models` through the existing `lib/storage` helpers, keyed by the same `provider::model` identity as `modelVisibilityKey`.

Scope: desktop only. #23117 also asks for the TUI/CLI picker and a `model.favorites` config key. That needs a separate decision about where favorites are stored, and this PR doesn't attempt it.

## Related Issues

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/49777
Refs https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/23117 (desktop side only; TUI/CLI remain open)

## Supersedes

- Supersedes #95090 by @SHL0MS. Its store, tests and authorship are carried here: the first commit, `feat(desktop): pin models to the top of the model menu`, is kept verbatim. That branch had fallen into conflict with the picker's row refactor.
- Supersedes #107926 by @JahazielHernandezHoyos. Its favorites design, section behaviour and tests are carried here (`Co-authored-by` on the shift-click commit). The "Favorites" name and the star come from it; here the star sits on the row instead of in the options submenu. Its branch predated the current menu and conflicted on every touched file.
- Supersedes #112123 by @terminamike666. Its per-row star toggle, the interaction this revision adopts, is credited with `Co-authored-by` on the star commit. Its branch rebuilt the same row extraction against an older menu.
- Credits @Noshkoto's [Model Favorites](https://github.com/Noshkoto/hermes-model-favorites) desktop plugin (catalog entry #129520), which put starred models at the top of a picker because the built-in menu had no hook for it. That design is credited with `Co-authored-by` on the star commit. The catalog entry is a separate plugin and is left open.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/store/favorite-models.ts` (new): `$favoriteModels`, `favoriteModelKey` (the visibility store's `provider::model` format), `setFavoriteModels` (deduping), `isModelFavorite`, `toggleFavoriteModel`. Grown from `model-pins.ts` in #95090.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/shell/model-catalog-menu.tsx`:
  - Favorites section above the provider groups, built by `resolveFavoriteRows`.
  - `ModelFamilyRow` extracted and shared by both sections, with the star button leading each row.
  - The star click, shift-click and Shift+Enter all toggle without selecting or closing.
  - `groupModels` drops favorites from their provider groups, except while searching.
  - The keyboard list includes favorites first, and its override is tracked by row key.
  - One `catalogGroupLabel` class for every group heading.
- `apps/desktop/src/i18n/{types,en,fr,de,es,ar,ja,ru,zh,zh-hant}.ts`: `shell.modelMenu.favorites`, `addFavorite`, `removeFavorite`, `favoriteShortcut` in every locale that has the neighbouring keys (fr/de/es are covered by the completeness check). `locales/_keys.desktop.json` is regenerated with `npm run i18n:keys`.
- `website/docs/user-guide/desktop.md`: "Favorite models" bullet under *Choosing a model*.
- Tests:
  - `store/favorite-models.test.ts`: order, persistence, provider scoping, dedupe.
  - `model-catalog-menu.test.tsx` (+6): section placement, no duplicates, disconnected provider, shortlist override, search hides the section but keeps the star, and star / shift-click / Shift+Enter toggling without selecting or closing.
  - All of these fail on `main` without this change.

## How to Test

1. Open the composer model picker. Every row has an outline star on the left, and there is no Favorites heading.
2. Click a star. The menu stays open, the star fills, and the model moves under **Favorites** at the top with its provider named. It no longer appears in its provider group.
3. Click the filled star (or shift-click the row). The model returns to its provider group, and the section disappears once it's empty.
4. Type in the search box, arrow to a row and press **Shift+Enter**. The row toggles and the highlight stays on it.
5. With favorites set, type a query. The section hides and matches appear under their own provider, favorites still starred.
6. A plain click on a row still selects it and closes the menu.
7. Restart the app: favorites are still there. Open a kanban card's model override: same Favorites section.
8. Automated, from `apps/desktop`: `npx vitest run --project ui src/app/shell/model-catalog-menu.test.tsx src/app/shell/model-edit-submenu.test.tsx src/store/favorite-models.test.ts`

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] `tsc -p apps/desktop --noEmit`, eslint on touched files, and the targeted vitest suites pass (no Python touched)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)

## Screenshots

<details>
<summary>Earlier revision of this PR (Pinned section + Pin item in the row options, since replaced by the star)</summary>

## What and why

The in-app Browser/preview pane can fill the layout with no way to dismiss it from the UI — no toolbar close, no context menu, and the only keyboard verb (Cmd+Shift+L) only ever opened it. Users resorted to asking the agent to close a panel (#92500). This consolidates the four open contributor PRs on that cluster into one change:

- **Visible close on the browser bar** — `PreviewPane` threads its existing `onClose` (the tab's X verbatim: console cleanup + tab removal) into `PreviewBrowserBar`, rendered as the trailing `PaneStripGlyph`. Embedders that pass no verb (the popped-out Browser shell) render no dead button.
- **Cmd+J / titlebar right-sidebar toggle is positional** — resolves the physically rightmost foldable root-row column from the live tree, so a Browser preview column (whose panes register `placement: 'main'` and were invisible to the semantic side derivation) folds to a minimized rail and round-trips like the zone chevron. Falls back to the semantic files branch when no right column exists.
- **Cmd+Shift+L is a true toggle** — `toggleBrowserTab()` checks whether the mirrored preview-tile pane is actually on screen; if yes it dismisses just that pane (tab survives), if no it re-fronts the Browser with the page it last showed. Command palette entry and labels follow ("Open browser" -> "Toggle browser").
- **Right-click zone menu on the pane body** — `PaneBody` gains a `wrap` slot; the zone's `ZoneMenu` (Close/Minimize/strip verbs) now attaches to the body element itself, so a zone with no visible header still offers Close from its own content.

## Tests

- `preview-browser-bar.test.tsx`: close fires the supplied owner once; no close button renders without a verb — **proven red without the change**
- `right-side-toggle.test.ts` (new): folds the browser column, round-trips, leaves the left stack untouched — **proven red**
- `preview-toggle-browser.test.ts` (new): blank open, dismiss-but-keep-tab, re-front last page, leaves other preview tabs alone — **proven red**
- `tree-group.test.tsx`: zone menu opens from pane body content — **proven red**
- Full `npm run check:lint` (typecheck + lint) green; sibling renderer suites (`floating-panes`, `tool-panel-close`, `tab-close-affordance`, `keep-alive-panes`) and `components/ui/__tests__` contract tests green.

`zones.zoneMenuLabel` and `commandCenter.toggleBrowser` added, `view.showBrowser`/`commandCenter.openBrowser` relabeled, in all seven locales (en/ar/de/es/fr/ru/zh).

Supersedes #91934 (visible close — @Trounaldo), #92745 (positional right-side toggle — @Treytucker05), #93194 (every-surface close — @andrexibiza), #95826 (browser hotkey toggle — @runninwithitmarketing). Each author's work is credited via `Co-authored-by` on the commit that carries it.

Captured from the real production components (`PreviewBrowserBar`, the command palette) mounted in an isolated harness with production CSS and dark theme. ## What does this PR do?

Saving a legacy `custom_providers:` endpoint from Desktop Settings (or `POST /api/providers/custom-endpoints` with `api_key` omitted) forked a new `providers.<id>` entry and dropped the credential. The writer only looked inside `providers`, and the plaintext-`api_key` migration never copied `key_env`. The legacy list row stayed, so the config held two entries and the new one had no key. The next request through that endpoint failed with 401.

The save now, when no `providers` entry matches, lifts the legacy list row through the same v12 conversion activate already uses (`key_env` included) and removes that list row. A new key typed in the panel still replaces the env var. An omitted key leaves the existing `key_env` in place. A row that cannot be converted is put back on the list.

Fixes #126589

raw.body:
A failed turn's unanswered user message is no longer lost from the transcript when the next turn merges into it, and the merged row is no longer double-counted toward compaction (#124731, salvage of #124770).

**Who / when / why:** @charan-rathore opened #124770 for #124731. This salvage rebases it onto current main unchanged and adds two follow-up fixes found in review, plus test cleanup.

**Root cause:** `_merge_consecutive_users` folds the current turn into an unanswered earlier user row. The clean-text persist override then replaced the whole merged content with the new turn only, so the earlier request disappeared from the durable row.

**Changes**
- @charan-rathore's 4 commits, unchanged:
  - `_merge_consecutive_users` records the unanswered prefix on the merged row.
  - `_content_with_turn_override` (used by `durable_user_row_content` and `_apply_persist_user_message_override`) keeps that prefix and replaces only the absorbed turn. This includes an empty incoming turn.
- Follow-up: the marker is named once as `MERGED_TURN_PREFIX` in `agent/message_metadata.py` and added to `PERSISTENCE_ONLY_MESSAGE_FIELDS`.
  - Before this, the rough token estimator priced it as payload. It repeats the row's own text, so a merged row with a large unanswered paste was estimated at about 2x its size for the rest of the session.
  - It is now also dropped from every outgoing request copy on every transport, not just by the chat-completions underscore sweep.
- Follow-up: the prefix is stored as the bare unanswered text and joined at override time with the same `"\n\n"` rule the merge uses.
  - Before this, a row merged with an empty turn stored the prefix without the separator, so a later non-empty override on that row came out as `RX` instead of `R\n\nX`.
  - A merge whose override is empty no longer leaves a trailing `\n\n` on the durable row.
- Tests: the three unit tests become two invariants (the non-empty merge now also checks the api_content sidecar and the token estimate). The ACP end-to-end test is kept. The two unit tests share one stub helper, and the empty-turn test also pins the override join.
- Attribution: two of the original commits were authored as `Instinct Agent <agent@instinct.com>`. They are re-authored to the PR's author, @charan-rathore.

**Validation**

| Check | origin/main | #124770 as submitted | this branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| E2E: real `SessionDB`, unanswered row R, then a gateway-timestamped turn U, repair, flush, restore | durable row loses R | keeps R, ends with clean U | keeps R, ends with clean U |
| Token estimate of the merged row ÷ estimate of its content alone | 1.00 | 1.99 | 1.00 |
| `test_merged_user_override.py` + `test_failed_turn_closure.py` | 4 fail / 2 pass (production files reverted) | pass | 5 pass |
| Remove the new field registration (mutation check) | — | — | estimate assert fails (48 vs 32) |
| Later non-empty override on an empty-merge row | — | `RX` | `R\n\nX` (the new assert fails on the previous head) |
| Real `AIAgent.run_conversation` + `SessionDB` + local fake provider, base vs head | R dropped from the returned transcript and from the heal/replay rows | — | R kept; prefix key absent from all 16 captured requests and every DB column; a plain 2-turn conversation writes identical rows and wire messages |
| `tests/agent`, `tests/acp_adapter` + 2 more files that reference the touched symbols (958 files) | 3 failures in `test_compaction_prompt_rebuild.py`, the same on base | — | 10,138 pass, same 3 pre-existing failures |
| 133 test files that reference the touched symbols | — | — | 2,567 pass; the only failures are in `test_tui_gateway_server.py` (macOS `Too many open files`, 256-fd limit; that file doesn't run on main locally either) |

Known and left alone: if a user row were ever merged *into* the current-turn row itself, the override would still be wrong (it was wrong before too). No current path appends a user row after the current-turn row before the first call, so this is latent. Interlock with #121837 (still open, same block): keep the prefix line before `drop_stale_api_content(prev)`.

Closes #124731. Supersedes #124770 (credit: @charan-rathore).

raw.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds `plugin-catalog/hermes-toon.yaml`. Owner submission (catalog rule 5): I maintain [drew-dot-com/hermes-toon](https://github.com/drew-dot-com/hermes-toon) and the node it pays.

hermes-toon registers a `toon` web provider, extract only (`web.extract_backend: toon`). Each `web_extract` is one `GET /extract?url=` against a local payer sidecar, which pays a [TOON](https://github.com/toon-protocol) node one micropayment (about $0.001 in USDC, off-chain claim on a payment channel). The node fetches the page through an [Anyone network](https://anyone.io) exit and answers with the page as markdown plus a content hash under [wuzzy/crawl v1](https://github.com/memetic-block/wuzzy/blob/main/VERIFY.md), so the result carries a hash an independent fetch can be checked against. The destination sees an Anyone exit, not the user's IP.

The plugin itself has one dependency (`httpx>=0.27,<0.29`, bounded), registers no tools, hooks or middleware, does not update itself, and talks only to the sidecar URL in `TOON_PAYER_URL`. The sidecar ([anonfetch/payer](https://github.com/drew-dot-com/anonfetch/tree/main/payer)) holds the wallet and the spending rules: a daily cap, a per-fetch price ceiling and an origin allowlist.

Disclosure, also in the entry's description and the README: with `TOON_PAYER_URL` set and `toon` selected, every `web_extract` spends from the sidecar's channel with no per-call confirmation, up to the sidecar's daily cap (default $0.10) and only for its allowed origins when that list is set. Same shape as `hermes-mpp`'s disclosure.

## Related Issue

None. Catalog entry only.

## Type of Change

## What does this PR do?

Adds Prompt Studio to the community plugin catalog. Prompt Studio is a Hermes Desktop plugin that turns a rough
request into a well-built prompt for Claude Opus 5.5 or GPT-6 Astra. It asks the few questions that change the
result, one step at a time, with a recommended answer and an optional AI suggestion on each step, then writes the
prompt and either sends it (F9) or places it in the composer for editing (Alt+E). Everything is keyboard-driven.

I am the owner and only maintainer of https://github.com/bwoliveira/prompt-studio.

- Pinned to the full commit SHA of release v1.8.0 (`51bd9330d4841de13624d3315cb4bec66434b71d`), not the annotated tag object.
- Unified package: `plugin.yaml` + `__init__.py` (registers one auxiliary task, `prompt_studio`), a dashboard API
  router (`dashboard/manifest.json`, `plugin_api.py`) and a Desktop half (`desktop/plugin.js`), all with the id
  `prompt-studio`.
- `capabilities` are empty: no tools, hooks, middleware or required env vars. The only agent-side registration is
  the auxiliary task, so users can route it with `auxiliary.prompt_studio.*`.
- Desktop half imports only `@hermes/plugin-sdk`; it reads and writes the message field only through
  `host.composer` (no app DOM, no internal stores, no `hermes:composer-*` events), listeners go through
  `ctx.addEventListener`, timers through `ctx.setTimeout`, preferences through `ctx.storage`, colors through theme
  variables. No `eval`/`new Function`, no network outside the SDK/plugin API,
  no self-updating code.
- Model calls: the dashboard backend calls Hermes's auxiliary client routed by its own `prompt_studio` task, not
  `ctx.llm` yet. In this Hermes, `ctx.llm.complete()` has no reasoning-effort option and denies a per-call `model=`
  unless the operator sets `plugins.entries.prompt-studio.llm.allow_model_override`, so the per-request model
  choice in the plugin's Settings would stop working on a default install. The README states this. Credential
  resolution stays with Hermes; the plugin does not ask for or store API keys.
- The plugin sends no temperature or other sampling parameters; Hermes decides them for each model.
- `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.5"`, because `host.composer` first ships in Hermes Desktop 0.21.5. On an older Desktop the
  bundle still loads (checked against the SDK export lists of 0.20.0 and 0.21.4) and the Studio shows an "update
  Hermes" notice instead of opening. Run for real on 0.21.5.
- Attachments: the SDK has no attachment API, so the plugin does not read or copy them. They stay in the composer and
  go with the prompt when it is placed there (Alt+E); "Send now" (`host.composer.submit`) sends text only, and the
  preview says so.

Salvages #126169 by @JoaoMarcos44. The commit is cherry-picked as-is, so authorship is kept. It's on a maintainer branch so CI can run (the fork PR reports no checks).

On a Desktop session, compaction rebuilt the system prompt without the cwd context files (AGENTS.md and friends). `_context_cwd_is_launch_artifact` marks every desktop-source session with no explicit cwd, and `agent/system_prompt.py` and `agent/context_file_sources.py` then passed `cwd=None`. The fix only skips the session-override half of the lookup and still resolves the profile's configured cwd, at both call sites. The install-tree suppression is unchanged. Profile scope goes through the routed terminal scope, and there's an A→B→A two-home test. It's cache-safe: the prompt only changes at build time and at the sanctioned compaction boundary.

Reviewed against current main: the premise holds, and the four affected test files pass (84).

Closes #126111
Supersedes #126169

If the resolved `Exec` still can't serve the app, the entry is left unwritten. When cherry-picked on top of #122442, both guards are kept together.
- **#126031** (@liuhao1024), for #126009: when a packaged Electron app already exists, the entry carries `--skip-build`, so a click launches the app instead of rebuilding for 60+ seconds (or failing) on any locally modified tree.

  - What's left of #126009 is the managed-CLI `Exec` target, which the two commits above cover.

The desktop model catalog menu (the composer model pill and every host that picks a model) can render per-model pricing on each row: input/output $/Mtok (e.g. `$1.60/$8.00`), a green `free` label for free-tier models, a sale tag when the portal reports a discounted list price, and — new here — the cached-read rate next to the uncached pair, so the prompt-cache saving is visible at selection time (#63125). `ModelPricing` was already present in the `model.options` payload; only the renderer was ignoring it. No backend change.

#84831 carried the right idea (the `ModelPrice` row label + two tests) and is salvage-kept here as the first commit, with two follow-on commits:

### What this PR does
- Puts pricing behind **Settings → Appearance → General → Model Pricing**, off by default (persisted, searchable in settings). With it off the menu is unchanged from main.
- Keeps @anotherchu's `ModelPrice` component and tests verbatim (commit is theirs, authorship preserved).

The CLI picker already renders this rate as a third column — the catalog menu was the only surface dropping it.

## Summary
- Fold the count into the Desktop context meter: once a session has compacted, the meter reads `… 38% ◈ 2` (the Codicon `layers` glyph the sidebar already puts on compression-continuation rows), and the meter's panel shows `Compressions: N` beside `N% Full`. The meter stays unchanged at zero so fresh sessions carry no noise; the panel shows zero explicitly.
- Project the existing canonical `usage.compressions` field (published by `tui_gateway/server.py::_get_usage`): no new backend counter, DB schema, or lineage traversal. This covers the default in-place compaction path that a lineage-derived count would miss (`compression.in_place` defaults to true — same session id, no parent link).
- Authoritative-snapshot semantics throughout: `session.info`/`session.resume`/create usage merges into the addressed `ClientSessionState` (including focused secondary tiles) and clears a stale count when the snapshot omits `compressions`; a cold session switch drops the previous session's live-only count immediately; background `session.usage` ticks cannot overwrite the focused session. Zero is real data; missing stays hidden.

Supersedes #38258, #109376:
- @Xipong's #109376 is the better core approach and this PR carries that commit (plus the `gaoanze888` review fixes: per-tile projection, omission clearing, accessible name).
- @sweetcornna's #38258 proposed a lineage-derived `compress_count`; as the sweeper review on that PR notes, a lineage count is zero on the default in-place compaction path, so this PR uses the canonical live `usage.compressions` instead. The `SessionInfo`/sidebar-history portion of that proposal is deliberately out of scope here.

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/38246 (acceptance: live count surfaced in the status bar's context meter with no-command parity to the CLI/TUI `🗜️ N`; tracked across cold switches and focused tiles; zero rendered explicitly in the panel). raw.body:
Salvage of #126307 by @100yenadmin (Eva), implementing #126265.

Context engines and plugins currently have no stable id for a message. A row id changes when compaction or a row-addressed rewrite re-inserts the row, list position changes on every merge, and the content hash changes on every edit. So a plugin cannot tell "the message I saw last turn" apart from a new one. With this stack, every persisted message carries a durable `message_uid` that survives restore, compaction copies, rewrites, export/import and branch copies. A consecutive-user merge records which uids it folded in (`_absorbed_message_uids`). Each tool call and its result share a per-occurrence uid (`_tool_call_uids` on the assistant row, `_tool_call_uid` on the result). None of these fields reach provider requests. Schema v30 → v31.

WHO / WHEN / WHY: Eva filed #126265 and opened #126307 on 2026-09-28. The 6 feature commits are hers and are cherry-picked with authorship kept. The follow-up commits are mine, from a review that found one startup blocker, two identity mismatches, and a set of cleanups.

## Salvage commits on top of Eva's work

- **Bounded legacy backfill (blocker).** The v31 migration minted uids for every legacy row in a single UPDATE at open. On an 837k-row / 4.8 GB store that took 261 s, and a second process trying to write gave up with `database is locked` after 120 s. The backfill now runs in 2,000-id autocommit chunks: each open spends about 1 s after its first chunk and resumes from a cursor in `state_meta`. New stores are marked done at creation.
- **TUI submit row and model-switch marker.** These rows were written to the DB with one uid while the live dict carried none, or a different one. `append_message` now takes the caller's uid and returns it, so both sides match.
- **Branch and seed copies.** TUI branch, lazy seed and CLI `/branch` wrote fresh uids while the child session kept the parent's live dicts. All three now write the uid the live history keeps. Tool-call uid maps are copied only where the copy also carries `tool_calls`.
- **Tool-call uid pairing (from review, including @andrexibiza's two threads on #126307).**
  - Folding two assistant turns that reuse a provider id (llama.cpp-style ids) keeps a uid for each occurrence instead of only the later one. When one response repeats an id, those calls share one uid, which every result carries. Before a fold appends the next turn's uid, that shared uid is copied into each of the row's own positions so every call stays lined up with its uid.
  - A merge that discards the later turn's text (text next to image content is never joined) no longer records that row as absorbed.
  - Rewriting a stored row no longer loses uids: a restored fold keeps its longer list, a dict that lost its map keeps the stored uids for the calls it still names, and a call the dict dropped doesn't get its uid back.
  - Chunked branch/seed copies pair a result with a call from an earlier chunk.
  - A non-dict uid map on either turn of a fold is ignored instead of raising.
- **Gateway replay keeps identity on plain rows** (Eva's follow-up, cherry-picked with her authorship). `_build_replay_entry` rebuilt plain user/assistant rows without `message_uid` or the merge witness; it now copies both on every role. Tool-call uid maps stay with the rows that still carry their calls.
- **Performance.**
  - The flush path now memoizes each assistant's call index, so pairing a result with its call no longer recomputes it per result. With 160 parallel results: 430 ms → 4 ms.
  - Restore builds that index only for results without a stored uid (an older build's rows).
  - The token-estimate cache key skips persistence-only fields.
- **Cleanups.**
  - One uid reader/stamper and one identity-field copier in `agent/message_metadata.py`, replacing two duplicate helper pairs and four copied blocks.
  - One restore decoder.
  - The four columns recorded as a single schema-history event.
  - The backfill cursor removed once done.
  - Rewind uses the shared helpers.
  - The uid read/write helpers moved into `hermes_state_identity.py`, keeping `hermes_state_messages.py` under 2,000 lines.
  - Three tests dropped that pass without the feature. One added that pairs a result with the assistant that named its call rather than the nearest one; it catches two mutations the existing tests missed.
- **Docs.** Session-storage (v31 row) and context-engine-plugin docs describe the bounded backfill and branch behaviour.

## Behaviour

- New rows get a uid at insert (trigger plus stamping). Legacy rows get one over later opens of any Hermes process. On the 837k-row store that took 85 opens, each about 1.5 s (3.5 s worst). Until then, older rows restore without a uid, as the docs note.
- Opening once the backfill is finished: 0.36 s (main: 0.54 s). During the backfill, a concurrent writer waited at most 1.41 s (p99 1.09 s over 440 attempts). Result: 0 rows without a uid, 0 duplicate uids.
- A v30 (main) build can open, append to, compact and replace in a v31 store, including one that is partly backfilled.
- None of the identity fields reach a provider request. Checked on the chat_completions, anthropic, bedrock and responses converters and on context-engine `select_context` output.

## Known limits (not changed here)

- A branch taken after in-place compaction duplicates the live tail in the child. The duplicate itself already happens on main (the display/live reconcile anchors on the summary row); with this stack the two copies share a uid. The docs already say uids are not unique per row.
- Tool-call uids on legacy rows copied by CLI `/branch` are minted on the copy, so they differ from the live dicts.
- The stored `tool_call_uid` column is kept. It can be derived from the preceding assistant row, but keeping it avoids a restore-time walk.

## Verification

- Uid, context-engine, sequence-repair, TUI submit-row, branch-command and schema-history test files: 127 passed on the rebased head. Each review fix has a test that fails when the old code is put back.
- Live E2E through the real CLI (`chat -q --oneshot` with two tool calls, then `--resume`): every row gets a distinct uid, resumed rows keep theirs, tool results carry the uid their call was given, and `HERMES_DUMP_REQUESTS` shows no identity field in the provider request.
- tests/hermes_state, tests/tui_gateway, tests/acp_adapter and tests/agent, plus targeted hermes_cli/gateway files, run with `scripts/run_tests.sh` on this branch and on main: no failure occurs only on this branch. The failures are local (sqlite `.recover`, holder gates, repair harness) and none are caused by this stack.
- `ty` on the touched files, compared with main: the only new diagnostics are two more `set_meta` calls on the schema mixin (the same pattern main already flags three times) and one `record_absorbed_message` call inside a `micro_compaction` block where main already reports six errors on that `Optional` narrowing.
- Backfill E2E on a copy of a real 837k-row store, with a concurrent writer thread (numbers above).

Closes #126265. Supersedes #126307; Eva's commits are kept as authored.

raw.body:
## What does this PR do?

Re-pins `plugin-catalog/telegram_dashboard_probe.yaml` from `v0.6.0` to [`v0.9.2`](https://github.com/bablobanov/hermes-agent-telegram-dashboard/releases/tag/v0.9.2). It closes both nits left in the review of #122408, gives the entry a card title and a screenshot gallery, and adds to the disclosure what 0.8.x and 0.9.0 read. I'm the author and maintainer of the plugin repo. (Opened for 0.7.0 on 2026-09-28, updated to 0.8.2, 0.9.0 and then 0.9.2 on 2026-10-01, before any review, so the maintainers look at one re-pin rather than four. 0.9.2 is a correctness fix: 0.9.0 showed the time to a limit's reset in whole days from two days on, cut down, so up to almost a day earlier than the real reset (`2d` for two days and 23 hours); 0.9.2 shows it to the minute under a day and to the hour from a day on, never earlier. It reads nothing new.)

Commits: [`v0.6.0...v0.9.2`](https://github.com/bablobanov/hermes-agent-telegram-dashboard/compare/v0.6.0...v0.9.2) (`a409e9a..d60eafc`, 56 commits).

**The two nits from #122408** (closed in 0.7.0):

- *"`_edit_text` is a private adapter method — fall back to `edit_message` first."* Every tick the plugin now reads the verb off the live adapter by signature, never by version number: the public `edit_message` when `inspect.signature` shows a parameter named `parse_mode` (positional-or-keyword or keyword-only; `**kwargs` does not count, since a verb that swallowed the keyword would send the markup as plain text and report success), else the adapter's `_edit_text`, else plain text through the public `edit_message`. On every engine I could check, main at `a3b56cac95` included, `edit_message` takes no parse mode (`plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py:3912`), so today the HTML form still goes through `_edit_text` (`:3892`); the day the public verb takes a `parse_mode`, the plugin uses it from the next tick, without a release. The delivery record names the verb in use (`html_verb`), and a refused HTML edit falls back to a plain edit in the same tick. A `parse_mode` parameter on the public `edit_message` would let the plugin drop the private call entirely; that is an engine change and not part of this PR.
- *"`links.py` is dead code."* Removed with its test.

Also new: the five properties the review checked by hand (no bot-token read in plugin mode, no listening socket, the drift command as argv without a shell, state only under `plugin-data/`, the one task through `ctx.spawn_task`) are now tests in the plugin repo (`tests/test_invariants.py`); 0.9.0 adds four more for what it reads, below.

**What 0.8.x and 0.9.0 read that 0.6.0 did not**, now in the disclosure:

- *External limit sources* (0.8.0, opt-in): up to four `limits_sources` from the config, each asked with one GET to `http` on loopback only (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `::1`), no proxy from the environment, no redirect, 64 KB at most, at most once per `limits_refresh_seconds`. A source may name an environment variable whose value is sent as `Authorization: Bearer`; bot-token variables (`TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `HERMES_DASHBOARD_BOT_TOKEN`, any `*_BOT_TOKEN`) are refused. Without `limits_sources` nothing is asked
- *Gemini refusals from the engine's log* (0.8.1, words of 0.8.2): Google reports Gemini quota only to a project with billing enabled, so the Gemini line shows the last HTTP 429 the engine logged. Every tick the plugin reads the tail of `HERMES_HOME/logs/errors.log` (the last 256 KB; the whole file, up to 4 MB, until the first successful read) and keeps four fields of the newest Gemini 429: the time, the `limit`, the retry and the `model`. The rest of the message never reaches the record or the screen, no other log is read, and nothing goes to the network
- *Failed sends from the same log* (0.9.0): the same tail is also read for the engine's own `Failed to send Telegram message` ERROR lines; only their time is kept
- *The cron line* (0.9.0): every tick `HERMES_HOME/cron/jobs.json` is read for each job's id, name, enabled flag, state, times, status and failure streak (never `prompt`, `script`, `deliver`, `skills` or the model), the ticker's marker files (`ticker_heartbeat`, `ticker_last_success`, `ticker_last_error`) for their epoch, and `HERMES_HOME/cron/executions.db` is opened read-only (`sqlite3` with `mode=ro` in the URI and `PRAGMA query_only`, in a worker under the tick's deadline, closed after the query) for the `job_id`, `status`, `delivery_outcome`, `claimed_at` and `finished_at` columns of failed or undelivered runs, never the `error` column and never `state.db`. The engine's error texts (`last_error`, `last_delivery_error`, the ticker's) are reduced to the kind of the error in a word and never reach the screen or the plugin's record. The rules are the engine's own (`hermes cron status`): a `last_status` outside `ok`/`delivery_failed`/`delivery_queued` is a failed run, a `last_delivery_error` an undelivered result, a heartbeat older than 200 s a dead ticker, a `next_run_at` more than 15 min in the past an overdue job
- *Whether the connected channel is deaf* (0.9.0), in a sentence of its own in the disclosure because one part of it is not the engine's public API: every tick the plugin reads the public property `send_path_degraded` of the connected Telegram adapter (`BasePlatformAdapter`, since 0.21.1; the Telegram adapter overrides it), and, as a capability and not a contract, four private attributes of the live adapter object (`_updates_received_total`, `_polling_generation`, `_polling_last_progress_monotonic`, `_polling_generation_started_monotonic`), read as attributes, with nothing called on the adapter (a test reads the plugin's source to pin that). An adapter without them shows `Telegram traffic: no data` with the reason and never raises; a public snapshot of the polling state on the adapter would turn the capability into a contract, which is an engine change and not part of this PR

0.9.1 and 0.9.2 read nothing beyond this: the `paused_at` stamp 0.9.1 reads is one of a job's times, and 0.9.2 reads the same fields as the engine's ticker reads them (`is_job_runnable`). The disclosure now also names the enabled flag, which 0.9.0 already read.

What the entry changes:

| key | v0.6.0 | v0.9.2 |
|---|---|---|
| `sha` | `a409e9a7e0…` | `d60eafca56…` (tag `v0.9.2`) |
| `version` | `"0.6.0"` | `"0.9.2"` |
| `title` | none | `Telegram Dashboard` |
| `description` | a long feature list, then the disclosure | a two-sentence summary, then the maintainer's disclosure word for word, our 0.8.2 sentence about errors.log extended with the failed-send lines, and the sentences above added after the Kimi Code one |
| `image` | `docs/social-preview.jpg` at the old sha | the same file at `682e20b` (tag `v0.7.0`) |
| `screenshots` | none | 4 PNGs at `682e20b`: the pinned screen healthy, with its details open, with a config-drift warning, and under the stale banner |

`image` and `screenshots` stay pinned at the `v0.7.0` commit: `docs/` has not changed since, and the files at `682e20b` are byte-identical to the ones at `v0.9.2`. The screenshots are the plugin's own demo states (`python -m telegram_dashboard --demo 14`, `15`, `16`) sent as a test message; the Hermes release dates in them are upstream's real ones, every other number is made up. They were taken on 0.7.0: 0.9.0 adds a `Cron` line to the top block (`Cron ✓ N jobs` after `Drift`), four sources to the coverage count in the details (`sources 10/10` where they show `6/6`: the Gemini log, the cron jobs, the cron history and the Telegram traffic), and lines about Gemini refusals, cron, the Telegram traffic and the dashboard's own version to the open details.

Everything else the disclosure describes is unchanged: the same hosts, the same writes (the plugin's record under `HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/`, which gains two keys, `cron_cache` and `traffic_cache`), the same optional `drift_command` subprocess; no hook, no tool, no new setting; the plugin still never reads the Telegram bot token itself.

Gate evidence (run for `v0.9.2` on 2026-10-01; Hermes v0.21.5 in a scratch venv, plugin folder exported from the tagged commit with `git archive`, 28 files = `SHA256SUMS`):

- `hermes plugins validate plugin/telegram_dashboard_probe` → 13 checks passed, `security scan — safe`, `Validation passed.`; `--json` → `"ok": true`, `"warnings": []` (Hermes 0.21.3: its 10 checks passed, `"ok": true`, `"warnings": []`)
- `python scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` (from main at `a3b56cac95`) on the entry → `OK: 1 file(s) valid`; with the whole `plugin-catalog/` → `OK: 349 file(s) valid`
- `plugin.yaml` at the pinned sha, the `image` and the four `screenshots` URLs return 200; the image files are byte-identical to the tagged ones

Other evidence: 0.9.2 runs on the author's live gateway (Hermes 0.21.3) since 2026-10-01; its delivery record shows `html_verb: _edit_text`, `screen_format: html`, `cron_cache` and `traffic_cache`, and the installed folder matches the tag's `SHA256SUMS`. Its limits read `⚠️ Claude 24% (3h8m) · 95% (4d6h)` and `Codex 34% (5d19h)`, where the code of 0.9.0 gives `95% (4d)` and `Codex 34% (5d)` for the same data. The first tick of 0.9.0 said `Cron ⚠️ 1 of 23 failing`: one job's result from 2026-09-27 had not reached one of its chats, which `hermes cron list` confirms and the screen of 0.8.2 did not show. The repo's CI at the pinned sha runs tests on Python 3.11-3.13 (705 passed), ruff, `mypy --strict`, and the manifest job (28 files).

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality): the entry is re-pinned to a new plugin release

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/telegram_dashboard_probe.yaml`: `sha`, `version`, `title`, `description` (the summary before the disclosure, the sentences above added to it), `image` re-pinned, `screenshots` added

## How to Test

1. `hermes plugins install telegram_dashboard_probe` installs 0.9.2 from the pinned sha (over 0.6.0: `hermes plugins update telegram_dashboard_probe`)
2. Restart the gateway; the pinned message keeps being edited every period
3. The delivery record under `HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/` shows `html_verb: _edit_text` on today's engines; the open details of the message carry `Cron N active · M paused · ticker HH:MM`, `Telegram last update seen …`, `Telegram send errors: …`, `Gemini refusals seen by Hermes: …` and, last, `Dashboard 0.9.2`

## Checklist

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide and the catalog README
- [x] My commit message follows Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains only this catalog entry
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q`: N/A, no engine code changes

feat(plugin-catalog): add minimax-search (community, web)

Adds a catalog entry for the MiniMax Token Plan web search plugin.

**What it does:** registers a web search provider named `minimax` that queries
`POST https://api.minimax.io/v1/coding_plan/search` with `{"q": <query>}` and maps
`organic[]` (title / link / snippet / date) onto the shared `web_search` row shape.
Search-only — the vendor returns snippets, never page bodies, so extraction is
unchanged and continues to use `web.backend` / `extract_backend`.

**Why it's useful:** SearXNG and other metasearch backends depend on third-party
engines (Brave, Google, Startpage, DuckDuckGo) that rate-limit or CAPTCHA
datacenter IPs. This provider goes straight to the vendor with a keyed request, so
it does not inherit those upstream blocks.

**Credential:** requires a MiniMax **Token Plan** key (`sk-cp-…`). Ordinary
MiniMax model API keys are rejected by the search endpoint — `is_available()`
reports the provider as unavailable rather than failing at call time, and
`get_setup_schema()` points at the Token Plan key page.

**Scope:** search backend only. No tools, hooks, or middleware are registered,
and `capabilities` declares exactly that (`requires_env: MINIMAX_API_KEY`).
SHA is pinned to the initial commit; `version` is a cosmetic label for it.

Plugin repo (author-owned): https://github.com/pdonizete/hermes-minimax-search

raw.body:
Persistent Modal sandboxes no longer lose their filesystem after 30 idle days: the snapshot is retained until Hermes deletes it, and the SDK pin moves to a version that has the knob.

## Changes
- `tools/environments/modal.py::ModalEnvironment.cleanup` passes `snapshot_filesystem(ttl=None)`. On modal ≥ 1.5 the default is `ttl=2592000` (30 days), after which the snapshot image is gone and the next session silently restarts from the base image.
- `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock`: `modal==1.3.4` → `modal==1.5.5` (+ its `synchronicity` dep). 1.3.4 has no `ttl` parameter at all (legacy `SandboxSnapshotFs` RPC), so the kwarg needs the bump to exist on every install; the venvs already on 1.5.x were sending the 30-day default.
- Dead code removed: `_modal.Mount.from_local_file(...)` credential-mount block. `modal.Mount` left the public API in modal 1.0, so that line raised `AttributeError` into the surrounding `except` on every sandbox start and mounted nothing. The `FileSyncManager` created right after already uploads the same credential, skills and cache files (`iter_sync_files`), so nothing is lost. The test fake stops exporting a `Mount` the real SDK does not have.
- Docs: `configuration.md` Modal persistence paragraph states the retention.

## Root cause
Modal added a default snapshot TTL in SDK 1.5; our call site predates it and never opted out.

## Validation
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/tools/test_modal_snapshot_isolation.py::test_persistent_cleanup_snapshots_without_expiry` | red on `origin/main` (`snapshot_calls == []`, the fake swallowed the kwarg-less call), green on head |
| Modal test files (6) + `tests/tools/environments` | 55 passed |
| `python -m pm.build_env --source . --check-lock` | resolves clean |
| `inspect.signature(modal.Sandbox.snapshot_filesystem)` on 1.5.5 | `(self, timeout: int = 55, *, ttl: int | None = 2592000)`; docstring: "Pass `ttl=None` to retain the image indefinitely" |
| Rest of our Modal surface on 1.5.5 (`App.lookup.aio`, `Image.from_registry/from_id`, `Sandbox.create.aio`, `exec.aio`, `terminate.aio`) | present, signatures compatible |

No Modal credentials on the dev box, so no live sandbox round-trip in this PR; the fix is the vendor-documented kwarg, proven at the SDK boundary.

## Follow-up context
Found while verifying vendor docs for #121169 (Bot Screen in the sandbox).

raw.body:
Fresh Vercel sandboxes start from a managed container image (`vercel/sandbox/universal:latest`) instead of the `runtime` preset Vercel deprecated, with a config migration so existing installs follow along and legacy pins keep working.

## Changes
- New `terminal.vercel_image` (default `vercel/sandbox/universal:latest`: Ubuntu, Node 24, Python 3.14). Accepts any Vercel managed image or a project VCR repository[:tag|@digest].
- `terminal.vercel_runtime` default `node24` → `""`. A pinned runtime (`node24|node22|python3.13`) still works, overrides the image and logs a deprecation warning; the two are never sent together (Vercel rejects that).
- Snapshot restores send neither `runtime` nor `image`: the snapshot carries its filesystem, and Vercel refuses `runtime` with a snapshot source. Persisted sandboxes are unaffected by the default change.
- `_migrate_to_49`: drops `terminal.vercel_runtime: node24` (the template default, never a choice) from config.yaml AND the `TERMINAL_VERCEL_RUNTIME=node24` mirror the setup wizard wrote to `.env`; `node22`/`python3.13` pins survive. `_config_version` 48 → 49.
- Surfaces: `TERMINAL_VERCEL_IMAGE` bridged like its siblings (`cli_config_load`, `config.py`, `gateway/run.py`, `terminal_tool.py`), setup wizard prompts for the image (and warns when a legacy runtime pin will override it), dashboard config gets an image field and a clearable legacy-runtime select, `hermes status`/`hermes config` show the effective image. Docs updated (`configuration.md`, `tools.md`).

## Vendor basis
- [Runtimes](https://vercel.com/docs/sandbox/concepts/runtimes): "Since August 7th, runtimes are deprecated and we recommend using Images for new sandboxes… sandboxes that specify neither `runtime` nor `image` use the `vercel/sandbox/universal:latest` managed image."
- [Images](https://vercel.com/docs/sandbox/concepts/images): `vercel/sandbox/universal:latest` = Node.js LTS (24), Python (3.14), coding agents, utilities.
- Python SDK 0.7.2 (our pin) `Sandbox.create` docstring: `runtime` "Mutually exclusive with `image` and unavailable when `source` is a snapshot"; `image` "Vercel Container Registry image… a bare repository name resolves to the `latest` tag."

## Validation
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/tools/test_vercel_sandbox_environment.py::TestImageSelection` (fresh → image only; legacy pin → runtime only; restore → neither) | green on head; the `runtime`/`image` keys did not exist on base |
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_config_migration_49_vercel_image.py` (seeded default dropped from config.yaml + .env, user pin survives, merged default resolves) | green |
| Vercel suite + terminal requirements + setup/status/doctor/cli_init + config env/migration suites | 184 passed, 0 failed |
| Real-import chain probe (temp `HERMES_HOME` → `_mirror_config_to_env` → `terminal_tool._get_env_config` → backend factory kwargs) | default: `{'runtime': None, 'image': 'vercel/sandbox/universal:latest'}`; with `TERMINAL_VERCEL_RUNTIME=python3.13`: runtime carried, image dropped in `__init__` |

No Vercel credentials on the dev box, so no live sandbox round-trip in this PR; behaviour follows the vendor docs and the pinned SDK's own contract.

## Follow-up context
Found while verifying vendor docs for #121169 (Bot Screen in the sandbox).

## Infographic

raw.body:
Re-pins `bot-forge` from v0.12.0 to **v0.15.0** (`58493c3236f4eec75395718765c3ad0a11f4e8af`, tagged [v0.15.0](https://github.com/BkashJEE/hermes-bot-forge/releases/tag/v0.15.0)). Follows #121190, which listed v0.12.0.

This PR previously proposed v0.13.0; it has been re-pointed rather than stacking a second bump of the same file, so there is one entry to review instead of two.

### A blocked Bot tells the user instead of waiting to be asked

`check_agents` gathers what needs the user; that is a pull. This adds the push: when a Bot journals a `blocked` or `failed` entry it sends one plain-text email, and a `digest` action sends the whole waiting queue on a schedule. It reuses Hermes' existing `EMAIL_SMTP_HOST` / `EMAIL_ADDRESS` / `EMAIL_PASSWORD`, so there is **no new credential and nothing to sign up for**, and it is skipped in silence when those are unset.

"An agent with email" is usually where this goes wrong, so the scope is deliberately narrow:

- **Outbound only.** Nothing reads a mailbox or accepts a reply.
- **The recipient is resolved from config alone** — never from a tool argument, a persona, or any text a model produced. There is no tool for mailing an arbitrary address, by design, so a Bot cannot be talked into contacting a third party and two Bots cannot start a reply loop.
- Rate limited per Bot, secret-scanned before sending, `Auto-Submitted: auto-generated`, and a failed send can never break a turn, a journal write or a routine.

### Acknowledgement reactions that fit the work

A Bot reacts to the user's own message as the turn runs. The reaction now reads the message — 🔧 a fix, 🔎 research, ✍️ writing, 📊 numbers, ⏳ scheduling, 📋 a review, 🛠️ something to build, 💬 a question — and the ending says what happened: 🚀 shipped, 📝 written, 📈 numbers, 🗓️ scheduled, 💡 found out, 🧹 cleaned up, with ✅ as the fallback and ✋ / ⚠️ taking precedence when the user is needed or something is blocked.

Three fixes behind that, all found by running it on a real machine rather than a fixture:

- **A profile running both the plugin and its `bot-forge-marks` companion appeared never to react.** Both registered the same turn hooks, and Hermes treats a second identical emoji on a message as a tapback toggle — so the reaction was placed and immediately cleared. The plugin now stands down when the companion is beside it.
- **A Bot could have the hook installed and enabled and still stay silent**, because Hermes' own `message_reactions` setting was never switched on and an unset value reads as off. Creation now sets both, and the plugin adopts every live profile on load — including Bots made through Hermes' New Agent dialog, which never heard of this plugin. `adopt_bots: false` switches that off.
- The numbers rule never matched a percentage: its pattern ended in a word boundary directly after `%`, which is already a non-word character.

### The workspace survey, corrected against a real machine

v0.12.0's survey was validated on a clean fixture. Against ten configured roots and thirty near-identical checkouts: one crowded root drained the whole scan budget; a directory with almost no words matched anything it shared one with; nested copies appeared several times. Each root now gets its own share of the cap, a place needs real vocabulary and two shared terms, duplicates collapse to the shallowest path, and the job's terms are widened with related ones before places are searched (job side only — never the corpus, never the duplicate guard).

139 tests pass on the pinned commit ([CI](https://github.com/BkashJEE/hermes-bot-forge/actions/workflows/tests.yml)); `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` passes on this entry. `image:` points at the repo's social-preview card at the same pinned SHA.

raw.body:
Salvages #121396 by @ajbmachon, with tests from #102987 by @shorehefei-ship-it and credit to #98523 by @salch-cred. The two gateway commits from #121396 are cherry-picked, so authorship is kept (the Desktop busy-turn deferral hunk from that PR is left out; it is a separate change). One commit on top.

The change watcher fingerprinted `sessions.changed` on the raw `state.db` / WAL mtime. The gateway heartbeat and the session activity stamp (`last_activity_at`) write to that same file about once a minute with no session change, so every write broadcast `sessions.changed` and the Desktop Sessions panel refreshed on its own every ~25–60s.

#121396 replaces the mtime with a blake2b digest of the session columns Desktop renders, read only when the DB/WAL mtime moved, so an idle pass is still just a stat. Its column list still included `last_activity_at` and `last_activity_description`, which the activity heartbeat restamps, so the refresh kept firing. This PR removes them from the digest. Creating, renaming, deleting, pinning or archiving a session, or a new message landing (`message_count`), still moves it.

What changed from the original PRs:

- `last_activity_at` / `last_activity_description` are no longer hashed. Desktop doesn't render either field from the list, and liveness comes from `session.active_list`.
- The probe opens through `_connect_tracked_db` + `read_only_db_uri`, the read-only connect other live `state.db` readers use, instead of a raw `sqlite3.connect`.
- If a read fails after a good one (locked or busy store), the last digest is kept and the next pass tries again, instead of flipping to the mtime signature and back (two false broadcasts). #102987 handled this case the same way.
- #102987's `SUM(...)`-based fingerprint is dropped (swapping two titles of equal length doesn't change it), and so is its `chat/index.tsx` hunk: it conflicts with main's `isRouteSessionMismatch` options API and isn't needed once the heartbeat broadcasts stop.
- Nothing from #98523 is used. Its `max(updated_at)` probe always throws because `sessions` has no `updated_at` column, so it falls back to mtime.

Tests (`tests/tui_gateway/test_change_watcher.py`, `test_change_watcher_sessions.py`):

- Three heartbeat windows (a `gateway_heartbeats` write plus a `last_activity_at` stamp each) broadcast nothing. On origin/main this fails, and it also fails on #121396 as submitted.
- A new session row, a rename, a `message_count` bump and a delete each broadcast.
- A store that becomes unreadable after a good read doesn't broadcast. This fails on origin/main and on #121396.
- On origin/main: 3 failed / 25 passed. On this branch: 28 passed (`scripts/run_tests.sh`), and `ruff check` is clean.

Supersedes #121396
Supersedes #102987
Supersedes #98523
Fixes #98005

Salvages #76838 by @webtecnica. Their commit is cherry-picked with the test file conflict resolved onto the current mock setup, so authorship is kept. One commit on top removes the refocus effect and extends the test.

In Settings → Gateway with SSH mode, an empty saved host, and aliases in `~/.ssh/config`, picking "Custom (enter manually)…" did nothing the first time. The host Select's controlled value fell back to the Custom sentinel whenever the saved host wasn't one of the aliases, so it was already `__custom__` before the click. Radix only calls `onValueChange` when the value changes, so `selectHost` never ran and the text input never mounted. It only worked after picking an alias first and then Custom. The trigger also showed "Custom (enter manually)…" as its value instead of the placeholder.

The fix is @webtecnica's: the Select's value falls back to `''` instead of the sentinel. The trigger shows the placeholder, and the first Custom pick goes from `''` to `__custom__`, which fires the callback and mounts the input.

What changed from the original PR:
- Re-applied on the current `gateway-settings.tsx`. The file was refactored since the PR opened, which is why it conflicted; the SSH host logic itself had not changed.
- Dropped the `requestAnimationFrame` refocus effect and the input ref. The issue came from the input never rendering, not from a focus race. Once it mounts, the existing `autoFocus` focuses it, and the test passes without the effect.
- Ported the regression test to the current hoisted store mocks. It also types into the field, then clears it and blurs to check that it goes back to the dropdown.
- No styling changes.

Tests:
- `npx vitest run src/app/settings/gateway-settings.test.tsx -t Custom` with `origin/main`'s `gateway-settings.tsx`: fails, no textbox after the first Custom click.
- `npx vitest run src/app/settings/gateway-settings.test.tsx` on this branch: 15 passed.

raw.body:
Salvages #125917 by @helix4u. Their two commits are cherry-picked as-is, so authorship is kept. No rework commit on top: the change applies cleanly to current main and does not clash with anything that landed since.

A completed tool card disappeared from Desktop chat and Bot Chat tiles once the transcript refreshed. When the newest stored page brought the final assistant reply without the turn's tool rows, the refresh took that page as the whole window, and the live tool card went with it. The Discord reporter hit this on KoboldCPP. It doesn't depend on the provider: any text-only page that carries the final reply triggers it.

#126409 was merged as the real fix and #125917 was closed. That PR fixed only the Codex `webSearch` projector, so Codex searches now get stored as `web_search` tool rows. Nothing on the Desktop side changed, and a refresh page without the tool rows still clobbers the live card for every other runtime. The three regression tests below fail on current main, which already includes #126409.

The fix follows the "Merge, don't clobber" rule in `apps/desktop/AGENTS.md`. After `graftRefreshedTailOntoBackfill` builds the refreshed window, completed live tool parts from the settled turn are carried onto the refreshed final reply, but only when:

- the durable user row and the final assistant row ids match the live turn,
- the final reply text is unchanged,
- the refreshed turn doesn't already have a tool part with that `toolCallId`.

Durable rows still win when the page has them. The standard runtime emits `tool.start` with the stored `tool_call_id`, and #126409 made Codex search rows use the live id too. So when the page has the tool row, the live copy is skipped and nothing renders twice. The same reply text on a different durable row doesn't inherit the tools.

What changed from the original PR
- Nothing. Rebased onto current main with no conflicts.

Tests (`apps/desktop`, `npx vitest run --project ui`)
- On main with only the test changes: `completed-reply-refresh.test.tsx` + `use-session-tile-delegate.test.ts` give 3 failed / 32 passed. The new cases (text-only refresh for active chat and tile, Bot Chat tile final-reply refresh) all end with `expected [] to match object [{ toolCallId: … }]`.
- This branch: those two files plus `transcript-backfill.test.ts`, `folded-tool-turn-refresh.test.tsx` and the `use-background-sync` suites give 6 files, 117/117 passed.
- `npx tsc -p . --noEmit` and eslint on the touched files: clean.

Supersedes #125917

raw.body:
If a Hermes.app that an earlier `hermes update` installed is later removed, `hermes update` now puts it back and says so. Finder, the Dock and Spotlight can find Hermes again.

**Who / when / why:** Found on 2026-09-28 while working out why Hermes had disappeared from Spotlight on a maintainer's Mac. A test had deleted `/Applications/Hermes.app`; the test side is fixed in a companion PR. Every `hermes update` after that skipped the missing copy without a word, so nothing ever brought the app back. The skip goes back to 032cf8438f (#113933, @teknium1, 2026-09-17), which refreshes only bundles that still exist. That was reasonable at the time: the ownership stamp that marks a copy as this checkout's lives inside the bundle, so it disappears along with the bundle.

**Changes**
- `hermes_cli/main_desktop.py`
  - `_refresh_installed_desktop_apps` records which installed copies the update keeps current, in `desktop-installed-apps.json` under the default Hermes root. Only the checkout that owns installed apps writes this file, never one running off macOS or from a dev worktree. A copy that failed to reinstall stays recorded, so the next update tries again. If the record can't be written, the update prints a warning and carries on.
  - A restored copy prints `✓ Reinstalled the Desktop app at … it had been removed, so Finder, the Dock and Spotlight could not find Hermes`.
  - When no owned copy is left, `_installed_desktop_apps` counts a recorded path that is now missing as installed, so the update rebuilds the Desktop app for it. A copy the user moved from `/Applications` to `~/Applications` (or back) keeps its stamp, so the update finds it there and doesn't install a second one.
  - `_install_rebuilt_macos_bundles` installs into missing paths as well as stale ones, using the same stage-and-swap with `ditto`, so the signature is preserved. `_install_rebuilt_desktop_app` now takes the candidate list from its caller rather than computing it a second time.
- `hermes_cli/gui_uninstall.py`: `desktop_install_record()` is the one place the record's path is defined. `uninstall_gui` deletes the record wherever the uninstall runs from, including a profile, since the installed apps are machine-wide. So `hermes uninstall` in any mode deletes it, including the in-app uninstall, which runs `hermes uninstall`, and the app stays uninstalled.
- Docs: `getting-started/updating.md` step 6.

**Validation**

| | before (origin/main) | after |
|---|---|---|
| Real rebuilt bundle, install path in a temp dir, copy deleted, then the update tail runs | nothing printed, app stays missing, update wouldn't even rebuild for it | `✓ Reinstalled …`, app present, `codesign --verify --deep --strict` passes |
| `uninstall_gui` then update | — | app stays gone, record removed |
| Copy moved to the other Applications folder, then update | — | no second copy is installed |

- Tests: one existing test flipped (a missing candidate path is now installed) and one new invariant test (macOS): a moved copy isn't doubled, a deleted copy comes back every time, and nothing comes back after a GUI uninstall run from a profile home. Both fail on origin/main. A mutation that stops uninstall from removing the record makes the new test fail.
- Local run of the 82 test files that reference the touched symbols (first revision): the same 38 environment failures as origin/main, no new failures, +1 pass. The touched test files were re-run on this revision: all pass, except one launchd-plist test that also fails on origin/main on this machine.
- Review: 4-angle review plus the reuse/quality/efficiency passes. I applied the moved-copy, profile-uninstall, stale-record, record-write-failure, `read_json_or_empty` reuse and single-computation findings.

**Known edge:** a user who drags an update-installed Hermes.app to the Trash by hand, instead of running `hermes uninstall`, gets it back on the next update. From inside the updater that looks exactly like the app being deleted by accident, which is the case this PR fixes.

raw.body:
A test that runs the real GUI uninstall or update swap can no longer delete or overwrite the developer's own installed Hermes desktop app. The test now fails and says so.

**Who / when / why:** On 2026-09-26, during review of #122553 (commit 954d90f15f by @dskwe, 2026-09-25), its `test_uninstall_gui_keeps_userdata_dir_when_told_to` called the real `uninstall_gui()` and stubbed only the userData dir. On macOS, `packaged_gui_app_paths()` returns the real `/Applications/Hermes.app`, and tests keep `HOME` intact, so the test deleted a maintainer's installed app. The open app started failing lazy chunk loads two minutes later, and Hermes was gone from Spotlight. That test was trimmed before it merged. Nothing stops the next one.

**Changes**
- `tests/conftest.py` captures `packaged_gui_app_paths()` at import time, before any test can patch `sys.platform`, `HOME` or `XDG_*`. The captured paths are `/Applications/Hermes.app` and `~/Applications/Hermes.app` on macOS, the desktop entry and icons on Linux, and `Programs\Hermes` on Windows.
- `tests/home_io_guard.py` fails the test on any delete, rename, replace, `chmod`, `utime` or write-mode `open` / `os.open` inside those paths, whether the path matches as written or only after resolving symlinks. Reads stay allowed, because update paths probe the installed app. Calls that don't delete or write pay nothing extra. The refusal uses `pytest.fail` rather than `AssertionError`: `gui_uninstall._remove_path` catches `Exception`, so an assertion would have been logged as a warning and the test would have passed.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_real_home_tripwire.py`: one invariant test. Reading is allowed; `rmtree`, `unlink`, replace, an in-place write, and an `rmtree` through a symlinked parent are all refused.

**Validation**

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| #122553's destructive test, run on a Mac with `/Applications/Hermes.app` installed | app deleted, test passes | test fails with `TEST BUG: changing the REAL installed Hermes desktop app: /Applications/Hermes.app`; app intact (`codesign --verify --deep` OK) |

- Local run of `test_real_home_tripwire.py`, `test_linux_desktop_entry.py`, `test_gui_uninstall.py` and `test_desktop_install_after_update.py`: 100 passed, 2 skipped. The only failure in that run was #122553's planted destructive test, which is the intended result.
- Review: I applied the in-place write and resolved-path findings. I kept `refuse()` for home-root I/O as it was, since changing it is out of scope.

raw.body:
Rebuilding Hermes Desktop no longer mangles output paths containing an apostrophe (`C:\Users\r'y'z` → `C:\Users\ryz`, EPERM), and no longer needs the `cross-env` bin to be installed.

Fixes #103010. Also fixes #110121.

Root cause: the desktop `builder` npm script was `cross-env NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=16384 node scripts/run-electron-builder.mjs`. `cross-env@10.1.0` strips every bare `'` from the arguments it forwards, on every platform. The rebuild passes its staging directory as `-c.directories.output=<path>`, so a profile path containing `'` reached electron-builder without it. The same prefix is also why a rebuild failed whenever the cross-env bin was missing (#110121).

## Changes
- `apps/desktop/package.json`: `builder` is now plain `node scripts/run-electron-builder.mjs`. `cross-env` is still a devDependency for the `dev:*` scripts.
- `apps/desktop/scripts/run-electron-builder.mjs`: the wrapper already spawns every child itself (native-deps staging, packaging-tool preparation, the strict builder, electron-builder). It now sets the heap flag on those children:
  - The flag is appended to any inherited `NODE_OPTIONS` without re-tokenizing it, so quoted preload paths survive.
  - It goes last, so 16384 still takes effect even when a smaller heap is inherited, as it did under cross-env.
- Behaviour differences from cross-env:
  - An inherited `NODE_OPTIONS` (for example a `--require` hook) now reaches the build children; cross-env used to replace it.
  - The release path (`scripts/bundles/desktop.py` → `run-electron-builder.mjs --prepared`) never went through cross-env. It now also gets the 16384 heap on electron-builder.

## Validation
| Check | Before (origin/main) | After |
|---|---|---|
| `npm run builder -- --dir --publish never "-c.directories.output=/Users/r'y'z/…"`, argv as received | `/Users/ryz/…` | `/Users/r'y'z/…`, verbatim through npm → wrapper → strict builder child |
| Heap on each child, with inherited `NODE_OPTIONS="--import=<probe> --max-old-space-size=4096"` | 16384 (inherited value dropped) | `--max-old-space-size=4096 --max-old-space-size=16384`, V8 `heap_size_limit` = 16480 MB; inherited preload kept |
| `vitest --project electron scripts/` | 6 failures (macOS-host environment) | the same failures, plus 2 new tests passing; neither new test passes on origin/main |

## Credit
- The approach and first commit come from @teknium1's #110142, cherry-picked to keep authorship and re-applied onto the prepared-packaging wrapper that has since landed on main.
- @liuhao1024 first fixed #103010 in #103035 (bypassing `npm run` from Python).
- @Ryfferty traced the stripping to cross-env and confirmed the fix end-to-end on the affected Windows machine.

## What

`tests/hermes_cli/test_local_runtime.py::test_ensure_local_runtime_serializes_racing_callers` fails deterministically on `main` since 65ff3ad35360 (*fix(local-runtime): reject reused legacy server pids*). Every PR rebased past that commit goes red on **Python tests / Run tests** (#126163, #126145 in the sweep6 train).

## Why main did not catch it

GitHub Actions has been failing to start the `ci.yaml` push run on `main` since 16:50Z today (zero-job runs; the run page says *"An unexpected error has occurred and we've been automatically notified"*), so 65ff3ad353 and everything after it landed with no main-side signal.

## Root cause

65ff3ad353 correctly made a bare legacy `{pid}` state record non-adoptable (a live PID is not evidence of the managed router) and moved the other tests in the file onto `_write_current_process_state`, but left the racing-callers `_FakeSupervisor.start` publishing the legacy shape. The second caller therefore can never adopt the first's state and spawns too → `assert 2 == 1`.

## Fix

The fake publishes what a real supervisor publishes (modern record via the existing helper). Test-only; the production change in 65ff3ad353 is right.

## Proof

Bisect: passes at `65ff3ad35360~1`, fails at `65ff3ad35360` (3/3 local runs). With this patch: `tests/hermes_cli/test_local_runtime.py` 45 passed × 3 runs.

## Summary
Add Hermes Notch Plugin to the community catalog, pinned to v0.3.0 commit c8a01b668836e5d9a49f92226f0f305b6decccb0.

- Renamed public repository: himanusia/hermes-notch-plugin. Stable runtime ID hermes-atoll preserves existing enabled installations.
- macOS session/turn status, title/request start preview, title/Complete finish preview, and dummy GIF/screenshots in README.

raw.body:
## What

Adds Claude Sonnet 5.5 (`claude-sonnet-5-5`), which Anthropic released on 2026-09-28, and fixes the one request shape that breaks on it.

**WHO / WHEN / WHY:** Anthropic launched Sonnet 5.5 on 2026-09-28 ([announcement](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-sonnet-5-5), [model page](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/sonnet-5-5/overview), [migration guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/sonnet-5-5/migration-guide)). As of this PR no open PR or issue covered it. It is already live on OpenRouter and on Nous Portal as `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`.

## Changes

| Surface | Change |
|---|---|
| `hermes_cli/models_catalog_static.py` | `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` added to `OPENROUTER_MODELS`; the `nous` list derives from it. `claude-sonnet-5-5` added to native `anthropic`, and `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5` to `bedrock`. The Bedrock default at `[0]` is unchanged. |
| `website/static/api/model-catalog.json` | Regenerated with `scripts/build_model_catalog.py` |
| `agent/usage_pricing.py` | Sonnet 5 and 5.5 share one native Anthropic row: $2 / $10, cache read $0.20, 5m cache write $2.50 (the migration guide says "the same prices as Claude Sonnet 5"). Main's Sonnet 5 comment said the $2/$10 intro price reverts to $3/$15 after 2026-08-31; Anthropic's [pricing page](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing) still lists $2/$10, so that stale instruction is removed. |
| `agent/anthropic_adapter.py` | Reasoning-off requests now send `thinking: {"type": "between_tools"}` to Sonnet 5.5 on anthropic.com. See below. |

These already resolve correctly through the existing `claude-sonnet-5` prefix entries, so they needed no change: 1M context (native + Bedrock), 128K max output, the adaptive-thinking / xhigh / no-sampling-params gates, and the 180s reasoning stale-timeout floor.

## Thinking-off breaking change

On Sonnet 5.5, `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` returns HTTP 400. The lowest setting is now `between_tools`, which turns off up-front thinking. It takes no other thinking field and returns 400 at `xhigh`/`max` effort. The disable path therefore sends it with no other fields and no `output_config`, so the API default effort of `high` applies.

Without this change, every path that turns reasoning off would 400 on native Anthropic: title generation, the compression fast lane, and `/reasoning none`. Opus 5.5 hit the same class of bug in #120069.

Relays behave differently. Live probe of Nous Portal `/v1/messages` with `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` on 2026-09-28:

| `thinking` sent | Portal response |
|---|---|
| omitted | 200 |
| `adaptive` | 200 |
| `disabled` | 400 "Reasoning is mandatory for this endpoint and cannot be disabled." |
| `between_tools` | 400 "Invalid Anthropic Messages API request" |

So on endpoints outside anthropic.com, the Sonnet 5.5 family keeps the mandatory-thinking omission. That includes Bedrock via the AnthropicBedrock SDK, which passes the `bedrock-runtime` URL, and Azure; neither was verified for `between_tools`. Omitting the field never 400s; the cost is that thinking stays on. `_accepts_thinking_disable` now returns False for this family, and `base_url` is keyword-only on `_thinking_kwargs`, so no caller gets the native shape by default.

## Verification

- `tests/agent/test_anthropic_thinking_disable.py`: Sonnet 5.5 gets `between_tools` (bare, even when xhigh is requested) on `None` / api.anthropic.com, and the omission on Portal and Bedrock; `claude-sonnet-5` still gets `disabled`. Mutation check: removing the third-party guard fails exactly the Portal and Bedrock rows.
- `tests/agent/test_usage_pricing.py`: Sonnet 5.5 rates equal Sonnet 5 rates (relationship test, not a snapshot).
- Targeted suite (75 files: every `tests/agent/test_anthropic*`, transports, model-switch, catalog, pricing, metadata, bedrock, auxiliary): 1393 passed, 42 failed. All 42 failures are identical by name on `origin/main` (re-run on the merge-base). After the follow-up commit, the touched files pass 434/434. Ruff is clean.
- Live, through Portal `/v1/messages` with this adapter's real kwargs: reasoning off → 200; high → 200 (adaptive + summarized); xhigh with a tool → 200 with `tool_use`. Also live through Portal `chat_completions` via `AIAgent` with reasoning off: returned `TEST-OK anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`.
- **Not live-tested on native anthropic.com** (no Anthropic key available). The `between_tools` shape there comes from the vendor's migration guide.

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- **Forced `tool_choice`** (`any`/`tool`) also returns 400 on Sonnet 5.5, as on Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1. No in-tree caller forces tool choice on the Anthropic path; auxiliary pass-through is the only route. #123690 adds the generic guard; Sonnet 5.5 belongs in its `_NO_FORCED_TOOL_CHOICE_CLAUDE_SUBSTRINGS`, but not in the mandatory-thinking set, since it accepts `between_tools`. I've commented there.
- Bedrock pricing is not added: AWS has not published a Sonnet 5.5 SKU rate that I could verify, so cost shows unknown there instead of a guessed number.
- OpenRouter's chat-completions path sends `reasoning: {enabled: false}` for reasoning-off. Whether OpenRouter maps that to Anthropic's `disabled` (which would 400) is unverified; there's no OpenRouter key here. Portal on chat-completions was verified: reasoning off returns 200.
- #121016 (Opus 5.5 → mandatory set) touches the adjacent tuple in `anthropic_adapter.py`. It composes with this PR (Opus 5.5 has no `between_tools`), and whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase.
