raw.body:
## Root cause

On Linux (Mesa/Wayland, several AMD iGPU generations), the bundled Chromium 144 GPU child can fail initialization with `error_code=1002` in three distinct ways, and `main` has no Linux recovery for any of them — the only `child-process-gone` ladder is Windows-gated:

1. A FATAL `GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.` SIGTRAP abort — a 100% crash loop on the affected hosts (#86073, #121954).
2. A silent sub-zygote init-retry loop: ~350–650% CPU, no `--type=gpu-process` child ever exists, no crash fires, and it survives restart, update and cache clears (#124843).
3. `HERMES_DESKTOP_DISABLE_GPU=1` only disables compositing — it never spawn-blocks the GPU process, so one still spawns and dies with 1002 on AMD/Mesa (#97616).

## What changes

- Keeps @Finn763's software ladder from #124898 (per-version marker, one-shot `--disable-gpu` relaunch, reveal/quit marker hygiene) and @dskwe's Linux extension of the #38216 `--no-sandbox` two-strike ladder from #126771, with authorship preserved.
- Coalesces the two `child-process-gone` handlers into one bounded decision (`linuxGpuChildDeathPath`): the sandbox signature (SIGTERM/exit 143) is tried first — on that host `--disable-gpu` still crashes, so software fallback would waste the one shot — and the software ladder takes the relapse after a `--no-sandbox` boot died again. One death produces exactly one relaunch; Windows keeps its existing fast path unchanged.
- Adds the #124843 silent-retry catch: `LINUX_GPU_SILENT_RETRY_GRACE_S` after the main window reveals, a boot with no GPU child in `app.getAppMetrics()` engages the same sticky software fallback for the next launch — the event-driven ladder can never see this manifestation because no `child-process-gone` fires.
- `HERMES_DESKTOP_DISABLE_GPU` now also appends `--disable-gpu` so the GPU child is fully spawn-blocked; remote-display detections keep their long-standing compositing-only behavior.

Fixes #86073
Fixes #124843
Refs #97616 — the `--disable-gpu` spawn-block is in; the intermittent launcher-vs-direct-binary race is not root-caused here and still needs a strace from a failing `hermes desktop` launch on Linux.
Refs #121954 — the recovery ladder bounds the FATAL crash loop; the systemd transient-scope hypothesis from that thread remains untested (the A/B the reporter could not run).

## Tests

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run electron/linux-gpu-fallback.test.ts electron/windows-sandbox-fallback.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` — 43/43 pass on this branch. Red proof: on the pre-coalescing cherry-picked tree (both source PRs applied as-is) 8 of the new tests fail, and on `origin/main` the module does not exist at all.
- `cd apps/desktop && npx tsc -p . --noEmit` — clean.

## Not exercised live

Authored and unit-tested on macOS. The decision functions are pure and platform-parameterized; the Electron integration (`child-process-gone`, `app.getAppMetrics`, `app.relaunch`, marker writes) is typechecked only here. Before merge this needs one real launch on an affected Linux host — ideally the #124843 silent-retry host (watch the fallback engage after the grace window) and one #86073/#121954 sandbox-signature host (watch the single `--no-sandbox` relaunch, then the software relapse) — with `~/.hermes/logs/desktop.log` attached to the issue threads. The durable fix for the underlying Chromium 144 failures remains the Electron bump tracked in #124032.

Supersedes #124898 (thanks @Finn763 — the marker/relaunch machinery is kept verbatim)
Supersedes #126771 (thanks @dskwe — the Linux sandbox-ladder gates are kept verbatim)

Co-authored-by: Finn763 <165816600+finn763@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Yuan Li <dskwelmcy@163.com>

raw.body:
## Root cause

`stopVoicePlayback()` reached only the newest playback through a single module-level
`currentStop` slot (`apps/desktop/src/lib/voice-playback.ts:23` at base, 7 writer sites).
When two playbacks overlap — `startSpeechStream` resolves its gateway URL/TTS config
asynchronously and only then calls `stopVoicePlayback()`, so a barge-in plus a next-turn
open can cross that gap — the overwritten session is never stopped: its WebSocket stays
open, its AudioContext keeps scheduling buffers, its `done` never settles (leaking the
150 ms feed timer in `use-voice-conversation` that clears after `await session.done`),
and its queued audio resurfaces audibly turns later (#91991).

## Fix

- Every live playback registers an idempotent stop in a `liveStops` set: client-direct
  sessions, streaming sessions (WebSocket close + AudioContext close), and data-URL
  audio elements. Each stop unregisters itself on settle, so the set self-cleans.
- `stopVoicePlayback()` drains the whole set, not just the newest slot, then clears it.
- Stale-start guard: if the voice-playback sequence advanced during `startSpeechStream`'s
  async discovery, it returns `null` instead of resurrecting stopped playback.
- Sequence-scoped settle: a session's completion only writes the idle state when no newer
  playback started since, so a settled session cannot stomp a newer turn's state.

## Coverage

- Fixes #91991 — interrupted/overlapping speech sessions are fully torn down on barge-in.

## Checks run

- `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/lib/voice-playback.test.ts` — 6/6 pass
  (2 of these fail on base: the stale-start and sequence-scoped-settle tests).
- `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-voice-conversation-boundary.test.tsx src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-voice-conversation.test.tsx` — 12/12 pass.
- Red-on-base proven by checking out base `voice-playback.ts` alongside the new tests:
  2 failed / 4 passed; branch passes 6/6.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/92334 — same three-part design
  (liveStops registry, stale-start guard, sequence-scoped completion), re-authored onto
  current main's voice-playback.ts (the PR's head predates the sentence-queue fallback,
  edge-TTS interim flushes and id-rewrite work, so hunks were re-authored rather than
  cherry-picked) and extended to all seven `currentStop` writer sites. Thanks @Finn763.

Fixes #91991

raw.body:
After the onboarding tour, the composer status stack no longer shows a stray preview row for the app's own page.

Linear: NS-1029 (B4)

## Problem

After the tour turn, a globe row "127.0.0.1:5174" appeared above the composer. In a packaged build the row reads "index.html". The row is the app's own page, not something the agent made.

Root cause: `apps/desktop/src/lib/tour/engine.ts::runTourEngine` returns the app's own `location.href` as `url` for the `gui_tour` action `targets`. `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/tool/fallback-model/index.ts::toolPreviewTarget` treats a top-level `url` in a result as a deliverable preview. Two paths record it:

- The live `tool.complete` handler (`app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event/tools.ts`). Its frames name the real tool, `gui_tour`.
- The tool row, when it mounts (`components/assistant-ui/tool/fallback.tsx`). A bridged `tool_call` reaches this path under another name. A labelled call renders through `components/assistant-ui/connector-tool.tsx::ConnectorExecution`, one row per inner call, and that row's `toolName` is the label title ("Gui Tour"). An unlabelled part keeps `toolName: 'tool_call'` with the real tool in `args.name` or in a one-entry `args.calls`.

So a guard on the tool name never saw `gui_tour` on the row path. I observed this in the live renderer: the preview atom write came from the `fallback.tsx` effect.

## What changes

- `toolPreviewTarget` returns no target for tools that only look at a page: `gui_tour`, `drive_preview`, `annotate_preview`, and `desktop_preview` unless its action is `open`. The file-read tools stay in the same set.
- `ConnectorExecution` passes each row's real tool name as `innerToolName`. For a `tool_call` entry this is the label's name. For any other tool it is the part's own tool. `buildToolView` uses this name for the preview check only. The row title does not change.
- `toolPreviewTarget` unwraps a one-call `tool_call` (legacy `name` form or a one-entry `calls`) to the inner tool and its arguments.

## Proof (observed at 075a544529)

I ran the dev app from this branch in an isolated home with a scripted model. The flow starts a background `python3 -m http.server`, then runs the tour turn twice. I hooked the preview atom to catch any write that holds `5174`.

- With every tool call id set to `call_0`: after the tour turn, the status stack held only the metrics row. The preview atom stayed `{}` and caught no write.
- The same held after a renderer reload, and after I expanded the tool groups so the "Gui Tour" rows mounted.
- Control with unique tool call ids: same result.
- `desktop_preview` with action `open` still gives its url as a preview target.

Before: origin/main, same flow with every id set to `call_0`. After: this branch, same flow.

| Before (Desktop) | After (Desktop) |
|:---:|:---:|
| ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8a43ed4d-727b-4da9-895b-151f65b83cee) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01124f9e-c76e-4b5e-ac2b-769975e5151b) |

raw.body:
## Root cause

`drive_preview type` clears the target field with a select-all chord before typing. `selectAll()` in `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/right-rail/preview-drive.ts` hardcoded `['control', 'meta']` — both modifiers held simultaneously. No OS treats Ctrl+Cmd+A (macOS) or Ctrl+Win+A (Windows/Linux) as select-all, so native select-all never fired, the pre-type clear silently no-op'd, and typed text appended to the existing value (a 9.99 price field became 19999.99) while the tool still reported success. Compounded by controlled React inputs that re-render on focus (money/date/number masks) and throw the selection away even when the chord is correct.

## Fix

Cherry-picked from #103785 (thanks @YTminiboss) and rebased onto current main, plus the exact-modifier test assertions from #98325 (thanks @guillaumehussong):

- `selectAll()` sends one platform-correct modifier: `['meta']` on macOS, `['control']` elsewhere (same `isMacPlatform()` helper shape as #98325).
- After the focus click, settle so a re-render commits, then select-all and **verify** via `document.activeElement` that the field actually emptied.
- If select-all silently failed, clear deterministically with End + N Backspaces instead of typing over stale content.
- If real keystrokes cannot empty a masked field at all, fall back to setting the value through the input's native prototype setter with input/change events.
- Fail closed: never type into a field that could not be emptied, so the driver can never silently corrupt a value.
- Thread `typeText`'s character count out through the type path so an interrupted type reports how many characters landed instead of claiming none did.

## Coverage

- #98324 — platform-correct chord + verify-and-fallback layers (fixes).
- #98325 — its narrower per-platform modifier assertions folded into the suite (superseded).

Fixes #98324

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/103785 — the complete fix this PR carries forward (thanks @YTminiboss)
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/98325 — its platform-native chord and test assertions folded in (thanks @guillaumehussong)

## Checks run

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/app/chat/right-rail/preview-act.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` — 26/26 pass
- Red on base proven: with `origin/main`'s `preview-act.ts`/`preview-drive.ts` checked out, the new "Command+A on macOS and Control+A elsewhere" test fails (`expected { keyCode: 'a', … } to match object { modifiers: ['meta'] }` — main sends `['control','meta']`)
- `cd apps/desktop && npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` — clean

## Add `healthrelay` to the plugin catalog

Submitted by the repository owner (rule 5).

**What it is:** a portable Agent Plugins v1 package: one stdio MCP server (a 20-line shell launcher around the read-only `health-bridge mcp start`; nine read-only tools, no raw SQL, no write tools) and three skills (setup, review, troubleshoot). It gives an agent read-only access to the user's own Apple Health data through a self-hosted HealthRelay receiver. The plugin ships neither the receiver nor the iPhone app.

- Repo: https://github.com/mwdearing/hermes-healthrelay, pinned to `fa8c31d67c01e28223b047191b26866faafb4a43` (0.2.2)
- License: Apache-2.0
- No credentials or database paths in the package; the path comes from `HEALTHRELAY_DB` or `~/.config/healthrelay/db-path`.
- No self-updating code, no Python dependencies, no hooks, no tools registered beyond the MCP server (capabilities block is empty and matches).

**Checks run at the pinned SHA**
- `hermes plugins validate` passes (portable manifest, manifest fields, security scan: safe).
- MCP handshake against the launcher lists the nine tools the skills reference.
- `hermes plugins install mwdearing/hermes-healthrelay --no-enable` from GitHub works.

**Disclosure (also in the entry description):** it exposes sensitive health data to whichever model the user runs, so it is meant for a local or trusted model. Enabling it grants full trust to the skills and launcher, as with any Agent Plugins v1 package.

## Root cause

Two layers in `apps/desktop/src/plugins/radio/plugin.js`:

1. The external `pause` event listener called `stop()` unconditionally —
   clearing `src`, calling `load()`, removing the element, advancing the
   generation — so any external media controller (macOS media keys, Fluid
   Voice pausing audio to hear the microphone) destroyed the stream it might
   resume.
2. But preserving the stream is not enough: the reporter's own identical
   experiment still failed the real Fluid Voice reproduction. Fluid Voice
   delivers the transcript into the focused editable field via macOS
   Accessibility APIs — a guarded paste (⌘V) in Chromium/Electron — and emits
   **no media-session resume signal** afterwards. Radio could stay
   non-destructively paused forever with nothing to tell it dictation ended.

## Fix

- External `pause` is now non-destructive: `status.set('paused')`, the
  element and its `src` survive (`stop()` → `status.set('paused')` in the
  external listener, credit to #108115 for the one-liner and survival test).
- The player tracks `playGeneration` — the generation that last reached
  `playing` — so it knows whether the paused element is the live stream.
- `resume()` resumes that intact element with a plain `element.play()`;
  it returns false when the stream is not intact (fresh start, the plugin's
  own destructive Pause, a stop from another window).
- On dictation completion — a `paste` event targeting a text field or
  contenteditable (the composer) — the plugin resumes the preserved stream.
  Never on window focus: that would override an intentional pause.
- The plugin's own Pause stays destructive by design: `toggle()` from `live`
  runs `stop()`, so a paste never resurrects a stream the user paused, and
  Play afterwards is a full reconnect.

## Coverage per requirement (#108113)

- External pause preserves the stream: survival test (status `paused`,
  same element, same `src`, later `playing` → `live`).
- Auto-resume after dictation: paste into a textarea while externally
  paused → same element resumes, status `live`, no teardown/reconnect.
- Plugin Pause stays destructive: after `toggle()` from `live` the element
  is gone, a paste does not resume, and Play creates a fresh element.
- Real-macOS Fluid Voice verification remains platform acceptance evidence
  the reporter can now run: dictate with the Option key, confirm insertion,
  radio resumes. The unit tests cover the renderer-visible contract.

## Checks run

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/contrib/radio-plugin.test.ts` — 5 passed
- Red on base: same suite with `origin/main`'s plugin.js — 2 failed (survival + dictation-resume), 3 passed
- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/contrib/radio-plugin.test.ts src/contrib/radio-artist-links.test.ts` — full radio suite green

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/108115

Thanks @kokhlo — the non-destructive external pause and the stream-survival
test are taken verbatim from #108115.

Fixes #108113

## Root cause

Vercel's WAF denies some residential IP ranges (e.g. Spamhaus-listed ones) for
the entire `hermes-agent.nousresearch.com` domain. The Bot Mode Skills Hub
picker (`apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/skills-hub.tsx`) hardcodes that
origin for its iframe with no fallback, so users on a flagged range get a
permanent 403 block page instead of the picker. Nothing in the repo or docs
mentioned the mirror or the workaround.

## Fix

- Re-land the surviving half of closed #118206 (its Capabilities-picker target
  was deleted by the native catalog): before each browse session the plugin
  HEAD-probes the primary picker URL and falls back to the equivalent GitHub
  Pages deployment (`https://nousresearch.github.io/hermes-agent/docs/skills?embed=picker`)
  when the probe is refused, fails, or hangs.
- The probe carries an `AbortSignal.timeout(8s)` deadline (the open review note
  on #118206) so a hanging connection cannot delay the fallback.
- Picker installs are accepted from either trusted origin, still gated on our
  own frame's `contentWindow` (the source check from #86243 stays).
- New FAQ troubleshooting entry: what the 403 is, that the picker self-heals
  via Pages, and to report affected ranges to the maintainers.

The Vercel-side action (WAF mitigation rules for the reporter's range) is a
deployment task outside this repo and still needs a maintainer answer on the
issue.

## Checks run (real commands + results)

- Red on base: with `skills-hub.tsx` reverted to origin/main, the four new
  tests fail (no fallback on refused/failed/hung probe; fallback-origin install
  rejected).

`main` fails the JS & TS checks on every desktop PR. This PR fixes the four failing tests in `clarify-hydration.test.tsx`. It changes no product code.

## The problem

Since #127760, a clarify request has one shape: `questions: [{question, choices?, multi_select?}]`. The desktop clarify handler (`server-requests.ts`) reads only `questions`.

Three later commits (`cc931d239c`, `adb1cbde32`, `73688014f7`) added tests that send the old shape: a top-level `choices` and `question`. The handler gets an empty list and returns at once. So it stores no card, `requestId` is `undefined`, and the hydrated part keeps `args: {}`. These four tests fail:

- hydrates an already-pending sparse clarify row from the live request
- keeps a live clarify card through a spurious message.complete
- keeps a live clarify card through a spurious error
- keeps a live clarify card through a stale session.info running=false snapshot (#83319)

The product code in those commits already works with the new shape. `restorePendingClarifyToolCall` gets its args from `pendingClarifyToolPayload`, which sends `questions`.

## What changes

- The four `clarifyRequest(...)` calls send `questions: [{ choices, qid: 'q0', question }]`.
- The re-arm test expects `args: { questions: [...] }`.
- Prettier reflowed one `act(...)` line in the same file.

## How to test

```bash
cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/clarify-hydration.test.tsx
```

The tests were not run on the author's machine. CI runs them.

raw.body:
## Root cause

Four failed sessions ([#125830](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/125830)): the agent does not know it owns a screen. When the user says "open chrome in screen 20", the model has never been told what "screen 20" is — nothing in the system prompt, tool descriptions, or session context names the Bot Screen, its display number, or the lease state — so it falls back to launching Chrome on the user's own display through the terminal. And even when a session happens to know, terminal children inherit the **seat** environment: `_make_run_env` never merges the bot desktop's published `DISPLAY`/`XAUTHORITY`/`DBUS`, so GUI apps open on the user's display anyway.

## What changes

**Terminal env half** (from #125835, kept): while this profile's Bot Desktop is running, `_make_run_env` merges `published_env()` — the pure read, no activity stamp (a plain `ls` must not keep the screen alive past `idle_stop_minutes`) — so `DISPLAY`/`XAUTHORITY`/`DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` route children to the bot screen, and `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is dropped (an X11 desktop; a leaked Wayland socket flips GTK/Chromium backends). A user who wants their own seat still can: an inline `DISPLAY=:0 cmd` prefix wins, since bash applies it after this env.

**Model-context half** (new):
- `agent/prompt_builder.py`: the environment-hints block gains one line — "Bot Screen: … RUNNING on display :N (you hold it / a human holds it…)" — naming the screen, the display, and the lease state, exactly the facts "screen N" / ":N" / "your screen" need to resolve. Local backends only: a sandboxed terminal cannot open windows on the gateway host. Pure reads, never raises, drops out entirely when no screen runs.
- `tui_gateway/methods_display_watch.py`: the runtime-file watcher (which already detects a screen start/stop from any process) now also stages the same sentence as a one-shot per-turn note on every live session of that profile — the system prompt is byte-stable and only rebuilt at compaction, so a screen started mid-session would otherwise stay unknown for the rest of the conversation. The note rides the existing `_gateway_turn_context_notes` channel behind the cached prefix, and another profile's sessions are never told.

## Acceptance coverage

- "screen N" / ":N" / "your screen" resolves to the bot screen — the hint line names it and its display directly. **Covered** (prompt line; the routing itself is behavioural and needs the reporter's babysit-style check below).
- GUI apps the agent launches from terminal open on the bot screen — **covered** by the env merge + `test_local_env_bot_desktop.py` (kept from #125835).
- Display introspection targets the bot display — **covered by the same env merge** (`xrandr`/`xdotool`/`wmctrl` read `DISPLAY` from the child env).
- Screen existence/display/lease reach the model — **covered**: prompt hints (rebuilt at compaction) + per-turn notes (immediately on start/stop).

## Tests

All on the Linux-and-macOS-runnable surface (pure functions + file-driven watcher; no X server needed):

- `tests/agent/test_prompt_builder.py` — running screen names display + holder (**red on main**, green with fix); human-held wording (**red on main**); stopped screen leaves no hint; remote backend never sees a host screen.
- `tests/tui_gateway/test_display_watch.py::test_screen_start_and_stop_reach_the_models_turn_notes` — a start/stop made by another process stages the note on that profile's live agent and not on another profile's (**red on main**, green with fix).
- `tests/tools/test_local_env_bot_desktop.py` (from #125835, kept): env merge, snapshot precedence, stopped-screen passthrough, no activity stamp. Green.

One pre-existing timing-sensitive failure, `TestContextFileReadTimeout::test_slow_hermes_md_is_skipped_and_agents_md_still_loads`, fails identically on `origin/main` on this loaded machine — unrelated to this change.

## Not exercised live

The end-to-end "model actually resolves screen 20" behaviour and the lease-note delivery in a real `hermes serve` session need a Linux gateway with a running Bot Desktop; the pure wiring is what this PR unit-proves.

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/125830
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/125835 (keeps its env-merge commit and tests, adds the missing model-context half). Thanks @liuhao1024.

raw.body:
## What

Adds GPT-6.1 Sol (`gpt-6.1-sol`, plus `-pro`), which OpenAI released on 2026-09-29, and fixes the one request shape that breaks on it: turning reasoning off.

**WHO / WHEN / WHY:** OpenAI announced GPT-6.1 Sol on 2026-09-29 ([announcement](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-1-sol/), [model page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.1-sol)). No open PR or issue covered it when this was opened. It follows the shape of #126842 (Sonnet 5.5), but 6.1 Sol needs more surfaces: none of the existing `gpt-6-sol` keys match it, because `gpt-6-sol` is not a substring of `gpt-6.1-sol`.

Where it's available, probed live on 2026-09-29:

| Route | Status |
|---|---|
| OpenRouter `/api/v1/models` | `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` and `openai/gpt-6.1-sol-pro`, 1.05M context |
| Direct OpenAI API | model page says `gpt-6.1-sol`, 1.05M context / 128K output |
| Nous Portal `/v1/models` | `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` and `-pro` (missing at the first probe; listed a few hours later) |
| Codex OAuth (our account) | missing from the live catalog; a direct request returns 400 "not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account" |

## Changes

| Surface | Change |
|---|---|
| `hermes_cli/models_catalog_static.py` | `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` and `-pro` added to `OPENROUTER_MODELS`. The `nous` list derives from it; the Portal now serves both. `gpt-6.1-sol` and `-pro` added to the `openai-api` picker. |
| `website/static/api/model-catalog.json` | Regenerated with `scripts/build_model_catalog.py` |
| `agent/model_metadata.py` | 1,050,000 in `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_LENGTHS`; 272K in `_CODEX_OAUTH_CONTEXT_FALLBACK`, so if Codex discovery surfaces it later, the context isn't over-promised at 1.05M. It is **not** added to the `-900k` opt-in because nothing has been verified above 272K. |
| `agent/auxiliary_client.py` | Added to the 272K compaction auto-raise family list. This only has an effect on the `openai-codex` route. |
| `agent/usage_pricing.py` | $2 / $10, cached input $0.10 (5% of input; 6 Sol is 10%), cache write $2.50. Above 272K: 2x input and cache, 1.5x output. `-pro` is aliased to the base row. |
| `agent/reasoning_effort.py` | `gpt-6.1-sol*` uses Astra's `low..max` effort ladder but not Astra's account gating, so it stays in the static catalogs. |
| `plugins/model-providers/openrouter/__init__.py` | Reasoning-off is omitted when the OpenAI ladder has no `none`. See below. |

`codex_models.py` is deliberately unchanged. The Codex backend rejects the slug for this account, and listing it would add a dead picker entry (#52492). Live discovery will pick it up once the account has access.

## Reasoning-off breaking change

GPT-6 Sol accepts `reasoning.effort: none`. GPT-6.1 Sol doesn't. Live via OpenRouter on 2026-09-29, both `reasoning: {enabled: false}` and `{effort: "none"}` return:

> 400 Unsupported value: 'none' is not supported with the 'gpt-6.1-sol-2026-09-29' model. Supported values are: 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'xhigh', and 'max'.

Before this PR:
- Direct API (Responses): `gpt-6.1-sol` fell through to the legacy ladder (`none..xhigh`). Reasoning-off sent `none` (400), and `max` was clamped down to `xhigh`.
- OpenRouter: the live catalog lists `none` as supported with `mandatory: false`, so the profile forwarded the disable (400). This affected `/reasoning none` on the main loop. Aux lanes already recover through `auxiliary_reasoning_floor`.

After this PR:
- Direct API: reasoning-off drops the field (with the existing once-per-model warning), and `max` passes through.
- OpenRouter: the disable is omitted whenever `codex_supported_efforts` for an `openai/` slug has no `none`. The OpenAI ladder overrides a wrong catalog entry. `gpt-6-sol` still sends its disable.

## Verification

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gpt6_tiers_registration.py`: 3 new relationship tests covering the effort ladder (Astra's, but not Astra-gated), the OpenRouter disable omission (6.1 omits, 6 keeps), and context/pricing parity with the tier (`-pro` is the base row; cached rate = input/20; not `-900k`-eligible). Mutation check: reverting the OpenRouter guard fails exactly 1 test, and reverting the ladder prefix fails 2.
- Targeted suite (57 files: codex models, catalog, pricing, metadata, reasoning effort, provider profiles, model-provider plugins, codex transports, model switch, aux reasoning floor): 1023 passed, 10 failed. All 10 fail identically on `upstream/main` (home-IO guard, local env). Ruff is clean.
- Real-import E2E from the worktree: `openai-api` picker leads with `gpt-6.1-sol`; context is 1.05M on `openai` and 272K on `openai-codex`; pricing resolves from `openai-api`; `_resolve_reasoning` gives `(None, False)` for off, `low` for minimal, `max` for max/ultra.
- Live, OpenRouter: the patched profile's reasoning-off kwargs (`extra_body: {}`) no longer return the 400. The request gets past parameter validation and hits a 403 account-policy block on our OpenRouter key, the same block every `openai/*` request returns on that key.
- **Live, Nous Portal, real `AIAgent`** with `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` + terminal tool: ran `echo HELLO-61` and replied `HELLO-61` / `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` (2 API calls, cost $0.0101). Passes with reasoning off too.
- **Not live-tested:** direct OpenAI API (no key here) and OpenRouter (our key is policy-blocked by OpenAI; the `none` 400 above came back before that block).

## Notes / follow-ups

- `/model gpt` version-sorts, so on a route that has both it now resolves to `gpt-6.1-sol` ahead of `gpt-6-astra`. That's the existing "newer version wins" rule. Astra is account-gated and absent from static lists, so on most routes this only replaces `gpt-6-sol`.
- Ultrafast for 6.1 Sol is announced but has no published rate yet. The `/fast ultrafast` tier lands in #128307; 6.1 Sol joins its model set once OpenAI publishes the rate.
- Codex OAuth: once the account catalog lists it, probe the real ceiling before adding it to the `-900k` opt-in.

## What does this PR do?

Adds `plugin-catalog/wiki-ref.yaml`, a community entry for **wiki-ref**: `@wiki:<title>` context references. Writing `@wiki:Alan_Turing` (or `@wiki:"Washington, D.C."`) in a message attaches the lead section of that Wikipedia article to the turn, `@wiki:Berlin#History` attaches one section of it, and typing `@wiki:` in the TUI or Desktop composer suggests article titles through `complete.path`.

It is built only on the plugin context-reference API (`ctx.register_context_reference`, #26193, shipped in #84937), which no catalog entry uses yet. Submitted by the owner (rule 5): I maintain `EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs`.

- Repo: https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs, subdir `wiki-ref`, release tag [`wiki-ref-v1.1.0`](https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/releases/tag/wiki-ref-v1.1.0) (rule 3)
- Pinned SHA: `0154f6bfaafc837cc4af78742e6db7c087d5b5a7` (1.1.0). First pinned at `e0395d4` (1.0.0), re-pinned to `4a5a257` to add the card, to `3cc4835` for 1.0.1 and to `0154f6b` for 1.1.0 (see Updates). The plugin's CI is green on all four: [e0395d4](https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/actions/runs/36607278067), [4a5a257](https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/actions/runs/36610548819), [3cc4835](https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/actions/runs/36637557550), [0154f6b](https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/actions/runs/36766709247)
- Category `web`: it pulls web content into the turn and registers no tools.

**Footprint** (also in the entry's `Disclosure —` sentence and the README's "Security and footprint" section):
- `register()` only calls `ctx.register_context_reference(...)`: no tools, hooks, middleware or commands.
- Network: HTTPS GET to `https://<language>.wikipedia.org/w/api.php` only. Redirects are followed only on the same HTTPS host; responses over 2 MiB are refused. The referenced title and the typed autocomplete prefix leave the machine, with a descriptive User-Agent as Wikimedia's API etiquette asks. A `#Section` reference is still one request to the same host: the article's plain text comes back and the section is cut locally, so the section name does not leave the machine.
- No API key, no dependencies, no files written, no subprocess, no self-update code. The only environment variables involved are the standard proxy ones `urllib` honours.
- Each reference is time-bounded (`timeout_seconds`, default 10; autocomplete 3 s). Requests run on a plugin-owned thread pool with an overall deadline: `preprocess_context_references` runs `asyncio.run()`, whose shutdown joins the loop's default executor, so a request parked there would hold the turn past the timeout. A test covers this through the sync wrapper.
- Settings (`language`, `max_chars`, `timeout_seconds`) come from `config_schema` and are read per reference. An unusable value becomes a context warning on that reference rather than a silent fallback.

## Related Issue

Uses the extension point from #26193 (shipped in #84937). Not a fix.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality): new catalog entry

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/wiki-ref.yaml` (new). All `capabilities` lists are empty, matching what the plugin registers at the pinned SHA.

## How to Test

1. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` → `OK: 350 file(s) valid`
2. Clone the repo at the pinned SHA → `hermes plugins validate --install-deps wiki-ref`: every check passes, security scan `safe`; the self-updater grep finds nothing.
3. `hermes plugins install wiki-ref --enable` with this branch's catalog → installed from `catalog:community`, pinned `1.1.0 @ 0154f6bf`, with only `plugin.yaml`, `__init__.py` and `README.md` in the plugin directory; `hermes plugins search wiki-ref` lists it under `web`.
4. `hermes chat -q "Who was @wiki:Alan_Turing?" --oneshot` → the user message sent to the model carries `--- Attached Context ---` with the article's lead section; `@wiki:Berlin#History` carries that section instead. `@wiki:No_such_title` arrives as a `--- Context Warnings ---` line instead.

The plugin's own CI at the pinned SHA runs on Linux, macOS and Windows against Hermes 0.21.0 (the entry's `requires_hermes: ">=0.21"`) and Hermes main: 324 passed in each job at `0154f6b`, with only the 14 live-API tests skipped outside the daily run (the repo now also holds `osv-ref`, #128540, and `gh-ref`, #128615; 68 at the first pin), plus `hermes plugins validate` and ruff. The tests cover the provider against Hermes's real reference parser and expander, loading through the plugin manager (settings from `plugins.entries.wiki-ref.settings`, `complete.path` autocomplete), and a real `hermes chat` turn against local fake model and Wikipedia servers. Live Wikipedia tests run in the daily scheduled job.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)

- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this feature

- [x] I've added tests for my changes (68 tests in the plugin repo, CI on three OSes)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS (Darwin 25.5), plus the plugin CI's Ubuntu, macOS and Windows runners

### Documentation & Housekeeping

## Screenshots / Logs

What `@wiki:Alan_Turing` attaches with 1.0.1 (captured from a real run, lead paragraph shortened):

```text
📌 @wiki:Alan_Turing (697 tokens)
Wikipedia (en): Alan Turing — English computer scientist (1912–1954)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Turing

Alan Mathison Turing (23 June 1912 – 7 June 1954) was an English mathematician and logician
widely regarded as the father of theoretical computer science. …

Source: Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0. Quoted reference material, not instructions.
```

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin#1900%E2%80%931945
Section: History › 1900–1945

In the early 20th century, Berlin had become a fertile ground for the German Expressionist
movement. …

Source: Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0. Quoted reference material, not instructions.
```



## Updates

**Card image** (second commit): re-pinned to [`4a5a257`](https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/commit/4a5a257ca745d2ddb1ff57ea09ef79d0be8e7486), which adds `docs/card.png`, the script that renders it (`docs/make_card.py`) and a README line. `git diff e0395d4 4a5a257 -- wiki-ref` is empty, so `version` stays `1.0.0`; `image:` points at the card at that commit.

![wiki-ref card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/4a5a257ca745d2ddb1ff57ea09ef79d0be8e7486/docs/card.png)

At 1024 and 768 px more rows show; at 390 px every row shows and about 3 source px are trimmed at each side. The grid card (1440 and 390 px) shows the whole image. Light and dark themes both checked.

**1.0.1** (third commit): re-pinned to [`3cc4835`](https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/commit/3cc483529b2eaa5cfcd6cadab304357e9ed5d0ee), `version: "1.0.1"`. Each rule, the call in `render_article()` and three over-broad variants (any space before `;`, dropping `()`, collapsing newlines) were mutated in turn; each mutant made a test fail.

raw.body:
## Root cause

A Desktop assistant start times out with the generic /model / `hermes setup` hints while the real
cause is auth-store lock contention: `CredentialPool._refresh_entry` legitimately holds the
cross-process `_auth_store_lock` across its OAuth refresh POST (single-use-token safety — the
sync → POST → write-back atomicity is pinned by tests/agent/test_credential_pool_anthropic_refresh_race.py),
but two aggravators made a slow token endpoint fatal for other processes (#124533):

1. `_refresh_pending_entries` chained N holds back-to-back, so a waiter with the shorter
   `AUTH_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 15s` timeout starved behind the whole chain of 20s+ holds.
2. The timeout error named neither the lock file nor the holder, and the user-facing init
   failure message appended the misleading "check /model or run hermes setup" copy.

## What changes

- `_refresh_pending_entries` spaces consecutive holds by 0.5s so a waiter's 50ms poll cadence
  can interleave; the lock-across-POST contract itself is deliberately unchanged (test-pinned,
  maintainer decision per the issue's investigating comment).
- `_file_lock` stamps the holder pid into the lock file on acquire and clears it on release;
  a timing-out waiter names the lock file and, when the pid is live, the probable holder
  (stale pids from dead processes are probed and stay silent). Permanent lock failures
  (flock-unsupported filesystem, ENOSYS) propagate immediately instead of burning the deadline.
- `agent_init_failed_message` recognizes auth-lock timeout prefixes and gives the
  contention-appropriate copy (wait / exit the other process) instead of the credential hints.

Thanks @liuhao1024 — the first commit is his #124933 rebased onto current main (his authorship
kept); this PR supersedes that PR by adding the sweep-spacing half.

## Acceptance coverage

#124533:
- Requirement 3 (timeout names lock file + likely holder, no misleading hints): covered by the
  cherry-picked commit (tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_lock_timeout_diagnosis.py,
  tests/tui_gateway/test_user_messages.py).
- Requirement 2-adjacent mitigation (bound aggregate holds via spacing): covered by the new
  tests/agent/test_credential_pool_refresh_sweep_spacing.py — a waiter window ≥ 0.4s must
  exist between consecutive holds of a 3-entry sweep.
- Requirements 1 and 4 (move the POST outside the lock; capture the dashboard holder path):
  **not** done — moving the POST outside the lock is a deliberate single-use-token tradeoff the
  existing race test pins; that redesign stays a maintainer decision. The spacing mitigation is
  the safe part of the verdict's plan.

## Tests run (real results)

- `bash scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/agent/test_credential_pool_refresh_sweep_spacing.py` on
  plain origin/main: **1 failed** (back-to-back holds starve the waiter); with the fix: **1 passed**.
- `bash scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2` over tests/agent/test_credential_pool_refresh_sweep_spacing.py,
  tests/agent/test_credential_pool_anthropic_refresh_race.py,
  tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_lock_timeout_diagnosis.py, tests/tui_gateway/test_user_messages.py
  on this branch: **4 files, 13 tests passed, 0 failed** — the pinned lock-across-POST contract
  is untouched and still green.

Refs #124533

Co-authored-by: liuhao1024 <sunsky.lau@gmail.com>

## Root cause

`planReload` / `planRestore` / `planEdit` in `usePromptActions`
(apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/index.ts:968, 1028, 1091) read their transcript
from `$messages.get()` — the global draft mirror. Active sessions publish their transcript into
`$sessionStates[runtimeId].messages`, so for any session with a runtime ID the mirror is empty (or
stale): `findIndex` returns `-1`, the plan comes back null, and refresh / restore / edit silently do
nothing.

## What changed

All three planners now read
`(sessionId ? $sessionStates.get()[sessionId]?.messages : null) ?? $messages.get()` — the runtime
slice when the session has one, the global mirror as fallback for draft (no-runtime) sessions. No
visual change; the same plan is derived from the store that actually holds the transcript.

## Acceptance coverage

Four new tests in `index.test.tsx` pin the primary path for all three actions: messages that exist
only in the runtime slice regenerate / restore / edit correctly with an empty global mirror, and the
runtime slice wins over a divergent mirror entry carrying the same id with different text.
Red-first verified on `origin/main`: all 4 fail without the fix; 141/141 pass with it.

## Tests

- `npx vitest run src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/index.test.tsx --maxWorkers=2` → 141 passed (base: 4 new tests red)
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` → clean
- `npx eslint` on both files → no new findings

## Root cause

`reconcileTileTranscripts` (apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/hooks/use-background-sync.ts:283) ran
`getLatestSessionMessages(storedSessionId, …, { passive: true })` — a 120-row transcript fetch —
BEFORE checking `sessionMessagesSignature(latest.messages)` at :322. The signature only gated the
paint, so every `sessions.changed` tick paid the full fetch per tile even when nothing moved.

## What changed

Before the fetch, the tile's sidebar row (in `$sessions` / `$messagingSessions`) is fingerprinted
with the new `sessionListFingerprint` (message_count / last_active / preview,
apps/desktop/src/lib/session-signatures.ts:55). On a fingerprint match the fetch is skipped
entirely; the fingerprint is (re)armed whenever the fetched transcript proves in sync or lands, so the
gate tracks the row that produced the last transcript. Tiles with no row (hidden bot chats) keep
fetching every tick, and closed tiles prune their fingerprint alongside their signature. Pure
perf: no visual change.

## Acceptance coverage

Two new tests in `use-background-sync.test.ts`:
- unchanged row fingerprint → `getLatestSessionMessages` is NOT called at all (the old
  "skips the tile fetch entirely" test never checked the fetch — only the paint);
- moved row (message_count/last_active/preview changed) → the gate breaks and the fetch + update run.

Red-first verified on `origin/main`: both fail without the gate; 48/48 pass with it.

#95798's edit-race half: a dirty edit followed by blur armed an 80ms cancel path; an Enter landing
inside that window could race a torn-down composer (edit silently dropped) or a wedged submit latch.
The edit-message path on current main carries the try/catch + error toast + rollback that closes the

raw.body:
## What it does

**hermes-anilist** tracks anime for Hermes Desktop. A status-bar chip names the next episode of your own
list with a countdown; its popover is the airing feed, sectioned by local day. A workspace tab holds the
season browser and a **My list** view, and each show gets a page: the next episode, a month calendar of
its air dates, an episode table, tracking controls, and a one-click alert. Alerts are cron jobs that
survive closing Hermes, and an optional daily digest carries what airs from your list. Two agent tools —
`anilist_list` and `anilist_show` — let the model read the list you actually track and answer about one
show, plus a bundled skill that teaches when to reach for them.

- Repo: https://github.com/BatataBF/hermes-anilist (MIT), pinned at
  `0081dfd7b45a469eef1ec35d3d0797318694c640` — the `v0.9.0` release commit plus a documentation-only
  commit on top of it. `git diff v0.9.0..<pin>` touches no file the plugin runs; the two commits differ
  only in `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and this entry's own local copy.
- One package: root `plugin.yaml` + `__init__.py` + `tools.py` (the two tools), `dashboard/plugin_api.py`
  (the only AniList client — routes, cache, rate budget, normalization) and `desktop/plugin.js`.
- `requires_hermes: >=0.21`; category `desktop`; 2 declared tools, 0 hooks, 0 middleware, no required env.
- The desktop half registers its chip, palette commands and panes only while its own backend answers on
  the **active connection**, so a device pointed at a host without the plugin shows nothing at all. It
  uses only the plugin SDK — no prototype patching, no `eval`/`new Function`, no script injection.

## Disclosures

- **No credential is required to install or to read.** The AniList token is optional, appears only after
  the user signs in from the pane, and lives in the profile's `.env`. The renderer never holds it: it
  only ever travels *to* the backend, and answers carry public data plus a `connected` flag.
- **One outbound host: AniList.** `graphql.anilist.co` only, through a single HTTP client and cache
  shared by the pane and the tools, inside AniList's ~30 req/min budget. No telemetry, no other endpoint.
- **No self-updater.** Updates arrive only through a new pin here plus `hermes plugins update hermes-anilist`.
- **No `tools.override`, no LLM access, no shell.** `hermes plugins validate` reports `safe`.

## Verification

Replayed this PR's own checks:

- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` → **`OK: 1 file(s) valid`**.
- Cloned the plugin and `checkout --detach` at the pin (what `pinned-source-validate` does):
  `hermes plugins validate` → **`Validation passed`** — `security scan — safe`,
  `desktop surface — stays inside the plugin SDK surface`, `declared tools — matches registrations`.
- Self-updater gate (`releases/latest|raw.githubusercontent.com` next to `writeTextFile|renamePath|writeFile(`)
  → **no hits**.
- `hermes plugins doctor --ci` → OK, 2 tools / 0 hooks.
- The plugin repo's CI runs the same validator on every push: **green** on this commit
  (`hermes plugins validate`, plus the backend suite — 104 tests — and the desktop half's checks).

## Screenshots

The status-bar chip and its popover, from the app itself:

![The chip and its popover: the airing feed sectioned by local day, a row's hover action, and the two doors out](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BatataBF/hermes-anilist/0081dfd7b45a469eef1ec35d3d0797318694c640/docs/screenshots/popover-upcoming.png)

The season browser, and a show page:

![The Catalog tab: a season and year with the search box above and starred rows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BatataBF/hermes-anilist/0081dfd7b45a469eef1ec35d3d0797318694c640/docs/screenshots/workspace-catalog.png)

![A show's page: the next episode card, the calendar of air dates and the episode list](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BatataBF/hermes-anilist/0081dfd7b45a469eef1ec35d3d0797318694c640/docs/screenshots/workspace-show-page.png)

raw.body:
## Root cause

Three stacked, individually deliberate denials crippled the Bot Mode Skills Hub
embed (`#91612`; the two other embeds named in the original report were since
deleted by the native catalog):

1. `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/skills-hub.tsx` — iframe sandbox
   omitted popups and had no `allow="clipboard-write"`, so external links and
   the Copy controls did nothing.
2. `apps/desktop/electron/window-open-policy.ts` — the CVE-2026-70608 handler
   denies every `window.open`/`target=_blank` with no trusted-origin delegation
   to the audited `openExternalUrl`.
3. `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` — `installMediaPermissions` refuses
   `clipboard-sanitized-write` for every origin.

Additionally no `will-frame-navigate` guard exists, so the hub frame can
self-navigate off the picker URL into the un-embeddable docs site (macOS data
point in the issue: `/docs/skills?embed=picker` → `/docs` →
`/docs/getting-started/installation`), after which its links are dead too.

## Fix

All carve-outs are gated on the EXACT hub origins (Vercel docs site + the
GitHub Pages mirror) via a new `hub-iframe-policy.ts` — an opaque sandboxed
frame (origin `'null'`, i.e. artifact previews) never qualifies.

- **iframe**: `allow="clipboard-write"` +
  `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox"`.
- **window-open policy**: `{action:'deny'}` stays unconditional (CVE-2026-70608
  posture preserved, comment block kept). New optional
  `TrustedWindowOpenOptions {getOpenerOrigin, openExternalUrl}`: a hub-origin
  opener plus an http/https/mailto URL delegates to the audited `openExternalUrl`
  as a side effect of the deny — a window is never created from this path, and
  non-hub openers trigger no side effect at all. Throwing probes/observers/
  openers cannot change the decision.
- **permissions**: `clipboard-sanitized-write` granted to hub origins only
  (request and check handlers); clipboard reads stay denied everywhere.
- **frame pinning (new vs both source PRs)**: `will-frame-navigate` in the main
  window denies a hub frame's escape off the picker URL and reloads it onto the
  picker; main-frame and non-hub-frame navigations are untouched.

## Security review note (please verify)

The maintainer should confirm (a) the `openExternalUrl` side effect is gated on
`getOpenerOrigin()` returning EXACTLY a hub origin and the URL scheme being
http/https/mailto (both asserted by tests), and (b) the deny envelope never
becomes allow (asserted for every test case, including throwing callbacks).

## Checks run (real commands + results)

- Red on base (policy): with `window-open-policy.ts` reverted to origin/main,
  `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism
  electron/window-open-policy.test.ts` fails 3/12 (the delegation cases — on
  base there is no trusted path at all).
- Red on base (component): with `skills-hub.tsx` reverted to origin/main, the
  picker suite fails the new sandbox/allow posture test 1/13.
- Green: `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism
  electron/window-open-policy.test.ts` — 12 passed.
- Green: `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism
  src/plugins/hermes-bots/skills-hub-picker.test.tsx` — 13 passed (fetch
  stubbed; no source-text reading anywhere).
- `npx tsc --noEmit --ignoreConfig --strict electron/hub-iframe-policy.ts
  electron/window-open-policy.ts` — clean.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/97945 — Thanks
  @sylvesterkaczmarek (the exact-origin/scheme predicate design and the
  permission-handler wiring are theirs; two of its three iframe call sites were
  deleted on base by the native catalog, and its source-regex test is replaced
  by component-behavior assertions).
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/116223 — Thanks @lepkov
  (its `allow="clipboard-write"` idea is folded in; its only target file was
  deleted on base).

Fixes #91612

raw.body:
## Summary

#99859: long-lived processes freeze `sys.modules` at boot. After `hermes update`, the code-skew watchdog (979c7baeef) retired stale backends — but only SSH-isolated ones — while Desktop-owned local `hermes serve` backends (which the updater equally never restarts) kept serving stale modules, and only the picker endpoint refused.

Two focused increments:

1. **Widen the self-heal (R1):** `start_code_skew_watchdog` is now also wired for Desktop-owned local backends (`is_desktop_owned_backend()`), not just `ssh_isolated` clients — both have the "updater never restarts me" property; the Desktop's ownership ledger drives the reconnect-respawn on new code.
2. **Centralize the skew refusal (R2):** `POST /api/model/set` and the tui_gateway `model.options` / `model.save_key` JSON-RPCs now refuse with the same "restart required" message `GET /api/model/options` and the gateway `/model` switch already return (new error code 5098, existing i18n key `gateway.model.err_skew`), so no model-mutating path can hand a stale-module string to a provider.

R3 (deleted-profile eviction) is partially covered on main by tombstones (7e34522454); R4 (Bots UI provisioning through `create_profile`) is deliberately out of scope here.

## Test plan

- [x] Green on this branch (rebased): `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_cli/test_code_skew.py tests/tui_gateway/test_model_rpc_skew_guard.py tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_skew_exit.py` → 19 passed, 0 failed (incl. new: stale `model.set` returns 503 and skips the assignment apply; stale `model.options`/`model.save_key` answer 5098 without reaching the payload build; fresh paths unchanged)
- [x] Red equivalents verified against origin/main sources by construction: the guard calls and the 5098 branch do not exist there.

## Limitations

- The watchdog widening trusts `is_desktop_owned_backend()` process identity the same way the existing cron-ticker path does.
- Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/100216 (stale since 2026-09-01, conflicting, predates the watchdog).

raw.body:
## Root cause

One typed message could be persisted into two sessions, and a single turn's rows could split across a parent and its continuation session, in two related ways:

1. **Off-turn writes used a stale `session_key` (#123545).** The submit path wrote the user row under `session['session_key']` while the turn's own rows flush under `agent.session_id`, and the two diverge for the whole of a turn that begins after a compression rotation moved the agent onto the continuation (`session_key` is re-anchored only at turn end). One message then landed as user rows in two sessions, and tool rows split across them.
2. **The busy-queue envelope held a dead row id across an in-place compaction (#123675).** `archive_and_compact`'s concurrent-append path deactivates the accept-time row and clones it to a fresh id, but the drain's `deactivate_message` and the merge's `set_user_message_content` addressed the dead original — leaving the queued prompt active twice after the drain, or a text-only merge a silent no-op.

## What changes

Combines #123635 and #123676 (their queue hunks overlap; the two fixes compose — owner-session addressing AND live-row re-resolution):

- `_submit_row_target_key` picks the session the turn will actually write (`agent.session_id` or `session_key`, recorded once on the staged dict) and every off-turn writer is addressed by it: `_write_submit_user_row`, the @-expansion rewrite, the queue merge/drain, `_append_model_switch_marker`, `message.react` newest_role, `session.history`, and the out-of-band probe.
- Model-switch durable rows no longer accumulate across switches: superseded markers are deactivated by `display_kind` (the durable counterpart of the in-memory strip), leaving one live row.
- New `SessionDB.resolve_active_row_id(row_id)`: the row itself while active, else the single clone with same role/content/timestamp, `None` when ambiguous. The drain deactivate and the merge update both re-resolve through it; the envelope's staged row is dropped when no live row remains.
- The transcript read addresses the rotated tip (continuation) after a rotation.

## Acceptance coverage per issue

- #123545: one typed message persists as a user row in exactly one session; a turn's rows never split across parent/child after a rotation; off-turn writers target the live session; model-switch rows don't accumulate — `tests/tui_gateway/test_submit_row_session_target.py` (9 tests) drives the real `publish_compression_child` rotation against a real SessionDB.
- #123675: a queued prompt is active exactly once after an in-place compaction + drain; a text-only merge updates the live clone — `tests/tui_gateway/test_queued_prompt_persistence.py` (2 new tests, real SessionDB + real `_handle_busy_submit`/`_drain_queued_prompt`).

## Tests run

- `HERMES_PYTHON=$RUN/test-venv/bin/python bash scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tui_gateway/test_submit_row_session_target.py tests/tui_gateway/test_queued_prompt_persistence.py` — on main: RED (11 failed across both files); with fix: **18/18 green**.
- Same runner for queue/submit-adjacent suites (`test_tui_gateway_queue_on_busy.py`, `test_submit_time_user_row.py`, `test_model_switch_marker_role.py`, `test_busy_compression_demotion.py`, `test_message_metadata.py`, `test_message_sequence_repair.py`, `test_merged_user_override.py`, `hermes_state/test_message_uid.py`, `agent/test_context_engine_message_uid.py`) — **all green (135 tests)**.
- The one failure seen in the huge `test_tui_gateway_server.py` file (`test_profile_scoped_agent_build_starts_mcp_discovery_in_profile_home`, an `agent_ready` Event 5s wait) reproduces identically on pristine `origin/main` under this machine's load — a pre-existing timing flake, not touched by this diff. This branch's modified test in that file passes.

Fixes #123545
Fixes #123675

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/123635 (Thanks @Halldrix — all 9 commits cherry-picked with authorship kept)
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/123676 (Thanks @Totoro-qaq — the composed commit is co-authored)

Notes for review:
- Composes with (does not collide with) #126999's queued-row restart retire: that PR's `_queued_prompt` display_metadata marker and this PR's owner-key/row-id re-resolution touch adjacent hunks of `_persist_queued_user_row`/`_replace_queued_user_row_for_turn` and should be merged in one coordinated pass.
- The model-switch deactivation interacts with the #65891 in-memory strip as documented in the code comments.

raw.body:
## Summary

On macOS, when the agent opens a file via a tool call (`open <file>` / `open -a <App> <file>`), the command returns exit 0 and genuinely opens the document — but the window lands **behind** the maximised Hermes window, so the user sees nothing while the agent reports success. Root cause: the tool shell runs as a child process of the Electron app, and macOS does not let a non-frontmost process hand activation to another app, so the implicit activation that normally accompanies `open` is silently ignored. `osascript … activate` alone is also unreliable — it returns 0 while focus lands elsewhere.

This PR appends a **verified raise-ladder** to file-opening `open` invocations instead of trusting the exit code:

- **`tools/terminal_tool_macos_open.py`** (new) — `_transform_macos_open_command()`, a pure deterministic string rewrite (no subprocess at transform time) gated to Darwin, that detects only file-opening `open` forms and appends a ladder: check `frontmost` → `osascript activate` → `lsappinfo setfront` → re-issue `open -a` → unminimise + activate, then settle ~0.8 s, re-check, and re-assert once to absorb a queued activation from another app. Each rung is verified before escalating. The not-front branch gets one extra activate + 0.4 s, and the tool output reports from the **final observed frontmost state** — naming the app that actually holds focus when another app wins the race, so a focus race can no longer read as plain success.
- **`tools/environments/base.py`** — `_prepare_command()` applies the transform before the existing sudo transform (they compose; `_prepare_command` is the single funnel every terminal backend routes through, so all sibling call paths are covered). No-op on Linux/Windows.
- **`tests/tools/test_terminal_macos_open.py`** — 24 regression tests passing the platform as data (`system="Darwin"` / `system="Linux"`) covering the transform matrix, no-op flags (`-R -e -t -f -W -n -g -h -b -D`), non-`open` commands, compound commands, and the final-outcome reporting.

## What is not exercised live

The ladder and its outcome reporting were validated as a pure decision-logic rewrite (transform matrix + unit tests) on this Mac. The **actual raise behaviour against the live macOS window server** — maximised Hermes, `open -a Preview <pdf>` through the terminal tool, confirming the Preview window lands frontmost — needs a real desktop session and is not covered by these tests; a ladder rung returning 0 is not a pass on its own. That live verification remains open for this issue.

## Tests

- Red on `origin/main`: `PYTHONPATH=<main-archive> pytest tests/tools/test_terminal_macos_open.py` → collection error, `ModuleNotFoundError: tools.terminal_tool_macos_open` (exit 2).
- With fix: `HERMES_PYTHON=<run>/test-venv/bin/python bash scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tools/test_terminal_macos_open.py` → **24/24 passed** (exit 0).
- Sibling regression: same runner, `tests/tools/test_terminal_tool.py tests/tools/test_base_environment.py` → **33/33 passed** (exit 0).

Fixes #95261

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/95286 (based on its raise-ladder approach; thanks @Jackal991 — its commit is cherry-picked here with authorship kept).

raw.body:
## Root cause

Both speech-text normalizers handle Markdown/URLs/symbols but have no pass
for identifier-dense tokens — `apps/desktop/src/lib/speech-text.ts`
(`sanitizeTextForSpeech`) and `tools/tts_text_normalize.py`
(`prepare_spoken_text`). A filename like `peyton-sample-20260922.wav` reaches
the TTS engine verbatim and is read character by character
("peyton dash sample dash two zero two six..."), so clean synthesized audio
sounds corrupted (#119207).

## Fix

One identifier-to-speech pass, mirrored token-for-token in both normalizers:

- `tools/tts_text_normalize.py` — `prune_identifier_tokens_for_tts`,
  wired into `prepare_spoken_text` after the symbols pass (gateway auto-TTS,
  voice-mode streaming, explicit TTS calls).
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/speech-text.ts` — `pruneIdentifierTokens` in
  `sanitizeTextForSpeech`, after code fences/links/URLs/MEDIA: tokens are
  consumed (Read Aloud, auto-speak replies).

Detection: filename-with-extension tokens, hex-hash runs and
`sha256:…`-prefixed digests, UUIDs, dense model/version IDs
(`meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct`, `v2.1.0-beta.3`), and filesystem
paths. Matched tokens become **silence** — never a hardcoded English
placeholder word, per the #86602 lesson (the reply may be in any language).
Ordinary prose, email addresses, dates (`2026/06/02`), ratios (`3:2`) and
short hyphenated words (`COVID-19`, `well-known`) pass verbatim.

Also fixes a pre-existing `smooth_whitespace_for_tts` bug the new corpus
surfaced: `user@example.com` was spoken as "user@example. com" because the
punctuation-spacing pass split any punctuation-followed-by-letter pair; it
now only splits when the punctuation is not glued to a word character.

## Coverage per requirement (#119207)

- Identifier pass in `speech-text.ts`: corpus tests fail on base (filenames
  spoken verbatim), pass with the fix.
- Same identifier policy in `tts_text_normalize.py`: same corpus, pytest.
- Both normalizers agree on the same tokens: one shared corpus
  (`tests/fixtures/identifier_speech_corpus.json`) asserted by both
  `tests/tools/test_tts_identifier_speech.py` and
  `apps/desktop/src/lib/speech-text.identifier-corpus.test.ts`.
- Normal replies no longer sound corrupted: prose around replaced tokens is
  asserted to survive ("Saved ... and ...").

## Checks run

- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tools/test_tts_identifier_speech.py tests/tools/test_tts_text_normalize.py tests/tools/test_tts_prepare_spoken.py` — 25 passed
- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/lib/speech-text.identifier-corpus.test.ts src/lib/speech-text.test.ts` — 36 passed
- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/lib/voice-playback.routing.test.ts src/lib/voice-playback.same-turn.test.ts` — 9 passed (downstream consumers)
- Red on base: corpus test against `origin/main`'s `speech-text.ts` — 2 failed / 2 passed; with the fix, 4 passed.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/119212

Thanks @KoNit-K — the desktop-half normalization approach and its test
corpus (filenames, paths, UUIDs, dense identifiers, ordinary-prose control)
are reused here; this PR extends the policy to the gateway/CLI normalizer
that #119212 left untouched and replaces the spoken labels with silence so
non-English voices are never handed English placeholder words.

Fixes #119207

raw.body:
## Root cause

The original misclassification (a 401 from `POST /api/auth/ws-ticket` reported as "Could not reach the remote Hermes gateway") was the fetch layer never attaching `err.statusCode`; that hole is **already fixed on main** by #95701 (shared `httpStatusError` in `api-transport.ts:183-191`, used by `fetchJson`, `fetchPublicJson`, and the OAuth-session fetch), and `gatewayTicketFailure` (`connection-config.ts`) classifies 401/403 → `needsOauthLogin`/`isReauthRequired` with sign-in copy. #96449/#98656 (the hand-rolled duplicates of that fix) were correctly rejected/withdrawn.

The **still-live defect** (djmango's fleet evidence in #98647): every non-auth mint failure — timeout, `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`, DNS failure, 502 — was wrapped in one undifferentiated sentence (`remote-oauth-ticket.ts:38` passed a static string as `transportMessage`), so ~1,100 log lines across three different upstream causes all read identically and the diagnostic cost stayed high even after the auth/transport split was fixed.

## What changed

- `connection-config.ts` — new exported `gatewayTicketTransportMessage(error)`: names the actual transport failure class in user-facing copy — timeout/unreachable/DNS → "timed out or the host could not be resolved… check your network/VPN path", `ECONNREFUSED` → "connection was refused… the gateway process is likely down", anything else keeps the legacy one-liner.
- `remote-oauth-ticket.ts` — `resolveRemoteOauthTicket` passes `gatewayTicketTransportMessage(error)` instead of the static sentence. Auth classification is untouched: 401/403 still route to the sign-in copy with `needsOauthLogin`/`isReauthRequired` (covered by the existing parametrized test).
- `remote-oauth-ticket.test.ts` — behavioural test: timeout/DNS/refused/ambiguous/500 produce the expected distinct copy, and none of the transport classes ever read as an auth failure (`isReauthRequiredError` false, no `needsOauthLogin` tag).

Refs #98647 (the primary requirement — 401 misreported as "could not reach" — is already met on main by #95701; this PR closes the remaining live sub-defect from the issue thread. #96449 was rejected as a duplicate of #95701, so nothing is superseded here.)

## Tests actually run

- `vitest run --project electron electron/remote-oauth-ticket.test.ts electron/connection-config.test.ts` — pass
- `npm run check:lint` — pass

## Auto-merge

Off (hitl): user-facing error-copy change in the remote-gateway auth path; per the sweep rules for auth-cluster PRs.

raw.body:
The desktop main process holds several module-level registries; #58485 reported its V8 heap climbing to the ~4GB ceiling over about an hour of normal use. The renderer-side leak fixes from the #77311 series never touched the main process, and a survey of the registries named in that issue shows most are bounded on current main — but one provably is not.

## Root cause

`remoteOwnerBySessionId` (main.ts, from #85834) memoizes which remote profile owns a session id when a `/api/sessions/:id` read arrives with no profile hint. The memo **only ever inserts**: the 30s TTL makes an entry stale but never removes it, and there is no delete call anywhere. A long-lived main process therefore keeps one Map entry per session id it has ever resolved — and session ids churn through normal use, so the map grows without bound for the life of the process.

## What changes

- The memo moves to `electron/remote-owner-cache.ts` as a pure, injectable cache (`limit` / `now` / `ttlMs`) with FIFO eviction past 500 entries — the same shape as the existing `titleCache` bound.
- `main.ts` wires `remoteOwnerProfileForSession` through it; behaviour (30s TTL, hint-less resolution, sweep across configured remotes) is otherwise unchanged.

Survey of the other registries named in the issue (all bounded on current main, no change needed): `titleCache` (500 FIFO), `hermesLog` (300), `recentFileReveals` (self-pruning), `renderTitleQueue` (drained by 2 concurrent 8s-timeout jobs), `sshConnections` (full lifecycle on teardown/close), and the baseUrl-keyed `gatewayAuthProvidersCache` / `_nativeTokens` (one entry per configured remote). `fetchJson` buffers one response at a time with no retained references after `JSON.parse` — a transient buffer, not retention.

## Acceptance coverage

- "Identify and fix the main-process heap retention" — one provable unbounded path fixed; a full attribution (heap-snapshot diff of the remaining growth) still needs a live long-run session and is not claimed here.
- "Verify the fix on macOS Apple Silicon" — not exercised live in this PR; the fix is platform-neutral main-process logic.
- "Add regression/leak coverage" — unit tests cover the FIFO bound and TTL behaviour.

## Tests

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 electron/remote-owner-cache.test.ts` → **1 file, 3 passed**.
- Red on main: `remote-owner-cache.ts` does not exist on `origin/main`, so the test file fails to import there.
- `npx tsc -p . --noEmit` (apps/desktop) → clean (exit 0).

## Not exercised live

The 1-hour heap ceiling reproduction needs a long interactive session on macOS; this PR fixes the provable unbounded path and bounds it, but does not claim the whole OOM is closed — the remaining gap (if any) needs the in-band heap sampler the issue's fix plan describes.

Refs #58485

raw.body:
## Root cause

Switching models mid-session could drop the next user prompt. The model-switch `[System:...]` marker is persisted as `role=user` on purpose (#48338). When alternation repair merges that marker with the following plain user row, `_merge_consecutive_users` kept the marker's `display_kind` and its `_row_id` — hiding the merged pair from every user-turn index and burying the plain row's durable id. `_resolve_truncate_row_id` read only the repaired durable view, so the absorbed row id could never resolve: `prompt.submit` failed closed with 4018 ("refusing truncation without fallback") and the user's input was silently dropped.

## What changes (combining #94500 + #99955)

- **Merge side (#94500, rebased):** when a display-marker user row merges with a plain user row, the merged pair drops the display classification and carries the plain row's `_row_id` (the marker's own id is retired onto `_absorbed_row_ids`), keeping the pair addressable for rewind/submit. The persist marker is popped — reclassifying stales the row even when the merged bytes reproduce the persisted content. Scope note: when BOTH rows carry `display_kind` (two consecutive markers) the pair keeps the first marker's classification — no plain row is swallowed there.
- **Resolver side (#99955):** `_resolve_truncate_row_id` now loads the durable transcript with `repair_alternation=False` for identity lookups. Repair merges any user;user run (marker runs, or an interrupted turn + resend) into its first row, so the repaired view cannot see absorbed ids; reading the physical rows resolves rows that are genuinely present.

## Acceptance coverage per issue

- Marker-merged rows keep the plain row's addressable identity (`test_repair_marker_user_merge_keeps_plain_row_addressable`, `test_repair_plain_user_then_marker_stays_addressable`).
- `prompt.submit` with `truncate_before_row_id` resolves after a marker merge instead of 4018 (`test_prompt_submit_resolves_row_id_absorbed_into_marker_merge`).
- The broader swallowed-id family — dual markers, and a plain-user merge with NO marker at all — resolves via the un-repaired transcript (`test_prompt_submit_resolves_row_id_swallowed_by_marker_merge`, `test_prompt_submit_resolves_row_id_swallowed_by_plain_user_merge`).

## Tests run

- On `origin/main`: all 5 new tests RED — including the exact 4018 "refusing truncation without fallback" from the report (`pytest ... -q`, 5 failed in 88.42s).
- With this branch: all 5 GREEN (5 passed in 51.55s); full `tests/agent/test_message_sequence_repair.py` suite 61/61 green; the gateway server file's `row_id or truncate or marker or repair or rewind` selection 35/35 green (the 2 selection-mode failures seen once were cross-test pollution in the huge file, reproduced as passing in isolation on both main and this branch).

Fixes #94486

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/94500 (Thanks @liuhao1024 — both commits cherry-picked with authorship kept)
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/99955 (Thanks @zengzheqing — resolver change + tests folded in as a co-authored commit)
Also supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/112908 (heavier resolver-signature variant made redundant by #99955's minimal read-side fix)

Notes for review: the issue's optional fail-open floor (skip truncation and submit as a plain append when the target still doesn't resolve) is deliberately NOT included — heliangwjq offered to PR it separately and it changes the fail-closed contract #82959 established; that is a maintainer call.

raw.body:
## What

Adds OpenAI **Ultrafast** as a `/fast` tier for GPT-6 Astra, and prices responses at the tier OpenAI actually served them at.

**WHO / WHEN / WHY:** At DevDay 2026 (2026-09-29) OpenAI launched Ultrafast, a `service_tier: "ultrafast"` request field ([guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/ultrafast-mode), [pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing?latest-pricing=ultrafast), [Codex speed docs](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/speed)).
- It is broadly available for GPT-6 Astra in the API, and in Codex on Pro 500 and Enterprise plans.
- It is billed at **6x Standard**: $60 / $300, cached $6, cache write $75, and 2x/1.5x again above 272K.
- GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast is announced as "coming soon" with no published rate yet.

Hermes had no way to request the tier. If it had been requested through `request_overrides`, cost would have shown Standard, one-sixth of the real bill.

Companion to #128248 (GPT-6.1 Sol). The two PRs don't touch the same files.

## Changes

| Surface | Change |
|---|---|
| `agent/fast_mode.py` | One tier table: `parse_service_tier`, `STATIC_TIERS`, `service_tier_word`. The CLI (`cli_config_load`), gateway (`run_config_loaders`) and TUI (`server._load_service_tier`) config loaders used three hand-copied parsers; all three now call this one. |
| `hermes_cli/models.py`, `models_catalog_static.py` | `model_supports_ultrafast` covers `gpt-6-astra` (vendor prefix and `-900k` alias stripped). `resolve_fast_mode_overrides(tier="ultrafast")` returns `{"service_tier": "ultrafast"}` only for Ultrafast models on the existing first-party route gate (api.openai.com / chatgpt.com). Any other model gets **nothing**, never a silent switch to Priority, which is a different paid tier. |
| CLI / gateway / TUI | `/fast ultrafast` works on all three. The gateway picker shows the choice only when the model supports it; a typed `ultrafast` on an unsupported model is refused with a clear message. Every place that attaches a static tier (`_resolve_turn_agent_config` on CLI and gateway, TUI `config.set fast`, TUI `session.info`) now passes the tier through instead of hard-coding `priority`. The TUI slash command and Desktop settings toggle recognise the new value. |
| Pricing (`usage_pricing`, `turn_usage`, `aux_accounting`, `codex_runtime`) | OpenAI reports the served tier on the response, not inside `usage`. `with_served_service_tier` folds it into `raw_usage`, and the Codex stream assembler now keeps `service_tier` from the terminal frame. A response served at `ultrafast` prices from a published `_OPENAI_ULTRAFAST_PRICING` row. A request that asked for Ultrafast but was served at `default` bills at Standard. A served-ultrafast model with no published rate reports unknown instead of guessing. |
| `locales/*` | 4 new keys in all 17 locales. The option lists in usage/description strings now mention `ultrafast`. |

## Verification

- New `tests/agent/test_openai_ultrafast.py`, 9 relationship tests:
  - all three config loaders agree on every tier word;
  - the tier is gated by model and route (6 Sol gets none; OpenRouter gets none);
  - CLI and gateway turn routes send `ultrafast`;
  - the CLI refuses it on 6 Sol;
  - served ultrafast costs exactly 6x Standard, below and above 272K;
  - requested-but-served-default costs Standard;
  - unpublished models report unknown;
  - the Codex assembler keeps the served tier.
- Mutation checks: removing the pricing branch fails 3 tests; dropping `tier=` at the CLI attach site fails 1; dropping `service_tier` from the assembler fails 1.
- Existing fast-mode, pricing, i18n-parity, codex-transport, TUI-server and gateway suites (26 files): 1150 passed, 39 failed. All 39 fail identically on `upstream/main` (home-IO guard in this local checkout). Ruff is clean, and `tsc --noEmit` + eslint are clean for `ui-tui`.
- **Live, Codex OAuth, real `AIAgent`** with `gpt-6-astra` and `/fast ultrafast` overrides: the wire request carried `service_tier: ultrafast`, the backend accepted it, and it reported **served `default`** because this account isn't on Pro 500. The run returned `PASS`. That's the exact case the served-tier pricing handles.
- **Not live-tested:** a response actually served at `ultrafast` (needs a Pro 500 account or an API key), and the direct API path (no OpenAI key here).

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- **Fast mode (Priority, 2x) is still priced at Standard for OpenAI.** This is pre-existing. The served-tier plumbing here makes adding those rows a data-only change; left out so this PR stays about Ultrafast.
- GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast: add `gpt-6.1-sol` to `_OPENAI_ULTRAFAST_MODELS`, plus its pricing row, once OpenAI publishes the rate.
- The Desktop settings toggle stays binary (fast/normal). It now shows "on" for an ultrafast config instead of "off"; there's no dedicated Desktop control yet.
