## Root cause

Renderer localStorage keeps dead session ids forever. `pullRemotePins` only consults
rows present in the list payload (a pin whose row was deleted never enters any branch),
composer drafts are pure localStorage with no backend validation, and queue entries are
retried 4x per boot with no prune — nothing ever drops references to ids removed from
`state.db`, so every boot re-probes them and logs "Session not found" 404s.

## What changes

- New `apps/desktop/src/store/dead-session-prune.ts`: probes each stored id on the active
  profile then each named profile, and drops it from pins, composer drafts, and the
  composer queue only when every probe 404s; defers on non-404 failures (gateway
  mid-restart / network) and guards verdicts against gateway switches.
- `session-pin-sync.ts` forgets the pin-sync bookkeeping before unpinning so reconcile
  doesn't re-PATCH the dead id; the `__new__` draft key is never discarded.
- The queue drain's 4x retry loop stops on dead entries.

## Acceptance coverage (#79001)

- Dead IDs dropped from pins, composer drafts, and composer queue on first boot (self-heal on 404)
- Profile-scoped semantics: drop only when every known profile probe 404s; defer on non-404
- Pin-sync bookkeeping forgotten before unpin; `__new__` draft key preserved
- Verdicts guarded against gateway switches; queue retry loop stopped on dead entries
- Regression tests covering all three surfaces + a state.db-deletion repro (40 tests)

## Tests

- `npx vitest run src/store/dead-session-prune.test.ts src/store/session-pin-sync.test.ts --maxWorkers=2`
  on the branch rebased onto current `origin/main`: **40 passed, 0 failed**.
- Same PR test file against pristine `origin/main`: **red** (`Failed to resolve import
  "./dead-session-prune"` — the module does not exist on main).

## Supersedes

- Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/81313 — cherry-picked with
  authorship kept; the fork rebase hit `RebaseConflictError` server-side. Thanks @DavidMetcalfe.

Fixes #79001

PR_TITLE=fix(desktop): keep rejected submit restore out of the newly focused composer
PR_BODY=## Root cause

When a submit is rejected by the gateway (or throws), `dispatchSubmit`'s
`restore()` re-painted the submitted text into the **live composer DOM**
unconditionally. If the user had already switched sessions (the gateway can
reject well after dispatch), the late repaint wrote session A's text into
session B's composer, and the paint-triggered debounced draft sync then stashed
it under B's draft key — permanent cross-session draft bleed. On a first send
from a fresh chat, the rejection was additionally stranded under the pre-session
`__new__` bucket instead of following the session the submit created.

## What changes

- `restore()` now **always stashes** under the scope captured at dispatch
  (as before, #54527), but **loads into the composer DOM only when the
  composer still owns that scope** — guarded via `draftScopeRef.current`
  captured inside the swap `useLayoutEffect` (it stays on the old session
  until the swap commits, so a suspended transition render cannot flip the
  predicate mid-restore).
- The **first-send handoff**: a submit from a pre-session (fresh) chat passes
  an `onComposerScopeAssigned` callback through `onSubmit` → `submitPrompt` →
  `createBackendSessionForSend` → `createBackendSession`, fired at the exact
  stored-id assignment (the same site that calls `announceNewSessionDraftKey`)
  — and only there, never for plain navigation. A rejection after
  `session.create` restores the text into the chat that was created for it,
  instead of stranding it under `__new__`.
- `clearSessionDraft` on success still addresses the captured submit scope.

## Acceptance coverage per issue (#66661)

- restore() must not paint the live DOM when the submitting session is no
  longer the active/loaded one — covered.
- Rejected text stays stashed under the scope captured at dispatch — kept
  (already held since #54527).
- The paint-triggered sync can no longer file the rejected text under the
  now-focused session's key — no repaint, no sync.
- Regression coverage for still-active vs switched-away restore branches,
  including the suspended-transition-render case and the first-send
  assignment path — 501-line regression suite
  (`use-composer-submit.restore-scoping.test.tsx`).

## Tests

- `npx vitest run src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-submit.restore-scoping.test.tsx src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-submit.test.tsx --maxWorkers=2`
  - with this branch: **52 passed** (2 files)
  - on `origin/main` (new test file only): **7 failed** — the rejected-restore
    bleed and first-send stranding reproduce red on main.

Fixes #66661
Supersedes #74800 (Thanks @wzslr321 — the draftScopeRef-based guard and the
switched-away/still-loaded regression tests are yours, cherry-picked with
authorship kept)
Supersedes #67317 (Thanks @Sora-bluesky — your activeQueueSessionKeyRef variant
covers the ordinary switch case; the thread's suspended-render comparison showed
the draftScopeRef predicate passes both contracts, so this branch builds on it)

Co-authored-by: Wiktor Zając <59893892+wzslr321@users.noreply.github.com>

raw.body:
## Summary

Two remote-backend fixes for the pooled/remote SSH family, salvaged from contributor PRs and rebased onto current `main` (the stale-attempt ControlMaster teardown half of #97264 landed separately in 05d832d685):

- **Pooled liveness window (#94381)** — `revalidatePool()` shared the primary connection's `RemoteLivenessTracker`, whose 60s failure window is sized for the primary's ~48s retry cadence. Pooled descriptors are probed on the renderer's reconnect cadence (minutes apart), so a dead pooled backend's failure streak reset to 1 on every tick and the 3-failure drop threshold was unreachable — the pool kept serving a dead descriptor (ECONNRESET on every use) until app restart. This adds a dedicated `pooledRemoteLiveness` tracker with a 15-minute window (`REMOTE_POOLED_LIVENESS_FAILURE_WINDOW_MS`), wired into `revalidatePool()`. A successful probe still clears the streak, so a healthy host is never falsely dropped.
- **Cold-start-tolerant ready timeout (#94642)** — the remote backend ready budget was hardcoded at 45s; busy remote hosts routinely take 60–150s to cold-boot a pooled `hermes serve --isolated` before printing `HERMES_BACKEND_READY`, so the desktop killed a healthy boot and surfaced a timeout. The default rises to 120s with a 45s floor (`MIN_READY_TIMEOUT_MS`), and `HERMES_DESKTOP_REMOTE_READY_TIMEOUT_MS` overrides it for busier hosts — mirroring the existing local `HERMES_DESKTOP_PORT_ANNOUNCE_TIMEOUT_MS` resolver pattern. `windows-remote-lifecycle.ts` (the Windows sibling connect path) resolves through the same function.

Together these close the loop reported in #97264's title: the too-tight 45s deadline killed slow-but-healthy boots, and the failed attempt's cleanup then tore down the shared ControlMaster (fixed on main by 05d832d685), which re-bootstrapped slowly, hit the deadline again, and cycled.

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/94416 and https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/94665 — thanks @mfwagner and @Finn763 for the original fixes, tests, and field reports; commits are cherry-picked with authorship preserved.

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/94381
Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/94642
Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/97264 (with the ControlMaster half already on main; the ready-timeout half is the remaining coverage)

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run electron/remote-liveness.test.ts electron/remote-lifecycle.test.ts electron/windows-remote-lifecycle.test.ts electron/ssh-connection.test.ts --maxWorkers=2 --testTimeout=120000` in `apps/desktop/`: 223 passed, 1 skipped — except `remote-lifecycle.test.ts > pidIsOurDashboard recognizes an installer wrapper after it execs python + entrypoint`, which fails identically on pristine `origin/main` on this loaded host (live-process probe; re-verified 4/4 on a clean checkout of main) — pre-existing flake, not touched by this diff.
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.electron.json`: clean.
- [x] New regression tests: pooled-cadence drop (4-minute gaps → drop on the 3rd failure), stale-streak reset past the window, timeout override honored / floor-clamped / fraction-rounded / malformed-fallback.

raw.body:
## Root cause

`hermes:openExternal` funnels every external open through `openExternalUrl` (electron/external-open.ts), which only accepted URL-parseable input. Every bare local filesystem path a chat media link, markdown href, or artifacts-panel value carried was a dead click:

- `C:\Users\x\a.md` — `new URL()` parses the drive letter as the bogus `c:` scheme, so the web allowlist rejected it with "Invalid external URL".
- `/tmp/report.pdf`, `~/logs/desktop.log`, `\\server\share\a.md` — the parser throws, same reject.
- `//cdn.example.com/img.png` — protocol-relative; the parser rejects it without a base, and it must not fall through to a local-path open.

Red on base (probed against origin/main's module directly): all four shapes resolved `{ok: false, reason: 'invalid'}`.

## Fix

- `electron/local-filesystem-path.ts` (new, from #84542): `looksLikeLocalFilesystemPath` (POSIX `/…`, `///…`, `~/…`, drive `C:\…`/`C:/…`, UNC `\\…`; never `//host`) and `absolutizeProtocolRelativeUrl` (`//host/…` → `https://…`, so it opens in the browser).
- `external-open.ts`: bare-path branch ahead of `new URL()` routes local shapes to a new `openLocalPath` dep. Unresolvable path → logged (with the path) + `invalid`; a thrown open → the existing failure modal channel.
- `main.ts`: `openLocalFilesystemPath` resolves via the same audited `resolveRequestedPathForIpc` as the `file:` route (device paths stay blocked, `~` expands), runs the existing pre-open missing-file stat guard ("File not found" modal instead of a silent no-op), then `shell.openPath` with a reveal-in-folder fallback — the reveal never re-opens, so archive artifacts with no usable association can't loop (#53170). Every failure log names the path so "Failed to open path" is diagnosable.

Renderer side is NOT re-fixed here: `mediaExternalUrl`'s `file://` string-concat escaping (`%`/`#`/`?`) and the MEDIA tag trailing-punctuation capture are already covered by open maintainer PRs #127248 and main's 9647f3505b. This PR is the main-process half of the shared root cause — the piece that makes any surviving bare path open correctly instead of erroring.

## Coverage per issue

- #80946 (bare Windows drive-letter artifacts/links): the `c:`-scheme reject is exactly the branch removed; drive paths now resolve and open.
- Issue #84361's opener half (bare-path acceptance + `//cdn` as https) from #84542's design.

## Checks run

- `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 --project electron electron/external-open.test.ts electron/local-filesystem-path.test.ts` → 15 passed (4 new bare-path/protocol-relative tests fail on base).
- `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 --project electron electron/open-missing-file.test.ts electron/preload-external-open.test.ts` → 6 passed (guard + preload wiring intact).
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json --noEmit` → clean.
- `npx eslint electron/external-open.ts electron/local-filesystem-path.ts electron/main.ts` → clean.
- Red-on-base probe (node against origin/main's external-open.ts): `C:\Users\x\a.md`, `/tmp/report.pdf`, `~/logs/desktop.log`, `//cdn.example.com/img.png` all → `{ok:false,reason:'invalid'}`.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/84542 — the opener half (predicate module + bare-path branch) is its design, cherry-picked with adaptation; its markdown-regex slice is already on main (9647f3505b) and its renderer slice is covered by #127248. Thanks @686f6c61 and @uttkarsh-26.
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/48620 — its main.cjs/open-target.cjs surface no longer exists; the bare/relative/`~` acceptance lives here against the current external-open.ts module. Its renderer `toLocalFileUrl` percent-encoding slice is covered by #127248. Thanks @professorpalmer.

Kept separate (not superseded — different layers, tracked under their own issues):
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/90669 — renderer href + reveal affordance; should build on the canonical helper once #127248 lands.
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/87624 — markdown tag-parsing slice of hermes-agent 84361; orthogonal to the opener.

Windows-only verification (drive letters, UNC) still needs a Windows host; the unit tests cover the classification, and `resolveRequestedPathForIpc`/`shell.openPath` are cross-platform.

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/80946

## Root cause

Two read-path halves kept pre-compression turns unreachable in the active Desktop session:

1. **Backend (already on main):** the gateway's `/api/sessions/{id}/messages` (`gateway/platforms/api_server.py::_handle_session_messages`) never parsed `include_compacted`, and neither REST endpoint walked the compression lineage. Desktop sends `include_compacted=true` precisely so pre-compaction rows stay reachable when scrolling back — dropping the flag made the transcript silently end at the compaction boundary (#101939), and rotation lineages truncated to the latest child segment (#79565). Both are fixed on `main` as of #59661 (verified compression-hop walker, `include_ancestors=True` on both endpoints, merged as cf63a03e392/cfd5dc38763/e5867d9bae0) and 7cadfaa6685 (`include_compacted` parsed via `_coerce_request_bool`).

2. **Desktop (this PR):** after a manual `/compress`, the handler replaced the live transcript wholesale — `updateSessionState(sessionId, state => ({ ...state, messages: toChatMessages(result.messages!) }))` — so every pre-compression bubble vanished from the active session with no way to scroll back to it (#105256). The post-compress history shares no anchor with the live transcript, so the normal graft path can't restore what the rewrite dropped.

## What changes

`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/slash.ts` — the `/compress` result no longer replaces `state.messages` outright. The post-compress history stays authoritative for overlapping rows, but the pre-compression segment is kept reachable by merging it as an older transcript page via the existing `mergeOlderTranscriptPage` helper (deduped by row/message id, older-wins ordering) — the same merge the transcript backfill scroll path already uses. Everything before the summary survives in the active session; scrolling up reaches it without a session switch.

## Acceptance coverage

- **#105256** (full fix — this PR): after manual `/compress`, pre-compression messages remain reachable in the same session. The backend half of that issue (auto-compression/rotation read path) was fixed on `main` by #59661 + 7cadfaa6685.
- **#79565** (covered on `main`, no code here): switching back to a compressed lineage shows the whole conversation — #59661 (merged) added the verified compression-hop walker (`include_ancestors`) on both REST endpoints with carried-row timestamp dedupe, and 7cadfaa6685 closed the gateway `include_compacted` gap.
- **#101939** (covered on `main`, no code here): `_handle_session_messages` now parses and forwards `include_compacted` (7cadfaa6685, Fixes #101939).

## Tests

- `npx vitest run src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/index.test.tsx --testNamePattern "compress" --maxWorkers=2` — **12 passed** (includes the new regression test). Red on the pre-fix handler: with `slash.ts` reverted to `main` the new test fails at `expect(renderedText).toContain('pre-compression user turn')` (**1 failed**); green with this change.
- `npx tsc -p . --noEmit` in `apps/desktop` — **exit 0**.

## Supersedes

- Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/106594 (same fix, cherry-picked with authorship kept). Thanks @Finn763.

Co-authored-by: finn763 <165816600+finn763@users.noreply.github.com>

## Root cause

`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/right-rail/preview-pane.tsx` had no Escape binding anywhere in the pane. `goBack` existed (:754-758) but was reachable only via the browser bar's Back button or mouse buttons 3/4. The reported dead end: after a local HTML report's in-page links navigate the preview webview, the keyboard user has no way back.

Prior routing re-verified on this base: the browser-bar gating itself is correct (the bar renders for local-HTML previews; remote data: reports have no webview and no history to go back to, so no chrome is right there), and #73899's other requirements are already met on main (`b08ec00a70` — target=_blank opens in the system browser; pane close is distinct from goBack). The remaining gap is exactly the Escape binding.

## Fix

A keydown handler on the pane's `<aside>` frame:

- Escape drives the webview back **only when `canGoBack()`** — a first-load preview or a remote-HTML report (data: document, no webview) claims no back that cannot happen.
- Editable surfaces inside the pane (the browser bar's address input, an annotate note) keep Escape's native meaning — the handler skips `input`/`textarea`/`contenteditable` targets, so clearing the address draft never also navigates.
- Same layer as the existing mouse-button back/forward on the same element: focus inside the out-of-process guest page is answered by main against the focused webContents and never reaches this renderer, so there is no double-handling.

## Checks run

- `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 --project ui src/app/chat/right-rail/preview-pane.test.tsx` → 27 passed, including 2 new:
  - "Escape goes back only when the webview has history" (red on base: no keydown handler on the pane, so `goBack` is never called)
  - "Escape keeps its native meaning for editable surfaces inside the pane"

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/73900 — the issue author's PR; its guest-open bridge half is superseded on main by b08ec00a70, and this PR covers the residual Escape-to-back ask. Thanks @chillerno1.

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/73899

raw.body:
**Desktop sessions now follow the agent into the worktree it works in, and each row records the branch it is actually on — so the sidebar's lanes stop lying.**

## What does this PR do?

Three defects on one session lifecycle, consolidated:

1. **A chat never followed its agent into a worktree.** `_reconcile_session_cwd_from_terminal` re-anchors a session whose agent settled in another worktree of the same repo, then emits the `session.info` the sidebar follows. Its pin keyed on `explicit_cwd`, which `session.create` sets for ANY session whose cwd exists on disk — i.e. every desktop session — so the follow was dead on that surface.
2. **Desktop rows never recorded their git metadata.** `session.create` runs `_hydrate_session_cwd` before any row exists, so its cwd claim no-ops; the row lands later on the first submit through `_ensure_session_db_row`, which wrote `cwd` and never scheduled the probe. Rows kept `git_branch`/`git_repo_root` NULL, so their lane label fell back to a synthetic `main`.
3. **"+" on that synthetic label ran `git switch main`.** On a repo whose trunk is `master` that dies with `fatal: invalid reference: main` and no session is created.

## Related Issue

Fixes #108784
Fixes #108694

(The follow fix has no issue: it is a regression introduced by the #72776 hardening on 07-31.)

## Changes Made

- `tui_gateway/session_workdir.py` — the settle guard pins on `cwd_pinned` (set only by the moves the user drives: `session.cwd.set` from the composer's folder picker, and `session.workspace.move` from move-to-project) instead of `explicit_cwd`; `_ensure_session_db_row` calls a new `_schedule_row_git_meta` (once per live session, only when a cwd-carrying row is missing its git metadata).
- `tui_gateway/server.py` — `_hydrate_session_cwd` enriches a row that already carries its cwd but no git metadata, so a pre-existing row heals on resume instead of waiting for a prompt.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/projects/workspace-groups.ts` + `workspace-group.tsx` — new pure `laneSwitchTarget(group, branches)`: a lane label is used as a `git switch` target only when git lists it (a local head, or a remote-tracking ref `git switch` can DWIM).
- Tests: `tests/tui_gateway/test_session_cwd_follow.py`, `test_desktop_session_row_git_meta.py`, `test_session_git_metadata_generation.py`, `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/projects/workspace-groups.test.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/sessions-section-new-session-drag.test.tsx`.
- `website/docs/user-guide/desktop.md` — one sentence on the follow behaviour.

## How to Test

1. In a chat whose workspace is a repo checkout, ask the agent to make a worktree and work in it: at the end of the turn the chat re-anchors and the sidebar moves it into that worktree's lane.
2. Deliberately move a chat's workspace (composer folder picker, or Move to project) and repeat: it stays put.
3. Start a chat in a project and check its row — `git_branch` / `git_repo_root` are recorded instead of NULL, so the lane is labelled with the real branch.
4. On a repo whose trunk is `master`, "New session in <lane>" opens a session instead of failing with `invalid reference: main`.

Verification on the merged shape (this branch rebased onto `origin/main` @ `fddab1ae8a`):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| E2E probe: real `session.create` → first submit → settle → emitted `session.info` | row gets `git_branch=main` + the real repo root; the settle emits `cwd=…/.worktrees/wt`, `branch=wt` and the DB row's cwd moves with it; after a deliberate move the cwd stays at the checkout |
| `tests/tui_gateway/` (mirror dir) | 243/244 files green; the one failure (`test_entry_rpc_stdin_cloexec.py`) fails identically on an untouched checkout here |
| Focused files (4) | 26 passed |
| `npx vitest run src/app/chat/sidebar/projects/ src/app/chat/sidebar/sessions-section-new-session-drag.test.tsx` | 7 files, 122 passed |
| `npx tsc -p . --noEmit` (apps/desktop) | clean |

## Sibling PRs — this supersedes two, with authorship preserved

- **#127011** (@austinpickett) — its lazy-row git enrichment and `laneSwitchTarget` land as-is, both commits cherry-picked.
- **#108789** (@fangliquanflq) — its resume-time hydration enrichment lands; its lazy-row half is the same fix as #127011's, so that half was dropped as superseded.
- One follow-up commit of mine adapts #108789's test: with the lazy-row enrichment in place a row built through `_ensure_session_db_row` is already enriched, so the test now builds the row directly (the state a pre-enrichment row is in) and both halves stay independently covered.
- **#108788** (@KoNit-K) was already closed onto #108789 before this.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate — this PR *is* the consolidation of them
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — ran the mirror dir (`tests/tui_gateway/`) plus the focused files; the full suite is CI's
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: NixOS, Python 3.14, node 26

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — the lane switch now goes through git's own branch list; no new path/process/platform branch

## Root cause

The REST transcript projection `hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py::_project_for_display` lagged the gateway projection (`tui_gateway/session_history.py`) in two ways:

1. **Untyped scaffold rows ship as visible user rows (#109921).** A `[System: …]` role=user row persisted without a `display_kind` (e.g. the stream-timeout nudge the turn-truncation path appends) reached Desktop's transcript prefetch as a visible user row. Desktop addresses visible user rows by durable row id for rewind/regenerate, but the gateway truncation resolver refuses scaffold rows fail-closed — so a retry targeting one dead-ends every time (`refusing truncation without fallback`). The gateway's own projection drops these rows.
2. **Stored steer rows ship marker-wrapped (#121978, mechanism 2 — diagnosed in the issue thread).** `session.resume`'s projection unwraps a `role=user` `display_kind=steer` row to the user's own words; the REST projection did not, so the persisted row never paired with the optimistic plain-text copy Desktop holds — the mid-turn correction rendered twice (marker-wrapped from REST + plain optimistic) and reordered below later tool work on refresh.

## What changes

- `_is_untyped_scaffold_notice` + a `display_kind="hidden"` branch in `_project_for_display` (cherry-picked from #109922, authorship kept): rows are hidden, never dropped, so pagination offsets and "Show earlier" stay stable; typed notices (`model_switch`, …) keep flowing as timeline rows. Grafted around main's newer read-side failed-turn typing (`untyped_failed_turn_display_kind`) and tool-call-label wiring added since the PR was opened.
- A steer-unwrap branch: for `role=user` `display_kind=steer` rows, `display_content = _extract_steer_text_from_message(message)` (same shape as the compaction display branch); `content` untouched for export/inspection consumers. Rows without a resolvable marker fall through unchanged.

## Acceptance coverage

- #109921: GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages no longer ships untyped `[System:` user rows as visible/addressable; typed notices keep flowing; rows kept (offsets stable). Fully covered → Fixes #109921.
- #121978: the REST projection now unwraps steer rows (mechanism 2). Mechanism 1 — optimistic-row re-anchoring between folded tool rounds — is NOT in this PR (it lives in #121990's renderer changes); the issue is only partially covered here → partial, tracked at https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/121978.

## Tests

- `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_sessions_rest_scaffold_notices.py` — on `origin/main` (7cadfaa668): **2 failed** (scaffold-hide + steer-unwrap, the two root causes); with this branch: **4 passed** in 16.7s.
- `pytest tests/gateway/test_api_server_compaction_projection.py` — 14 passed (main's new include_compacted suite on the same projection).
- `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_session_messages_inline_images.py tests/hermes_cli/test_session_message_page_owner.py tests/hermes_cli/test_history_commentary_display.py` — 29 passed.
- `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_session_timeline.py` — 6 passed.

## Supersedes & credit

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/109922 — thanks @jahfaliabdulrahman-dev (commit f7b1d6e4bc7 cherry-picked, authorship kept, grafted onto main's current projection). #121990 remains the home for mechanism 1 (optimistic re-anchoring) and is noted as the complementary renderer-side fix; thanks @Xipong for the mechanism-2 diagnosis in the issue thread.

raw.body:
## Root cause

The Electron `hermes:api` ipcMain.handle transport logs a full "Error occurred in handler" stack for EVERY rejected invoke, with no opt-out. Desktop's session resolution is a deliberate probe ladder (`resolveStoredSession`: cache -> active backend -> each other profile), so a cross-profile 404 is a normal rung outcome the renderer already handles — but each one printed a multi-line stack into the launching terminal (the reporter's ~30 traces per boot).

## What changes

- New `apps/desktop/electron/api-expected-404.ts` sentinel seam (`HERMES_API_EXPECTED_404`): the main-process handler RESOLVES an expected 404 with a sentinel instead of rejecting, so Electron's per-rejection stack log is bypassed for that one case.
- `preload.ts` unwraps the sentinel and rethrows it as an ordinary `Error` carrying the identical `404: <body>` message — the renderer contract is unchanged; only Electron's logging is bypassed.
- The 404 check is narrow (a 404 word-boundary match on the `fetchJson` error message shape) and runs BEFORE `formatApiRequestFailure`, so every other handler failure still rejects, still persists its full stack to desktop.log, and still prints.

Rebased onto the grown `hermes:api` handler (registry-pinned dispatch, profile rename/delete gate, `formatApiRequestFailure`): the sentinel return sits inside the existing catch, ahead of the failure logging, so profile-deletion and rename gating are preserved untouched.

## Acceptance coverage (#79265)

- Expected 404 from the session probe ladder no longer prints an ipcMain "Error occurred in handler" stack trace
- Every other `hermes:api` handler failure still logs in full (the sentinel is the only bypassed case; non-404 failures still hit `rememberLog(formatApiRequestFailure(...))`)
- 5 unit tests on the sentinel seam: narrow-sentinel discrimination (backend payloads can't be mistaken for one), unwrap rethrows the identical message, non-sentinel pass-through

## Tests

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run electron/api-expected-404.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` on the rebased branch: **5 passed, 0 failed**.
- Sibling suites on the same tree: `session-pin-sync` + `gateway-switch` **40 passed** (probe consumers unchanged); the PR's test file against pristine `origin/main`: **red** (`Cannot find module './api-expected-404'`).
- `npx tsc -p . --noEmit`: **exit 0**.

## Supersedes

- Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/79266 — the contributor's single commit cherry-picked with authorship kept; the branch had drifted (a merge of an old main plus unrelated in-flight commits), so the server-side rebase hit conflicts and a replacement branch was opened per the landing policy. Thanks @hernanda-git.

Fixes #79265

## What does this PR do?

Bumps the `hindsight` catalog pin from `176f8c2` (v1.0.1) to `eb021da3` (vectorize-io/hindsight main) so `local_embedded` works on PM-managed Hermes, and removes the `known_issues` entry that said it doesn't.

## Root cause

Two scanner blind spots in the skills security guard, plus a swallowed scan verdict on the TUI-gateway install RPC (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/63307):

1. `destructive_home_rm` matched only a literal `$HOME` — `rm -rf ~/Documents` (bare tilde) scanned **safe** for every trust tier.
2. No pattern keyed on the `` !`cmd` `` inline-shell auto-exec DSL that `agent/skill_preprocessing.py` expands via `bash -c` on skill view/load when `skills.inline_shell` is enabled — a skill carrying `` !`rm -rf ~/Documents` `` scanned safe, then detonated on the next view.
3. `tui_gateway/methods_tools.py::_skills_install` ran `do_install(skip_confirm=True)` with a sink console and unconditionally returned `installed: True` — a security-scan block read as success to every RPC caller.

## What changes

- `tools/skills_guard.py`:
  - `destructive_home_rm` now matches bare-tilde forms (`~/`, `~ `, `~*`, `~$`) in addition to `$HOME`, for both `rm` and `rmdir`.
  - New `inline_shell_exec` THREAT_PATTERN (high, execution) for `` !`cmd` `` snippets; requires a non-space payload so a skill that merely documents the DSL (`!` `` with no command) is not flagged.
  - `SCANNER_VERSION` bumped to `skills-guard-v7` so cached safe verdicts are invalidated and quarantined/hub rescans pick up the new findings.
- `tui_gateway/methods_tools.py`: `skills.manage` install now keys its response off `do_install`'s verdict — `installed: True` only on a real install; a failure answers an error envelope (code 5031) whose message and `data.log` carry the printed tail (the scan-block message, the ambiguity candidate table, or the fetch failure) instead of discarding it into a sink.
- The Desktop one-click hub install path is covered by the companion PR's non-zero exit on failed installs (`hub-actions.ts` already parses the spawned CLI's exit code into a blocked/failure toast).

Deliberately NOT in this PR: trust-scoping the `skills.inline_shell` config flag (issue Part A1). The flag is documented as an explicit opt-in for trusted sources only; changing its scope is a design decision for maintainers, and the scanner pattern makes the risk visible at install time either way.

## Tests (prove red → green)

`unset PYTHONPATH && scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tools/test_skills_guard.py tests/tui_gateway/test_skills_manage_install.py`

- On `origin/main` (sources reverted, new tests kept): **6 failed** — bare-~ detection, inline-shell snippet detection, the pattern-shape test, the cache-invalidation regression, and both RPC failure tests (`installed: True` returned on scan-block/decline).
- With the fix: **64 passed, 0 failed** across both files.
- Sibling guard suites stay green: `tests/tools/test_skills_guard_agent_config.py tests/skills/test_openclaw_migration.py tests/agent/test_project_skills.py` — 64 passed, 0 failed.

New coverage: bare-~ `rm -rf` detection, inline-shell snippet detection, pattern-shape precision (plain code spans / markdown images / empty DSL markers not flagged), scanner-version cache invalidation (a verdict cached under the prior version is rescanned and returns the new finding — the cache stays useful when version and content are unchanged), and the RPC contract (success → `installed: true`; scan-block → 5031 error with the verdict tail; declined/no-op → not reported as installed).

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/63325 — rebased onto scanner v6 (→ v7; the PR's v1→v2 hunk no longer applied) and extended with the cache-invalidation regression test the 2026-07-24 triage comment required, plus the RPC verdict-surfacing leg. Thanks @liuhao1024 for the original patterns and tests.

## Limitations

- The desktop hub's separate on-demand scan UI is unchanged; this PR guarantees the *install-time* verdict can no longer be swallowed on any path.

raw.body:
Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/122206

## Root cause

Three gaps together strand the Desktop app through a legitimately long or failed source-update completion:

1. **The boot update gate polls only the update marker** (`update-gate.ts`): a `hermes update` that failed during preparation (uv sync network error) can exit with the marker left pointing at a dead or recycled pid — `readLiveUpdateMarker`'s liveness probe keeps answering true on Windows — so `waitForUpdateClearance` parks the full 20-minute `UPDATE_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS` on an updater that already finished with a failure (486 silent polls measured in the issue).
2. **The 90s cold-start port-announce budget kills a healthy repair** (`backend-ready.ts`): when the backend is finishing an owed source-update tail before `hermes serve` starts, the tail legitimately runs minutes (dependency sync measured at 19–22 min) — killing the child mid-repair and respawning re-runs the repair from scratch on every boot.
3. **Relaunch-driven completion retries are unbounded** (`venv_sync.py`): a tail that keeps failing re-runs on every launch ("every launch burns ~4 minutes") with no backoff or cap.

## What changes

- **`update-gate.ts`** — a fourth, optional gate signal `hasFailedReceipt` (the cross-process update receipt; only a TERMINAL `failed` outcome counts, `running` still parks, `partial` keeps the install usable). It outranks a live marker as the reported reason (`failed-receipt`), and `waitForUpdateClearance` gains an `abandonOn` callback returning a new `'abandoned'` outcome instead of parking. `main.ts`'s boot path wires it via `readLatestSyncReceipt()`, logs the decision, skips the swapped-bundle relaunch (the update never succeeded), and proceeds with the backend start so the existing failure dialog carries the recovery guidance. Older callers and the pool spawn path (not user-visible) keep the historical parking behavior when the dep is omitted.
- **`backend-ready.ts`** — while the child prints venv_sync's source-completion banners, the port-announce deadline is re-armed: a 5-minute grace re-armed per banner, capped at a 30-minute total (resolved against the real wall clock — `process.hrtime` — so a faked `Date.now()` in tests can't defeat the cap). A banner present in the spawn-time buffered tail seeds the same re-arm. Past the cap the timeout fires with the banner text in the message: truthful and actionable.
- **`venv_sync.py`** — completion-tail retries are recorded in an attempts file beside the pending marker (same lifetime, same install scope): after 2 consecutive failures the tail waits out a 15-minute backoff window before retrying, and past 6 attempts it stops self-starting entirely — the launch keeps the marker, prints one line pointing at `hermes update`, and boots. Success clears both the marker and the record. An unreadable/corrupt record degrades to the historical unbounded behavior (bookkeeping must never block boot).

## Acceptance coverage (#122206)

- Desktop no longer parks 20 minutes behind a receipt that already says failed; it boots the current build and surfaces the terminal failure.
- A multi-minute completion repair ahead of `hermes serve` is not killed and re-run per boot (bounded by a real-clock cap so a truly wedged tail still times out truthfully).
- A repeatedly failing tail backs off and finally stops self-starting, leaving the obligation to an explicit `hermes update`.

## Tests

- **Red on base** — on a clean `origin/main` worktree with only the new test file copied in: `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 --file-timeout 1200 tests/pm/test_source_update_launch.py -k 'retry_backoff_and_cap or capped_completion_attempts or failed_tail_attempt'` → **3 failed** (ImportError: `_completion_attempts_path` missing, as expected on base).
- **Green with fix** — same command in the fix worktree → **3 passed**. Full files locally: `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 --file-timeout 1200 tests/pm/test_source_update_launch.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_launch_completion.py` → **46 passed (19 + 27)**, including the pre-existing `test_failed_completion_tail_is_retried_without_rebuilding_dependencies` contract (first failure still retries on the next launch; the test now ages the record past the backoff window before the successful retry).
- Electron gate/port-wait tests: `npx vitest run electron/update-gate.test.ts electron/backend-ready.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` → **42 passed (2 files)**, covering the failed-receipt reason ranking, abandonOn (immediate, mid-wait, declining), the banner re-arm past the original timeout, the 30-min cap, and the spawn-time-tail seeding.
- `python scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all` → clean.

## Limitations

- Windows-specific marker liveness behavior (the recycled-pid probe) can't be exercised on this macOS host; the failed-receipt signal is platform-independent, but the Windows reporter's exact stale-marker sequence is unverified here.
- The in-app "finish the owed completion" recovery action from the issue's requirements is UX follow-up; this PR makes the failure visible and non-blocking instead of silently parking.

raw.body:
## Root cause

`isInstalled()` in `apps/desktop/src/app/capabilities/catalog/skill-catalog.tsx` falls back to `catalog.skillsByName.has(entry.name)` for every catalog row. That guarantee ("skills install by name, so a same-named entry can never be added beside the installed one") only holds for first-party namespaces — public community feeds carry **distinct** skills reusing popular names (`docx`, `xlsx`, `pdf`). Every community lookalike of an installed skill rendered with the installed ✓, an ON/disabled `CatalogInstallSwitch`, passed the **Installed** facet, and polluted "More like this" (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/126072).

## What changes

- `catalog-browser.tsx` gains an optional `isSuperseded(entry)` predicate; when provided, superseded rows are dropped from the **visible** set before `filterCatalog`/facet counts/`catalogSources`/`catalogTags`/sort options/selection operate on it — so hidden rows leave the Installed facet, the ✓/ON state, and "More like this" together.
- `skill-catalog.tsx` defines `isSuperseded`: a **community** row (non-official source, not an `installed:` merged row) whose name is taken by an installed skill. Official rows keep the legacy name match so behavior pinned by existing specs is unchanged — the same rule 0150fb3a85 already applies to same-named official optional rows.

## Tests (prove red → green)

`cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 --testTimeout=120000 src/app/capabilities/index.test.tsx`

- On `origin/main` (source reverted, new test kept): **1 failed** — two `docx` rows rendered (bundled + community lookalike both matching the installed name).
- With the fix: **11 passed, 0 failed**.

New spec: bundled `docx` installed + a ClawHub `docx` feed row → exactly one `docx` row; the distinct community skill (`gif-search`) stays installable.

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/126072

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/126136 — rebased onto current main (cherry-picked cleanly; no source changes needed). Thanks @kokhlo.

## Limitations

- Hiding (rather than identity-matching the toggle) is the coherent fix because skills install by name: a same-named community skill can never coexist with the installed one, so it is neither the installed skill nor installable beside it.

raw.body:
## Root cause

The pre-send stale-transcript guard treats *any* remote-ahead transcript as a competing view. When a turn dies on an approval timeout (or completes without streaming its tool rows back), the server keeps the turn's residue rows under durable ids this window never saw — the window holds only its optimistic user message under a local id. The graft can't anchor, `authoredMessageCount` reports the window behind, and `submit.ts` refuses the send with the "Chat out of date" dialog — on every send, in a single-window setup where the dialog's "another view" text is false. The state self-heals after minutes, so the refusal adds no value in the own-residue case.

## What changes

- `stale-transcript-guard.ts`: new `surplusIsCompetingView(local, refreshed)` — a user row is *known* when its durable id, stored `rowId`, or text matches a local one; only an unaccounted **user** row is another view's message. New `transcriptRefreshIfBehind()` returns `{ messages, competingView }`.
- `submit.ts`: the pre-send guard now refuses (dialog + release) only when `competingView` is true. This window's own turn residue grafts silently into the view and the send proceeds.
- Tests: new `surplusIsCompetingView` coverage — approval-timeout turn-death residue with an unreconciled optimistic user row, a plain completed tool turn (single-window, issue comment 2), unknown-text user row = competing view, rowId/id matching, assistant/tool-only surplus. The existing #65047 notice-length and #125975 tip-compare regressions are kept intact.

## Acceptance coverage per issue

- #124005: own turn residue (approval-timeout death, completed tool turn, reconnect drift with no foreign user row) grafts silently and sends — covered. Refusal is reserved for a genuine competing view (unaccounted user row from another window) — covered. Single-window tool-using turns no longer trip the guard — covered.

## Tests run

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/lib/stale-transcript-guard.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` — **red on origin/main** (5 new tests fail: `surplusIsCompetingView` does not exist there), **green with fix** (11/11 passed).
- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/ --maxWorkers=2` — 265/265 passed (submit-path sibling suites).
- `cd apps/desktop && npx tsc -p . --noEmit` — exit 0.

Fixes #124005

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/126598 — the fix hunks are cherry-picked from it verbatim. Thanks @Sahilvishnaliya.

raw.body:
## Root cause

On local connections, `workspaceCwdKey()` returned the single key `hermes.desktop.workspace-cwd` for every profile. Picking a project in profile A wrote A's folder there. Switching to profile B:

- `$currentCwd` was reseeded from the same key.
- When B had nothing remembered, `ensureDefaultWorkspaceCwd` left the live cwd alone.

Either way, B's new chats started in A's project and got auto-grouped under it in the sidebar.

## Change

- Named local profiles remember their workspace under `hermes.desktop.workspace-cwd.profile.<encoded>`. The default profile keeps the bare key, so single-profile users are unaffected and nothing needs migrating. This follows the `connection-scoped.ts` contract ("local keeps the bare key"). Remote keys are unchanged.
- An empty memory on the local reseed now clears the live cwd, matching the remote branch (#114306). A profile with nothing remembered no longer inherits the outgoing profile's folder.

This takes the per-profile idea from #96844 by @liuhao1024. Unlike that PR, it doesn't discard the legacy key, which would have reset every single-profile user's remembered workspace.

## Tests

- `session.test.ts`: per-profile keying (default keeps the bare key; A and B are isolated), and a switch to a profile with no memory clears A's folder while switching back restores it.
- vitest `store/session.test.ts` plus the neighbouring suites: all pass. `tsc --noEmit` clean.

Auto-merge off: this changes where new chats start on a profile switch.

Fixes #96834

Co-authored-by: liuhao1024 <sunsky.lau@gmail.com>

raw.body:
## Root cause

Two stacked defects kept a fully configured install flashing the blocking onboarding overlay ("No usable credentials found for openrouter") after every update restart:

1. **Wrong blame** — `tui_gateway/methods_config.py` `setup.runtime_check`, without an explicit `provider`, runs the startup pin and then the configured fallback chain. When the chain only resolves at its tail, `runtime` stops there and the failure text named that tail provider — one the user never pinned.
2. **Race downgrade + skip erase** — an update restart re-opens the backend before its external secret source (BWS-backed `.env`) hydrates, so the probe *answers* `ok:false` a few seconds after boot. `refreshOnboarding` wrote that transient as a durable `configured:false` and deleted the onboarded cache; and `completeDesktopOnboarding` cleared the persisted "choose a provider later" skip on ANY completion, so a later not-ready round re-armed the blocking picker on every launch.

## What changes

- **Pin attribution** (from #124963 by @liuhao1024): the failure names the pinned provider — explicit request, else the startup env pin, else the config `model.provider` — falling back to the resolved route only when nothing is pinned.
- **Skip lifecycle** (from #113988 by @sly321-pixel): `completeDesktopOnboarding(connected)` clears the "choose later" skip only on user-driven completions (provider connect, local endpoint, model confirm); a passive readiness round leaves it. The overlay's skip gate lets `requested` (a real credential wall) outrank the skip, and treats an unresolved (`null`) readiness state as still-booting.
- **Boot-race guard** (new): `$gatewayBootGeneration` in `live-sync.ts` (bumped by `setup.ready` and gateway switch/wipe) plus a 15 s grace in the onboarding store: inside the window, an answered `runtime_check` `ok:false` against an already-configured install is preserved as not-ready and re-checked on the `setup.ready` tick — never written down as `configured:false`. Outside the window, or on an unconfigured install, the verdict still lands.
- The fallback notice (`runtime-not-ready`) is now only shown when a previously verified install lost its backend, not on every cold launch.

## Test evidence

Red on origin/main (`7cadfaa668`):

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py -k setup_runtime_check -j 2
  × test_setup_runtime_check_failure_names_the_configured_pin_not_the_chain_tail
    (provider reported 'openrouter', the chain tail — expected the pin 'zai')
npx vitest run src/store/onboarding.test.ts  (boot-race scenario)
  × a boot-window ok:false must not downgrade a configured install
    (configured downgraded to false, onboarded cache wiped)
```

Green with the fix:

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py -k setup_runtime_check -j 2
  → 9 tests passed, 0 failed
npx vitest run src/store/onboarding.test.ts src/components/onboarding/skip-gate.test.tsx
  → 29 passed (incl. boot-race preserve, downgrade-after-grace, skip persistence,
     credential-wall outranks skip, fallback keeps unknown)
```

## Limitations

- Requirement 3 of the issue (gateway-side retryable "external secret source not yet hydrated" classification) is left as optional hardening; the renderer-side guard closes the user-visible loop without it.
- The 15 s grace is sized to the observed ~2–5 s BWS hydration; a slower secret source could still flash if a probe answers after the window, but the `setup.ready` re-check then corrects it.

## Credit

- Pin attribution from #124963 by @liuhao1024 (cherry-picked, authorship preserved as committer credit via Co-authored-by after the push hook required a GitHub-ownable email).
- Skip-lifecycle gate from #113988 by @sly321-pixel (`Co-authored-by`).
- Supersedes both.

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/124939

raw.body:
## Root cause

The Desktop artifact registry enforces only count caps (40 sessions × 24 artifacts × 20 versions), which still admits up to 19,200 unbounded `ArtifactVersion.content` strings. The registry is an additional strong in-memory owner of every retained version while the transcript remains the durable copy, so a session that repeatedly regenerates large HTML/SVG/code artifacts pins unbounded MB in `$artifactRegistry` with no content-size accounting anywhere.

## Fix

Enforce a global 4 Mi UTF-16 code-unit budget inside `pruneRegistry()`, after the existing count caps:

- Evict the globally-oldest **historical** versions first; every record's latest version survives that pass.
- If latest-only records still exceed the budget, evict the oldest whole records. The registry's single newest record is always retained, even when it alone is oversized.
- Never truncate or rewrite content — eviction removes whole version entries / whole records only. Evicted cards re-register on render; the transcript stays the durable source.
- Reconcile `$artifactVersionSelection` by the selected version's hash (captured before pruning) so a pinned surviving version keeps pointing at the same content after index shifts; an evicted selection snaps back to newest (absent = newest).

## Coverage

Fixes #108172

All five regression cases from the report:
- over-budget versions evict oldest history first (newest byte-exact)
- cumulative retained content falls under the budget, including the latest-only whole-record case
- the single newest record survives even when it alone exceeds the budget
- a pinned selection follows its hash when pruning shifts version indexes
- existing count/dedupe/session-scoping/open-preview tests unchanged (12 existing tests still pass)

## Checks run

- `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/store/artifacts.test.ts` — 16/16 passed (12 existing + 4 new)
- RED on base: same suite with `origin/main`'s `artifacts.ts` — the 3 eviction/hash tests fail, proving the budget is what makes them pass
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` (apps/desktop) — clean

Design credit: the deleted PR #108178 (by @KoNit-K) proposed this exact shape — budget applied post-count-caps, hash-based selection reconciliation, focused vitest cases. This PR implements that design fresh against current `main` (the original branch is gone, so no commit could be cherry-picked).

Closes #108172

raw.body:
## Root cause

`captureSteeringSession` (added by #117131) refuses whenever route/selection/runtime disagree, with no bridge for the brief window after a stored-id rotation when the runtime binds the new tip before the sessions list exposes its lineage. In that window steerDraft re-queues silently and no RPC leaves the renderer — the composer swallows the steer and the "Steer" button is a no-op (#119021, regression from #117131).

## What changes

Cherry-picked from #119037 (authorship kept, 3 commits) onto current `origin/main`:

- `rotationBridgesUnloadedTip` in `steering-session.ts` — a rotation record matching runtime + previous selection + bound id bridges the gap when the refreshed session row has not loaded yet, or when the previous tip was evicted from the session list before the rotation event was consumed.
- Owner fallback to the previous stored id.
- `use-session-actions` keeps the rotation proof available for steering instead of consuming it when focus briefly moves to an unrelated tile — consuming early is exactly what killed the bridge window.

## Root cause

The Desktop routes a session that cannot start for lack of a configured provider by matching the error **sentence** — and the sentences moved. `provider-setup-errors.ts` matched `No (?:inference|Hermes) provider configured`, but agent init actually raises:

- `No LLM provider configured. Run `hermes model`…` (`agent/agent_init.py`, blank install) — ❌ not matched
- `Provider 'openai' is set in config.yaml but no API key was found…` (`missing_provider_credentials_message`) — ❌ not matched

Both reach the client wrapped in `agent_init_failed_message`, and the gateway error event carried no machine-readable code, so all three client gates (status.ts toast routing, onboarding.ts submit-time prompt blocking, onboarding overlay raw-sentence suppression) fell through to a generic dead-end toast (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/119388).

## What changes

- `agent/auxiliary_unavailable.py`: new `ProviderNotConfiguredError(RuntimeError)` type (subclass, so existing `except RuntimeError` handlers keep catching it). Both "cannot serve this session" paths in `agent_init._routed_client_kwargs` now raise it.
- `tui_gateway/server.py`: the agent-build failure `error` event stamps `code: "provider_not_configured"` when the exception is that type. The sentence still reaches the reader; the code survives rewording.
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/provider-setup-errors.ts`: `isProviderSetupErrorCode(code)` (preferred), plus the sentence fallback extended to match both agent-init shapes — and deliberately NOT the auxiliary-model warning ("No auxiliary LLM provider configured"), which is not a provider-setup failure.
- `status.ts` prefers the gateway code, then the sentence. Older gateways without the code keep working via the fallback.

## Tests (prove red → green)

Desktop: `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 --testTimeout=120000 src/lib/provider-setup-errors.test.ts src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event/status.test.ts`
- On `origin/main` (sources reverted, new tests kept): **4 failed** (both sentence shapes unrecognized; code-based routing absent; unrelated-failure guard).
- With the fix: **13 passed, 0 failed**.

Python: `unset PYTHONPATH && scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tui_gateway/test_provider_not_configured_code.py`
- On `origin/main`: ImportError (`ProviderNotConfiguredError` does not exist).
- With the fix: **5 passed, 0 failed** — the error event carries the code only for this type, both raise paths raise it, unrelated build failures carry no code, and the type stays a `RuntimeError`.

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/119388

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/119390 — rebased onto current main (cherry-picked cleanly, no source changes needed). Thanks @rodricksz4h5.

## Limitations

- Renderer tolerates older gateways (no `code` on the error event) via the extended sentence fallback.

raw.body:
## Root cause

Composer-queue mutators built the session's next queue from the window's own in-memory atom copy (`writeSession` replaced the whole per-session list), so a same-session concurrent write from a window whose `storage` event had not fired yet was clobbered — a queued prompt could be LOST. And the background auto-drain's guard (`drainingSessionIdsRef`) is renderer-local, so two idle windows could both pick the same head entry and submit it — the gateway queues the second copy server-side and runs it as its own turn (#123249, races surfaced by #122953's cross-window sync).

## What changes

Cherry-picked from #123250 (authorship kept, 2 commits) onto current `origin/main`:

- `mutateSession(sid, op)` applies every queue op to the live persisted queue (re-read from storage), with a `storageCurrent` fallback flag so a quota/unavailable-storage failure degrades to in-memory without breaking the queue (#69638's concern).
- `withQueueDrainClaim` — a per-session Web Lock arbitrates the drain across windows (re-reads the queue inside the claim; a window that waited finds the entry gone and sends nothing). ChatBar auto-drain re-locates its entry by id and does not count "already sent elsewhere" as a failure. Runtime-checked and falls back gracefully where `navigator.locks` is absent.
- Graft fix: main's #98015 budget helpers (`noteQueuedPromptDrainFailure`/`clearQueuedPromptDrainFailures`) were left calling the removed `writeSession` after the graft — ReferenceError at drain time. Converted both to `mutateSession`, which also makes the budget merge-safe across windows.

#122953's cross-window sync and #78456's watch-window exclusion are preserved (both suites pass).

## Tests

- `npx vitest run src/store/composer-queue.test.ts src/app/session/hooks/use-background-queue-drain.test.tsx --maxWorkers=2` — on `origin/main` (PR tests grafted): **2 failed** (exactly the two races: same-session double-queue, double drain), 44 passed; with branch: **48 passed**.
- `npx vitest run src/app/session/hooks/use-background-queue-preservation.test.tsx --maxWorkers=2` — 18 passed.
- `npx vitest run src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/index.test.tsx --maxWorkers=2` — 137 passed.
- `npx vitest run src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-queue.test.tsx --maxWorkers=2` — 12 passed.

raw.body:
Fixes #119111 — `hermes_cli.windows_ssh_runtime write-lock` takes the ownership
ID as its single argv element and reads the lock JSON on **stdin**
(`hermes_cli/windows_ssh_runtime.py` dispatch raises `invalid operation` on an
arity mismatch). The desktop's atomic Windows spawn command appended `$lock` as
a second positional argument instead of piping it, so every reservation-backed
Windows SSH backend spawn was rejected with `{"error":"invalid operation"}` and
the backend could never claim ownership of its process.

## Root cause

`apps/desktop/electron/windows-remote-lifecycle.ts:281` — the reservation
branch built `& <python> -m hermes_cli.windows_ssh_runtime write-lock
'<ownershipId>' $lock|Out-Null`, passing the lock JSON as argv; the trailing
`|Out-Null` shows the pipe was meant to carry it.

## What changed

- `windows-remote-lifecycle.ts` — pipe the serialized ownership record into the
  `write-lock` helper's stdin (`$lock | & … write-lock '<ownershipId>' | Out-Null`),
  preserving the ownership-ID argument, non-zero-exit propagation, and
  `$spawnLines|Write-Output`.
- `windows-remote-lifecycle.test.ts` — the spawn script shape test now asserts
  the stdin pipeline (`$lock | & … write-lock`) and forbids the old
  `$lock`-as-argv form.

The non-reservation `helper()` path already passed JSON via `stdinData`
correctly; only `atomicWindowsSpawnCommand`'s reservation branch was affected.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/119113 (KoNit-K) — carried
  the exact correct hunk; this PR re-lands it on current main with the same
  test. All credit to @KoNit-K; please close that PR in favour of this one.

## How to test

- RED on base: the new shape assertion fails 1/15 against `origin/main`
  (`write-lock … $lock|Out-Null` — lock JSON as argv).
- `cd apps/desktop && ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run --project electron electron/windows-remote-lifecycle.test.ts` — **15/15 passed**.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` (apps/desktop) — clean.
- eslint + prettier on both touched files — clean.

Fixes #119111

raw.body:
## Root cause

The right Files rail keyed its tree off the app-global `$currentCwd` +
`$workspaceCwdOwner`/`$selectedStoredSessionId` pair (the MAIN pane's selection),
while tile focus is a separate derivation (`$focusedStoredSessionId`) nothing
wired into the rail. Focusing tile B never rebinds the rail: it keeps showing
A's directory, and file operations act on that stale root.

Two adjacent gaps in the same chain:

- `$focusedStoredSessionId` fell back to the primary's selection whenever the
  interaction tracker sat on sidebar/tool chrome, so clicking into the Files
  rail dropped the on-screen tile's identity.
- the primary session whose cwd owner had not (yet) been confirmed showed an
  empty rail even when the session row knew the folder.

## Fix

Cherry-picked from #98652 (@pyr0ken) with conflicts resolved against current
main:

- Rebind the rail to a new `$focusedWorkspaceCwd` derivation: the focused
  tile's cwd (live session state, then the stored session row), else the
  primary's confirmed workspace cwd, with a session-row fallback when the
  owner check has not confirmed yet. No workspace → the rail's empty state
  ("No project open") as before.
- `$focusedStoredSessionId` retains the active main-zone tile while the
  interaction tracker sits on side chrome (files, terminal, sessions list,
  bots roster), so clicking sidebar chrome does not drop the on-screen session.
- The rail registers its active cwd with the repo-status watcher and refreshes
  git change tints along with the tree on multi-cwd switches and manual
  refreshes.
- The session.info writer gating stays as-is: background tiles still never
  re-point the global `$currentCwd` (the composer's coding rail is untouched).

Single-pane users see no change: when the primary pane is focused the new
derivation resolves to the same confirmed pair as before.

## Coverage

- #79506 — Files rail follows the focused session tile; empty hint when
  the focused session has no cwd; sidebar file operations act on the displayed
  (focused) folder.
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/79724 — right Files rail
  requirement is the same root cause and is covered by this PR; the issue also
  asks for the left sessions sidebar's project grouping to follow focus and a
  broader per-tile workspace redesign, which remain open product questions.

## Checks

- `npx vitest run src/store/session-states.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` — 96 passed
- `npx vitest run src/app/right-sidebar/index.test.tsx src/store/coding-status.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` — 18 passed
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/desktop` — clean
- The focused-tile tests fail on base: `$focusedWorkspaceCwd` does not exist
  there and the rail consumed `$currentCwd` directly.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/98652 — thanks @pyr0ken
  (its branch could not be rebased as-is; the four fix commits are cherry-picked here)
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/85999 — thanks @x7peeps
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/95587 — thanks @arthurbkeller
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/96982 — thanks @bardioc1977

Fixes #79506
Fixes #79724

## Root cause

A `providers.<built-in-slug>` block carrying **settings only** (no `base_url`/`url`/`api` — e.g. `providers.openai-codex: {request_timeout_seconds: 3600}`) silently re-routed model validation into the custom-endpoint branch, hard-rejecting the model (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/120020). Two layers, both on current main:

1. **Resolver (root rung):** `resolve_user_provider` returned a `source="user-config"` `ProviderDef` with `base_url=""` for ANY dict under `providers.<name>` — an empty `openai_chat`/`api_key` stub that shadowed the built-in overlay's real transport/auth (`bedrock_converse`/`aws_sdk` for Bedrock; the documented tuning path `providers.bedrock: {stale_timeout_seconds: 600}` broke Bedrock the same way, #110402).
2. **Switch guard (second layer):** `_validate_switch` remapped `validate_as` to `custom:<slug>` purely on `pdef.source == "user-config"`, with no endpoint check — so `openai-codex` (whose endpoint exposes no `/models` listing) got the generic `GET {base}/models` probe and a hard reject on every assignment path (CLI `/model --provider`, desktop Settings, desktop onboarding confirm — all funnel through `_validated_main_model_selection` → `switch_model`).

## What changes (consolidation of the four open PRs on this defect class)

- `hermes_cli/providers.py` — `resolve_user_provider` requires a real endpoint before resolving an entry; a settings-only block is tuning for a built-in of the same name and falls through to `resolve_provider_full`'s built-in overlay. Covers switch, picker, and onboarding paths at once. (from #112034)
- `hermes_cli/model_switch.py` — `_validate_switch` only remaps to the custom branch when the user-config entry declares a `base_url` (mirrors `_lap_lmstudio_row`'s endpoint test). Cheap second layer, still correct against `custom_providers`-sourced pdefs. (from #121171)

Blocks that DO declare an endpoint keep overriding/routing as custom — pinned by tests on both layers.

Deliberately not taken: #120854's resolver variant (its `get_provider`-based semantics differ subtly — it would still resolve a non-built-in settings-only block as user-config; #112034's rule is cleaner) and #101730's picker-row guard (targets the separate #101711 phantom-row symptom and its context has drifted far from main; the resolver fix already prevents the stub pdef from existing).

## Tests (prove red → green)

`unset PYTHONPATH && scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_cli/test_user_provider_timeout_only_entry.py tests/hermes_cli/test_settings_only_provider_block_validation.py`

- With the fix: **6 passed, 0 failed** (the 2 endpoint-bearing pins pass on both).
- Sibling suites stay green: `test_user_providers_model_switch.py` (17), `test_custom_provider_model_switch.py` + `test_model_switch_configured_provider_routing.py` (25) — 0 failed.

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/120020

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/112034 — resolver rule + Bedrock regression, taken as the root fix. Thanks @Bardioc1977.
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/121171 — switch-path guard + hermetic Codex suite, kept as the second layer. Thanks @Finn763.

## Limitations

- #120854 and #101730 remain open for their maintainers to close; neither is required for this fix.

raw.body:
fix(desktop): give every new chat its own draft key instead of a shared __new__ bucket

## Root cause

`draftKey()` in `apps/desktop/src/store/composer.ts` mapped every null/empty
scope to the single `NEW_SESSION_DRAFT_KEY = '__new__'` bucket, so all
concurrent unsaved "New Chat" sessions read and wrote one shared draft stash.
Opening a second new chat showed (and could overwrite) the first one's unsent
text.

## What changes

- `store/session.ts` holds a persisted, per-instance `$freshDraftKey`
  (`__new__:<uuid>`); `rotateFreshDraftKey()` runs on every genuinely-new-chat
  lifecycle, so each unsaved chat gets an isolated draft bucket.
- `store/composer.ts` threads the active fresh key through
  `draftKey()`/`getDraftIds()`, and the re-homing paths
  (`announceNewSessionDraftKey`/`adoptNewSessionDraft`/`adoptGoneSessionDraft`
  / `migrateSessionDraft`) now address the *active* fresh-draft key instead of
  the literal `'__new__'`, so migrated text still follows the first send into
  the persisted session.
- Composer / route-resume / session-actions seams pass the fresh key through
  so drafts survive reloads and re-home on first send.

Supersedes #67197 (rebased onto the `a4b48064b1b` announcement-based re-homing
seams that landed after it was authored). #62586 touched only the hook layer
and could not isolate two new chats at the store level, so it is covered by
this store-level fix.

## Acceptance coverage

- #66662: two concurrent new chats no longer share draft text (isolation +
  rotation tests in `store/session.test.ts`, `store/composer.test.ts`); draft
  re-homing for persisted sessions preserved (route-resume / session-actions /
  use-composer-draft tests). Full: `Fixes #66662`.
- #62586: partial — same symptom family, hook-layer only; superseded by the
  store-level keying here.

## Tests

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/store/session.test.ts
  src/store/composer.test.ts src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-draft.test.tsx
  src/app/session/hooks/use-route-resume.test.tsx src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions.test.tsx --maxWorkers=2`
  — with fix (rebased onto current main): **5 files / 304 tests passed**.
- Same scope on `origin/main` (red check, isolated worktree): **9 tests
  failed** (fresh-draft identity rotation/persistence, two-new-chat isolation,
  re-home-through-active-lifecycle-key) — the suite is red on main and green
  with the fix.

## Credit

Thanks @deniqlab for the original per-instance fresh-key design and tests in
#67197 (commits cherry-picked with authorship kept), and @pushpitkamboj for
the earlier hook-layer investigation in #62586.

raw.body:
## Summary

A desktop that *attached* to an externally supervised backend (launchd `KeepAlive`, not a child of the app) adopted the local served session token once at boot and never re-read it. The 15s liveness monitor probed with the stale token only — but `/api/health` is a public route, so a backend recycled by its supervisor into a new process (serving a brand-new served token) still answered 200: the probe passed while every authenticated call 401'd forever. Child-exit recovery can never fire for a backend the app did not spawn, so both recovery triggers were blind to this state. This is https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/121988.

Two changes (cherry-picked from @chelsealong's #122056, rebased onto current main):

- **Detect token drift, not just liveness**: every monitor tick re-reads the served token (`resolveServedDashboardToken`) and `isAttachedBackendTokenDrifted` treats drift the same as "gone", routing into the existing supervisor recovery path that re-runs discovery and re-adopts the token on respawn.
- **Don't suppress the attach-monitor's own recovery claim**: the recovery handler now clears the slot via `backendConnectionState.invalidate()` instead of `invalidatePrimaryConnection()` — the latter also sets `primaryRecoverySuppressed`, which `scheduleUnexpectedPrimaryRecovery()` would read back as intentional teardown and refuse to claim, leaving the app with no backend *and* no respawn scheduled (a regression the first commit alone would have introduced).

## Acceptance coverage

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/121988 — recycled attached backend detected on the next tick (requirement 1); recovery runs the existing supervisor re-discovery/re-adopt path (requirement 2); the recovery claim is not swallowed by the intentional-teardown latch (requirement 3, pinned by a regression test that fails without the second commit).

## Test plan

- Red on base (`47310227c2`, fix's tests checked out over main): `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run electron/dashboard-token.test.ts electron/backend-exit-recovery.test.ts` → **1 failed / 19 passed** (`isAttachedBackendTokenDrifted is not a function`).
- Green with fix (head `e578c6d0`, rebased): same command → **20 passed**.
- The rebase conflict in `main.ts` (HEAD changed `waitForHermes`'s call signature with `{ alreadyBound: true }`) was resolved by keeping the PR's drift-chained probe with main's current signature semantics.

CI: not run (CI down).

Fixes #121988 — full URL: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/121988

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/122056 (rebased onto current main after its `main.ts` conflict; authorship preserved via cherry-pick).

Thanks @chelsealong.

raw.body:
## Root cause

The titlebar's left hide/show button stayed pane-bound (`toggleSidebarOpen`)
while commit 0c208aa7ec made the right button positional (`toggleRightSide`,
resolving the physically-right column from the live tree). After the "Swap the
session and file browser sides" flip the sessions pane sits physically right,
so both edge buttons acted on the sessions column and the physically-left file
tree was unreachable from the titlebar — contradicting the titlebar's own
"POSITIONAL toggles" contract in `titlebar-controls.tsx`.

## Fix

Add `toggleLeftSide()` as the exact mirror of `toggleRightSide()`:

- resolve the outermost root-row column left of main from the live tree
  (`leftSideGroup()`), fold/unfold it through the tree's zone minimize so it
  round-trips like the rail chevron;
- reopen a side-collapsed column through its owner store (sidebar or files,
  whichever owns the physical side) so the persisted flags stay truthful;
- fall back to the semantic sidebar branch when no leaf column lives left of
  main (main leftmost, or a nested split);

raw.body:
Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/87514
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/87536 (rebased + conflicts resolved, authorship kept via cherry-pick — thanks @jackulau)

## Root cause

`_is_ancestor_pid()` asked psutil for the whole parent chain at once:

```python
return any(parent.pid == pid for parent in psutil.Process().parents())
```

`parents()` materializes the entire chain before returning and only tolerates `NoSuchProcess` per link, so any unreadable process anywhere above us — `/proc/1` under firejail with `ptrace_scope=1`, hardened containers, yama — raises `AccessDenied` and discards the ancestors already collected. The update child then refused its own orchestrator's fresh marker and exited `UPDATE_EXIT_CONCURRENT` (2) on every GUI update, forever (the reporter's openSUSE Tumbleweed + firejail loop).

## What changes

- `hermes_cli/update_lock.py::_is_ancestor_pid` walks the chain **one link at a time**, testing each ancestor as it is discovered (`proc.parent()`), so a failure *above* the match can no longer hide it.
- `_MAX_ANCESTRY_DEPTH = 128` caps the walk; a seen-set guards against cycles.
- Contracts preserved: failure before any match still returns `False` (conservative refusal), our own pid is never an ancestor, psutil's create_time check keeps rejecting recycled pids, and the `ImportError` stdlib fallback (`-I -S -B` takeover child) is unchanged.
- Kept main's newer `os.getppid()` fast path and the `other_pid` fixture shape in the surrounding tests.

## Acceptance coverage (#87514)

- Hand-off child recognizes its own orchestrator's marker even when a process ABOVE the orchestrator is unreadable ✅ (`test_ancestor_below_an_unreadable_process_is_still_found`, `test_acquire_accepts_the_orchestrator_behind_an_unreadable_init` — the reporter's end-to-end symptom)
- Conservative refusal before a match preserved ✅ (`test_unreadable_process_below_the_match_still_refuses`)
- PID-reuse / no-self-pid guarantees preserved ✅ (`test_our_own_pid_is_never_an_ancestor`, seen-set + psutil create_time)
- Walk bounded ✅ (`test_walk_is_bounded`)

## Test results

Red on `origin/main` (regression class copied onto a detached main worktree):
`scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_cli/test_update_lock.py` → **31 passed, 4 failed** — the four `TestAncestryUnderUnreadableProcesses` sandbox tests fail exactly as the issue describes.

Green with the fix:
`scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_cli/test_update_lock.py` → **35 passed, 0 failed**.

## Limitations

End-to-end verification under a real firejail/yama environment is not possible from this host (macOS); the sandbox scenario is exercised with stubbed ancestry chains that raise `psutil.AccessDenied` at the exact link positions, both directions. The issue reporter offered to verify end-to-end once landed.

CI: not run (CI down).

## What this changes

Two fixes for the SSH route-identity drift that made an SSH-primary Desktop mislabel the live window as **"This device"** and force-spawn a phantom local backend even though it was connected to the remote.

## Root cause

1. **Cleared SSH fields could never be cleared.** `apps/desktop/src/app/settings/gateway-settings.tsx` (payload builder) serialized a cleared **Identity file** / **User** as `undefined`. Main merges SSH settings with `??` (`buildSshBlock` in `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts`), where `undefined` means *inherit the saved value* and only `''` means *cleared* — so a stale keyPath was refilled on every Save, and the form could never drop it.
2. **Drift heal's "already registered" test was weaker than the router's match.** `reconcileRegistryDrift` in `apps/desktop/electron/connection-registry.ts` treated a v1 SSH route as known on host/user/port alone (`normalizedSshTarget`), while the router tags the live window by the **full** route identity (`matchingConnectionId` in `connection-route-identity.ts` also compares keyPath, remoteHermesPath, remoteProfile). A v1 route carrying a keyPath the registered entry never had resolved to no connectionId — the untagged window read as the unscoped local device and the roster spawned a local child nobody asked for.

## What changed

- The Gateways form now sends an explicit `''` for cleared `sshUser`/`sshKeyPath`, so the `??` merge in main sees "cleared" and the stale identity file can actually be removed.
- `reconcileRegistryDrift` now, when the registered entry matches by target but the **full-identity** match fails, aligns the registered entry's identity fields (keyPath, remoteHermesPath, remoteProfile) with the route the app actually dials — via delete + assign so label, headers, and the user's primary pick survive untouched.

## Acceptance coverage (#103053)

- "A cleared SSH field can actually be cleared on save" — covered: `''` now wins the `??` merge.
- "Drift heal aligns the registered entry's identity with the v1 route so the router resolves the connectionId (no 'This device', no phantom local spawn)" — covered by the new regression test, which asserts `matchingConnectionId` resolves the drifted route to the registered entry's id after heal, and that clearing the keyPath re-aligns back.

## Tests

- `vitest run --project electron electron/connection-registry.test.ts` — 104 passed (new test included).
- The new drift-align test **fails on `origin/main`** (verified on a temp branch of main + the test file: `drifted.changed` stayed `false`) and passes with the fix.
- eslint + prettier clean on all three touched files; `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` in apps/desktop clean.

## Supersedes

- Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/101671 (thanks @LordMelkor — both fixes and the drift/re-align test are yours, cherry-picked as 40846e5e and adapted to current main: the gateway-settings payload block moved, and the conflict was resolved to keep main's `remote.payload` spread while sending `''` for the cleared fields.)

Fixes #103053
