raw.body:
## Why

`llamacpp-cuda` was Windows-only: the pinned `b10964` has no Linux CUDA archive, so NVIDIA Linux users got Vulkan. Upstream llama.cpp v0.5.0 (`b11146`) ships Linux CUDA builds for x64 and arm64, so this pins every llama.cpp backend to it and brings CUDA to both Linux targets. Getting there end to end (a fresh WSL arm64 box with an NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X) turned up the rest of this PR: upstream's Linux builds need a system library minimal hosts don't have, there was no terminal path to set up local models, and only the desktop backend ever freed the server's VRAM.

## What changes

### Engine pins (PM)
- All five llama.cpp pins move `10964` → `11146` (`pm lock --bump`; digests match upstream's release API). **Every platform with an installed engine will be offered an update**; installed engines keep working until then.
- `llamacpp-cuda` gains `linux-x64` and `linux-arm64` (CUDA 13.4). Its Linux cudart tarball has the build tag in its name (the Windows zip doesn't), so asset names are built per target, and `stage()` hoists the tarball's top-level dir next to `llama-server` (`RUNPATH` is `$ORIGIN`).
- `win32-x64` moves from CUDA 13.3 to 13.4 because upstream dropped `win-cuda-13.3`; this matches `win32-arm64`.
- `auto` now resolves NVIDIA Linux (x64 and arm64) to CUDA instead of Vulkan.

### Bundled libgomp on Linux
- Every upstream Linux llama.cpp build, CPU included, links the system `libgomp.so.1`. Minimal hosts (WSL, containers) don't have it, and a normal install never touches the system package manager.
- Each Linux engine (cpu, vulkan, cuda, hip) now also pins Ubuntu 24.04's `libgomp1` `.deb` and stages `libgomp.so.1` beside `llama-server`. 24.04's build needs glibc 2.38, the floor upstream's builds already set. **This adds a download host for Linux engine installs** (`archive.ubuntu.com` / `ports.ubuntu.com`); the artifact mirror is the fallback once `archive_inputs` has archived the pin.
- `DebPackage`'s ar+tar unpack is extracted to `pm.package.unpack_deb` and now accepts zstd `data.tar` (Ubuntu's default) via the stdlib codec in PM's 3.14 runtime. Termux behaviour is unchanged.
- Pre-PM Linux engines are still adopted, but count as outdated (update offered), since they lack the libgomp archive. Windows and macOS adoption is unchanged.

### Desktop
- The `localModels` flag ships on Linux x64 and arm64 (Windows and macOS unchanged). Other Linux targets still need `--local`.

### `hermes model` → Local models (new)
- `hermes model` and `hermes setup` gain a **Local models** row wherever PM pins an engine.
- The flow drives the handlers behind the desktop's Local Models pane in-process, so both surfaces run one code path:
  - the catalog priced for this machine (★ marks the recommendation), plus models already on disk
  - quickstart: pinned engine, model download, server start, default assignment
  - activate for a model already downloaded
- Progress renders from the job view the desktop polls. Ctrl+C pauses a download; picking the model again resumes it.

### Managed server lifetime
- **Boot-relative identity.** `server.json` also records `start_time`/`owner_start_time` (boot-relative on Linux). WSL steps its clock within minutes, which moved psutil's `create_time`, so a live router stopped matching its record and every turn failed with "the local model server isn't running". Records without `start_time` keep the original comparisons.
- **Fixed: the old server was never actually stopped.** `_stop_state_server` read a `pid` from `_state_endpoint()`'s `{base_url, api_key}` dict, which never has one, so stale-preset replacement and the rescan bounce never stopped the old router: it kept its VRAM and the new one fell back to an ephemeral port. Its tests mocked a `pid` in. It now resolves the process from the identity-guarded state record and stops it **only when its recorded owner is gone**. A live owner's server is left alone and the replacement boots beside it, exactly as before.
- **The process that boots the server stops it on a clean exit.** It's an atexit hook; `-z` calls it from its `os._exit` cleanup table instead. Before, only the desktop backend's shutdown handler did this:
  - Desktop: unchanged; the second call is a no-op.
  - CLI, `-z` and `hermes model`: now free the VRAM on exit.
  - **Gateway: a stop or restart (including `hermes update`'s fleet restart) now frees a server it booted, and the next local-model turn reloads the model.**
  - A process that only adopted another's server never stops it. A hard kill still leaves an orphan, which the next boot adopts or replaces.

## Verified

- RTX 4060 Ti, driver 610.57: `ensure_engine("cuda")` through PM's real download/stage/verify path; `llama-server --list-devices` reports `CUDA0`.
- RTX Spark N1X, WSL, Ubuntu 26.04 arm64, **no system libgomp**: cuda, cpu and vulkan installed through PM's real path; `ldd` resolves `libgomp.so.1` from the entry; `llama-server` serves completions (CUDA0, 445 tok/s on a tiny model).
- linux-x64 cpu and vulkan staged through the same path. Nothing in `NEEDED` is missing beyond glibc, libstdc++ and OpenSSL 3.
- `hermes model` → Local models:
  - a catalog download paused at 3% and resumed to completion
  - activating an on-disk Qwen3.5-9B, then `hermes -z` and interactive `hermes` chats against it
  - after exit, `hermes model`, `-z` and interactive `hermes` each leave no `llama-server` running
- Windows: validated as non-breaking.
- Tests:
  - New invariants, each red on the base:
    - cudart and libgomp land beside the server
    - every Linux engine pin includes the libgomp `.deb`
    - zstd `.deb`s stage under the same containment
    - only an orphaned router is stopped (real processes)
    - the booting process stops the server on a clean exit
    - a stepped clock never makes a live owner of an older record read as dead
    - the CLI flow reports the quickstart job's terminal state
  - CI green.

## Not exercised / follow-ups

- The CUDA build needs a CUDA 13 driver. The `--version` verify probe doesn't load the CUDA backend, so PM would still select cuda on an older driver.
- The planner prices the N1X's shared GPU memory (46 GB) without WSL's VM RAM cap (14.7 GB by default, on a 30 GB host), so its ★ pick there OOMs while loading. Separate fix.
- With two CLIs on one server, the one that booted it takes it down on exit, and the other reloads the model on its next turn. An ownership handoff would fix that.
- Peeking at the llamacpp provider (picker, config reload) can boot the server in a process that never chats with it.

## What does this PR do?

Fixes the packaged Windows app's update check failing with "we couldn't reach the update server, Microsoft Store returned invalid JSON".

Root cause: the Store checker (`check-store-update.py`), the App Installer checker (`check-appinstaller-update.py`) and the relaunch waiter (`update-relaunch-waiter.ps1`) were resolved under the payload's repo snapshot, `<payload>/hermes-agent/apps/desktop/scripts/`. Since f6713f2762 (`perf(bundles): bake payload bytecode; ship only what the sealed runtime reads`), `INERT_SNAPSHOT_DIRS` excludes `apps/` and `scripts/` from that snapshot, so the scripts are not in the package. The payload python cannot open the missing script, exits 2 with empty stdout, and `store-client.ts::parseResult` reports `invalid JSON (exit 2)`.

The fix moves the two python checkers into the bundled core code and runs them as modules, like the other `hermes_cli` helpers the desktop runs with `-m`. The relaunch waiter is PowerShell run outside the package, so it ships as an app resource. The snapshot exclusion stays as it is.

## Related Issue

No existing issue.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/scripts/check-store-update.py` → `hermes_cli/windows_store_update.py`, and `check-appinstaller-update.py` → `hermes_cli/windows_appinstaller_update.py` (`git mv`; only the shebang and the usage docstring change).
- `apps/desktop/electron/appinstaller-checker.ts`: the runner takes a module name and spawns `python -P -m <module>`. `-P` keeps the working directory off `sys.path`. The strategy deps and `PayloadPythonRunner` rename `script` to `module`.
- `apps/desktop/electron/payload-backend.ts`: `payloadPythonPath(payload)` returns the bundled core code, then the venv dependencies, the order the bin launchers give `sys.path` (`scripts/build/launcher_wrapper.py`). `main.ts` passes it as `PYTHONPATH` for both checkers.
- `apps/desktop/electron-builder.config.cjs`: `win.extraResources` ships `scripts/update-relaunch-waiter.ps1` at the resource root. `relaunch-waiter.ts::relaunchWaiterScript(resourcesPath)` resolves it, and `main.ts` uses it in both relaunch registrations.
- Tests: the two Python test files import the modules; a new `python -P -m` subprocess test checks a Store checker failure still reaches the desktop as JSON; new vitest cases cover the packaging config entry and `payloadPythonPath`; existing vitest files follow the rename.

## How to Test

Diagnosis, on the affected install (Store build 2026.6523.3313.0, arm64, built from upstream/main at 018d982):

1. `resources\agent-payload\hermes-agent` has no `apps\` or `scripts\` directory, and no `check-store-update.py` exists anywhere under `resources`.
2. `git archive HEAD` with the exclusions from `INERT_SNAPSHOT_DIRS` yields no `apps/` directory.

Fix:

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/desktop/test_check_store_update.py tests/desktop/test_appinstaller_check_script.py`: 24 passed.
2. From `apps/desktop`: `vitest run --project electron electron/updater electron/appinstaller-checker.test.ts electron/payload-backend.test.ts electron/app-updater.test.ts`: 186 passed. The 4 failures are in `checkout-legacy`, `checkout-source` and `state-db-preflight`, which this PR does not touch; they fail here on `python3` and `git` spawn errors on this host.
3. Run the entry the desktop spawns, from a neutral directory, with the same import roots: `PYTHONPATH=<core code>;<site-packages> python -P -m hermes_cli.windows_store_update --mode check` prints `{"available": null, "ok": false, "error": "Microsoft Store request failed: ..."}` and exits 1 (outside a Store install that is the expected error). `python -P -m hermes_cli.windows_appinstaller_update` prints `{"available": false, "reason": "not-packaged"}` and exits 0. The old failure shape was `python <missing script>`: exit 2, empty stdout.
4. `electron-builder --win --arm64 --dir` with the real `win.extraResources` entry puts `update-relaunch-waiter.ps1` at `resources/`.
5. `tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json --noEmit` and the `electron-builder.config.cjs` checkJs pass; eslint on the changed files reports no new warnings.

Not verified: a full packaged build that then runs the Store check. That needs a Store-acquired install, so it needs a fresh bundled build from this branch.

raw.body:
Every desktop chat can now find and install catalog plugins and hub skills through the approval card. The install goes into that chat's own profile, not into `default`.

Linear: NS-1015. Base: `onboarding/next` (the onboarding integration branch; lands on `main` later as a whole).

## Background

- **`manage_catalog`** is the model tool that searches the Hermes plugin catalog and the skills hub. With `install`, it shows the user one approval card with one row per item. Nothing installs until the user approves a row. The host does the install the same way the Plugins tab does: pinned commit, kill list, security scan, and live activation.
- A **toolset** is a named group of tools. A profile's config chooses which toolsets its chats get.
- A **client-surface toolset** (`project`, `desktop_ui`) is not chosen by config. The desktop app adds it to its own sessions, whatever backend it is connected to (local, SSH, URL, or Hermes Cloud). `TOOLSET_SESSION_PLATFORMS` removes its tools from every other surface (CLI, TUI, `hermes -z`, cron, messaging).
- **Deferred** means the tool's full schema is not sent on every call. The model sees a stub and loads the tool through `tool_search` when it needs it. The `tools.tool_search.defer` list in config decides which tools are deferred.
- The **setup profile** is the profile the desktop onboarding chat runs in.

## The problem

`manage_catalog` was only in the `setup` toolset. So only the onboarding chat could use it. A user in a normal desktop chat who asked "install the Linear plugin" got a CLI command to run instead of the card.

The install target was also fixed to the `default` profile. A chat in profile `work` that installed a plugin put it into `default`. The `work` chat did not get the new tools. The search also reported "installed" for `default`, not for the chat that asked.

## What changes

`manage_catalog` moves to a new `catalog` toolset. It is a client-surface toolset, like `project` and `desktop_ui`. Every desktop session gets it. CLI, TUI, `hermes -z`, cron and messaging sessions do not get it. `all` does not include it. It is on the default defer list, so it costs a stub, not a full schema, until the model needs it. A user defer list still decides for itself. A user can remove the toolset with `agent.disabled_toolsets: [catalog]`.

The install target is now the profile of the chat that calls the tool. The runner reads it once, in `prepare`, from the calling thread's home. The Advanced modal on the card can still name another profile, and that choice still wins. The search reports `installed` for the chat's profile too.

The `setup` toolset stays, now empty. P15 puts `setup_choose` into it.

The metrics schema's toolset enum gains `catalog`. The tools, toolsets and tool-search reference pages follow.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Which chats get `manage_catalog` | Only the setup profile's desktop chat | Every desktop chat, on every backend |
| CLI, TUI, cron, messaging, `all` | Do not get it | Do not get it (no change) |
| Schema cost per call | Full schema in the setup chat | A deferred stub by default |
| Where an approved row installs | `default`, unless Advanced names another profile | The calling chat's profile, unless Advanced names another profile |
| What "installed" in search results means | Present in `default` | Present in the calling chat's profile |
| How to turn it off | Remove `setup` from the setup profile's config | `agent.disabled_toolsets: [catalog]` |

## What this deliberately does not do

- **It does not turn the tool off in the setup profile.** That config is written by P12 (NS-1016). Review found that limiting `platform_toolsets.cli` cannot remove a client-surface toolset. Only `agent.disabled_toolsets` removes it. P12's hand-written defer list also leaves out `manage_catalog`, so the tool would be eager (full schema) there. The fix belongs in P12's `_write_setup_config`: add `agent.disabled_toolsets: [catalog]`. Until P12 or the Wave B integration adds that entry, the setup chat gets `manage_catalog`, deferred.
- **It does not add `setup_choose`.** P15 (NS-1019) adds it to the `setup` toolset. When P15 merges after this PR, `setup` must hold `setup_choose` only, not `manage_catalog`. P14 and P15 touch the same lines in `toolsets.py` and `tools/tool_search.py`, so expect textual conflicts there.
- **It does not change the onboarding cards or the renderer flow.** The one question card is P16 (NS-1020). The old onboarding script still tells the setup chat to call `manage_catalog`; P19 (NS-1023) deletes that renderer flow.
- **It does not bring the tool to the TUI or the classic CLI.** Those are P21 (NS-1025) and P22 (NS-1028). There, the call still answers with the `hermes plugins install` / `hermes skills install` command.

## Check

At `b22c1c20ad`:

- `ruff check` on every changed Python file: all checks passed. The metrics schema file parses as JSON.
- One in-process script with the worktree `.venv`, under `env -i` with a fake `HOME`, a temp `HERMES_HOME` and its own `HERMES_SHARED_AUTH_DIR`. It resolves toolsets per session platform, drops session-gated tools, checks deferral, and runs the catalog runner with a fake installer in profile scope, in the order `default` → `work` → `default`:
  - `catalog` resolves to `['manage_catalog']`. `setup` resolves to `[]`. `all` does not include `manage_catalog`.
  - Desktop: `catalog` is enabled, `manage_catalog` survives the session drops, and the default defer list defers it. With a user `defer: []` it is direct.
  - TUI and classic CLI: neither the toolset nor the tool is present.
  - `default` session: row and install target `default`, install runs under the root home.
  - `work` session: row and install target `work`, install runs under `profiles/work`. With Advanced `target_profile=default`, the install goes to `default`.
  - `default` again: target `default`. No profile leak between the three runs.
- Two existing tests changed only because this change broke them. The catalog install test now asserts that a row approved in profile B installs into B (it fails on the base branch). Two toolset lists in the TUI gateway tests now include `catalog`. No new tests.
- Test suites were not run locally; CI runs them. No live desktop E2E in this wave. The script used a fake installer, and it did not call the live `search()` against the catalog.

Any agent in a Hermes desktop chat can now open a new, visible chat in an existing profile and send it a first message, through one backend tool called `start_chat`.

Linear: NS-1018. Base: onboarding/next (the onboarding integration branch; lands on main later as a whole)

## Background

- **Profile**: a separate Hermes home with its own config, memory, skills and chat history. The desktop app can switch between profiles.
- **Setup profile**: a marked profile (`hermes-setup`) that holds the onboarding "setup chat". That chat helps a new user install and configure things.
- **Handoff**: the end of the setup chat, where the user moves to a normal chat that starts working on their task.
- **Toolset**: a named group of tools. A session gets a tool only when one of its enabled toolsets holds it.
- **Session platform**: which surface the chat runs on (`desktop`, `cli`, `telegram`, ...). The backend reads it from the session record, not from an environment variable, so it is also correct when the desktop app talks to a remote backend.
- **Deferred tool**: a tool whose full schema the model sees only after a `tool_search` call. A direct tool is in the schema from the start.
- **Subagent**: a child agent that `delegate_task` starts. It gets a reduced tool set.
- **First-contact note**: a one-time instruction that the backend adds to the first turn of a new install ("introduce yourself, mention /help"). A per-profile `onboarding.seen.profile_build_offered` flag (the "latch") turns off the longer version of it.

## The problem

Today the desktop renderer does the handoff. About 500 lines of TypeScript (`handoff-leg.ts`, `onboarding-handoff.ts`, `handoff-receipt.ts`, `persisted-handoff.ts`) create the new chat, keep a localStorage receipt and map 12 rejection codes. That code always builds the chat in the `default` profile and always switches the user to it. Only the renderer can do this, so no agent can start a chat on its own, and the behaviour is different on every surface.

## What changes

A new backend tool, `start_chat`, does the handoff. It takes `message` (required, the new chat's first user message), `title` (optional, at most 40 characters) and `profile` (optional, an existing profile; the default is the caller's own profile).

The backend finds the calling desktop session. It rejects an empty message, a title that is too long, an unknown profile, or a call that does not come from a desktop chat. It never creates a profile. Inside the target profile's scope it creates a normal top-level chat with fresh history. The new chat gets the caller's source and transport, so it runs as a desktop chat, also on a remote backend. The backend sets the `profile_build_offered` latch in the target profile and submits the first message, which starts the chat's first turn. If the submit fails, the backend closes the new chat and returns `rejected`.

The call is not idempotent and keeps no receipt: every call opens one more chat. The result tells the model this directly ("Do not call start_chat again for this task.").

The tool has its own `start_chat` toolset. Only desktop sessions get it (keyed on the session platform). The `all` toolset does not include it, `hermes tools` does not list it, it stays a direct tool (not deferred behind `tool_search`), and subagents never get it (`DELEGATE_BLOCKED_TOOLS`). The tools and toolsets reference pages, the delegation guide and `tools/AGENTS.md` now list it.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Who can start the new chat | Only the renderer's onboarding code | Any agent in a desktop chat, through `start_chat` |
| Target profile | Always `default` | The profile the agent names, or the caller's own |
| Unknown profile | Not possible to ask for one | `rejected` with a reason; no profile is created |
| Remote backend | Renderer-only path | The new chat takes the caller's platform, so it gets desktop tools there too |
| Repeated call | Receipt in localStorage | Each call opens one chat; the result tells the model not to call again |
| Subagents | Not applicable | Cannot see or call the tool |
| CLI, TUI, messaging chats | Not applicable | Do not get the tool |

## What this deliberately does not do

- **The renderer does not call `start_chat` yet.** The old renderer handoff code stays in place. P16 (NS-1020) adds the handoff card that shows the new chat, and P19 (NS-1023) deletes the old renderer flow.
- **No `completed_at` or `intro: seen` write.** NS-1018 says a handoff from the setup profile writes these. That write moves to Wave B, together with the rest of the backend onboarding state.
- **No new tests and no live E2E in this wave.** The invariant tests from NS-1018 ("two calls give two chats", "a subagent cannot see the tool") and the live check (the new chat reattaches when the user opens it) come later. The in-process checks below cover the same behaviour for now.
- **No change to the first-contact note.** On a fresh install the setup chat lives in the separate setup profile, so the handoff chat is the first session in the target profile. It then still gets the short plain intro note ("introduce yourself, mention /help"). It does not get the longer one, because the latch is set. NS-1018 says "no first-contact note in the new chat". **Reviewer decision:** accept the plain intro and record that on NS-1018, or add a session flag that `start_chat` sets and the first-contact code reads (in this PR or in Wave B).
- **No check that a title is free.** The title reaches the database after the first turn completes. If the title is already in use in that profile, or the first turn fails, the chat keeps its automatic title. The tool result still shows the requested title.

## Check

All at `f154f55c1b`. CI runs the test suites. I ran none locally.

- `ruff check tools/start_chat_tool.py tui_gateway/start_chat.py toolsets.py tools/tool_search.py tools/delegate_tool_toolsets.py`: all checks passed.
- In-process run with `env -i`, a fake `HOME`, a temp `HERMES_HOME` and its own `HERMES_SHARED_AUTH_DIR`. The script created a profile `work`, opened a desktop caller session, and called `start_chat` through `registry.dispatch` against a local fake model endpoint:
  - Two calls into `work` returned `started` with two different session ids. Both turns completed. In `work`'s `state.db` both chats have `source='desktop'`, the requested titles ("Pune trails", "Grocery plan") and the first user message.
  - `profile: "missing-profile"` returned `rejected` ("Profile 'missing-profile' does not exist.").
  - A 41-character title returned `rejected` ("title has 41 characters; the limit is 40.").
  - The launch profile's `state.db` had no session rows, so nothing leaked into `default`.
  - `work`'s `config.yaml` had `onboarding.seen.profile_build_offered: true`.
  - A call from outside a desktop turn returned `rejected` ("... only from a chat in the Hermes desktop app").
- Subagent check with a real parent `AIAgent` (`platform=desktop`, toolsets including `start_chat`) and `tools.delegate_tool._build_child_agent`: the parent has `start_chat`. The child does not, also when the child asks for `toolsets=['start_chat', 'terminal']`.
- Toolset resolution: `resolve_toolset('all')` does not include `start_chat`. The session-platform filter drops it for `cli` and keeps it for `desktop`. `is_deferrable_tool_name('start_chat')` is `False`.
- Not checked: the desktop app itself, and a full `delegate_task` turn.

raw.body:
The setup bot now has one tool, `setup_choose`, to ask the user a question or show a picker as a card in the setup chat, and the backend half of that card is wired end to end.

Linear: NS-1019. Base: onboarding/next (the onboarding integration branch; lands on main later as a whole)

## Background

- **Setup profile / setup chat.** On first launch, the desktop app opens a chat with a separate Hermes profile (the "setup profile"). A model in that chat walks the user through onboarding: accent colour, theme, layout, connectors, plugins.
- **`setup` toolset.** The tools only that setup profile gets. Only desktop sessions receive it. CLI, `hermes -z`, cron, kanban and messaging sessions never do, and `all` does not include it. Before this PR it held one tool, `manage_catalog` (plugin and skill installs through an approval card).
- **Server request.** The backend asks the desktop renderer a question over JSON-RPC and waits for the answer. `clarify` and the tour already work this way. The wire shapes live in `tui_gateway/contracts/server_requests.py`. A script generates the TypeScript and OpenRPC copies in `apps/shared` from that file.
- **Directives.** Today the setup script makes the model write special text lines (`::onboarding{step}`, `::ask{…}`). The app parses those lines out of the reply and draws cards from them.

## The problem

Cards come from text the model writes. The app has to parse them back out of the reply, and nothing checks their shape. The model also tends to write the question in its message and then again in the directive. That happened in a real user run, where the same question appeared twice. The pickers must also show fixed lists (the app's own accents, layouts, connectors). A text directive has no clean way to say "use the app's list".

## What changes

`setup_choose` joins the `setup` toolset. It is a direct tool there: tool search never defers it unless a defer list names it. A call takes a `kind` (`question`, `accent`, `theme`, `layout`, `connectors` or `plugins`), a `question` that becomes the card's heading, and optional `options` (up to 12 rows of `{id, label, detail?}` with unique ids). When `options` is omitted, the payload carries `options: null`. That tells the app to show its own fixed list, or a free-text box for kind `question`. `multi_select` lets the user pick several rows. `intent` (connectors and plugins only) adds a now / later / save choice to each row. The tool description tells the model that the card shows the question, so the message text must not repeat it.

The tool checks its input before it asks. Bad kinds, empty questions, bad or repeated options, and `intent` on the wrong kind come back as errors the model can fix. A valid call goes to the renderer as a `setup_choose` server request. It uses the same wait timeout as `clarify`. The result is `{outcome, picked, intent?}`. `outcome` is `submitted`, `cancelled` or `no_answer`. `no_answer` also carries a notice that says why: a timeout, an interrupted turn, or no desktop window answered. A desktop build that does not know the method answers "method not found", so the tool reports `no_answer` at once and does not wait for the timeout. The tool stores nothing.

The wire contract is added to `server_requests.py`, and the `apps/shared` contract files are regenerated. `setup_choose` is also added to the tool-name list in the published v3 metrics schema. Without it, the client would accept a `tool_unavailable` row that the published schema rejects. The tool reference and toolset reference docs describe the new tool.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| How the setup bot asks a question | Writes an `::ask{…}` text line that the app parses | Calls `setup_choose` with `kind: "question"` |
| How it shows a picker | Writes an `::onboarding{step}` text line | Calls `setup_choose` with `kind: "accent"`, `"theme"`, `"layout"`, `"connectors"` or `"plugins"` |
| Fixed lists | Up to the directive text | `options` omitted, so the app fills its own list |
| Shape checks | None; the app parses free text | The tool validates kind, question, options and intent before it asks |
| Duplicate question | The model can write it in the message and the directive | The description says the card shows the question; the message must not repeat it |
| Answer the model sees | Next user message | `{outcome, picked, intent?}` with an explicit `cancelled` or `no_answer` |
| Outside a desktop setup session | n/a | The tool is not in the toolset; a direct call returns an error |

## What this deliberately does not do

- **No desktop card yet (P16, NS-1020).** The renderer does not draw the `setup_choose` card or its fixed lists in this PR. A current desktop build answers "method not found", and the tool returns `no_answer`. `setup_choose` is in the gateway's `_TOOL_LIFECYCLE_UI_TOOLS` set now. The matching desktop entry in `CARD_TOOL_NAMES` arrives with the card in P16. Until then, the two sets differ on one side only.
- **The `::onboarding` / `::ask` directives stay (P19, NS-1023).** The old renderer flow and its parser stay until P19 deletes them.
- **The meaning of intent "now" is not here.** It belongs in the setup skill text (Wave B, P13, NS-1017). The setup script does not call `setup_choose` yet.
- **No new tests.** The invariant test that NS-1019 names ("options omitted gives the app's fixed list; `picked` matches the click") needs the P16 card, so it is left for that PR.
- `setup_choose` is not added to `AGENT_RUNTIME_POST_HOOK_TOOL_NAMES`. Only one test reads that set, and it has no runtime effect.

## Check

All at `1bef033ea9`. No live end-to-end run in this wave.

- `ruff check` on every changed Python file: passed.
- `scripts/gen_gateway_contracts.py --check`: rc=0. The generated TypeScript and OpenRPC files match `server_requests.py`.
- `tsc --noEmit -p apps/shared`: rc=0.
- Metrics schema against `toolsets.BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES`, in-process: `missing=set()`, `extra=set()`.
- `resolve_toolset('setup')` returns `['manage_catalog', 'setup_choose']`.
- In-process handler run (env -i, temp `HOME`, `HERMES_HOME` and `HERMES_SHARED_AUTH_DIR` under `/tmp/lane1/p15/`, fake callback):
  - a question with two options sends the normalized options and returns `{"outcome": "submitted", "picked": "b"}`
  - a layout without options sends `options: null`
  - connectors with `multi_select` and `intent` returns the picked ids and a per-id intent map
  - a `{}` reply gives `cancelled`, and a `None` reply gives `no_answer` with its notice
  - no callback gives the desktop-only error, and `intent` on a layout gives an error
  - the inline executor path returns the callback's pick
- Test suites were not run locally. CI runs them.

The backend now decides whether a user sees the first-run guide, counts failed starts, and hands out one setup chat, and the setup profile is written with only the tools the guide's steps use.

Linear: NS-1016. Base: onboarding/next (the onboarding integration branch; lands on main later as a whole)

## Background

- **Setup profile.** On first run the desktop app creates a separate Hermes profile (its own home folder, config and chat history) named `hermes-setup`. A marker file in that folder, `.setup-profile.json`, tells Hermes it is the setup profile (P10 made it a plain profile with this marker).
- **The guide / beats.** The first-run guide is a scripted chat in that profile. Each "beat" is one step of the script: pick a look, connect apps, arrange the layout, start a first job.
- **Setup chat.** The one chat in the setup profile where the guide runs. It has the title "Welcome to Hermes".
- **Deferred tools.** Tools on the `tools.tool_search.defer` list are not sent to the model up front. The model finds and calls them through `tool_search` / `tool_call`. Tools not on the list are "eager": the model sees them on every turn.
- **Toolset.** A named group of tools. `platform_toolsets.cli` picks the toolsets a profile's sessions get. `no_mcp` is a sentinel that turns off MCP servers.
- **Wave A.** P11, P12, P14 and P15 all branch from P10 and merge into onboarding/next side by side.

## The problem

The renderer owned all onboarding state. It kept the guide's phase in localStorage (`hermes-onboarding-phase-v1`), so the backend and other clients could not see it. One failed start was saved as `skipped` forever, so a single network error meant the user never saw the guide again. The renderer also kept its own copy of the guide's persona prompt next to the one in `SOUL.md`.

The setup profile also cloned the user's whole config and then only added the `setup` toolset. The guide chat therefore got whatever the user had: terminal, files, web, browser, memory, delegation, code execution, MCP servers. A cloned `agent.coding_context: focus` could swap in the full coding toolset in a code folder. A cloned `tool_search` block could turn deferral off, and the bool form `tool_search: true` crashed profile creation. Creation also copied `MEMORY.md` and `USER.md` in, and the built-in memory store loads those even with the memory toolset off.

## What changes

The marker file now holds the onboarding state: `{intro: "unseen" | "seen", failed_starts: 0..3}`. Three RPCs read and change it. `onboarding.state` returns the state plus `eligible`, which reads only the `HERMES_GUEST_ONBOARDING` flag (not `guest_enabled()`). `onboarding.record_failed_start` adds one failed start, and the third one marks the intro seen. `onboarding.mark_seen` marks it seen. `onboarding.reset_setup_profile` (the Settings "Reset onboarding" path) now also resets the marker.

A fourth RPC, `onboarding.ensure_setup_session`, creates the setup profile if needed and finds or creates the setup chat by title. Every call returns the same `session_id` and an `empty` flag. It writes optional seed messages only into an empty chat. The desktop kickoff now seeds the guide through this RPC and no longer makes its own titled `session.create`. The kickoff adopts an existing chat only when it has messages, so an empty row left by an earlier call gets seeded, not adopted.

The renderer no longer stores the phase. The gate reads `onboarding.state` when the gateway connects and starts the guide only for an eligible user whose intro is `unseen`. Skip and the app handoff call `mark_seen`. A failed kickoff calls `record_failed_start`. A kickoff that stops because no provider is ready counts nothing and tries again on the next launch. `requestDesktopOnboarding` and the free-tier ready screen wait until the state read finishes, so they do not see "idle" and cover the guide. The duplicate `PERSONA` block is gone, and `SOUL.md` is the only copy.

The setup profile's `config.yaml` is now written with fixed values, not appended to:

- `platform_toolsets.cli: [setup, no_mcp]`
- `agent.disabled_toolsets` gets `catalog` (merged with the cloned list), and `agent.coding_context: "off"`
- `tools.tool_search` is replaced by a hand-written `defer` list: computer use, session search, image generation, todo, process and cron management, the desktop pane and preview tools, and `react_to_message`. `apply_layout` stays eager.
- `display.show_reasoning: false`

Creation and reset leave `memories/` empty.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Where the guide's state lives | localStorage in one renderer | the setup profile's marker file, read over RPC |
| One failed start | saved as `skipped` forever | counted; the guide stops after the third |
| Who decides eligibility | the renderer's own flag | `HERMES_GUEST_ONBOARDING`, read by the backend |
| Setup chat on relaunch | renderer looks it up by title, creates it itself | `onboarding.ensure_setup_session` returns the same chat every time |
| Setup chat tools | the user's cloned toolsets, MCP included | `setup` + the desktop fold-in; 5 model-visible tools (see Check) |
| Cloned `coding_context: focus` in a repo | full coding toolset | pinned `off` |
| Cloned `tool_search: true` | profile creation crashes | block replaced |
| Memories | copied from the launch profile | empty |
| Persona prompt | in `SOUL.md` and in the renderer | `SOUL.md` only |

## What this deliberately does not do

- **`start_chat` (P14) and `setup_choose` (P15) are not here.** They live on sibling Wave A branches. `start_chat` is left out of `platform_toolsets.cli` because the toolset does not exist on this base, and naming it made config validation warn. When P14 merges, `"start_chat"` goes back into `_SETUP_TOOLSETS` in `hermes_cli/setup_profile.py`. Setting `completed_at` when the setup chat calls `start_chat` also lands with P14.
- **`manage_catalog` is still in the setup chat on this base.** The `setup` toolset still holds it. P11 moves it into its own `catalog` toolset, and the `catalog` entry in `disabled_toolsets` then removes it.
- **Wave B is not here.** The `/initiate-setup` prompt and skill (P13) and the intro view that boots into the setup chat (P18) build on these RPCs. For now the kickoff still seeds the old scripted prompt.
- **The question cards (P16) are not here.**
- **The old renderer flow stays.** `ONBOARDING_PHASES` and the in-memory phase logic remain until P19 deletes them.
- **No new tests.** NS-1016 lists two invariant tests. The maintainer asked for no new tests in this wave. CI runs the existing suites.
- **Known behaviour changes for review.** The seeded chat now uses the setup profile's config, not the composer's cwd and model pick. Free-tier reasoning is still set to minimal after resume. Because the phase stays "idle" until `onboarding.state` returns, the "Connecting…" overlay can now show briefly on a guided first launch.

## Check

At `074d73f39c`. No live E2E this wave. I ran no test suites.

- `ruff check` on the changed Python files: pass.
- `tsc -p . --noEmit` in `apps/desktop`: exit 0.
- `eslint` and `prettier --check` on the changed desktop files: pass.
- `scripts/gen_gateway_contracts.py --check`: the generated contract is current.
- In-process RPC run (`env -i`, fake `HOME`, temp `HERMES_HOME`, own `HERMES_SHARED_AUTH_DIR` and `HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR`, no servers):
  - Two `onboarding.ensure_setup_session` calls returned the same `session_id`, both `empty: true`. A separate run passed seeds: the third call returned `empty: false`, a fourth call did not write the seeds again, and the database held one "Welcome to Hermes" row with `message_count` 2.
  - `onboarding.state` returned `{eligible: false, intro: "unseen", failed_starts: 0}` (the flag was not set). Three `record_failed_start` calls gave `failed_starts` 1, 2, 3, and `intro` changed to `seen` only on the third.
  - With `HERMES_HOME` set to the setup profile and platform `desktop`: enabled toolsets `desktop_ui, project, setup`; disabled `catalog`. The model-visible tools were `apply_layout, manage_catalog, tool_call, tool_describe, tool_search`. The ten desktop pane and preview tools were deferred.
  - `validate_platform_toolsets` returned no warnings for the setup config.

Fixes #128942.

ptyProcess.onExit forwarded the exit to the output gate but never killed the session: the map entry only dropped on flush and pty.kill() never ran, leaking /dev/ptmx handles until macOS cannot allocate a PTY.

Kill the PTY inside onExit (map entry still drops on flush so late attach keeps working; onExitFlushed calls disposeTerminalSession). Renderer exit handler sends hermes:terminal:dispose explicitly instead of relying on unmount timing. Tab-close audit: unmount cleanup already disposes, no other gaps.

Note: complementary to #128943, which reaps PTYs on renderer crash. This covers the normal shell-exit path.

Tests: new electron/terminal-pty-dispose.test.ts red-first; 4 electron files 10/10 plus terminals.test.ts 17/17.

raw.body:
## What does this PR do?

A Windows update can restore the prior Python runtime, then still fail with `WinError 5` when a process holds `libcrypto-3-x64.dll` in the discarded `.displaced-*` tree. The cleanup exception currently aborts the update and can mask the error that triggered a rollback.

After the prior entry has been restored, a locked displacement is now retained with a sidecar marker instead of failing that cleanup step. `hermes pm gc` reclaims only marked displacements once the handle is gone. An unmarked displacement from an interrupted restore remains untouched.

## Related Issue

Refs #124807. This covers the `.displaced-*` restore path left out of the open `.previous-*` cleanup proposals #124819 and #124858. It does not replace or claim to resolve those PRs.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `pm/install.py`: tolerate a Windows hold only after the previous entry has been restored, and mark the retained displacement as safe to reclaim.
- `pm/cli.py`: let `hermes pm gc` remove marked displacements while preserving unmarked restore points.
- `tests/pm/test_pm_core.py`: drive an explicit install through a locked-displacement restore, then verify recovery and selective GC with a real PM store and facts.

## How to Test

1. Run `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/pm/test_pm_core.py -j 4` on Windows. Result: 34 passed, 1 macOS-only test skipped.
2. The new test corrupts a recorded entry, provides a prior entry, and injects a persistent `PermissionError` during displaced-tree removal. `ensure(..., explicit=True)` restores the prior entry without failing.
3. The same test verifies that `hermes pm gc` later removes the marked tree, leaves an unmarked interrupted-restore tree alone, and keeps the live entry.

`ruff check pm/install.py pm/cli.py tests/pm/test_pm_core.py` and `git diff --check` pass. I also ran `tests/pm/test_recovery.py`: 3 passed and 8 failed during `uv lock` because the host uv cache reported "too many temporary files exist". That file is not claimed green.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11 x64

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — N/A; no user-facing command or setting changed
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility)
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

The support failure was `Source update preparation failed: [WinError 5] Access is denied` while deleting `DLLs/libcrypto-3-x64.dll` inside a `.displaced-*` Python tree. No account-specific paths or identifiers are included here.

raw.body:
Since entry.ts shipped again (c0a0f097a8), local WSLg launches relaunch on --ozone-platform=wayland. main.ts still forced --ignore-gpu-blocklist on every /dev/dxg host, and on Wayland ozone that re-enables GPU compositing Chromium had correctly disabled: WSL has no DRM render node, so the GPU process segfaults (exit 139, null deref) on every start until Chromium aborts with "GPU process isn't usable". hermes desktop never shows a window.

Keep the override on X11 ozone, where it enables full GPU compositing on D3D12. On Wayland, leave Chromium's defaults: rasterization and WebGL stay on the GPU, compositing falls back to software, and the #57614 maximize fix from #113247 stays intact.

## Root cause

Busy-turn steer and queued prompts sent bare `@terminal:N` chips because only idle submit expanded `$composerTerminalSelections` — the busy path read the chip placeholder directly instead of freezing the terminal selection content at the transport boundary.

## Fix

- Freeze `@terminal` context at the transport boundary: busy steer and idle submit both snapshot the selection content when building the payload, so later Cmd+L label reuse can't rewrite a queued payload.
- Raw terminal selection **content is runtime-only**: the persisted queue stores chip/display text only, while fenced contents live in an in-memory map keyed by queued entry id. A renderer restart fails closed with a recovery message (`queuedTerminalSelectionExpiredBody`) instead of leaking terminal contents; ordinary text queue entries stay durable across reload.
- Adapted to current main: `toPersistedEntry` now spreads the entry so newer `QueuedPromptEntry` fields (`displayKind`, `drainFailures`) ride persistence — the PR's original explicit field list would have dropped them.

## Tests

`cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/store/composer.test.ts src/store/composer-queue.test.ts src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-submit.test.tsx src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-queue.test.tsx src/app/session/hooks/use-background-queue-drain.test.tsx` — **142 passed** on rebased head 260f7cec760df96ce823e7250bb03a65ac5470a9.

Adds **Chat Text Size** beside UI Scale in Appearance → Typography. Users can keep compact sidebars and controls while enlarging conversation text. Defaults are **90% UI Scale / 110% Chat Text Size**; saved choices still take precedence.

Chat Text Size is relative to UI Scale. It changes transcript typography and message editors, not window zoom, pane geometry, or the sidebar.

Overlaps the chat-size portion of https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/125904. This is the separately requested, visually approved implementation: it scopes conversation tokens to transcripts/editors rather than overriding root tokens used throughout Settings and chrome. raw.body:
**Settings → Advanced → Keep computer awake** now has three modes: off, while working, and always. **While working** holds the machine awake only while a turn is in flight and releases it at idle. Overnight runs keep going, but the laptop isn't pinned awake for the rest of the week. Existing users keep exactly what they had: a saved "on" migrates to **always**, and the default stays **off**. Fixes #101991.

Salvage of #102209 by @jonpol01. Both commits are carried with authorship kept and rebased across about 18,800 commits of main.

## Why

The toggle was a boolean: off, or a machine-wide `powerSaveBlocker` held for as long as Desktop is open. An overnight run died on sleep unless the user had remembered to flip the toggle first. Once flipped, it kept the machine awake through every idle hour afterwards (#101991).

Main already tracks whether any turn is in flight. `mergeActiveWork(activeWorkByWebContents.values()).count > 0` drives stream throttling. This PR wires the blocker to that same signal, so it adds no new listener, timer or IPC channel.

## What changed

- **Mode setting** (from #102209):
  - `power-save.ts` gains three pure functions: parse, read and wanted.
  - `updateStreamThrottleFromActiveWork` hands the merged work picture to both throttling and keep-awake.
  - The Settings row becomes a segmented control.
- **Migration** (from #102209):
  - Both persisted copies migrate in place, `true → always` and `false → off`: the renderer's `hermes.desktop.keepAwake.v1` and main's `keep-awake.json` `{ on }`.
  - An explicit `mode` wins over a stale `on`, and an unrecognised value falls back to `off`.
  - The `hermes:keep-awake` IPC channel accepts either a mode or the old boolean.
- **Rebase onto current main.** Conflicts with the newer minimize-to-tray setting, the lag watchdog, the settings deep-link ids and the ja / zh-hant catalogs were resolved by keeping both sides.
- **Dead renderers release the blocker (ours).** `activeWorkByWebContents` only dropped an entry when its webContents was destroyed. A renderer that dies keeps its webContents, and some `render-process-gone` exits never reload. Its last in-flight count therefore stayed in the merged picture until quit, which disabled stream throttling and now also kept the "while working" blocker held. The entry is now forgotten on `render-process-gone` too. A reloaded renderer re-reports its live turns on mount.
- **One mode list (ours).** The renderer store and the preload typing import `KeepAwakeMode` / `parseKeepAwakeMode` from `electron/power-save`, so the modes cannot drift between main and the picker.
- **i18n (ours).**
  - de, fr and es only had the old description and fell back to English labels; they now have the three labels and the new description.
  - Settings search gains "while working" and "turn" as keywords.
  - The three new keys are registered in `locales/_keys.desktop.json`.

Compared with #102274 by @CookPiu, which rescopes the existing toggle to runs only: it would silently remove "always", which cron, kanban and gateway work that runs without an open Desktop turn relies on. @CookPiu reviewed #102209 on Windows 11 with `powercfg /requests` and endorsed it (legacy `{ on: true }` armed on ready; while-working held only during a turn).

## Live check (real Electron app, macOS)

The real dev build ran against a fresh profile. I drove it through the real preload bridge (`window.hermesDesktop.setKeepAwake` / `setActiveWork`) and read the OS power assertions with `pmset -g assertions`, filtered to the app's pid.

| Step | main (`f42f579cf8`, toggle on) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| cold start, nothing set | none | none |
| enable (`true` on main, `while-working` here), idle | **NoIdleSleepAssertion held** | none |
| turn in flight (active-work count 1) | held | **held** |
| turn finished (count 0) | **still held** | **released** |
| `always`, idle | — | held |
| `off` | — | none |
| legacy boolean `true` / `false` over IPC | — | held / none |
| cold start with legacy `keep-awake.json` `{ "on": true }` | — | held on ready (migrated to `always`) |

## Tests

- `electron/power-save.test.ts` (6) and `src/store/keep-awake.test.ts` (5) pass. They cover mode parsing including the legacy boolean and junk values, persisted `{ mode }` / `{ on }` precedence, the wanted truth table, the real blocker driven in and out of a turn without stacking, and both renderer migrations.
- `src/app/settings` UI tests: 420 pass. `tsc` is clean for both the electron and renderer projects, eslint is clean on changed files, and `npm run i18n:keys -- --check` is clean.
- Not covered by a test: the `main.ts` wiring. It is exercised by the live check above, since `main.ts` is never imported by tests. The `render-process-gone` release was not live-tested, because the exits that don't reload (`clean-exit`, `launch-failed`) can't be triggered on demand.

Limitation, as in #102209: "working" means Desktop chat turns in flight. Work that runs entirely in the gateway (cron, messaging sessions not open in a window) arms the blocker only under **always**.

Supersedes #102274.

raw.body:
## Summary

Bot Mode is the #2 community complaint, behind a mobile app. Most reports come down to a few broken paths: messages between bots fail, a bot's own chat refuses you, clicking a bot does nothing, and replies go missing. This PR fixes each of those, using the strongest open community PR for each one and keeping the original authors on their commits.

**Bot-to-bot messaging**
- If a reply arrives after the 300 s live wait, it now still reaches the sender. The runner keeps waiting while the live owner is alive, up to 30 minutes, then reports the delivery as pending (do not resend). An owner it can't look up gets one more window, like one that went away. When the owner goes away, it cancels only receipts that are still queued and unclaimed, so a delivery never runs twice. From #123684 (z0zero), fixes #123034.

**"This chat is open somewhere else" (#122725, #122770, #122370)**
- A one-shot turn now releases its session lease as soon as the session is settled, instead of holding it through the exit linger. The order is: flush the transcript, run the finalize hook, commit the memory provider, release the lease, then linger and tear down. Memory is committed before the release so a later turn cannot collide with it. From #122773 (Zheqing Zeng).
- A turn that is still running when its session closes no longer leaks the lease. From #128951 (Iain Lane).

**Bot Chat opening (#125899, #126272, #120810)**
- Clicking a bot whose Bot Chat is already in the main tab now brings that tab forward. Before, the click did nothing whenever another bot's tab was active. From #125921 (liuhao1024).
- The wait for history now counts only messages the chat can actually show (`live_message_count`), not the stored total. A chat whose messages are all folded away opens right away instead of stalling for 60 s and then failing. From #126328 (kokhlo).
- After compression, the tile for the old segment is dropped before the new tip opens, so you get one tab instead of two. From #122192 (finn763). I also replaced its cast with the SDK's typed hook.

**Model pick (#127449)**
- A `/model` pick made in a session now survives the agent being rebuilt. Before, the bot quietly went back to the profile's default model. From #127455 (chelsealong).

**Docs**
- Added a "Coming from profiles?" section to Bot Mode. "What does it add over profiles?" has been the top question since launch, and the page answered it with "a Bot is a profile" and nothing more.

Closes #122697, #123034, #122725, #122770, #125899, #126272, #120810, #127449.
Supersedes #123684, #122773, #128951, #125921, #126328, #122192, #127455, and the other runner fixes #122945, #127792, #128912. Stale: #120247 duplicates the merged #121372.

Not in this PR: queuing for relayed DMs while a one-shot holds the lease (#122370; releasing the lease earlier makes the refusal window much smaller), Telegram/WhatsApp DMs appearing in Bot Mode (#126732, which has an active assignee), per-bot session tabs (#124814), Bot Mode outside the desktop app, and Bot Screen.

## Test plan

- [x] `scripts/run_tests.sh` on `test_bot_relay`, `test_bot_mode_dm`, `test_bot_live_owner_delivery`, `test_single_query_session_finalize`, `test_oneshot_completion_linger`, `test_closed_session_turn_lease`, `test_profile_rebuild_commit`, `test_profiles_list_canonical_session`: 190 passed. The one failure, `test_canonical_session_scoped_per_profile_db`, also fails on `main` on this host because the test guard flags `~/.local/bin/node`.
- [x] Desktop vitest across `hermes-bots`, `session-states`, and `open-session`: 935/935. `tsc -p .` is clean.
- [x] Checked by hand that `<checkout>/.hermes/bin/hermes --run-module tools.bot_mode_dm` starts with dependencies loaded. The real-subprocess argv tests are pinned to the script form, because under pytest `HERMES_HOME` points at an empty sandbox root with no dependencies to select.
- [x] Live check on a managed install: bot A sends `message_agent` to bot B; the reply comes back and no failure is shown.

raw.body:
## Summary

Enter while the agent is busy is supposed to steer: the text shows up as a user bubble in the live turn. In practice it often went into the queue, and a second Enter then interrupted the turn and waited for it to settle before sending. This PR fixes both halves of that, plus a display bug in the steer bubble.

- **Stale compaction flag no longer blocks steering.** The composer refused to steer whenever it thought the session was compacting. A compaction that aborts after announcing itself never sends the terminal `compacted` edge, so the flag stayed on for the rest of the turn and every correction was queued. The gateway already checks the real compression lock and answers `queued` while one runs, so the client-side gate only caused harm. It's gone from the Enter path and the external-submit path.
- **Double-Enter on a queued text entry steers it.** An empty Enter while busy used to promote the head and interrupt. Now a text-only head is steered into the live turn first: it becomes a bubble right away, with no interrupt and no wait for the turn to settle. Send-now's interrupt is still the fallback when the steer can't carry the payload (attachments, hidden notes, expanded skills) or the turn refuses it. Repeat Enters while a steer is in flight don't escalate to an interrupt.
- **The steer bubble keeps the user's words.** When a steer lands at a tool boundary it is stored as a steer row. `session.resume` unwraps that row, but the REST history the desktop hydrates from after a turn did not. The bubble got swapped for the model-facing `[OUT-OF-BAND USER MESSAGE …]` wrapper. The REST projection now unwraps it the same way.

## Test plan

- [x] `vitest run src/app/chat/composer`: 78 files / 582 tests pass, including new `deliverQueuedNow` cases (steer instead of interrupt, fallback on refusal, attachments interrupt directly, no escalation while in flight)
- [x] `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_history_commentary_display.py`: REST and RPC show the same unwrapped steer text
- [x] `tsc -p apps/desktop --noEmit`, eslint and prettier on the touched files
- [x] Real Electron + `hermes serve` against the scripted provider (core e2e harness, local probe):
  - steer mid-stream, on the second API call of a tool turn, during a running tool, and after a Stop all go out as `session.redirect` → `redirected`, with the bubble in place
  - queued entry + empty Enter while busy: before, `session.interrupt` → drain; after, `session.redirect` → `redirected`, reply visible in 0.8 s, no interrupt
  - steer during a tool: after the turn settles the bubble reads `U7 … correction`, not the OUT-OF-BAND wrapper

raw.body:
Preserves the native Discord auto-thread semantic rename when the LLM title lands on a retry turn after the gateway rebuilt the session agent — the thread now renames instead of keeping its placeholder name.

Salvage of #127673 by @anpicasso (fixes #127667): the fix commit is cherry-picked unchanged at the base of this branch so authorship survives; the follow-up commit folds review findings from the 6-agent gate (hermes-pr-review phases 2a/2b/2c + /simplify-code reuse/quality/efficiency).

## What was wrong

The native Discord adapter stamps `auto_thread_created` / `auto_thread_initial_name` only on the opening parent-channel event. `TurnRunner._attach_session_title_callback` wired the rename callback only when the **current turn's** source carried those markers — so on a title-retry turn with a freshly built agent (gateway restart, cache miss, config-signature change), no callback was attached: SQLite stored the LLM title while Discord kept the placeholder. A cached agent masked this because its first-turn callback survived.

## What it does

When the current source is a native Discord in-thread follow-up without markers, the wiring recovers the persisted markers from the session row's `origin_json` — accepted only for the same Discord thread, and only when the recovered origin passes the real `_is_discord_auto_thread_lane` predicate — then grafts them onto the live source via `replace_source()`, keeping the live message metadata, transport owner, and routing identity. Relay-delivered events, Telegram topics, and user-created threads are untouched.

## Changes

- `gateway/run_turn_runner.py` — contributor's recovery block (cherry-picked), then folded: gate on `SessionSource.from_dict(origin)` + the real lane predicate instead of a hand-copied field-by-field reimplementation (a second copy of the lane definition that would drift); module-level `replace_source` / `SessionSource` imports replace the inline one.
- `tests/gateway/test_session_title_rename_lane.py` — the contributor's regression test, then folded: the fake runner binds the REAL `GatewayRunner._is_discord_auto_thread_lane` (matching the file's `NativeRenameRunner` pattern) instead of a hand-written lambda; added negative cases (wrong thread id, user-created thread, blank origin), a broken-DB degradation case, and a transport-owner preservation case for the recovered source.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Regression test on origin/main (source reverted, test kept) | 1 failed — fresh agent has no `_on_session_title` (red as expected) |
| Same test with fix | green |
| Lane suite on final stack | 10 passed, 0 failed |
| Title/thread/topic/turn-runner slice on final stack | 84 passed, 0 failed |
| Mutation check (source file reverted to base on final stack) | both recovery tests red; no-op/DB-failure tests stay green (main's behaviour preserved) |
| E2E, real imports + real `SessionDB` row | callback wired from a real persisted `origin_json`, markers recovered, `_transport_adapter_ref` + profile kept; wrong-thread and malformed origins never wire |
| ruff, check-windows-footguns, git diff --check | clean |

The `tests/gateway/test_title_command.py` failures seen locally reproduce identically on the base commit — they are a worktree-location artifact (`home_io_guard` firing because the review worktree sits under `~/.hermes/cache/`), not caused by this change.

The markers provably survive agent rebuilds: `origin_json` is first-writer-wins in the session-row upsert (immutable provenance), the gateway writes the full `source.to_dict()` including both markers, and the agent-side lazy upsert writes a reduced dict that cannot clobber them.

raw.body:
When the setup chat hands the user off to another profile with `start_chat`, the backend now records that onboarding is complete.

Linear: NS-1018. Base: onboarding/next (the onboarding integration branch; lands on main later as a whole)

## Background

- **Setup profile:** a normal Hermes profile that the desktop app creates for the first run. A marker file, `.setup-profile.json`, in its home identifies it. The marker also holds the onboarding state: `intro` (`unseen` or `seen`), `failed_starts`, and, after this PR, `completed_at`.
- **Setup chat:** the chat in the setup profile where the `initiate-setup` skill walks a new user through setup.
- **`start_chat`:** a desktop-only tool. It opens a new visible chat in a named profile and sends it a first message. The setup chat uses it for the handoff: "your setup is done, here is your first real chat".
- **`onboarding.state`:** the RPC that the desktop app reads to decide whether onboarding still applies. It passes the marker keys through. Its wire contract already declares `completed_at: str | None`.

## The problem

The handoff is the end of onboarding, but nothing recorded it. After a successful handoff, the marker still looked like onboarding had not finished. The backend is meant to own onboarding state (P12), so the app had no backend fact to read for "onboarding is done".

## What changes

`hermes_cli/setup_profile.py` gets `mark_completed()`, next to `mark_seen()`. It uses the same state-change path. It sets `intro` to `seen` and writes `completed_at` as a UTC ISO timestamp.

`start_chat` calls `mark_completed()` after the new chat has started, and only when two conditions are true: the calling chat's profile home carries the setup marker, and the new chat runs in a different profile home. A rejected call writes nothing. A call from any other profile writes nothing. A call from the setup chat into the setup profile itself writes nothing. Resetting the setup profile writes the fresh state, which has no `completed_at`, so a reset clears the completion.

The `start_chat` row in `tools-reference.md` gets one sentence that states this rule. There is no contract or codegen change.

| Call | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Setup chat -> another profile, started | Marker unchanged | `intro: seen`, `completed_at` set |
| Setup chat -> setup profile (profile omitted or named) | Marker unchanged | Marker unchanged |
| Chat in any other profile -> any profile | Marker unchanged | Marker unchanged |
| Rejected call (empty message, title too long, unknown profile, create or submit error) | Marker unchanged | Marker unchanged |
| Reset of the setup profile | Fresh state | Fresh state, `completed_at` removed |

Two points for the reviewer to decide:

- A second handoff from the setup chat writes `completed_at` again. The value is the time of the latest handoff, not the first. The setup soul offers "a second build based on the first", so a second handoff can happen. If `completed_at` must mean the first completion, keep a stored value instead.
- The `initiate-setup` skill's fallback for a rejected handoff calls `start_chat` again without `profile`. That call targets the setup profile itself, so it does not complete onboarding under this rule. The skill is out of scope here. The fix, if wanted, belongs to the skill (for example, retry with `profile: default`).

## What this deliberately does not do

- No desktop code reads `completed_at` yet. The app keeps its own phases until the intro rebuild (P18) replaces them.
- The renderer handoff files (`handoff-leg.ts`, `onboarding-handoff.ts`, `handoff-receipt.ts`, `persisted-handoff.ts`) stay. P19 deletes them with the rest of the old onboarding renderer flow.
- The Skip button and "leave freely" paths that mark `seen` are P18. They do not write `completed_at` here.
- Window sizing at the end of onboarding (grow to normal size, never saved) is P17. This PR does not touch the window.
- The `initiate-setup` skill and the handoff card (P16) do not change.

## Check

At `2c509ed02e`:

- `ruff check hermes_cli/setup_profile.py tui_gateway/start_chat.py`: passed.
- `python -c "import tui_gateway.start_chat, hermes_cli.setup_profile"`: passed.
- In-process run of the real `start_chat` with `env -i`, a fake HOME, a temp `HERMES_HOME` and its own `HERMES_SHARED_AUTH_DIR`. The setup profile came from the real `ensure_setup_profile()`, a second profile from the real `create_profile()`. Only `_create_session` and `prompt.submit` were stubbed, so no agent turn ran. Results: setup chat -> `default` wrote `intro: seen` and an ISO `completed_at`. A chat in the second profile -> `default` left the marker byte-identical, before and after the setup handoff. An earlier run with the same isolation covered the other rows of the table, and all matched.
- No new tests, per the lane rules. No live E2E this wave. No CI result: GitHub's large runners are blocked for this org.

Any user on the CLI, the TUI, the desktop app or a messaging chat can now type `/initiate-setup` to start the first-run setup, and the agent's first reply ever offers that command in one closing line.

Linear: NS-1017. Base: `onboarding/next` (the onboarding integration branch; lands on `main` later as a whole).

## Background

- **The setup skill.** `optional-skills/productivity/initiate-setup/` is the runbook for first-run setup. The agent reads it, learns about the user, and sets Hermes up for them. It is an *optional* skill: it ships in the repo, but Hermes never installs it into a profile. Its `scripts/host_facts.py` collects facts about the machine (OS, RAM, GPU class, account state and similar).
- **Prompt built-in.** A slash command that adds no model tool and no engine. It turns into one normal user turn with a prepared body. `/plan`, `/learn` and `/init` already work this way. The system prompt does not change, so the per-conversation prompt cache stays valid.
- **First-contact note.** A one-time note that Hermes attaches to the first message a profile ever receives. It asks the model for a short introduction. It is latched in `onboarding.seen` so it fires only once.

## The problem

- No command started the setup skill. The desktop app kept its own ~23k-character setup runbook in TypeScript, and the other surfaces had nothing.
- The model had no reliable way to learn the facts the skill needs (which surface it is on, which tools it can call, the machine). It had to guess or call tools to find out.
- The first-contact note carried a separate profile-building script (`profile_build_directive`). That script told the model to interview the user, run web lookups and write memory. This was a second setup flow that competed with the skill.
- The classic CLI never received the first-contact note.

## What changes

`/initiate-setup` is now a prompt built-in on every surface. On Telegram, which does not allow hyphens in command names, it is `/initiate_setup`. Both spellings resolve to the same command everywhere. When a user sends it, Hermes builds one user turn. The turn has three parts: a fixed `[/initiate-setup]` header, the skill's `SKILL.md` read in place, and a JSON block of facts. The facts are the surface name, the tools present in this session, the primary profile, whether the user is on the guest free tier, and everything `host_facts.py` collects. So the model gets every fact in the turn and does not need a tool to read the machine. Each surface builds the turn under the session's own profile scope. The desktop decides the surface from the session's source, not from an environment variable.

The transcript shows the user's row as `/initiate-setup`, not as the whole skill text.

The first-contact note loses the profile-building script. When `onboarding.profile_build` is `ask` (the default), the note now asks for a short intro that ends with one line: "I can run a quick setup so I can help you better. Send /initiate-setup when you want it." The line names `/initiate_setup` on Telegram. The note still tells the model to do a real first-message task first. When the first message is `/initiate-setup` itself, no note is attached. `off` removes only the offer line; the plain intro stays. The classic CLI now attaches the same note.

Slack allows at most 50 native slash commands, and the registry was already at 50. The new command pushed `/usage` out. `/commands`, a lookup that `/help` also covers, now goes through `/hermes commands` on Slack instead. `/usage` and `/initiate-setup` stay native.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Start setup from the CLI, TUI or a messaging chat | Not possible | `/initiate-setup` (`/initiate_setup` on Telegram) |
| How the model learns the surface, tools and machine | Guesses or calls tools | One JSON fact block inside the setup turn |
| First reply ever, `profile_build: ask` | Offers to build a profile: interview, web lookups, memory writes | Short intro plus one line offering `/initiate-setup` |
| First reply ever, `profile_build: off` | Plain intro | Plain intro (no change) |
| First message is `/initiate-setup` | n/a | No first-contact note |
| Classic CLI first message | No note | Same note as the other surfaces |
| Transcript row for the command | n/a | `/initiate-setup` |
| Slack native slashes | 50, includes `/usage` and `/commands` | 50, includes `/usage` and `/initiate-setup`; `/commands` goes through `/hermes` |

## What this deliberately does not do

- **P17 (NS-1021), window sizing.** The desktop window sizing for onboarding does not change.
- **P18 (NS-1022), the intro.** The desktop does not boot into the setup chat, and it does not type and send `/initiate-setup` by itself. There is no Skip button. This PR only gives P18 the command to send.
- **P19 (NS-1023), deleting the old renderer flow.** The desktop's TypeScript setup runbook, the onboarding directives and the onboarding checks in shared renderer code all stay. They are dead weight after P18 and are deleted in P19.
- **The skill content.** `SKILL.md` and `host_facts.py` do not change. Other lanes own them.
- **Reload display (P16).** After a desktop reload, chat history is rebuilt from stored messages. That code does not know the command's short label, so the row shows the full skill body again.
- **Open questions, left as they are:**
  - `hermes chat -q` on a fresh home also gets the first-contact note. Scripted first runs can get an intro line appended.
  - `tools_present` comes from the toolset configuration, the same source that `/tools` uses, not from the live agent. It is exact for the setup profile. On other profiles it leaves out memory-provider and context-engine tools and lists deferred MCP and plugin tools.
  - The NS-1017 comment asks for unified memory, the CUDA pool, and the connected connectors in the facts. The builder does not add them, and the current `SKILL.md` does not read them.

## Check

All results are at `c66e273598`.

- `ruff check` on all 14 changed Python files: all checks passed.
- `python -c` import check of `agent.initiate_setup_prompt`, `agent.onboarding`, `gateway.slash_commands`, `hermes_cli.cli_chat_turn_mixin`, `hermes_cli.commands_platforms`, `tui_gateway.methods_tools` and `tui_gateway.prompt_turn`: all import.
- `slack_native_slashes()`: 50 entries. The list includes `usage` and `initiate-setup`.
- In-process checks under `env -i` with a fake `HOME`, a temp `HERMES_HOME` and its own `HERMES_SHARED_AUTH_DIR` (no server or app started):
  - Desktop `command.dispatch` for `/initiate-setup` gave `type: send` and `display: /initiate-setup`. The alias `initiate_setup` also gave `send`. The turn starts with `[/initiate-setup]`, then `SKILL.md`. The JSON keys are `surface`, `tools_present`, `primary_profile`, `guest_free_tier`, `schema_version`, `machine`, `account`, `signals`, `plugin_tasks`, `fork`, `scan`, with `surface: desktop`.
  - CLI `_slash_handler("initiate-setup")` resolves to `_handle_initiate_setup_command`. With the real CLI toolsets, it queues the turn with `display: /initiate-setup` and `surface: cli`. `tools_present` lists 24 tools and no desktop-only tools.
  - First-contact note: the first message ever gets the offer line. A second first contact gets the plain intro. The Telegram form names `/initiate_setup`. A message that starts with `[/initiate-setup]` gets no note.
- Earlier, at `0d16673a74` (before the rebase): `scripts/dump_desktop_slash_registry.py --check` passed, and all 17 locale files hold the 3 new keys.
- No new tests, per the maintainer's rule for this branch. The branch changes three existing tests only where this change broke them: two tests that imported the deleted directive, and one CLI test stub that needed the new note method.
- No live end-to-end run in this wave. The gateway path (Telegram, Slack) has not been exercised live.
- No CI result: GitHub's large runners are blocked for the org.
