raw.body:
The setup bot now knows who it is talking to before it says a word. When `/initiate-setup` loads the skill, a scan of the machine runs, code reads it, and a short pre-read block lands in the skill's host facts. The bot never runs the scan and never sees raw scan data.

Base: `onboarding/next`

## What it is

- **Collector inside the skill.** The user-insights collector (stdlib only, ~20k lines) is copied into `optional-skills/productivity/initiate-setup/scripts/userscan/`, with its `run.py` CLI. No outputs, verify reports, test helpers or captured data came with it.
- **Skill-load hook.** `SKILL.md` has one inline line in its host facts section: `` !`"${HERMES_PYTHON}" scripts/host_facts.py` ``. When the skill loads, the line is replaced by the script's JSON. The path is quoted because Windows home folders can contain spaces.
- **Code interprets.** `host_facts.py` runs the collector's T1 pass and applies the interpretation rules in code. The new `scan` object carries: machine state (fresh / settling / established), user level and a `beginner_framing` flag, `runs_agents` with its evidence (operator homes and sandbox accounts count as evidence), apps used versus installed with no use seen, per-machine game hours, `crash_30d` as the only health fact, "unknown" where a source is missing, and the list of facts hidden at T1. It never carries power events, user or host names, paths, account or session names, search terms or domains. All the existing fields stay. `signals.looks_new` now means `machine_state == "fresh"`, so the fork order follows the scan.
- **Cache.** The raw T1 result is written to `HERMES_HOME/insights/profile.json` (mode 0600) with a `run.started` timestamp. A later load reuses it if it is less than 24 h old and the collector's L1 detectors still fire the same way (about 0.1 s to re-check on a Mac). Otherwise it scans again.
- **Hard deadline.** The scan runs in a worker thread with an 11 s limit. On a timeout or error the block still prints, with `scan: {source: "unavailable"}`, and the machine state falls back to home-folder age.
- **Setup profile only.** `hermes_cli/setup_profile.py` writes `skills.inline_shell: true` and `skills.inline_shell_timeout: 15` into the setup profile. No other profile changes.
- **`${HERMES_PYTHON}`.** A new template token in `agent/skill_preprocessing.py`, set to `sys.executable`. It is documented next to `${HERMES_SKILL_DIR}` (English and zh-Hans).
- `SKILL.md` describes the new fields, how to read them, and what to do if the hook did not run. `MAPPING.md` records the new fact sources.

## Done-when grading

Blocks were made with `host_facts.py --from-json` from the two real T1 scans in the handoff. The `machine` and `account` fields come from the Mac that ran the check, so the grading uses the `scan` object and the signals it drives.

| case | vespyr (Win x64, established) | rtxspark (Win ARM64, 41 days) | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| established vs fresh ordering | `machine_state: established`, `looks_new: false`, `machine_setup_leads: false`. The fork leads with a real job, and machine setup is one option of six | `machine_state: settling`, `looks_new: false`. On the real machine the Spark rule still leads with setup, with no "new machine" framing | pass. The fresh case had no real input to grade (see below) |
| expert user | `user_level: power-user`, `beginner_framing: false` | `user_level: expert`, `beginner_framing: false` | pass |
| operator data means "runs agents" | `runs_agents: true` (Hermes 28, Claude Code 5 sessions, browser automation) | `runs_agents: true` (4 Hermes test homes, 2 agent sandbox accounts, Codex 5 sessions, computer-use driver) | pass |
| no power-fault material | 11 `power_removed` events in the input, none in the block. Only `crash_30d: 0` | `crash_30d: 0` only | pass |
| 0 vs unknown | `unknown: [hands-on vs remote, own commit count]` | same | pass |
| hidden at T1 | `not_visible_at_tier` lists 6 fact groups | same | pass |
| no private strings | 0 hits for 14 candidate strings (account name, home paths, host name, Steam logins, known host names) | 0 hits for 13 candidates | pass |
| block size (≤ 3500) | 1805 chars | 1835 chars | pass |

Live run on a Mac: 3.9 s on the first load with a real home, 0.3 s from the cache, 1891 chars. The same run in an isolated `env -i` home took 1.6 s and gave 1714 chars. In process, `preprocess_skill_content` with inline shell on replaced the line with the JSON in 3.4 s.

## What it does not do

- No background pre-scan at `ensure_setup_session`. That is phase 2, after P13. Until then the first load waits for the T1 pass (about 4 to 6 s), and later loads use the cache.
- The deep pass is not used in onboarding.
- The collector bugs listed in the handoff (SRUM on ARM64, Steam hours added across accounts, agent-launched OBS, Discord usage) are worked around in the interpretation, not fixed. For example, hands-on vs remote is "unknown" unless SRUM input data exists, and only per-machine Steam hours are used.
- A fresh machine could not be graded with real data. An empty home on this established Mac came out as `settling` (owned 0 days, lived-in 3/10), because system-wide signals count toward lived-in. That is the collector's rule (fresh needs lived-in below 3).

No new tests. No CI result: the org's large runners are blocked. Static checks: `ruff check` passes on every changed and added Python file, including the copied collector.

raw.body:
Codex OAuth users can now pick `gpt-6.1-sol-900k` to use 6.1 Sol's large window; the base slug stays at the advertised 272K.

Salvage of #128288 by @GodsBoy (commit cherry-picked, authorship kept). Fixes #128290.

**WHO / WHEN / WHY:** #128248 registered `gpt-6.1-sol` on 2026-09-29 but kept it out of the `-900k` opt-in until the real Codex ceiling was probed. @GodsBoy probed it the same day on a ChatGPT account whose catalog lists the slug (`context_window` 272000, `max_context_window` 872000): accepted at 684,566 / 898,681 / 918,137 input tokens, `context_length_exceeded` at ~931K and above. That matches the model page (1,050,000 context minus 128,000 max output = 922,000 input).

## Changes

- `agent/model_metadata.py` (contributor): `gpt-6.1-sol` joins the exact-slug 900K table and the `-900k` eligible bases. Exact, not a prefix, so no `-pro-900k` or dated `-900k` variant is created. The live catalog's `max_context_window` still caps the bump.
- `agent/usage_pricing.py`: the `-900k` variant is billed as the base. Follow-up: the aliases now come from the existing tier loop instead of two hand-written lines.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gpt6_tiers_registration.py`: one relationship test (contributor). Follow-up: the cap is bounded by its own ceiling (272K < cap < 922K) instead of equal to Astra's separately probed cap; dropped a negative for the unreleased `gpt-6.1-luna-900k` and a duplicate eligibility assert.
- Docs: `gpt-6.1-sol-900k` added to the `-900k` examples; dropped `gpt-6-terra-900k`, which was never published and `/model` rejects.

## Validation

| Check | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `gpt-6.1-sol` context (Codex) | 272K | 272K |
| `gpt-6.1-sol-900k` context, no catalog entry | 272K | 900K |
| `gpt-6.1-sol-900k` context, catalog max 872K | 272K | 872K |
| `/model gpt-6.1-sol-900k` | rejected | accepted |
| `gpt-6.1-sol-pro-900k` | rejected | rejected |
| wire slug for `-900k` | sent unchanged | stripped to `gpt-6.1-sol` |
| picker, discovery lists `gpt-6.1-sol` | no variant | variant right after the base |

- Real-import probe run against a real Codex OAuth token on both trees. Our account's catalog doesn't list `gpt-6.1-sol` yet, so the picker there gains nothing (no dead entry). The catalog-listed case was checked with a seeded catalog cache.
- Mutation check: reverting the two source files fails the new test.
- Targeted tests (32 files that touch 900k / 6.1-sol / pricing / codex models): 844 passed, 41 failed. The failing set is identical on the base commit. Every failure is the test suite's real-home I/O guard firing because the local worktree sits under `~/.hermes`, not a code failure.

raw.body:
Multi-turn chats against a llama.cpp `/v1/responses` server no longer fail with HTTP 400 "Cannot determine type of 'item'". Every Responses input role item now carries `type: "message"`.

Salvage of #91742 by @huanshan5195. Their commit is cherry-picked with authorship preserved. Our follow-up fixes a regression in the original PR. Its routing (typed user items go through the existing role validator) was first proposed in #126090 by @hosakb.

## Why

llama.cpp's `server-chat.cpp` requires `type: "message"` on assistant input items. Hermes sent every replayed assistant turn without a type: plain replies, and the `" "` follower after a replayed reasoning block. As a result, any second turn against a self-hosted llama.cpp Responses endpoint was rejected. User items without a type are accepted there, but stamping both roles keeps the wire shape uniform, and the OpenAI spec allows it.

## Changes

- Contributor commit (fc6d0e0c):
  - `_role_message_item()` builds every converter/preflight role item with `type: "message"`.
  - The auxiliary Codex adapter's empty-input fallback uses it too.
  - Test expectations are updated to the typed shape.
- Our follow-up (ecdda9cd):
  - `_preflight_message` keeps its strict `output_text` path only for replayed assistant output: list content that carries `id`/`status`/`phase`.
  - All other typed messages go through `_preflight_role_message`, the existing role validator. Without this, the original PR routed typed user items to a text-only validator. Every turn with an image in its history then failed preflight with `unsupported type 'input_image'`, on every `codex_responses` route.
  - Preflight is now a no-op on the converter's own output. It no longer adds a `status` the converter never sent.
  - The `content` annotations widened to `Any` are back to lists.
  - The native-compaction summary carrier also carries the type.
  - The PR's 9 new adapter tests are collapsed into 1 converter → preflight invariant, parametrized over the default and `codex_backend` issuers, including a user image turn.

## Validation

| Check | origin/main | #91742 head | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Live llama.cpp (llama-server, Qwen2.5-0.5B): real `_build_api_kwargs` + preflight, POST `/v1/responses`, 2-turn history | 400 "Cannot determine type of 'item'" | 200 | 200, correct answer |
| Real `AIAgent` kwargs + preflight, vision model, image in history (custom base_url and ChatGPT Codex backend) | passes | `ValueError: unsupported type 'input_image'` | passes, image part kept |
| New invariant test | fails | fails | passes |

- Targeted suites (adapter, native compaction, provider parity, empty-tool replay, stale replay prune, Codex transport, estimator parity, and more): every local failure also fails on origin/main with the same test IDs. They are environment-only (a home-I/O test guard and macOS fd limits).
- Replayed `codex_message_items` bytes are identical to origin/main for both issuers. Preflight run twice on its own output gives the same result.
- Plain role items gain one `type` key, so an in-flight conversation takes one prompt-cache miss on the first request after upgrade, then stays stable.
- `ruff` and `check-windows-footguns` are clean.

### Summary Owner-submitted pin bump for **whatsapp-agent-platform**: v0.1.1 → [v0.2.0](https://github.com/ahtishamdilawar/hermes-whatsapp-agent-platform/releases/tag/v0.2.0), which adds media support (receive and send photos, voice notes, audio, video, documents and stickers). Because that changes what the plugin sends and stores, the `description` Disclosure changes too (see below). Fields changed in `plugin-catalog/whatsapp-agent-platform.yaml`: - `sha`: `b2443012d5cdfcae949c3aa6996702f0b650f3ab` → `4d8fc1c482ed06a34b6609b1dcdf59e370de7d40`, the `v0.2.0` **commit** (not the annotated-tag object) - `version`: `"0.1.1"` → `"0.2.0"` (matches `plugin.yaml` at the pin) - `docs_url`: README pinned to the new sha - `description`: see "Description change" `requires_hermes` (`>=0.21.4`), `capabilities` and everything else are unchanged. ### Upstream range being adopted [`v0.1.1...v0.2.0`](https://github.com/ahtishamdilawar/hermes-whatsapp-agent-platform/compare/v0.1.1...v0.2.0) (full notes in the [release](https://github.com/ahtishamdilawar/hermes-whatsapp-agent-platform/releases/tag/v0.2.0) and `CHANGELOG.md`): - **Receive media**: downloaded only from Meta's media host (`lookaside.fbsbx.com`: https, no redirects, byte cap, sha256 check), only for authorised senders, into Hermes's own media cache via the kind-specific `cache_*_from_bytes_async` helpers; voice notes go to Hermes STT; failures reach the agent as a note and never stop polling. - **Send media**: `send_image_file`, `send_video`, `send_voice`, `send_document`, `send_image` overrides (upload → message); formats WhatsApp refuses are converted or sent as files; image decoding is bounded (25 MP) so a decompression bomb can't exhaust memory; a send whose outcome is unknown is never retried. - **Image URLs in replies** are fetched with Hermes's SSRF-guarded `cache_image_from_url` (no plugin key involved). - **Cron / standalone attachments**, **reactions** forwarded to hooks and `gateway_platform_event` (no agent turn), and an off switch `WHATSAPP_AGENT_PLATFORM_MEDIA_ENABLED`. - A narrow name-based never-upload list on top of Hermes's delivery policy; a hardening fix for malformed inbound messages. ### Description change 0.2.0 adds media, so the Disclosure changes as well as `sha`/`version`/`docs_url`. The feature list is shorter and now says "text and media". The Disclosure adds: the second Meta host `lookaside.fbsbx.com`, which receives the same key for downloads (other hosts and redirects are refused), and that files are part of what goes to Meta; that image URLs in replies are fetched by Hermes's SSRF-guarded downloader without the key, which reveals the server's IP to that host; that files go only to the creator and Meta keeps uploads for up to 30 days; that received files are cached under `HERMES_HOME` (deleted by Hermes after about 24 h while the gateway runs) and may reach the configured model, vision or speech-to-text provider; and that `WHATSAPP_AGENT_PLATFORM_MEDIA_ENABLED=false` disables media. The two sentences added at merge (sender policy, key storage) and the "; stores … no self-update." clause are unchanged, word for word. Each claim is backed below by a file:line or test at the pinned sha.

raw.body:
The desktop app now draws the setup bot's `setup_choose` questions and its `start_chat` handoff as native chat cards, and a handoff moves you into the new chat only when you are watching the chat that started it.

Linear: NS-1020. Base: onboarding/next (the onboarding integration branch; lands on main later as a whole)

## Background

- **Setup chat.** The first-run onboarding is being rebuilt as an ordinary chat with a "setup bot": a plain Hermes profile (the setup profile) that runs a skill and talks to the user.
- **`setup_choose`** (backend tool, P15 / NS-1019). The setup bot calls it to ask one question or show one picker. `kind` is `question`, `accent`, `theme`, `layout`, `connectors` or `plugins`. The answer goes back as `{picked, intent}`. Skip sends `{}`, which the backend reports as `cancelled`.
- **`start_chat`** (backend tool, P14 / NS-1018). The setup bot calls it to start a new chat, possibly in another profile, and hand the user over to it.
- **Clarify card** (P03 / NS-1007). The existing card the desktop app draws when the agent asks the user a question (`clarify`). It owns the card shell, the letter/digit key shortcuts, the confirm bar, the "needs input" dot and notification, type-in-the-composer-to-skip, and restore after reload or reconnect.
- **Foreground.** The calling chat is "in the foreground" when it is the session the user has focused on screen.

## The problem

P15 and P14 added the two tools on the backend, but the desktop app had no card for either. A `setup_choose` call showed as a generic tool row and the user could not answer it. A `start_chat` call showed nothing useful. The old onboarding UI draws its pickers from separate components driven by text lines, applies the accent through a one-off card, and watches for a text line to do the handoff. None of that works with the new tools.

## What changes

`setup_choose` goes through the clarify path. The renderer answers the `setup_choose` server request, parks it in the clarify store, and draws it with the clarify card's shell, key handling and confirm bar. So the needs-input dot, the notification, the composer skip, and resume restore all cover it for free. Kind `question` uses the clarify question block. `accent`, `theme` and `layout` reuse today's onboarding swatches, the settings mode labels and the layout preview cards, and apply the pick in the app as soon as the user picks it. `connectors` and `plugins` use the onboarding chips. With `intent` on, each picked row gets a now / later / save control. Connectors are read on the account owner's profile, because the setup profile has no `manage_connections`. When the agent sends its own `options`, the card shows those rows in place of the app's list. Activate and resume now also settle a stale open `setup_choose` row as cancelled, the same way they settle a stale clarify row.

The `start_chat` card shows the new chat's title and profile with an Open button. The Open button always works. A live completion moves the user into the new chat only when the focused session is in the calling chat's lineage. A new-chat draft, a settings page or another chat does not count as watching. Replayed history and background completions never move the user. `start_chat` joins the backend lifecycle UI set in `tui_gateway/server.py`, so its card shows even with tool progress turned off.

Picker cards with a search field (more than 12 rows) give no letter or digit shortcuts. Hidden rows never toggle, and typing in the composer still works there. `tools-reference.md` now says that accent, theme and layout picks apply live.

| Situation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Setup bot calls `setup_choose` with kind `question` | Generic tool row. The user cannot answer. | Clarify-style question card. Typed or picked answer returns as `picked`. |
| `setup_choose` with kind `accent`, `theme` or `layout` | Generic tool row. | Swatches, mode choices or layout cards. The pick applies in the app at once and returns to the agent. |
| `setup_choose` with kind `connectors` or `plugins` | Generic tool row. | Chip picker. With `intent`, a now / later / save control per picked row. |
| The user reloads or reconnects with a setup card open | Nothing to restore. | The card comes back, with its needs-input dot and notification. |
| Chat activates with a stale open `setup_choose` row | Row stays open. | Row settles as cancelled ("Skipped"). |
| `start_chat` completes while the user watches the setup chat | No card. | Card with title and profile. The app opens the new chat. |
| `start_chat` completes while the user is elsewhere (another chat, a new-chat draft) | No card. | The app stays where the user is. The new chat shows in the sidebar, and the card's Open button opens it later. |

## What this deliberately does not do

- **No window sizing (P17 / NS-1021).** Onboarding still does not make its one window sizing call.
- **No new intro (P18 / NS-1022).** The app does not boot into the setup chat or auto-type `/initiate-setup` yet.
- **No deletion of the old flow (P19 / NS-1023).** The old onboarding renderer components under `components/onboarding-chat/cards/` stay in place. Only the plugin-list hook they share changed shape.
- **No new tests.** The lane rule for this wave adds no tests. The NS-1020 invariant test (the handoff card does not navigate when the calling chat is not in the foreground) is not in this PR.
- **One pending component, not one renderer.** `setup_choose` has its own pending component (`SetupChoosePending`). It shares the clarify shell, question block, key hook and confirm bar, but not the clarify submit and skip code. NS-1020 asked for one renderer. Folding the two together is a follow-up if the maintainer wants it.

Open decisions for review:

- Accent and theme picks apply live only. The accent override is not persisted, and the theme mode lands on the setup profile.
- Skip or clear after a live pick leaves the applied accent, theme or layout in place, but the agent sees `cancelled`. Either restore the old value on skip, or send the live pick as the answer.
- The theme card offers light, dark and system.
- `locales/_keys.desktop.json` also gains three `rightSidebar.terminal*` keys. They fix drift that was already on the base, and the keys check needs them.

## Check

At e0978b0a72 (rebased on the current onboarding/next), in `apps/desktop` unless noted:

- `npx tsc -p . --noEmit`: no errors.
- `npx eslint` on the 34 changed `.ts`/`.tsx` files: no findings.
- `npx prettier --check` on the same files: "All matched files use Prettier code style!"
- `node scripts/i18n-keys.mjs --check`: "verified locales/_keys.desktop.json".
- `ruff check tui_gateway/server.py` (repo root): "All checks passed!"

No live E2E this wave. The card behaviour above comes from review of the code, not a run of the app. No CI result: GitHub's large runners are blocked for the org.

raw.body:
## Outcome

`${HERMES_PYTHON}` now runs a skill script with Hermes's live code and its committed dependencies, and with lazy installs off. `/initiate-setup` gets its host facts JSON on store installs and in developer checkouts.

## What the token resolves to now

A shell-quoted command prefix. Write it unquoted: `${HERMES_PYTHON} scripts/host_facts.py`.

```
HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS=1 <python> -I -c '<runtime_command bootstrap>; runpy.run_path(<script>)'
```

- The prefix comes from `hermes_cli/_launchers.py::runtime_command`, the existing helper that services and the dashboard already use to start Hermes. It puts the checkout root first and imports `hermes_bootstrap`, which selects and leases the committed generation.
- `<python>` is the store Python on a store install (from the store facts, so it follows a Python pin bump). When Hermes runs on a venv interpreter (a developer `.venv`, Nix), it is that interpreter. Without that check, a developer worktree on a machine with a store Python fails with "no dependency environment is committed".
- `HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS=1` keeps `prepare_launch` from finishing a source update inside a skill load, the same reason cron sets it for scripts.
- The script runs like `python script.py`: `sys.argv` and `__main__` are the script's, and its directory is `sys.path[0]`.

Before, the token named `project_python`, the generation venv interpreter. Its Hermes package is the build-time workspace snapshot, lazy installs stayed on, and on Windows it names the uv redirector.

## Checked

- ruff, `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all`.
- `preprocess_skill_content` on the initiate-setup SKILL.md with `inline_shell: true` under `env -i` and a temp home: the facts JSON expands. Run in two shapes on macOS: (1) a developer venv host, and (2) the store Python as host, with a committed generation in the temp home. A probe script shows live checkout code, dependencies from the committed generation (store shape) or the `.venv` (developer shape), `HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS=1`, and the script's own argv.
- Windows, Nix, and sealed desktop payloads: checked by reading the code only. Nix extra packages that arrive through the wrapper's `PYTHONPATH` are not visible, because `runtime_command` runs with `-I`.

## Not covered here

This PR fixes the token only. Filed for the rest:

- #129098: one owner for starting a child Python with Hermes's environment (a `pm/interpreters.py` helper; the token would move to its `script_command`).
- #129097: the terminal's `python`/`pip` are the store Python, and `pip install` writes into the store.
- #129099: the Codex `hermes-tools` MCP entry pins a versioned interpreter.
- #129100: webhook `.py` scripts run without Hermes's dependencies.
- #129101: the `execute_code` schema promises the project venv and parity with the terminal.
- #129102: Windows `python`/`python3` Store stubs are not detected.
- #129103: the terminal snapshot never reads zsh startup files.
- #129104: gateway and cron disagree on the Windows uv redirector.
- Existing: #123316 (redaction mangles store paths), #122928 (terminal `PYTHONPATH` leak; the payload trigger is added as a comment).

raw.body:
Moves `sha` and `version` together to the released commit: vectorize-io/hindsight `d56c4acdf`, tag [`integrations/hermes/v1.2.1`](https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight/releases/tag/integrations/hermes/v1.2.1). The `image` URL is repinned to the same sha.

Thanks for already dropping the `known_issues` entry and repinning to `eb021da3` in 5e4857bf — this is the tagged release of that same work plus two fixes on top, so the pin now points at a version rather than a commit-suffixed one.

## What changed in the plugin since 1.1.0

`local_embedded` no longer imports the Hindsight server into Hermes' venv. It could not be installed there in the first place: `hindsight-all` pulls `hindsight-api-slim`, which needs `protobuf>=7.35.1` against `mem0ai==2.0.10`'s and `modal==1.5.5`'s `protobuf<7.0`, and `opentelemetry-semantic-conventions>=0.65b0` against `mistralai==2.4.8`'s `<0.61`. Relaxing one pin only uncovers the next.

Instead the plugin composes what the old wrapper composed internally — `hindsight_embed.get_embed_manager()` plus `hindsight_client.Hindsight` — and the server runs as its own process (an installed `hindsight-api` binary, else the `uvx` fallback in its own environment). Hermes' venv keeps only `hindsight-client` and `hindsight-embed`, both declared in the plugin's `pyproject.toml`, so nothing is fetched at runtime and cloud-mode users never pay for the local-ML stack (482 MB on macOS arm64, 3.2 GB on Linux x86_64 with the CUDA wheels).

Existing embedded users keep their data: the profile decides the daemon, so the pg0 database (`~/.pg0/instances/hindsight-embed-<profile>/`) and the profile env (`~/.hindsight/profiles/<profile>.env`) are the same files. Verified against a real database in both directions.

## In v1.2.1 specifically

- **First-run notice.** With no `hindsight-api` binary the daemon comes down through `uvx` (0.5-3 GB depending on platform) and nothing reached the user during it — the manager's panel lands in a log file only after the attempt ends, so a first run looked like Hermes hanging (the 6m23s reply in #4936 that retained nothing and printed no error). One line now goes through the same gated warning sink as the root-refusal notice.
- **One daemon, one client.** `_get_client` was an unguarded check-then-set and in embedded mode the "set" starts the daemon, so the background start worker and the first memory operation could each start one, with the loser's client dropped unclosed. Now serialised.
- **Repair hints point at PM**, since `hermes plugins install hindsight` refuses with *"Plugin 'hindsight' already exists"* once installed (verified) — they now say `hermes pm repair` / `hermes plugins update hindsight`.
- **`plugin.yaml` carries no dependency list**, with a comment saying why: PM reads the plugin's own `pyproject.toml` and ignores the manifest lists, so a copy could only drift. Consent and install still list both packages.

## Also fixed earlier in the 1.2.x line

Nothing calls `tools.lazy_deps.install_specs` any more (it was reached from the availability probe, the setup wizard and the client auto-upgrade) — the loop in #126494; thanks for `af26acab73`. And the plugin works around `hindsight-embed <= 0.10.2` copying `os.environ` into the daemon by starting it from a child without `PYTHONPATH`/`PYTHONHOME`/`PYTHONSAFEPATH`/`VIRTUAL_ENV`; verified by forcing `UV_PYTHON=3.12` against a 3.14 host, where the direct call dies in 5s on `pydantic_core._pydantic_core` and the child path starts in 17s. It detects the fix from #4936 in a future embed release and steps aside.

## Verified on a package-manager install

Hermes `v0.21.5+4560.gbca2e3c`, embed 0.10.2, isolated profile, local ollama:

| | result |
|---|---|
| cloud | in daily use |
| local_external | loads, initializes, retain/recall/sync_turn/shutdown |
| local_embedded `is_available()` | True (previously False: asked for `hindsight-all`) |
| local_embedded daemon start | out-of-process, reuses a running daemon |
| local_embedded retain via `sync_turn` | reaches the daemon, `mode=append` |
| local_embedded recall via `queue_prefetch` + `prefetch` | returns the fact, `recall_status count=3` |

## Known rough edges, not blockers

- A `pip install --target` layout is not covered by the binary probe, so such a user may see the download notice and then no download. Harmless direction; missing the notice was the real problem.
- pg0 refuses to run as root (reported with a clear message), and a machine with many embedded instances can exhaust SysV shared memory — I hit that myself while testing.

## Problem

When the user picked "Show me everything" in the setup chat, the tour started late. The model first called `gui_tour action:"targets"`. That call returned 71 raw DOM items with junk labels such as "New session⌘NCapabilitiesMessagingPinned…". A second round trip then called `action:"start"` with 6 steps the model wrote itself. On the slow free model, each round trip takes 5 to 25 s.

Separately, the rendered `/initiate-setup` prompt still contained the raw line ``!`${HERMES_PYTHON} scripts/host_facts.py` ``. It also carried the host facts a second time, inside the session JSON block.

## Change

- `gui_tour action:"start"` with no `steps` now runs the app's own tour. `preset:"quick"` shows the three essentials. `preset:"full"` (the default) adds the model picker and what the interface mode shows. The renderer (`app/chat/built-in-tour.ts`) owns the stops, which are stable `data-tour` handles, and the copy (`appTour` in i18n). It drops a stop whose handle is not on screen. `targets` plus `start` with `steps` still works for a custom tour.
- The model picker step says the picker chooses which model answers. It adds a local-model line only when the local-setup tip's rule (`localSetupEligible`) says yes. That rule uses the backend catalog's `fits` check, needs a local connection and nothing set up yet, and applies only where the Local Models pane exists. If the answer takes longer than 2 s, the step leaves the line out and does not hold the tour.
- The schema adds one optional `preset` enum. The tool contract (`TourRequestParams`) and the generated TS/OpenRPC files are updated to match.
- In `initiate-setup` SKILL.md (Prerequisites and beat 7), MAPPING.md and the old runbook in `onboarding-script.ts`: "Quick tour" now maps to `preset:"quick"` and "Show me everything" to `preset:"full"`. Each is one call.
- `agent/initiate_setup_prompt.py` now puts the host facts it collects in-process in place of the hook line. The facts appear once, where the skill says they go, and the session block holds only session facts. I did not route this through `skill_preprocessing` because `/initiate-setup` runs on every surface and profile. `skills.inline_shell` is on only in the setup profile (7bb99d1cff), and on Windows inline shell needs Git Bash. The in-process collector already works everywhere.

## Before / after

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| "Show me everything" | `targets` (71 raw items), then `start` with 6 steps the model wrote: 2 model round trips | `start` + `preset:"full"`: 1 call |
| Tour copy | Written by the model from DOM labels | Fixed app copy, translatable |
| Model picker step | Only if the model picked it from `targets` | Always in the full tour, with a local-model line when the hardware fits |
| `/initiate-setup` prompt | Raw ``!`...host_facts.py` `` line, host facts in the session block | Host facts JSON in place of the line, once |

## Problem

On a real first run, the "Help improve Hermes?" strip showed in the onboarding setup chat. That chat runs in the internal `hermes-setup` profile. Consent is stored per profile, so the strip showed again in the first task chat (default profile). The setup profile's answer counts for nobody. The copy was also long and full of jargon ("bounded counters", "consent window", "install ID").

## Change

- **Gate.** `onboarding.state` now also returns the setup profile's name (`profile`), read with `find_setup_profile()`. The consent host (`consent-dialog.tsx`) reads consent only when both of these are true:
  - Guided onboarding is settled. `$guidedOnboardingSettled` is true only after the backend's `onboarding.state` has been read and the phase is not `pending`, `guided` or `handoff`. Skip and handoff both call `onboarding.mark_seen` (`intro: "seen"`). `start_chat` calls `mark_completed()`, which also sets `intro: "seen"`. So a finished onboarding and a skipped one both count.
  - The focused profile is not the setup profile. The name comes from `onboarding.state`, or from the kickoff that creates the profile.

  When the host does not read consent, the strip and the dialog stay hidden. There is no new flag or env var.
- **Copy.** English strip, dialog and Settings text are rewritten. Each "What is counted" item was checked against `website/docs/developer-guide/relay-shared-metrics.md` and the shared-metrics contract. The list is now collapsed by default. The sending paragraph sits outside the collapsed part. Keys `collectedIntro`, `installId`, `consentWindow` and `changeLater` are removed. `dialogTitle` and `sending` are added. Other locales keep their old text under the new keys.
- The developer doc now uses the new strip labels and states the gate.

## Before / after

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Strip | **Help improve Hermes?** Bounded counters only, never prompts or files. · Send to Nous · Local only · No thanks · Details | **Share usage stats?** Counts only. Never your messages or files. · Share with Nous · Keep on this computer · No thanks · Details |
| Dialog title | Help improve Hermes? | Usage stats |
| Dialog intro | Shared metrics contain only bounded counters. Never prompts, files, paths or error text. Collection is local. Sending them to Nous is a separate opt-in. | Hermes can count how you use it: session length, which models and tools run, and when something fails. It never records your messages, files, paths or error text. |
| List (expanded by default before, collapsed now) | "What is collected": 7 long items (activity, model routes, names, bucketed setup counts, reliability, a 60-word usage item, machine facts) | "What is counted": Sessions: length, outcome, error type, active time per day · Models: which ones, token totals · Features: built-in tools, commands, app areas and settings used or turned off · Agent quality: missed edits, broken tool calls, stuck loops, cost per task · Setup: which steps finished, provider connections, how many skills, plugins and jobs · App health: crashes, startup and reply speed, updates, messaging connections · Machine: OS, RAM range, GPU type, Hermes version, local model use |
| Sending | Two paragraphs (install ID UUID, consent windows) + "You can change this any time in Settings → Safety." | Stats stay on this computer unless you choose Share. Shared stats go to Nous once a day with a random ID for this profile. Stats from before you opted in are never sent. Change this anytime in Settings. |
| Dialog buttons | Collect and send to Nous · Collect locally only · No thanks | Share with Nous · Keep on this computer · No thanks |
| Settings | Bounded counters kept on this device… / Send usage stats to Nous: Upload each daily package to the Nous telemetry service. Only data from inside a consent window is sent… | Counts only, kept on this computer. Never your messages, files, paths or error text. / Share usage stats with Nous: Sends stats to Nous once a day with a random ID for this profile. Stats from before you opted in are never sent. Needs collection on. |

Three items were added to the list you proposed because the collector records them: agent quality, active time, and provider connections plus config counts.

- `npm run typecheck` (apps/desktop): pass
- eslint and prettier on changed files: pass

raw.body:
## Problem

On a fresh desktop first run (free tier on Nous, no keys), the setup chat's apps card showed no apps (Gmail, Slack, Calendar and so on). It showed only the Blender plugin row and "None of these", and it gave no sign that anything was missing.

## Root cause

- `apps/desktop/src/store/connector-catalog.ts:48` asked `connectors.list` with the **setup session** as the owner (`{ owner: { session_id, type: 'session' } }`).
- A session-owned list only reports connectors the session itself can use. `tui_gateway/methods_connectors.py:110` (`_session_connector_gate`) returns `available: false` when `manage_connections` is not among the session's tools.
- The setup profile only has the tools for its setup steps (`hermes_cli/setup_profile.py:22`, `_SETUP_TOOLSETS = ["setup", "start_chat", "no_mcp"]`, since d8ddf55022). So the gate always said no.
- `apps/desktop/src/components/onboarding-chat/cards/setup.tsx:86` shows the "not available" line only when there are no plugins. With Blender listed, the card showed plugin rows and nothing else.

## Live repro

Setup: a copy of the play sandbox, run as the setup profile's backend (`HERMES_HOME=<copy>/profiles/hermes-setup`, `HERMES_GUEST_ONBOARDING=1`). The calls are real transport-bound JSON-RPC to the real Nous gateway, and the agent is really built. The free-tier identity is the one in the root `auth.json`, which profiles fall back to.

| Call | Result |
|---|---|
| Before: `connectors.list {owner: session}` (what the apps card sent) | `available=false`, 0 connectors. The session's toolsets are `catalog, desktop_ui, setup, start_chat`, with no `manage_connections` |
| After: `connectors.list {owner: account, profile: hermes-setup}` (what both cards now send) | `available=true`, 59 connectors (gmail, googlecalendar, notion, googlesheets, slack, …) |

## Fix

- The catalog now reads the **account-owned** `connectors.list` on the backend that owns the session. This is the same read the Connectors page makes. The setup session's toolset is left alone on purpose: the setup profile stays narrow.
- The setup card (`setup-rows.ts`) now reads the same cached catalog instead of running its own query, so both cards give the same answer.
- If the account really has no connectors, the combined card now says so in one line above the plugin rows, instead of showing the plugins alone.

## Copy change

- `gui_tour` preset `quick` now includes the model picker step, so it has four steps. The local-model line logic is unchanged. `full` = quick + the extra steps for the current layout.
- Removed the separate model-picker text step before the tour offer from `onboarding-script.ts` and from `initiate-setup` step 7 (and its `MAPPING.md` row). The skill docs are regenerated.
- The `gui_tour` preset description says "four essentials".

Checks: desktop typecheck, eslint on changed files, `check-windows-footguns.py --all`, and `generate-skill-docs.py` (no leftover diff). No gateway contract changed.

## Problem

From play-testing the desktop setup chat:

- The window stays too small when you pick a layout. Only the first pick grew the window, by fixed pixel amounts. Pick Basic first and you get 845x640. Switch to Elite after that and the window does not grow.

- **One sizing function, two modes.** `windowSize(mode, workArea)` in `electron/window-state.ts` replaces `firstLaunchSize`. Each mode is a share of the display work area, clamped, and never larger than the work area.
  - `normal`: 85% x 85%, clamped 1220x800 to 1600x1000. The first window and every layout pick use it. This raises P01's 75% x 80%.
  - `onboarding`: 45% x 80%, clamped 660x700 to 820x900. This is the setup chat before a layout exists. The old fixed 600x640 was only 545 CSS px wide at the 110% default zoom.
- **One IPC.** `hermes:window:size` (in `electron/window-growth.ts`) replaces `grow` and `solo-boot`. `chat-onboarding-window.ts` and `LAYOUT_GROWTH` are gone. `normal` grows each axis, centered, and never shrinks a window the user made bigger. It skips maximized and full-screen windows.

raw.body:
## Problem
1. After a setup card is submitted, the next model turn takes 5-25 s and the thread shows nothing useful.
2. The plugin install card says "Installing…" with an indeterminate bar and nothing else.

## Root cause
- **Hidden `[setup]` prompt** (`cards/frame.tsx:22`): `submit.ts:462-467` appends no user row for a hidden send. The runtime then sees the card's assistant message as the tail (`hasUpcomingMessage` in `@assistant-ui/core`, used at `lib/incremental-external-store-runtime.ts:225`), so no pre-first-token placeholder row appears. The card message's gap row (`TurnActivityIndicator`, `status.tsx`) timed the wait from the card's last change, so it read as a stale "2m 10s" and not as "working".
- **setup_choose path**: `toolNarratesWait` (`turn-activity.ts:60`) treated the answered but still open `setup_choose` call as a tool that carries its own timer, so the row stayed hidden. When the result landed, the row waited out the 2 s quiet window.
- **Both paths, guided chat**: the guided chat does not draw reasoning (`message-parts.tsx:398`), but `activitySignature` counted streamed reasoning as progress. The placeholder vanished on the first reasoning token, and the gap row never qualified while the model thought (observed live: 13 s blank).
- **Install card**: the catalog worker (`tools/connectors/catalog.py`) moved a row to `initiated` with `detail=""` and reported nothing until it finished.

## Change
- `TurnActivityIndicator` counts the user handing the turn back (a new turn under the card, or an answered question card) as progress. The row shows at once and times from that moment. Question cards neither narrate the wait nor count as agent progress. Reasoning that the transcript does not draw is not progress. A reply that has only thought so far keeps `ResponseLoadingIndicator`, the same row a normal send shows.
- Catalog installs report their phase through the existing `operation.refresh` → `connection.update` detail: "Downloading…", "Installing Python packages…" (only when the plugin declares dependencies), and "Loading its tools…". `dashboard_install_plugin` takes an optional `on_step` for this. The card draws the step as one muted line under the bar. No new RPC and no contract change.

Verified live in a scratch Electron run (guest onboarding, free model): the look/connectors/layout cards, a forced setup_choose accent card, and a real Blender install ("Downloading…" for 21 s, then "Loading its tools…", then Installed).

raw.body:
## Problem

`/initiate-setup` ran the full user scan on the first model turn. The user waited for the scan (about 5 s on a real machine) before the model could answer. Ledger R-BS-06 asked for a background scan that starts when the setup profile is ensured.

## Change

- `agent/initiate_setup_prompt.py` now owns one in-flight scan per Hermes home (`start_user_scan()`, keyed by `hermes_home_key()`). The job lives here because `host_facts.py` is loaded fresh on every call. The worker starts through `spawn_context_thread`, so it keeps the caller's profile scope.
- `onboarding.ensure_setup_profile` and `onboarding.ensure_setup_session` start the scan after they succeed. They bind the setup home with `_session_profile_runtime_scope(..., hydrate_secrets=False)`. A failed start logs a warning and does not fail the RPC, because the first turn can still scan on its own.
- `build_initiate_setup_prompt` joins a running scan within the existing deadline (`SCAN_DEADLINE_S`) and does not scan a second time. When the scan has already finished, the next build starts a new job that reads `<setup home>/insights/profile.json` (source `cache`).
- Across processes: on the desktop, the setup RPCs run in the primary profile's backend, and the setup chat's `/initiate-setup` runs in the setup profile's own backend. `host_facts.py` now holds a lease file, `<home>/insights/profile.json.scanning`, for each full scan. It creates the file with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` and removes it in `finally`. A second process that finds a live lease does not scan. It polls until the owner publishes `profile.json`, then returns it as `cache`. A lease older than `2 × SCAN_DEADLINE_S` (22 s) counts as abandoned, and the next process removes it and scans. Staleness uses the file's mtime, not a pid check (`os.kill(pid, 0)` is not safe on Windows). The same lease covers the inline-shell hook, which runs `host_facts.py` as its own process.
- `host_facts.py`: the thread body is split into `scan_into(box)` and `scan_outcome(worker, box)`. `collect()` takes a `(profile, source)` pair in place of a JSON path. The `--from-json` CLI flag and the inline-shell hook still work.

Paths come from `get_hermes_home()` and `hermes_home_key()`. The code uses plain `threading`. Nothing here is specific to one OS.

## Before / after (live, `env -i` temp home, macOS, real RPC through `tui_gateway.server.handle_request`)

| Step | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `ensure_setup_profile` RPC | no scan | scan thread starts; start cost under 1 ms; the RPC took 0.5–1.0 s, all of it profile creation |
| Scan finishes | on the first turn | 2.05 s after the RPC started; cache written to the setup home only (none written to the launch home) |
| `build_initiate_setup_prompt` after the prescan | full fresh scan (1.19 s in this empty temp home; ~5 s on a lived-in machine) | **0.09 s**, `source: cache`, 1 full scan + 1 L1 re-check |
| `build_initiate_setup_prompt` right after the RPC | full fresh scan | **0.59 s** (waits for the rest of the running job), `source: fresh`, 1 full scan in total |
| `ensure_setup_session` while the scan runs | — | joins the same job (1 scan thread alive) |

After the RPC returns, `get_hermes_home()` on the caller's thread is still the launch home, so the scope does not leak. `python host_facts.py`, `--from-json <file>` and `--from-json <missing>` return `fresh`, `file` and `unavailable/file`, as before. `check_profile_scope_patterns.py --files ...` reports 0 findings. The Windows footgun check passes.

### Two real processes (primary backend + setup backend, `env -i` temp home, macOS)

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Process A: `onboarding.ensure_setup_profile` RPC | 0.44–0.58 s; A runs 1 full scan (done 1.1–1.6 s after the RPC started) |
| Process B (`HERMES_HOME` = setup home), started when the RPC returns: `build_initiate_setup_prompt` | **0.71–1.04 s, `source: cache`, 0 full scans in B** (it waited on A's lease) |
| Lease file after both exit | removed |
| Cache | written to the setup home only (none in the launch home) |
| Two `python host_facts.py` hook processes, 0.3 s apart | first `fresh`, second `cache` |
| Lease with an old mtime left behind | removed; the scan ran (`fresh`) in about 1 s |

Before this fix, a reviewer ran two processes on one setup home: both returned `fresh` (1.229 s and 1.234 s), so two full scans ran.

### Multiplex A→B→A (one process, `set_multiplex_active(True)`, two setup homes)

`start_user_scan` under A, then B, then A again: A returned the same job twice, and B got its own job (2 keys). 2 full scans in total. Each home got its own cache, and the launch home got none. After that, `build_initiate_setup_prompt` under A, B, A returned `cache` in 0.08 s each, with no further full scan. The caller's `get_hermes_home()` was still the launch home at the end.

## Not verified

- Linux (DGX Spark) and Windows runs. The owner will test the scan on rtxspark separately.
- If a backend dies during a scan, its lease stays for up to 22 s. A `/initiate-setup` in that window waits, and after its 11 s limit it reports the scan as unavailable (`timeout`). Later calls remove the stale lease and scan.
- No committed tests: this wave's rules exclude new tests. The live runs above are the proof.
- No Electron run.

The `initiate-setup` skill still described the old flow. It had a theme beat, an install beat in the setup chat, and `setup_choose` `intent` (now / later / save). It carried its own Voice section next to `SETUP_SOUL`. It was 39,255 bytes.

## Change

- **The model starts after the accent answer.** The Opening section says the app plays the welcome, `name` and `accent` cards, and their results are in the history. Beats 1-8 are the model's: apps, plugins, layout, tour offer, fork, narrowing, handoff, after. A new "Shape it to them" section says how the scan and the user's words shape the text and the first-task options. The card lists stay fixed. When the history has no name answer (setup started by hand, or another surface), the skill asks the name and accent itself.
- **Removed:** the theme beat (the `theme` kind is used only when the user asks for light or dark), the install beat, every `intent` mention, and `manage_catalog` from the tool list and the beats.
- **Connect-now** is allowed only for apps the user asks to connect now. All five "nothing connects" lines are fixed.
- **Handoff:** part 4 tells the task chat to use its first turn for one `manage_catalog` install (the plugins the task needs) and then one `manage_connections` connect (the apps the task needs that setup did not connect). It also lists picks the task does not need. Part 3 names the apps connected during setup.

## Problem

The D7 card taste decisions and Canon A are not built yet:
- Setup question cards fall back to letter-badged rows when an option has a detail, a label is long, or there are more than 6 options.
- Setup pickers show key letters.
- The theme card still has a System tile.
- The handoff (`start_chat`) card title can differ from the new chat's sidebar title.
- A failed handoff says "The chat didn't start" and gives the user no way to try again.

## Change

**Question cards (renderer)**
- `setup_choose` question cards always use pills. The rows fallback (`pillQuestion` + the `QuestionBlock` branch) is gone. `QuestionBlock` stays because `clarify` uses it.
- The focused pill's `detail` shows as one line under the pills (full text in its tooltip). The line has a fixed height, so moving the cursor does not reflow the card. It shows only when at least one option has a detail.
- A pill that has a detail carries a small dot. The cursor (ring + detail) follows keyboard focus and mouse hover, so Tab and the mouse show the right detail.
- A free-text question (no options) uses the "Type your answer…" placeholder on its single pill.

**Key letters**
- Setup pickers (question, accent, layout, connectors, plugins, theme) show no `Kbd` badges and bind no letter or digit keys. Arrows and Enter still work.
- `useClarifyKeys` `shortcuts` is now a boolean. Setup cards pass `false`.
- The setup form sends `data-clarify-choices="0"` and `data-clarify-other="false"`. This keeps the form the live card for Enter and arrows, and letters go to the composer.
- `clarify` cards keep their badges and shortcuts (plan question 4 default).

**Theme picker**
- The theme card drops `system` in `useSetupRows`, so a model-supplied `options` list cannot bring it back. The tiles use a 2-column grid. The System capability stays in Settings.

**Handoff card**
- The title comes from the new chat's `$sessions` row through `sessionTitle()`, the same function the sidebar row uses. It falls back to the old title logic until the row lands.
- Rejected: "Couldn't start that chat." plus a **Retry** button. The backend reason stays as the caption.
- A rejection now says `retryable` (true only for a failed session create or submit; bad arguments, a bad profile, or a non-desktop caller are false). Retry shows only when `retryable` is true and no later `start_chat` in the chat started. It is disabled while the chat's turn runs, because the turn owns its own retries.
- Retry calls a new RPC, `session.start_chat {session_id, tool_call_id, args: {message, title?, profile?}}`. It needs an explicit live session (an empty id is `4001`, not the ambient env) and a saved tool row for `tool_call_id` (else `4004`). It refuses while the caller is running. It runs the same `tui_gateway/start_chat.py` path, with the card's session as the caller.
- A started retry is recorded on the original tool row's `display_metadata.retried` (new `hermes_state_tool_retries.py` mixin). The row the model replays is unchanged, so the prompt cache holds. A second Retry (another window, or after a reload) returns the recorded result and starts nothing. History hydration puts it on the part's `toolResultMetadata.retried`, so a reload shows the started card.
- The next user turn tells the model once: `[The user pressed Retry on your rejected start_chat call. Started '…' in …. Do not call start_chat again for this task.]`. This is the same one-shot note channel and `announced` stamp as message reactions.
- If the chat starts but cannot open, the toast is "Couldn't open the chat", not "Couldn't start that chat."
- `start_chat()` takes an optional `caller_id`. The tool path (`None`) still reads `HERMES_UI_SESSION_ID`.
- The contract is in `tui_gateway/contracts/sessions.py`, and `apps/shared` is regenerated.

## Before / after

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Question with details or more than 6 options | letter-badged rows | pills, with the focused pill's detail on one line |
| Setup picker keys | A/B/C badges, letters pick | no badges; arrows + Enter |
| Theme card | Light / Dark / System | Light / Dark |
| Handoff title | the tool's `title` or the start of the message | the sidebar row's title |
| Failed handoff | "The chat didn't start" | "Couldn't start that chat." + Retry |

## Decisions I made (not in the plan)

- R-CA-03 describes a full-width expanding row. This PR does what the Wave 1 item says instead: one detail line under the pills. The R-CA-02 dot is in.
- The cursor still starts on the first pill, as in every clarify card. So the first pill's ring and detail show before the user touches the card.
- Setup cards also drop digit shortcuts, because they have no visible badges either.
- The other locales keep their current `notStarted` strings, which have almost the same meaning. `retry` falls back to English.

## Checks

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` (desktop): clean. `eslint` and `prettier --check` on the changed TS files: clean.
- `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all`: clean. `website/scripts/generate-skill-docs.py`: no diff. `scripts/gen_gateway_contracts.py`: output committed.
- Live backend probe against a temp `HERMES_HOME`, with `HERMES_TEST_ISOLATION=1` so the contract is checked:
  - unknown caller → `rejected`
  - an extra arg key → `4000`
  - a title longer than 40 characters → `rejected`
  - a missing profile → `rejected`
  - a valid request from a live session → `started` with `session_id`, `profile` and `title`
- Second live probe (temp `HERMES_HOME`, real `SessionDB` and `tui_gateway.server`):
  - the mixin finds the tool row, stamps it, returns the stamp, and announces it exactly once; the row's `content` is unchanged
  - RPC: running caller → `rejected` + `retryable`; no `tool_call_id` → `4002`; unknown call → `4004`; empty `session_id` → `4001`; an already retried call → its recorded `started` result; an empty message → `rejected`, `retryable: false`
  - `_pending_tool_retry_notes` returns the note once, then `""`

## Unverified

- I did not look at any of the UI changes in a running app. I launched no Electron windows, and the browser lab still scripts the old flow.
- I ran no test suite.
- I did not click the Retry button end to end in the desktop app. A real `started` retry (stamp written after a real session start) and the reload hydration were not run; the stamp and hydration pieces were tested apart.

raw.body:
## Problem

Onboarding now only records the user's app and plugin picks. The task chat installs and connects them on its first turn (D4). The code still did the old thing:

- `setup_choose` still had `intent`, which drew a now / when needed / just note it control on each row.
- `manage_catalog` was still on the setup chat's eager tool list. The desktop session adds `catalog` as a client-surface toolset, and the setup profile did not disable it.
- A catalog install from the setup chat went to the launch profile (P11's `default_target_profile` special case).
- The plugins card said "Nothing connects or installs yet…". The apps card had no note.
- One turn can ask twice: an install card, then a connect card. The renderer keeps one connection operation per session, so when the second one opened, the finished install card turned into a plain tool row.

## Change

- `setup_choose`: `intent` is gone from the tool, the inline executor, the wire contract (contracts regenerated) and the cards. The result is `{outcome, picked}`.
- `_SETUP_DISABLED_TOOLSETS` now also disables `catalog`.
- `default_target_profile` is deleted. `manage_catalog` install and search target the calling chat's own profile. `/initiate-setup` still needs "the launch profile when run from the setup home". That check moves to `hermes_cli.setup_profile.primary_profile(launch_home)`, called with `server._launch_home()` (call-time launch home, not the import-time global). The CLI and messaging `/initiate-setup` builders already use the current profile, so they do not change.
- The apps and plugins pickers have one footnote: "We'll set these up when you start." The other 8 locales have translations. `locales/_keys.desktop.json` is regenerated. It was also behind `en.ts` on `appTour.*` and `sharedMetrics.*`, so it picks those up too.
- Stacked cards: the renderer keeps one connection operation per session. When a new operation replaces a settled one of the other kind (install vs connect), the settled one is kept for that session. The catalog, connector and MCP cards read their own row's operation. So an install card and a connect card stay stacked in either order. A later call of the same kind still takes over its card, so consecutive `manage_connections` calls keep one connect card (R-AP-15). `clearConnectionRequest` clears both caches.

## Before / after (real runs against an `env -i` temp home, guest identity, desktop session)

Setup profile, eager tools the model gets:

- before: `apply_layout, gui_tour, manage_catalog, manage_connections, setup_choose, start_chat` + `tool_search/tool_describe/tool_call`
- after: `apply_layout, gui_tour, manage_connections, setup_choose, start_chat` + `tool_search/tool_describe/tool_call`. The deferred tools are the `desktop_ui` panes only.

Launch profile (the task chat): `manage_connections` is eager and `manage_catalog` is behind `tool_search`. Both are `_NEVER_PARALLEL_TOOLS`, so a first turn that calls both runs them one after the other, and neither hits `OperationAlreadyOpen`.

Install target (`_Runner.prepare`): launch home → `default`, `work` home → `work`, setup home → `hermes-setup` (it was the launch profile before).

`primary_profile(launch=work)`: setup home → `work`, `work` → `work`, `other` → `other`.

## Decisions taken (plan and ledger)

- Q8 (plan default): there is no "now-or-not boolean" outside onboarding. `intent` is deleted with nothing in its place.
- Existing setup profiles keep `catalog` until they are reset or created again. No back-compat, and these profiles are dev-only.
- Skill text (`SKILL.md`, `MAPPING.md`) still mentions `intent` and the install beat. The skill PR (#129242) owns those files. **Merge order:** land #129242 first or together with this PR, so `onboarding/next` never tells the setup chat to call `manage_catalog` or to read an intent map. A leftover `intent` argument is ignored, not an error (checked through `INLINE_TOOL_EXECUTORS["setup_choose"]`).
- R-AP-16 (setup chat knows which connectors are connected) is not in this PR. The setup chat has `manage_connections`, whose `status` action answers it; the skill PR decides whether to call it.

## Unverified

- I did not run the test suite (lane rule). Checks done: desktop `tsc`, eslint on the changed TS files, ruff on the changed Python, `check-windows-footguns.py --all`, `generate-skill-docs.py` (no diff) and the contract generator.
- I did not look at the stacked install card and connect card in a live Electron window. A throwaway store check (not committed) confirmed: install then connect and connect then install both draw two cards; a second connect or a second install replaces its own card only. I also did not look at the new footnote there.

raw.body:
P07 step 1 of 3 (NS-1011): Blender detection.

## Problem

An app declaration could name only one fixed path. Blender does not live at one fixed path: on Windows the folder name carries the version (`Blender 5.2`), on Linux it can be a distro package, a flatpak or a snap. The Blender plugin also declares no app yet. So the plugins card shows Blender as `unknown`, the install is never refused, and the setup offers a Blender task on every machine.

## Change

- `hermes_platform/resolver/app.py`, `declaration.py`: `app.<os>.location` may be a list, tried in order. The first present entry wins. An item is a path (a `*` stands for a versioned folder, highest version first) or a location kind: `command` (PATH), `uninstall_registry` (`InstallLocation` of each matching uninstall entry, joined with `file`; Windows), `app_bundle` (`/Applications`, `~/Applications`), `flatpak` (app id) and `snap`. The locators are one table. Their directories live in `known_dirs.py`. A single string still works, so the NVIDIA manifests are unchanged.
- `requires.min_version` needs a version source under every Windows and macOS block. Only Linux may have none, and it is then gated on presence only.
- With `min_version`, `availability()` reads the version of every present copy. The first copy that meets the minimum wins, so an old copy found first no longer hides a newer one. When none qualifies, it reports the highest version found.
- `host_facts.py`: the Blender task is hidden only on proof of absence. Proof is `presence()` saying `missing_app` (the same check the plugins card and the installer use), or, when `presence()` has no answer (offline, or today's pin, which has no `app:` block), a scan whose app inventory ran and has no Blender. No evidence keeps the task. Reading the declaration takes the network, so it runs on a thread beside the scan and under the same 11 s deadline. It adds no wait when the scan is slower, and it never extends the deadline.
- Install refusal and the card's `missing_app` state need no new code: they already run through `availability()`, and they work once the plugin declares its app.
- Docs: `developer-guide/plugins/application-declarations.md`.

Decisions not in the plan:
- Windows also looks in `%ProgramFiles%/Blender Foundation/Blender */blender.exe`. Blender's MSI does not set `ARPINSTALLLOCATION` (`release/windows/installer_wix/WIX.template` in the Blender source), so its uninstall entry has no `InstallLocation`. Only Steam's entry has one.
- The Windows version is read from `blender.exe` (`pe_resource`), not from the uninstall entry. It is the version of the exact file that was found, and Steam entries have no `DisplayVersion`.
- When `presence()` is `unknown`, the task falls back to the scan. Without this fallback the Blender task would disappear on every machine until step 3 ships.
- The desktop app's old seeded runbook (`apps/desktop/src/store/onboarding-script.ts`) still offers Blender on every machine. It is not changed here: P18 replaces that seed with `/initiate-setup` (which uses `host_facts.py`), and P19 deletes the file. R-P07-10 is met on the desktop only once P18 lands.

## Before / after (live, this Mac, `env -i` temp home, Blender 5.2.1 in `/Applications`)

| check | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `presence()`, catalog pin today | `unknown` | `unknown` (the pin has no `app:` block) |
| `presence()`, pin = plugin PR head `a75e7a7` | n/a | `present` |
| same manifest, darwin location = empty temp folder | n/a | `missing_app` "needs Blender" |
| same, fake 4.2 bundle there | n/a | `missing_app` "needs Blender 5.1 or newer (found 4.2.0)" |
| `_refuse_unavailable_portable_plugin` on the PR-head tree | allowed | allowed; refused (`missing_app`) with the temp location |
| host_facts `plugin_tasks` | always Blender | Blender when present; not offered with the missing location; today's pin: from the scan (sees Blender) |
| host_facts, no scan and no declaration | always Blender | Blender (no evidence keeps it) |
| `collect()`, declaration read hangs, deadline 3 s | n/a | returns at 3.00 s, Blender kept |
| `availability()`, 4.2.0 copy first, 5.2.1 copy second, min 5.1 | `version_too_old` (4.2.0) | `available` (5.2.1, second path) |
| parser: macOS `version: none` + Windows `pe_resource`, min 5.1 | accepted | rejected (`app.darwin`) |

## Step 2 and step 3

- Step 2 (plugin declaration): https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-plugin-blender/pull/2 (head `a75e7a7475512e1054092beb8dc48bd172ffffc0`; now also the Steam library on macOS and Linux, and a list of known gaps). Merge it after this PR.
- Step 3 (pin bump in `plugin-catalog/blender.yaml`): not in this PR. `load_catalog_live()` reads the catalog published from `main` (`deploy-site.yml` republishes it on every `plugin-catalog/**` push to `main`). An in-tree pin wins only in a git checkout whose catalog commit is newer than that doc. So a bump reaches every installed client, and releases without this PR reject a `location` list, which makes them refuse the install. Bump the pin only after a Hermes release that contains this PR.

## Not checked

- Windows (MSI, winget, Steam) and Linux (distro, flatpak, snap, Steam) on real machines. The Windows registry path and the `*` folder match run only on Windows.
- Known gaps (install refused although Blender is there): a custom MSI folder, the Microsoft Store package, a non-default Steam library, a Linux tarball not on `PATH`.
- The Windows version source is `pe_resource`, not the ledger's `uninstall_registry` (R-P07-02). This needs the owner's OK.
- No tests were run (lane rule). Four existing test call sites now pass `(AppLocation("path", ...),)`.

raw.body:
Bumps the `provider-status` catalog card to 1.5.11, a scoping fix.

## What changed in the plugin

Two pieces of the plugin reached past its own elements and restyled the app around them, so two plugins touching either seam would have fought each other.

The injected theme stylesheet matched `[data-slot="checkbox"]` with no ancestor scope, so it repainted every checkbox in the app. It is now `[data-ps-row] [data-slot="checkbox"]`, and `data-ps-row` is set on this plugin's own provider rows, the same pattern `memory-review` uses with `data-mrc-row`.

The glass effect restyled every `[data-slot="dialog-overlay"]` in the document while the dialog was open, which included dialogs owned by other plugins. The house overlay is a sibling of the dialog content inside the Radix portal rather than a descendant of it, so a descendant selector cannot scope it. The `DialogContent` now carries `data-ps-dialog`; the effect reads that node, takes the overlay sitting in the same portal wrapper, stores that element reference, and clears that exact reference on close. Cleanup no longer queries the document.

Behaviour is unchanged. The overlay is still `bg-black/6%` with a 10px blur, only while this dialog is open and the Glass option is on, and it reverts on close.

The `select[data-ps-select] option` rule was already scoped by the plugin's own attribute and is untouched.

## Changes in this file

Three lines: `sha`, `version`, and the `image` URL, which embeds the same sha.

- `sha`: `1264a8e112f1b2133f3f02b89e230e0df538a80f` -> `517dc1aa4047686a8899f3d81befe66d2d8cda4c`
- `version`: `1.5.10` -> `1.5.11`

`subdir` remains `public/provider-status`. Description, `docs_url` and `capabilities` are unchanged.

## Verification

- The pinned `public/provider-status` tree reports `version: 1.5.11`, matching the card, in both `plugin.yaml` and `dashboard/manifest.json`.
- The pinned `desktop/plugin.js` parses as an ES module, checked with `node --check` on a `.mjs` copy. A plain `.js` check parses as CommonJS and can pass a file the loader rejects.
- Every selector in the file that targets a house-rendered element is behind a plugin-owned attribute. The stylesheet's two checkbox rules sit under `[data-ps-row]`; the overlay lookup runs against the portal wrapper of `[data-ps-dialog]`. The other three DOM queries (`[data-pid]`, `[data-add-picker]`, `[data-ps-dialog]`) already matched the plugin's own elements.
- No cleanup path re-queries the document for overlays.
- The `image` URL returns HTTP 200 at the new sha.

Tag `provider-status-v1.5.11` on the plugin repo points at that same commit, as a lightweight tag like the previous ones.

raw.body:
P24 part 1 (NS-1027).

## Problem

A `MEDIA:/path` tag in a reply was parsed in four places on the client side: desktop chat parts, desktop speech text, the desktop Artifacts scan, and the TUI markdown. None of them matched the gateway's own `extract_media`, so a file could show on one surface and not on another. `::preview` also rendered model-written HTML live in the chat, and that HTML could send hidden user turns back.

## Change

- **Backend**: `agent/media_attachments.py` wraps the gateway's `extract_media`. It imports it; it does not copy it. It does not use `extract_local_files`.
  - Live stream (`prompt_turn._stream`): the splitter works one line at a time. Each completed line goes through `extract_media`'s rules once, and the code-fence state carries from line to line. Inside the open line, text streams up to a possible tag start. The rest of the line waits for its newline. Then the clean text and the file go out on that `message.delta`. The held text is also released at the interim seal and at the end of the turn. Text that has gone out is never parsed again, so the cost grows linearly with the reply length.
  - Subagent child windows: the mirrored `subagent.text` deltas go through their own splitter. The splitter is flushed at each tool call and at the end.
  - `message.interim` and `message.complete` send clean `text` plus `attachments`. `raw` stays for the persisted-row receipt, the interim match and the hosted-room relay.
  - History: `project_history_commentary` now runs the same projection on every assistant row. That one function covers `session.resume`, which also serves group rooms and the TUI, and the REST `/api/sessions/{id}/messages` route.
  - The inflight record and the resume snapshot also carry attachments.
  - Stored rows keep their raw tags, so messaging re-delivery and `media_repair` do not change.
- **Contract**: `MediaAttachment {path}` is added to `message.delta`, `message.interim`, `message.complete`, `TranscriptMessage` and `InflightTurn`. `apps/shared` is regenerated. The plugin SDK exports the type.
- **Desktop**:
  - Attachments are `data` parts named `attachment`. They render through `MediaPathAttachment`, the same routing that `#media:` links use: images, audio and video play inline; everything else, HTML included, becomes a file card with Download and Open preview.
  - A card stays after the text of its response, live and after reload.
  - Group rooms: `MessageTextContent` gets an `attachments` prop, and group replies carry their files. Rows that an outside writer (CLI resume, cron, the agent's tools) puts into a member session keep their files too, and so do rows that only deliver a file. The ui_meta sync copy carries up to 8 attachment paths for each entry. The echo guard compares files as well as text, so two back-to-back file-only replies are not merged.
  - Three parsers are deleted: `renderMediaTags`/`mediaTagValues` plus the extension mirror in `parts.ts`, `MEDIA_PATH_RE` in `speech-text.ts`, and the scanner in `artifact-utils.ts`.
- **TUI**: attachments show as `▸ path` link rows under the reply. `MEDIA_LINE_RE` is deleted. A delta that brings a new file seals the text so far together with its file row, so the row shows when the tag's line completes.
- **`::preview`**: `inline-preview-directive.tsx` and its test are deleted, with its registration, the prompt recipe and the doc sections. The `transcript.directives` area, `lib/transcript-directives.ts` and `TRANSCRIPT_DIRECTIVE_AREA` stay until P19, because `::onboarding` and `::ask` still use them.
- **Hints**: the desktop hint now says HTML becomes a file card with preview. The TUI hint says the TUI shows files as links. It used to say the tags print as literal text.

## Before / after (backend-only live run)

Setup: `env -i` temp home, the real `python -m tui_gateway.entry` over stdio, and the scripted `FakeLLMServer`. The reply was `Here is your chart:\nMEDIA:<tmp>/chart.png\nDone.`

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| streamed text | raw tag in the deltas | `"Here is your chart:\n\nDone."`, with the attachment on delta 4 of 6 (mid-stream) |
| `message.complete` | raw tag in `text` | clean `text` plus `attachments: [{path: <tmp>/chart.png}]` |
| `session.resume` in a new gateway process | raw tag in `text` | clean `text` plus the same attachment |
| REST projection | raw `content` only | `content` stays raw; clean `display_content` plus `attachments` |

A reply that ends on the tag line gave clean text plus the attachment. The file went out when the turn ended, before `message.complete`.

Second turn, streamed in 3-character deltas: `Social media: it matters.` + four newlines + an example tag in inline code + `MEDIA:<tmp>/page.html` in the middle of the reply. The first version of the splitter stalled on this input. Now the stream runs to the last word, and the HTML attachment arrives on delta 14 of 30. The streamed text equals the `message.complete` text after blank-line runs are collapsed (`\n{3,}` becomes `\n\n`). `session.resume` in a new process and the REST projection give the same clean text plus the HTML attachment.

Scratch checks (not committed): for 13 inputs (spaced paths, fences, blockquotes, JSON values, `[[audio_as_voice]]`, list items, "stream"/"team"/"PM"), fixed and random delta sizes gave 0 differences from `split_media` of the whole text. A 60k-character reply that opens with "Social media:" takes 0.02 s of CPU and 2 `extract_media` calls. The first version took about 39 s.

## Decisions taken (plan and ledger were silent)

- HTML becomes only a file card with a preview in the rail. No inline iframe remains.
- Cards appear mid-stream, on the delta where the tag's line completes.
- Tool rows get no backend attachments. The Artifacts panel no longer reads `MEDIA:` tags inside tool payloads. Files the reply delivers still come in through `attachments`, and structured keys such as `file_path` and `screenshot_path` still count.
- The hosted-room `terminal_callback` still gets raw text, so the peer can extract the files again.
- `is_voice` is not on the wire. No surface renders it.
- The tag shapes are the messaging parser's rules, on purpose (one parser). A backtick-wrapped tag becomes a file only when the path exists (#35695). A tag followed by `!` stays as text. A sentence-final `.` after the path goes with the tag. The desktop and TUI hints ask for the tag on its own line.
- Text that never passes the backend keeps its raw tags as literal text: group room entries stored before this change, kanban task bodies, and a Desktop connected to an older remote gateway. The path stays readable, so nothing is lost. There is no migration and no version gate, because a renderer parser would bring back the second parser that this PR removes.
- A code fence that never closes is treated as code while it streams. `message.complete` carries `split_media` of the whole text, which reads tags in an unclosed fence.

## Unverified

- I did not launch the Desktop or TUI UI. The renderer changes pass typecheck and eslint only.
- I did not run the full test suite, as instructed. I edited or deleted the existing tests that asserted the old renderer parser. I did not add new tests (the brief for this pass says no new tests). The group render fixture now feeds attachment payloads in place of raw tags.
- Targeted runs through `scripts/run_tests.sh` pass: `test_warning_callback_conservation.py` and `test_tui_gateway_server.py` (670 passed, including the 4 tests that failed depending on test order in review), `test_subagent_child_mirror.py`, `test_show_reasoning_display_gate.py` and `test_history_commentary_display.py`.
- Vitest could not run in this worktree (`React.act is not a function`, from the shared `node_modules` symlink). Tests that this PR does not touch fail the same way.
