## Problem

The first run still seeded the old 24k runbook into the setup chat. The app never sent `/initiate-setup`. After a reload, a `/initiate-setup` row showed the whole 36k skill body. The renderer phase stayed `guided` after `start_chat`, so the free-tier chip stayed hidden, the consent prompt waited and the completion metric was never recorded. Skip stayed in the setup profile. Reset existed only as a DEV console hook.

## Change (P18b, renderer side; pairs with the P18a backend prelude)

- **Boot into the setup chat.** The kickoff no longer seeds the runbook. When `onboarding.ensure_setup_session` reports `empty`, the app sends `/initiate-setup` through the normal slash-to-skill path with a hidden user row (`display_kind: hidden`). The thread shows nothing for it, live or after a reload. `onboarding-script.ts` is untouched (P19 deletes it).
- **Reload projection.** `[/initiate-setup]` rows project to `/initiate-setup` in the TS twin `apps/shared/src/skill-scaffold.ts`. The backend half (`agent/skill_commands.py::describe_skill_invocation`) is in P18a only, so the two PRs do not conflict.
- **Relaunch.** A relaunch reopens the same setup chat. If that chat has no live turn and no model words after the last answered card (the app quit during the name/accent cards or before the model's first reply), the app sends the hidden `/initiate-setup` again.
- **Intro view state** (`store/onboarding-intro.ts`): `off | starting | intro | ended`, in memory only. The boot overlay (`gateway-connecting-overlay`) is the `starting` screen: it stays up until `onboarding.state` answers and the setup chat is open. The old `GuideLoading` screen is gone. The window takes the demo shape only after `setup.status` confirms inference. `starting` has a 45 s deadline: past it the start counts as failed (`failed_starts`), and a kickoff that finishes late undoes itself. In `ended` or `off` the setup chat renders as a normal chat.
- **`demo` layout**: registered with `listed: false` (off pickers and `apply_layout`). It shows the chat only, a narrower column (36rem), the `minimal` composer and no status bar. It is applied while layout persistence is held (`modeLayout.hold`), so it is never written over the user's layout. A relaunch mid-intro opens on the user's own layout.
- **Intro copy**: "Hi, I'm Hermes." / "Let's set things up for you. Then we'll get something cool done." (English, app-owned). It types centred (never past 2.5 s), holds 250 ms, springs up in 530 ms, then gives way to the backend prelude's first assistant row (the same words), so the text is not shown twice. Reduced motion jumps to the end.
- **Leave actions** end the intro: the sidebar toggle, another chat or a new chat, a profile switch, any layout change (card, picker, `apply_layout`, Cmd-K) and any Cmd-K command. The window grows (P17) and the backend marks `seen` (new phase `left`). A layout pick keeps the picked layout and saves it; the other leave actions bring back the user's own layout. New chats go to the launch profile by name, unless the leave action picked a profile.
- **Skip** ("Switching you over to your default profile"): it switches to the launch profile (`selectProfile`), marks `seen`, and retires the tutorial tips and the local-model tip. No handoff tour follows.
- While the intro runs, the tip rotation pauses, and the provider picker and free-tier ready screen wait (the `onboarding-presence` check now follows the intro state). The free-tier notice is acked when the intro opens.
- **`start_chat` from the setup chat** ends the guided phase (`done`) and ends the intro. It shows the handoff tour when tours are on, unless the user skipped.
- **Settings → Advanced → Developer → Reset onboarding** (shown only with guest onboarding on): it calls `onboarding.reset_setup_profile` through the ambient gateway requester (bare params), clears the stored answers and the retired tips, and then reloads the window, so the first run starts from zero. The `window.__onboarding` hook is removed.
- **Rebase onto #129336:** its `useSetupChatView` (the setup-chat chrome and the 15 px setup text) now follows the same rule as `useOnboardingChatActive` and the composer: it holds only while the intro runs. After the intro ends, the setup chat is a normal chat.
- Only the main window runs the intro (`isMainWindow`: not auxiliary, not a Cmd-Shift-N peer, not a watch window). The gate, the boot-overlay hold and the intro copy use the same check.

## Before / after

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| First turn | Hidden 24k runbook + greeting row | Hidden `/initiate-setup` (skill + facts) |
| Reload of `/initiate-setup` | 36k skill body in a bubble | Nothing (hidden); a typed one shows `/initiate-setup` |
| Starting screen | Separate "Starting Hermes Desktop" overlay | The boot overlay holds |
| Demo layout | `chat-solo`, persisted as the user's layout | `demo`, unlisted, never persisted |
| After `start_chat` | Phase stays `guided` | Phase `done`, and the handoff tour plays |
| Skip | Stays in the setup profile, applies Basic | Switches to the launch profile, restores the layout, retires tips |
| Reset | DEV console hook only | Settings → Advanced → Developer |

## Checks

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` (desktop): clean.
- eslint and prettier on the changed files: clean (two warnings in lines this PR did not touch).
- `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all`: clean. `website/scripts/generate-skill-docs.py`: no change. No gateway contract change.
- `surfaces.test.tsx`, `surfaces.app-routes.test.tsx`, `surfaces.late-routes.test.tsx`: pass (the shell reads the demo flag from `store/onboarding-intro.ts`, not from the layout code).
- After the rebase onto `onboarding/next` (with #129336): `tsc` clean, eslint clean on the changed files (one old warning on an untouched line), prettier clean. The three `surfaces*` vitest files now fail in this worktree with `React.act is not a function`; the same failure happens on the untouched base tree, so it is the worktree's React install, not this PR.

## Not verified

- No live run (no Electron window was opened). Not checked: the motion timing and the landing position against the real first assistant row, the leave actions, Skip, Reset and reload, and a relaunch mid-intro.
- The flow needs P18a (the backend prelude, `sid/wave2-p18-prelude`) for the first assistant row to carry the intro words. Without P18a, the intro copy gives way to whatever the model writes first.
- No new tests (per the lane rule). The full test suite was not run.
- **With P18a (#129346, merge it first):** after a relaunch that cut the opening off, the prelude plays only the name/accent cards that have no answer and does not repeat a line already in the chat. While the intro is `unseen`, the backend's desktop auto-continue no longer races this PR's resend (before, the resend became a redirect and its row showed after a reload). The intro text is kept in two places: `LINES` in `intro-copy.tsx` and `INTRO` in `agent/initiate_setup_prompt.py`. They must stay equal.
- **Copy:** the owner decided English only, so the intro text and the Skip strings stay as English literals. The `/initiate-setup` row is sent directly (hidden), not typed into the composer. Ledger rows R-P18-14 and R-P18-19 need updating to match.

## Left for P19 to delete

`store/onboarding-script.ts`, `store/machine.ts` (`loadMachineProfile` has no callers now, so `machineUserName()` is always null), and the old build-card handoff path in `components/onboarding-chat/setup-profile.ts` / `app/contrib/onboarding-handoff.ts`, which only the old runbook reached.

## What does this PR do?

`release.py --channel NAME --branding stable --build-commit SHA` builds an exact commit as the regular Hermes app: same name, icon, package ID and desktop settings as installed stable.

Before, a commit build could only be branded two ways:

| Command | App name | Package ID | Icon |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--build-commit SHA` | `Hermes Agent <sha7>` | `com.nousresearch.hermes-bundled-<sha7>` | red, sha badge |
| `--channel NAME --build-commit SHA` | `Hermes NAME` | `ai.hermes.channel.h<token>` | regular |
| `--channel NAME --branding stable --build-commit SHA` (new) | `Hermes Agent` | `com.nousresearch.hermes-bundled` | regular |

### How it works

- Channel creation (in the CI allocation step) copies the identity from the published `stable` channel record instead of reserving a new token.
- Branding is fixed at creation, like the rest of the channel identity. Re-dispatching with the other branding is refused; use a new channel name to change it.
- Refused: stable branding before a stable is published, in a disposable namespace, or without `--channel`. The last case matters because otherwise `--branding stable --build-commit X` would silently fall back to a sha-branded one-off build.
- The workflow gets a `branding` choice input, forwarded to the allocation step and to the dispatch log, so the printed `release.py` replay matches what was sent.
- Desktop (second commit): a channel identity carries a token for the updater. The runtime used it to pin `appData/HermesBundled` and Electron's early `productName` became `Hermes Agent`, so a stable-branded build had separate desktop settings and a separate single-instance lock from installed stable. When the request's identity equals the plain stable bundled identity, `product-identity.cjs` now exports it without the token, and `electron-builder.config.cjs` skips the `productName` override, exactly as a tag build does. The updater reads the token from the stamped request, so channel updates are unaffected.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] 📝 Documentation update (`stable-releases.md`)

## Changes Made

- `scripts/releases/channels.py`: `create(name, branding)`, `_stable_identity`, `_require_branding`.
- `scripts/releases/channel_build.py`: `--branding {preview,stable}`, dispatch `-f branding=stable` (only when not `preview`), argument validation.
- `scripts/releases/channel_disposable.py`, `scripts/releases/dispatch_log.py`, `.github/workflows/desktop-bundled-release.yml`: plumb `branding` through.
- `apps/desktop/product-identity.cjs`, `apps/desktop/electron-builder.config.cjs`: stable-branded channel runs as stable.
- `website/docs/developer-guide/stable-releases.md`: usage and semantics.

Unchanged: default (`preview`) dispatches are byte-identical to before, and preview channels keep their own identity.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/scripts/test_release_channels.py tests/scripts/test_release_channel_build.py tests/scripts/test_dispatch_log.py`
2. `python scripts/release.py --channel my-commit --branding stable --build-commit HEAD --remote origin` (dry run; prints `-f branding=stable` in the workflow command).
3. Desktop: `channel-build-version.test.ts` and `product-identity.test.ts` under vitest.

| Check | Without the change | With it |
|---|---|---|
| Python tests above | 5 failed | all pass |
| Desktop test "channel that copies the stable identity packages and runs as the regular app" | fails (token leaks into the runtime identity) | passes; `product-identity.test.ts` still passes (14 tests across the two files) |
| electron-builder config for a stable-branded request vs a real stable tag build | n/a | `appId`, `productName`, `executableName`, `icon`, `extraMetadata`, `artifactName` identical apart from the channel's version fields |

Also run: the commit-admission, tag-admission, stable-release-graph and release-artifacts CI tests (28 pass). `ruff check` is clean on the touched Python.

## Not verified

- No real workflow dispatch or native macOS/Windows build has been run with `--branding stable`.
- The desktop vitest run used a scratch config, because the main checkout's `node_modules` lacks `@rolldown/plugin-babel` and the repo's own vitest config would not load.
- Disposable receiver candidates use the official identity, so they now take the no-token path too. That matches what they represent, but I have not run them.
- Full `pytest tests/` was not run; CI runs the suites.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass (targeted suites only; see above)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Linux (NixOS)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [ ] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — the packaging change is shared by macOS and Windows; neither was built
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

raw.body:
## Summary
Fix the gateway freeze from #129281 on the whole terminal path: the lifecycle guard's profile-flag scan, and the seven dangerous-command rules that run right after it and had the same ambiguous global-flag repetition. Long self-targeted gateway stop/restart commands are still caught.

Fixes #129281

## Root cause
The flag repetition `-{1,2}\S+(?:\s+\S+)?` (and `(?:[=\s]\S+)?` in the Docker/Podman rules) gives each flag several parses: `--x` splits as `-`+`-x` or `--`+`x`, and a following flag can be either its own token or the previous flag's value. A failed match explores exponentially many parses inside one C-level `re.search` that holds the GIL, so a thread deadline cannot interrupt it.

The terminal tool runs the lifecycle guard first (on a deadline worker), then `detect_dangerous_command()` on the tool thread. Fixing only the guard moves the freeze to the approval check: on the guard-only fix, the reported rclone command took 6.2s at 14 flags and did not finish at 20 or 58.

## Fix
- `cron/lifecycle_guard.py`: keep the optional-value disambiguation from #129282, drop its 12-flag ceiling, give each flag token one dash split, and use possessive token/whitespace runs. Standalone `-` option values are still accepted. Applies on both sides of the profile selector; self/sibling policy is unchanged.
- `tools/approval_detection.py`: the same one-parse flag shape for the `hermes … gateway stop|restart`, `docker -H/--context`, `podman --url/--connection/--identity`, `podman -r/--remote`, `docker compose … restart|stop|kill|down` and `docker … restart|stop|kill` rules. `_GLOBAL_FLAGS` (hermes) allows a whitespace run before a flag's value, as before; `_CONTAINER_GLOBAL_FLAGS` (docker/podman) keeps the old rules' exactly-one-whitespace value separator. Old and new rules agree on every command built from a 23-token flag/value/target alphabet: up to four tokens with single spaces (10,239,635 checks) and up to three tokens with any mix of single spaces, double spaces and tabs (42,000,840 checks), 0 differences. These comparisons are exhaustive over that alphabet, not over every possible command.
- Subprocess-bounded regression tests for both files: benign long flag runs finish, long flag runs before the target flag or verb are still detected, and whitespace before a flag value gives the same approval decision as before.

No configuration, dependency, profile-resolution or approval-policy changes. One existing gap is deliberately left as it is: the docker/podman rules do not look past a flag whose value follows two or more spaces (`docker --log-level  debug stop app` is not flagged on main or here). Widening detection changes approval policy, so it belongs in a separate change. Python >= 3.11 (already required) supports possessive quantifiers. A sweep of all 107 dangerous-command rules and all 14 lifecycle-guard regexes with long flag runs found no remaining hang.

## Prior work and credit
- @freakinghappy reported #129281 with the production command and the GIL diagnosis.
- @dskwe's #129282 supplies the optional-value disambiguation. Production commit 9546b9dd687606d676799b50a0df6e136fc6db8a is cherry-picked with original Yuan Li authorship and `-x` provenance. Their later 897fd61c2a (fork branch) also removes the cap. It rejects standalone `-` values, so `hermes --usage-file - -p <self> gateway stop` is no longer blocked there. It is credited, not carried.
- @kokhlo's review on #129282 independently confirmed the cap's false negatives.
- @starship-s reported the same freeze in `tools/approval_detection.py` on #129281; that is the approval-detector follow-up here.
- @liuhao1024's #129310 and @JerryLiu369's #129465 target the same pattern in the lifecycle guard. Neither touches the approval rules. #129310 loses the standalone-dash case, and #129465 also stops blocking an absolute-path `/usr/local/bin/hermes -p <self> gateway stop`.
- @webtecnica's #78044, landed via #93291, defines the self-profile/sibling behaviour preserved here.
- Open #88745, #98875, #98877 and #129505 are independent and not superseded.

## Test plan
- Reported 58-flag command, lifecycle guard: main hangs past a 5s subprocess timeout; this branch returns False in ~2ms. `detect_dangerous_command()`: main times out; this branch returns not-dangerous in 4.4ms once warm (~1.3s one-time cold import, the same for a 2-flag command).
- Related suites via `scripts/run_tests.sh` (lifecycle budget, gateway restart loop, live-system self-test, approval, launchctl performance, bun/deno, deny rules, grep-in-substitution, mode/outcome parity, Windows, smart approval, cron approval mode): main 686 passed; this branch 692 passed (686 + 6 new), 0 failed.
- New lifecycle tests with `cron/lifecycle_guard.py` restored to main: 0 passed, 3 failed (child timeouts). New approval tests with `tools/approval_detection.py` restored to main: the two long-flag tests fail (child timeouts); the whitespace-decision test passes there by design, and it fails on an earlier draft of this fix that widened the docker/podman rules. All pass on this branch.
- `ruff check`, `python3 scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all`, `git diff --check` and contributor attribution all pass.

These are scanner and entry-point measurements on Linux, not a live gateway outage reproduction. Full repository suite and native Windows runtime tests not run locally.

raw.body:
If you type in the composer while a setup card or question card is waiting, your words now become the card's answer. Before this change, the card was skipped and the turn was interrupted.

**Live repro:** Before: play 4 `state.db` msgs 21 to 23. Typing while the first-task card waited produced `{"outcome":"cancelled","picked":null}`, then `[response interrupted]`, then the words as a new message. The card collapsed to an "Asked a setup question" tool row. After: no Electron window is allowed in this lane, so the after-proof is a throwaway render probe (not committed). It mounts the real `ClarifyTool` against the real clarify and server-request stores, and it records the response frame. Same probe, before this fix pass (a4a1019) and after it (8034122):

| Probe | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Restored batch, `lockedAnswers = {q0: "red"}`, type "Ada" | wire `{"answers":{"q0":"Ada"}}`; card reads `Color? Ada / Name? No answer` | wire `{"answers":{"q1":"Ada"}}`; card reads `Color? red / Name? Ada` |
| Same row remounted, turn stopped, no `tool.complete` | "Result unavailable" | `Color? red / Name? Ada` |
| Connectors card, gmail and slack staged, type "also linear" | wire `{"picked":["also linear"]}` | wire `{"picked":["gmail","slack","also linear"]}` |
| Skip a setup card, then remount the row | "Skipped", then "Result unavailable" | "Skipped", then "Skipped" |

The existing `clarify-tool.test.tsx` and `use-composer-submit.test.tsx` pass (86 tests). Typecheck, eslint and prettier are clean.

## What changes for the user

| Situation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Type in the composer while a card waits | Card skipped, turn interrupted, words sent as a steer. Card becomes a tool row | Words sent as the card's answer. The turn goes on. The card shows the words |
| Skip a card, then the turn stops before `tool.complete` | Disabled card or tool row | Card shows "Skipped" |
| Skip a clarify card | "No answer" | "Skipped" (same as a setup card) |
| Slash command or attachment while a card waits | Skip, then route as normal | No change |
| Settled card | Question and answer each carry an icon at the right edge (the circled "A") | Text only |

## How it works

- `store/clarify.ts`: a new function, `answerClarifyRequest(sessionId, text)`, answers the parked request. A setup card gets `picked` (a list for a multi-select picker). A multi-select setup card keeps the rows already staged on it, the same as its Confirm. A clarify card gets the text as the answer to its first question that has no lock. A reconnect replay can bring locks, and the backend merges the response over them, so the locks stand. The local settled rows merge the locks with the new answer, the same way the tool result does. `skipClarify(request)` now holds the skip. The card's Skip button and the composer both use it.
- A new store, `$settledClarifyResults`, holds the result the renderer already knows for each request id. `ClarifyToolLive` records the request id it showed in a module map keyed by tool-call id, so the link survives a remount (a session switch, a stopped turn). When the store has a result for that id, it renders the settled card. The card no longer waits for `tool.complete`. `setClarifyRequest` clears the store entry when a live request arrives with the same id.
- `use-composer-submit.ts`: for plain text, it calls `answerClarifyRequest` and returns before the steer and queue branches. If the answer fails, the old skip-and-route path runs.
- `settled.tsx` / `setup-settled.tsx`: the `ClarifyLine` icon column is gone, and `ClarifyLine` is removed from `core/shell.tsx`.
- I changed two existing tests in `use-composer-submit.test.tsx` to the new behavior (answer instead of skip-then-steer). I added no new tests.

## Text and window size

- Chat text: `--conversation-text-font-size` changes from 13 px to 14 px everywhere. The composer input now uses this token too. Before, it was fixed at 13 px.
- Markdown: headings size in em (h1 1.25em, h2 1.15em, h3 1.075em, h4 1em), so they step up from the body text at any token size. Table text and the `::ask` question use the text token; table headers use the caption token. Before, all were fixed at 12 to 13 px.
- Setup chat: the chat surface gets `data-setup-chat` when the setup chat is shown solo, or when its session is in `$chatOnboardingThreadIds`. One hook, `useSetupChatView`, decides this for the chat root and the composer. That surface uses 15 px text, 12 px tool text, 13 px captions and a 22 px line height. The default zoom stays at 110%.
- Windows (`electron/window-state.ts`, `WINDOW_SIZES`). The work areas use the default scaled resolution, minus the menu bar:

| Window | 14" MacBook Pro (1512x945) | 16" MacBook Pro (1728x1080) |
|---|---|---|
| Onboarding, before (45% x 80%, 660x700 to 820x900) | 680x756 | 778x864 |
| Onboarding, after (50% x 85%, 760x760 to 960x1000) | 760x803 | 864x918 |
| Normal, before (85% x 85%, 1220x800 to 1600x1000) | 1285x803 | 1469x918 |
| Normal, after (88% x 88%, 1280x820 to 1760x1100) | 1331x832 | 1521x950 |

## Things this PR does not do

- It does not touch the runbook seed or the scripted prelude. Those belong to the wave 2 branches.
- It does not touch the backend. The tool results are the same shapes (`submitted` with `picked`, and `answers`).

## Decisions for the reviewer

- In a clarify batch with several questions, typed text answers only the first open question. The other open questions come back as unanswered.
- Option pills and chips (`::ask` options, `onboarding-chat/chip.tsx`) stay at 12 to 13 px. They are controls, not chat text.
- A clarify batch that was cancelled by a stopped turn now also reads "Skipped", because the tool result cannot tell a stop from a Skip.

raw.body:
The setup scan runs inside the backend again without side effects on the backend process, the lint lane goes green, and the slow setup RPCs leave the RPC reader thread. These are the fixes from the skills audit of `onboarding/next`.

**Live repro:**
- RPC reader: before, `dispatch(onboarding.ensure_setup_session)` held the reader thread for 626 ms (inline). After, it returns in 1 ms and runs on the RPC pool. Same for `ensure_setup_profile`.
- In-process scan (`start_user_scan()` in a temp `HERMES_HOME`): before, `sys.path[0]` became the scanner folder and `userscan.host` (with the `open`/`Popen`/environ patchers) was importable in the backend. After, `sys.path`, `os.environ`, `builtins.open`, `io.open`, `sqlite3.connect` and `subprocess.Popen` are unchanged, no top-level `userscan` module exists, and the scan still writes `insights/profile.json` (0600).
- Child env: a spawn through `HostAccess.run` now gets the env that the caller passes (the backend passes `served_profile_child_env()`), with stdin closed. Before, it got the launch profile's environ and inherited the JSON-RPC stdin.
- `check_no_tmp_literals.py`: 4 hits before, 0 after.
- Overlapping setup RPCs (6 threads start `onboarding.ensure_setup_profile` at one barrier, temp `HERMES_HOME`): without the lock, 5 of 6 fail with ENOENT on the half-made profile. With it, all 6 succeed and 1 creates the profile.
- Linux locale probe (`run.py --os linux --only locale.user`): `LANG=en_GB.UTF-8` gives `%d/%m/%Y` and `%H:%M:%S` from a child `locale` run. A locale that is not installed gives no formats, the same as the old `setlocale` error path. The backend process never calls `setlocale`.

**Commits**
1. `fix:` Marks the 4 tmux and zellij socket-path lines so the `/tmp` check passes. That check is a blocking step in `lint.yml`.
2. `fix:` Adds `onboarding.ensure_setup_profile`, `onboarding.ensure_setup_session`, `onboarding.reset_setup_profile` and `session.start_chat` to `_LONG_HANDLERS`.
3. `fix:` Every userscan spawn now closes stdin and takes its env from the new `HostAccess.child_env()`. `check_subprocess_stdin.py` now scans `optional-skills/`. The nested `scripts/` skip made it miss the in-process skill scripts. It also flagged 3 model-run skill scripts, which now close stdin too.
4. `refactor:` Splits the six spec files over 2,000 lines into `<stem>_<topic>.py` siblings. The code moves verbatim and nothing else changes. `run.py --list` is byte-identical, and scans under `--os darwin/linux/windows` give the same statuses, errors and insights.
5. `fix:` Moves `override_env`, the read guard and `scan_accounts` into `userscan/cli.py`, which only `run.py` imports. The package now uses relative imports. `host_facts` loads it once per process as `initiate_setup_userscan`, without touching `sys.path`.
6. `refactor:` Splits `runner._run` (CC 66) into `_Pass.run_l1/run_l2/run_l3`. The highest CC in the file is now 21, and the scan output is the same.
7. `chore:` Renames `setup_profile.mark_seen` to `mark_intro_seen` (the RPC name stays). Documents the `gui_tour` built-in `preset`. Removes the blank line at the end of `media.ts`.
8. `docs:` The desktop guide now describes the automatic scan: when and where it runs, what it reads, what reaches the model provider, and where the cache lives. The skill's own docs page is generated from SKILL.md, which is the model prompt, so the text goes in the desktop guide instead.
9. `fix:` A module lock in `methods_onboarding.py` serializes `ensure_setup_profile`, `ensure_setup_session` and `reset_setup_profile` again. Commit 2 moved them to the RPC pool, so two kickoffs could overlap. The prescan stays outside the lock.
10. `fix:` `locale.user` on Linux no longer calls `setlocale` in-process. That call is process-wide and not thread-safe. It now runs `locale d_fmt t_fmt` with `LC_ALL=<locale>` through `HostAccess.run`, which takes a new `env` overlay on `child_env()`. It checks `locale -a` first.
11. `docs:` The scan section now says that the names of up to three search engines, with counts, are kept, and that the scan also runs in the CLI and the gateway. The `/initiate-setup` row in `slash-commands.md` and the `profile_build` bullet in `configuration.md#onboarding` link to it.

**Declined from the audit**
- Scan text on the generated skill page (`productivity-initiate-setup.md`): the generator copies SKILL.md verbatim, and SKILL.md is the model prompt that `/initiate-setup` sends. User docs there would add prompt bytes to every setup turn and collide with the wave-2 SKILL.md work. The desktop guide holds the text, and the two reference pages now link to it.
- 8.1 consent step: the owner decided the scan stays automatic. Commit 8 documents it instead.
- 5.x new tests, 5.3/5.4 test edits: this lane adds no tests.
- 7.1 squash merges: the owner allows squash merges. 7.2 and 6: these are old commit and PR text, not code.
- 2.4 raw `::preview` in old resumed sessions: the prompt must stay as it is for the cache. A renderer fallback is a separate UX decision.
- 2.5 write lock in `take_unannounced_tool_retries`, 2.6 defensive wrappers, 3.7 private `gateway` helpers imported into `agent/`, 3.9 second reader of `HERMES_GUEST_ONBOARDING`: these are outside this item's scope. Each needs its own proof on its own surface.
- 3.2 other functions over CC 30 (`derive.*`, `tour_tool`, `_complete_turn_payload`), 3.3 the `_bkv` ladder, 3.6 swallowed `ImportError` and the unused `text` parameter: the item asked for the worst case only (`runner._run`).
- 4.2: the audit already confirmed this is correct. No change.

**Checks:** `ruff check` on touched .py, `check-windows-footguns.py --all`, `check_subprocess_stdin.py`, `check_no_tmp_literals.py`, `git diff --check`, `gen_gateway_contracts.py --check`, `generate-skill-docs.py` (no diff), desktop `tsc -p .` and eslint on `media.ts`. I did not run the test suite (lane rule).

raw.body:
The model can no longer break the tour, fork and machine-use cards. Their rows come from the backend. The apps and plugins cards start with what the scan saw. After each card, the backend tells the model the next step, so setup always reaches a handoff or a clean stop. The skill tells the truth about the scan.

Rebased onto `onboarding/next` with P18 (#129346, #129318) merged.

**Live repro:** I ran these on the Nous guest route (`nous/welcome`) from a copy of the play 4 home under `env -i`. Each card call went through the real `setup_choose_tool`.
- Before (play 4, old skill and schema): the tour card had its rows in 0/5 calls, the fork card in 1/5.
- After, final code: tour 5/5, fork 10/10 (two batches of 5). The rows matched `fork.options` from the play 4 host facts. One earlier fork miss (the model called `gui_tour` after a cancelled tour) led to the tour result's `next` saying "No tour" or "After the gui_tour call"; the 10/10 is after that change.
- First turn with no opening in the history: the prompt is 21,611 characters (it was 26,930). Five calls used 289, 192, 171, 217 and 287 reasoning tokens. All five ended in the name card. Before this pass, the same probe gave 164 to 803 tokens, and 1 of 5 ended with no card.
- I did not re-run the play 4 replay to `start_chat` on the final code. The orchestrator asked to stop live E2E; the lab tests it next.

## What changed

**`setup_choose`** (`tools/setup_choose_tool.py`)
- `options` is required. `[]` means the app's list for a picker, or free text for a question.
- The backend fills the rows for `tour`, `fork` and the new `machine_use` kind. It drops the rows the model sends before validation, so a bad copy (13 rows, a repeated id, a row with no label) cannot fail the card.
- `connectors` and `plugins` always go out as multi-select, with `preselected` from the scan. So a single-select confirm can never lose a preselected row.
- The result can carry `next`: the flow's next step, with the exact arguments of the next card. It covers:
  - the next beat's card (plugins after apps, layout after plugins, tour after layout, fork after tour);
  - a skip ladder from the fork on: a skipped fork asks for a card of 3 or 4 first tasks from the scan, a skipped task card steps to ONE task with a handoff, and a skipped single task steps to the stop line;
  - typed text that is not one of the card's rows: answer it, then send this same card again.
- The fork result also carries `handoff`: the message parts and the plan (build or machine) for `start_chat`.

**Card facts, per conversation** (`hermes_cli/setup_profile.py`, `agent/initiate_setup_prompt.py`, `agent/inline_tool_executors.py`)
- The facts live in `<HERMES_HOME>/setup-cards/<session_id>.json`, not in one file per setup profile. The desktop `/initiate-setup` builder passes the session key. The inline executor passes `agent.session_id`. A second setup conversation no longer overwrites the first one's fork rows.
- A fork card with no recorded facts (for example, the skill loaded through the inline-shell hook) collects them fresh from the same `collect()`.

**Handoff text out of the first turn** (`templates/handoff.md`, `host_facts.py::_handoff`)
- The handoff message parts, the build plan and the machine plan moved out of SKILL.md into `templates/handoff.md`. That is about 6 KB less for the first turn to read.
- `host_facts.setup_cards()` cuts the machine plan to this computer: only the drivers line for this OS, the Arm lines only on Arm, the NVIDIA lines only with an NVIDIA GPU, and the crash line only when crashes were seen. The fork result delivers it.

**SKILL.md** (19,321 bytes, was 24,998)
- The first turn reads only the Opening or beat 1. The Opening now says "when the history holds the name and accent answers", which matches the P18 prelude.
- Beat 6 and failure handling follow `next`. Beat 7 uses `handoff`.
- The off-desktop voice rule is back ("short plain sentences, no em dashes, no exclamation marks, no stock lines").
- The honesty rule and the rule against reciting the scan unprompted are unchanged.

**Renderer and contract**: the `machine_use` kind is drawn as question pills, like `tour` and `fork`. I regenerated the contract.

## Where preselection lives, and why

The backend fills `preselected`, and the renderer only trims it to the rows it lists.
- Only the backend has the scan. `host_facts.setup_cards()` maps `scan.apps_used` to connector ids, and adds Blender when `signals.has_blender` is true.
- Only the renderer knows the live connector list, so the card intersects `preselected` with its rows once they load. The model never sees the list and cannot drop it.

## Reviewer findings

| Finding | Status |
|---|---|
| Model rows for tour/fork still validated (major) | Fixed: dropped before validation |
| connectors/plugins single-select loses preselects (minor) | Fixed: forced multi-select |
| `.setup-cards.json` in the wrong home, never cleared (minor) | Fixed: under `get_hermes_home()`, one file per session |
| Off-desktop voice rule deleted (minor) | Fixed: restored |
| Card facts per profile, not per conversation (major) | Fixed: keyed by session id |
| Flow depends on prose alone (major) | Partly fixed: `next` and the skip ladder are backend state. Declined: a hard gate on turn completion. The model can still end a turn without a card. A gate would need a change to the turn loop, which is out of scope for this PR. |
| First turn still carries handoff and plans (major) | Fixed: moved to `templates/handoff.md`, sent with the fork result |
| No tests (major) | Declined: the lane rules say no new tests. Follow-up: `tests/skills/test_initiate_setup_skill.py` and invariant tests for session-keyed facts and model-proof rows. |

## Not in this PR (follow-ups)

- A live CDP check of the tour, fork and machine-use pill skeletons, the preselect effect, and the "Something else" second request. The lab does this next.
- The "Something else" path on a machine-first fork was checked only against the tool, not live.
- The card-facts files are never deleted. They are small, and each setup conversation has its own.

Checks: `ruff`, the Windows footgun check, the `/tmp` literal check, `git diff --check`, `gen_gateway_contracts.py --check`, desktop `tsc` and `eslint` on the changed files, and the skill docs generator (I committed the regenerated page). `check_subprocess_stdin.py` flags one file, in a plugin under `~/.hermes`, outside the repo. No tests were added or run, per the lane rules.

raw.body:
## Problem

P18 wants the fixed opening of the desktop setup chat (hello, name, accent) to be real `setup_choose` tool calls that the backend plays with no model call. Today the model writes them, so the first card waits on a model call. Also, a reload showed the whole ~27k-character skill body as the `/initiate-setup` user bubble. The first-contact offer line was blocked only when the first message started with `[/initiate-setup]`.

## Provider test (step 1, live)

History: user (`/initiate-setup` rendered turn), then assistant (intro text + `setup_choose` name call the model did not write), tool result, assistant (`setup_choose` accent call), tool result. Then ONE real model call.

- **Nous free tier (`nous/welcome`, guest minted with `HERMES_GUEST_ONBOARDING=1` in an `env -i` temp home): accepted.** The model continued the same turn with "Ultraviolet, done. I'd read and act inside these apps for you, …" and called `setup_choose` kind `connectors`. That is the skill's beat 1, as planned.
- **Anthropic with extended thinking on: not verified.** The only reachable Anthropic key outside `~/.hermes` has no credit. Every request returned `400 Your credit balance is too low` before validation (a malformed request gets the same answer). The request Hermes built was well-formed: `thinking: {type: enabled, budget_tokens: 8000}` and assistant turns `[text, tool_use]` with no thinking block. The Bedrock credentials on disk are invalid.

## Change

- `agent/turn_scripted_prelude.py` (new turn phase): plays a prelude generator of `(text, tool, args)` steps through the unchanged `run_tool_round`, so rows persist before the tool runs, interim text and tool events go out, and tool hooks run. It runs before the first model call. It changes no system prompt, adds no user row and counts no API call. When the tool round ends the turn (`break`/`return`), the loop does not call the model.
- `conversation_loop.run_conversation` / `AIAgent.run_conversation` take an optional `prelude`.
- `agent/initiate_setup_prompt.initiate_setup_prelude`: the opening is owned by the `/initiate-setup` built-in. Beat 1: "Hi, I'm Hermes." / "Let's set things up for you. Then we'll get something cool done." + `setup_choose` question "What should I call you?" (option `suggested` = `account.suggested_name` when not null). Beat 2: "Good to meet you, <name>." + `setup_choose` accent (no options). It runs only when the surface is `desktop`, `setup_choose` is in the tools, the message is the `[/initiate-setup]` turn, and the history has no answer yet for the name card or the accent card. CLI, TUI and the gateway keep the model-only opening.
- **Relaunch mid-opening.** The desktop intro (#129318) sends `/initiate-setup` again when the app quit during the opening. The prelude then plays only the cards that have no answer. It does not repeat a line that is already in the chat. It matches lines by their text, because a resumed history keeps the row of an unanswered card but drops its tool call. A history that already holds any other setup card gets no prelude (the model owns the chat from there).
- **One recovery owner.** The same relaunch also started the desktop auto-continue of the cut-off turn. The two raced: the app's resend became a redirect, its row lost `display_kind: hidden` (a visible `/initiate-setup` bubble after a reload), and a "resumed interrupted turn" row appeared (seen live). Now `tui_gateway/session_auto_continue.py` skips the auto-continue of an `/initiate-setup` turn while the setup intro is `unseen` (`initiate_setup_prompt.intro_resends`), because the app resends it itself. Every other turn auto-continues as before.
- Docs: `configuration.md` (no setup offer line in the setup profile) and `slash-commands.md` (the desktop app asks the opening questions itself).
- `tui_gateway/prompt_turn.py` passes the prelude into the turn.
- `host_facts.suggested_name()` (no scan) for the name card.
- `agent/onboarding.first_contact_turn_note` returns None in the marked setup profile, whatever the first message says (R-P18-38).
- `describe_skill_invocation` projects a `[/initiate-setup]` row as `/initiate-setup` (reload bubble, previews, titles).

## Before / after (real `tui_gateway` over stdio, desktop surface, guest free tier)

Before (base): the model writes "Hey, come on in. I'm Hermes. …" and then the name card; after reload the user row is the full skill body.
After: `message.interim` intro → `setup_choose` name (no model call) → "Good to meet you, Ada." → `setup_choose` accent → the model starts at "Ultraviolet, done. …" + connectors card. After reload the user row is `skill_invocation` `/initiate-setup`, then the assistant/tool rows above.

Relaunch (the backend is killed while the accent card waits, then started again on the same home; resume, then the hidden `/initiate-setup` again):
- Before this fix: the auto-continue turn and the resend raced (`prompt.submit` answered `redirected`), the resent row was `skill_invocation` instead of hidden, a `resumed interrupted turn` row appeared, and the greeting line was said twice.
- After: `prompt.submit` answers `streaming`. Only the accent card plays, with no line. The model starts at "Ultraviolet, done. …" + the connectors card. After a reload: the intro once, the greeting once, no user rows (both are hidden), no auto-continue row.

## Merge order

Merge this PR before #129318. Alone it is inert on desktop: nothing sends `/initiate-setup` until #129318 does.

## Checks

- `ruff check` on the touched Python: clean. `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all`: clean. `git diff --check`: clean.
- `scripts/check_subprocess_stdin.py`: one finding, in a local user plugin outside the repo (`~/.hermes/plugins/herdr-agent-state`). `scripts/check_no_tmp_literals.py`: four findings, all in `userscan/specs/*` files this PR does not touch (already on `onboarding/next`).
- `website/scripts/generate-skill-docs.py`: no change. No gateway contract change.

## Unverified

- Anthropic (thinking on) acceptance, see above.
- The renderer side live (no Electron window was opened): the auto-send, the hidden row and the relaunch resend are in #129318. The relaunch path above was driven over stdio with the same RPCs the renderer sends.
- A crash while a non-card tool runs in the setup turn (for example mid `manage_connections`) while the intro is still `unseen`: the app does not resend there (it sees a tool call after the last answered card) and auto-continue now steps aside, so the chat waits for the user's next message.
- Accent live-apply with the prelude card in the real app (the card is the same `setup_choose` request the model path uses).
- No tests added or run (as instructed).
- Seen during local E2E, not caused by this PR: `session.resume` sometimes fails with `deadlock detected by _ModuleLock('hermes_cli.local_runtime.processes')`. It reproduced on base `onboarding/next` too, before any code this PR adds runs. The likely cycle is the package `__init__` eagerly importing `supervisor` → `processes`, while another thread lazily runs `from hermes_cli.local_runtime.processes import …` (`_subprocess_compat.bounded_probe_run`). Worth its own fix.

raw.body:
Setup cards now tell the model the name the user saw, the apps card no longer shows a dead end, and the intro no longer shows the name card mid-motion.

**1. The pick's name reaches the model.** The accent card showed "Ultraviolet". The result held only `#8a2be2`, so the model guessed "BlueViolet". Now the card sends the label of each picked row next to its id. The backend passes it through for the lists it cannot name itself (accent, theme, layout, connectors, plugins). Rows the backend fills (tour, fork, machine_use) were named already, and the backend's names still win. The tool description gained one clause: say the label, never the id. The skill says the same. The contract `SetupChooseResult` gains `label?: string | string[]`, and the generated files are regenerated.

**2. An empty apps or plugins list shows no card.** Without a Nous identity, connectors are off. The apps card then said "This list isn't available right now. Reply in chat instead." Now `setup_choose kind:"connectors"` checks before it sends a card:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[connectors card] --> B{connectors_available}
  B -- yes --> C[show card]
  B -- no --> D{config on, no identity, free tier on}
  D -- yes --> E[one ensure_portal_identity attempt] --> F{available now}
  F -- yes --> C
  F -- no --> G[no_answer + notice + next]
  D -- no --> G
```

An empty plugins list (`onboarding_entries()` returns nothing) returns `no_answer` the same way. The skill tells the model to say one line: connecting apps needs a Nous account, which is free, and it can be set up later. Then it goes on to plugins.

*Why the check is in the backend:* the renderer's `connectors.list` (account owner) calls the same gate, `connectors_available()`, in the setup profile's scope. The tool runs in the setup session's turn, so it gets the same answer, and it gets it before any card is sent. So no card flashes, and the model gets a reason it can say. A check in the renderer could only take down a card that was already on screen.

*Guest sign-up on demand:* the attempt uses the existing mint path, `ensure_portal_identity(explicit=True)` without `force`. So the mint memo's cooldown (Retry-After) still applies, and a second card in the cooldown does not reach the portal. The memo is kept per profile, so the boot failures of the launch profile do not block this one attempt in the setup profile. The docstring's list of callers now names this one. The renderer reads a cached `unavailable` connector catalog again when the card mounts, so a guest minted by the card is not hidden by the prefetch from the start of setup.

raw.body:
A first-run user who hits the free tier's capacity pause now gets a clear card within a second, and a retry that outlives the 15-minute guest token renews it instead of telling the user that signing-in is switched off.

**Live repro:** backend-only desktop setup chat (`hermes_cli.main serve` + WebSocket kickoff) in an `env -i` temp home, against a local stub for the portal and the welcome host (all other https egress blocked by a dead proxy).
- Before (`fe50fc8b60`): 429 `retry_after=25`, then the token expires during the wait → `403 invalid jwt` on the same token → "Using Hermes without signing in is switched off right now" (`free_tier_disabled`). The wait's `status.update` arrives at turn end (t=32.8 s, not t=7.8 s) and says "attempt 2/3" while the thinking line says "attempt 1/3". 429 `retry_after=1069` → "retrying in 600s", silent. `session.resume` says `z-ai/glm-5.2`, no provider. The prelude's `setup_choose` args have no `options`.
- After (this branch): the same 25 s wait ends with a new token (`POST anonymous/token`, new jti) and a 200 reply. A revoked token (`403 invalid jwt` with no expiry) heals the same way. `status.update` "The free model is busy. Retrying in 25s (attempt 2/3)" arrives when the wait starts, and every line says 2/3. `retry_after=1069` ends the turn 0.6 s after the 429 with the `free_tier_at_capacity` card ("…or try again in about 18 minutes", sign-in button, Retry). `session.resume` says `nous/welcome` via `nous`. Both prelude cards carry `"options": []`.

## What was wrong

Lab run `20260930-201200`: the welcome host answered `429 at_capacity, retry_after: 1069`. Hermes waited 600 s (the Retry-After cap), retried inside the same pause, waited 469 s, and sent the third attempt on a guest JWT (a short-lived signed token, 15 minutes here) that had expired during the wait. The host answered `403 {"error": "invalid jwt"}`. Any plain 403 from the welcome host is read as "the free tier is switched off", so that is what the user saw, after 18 minutes of a thinking line.

## What changes

| Bug | Root cause | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Expired token read as "switched off" | The key is only refreshed before an iteration (`turn_iteration_prep.py`), never between retries; `welcome_route_refusal` maps every welcome-host 403 to `tier_disabled` | `interruptible_backoff_sleep` adopts a fresh key after each wait. A 403 that says `invalid jwt` is a new route kind, `session_expired`, which the existing one-shot route heal (`_recover_welcome_tier`) fixes by re-exchanging the guest credential. If that fails, the copy says Hermes could not renew the connection and the card is the retryable outage card |
| 2. Up to 18 silent minutes | `compute_error_backoff` sleeps `min(retry_after, 600)` on every surface | On desktop and TUI a cooldown longer than 60 s ends the attempt cycle at once: fallback first, else the terminal result with the reset time. For the free tier that is the existing at-capacity card with its sign-in button (the setup chat keeps Skip). Cron, messaging platforms and `hermes chat -q` keep the long wait |
| 3. Status lines late and misnumbered | Rate-limit statuses always went to the end-of-turn buffer; the three lines used `retry_count` and `retry_count + 1` | A wait over 60 s, or any rate-limit wait on desktop/TUI, emits its status when it starts. Every line names the attempt that runs after the wait |
| 4. Resume reports the silent default | Lazy session info used the configured default; the agent build later pins `nous/welcome` | `_session_default_route` reports the pinned route when the profile routes to the free tier (resume, create, lazy fallback info, live identity) |
| 5. Prelude calls lack `options` | `initiate_setup_prelude` built the cards before #129344 made `options` required | Name card: the suggested-name row or `[]`. Accent card: `[]` |

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[429 with retry_after] --> B{desktop or TUI and retry_after > 60 s?}
  B -- yes --> C[fallback, else card: busy, reopens in N min, sign in]
  B -- no --> D[wait, status shown now]
  D --> E[adopt a fresh key if the old one is near expiry]
  E --> F[retry]
  F -- 403 invalid jwt --> G[re-exchange the guest credential once, retry]
  G -- fails --> H[card: could not renew, Retry]
```

## For the reviewer

- The 60 s live cap also applies to paid providers on desktop/TUI. An Anthropic 429 with `Retry-After: 171` now ends the turn with "resets in ~3 min, send /retry" instead of waiting 171 s. It also takes precedence over `fallback.min_switch_reset_seconds` on those surfaces. Say if you want the cap limited to the free tier.
- Waits over 60 s now announce their status when they start on every surface, including messaging platforms (where the existing noise filter still applies).
- No new tests (lane rule). Proof is the live runs above, plus a direct check that `cli`/`cron`/`telegram` still wait 600 s for `retry_after=1069`.

raw.body:
On desktop and TUI, a rate limit from a paid provider waits out its `Retry-After` again; only the free Nous tier still ends the turn at once.

## What changed

#129396 made desktop and TUI stop retrying when a provider's cooldown (the wait the provider asks for in `Retry-After` or a `retry_after` body field) is longer than 60 s. The turn then ends and shows the reset time.

That fits the **free tier** (the no-sign-in Nous route on the welcome host). Its pause covers the whole service, so an early retry only gets the same 429.

It does not fit **paid providers** (paid Nous, Anthropic, OpenRouter, and others). Their limit reopens on time. Before this fix, a 429 with `Retry-After: 75` ended the turn with "wait a minute and send /retry" instead of retrying after 75 s. It also broke `fallback.min_switch_reset_seconds`: the turn ended instead of waiting on the primary.

The fix adds one condition to `cooldown_outlasts_live_wait`: the call must go to the welcome host. It uses the existing routing check `hermes_cli.anon_auth.route_is_welcome_host(agent.base_url)`. That check reads the endpoint the call actually used, not profile state, so a paid pool key next to a guest profile is not treated as free tier.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[429 with cooldown over 60 s on desktop or TUI] --> B{Call went to the welcome host?}
  B -- yes, free tier --> C[End the turn now: fallback, else the at-capacity card]
  B -- no, any other provider --> D[Announce the wait now, sleep Retry-After, retry]
```

| Case (desktop, cooldown over 60 s) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Free tier, `retry_after` 1069 | Turn ends, at-capacity card | Same |
| Paid provider, `Retry-After` 75 | Turn ends, "wait a minute and send /retry" | Wait status shows at once, retry after 75 s, reply arrives |
| Paid provider, cooldown under 60 s | Waits | Same |

Kept from #129396: a rate-limit wait on a live surface is announced when it starts, not only at the end of the turn.

Also removed: `retry_utils.retry_wait_cap`. Nothing called it.

Docs: `website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md` now says that the 60 s cutoff applies only to the free tier.

**Live repro:** real `hermes serve` backend over WebSocket, `env -i` temp home, local stubs only. An egress guard (dead HTTPS proxy) blocks real hosts.
- Before, paid-shaped stub, 429 `Retry-After: 75`: at +4.46 s `❌ Rate limited after 1 attempt … (resets in ~1m)`, then `message.complete status=error` ("custom is rate-limiting requests right now … send /retry"). The stub got 1 request.
- After, same stub: at +3.76 s `⏱️ Rate limited. Resets in ~1m. Waiting 75.0s (attempt 2/3)...`. The retry reached the stub 75.2 s after the 429. At +78.96 s `message.complete status=complete` "Stub reply: the paid model answered."
- After, free-tier stub (welcome host), 429 `retry_after=1069`: at +7.2 s `❌ Rate limited after 1 attempt`, then `message.complete status=error` with `error_surface.code=free_tier_at_capacity`. The stub got 1 request. This matches the behavior before the fix.

Checks: `ruff check` on touched files, `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all`, `scripts/check_no_tmp_literals.py`, `git diff --check`. No new tests (lane rule).

raw.body:
The 32-core runner pool is backed up behind the slow CI lanes. The four E2E suites, the two Windows E2E jobs, the Docker image build and the Nix flake check account for about 120 of the ~140 larger-runner minutes each PR push spends, and they fired on nearly every PR (66–98% of the last 200 merged PRs).

On a pull request, each slow lane now runs only when the diff touches that suite, its harness, or the code it guards, or when the PR carries the `run-e2e` label. Every push to `main` still runs all of them, and a stable-release run still forces every lane on.

## Lanes

| Lane | What starts it on a PR | Last 200 merged PRs (before) |
|---|---|---|
| `e2e` + Windows E2E | `tests/e2e/`, the shared test harness, `hermes_state*` | 4% (66%) |
| `e2e-upgrade` + Windows install/update | updater, installer, `pm/`, dependency manifests, the upgrade suites | 6% (66%) |
| Desktop core E2E | its specs and harness, `electron/backend-*`, `apps/shared/src`, session/transcript stores, packaging | 13% (98%) |
| Desktop update E2E | its specs, the Electron updater, `scripts/desktop-update/`, `install.sh`, `hermes_cli/update_*` | 6% (98%) |
| Docker / Nix | their own files, dependency manifests, `pm/`, `tests/docker/` | 2% (98%) |

Replayed over those 200 PRs with measured job times, the modelled 32-core cost of one push per PR drops from about 120 to about 10 runner-minutes.

## Changes

- `scripts/ci/classify_changes.py`: the path lists live in one table (`_E2E_LANES`, `_DOCKER_PATHS`, `_NIX_LANE_PATHS`). The classifier reads the `run-e2e` label from the API, because a rerun replays the original event payload. The fail-open contract now names these lanes as its one deliberate exception.
- `ci.yaml`, `tests.yml`, `tests-os.yml`: each lane's answer is passed to the job it gates. Called with no inputs, those jobs still run.
- `label-rerun.yml`: adding `run-e2e` cancels and reruns the head commit's CI, Docker and Nix runs.

## Tests

- `tests/ci/test_classify_changes.py`, 95 tests, green. New tests check that:
  - the label turns every slow lane on and changes nothing else;
  - every path in the lane tables still matches a tracked file, so a rename cannot quietly stop a lane from running on PRs;
  - no job gates on, or passes on, a detect output that detect does not declare.
- Four deliberate sabotages each turned the suite red: nix always on, label ignored, a dead path prefix, an undeclared output passed through `with:`.
- actionlint passes on every workflow this PR edits.

This PR edits `.github/`, so the classifier turns every lane on and its own CI runs the full suite.

## Known gaps

- On a rerun, Docker and Nix may not see the label. Those workflows grant only `contents: read`, and I have not confirmed that token can read a PR's labels. Adding the permission means changing the stable-release caller too. The four E2E suites pick up the label through `ci.yaml`.
- On a fork PR the label's rerun job cannot rerun anything, because the token is read-only. `ci-reviewed` already has the same limit. A maintainer clicking "Re-run all jobs" gets a run that sees the label.
- An E2E regression the path lists miss now first shows up as a red `main`, and nothing alerts anyone when that happens.

The task chat that setup opens now starts from what setup learned, and it talks before it builds.

## What changes for the user

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| What the task chat knows | Only what the setup model chose to write. The scan never reached it. | The model's message, plus a block the backend adds: the user's picks and a plain summary of the scan. |
| First turn | Plans and builds at once, pushed toward "one HTML page". | Says what it took from setup, asks one plain-text question with 2 to 4 concrete directions, offers to connect the apps they need, and builds after a pick or "go". |

## How

- `tools/setup_choose_tool.py::_remember` records the name, apps, plugins and layout picks into the setup conversation's card facts (`setup-cards/<session>.json`). The scripted opening goes through the same tool, so the name is recorded too.
- `host_facts.py::_learned` turns the interpreted scan into plain first-person lines (machine, RAM, apps in use, runs agents, level). `setup_cards` stores them beside the fork rows. Only interpreted fields go in, no raw scan values or private strings.
- `tui_gateway/start_chat.py`: when the caller is the setup profile, it reads those card facts in the setup profile's scope and appends the "What setup learned about me" block under the model's message. The model's message stays first. Other profiles get no block.
- `templates/handoff.md` and the SKILL.md handoff lines: the plan now asks the task chat to talk first. The "one HTML page" push is gone. These rules stay: no mock data, no routing around connectors, ask before sending, deleting or scheduling. The "I use:" line is gone, because the block carries the exact picks. The install/connect step now runs after the user picks a direction, not before the first reply. SKILL.md is 20.5 KB. Skill docs are regenerated.

## Before / after: the task chat's first user message

**Before.** This is the real message from the play-onboarding run (`start_chat` call in the setup session, read-only):

```text
Figure out what to automate for me by looking at my machine and setup, propose the top candidates, and build the first one as a working result.

Call me sid. You're figuring out the automation from my machine because I don't know what to pick.

I use: gmail, googlecalendar, linear.

Plan briefly, then build: scaffold, research, first artifact. Use real data only from connected apps and find their tools with tool_search; tools already signed in on this computer, like a logged-in gh, are fair to use, and say so in one line. Never route around a connector: no IMAP client, app password or other way into the same account; if I decline one, that app is out of this build. Ask before sending, deleting or scheduling anything, and set up no recurring job unless I asked. Make the result something I can open: one HTML page if the idea allows it. Make this first version finishable with no account I have not connected: web research with the browser visible to me, scripts, a small app, a file-based tracker, a generated page. If the idea needs an account, build the no-account core first and offer the connection next.

As you start, tell me in one short sentence that you'll ask for permissions as you go and I can say no or redirect you. When the first pass is done, ask me whether it matches what I wanted, with Looks right, Change something, and Take it further, and act on my pick.
```

**After.** The backend path ran in an `env -i` temp home. `setup_choose_tool` got stubbed card replies, the same picks as the run. `record_cards` got that run's collected facts. Then `start_chat` ran from a setup-profile session. Session creation and `prompt.submit` were stubbed, so no agent started and no endpoint was called. The lead paragraph is the new template filled by hand for the same ask. The block under it is the real backend output.

```text
Figure out what to automate for me by looking at my machine and setup, propose the top candidates, and build the first one as a working result.

Call me sid. You're figuring out the automation from my machine because I don't know what to pick.

Talk with me before you build. In your first reply, say in two or three plain lines what you take from what setup learned, then ask me in plain text, not a card, one short question with two to four concrete directions drawn from my apps and this computer, like: Should I start with A, B or C? Or tell me more about what you want. Name the apps each direction needs and offer to connect them. Build only after I pick one or say go; then plan briefly and build. Use real data only from connected apps and find their tools with `tool_search`; tools already signed in on this computer, like a logged-in gh, are fair to use, and say so in one line. Never route around a connector: no IMAP client, app password or other way into the same account; if I decline one, that app is out of this build. Ask before sending, deleting or scheduling anything, and set up no recurring job unless I asked. Never use mock or sample data. Make this first version finishable with no account I have not connected: web research with the browser visible to me, scripts, a small app, a file-based tracker, a generated page. If the idea needs an account, build the no-account core first and offer the connection next.

When you start building, tell me in one short sentence that you'll ask for permissions as you go and I can say no or redirect you. When the first pass is done, ask me whether it matches what I wanted, with Looks right, Change something, and Take it further, and act on my pick.

What setup learned about me:
- Name: sid
- Apps I picked: Gmail, Google Calendar, Linear
- Plugins I picked: Blender
- Layout: Basic
- This Mac: Apple M4 Pro, darwin 24.6.0, arm64, 24 GB RAM.
- Apps I use on it: Discord, Obsidian, Slack, Spotify, Steam, Teams, Zoom.
- I already run AI agents here.
- I am a power user, a developer.
Start from this; look at my computer again only when the task needs more.
```

With the setup-profile marker removed, the same call adds no block.

raw.body:
A portable plugin can now say its MCP server needs an NVIDIA GPU (`requires: {gpu: nvidia}`). On a machine without one, Hermes refuses the install, hides the server's tools, and says why.

## The problem

A portable plugin (a `plugin.json` + `mcp.json` + skills package that points Hermes at an app's MCP server) can already declare the app it drives. Hermes then checks that the app is installed at a fixed path, at a minimum version, before it offers the tools. NVIDIA App and NVIDIA Broadcast use this.

Some apps have no fixed path to check. The RTX Remix Toolkit ships as a zip that NVIDIA's own README says to "extract anywhere". It has no installer and no registry entry. What it does need is an NVIDIA GPU. Without a way to say that, its plugin installs on a Mac or an AMD PC, and the tools never appear, with no explanation.

## What changes

```json
"extensions": {"com.nousresearch.hermes": {"servers": {"rtx-remix": {
  "requires": {"gpu": "nvidia"}
}}}}
```

`requires.gpu` works with or without an `app:` block. The check is `hermes_platform.host.facts.gpu_class()`, which already exists: it reads the registry on Windows and sysfs on Linux, never a subprocess or a driver library, and is cached per process.

| Where the user meets it | On a machine without an NVIDIA GPU |
|---|---|
| `hermes plugins install` | Refused: `Plugin 'rtx-remix' server 'rtx-remix' is unavailable: unsupported_gpu, needs an NVIDIA GPU.` Nothing is written. |
| `hermes plugins validate` | `server availability: rtx-remix — unsupported_gpu` |
| Tools in a chat | Hidden. The MCP `check_fn` already asks `availability()` for any registered declaration. |
| Plugin catalog card | "needs an NVIDIA GPU" |
| Plugins tab and tool errors, if the plugin got installed anyway (for example a synced home) | New state `unsupported_gpu`, pill "GPU not supported", sentence "rtx-remix needs an NVIDIA GPU; none was found on this machine. Use rtx-remix on a machine with an NVIDIA GPU." |

On a machine with an NVIDIA GPU, nothing changes: the state is `no_requirements`, as for a plugin with no declaration, and the connection check still decides.

The new state is added to `PluginServerState` in the gateway contract (regenerated `gateway-contract.*`), the Desktop store type, the Plugins tab tone map, and the label in en/de/es/fr. `locales/_keys.desktop.json` is regenerated.

## Decisions to check

1. **An unreadable GPU passes.** `gpu_class()` returns `unknown` when the registry or sysfs read fails, and on Intel Macs. Refusing on `unknown` would lock out a machine that has the GPU; passing costs what happens today (the tools don't connect). The alternative is to fail closed.
2. **Only `nvidia` is accepted.** `gpu_class()` reports the highest-priority vendor present (NVIDIA, then AMD, then Intel). That answers "is there an NVIDIA GPU" exactly. It would give the wrong answer for `amd` or `intel` on a machine that also has an NVIDIA GPU, so those values are rejected at parse time until someone needs them and the fact returns the full vendor set.
3. **A new wire state instead of reusing `missing_app`.** Reusing it would avoid the contract and Desktop changes, but the sentence would say "Install rtx-remix", which cannot fix a missing GPU.

## Not in this PR

- The `rtx-remix` plugin's declaration: NousResearch/hermes-nvidia#3. That plugin must merge after a Hermes release that contains this change. Older releases reject the unknown key with `requires has unknown keys ['gpu']`.
- The catalog entry for `rtx-remix`: #129444, stacked on this PR and pinned to hermes-nvidia#3.
- `unsupported_os` still produces "Install <app>" in the status sentence. That is existing behavior and a separate change.

## Live verification

Hermes at `38505e27f1`, this change before the rebase onto `main` at `653bc4f288`; the rebase changed no line of the diff outside `locales/_keys.desktop.json`. The plugin was the `rtx-remix` package from hermes-nvidia#3 with the declaration above added.

| Machine | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| macOS, Apple silicon | `hermes plugins validate` | `server availability: rtx-remix — unsupported_gpu` |
| macOS, Apple silicon | `hermes plugins install` (fresh `HERMES_HOME`) | Refused with `unsupported_gpu, needs an NVIDIA GPU.`; `plugins/` stays empty |
| Windows ARM64 laptop with an NVIDIA GPU | `facts.gpu_class()` | `nvidia` |
| same | `hermes plugins validate` | `server availability: rtx-remix — no_requirements` |
| same | `hermes plugins install` | Passed the availability check. It then failed later, at publish, because the ARM64 native-build-tools step (`windows-deps.ps1`) fails on that machine, which has a partial Visual Studio install. That step is unrelated to this change. |
| same, RTX Remix Toolkit running | a chat turn with the declared plugin in place | `MCP server 'rtx-remix' (HTTP): registered 39 tool(s)`. The model called `remix_get_loaded_project` and relayed the Toolkit's answer. |

raw.body:
Adds one entry to `plugin-catalog/`: **dashboard-button** (community, `desktop`).

### What it does

One-click access to the Hermes Web Dashboard (`http://127.0.0.1:9119`) from the Desktop app:

- a **sidebar row** that opens the dashboard inside the main pane (no browser tab),
- an **in-app page that loads itself** — while the server is down it shows status and opens the dashboard the moment the port answers; if the connection drops it reloads when the server returns,
- a **status-bar chip with a live dot** (green/red/grey) that opens the dashboard in the default browser, waiting for the server to come up before it does.

Pure front-end — the desktop half is the entire plugin. It registers no tools, hooks or middleware, spends no tokens, and the only network traffic is a liveness probe against the local dashboard port. It never starts the dashboard itself; the repo ships an optional Windows watchdog (`companion/dashboard_watchdog.py`) for people who want it always up, wired as a no-agent cron job.

### Pin

- repo: https://github.com/g3org3yo/dashboard-button
- sha: `cd0837e50e46bb8efca6e66d63a264325a5cbcb2` (tagged `v1.0.0`, released)
- layout at the pin: `plugin.yaml` (manifest) + `__init__.py` (agent half, intentionally empty — `def register(ctx): del ctx`) + `desktop/plugin.js` (the whole feature)

### Validation (run locally at the pinned commit)

`hermes plugins validate .`:

```
✓ manifest — plugin.yaml parses
✓ manifest fields — name, version, description present
✓ requires_hermes — spec '>=0.20' parses
✓ config schema — not declared
✓ requires_env — all entries UPPER_SNAKE
✓ loadable — entry: __init__.py, desktop/plugin.js
✓ python dependencies — none declared
✓ capability probe — register() ran in isolation
✓ declared tools — matches registrations
✓ declared hooks — matches registrations
✓ declared middleware — matches registrations
✓ built-in tool collisions — no tools to check
✓ security scan — safe
✓ desktop surface — stays inside the plugin SDK surface

Validation passed.
```

`hermes plugins doctor .` → `manifest: dashboard-button 1.0.0 (standalone)` / `OK: runtime discovery, manifest parsing, import, and registration passed` / `registrations: 0 tool(s), 0 hook(s)`.

### Policy notes

- **Capabilities** are declared empty and are empty in reality (rule 6): nothing registered, no env vars, no `config_schema`, no `python_dependencies`.
- **No self-updating code** (rule 3): the plugin reads no remote `plugin.js`, has no updater, and does not touch its own files. Updates only arrive via a SHA-bump PR here.
- **Desktop surface** (rule 8): `desktop/plugin.js` uses only `@hermes/plugin-sdk` — no prototype patching, no `eval`/`new Function`, no dynamic `import()`, no script-tag injection, no app internals.
- **Owner submission** (rule 5): this PR is from the repo owner.

`docs_url` is left empty; the catalog page can render the repo README at the pin (`readme: true`), which documents the Desktop 0.20.x SDK-loader bug this plugin was built alongside, plus the standalone hotfix tool it ships for it (upstream issue #107304 / PR #107303).

The local-setup offer from #121969 now works on top of the new onboarding (`onboarding/next`). A machine that can run a local model hears about it at three moments, and none of them lands inside setup.

## What the user sees

| Moment | When | Checked live |
|---|---|---|
| Tour model stop | The quick tour's "Model picker" step adds "This computer can run one locally". | yes |
| Handoff tour, last step | After `start_chat`, the handoff tour ends on the model pill: "This machine can run models locally. Qwen3.6 35B-A3B fits your hardware…" | yes |
| Card above the composer | After the first **finished task** in the task chat. It does not show on the setup chat's turns or on the task chat's opening question. | yes |
| "Run locally" row | At the top of the model menu, until local models are set up. **Show me** opens it. | yes |

## What changed from #121969

The first two commits are #121969, cherry-picked with authorship kept. Conflicts were resolved in favour of both sides: the locale files, and `signpost.ts` (its header comment was dropped to match the trimmed file on this branch). The third commit fits the offer to the new flow:

- **Setup chat turns do not count.** The setup chat's closing words after `start_chat` are not a finished task.
- **The task chat's opening turn does not count.** Since #129419, the task chat speaks first and asks which direction to take. The card waits for the next completed turn. If the task is concrete and the first turn already builds, the card comes one turn later. That is the tradeoff.
- **"The guide will not start" now reads `onboarding.state`.** The intro film and its `intro-reveal` store are gone (#126139).
- **The `gui_tour` model stop reads the same eligibility** as the card and the menu row. The old `localSetupEligible` helper is gone.
- **Skip still retires the tutorial tips.** The offer arms, and its card waits for a finished task. Before, Skip also retired the old local-setup tip, which this PR deletes.

## Verification

- `tsc -p apps/desktop` is clean. eslint on the changed files is clean.
- vitest, one file at a time: `components/tips/*` (32), `lib/tips/*` (4) and `i18n/*` (76) all pass. No new tests.

The card appeared after the next finished turn (a habit-board HTML build). **Show me** set `accepted` and opened the menu with the row on top.

Three Krea / managed-image changes by @entropidelic, salvaged together onto current `main` with follow-up fixes:

- `hermes portal tools` names the partner behind the managed image pick (FAL, Krea or Nous Portal) instead of always saying FAL. The Tool Gateway docs page now describes the single picker. (salvage of #114418)
- Local image files work as Krea style references. Before, a path from disk was sent to Krea as-is and rejected. (salvage of #118444)
- The Krea 2 sliders (`intensity`, `complexity`, `movement`) and `creativity` are offered to the agent, but only while a Krea model is active. (salvage of #119267)

Based on #114418, #118444 and #119267 by @entropidelic. All six of their commits are cherry-picked with authorship kept. The mapping `contributors/emails/mariano.nicolini@lambdaclass.com` was already on main.

## Follow-ups on top (ours)

- **Portal partner:** the routing rule moves into one pure function, `tools.image_generation_managed.managed_route()`.
  - The dispatcher (`_managed_model_plugin`) and the new `managed_image_partner()` both call it, so the partner label and the actual route can't disagree.
  - Dispatch behaviour is unchanged: all 36 provider × model combinations I checked give the same result as before the refactor.
  - The label now follows the actual route:
  - A direct vendor selection returns nothing. Before this, `provider: openai` with `gpt-image-2` printed "partner: Nous Portal".
  - An unset provider (or legacy `use_gateway: true`) with a Portal model id reads FAL, because that is the path it actually runs.
  - Dropped the "Nous Subscription (Krea)" feature label. Every consumer prints "via Nous Portal" in the only state that label can reach, so no screen ever showed it.
  - Dropped the krea readiness-probe switch. `is_managed_tool_gateway_ready` is a local URL+token check, so fal-queue and krea give the same answer.
  - The gateway-offer checklist no longer says "Image generation (FAL)".
- **Krea local refs:**
  - The credential-read guard now runs before `is_file()` / `stat()`. A denied path such as `HERMES_HOME/.env` no longer answers "not found" or "over 3 MB", which would reveal whether it exists and how big it is.
  - A denial is returned as the plugin's normal error dict instead of an exception.
  - Local files are read only after the managed LoRA/moodboard fail-fast, so a request that is about to be refused never reads them.
  - Each file is read once, at most one byte past the remaining budget, so the 3 MB cap applies to the bytes actually sent.
  - Legacy non-dict references pass through untouched instead of raising.
- **Sliders:** each plugin route passes a provider only the controls listed in its `capabilities()["creative_controls"]`.
  - The case this covers: after the user switches backends, a model can copy slider values from earlier turns.
  - Without the filter, a third-party `generate()` without `**kwargs` would raise TypeError and break plain text-to-image.
- **Docs:** `supports_upscale` and `creative_controls` are now documented in the `ImageGenProvider.capabilities()` docstring and the provider-plugin guide.
- **Tests:** the contributor tests were trimmed to behaviour contracts. That means one parametrized refusal test instead of three, and one relationship test for the schema instead of pinned enum and bounds values.

## Validation

| Check | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `portal tools`, nous + `krea-2-medium` | partner: FAL | partner: Krea |
| `portal tools`, nous + `openai/gpt-image-2` | partner: FAL | partner: Nous Portal |
| `portal tools`, `provider: openai` or `provider: fal` + a Krea model | FAL | FAL (unchanged) |
| `managed_image_partner`, provider unset + `openai/gpt-image-2` | — | FAL (the runtime route) |
| Krea, local `image_url` | raw path posted | `data:image/png;base64,…` posted |
| Krea, missing file / `.env` / `auth.json` / symlink to `auth.json` | path posted, success | `invalid_image_url` error, no POST |
| Krea, 3 MB+1 file or 4×900 KB | posted | `source_too_large` error, no POST |
| Schema, nous + Krea model | no sliders | `creativity`, `intensity`, `complexity`, `movement` |
| Schema, fal / openai / unset / Portal model | — | byte-identical to main |
| Krea payload for `intensity=80, complexity=-100, movement=150, creativity=raw` | no sliders, creativity `medium` | intensity 80, complexity -100, creativity raw; out-of-range movement dropped |
| openai plugin given the same args | — | receives no controls |

- The live probes ran against real imports with a temp `HERMES_HOME`. Network access was blocked by socket patches, and Krea/FAL requests were patched out.
- Targeted suites: 41 files, 639 passed, 0 failed.
- Each new test was run with the production file reverted to main and fails there. The guard-order and control-filter tests were also mutation-checked: re-introducing either bug turns them red.
- Krea's API docs confirm that data URIs are accepted for style references and that all three Krea 2 endpoints, including Medium Turbo, accept the sliders.
