raw.body:
When rotation compaction adopts a durable parent that grew past the in-memory transcript, the current user prompt now appears once in the compression child instead of twice.

Fixes #125888

## What happened
`_adopt_grown_durable_parent` flushes the turn's unpersisted prompt to the parent and then re-reads it, but `lease.watermark` stayed at the value captured when the lease was acquired. At publish time every parent row above that watermark, including the flushed prompt the compressor had already kept in the handoff tail, was cloned into the child as concurrent foreign tail, so the prompt showed up twice.

## Change
- `agent/conversation_compression.py`: the adopted snapshot is loaded with `include_row_ids=True`. The row ids are popped from the messages in a single pass, and `lease.watermark` is moved up to the newest adopted row. It never moves down, and it is left alone when the watermark is `None` or the snapshot has no ids. The watermark comes from the snapshot rows themselves rather than a fresh `MAX(id)` read, so a row committed after the snapshot read is still cloned once.
- `hermes_state_compression.py`: the `publish_compression_child` docstring now defines `watermark` as the parent's highest row already represented in the handoff. That is either the start watermark or the newest row of an adopted snapshot.
- `tests/agent/test_compression_adoption_preserves_live_tail.py`: two regressions.
  - Adopted snapshot rows are not re-cloned as foreign tail.
  - A row committed between the snapshot read and its return reaches the child exactly once, and no `_row_id` leaks into the compressor input.

## Credit
- @100yenadmin (Eva) wrote the fix and first submitted it in #125908. Three of their commits were cherry-picked with authorship kept: the watermark advance, the docs plus explicit row-id strip, and the snapshot-window tests.
- @kshitijk4poor added two commits on top:
  - Trimmed the regressions to the two invariants above.
  - Folded the row-id strip and the max into one pass, and restored two unrelated docstrings to their main wording.

## Verification
- Ran on the rebased head in a clean archive copy, in two batches:
  - Batch 1, 31 passed: `test_compression_adoption_preserves_live_tail.py`, `test_compression_child_source.py`, `test_compression_closed_adoption.py`, `tests/hermes_state/test_compression_watermark_commit.py`.
  - Batch 2, 24 passed: `tests/hermes_state/test_watermark_interplay.py`, `test_conversation_compression_manual.py`.
- Red on base: with the production files swapped back to base, both new tests fail. Replacing the watermark advance with `pass` turns both red again (2 failed / 4 passed).
- Probe with the real imports:
  - Base: child is `[summary, concurrent row 2, LIVE, LIVE]` (2 copies of the prompt). A row appended during the snapshot read is also duplicated.
  - Head: the prompt appears once and the window row once. The no-adoption control stays at 1 copy on both.
- `ruff` F401/F811/F821 shows no new findings vs main. `git diff --check` is clean, and the Windows footgun check is clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- #130354 (opened 2026-10-01) makes the same watermark advance. #125908 was submitted first and is the base here.

raw.body:
`hermes profile export` no longer packs credential stores such as `.op.env`, `npmrc`, `mcp-tokens/`, `vault/`, platform pairing and session stores, `home/.git-credentials`, `honcho.json`, `mem0.json` or browser profiles (or Hermes' backup copies of them), and a profile distribution can no longer plant or replace those stores on install.

Fixes #126114

## What happened
The named export filtered out only `auth.json`, `.env` and the desktop bot dir (`_EXPORT_CREDENTIAL_FILES`). Any other credential store in the profile home, and Hermes' own `.bak-*`/`.corrupt` copies of `auth.json`, `.env` and `config.yaml`, went into the archive. The distribution installer applied the same narrow notion of "private", so an archive could write a nested store, or replace a store's parent directory with a file.

## Change

raw.body:
Recurring cron jobs now get rescheduled and show as `scheduled` again once croniter imports successfully after a transient ImportError. Before this, they stayed stuck with no next run until the gateway restarted.

Fixes #127182

## What happened
`cron/jobs.py` stored a single failed `import croniter` as `HAS_CRONITER = False` and kept it for the life of the process. After that, `compute_next_run()` returned None for every cron job, so the due-scan recovery path had nothing it could re-arm. Each job stayed enabled with `next_run_at=None` and `state=error`. `cron/scheduler.py`'s `_cron_interval_minutes` cached None the same way.

## Change
- `cron/jobs.py`
  - A failed croniter import leaves `HAS_CRONITER` as None, so a later call tries the import again.
  - Retries are spaced at most once every 60s (monotonic `_croniter_retry_at`). A package that is really missing therefore doesn't re-run the import finder on every due-scan tick while `_jobs_lock` is held.
  - Explicit True/False overrides still take precedence, and a successful import is still cached.
  - The import warning now logs `sys.executable`, which makes a scheduler running under the wrong interpreter easy to spot.
  - `_recover_missing_next_run`: when a recurring (cron/interval) job is re-armed after an `error` state, its state is set back to `scheduled` in the same persist. Without this, `hermes cron list` kept reporting a job that was healthy and due as broken. One-shot jobs are not touched. Docstring updated.
- `cron/scheduler.py` `_cron_interval_minutes`: a None result caused by a failed croniter import is no longer cached, so the in-flight allowance recovers once the import works. A None from a malformed expression (croniter loaded, expression invalid) is still cached.
- `tests/cron/test_jobs.py`: the regression test from the cherry-picked commit (`TestMarkJobRun::test_transient_croniter_import_error_not_latched`) was extended to cover:
  - the outage leaving the job in error
  - the 60s backoff window
  - recovery to `state == "scheduled"` once the import works again
  - the scheduler cadence cache skipping an import-failure None

## Credit
- @liuhao1024 (#127195) was the first to submit the core fix: re-probe instead of latching, plus the regression test. Their commit bb48a7b48f was cherry-picked with `-x` and they remain its author.
- @itsflownium (#127202) contributed the idea of resetting the re-armed job from `error` to `scheduled`. That follow-up commit includes `Co-authored-by: itsflownium`.
- @JerryLiu369 (#129719) independently found the same fix.
- The follow-up commits (state reset, retry backoff, scheduler cadence cache) are by kshitijk4poor.

## Verification
- On the rebased head, `tests/cron/test_jobs.py` + `tests/cron/test_scheduler.py`: 206 passed. Earlier gate rounds also ran `test_inflight_stale_guard.py`, `test_recurring_wedge_selfheal.py` and `test_cron_multiplex_inflight_release.py`, and they passed.
- Red on base: the kept test fails against the current `cron/jobs.py` ("a transient ImportError was latched"). With only the cherry-pick applied it fails with `'error' == 'scheduled'`. With the backoff gate reverted it fails inside the backoff window. With the always-cache scheduler restored it fails with "import-failure None was cached".
- Probe (forced import failure in-process, then recovery):
  - base: `after recovery tick: error None` → BUG_FIRES
  - head: `after recovery tick: scheduled 2026-09-29T08:30:00+00:00` → "cron job due again"
  - Both: interval jobs still due, successful import still cached, False override still honoured.
- Mutation: reverting either behaviour commit (the contributor's or the follow-up) turns the kept test red.
- Lint: ruff F401/F811/F821 shows no new findings vs main. `git diff --check` is clean. `check-windows-footguns.py` is clean on `cron/jobs.py` and `cron/scheduler.py`.
- Reviewed over 3 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

raw.body:
Switching connection or profile while a preview Save or a project creation is still in flight no longer overwrites a file on the newly selected connection, profile or local device.

Fixes #127659
Fixes #127676

## What happened
`writeDesktopFileText` routes each call through the window's current connection, and both of its callers await before writing. In the preview editor, Save validated the file on connection A and then, if the user switched mid-await, wrote the draft to the same path on B. `createProject` sent the RPC to the captured gateway A, then wrote `IDEA.md` and updated the sidebar/store for whatever owner was current, so A's idea could replace B's `IDEA.md` at the same path.

## Change
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/right-rail/preview-file.tsx`: Edit records a scope key (desktop FS cache key + REST request connection). Save checks it before the disk re-read and again right before the write, which also covers the Overwrite path. On mismatch the save fails with "Switch back to the original connection and profile to save this draft." and the draft is kept.
- `apps/desktop/src/store/projects.ts`: new `stillOnWritableProjectOwner` predicate (active gateway + live active profile; the All profiles view filter does not change the write owner). `createProject` returns `null` without writing `IDEA.md` or touching the store when the owner changed during the RPC, and shows an info toast if the project was created on the previous owner. A missing-RPC error that arrives after an owner switch no longer marks the new owner's backend stale. `activeProjectsContext` reuses the same predicate.
- i18n: `preview.saveScopeChanged` and `sidebar.projects.createdInPreviousContext` in en/de/es/fr/ja/ru/zh/types, and in the split `ar_*` / `zh-hant_*` locale files.
- Tests: `preview-file-save-scope.test.tsx` (new, it.each over connection / profile / local / API route, real temp files) and `projects.test.ts` (createProject owner-switch it.each for connection and profile, plus an owner-switch case in the existing missing-RPC test). The projects tests now use the shared `@/test/deferred` helper.
- `locales/_keys.desktop.json`: regenerated (`npm run i18n:keys`) for the two new strings.

## Credit
- @Froraut (FroRaut) reported both issues and wrote both fixes: #127662 (preview save scope) and #127677 (project IDEA.md owner). Both were cherry-picked with `-x` (d92993cabc03, f968d4ca8d57) and keep FroRaut's authorship. The `ar.ts` / `zh-hant.ts` conflicts were resolved by moving the new keys into the split locale files that main now uses.
- Follow-up commits by kshitijk4poor: a test for the missing-RPC owner guard, a single owner predicate and a live edit scope key, test cleanup (removed unused temp-file scaffolding, replaced a hedged assertion), reuse of the shared deferred helper, and the regenerated locale key catalog.

## Verification
- Rebased onto current main with no conflicts. vitest on the rebased head: `preview-file-save-scope.test.tsx`, `store/projects.test.ts`, `preview-file.test.tsx` and `i18n/catalog-completeness.test.ts` ran 4 files, 84/84 passed.
- Red on base: with `preview-file.tsx` and `projects.ts` at base, the save-scope test fails 4/4 (`expected 'draft for origin' to be 'unrelated valuable contents'`) and createProject fails on 2 cases (new connection, new profile).
- Probe (the head test fixtures run against a base tree and the head tree): on base, save-scope fails 4/4 and createProject fails 3 of 7 (new connection, new profile, missing-RPC after an owner switch). On head, save-scope passes 4/4 and createProject passes 7/7. The same-owner create paths pass on both.
- Mutation: reverting the preview fix turns the 4 save-scope cases red. Reverting the projects fix, or forcing the post-RPC owner check off, turns the 2 owner-switch cases red. Forcing the missing-RPC guard to `true` turns the extended missing-RPC test red.
- `git diff --check` clean. The Windows footgun check is clean. No Python files changed, so ruff does not apply.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- Neighbouring open PRs also edit `apps/desktop/src/store/projects.ts`. #129788 (@Froraut, opened 2026-10-01) adds a broader route-epoch fence across project reads, mutations and dialogs, including stale create completions. #129276 (@sy0u1ti) fences optimistic rollbacks for update, folder and delete, and leaves create/IDEA unchanged. Neither one duplicates this PR, but expect textual conflicts in `projects.ts` with whichever lands second.
- Other desktop-fs mutators (rename/delete dialogs) were not audited for the same pattern.

raw.body:
Write/terminal tool calls carrying a truncated context-compression marker are now refused before they run, and long interactive turns keep going when the user sends corrections or answers clarify cards while the model works.

Fixes #128000
Refs #127260

## What happened
The dispatch guard only recognized a compression marker when its full first sentence was present, so a marker cut by a later boundary (`⟪HERMES-CONTEXT-COMPRESSION: 1,800 of`) slipped into effectful tool arguments. Separately, the redirect/rebuilt restart cap counted every restart for the whole turn, so a turn ended as `redirect_restart_limit_exceeded` on the (`max_retries` + 1)th mid-turn message even when the model had answered in between.

## Change
- `agent/compression_marker.py`: new `_COMPRESSION_MARKER_ARTIFACT_RE` matches the marker prefix plus its first rendered count; the count fragment is shared with `_COMPRESSION_MARKER_RE` as `_MARKER_COUNT_RE`. The bare prefix and the literal template still do not match, so source and docs that mention them stay editable.
- `agent/tool_dispatch_helpers.py`: `_context_pruned_argument_paths` uses the artifact regex. Read-only tools may still quote markers.
- `agent/turn_iteration_prep.py`: `apply_retry_restarts` resets `restart_count` when a response arrives, so the cap now bounds restarts since the last response. Back-to-back cancelled requests still end the turn at `max_retries` + 1.
- `agent/conversation_loop.py`: updated the `_LoopState.restart_count` comment (no code change).
- Tests: the existing dispatch-guard test also covers the template and the three cut-short marker forms; a new `test_response_between_restarts_resets_the_bound` (parametrized over both restart flags); `test_restart_refunds_are_bounded_per_turn` is renamed to `test_back_to_back_restart_refunds_are_bounded`.

## Credit
- @JoaoMarcos44 wrote the partial-marker guard in #127613. Commit cherry-picked with authorship kept.
- @Froraut wrote the restart-cap reset in #128682. Commit cherry-picked with authorship kept; their run_agent end-to-end test was folded into a unit-level invariant test.
- Follow-up commits by @kshitijk4poor: docstring/comment wording, the shared count fragment, and test folding.
- Related: #128004 (@dskwe, opened earlier) addresses #128000 differently with a separate `agent.redirect_restart_limit` config knob. Not included here; see Maintainer notes.

## Verification
- On the rebased head: `test_tool_call_guardrail_runtime.py`, `test_turn_iteration_prep.py`, `test_tool_dispatch_helpers.py`, `test_compression_marker.py`: 60 passed. Related marker consumers (`test_pre_compress_memory_context_handoff.py`, `lsp/test_reporter.py`, `test_trajectory_compressor.py`, `test_truncated_tool_call_boost.py`): 34 passed.
- Red on base: with the behaviour files reverted, the cut-short marker assertions fail and both params of `test_response_between_restarts_resets_the_bound` fail.
- Probe, base vs head: cut-short markers in `write_file` args were allowed on base and are blocked (`['$.c']`) on head. The field-report sequence (redirect, response, redirect, response, redirect, redirect) gave `break:4 redirect_restart_limit_exceeded` on base and continues on head. These are unchanged between base and head: bare prefix, template, prefix+word, `read_file` quotes, and four back-to-back redirect/rebuilt restarts (still break at 4).
- Mutation: reverting either contributor commit turns its kept test red.
- ruff F401/F811/F821: no new findings vs main. `git diff --check` clean. Windows-footguns check clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- The reset also relaxes the rebuilt-for-fallback cap when responses land between stalls (B, resp, B, resp, B, B, B, B now breaks on the 4th back-to-back B). `max_iterations` still bounds it.
- #128004 adds a separate `agent.redirect_restart_limit` knob. This PR fixes #128000 without new config; #128004 can be taken on top or closed as superseded.
- #129895 (opened 2026-10-01) gives the rebuilt restart its own counter sized by fallback-chain depth. It is complementary, but it edits the same function and the renamed test, so whichever lands second needs a rebase.
- #127260 stays open: the token-insertion and BOM parts are not addressed here.

raw.body:
`kanban gc`, archiving and task completion no longer delete a scratch dir or linked worktree while another non-terminal task, on this board or another board, still points at it.

Fixes #126508

## What happened
Cleanup ran `rmtree` on a task's `workspace_path` as soon as that one task went terminal. It never checked whether other tasks shared the path. A ready or running task that shared the directory lost its files, and so did a task on a named board, since the guard only looked at the current board.

## Change
- `hermes_cli/kanban_db_workspace.py`
  - `_workspace_in_use_by_other` compares resolved paths against live tasks on the current board, then on each sibling board DB (opened read-only). It returns `"shared"`, `"unknown"` or `None`. If the board list or a sibling DB cannot be read, it returns `"unknown"` and the dir is kept, so failures never lead to a delete.
  - `_defer_shared_workspace_cleanup` logs the reason and records a `workspace_cleanup_deferred_shared` event (`path`, `reason`). `_defer_shared_worktree_cleanup` runs that check only for real linked worktrees.
  - `_cleanup_workspace` and `_try_cleanup_parent_workspaces` check containment / linked-worktree first and run the sharing check just before removing anything. tmux and parent cleanup still run on the normal path.
  - `_is_linked_worktree_checkout` now uses a single `rev-parse --git-dir --git-common-dir` call. The `_git_dir` helper had no callers left and is removed. A shared `_TERMINAL_STATUSES_SQL` constant now feeds the active-children and live-path queries.
- `hermes_cli/kanban_ops.py`: `_cmd_gc` runs the same guard before it removes a scratch dir or worktree. Most of the diff is re-indentation into the `with conn` block.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_gc_retention.py`: 2 tests.
  - `gc` keeps a scratch dir that a live task still uses, and records the deferred event.
  - Cleanup keeps the scratch dir when a named board has a live user, and also when the boards directory cannot be listed.

## Credit
- @686f6c61 wrote the fix in #126513 and submitted it first. Their commit (`fix(kanban): keep a scratch dir another live task still uses`) is cherry-picked with authorship kept.
- Follow-up commits by @kshitijk4poor: tighten the guard order, harden the tests, return a fail-closed `"unknown"` reason, reuse existing helpers, and use one git call for the linked-worktree check.
- #126617 by @JoaoMarcos44 addressed the same bug. Its per-gc snapshot was not adopted, and its board-discovery path deleted the dir on failure instead of keeping it.

## Verification
- On the rebased head: `test_kanban_gc_retention.py`, `test_kanban_worktree_teardown.py`, `test_kanban_swarm.py` and `test_kanban_db.py` give 82 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is `test_infrastructure_spawn_refusal_never_charges_the_card`, and it fails the same way on main.
- Both new tests fail when run against the main versions of `kanban_db_workspace.py` and `kanban_ops.py`.
- Probe (real import, isolated HOME):
  - Main: the shared dir is deleted in the same-board gc, cross-board, board-listing-failure and deferred-parent cases.
  - Head: the shared dir is kept in all 5 shared cases, and unshared or all-terminal dirs are still removed.
- Mutation checks:
  - Reverting the contributor fix turns both tests red.
  - Reverting only the gc path turns the gc test red.
  - Changing the board listing to delete on failure turns the board-listing test red.
- ruff F401/F811/F821, `git diff --check` and `check-windows-footguns.py --all` are clean.
- Reviewed over 4 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- `gc` scans the sibling boards once per candidate row, which is O(rows × boards). This is fine at current board counts; a per-run snapshot (the approach in #126617) could be a follow-up.
- Producer-side path sharing, where decompose children inherit a root's workspace (#103303 / #103325), is out of scope here.

raw.body:
`/snapshot restore` no longer signs you out of OAuth providers by rolling a rotated single-use refresh token back to the spent one, no longer writes a corrupt snapshot `auth.json` over the live one, and says so when a restore was incomplete instead of claiming the snapshot does not exist.

Refs #127010

## What happened
`restore_quick_snapshot` copied the snapshot's `auth.json` over the live file with `shutil.copy2`. OAuth providers such as Codex rotate single-use refresh tokens, so the restored file held an already-spent grant and the next refresh failed; a malformed snapshot `auth.json` was also published verbatim, and the function still returned success as long as any other file was restored.

## Change
- `hermes_cli/backup_restore.py`, `hermes_cli/auth_oauth_grants.py`: `auth.json` is restored through a merge under the auth-store lock. Static entries (API keys, config-like rows) come from the snapshot; live OAuth grants (provider tokens and OAuth credential-pool rows) keep the live generation. An unreadable or invalid snapshot `auth.json` is refused and the live file is left untouched.
- `hermes_cli/backup.py`:
  - `restore_quick_snapshot` returns False when `auth.json` was listed in the snapshot but was refused, skipped, missing from the snapshot dir, or escaped the home directory, even if other files were restored.
  - A root-profile `auth.json` alias is trusted only when the home is not the root itself and the target stays under the root.
- `hermes_cli/cli_commands_mixin.py`: when the restore returns False for a snapshot that exists, `/snapshot restore` prints the new `snapshot.restore_incomplete` message ("Snapshot {id} was not fully restored; some files were refused (see logs)") instead of "Snapshot not found".
- `locales/*.yaml`: `snapshot.restore_incomplete` added to the 17 catalogs that carry `snapshot.not_found`.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_snapshot_restore_oauth.py`: two tests.
  - A rotated Codex grant survives a restore while static auth is restored.
  - A refused `auth.json` makes the restore and the CLI report incomplete, with the live file byte-identical. The test covers two cases: a corrupt snapshot `auth.json`, and one listed in the manifest but missing from the snapshot dir.
- `contributors/emails/`: map for Lion-Leporidae.

## Credit
- @JoaoMarcos44 was the first to submit this fix, in #127063. Commit 303ca2e738 (OAuth-preserving merge, `_restore_auth_json`, trusted root-auth alias) is cherry-picked with `-x` and keeps its authorship and its `Co-authored-by: FroRaut` trailer. @Froraut reported #127010.
- @Lion-Leporidae wrote the follow-ups in #128351. Commits 9e15369ff6 (propagate a refused auth restore as failure) and 8d43b16d66 (fail closed for skipped or missing auth and tighten the root alias) are cherry-picked with `-x` and keep their authorship.
- Commits by @kshitijk4poor: trim the salvaged tests from 17+ cases to two, the CLI "not fully restored" message and its locale keys, and test coverage for the missing-auth fail-closed path.

## Verification
- On the rebased head: `test_snapshot_restore_oauth.py`, `test_restore_own_holder_guard.py` and `test_restore_source_integrity.py` 30 passed. `test_backup.py` 92 passed, 1 skipped. `tests/agent/test_i18n.py`, `test_i18n_layers.py`, `tests/scripts/test_contributor_map.py` and `test_credential_pool_profile_oauth_fork.py` 104 passed. `test_cli_model_once.py`, `test_backup_all_profiles.py` and `test_backup_stability.py` 19 passed.
- Red on base: both kept tests fail with the base production files (`'refresh-spent' != 'refresh-rotated'`; live `auth.json` overwritten with invalid JSON).
- Probe (real import, scratch home). Base: the restore leaves a rotated Codex grant at `codex-rt-1`, i.e. spent. A corrupt snapshot `auth.json` returns ok=True and the live file becomes garbage, and the CLI prints "Restored state from". Head: the grant stays at `codex-rt-2` and the static OpenRouter key is restored. The corrupt case returns ok=False with the live file unchanged, and the CLI prints "was not fully restored". A missing id still prints "not found", and a healthy restore is unchanged.
- Mutation: reverting 303ca2e738 turns both tests red. Reverting 9e15369ff6, 8d43b16d66 or the CLI/locale commit each turns the refusal test red.
- ruff F401/F811/F821 clean, `git diff --check` clean, `check-windows-footguns.py --all` clean.
- Reviewed over 3 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- Policy choice: the live OAuth generation always wins, which is #127063's behaviour. #128671 (@jonpol01) carries the same base commit plus a "later-issued generation wins" rule via `_oauth_freshness`. That rule would also recover after `hermes import` of an older backup, and @Lion-Leporidae raised the same question in #128351. This PR does not include it, so it can go in as a follow-up if preferred.
- Our builder wrote the 17 non-English translations of `snapshot.restore_incomplete`, and a gate reviewer checked each one against the English text. No native speaker has reviewed them.
- The same `auth.json` rollback may happen in `hermes import`. It has not been probed and is not changed here.

raw.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the `Python tests / e2e` lane, which has failed on every run on `main` since #130167 merged. Also stops a test in `Python tests / Run tests` from depending on which process holds a given PID on the runner.

### 1. `chat -q` approvals hang until the subprocess is killed

`ea5b89fa359` (part of #130167) made CLI approval and clarify prompts wait until answered. It did that in two places:

- `cli_chat_turn_mixin._chat_run_agent` sets `set_prompts_wait_for_answer()` around **every** CLI turn, including `chat -q`.
- `CLIModalMixin._approval_callback` dropped its deadline (`_approval_deadline = None`) and its `"timeout"` return.

`chat -q` never builds the prompt_toolkit app, so nothing can answer the panel. Before #130167, a single-query approval was denied after `approvals.timeout`. That was the tracked symptom #121296, which the e2e test records as a known gate. After #130167 it waits forever.

In `tests/e2e/core/providers/test_native_codex_app_server_faults.py`, the `q_approval` scenario hits its 120s `subprocess.run` timeout. Its module-scoped fixture then fails all 8 tests in the file.

Bisect, running the `q_approval` scenario on its own:

| commit | result |
|---|---|
| `4e7403130e` (last green `main` e2e) | exit 0, 15.5s |
| `e57fa350cbf` (#130167, approval context only) | exit 0, 15.7s |
| `ea5b89fa359` (#130167, CLI panels) | **hangs** |
| `0bc5d9688b5` (`main` after the merge) | **hangs** |

Fix:

- Single-query turns no longer set wait-until-answered, so `approval_wait_seconds()` returns `approvals.timeout` again.
- When `_single_query_mode` is set, `_approval_callback` gets back its `approvals.timeout` deadline and returns `"timeout"`.
- The two strings it prints (`cli.approval.timeout_denying`, `cli.approval.timed_out_no_response`) are restored in all 17 locales with their original translations.
- Attended CLI turns behave as #130167 intended: the panel waits until answered.

### 2. `test_ps_fallback_when_proc_unavailable` depends on PID 873

`_read_process_cmdline` tries `/proc`, then `psutil`, then `ps`. The test stubs `/proc` and `ps` but leaves `psutil` real. So it passes only while PID 873 doesn't exist on the host. One runner had `haveged` at 873 and got `/usr/sbin/haveged --Foreground --verbose=1` back (job 110383223924 on #130468). The test now stubs `psutil` to raise.

## How the regression got through

- **The PR-time e2e lane was skipped.** On pull requests, `scripts/ci/classify_changes.py::_E2E_LANES` runs `e2e` only when the diff touches the test harness, `tests/e2e/` or `hermes_state`. #130167 changed `hermes_cli/` and `tools/`, so its CI run (36837416793) skipped `Python tests / e2e`, and `All required checks pass` went green.
- **That's the documented trade-off.** `ci.yaml` says regressions the path lists miss turn `main` red after the merge, and that's what happened: the first `main` e2e after the merge (09:50Z) failed, and every later one did too.
- **There was a test for exactly this path.** `test_single_query_approval_resolves_without_waiting_for_a_human` already tracked #121296. It catches the 8s wait as a known gate, but an unbounded wait kills the module fixture before the gate runs.
- **#130468 only exposed it.** It changes `scripts/`, which is in the harness path list, so it ran e2e and showed the existing failure.

## How to prevent it next time

1. **Widen the e2e path list for prompt and approval code.** Add `hermes_cli/cli_chat_turn_mixin`, `hermes_cli/cli_modal_mixin`, `hermes_cli/cli_single_query`, `tools/approval` and `tools/clarify` to `_E2E_LANES["e2e"]`, so changes to approval or prompt lifetime run the CLI e2e suites before merge. I left this out of this PR because it changes CI cost policy and needs the CI owner's sign-off.
2. **Treat "wait until answered" as a property of the surface, not the CLI process.** Any change that removes a prompt deadline should state which entry points can't answer (`chat -q`, cron, ACP, piped stdin) and keep a deadline for them. The new unit tests pin the `-q` side.
3. **Fix #121296 properly.** `-q` should resolve approvals right away from `approvals.single_query_mode` instead of waiting for `approvals.timeout`. Then this path has no timer to get wrong.

## Related Issue

Regression from #130167. Related: #121296 (still open; this PR restores its pre-#130167 symptom, it doesn't fix it).

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/cli_chat_turn_mixin.py`: don't set wait-until-answered when `_single_query_mode` is set.
- `hermes_cli/cli_modal_mixin.py`: in single-query mode, `_approval_callback` has an `approvals.timeout` deadline and returns `"timeout"`.
- `locales/*.yaml`: restore `cli.approval.timeout_denying` and `cli.approval.timed_out_no_response`.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_single_query_prompt_window.py` (new): an attended turn sets wait-until-answered, a `-q` turn doesn't, and neither leaks it.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_approval_ui.py`: a single-query panel times out at `approvals.timeout`.
- `tests/gateway/test_status.py`: stub `psutil` in the ps-fallback test.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh --include-integration tests/e2e/core/providers/test_native_codex_app_server_faults.py`: on `main` this gives 8 errors (`TimeoutExpired` after 120s). With this PR it gives `4 passed` (the rest are its known gates, as before #130167).
2. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_single_query_prompt_window.py tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_approval_ui.py`: 20 passed. Without the fix, `[True-False]` fails and the single-query panel test hangs.
3. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_status.py::TestReadProcessCmdlinePsFallback` with the PID changed to `1` (a live process): fails before this PR, passes after.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass: I ran only the related suites (`tests/hermes_cli/`, `tests/tools/`, `tests/gateway/test_status.py`, i18n): 23,629 passed, 18 failed. The 18 failures are in 5 unrelated files (memory-provider setup, web server profile, bot relay paths, keyless web fallback). They fail the same way on the unmodified base `666b9f04c42`.
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux 6.8)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Docstrings updated; N/A for docs/config
- [x] Cross-platform: POSIX and Windows behave the same; only the `-q` deadline changes

raw.body:
When a Codex auxiliary call (for example, a compression summary) times out, the watchdog no longer closes the attempt stream's TLS socket from its own thread. Previously the freed file descriptor could be recycled while the owning thread was still reading it, which corrupted SQLite files.

Fixes #130115

## What happened
`_CodexStreamGuard._close_client_on_timeout` runs on the watchdog `threading.Timer`. Two of its branches called `close_attempt_stream` from that thread: the timeout-won branch and the "owner already hard-cancelled" branch. For a real `openai.Stream`, that call ends in httpcore `SyncStream.close()` → `sock.close()` off the owner thread. That breaks the FD-ownership contract from #70773: the owner can still be inside `SSL_read` on an FD number the kernel has already handed to another file, such as a SQLite database.

## Change
- `agent/auxiliary_client.py`:
  - `close_attempt_stream` checks the owner thread id. Off the owner thread, it only `shutdown()`s the stream's socket through the existing `_shutdown_socket`. That wakes the blocked reader without releasing the FD. The owner still does the real close in `release_stream` and on the late-cancel path. A stream with no reachable socket (a socketless double) is still closed so its reader wakes up.
  - New `_attempt_stream_socket` reads the socket from `response.extensions["network_stream"]` through the existing `agent_runtime_helpers._socket_from_stream`.
  - Both stranger-thread branches go through this one check, so the change covers both.
- `tests/agent/test_codex_aux_timeout_fd_ownership.py`: new `test_timer_thread_never_closes_a_real_sdk_stream`. It drives the guard from a Timer against an SDK-shaped stream and asserts that the stranger thread's only action is `stream.sock.shutdown`.
- `contributors/emails/justas.cesnauskas@mygom.tech`: contributor map entry.

## Credit
- @justascesnauskas (Justas Cesnauskas) reported #130115 with the diagnosis and wrote the complete fix and regression test in #130176. Commit 33cfb5ea65 was cherry-picked with authorship kept.
- @dskwe (Yuan Li) submitted first, in #130120. That PR fixed the timeout-won branch and is credited with `Co-authored-by`.
- @kshitijk4poor added three follow-up commits:
  - Removed a redundant try/except around `_shutdown_socket`, which already swallows `OSError`.
  - Moved the socket lookup onto `_socket_from_stream`, which removes a blanket try/except.
  - Tightened the test asserts and removed a no-op sleep.
  - There is also a separate contributor-map commit.

## Verification
- Tests ran on the rebased head in a clean archive copy:
  - `test_codex_aux_timeout_fd_ownership.py`, `test_codex_aux_no_progress_timeout.py` and `test_tls_fd_recycle_corruption.py`: 14 passed.
  - `test_auxiliary_client.py`: 219 passed.
  - `test_context_compressor.py -k "codex or stream or aux"`: 15 passed.
- Red on base: the new test fails with base `auxiliary_client.py` (`stranger-thread FD release: [('stream.close', …), ('stream.sock.close', …)]`) and passes on head.
- Probe: a real `openai.Stream` over a local stalled HTTP/1.1 server, with the guard driven from a Timer thread.
  - Base: the won and cancelled branches both call `sock.close` from `Timer`.
  - Head: in both branches the Timer only calls `shutdown`, and `sock.close` happens on the owner. Owner-thread timeouts and socketless doubles behave the same on base and head.
- Mutation: reverting the contributor fix turns the new test red (1 failed / 13 passed). Reverting the redundant-guard trim keeps everything green, as expected for a no-behaviour-change refactor.
- `ruff` F401/F811/F821 shows no new findings vs main. `git diff --check` and the Windows footgun check are clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- A real stream with no reachable `network_stream` socket (for example, an HTTP/2 transport) is still closed from the Timer. The current OpenAI client uses HTTP/1.1, so this case doesn't come up today.
- Unprobed edge: a Timer firing just as the owner reads to EOF could `shutdown()` a socket that has already been returned to the pool. httpcore's idle readability check should drop that connection before it is reused.
- #130481 (opened 2026-10-01) includes a narrower version of this change in commit e509a8cea7. It skips the stranger-thread wake entirely, so socketless streams are no longer woken. It is bundled with ~19 unrelated commits.

raw.body:
Strict URL-credential redaction (used by `hermes dump`, debug share, `/debug`, context compaction, kanban notifications and cron job args) now masks the whole URL userinfo, so a token stored in the username slot such as `https://TOKEN:@proxy/v1` no longer appears in the output.

Fixes #129983

## What happened
`_redact_strict_url_credentials()` in `agent/redact.py` kept `userinfo.partition(":")[0]` whenever the userinfo had a colon. It assumed the username is never secret. For URLs like `https://TOKEN:@host`, `https://TOKEN:x-oauth-basic@github.com/...` or `http://alice:pw@proxy`, the token or username stayed in strict egress output as `TOKEN:***@`.

## Change
- `agent/redact.py`: the strict pass now replaces any `//userinfo@` with `//***:***@`. The regex has no capture groups and the substitution is a constant string. Its only caller is `_redact_strict_url_credentials`. The `redact_sensitive_text` docstring now describes the full userinfo mask. Non-strict (default) redaction is unchanged.
- `tests/agent/test_redact.py`: updated the strict-userinfo expectations. Added an opaque token-as-username row to the existing parametrized strict test, which also checks that the value is left untouched when strict mode is off.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_debug.py`: the share-bundle redaction test now expects the username to be masked too.
- `tests/agent/test_pre_compress_memory_context.py`, `tests/agent/test_pre_compress_memory_context_handoff.py`: updated the pre-compress strict-redaction expectations to `***:***@`.

## Credit
- @dskwe (Yuan Li) wrote the fix and its tests in #129985 and was the first to submit. Both commits are cherry-picked with `-x` and keep their original author: 526f376c3c (fix + tests) and 0bcf6f5baa (debug-share test expectation, added after @ehz0ah's review).
- @JoaoMarcos44 submitted the same fix independently in #130027. It is closed as a duplicate, with credit given here.
- @100yenadmin reported the bug in #129983.
- Follow-up commits by the maintainer: updated the pre-compress test expectations, and simplified the regex and substitution with no change in behaviour.

## Verification
- Rebased onto current `main` with no conflicts. On the rebased head, `tests/agent/test_redact.py` + `tests/hermes_cli/test_debug.py` give 269 passed. `tests/agent/test_compaction_redaction_boundaries.py` + `test_pre_compress_memory_context.py` + `test_pre_compress_memory_context_handoff.py` give 17 passed.
- Red on the old code: with the base `agent/redact.py`, the new strict rows in `test_redact.py` (`//user:NET_SECRET@` and the opaque username) fail, and so does `test_debug.py::TestCollectShareBundle::test_redaction_masks_url_credentials`. Reverting the fix turns those 3 tests red.
- Probe results: on base, strict output for token-as-username, `x-oauth-basic`, `user:pass` and multi-URL text all leak (`BUG_FIRES`). On head, every strict case gives `//***:***@host` (`NO_LEAK`). Default non-strict output is byte-identical between base and head, and benign strings (prose email, `//x.test/path`, `/users/@bob`) are unchanged.
- ruff F401/F811/F821 reports nothing new compared with `main`. `git diff --check` is clean. The Windows-footgun check is clean on `agent/redact.py`.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds covering regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, and tests/probe/mutation. The simplified substitution is also cheaper per match.

## Maintainer notes
- Colon-less userinfo now also comes out as `***:***@` in strict mode (`https://***@gitlab…` and `ssh://git@…` both become `***:***@`). This only changes the look of the output and leaks nothing. #130027 kept the `***@` form; we did not adopt it.
- Older open PRs #125680 and #125677 would bring back the username-preserving form if they merge as they are now.

raw.body:
An image-bearing user turn that comes back into history in its stored encoded form now reaches the model as an image again, and is never merged into a neighbouring text turn as a huge base64 string.

Fixes #125299

## What happened
SessionDB stores list (multimodal) content as a `\x00json:[…]` string. When such a row comes back into the live history still encoded (for example after a proactive prune re-inserts history), the alternation repair treated it as plain text. It merged the row into an adjacent user turn, so the model received hundreds of thousands of characters of base64, and the persisted row could no longer be decoded.

## Change
- `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`
  - New pre-pass `_normalize_sentinel_encoded_content`, run at the start of `repair_message_sequence`. It decodes sentinel-encoded row content in place through `SessionDB._decode_content`, so the persistence layer stays the only owner of the codec. It keeps the `_db_persisted` marker, because re-encoding the decoded value gives back the stored string; dropping the marker would make the append-only flush write the turn a second time.
  - `_merge_consecutive_users` only merges content that is a string and does not start with `SessionDB._CONTENT_JSON_PREFIX`. A corrupt sentinel row that cannot be decoded is therefore left as its own row, not welded into text.
  - A decoded multimodal row next to a text user row stays as two consecutive user rows. This is the existing policy for native list content.
- `tests/agent/test_message_sequence_repair.py`: two regression tests. One covers decoding plus no text merge, including the corrupt-sentinel case. The other covers a durable sentinel row that keeps its marker and is not re-appended.
- `contributors/emails/prathamesh290504@gmail.com`: contributor mapping.

## Credit
- @PRATHAMESH75 (#125331, first submitter). Two commits were cherry-picked with authorship kept:
  - "decode sentinel-encoded multimodal turns before the alternation repair": the decode pre-pass and its regression test. This is the core fix.
  - "keep the durable marker on a storage-equivalent sentinel decode": despite the title, this commit changes no behaviour. The marker was already kept by the previous commit. Its diff adds a comment explaining why the marker must stay, plus a regression test that pins marker retention. That test goes red if the marker is popped after decode.
- Yuan Li (@dskwe, #125335), credited as `Co-authored-by` on the follow-up commit. #125335 proposed a structural merge for the same bug. This PR keeps the decode-and-skip approach from #125331.
- Maintainer follow-ups (kshitijk4poor):
  - refuse to merge undecodable sentinel rows
  - replace the copied sentinel helpers with `SessionDB._decode_content` and `_CONTENT_JSON_PREFIX`
  - fold the corrupt case into the decode test
  - trim dead code and comments

## Verification
- Tests on the rebased head:
  - `test_message_sequence_repair`, `test_merged_user_override`, `hermes_state/test_restore_alternation_repair` and `test_identity_flush`: 75 passed.
  - `test_context_engine_message_uid` and `hermes_state/test_message_uid`: 51 passed.
- Red on base (production file reverted to main): both new tests fail. One fails with the rows welded (`assert 1 == 2`). The other fails because the content is still the encoded string.
- Probe, base vs head:
  - On base, encoded image rows leak base64 as str (text+enc, enc+text, enc+text+text and a lone enc row), and a corrupt sentinel row is welded into text.
  - On head, encoded rows decode to lists and a corrupt row stays separate. The benign neighbours are the same on base and head: text+text merges, list+text stays as 2 rows, and native lists keep their identity.
- Mutation: reverting each production commit, or popping the marker after decode, turns a kept test red. Reverting the comment-only commit leaves its own test green, which is expected because that commit changes no behaviour.
- ruff F401/F811/F821 clean on head and base, `git diff --check` clean, Windows footgun check clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- Alternative not taken: #125335 merges the decoded list and the text row structurally. That would also change how native list+text rows are handled, and it does not cover a lone encoded row.
- Known gap (Low): a corrupt sentinel row that cannot be decoded is parse-attempted on every API iteration and logs one warning each time. This is bounded, and the case is pathological.
- The root cause of encoded rows re-entering the working set (the prune / re-insert path) is not addressed here.

raw.body:
A model stuck in a verbatim repetition loop now has its stream closed while it is still streaming, so an uncapped endpoint (LM Studio, `custom`) can no longer keep a looping turn running until someone sends `/stop`. This also covers runs with no stream callback (cron, subagents, non-streaming gateway platforms).

Fixes #127234

## What happened
Every repetition check (`turn_api_call`, `turn_truncation`, `turn_final_response`, `conversation_loop`) ran only after the stream ended. The stale detector fires only on silence, and no `max_tokens` is sent to these endpoints by design. A looping model on an uncapped endpoint therefore streamed with no end.

## Change
- `agent/repetition_guard.py`: new `RunawayStreamWatch`. It applies the stop path's existing criterion (`is_runaway_repetition`, at least `STOP_PATH_MIN_CHARS` = 16k chars) to a bounded 64k tail of one raw channel. Checks run at 16k, 32k and 64k chars, then once every 64k chars. Memory stays under two tail windows plus the latest delta.
- `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py`: the chat-completions and Anthropic Messages stream loops feed the watch from the raw channels: `delta.content`, `reasoning_content`/`reasoning`, `reasoning_details` text (in its own watch), and Anthropic `text`/`thinking` deltas. On a hit, the stream is closed on its owner thread the same way `/stop` closes it (shared `_close_half_read_stream` helper), and the response comes back tagged as a `length` cut.
- `agent/turn_truncation.py`: `recover_from_truncation` handles the `_runaway_repetition` tag first. The turn ends with the "Repetition Detected" notice and no continuation.
- `tests/agent/test_stream_runaway_repetition.py`: a looping stream is cut with no stream callback. Covered cases: chat content, chat reasoning behind `reasoning_details`, Anthropic text, Anthropic thinking, and a loop after about 100k chars of distinct prefix. Legitimate repetitive output (30k distinct rows, an asked-for 50x repeat) is delivered intact.
- `website/docs/integrations/providers.md` (en + zh-Hans): states the bound. A loop is stopped within about 130,000 characters of when it starts.

## Credit
- @jonpol01 reported #127234 and wrote #127242, the first submission for this issue. Both of its commits are cherry-picked with authorship kept: `5379a417c5` (cut the loop while it streams) and `53dcaecc96` (bounded tail, both reasoning fields watched). Its commit message carries Co-authored-by for @auroracapital (#125650), @BrunoBza (#94348), @gkd2323c (#125351) and @enzo-adami (#78551). Their reported loops are the test cases.
- @ehz0ah, @arkheioncorp and @JoaoMarcos44 reviewed #127242.
- Follow-up commits by @kshitijk4poor: trimmed the tests to the two behaviour invariants; fixed the check stride at one tail window once the reply is long, so a loop after a long prefix is still cut promptly; fed both reasoning watches in one short-circuit check; removed a redundant pre-trim; corrected the documented bound.
- #129709 (@JerryLiu369) is an independent fix for the same issue that arrived later.

## Verification
- On the rebased head: `test_stream_runaway_repetition.py`, `test_repetition_guard.py`, `test_continuation_repetition_guard.py`, `test_chat_completion_helpers_provider_sort.py`: 22 passed.
- Red on base: with base `chat_completion_helpers.py` + `turn_truncation.py`, the loop-cut cases fail (chat content, chat reasoning, reasoning behind details, Anthropic text, Anthropic thinking), while legitimate delivery passes.
- Live probe (local SSE server streaming an endless loop to a real `AIAgent`, `custom` provider, no stream callback): on base, chat content, Anthropic text and chat `reasoning_content` loops were still streaming after 12s. On head, all three ended as `truncated` with "Repetition Detected". The benign 30k distinct rows and the asked-for 50x repeat completed intact on both.
- Mutation: reverting each behaviour commit's `agent/` changes turns tests red (5, 2 and 1 cases respectively). The short-circuit refactor is behaviour-neutral, so reverting it turns none red.
- A randomized buffer probe (200 seeds x 500 deltas) and a feed-equivalence diff (150 seeds) confirm the pre-trim removal is behaviour-equivalent and the watch stays within two tail windows plus the latest delta.
- ruff F401/F811/F821: no new findings. `git diff --check` is clean. Windows footgun check is clean.
- Reviewed over 3 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- @alt-glitch asked us to pick one implementation. This PR builds on #127242. #129709 is the alternative, but it wraps `contextlib.suppress(Exception)` in `turn_final_response.py`.
- #129031 (reasoning-only rolling window) and #125650 (callback-path checks in `stream_delivery.py`) overlap with this change. This PR covers both cases on the raw channels.
- Known gap (pre-existing criterion limit): loops where each line carries a changing counter are not flagged. A per-turn ceiling could be a follow-up.

raw.body:
Desktop no longer paints the same assistant reply twice on two of the routes reported in #123801: a reply first sealed as an interim, and a reply that shows up again when "Show earlier" loads an older transcript page.

Refs #123801

## What happened
Route 1: the turn sealed the reply as an interim, then streamed and completed the same text. The completed bubble was settled as a new message next to the identical interim, so the reply appeared twice. Route 2: `mergeOlderTranscriptPage` matched fetched folds only by their message `rowId`. A fold whose final reply was already held by the settled live bubble as a text part (`sourceRowId`) got appended next to that bubble.

## Change
- `use-message-stream/collapse-duplicate-final.ts`, `index.ts`: when `message.complete` carries the same text as the sealed interim of the current occurrence, the reply settles onto that interim and the duplicate live bubble is dropped. The match stops at a `message.start` boundary and is skipped when the completion failed. A private `mergeLiveIntoKept` helper now holds the merge-and-drop tail both collapses share.
- `chat/transcript-backfill.ts`: part rows held by live bubbles are indexed. A fetched fold is dropped only when every source row it carries is already held. A fold that also carries unheld rows (tool calls, narration) is appended as before, so nothing is lost. A fold is no longer dropped just because its first row is held as a part of a different bubble.
- Tests: `transcript-backfill.test.ts` gets one `it.each` with 3 cases (all rows held → dropped; tool call + unheld narration → kept; first row held only as a part elsewhere → kept). `interim-redelivery-duplicate.test.tsx` adds 2 specs (identical sealed interim → one bubble; no settling across a `message.start` boundary).
- `contributors/emails/`: adds the jiangkoumo mapping.

## Credit
- @jiangkoumo (#126023): the identical-interim settle (`f2980a9c98`) and the current-occurrence bound (`45ced2713e`). Both are applied as their own commits with jiangkoumo as author. Those two upstream trees were missing from the local object store, so the commits were rebuilt from GitHub's per-commit patches with the original message, date and a `cherry picked from` trailer. The content is identical.
- @Finn763 (#124472): the part-row index for backfilled folds (`50021e8c0a`). Cherry-picked with `-x`, authorship kept. That commit's message says `Closes #123801`. This PR only partly fixes the issue, so treat it as Refs.
- Follow-ups by kshitijk4poor: the every-row-held rule, dropping the first-part-row anchor, consolidating the failure gate, and trimming the tests. The every-row-held commit is co-authored with Finn763.

## Verification
- vitest (apps/desktop), on the head rebased onto current main: 20 files, 170 tests passed. This covers the 2 touched spec files, `transcript-backfill.stale-guard-loop`, `api/session-transcript-paging`, and 16 neighbouring use-message-stream/backfill files (completion boundaries, duplicate completion and delivery, interim history/sealing/redelivery, late tool events, folded-segment refresh, and others).
- Red on base: with the 3 production files reverted to main, `drops a fold whose every row is already held` and `keeps one bubble when the sealed interim already carries the final reply` fail (2 failed / 43 passed).
- Probe (real `useMessageStream` harness, interim(R) → delta(R) → complete(R)): base paints 2 bubbles [interim R, R]; head paints 1 settled bubble. The neighbouring cases are identical on base and head: failed completion, completion with no live bubble, a different interim text, and a `message.start` boundary.
- Mutation: reverting each behaviour commit turns its spec red. The failure-gate consolidation is a refactor and stays green; probes show no reachable change.
- Reviewed over 3 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- #123801 has more routes than these two. Refresh/compaction (#126834) and several open sibling PRs (#127666, #127282, #129354, #129810) are not covered, so the issue stays open.
- A backfilled fold that mixes held and unheld rows is still appended whole, so its final reply can still paint twice. Fixing that needs part-level merging.
- #126834 and #130448 (sealed post-tool reply, opened 2026-10-01) also edit `use-message-stream/index.ts` and/or `transcript-backfill.ts`. Whichever lands second will need a rebase.

raw.body:
When a Codex Responses stream outlives its drain budget after the final event, Hermes no longer closes the connection while another thread is still reading it, so the freed file descriptor can't be reused and written into an unrelated file (the same corruption class as #29507).

Fixes #127390

## What happened
After `response.completed`, the post-terminal drain read the rest of the stream on a daemon thread. When the drain budget expired, the owner thread `close()`d the raw and managed streams while the drain thread was still inside a TLS read. That released the fd under the reader, and the OS could hand the number to another file (for example a SQLite DB) that then received TLS bytes.

## Change
- `agent/codex_runtime.py`: the owner thread now does the post-terminal drain and the close itself. A `codex-post-terminal-watchdog` timer only `shutdown()`s the socket to wake a stuck read once the budget runs out (the existing #29507 helpers); it never closes. If no socket can be found, the drain is skipped, which matches `stream_drain_timeout=0`. Once the managed close has run, a failed managed close no longer triggers a second raw close. `_close_event_stream` goes back to returning `None`, and the `suppress(Exception)` wrappers around logger calls are gone.
- `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`: new `_socket_from_response(response)` finds the socket behind an httpx response (the `network_stream` extension first, then `response.stream`).
- `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py`: the stale-stream socket shutdown in `_StreamingCall` now uses `_socket_from_response` instead of its own copy of the same lookup. No behaviour change.
- `tests/agent/test_run_agent_codex_responses.py`: two new tests check that on timeout the shutdown runs on the watchdog while the close stays on the reader thread, and that a clean drain never shuts the socket down. Two existing tests are renamed and updated for the no-socket skip and the single-close rule.

## Credit
- @JoaoMarcos44 (#127615) wrote the fix. Three commits were cherry-picked with `-x`, authorship kept: "keep post-terminal stream close on reader thread", "avoid duplicate raw stream close", "pin managed close ownership".
- @100yenadmin (#127391) submitted first, with the same root cause and a different design (the drain thread owns the close). Credited as `Co-authored-by` on the follow-up commit.
- Follow-up commits by @kshitijk4poor: dropped the unused return value and the logger suppress wrappers, moved the socket lookup into a shared helper, and tightened the tests.

## Verification
- Tests on the rebased head: 81 passed across 6 files (`test_run_agent_codex_responses.py`, `test_stream_interrupt_abort_socket.py`, `test_stream_stale_kill_unwedge.py`, `test_codex_runtime_history_seed.py`, `test_codex_runtime_live_events.py`, `test_codex_runtime_prompt_handoff.py`). Probe: 3 passed.
- Red on base: the 3 kept tests fail with `agent/codex_runtime.py` from main (timeout close stays on the reader thread, clean drain never shuts down, owner close does not retry raw).
- Probe: on base, `close()` runs on MainThread while `codex-post-terminal-drain` is reading, so it fires. On head, shutdown runs on `codex-post-terminal-watchdog` and close on MainThread (the reader), so it passes. `_socket_from_response` resolves through extensions and through `.stream`, and returns None otherwise.
- Mutation: reverting the core fix turns both new thread-ownership tests red. Putting back the raw close after the managed close turns the single-close test red. Breaking `_socket_from_response` turns 4 tests red in `test_stream_interrupt_abort_socket.py` / `test_stream_stale_kill_unwedge.py`. Disabling the no-socket skip turns its test red.
- ruff (F401/F811/F821) shows no new findings; the only hit is the unused `import os` in `codex_runtime.py`, which is already on main. `git diff --check` is clean. The Windows footgun check flags one `encoding="utf-8"` read in the test file, which is also already on main.
- Reviewed over 3 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- If httpcore exposes no socket, the post-terminal drain is skipped instead of running unbounded on another thread. That is the same as setting `stream_drain_timeout=0` for that response.
- #130176 (auxiliary Codex watchdog, same fd-reuse class) is a separate surface and merges cleanly with this PR. Its local socket lookup could later move onto `_socket_from_response`.

raw.body:
Exiting a `hermes --worktree` session no longer deletes the worktree when it holds uncommitted, staged or untracked work; the CLI keeps it and says it has uncommitted changes.

Fixes #129482

## What happened
On exit, `_cleanup_worktree` in `cli.py` kept the worktree only when its branch had unpushed commits. Anything else went to `git worktree remove --force`, so uncommitted edits and untracked files were deleted, even though the docs say dirty trees are kept.

## Change
- `cli.py`: `_cleanup_worktree` checks `_worktree_is_dirty` before the unpushed-commits check. A dirty tree is kept and the CLI prints a new `cli.worktree.uncommitted_keeping` message. Dirty trees get no `--force` cleanup hint, because `--force` would delete the work. `_active_worktree` is cleared once, near the top of the function.
- `hermes_cli/worktree_ops.py`: `_worktree_is_dirty(worktree_path, repo_root, ...)` now skips untracked `.worktreeinclude` directory symlinks that point back to the same entry in the main checkout. A trailing-slash gitignore pattern such as `node_modules/` never matches a symlink, so before this every worktree of a repo with a `.worktreeinclude` counted as dirty and would never have been cleaned up. It now uses `git status --porcelain -z` and still treats any failure as dirty. Parsing `.worktreeinclude` moved into a shared `_worktreeinclude_entries` helper, which `_copy_worktree_includes` reuses. The main checkout comes from git instead of `--git-common-dir`'s parent, so submodule and `--separate-git-dir` layouts work.
- `hermes_cli/kanban_db_workspace.py`, prune classifier: pass `repo_root` to the new required parameter.
- `locales/*.yaml`: `cli.worktree.uncommitted_keeping` added to the 17 locale files that have `cli.worktree` keys.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_worktree.py`: `test_exit_cleanup_preserves_dirty_worktree` is parametrized over untracked, modified, staged, an include-symlink-only tree (removed), include symlink plus a real untracked file (kept), and a `--separate-git-dir` repo's include-only tree (removed). `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_worktree_teardown.py`: the stub signature is updated.

## Credit
- Yuan Li (@dskwe, #129489), first to submit the fix. Two commits are cherry-picked with authorship kept: `fix(cli): preserve dirty session worktrees` and `test(cli): cover dirty worktree exit cleanup`.
- @Sahilvishnaliya (#129866) sent an equivalent `cli.py` fix the next day.
- Follow-ups by @kshitijk4poor (Co-authored-by: Yuan Li): the uncommitted-changes message, the `.worktreeinclude` symlink handling, main-checkout resolution for submodule and `--separate-git-dir` layouts, and test rows.
- @artyficialmind reported the issue (#129482).

## Verification
- On the rebased head, `test_worktree.py`, `test_kanban_worktree_teardown.py`, `test_worktree_selfheal.py` and `test_kanban_worktree_unicode_path.py`: 52 passed, 7 skipped. `test_i18n.py`, `test_i18n_languages.py` and `test_i18n_layers.py`: 66 passed.
- Red on base: with base `cli.py`, `test_exit_cleanup_preserves_dirty_worktree` fails. With the pre-resolution `worktree_ops.py`/`cli.py`/`kanban_db_workspace.py`, the `--separate-git-dir` row fails.
- Repro probe: on base, untracked, modified and staged trees are deleted on exit (fires). On head, all 6 rows behave as intended (pass): normal, submodule and `--separate-git-dir` layouts, each with an include-only tree and an include-plus-untracked tree.
- Mutation: reverting each behaviour commit turns at least one test red.
- ruff F401/F811/F821: no new findings. `git diff --check` and `check-windows-footguns.py --all` are clean.
- Reviewed over 4 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- `kanban_db_workspace._cleanup_worktree_workspace` still derives `repo_root` as `--git-common-dir`'s parent. For a `--separate-git-dir` repo that path has no `.worktreeinclude`, so include symlinks there still count as dirty. Kanban then keeps that worktree, which errs on the safe side. Not changed here.
- #128887 (the startup pruner dropping `--force`) is a separate seam and stays open.

raw.body:
A cron job chained with `context_from` now receives the complete previous answer, even when that answer contains its own `## Response` heading. Before this change only the text after the last such heading came through.

Fixes #128543

## What happened
`_inject_context_from` pulled the answer out of the stored run document with `archive.rpartition("## Response")`. If the agent's answer contained that heading, either on its own line or quoted, the split landed inside the answer, and the next run got only the tail.

## Change
- `cron/scheduler.py`: the run-document writer puts `**Prompt Characters:** N` before `## Prompt` and `**Response Characters:** M` before `## Response`. Line endings are normalised before counting. The header and the response body are built from shared frame constants imported from `cron.scheduler_prompt`.
- `cron/scheduler_prompt.py`: `_archive_answer` reads the one enclosing response frame at exactly its declared length. A truncated or invalid frame is rejected, so the reader falls back to an older usable archive and never promotes a quoted inner frame. Archives without frames (pre-upgrade runs, script-mode output, FAILED docs) keep their old handling, and script-mode archives are trimmed as before. The frame labels and their compiled patterns are module constants. An unshipped fallback for "prompt-less frame" archives was removed.
- `tests/cron/test_context_from_response_extraction.py`: two tests round-trip the real writer through the reader. One covers nested and embedded frames, the other a truncated outer frame. There is also a whole-document check for script-mode archives.
- `contributors/emails/`: author map entry for itsflownium.

## Credit
- @dskwe (Yuan Li) submitted first, in #128555. Their commits "fix(cron): preserve embedded response headings" and "test(cron): cover framed embedded response headings" are cherry-picked with authorship kept.
- @itsflownium wrote #128685, which builds on #128555. Their commits "fix(cron): validate complete archive frames before normalization" and "fix(cron): reject invalid enclosing response frames" are cherry-picked with authorship kept.
- @liuhao1024's #128565 took the same response-length approach independently.
- Follow-up commits by kshitijk4poor: trimmed the tests to two invariants, removed the unshipped fallback branch, restored the script-mode trim, and moved the writer and reader onto shared frame constants.

## Verification
- Ran on the rebased head: `test_context_from_response_extraction.py`, `test_continuity_silent_audits.py`, `test_cron_context_from.py`, `test_scheduler.py` gave 119 passed, 0 failed (5+2+19+93). During review, `test_cron_empty_payload.py`, `test_notepad.py` and `test_web_server_cron_profiles.py` also passed.
- Red on base: the new writer/reader tests fail on main.
- Probe (real `_run_doc_header` writer → `_archive_answer`): for an answer with an embedded `## Response` heading, base returned `'subsection body'` and head returns the full answer. For a truncated framed doc, base accepted the partial text and head rejects it. The plain, `[SILENT]`, CRLF, prompt-quoting-a-frame and legacy unframed cases match between base and head.
- Mutation: reverting each behaviour commit turns at least one kept test red. None of the commits is toothless. The final commit is a pure refactor, and its writer output was byte-identical before and after.
- ruff F401/F811/F821: no new findings. `git diff --check` is clean. `check-windows-footguns.py --all` is clean.
- Reviewed over 3 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- The FAILED-run document is still written without frames. If its prompt quotes `## Response`, the legacy `rpartition` path behaves exactly as it does on main. Framing it would need a separate reader branch, so it is left out of this PR.
- #130524 (opened 2026-10-01) carries #128685 forward with extra compatibility commits on the same three files. It overlaps this PR.

raw.body:
The bundled disk-cleanup plugin now auto-deletes only `test_*`/`tmp_*` files a tool call actually created. Existing user files the agent patched, ran, or listed survive the end of the turn.
Refs #107343

## What happened
`post_tool_call` tracked every existing path that matched `test_*`/`tmp_*`, whether it came from `write_file`/`patch` args, a terminal command, or terminal output. Category `test` is removed at age 0 by the `quick` cleanup that runs at session end, and directories are rmtree'd. So a cron script the agent only patched, or a hook directory it listed with `ls`/`find`, was deleted irreversibly after one turn.

## Change
- `plugins/disk-cleanup/__init__.py`:
  - New `pre_tool_call` hook records which paths named in the call's args do not exist yet. The record is keyed by `(task_id or session_id, tool_call_id)` because llama.cpp reuses one constant id. The hook never raises, and entries expire after an hour.
  - `post_tool_call` tracks a path only if its own snapshot saw it absent and it exists now. Any path the snapshot did not cover fails closed. That includes a path another plugin's `modify` hook swapped in after the snapshot.
  - Paths seen only in terminal output are no longer tracked, so the output-scanning regex is removed.
  - A shared `_owner()` helper builds the keys for both the snapshot map and the per-session tracking bucket.
- `plugins/disk-cleanup/plugin.yaml`: declares `pre_tool_call` under `provides_hooks`. Without it, `plugin doctor` warns about an undeclared hook.
- `plugins/disk-cleanup/README.md`: documents the pre/post hook contract and the fail-closed rule. Calls without a `tool_call_id` (execute_code RPC) are not tracked.
- `tests/plugins/test_disk_cleanup_plugin.py`:
  - Existing tests now drive the real pre → side effect → post order.
  - Two new tests: a patched 90-day-old script and a listed hook directory are never tracked, and a call never uses another session's snapshot.
  - The kanban test now checks a kanban file that a call created.

## Credit
- @Froraut wrote the fix in #128090 (first submitter). Two commits were cherry-picked with `-x` and keep their authorship:
  - `e0e0e1f745`: track only files a tool call created.
  - `8d0b853981`: per-session snapshot keys, fail closed on unsnapshotted paths.
- Maintainer follow-ups by @kshitijk4poor:
  - New tests trimmed from 3 to 2. The rewritten-args case hits the same fail-closed branch as the headline test.
  - `provides_hooks` declaration, `_owner()` helper and README note.
  - The kanban test leg now covers a call-created file.

## Verification
- On the rebased head:
  - `tests/plugins/test_disk_cleanup_plugin.py`: 33 passed. On base, 31 passed, and the two new invariant tests fail there.
  - Plugin CLI mirrors:
    - `test_plugin_validate.py`, `test_plugins_cmd_list.py` and `test_plugins_cmd_category_discovery.py`: 71 passed, 1 failed with the disk-cleanup file. The failure is `test_portable_validation_fails_orphan_and_reports_availability`, which also fails on base and is in code this PR doesn't touch.
    - `test_plugin_dev.py`: 9 passed.
- Live probe against the real plugin module:
  - Base: a patched existing script, a `find`-listed hook dir, an `ls`-listed hook dir, and a user file under a constant tool-call id were all deleted.
  - Head: all four survive. Files the call created are still cleaned up and non-pattern files are kept on both.
- Mutation testing:
  - Reverting the created-only commit turns 7 tests red.
  - Reverting the session-keying commit turns 1 red.
  - Reverting the `provides_hooks` line is caught by `doctor_plugin`.
- Lint: ruff F401/F811/F821 clean, `git diff --check` clean, and Windows-footgun check clean on the plugin module.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- #109355 is a larger redesign that limits auto-delete to Hermes-owned roots. This PR is narrower and does not conflict with it in intent.
- #107343 is only partly addressed. A `test_*` file the agent newly creates under `scripts/` is still tracked as disposable.

raw.body:
While `hermes pause` is engaged, a due heartbeat no longer sends the paused notice to the chat on every 5s poll (it fires once after `hermes resume`), and scheduled /loop wakeups no longer start agent turns until resume.

Salvages #126905; supersedes the duplicate #127525. No linked issue.

## What happened
The heartbeat poller had no pause check, so it injected the due tick on every poll; `_hm_estop_gate` answered each one with the paused notice and the tick stayed due, so the notice repeated indefinitely (reported as ~10k Telegram messages in 6h and a flood ban). /loop wakeups are injected as internal events, and `_hm_estop_gate` returns early for internal events, so `hermes pause` did not stop them at all.

## Change
- `gateway/run_goals.py` `_heartbeat_poll_watch`: skip while paused, before the tick is claimed, so it fires normally after resume.
- `gateway/run_goals.py` `_loop_wakeup_fire_one`: `check_paused("loop", logger)` after `is_due` and before `fire_tick`. `is_due` only reads state, so the tick stays due for the first scan after resume; the watcher's 15s sleep per scan means no busy loop.
- `gateway/run_inbound.py` `_hm_estop_gate`: a heartbeat event that slips past the poller check is dropped silently (`""`). Real user messages still get the paused notice. Docstring explains why.
- Tests: 2 new in `tests/gateway/test_heartbeat_poller.py` (contributor); a pause/resume leg folded into the existing `test_loop_wakeup_from_secondary_route_fires_through_its_own_bot` in `tests/gateway/test_multiplex_notice_egress_profile_adapter.py` (no new test function).
- `contributors/emails/`: map entry for the contributor.

## Credit
- @dzianisv wrote the heartbeat fix and its two tests in #126905 (first submitter, 2026-09-28). Commit cherry-picked with authorship kept.
- #127525 by @creditlabsonarc-rgb (opened 2026-09-29) proposes the same heartbeat fix; #126905 was earlier.
- Follow-up commits by @kshitijk4poor: the /loop pause check and its test leg, the `_hm_estop_gate` docstring, and the contributor email map.

## Verification
- On the rebased head: `test_heartbeat_poller.py`, `test_loop_command.py`, `test_multiplex_notice_egress_profile_adapter.py`, `cron/test_estop.py`: 37 passed. `test_heartbeat_acceptance.py`, `test_heartbeat_execution_ownership.py`, `test_heartbeat_watch_lifecycle.py`, `test_telegram_reply_mode.py`: 33 passed. `tui_gateway/test_notification_turn_release.py`: 6 passed.
- Red on base: both new heartbeat tests fail on main (a heartbeat MessageEvent is received and the paused notice is sent). With the /loop check reverted, the folded test fails with `assert ([1], ['tick']) == ([], [])`.
- Probe, base vs head: a due `/loop 5m /status` under `hermes pause` ran on main (handled `['/status']`, 1 tick fired) and is held on head (`[]`, 0 ticks), then fires once after resume.
- Mutation: reverting the poller check, the gate's heartbeat drop, or the /loop check each turns a kept test red.
- ruff F401/F811/F821: no new findings vs main. `git diff --check` clean. Windows-footguns check: no new findings (one existing `write_text` without `encoding=` at line 67 of the multiplex test file is on main and untouched here).
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- The stack also fixes `hermes pause` not stopping /loop wakeups: they are internal events, which bypassed `_hm_estop_gate`. This was found in review and is not part of #126905.
- Other internal-event producers (process-completion notifications, wake, CLI handoff, plugin injection) still bypass the gate, as they do on main. They are one-shot continuations of in-flight work, not recurring ticks, so they are left as they are.
- Pause expiry stays out of scope (#121054).
