raw.body:
On Windows and Linux, closing the last desktop window now quits the app even while a hidden helper window (Quick Entry, HUD, pet overlay) is still alive. A second launch now restores and focuses a minimized or tray-hidden window instead of doing nothing.

Fixes #130810

## What happened
On Windows and Linux the only `app.quit()` for a window close lives in `window-all-closed`. `registerChatWindow`'s `closed` handler only removed the window from `chatWindows`. Any hidden helper `BrowserWindow` blocks `window-all-closed` from firing, for example Quick Entry, which hides on blur instead of closing. When that happened the process kept running with no UI and kept holding the single-instance lock. A relaunch then went to the `second-instance` handler, which called `restore()`/`focus()` but never `show()`, so a tray-hidden window stayed invisible. Separately, `shouldFocusToTakeKeyboard` destructured `{ isFocused }` and called it without its receiver. On a real Electron `BrowserWindow` that throws `TypeError: Object has been destroyed`. This bug has been latent on main since #83998.

## Change
- `apps/desktop/electron/main-window-lifecycle.ts`:
  - New `shouldQuitOnLastChatClosed`: a single boolean expression that is true only off macOS, with no handoff in progress, no quit already in progress, and zero remaining surfaces.
  - New `activateWindow`: restore if minimized → show if hidden → focus if not focused (through `shouldFocusToTakeKeyboard`). It is a no-op for a missing or destroyed window.
- `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts`:
  - New `quitIfNoSurfaceLeft()` counts `chatWindows.size + browserWindows.size`. It runs from `registerChatWindow`'s `closed` handler and, deferred with `setImmediate`, from `spawnBrowserWindow`'s `closed` handler. The deferral is needed because the browser registry deletes its entry in a listener that is attached after the factory returns.
  - New `quitInProgress` latch. It is set in `before-quit` and cleared next to `appQuitting` when a re-entered quit is held ("Keep Running").
  - The primary window's `close` handler returns early on `event.defaultPrevented` (tray absorb, active-work guard), so a prevented close does not latch a quit.
  - The `second-instance`, tray restore and dock `activate` paths go through `ensureMainWindow(focusWindow: activateWindow)`. The `second-instance` path adds one `rememberLog('[second-instance] relaunch (deepLink=…)')` line so relaunches show up in desktop.log.
  - `handleDeepLink`'s live-window branch calls `activateWindow`. The close-preview branch keeps its unconditional `focus()` (#83998) and gains a `show()` for tray-hidden windows.
- `apps/desktop/electron/window-focus-policy.ts`: `shouldFocusToTakeKeyboard` calls `window.isFocused()` on the receiver instead of destructuring it. This fixes `activateWindow` and both `focusWindow` call sites in `main.ts` without touching the call sites.
- `apps/desktop/electron/main-window-lifecycle.test.ts`: two tests. One is a table-driven `shouldQuitOnLastChatClosed` matrix. The other drives `activateWindow` against a `class FakeWindow` whose methods read `this`, so the test fails if `isFocused` is destructured again. The 4 existing `ensureMainWindow` tests are unchanged.

## Credit
- @JerryLiu369 opened #130835, the first and only PR for #130810. It added the last-chat-window quit fallback, the `quitInProgress` gate and the show+focus restore. Both commits were cherry-picked with `-x` and authorship kept: 941845f8eb (from 14711fc196) and 62c463bbed (from ec53f082ba). @ehz0ah had approved its final head.
- @kshitijk4poor added seven follow-up commits:
  - aca8c1461e: `second-instance` now reuses `ensureMainWindow` in place of a re-implemented `decideSecondInstanceAction`. Inlined the `window-all-closed` condition again. Removed the try/catch blocks and `typeof` probes in `activateWindow`. Fixed a typo.
  - 663abd3045: trimmed the PR's 8 tests to the two invariants. Two of the dropped tests rebuilt `main.ts` state locally and then asserted it.
  - 2237854bf2: clear `quitInProgress` when a re-entered quit is held, so a later close still quits.
  - 0cb56f85a1: count open Browser pop-outs as surfaces, so closing the primary no longer kills a pop-out.
  - cc6b734cc0: route the deep-link live-window branch through `activateWindow`, and give the #83998 focus rule a single owner.
  - 2ea493de58: run the fallback when the last Browser pop-out closes after the primary is already gone.
  - fcc2129177: call `isFocused` on its receiver (the latent #83998 `TypeError`).
- The contributor email is already in `contributors/emails`, so no map commit was needed.

## Verification
- Tests (vitest, `apps/desktop`):
  - Gate run on the pre-rebase head: `main-window-lifecycle.test.ts`, `window-focus-policy.test.ts` and `session-windows.test.ts` gave 33 passed / 0 failed.
  - Re-run on the rebased head fcc2129177: 33/33.
  - On base, the two existing files gave 27/27.
  - With base `main-window-lifecycle.ts`, both kept lifecycle tests fail (`activateWindow is not a function`, `shouldQuitOnLastChatClosed is not a function`).
- Probe: real Electron 40, with `main-window-lifecycle.ts` bundled by esbuild from the tree under test.
  - Base: primary close with a hidden helper → `NO QUIT window-all-closed=false remaining=1`.
  - Head: the same scenario → `QUIT-EMITTED`, exit 0.
  - Head predicate: linux/win32 with 0 remaining → true. darwin, 1 remaining (Browser pop-out), quit in progress and handoff → false.
  - Head `activateWindow`: a hidden window ends up `visible=true`, and a null window does not throw.
- Mutation:
  - Reverting the receiver fix turns "explicit relaunch activates a minimized tray-hidden window" red.
  - Reverting 941845f8eb gives 2 red; reverting 62c463bbed gives 1 red.
  - The `main.ts` wiring commits (2237854bf2, 0cb56f85a1, 2ea493de58) have no unit-test seam. They were proven red→green with source-level probes only.
- Lint and checks: `git diff --check` is clean and the Windows footgun check is clean. ruff is N/A because only TypeScript changed. tsc was not run.
- Reviewed over 3 rounds plus a final gate (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation). The final round approved with no findings.

## Maintainer notes
- fcc2129177 also repairs a latent bug on main: since #83998, `focusWindow` and `shouldFocusToTakeKeyboard` threw `TypeError: Object has been destroyed` against a real `BrowserWindow`. Plain-object test mocks hid it. `window-focus-policy.test.ts` still uses closure mocks, but the receiver dependence is now pinned by the class-based test in `main-window-lifecycle.test.ts`.
- Not run on Windows. The probe ran on macOS with the platform passed to the predicate, so Windows-only foreground activation (`show()`/`focus()` on win32) is unverified.
- It is not proven that the reporter hit the hidden-helper path rather than a stalled `before-quit` teardown. Open #123845 (@edosulai) covers the stalled-teardown path with an `app.exit` deadline. The two are complementary, but they edit the same `app.on('before-quit')` handler, so whichever lands second needs a rebase.
- Behaviour change: on Windows/Linux, closing the last chat window quits even while helper windows are alive. Open Browser pop-outs keep the app running, and the app quits when the last one closes.
- `main.ts` is about 19.8k lines. This PR adds a net +47 there (+69/-22) and moves the decision logic into `main-window-lifecycle.ts`.
- The issue's right-click tab menu remark is a separate item and is not addressed here.

raw.body:
After a rotated `/compress` (or a rotating session-hygiene compaction) in the gateway, the new session keeps the rows that were published with it, and a transient DB error no longer surfaces as "failed to persist compressed transcript" over a compression that already committed.

Refs #131756

## What happened
On rotation, `publish_compression_child()` writes the child's handoff plus any cloned foreign-tail rows (turns that landed during compression) in the same transaction that ends the parent. The gateway then rewrote that child again from the in-memory handoff with `rewrite_transcript()` → `replace_messages(active_only=False)`, at both `gateway/slash_commands_session.py` (manual `/compress`) and `gateway/run_turn.py` (hygiene). The in-memory handoff does not contain the cloned rows, so the rewrite DELETEd them. Any failure in that redundant rewrite raised a false persist error. Skipping the rewrite alone was not enough: for `/compress here N`, rotation published only head + summary and `compress_now` rejoined the kept verbatim tail in memory, so the gateway rewrite was the only thing making the tail durable. CLI/TUI/ACP never rewrite, so on those surfaces a rotated `/compress here N` already persisted only the head.

## Change
- `gateway/session_transcript.py`:
  - New `is_published_compression_child(parent, child)`. It returns True when the child row points at the parent, is a compression child, and has active messages. It looks the child up through the parent's store, because the child id is not in the routing index yet when the probe runs. Fails open (False) on any DB error so callers fall back to the old rewrite.
  - New `persist_rotated_compression_child(parent, child, messages)`: a published child is already durable; anything else gets the existing rewrite.
- `gateway/slash_commands_session.py`, `gateway/run_turn.py`: both rotation call sites call `persist_rotated_compression_child` instead of `rewrite_transcript`. One-line comment and docstring updates.
- `agent/conversation_compression.py` (`_commit_compaction`, rotation branch): when `verbatim_tail` is set, publish `rejoin_compressed_head_and_tail(compressed, verbatim_tail)` (as the in-place branch already stores it) and stamp the tail rows. The two helper imports move above the `in_place` split.
- `agent/conversation_compression_manual.py`: comment only. Stamped tail rows now also mean a rotated commit stored the tail, so `compress_now` skips its in-memory rejoin.
- `tests/gateway/test_compress_command.py`: new `test_rotated_compress_keeps_atomically_published_foreign_tail`, parametrized `main` / `fitness`. `fitness` is a multiplexed named profile backed by its own `profiles/fitness/state.db`.
- `tests/agent/test_conversation_compression_manual.py`: new `test_rotated_here_n_publishes_the_kept_exchanges`. It checks that the durable child equals `after_messages` and that the last 4 rows are the kept history.
- `contributors/emails/ned@nanobro.local`: contributor map entry.

## Credit
- @nanobro (Ned) found the destructive second rewrite and the false persist error and fixed them in #131756, which adds the published-child probe, both call-site guards and the regression test. Commit 7e023fae82 was cherry-picked as 54c6e29e26 with authorship kept. First submitter, and triage found no competing PR.
- @kshitijk4poor added follow-up commits:
  - eadb31a6aa: rotation publishes the `/compress here N` tail. Without it, skipping the rewrite lost the kept exchanges. This also fixes the latent head-only persist on CLI/TUI/ACP.
  - 0203d3bb53: the probe goes through the parent's store. Before this, under `multiplex_profiles` a named-profile child fell back to the root `state.db`, the probe returned False, and the destructive rewrite still ran.
  - bf177cdec1: one `persist_rotated_compression_child` shared by both call sites, which removes the inline duplication and a temp flag. 78a1bbc4cd: import hoist. 6e39a08185: comment wording. All three have no behaviour change.
  - a320400d5c and a81344076a: test trims. These dropped a parametrize that exercised no profile shape and a fallback test that already passed on base.
  - 9e50c227f5: contributor map.

## Verification
- Tests on the final head (clean env, no `PYTHONPATH`):
  - `test_compress_command.py`, `test_conversation_compression_manual.py`, `hermes_cli/test_partial_compress.py` and `hermes_cli/test_compress_here.py`: 42 passed.
  - `test_session_hygiene.py`, `test_hygiene_warning_lifecycle.py`, `test_session_hygiene_turnhold_adoption.py` and `test_multiplex_session_db_profile_scope.py`: 41 passed.
  - `test_compression_concurrent_sessions.py`, `hermes_cli/test_manual_compress.py`, `test_hygiene_no_commit_reason.py` and `test_codex_hygiene_compaction.py`: 24 passed.
  - Each run separately on head and base, with identical results: `test_compression_rotation_state.py` 40/40, `test_compression_persistence.py` 10/10, `test_compression_concurrent_fork.py` 48/48, `test_compression_failure_session_sync.py` 2/2.
- Red on base: `test_rotated_compress_keeps_atomically_published_foreign_tail` fails with base gateway files. `test_rotated_here_n_publishes_the_kept_exchanges` fails with base `agent/conversation_compression.py` plus the cherry-pick. Both pass on head.
- Probe: real `SessionDB` + gateway mixin, imported from each tree.
  - Base: full compress with a concurrent foreign turn leaves the child as `['[summary] compressed']`, so the cloned foreign row is deleted.
  - Head: the same case gives `['[summary] compressed', 'FOREIGN concurrent turn']`. A plain full compress is the same on both.
  - The probe's hand-built `partial-here-N` case publishes a head-only handoff and bypasses the agent, so it no longer models the real flow after eadb31a6aa. The real flow is covered by the new agent test.
- Mutation (prod files reverted per commit, then the two touched test files run):
  - 54c6e29e26 → red `[main]` + `[fitness]`.
  - eadb31a6aa → red `test_rotated_here_n_publishes_the_kept_exchanges`.
  - One-line revert of 0203d3bb53's parent-store lookup → red `[fitness]` only.
  - bf177cdec1 and 78a1bbc4cd stay green, as expected for refactors.
- `ruff` (F401/F811/F821) shows no new findings. The remaining hits are on base (`datetime` in `agent/conversation_compression.py`, `build_session_key` in `gateway/slash_commands_session.py`). `git diff --check` and the Windows footgun check are clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation) plus a final gate. One Medium (multiplex store lookup) and four Lows were fixed in-stack.

## Maintainer notes
- The hygiene call site (`gateway/run_turn.py`) has no test of its own. It calls the same `persist_rotated_compression_child` as the tested manual `/compress` path, and the hygiene suites stay green, but the hygiene rotation flow was not live-probed.
- The multiplexed named-profile case is covered only by the `fitness` row of the gateway test.
- Behaviour change: a rotated child that is published and verified is no longer rewritten from memory. When the probe can't confirm publication (no compression child row, no active messages, or a DB error), the old rewrite still runs, unchanged.
- `is_published_compression_child` calls the private `SessionDB._is_compression_child_row`, as other gateway code in the same module family already does.
- Overlap: our merged #130523 changed the same rotation branch of `_commit_compaction`. This branch is rebased on it and the conflict is resolved.
- File sizes: `agent/conversation_compression.py` (~4.3k lines) and `gateway/run_turn.py` (~4.4k lines) were already over 2000 lines. This stack adds only a few net lines to each.

raw.body:
When compaction restates a request that is still in progress, the transcript now holds one active row for it instead of two rows sharing the same `message_uid`, and the compacted window still opens on a user turn.

Refs #131104

## What happened
`ContextCompressor._reappend_inflight_user_task` appends a `[STILL IN PROGRESS]` replay of the in-flight user request after compaction. When that request was the first user row in the protected head, the original row survived as well. The durable transcript then had two active rows with the same `message_uid`, and the request rendered twice after reload (#131104, reported by @Lee-Shon on 2026-10-02). Removing the original row (the contributor fix) exposed a second problem. The summary role had already been chosen against a head that ended on that user row, so the window could open `system → assistant(tool_calls) → tool → assistant summary`. Strict-alternation chat templates reject that sequence, and native Gemini rejects a leading model `functionCall` turn.

## Change
- `agent/context_compressor.py` (`_reappend_inflight_user_task`, +40/-2):
  - When the replay has a `message_uid`, user rows other than the carrier that carry the same uid are dropped from the compacted window. This uses `message_uid_or_none` and `MESSAGE_UID`. The existing lazy `message_metadata` import is moved up so that `record_absorbed_message` is covered by it too.
  - If a row was removed and the first non-system row is no longer `user`, the standalone summary carrier moves to that position.
  - If the carrier is itself a merged tail `assistant(tool_calls)` row (`_template_visible_role(carrier) is None`), the pre-dedup list is restored for this cycle. Moving that row would split it from its tool results.
  - If an assistant carrier has no visible user turn before it after the removal, it switches to the existing `_force_user_leading` layout: carrier `role=user`, with the request merged after `_SUMMARY_END_MARKER`. The merge path records the uid as absorbed, so the uid still belongs to one row.
- `tests/agent/test_cron_inflight_prompt_reappend.py` (+52): the contributor's `test_replay_replaces_surviving_user_row_with_same_message_uid` is extended and no new test function is added. The test now checks:
  - exactly one holder per uid, counting `ABSORBED_MESSAGE_UIDS`;
  - after a real `compress()` on a head-protected uid row, the raw `compressed[1]["role"] == "user"`, strict alternation holds, and the request appears after the end marker;
  - for a merged-tail tool-call carrier, the window still opens on a user row and each `tool_calls` row is immediately followed by its tool results.

## Credit
- @dskwe (Yuan Li) wrote the uid-matched removal and its regression test in #131110. That was the first and only PR for this issue (opened 2026-10-02). Commit ff89a5cf8c was cherry-picked with authorship kept (`-x 581719d1da`). Their contributor-map entry was already on main.
- @Lee-Shon reported #131104.
- @kshitijk4poor added follow-up commits after review:
  - b6e18ac0dd: when the removal leaves no user turn before the carrier, use the user-leading layout. Carries `Co-authored-by: Yuan Li`.
  - b5039e6a3e: move the carrier to the window opening so a leading tool-call row cannot be first (Gemini).
  - 69769365d0: do not move a merged tail tool-call carrier, so its tool pairing stays intact.
  - 2af1339013 and 0b37f4ca4c: behaviour-neutral refactors (`!= "user"`, `message_uid_or_none` / `MESSAGE_UID`).
  - 991506dc5e: the test uses `ABSORBED_MESSAGE_UIDS` and `_template_visible_role` instead of copies.

## Verification
- Tests were run on the head in a clean archive copy:
  - `test_cron_inflight_prompt_reappend.py`, `test_context_engine_message_uid.py`, `test_context_compressor_zero_user_provenance.py` and `test_summary_role_template_alternation.py`: 55 passed.
  - `test_context_compressor.py`: 276 passed.
- Red on base: the kept test fails with base `context_compressor.py`, and it also fails with the contributor-only prod file (before the follow-ups). It passes on head.
- Probe: real `compress()` on the head-protected in-flight shape.
  - Base: `DUP_UIDS={'U1': 2}`.
  - Head: `DUP_UIDS={}`, first non-system role `user`, Gemini's first content is `user`, alternation OK.
  - Three benign shapes (completed turn, newer user in the tail, legacy row without a uid) give the same output on base and head.
  - Merged-tail tool-call carrier shapes give row-for-row the same output as base, with pairing intact.
- Mutation: reverting any one of the four behaviour commits (ff89a5cf8c, b6e18ac0dd, b5039e6a3e, 69769365d0) turns the kept test red. The three refactor/test-only commits are behaviour-neutral.
- `ruff` (F401/F811/F821), `git diff --check` and the Windows footgun check are clean.
- Reviewed over 4 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation). Rounds 2 and 3 found the leading-tool-call (Gemini) and split-pairing issues, which are fixed above. Round 4 approved with no findings.

## Maintainer notes
- Trade-off: when the summary is merged into a tail `assistant(tool_calls)` row, the dedup is skipped for that compaction. The output is identical to base for that shape: the duplicate uid remains, tool pairing is intact, and the window opens on a user row. The duplicate is cleaned up on a later compaction, once the carrier is a standalone row.
- Unverified rare shape: a merged carrier that is an assistant *text* row (no tool_calls) at the same time as a removed head row. In that case the move-and-flip would make that row `role=user`, putting the prior assistant narration, still framed as `[PRIOR CONTEXT — for reference …]`, into a user row. Three real-compress sweeps (budgets 60–3000, protect_first_n 2/3/4) never produced that shape. Every merged carrier was the tool-call row, which the restore branch covers. Calling the function directly on that shape keeps alternation and pairing valid.
- Gemini: the leading model `functionCall` turn is fixed for the standalone carrier (b5039e6a3e). The Gemini 400 itself is based on the documented turn-order rule; no live API call was made.
- Scope: the second half of #131104 is not addressed here. That half is the model echoing the `[PRIOR CONTEXT — for reference only; not a new message]` frame of a merged carrier, i.e. the "re-delivers the previous reply" behaviour. On the DB side it is already correct (old row inactive, carrier active), so this PR uses `Refs`. It is recommended to track it separately with the merged-carrier frame work.
- Not changed: `agent/conversation_compression.py` `_ensure_compressed_has_user_turn` copies a user row while keeping its `message_uid`, which is the same class of bug. It is not reached when a real user row is present or when the merged replay is recognised.
- `agent/context_compressor.py` is about 5.8k lines; this PR adds 40.
- No overlap with other open compaction PRs: #130672 and #130523 do not touch `_reappend_inflight_user_task`.

raw.body:
Profile export no longer puts a profile's `.ssh/`, `.aws/`, `.gnupg/`, `.kube/` or direnv `.envrc` into the archive, whether they sit at the profile root or are nested under a skill. A distribution install can no longer plant or overwrite these stores either.

Refs #126114

## What happened
#126114 (merged in #130525) kept `auth.json`, `.env`, OAuth tokens and similar stores out of exports, but it did not cover OS credential stores. `PROFILE_CREDENTIAL_PATHS` covered only the subprocess `home/` subtree. So `export_profile` copied a named profile's private SSH keys, AWS credentials, GPG secrings and kube tokens into an archive that the docs describe as shareable. A distribution could also plant or replace those files on install. `agent/file_safety.py` already denies writes to the same stores under a home, so export and install were the gap. Separately, the default-profile export (`_default_export_ignore`) only allow-lists entries at the root. It never consulted `_EXPORT_CREDENTIAL_FILES`, so a store nested under `skills/` still shipped from the default profile.

## Change
- `hermes_cli/profiles.py`:
  - New `_OS_CREDENTIAL_STORES` tuple (`.ssh`, `.aws`, `.gnupg`, `.kube`, `.envrc`). It is added to both `PROFILE_CREDENTIAL_PATHS` and `_EXPORT_CREDENTIAL_FILES`, so the two lists cannot drift apart.
  - In `PROFILE_CREDENTIAL_PATHS`, the stores become private for export and user-owned for distribution install through the existing `profile_path_is_private`.
  - In `_EXPORT_CREDENTIAL_FILES`, a nested copy (`skills/x/.ssh`) is dropped at any depth.
  - `_default_export_ignore` now also drops `_EXPORT_CREDENTIAL_FILES` names at every depth, so default-profile exports get the same nested drop as named profiles.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_profile_export_credentials.py`: the existing invariant tests now seed the five stores at the root and nested under `skills/s/`. `test_named_export_ships_no_credential_store_or_copy_of_one` now also exports `default` and checks its members. No new test functions.
- `website/docs/user-guide/profile-distributions.md` (and the zh-Hans copy): the stores are listed in the "Always excluded" export list and in the distributions credential bullet.

## Credit
- @JerryLiu369 (Jerry Liu) wrote the fix in #130398 (commit 2bed1fbee8). That commit targeted `_EXPORT_CREDENTIAL_DIRS`, which has since been removed from main, so it could not be cherry-picked. It was rebuilt onto the current lists as 0cf0499d80 with authorship kept (`--author`). #130398 was the only PR for this gap.
- @kshitijk4poor added five follow-up commits after review:
  - 0ab157befe: drop nested credential stores from the default-profile export too.
  - 8a2e3d8862: name the OS stores once (`_OS_CREDENTIAL_STORES`). The resulting sets are identical to before.
  - 441b4f8c63: seed all five stores nested under a skill, so each name in the any-depth list is pinned.
  - 19bf7f2a27 and d4bda6de46: docs (English and zh-Hans).

## Verification
- Tests ran on head in a clean archive copy:
  - `test_profile_export_credentials`, `test_profile_distribution`, `test_profile_credential_collisions` and `test_profile_export_special_files`: 65 passed, 1 skipped.
  - `test_profiles` and `test_profile_export_default_path`: 114 passed, 6 skipped.
- Red on base: with `profiles.py` from main, `test_named_export_ships_no_credential_store_or_copy_of_one` and both `test_distribution_can_neither_plant_nor_replace_a_store[False|True]` cases fail.
- Probe: a named profile and the default profile, each seeded with the five stores at the root and under `skills/myskill/`.
  - Base: the named export leaks 10 entries (5 root + 5 nested), and the default export leaks the 5 nested ones.
  - Head: 0 leaks in both.
  - Benign neighbours (`skills/aws/`, `skills/kube-helper/`, `ssh_notes.md`, `envrc.example`, `memories/.kube_notes.md`) still export, and none is treated as user-owned on install.
- Mutation (each revert turns tests red):
  - Reverting the contributor commit: the 3 tests above go red.
  - Dropping the names from only `_EXPORT_CREDENTIAL_FILES`: the named-export test goes red.
  - Dropping them from only `PROFILE_CREDENTIAL_PATHS`: the 2 distribution cases go red.
  - Reverting 0ab157befe, or deleting just its `ignored.update(...)` line: the default-export assertions go red.
  - Removing `.gnupg` from `_OS_CREDENTIAL_STORES`: the 3 tests go red.
- `ruff` (including F401/F811/F821), `git diff --check` and the footgun check are clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation). The round-2 docs-parity finding is folded in d4bda6de46, a docs-only commit after the gated head 19bf7f2a27.

## Maintainer notes
- Behaviour change (security tightening): the default-profile export now also drops nested `auth.json`, `.env` and `bot-desktop` under `skills/`, `cron/` and `plugins/`. Before this change, only the root copies were excluded for the default profile. No existing test pinned the nested copies as shipped.
- A skill that ships a non-secret `.envrc` loses it in export. This matches `file_safety`'s `.envrc` deny.
- Out of scope: a distribution that ships these stores inside its own skill (`skills/x/.ssh`) still installs them. That content comes from the distribution, not from a user store, and nested `auth.json` behaves the same on main. A follow-up could have `_merge_dir`/`_owned_entries` skip `_EXPORT_CREDENTIAL_FILES` names.
- Open question: `file_safety` also write-denies `.docker`, `.azure`, `.config/gh` and `.config/gcloud` under a home, but this change does not exclude them from export. Should it?

raw.body:
A `/save json` snapshot from the CLI or a messaging platform now keeps the turns that in-place compaction archived, so importing it restores the whole session history instead of only the rows left after the last compaction.

Fixes #130339

## What happened
#130339 reported that session backups lost compacted history. #130623 fixed `hermes sessions export` (and GitHub auto-closed the issue), but the `/save json` paths were not touched. The CLI `/save` (`hermes_cli/cli_session_mixin.py`) and the gateway `/save` (`gateway/slash_commands_session.py`) still called `export_session(include_compacted=False)`, so the JSON held only live rows. A comment justified this by saying `import_sessions` would replay archived turns as live context. That stopped being true once import began restoring the `active`/`compacted` flags. On a compacted session, the probe on main writes 3 rows to `/save json` while the session displays 9, and the first prompt is missing.

## Change
- `hermes_cli/session_export.py`:
  - New `export_projection(transcript)`. It returns the `export_session` flags for each format: display history (`include_compacted`) for md/html, and every stored row with its flags (`include_inactive`) for JSON.
  - New `drop_undone_rows(export)`. For a `/save` JSON snapshot it keeps live and compaction-archived rows and leaves out rows removed by `/undo`, rewind or edit. It then rebuilds the `timings` block from the kept rows, so the block names no dropped row.
- `hermes_cli/cli_session_mixin.py` and `gateway/slash_commands_session.py` (`/save`):
  - Both now use `export_projection()`, and JSON output goes through `drop_undone_rows()`.
  - Before building the JSON, both call `assert_export_safe`, the same `sessions.max_export_messages` guard `hermes sessions export` uses. The CLI prints the refusal and writes no file. The gateway returns the refusal text.
- `hermes_cli/sessions_cmd.py`: `hermes sessions export` uses `export_projection(shown)` in place of its inline dict.
- `hermes_cli/console_engine.py`: `sessions export` in `hermes console` uses `export_projection(False)` instead of hard-coding `include_inactive=True`.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_save_transcript_history.py`: new `test_save_json_restores_compacted_history_as_archived`, parametrized for `cli` and `gateway`. It checks:
  - the snapshot's row ids equal the stored active-or-compacted rows, and a `model_only` live row is included;
  - a rewound "undone secret" turn is absent;
  - `timings.role_counts` covers only the kept rows;
  - an import restores display and live parity;
  - with `max_export_messages` patched to 5, the save is refused.
- `website/docs/user-guide/sessions.md` and the zh-Hans copy: the backup and `max_export_messages` text now covers CLI/messaging `/save json`, and the old "`/save json` remains live-only" line is removed.

## Credit
- @jonpol01 (John Paul Soliva) wrote the `/save json` fix in #130340. Commit 12f98c891c was cherry-picked with `-x` as 94f2a3bbd5, authorship kept. The sessions-export commits from the same PR had already landed via #130623. One conflict in `sessions_cmd.py` (the projection line) was resolved to `export_projection(shown)`.
- First submitter for the `/save json` half of #130339: @jonpol01 (#130340, 2026-10-01).
- @kshitijk4poor follow-up commits:
  - 6423112fba: tidied the test shape helper.
  - 9c2863f365: `hermes console` export uses the shared `export_projection()`.
  - f5b9864930: docs say which `/save` surfaces (CLI and messaging) write the full backup.
  - c24cea6961: `/save json` is capped by `sessions.max_export_messages` through `assert_export_safe`.
  - 1a4efa3f8e: rows removed by `/undo`/rewind/edit stay out of `/save json`.
  - 3cb78b4eca: the test pins the projection by exported row ids.
  - f88e99dead, plus a test-only commit pinning timings intervals: `drop_undone_rows()` replaces the duplicated filter and rebuilds `timings`.

## Verification
- Tests on the final head, in a clean archive copy: `test_save_transcript_history`, `test_save_command_delivery`, `test_save_conversation_location`, `test_sessions_export_backup_round_trip`, `test_console_engine`, `test_session_export`, `test_sessions_export_retention`, `test_session_save` and `test_sessions_export_md_cli` gave 44 passed. At the r2 gate, `test_session_archived_round_trip`, `test_sessions_export_output_dir`, `test_session_import_keep_flags`, `test_session_snapshot_removal` and `tests/hermes_state/test_hermes_state.py -k export` were also green.
- Red on base: with the base `/save` code, `test_save_json_restores_compacted_history_as_archived[cli]` and `[gateway]` fail. They pass on head.
- Probe (a real compacted session: display 9 rows, live 3):
  - Base: `/save json` writes 3 rows without the first prompt, and an import loses display parity. With a 5-row cap, the CLI and gateway still write the JSON.
  - Head: `/save json` writes 9 rows including the first prompt, and the import restores display and live parity. Rewound content is absent. Over the cap, the CLI and gateway refuse the JSON and still write md under the cap. `/save md` and `/save html` output is byte-identical to base (446 and 26220 bytes).
- Mutation:
  - Reverting the contributor commit turns `save_json[cli,gateway]` and 4 `test_console_engine` tests red.
  - Forcing `export_projection` to always return `include_compacted` turns `save_json[cli,gateway]` red.
  - Removing the cap or the `/undo` filter turns `save_json[cli,gateway]` red.
  - Removing the `timings` rebuild turns `save_json[cli,gateway]` red (2 failed / 2 passed).
  - The console refactor (9c2863f365) stays green, as expected for a behaviour-equivalent change.
- `ruff` F401/F811/F821 finds nothing new. The 3 existing F401s in the touched files are also on main. `git diff --check` and the Windows footgun scan are clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation). The single Low finding from r2 (stale `timings` after the `/undo` filter) is fixed in f88e99dead, plus a test-only commit pinning timings intervals.

## Maintainer notes
- Behaviour change: `/save json` now refuses sessions with more stored rows than `sessions.max_export_messages`, the same as `hermes sessions export`. Before this change it had no cap. The count includes rewound rows that the snapshot then drops, so the cap is conservative.
- `/save json` now holds compaction-archived turns, and anyone receiving a shared snapshot sees them. Turns removed by `/undo`/rewind/edit stay out (unlike `hermes sessions export`, which keeps them). `/save md|html` are unchanged.
- Not covered: the TUI/Desktop `/save` (`tui_gateway` `session.save`) still dumps in-memory history with no archived turns and no cap. That is a separate follow-up, and the docs now name only CLI and messaging.
- Overlap: open #130477 (@Sahilvishnaliya) edits the same `/save` paths. Its export hunk matches #130340's but has no tests or docs, and it bundles unrelated commits.
- I reopened #130339 after #130623 auto-closed it, because #130623 fixed only `hermes sessions export`.

raw.body:
On POSIX SSH hosts, a Desktop-owned `hermes serve --isolated` backend now shuts itself down between turns once the remote ownership lock names a newer spawn, so a reconnect storm no longer stacks detached backends that each write to `state.db`.

Refs #132034

## What happened
When a Desktop reconnect cannot prove that the recorded pid belongs to it (the pid looks dead, or the argv proof says FOREIGN), `cleanupStale` removes `desktop-ssh/<ownershipId>/backend.lock.json` without signalling that pid. `connect()` then spawns a new backend with a new nonce. The old backend never learned it had lost ownership. Its only exit was the idle watchdog: a 900s grace period that is gated on zero live WebSockets, and a half-open tunnel keeps the count above zero for up to the 600s ping timeout. During a reconnect storm these superseded backends piled up, each one an extra writer on `state.db`.

## Change
- `hermes_cli/web_server_owner_exit.py` (new):
  - `should_retire_superseded` is a pure decision. It returns true only when the lock is valid, names another `spawnNonce`, and the process has outlived the settle window. A missing, unreadable or skewed lock keeps the backend up.
  - `start_owner_watchdog` polls the lock every 15s. It needs two consecutive confirmations, then exits through the retirement fence (`prepare`/`commit`, then `server.should_exit = True`), so it never tears down mid-turn and admission is closed first.
- `hermes_cli/web_server_skew_exit.py`: the confirmation, fence and exit loop moved into a shared `_run_retirement_watchdog`. `start_code_skew_watchdog` and `start_owner_watchdog` are thin callers, and the public signatures are unchanged.
- `hermes_cli/dashboard_procs.py`:
  - The existing lock parse is split out as `read_valid_backend_lock(path)` and reused by `_lock_owned_serve_pids`, so there is no second parser.
  - The read is bounded to 65537 bytes, and the >64 KiB → None cap is unchanged.
  - New `BACKEND_LOCK_NAME` constant.
  - The settle window reuses the orphan reaper's `_REAP_MIN_AGE_SECONDS` (180s).
- `hermes_cli/web_server.py`: `start_server`/`_on_server_started` take `ssh_lock_path` and start the owner watchdog next to the skew watchdog, only when the backend is SSH-isolated, has an owner nonce, and has a lock path.
- `hermes_cli/main.py`: `cmd_dashboard` passes `ssh_lock_path` = the validated `--ssh-session-token-file`'s directory / `backend.lock.json`.
- Tests:
  - `tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_owner_exit.py` (new, 2 tests): a table test for the decision, including benign neighbours, and a loop test with an injected fence.
  - `test_web_server_ws_ping.py` and `test_resource_limits.py` gained assertions that pin the wiring through `start_server` and `serve`.
- The client side is unchanged: `cleanupStale` is not touched, so this composes with #126035.

## Credit
- @VexterZ (0xVexter) reported #132034 with the root-cause analysis and proposed the server-side watchdog design this PR implements.
- #89452 by @pmwanje2 (draft) first drafted a lock-ownership watchdog. It is linked as prior art. No code from it was reused, so there is no `Co-authored-by`.
- @kshitijk4poor wrote the fix in dbefa10135, plus follow-ups from review:
  - 71d47dbf00: dropped provenance from the module docstring.
  - ab6058025b: bounded the lock read.
  - 9813df811b: named the lock file once.
  - 946970a53c: shared the 180s settle window with the orphan reaper.
  - d83538f2ea: pinned the watchdog wiring in tests.
  - defc6472b2: one fenced retirement loop for the skew and owner watchdogs.

## Verification
- Tests ran on a fresh archive of the reviewed head, each file run alone:
  - `test_web_server_owner_exit` 2 passed
  - `test_web_server_skew_exit` 6 passed
  - `test_orphan_desktop_serve_reap` 13 passed
  - `test_web_server_idle_exit` 4 passed
  - `test_web_server_ws_ping` 7 passed, 3 skipped
  - `test_resource_limits` 21 passed, 1 skipped
  - `test_dashboard_admin_endpoints` 42 passed
  - `test_backend_retirement` 2 passed
- Red on base: the new test file fails at collection on main because the module and `read_valid_backend_lock` don't exist there. The two extended wiring tests fail when the fix commit is reverted.
- Probe: real-import Python, using the real lock reader and the real `RetirementFence`.
  - Base: `No module named 'hermes_cli.web_server_owner_exit'`, so nothing on the server side retires a superseded backend.
  - Head, benign cases: a lock that names this backend, a missing lock, and a newer spawn while busy all give `should_exit=False` with admission still open.
  - Head, bug case: a lock that names a newer spawn gives `should_exit=True` with admission closed.
  - The reaper neighbour `_lock_owned_serve_pids` returns `[4242]` on both base and head.
- Skew watchdog parity after the shared-loop refactor: five cases (stale ×2, none, alternating, update in progress, busy) give the same results and log text on base and head.
- Mutation:
  - Reverting the fix turns the owner-exit tests and both wiring tests red.
  - Going back to a 90s window turns the decision test red.
  - Dropping the confirmation reset, or changing `ok and commit` to `ok or commit`, turns both the owner and skew tests red.
  - Each of the three wiring mutations (web_server arm, `_on_server_started` kwarg, `main.py` path) is red.
  - The bounded read, docstring and constant commits stay green, as expected for changes with no behaviour difference.
- `ruff`, F401/F811/F821 on touched files, `git diff --check` and the footgun scan are clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation). The branch was later rebased onto current main with identical patches (`range-diff` shows all 7 commits as `=`).

## Maintainer notes
- POSIX SSH hosts only. On Windows hosts the Desktop writes `backend.lock.json` without `logPath`, so `read_valid_backend_lock` returns None and the watchdog never retires anything there. This fails safe: there is no false retirement, and `_lock_owned_serve_pids` already had the same blind spot. The shared validator was left alone because it also gates the orphan reaper's exclusion set. Windows needs a follow-up, so this PR uses `Refs`, not `Fixes`.
- Fence wait vs hard cap: this PR waits on the retirement fence, the same as the skew watchdog. A superseded backend with a stuck turn stays alive until the fence frees it or idle-exit fires. A hard cap (force exit N minutes after confirmed supersession) was not built, because the superseded backend's turn may still be streaming to the user. Is the fence the behaviour we want?
- The settle window is the orphan reaper's `_REAP_MIN_AGE_SECONDS` (180s), not a separate constant. Retirement can happen up to 90s later than a dedicated 90s window would allow, but the reaper and the watchdog can't drift apart.
- `fence.cancel(token)` is not called when `commit` fails. This was already true of the skew watchdog, and it is now in one shared loop, so a follow-up fixes both.
- The lock path comes from the validated token directory (`~/.hermes/desktop-ssh/<oid>`), not from `get_hermes_home()`. That matches the token validation and where the Desktop writes the lock.
- #126035 (open) edits `cleanupStale` on the client. This PR does not touch it, so there is no overlap.
- #89452 (draft) takes a different approach: `os._exit`, exit on a missing lock, and a classifier rewrite. It is left open.

raw.body:
`/goal resume last goal`, `/goal continue` on a paused goal and `/goal pause for now` now run the control command instead of silently replacing the standing goal with that sentence.

Salvage of #127367 (core fix only; no linked issue).

## What happened
`dispatch_goal_command` only treated a control verb as control when the whole argument matched a key in `_EXACT_HANDLERS`. Anything with trailing words, such as `resume last goal` or `pause for now`, fell through to `_set`, which replaced the goal text. `continue` was not a control word at all, so `/goal continue` on a paused goal also set the goal to "continue". `is_goal_control`, which the gateway's busy path uses, had the same whole-argument check. Mid-run, it rejected `/goal pause for now` with `gateway.busy.reject_goal`.

## Change
- `hermes_cli/goal_command.py`:
  - Adds `continue` and `unpause` as aliases for `resume`.
  - New `_BARE_CONTROL_VERBS` (resume/continue/unpause/pause/status/show/unwait). When one of these is the first word, the verb runs and `_bare_control` appends an `(ignored '<rest>': …)` hint that points to `/goal -- <text>`. `clear`/`stop`/`done` keep their existing behaviour, so they still set goal text when followed by words. This avoids ending a goal the user meant to keep.
  - `/goal -- <text>` sets goal text verbatim. It only matches a standalone `--` token, so `/goal --dry-run the migration` is still kept literally, as on main. `/goal --` on its own reports an empty-goal error and keeps the goal.
  - A plain replace now names the goal it replaced (`(replaced the previous goal)\n  was: …`). This only happens when a goal was still live (`mgr.has_goal()`), so there is no notice after `/goal clear`.
  - `is_goal_control` reads one `_CONTROL_FIRST_WORDS` set (the bare verbs plus `wait`/`gate`). The gateway busy path in `gateway/run_busy.py` therefore dispatches `/goal pause …` / `/goal continue …` mid-run instead of rejecting them.
- `hermes_cli/commands.py`: `/goal` args_hint shows `-- <text>`, so autocomplete and `/help` list the escape.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_goal_dispatch.py`: two tests.
  - A parametrized trailing-words test. For each case it checks that the goal text survives, the expected status after the verb, the exact ignored-words hint, and that `is_goal_control` is True.
  - A `--` escape test. It covers escape + replace notice, no notice after clear, and `--dry-run …` kept literally.
- `website/docs/user-guide/features/goals.md`: a `/goal -- <text>` row in the command table.
- `contributors/emails/barnicskolaci@gmail.com`: contributor map entry.

## Credit
- @barnicskolaci reported and fixed this in #127367, the first and only PR for this bug. The `goal_command.py` core of that PR was rebuilt narrowly as 0d8565c736, with authorship kept.
- The contributor's other changes were intentionally left out, to keep this PR to the bug: criteria-line parsing (`parse_goal_input`/`_CRITERIA_ALIASES`), durable `/goal history` (`GoalState.superseded`), and refusing `clear`/`stop` with trailing words. Together they made up most of the +475-line PR.
- @kshitijk4poor added follow-up commits:
  - 44d99ccdcb: contributor map.
  - aec7c0f99c, 569634f5da, 34c527a29d: test teeth. They assert the ignored-words hint, `is_goal_control`, and that the verb actually ran, not just that the goal survived.
  - bb0217ff70: no "replaced" notice for a goal that was already cleared or done.
  - 1279d4f33b: `--` is an escape only when it is its own token.
  - 16a4ecf2ac: one `_CONTROL_FIRST_WORDS` set, with no behaviour change.
  - 0882ae0c7c and 2d509627ed: docs row and args_hint.

## Verification
- Tests ran on head 2d509627ed in an archive copy:
  - `test_goal_dispatch.py`, `tui_gateway/test_goal_command.py`, `gateway/test_goal_resume_restart.py` and `test_cli_goal_parked_resume.py`: 99 passed.
  - `test_commands.py` and `gateway/test_unknown_command.py`, which cover the args_hint change: 59 passed.
- Red on base: head `test_goal_dispatch.py` against base `goal_command.py` gives 5 failed / 69 passed. The failures are the 4 trailing-words params plus the `--` test.
- Probe (real import, base vs head):
  - Base: `resume last goal`, `continue` (paused) and `pause for now` all replace the goal. `is_goal_control('resume last goal')` is False, and `-- pause the cron` sets the goal to the literal `-- pause the cron`.
  - Head: the same three keep the goal and end resumed / resumed / paused, with the hint shown. `-- pause the cron` sets `pause the cron`, and `--dry-run the migration` and `---x` are kept literally. The replace notice shows after an active or paused goal but not after clear.
  - `is_goal_control` gives the same answers for `''`, `wait`, `gate add x`, `clear the deck` and `write docs` on base and head.
  - Bare `resume`, plain replace, `status` and `wait 5m` behave the same on base and head.
- Mutation (revert each commit's `goal_command.py`, then run `test_goal_dispatch.py`):
  - 0d8565c736 → 5 red.
  - bb0217ff70 → 1 red.
  - 1279d4f33b → 1 red.
  - 16a4ecf2ac (pure refactor) → green, as expected.
  - Removing the `(ignored …)` hint now fails 3 params. It survived before, which was a reviewer gap on #127367.
- `ruff` (incl. F401/F811/F821), `git diff --check` and the Windows footgun check are clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation). Round 1 raised 6 Low/Medium findings, which were folded in. Round 2 approved with no findings.

## Maintainer notes
- Behaviour change: goal text whose first word is `resume`/`continue`/`unpause`/`pause`/`status`/`show`/`unwait` now needs `/goal -- <text>`. For example, `/goal show me the flow then fix it` now shows the status, plus the ignored-words hint. The hint, docs and args_hint all point to `--`. Alternative if this is too strict: treat these words as commands only when a goal exists (or its state matches), and keep the old set-path otherwise.
- Behaviour change: on a busy gateway, `/goal pause …` / `/goal continue …` (with trailing words) now run mid-run instead of being rejected, because `is_goal_control` is wider.
- Plain `/goal <text>` over a live goal now prints a `was: <previous>` line.
- Left out of #127367 for a separate decision: criteria parsing, `/goal history`, and refusing `clear`/`stop` with trailing words.
- Possible textual overlap with #115243 (CLI inline `/goal` control dispatch). It has not been diffed against this branch.

raw.body:
The email gateway no longer accepts a forged lower `Authentication-Results` header or a subdomain of the pinned `authserv_id` as proof of sender identity, and it no longer downloads the full message body of mail it is about to reject.

## What happened
`_verify_sender_authentication` searched every `Authentication-Results` field for one whose authserv-id matched the pin, and it also accepted a subdomain of the pin. A sender could therefore add their own `mx.example.com; dmarc=pass` line below the receiving server's real stamp, or stamp from `evil.<authserv_id>`, and a spoofed `From:` would authenticate. Separately, `_fetch_new_messages` fetched the full RFC822 payload (decoding attachments too) for each unseen UID before `_sender_accepted` decided whether the sender was allowed. Our merged #125488 and @dborosev's c2f595d6af changed the warnings and the open-access policy in this area, but they did not change which header is trusted or when the body is fetched. On base 2b52acc2d8 a probe still authenticated the forged and subdomain stamps and RFC822-fetched UIDs 1, 2 and 3 when only UID 2 was allowed.

## Change
- `plugins/platforms/email/adapter.py`:
  - `_verify_sender_authentication` trusts only the topmost `Authentication-Results` field (the one the receiving server prepends). A set `authserv_id` must match it exactly. RFC 8601 CFWS comments are parsed through the existing `_ar_clauses`. Main's `_NO_AUTH_RESULTS_REASON` / `_UNTRUSTED_AUTHSERV_REASON` constants are kept, so the `_DROP_HINTS` lookup still resolves.
  - `_fetch_new_messages` first sends a bounded `BODY.PEEK[HEADER.FIELDS (...)]<0.N>` preflight for each unseen UID. It runs `_sender_accepted` on the event loop through `safe_schedule_threadsafe` (fails closed if the loop is closed) and requests RFC822 only for UIDs that pass. Rejected, automated and unparseable UIDs are STOREd `\Seen` through `_mark_uid_consumed` without fetching the body.
  - The `preauthorize` gate is a required parameter. The preflight field list is built from `_AUTOMATED_HEADERS`, so the IMAP command is byte-identical today and stays in sync with the registry. The new `_imap_payload` helper is shared by the header unwrap and the RFC822 unwrap.
  - `_message_metadata` is split out of the parse so the preflight and the full parse use the same sender verdict.
- `tests/gateway/test_email.py`:
  - `test_only_topmost_exact_authserv_id_is_trusted` replaces `test_injected_header_below_trusted_does_not_authenticate`. The subdomain/CFWS rows carry `dmarc=pass`, so only the exact pin can reject them.
  - New `test_rejected_sender_is_not_full_fetched_before_authorization`. It also calls the gate after its loop has closed.
  - Poll-loop mocks now answer the header-fetch spec and authorize their test senders. They no longer force open access. The mid-batch test keys on UID instead of fetch count.
- `tests/gateway/test_email_robustness.py`, `tests/gateway/test_email_imap_id_protocol.py`, `tests/gateway/test_poller_fd_lifecycle.py`: direct `_fetch_new_messages` calls pass `lambda _c: True`. The robustness mock gains a `BODY.PEEK` branch.
- `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/email.md`: documents that only the topmost header counts and that `authserv_id` must equal the exact host. If that host varies per message, leave `authserv_id` unset.

## Credit
- @Froraut (FroRaut) wrote the design and the fix in #129772: topmost-only exact pin, header-first fetch gate and the `_message_metadata` split. That PR conflicted with main and called `self._open_access()`, which main removed in c2f595d6af. It was therefore rebuilt by hand on current main as b4777c9255, with authorship kept (originally ebce1430b8). The rebuild keeps main's reason constants and runs the preflight gate always. @Froraut was the first to submit the combined fix (2026-10-01).
- Earlier partial overlaps, none of which gated the body fetch: #88560 by @JiuYue0820 (require a pin, 2026-08-17), #125405 by @dskwe (CFWS around the pin, 2026-09-27), #98611 by @kokhlo (default `authserv_id`).
- @kshitijk4poor added seven follow-up commits:
  - 8efab1e27e, 401b1dda65: docs for the topmost-only exact match, plus a note telling operators with per-message receiver hosts to unset `authserv_id`.
  - dad53053f0: gives the exact-pin test rows a passing verdict so the test has teeth.
  - 3a44d76f08: schedules the gate through `safe_schedule_threadsafe`. Before this, a closed loop raised and leaked a never-awaited coroutine.
  - 329224f6b7: makes the gate a required parameter, so no gateless RFC822 path is left.
  - d2f5d3679b: derives the preflight fields from `_AUTOMATED_HEADERS`, shares the payload unwrap, and collapses the three rejection branches.
  - d6e1201e4b: annotation-only cleanup.

## Verification
- Tests were run on the pre-rebase head 13b33e8518. The rebase onto current main is patch-identical (`git range-diff` shows `=` for all 8 commits).
  - `test_email.py`, `test_email_robustness.py`, `test_email_imap_id_protocol.py` and `test_poller_fd_lifecycle.py`: 57 passed, 23 subtests passed (base: 56 passed, 19 subtests).
  - `test_email_secret_scope.py`: 7 passed.
- Red on base: with base `adapter.py`, `test_only_topmost_exact_authserv_id_is_trusted` fails 3 subtests and `test_rejected_sender_is_not_full_fetched_before_authorization` fails. Both pass on head.
- Probe (real import, mocked IMAP):
  - Base: forged lower header gives `(True, dmarc=pass)`; subdomain id gives True; CFWS `mx.ex.com (r (a;b))` gives False; RFC822 fetched for `['1','2','3']` under allowlist and under open access.
  - Head: forged and subdomain give `(False, untrusted authserv-id)`; exact top id (any case) and CFWS give True; RFC822 fetched only for `['2']` under allowlist and under open access; only the owner is dispatched.
  - Open access with `require_authenticated_sender=false`: the dispatched set is identical on base and head. The always-on gate admits no fewer senders than base.
- Mutation:
  - Reverting the contributor commit: 11 red, including both invariant tests.
  - Unwiring the gate: 1 red.
  - Restoring subdomain alignment on the topmost field: red after dad53053f0 (it was toothless before that commit).
  - Reverting the `safe_schedule_threadsafe` commit: 1 red (closed-loop assert).
  - Reverting the annotation, required-parameter or registry/unwrap refactors: green, as expected for no-behaviour-change commits.
- `ruff` is clean on the touched files except a pre-existing F401 (`os`) in `adapter.py` that is also on base. `git diff --check` is clean. The Windows footgun scan found 0 issues.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation). Round 1 asked for the docs sentence and the required gate. Round 2 approved with no findings.

## Maintainer notes
- Behaviour change: the `authserv_id` pin is now matched **exactly** against the topmost `Authentication-Results` header. Main also accepted a subdomain of the pin (added in 85e084d60d). Operators who pinned a parent domain because their provider stamps from changing MX hosts (pin `example.net`, stamp `mx3.example.net`) will see every message dropped with the "check authserv_id" warning. They need to unset `authserv_id`; the docs now say so. The alternative is to keep subdomain alignment on the topmost header only. That still rejects forged lower fields but accepts `child.<authserv_id>` stamps. Which do you prefer?
- The preflight gate runs under open access too, because open access has also authenticated `From:` since c2f595d6af. The round-1 probe found no sender that base admitted and head now locks out.
- Rejected UIDs are explicitly STOREd `\Seen` without a body fetch. On base the non-PEEK RFC822 fetch marked them seen implicitly, so the visible result is the same. This overlaps the open BODY.PEEK PRs #122700 and #43018: whichever lands second has to reconcile the `\Seen` semantics.
- The real IMAP partial fetch `BODY.PEEK[HEADER.FIELDS (...)]<0.N>` is exercised through mocks only. That includes the assumption that the server returns fields in their original, topmost-first order.
- Efficiency (Low): each unseen UID costs one serial header-fetch round trip, plus a STORE when rejected. This is a background poll (default 15s) and each UID pays the cost once. A batched UID-set FETCH/STORE would reduce it but was left out of scope.
- `fut.result()` in the gate has no timeout. A loop stopping mid-poll could block the worker thread until exit. This is shutdown-only and was not probed.
- File sizes: `adapter.py` is about 1000 lines and `test_email.py` about 1420.
- After landing, close or rebase the open overlaps #88560, #125405 and #98611.

raw.body:
When one Telegram chat's turn runs long (a slow provider retry, a vision call, compaction), updates from other chats, topics and local `/commands` are now dispatched straight away. Messages within a single chat still arrive in order.

Refs #125098

## What happened
The adapter built the python-telegram-bot `Application` without calling `.concurrent_updates(...)`. PTB 22.x then falls back to `SimpleUpdateProcessor(max_concurrent_updates=1)`, and its update fetcher awaits each update's full handler chain before it pulls the next one. One slow handler therefore left other chats' updates queued until it finished. The ingress watchdog could see the stall, but nothing in config could change it. #125113 enabled plain PTB concurrency, which removes the stall. On its own, though, that lets a chat's second update finish before its first. The triage probe saw this on the #125113 head: chat 42 got `['second', 'first']`.

## Change
- `plugins/platforms/telegram/update_admission.py`:
  - New `PerChatUpdateProcessor(SimpleUpdateProcessor)`. Updates run concurrently across chats, up to the pool limit. Within one chat, each update waits on the previous update's tail future, so the chat runs FIFO. Updates with no `effective_chat` (inline queries) are not chained.
  - The predecessor wait uses `asyncio.shield`, so cancelling a waiter can't cancel the predecessor's future. A cancelled waiter passes its turn on only after its predecessor finishes, which keeps FIFO across a cancellation. `_tails` entries are removed once the chain drains.
  - New `build_update_processor(extra, name)`. It reads `platforms.telegram.extra.max_concurrent_updates` (default `DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_UPDATES = 32`) through `coerce_port`. Missing values, values below 1 and unparseable values log a warning and use 32.
- `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py`:
  - `builder.concurrent_updates(build_update_processor(...))` in `connect()`. The builder keeps this processor instance, so the connect-retry rebuild in `_initialize_app_with_retries` also uses it. No other `builder.build()` sites exist.
  - The stale "PTB dispatches sequentially" watchdog comment is updated. The watchdog budget is unchanged.
- `gateway/platforms/_shared.py`: `coerce_port` now also catches `OverflowError`. A YAML `.inf` value now returns the default instead of raising.
- `tests/plugins/test_telegram_update_admission.py`: the 2 tests from #125113 are kept and extended. No new test functions were added.
  - `test_connect_builds_concurrent_update_processor` now checks:
    - the processor type and its default limit;
    - the invalid-value and `float("inf")` fallback;
    - a cancel block: A is parked, B (waiting on A) is cancelled, C must start only after A ends.
  - `test_slow_update_does_not_block_other_chats` also queues a second chat-42 update behind the parked one and asserts the chat's text is `"hello\nsecond"`.
- `tests/gateway/test_telegram_conflict.py`, `test_telegram_polling_progress.py`, `test_gateway_platform_event_hook.py`: the fake and MagicMock builders now support `concurrent_updates()` (7 + 2 + 1 sites).
- `tests/gateway/conftest.py`: the telegram stub now provides a real `SimpleUpdateProcessor` class. With a MagicMock base, the subclass became a mock itself and failed on the second `connect()`.
- `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/telegram.md`: new "Concurrent update handling" section covering `max_concurrent_updates` and per-chat ordering.

## Credit
- @dskwe (Yuan Li) found that PTB's default processor processes updates one at a time. They wrote the fix and regression tests in #125113. Their commits 366ad0ec8b and 717163338c were cherry-picked with `-x` from 443c8b585a and 64cc98fb15, with authorship kept. The contributor map entry was already on main.
- @fortona-space submitted first, in #74652 (2026-07-30). That PR proposed the same builder change as an opt-in setting (`extra.concurrent_updates`, default off), and its warning on an invalid value was adopted here. They are credited with `Co-authored-by` on 85fc219332.
- @kshitijk4poor added follow-up commits:
  - 85fc219332: per-chat FIFO processor plus `build_update_processor`, with the bad-value warning.
  - d156636594: docs.
  - 46a44ec878: taught the existing connect-test doubles about `concurrent_updates()`, and the conftest stub fix.
  - 05f1afaee7: kept the per-chat chain intact when a waiting update is cancelled (shield plus deferred release).
  - dc4c44c7c7: built the processor on `SimpleUpdateProcessor` and dropped the no-op `initialize`/`shutdown`.
  - d78e191aa9: parsed the limit with `coerce_port` and made it tolerate `.inf`.
  - 97118b619a: pinned FIFO order after a cancelled waiter.

## Verification
- Test results (head, one process per line):
  - `tests/plugins/test_telegram_update_admission.py`: 94 passed (re-run on 97118b619a).
  - `test_telegram_conflict` + `test_telegram_polling_progress` + `test_gateway_platform_event_hook` + `test_telegram_closewait_limits`: 53 passed. Before the test-double fix, 14 of these were red on head and green on base.
  - `test_send_message_telegram_proxy` + `test_telegram_network_reconnect` + `test_telegram_forum_commands`: 39 passed.
  - `test_telegram_polling_progress_ptb`: 6 passed. `test_telegram_ingress_delivery_gap`: 5 passed. `test_telegram_callback_auth_fail_closed`: 4 passed.
- Red on base: with base production code, both kept tests fail (`1 > 1`; the fetcher never dequeues update 11). With the #125113 adapter alone (plain concurrency), the end-to-end test fails on same-chat reorder (`['43','42'] == ['43']`).
- Probe: two chats driven through the real PTB update fetcher, with the handler parked on chat 42.
  - Base: `concurrent_updates=1`; the other chat is not delivered while chat 42 is parked (`STALL_FIRES=True`).
  - Head: 32; the other chat is delivered during the park (`STALL_FIRES=False`); same-chat final is `['first\nsecond']` (`REORDER_FIRES=False`).
  - Other probe results:
    - An `.inf` limit gives 32 on head and no crash.
    - The cancel chain runs `start A, end A, start C, end C` and leaves `_tails` empty.
    - A handler exception still releases the chain.
- Mutation (semantic mutants; files restored and checked with cmp). Each one turns at least one kept test red:
  - revert the contributor builder change;
  - drop per-chat chaining;
  - drop the shield;
  - drop the deferred release;
  - wire a plain `SimpleUpdateProcessor(32)`;
  - drop `OverflowError` from `coerce_port`.

  The deferred-release mutant was green in review round 2. 97118b619a closes that gap, and I re-checked it on this head: 1 failed, `'start C' != 'end A'`.
- `ruff` plus F401/F811/F821 report no new findings. Two F401s in `adapter.py` already exist on main. `git diff --check` and the Windows footgun scan are clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation). Both reviewers approved round 2, and its one Low finding is fixed in 97118b619a.

## Maintainer notes
- Behaviour change: concurrency is on by default (32 in-flight updates, FIFO within a chat). The alternative is the #74652-style opt-in (default 1), which would leave default users with the stall. Set `max_concurrent_updates: 1` to restore serial dispatch.
- A same-chat update that is waiting on its predecessor holds one of the 32 pool slots. A burst of more than 32 updates from one chat can fill the pool and delay other chats until it drains. The delay is bounded and cannot deadlock, because chain order equals slot acquisition order.
- `coerce_port` has 9 other callers (api_server, a2a ×3, email, irc, photon, raft, teams). For them, the only change is that `±inf` now returns the default instead of raising `OverflowError` at startup. No tests reference `coerce_port`.
- `tests/gateway/conftest.py`: the telegram stub now provides a real `SimpleUpdateProcessor`. It applies only when PTB is not installed.
- #125098 is already marked closed (2026-09-27), but base had no concurrency setting, so this PR uses `Refs`.
- `adapter.py` is about 7.4k lines. This stack nets +5 there and puts the new class in `update_admission.py`.
- Overlap: #121791 (telegram edit flood) also touches `adapter.py`, but only the streaming path, so the changes don't conflict.

raw.body:
When an older session store holds duplicate titles, opening it no longer erases titles the user typed. User-owned duplicates are kept as `Title #2`, `Title #3`, and the unique title index is always restored.

Fixes #126764

## What happened
Stores created before the unique title index (60b6abefd9, 2026-03-08) can contain duplicate session titles. On open, `_ensure_unique_title_index` hits an `IntegrityError` and runs a repair that kept only the highest-`rowid` row of each duplicate group and NULLed the title on every other row. It never looked at `title_source`, so it cleared names the user typed and pre-provenance (NULL-source) titles, which `_title_rank` treats as user-owned. Because the survivor was chosen by `rowid`, a newer session with a lower rowid also lost its title. Reported by @aniruddhaadak80 in #126764.

## Change
- `hermes_state_schema.py` (`_ensure_unique_title_index`):
  - The repair loads each duplicate group and sorts it by (`_title_rank`, `started_at`, `rowid`), descending.
  - User-owned rows (user or NULL source) are never cleared. The oldest keeps the base title, and newer ones are renamed `Title #k` in `started_at` order. `resolve_session_by_title` prefers the highest `#N`, so it still opens the newest session, as it did before the repair.
  - A user title beats llm/derived ones. When a group has no user row, the newest highest-ranked auto title is kept. Lower-ranked auto titles are cleared. Each rename and clear is logged at WARNING.
  - The repair runs inside `SAVEPOINT title_repair`. If it fails part-way, it rolls back as a whole, so the store is not committed half-repaired without the index.
  - The index is created after the repair. The PR's skip-index fallback is not included.
- `hermes_state_titles.py`: the body of `get_next_title_in_lineage` moved to a module-level `next_title_in_lineage(conn, base)` so schema init can number renames on its own connection. The method delegates to it and behaves the same.
- `tests/hermes_state/test_hermes_state.py`:
  - Updated `test_duplicate_titles_are_repaired_without_deleting_sessions`: its NULL-source rows now end as `shared-title` (older) and `shared-title #2` (newer) instead of the older title being cleared, and resolving `shared-title` opens the newer session.
  - New `test_repair_keeps_highest_ranked_newest_title`, parametrized on `broken_rename`: a user title beats a newer llm one; between derived titles the newer `started_at` wins over a higher rowid; the index exists. The `[True]` case breaks the rename and checks that the store is rolled back untouched.
- `contributors/emails/66773372+Tranquil-Flow@users.noreply.github.com`: contributor map entry.

## Credit
- @Tranquil-Flow wrote #127743 (head 422819b130, 2026-09-29). It contributed the `started_at`-then-rowid survivor ordering, the logging before each clear, and the test seed helper. The PR treated NULL-source titles as auto and skipped the index whenever user titles collided, so it was rebuilt by hand on current main rather than cherry-picked. The rebuild is commit 1aae803449, authored by Tranquil-Flow.
- First submitter: Tranquil-Flow. An earlier PR, #127082, was closed by its own author and was not inspected.
- @kshitijk4poor added four commits:
  - 8cd3b3725a maps the contributor email.
  - ef267aae78 numbers user duplicates chronologically, so the oldest keeps the base title and title lookup still opens the newest session.
  - bcb564f495 wraps the repair in a SAVEPOINT so a failure rolls it back as a whole.
  - 5a072c7aa8 tidies the sort key and user rank, with no behaviour change.

## Verification
- Tests on head 5a072c7aa8, run in a clean archive copy:
  - `test_hermes_state.py -k "title|Title|lineage"`: 25 passed.
  - `test_canonical_title_guard.py`, `agent/test_title_generator.py` and `gateway/test_session_boundary_security_state.py`: 109 passed.
  - `cron/test_scheduler.py` and `tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py`: 764 passed.
  - Full `test_hermes_state.py`: head 13F/265P/13E and base 12F/265P/12E. Every other failure and error also occurs on base.
    - The extra failure, `TestInsightsToolCallIndex::test_index_created_on_existing_db`, and the extra error, `TestGatewayRoutingPkHeal::test_current_shape_left_untouched`, are not title tests. Both pass when run in isolation, and they match the load flake noted in the build report.
- Red on base: both repair tests fail with base `hermes_state_schema.py` and `hermes_state_titles.py`, and pass on head.
- Probe: duplicate-title stores seeded on base and head.
  - Base drops user titles. In T1 (user/user) and T2 (NULL/NULL), the older row's title becomes NULL. In T3 (older user, newer derived), the user title is dropped. In T4, the newer derived row with the lower rowid loses its title.
  - Head: T1/T2 `{older: Trip, newer: Trip #2}`. T3 keeps the user title and clears the derived one. T4 keeps the newer row. With an existing `Trip #2`, the rename skips to `Trip #3`. Three user rows become `Z`, `Z #2`, `Z #3`.
  - Neighbours are unchanged on base and head: llm/llm keeps the newer, a newer llm beats an older derived, and `get_next_title_in_lineage` returns the same results. The index is created in every case on both trees.
- Mutation (each commit's prod files reverted, 17 repair and lineage tests):
  - 1aae803449: 3 red.
  - ef267aae78: 3 red.
  - bcb564f495: 1 red (`[True]`).
  - 5a072c7aa8: 0 red, as expected for a commit that changes no behaviour.
- `ruff` is clean on touched code apart from a pre-existing F401 in `hermes_state_schema.py` that is also on base. `git diff --check` and the Windows footgun check are clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation). Round 1 found two issues, both fixed: user renames went to the older session, so `Title` lookup opened the old one; and a failed repair could commit half-done.

## Maintainer notes
- Behaviour change: user-owned duplicate titles are renamed to `Title #N` rather than cleared. The oldest keeps the base title, and newer ones are numbered by `started_at`. Users will see the renamed titles in session lists. Please confirm this is acceptable; it was chosen over skipping the index, which would rerun a failing `CREATE INDEX` and log a warning on every open.
- This only affects stores created before the unique index (60b6abefd9, 2026-03-08). Newer stores cannot hold duplicates, and the repair code does not run for them.
- The unique index is always created after the repair. The PR's branch that skipped it is not included.
- Unprobed edge: if an error during the repair makes SQLite roll back the whole outer transaction (some IOERR/NOMEM cases), `ROLLBACK TO title_repair` could raise "no such savepoint" outside the guard and abort the DB open. Only SQLITE_FULL was probed, and there the transaction survives.
- #108677 (opened 2026-09-12, excludes empty ghost sessions from title uniqueness) may touch the same index. Not diffed.

raw.body:
Stale-worktree reaping, both the startup pruner on `-w` launch and `hermes worktree prune`, no longer deletes a tree that got a tracked edit or a new unpushed commit after it was classified for removal.

Refs #128887

## What happened
Both reap paths classify candidate trees first and remove them later. The startup pruner (`_reap_prune_verdicts` in `worktree_ops.py`) and attended reclaim (`reclaim_worktrees` in `worktree_gc.py`) then ran `git worktree remove --force` on the stored verdict without checking the tree again. If a tree picked up uncommitted tracked changes or a commit not found upstream between classification and removal, it was deleted anyway, and attended reclaim also ran `branch -D` on its branch. On main, a probe shows both paths removing the tree (`tree_exists=False`, `removed scratch`) in the edit case and in the commit case.

## Change
- `hermes_cli/worktree_ops.py` (startup pruner):
  - Each reap candidate is re-classified right before removal. If the verdict changed, the tree is kept.
  - A plain `git worktree remove` replaces `--force`. It runs under `noninteractive_repo_git_env(<tree>)` with `stdin=DEVNULL`, and the tree is kept when env discovery fails.
  - `.worktreeinclude` symlinks (found by the existing `_include_symlink_paths`) are unlinked before the plain remove. Without this, include-only trees could never be reaped, which would undo #130595's startup behaviour.
  - Clean trees that contain submodules: if the plain remove refuses with "submodules" and a fresh `_worktree_is_dirty` check is False, the remove is retried once with `--force` under the same env.
  - `_classify_prune_candidates` takes optional `merge_cache=` / `get_remote_heads=` (new `_remote_heads_getter` memo). A sweep now loads and saves the merge cache once and runs `ls-remote` once, instead of once per revalidated tree.
- `hermes_cli/worktree_gc.py` (attended reclaim):
  - Each reap record is re-checked with `_classify_tree` right before removal. When it is kept, the message names what changed (`verdict` / `untracked files` / `branch`) and the new reason.
  - The plain remove and the submodule `--force` retry run through `_run(..., env=noninteractive_repo_git_env(record.path))`. That env is built from the tree's own config, so `config.worktree` filter drivers are neutralised. If discovery fails, the result is `kept NAME (git filter discovery failed)`.
  - The `--force` retry happens only when the record has no untracked files and a fresh `_dirty_split` is clean.
  - The merge cache is seeded from `_load_worktree_merge_cache()`. It is skipped on dry runs and saved once if it grew.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_worktree_reclaim_revalidation.py` (new): 2 parametrized tests.
  - Startup rows: edit, commit, include-symlink-only, submodule.
  - Attended rows: edit and commit, with an exact assertion on the kept message.
- `tests/security/test_gitspawn_config_injection.py`: the existing `test_index_reading_probes_and_kanban_gc_git_are_safe` is extended rather than duplicated. It now covers `reclaim_worktrees` on a malicious repo and a tree-scoped `config.worktree` clean filter with a stat-dirty file, on both paths.

## Credit
- @rudycelekli (Rudy Celekli) found the race and wrote the revalidation fix and tests in #128887. Commit c2c1ca975f (cherry-pick -x of 86fad9bd60) keeps his authorship. He was also the first submitter.
- @kshitijk4poor added 8 follow-up commits:
  - e227770893: unlink `.worktreeinclude` symlinks before the plain startup remove.
  - a44d922110: run the startup plain remove under the repo-safe git env. This closes the `core.fsmonitor` vector that dropping `--force` reopened.
  - 4f132c1237: fold the include-symlink case into the startup parametrize.
  - f6f9848224: `--force` retry for clean submodule trees, after a fresh clean check.
  - d955a739e4: share one merge cache and one `ls-remote` across revalidation.
  - 5f12ed46ed: name what changed when attended reclaim keeps a tree.
  - 9bcc8c6ec0: run the attended remove under the tree's own git env.
  - 0e73737042: load the reclaim merge cache only when it is used.

## Verification
- The branch was rebased onto main 7533bd2756 after the gates. Tests, probe and mutation ran on the pre-rebase head dcc4de23c9. The rebased diff against its merge-base is byte-identical to the gated diff (+205/-22, 4 files).
- Tests (clean archive copy):
  - `test_worktree_reclaim_revalidation.py`, `security/test_gitspawn_config_injection.py`, `test_worktree_gc.py` and `test_worktree_pushed_tier.py`: 74 passed, 0 failed.
  - `test_worktree_security.py`, `cron/test_worktree_maintenance_isolation.py` and `test_worktree.py`: 31 passed, 4 failed, 6 skipped. The 4 failures also fail on main (see notes).
- Red on base: with main's prod files, the 4 revalidation cases (startup/attended × edit/commit) fail. With the contributor commit alone, the include-symlink row fails because the tree is kept, and the submodule row fails too. Both pass at head.
- Probe (real imports, base vs head):
  - Edit/commit rows: removed on base. On head they are kept with `state changed since audit: verdict; now …` on both paths.
  - Clean tree and startup include-symlink tree: removed on both base and head.
  - Submodule trees: a clean one is removed on head. Untracked, submodule-commit and staged ones are kept on head.
  - fsmonitor, tree-scoped clean filter and `includeIf gitdir:**/worktrees/**`: did not fire on either path at head.
  - Perf, startup sweep of 3 pushed-tier trees: `{load:1, ls_remote:1}` at head, versus `{load:4, ls_remote:4}` before d955a739e4. Attended dry run: `load:0`.
- Mutation:
  - Disabling the contributor's revalidation turns rows red: startup `[commit]`, plus attended `[edit]` and `[commit]`. These were targeted mutations, because reverting the whole commit conflicts with the follow-ups.
  - Reverting e227770893 or f6f9848224 turns its row red.
  - Reverting a44d922110 or 9bcc8c6ec0 turns the security test red (`['fsmonitor']` / `['clean']`).
  - Reverting 5f12ed46ed turns the attended message assertion red.
  - d955a739e4 and 0e73737042 are perf-only: tests stay green, and the effect shows in the probe load/ls_remote counts.
- `ruff`, F401/F811/F821 and `git diff --check` are clean. The Windows footgun check reports 0 found.
