raw.body:
Telegram now sends a push notification for text-fallback exec-approval and clarify prompts in the default "important" notification mode. Before, these prompts arrived silently and could time out with no answer.

Fixes #132516

## What happened

In "important" mode, `TelegramAdapter._notification_kwargs` sends messages with `disable_notification=True` unless its metadata has `notify`. The exec-approval text fallback (`TurnRunner._approval_notify_sync`) sets only `is_approval_prompt`, and the clarify text fallback (`text_fallback_coro` → base `send_clarify`) sets neither key. So when a human-decision prompt went out as plain text instead of a button card, it arrived silently and the request could time out. Button cards (exec approval, clarify, slash-confirm, update prompt, model picker) go through `_send_prompt`, which does not apply that silencing, so they already pushed.

## Change

- `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py::_notification_kwargs`: in "important" mode, `is_approval_prompt` now forces a push, the same as `notify` (contributor commit). Ordinary progress sends stay silent.
- `gateway/run_turn_runner_clarify_delivery.py::text_fallback_coro`: the clarify text fallback is tagged `is_approval_prompt` and merged into a copy of the caller's metadata.
- `gateway/run_turn_runner.py`: changes only a comment. The approval text fallback still goes out as an interim send tagged `is_approval_prompt` and never `notify`.
- `tests/plugins/platforms/telegram/test_notification_kwargs.py`: an `important + is_approval_prompt` parametrize row, plus a clarify-fallback test that drives a real `TelegramAdapter.send` against a stub bot.
- `tests/gateway/test_exec_approval_timeout_notice.py`: checks that the approval card and the text fallback are sent without `notify`.

## Credit

@liuhao1024 reported #132516 and opened draft #132527. Their commit `e52a69591f` is cherry-picked with authorship kept (`-x 576fec2ab6`).

@ehz0ah's blocking review on #132527 set the design. A2A reads `notify` as the turn-final reply, and A2A uses the text fallback, so tagging an approval prompt with `notify` would complete the caller's task. Following that review, `d936e3249e` drops the draft's `notify` tag so both approval sends stay interim, and Telegram pushes based on `is_approval_prompt` instead.

Our other follow-ups:
- `3a0d98e476`: tags the clarify text fallback, which had the same silent-delivery bug.
- `b5b41a13d0`, `eb80e0162f`, `786024f3d0`: tests. The draft's runner-metadata tests were dropped because they only pinned behaviour that main already has.

## Verification

| Live probe: real `TelegramAdapter`, stub bot, mode `important`; value shown is `disable_notification` | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| exec-approval text fallback | `True` (silent) | push |
| clarify text fallback | `True` (silent) | push |
| exec-approval button card | push | push |
| progress message | `True` (silent) | `True` (silent) |
| final reply (`notify`) | push | push |
| `notify` on approval sends (A2A turn-final hazard) | absent | absent |

- Red on main: the `important + is_approval_prompt` row and `test_clarify_text_fallback_pushes_in_important_mode` both fail on main and pass here.
- Mutations:
  - Reverting the contributor's adapter change fails both tests above.
  - Reverting the clarify tag fails the clarify test.
  - Putting `notify` back on the approval sends fails 3 tests in `test_exec_approval_timeout_notice.py`: both card rows and the text-fallback row. Review round 1 found this guard was missing and it was added.
- Test runs:
  - `test_exec_approval_timeout_notice`, `test_decline_fallback_suppression`, `test_wecom` and Telegram `test_notification_kwargs`: 77 passed.
  - On the round-1 head, the neighbouring clarify, approval-redaction, prompt-decline and Telegram clarify-button suites also passed.
- ruff (F401/F811/F821) is clean on the touched files.

Independent review: in round 1, the correctness/scope pass approved (it confirmed @ehz0ah's concern is addressed). The tests/probe/mutation pass asked for the missing no-`notify` guard, which is now folded in. In round 2, the reuse, efficiency and quality passes approved, and the quality pass's one-line cleanup is folded in.

## Maintainer notes

- Behaviour change: Telegram users in "important" mode now get a push for text-fallback approval and clarify prompts. "all" mode is unchanged.
- Other readers of `is_approval_prompt`:
  - WeCom uses it for lane routing, but WeCom has no native `send_clarify`, so the clarify fallback never reaches it.
  - A2A has no native `send_clarify` either, and the approval path is the same as on main.
  - Relay has a native `send_clarify`, so the clarify fallback now carries the key over the relay wire. The approval fallback already did this on main.
- Not changed: the update-prompt text fallback (`_forward_update_prompt`). Telegram has a native `send_update_prompt`, so that fallback can't be reached on Telegram.
- Overlaps:
  - #131933 and #47004 touch `_notification_kwargs`.
  - #125961, #117842, #104385, #131442, #56575, #123443 and #124023 touch the approval text-fallback send in `_approval_notify_sync`.

raw.body:
`hermes sessions recover` no longer drops cron, `/bg`, room, API-server and ACP sessions, and a derived parent id no longer forces the whole sessions table onto positional mapping.

Salvages #132230

## What happened

The salvage classifier (`_is_session_id` in `hermes_cli/session_lost_and_found.py`) accepted only the `new_session_id` shape (`^\d{8}_\d{6}_`). Ids that other surfaces derive (`cron_{job}_{ts}`, `bg_…`, `room_{sha256[:32]}`, `api_…`, `api-…`, `run_…`, bare uuid4) failed that check. This caused two problems. First, `classify_lost_and_found_row` returned None for those rows, so recovery dropped them without a message. Second, a timestamp-id child whose `parent_session_id` was derived vetoed every candidate layout, so the whole sessions table fell back to positional guessing. @adurham measured this on a copy of a real 3,373-session store: 379 rows (11.2%) were dropped. Of those, 375 were cron, 1 was `/bg`, and 3 were non-session test artifacts that are still correctly rejected. After the fix, 3,370 of 3,373 rows are kept.

## Change

- `hermes_state_ids.py`: adds `SESSION_ID_RECOGNIZERS` and `is_known_session_id()` as the recognition side of the minting contract. There is one anchored pattern per persisted mint site:
  - From the contributor commit: `cron_`, CLI/gateway `bg_{HHMMSS}_{hex6}` and `room_`.
  - From our follow-up: TUI/Desktop `bg_{hex6}`, `api_{epoch}_{hex8}`, `api-{hex16}`, `run_{hex32}` and uuid4.
- `hermes_cli/session_lost_and_found.py`: `_is_session_id` delegates to `is_known_session_id`. This one predicate is used for the row classifier, the `id` sentinel and the `parent_session_id` text-shape rule. The `# noqa` re-export of `SESSION_ID_PATTERN` is dropped; nothing imported it.
- `tests/hermes_state/test_session_id_recognition_recovery.py` (new) has two tests:
  - a parametrized recognize/reject table covering the 9 minted shapes plus 34 near-misses;
  - an end-to-end test that writes a `lost_and_found` table with each shape as a parent id and runs the real `map_lost_and_found_rows`.
- `tests/hermes_state/test_hermes_state_ids.py`: drops the identity assertion that pinned the re-export.

## Credit

@adurham (Adam Durham), draft #132230: commit `42747686b9` is cherry-picked with authorship kept (`-x f82b7182f0`). It adds the recognizer plus the cron/bg/room shapes and has the real-store measurement above.

Our follow-ups:
- `e02464b32e`: covers the 5 shapes the draft missed. These came from a census of every site that hands an id to `SessionDB`.
- `870f55ae01`: drops the re-export.
- `799490fe49`: trims the tests to two invariants.
- `07019b04b4`: trims the source comments to the contract.
- `24c4664fd0`, `a3b206bd8a`, `0e4b4ccfbc`: the test reuses `session_recovery` column helpers, closes its `SessionDB` and drives the real salvage mapper.

## Verification

| Live probe: real `SessionDB` → `lost_and_found` → real `map_lost_and_found_rows`, 29 sessions | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| sessions mapped | 21 / 29 (8 dropped) | 29 / 29 |
| positional (no inferred layout) | 21 | 0 |
| layout inferred | no | yes |
| cron, bg ×2, room, `api_`, `api-`, `run_`, uuid4 | dropped | kept |
| 9 junk cells (model name, path, free text, `call_<hex16>`, `toolu_…`, bare hex32, `bg_xyz`, `cron_`, ISO timestamp) | rejected | rejected |

- `test_session_id_recognition_recovery.py`: 44 passed. On main, 10 fail: the 9 derived-id recognize rows and the layout test. The rewritten layout test fails on main with `29 == 38` (9 derived-id parents dropped). The 34 reject rows pass on both.
- Other suites:
  - `test_hermes_state_ids.py`: 3 passed.
  - `test_session_recovery.py`: 12 passed.
  - `test_session_recovery_lost_and_found.py`: 11 passed, 4 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is `test_unreadable_schema_without_cli_names_the_sqlite3_requirement`. It fails the same way on main because of the host `sqlite3` CLI; this stack does not touch that file.
- Mutations:
  - Reverting the contributor commit turns 10 tests red.
  - Reverting `e02464b32e` turns 6 red (the 5 added shape rows plus the layout test).
  - The re-export drop is a refactor, so reverting it turns none red, as expected.

Independent review approved in two rounds: correctness/tests/probe/mutation and false-positive passes in round one, then quality, reuse and efficiency passes in round two. Their five Low cleanups (comment trim, test fixture and test helpers) are folded in.

## Maintainer notes

- False positives: in the classifier, `cells[0]` is gated on this predicate only for sessions-shaped rows (nfield ≥ 14 plus a source-shaped `cells[1]`). Other wide tables lead with `deleg_{hex8}` or `sha256[:24]`, and every recognizer rejects both. `messages.session_id` is unchanged.
- Patterns follow each mint site's inline f-string. No shared mint helpers exist, so moving the f-strings into `hermes_state_ids` mint helpers (one source for shape and recognizer) is left as a follow-up; it would touch 8 files.
- Known limit: an arbitrary client-supplied id (`X-Hermes-Session-Id` / body id) used as `parent_session_id` can't be recognized by shape and still vetoes layout inference. This is pre-existing.
- Cold path only (`hermes sessions recover`). There are 8 precompiled patterns, and the timestamp shape is tried first.
- `agent/transports/codex.py` `_CRON_SESSION_ID_RE` and `hermes_cli/web_routers/cron.py` `_CRON_RUN_SESSION_ID` are looser, capture the job id and serve other purposes. They are deliberately not consolidated.
- No open PR overlaps `_is_session_id`, `hermes_state_ids` or `session_lost_and_found`.

raw.body:
A turn that outgrows the protected tail now gets split and compacted even when its opening request (for example a long `/goal` prompt) is over 1,400 characters, so the session no longer grows until it hits the provider context limit.

Refs #131412 (same `middle_window_tokens=0` / `no_progress` symptom with a different trigger; that issue is already closed)

## What happened

The oversized-active-turn split added in #80449 only ran when the authored opening request was at most `_ACTIVE_TASK_MAX_CHARS` (1,400 chars). During a `/goal` run the continuation prompt is the only real user turn and is often longer than that, so the whole run counted as one active turn and was kept verbatim in the tail. Every automatic pass then found an empty compress window, recorded `no_progress` and armed the structural backoff. Manual `/compress` hit the same empty window. #130506 fixed the reply-quote form of this; the character cap still blocked any request that was long on its own. The cap isn't needed for correctness. The request row is already bounded by the token soft ceiling, and after the split `_reappend_inflight_user_task` restates the request verbatim via `_restated_request_text`, which has no cap.

## Change

- `agent/context_compressor.py::_find_tail_cut_by_tokens`: drop the `_ACTIVE_TASK_MAX_CHARS` conjunct from the split gate. The token soft-ceiling check on the request row, `_is_text_only_content`, the real-tool-group requirement and the over-ceiling anchored-region check are unchanged (contributor commit).
- `agent/context_compressor.py::_latest_user_task_snapshot`: the cap and reply-quote elision stay as they are (this is a historical hint only). Comment updated so it no longer says the split gate measures authored text.
- `tests/agent/test_split_turn_compaction.py`: adds `test_a_long_active_request_still_splits_and_survives_verbatim` (a ~3.3k-char request under the soft ceiling must split, shrink the transcript, keep tool pairs intact and appear exactly once after the summary end marker). Two older docstrings now describe the current gate. The new test reuses `_oversized_active_turn`, and a test-local `_actionable_user_text` helper replaces three copies of the same join.
- Net size: `context_compressor.py` +5/−5 (unchanged at 5,970 lines); test file +37/−15, now 16 tests (one new).

## Credit

@0xble (Brian Le) wrote the fix and the test in draft #132487. Cherry-picked as `62e68e2de5` with authorship kept (`-x 0081611ff1`, no conflicts); `brian@brianle.xyz` was already in `contributors/emails`, so no map commit was needed. Our follow-ups are review cleanups only: `e9d6c35b5a` (stale snapshot comment), `487ae756dc` (test docstrings), `be17ea6fb5` (test helper reuse). None of them change behaviour.

## Verification

| Live probe — real `compress()`, summary stubbed | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| 5,000-char request, `tail_token_budget=2000` | `cut=3 split=False`, 84→84 (stall) | `cut=52 split=True`, 84→58, request verbatim once, tool pairs intact |
| 1,300-char request | splits, 84→58 | identical |
| 3 cycles, 5,000-char request | 84→84, 144→142, 202→56 with the request **dropped** | 84→58, 118→56, 116→56, one verbatim copy each cycle |
| 40k / 50k-char request, 200k ctx, 10k budget (15k ceiling), 3 cycles | 244→244, 484→482, request lost on cycle 3 | 244→214, 454→212, 452→212; one copy each cycle; ~21.4k tokens after compression vs 100k threshold (no compress loop) |
| 60k-char request (~15.6k tokens, over the ceiling) | pinned, no split | byte-identical to main (token gate still pins it) |
| 5k text + `image_url` request | no split | identical (`_is_text_only_content` still gates it) |

- Kept test: red on main (`assert 2 > 3` on the cut) and green here. In the fold2 rerun, reverting `62e68e2de5`'s prod change alone gives 1 failed, 15 passed.
- Mutation: reverting the one behaviour commit turns the kept test red.
- Tests: 16 compression test files plus `tests/gateway/test_compress_plugin_engine`, 422 passed, 0 failed, run at the contributor commit. On HEAD, `test_split_turn_compaction` + `test_context_compressor` pass 318 of 318 (the follow-ups touch comments and tests only).
- ruff, `git diff --check` and the Windows footgun scan are clean.

Independent review: round 1 correctness/tests/probe and edge-case passes approved, with one stale-comment nit (folded). Round 2 reuse, quality and efficiency passes approved, with three Low test cleanups (folded).

## Maintainer notes

- Behaviour change: requests longer than 1,400 chars that fit under the token soft ceiling now split like short ones. Requests of 1,400 chars or less behave as before. Requests over the ceiling and non-text requests stay pinned.
- The restated request after the marker is no longer char-capped. It is bounded by the soft ceiling, so the tail after compression is at most about the ceiling plus that one row.
- The gate now runs the `any(tool_calls)` scan and `_walk_tail_budget` for long requests that the cap used to short-circuit. This is once per compression, on a cold path.
- Pre-existing and not changed here: with `protect_first_n=3`, cycle 0 holds 2 copies of the request on both main and this branch.
- Overlaps: #83331, #107159 (touches the `_find_tail_cut_by_tokens` region) and #60662 also edit `context_compressor.py`. None of them edit this gate line.

## Summary

Supersedes #132025: a salvage that keeps @helix4u's commit unchanged.

With `terminal.backend: ssh`, Hermes runs its terminal and file tools on a remote machine. After a TUI session is resumed, every terminal and file call can fail with `cd: <path>: No such file or directory` (exit 126), because Hermes sends the remote a directory that only exists on the machine running Hermes.

That directory is the one the TUI gateway process was started in. It is saved as the session's cwd on the first prompt, and resume adopts a saved ssh cwd as the remote workspace. In the Docker image the launch command decides the path: `docker exec -it <container> hermes --tui` saves `/opt/hermes`, adding `-w /opt/data` saves `/opt/data`, and `-w /opt/data/home` saves `/opt/data/home`. With a direct install outside Docker, the directory `hermes --tui` was started from fails the same way.

![Sequence: a new session saves the gateway's launch dir; on main, resume sends cd /opt/hermes to the remote and fails with exit 126; with this PR nothing is saved and resume starts in terminal.cwd or ~](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee57c967-d94d-4011-ae73-f0c57989852a)

#132025 by @helix4u fixes the `/opt/data/home` case at the terminal tool. Its commit is included here with authorship kept. This PR adds the fix where the path is first saved, plus recovery for sessions saved before it.

## Expected behaviour

With the ssh backend:

| Situation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| New session | starts in remote `terminal.cwd`, else `~` | same |
| Resumed session, no directory picked | `cd <Hermes launch dir>`, exit 126 | starts where a new session would |
| Resumed session saved by an older version (`/opt/hermes`, `/opt/data`, `/opt/data/home`) | exit 126 | starts where a new session would |
| Session with a directory picked explicitly, including remote `~/proj` | used on resume | same, unless its path is inside the host's Hermes home or install tree (see limitation below) |
| Context files (AGENTS.md and similar) | loaded from the launch dir | same |

Local and docker backends: no change.

## Changes

- `fix(tools): coerce restored SSH session working directories` (@helix4u, from #132025, unchanged).
- `fix(tui): never persist an ssh session's launch directory as its workspace`. The launch directory stays in memory, so context files load as before, but the gateway no longer saves it as the ssh workspace on first prompt, resume or branch. Branching a session saved by an older version can still copy its already-stored path; resume ignores that inherited path when it is inside the host's Hermes home or install tree. Desktop sessions already follow this rule (`_persisted_session_cwd`).
- `fix(tui): don't resume an ssh session into Hermes's own host tree`. Rows saved before this change still hold the launch directory. On resume, a saved ssh cwd that is an absolute path inside the Hermes home (including the root that holds named profiles) or the install tree is ignored and the session starts in the default (`terminal.cwd`, else `~`). Both places that read the saved cwd on resume (`session.resume` and `_hydrate_session_cwd`) apply the same rule.

Nothing from #132025 was dropped.

## How this avoids breaking other setups

- Every new check runs only when `_cwd_is_remote()` is true, which means `terminal.backend: ssh`. Local and docker backends never reach the new code. The table below also runs the local backend through the same image, launch commands and upgrade path and compares it with main.
- A saved path is only ignored if it is absolute and inside `HERMES_HOME` or the install dir, i.e. a directory Hermes created for itself. Any other saved path is used exactly as before. Nothing is probed on the remote and no existing row is rewritten.
- Known limitation: whether a cwd was picked explicitly is not stored, so this check goes by path alone. A remote directory picked explicitly whose absolute path is also inside the host's Hermes home or install tree is not restored on resume; the session starts in the default instead.
- Upgrading in place was run on the same data volume: sessions created on the stock image resume correctly after switching to this branch.

## Desktop

The desktop app talks to the same backend, and no desktop code changes. Sessions created in the desktop already never saved their launch directory, so they are unaffected. With an ssh backend two things look different: a TUI-started session in the sidebar is labelled "Home" instead of the launch directory's name, because its row no longer has a cwd; and resuming an older session whose saved path is inside Hermes's directories shows the remote default in the status bar's workspace item instead of that path. Both follow from the backend data (`session-row.tsx`, `use-statusbar-items.tsx`); the desktop app itself was not driven.

The TUI banner still shows the launch directory, as on main, since context files load from there.

## Before / after

Real `hermes --tui` in the stock image with an ssh backend, started with `docker exec -it <container> hermes --tui`: a new session runs `pwd`, `/exit`, then `hermes --tui --continue` and `pwd` again.

| main | #132025 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| ![main: after resume, pwd fails with cd: /opt/hermes: No such file or directory, exit 126](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aeb4d2c9-9550-4093-b349-a3311640148b) | ![#132025: after resume, pwd still fails with cd: /opt/hermes: No such file or directory, exit 126](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6c67034f-ea27-4e46-bd5c-daf95f9be49d) | ![this PR: after resume, pwd returns /home/parallels, exit 0](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2eb283a1-3d4c-43cb-9fe8-f19b5f17a37e) |

## Test plan

- New `tests/tui_gateway/test_ssh_session_cwd_persistence.py` (21 tests, including `session.resume` through the RPC and a named profile); each fix-dependent test fails without its fix. Targeted `tests/tui_gateway/`, terminal, file-operation and runtime-cwd suites show no failures beyond those on main in the same environment.
- End to end: stock `nousresearch/hermes-agent:main` image with this branch's changed files mounted over it, ssh backend to an Ubuntu 24.04 VM, stub model. Each case runs terminal and `write_file` calls in a new session, restarts the gateway, resumes, and runs them again.

| Setup | main | #132025 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| ssh, `docker exec` default (`/opt/hermes`) | exit 126 | exit 126 | works |
| ssh, `-w /opt/data` | exit 126 | exit 126 | works |
| ssh, `-w /opt/data/home` | exit 126 | works | works |
| ssh, sessions created on the stock image, resumed after upgrading in place (all three) | | | works |
| ssh, named profile, sessions created on the stock image, resumed after upgrading in place (all three) | | | works |
| ssh, explicit remote directory | works | works | same |
| ssh, `terminal.cwd` set | works | works | same |
| direct install on macOS (no Docker), ssh, no directory picked | exit 126 | exit 126 | works |
| local backend, all three launch commands: new, resumed, upgraded in place | baseline | | identical to main: saved cwd, `pwd`, write locations, context files |

The ssh rows run with the image's `HERMES_WRITE_SAFE_ROOT=/opt/data` unset. With it set, remote file writes are refused on every version, which is tracked separately in #132620.

Credit: @helix4u (primary for the terminal-tool fix).

The Discord invite link from `hermes gateway setup` and the Discord docs no longer request **Use External Emojis**. Hermes never uses that permission, and no permission list in the docs names it (#73657).

raw.body:
`hermes profile export` no longer archives Docker, Azure, GitHub CLI or gcloud credential stores found in a profile, and `@file:~/.config/gcloud/...` no longer expands the gcloud token into context.

Follow-up to #132201

## What happened

#132201 stopped profile export shipping `.ssh`, `.aws`, `.gnupg`, `.kube` and `.envrc`, but the other credential dirs that the file tools already write-deny (`.docker`, `.azure`, `.config/gh`, `.config/gcloud`) still shipped. A skill dir copied from a home could carry `.docker/config.json` (registry auth), `.azure/accessTokens.json`, `.config/gh/hosts.yml` (GitHub token) or `.config/gcloud/` (ADC, `credentials.db`). Default and named exports archived them as-is, and binary DBs skip the redact pass. The cause was three hand-copied lists of the same dirs: the write denylist in `agent/file_safety.py`, the export filter in `hermes_cli/profiles.py`, and the `@file` refusal list in `agent/context_references.py`. The export filter also matched only top-level names, so nested `.config/<tool>` stores could never match. The `@file` list was also missing `.config/gcloud`. The gateway feeds untrusted remote text through `@file` expansion, so that was the same leak class. The user decided to exclude `.docker`, `.azure` and `.config/gh` too. `.config/gcloud` is included because `file_safety` already write-denies it.

## Change

- `agent/file_safety.py`: new `HOME_CREDENTIAL_DIRS` holds the 8 home-relative credential dirs. `build_write_denied_prefixes` derives from it and returns the same set as before (only the order changed; the only caller does a `startswith` check over every prefix, so order doesn't matter).
- `hermes_cli/profiles.py`: `_OS_CREDENTIAL_STORES = (*HOME_CREDENTIAL_DIRS, ".envrc")`, so `PROFILE_CREDENTIAL_PATHS` and the export filter pick up the four new stores. New `_export_credential_entries()` matches stores on trailing path components and is used by both the default and named export ignores. `.config/gh` and `.config/gcloud` are dropped at any depth. Other `.config/*` content (`.config/other`, `.config/ghost`, `.config/gh.bak`) still ships.
- `agent/context_references.py`: the `@file` credential-dir block reads `HOME_CREDENTIAL_DIRS` directly. The hand-copied `_SENSITIVE_HOME_DIRS` is removed, which adds `.config/gcloud`.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_profile_export_credentials.py`: the existing `test_named_export_ships_no_credential_store_or_copy_of_one` gains nested-store rows and a benign `.config/other/settings.json` that must stay in both export kinds. `_DOT_DIRS` is now derived from `HOME_CREDENTIAL_DIRS`.
- `tests/agent/test_context_references.py`: the canonical-denylist test gains a `.config/gcloud` ADC row.
- `website/docs/user-guide/profile-distributions.md` (2 lists) and the zh-Hans mirror list the new stores.

No new test functions.

## Credit

@keiranhaax (Keiran Haax) was the first to propose excluding `.docker`, `.azure`, `.config/gh` and `.config/gcloud` from exports, in #35601. That PR is an open 6-commit rewrite of the export security boundary and only touches `home/`, which main already drops whole, so no commits were cherry-picked. Credit is a `Co-authored-by: Keiran Haax` trailer on the export commit `dd1f57eeff` (and on `755b920de7`). #35601 stays open.

Our commits: `dd1f57eeff` (shared list + export filter), `755b920de7` (`@file` block from the shared list), `1d303af506` (drop the alias), `433cda7209` (test constant derived from the shared list).

## Verification

| Live probe: named export seeded at root, `skills/s`, `skills/a/b/c` | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| credential files in archive | 12 (`.azure`, `.config/gcloud`, `.config/gh`, `.docker` × 3 locations) | none |
| benign neighbours dropped (`.config/other`, `.config/ghost`, `.config/gh.bak`, bare `gh/`, `gcloud/`, `docker/`) | none | none |
| `profile_path_is_private(.config/gh)` / `(.docker)` | False / False | True / True |
| `@file:~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json` | expands the secret, no warning | refused with the credential warning |

- Red on main: the extended export test fails (it leaks `.azure`, `.config/gcloud`, `.config/gh` and `.docker` in both default and named exports). The `.config/gcloud` row in the context-refs test fails (`'GCLOUD-SECRET' not in ...`). Both are green here.
- Mutations: reverting the export commit turns the export test red. Reverting only the component matcher (back to set intersection, constants kept) also turns it red on the nested `.config/gh` and `.config/gcloud` rows.
- `test_profile_export_credentials`, `agent/test_context_references`, `agent/test_file_safety`, `test_profiles`: 159 passed, 6 skipped. `test_profile_distribution`: 55 passed, 1 skipped. `tools/test_write_deny`: 10 passed. Context-ref and gateway expansion tests: 47 passed.

Independent review: round 1 approved (tests/probe/mutation, correctness). Round 2 approved (correctness, efficiency, quality, reuse). The two Low cleanups from round 2 (alias, hand-copied test constant) are folded in.

## Maintainer notes

- Behaviour change: distribution installs now also refuse writing `.docker`, `.azure`, `.config/gh` and `.config/gcloud` at the profile root, through `PROFILE_CREDENTIAL_PATHS`. Root `.config` becomes a store ancestor: it is merged per entry instead of replaced whole, and a payload file named `.config` over an existing `.config/` dir is refused. `platforms` already works this way.
- Remaining gap, separate surface: the `read_file` and terminal read deny-list (`get_read_block_error`) still doesn't cover `.config/gcloud`, `.docker` or `.azure`.
- Not consolidated on purpose: `gateway/platforms/base.py` `_MEDIA_DELIVERY_DENIED_HOME_SUBPATHS` is broader (all of `.config`, `.gcloud`, `Library/Keychains`). Folding it into the shared list would narrow it.
- Pre-existing, unchanged: the export matcher is case-sensitive, while `profile_path_is_private` ignores case.
- Import cost: `hermes_cli/profiles.py` now imports `agent.file_safety` at module top. That adds about 2–4 ms to a standalone `import hermes_cli.profiles` and 0 ms on the CLI path (`hermes_logging` already loads it). `file_safety` imports only stdlib at top level, so there is no cycle.
- Overlaps: #35601, #129891, #129654, #129909, #116098 and #130525 touch the export/credential-store code. #32262, #83787 and #128173 touch `build_write_denied_prefixes` / the `file_safety` denylist.

raw.body:
Email sender auth no longer accepts a forged `dmarc=pass` written by the sender: with sender auth on, Hermes now requires an `authserv_id` pin and drops mail until one is set.

Refs #103093 (fixes its fail-closed-without-pin row only; the other rows are already fixed on main)

## Behaviour change

- **Who is affected:** deployments that have sender authentication on and no pin set. Sender auth is on by default, including with open access (`EMAIL_ALLOW_ALL_USERS` / `GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS`).
- **What happens:** after upgrading, these deployments drop every message that needs an authenticated `From:`, allowlisted senders included, until the operator does one of these:
  - sets `EMAIL_AUTHSERV_ID` (or `platforms.email.authserv_id`), or
  - opts out with `platforms.email.require_authenticated_sender: false` (or `EMAIL_TRUST_FROM_HEADER=true`).
- **What the operator sees:** each unpinned account logs one WARNING when it connects: `[Email] <address>: authserv-id is not configured; refusing to trust Authentication-Results. Set EMAIL_AUTHSERV_ID (or platforms.email.authserv_id) to the receiving MTA's exact authserv-id, or set platforms.email.require_authenticated_sender: false (or EMAIL_TRUST_FROM_HEADER=true) to accept the risk.` The warning also fires when an account's first connect fails and the reconnect watcher brings it up later.
- **How to find the value:** open a message your server delivered (raw source / "show original"). Copy the token before the first `;` of the **topmost** `Authentication-Results` header. For Gmail that is `mx.google.com`. If the token changes between messages, it is a per-relay hostname. Configure the MTA to stamp a stable authserv-id (for example `AuthservID` in OpenDKIM / OpenDMARC) and pin that.
- **Unchanged:** pinned deployments, and deployments that opted out, behave exactly as before.

## What happened

`_verify_sender_authentication` trusts only the topmost `Authentication-Results` header. When no pin is set, main accepted that header whatever its authserv-id. A self-hosted MTA that doesn't stamp its own results leaves the sender's header on top. So on such a server, a sender-written `attacker.self; dmarc=pass header.from=allowed.example` authenticated a forged `From:`. On top of that, main's docs told operators to "leave `authserv_id` unset" when the host varies.

## Change

- `plugins/platforms/email/adapter.py`:
  - `_verify_sender_authentication`: when there is no pin it returns `(False, "authserv-id is not configured; …")` (contributor commit). `authserv_id` is now a required, pre-normalised keyword argument.
  - `connect()`: warns once per account address after the IMAP and SMTP probes succeed. Accounts already warned are tracked in a class-level `_missing_pin_warned` set, so multiplexed accounts each warn, and an account that comes up through reconnect still warns.
  - The opt-out wording is shared between the existing no-header hint and the new pin hint (`_OPT_OUT_HINT`). The rendered text is unchanged.
- `plugins/platforms/email/plugin.yaml`: adds `EMAIL_AUTHSERV_ID` to `optional_env`, which feeds the setup prompt (contributor commit).
- Docs (`email.md` and the env-var reference, English and zh-Hans):
  - The pin is now documented as required, with how to find the value, what to do if it varies, and the explicit opt-out.
  - The "leave `authserv_id` unset" sentence is removed.
  - Adds a troubleshooting row for `authserv-id is not configured`.
- `tests/gateway/test_email.py`: two existing tests extended (details under Verification), no new test functions.

## Credit

- @JiuYue0820 (#88560): commit `02cf3130e8` cherry-picked with authorship kept (`-x e013fda3fa`; authored as MoonsvnLyn <287222957+FirmaSpring@…>).
  - Mapped to JiuYue0820 in `d0d7c02e8a`.
  - The adapter conflict was resolved in main's favour: main's topmost-only check and exact pin are kept. From #88560 we kept the fail-closed-without-pin guard, the `plugin.yaml` entry and the docs edits.
  - #88560's test hunks and its `1634a2ffa7` were not picked, because main already covers topmost/exact-pin and dispatch.
- Reviewers on #88560:
  - @andrexibiza: trust-boundary review and consolidation plan.
  - @StevenQinDev: rebase audit on #101282 and the #103093 tracking issue.
  - @FirmaSpring.
- Our follow-ups:
  - `9f65c7190d`, `23440f74ae`, `2b48c72f71`: the missing-pin warning, moved to `connect()` and deduped per account address.
  - `68b14a3d04`, `03df882019`: docs and comment.
  - `837cef678d`: test rows pinned to a fixed literal.
  - `ee5a788fa2`: shared hint text.
  - `033d298505`: required pin argument.

## Verification

| Live probe — adapter imported from the tree under test | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| no pin, forged topmost `attacker.self; dmarc=pass` | `(True, dmarc=pass)`, accepted | `(False, authserv-id is not configured…)` |
| allowlist / open access with no pin, 2 messages | accepted [True, True] | refused [False, False] |
| connect warnings: one@ fails then reconnects ×2; two@; pinned; opted out | none | one@: 0 / 1 / 0; two@: 1; pinned: 0; opted out: 0 |
| pinned exact; pinned case + CFWS; forged-lower under pin | True; True; False | unchanged |
| `require_authenticated_sender: false` / `EMAIL_TRUST_FROM_HEADER=true` | accepted [True, True], no warnings | unchanged |

- Extended tests:
  - `test_only_topmost_exact_authserv_id_is_trusted`: adds the unpinned forged row. Red on main, which returns `(True, 'dmarc=pass')`.
  - `test_only_a_missing_auth_results_header_warns_with_the_opt_out_hint`: adds real `connect()` calls (failed first connect then reconnect, a second account, pinned, opted out). Red on the pre-fold heads.
  - Helper rows now stamp a fixed `mx.ourserver.com` instead of pinning to their own topmost id, so the pin compare is actually tested.
- Mutations that turn tests red:
  - reverting the contributor commit;
  - removing only the no-pin guard;
  - dropping the per-address dedupe, the `_authserv_id` check or the `_require_authenticated_sender` check in `connect()`.
- Tests: `test_email`, `test_email_secret_scope`, `test_adapter_authz_secret_scope`, `test_email_robustness`: 83 passed (+23 subtests). `test_email_imap_id_protocol`: 3 passed.
- Ruff clean apart from an unused `import os` that already exists on main.

Independent review: three correctness rounds.
- r1 found that a process-wide warn-once flag silenced a second mailbox, and that pairing-only deployments got no WARNING.
- r2 found that an account failing its first connect never warned.
- Both are fixed and r3 approved.
- The reuse, quality and efficiency passes approved, and their cleanups are folded in.

## Maintainer notes

- **Policy call:** the alternative is to keep main's "unpinned = trust the topmost header" and only document it. This PR takes fail-closed, so it needs a release-note line (see Behaviour change).
- **Per-message logging is unchanged from main:** when a pin is missing, a listed sender's drop logs WARNING with the greppable reason, and strangers log at debug. The fix text is only in the connect line.
- **`_missing_pin_warned` is never cleared:** a same-process sequence on one address of unpinned, then pinned, then unpinned again won't re-warn. This is a cold edge case.
- **Overlaps:** these open PRs call or touch `_verify_sender_authentication`: #56608, #110209, #94617, #40016, #68606. These touch `_sender_accepted`: #128118, #113192, #28702, #105450, #110777. Their tests that call the verifier without a pin will need one, since `authserv_id` is now a required keyword.

raw.body:
The documented Linux install (`curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash`) works again on hosts without `libatomic1`. Before this change it ended in `✗ pm install failed` and no `hermes` command.

Fixes #124926. Salvages #124961 by @JoaoMarcos44. The contributor's commit is cherry-picked, so authorship is kept. Supersedes #124929 by @z23, who filed first with a different design.

**Root cause:** official Node 26 Linux builds link `libatomic.so.1`. Stock Ubuntu 24.04 server images don't ship it, and neither do minimal Debian or RHEL/Alma hosts. `install.sh` used to preinstall it: 8f8351aff3 by @liuhao1024, salvaged as #99481 on 2026-08-31. The unified-installer rewrite 27df3b8847 (#102765, 2026-09-24) moved Node staging into PM and dropped that step. Nothing replaced it, so PM's Node smoke probe exits 127 and the install aborts. `hermes update` on AlmaLinux/RHEL fails the same way (#124926).

## Changes

- `pm/libatomic.py`, `pm/packages.py`, `pm/package.py`, `pm/install.py` (from #124961): PM gets an install-time repair hook. When a freshly staged Node fails its probe on `libatomic.so.1`, PM installs the distro package and probes once more:
  - Debian/Ubuntu `libatomic1`, dnf/yum `libatomic`, zypper `libatomic1`, pacman `gcc-libs`, apk `libatomic`.
  - Root runs the install directly. Everyone else uses `sudo -n` with stdin closed, so it never prompts while PM holds its install lock.
  - `verify()` stays read-only, so `hermes pm doctor` and status checks never install anything.
- Follow-ups on top:
  - `install.sh`: on a glibc host without the library, a non-root user and an attached terminal, the installer runs `sudo -v` once during prerequisites. It refreshes that ticket non-interactively right before PM runs. Without this, PM's `sudo -n` can never succeed for a user whose sudo needs a password.
  - The repair runs at most once per process. Before, it re-ran under the lock for every root that depends on Node, which was two attempts in one failing install.
  - On minimal images with empty package lists, apt runs `apt-get update` once and retries the install.
  - The remedy goes into `InstallError`'s remedy field. Before, the error ended with a second, wrong fix: "retry, or run `hermes pm doctor`".
  - `platform.freedesktop_os_release()` replaces a hand-written os-release parser.

Flaked on a one-YAML catalog PR (run 37198702518): `assert ['interrupted', 'interrupted'] == ['completed', 'interrupted']`.

**Cause:** the test stopped the parent once the completed sibling's `close()` fired. `close()` runs inside the child's worker (`run_child`) *before* its future resolves, so the parent's interrupt branch in `_run_children_parallel` could still see that future pending and fabricate an `interrupted` entry for a child that had finished.

**Fix:** wait until the parent has actually collected the sibling (`_report_child_done` fired from the poll loop), then interrupt. Test-only; dispatch behaviour unchanged.

Validation: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_finite_delegation_outcomes.py` passes (11/11).

## What does this PR do?

The batch (multi-question) clarify panel renders into an unsized Window. On a short terminal the layout clips the panel's bottom rows, and those rows are the active question's choices. Up/down only move the choice cursor and there is no scroll binding, so the options can't be seen. On main, a 24-row terminal with three long questions draws a 41-line panel into 18 available rows.

When the panel body is taller than the rows left under the shared `_PANEL_RESERVED_BELOW` reserve, the panel now shows the slice of rows that ends with the active question's choices. The slice moves up when needed so the selected choice is always on screen. A panel that already fits is unchanged.

This is a narrower version of #132821 by @xxxigm. It uses the same row budget and keeps that PR's regression test (cherry-picked with authorship), but slices the existing rows instead of adding a separate fitting helper and restructuring the row builder (+22/−3 in production instead of +132/−17). It also keeps the selected choice on screen when the choices alone overflow; #132821 clips those from the top, so a selected choice further down stays hidden.

## Related Issue

No GitHub issue. Reported by Ben Eng in the Hermes Discord support thread "clarifications with long text in…": with long questions in a batch clarify, the TUI cut off the active question's choices, which made choosing impossible, and there is no key to scroll to them. #126970 lists this height gap as out of scope. Supersedes #132821.

The same report also points out the narrow (~67-column) panel. That is #126970 / #126992 and is not changed here. The two PRs touch the same three lines that build `preview_rows` and `rows`, so whichever merges second needs a small conflict resolution: keep #126992's width lines and this PR's `rows, focus = ...` unpacking. With both merged locally, the height, width and batch clarify tests pass (19/19), and a panel matching the report's screenshot fits in 19 rows with every choice and Other visible.

When the active question and its choices don't fit, the top of the active question text and the earlier questions scroll out of view rather than being collapsed. ## Problem

After context compression (rotation mode), the Desktop app only shows the child continuation session's messages — the parent session's pre-compression transcript becomes invisible. Reported by @Kombuchameister on #51058.

## Root Cause

The Desktop app runs two requests concurrently when resuming a session:

1. **REST prefetch** — `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages` → `db.get_messages(sid)`
2. **Gateway resume** — `session.resume` RPC → `get_messages_as_conversation(sid, include_ancestors=True)`

The REST prefetch only loads the **child continuation's** messages (no ancestor stitching). When it arrives first and renders, the resume's complete lineage (which includes parent messages) is skipped because `localSnapshot.length > 0`.

## Fix (3 files)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `hermes_state.py` | Add `include_ancestors` param to `get_messages()`. When True, uses `_session_lineage_root_to_tip()` to query messages across the full parent→child chain — same mechanism as `get_messages_as_conversation(include_ancestors=True)`. |
| `hermes_cli/web_server.py` | Pass `include_ancestors=True` in `/api/sessions/{id}/messages` REST endpoint. |
| `gateway/platforms/api_server.py` | Pass `include_ancestors=True` in `_conversation_history_for_session` (same bug class, OpenAI-compatible API server). |

No TypeScript changes — the REST response shape is unchanged, just with more rows (parent messages prepended).

## Why `ORDER BY id` still works

AUTOINCREMENT id is globally monotonic across sessions — parent messages were inserted before child messages, so ordering remains correct.

## Testing

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/test_hermes_state.py -q` — 325 passed ✓
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server.py -q` — 341 passed ✓
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_api_server.py -q` — 193 passed ✓
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_compression_rotation_state.py -q` — 5 passed ✓

Total: 864 tests, 0 failures.

Closes #51058 (parent transcript visibility after compression)

## Fix: Disable the web-haptics audio fallback on desktop to prevent CoreAudio stutter

Fixes #68894

### Problem

On macOS, when music is playing and the user presses Enter to submit a prompt in Hermes Desktop, there is a consistent fraction-of-a-second interruption to audio playback (Spotify, Apple Music, Bluetooth streams, etc.).

### Root cause

The `web-haptics` library is initialized with `debug: true` in `HapticsProvider`. `debug` is the library's desktop audio fallback: on platforms where `navigator.vibrate` exists (Chromium exposes it as a no-op on desktop), it plays synthesized click sounds through an `AudioContext` on every haptic trigger — `triggerHaptic('submit')` fires on every prompt submission, and `triggerHaptic('streamStart')` on first token. This briefly seizes the audio device, interrupting other streams.

The existing warmup effect (`new AudioContext().close()` in `requestIdleCallback`) was ineffective — closing the context immediately releases CoreAudio, so the real one still had to re-acquire the device from scratch — and it constructed an `AudioContext` of its own.

### Fix

Desktop has no vibration motor, so haptic output is inert here. Narrow the change to the audio path only: omit the `debug` option (default `false`), which removes the `AudioContext`/CoreAudio interaction entirely, and drop the ineffective idle warmup. The provider and the persisted titlebar mute/unmute control keep working unchanged.

### Changes

- `apps/desktop/src/components/haptics-provider.tsx`: stop passing `debug: true` to `useWebHaptics`, remove the AudioContext warmup effect.
- `apps/desktop/src/components/haptics-provider.test.tsx` + `haptics-provider.registration.test.tsx`: provider-level regression tests — no `AudioContext` is constructed on trigger or mount, a live trigger is registered while unmuted (`null` while muted), haptics are suppressed while muted. All four tests are mutation-checked (re-adding `debug: true`, permanent null registration, the warmup effect, or a mute-ignoring provider each fails the corresponding test).

### Notes

- All `triggerHaptic()` call sites are unaffected — they call through `@/lib/haptics`, which already guards on `registeredTrigger` being non-null and on the muted flag.

Fixes model switching on sessions running under `dashboard.turn_isolation`. Today a model pick on an isolated session looks successful (picker updates, `config.set` returns ok) but every subsequent request keeps the old model — the live agent runs in the compute-host child, and the switch machinery only operates on the serving process. Found while canarying turn isolation on a real deployment; full analysis in the linked issue.

The fix keeps the existing pending-switch design and extends it across the process boundary:

- Compute-host sessions **always defer** (busy or idle) instead of the idle path building and switching a second, unused agent inside the serving process.
- `_compute_host_turn_frame` carries `pending_model_switch` to the child — **copied, not popped**, so the fail-open in-process path still has it if host dispatch fails.
- The child adopts the stash in `_ensure_server_session` (both branches); its turn thread then applies it through the existing `_apply_pending_model_switch`, where the real agent is present.
- The server clears the stash only after a **successful** isolated turn (kept on `turn.error` for the fail-open path).

## Related Issue

Fixes #79509

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `tui_gateway/server.py` — defer on `_compute_host_active` in `config.set model`; include `pending_model_switch` in the compute-host turn frame; clear the stash in `_on_compute_host_turn_done` on success only.
- `tui_gateway/compute_host.py` — adopt the forwarded pending switch in `_ensure_server_session` (existing-session and new-session branches).
- `tests/test_tui_gateway_server.py` — three regression tests: idle defer (asserts no server-side agent build), frame handoff (copied-not-popped), clear-on-success / keep-on-error.

## Testing

- `tests/test_tui_gateway_server.py` — 520 passed on this branch (`python -m pytest`, macOS arm64, Python 3.13).
- Verified live on a remote-mode deployment: with isolation on, an idle-session picker switch previously left requests on the old model; after this change the next turn runs on the picked model and the stash clears.

items.body:
## Problem

Hermes Desktop creates each SSH tunnel through a background ControlMaster with `ControlPersist=300`, then installs the local listener with `ssh -O forward`. A static mux forward does not keep the master's persist timer refreshed. When a remote profile has no multiplexed SSH client for five minutes, OpenSSH can exit the otherwise healthy master and remove the local listener while Desktop retains its `http://127.0.0.1:{port}` descriptor. The next renderer request fails with `ECONNREFUSED`, even though the remote `hermes serve --isolated` backend is still healthy.

This is distinct from the half-open network path in #74998 / #75044 and complements the remote pool-reaper fix in #75398: in this case OpenSSH intentionally expires a healthy idle control master.

## Fix

- Track active mux forward specs on `SshConnection`.
- While at least one forward is owned, issue an unref'd `-O check` every 60 seconds through the existing `isAlive()` path. This refreshes the finite ControlPersist timer.
- Stop the refresh after the final forward is cancelled or the connection closes.
- Leave no-mux/Windows behavior unchanged.

The finite 300-second persist timeout remains in place, so an orphaned master still cleans itself up after a Desktop crash.

## Verification

A real OpenSSH probe with `ControlPersist=5` remained alive for more than 12 seconds when `-O check` ran every four seconds, then exited cleanly on `-O exit`.

- `npx vitest run --project electron electron/ssh-connection.test.ts` — 59 passed
- `npx vitest run --project electron` — 939 passed, 2 skipped
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json --noEmit`
- `npx eslint electron/ssh-connection.ts electron/ssh-connection.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

items.body:
## Problem

Closes #79833 — with Inline Embeds set to "Always", an X/Twitter card that auto-loads in one session keeps painting over the whole UI after switching to another session, the Artifacts view, or Settings. It also survives a renderer reload (Ctrl+R).

## Root cause

Keep-alive tabs stay **mounted** when inactive and are hidden with `visibility: hidden` (not `display: none`) so their layout box — and with it the scroll position — survives a tab round-trip (`pane-shell/tree/renderer/tree-group.tsx`). But CSS `visibility` is inherited-*and-overridable*: Twitter's embed script renders its card into a sandbox element with an **inline** `visibility: visible` (`platform.twitter.com/widgets.js`), which CSS then lets paint through the hidden pane over the active view. It returned after Ctrl+R because the tab layout and the embed mode ("always") are persisted, so the embed re-auto-loads.

Plain-iframe embeds (YouTube, Spotify, maps) do not set inline `visibility`, which is why only the X/Twitter card was affected.

## Fix

One pane-level CSS rule — every descendant of a `[data-pane-hidden]` pane follows the pane's visibility (`visibility: inherit !important`). An author `!important` rule beats the widget's inline non-important style. The fix does not require additional unmounting: the embed stays mounted and renders exactly as before when its tab is active (no re-fetch, no flicker), and scroll preservation is untouched.

## Verification

- New "hidden pane painting contract" tests in `pane-visibility.test.ts` validate the rule against the **live stylesheet** (extracted by an anchored regex, so removal/rename fails loudly): a `visibility: visible` descendant inside a hidden pane computes `hidden`; an element outside is unaffected.
- Real-Chromium (Electron 40) probes: with the rule, a widget-style card inside a hidden pane computes `hidden`; without the rule it computes `visible` (bug mechanism reproduced); cards outside hidden panes stay `visible`.
- Full desktop UI suite: 4525 tests passed (480 files, 2 skipped); `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Notes

- **Open question:** a widget that set `visibility: visible` on elements *inside* a shadow root (rather than on the host, which is what Twitter's script does) would not be covered — CSS cannot select into shadow roots. No known provider (Twitter/Instagram/TikTok, all checked) does this; if one appears, the follow-up is gating widget embeds on pane visibility in `social-embed.tsx`.
- **Open question:** the rule cannot win against a widget that set inline `visibility: visible !important`; today's widget scripts use plain inline styles.

items.body:
## Summary

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/80621 — Desktop can blank the rendered transcript when a completed assistant response contains a `MEDIA:` directive or plain absolute paths.

Root cause: `stripGeneratedImageEchoes` (apps/desktop/src/lib/generated-images.ts) stripped **every** markdown image and `#media:` link (the internal link form produced when a `MEDIA:` directive is parsed for display) from a final message whenever the same turn's parts contained a completed `image_generate` tool result. A `MEDIA:` directive for a file *other than* the generated one was silently deleted, and a message whose only content was such a directive rendered completely blank (the emptied text part was dropped by `dedupeGeneratedImageEchoesInParts`, and `toChatMessages` drops a message with no surviving parts). The messages were intact in `state.db` — the loss was purely Desktop-side, matching the report.

## Changes

**`apps/desktop/src/lib/generated-images.ts`** — scope the echo-strip to the actual generated source:

- Markdown images are removed only when their `src` matches a known generated source, with a lookahead so a longer path (e.g. `/tmp/a.png.bak`) is not eaten by a prefix source (`/tmp/a.png`).
- `#media:` links (derived from `MEDIA:` directives) are removed only when their encoded path matches a known source, anchored to the closing paren (case-insensitive so lowercase hex like `%2f` is caught too).
- Bare-path stripping no longer matches inside markdown link destinations, so `[label](/tmp/a.png)` is not corrupted into `[label]()`.
- A `MEDIA:` directive pointing at a different file always survives, as does surrounding prose.

**`apps/desktop/src/lib/markdown-blocks.ts`** — defensive fallback: if the markdown lexer throws on a pathological message, return the raw text as a single block (rendered through the same safe markdown pipeline as every other message — no HTML evaluation) instead of letting the exception unwind through `MessageRenderBoundary` to the root boundary, which blanks the entire transcript. Partial cache entries are dropped so a retry isn't served stale data.

## Tests

- `stripGeneratedImageEchoes` keeps a `#media:` link for a file that is not a generated source; keeps a different-file `MEDIA:` directive while stripping the same-file echo; keeps backticked absolute paths inert; does not over-match a longer path; does not corrupt a markdown link destination.
- `dedupeGeneratedImageEchoesInParts` keeps the MEDIA attachment link and does not drop a message whose only content was a MEDIA link to a different file.
- `parseMarkdownIntoBlocksCached` falls back to the raw text block when the lexer throws.

Verification:
- `vitest run` (full desktop UI suite): **480 files / 4531 tests passed, 0 failures**
- `tsc -p . --noEmit` clean; eslint clean on changed files

## Notes

The reporter's case B (backticked absolute paths alone, no `MEDIA:` directive) passes through the lib layer untouched on current main; the defensive parser fallback covers the reported whole-transcript blanking class without masking real bugs (non-transient errors still reach the root boundary — only lexer failures degrade to a visible raw-text block).

## Checklist

- [x] Read Contributing Guide + Desktop AGENTS.md
- [x] Conventional commit message
- [x] Tests for the regression
- [x] Typecheck + lint clean
- [x] Full desktop test suite green

items.body: ## Description In Hermes Desktop, sending a message that combines an image or file attachment with a slash command (e.g. `/moa `) silently degraded: the command was **not executed**, the user received **no indication**, and the command text was delivered to the model as ordinary prose processed by the current base model. I traced the root cause to two layers: 1. Desktop skipped slash command dispatch whenever `attachments.length > 0` across all three submission paths (`use-prompt-actions/index.ts`, `use-composer-submit.ts`, `session-tile-actions.ts`). Instead of notifying the user of the conflict, the draft silently fell through to `submitPromptText`. 2. Gateway `MessageEvent.is_command()` only checked `lstrip().startswith("/")`, which failed when Desktop prepended attachment reference tags like `@image:` or `@file:` to the payload. ### Fix Details - **Desktop UI**: Restructured the slash command check in `use-prompt-actions/index.ts`, `use-composer-submit.ts`, and `session-tile-actions.ts`. When a slash command is submitted alongside attachments, I now trigger an explicit warning toast (`slashCommandIgnoredTitle` / `slashCommandIgnoredBody`) rather than silently routing to plain prompt submission. - **i18n**: Added missing translation strings for the warning toast in `types.ts`, `en.ts`, `ar.ts`, `ja.ts`, `zh.ts`, and `zh-hant.ts`. - **Gateway**: Added a private `_command_text()` helper in `gateway/platforms/base.py` that strips Desktop attachment-ref tags (`@image:`, `@file:`, `@url:`) before command matching, and updated `is_command()`, `get_command()`, and `get_command_args()` to use it consistently. - **Tests**: Added unit test coverage in `tests/gateway/test_platform_base.py` verifying `is_command()` and `get_command()` with various attachment-ref prefixes (including Windows paths containing spaces). Fixes #81798 Related: #79765 --- ## Environment Info - **OS**: Windows 11 - **Python**: 3.11.15 - **Hermes Version**: v0.20.0 (`main` branch) --- ## How to Reproduce & Verify ### 1. Minimal Reproducer (Python / Gateway) I created a reproducer script that verifies the Gateway payload parsing: ```python from gateway.platforms.base import MessageEvent # Desktop payload with image attachment ref prepended before slash command payload = "@image:C:\\Users\\User\\Pictures\\test.png\n\n/moa Explain this" event = MessageEvent(text=payload) assert event.is_command() is True assert event.get_command() == "moa" assert event.get_command_args() == "Explain this" print("OK") ``` ### 2. Manual Verification (Hermes Desktop UI) 1. Launch Hermes Desktop (`npm run dev` in `apps/desktop`). 2. Attach an image using the paperclip icon. 3. Type `/moa Explain this image` into the composer and press Enter. 4. **Expected**: A warning toast appears (`Command not sent — Slash commands cannot be combined with attachments...`) and the prompt is not silently sent to the base model. 5. **Control**: Remove the attachment and type `/moa Explain this image` — the MoA command executes as expected. ### 3. Automated Tests ```bash python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_platform_base.py::TestMessageEventIsCommand tests/gateway/test_platform_base.py::TestMessageEventGetCommand -v ``` All 10 tests pass clean. ### Screenshots - **With attachment**: command is blocked and warning toast is displayed. - **Without attachment (control)**: slash command executes normally. --- ## What platforms tested - **Windows 11** (primary Desktop target — Windows path handling, C:\\Users\\... refs) - **Linux** (gateway unit tests via pytest; path-agnostic cases) - macOS: not directly tested — changes are path-agnostic string handling, no platform-specific APIs introduced ## Known limitations (tracked as follow-up) - **Inline palette refs vs gateway**: Desktop now detects commands after any ref kind (folder/line/terminal) and blocks the attachment+command combo. The gateway-side ref strip still covers the wire kinds that can actually reach it from Desktop (image/file/url). Aligning the gateway regex with every palette kind, and reconciling the "Desktop blocks vs gateway executes" semantics for mixed-version clients, is a separate design change — intentionally kept out of this PR to keep the fix narrow. - **Ref and command on the same line** (command eaten by the ref pattern): not produced by the real composer format (buildContextText always joins refs and text with newlines), so it is out of scope here.

## What does this PR do?

Fixes the floating pet sitting in `idle` while a **background** session runs an agent task (#84282). It only reacted to the foreground session.

## Root cause

`setPetActivity({ toolRunning })` / `{ reasoning }` are pushed to `$petActivity` exclusively from the per-session message-stream hook (`use-message-stream/gateway-event.ts`), which is mounted for the **rendered** session only. Background sessions have no mounted stream handler, so their tool-start/tool-end/reasoning events never reach `$petActivity` — the pet has no idea they are working.

The `waiting` pose already gets this right: `awaitingInput` is driven in `use-pet-bridge.ts` from the store-level `$attentionSessionIds` subscription, which is always live regardless of which session is on screen.

## Fix

Add the twin of that subscription for busy state. `use-pet-bridge` now also subscribes to `$workingSessionIds` — the existing `computed` over every session's authoritative `busy` flag (the same store `$attentionSessionIds` lives beside) — and mirrors it into `$petActivity.busy`. `derivePetState` already maps `busy → run`, so:

- any working session (foreground **or** background) drives the `run` pose;
- the foreground stream's finer `toolRunning` / `reasoning` signals still refine run-vs-review for the visible session (they gate on `live`, which the aggregate `busy` now satisfies cross-session);
- when every session is at rest the flag clears and the pet returns to `idle`.

No new atom needed — `$workingSessionIds` already exists and is what the sidebar running indicators read, so the pet now agrees with them.

## Tests

Extracted `syncPetBusyFromSessions()` as a pure function (mirroring `rehydrateLiveSessionStatuses`) and unit-tested the cross-session behavior in `use-pet-bridge.test.ts`:

- a background-only working session → `$petActivity.busy === true` and `$petState === 'run'`;
- one session finishing while another still runs → stays `run`;
- all sessions at rest → `busy` clears and `$petState === 'idle'`.

Renderer eslint clean on the touched files; `pet.test.ts` and `use-background-sync.test.ts` still green. (The two `frimousse`/`bippy` `tsc` errors present locally are pre-existing missing-dep noise in unrelated files, installed in CI — none in the touched file.)

Fixes #84282

## Summary

Fixes #83319 (Desktop HUD mode: clarify choice dialog appears, disappears, turn hangs — family E desktop member in the stall triage #84047).

The dialog-vanish and the hang are the same bug: the desktop stream pipeline's turn-end (`message.complete`) and `error` handlers clear the parked clarify dialog **unconditionally**. The Python side stays blocked on `clarify.respond` until the user answers or the server's clarify timeout expires. In HUD mode (separate overlay window with its own stream lifecycle) a spurious turn-end/error event arrives while the bridge is still blocked → dialog wiped → user has nothing to answer → turn hangs until timeout or /stop.

## Root cause

- `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event.ts` (~L764, ~L1299): `clearClarifyRequest(undefined, sessionId)` on turn-end/error with no check of whether the server bridge is still waiting.
- The normal flow needs a clear *somewhere* (the `tool.complete` handler only drops the `needsInput` flag), so the fix is a deadline-aware guard, not a removal.

## Changes

- **Server** (`tui_gateway/server.py`, `_block`): the blocking-request payload now advertises the bridge deadline — `timeout_seconds` when finite, **omitted** when the server waits forever (`clarify_timeout <= 0`). Additive field; older renderers ignore unknown fields (same contract as the `multi_select` hint).
- **Client store** (`apps/desktop/src/store/clarify.ts`): `ClarifyRequest` gains `receivedAt` + `timeoutSeconds`; new pure guard `clarifyStillBlocking(request, now)` — true while a finite server deadline hasn't elapsed, true forever for wait-forever requests, false when nothing is parked.
- **Client stream handler**: both turn-end and error clear sites now call `clearClarifyRequest` only when `!clarifyStillBlocking(...)`.

## Semantics

| case | behavior |
|---|---|
| user answered, turn ends | request already cleared by the tool's answer path — no-op, unchanged |
| server timed out (finite), turn-end arrives late | deadline elapsed → dialog dropped (stale) |
| spurious turn-end while bridge still blocked | dialog **survives**; user can answer; `respond` succeeds (server still waiting) |
| wait-forever request (`clarify_timeout <= 0`) | dialog survives turn-end/error; only an explicit answer/skip clears it |
| /stop interrupt | dialog survives; `respond` fails gracefully; the #84560 interrupt path unblocks the turn |

## Validation

- Desktop: `npx vitest run src/store/clarify.test.ts src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream` → **21 + 79 passed, 0 failed** (5 new guard tests: no-request false, pre-deadline true, post-deadline false, wait-forever true, parked survival).
- Python: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/test_tui_gateway_server.py` → **553 passed, 0 failed** (2 new payload tests: finite → `timeout_seconds` emitted; `None` → omitted). One unrelated flaky (`test_compute_host_turn_end_updates_metadata_mirror`) passes on re-run and is untouched by this diff.
- Red proof: the guard tests fail against the pre-change clear semantics (unconditional clear wipes a still-blocked request).

Credit to @cycocyco for the HUD-mode reproduction; composes with #84560 (interrupt unblocking) — that PR lets /stop out of the wedge, this one stops the wedge from forming.

Fixes #88282.

**Root cause:** A Desktop profile with a per-profile URL-remote/cloud gateway override sent its own routing label as the `?profile=` scope on every scoped REST call (e.g. `/api/cron/jobs?profile=gris`). On a remote backend whose actual profiles are named differently (e.g. `main-gris`), every scoped request 404'd — cron lists, bot chats, and session listings. The managed-SSH path already handled this via a `remoteProfile` mapping fed into `translateSelfProfileQuery`/backendProfile, but URL-remote overrides had no equivalent field and dropped any such value on read/save.

**Fix:** Mirror the SSH mapping for URL-remote/cloud per-profile overrides, entirely in the routing/config layer:
- `connection-config.ts`: `normalizeRemoteProfileName()` validates a remote profile name (same rules as SSH), and `profileRemoteOverride()` now preserves it on the resolved override.
- `main.ts`: `profileRouteOptions()` feeds the URL override's `remoteProfile` into `backendProfile`, so the existing `translateSelfProfileQuery` path rewrites the self-profile scope (`?profile=gris` → `?profile=main-gris`); `sanitizeConnectionProfiles`, `buildRemoteBlock`, and `coerceDesktopConnectionConfig` now round-trip the field so it survives saves. The upstream #88296 routing additions are preserved.
- `global.d.ts`: `DesktopConnectionConfigInput.remoteProfile?` documents the save-payload field.
- Tests: 5 new `connection-config` tests covering preservation, invalid/reserved rejection, and the translate-vs-fallback path.

The per-profile settings UI was removed upstream (commit 6170f844c), so there is no Settings field for this; the mapping is configured via the connection config file's `profiles.<name>.remoteProfile`, consistent with how per-profile overrides are stored.

**Verification:** electron vitest `connection-config` (109 pass incl. 5 new), ui settings + boot-failure tests (24 pass), `tsc -p .` and `tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json` clean, eslint + prettier clean on touched files.

## Summary

items.body:
## Summary

React 19 only ships `act` in its development build. The jsdom suites in `web/` drive components through `act()`, so when vitest inherits an ambient `NODE_ENV=production` — the shell that launched the app, a packaged CI step, an editor terminal — `React.act` resolves to `undefined` and every `createRoot` test in the project dies with `TypeError: act is not a function`.

I hit this on Windows while trying to run the dashboard suite before touching `ChatPage`: the whole file was red and it looked like I had broken something, when the only difference was the `NODE_ENV` my terminal happened to export.

## Root cause

`web/vitest.config.ts` never pins the worker's environment, so `NODE_ENV` leaks in from whatever launched vitest. `@testing-library`-style `act()` resolution is `React.act ?? reactDomTestUtils.act`, and `react-dom/test-utils.act` forwards to `React.act` as well — under `production` both are `undefined`, so there is no fallback. The failure is entirely environmental: the same commit passes or fails depending on the shell.

This is the same failure class as #77409, one workspace over. That issue (and @derekm's #77421) covers `apps/desktop/vitest.config.ts`; `web/vitest.config.ts` has no equivalent guard, so the dashboard project is still exposed. I deliberately left `apps/desktop` alone to avoid overlapping with that PR.

## Changes

- `web/vitest.config.ts`: set `test.env.NODE_ENV = "development"` for the project, plus a comment recording *why* it has to be pinned so it does not get "simplified" away later.

Only the vitest worker is affected — app runtime, `vite build`, and the production bundle all keep their own `NODE_ENV`.

## Test plan

Both runs below are `web/`, on this branch, with the ambient production env that triggers the bug:

- [x] `NODE_ENV=production npm run check` → typecheck clean, **36 files / 275 tests passed**, lint 0 errors (26 pre-existing warnings, unchanged)
- [x] Reverted just this diff and re-ran the same command → **3 files / 43 tests fail** with `act is not a function`, confirming the config is what fixes it
- [x] `npm run check` with no `NODE_ENV` set at all → 275 passed (no regression for the normal case)

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Related Issue

Relates to #77409 — same root cause, different workspace. Complements #77421 rather than replacing it.

## What does this PR do?

`useStatusbarContributions` (`apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/panes.tsx`) rebuilds a fresh `render()` closure for every render-item on every call. `ContribRender` mounts that closure via `createElement(render)`, so a new closure identity reads as a different component **type** — React tears down and remounts the whole contributed subtree on any unrelated statusbar re-render, dropping any state it held (e.g. an open Dialog).

The fix wraps the mapping in `useMemo` keyed on `items`, which `useContributions` already returns as a stable reference (`registry.getArea` caches per area) until the area actually mutates — confirmed by reading `registry.ts`, not assumed.

## Important caveat — please read before reviewing

This repo enables the React Compiler for files matching the JSX/react-import filter in `vite.config.ts`, and `panes.tsx` matches it. **With the compiler on (the shipped build config), it already auto-memoizes this exact pattern**, so I could not reproduce user-visible state loss against a compiler-enabled build. I verified this by toggling the compiler filter off/on against both the pre-fix and fixed source, running the same test each time:

| | compiler ON (current config) | compiler OFF |
|---|---|---|
| pre-fix source | test **passes** (no repro) | test **fails** (remounts, state lost) |
| fixed source | test passes | test passes |

So this isn't "fixes a live bug users are hitting right now" — it's "stops a correctness property (contribution state survives unrelated re-renders) from silently depending on the compiler's memoization heuristics staying happy for this function forever." If the compiler ever bails out here (a Rules-of-React violation added elsewhere in the function later, a filter change, compiler disabled for debugging), the state-loss bug returns with nothing to catch it. The added test guards that regardless of compiler state.

I'm flagging this plainly rather than claiming more than I can back up. Happy to close if maintainers consider compiler-masked issues out of scope — but the underlying fragility seemed worth a small, targeted fix either way, and the root-cause analysis in #91603 is correct about the mechanism even if its current real-world impact is uncertain.

## Related Issue

Closes #91603

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/panes.tsx`: memoize `useStatusbarContributions`'s return value on `items`
- `apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/panes.test.tsx`: new regression test mirroring the real consumer (`statusbar-controls.tsx`'s `<ContribRender render={item.render} />` pattern exactly, not a simplified stand-in) — a stateful contribution opens a panel, an unrelated host re-render fires, panel state must survive

## What does this PR do?

Stops the Hermes Desktop app from spamming a console stack trace for every missing-file preview read at startup.

**Problem:** When the desktop app restores persisted state (preview tabs, pane shares, session transcripts), the renderer re-probes every file reference. References to files that no longer exist — deleted, moved, or cleared from `/tmp` on reboot — caused the `hermes:readFileText` / `hermes:readFileDataUrl` / `hermes:readFileDataUrlForAttach` IPC handlers to **reject** with `ENOENT`. Electron logs every rejected `ipcMain.handle` handler with a full stack trace, so a single stale `/tmp` reference produced 12+ noisy error blocks per launch — even though the renderer already handled the rejection gracefully as "preview unavailable".

**Fix (whole bug class, not just the symptom):**
- **Main process** (`electron/hardening.ts`, `electron/main.ts`): added `isMissingFileError()` (classifies `ENOENT`/`ENOTDIR`). All three preview-read handlers now return a structured `{ ok: false, error, message, path }` result instead of rejecting when the file is simply not on disk. All other errors still reject as before.
- **Renderer** (`src/lib/desktop-fs.ts`, `src/global.d.ts`): new `HermesReadFileErrorResult` type + `isReadFileErrorResult()` guard. The facade (`readDesktopFileText`, `readDesktopFileDataUrl`, `readDesktopFileDataUrlLocalFirst`) converts the structured result back into a thrown error, so every existing `try/catch` caller behaves identically to a rejection.
- **Raw bridge callers**: all 7 call sites that use `window.hermesDesktop.readFileText/readFileDataUrl` directly (inline preview directive, directive image, media resolution, generated image, file preview fallback, attach utils, runtime plugin loader) now guard the union result — showing "unavailable" / returning null / falling into their existing catch.

## Related Issue

Fixes #92222

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/electron/hardening.ts` — `isMissingFileError()` classifier + export
- `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` — wrap `hermes:readFileText`, `hermes:readFileDataUrl`, `hermes:readFileDataUrlForAttach` to return `{ok:false,...}` on missing files instead of rejecting
- `apps/desktop/src/global.d.ts` — `HermesReadFileErrorResult` interface; read methods return the union type
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/desktop-fs.ts` — `isReadFileErrorResult()` guard; wrappers throw on error result (preserving existing caller behavior)
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/media.ts`, `src/components/assistant-ui/inline-preview-directive.tsx`, `src/components/assistant-ui/directive-text.tsx`, `src/components/chat/generated-image-result.tsx`, `src/app/chat/right-rail/preview-file.tsx`, `src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/utils.ts`, `src/contrib/runtime-loader.ts` — guard the structured error result at raw bridge call sites
