items.body:
## Symptom

Every conversation started by hand in Bot Mode disappears. Right-click a bot → **New chat with this bot** (or the Bot Mode tab-strip `+` / ⌘T), talk to it, close the tab — the chat is gone:

- no row in the Sessions sidebar, under the bot's profile or under **All profiles**
- not offered by `/resume`
- not reachable from the bot row (that opens the canonical Bot Chat) and not from **Open recent session** either, because that reads `last_session`, which never reports a hidden row

So there is no way to find, rename, or delete a bot conversation you started yourself. Reported on Discord ("Chats in Bot mode": *"I don't know how to remove a chat with a bot, and if I make a new chat with the bot, I will not see this chat in the future"*), and reproduced earlier in #91740 with a controlled experiment that isolated the Bots-tab creation path as the deciding variable.

## Root cause — one line

`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/index.ts`, in `openNewSessionTile`:

```ts
...(workspaceScope.workspaceMode === 'bots' ? { hidden: true } : {})
```

The flag is applied to the whole mode, but this path only ever mints **side chats**. Both callers prove it:

- `sdk/index.ts` → `newChat(route, { workspaceMode: 'bots' })` → `$newSessionTabAction` — the roster context menu's "New chat with this bot"
- `app/contrib/wiring.tsx` → `openNewSessionTab()` — the tab-strip `+` / ⌘T while Bot Mode owns the workspace

Bot Mode's **plumbing** sessions never come through here; each mints its own row and sets the flag itself — the canonical Bot Chat in `plugins/hermes-bots/canonical-chat.ts` (`title: 'Bot Chat', hidden: true`) and group member sessions in `plugins/hermes-bots/group-turns.ts`. So the blanket flag hid nothing that wasn't already hidden, and hid every side chat forever.

## Why this is a bug and not the design

Three places in the tree already say side chats stay listed:

- `apps/desktop/src/AGENTS.md`: side chats *"are not plumbing-titled, **stay visible in the sidebar**, and are never the row's target"*
- `plugins/hermes-bots/session-sweep.ts`: the hide sweep's title allow-list is exact on purpose — *"a user's real conversation inside a bot profile keeps whatever title the user gave it and is never touched"*. The birth flag defeated that care.
- the maintainer ruling closing #91740: *"Side chats started via 'New chat with this agent' are NOT hidden and remain reachable in the Sessions sidebar; only the canonical row is."*

The canonical Bot Chat's unconditional hiding is untouched, and so is every invariant around it: one bot = one forever-chat identified by the `Bot Chat` title, no session-id pin, recency never wins.

## The fix

Drop the blanket flag. Nothing replaces it, because the sidebar concern it was reaching for (#113273 — hidden rows resurrected by the refresh keep-list) is already handled where it belongs: `mergeSessionPage` and `sessionsToKeep` in `store/session.ts` drop `hidden === true` rows, so a canonical Bot Chat cannot re-enter the list no matter what holds it live.

`listTileSessionRow`'s Bot Mode guard (`app/chat/session-tile-actions.ts`) stays as-is — the canonical chat does reach it, and it must not seed an optimistic row for a hidden session. A side chat therefore surfaces on the next list refresh once its first turn persists, exactly like a Sessions-mode ⌘T tab created with `listed: false`.

## Result

A Bot Mode side chat behaves like any other conversation: it appears in the Sessions sidebar under the bot's profile (or All profiles), `/resume` lists it, and its row menu offers Rename / Archive / Delete. Deleting a bot's hand-started chats no longer needs `state.db` surgery.

## Test plan

- New invariant test in `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions.test.tsx`: drives `openNewSessionTile` with a bots workspace scope and the bot's own route (the exact shape both callers use) and asserts `session.create` carries no `hidden` param. **Red on the unfixed tree** (received `hidden: true`), green after.
- The neighbouring bot-workspace test lost its incidental `hidden: true` assertion; its actual subject (the ambient composer selection is not leaked into a bot tile) is unchanged.
- `npx vitest run src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions.test.tsx src/app/chat/session-tile-actions.test.ts src/plugins/hermes-bots/ src/store/session.test.ts` → 93 files, 984 tests passing, including every Bot Mode canonical-chat contract test (`canonical-chat-registry`, `canonical-chat-creation`, `canonical-chat-adopt-on-conflict`, `bot-row-opens-canonical-chat`, `hide-bot-chats`).
- `npm run typecheck` (renderer project), `npx eslint`, and `npx prettier --check` clean on both changed files.

Refs #91740.

Fixes #105162

## What does this PR do?

`hermes update` on a systemd host never restarted `hermes-dashboard*` units: the systemd fleet-restart pass listed and name-gated only `hermes-gateway*`/`hermes-serve*`, and the abort-recovery serve pass enumerated `hermes-serve*` only. A systemd-supervised dashboard (`hermes-dashboard-<profile>.service`) therefore stayed on pre-update code after every update — the receipt recorded `outcome: deferred`, nothing ever restarted it, and the update still exited 0 with `outcome: success` (5 of 5 updates in #125297's receipts). The Desktop app then hits the stale dashboard over SSH (`/api/profiles` failing) until someone restarts the unit by hand.

The runtime-outcome reconciliation already credits `hermes-dashboard{,-<profile>}` unit restarts via `_serve_unit_matches_profile` — the unit pass simply never produced one, so this wires the existing sanctioned vocabulary into the two restart channels:

- the in-process systemd unit pass (`_LIST_GATEWAY_UNITS` glob + `_is_hermes_gateway_unit` name gate), and
- the fresh-process abort-recovery serve pass (`_UNIT_RE` + the `list-units` patterns in `update_restart_recovery.py`).

SIGUSR1 drain eligibility is intentionally unchanged: dashboard units don't run `gateway/run.py`, so like `hermes-serve*` they go straight to the blunt `reset-failed` + `restart`, which is what the workaround in the issue (`systemctl --user restart hermes-dashboard-<profile>`) already proved correct.

This mirrors the #83438 fix, which added `hermes-serve*` to the same pass for exactly this class of stale backend.

## Related Issue

Fixes #125297

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/update_cmd_fleet.py`: `_LIST_GATEWAY_UNITS` also lists `hermes-dashboard*`; `_is_hermes_gateway_unit` accepts `hermes-dashboard.service` and the `hermes-dashboard-<profile>` family (same exact/hyphenated shape that rejects `hermes-server.service`, per the #83595 review).
- `hermes_cli/update_restart_recovery.py`: `_UNIT_RE` covers the dashboard family; `_listed_serve_units` queries both `hermes-serve*` and `hermes-dashboard*` patterns.
- `hermes_cli/update_abort_recovery.py`: docstring for `_serve_unit_recovery_available` names the dashboard family.

## How to Test

1. On a Linux host with systemd, run `hermes dashboard` under a `hermes-dashboard.service`/`hermes-dashboard-<profile>.service` user unit.
2. Run `hermes update`.
3. Before: the receipt under `logs/update_receipts/update_*.json` shows `runtime_outcomes` with `{"kind": "dashboard", "outcome": "deferred"}` and the unit's MainPID is unchanged. After: the unit pass restarts the dashboard unit, the survivor probe no longer sees the old incarnation, and the row reconciles as `restarted`.

Unit level: `./venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_update_fleet_restart_timeout.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_serve_generation_recovery.py -q` (61 passed). Regression tests pinning the new dashboard-family coverage are coming as a follow-up commit on this branch (WIP first version — core fix posted early to claim the issue).

items.body:
## plugin-catalog: add memex8 memory provider

Adds Ex8-ca/memex8 to the Hermes plugin catalog as a community-tier memory provider.

### What it is

memex8 is a self-hosted vector memory backend (Qdrant + TurboQuant compression) that gives the agent deep semantic recall across all past conversations and ingested documents. It replaces Hermes's built-in flat-file memory (MEMORY.md / USER.md) with:

- **Unlimited capacity** — vector store vs. 2,200-char hard limit
- **Semantic search** — relevance-ranked retrieval, not linear scan
- **Auto-discovered knowledge realms** — content clusters itself by topic
- **Slumber pipeline** — periodic memory consolidation, dedup, and verification
- **Hook integration** — implements `on_session_end` and `on_pre_compress` for durable checkpoint storage before lossy context compression
- **Cross-platform** — Rust core with REST API; works from any Hermes surface (CLI, TUI, gateway)

### Repo

- **URL**: https://github.com/Ex8-ca/memex8
- **Pin SHA**: `b5e87b7b9a537ec663dd0c5d68a5ebf819976abc`
- **Subdir**: `plugins/memex8`
- **Maintainer**: @Ex8-ca

### Plugin contract compliance

The plugin source at `plugins/memex8/` ships:

- `plugin.yaml` — manifest with `name`, `version`, `description`, `requires_env`, `hooks`
- `__init__.py` — implements `MemoryProvider` ABC and exports `register(ctx)` entry point
- **`pre_compress_checkpoint_api_version = 2`** — opts into the fail-closed pre-compress
  checkpoint contract. `on_pre_compress(messages, *, require_checkpoint)` synchronously
  archives the transcript to memex8; when the operator enables `compression.checkpoint_required:
  true`, a failure raises `RuntimeError` and BLOCKS the lossy rewrite. With the default
  (`require_checkpoint=False`), failures are logged and compression proceeds — matching
  the documented best-effort default for non-archiving providers, while the archive is
  still attempted on every cycle.
- **All background threads use `spawn_context_thread`** — `queue_prefetch`, `sync_turn`,
  `on_session_end`, and the `initialize` health probe. Bare `threading.Thread` runs with
  empty contextvars and would silently write to the default profile under multiplex;
  the host's wrapper propagates the spawning context so per-profile writes (config,
  secrets, logging scope) bind correctly.
- `README.md` — setup, configuration, and operations guide
- `docs/banner.png` — 1200×630 catalog card image

### Install/UX after merge

Users on Hermes `>=0.21.4` can run:

```bash
hermes plugins install memex8
hermes memory setup        # pick "memex8", enter MEMEX8_API_KEY + URL
```

…or configure manually in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:

```yaml
memory:
  provider: memex8
plugins:
  - memex8
```

…with secrets in `~/.hermes/.env`:

```
MEMEX8_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080
MEMEX8_API_KEY=<token>
```

### What this PR does NOT include

- No bundled-tree changes — memex8 lives in its own repo per Hermes's
  third-party-product policy (observability/SaaS plugins ship standalone).
- No auto-migration wiring — users upgrading from `memex8` referenced
  pre-catalog can re-install with the command above.
- No `config_schema.py` or `cli.py` — those would add a Desktop dashboard
  config panel and `hermes memex8 <subcmd>` tree. Optional; can land in a
  follow-up.

### Validation

- [x] Local `hermes plugins validate memex8` passes against `HERMES_HOME=/tmp/hermes-test`
- [x] `MEMORY.md` and `USER.md` continue to mirror to memex8 alongside the built-in store
- [x] Both YAML files parse cleanly; all required catalog fields present
- [ ] Catalog CI clone-and-validate expected to pass (will report via PR check)

---

**Checklist for reviewer:**

- [ ] `sha:` in catalog matches `origin/main` HEAD of `Ex8-ca/memex8` (currently `b5e87b7b`)
- [ ] `image:` URL resolves (raw GitHub CDN)
- [ ] `subdir: plugins/memex8` matches the actual repo layout
- [ ] `tier: community` is appropriate (no NousResearch sponsorship claimed)
- [ ] `category: memory` matches the `kind` of the plugin (MemoryProvider ABC)

items.body:
Cron Python scripts can now run under a user-managed venv: `hermes cron create/edit --interpreter ~/venvs/x/bin/python`. Before this, a `script` / `monitor_script` always ran on Hermes' own Python, so `import openpyxl` (or any package the user installed) failed with `ModuleNotFoundError`, and a package installed into Hermes' venv disappeared on the next rebuild.

Salvage of #70500 by @M1racleShih (co-author @MestreY0d4-Uninter), which revives #8741. Closes #8714. The PR was ~21k commits behind and conflicted in all 6 production files: script execution has since moved to `cron/scheduler_script.py`, and the CLI and tool are now table-driven. The feature commit keeps the contributor's authorship and was re-applied to that layout.

## What changed

1. **feat(cron): external interpreter** (@M1racleShih, ported)
   - `cron/jobs.py`: `interpreter` goes through the existing field-normalizer tables; `""` clears it on edit.
   - `cron/scheduler_script.py`: `_resolve_cron_interpreter()` checks the path at run time (absolute or `~` path, regular file, executable on POSIX). `_script_argv` then runs `[interpreter, script]` and skips the managed-install bootstrap and PYTHONPATH additions, which exist for Hermes' own venv. A straight port would have put Hermes' repo onto the user's venv path (POSIX) or silently ignored the interpreter (Windows managed installs). The field is passed through all four script entry points: no-agent, pre-run, heartbeat wrapper, monitor.
   - CLI: `--interpreter` on `cron create` / `cron edit`; shown in `cron list` and job details.
   - `cronjob()`: available to the CLI and direct callers only, the same as `model` and `reasoning_effort`. It is not in the model-facing schema, so the always-sent tool description gains 0 characters and the model cannot choose an interpreter for unattended jobs.
2. **fix(cron): only accept a Python executable** (ours). The lifecycle guard treats a `.py` script as Python and skips its shell-reference walk. At the PR head, `interpreter=/bin/bash` plus a `.py` whose body is `bash restart.sh` was accepted and then executed as shell. Now the interpreter's name, and its symlink target's name, must match the guard's own `_INTERPRETER_IMAGE_RE`.
3. **refactor(cron): simplify after review** (ours). `pythonw` is refused because it discards captured output, which would make an agent job go quiet with no error. A cleared value is stored as null, like `workdir`. Minor tidy-ups.

Tests: I kept 2 of the PR's 34 tests (the end-to-end no-agent and monitor tests, which run a real wrapper interpreter) and added one parametrized test covering the 7 refusal cases. The rest were signature-order checks, mock-argument-only tests, a faked `sys.platform`, and argparse checks.

## Verification

- `tests/cron` + `tests/hermes_cli/test_cron*.py` + `tests/tools/test_cronjob_tools.py`: 1483 passed, 11 skipped (clean env).
- Full `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/`: every file that failed locally was rerun on this head and on its base on main (`6f7a7991bb`), in clones outside the real Hermes home. The failures are identical on both, 236 tests in 62 files, none only on this branch; all are host-environment failures that also happen on main.
- Mutation checks:
  - Ignoring the interpreter in `_script_argv` turns all 8 interpreter tests red.
  - Removing the Python-name check turns the bash and symlink-to-bash cases red.
- Live, real CLI, throwaway venv, temp `HERMES_HOME`:
  - With `--interpreter ~/extvenv/bin/python` the script imports the venv-only module (`EXTMARK-42`, venv prefix).
  - After `edit --interpreter ''` it is back to `ModuleNotFoundError`.
  - `interpreter=/bin/bash` on the `.py` wrapper fails at run time with "Interpreter must be a Python executable".
  - The same content as a `.sh` is still blocked at create.
  - The model handler drops an `interpreter` argument.
- Probe with a simulated managed-store install: with an interpreter set, argv is `[interpreter, script]` and the environment overlay is empty.
- ruff, windows-footguns, compat pointers and subprocess-stdin checks are clean. `ty` on the 8 touched files: 22 diagnostics, the same as main.

## Known limits

- The check is name-based: a non-Python binary renamed `python3` passes. The field is user-owned (CLI only), so this closes the accidental and agent-driven paths, not a deliberate local user.
- Free-threaded and debug builds (`python3.13t`, `python3.12d`) and PyPy are refused; the error says why.
- `~` expands against the scheduler process's HOME, which can differ from the CLI user's in container setups; the failure is a clear "not found".

## What does this PR do?

`_check_gates()` called `run_gate(gate)` with no `cwd`, so gates ran in the backend process's directory. In Desktop that's the default project or `$HOME`, not the session's workspace. A relative gate (`scripts/run_tests.sh …`, as the docs show) checked a different project, and when that project passed, the judge ran and a failing goal was saved as **done**.

`_gate_workspace()` resolves the directory once per check:

- **Session workspace declared and present:** gates run there.
- **No session workspace:** the existing resolution applies (`TERMINAL_CWD`, else the launch directory), so the classic CLI started inside the project is unchanged.
- **Session workspace declared but not a directory on this host** (deleted project, remote or container path): the goal pauses on that check with a reason naming the workspace, and no gate runs in the backend's directory. No retry is charged, since another agent turn can't fix a missing workspace.

## How this differs from #125377

#125377 uses `resolve_agent_cwd()`, which falls through to `TERMINAL_CWD` and then `os.getcwd()` when the declared session workspace doesn't exist (its docstring says so). That's the same false pass in another form: the gate runs in the backend's directory and can pass for the wrong project. `test_missing_session_workspace_pauses_instead_of_running_elsewhere` fails on #125377's head and passes here. The other two tests pass on both.

Tradeoff: in a session whose workspace is remote/container-only, a gate that `cd`s to an absolute host path used to run and now pauses the goal with the workspace message. Gates run on the Hermes host, so such a session has no local project for a relative gate to check, and I preferred failing loudly over a silent false "done". Happy to narrow this if you'd rather keep those running.

## Related Issue

Fixes #125369

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## How to Test

1. The issue's `repro_goal_gate_cwd.py`: on `main` it prints `gate recorded exit: 0 ran in: …/project-passing` and `goal status: done`. On this branch it prints `gate recorded exit: 1 ran in: …/project-failing` and `goal status: active | ✗ Quality gate failed`.
2. `tests/hermes_cli/test_goal_gates.py`: 3 new tests (session workspace used; missing workspace pauses without running a gate; no workspace keeps the launch directory). On `main` the first two fail.
3. Every test file that references goals/gates (59 files): 848 passed, 0 failed, 38 skipped.

items.body:
Fresh Windows and Linux installs download ffmpeg again, and `pm update ffmpeg` can no longer write a pin that expires two weeks later.

**Why it broke.** BtbN deletes its daily autobuild tags after 14 days. It keeps the last build of each month for two years (`util/prunetags.sh`, and the "Release Retention Policy" in its README). Our pin was the daily `autobuild-2026-09-10-15-31`, which is now deleted. Where the artifact mirror is also refused (the regional 403 in #125350 and #122240), the install stops with an HTTP 404. `btbn_index` always picked the newest daily, so every `pm update ffmpeg` wrote a pin that would expire the same way.

**Changes**
- `pm/update.py` `btbn_index`: only month-end tags count. The current month's newest tag is skipped because the next daily build replaces it. In each finished month only the last tag counts. `latest` stays excluded.
- `pm/lock.json`: the 4 BtbN rows (win32-x64, win32-arm64, linux-x64, linux-arm64) now point at `autobuild-2026-08-31-13-27`, snapshot `n9.0.1-11-ge47273f4d9`. That snapshot matches the locked `9.0.1` label, and it is exactly what the new resolver picks against the live API. The sha256 values are GitHub's release digests. The source, build config, native arm64, x11grab and ffprobe are unchanged, and macOS and Termux rows are untouched. BtbN keeps this tag until about Aug 2028.

**Validation**

| | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| win32-x64 install, mirror forced to 403 | HTTP 404 | 145 MB `ffmpeg.exe`, sha OK, 85 s; rerun 0 s |
| linux-arm64 install, mirror forced to 403 | (same row class) | 108 MB `ffmpeg`, sha OK, 71 s; rerun 0 s |
| live `resolve_package(Ffmpeg, BtbN targets, "9.0.1")` | newest daily | `autobuild-2026-08-31-13-27` for all 4 targets |

- `tests/pm/test_ffmpeg_resolution.py` adds one invariant test. It fails if either rule is removed (current month, or older daily in a finished month); both mutations were checked red.
- `tests/pm/`: 778 passed, 39 failed. Every failing file fails the same way on origin/main (this macOS baseline).

**Who / when:** the original re-pin in #125371 was by @dskwe (Yuan Li), who is credited as co-author on the lock commit. That version pinned another daily tag, so it would have expired around Oct 11; this PR replaces it with the retained month-end build and fixes the resolver behind it. It supersedes the local re-pin approach in #125510, which I'm closing. Before, bumps were forced every two weeks; now a bump is a deliberate choice, needed about once a year at most.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes a permanently non-convergent "Chat out of date" refusal loop on long, tool-heavy desktop chats (#123909).

Two consumers of the same session store hold incompatible assumptions:

- `boundRetainedTranscript` (`app/chat/transcript-retention.ts`, #77311) intentionally releases the store's **head**, keeping the live window plus one weight-budget page of slack. A tool-heavy coordinator transcript burns that budget quickly, so the trimmed store holds far fewer rendered messages than the session has.
- `messagesIfTranscriptBehind` (`lib/stale-transcript-guard.ts`) compared **authored counts**: the latest 120-row page (`includeCompacted: true`) folded to e.g. 85 chat messages vs a trimmed store of fewer than that. `85 > trimmed` → refuse the send and install the refreshed page → the next window-anchor move re-trims → the next send is refused again. Non-convergent by construction, and it survives reload/relaunch because hydration re-trims once the window cut is established. Short chats never cross the budget, which is why this only bites long heavy chats (including the canonical Bot Chat, which is a forever-chat by design).

The fix compares **tips, not totals**: when the last durable `rowId` of the local view equals the page's own last durable `rowId`, the view is current however much head retention has paged out — retention only ever releases the head, so the last durable row is always the live tail. A peer window's newer row still changes the tip, so the #65047 second-window protection is intact. The count comparison remains as the fallback when tips cannot be established (views/pages with no durable ids), matching the pre-fix behavior exactly on that shape.

## Related Issue

Fixes #123909

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/lib/stale-transcript-guard.ts` — added `lastDurableRowId` (last persisted row of a view, skipping unpersisted tail rows such as live stream bubbles) and a tip-equality short-circuit ahead of the count comparison in `messagesIfTranscriptBehind`; updated the doc comment to describe tip-first semantics.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/transcript-backfill.test.ts` — new `messagesIfTranscriptBehind retention tips (#123909)` block: trimmed-store-with-matching-tip is current, unpersisted tail rows are skipped when establishing the tip, a peer's newer row still refuses (#65047), and counts remain the fallback without durable ids.

## How to Test

1. `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/app/chat/transcript-backfill.test.ts` — should pass (32 tests, including the 4 new ones).
2. Confirmed the two tip short-circuit tests **fail against the pre-fix code** (`git stash push -- apps/desktop/src/lib/stale-transcript-guard.ts` → `2 failed | 30 passed`; restored afterwards).
3. Regression sweep across the affected surfaces, all green: `npx vitest run src/app/session/ src/app/contrib/ src/store/transcript-sync.test.ts src/app/chat/` → 2454 passed (one pre-existing suite failure, `sessions-pane-tab-title.test.tsx`, fails identically on an unmodified checkout — missing optional `@novnc/novnc` dep locally, unrelated to this change).
4. `npx tsc -p . --noEmit` and `npx eslint src/lib/stale-transcript-guard.ts src/app/chat/transcript-backfill.test.ts` are clean.

items.body:
## Summary

The desktop voice conversation hardcoded its silence hold at 1,250 ms and ignored the existing `voice.silence_duration` config key that the CLI, TUI, and gateway capture paths already honour, so:

- a mid-thought pause cut the turn off and submitted a partial recording, with no way to raise the threshold (`hermes config set voice.silence_duration 10` had no effect on desktop),
- fast local STT/TTS stacks sat through a rigid extra second of dead air on every turn.

The loop now reads a `$voiceSilenceMs` nanostore seeded from `/api/config` on every refresh (the same `useHermesConfig` path as `voice.stop_phrases` and barge-in sensitivity), so config edits apply live without a restart. Two guards keep current behaviour:

- **Only a user-set value overrides the 1.25 s desktop hold.** `/api/config` merges `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, so an untouched install reports the backend default (3.0) rather than omitting the key; reading it unconditionally would triple the hold for everyone. A value equal to the `/api/config/defaults` payload keeps the tuned desktop default.
- **Malformed values fall back like the gateway's shape-safe lookup** — non-numeric, non-positive, or boolean (`true` must not coerce to 1 s) keeps the default.

The barge-in utterance endpoint reads the same atom live per frame instead of its own matching constant, so barge-in capture and the voice loop stay matched across config refreshes.

**Supersedes** (both read the key unconditionally, raising the hold from 1.25 s to 3 s for untouched installs; #85772 additionally coerces `true` to 1 s):

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/83572 — credit @chelsealong for the live-atom shape and the barge-in live read, both kept here
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/85772 — credit @Natetgmaxwell for the same shape and its tests

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/83518
Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/124760

## Test plan

- [x] New `applyVoiceSilenceMsFromConfig` tests proven red on base (import fails — the seam didn't exist) and green with the fix: user-set override (0.7 s → 700 ms, `'2'` → 2000 ms), untouched install keeps 1,250 ms (config == defaults, defaults endpoint unavailable, key absent, null payload), malformed values keep the default
- [x] `vitest run --project ui` on voice-prefs, voice-barge-in, use-voice-conversation, thinking-sound, voice-stop-word: 47 passed
- [x] `tsc -p . --noEmit` clean; eslint/prettier clean on touched files

items.body:
## Problem

Bot-Mode deliveries spawn each DM/relay turn through the console script beside the caller's interpreter, so a long-lived caller pinned to an old dependency generation keeps launching that generation even after a newer one is selected. Plugin dependencies installed after the pointer was recorded are then invisible to every Bot Chat (`No module named 'hindsight_client'`), while the same profile works from the CLI.

https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/124868

## Root cause

`tools.bot_relay._hermes_cli()` prefers `sys.executable`'s sibling console script. Every Bot delivery path (`local_delivery_command`, local/peer `message_agent`) reuses it, so the spawned child boots the recorded generation's entrypoint instead of the installation-bound launcher whose bootstrap leases the currently selected generation at child start.

## Change

- `_hermes_cli()` now prefers this install's already-published `.hermes/bin/hermes` launcher (`hermes.exe` on Windows) — the same installation-bound command `hermes_cli/_launchers.py::installation_command()` persists for the systemd unit. Bootstrap/PM dependency selection stays owned by the launcher; no new selector.
- Interpreter-sibling, `shutil.which` and bare-name fallbacks remain for external/developer installs without a published launcher (#93590, #108628).
- Batch `.cmd` shims are never selected: `cmd.exe` reinterprets otherwise literal argv (e.g. an ampersand in a query-file path) even with `shell=False`.
- Existing fallback-ladder tests now isolate `bot_relay.__file__` so the checkout's own published launcher does not shadow the fallback they probe — without this they fail on any source install that has run the launcher publication step (found while validating the superseded PR on a real checkout; that PR's head reds `test_delivery_pins_the_hermes_entrypoint_beside_this_interpreter` and `test_bot_relay_windows_paths` in that environment).

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/124913 — same fix, cherry-picked with authorship preserved (`fix(bot-mode): prefer installation-bound delivery launchers`, `fix(bot-mode): avoid selecting batch shims for literal delivery argv` by @Wenfengcheng). The fallback-ladder test isolation and the base-`origin/main` rebase are added on top.

Credit: @Wenfengcheng for the resolver fix, the batch-shim guard, and the launcher test suite.

## Verification

Base `9fa23760bc` (current `origin/main`).

- RED on base: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_bot_delivery_install_launcher.py -q` → 1 failed (`test_delivery_prefers_install_launcher_over_old_generation`: resolver picked the old-generation sibling over the published launcher); reverted fix → 5 passed.
- GREEN with fix: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_bot_delivery_install_launcher.py tests/tools/test_bot_mode_dm.py tests/tools/test_bot_relay_windows_paths.py tests/tools/test_bot_retry_policy.py -q` → **97 passed, 0 failed, 7 skipped** (skips are `platforms('windows')` probes; they run on the Windows CI lane).
- Windows real-PM generation-selection test and native Windows validation were performed by the contributor on Windows (see superseded PR); this host (macOS) covered the POSIX paths.

## Non-goals

Batch-only Windows installs, dashboard service launchers, and the #106742 unified-gateway architecture that retires this transport are unchanged.

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/124868

items.body:
Hermes no longer picks up the user's own `node`/`npm`/`npx`/`uv` when its PM-managed copy is missing. It provisions its own copy instead, or reports a clear error.

Maintainer ruling: *"only hermes and only packaged package managers (uv/pip/node/npm) should ever be used."*

## Changes
- **`hermes_constants.find_node_executable`**: `node`/`npm`/`npx` now resolve to PM's installed copy or `None`, with no PATH fallback. Every production caller (WhatsApp, Photon, `hermes whatsapp`, dashboard pairing, tools setup) already runs `pm.ensure()` when it gets `None`, so a missing runtime now gets provisioned instead of borrowing the user's Node.
- **`agent/lsp/install._install_npm`**: runs `pm.ensure("npm")` when PM's npm is absent, instead of dying or using PATH npm. pnpm and yarn stay an explicit user choice via `lsp.package_manager`.
- **`hermes_cli/gateway._append_node_dir_for_service`**: generated systemd units and launchd plists no longer bake in the invoker's PATH node dir.
- **`hermes_cli/main_install_repair._resolve_node_runtime_npm`**: no longer re-scans PATH for another npm (the old updater keeps importing it).
- **`hermes_cli/source_build.source_product_current`**: the build-freshness reader runs only under PM's node. Before, `env_for("node")` fell back to the ambient PATH.
- **`hermes doctor`**: the Node row and `npm audit` use PM's node and npm, and the audit runs under `with_hermes_node_path()`. Termux keeps its system Node because the Termux APT distribution relies on `pkg install nodejs`.
- **`scripts/install.sh::ensure_uv` / `scripts/install.ps1::Get-Uv`**: the "uv on PATH if at least the pin" developer shortcut is deleted, so the installers always stage the pinned artifact. The dead `version_at_least` helper is removed too.
- **Docs**: `getting-started/installation.md` no longer says an existing uv can bootstrap PM.
- **Test stand-ins**: Photon, WhatsApp, and source-build tests used to pass by implicitly borrowing the CI host's PATH node. They now stub the adapter's `find_node_executable` or `pm.installed_package("node")` with an explicit stand-in (`use_host_node_as_pm_node` in `test_source_build.py`). Test intent is unchanged.
- Allowlists: removed the `_ALLOWED` rows for `gateway.py` node and `main_install_repair.py` npm, plus 3 `resolution_allowlist.json` rows. The `main_tui_launch` reasons are corrected: those lookups run against a PATH composed by `pm.ensure`, not the ambient one.

## Validation

**Live repro:** in a scratch `HERMES_HOME` with an empty PM store and a fake user `node`/`npm`/`npx` 99.0.0 first on PATH:

| | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `find_node_executable("node"/"npm"/"npx")` | the user's `…/usernode/{node,npm,npx}` | `None` (caller runs `pm.ensure`) |
| `_append_node_dir_for_service` (unit PATH) | `['…/usernode']` | `[]` |
| `install.sh ensure_uv` with a fake `uv 99.0.0` on PATH | `UV_CMD=…/fakeuv/uv` | downloads the pin: `UV_CMD=$HERMES_HOME/tools/uv-0.12.3-linux-x64/uv` |

**Tests:** each changed invariant test is red on origin/main and green here.

| Test | Base |
|---|---|
| `tests/pm/test_node_resolution.py::test_passive_discovery_never_installs_or_repairs_a_legacy_tree` | red |
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_service.py::…test_no_pm_node_never_bakes_the_invokers_path_node` | red |
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_service.py::…test_stale_pm_facts_without_dirs_contribute_nothing` | red |
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_node_runtime_npm_resolution.py::test_resolve_node_runtime_npm_never_rescans_path_past_a_windows_shim` | red |
| `tests/scripts/install/test_install_sh_repository_stage.py::test_path_uv_is_never_used_even_when_newer_than_the_pin` | red |

**Why existing tests changed:** each rewritten assertion pinned the fallback that the ruling bans.
- `test_node_resolution` asserted that "a user-owned PATH toolchain remains usable". It now asserts `None`.
- In `test_gateway_service`, the `*_ambient_fallback` tests now expect `[]`. `test_node_path_lookup_remains_fallback_without_managed_node` duplicated one of them and is deleted. The two #48700 symlink-leak tests are also deleted: they could only fire through the removed `which("node")` rung, so that leak can no longer happen.
- The WSL npm re-scan test is flipped to "no re-scan".
- The installer test that accepted a new-enough PATH uv is flipped.

## Not in this PR
Product calls and borderline items are listed in the audit on the parent task. items.body:
Fresh Windows 10 installs no longer fail at `prerequisites` with `tar.exe: ... unable to run program "bzip2 -d"`. Pinned Git is now staged from Git for Windows' PortableGit self-extractor, so tar and bzip2 aren't needed at all.

Salvage of #123094 by @Finn763. His two commits are cherry-picked unchanged with authorship kept, on top of current `origin/main`. Two follow-up commits from review sit on top (below).

Fixes #122512, fixes #122774. Covers the git part of #125350 (the ffmpeg and `-SkipSetup` parts of that issue are separate).

## Why

- Windows 10's `System32\tar.exe` is `bsdtar 3.5.2 - libarchive 3.5.2 zlib/1.2.5.f-ipp`. It has no built-in bzip2 filter, so it shells out to a `bzip2` that a stock machine doesn't have.
- Newer Windows 11 builds ship `bsdtar 3.7.x ... bz2lib/1.0.8`, which is why Windows 11 hosts and CI never hit this.
- Hermes staged Git from PortableGit before the pm store landed (3601e20f47c). The `.tar.bz2` pin came with the pm store foundation (3d12e86ef13).
- PortableGit is also what Scoop (`Main/bucket/git.json`) and Chocolatey (`git.portable`) pin.

## Changes (from #123094)

- `pm/lock.json` and the generated pin fragment in `scripts/install.ps1`: both win32 git targets now point at `PortableGit-2.53.0.3-{64-bit,arm64}.7z.exe`. Same Git version; the sha256s match GitHub's published asset digests.
- `scripts/install.ps1::Get-PinnedGit`: runs the self-extractor with `-o<dir> -y`, waits on it through `Process.WaitForExit` (the stub is a GUI-subsystem exe, so `&` wouldn't wait), stops after 600 s, and reports the exit code. The `System32\tar.exe` call and its MSYS exclude list are removed.
- `pm/packages.py::Git.unpack`: runs a scratch copy of the sha256-verified artifact, never the cached bytes. This fixes the WinError 32 the PR's first CI round hit. On a non-Windows host it refuses with a clear message.
- `pm/store.py`: removes `extract_tar(git_msys=...)`, which no longer has a caller.
- Tests and docs: pm invariants now check the subprocess argv, plus one real-download `Get-PinnedGit` test that uses a bzip2-less tar stub. The `pm install --target` doc row notes the Windows-host requirement.

## Review follow-ups (two commits on top)

- `066c425` pm: refusal, non-zero exit and timeout raise `InstallError` (`pm/client.py` only catches `InstallError`; `TimeoutExpired` escaped). The extractor's stdio is `DEVNULL`: with `capture_output` the `RunProgram` children inherit the pipes and can hold `run()` open after the stub exits. The dead output-tail branch is gone. The off-Windows refusal now gives a real remedy instead of "retry". Tests use `CompletedProcess`, drop `raising=False`, add a timeout case, and the pin-suffix change-detector test is removed.
- `5660a6f` install.ps1: on timeout, `taskkill /T /F` kills the whole extractor tree (PS 5.1 `Process.Kill()` only kills the stub, so its children kept `%TEMP%` held). The single-wrapper-dir flatten is removed: the sha-pinned archive roots `cmd\git.exe` directly.

## Self-extractor behaviour, checked against source

Checked against `git-for-windows/7-Zip` `v26.03-VS2022-sfx` `CPP/7zip/Bundles/SFXSetup/SfxSetup.cpp`:

- Only `-y` and `-o` (quoted or unquoted) are parsed. Any other switch is appended to the `RunProgram` command line. The `-gm2` switch on the gitforwindows.org "zip archives" page belongs to the old 7zsfx.info module and would be passed through to `post-install.bat`, so it is deliberately not used.
- The stub waits on `RunProgram` (`WaitForSingleObject(..., INFINITE)`) and then returns 0. So when the process exits, extraction and the vendor post-install have both finished.

## Trade-offs (from the maintainer round-2 review)

- A 58 MB sha256-pinned, `Unblock-File`d PE now runs during bootstrap. An "Extracting..." progress window shows even with `-y`.
- `Git.unpack` for the win32 target now needs a Windows host. Bundled win32 builds already run on native Windows runners (`windows-latest-32-core`, `windows-latest-32-arm-core`).
- **hermes-assets mirror:** the two new objects (`upstream/sha256/b365da79…`, `upstream/sha256/0db54010…`) return 404 until merge. No manual upload is needed: `archive-inputs.yml` runs on any push to main that touches `pm/lock.json`. It downloads each pin from upstream, checks its sha256 and uploads it to R2 under the release-signing environment, which is limited to main and tags. The ffmpeg re-pin (#125350, run 36344056098) went through that path, and its object now returns 200. GitHub stays the primary URL, so the ~1 minute gap after merge doesn't matter.

## Validation

- `scripts/gen-bootstrap-pins.py --check`: clean. `check-windows-footguns.py --all`: clean. Ruff: clean.
- `tests/pm` and `tests/scripts/install` on macOS: 846 passed, 39 failed, 68 skipped. The 39 failures are the same 10 files and counts as on the untouched merge-base (846 passed, 39 failed), all pre-existing macOS environment failures. `tests/pm/test_store_extract.py` passes.
- On #123094's head `adaf76a`: 57 check runs succeeded, 23 skipped, 0 failed. That includes the Windows-only lane and `Windows E2E (real processes)`, which ran `git: unpacking` for real.
- The real x64 pin (downloaded on macOS, sha256 matches the lock and install.ps1): the SFX config is `RunProgram="git-bash.exe --needs-console --hide --no-cd --command=post-install.bat"`. `7zz l` lists `cmd/git.exe`, `usr/bin/bash.exe`, `bin/bash.exe` and `post-install.bat` at the archive root, with no wrapper dir and no symlinks. So every path `Git.binary_rel`, `env()`, `pm/shell._staged_bash` and `Get-PinnedGit` expect is present.
- Real `pm install --target win32-x64 git` on macOS (isolated HOME and HERMES_HOME): refuses before running anything and leaves no store entry.
- Follow-up commits: mutation-checked. Piping stdio again, dropping the timeout handler, dropping the remedy, or executing the cached bytes each fail a test. Consumer tests outside `tests/pm` (16 files) show the same result as the merge-base. `install.ps1` parses with 0 errors.
- Still needs the Windows lane on this PR's head.

items.body:
Windows install wrappers that still pass `-SkipSetup` work again, instead of dying at parameter binding with `NamedParameterNotFound` before any stage runs (#125350 item 3).

**Why.** The staged-installer rework dropped `-SkipSetup` from `install.ps1`'s `param()` block. PowerShell refuses an undeclared switch outright, so an old spelling can't be ignored; it has to be declared. `install.sh` still accepts `--skip-setup` as an alias for `--non-interactive` (kept in f91bd82286), so Windows was the only installer without it. The most-used community wrapper, fathah/hermes-desktop, passes it in two places:
- `src/main/installer.ts`: `-SkipSetup -NonInteractive …`
- the copy-paste command in `src/renderer/src/constants.ts`: `-SkipSetup` **without** `-NonInteractive`, so the alias has to mean "skip the prompts", not just bind.

**Changes**
- `scripts/install.ps1`: declares `[switch]$SkipSetup` and folds it into `$NonInteractive` before anything reads the parameters. It is documented in the header as a deprecated alias.
- The docs (English + zh-Hans `windows-native.md`) list it as a deprecated alias. `-NoVenv` and `-Tag` stay rejected.
- `tests/scripts/install/test_install_ps1_skipsetup_alias.py` (Windows lane) has two tests:
  - `-SkipSetup` binds.
  - `-SkipSetup` alone, with `-Stage setup -Json`, emits the `skipped / needs user input` frame. Only the fold can produce that frame, so deleting the fold line makes the test fail.

**Behaviour note (from @teknium1's review):** the old `-SkipSetup` skipped only the setup wizard. The alias skips every stage that needs input, which includes the gateway stage. That is what an unattended wrapper needs, and hermes-desktop already passes `-NonInteractive` anyway.

**Who / when:** this is a salvage of #125371 by @dskwe (Yuan Li), with authorship kept on the cherry-picked commits. It also includes Teknium's review fix-up commit (the doc line and header comment). The PR's `pm/lock.json` re-pin and the since-deleted liveness test are dropped. Its ffmpeg hunk pinned the 2026-09-27 daily, which BtbN deletes around Oct 11, and #125468 supersedes it with the retained month-end build. Merging #125371 as it stood would have reverted that pin.

**Validation:** macOS has no PowerShell, so the two Windows tests run in the Windows CI lane. `tests/scripts/install/` passes on macOS (69 passed, 20 skipped). ruff, windows-footguns and `git diff --check` are clean.

items.body:
## Problem

Two sidebar state bugs:

1. **Archiving a session resurrects it** (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/123685). Archiving or deleting a chat from the sidebar could make it reappear a moment later, on the same profile, without touching the backend row.
2. **Renaming leaves project-scoped and other-slice rows stale** (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/123337). Renaming a session updated the recents list, but project overview previews, entered-project lanes, and cron/messaging rows kept the old title until an unrelated refetch (e.g. a profile switch).

## Root cause

**123685:** `applyProjectTreePayload` in `apps/desktop/src/store/projects.ts` prunes an archive tombstone once the authoritative projects tree no longer lists the id — correct for the tree overlay, but it strips the removal guard while a sidebar page **read before the archive RPC committed** is still in flight. When that stale page lands, tombstone membership is already empty, so `dropTombstoned` / the `mergeSessionPage` survivor filter have nothing to veto and the row re-enters through the keep set (the 30s settle grace still names it). Tombstones also matched only the row's tip id + lineage root, so the same conversation could sneak back under an intermediate lineage segment id.

**123337:** the rename flow (`RenameSessionDialog` submit, `/title` slash, `session.title` gateway event) patched only `$sessions` by bare id. Compressed rows matched by lineage, project-scoped snapshot rows, cron rows, and messaging rows never saw the new title until a refetch overwrote them.

## Fix

- `store/session-removal.ts`: track the direction of the last removal edge per id. `sessionRemovalIntersected(snapshot, id)` answers "did this id's removal lifecycle move **toward removal** since this fetch started" — the generation counter and edge direction survive the tombstone prune. `tombstoneRowIds(session)` names every id a row answers to (tip, lineage root, and all intermediate segments), replacing the tip+root-only match in `dropTombstoned` and `mergeSessionPage`.
- `use-session-list-actions.ts`: every fetch (recents `refreshSessions`, messaging refresh, platform load-more, cron slice) captures a tombstone-generation snapshot **before** the first read and rejects rows raced toward removal, filtering after the merge so survivor-path rows are covered too.
- `store/projects.ts`: `fetchProjectSessions` (project drill-in) applies the same guard through the existing `excludeProjectSessions` helper, keeping the project reference when nothing matches so the drill-in memo stays stable.
- `store/session.ts`: new `applySessionTitle(id, title)` patches the title across **every** sidebar slice (`$sessions`, cron, messaging, unlisted owner rows), matching lineage-aware via the existing `sessionMatchesStoredId`, reference-stable per slice when nothing changes.
- `store/projects.ts`: new `applyRenamedSessionTitle(id, title)` mirrors the rename into the cached project tree (lane rows + overview previews, recomputing counts) and re-pulls the authoritative tree.
- The rename dialog, `/title` slash command, and `session.title` gateway event all route through the new helpers.

Release edges (failed archive RPC, explicit unarchive) still re-admit the row: only edges that moved **toward** removal are vetoed.

## Tests

6 new behavioral tests, proven red on base `9fa23760bc` and green with this patch:

- `use-session-list-actions.test.tsx`: a doomed row whose tombstone was pruned mid-flight is dropped instead of resurrected through the keep set; a rolled-back archive mid-flight is re-admitted; a pruned-tombstone row is matched by any lineage segment and the cron slice is filtered too.
- `session.test.ts`: `mergeSessionPage` matches a tombstone by intermediate lineage segment; `applySessionTitle` patches every slice lineage-aware and stays reference-stable on no-op.
- `projects.test.ts`: `applyRenamedSessionTitle` mirrors into cached tree rows + previews (matched by tip and by lineage root) and re-pulls the tree; keeps the tree reference on no-match.

Full local validation in the worktree (rebased on current main):

- `npx vitest run use-session-list-actions.test.tsx session.test.ts projects.test.ts session-removal.test.ts` → **217 passed** (4 files)
- `npm run typecheck` (apps/desktop, all 4 tsconfigs) → clean
- `npx eslint` on all 10 touched files → clean

Store/hook logic only, no visual or behavioral surface a user could see change beyond the two fixes.

Bumps the mnemostack memory provider to 1.0.3 (`08bdc8c` = tag v1.0.3).

- **Fix: memory tools were never registered on a freshly built agent.** `MemoryManager.add_provider` snapshots `get_tool_schemas()` before `initialize_all` builds the provider's client; the provider returned no schemas until the client existed, so `mnemostack_search` / `mnemostack_remember` / `mnemostack_forget` answered "Unknown tool" while the system prompt advertised them. The schemas are now static.
- **Fix: the shim copy written by the provider's own `hermes-mnemostack install` into a profile no longer pins its dependency**, so a stale pin cannot downgrade the package on setup after an upgrade. The catalog-pinned tree is unchanged in that respect: `plugin.yaml` still pins `hermes-mnemostack==1.0.3`, and the description's disclosure is updated to match.

Same tools, same `subdir`, no new hooks, middleware or env requirements.

items.body:
`hermes update`, `hermes update --check` and installer re-runs now work on the tag-pinned `--depth 1 --single-branch` checkouts older installers made, instead of reporting an existing `main` as missing.

Fixes #125112. Salvages #125123 by @dskwe (the fix and the forced-refspec test) and the end-to-end check test from #125132 by @kokhlo; both are cherry-picked with authorship kept.

Root cause: on these checkouts `remote.origin.fetch` maps only the tag, so a by-name `git fetch origin main` writes `FETCH_HEAD` and never creates the `origin/main` that everything afterwards resolves.

## Changes

- **Updater fetches** (`--check`, the apply fetch, the fork upstream sync) use an explicit forced refspec, `+refs/heads/<b>:refs/remotes/<r>/<b>`, built in one place: `update_cmd_check.tracking_refspec`. The `+` matters: on a depth-1 clone the new tip is not a descendant of the old one. (@dskwe)
- **Update count on these checkouts.** They are always detached with no local `main`, so the updater lands them with `checkout -B main origin/main`, which puts HEAD on the target before `rev-list HEAD..origin/main` counts. With the fetch fixed alone, that count read 0: the update moved the code, printed "Already up to date!", and skipped dependency sync, config migration and restarts. HEAD is now captured before that checkout, the count starts from it, and it reaches the pull phase as `pre_sync_sha` (the channel the fork upstream sync already uses), so the did-HEAD-move guard and the syntax rollback compare against the code that was running.
- **Installer re-runs** (`install.sh`, `install.ps1`) fetch by the same refspec. When there is no local branch they create it at the fetched tip, because `git checkout main`'s branch guess ignores remote refs the configured refspec does not map. The remote's fetch config is never rewritten.
- **Tests.** One invariant per surface, each red on `origin/main`: the end-to-end `--check` test (@kokhlo), the forced-tip advance (@dskwe), and the count from the pre-checkout HEAD. The narrow-clone fixture now creates its origin on `main` explicitly; before, it only passed where `init.defaultBranch=main`.
- **Typing.** `SourceTarget` carries either a commit or a branch but types both as optional. The branch arm now asserts that invariant where it takes the branch, so the typed helper receives a `str`. `ty` against main: 9 vs 10 diagnostics, none new.
- Not carried over from #125132: the `ls-remote` probe and its new message. With an explicit refspec, a genuinely missing branch fails the fetch itself, which already names it: `✗ Failed to fetch updates from origin.` / `fatal: couldn't find remote ref refs/heads/<b>`, verified on both `--check` and apply. So the probe's branch was unreachable. It also duplicated `source_check._branch_tip` without the timeout.
- Side effect, accepted: a fetch with an explicit destination auto-follows tags that point into the fetched history, where a by-name fetch did not.

## Validation

Each surface was run against a real narrow clone of this repo: a local origin plus `git clone --depth 1 --single-branch --branch v2026.9.24`, 335 commits behind.

| Surface | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `hermes update --check` | `✗ Branch 'main' not found on origin.` | `Update available: 335 commits behind origin/main` |
| apply fetch + checkout | `✗ Branch 'main' does not exist locally or on origin.` | lands `main` |
| apply count (fetch fix only) | `commit_count=0` → "Already up to date!" | counted; applied d25bbd01 → 7d7f712a; post-pull phase runs |
| same, parked on a merged branch | same miscount | applied |
| fork upstream sync, tag-only `upstream` | `Could not compare branches` | up to date with upstream |
| `install.sh --stage repository` re-run | `pathspec 'main' did not match` → failed | `main` at the tip; idempotent re-run |
| normal / treeless clones | — | identical refs and result to `origin/main` |

The neighbouring update, shallow, gitlock, source_check and installer test files run one per process: 107 files pass. The 15 that fail locally fail the same way on the base commit: identical test IDs in the 4 files that exercise the changed checkout code, identical counts in the rest. The cause is a local guard that trips on this machine's checkout location. The windows-footguns lint and `ruff check` are clean.

`install.ps1` was not executed; no PowerShell runtime is available here, so Windows CI covers it.

Reverts #124792: MCP stdio children get the PATH order they were configured with again. That PR moved the resolved command's directory to PATH[0], which leaves the #82309 layout unchanged and puts a later directory's node/python3/git ahead of the Hermes-managed ones.

WHO/WHEN/WHY: follow-up to the post-merge review on #124792 by @andrexibiza (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/124792#pullrequestreview-5328958540). I reproduced its F1/F2 findings on macOS, found the default Hermes PATH is also affected, and am opening the revert rather than patching on top, because whether managed Node should be authoritative for MCP children is a policy question (#125589, #124304, #125318).

## Changes
- Revert 79dbb145: `_prepend_path` goes back to prepending only when the directory is absent. The four tests it added are removed along with it.
- One invariant test: when a bare command is found in a later PATH directory, the child's PATH comes back unchanged. It fails on 79dbb145 and passes after the revert.

## Root cause
`_resolve_stdio_command` passes `_prepend_path` the directory the **command** was found in, not the managed Node directory. After 79dbb145, a command found anywhere on PATH pulled its directory ahead of every earlier entry.

## Live repro (real spawned children, macOS)

| Layout | before #124792 | on main (79dbb145) | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| System Node + npx first, managed behind (the #82309 shape) | system | system (no change) | system |
| Managed first, absolute foreign `npx` later | managed | **system** | managed |
| Managed first, bare `uvx` in a later dir that also has `node` | managed | **later dir's node** | managed |
| Real Hermes PATH (store dirs first, as `pm.activate()` sets it), `command: gh` from `/opt/homebrew/bin` → child's `node` / `python3` / `git` | store / store / /usr/bin | **brew / brew / brew** | store / store / /usr/bin |
| Real MCP server (`mcp` client), env.PATH `A:/usr/bin:/bin:B`, launcher in B | PATH[0]=A | PATH[0]=B | PATH[0]=A |

## Validation
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_mcp*.py`: 824 passed, 2 failed. The same 2 fail on main and before #124792 (`test_mcp_shared_connection_resolved_identity.py`); they trip the home-I/O guard because my worktree lives under the real hermes home.
- The new test is red with main's `tools/mcp_tool_common.py` swapped in and green on this branch.
- ruff, `check-windows-footguns.py --all`, `check_compat_pointers.py`: clean.

#82309 stays closed: its desktop dependency-install surface was already fixed on main by the PM refactor (`with_hermes_node_path` → `pm.env_for("npm")`), which both #124792's own scope note and the post-merge review verified.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

The stable release's signed-candidate legs died before building anything: every job inside `desktop-bundled-release.yml`, `docker.yml` and `termux-verify.yml` that declares a protected environment attached its deployment and read the environment's `vars`, but resolved `secrets.*` to the empty string. This PR lets those secrets reach the three callees that need them, and nothing else.

Root cause: a called workflow receives no secrets by default. A job-level `environment:` inside it is required but not sufficient — and a caller job that `uses:` a reusable workflow cannot declare `environment:` at all, so `secrets: inherit` is the only mechanism that can carry them across the boundary ([actions/runner#1490](https://github.com/actions/runner/issues/1490)).

Precedent, deliberately checked: #69803 hit the same symptom on the CI → Docker publish path and fixed it by making that publish top-level, adding *no* `secrets: inherit`. This PR takes the other branch of that fork on purpose — the stable release's callees hand receipts and artifacts back through `needs.*.outputs`, so they cannot become top-level dispatches without re-architecting the handoff. If "trusted work runs top-level" is the preferred shape here too, the two `docker.yml` calls are the one place it could be hoisted instead; say the word and I'll move the docker publish out of the call.

## Related Issue

No tracking issue — caught live on the first full stable-release dispatch: run [#36194968007](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/36194968007), job `108268960023` (`Build signed release candidates (win32-arm64) / Pre-build setup`) failed with `missing env CLOUDFLARE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`.

Fixes # (none — the failing run above is the report)

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `.github/workflows/stable-release.yml` — `secrets: inherit` on the 7 `desktop-bundled-release.yml` calls, the 2 `docker.yml` calls, and the `termux-verify.yml` call, plus a header comment stating why those three need it.
- `.github/workflows/desktop-bundled-release.yml` — the header contract now says callers must pass `secrets: inherit`; the previous wording implied repo-level or environment secrets would arrive on their own.
- Not added where it buys nothing: `ci.yaml` (its header forbids it — it runs PR-controlled code), `nix`, `pm-bundle`, `windows-venv-e2e`, `install-e2e*` reference no secrets.
- Credential boundary unchanged: a secret still reaches only jobs that declare the environment *and* whose ref its deployment policy allows. `secrets: inherit` changes what the callee's own environment-gated jobs can read, not which refs may deploy.

## How to Test

1. **Before** — run [#36194968007](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/36194968007), job `108268960023`: the step env showed the R2 secrets empty while the `vars` value arrived, i.e. environment attached, secrets withheld:

   ```text
   CLOUDFLARE_R2_ACCOUNT_ID: (empty)
   CLOUDFLARE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID: (empty)
   CLOUDFLARE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: (empty)
   CLOUDFLARE_R2_BUCKET: hermes-agent-artifacts
   ```

2. **Control** — same three secrets, same `release-signing` environment, same tag ref, but in a *top-level* job: `archive-inputs.yml` run [#36205453828](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/36205453828) shows all three masked (`***`) and archived the pinned inputs to R2. The credentials are fine; the boundary is the `workflow_call` hop.
3. **After** — needs a claim dispatch (the next `rc.N` cut). Check the first `Pre-build setup` step env: the three values should read `***`, and `Archive every pinned input` should get past its first line. Note this PR's own CI cannot exercise it — dispatching `desktop-bundled-release.yml` directly runs it top-level, where the secrets resolve anyway, which proves nothing.

`nix run nixpkgs#actionlint -- -shellcheck= -pyflakes= .github/workflows/stable-release.yml` exits 0. The 10 `cache-mode` complaints in `desktop-bundled-release.yml` are pre-existing (identical set at `origin/main`; actionlint's bundled schema predates the key).

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(ci):`, `feat(ci):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate

items.body:
When a stdio MCP server's native addon was built for a different Node.js, Hermes now shows the failure and gives the exact rebuild command with its own Node's paths. Before this, the server was parked silently behind "Connection closed".

Fixes #124264. The report and diagnosis came from @michael2608H, and @rodricksz4h5 did the analysis in #124304.

## Ruling applied
Maintainer ruling: *"only hermes and only packaged package managers (uv/pip/node/npm) should ever be used."* Managed Node stays first for MCP children. The user's Node never runs them, and nothing suggests pinning `command:` to it. #124304 (managed Node moved behind the user's for MCP) was closed under this ruling.

## Changes
- `tools/mcp_tool_config.py::_StderrTee`: the stdio child's stderr now goes through a pipe. Every byte is still copied into `logs/mcp-stderr.log`, and the last 16 KB stay readable.
- `tools/mcp_tool_node_abi.py` (new): when a failed session's stderr shows `NODE_MODULE_VERSION` / `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED`, it builds a `NodeAbiMismatchError`. The error names the addon, both ABI numbers and the fix, using PM's own node/npm paths:
  - addon in an `~/.npm/_npx/<hash>` entry: `rm -rf <entry>`, and Hermes's npx reinstalls it on the next start;
  - either way: `PATH=<managed node dir>:"$PATH" <managed npm> rebuild <pkg> --prefix <root>`. Managed Node has to be first on PATH because npm's shebang and its install scripts both run the first `node` they find.
  - On Windows the same commands are rendered in PowerShell syntax. If PM has no Node installed, the message says `hermes pm install npm`.
- `tools/mcp_tool_transport.py::_run_stdio`: raises that error, chained to the SDK's error.
- `tools/mcp_tool_errors.py`: the error is classified as permanent, so the server parks at once instead of retrying 3 times. It self-probes, so it comes back after the rebuild. `_format_connect_error` returns the error's message on its own.
- `hermes_cli/mcp_config.py`: after the error, `hermes mcp test` says "After rebuilding it under Hermes's Node as above, run: hermes mcp test <name>".

Every place MCP status already shows up reads the error through `_format_connect_error` / `str(exc)`, so the new message reaches all of them without further changes: the startup banner (whose first ~120 characters carry the diagnosis), `/mcp` status, `hermes mcp test`, the TUI `mcp.test` RPC, the Desktop probe and the dashboard `/test` route.

## Validation
| | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `hermes mcp test` on a server whose stderr is Node's real ABI error | `✗ Connection failed (8.3s): Connection closed` / "Check the server is running…" | `✗ Connection failed (2.9s): native addon built for a different Node.js (NODE_MODULE_VERSION 127; Hermes's Node 26.7.0 needs 147): …/_npx/abc123/node_modules/better-sqlite3/…node. Hermes runs MCP servers on its own Node; rebuild the server under it: rm -rf …/_npx/abc123 (Hermes reinstalls it on the next start), or PATH=~/.hermes/tools/node-26.7.0-linux-x64/bin:"$PATH" ~/.hermes/tools/npm-12.0.2-linux-x64/bin/npm rebuild better-sqlite3 --prefix …/_npx/abc123` |
| Spawns before parking | 4 (initial attempt + 3 retries) | 1 |
| `logs/mcp-stderr.log` | has the child's stderr | still has it |
| hosts E2E `test_path_shapes` MCP cell (real `install.sh`, a stand-in user Node v22.11.0 first on PATH) | **red** at the remedy assertion. Managed Node already ran the server; the output was just "Connection closed" | **green** |
| `tests/tools/test_mcp_node_abi.py` (2 tests) | real stdio-child test red (`'Connection closed'`, 3 attempts) | green |
| `tests/tools -k mcp` | — | 922 passed |
| `tests/hermes_cli tests/tui_gateway -k mcp` | 4 fake-HOME env failures | the same 4 fail identically on base |

**E2E cell rewritten:** `test_mcp_server_configured_with_the_users_node_runs_on_the_users_node` asserted the user's Node wins, which contradicts the ruling. It was gated with `known_failure` on #124264. It is now `test_mcp_server_runs_on_the_managed_node_and_an_abi_mismatch_names_the_rebuild`. It asserts that the user's Node never runs the server, that the marker shows Hermes's managed Node ran it, that `hermes mcp test` exits 1, and that the output carries `NODE_MODULE_VERSION 127`, `rm -rf <sandbox>/.npm/_npx/<entry>` and `PATH=<managed node dir>: … rebuild better-sqlite3 --prefix`.

## What

After the Linux launcher rename (`com.nousresearch.hermes.desktop`), `install_desktop_entry()` deleted the pre-rename `hermes.desktop`. Shells resolve a taskbar pin by the entry file name it was pinned against, so that deletion silently killed existing pins: GNOME drops the favourite, Plasma leaves an inert item, and the shell has no mechanism to re-point the association for the user.

Instead of deleting the legacy entry, rewrite it as a `NoDisplay=true` alias with the same `Exec`/`Icon`/`StartupWMClass` as the app-id entry — invisible in the app grid (no second Hermes), still launchable and window-matched for old pins. Only a file that still names this app is converted; foreign files stay untouched, and the launcher-management opt-out still protects it. `gui_uninstall` now removes the alias together with the real entry.

## On-disk effect (Linux install/uninstall)

Install writes $XDG_DATA_HOME/applications/com.nousresearch.hermes.desktop as before, and now also rewrites $XDG_DATA_HOME/applications/hermes.desktop (only if it is our own pre-rename entry) to the same entry text plus a `NoDisplay=true` key; GUI uninstall additionally removes that hermes.desktop alias.

## Verification

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_linux_desktop_entry.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gui_uninstall.py tests/hermes_cli/test_linux_launcher_management.py` (HERMES_TEST_FILE_RETRIES=0): 55 passed, 0 failed, 3 platform-skips that run on CI lanes.
- The new alias test fails against origin/main's product code (scratch copy via `git show`, no stash): the legacy entry is deleted instead of aliased.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/124567 — notification-only approach (prints re-pin guidance once a migration renames the entry); this PR fixes the root cause so no pin ever breaks and no user action is needed.

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/124492

items.body:
## Summary

A finished assistant reply could render twice after settle, via two independent paths, each keying on stale identity instead of the durable one:

- **use-message-stream**: a rewritten final (`response_previewed` / `response_transformed`) shares no text prefix with the streamed interim, so the prefix heuristics missed — and the volatile boundary flag could no longer speak for the bubble once a chained `message.start` reset it. The terminal frame carries a `persisted_turn` receipt naming the stored row it settled (`final_assistant_row_id`); the fix settles onto the display-only interim keyed on that durable receipt instead of appending a second bubble for one stored row.
- **use-session-actions `overlayConcurrentMessageChanges`**: the committed row and the settled live row capture the same reply at two moments while it kept streaming, so the strict text-equality guard rejected their fold and kept both. The fix accepts either side as a forward text-extension of the other via the existing `isStrictAnswerTextExtension` helper — the same trade `removeRepresentedLocalLiveProjection` already made.

Four new tests pin the rewritten-previewed, rewritten-transformed, lagging-live-row, and ran-past-committed-row shapes; all four fail on main and pass with this change.

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/123993
Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/124128

items.body:
Desktop's own children (the `hermes serve` backend, its probes, the update hand-offs and the bootstrap installer) now resolve the PM store's node/npm/uv ahead of the user's nvm/Homebrew/`~/.local/bin` copies, even after the login-shell PATH merge.

Maintainer ruling: "the principle is now that only hermes and only packaged package managers (uv/pip/node/npm) should ever be used."

**Root cause:** `shell-path.ts` writes the user's interactive login-shell PATH into `process.env` with login entries first and the inherited PATH appended. When Desktop is started by `hermes desktop`, the inherited PATH is exactly where the store dirs sit (`with_hermes_node_path` / `pm.activate`), so every child env built from `process.env` put the user's toolchain first, and the backend's `pm.activate()` left the already-present store dirs where they were.

## Changes
- `electron/backend-env.ts`: new `storeFirstPath()` moves PATH entries under the PM store root to the front and keeps every other entry in its existing order. The store root is resolved like `pm.environments.store_root`: `HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR`, else `<hermes home>/tools`. Ownership is decided by path containment, so a look-alike prefix such as `~/.hermes/tools-old` does not count.
- `buildDesktopBackendEnv()` applies it. That covers every backend spawn (bundled payload, source, `HERMES_DESKTOP_HERMES`, Windows venv unwrapping), the backend probes, and the source/POSIX/Windows update hand-offs, which build their env through `sourceUpdateEnvironment`.
- `electron/bootstrap-runner.ts`: the install.sh/install.ps1 child env goes through the same helper. `install.sh` takes a uv from PATH when it is new enough, so a store uv that is already on PATH now wins.
- `process.env` itself is **not** reordered, so the embedded terminal (`terminal-ipc.ts`) and external terminal keep the user's own PATH order. A test asserts this.
- In-process half: the sibling Python PR (`fix/toolchain-principle-2`) makes `pm.install.activate()` always move store dirs to the FRONT of `os.environ["PATH"]`. At the moment it only prepends dirs that are missing. This PR is the spawn-env half, so the order is right before Python starts and for children that never run `activate()`.

## Validation

| Check | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| New `backend-env.test.ts` "backend runs the store toolchain even after the login-shell PATH is merged in front of it" | ✗ red | ✓ |
| New `backend-env.test.ts` "HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR names the store; look-alike prefixes are not Hermes-owned" | ✗ red | ✓ |
| Live probe: real `applyLoginShellPath` (host's real `bash -il`), inherited PATH = `<home>/.hermes/tools/node-26.7.0-linux-x64/bin:/usr/bin:/bin`, then `command -v node` in a child spawned with the backend env | `~/.local/bin/node` (user's) | `…/.hermes/tools/node-26.7.0-linux-x64/bin/node` → `HERMES-STORE-NODE` |
| Same probe, `process.env` (terminal base) | `~/.local/bin/node` | `~/.local/bin/node` (unchanged) |
| `npm run check:lint` (apps/desktop) | n/a | 0 errors |
| `vitest` backend-env, shell-path, bootstrap-runner, bootstrap-runner-git-binary, backend-probes, windows-hermes-path | n/a | green |

Locally, `source-backend.test.ts` (PM source launcher) and `updater/checkout-source.test.ts` fail on this host both on origin/main and on this branch. The cause is the host environment: no prepared PM Python env, and `ruamel` is missing from the Python those tests pick up. They are not affected by this change; CI runs them in a prepared env.

## Deliberately unchanged
- `terminal-ipc.ts` / `external-terminal.ts`: the user's shell is the user's environment.
- `shell-path.ts` merge order into `process.env`: it feeds the terminal, so the fix lives in the Hermes-child env builders instead.
- The Windows staged-installer recovery hand-off (`main.ts`, `spawnUpdaterProcess` with `process.env`): Windows-only, and the login-shell merge never runs on win32, so the store order there is whatever was inherited.
- Desktop uninstall (`hermes_cli.main uninstall`): out of scope.
- No facts.json parsing in Electron. Every store tool dir lives under the store root, so a containment rule is enough.

`hermes update` no longer exits 1 when a dashboard it just stopped and respawned is a not-yet-reaped zombie, and the handoff E2E (`test_update_exit_status_matches_what_came_back`) stops failing on unrelated branches because of it.

This PR carries @kshitijk4poor's fix from #125682 unchanged (their commit, their authorship) and adds a deterministic reproduction of the CI failure plus the removal of the now-obsolete HEAD dashboard gate. If #125682 lands first, this PR shrinks to the gate commit.

## Root cause (product bug, not a harness race)
The update stops the manual dashboard (`dashboard_procs._wait_gone` → `gateway.status._pid_exists` counts a **zombie as gone**), respawns it with a non-waiting `Popen`, and runs the survivor probe (`_surviving_pre_update_serve_runtimes` → `ledger_entries()`) milliseconds later. The ledger's non-strict liveness check (`process_identity._pid_alive_matches` → `_same_incarnation`) compares only `create_time`, which a zombie keeps until its parent reaps it, so it reads the old dashboard as **alive**. The runtime is booked `unaccounted` and the update exits 1 while the new dashboard is serving. Users whose dashboard's parent reaps lazily or never (a container PID 1 without an init, a supervisor script that doesn't `wait()`) get that false failure on every update.

The handoff sandbox agent reaps its children every 0.1 s, so CI lost the race sometimes. The cgroup was a red herring: after #124940 the CI dashboard takes the respawn path, same as on a dev box.

CI evidence: job 108684143708 (fix/ffmpeg-btbn-repin) and job 108695482545 (#125589) both show `✓ stopped PID 14x` → `✓ restarted: … dashboard --port …` → `These serve/dashboard processes still run pre-update code: pid 14x` → `✗ dashboard [default] pid 14x — planned mechanism: respawn-argv`, rc=1, with the new dashboard up.

## Changes
- `hermes_cli/process_identity.py` (#125682, @kshitijk4poor): the non-strict `_pid_alive_matches` reports a zombie as dead, as the strict path and `_pid_exists` already do. Test: `ledger_entries()` excludes a real killed-but-unreaped child.
- `tests/e2e/core/upgrade/handoff/_scenario.py`: drop `DASHBOARD_GATES["head"]`. #124940 makes the HEAD update respawn a dashboard started inside `hosted-compute-agent.service` instead of restarting the unit. In the failing CI runs above, `test_dashboard_is_back_on_its_port` passed rather than xfailed. The N-1 column keeps the gate until a release carrying #124940 is N-1.

## Validation
Handoff HEAD column run inside a transient user unit (`systemd-run --user`, same shape as the CI job running inside a systemd service). The injection is a scratch copy of `tests/e2e/core/upgrade/handoff/_ns_agent.py` whose reaper runs every 3 s instead of every 0.1 s (a parent that reaps lazily); it is not committed.

| run | base (origin/main) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| clean, systemd-run --user | 7 passed (the race is intermittent) | 7 passed |
| lazy-reap injection | **1 failed**: `update exited 1 though the gateway and the dashboard came back`, `dashboard pid 147 — planned mechanism: respawn-argv` (exact CI signature) | **7 passed** |

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_process_identity.py::test_ledger_entries_excludes_a_killed_but_unreaped_process`: fails on base, passes here.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_process_identity.py` + `test_update_serve_generation_recovery.py`: 79 passed.
- ruff, `check_no_tmp_literals.py`, `check_compat_pointers.py`: clean.

## Summary

Plugin inventory can take 40–80 seconds on a treeless (`tree:0`) source checkout because the catalog's path-scoped `git log` lazily fetches missing historical trees. This can exceed the Desktop's 30-second gateway request timeout.

- Use the existing `bounded_git_probe()` helper for the catalog date. It scopes `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` to the child, disables interactive Git behavior, and bounds process-tree cleanup on timeout.
- When history is unavailable in a Git checkout, use the newest checked-out catalog file's mtime. This preserves the fresh checkout's pin over an older live document, including equal or absent version labels. Full clones retain the precise commit time; release installs and never-checked-out clones retain the `None` fallback.
- Resolve pins, versions, and titles from one `load_catalog_live()` pass per plugin listing instead of three.

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/125683

## Verification

On head `db6ec3aab608b9aada68d4190c1eb9c5dd04271e`, the canonical runner reports **50 passed, 0 failed across seven files**:

```sh
HERMES_TEST_FILE_RETRIES=0 scripts/run_tests.sh \
  tests/agent/test_subprocess_env_guard.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_catalog.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins_cmd_catalog.py \
  tests/tui_gateway/test_plugins_manage_install.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_git_probe_no_lazy_fetch.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_bounded_probe_run.py \

```

The subprocess environment guard was reproduced failing before the helper change and passes afterward. Coverage includes real `file:// --filter=tree:0` clones, fresh/stale checkout pin precedence, one catalog resolution per listing, and bounded process-tree cleanup.

An additional local run of `tests/test_windows_subprocess_no_window_flags.py` hit a home-I/O isolation assertion in the unrelated `shell.exec` test; it is not included in the passing count above. Hosted CI remains the cross-platform gate.
