Remaining items from the packaged-toolchain-only audit: "only hermes and only packaged package managers (uv/pip/node/npm) should ever be used". The Electron half is #125681.

## What changes

- **Post-write lint** (`tools/file_operations_lint.py`). On the local backend, `.js`/`.ts` lint (`node --check`, `npx tsc --noEmit`) used to run through the terminal shell. That shell's PATH puts the user's dirs first, so on this machine it picked `~/.local/bin/node` v26.5.1. It now runs PM's node/npx directly with `with_hermes_node_path`. If PM has no Node, the lint is skipped; it never falls back to the user's copy. Remote backends (docker/ssh/modal) are unchanged because PM's Node isn't there. The user's interactive terminal PATH order is also unchanged.
- **`pm.activate()` / drift** (`pm/install.py`). Before, any drift made activate prepend nothing at all, and a store dir already on PATH was never moved forward. Now the store dirs always go to the front, including ones already on PATH behind a user dir. The drift case still returns the problems, and it keeps the property it protected (git log `3d12e86ef13e`, "fail fast rather than serving a partial PATH"), now enforced per package: `_store_path_dirs` drops any package whose dependency chain isn't fully installed, so store npm over a missing store node never reaches PATH. New `pm.store_first_path(path)` does the same for child PATHs that get dirs prepended after activate.
- **tui_gateway** `_prepend_tool_paths`. PM store dirs now go ahead of `~/.local/bin`, which is where a user-installed uv lives, and ahead of the venv/managed bin.
- **MCP stdio launchers** (`tools/mcp_tool_config.py`). A bare `npx`/`npm`/`node`/`uv`/`uvx` (including `.cmd`/`.exe` spellings) now resolves to PM's copy, with PM's toolchain dirs first on the child PATH (npx re-execs `env node`). The old system fallback table is gone: `uv_tool_dirs` (`~/.local/bin`, Homebrew) and `/usr/local/bin` + `~/.local/bin` for node. If a `command:` is an absolute path, the user's choice is kept. PM ships no build on Termux, so Termux keeps the platform copy. `pm.uv_launcher(name)` is a new read-only accessor for PM's installed uv/uvx. Hermes's own Python work still goes through PM operations.

## Tests
One or two per behavior, each red on `origin/main`:
- `tests/pm/test_startup_activation.py`: store dirs move ahead of a user dir; drift activates intact chains only.

## What does this PR do?

The Docker build sets `HERMES_PYTHON=/usr/local/bin/python3` for build helpers and leaves that value in the final image. The TUI launcher accepts the executable and gives it to the JSON-RPC gateway child. That child then exits with `hermes: no dependency environment is committed for this install`, although the image has a sealed dependency environment at `/opt/hermes/.venv`.

Keep system Python for the build steps, then point `HERMES_PYTHON` at the packaged venv in the final image. This matches the interpreter used by the image's `hermes` launcher.

## Related Issue

No public issue. Reproduced from a fresh local Docker image launched with `--tui`.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `Dockerfile`: switch `HERMES_PYTHON` to `/opt/hermes/.venv/bin/python` after the image build has finished using system Python.
- `tests/docker/test_tui_prebuilt_bundle.py`: exercise the image's real TUI interpreter selection as the container user, then import the gateway in the selected child Python. The test avoids `su`, which would clear the image environment and hide the regression.

## How to Test

1. Build the image: `docker build -t hermes-agent-tui-runtime-python:local .`
2. Run the focused Docker regression with that image: `HERMES_TEST_IMAGE=hermes-agent-tui-runtime-python:local scripts/run_tests.sh tests/docker/test_tui_prebuilt_bundle.py -k tui_gateway_child -j 4`
3. Start the image with `--tui` and no `HERMES_PYTHON` override. The gateway child should use the packaged venv and stay up.

Local verification on Docker Desktop's Linux/amd64 builder: the image build completed, and the new test function passed against the built image. Forcing the old `HERMES_PYTHON=/usr/local/bin/python3` value on the same image reproduced exit 1 with the original dependency-environment error. The canonical targeted runner on this Windows host stopped in its global fixture before running the test because the host's Python test environment lacks `ruamel.yaml`. The Docker CI lane builds the image and runs `tests/docker/` with its prepared test environment.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)

- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass. Full-suite coverage belongs to CI; the focused canonical run was blocked by the local host test environment as described above.

- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A

exit=1

items.body:
Agent-run children (terminal, `execute_code`, background processes, helper tools) no longer receive platform adapter secrets such as `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `WEIXIN_TOKEN`, `FEISHU_ENCRYPT_KEY` or `PHOTON_SIDECAR_TOKEN`, or Hermes' own dashboard-auth secrets. Language servers and their installers, the raft bridge, the buzz CLI, openviking-server, the bot desktop and the Telegram gmail-triage scripts now start from the scrubbed environment instead of Hermes' full one. Variables that belong to the user, such as `SLACK_USER_TOKEN` or `LOCAL_LLM_API_KEY`, are left alone.

Salvage of #122751 and #125191 by @jonpol01. Those PRs also carry commits from @andrexibiza and @necoweb3. All 11 of their commits are kept with authorship. Twelve follow-up commits from review and CI sit on top.

## Why

The child-env scrub strips credentials Hermes knows about: provider keys, bot tokens, and `OPTIONAL_ENV_VARS` messaging entries. Adapters read more secrets than that list names. Webhook signing secrets, app secrets and sidecar tokens read straight from the environment therefore reached every terminal command the agent ran. Several spawn sites also either built the scrubbed env and then spread `os.environ` back over it, or skipped the builder altogether.

## What changed

From #122751 / #125191:
- Adapter secrets are always stripped (Tier 1), including from children started with `inherit_credentials=True`, and skill or config passthrough refuses them. OAuth provider-profile keys join the blocklist.
- A passthrough accepted before an adapter claimed the name stops forwarding it once the adapter registers.
- LSP servers, the npm and `go install` installers, the raft bridge, the buzz CLI and openviking-server spawn from the scrubbed env.
- The spawn-env guard test now also catches `**os.environ` spreads and scans `plugins/`.

Follow-ups from review:
1. **Adapter secrets are the declared ones.** The PR matched any `<platform>_…_TOKEN/_SECRET/_PASSWORD/_KEY` name. Its platform list includes plain words (LOCAL, GATEWAY, WEBHOOK, SLACK), so the rule also stripped user variables Hermes never reads, and `terminal.env_passthrough` could not restore them. The list also failed open: one unreadable plugins dir cached an empty set. The set now has three sources:
   - Core `password` messaging entries of `OPTIONAL_ENV_VARS`, plus the secret entries of the bundled platform plugin manifests (Tier 1).
   - The secret entries of the bound profile's own user-installed platform plugins (Tier 1). These are read per spawn, per profile, and refreshed when a manifest changes, so under multiplex one profile's plugin never strips a same-named variable from another profile's children.
   - Secret-named keys that the gateway env-override table reads (Tier 1).
   - Secret-named `required_env` of adapters registered in the current profile, read per spawn without loading deferred adapters. These are Tier 2 only, because `required_env` is an unchecked setup list and a plugin that lists `OPENAI_API_KEY` must not strip it from credentialed children.

   Five secrets that nothing declared got a manifest entry. Three names read only in code sit in a short list in the policy module. One suffix rule (`PLATFORM_SECRET_ENV_SUFFIXES`) decides what counts as secret-named everywhere.

   None of these sources fail open. An unreadable bundled or `plugins/platforms/` manifest, or a registry error, fails the spawn instead of dropping the declaration. A manifest that doesn't parse declares nothing, because its adapter can't load either. An unsearchable dir such as a root-owned `__pycache__`, or an unreadable flat `plugins/*` manifest, is skipped with a warning.
2. **The compute host keeps Hermes' full environment.** It runs dashboard agent turns, and its `os.environ` layer is deliberate (#65895). Without it, keys that exist only in the process env (Docker `-e`, systemd) disappeared from turns, for example `HASS_TOKEN`, `MODAL_TOKEN_ID` and `DAYTONA_API_KEY`. `.env` keys came back anyway because the host reloads `.env`.
3. **openviking, raft and buzz keep the user's HOME** (`HERMES_REAL_HOME`). Their config and logins live there, and the builder rewrites HOME to the profile home in containers, including the official image.
4. **Hermes' own secrets that no source covered are now blocked:** the dashboard basic-auth password and signing secret, the dashboard drain and OIDC client secrets, `HERMES_ANON_API_SECRET`, and the Google Meet realtime key. The dashboard ones are Tier 1, so credential-inheriting CLIs such as claude and codex don't get them either. The session token next to them was already stripped.
5. **openviking-server takes provider keys from the bound profile,** not the launch profile. It then gets a second Tier 1 scrub, because the profile overlay would otherwise re-add that profile's bot and dashboard tokens. With no profile bound under multiplex, it refuses to start.
6. **Two more full-env spawns are fixed.** The bot desktop launcher now builds from `served_profile_child_env()`, like the agent browser. The agent drives that desktop, and its dock opens a terminal. The Telegram gmail-triage buttons run a script under `HERMES_HOME` that the agent can write. It now uses `build_subprocess_env`, like cron and webhook-filter scripts. In containers, those scripts therefore see the profile HOME, as cron scripts already do.

## Behaviour to know

Declared adapter secrets are now also stripped from children that run Hermes itself with inherited credentials: the restart watcher, the launchd fallback, the slash worker and `cli.exec`. Main already did this for `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` and `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`. Values from `.env` are re-read by those children. A value supplied only through systemd `Environment=` or `docker -e` is not passed to them.

## Not changed (follow-ups)

- **`key_cmd` token helpers still receive the bound profile's full `.env`, bot tokens included.** They run the user's own command and use the same overlay openviking now scrubs a second time. They are left alone here, because a `gh auth token` helper may legitimately need `GH_TOKEN`. That needs its own decision.
- **A detached `/restart` whose watcher env fails to build still stops the gateway.** That's existing behaviour for any helper-launch failure, such as a missing binary. This PR adds one more way the env can fail: an unreadable platform manifest.
- **The spawn-env guard does not yet match `{k: v for k, v in os.environ.items()}` or `dict(os.environ)`.** That shape is how the bot desktop slipped past it. Widening the guard flags about ten more sites, which each need a judgement call.
- **The raft bridge uses the launch profile's scrubbed env, not `served_profile_child_env()`.** The raft CLI reads its own `RAFT_PROFILE`, and the routed builder can raise when no scope is bound at connect time.

## Verification

- Live check on the final tree, with the plugins-dir scan forced to raise:
  - Declared secrets reach no child: terminal, non-terminal, or inherit.
  - Five user variables reach all three.
  - Passthrough accepts the user names and refuses the secrets.
- A plugin whose `required_env` lists `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` and `SLACK_USER_TOKEN`: credentialed children keep all of them, and the terminal drops them.
- Full suite, run from a clean clone of this branch before the last two commits: 53,869 passed and 301 failed. Re-running each failure on its own against origin/main: 2 were caused by this branch, both in `test_modal_snapshot_isolation.py`, which stubbed `hermes_cli.config`. They are fixed. All the others fail on origin/main too, from the local Python version, a missing `tomli_w`, and a full disk partway through the run.
- Targeted suites on the final tree (env policy, spawn sites, passthrough, modal, provider import order, platform registry, plugin env injection, openviking, bot desktop, session API): 296 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `test_runtime_provenance_is_independent_of_aliases_and_virtual_env[True]`, which fails on origin/main too.
- New tests cover per-profile plugin secrets under multiplex, in-place manifest edits, unreadable manifests (strict vs skipped), openviking with a routed profile's `.env`, a bundled manifest read failing closed, manifest deletion, and a symlinked home alias. Mutation checks: removing the openviking fix, keying the cache by the raw path, re-raising on an unsearchable dir, and keeping a partial bundled set each make a test fail.
- The per-home manifest stamp is one `scandir` per root, taken once per scrub. With 60 user plugins, `hermes_subprocess_env()` takes about 1.6 ms.
- The spawn-site test runs in profile-home mode and checks HOME for each child. Removing the raft HOME line makes it fail. `ty` gives the same output on the changed files as on origin/main.
- The bot desktop launcher and the gmail-triage spawn have no test harness. A probe showed their env drops only the intended secrets (plus `PYTHONPATH`) and keeps `LANG`, proxies, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`.

A fresh install comes with computer use and the Browser Use CLI working again: cua-driver is a default PM package, and the installers and `hermes update` provision the Browser Use CLI.

## Root cause

The unified package manager (3d12e86ef13) and the MSIX installer rework (47f4ab3a178) removed the install-time cua-driver fetch (7060ac7bedd) and the Browser Use CLI install (baa6b2e34d8), and the only PM default left was `agent-browser`. On a fresh install the `computer_use` check_fn stays False, so the tool never reaches the model and `cua_backend.start()`'s lazy ensure never fires. `browser_exec` silently falls back to the built-in tools.

## Changes

- `pm/packages.py`: `CuaDriver.default = True`, so the installers' PM stage, a bare `hermes pm install` and `hermes update` install it on every target it builds for (macOS, Windows, glibc Linux). Adds the missing `linux-arm64-bionic` gap: the lock has no Android artifact, and without the gap a default would fail every Termux install.
- `hermes_cli/update_cmd_maint.py`: the default-tool step, which the installers (via source completion) and `hermes update` both run, now provisions the Browser Use CLI for the default and explicit `browser-use` backends, with a 180 s timeout. `--skip-browser` declines it together with agent-browser; `off` and Camofox never use it. The per-package message stops calling every default "browser tools".
- `scripts/install.sh` / `install.ps1`: bring back `--skip-computer-use` / `-SkipComputerUse`, recorded as `--without cua-driver`.
- Docs: installation, computer use, browser, package management.

Salvages #122428 by @whyyagswhy (its commit is kept as authored). This PR widens it to the installers, cua-driver and the opt-out, and trims its tests to one invariant.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Live, fresh isolated home + PM runtime (`HOME`, `HERMES_HOME`, `HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR` in scratch), origin/main | `computer_use check_fn: False`, `is_browser_use_cli_mode: False`, PM defaults `['agent-browser']` |
| Same probe, this branch, running the real default-tool step | 40 s. cua-driver 0.21.0 installed into the runtime, Browser Use CLI in `environments/browser-use`, `computer_use check_fn: True`, `is_browser_use_cli_mode: True` |
| Real `browser_exec` through the provisioned CLI + packaged Chromium | `success: true`, printed `Example Domain` |
| Negative: `agent-browser` + `cua-driver` declined, fresh runtime | nothing installed, runtime dir empty, CLI absent |
| `tests/pm/test_install_default_closure.py` new invariant | red on origin/main (cua-driver not in defaults), red without the bionic gap (default target with no artifact), green here |
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_browser_use_cli_provision.py` | red on origin/main, green here |
| tests/pm, installation, scripts, computer_use, update/install/tools_config | identical 81 host-environment failures on origin/main and this branch (worktree + fake-home git/runtime tests), 0 new |

## Not covered

- Desktop sealed bundles already ship cua-driver (every lock package), but not the Browser Use CLI: it is a per-home PM tool environment, not a store package, and sealed installs skip the maintenance step.
- PM tool environments are anchored to `get_hermes_home()`, so a non-default profile does not see the CLI installed in the root home.
- macOS and Windows were not live-run. The macOS LaunchServices registration still happens on the next `hermes update` or `hermes tools` enable, same as the existing lazy path.

## Infographic

`⌘1…⌘9` is one chord with two meanings: the Nth tab of the pane under the pointer (else the focused pane, else the workspace's) when that pane is a real tab strip, and the Nth profile otherwise. #92639 (for #92569) removed the tab half entirely — `profile.switch.N` became unconditional and `view.tabSlot.N` shipped unbound — so holding ⌘ still painted the tab-number hints while the chord switched profiles. The legitimate complaint in #92569 was narrower: the tab dispatch was hardcoded inside the profile handler, so rebinding the chord could not separate the two.

This restores the contextual behavior as two independent actions on the same chord.

- `KeybindActionMeta.passthrough`: the handler may return `false` to decline, handing the chord to the next action bound to it.
- `$comboIndex` keeps every action on a chord in registration order; the dispatcher walks it and stops at the first action that runs.
- `view.tabSlot.N` defaults to `mod+N` ahead of `profile.switch.N` and declines when no zone is a tab strip or the strip has no Nth tab. Rebind either and only that one moves.
- `conflictsFor` does not report a passthrough action layered over a later one, so the panel stops flagging the shipped pair; a non-passthrough action landing on someone else's chord is still a conflict.
- The held-⌘ tab hints key off `view.tabSlot.N`, the action they describe.
- Docs (`desktop.md`, `multi-connection-desktop.md`) describe the chord's two meanings.

Tests: a dispatch test drives real `keydown` events through `useKeybinds` for hover → tab, no strip → profile, and no Nth tab → profile; store tests pin combo-index order, per-action rebinding, and conflict reporting. Verified live in a dev instance: ⌘1/⌘2 switch the main strip's tabs with the pointer over it and the hints render on the tabs.

Fixes #92569 regression from #92639.

Four commits, each one catalog change for `memory-rewind`:

1. **`fix(plugin-catalog)`: fit the card inside the plugin page header.** Re-pins `b747327` → `e5b139b`, which only redraws `docs/card.png`.
2. **`feat(plugin-catalog)`: bump to 1.3.0.** Re-pins → `5f935c2` ([range](https://github.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-memory-rewind/compare/e5b139b...5f935c2)), fixes wrong provenance, and adds `pre_llm_call` to `provides_hooks`.
3. **`feat(plugin-catalog)`: bump to 1.3.1.** Re-pins → `b9af50b` ([range](https://github.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-memory-rewind/compare/5f935c2...b9af50b)). Importing a Hermes backup no longer cuts off the history recorded after it.
4. **`feat(plugin-catalog)`: bump to 1.3.2.** Re-pins → `3549271` ([range](https://github.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-memory-rewind/compare/b9af50b...3549271)). `restore` no longer replaces a running agent's memory write, and its plan lists the memory entries it brings back and removes.

`image` stays at `e5b139b` throughout. Commits 3 and 4 change only `sha` and `version`, and each pinned sha passes the pinned-source validate on its own, so the branch can land commit by commit. The branch is rebased onto current `main`; the first two commits' content is unchanged.

## 1.3.1: `hermes import` cut off the history recorded after the backup

`hermes backup` archives `plugin-data/memory-rewind/history.git`. `hermes import` (the dashboard's import runs the same command) overwrites every file the archive holds and leaves the rest, so the history's ref went back to the backup's head. Every version recorded after the backup, the state right before the import included, dropped out of `log`, and `gc` later deletes it for good.

Real `hermes backup -o` → two more memory writes → `hermes import --force` → one more turn, on Hermes main:

| | 1.3.0 (`5f935c2`) | 1.3.1 (`b9af50b`) |
|---|---|---|
| `hermes memory-rewind log` after the import | 3 versions; both written after the backup are gone | 6 versions |
| Unreachable commits (`git fsck --unreachable`) | 2, pruned by `gc` later | 0 |
| The import itself | not visible | one version, `history restored from an older copy; later versions kept`, that `restore` can undo |

**Fix.**
- Each published head leaves an empty marker file under `plugin-data/memory-rewind/tips/`. A marker newer than the backup survives the import, and a marker the head does not contain names cut-off history.
- `log` includes such tips, and the next snapshot builds on the newest one, so the import is recorded as one change.
- A copy from an unrelated history (a backup from another machine) is joined as a second parent instead of dropped; `log` lists a join's changes against the first parent.
- The usual case (one marker, the head's own) costs a directory listing and no git call.
- It protects any import made after 1.3.1 has run once (a session start is enough), whichever version made the backup.

It also fixes the plugin page's link to the design notes. The page resolves relative links against `memory-rewind/`, so `docs/DESIGN.md` was a 404; the link is now absolute.

## 1.3.2: `restore` could replace a running agent's memory write

`restore` wrote `MEMORY.md`/`USER.md` without the memory tool's lock and never checked the file against the plan it had shown. Both cases on Hermes main, with the real `MemoryStore`:

| What happened | 1.3.1 | 1.3.2 |
|---|---|---|
| A memory write is in flight (`MemoryStore._mutate` holds the lock and has read the file) when the restore applies | prints `Done`; the agent's write then lands on top and the restored entry is gone | waits for the lock, sees the file changed since its plan, refuses; the agent's entry is kept |
| One entry is deleted (Star Map / `hermes journey delete`), the agent adds another, and the user restores the version before the delete | the plan says only `write memories/MEMORY.md`; the newer entry is removed without a word | the plan lists `brings back: Project Atlas uses Postgres 16` and `removes: Editor: Helix` |

**Fix.**
- Restore holds the memory tool's own lock while it checks and writes a memory file, waiting up to 10 s. The lock is `<file>.lock`: `flock` on POSIX, a one-byte `msvcrt` lock at offset 0 on Windows. It is the lock `MemoryStore._file_lock` takes on both v0.21.5 and main, and the one journey edits moved under for #119668.
- It refuses when any file the plan looked at changed since the plan was made.
- A lock error other than "held by someone else" fails at once instead of waiting.
- For `MEMORY.md`/`USER.md`, the plan lists the entries the restore brings back and the entries it removes, split the way the memory store splits them.

**Tests** (extending the existing files):
- Real `hermes backup` / `hermes import` end to end.
- Emulated imports: a backup made by 1.3.1 and by 1.3.0, unchanged files, an unrelated history, stale and foreign markers, and no git call in the usual case.
- A real in-flight `MemoryStore._mutate` during a restore.
- The lock held the way Hermes holds it: wait, give up, lock error.
- A memory file and a skill changed after the plan; the entry preview through the CLI.

**Verification.**
- **Old code:** on Hermes main the new end-to-end tests fail on the previous plugin code: `log` lacks the post-backup version, `DID NOT RAISE RestoreError`, and no preview lines.
- **Mutation** (Hermes main): 15/15 mutants killed for 1.3.1 and 14/15 for 1.3.2. The survivor drops the explicit unlock, which closing the descriptor also does on POSIX. It stays for Windows, where Hermes unlocks explicitly too.

**Scope note.**
- Skills are not locked during a restore: `skill_manage` keys its per-skill lock on an internal digest of the skill name, not a documented contract. The changed-after-plan check still covers them.
- Bringing back a single entry while keeping the rest is not in this PR. This PR makes the whole-file restore say what it removes.

## 1.3.0: changes made outside the agent's turns were credited to the next call or session

A version recorded after a tool call, or at turn end, took everything that had changed since the previous version and credited it to that call or session. Two cases, run end to end on Hermes main with real `AIAgent` turns (FakeLLMServer), `memory.write_approval: true`, and the functions the handlers themselves call. The output is `hermes memory-rewind log`:

| What happened | 1.2.0 (`e5b139b`) | 1.3.0 (`5f935c2`) |
|---|---|---|
| Turn 1 stages a memory `add`. `/memory approve` applies it (`handle_pending_subcommand`). Turn 2 stages a `remove`, which changes nothing | `after memory` · `via memory: remove (memory)` · `from telegram, session tg-session`, holding the approved **add** | `turn start`, with no `via` and no `from` |
| The curator archives a skill while no session runs (`_archive_as_curator`). A new session starts on Discord | `session start` · `from discord, session dc-session` | `session start`, with no `from` |

Same results on v0.21.5. The catalog's `memory-review` Desktop plugin exists to approve staged memory writes, so the first case is a real workflow.

**Fix.**
- Every turn now starts with a synchronous baseline on `pre_llm_call`, and the session-start baseline no longer names the session.
- Both baselines name no call and no session. They first let queued snapshots land, with a 5 s cap, so a queued version keeps its call's change.
- The `pre_llm_call` callback declares only `session_id` and `platform`. Hermes passes a narrow-signature callback only the fields it declares (`_hook_callback_kwargs`), so the plugin never receives the user message or the conversation. It returns `None`, so nothing is injected into the prompt.
- Cost is one no-change snapshot per turn: 43 ms median, 45 ms p90, on the 333-file default tree.

**Tests** (extending the existing files):
- The approve-between-turns and archive-between-sessions cases, through the real memory tool, the real approval flow and `skill_usage.archive_skill`.
- A queued version landing before the baseline.
- The narrow `pre_llm_call` signature.
- `pre_llm_call` running in a multiplexed profile's scope.

**Verification.**
- **Mutation:** 9/9 mutants killed on both v0.21.5 and main (dropping the flush, dropping the turn-start baseline, the session claim back, a wide or context-returning callback, and others).
- **Old code:** both new tests fail on the 1.2.0 plugin code, with `'after memory' == 'turn start'` and `[('s2', 'discord')] == []`.

**Scope note.**
- **Not `pre_tool_call`.** It would isolate each call exactly, but Hermes fails it closed: a slow or raising callback blocks the tool, and a history plugin must never block a memory write.
- **Not `on_skill_lifecycle`.** `archived` also fires inside a background-review `skill_manage` delete, with no session id, so a separate version there would take the change away from its call.
- **Known gap, documented in the README's Limits.** Snapshots after a call and at turn end still run in the background and land within a fraction of a second. A change something else makes in that window, or while a turn is running, still goes with that call or turn.
- **`requires_hermes` stays `>=0.21.5`.** A probe with a real `AIAgent` turn showed the same hook order and payloads on v0.21.5 and main: `on_session_start → pre_llm_call → pre_tool_call → post_tool_call → on_session_end`.

## Card: fit inside the plugin page header

The plugin page header renders `image` at full width with `max-height: 360px; object-fit: cover`. At viewports of 1200px and wider the header is 1134×360, so only rows 110–490 of a 1200×600 image are visible. On the `b747327` card, https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/plugins/memory-rewind cut off the title and clipped the last history line.

The redrawn card puts the title and tagline on one row and centres the content vertically, so every drawn pixel sits in rows 127–477. It is still 1200×600 and still the plugin's real `/memory-history` output. Same shape as #124991 / #124992.

Measured in Chrome on the live site, with the entry's image URL served from each file:

| Where | Viewport | Rows visible (of 600) | `b747327` | `e5b139b` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Plugin page header | 1200, 1280, 1440, 1920 | 110–490 | title and last line cut | all visible |
| Plugin page header | 1024 | 75–526 | all visible | all visible |
| Plugin page header | 768 | 6–594 | all visible | all visible |
| Plugin page header | 390 | all rows (3px off each side) | all visible | all visible |
| Catalog grid card (2:1 slot, #125538) | 1440, 390 | whole image | all visible | all visible |

The Desktop catalog card and detail view use a 2:1 frame (`aspect-[2/1]`), so they show the whole image either way.

## Checked

- `validate_plugin_catalog.py` with `ruamel.yaml==0.18.17`: 338 files valid at commits 3 and 4.
- Pinned-source validate at `b9af50b` and at `3549271`: `plugins validate --install-deps` passed, the security scan reported safe, and the self-updater gate is clean. Scanner findings are the same as at 1.3.0: one medium `python_subprocess` for the git call.
- Plugin CI 8/8 at both pins:
  - `b9af50b` ([run](https://github.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-memory-rewind/actions/runs/36380745016)): end to end 170 on v0.21.5 and on main; unit 155 on Linux and macOS, 150 on Windows.
  - `3549271` ([run](https://github.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-memory-rewind/actions/runs/36380961242)): end to end 182 on v0.21.5 and on main; unit 165 on Linux and macOS, 160 on Windows. The Windows skips are the existing six.
- Installing by name from this branch's catalog gives revision `3549271`, pinned, at 1.3.2. A real oneshot agent turn with the GitHub-pinned install records the memory write on v0.21.5 and on main.
- The README at both pins and the image URL return HTTP 200.
- No other open PR touches the `memory-rewind` entry.

![memory-rewind card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-memory-rewind/e5b139b1059a47df34002e76a7bfd84bc60d9f35/docs/card.png)

## Summary

Two Desktop/TUI session-management gaps, one small PR:

- **`session.archive` RPC** (#47168): the TUI gateway had no JSON-RPC equivalent of the Desktop `PATCH /api/sessions/{id}` archive flow, so TUI clients had to keep every session visible or delete it permanently. The new method sits next to `session.set_hidden` in `tui_gateway/methods_session.py` and mirrors its two-tier resolution: a live runtime id first (a not-yet-persisted draft defers via `pending_archived`, applied by `_ensure_session_db_row` exactly like `pending_hidden`), then a stored id/key resolved through the profile db — which covers the historical rows the `session.list` picker shows, the gap open PR #47184 was held open for. Wire contract declared in `tui_gateway/contracts/sessions.py` and rendered into the generated TS/OpenRPC catalog.
- **`inline_images=false` on history reads** (#116511): `_history_dict_text` has always had both image renderings, but `_coerce_message_text` hard-coded `image_urls=True` at both call sites, so a remote client re-read the sum of every attachment the conversation ever carried (26.30 MiB `session.resume` / 26.33 MiB per REST page read on the measured conversation, paid on every reconnect) with no way to ask for less. `session.resume` now accepts `inline_images` (default `true`) threaded through every path that carries messages — cold/lazy/eager resume and the live reattach via `_live_session_payload` — and `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages` accepts the same query param, routing content through the identical projection so both surfaces agree by construction. `false` renders `[image]` in place of the data URI; the default is byte-identical to before.

## Behaviour

- `session.archive {session_id | session_key, archived, profile?}` → `{archived, session_key}`; unknown id → 4001, missing id → 4006; archives the whole compression lineage (`SessionDB.set_session_archived`), messages kept.
- `session.resume {..., inline_images?: bool = true}` — `false` renders image parts as `[image]`; text/audio/other parts and non-image rows unchanged.
- `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages?inline_images=false` — same projection on the REST pages the Desktop hydrates over; default unchanged.

## Summary

Adds configurable **Reasoning level up / Reasoning level down** actions to Desktop's keyboard-shortcuts panel, stepping the active session's effort one notch through `off → minimal → low → medium → high → xhigh`.

- Two new Composer rows in the Ctrl+/ panel, shipped unbound (like dictation) so users pick their own chord — Alt+., Ctrl+Alt+↑/↓, Numpad +/-, etc.
- Stepping clamps at both ends and never crosses into `max`/`ultra`; those expensive tiers stay behind an explicit menu pick. Stepping *down* from one rejoins the ladder at `xhigh`.
- Session-scoped writes via the same `config.set reasoning` RPC the model menu uses — the global default is never touched. Without a live session, the composer draft still steps and no RPC is issued (the RPC would otherwise fall back to persistent profile config).
- Optimistic store update with rollback and a monotonic request sequence: rapid repeated presses can't have a slow earlier response revert a newer one, and the pill repaints immediately.
- A new `editableTargetPolicy: 'modified'` field on the keybind action opts it into firing while the composer is focused for any combo with a real modifier — including Alt/Numpad chords without a primary modifier, which the existing mod/ctrl rule never covered. Bare and shift-only rebinds stay with the input, so normal typing is never hijacked.
- Desktop only: the Ink TUI has no rebindable keybind registry (its handlers are hardcoded `useInput` chains), so there is nothing to register there yet.

Builds on the approach of the closed-unmerged #46174 (handler shape, editable-target policy, stale-response guard).

## Test plan

Behaviour-contract tests, verified red on base before the change:

- `npx vitest run --project ui src/lib/reasoning-step.test.ts` — ladder order, clamping, max/ultra exclusion, fallback resolution, session write shape and echo normalization (5 tests)
- `npx vitest run --project ui src/lib/keybinds/actions.test.ts` — registry rows unbound with English labels; editable-target policy allows modified combos and rejects bare/shift-only (9 tests)
- `npx vitest run --project ui src/lib/keybinds/combo.test.ts` — `actionAllowedInInput` fires the new actions from an editable target on Alt/Numpad/mod chords, never on bare keys (23 tests)
- `npm run typecheck` (apps/desktop) — 0 errors
- `npx eslint` on all touched files — clean
- Existing surfaces re-run green: find-bar keybind gate, terminal reveal-focus, contributed keybinds, settings subpages, i18n catalog completeness/languages

## Summary

OS drag-drop files were unconditionally staged into the gateway's attachments dir via `file.attach` — even when the gateway runs on the same machine and can read the dropped path directly. Local-mode users paid a duplicate disk copy per drop and lost the original path semantics (#52427).

- `partitionDroppedFiles` now takes an optional staging context (`remote` from the connection store, backend cwd, terminal backend). When the session's backend resolves this machine's paths as-is — a local connection on a non-container backend — a non-image OS drop keeps its original-path inline `@file:` ref, exactly like in-app project-tree drags.
- Drops that still need bytes keep the upload pipeline: remote gateways, container terminal backends (docker/ssh/…, #76577), Windows-host → POSIX-backend crosses (#15317), images (vision needs the bytes queued gateway-side), and path-less drops.
- The byte-vs-path decision (`attachmentPathNeedsUpload`) is extracted into `src/lib/attachment-upload-policy.ts`, now shared by the submit-time upload pipeline and drop-time routing so the two cannot drift.
- Applied across every drop surface: conversation area, composer form, contenteditable input, and the message-edit composer. Each reads the staging inputs at drop time; the wiring mirrors `uploadComposerAttachment`'s existing submit-time decision.

## What does this PR do?

Desktop file attachments stage into `<profile home>/attachments`, which sits outside the session workspace. An agent with a restricted workspace can then be unable to read the very files the user attached to it, and per-profile agents each have to be granted access to the shared Hermes-managed dir (#110662).

This adds a top-level `attachments.storage` config key:

- `hermes-home` (default, current behaviour): keep `<profile home>/attachments` — the directory container backends bind-mount, so `@file:` refs resolve in the sandbox (#76577).
- `workspace` (opt-in): stage into `<session workspace>/.hermes/attachments` — inside the allowed ref root, so the `@file:` ref stays workspace-relative and the profile's agent can always read its own attachments back.

The key is read **per profile** from the session's own `config.yaml` (`file.attach` runs before `prompt.submit` installs the profile scope, so the process config still belongs to the launch profile — the same reason as `_profile_configured_cwd`): one serve process can host an opt-in profile and a default profile side by side, each session following its own profile's config. A remote (ssh) profile keeps the profile home dir either way — its workspace lives on the execution host, and the bind-mounted home attachments dir is what container/remote backends receive. Workspace-boundary and path-traversal protections are unchanged: only the staging root moves, inside the allowed root.

## Related Issue

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/110662

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py`: new top-level `attachments.storage` key (`"hermes-home"` default) with user-facing comment docs.
- `tui_gateway/prompt_attachments.py`: `_session_home_dir` honours the opt-in for `attachments` — `_profile_attachments_storage` reads the session profile's config, `_session_attachments_workspace` returns the workspace only when it's a local, existing directory (ssh/remote cwds fall back to the profile home dir). Staging name sanitization and traversal checks untouched.
- `cli-config.yaml.example`: documented the new key with the two modes and the remote caveat.

## How to Test

1. Create a profile whose `config.yaml` sets `attachments.storage: workspace` and whose `terminal.cwd` is a workspace directory.
2. From Desktop, attach a file that lives outside the workspace (e.g. something from `~/Downloads`).
3. The staged copy lands at `<workspace>/.hermes/attachments/...`, and the `@file:` ref is workspace-relative (`.hermes/attachments/...`), so the agent reads it back without any extra allowlist.
4. A profile without the opt-in keeps staging into `<profile home>/attachments`; a profile bound to an ssh workspace does too.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — ran `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py` (653 passed, 0 failed) plus the config seed/migration suites
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26.6

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — pure `pathlib` path joins, no platform-specific code
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

## What does this PR do?

Adds `plugin-catalog/unbrowse.yaml`, the Unbrowse plugin for Hermes. It is submitted by the owner: I maintain Unbrowse and the `unbrowse-ai` org (catalog rule 5).

Unbrowse turns websites into APIs agents can call. The plugin registers 24 `unbrowse_*` tools: read a page as markdown, discover and run a learned site API, a cloud browser with saved logins that learns the route so later calls are browserless, credential requests, and usage. It also:
- registers an Unbrowse `web_extract` backend (`web.extract_backend: unbrowse`);
- adds one `pre_tool_call` guard that sends public-web `browser_*` / `web_extract` calls to Unbrowse. Local and private addresses pass, and `UNBROWSE_ALLOW_BUILTIN_BROWSER=1` turns it off.

It has no runtime dependencies (the MCP client is stdlib `urllib`), does not update itself, and talks only to `https://unbrowse.ai/mcp`.

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality). New catalog entry.

## Summary

The right-rail file browser's "Show gitignored files" eye toggle could never reveal entries the renderer's `ALWAYS_EXCLUDED` hygiene set dropped unconditionally — `out/`, `vendor/`, `coverage/`, `.DS_Store` and friends stayed invisible even in a project that explicitly opted in. Deny-by-default `.gitignore` layouts rely on exactly those names for real build output, which is what #55169 reports.

The fix splits the exclusion set instead of adding a new setting:

- `SHOW_IGNORED_EXCLUDED` is the reveal floor — the names both listing transports already strip (`FS_READDIR_HIDDEN` in the Electron bridge, `_FS_READDIR_HIDDEN` in the dashboard's `/api/fs/list`), so the tree keeps its `.git`/`node_modules`/build-dir hygiene in every mode.
- `readProjectDir` filters with that floor when the project is opted into showing ignored files; the existing `ALWAYS_EXCLUDED` pass plus the gitignore pass apply unchanged otherwise.

This reuses the existing per-project, connection-scoped persisted preference from #101065 — no new config key, no IPC or transport changes, no visual change.

## Behaviour

- Eye toggle off (default): unchanged — hygiene dirs and gitignored entries stay hidden.
- Eye toggle on: `out/`, `vendor/`, `coverage/`, `env`, `.DS_Store`, `Thumbs.db` etc. now appear, local and remote backends alike (both transports list them).
- VCS internals, dependency/build/cache dirs (`.git`, `node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `target`, …) remain excluded even when opted in — pinned by an existing test.

## Tests

- New: `reveals revealable hygiene entries (out, vendor, coverage) when the root opted in (#55169)` — proven red on base (fails against `origin/main`), green with the change.
- New: `keeps revealable hygiene entries hidden when the root has not opted in` — guards the default path.
- `npx vitest run src/app/right-sidebar/files/ src/app/right-sidebar/index.test.tsx src/store/review.test.ts` — 81 passed (the review store shares `isExcludedPath` and is unaffected).
- `npm run typecheck` (all projects) — passed.
- `npx eslint` on touched files — clean.

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/55169

## What does this PR do?

Bumps the `hermes-switchyard` pin from `22cd6bc` (v0.5.3) to `b3cf54676aa0244c55b448fe84a2eb93061d91a8` (v0.5.6). The new pin is the signed release commit of the published [v0.5.6 release](https://github.com/bgrablin/hermes-switchyard/releases/tag/v0.5.6). I am the plugin repository owner.

**Note on history:** I rewrote the plugin repository history on 2026-09-28 to remove unwanted example text. The `v0.5.3` tag now points to `2351efd`, the rewritten equivalent of the currently listed pin `22cd6bc`. The old commit can still be fetched by SHA for now, so current catalog installs keep working until this PR merges.

Commit range for review: [`v0.5.3...v0.5.6`](https://github.com/bgrablin/hermes-switchyard/compare/2351efd010310cd28372ac3202ce75601a6a5618...b3cf54676aa0244c55b448fe84a2eb93061d91a8) (115 commits). All of them are signed by `bgrablin`.

## Changes Made

`plugin-catalog/hermes-switchyard.yaml` only:

- `sha`, `docs_url` and `image` re-pinned to `b3cf546`; `version: "0.5.6"`.
- **Disclosure update (egress changed since 0.5.3).** The current entry says adaptive effort sends no user-message text; that is no longer true. The default-on adaptive `llm_request` sends up to 1,200 characters of the current user message after Hermes `redact_for_egress`. It sends no history or tool output. Greetings and thanks are decided locally with no call. Without the Hermes redactor it sends metadata only. Hosted skill routing now also uses `redact_for_egress` and stays local when the redactor is not available. Opt-outs are unchanged: `adaptive_reasoning_effort false` and `local_only`.
- **Capabilities:** adds the `post_llm_call`, `transform_llm_output` and `post_api_request` hooks that the plugin registers at this commit. Tools and middleware are unchanged.

## What changed in the plugin (0.5.3 → 0.5.6)

- Adaptive reasoning effort: `/reasoning` is the cap; delegated-task state is isolated; Jev gets bounded task semantics; the decision deadline defaults to 0.4 s and keeps your level on timeout.
- Visible receipt: one line after each foreground reply where the plugin did work, for example `switchyard: effort high→low · local (no Jev call)`. `transform_llm_output` adds the line, and the `llm_request` middleware removes it from later requests, so the model never gets it back. `post_api_request` reads token counts only, for the saved-token estimate.
- Egress changed from blocking to redacting (`redact_for_egress`), with a metadata-only fallback.
- Public DOM browser: stable element identity, confirmed typed values, and same-URL document replacement.
- v0.5.6 is content-only over v0.5.5 (example text, reason-code names, version). Runtime behavior is the same.
- No self-updating code; no Python dependencies; no required environment variables.

## How to Test

Checks at the pinned SHA (a fresh clone checked out at `b3cf546`), following `plugin-catalog-ci.yml`:

1. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` → `OK: 338 file(s) valid`.
2. `hermes plugins validate --install-deps --json <clone>` → `ok: true`, `warnings: []`. Declared tools, hooks and middleware all report "matches registrations", and the security scan reports `safe`.
3. Self-updater grep from the CI job → no matches.
4. The re-pinned `docs_url` and `image` URLs return HTTP 200.

Plugin-side evidence at the same SHA:

- The [release-candidate workflow](https://github.com/bgrablin/hermes-switchyard/actions/runs/36378819569) passed archive build, source verification, native Hermes loading, and Windows install of the candidate ZIP. That artifact is byte-identical to the release ZIP (SHA-256 `fc74bffe3d03ef71e4348fbd2feae8ad3d5f9248815867f5ec805ed1e988a71b`).
- The [compatibility workflow](https://github.com/bgrablin/hermes-switchyard/actions/runs/36379642616) passed on Ubuntu and Windows with Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13.
- The tag `v0.5.6` and commit `b3cf546` are both GitHub `verified: true`, `reason: valid`.

## Known limits

- Two proposed Jev features did not pass their frozen evaluations against the plugin-disabled and v0.5.4 baselines, so they are **not** in this release: [Research Navigator](https://github.com/bgrablin/hermes-switchyard/pull/132#issuecomment-5859656369) and [DOM Progress & Recovery](https://github.com/bgrablin/hermes-switchyard/pull/135#issuecomment-5859656659). bgrablin/hermes-switchyard#139 tracks the follow-up.
- The Hermes status bar shows the `/reasoning` level (the cap). The per-turn level appears in the receipt line.

## What does this PR do?

A background Bot Mode roster poll enumerates every saved connection, including expired remote gateways while Local is selected. Its cookie 401 path could open the Dashboard sign-in window over the active local workspace. This keeps roster authentication non-interactive. A failed saved source reports that it needs sign-in, while an explicit foreground sign-in still opens normally.

The non-interactive intent is scoped to the async roster enumeration, so concurrent foreground requests keep their existing login behavior. A Cloud silent cascade may still run in a hidden window, with a bounded timeout and no focus steal.

## Related Issue

No GitHub issue filed. Reported through support.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Security fix
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts`: scope roster reads as non-interactive, keep silent recovery hidden, and classify an OAuth auth rejection as needing sign-in.
- `apps/desktop/electron/oauth-rest-request.ts`: skip cookie 401 re-login and retry during background roster reads, preserving the existing foreground retry.
- `apps/desktop/electron/oauth-rest-request.test.ts`: cover background rejection, concurrent foreground recovery, and failed foreground login behavior.

1. Save an OAuth remote connection, let its session expire, select Local, and open Bot Mode. The roster may show that the saved source needs sign-in, but no login window should appear.

The Desktop app now ships the default browser driver: `browser_exec` works on a fresh Desktop install, offline, without a separate download.

## Infographic

![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aac31a3/KGkY_BnnTnpOJJsXdrZrT_yOm9djQx.png)

## Why it was missing

`browser_exec` ran the `browser-use` CLI from a PM side environment (`browser-use==0.13.10` in `<home>/environments/browser-use`), provisioned by the installers and `hermes update`. Sealed Desktop payloads skip that step (`_install_default_tools_after_update` returns early when `sealed()`), so the Desktop app never had it and silently fell back to the built-in browser tools. The side environment was also per-profile and 225 MB (93 MB of it `googleapiclient`).

The CLI's execution path is only `browser_harness.run.main()` (its module docstring: "Browser Use CLI backed by Browser Harness"); the browser-use agent framework and its anthropic/openai/google pins are never imported. `browser-harness` is 2.6 MB of MIT pure Python, and its pins (Pillow 12.3.0, websockets 15.0.1) already equal Hermes's own.

## Changes

- `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock`: `browser-harness==0.1.13` as a core dependency (adds `cdp-use`, `fetch-use`; exact pin exempted from `exclude-newer` like the others).
- `tools/browser_use_cli.py`: `_find_cli()` returns `[sys.executable, "-m", "browser_harness.run"]`. The child env sets `PYTHONPATH` to the harness's site dir, replacing whatever the agent inherited: the Desktop store interpreter boots with no venv to activate, and the harness daemon re-runs `sys.executable`.
- The side-environment provisioning goes: `install_cli`, the `hermes update` / installer step added in #125769, and the `--skip-browser` wording about it. `hermes tools post-setup browser_use_cli` now only checks the harness and points at `hermes update` on a miss.
- `scripts/smoke-payload.sh`: the relocated-payload smoke runs the harness on the store interpreter the same way, so a payload that cannot start the browser driver fails the release build.
- Docs: installation + browser pages.

## Validation

**Live repro:** real Linux x64 Desktop payload built from this branch (`native_build.py --prepare-only` + `--prepared`, 6.9 GB), moved to a path with a space, fresh `HERMES_HOME`, launched like the Desktop backend (store interpreter, `PYTHONPATH=<repo>:<site>`):

| | origin/main code in the payload | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `sealed()` | True | True |
| `_find_cli()` | `None` | `[<payload>/tools/python-3.14.7…/bin/python3, -m, browser_harness.run]` |
| Browser Use mode | off (built-in tools) | on |
| `browser_exec` on example.com | "The PM-managed browser-use CLI is not installed" | `{'url': 'https://example.com/', 'title': '🐴 Example Domain', …} (the harness prefixes its tab titles)` |

`scripts/smoke-payload.sh` under `unshare --net`: all published commands pass and `browser-harness on the store interpreter` prints `0.1.13`, then `SMOKE OK`.

Tests: `tests/tools/test_browser_use_harness.py` runs the real harness on `sys.executable -S` with a poisoned inherited `PYTHONPATH`/`PYTHONHOME` (red on origin/main: `_find_cli()` is `None`) and keeps the browser_exec child-env contract; 695 passed across the browser, tools-config, PM-closure and packaging-metadata suites.

Real payload builds on every Desktop target (`pm-bundle` dispatch, run 36381031101): darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, win32-x64, win32-arm64 all built and passed the relocated smoke including the harness check. The first Windows attempt exposed that browser-harness telemetry spawns a detached sender (the smoke now disables it the way Hermes's runtime env already does, `ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=false`).

Not covered: existing installs keep an orphaned `<home>/environments/browser-use` from the old provisioning.

Desktop test runs no longer leave their temp dirs behind in `TMPDIR`. Under Hermes, `TMPDIR` is `~/.hermes/cache/scratch`, so those leftovers were filling the scratch dir.

## What piled up (one dev host, one day)

- 688 `playwright-tracing-*`, 152 `playwright-artifacts-*`, and 75 `hermes-e2e-mock-*` sandboxes
- about 600 small dirs left by vitest tests (`handoff-result-*`, `hermes-compat-*`, `media-range-*`, `msix-roundtrip-*`, …)

## Root cause

Playwright, Electron, the backend and the sandboxes all create their temp dirs under `os.tmpdir()`, and several paths never remove them. `fix-electron-tracing.ts` orphans two stack-trace sessions per Electron launch, even on green runs. A failed or timed-out `setupMockBackend` never cleans up its sandbox. A killed run skips Playwright's exit cleanup. In the `electron` vitest project, 54 dirs are created by tests that never remove them.

## Changes

- `e2e/run-tmp.ts`, imported first by the main and core Playwright configs: gives each run one temp root that workers, Electron and the backend inherit through `TMPDIR`, and removes it when the runner exits. A SIGKILLed run now leaves one `pw-*` dir for the 24h pruner instead of dozens.
- `vitest.run-tmp.ts` (globalSetup in `apps/desktop/vitest.config.ts`): does the same for vitest runs.
- The update suite is untouched. Its seeded install is reused across runs (`HERMES_E2E_UPDATE_REUSE`) and bakes its path into AF_UNIX sockets.

This matches what #118725 did for pytest: one root per run, removed at the end, and killed runs left to the idle pruner.

## Validation

Every run below used `TMPDIR` pointed at an empty dir. The count is the entries left in that dir after the run. `node-compile-cache` and `playwright-transform-cache-1000` are persistent caches, excluded from the counts.

| Run | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `playwright test boot + sidebar-states` (6 passed) | 11 left (8 `playwright-tracing-*`, 3 `hermes-snap-*.sh`) | 0 |
| same with no display (`beforeAll` timeout) | 1 sandbox left | 0 |
| core: `onboarding-first-chat` + `boot-lifecycle` (3 passed) | n/a | 0 |
| `vitest run --project electron` | 54 left | 0 |

- While a run is in progress, everything lands inside `pw-XXXXXX` (`playwright-artifacts`, 8 × `playwright-tracing`, the mock sandbox, `hermes-snap-*`), and the dir is gone once the runner exits.
- vitest `electron` failures are the same set before and after (pre-existing, environment-only: packaging/MSIX/icon tests).

items.body:
A fresh NixOS or Home Manager install no longer logs "This config predates version 12 … can no longer be auto-migrated" at every gateway boot.

**Root cause:** the modules render `config.yaml` without `_config_version`. Hermes reads a missing key as version 0. In managed mode `save_config()` refuses to write `config.yaml`, so `migrate_config()` can never persist the stamp, and the post-update step warns again on each boot. `hermes config check` shows `Config version: 0 → 46 (update available)` on a brand-new install.

## Fix

`mkConfigFiles` (shared by both modules) now builds the generated config with the package's own interpreter and adds `DEFAULT_CONFIG["_config_version"]`. The stamp always matches the package it ships with; there is no hardcoded number to bump. An explicit `settings._config_version` still wins. A user-supplied `configFile` is installed unchanged.

Why not in Python: the unversioned-config path in `migrate_config()` already works (a88bef98b2), but in managed mode it cannot save. Checked directly with `HERMES_MANAGED=nixos`: `migrate_config()` prints "Cannot save configuration: this Hermes installation is managed by nixos" and the version stays `(0, 46)`. The module owns the file, so the module stamps it.

## Evidence

runNixOSTest VM (module + gateway, fresh `/var/lib/hermes`), same test against the parent commit and this branch:

| | parent `d4720b4ea8` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `_config_version` in `config.yaml` | absent | `46` |
| `hermes config check` | `Config version: 0 → 46 (update available)` | `Config version: 46 ✓` |
| "predates version 12" in `logs/*.log` | 1 line (`hermes_cli.post_update`) | 0 |

Also ran:
- New check `checks.x86_64-linux.generated-config-version`: it merges the generated config into an empty `HERMES_HOME` and asks the packaged `check_config_version()` whether the file is current. It passes on this branch and fails on the parent with `generated config.yaml reads as v0, package is v46`.
- `nixos-module`, `home-manager-module`, `home-manager-desktop`, `config-roundtrip`, `managed-guard`, `module-option-parity`, `cross-eval`: all build.
- A NixOS e2e lab (Matrix gateway DM round trip through the module) passes with this branch. The "predates" warning drops from 2 log lines to 0.

Written by Hermes Agent (claude-opus-5.5).

Adds a catalog entry for **antigravity-oauth** (`plugin-catalog/antigravity-oauth.yaml`), a `models` provider that runs Hermes on a Google Antigravity plan through the official `agy` CLI. I own the plugin repo: https://github.com/neerazz/hermes-antigravity-oauth

It builds on `antigravity-subscription-directsdk` (MIT, credited) and adds:

- **`hermes auth add|status|logout antigravity-oauth`** through `ProviderProfile.auth_handler`. `add` runs agy's own Google sign-in flow and confirms it with a live `agy models`. `status` does the same live check, which catches a stale keychain item. `setup_status` gates `hermes model`.
- **SOUL delivery.** The Hermes system prompt, which starts with `$HERMES_HOME/SOUL.md`, is written to agy's private workspace as `GEMINI.md`. agy loads that file as first-class rules. SOUL.md is prepended directly if the system prompt is missing it.

items.body:
Compaction fires at `compression.threshold` × window again (50% by default). The 256K token cap that #115986 made the default is back to opt-in. Fixes #117915, fixes #125235.

## The problem

- Since #115986, `compression.threshold_tokens` defaulted to `256000`. Compaction fires at whichever comes first, the ratio trigger or the cap, so every window above ~341K compacted at 256K.
- A 1M-window model compacted at 25% of its window. Setting `threshold: 0.8`, or a `model_thresholds` entry, changed nothing on those models, because the cap always came first (#117915).
- A fixed token count can't be the default: the same number means different things on a 64K, a 200K and a 1M window. Users who want a per-call cost ceiling can still set `threshold_tokens` themselves.

| Config (1M window unless noted) | Before (main) | After |
|---|---|---|
| no `compression` section | 256,000 | 500,000 |
| `threshold: 0.8` | 256,000 | 800,000 |
| `threshold_tokens: 256000` written by the template or `doctor --fix` | 256,000 | 500,000 (config v47 removes the value) |
| `threshold_tokens: 100000` | 100,000 | 100,000 |
| `threshold_tokens: null` | 500,000 | 500,000 |
| any of the above on a 200K window | unchanged | unchanged |

## What changes

- `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py`: `threshold_tokens` defaults to `None` (ratio only), as it did before #115986.
- `cli-config.yaml.example`: the `threshold_tokens` line is commented out again. The template is copied into `config.yaml` on first run and by `hermes doctor --fix`. An active value there looks like a user choice and freezes the default into the file.
- Config v47 (`hermes_cli/config_migrations.py`): removes `compression.threshold_tokens` only when it equals `256000`, the value the template wrote. Any other explicit cap stays, and so does an explicit `null`. It uses the same `_rewrite_stale_default` helper as the earlier default flips (v25, v32, v36, v44).
- Docs: the user guide, developer guide and delegation page describe the ratio as the default and `threshold_tokens` as an opt-in.

Kept from #115986: the model-switch warning quotes the trigger the compressor will actually use, and `_derive_trigger` is shared between the compressor and that warning. Both stay correct whatever the default is.

**Tradeoff:** a user who typed exactly `threshold_tokens: 256000` on purpose, before updating to v47, loses it once. To cap at 256K again they set it back; files already at v47 keep it (checked below).

## Live verification

A probe writes each config into a temp `HERMES_HOME`, runs `migrate_config()` (what startup and `hermes update` run), loads it through both real loaders (`load_config()` for the CLI, `load_user_config_effective()` for the gateway and TUI), parses it with `agent_init._parse_compression_config`, and builds a real `ContextCompressor` at 1M and 200K.

| Config (file at v46) | `989798cd5e` 1M / 200K | `cf2d3a92c3` 1M / 200K | `threshold_tokens` after migrate |
|---|---|---|---|
| no `compression` section | 256,000 / 150,000 | 500,000 / 150,000 | absent |
| seeded `threshold_tokens: 256000` | 256,000 / 150,000 | 500,000 / 150,000 | removed |
| `threshold: 0.8` | 256,000 / 160,000 | 800,000 / 160,000 | absent |
| `threshold_tokens: 100000` | 100,000 / 100,000 | 100,000 / 100,000 | kept |
| `threshold_tokens: null` | 500,000 / 150,000 | 500,000 / 150,000 | kept |
| `threshold_tokens: 256000` in a file already at v47 | — | 256,000 / 150,000 | kept |

Both loaders agree on every row. The 200K column is 150K because of the existing 75% minimum for windows under 512K, which this PR does not touch. Not exercised live: a running TUI session editing `config.yaml` mid-session. The hot-reload tests cover that path, and the only change it sees is the default value.

## Related PRs

With no default cap, there is nothing for a user-set ratio to yield to. That makes #119441, #119394, #117961 and #119247 unnecessary. I've left closing them to their reviewers.

items.body:
Desktop first-run and repair now run the installer script from the same ref the install stages use, so installer fixes on main actually reach an older Desktop build's repair.

This is a salvage of #125522 by @JoaoMarcos44. The commit is cherry-picked with authorship kept. It came out of the #125350 audit, where @andrexibiza's closure review flagged it as the remaining P1.

## Root cause

For an existing checkout, `runBootstrap` sets `pinCommit = false`, so the install stages follow the branch. `resolveInstallScript` still fetched `install.ps1`/`install.sh` from the old packaged commit. The result was that an old installer drove a newer checkout. Two fallbacks made this worse:
- A cached script was reused without refreshing.
- A failed download copied the checkout's own script into the requested commit's cache slot and reported it as that commit.

## Changes

- `resolveInstallScript` receives the same `pinCommit` decision:
  - fresh install: the packaged SHA for both the script and the stages;
  - existing checkout or all-zero fallback stamp: the branch for both.
- The script is downloaded on every run. The cache file is only this run's `-File` target.
- A failed download is fatal and Retry downloads again. The installed-checkout fallback is removed.
- This matches the standalone Hermes-Setup installer, which a maintainer made download-every-run and fail-closed in 274b412aa7 (#122025).
- Follow-up commit (ours): `cachedScriptPath`'s parameter is renamed to `cacheKey`, and the `downloadInstallScript` comment now describes the new ref policy.

## On keeping the fallback (@Enough1122's question)

The removed fallback read `<HERMES_HOME>/hermes-agent/scripts/install.*`. That is the same directory as `activeRoot` (`main.ts`: `ACTIVE_HERMES_ROOT = path.join(HERMES_HOME, 'hermes-agent')`), and `hasExistingGitCheckout(activeRoot)` checks it for `.git`.
- **The unpushed-HEAD case is covered.** A self-built app stamped to an unpushed HEAD, run with an existing checkout, now takes the branch path. It never asks GitHub for the unpushed SHA.
- **Offline repair failed before this PR too.** The repository stage always runs `git fetch origin +refs/heads/<branch>` on an existing checkout (`install.ps1` ~L769, `install.sh` ~L466), which fails without network. This PR makes it fail one step earlier, with a Retry that downloads again.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `electron/bootstrap-runner.test.ts` with main's `bootstrap-runner.ts` | 6 failed (the new ref/refresh/fail-closed tests) |
| same tests on this branch | 13 passed; with `bootstrap-quit.test.ts`, 15 passed |
| `tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json`, eslint | clean |

Review: a code reviewer and three /simplify-code reviewers (reuse, quality, efficiency) looked at it, with no blocking findings. The two naming points are applied in the follow-up commit.

Not done here:
- The pin check is spelled out three times (`installRefForStamp`, `buildPinArgs`, `buildPosixPinArgs`). Merging them into one resolver also changes the branch-argument default, so it belongs in its own change.
- The download URL is hard-coded to `NousResearch/hermes-agent`, while the stages honour `HERMES_REPO_URL`. That predates this PR.
- Nothing tests that `runBootstrap` passes `pinCommit` through. `runBootstrap` has no download injection point.

`main.ts` is untouched.

Related to #125350.

items.body:
A leftover `/steer` or interrupt text that becomes the next turn now keeps the channel prompt of the turn it follows. Before this change, that turn ran with `channel_prompt=None`, which dropped the Telegram group identity line / YAML `channel_prompts` / Slack identity from the system prompt, rebuilt the cached agent, and re-prefilled the whole conversation. The next human message flipped the prompt back and paid again.

Fixes #125763 (reported by @aidiffuser). Salvage of #125783 by @JoaoMarcos44: all four commits are cherry-picked with authorship preserved. The empty/None prompt matrix comes from the duplicate #125784 by @Wenfengcheng (credited via `Co-authored-by`).

## Change

- `gateway/run_turn.py::_run_agent_queued_followup`: when there is no `pending_event`, `next_channel_prompt = turn_ctx.channel_prompt`. This is the already-pinned value the finished turn ran with. Event-backed follow-ups still resolve their own prompt through `_pinned_channel_inputs`, so the #124179 behaviour is unchanged.
- Tests (`tests/gateway/test_internal_event_pin_wiring.py`):
  - one parametrized continuity test (leftover steer / interrupt text × `"Channel hint."` / `""` / `None`) drives the real drain → follow-up → next-human path through the real ephemeral-prompt combiner;
  - one negative control: a queued `MessageEvent` with its own prompt still overrides the inherited one.
- Our follow-up commit adds #125784's prompt matrix, drops two assertions that could never fail, and removes a trailing blank line that failed `git diff --check`.

Root cause: `next_channel_prompt` was initialised to `None` and only resolved inside `if pending_event is not None:`, while `context_prompt` and `source` were already carried over from `turn_ctx` on the same call.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_internal_event_pin_wiring.py` on this branch | 9 passed |
| Same tests with `origin/main`'s `run_turn.py` | 4 failed: both leftover kinds, for `"Channel hint."` and `""`. The `None` rows pass on both, as expected |
| Mutation: assign `turn_ctx.channel_prompt` unconditionally after the event branch | negative control fails (`'Inherited prompt.' == 'Queued event prompt.'`) |
| 15 gateway/plugin test files that reference these symbols | 237 passed; the 11 failures also fail with `origin/main`'s production file (local env, unrelated) |
| ruff, windows-footguns, compat-pointers, `git diff --check` | clean |

Regression review: the eventless path reuses the finished turn's `source` and `session_key`, so the inherited prompt always belongs to the same chat/thread. Every platform builds `channel_prompt` from the channel, not the sender, so a different group member's steer gets the prompt their own event would have carried. The Telegram observed-group-context history split (`_build_gateway_agent_history`) now also matches the parent turn, so observed chatter is no longer replayed as ordinary user turns on these follow-ups.

Out of scope, not changed here: the restart pin gap (#125793 / #125832), and non-internal synthetic events such as heartbeat due-prompts that store `None` as the channel pin.

items.body:
A live gateway's identity files survive an identity mismatch, its persisted record names its entry point under the inline launcher, and a held `gateway.lock` without `gateway.pid` no longer aborts the Windows update pause gate.

## Root cause (one sentence)

Three readers of gateway identity still assumed "the argv matcher rejected it, so it is stale": the unscoped `get_running_pid()` cleanup unlinked a HELD lock, the persisted record under the published `bin/hermes` launcher carried `["-c", "gateway", "run"]` (no entry point to match), and the strict Windows gate raised on a held lock whose PID file the updater's own `--replace` had removed.

## Changes

- `gateway/status.py::get_running_pid` — while the runtime lock is held, a live recorded PID is never cleanup-unlinked on the unscoped path either (was: scoped only). A held lock is a gateway's whatever its command line reads as; unlinking it left the holder on a deleted inode and the next starter double-ran. Dead records and inactive-lock metadata still take the #89315 poison-file cleanup. **Fixes #125610**, salvages #125679 by @JoaoMarcos44 (its `get_running_pid` hunk + invariant test; the Windows command-line splitter and `ast` argv parser are not carried — every Hermes launcher form already resolves to `run` on main since 60e531cb52, verified with the real producers below).
- `gateway/status.py::_record_argv` — `_build_pid_record` persists the entry module's path in place of `-c` (runpy's `alter_sys` convention, what the store launcher and `--run-module` forms already record), so `gateway.pid` / `gateway.lock` / `gateway_state.json` written by a `python3 -I -c "<launcher script>" gateway run` gateway read as `hermes_cli/main.py gateway run` in the record fallback (`_record_matches_live_gateway_pid` when the live cmdline is unreadable). **Fixes #124029**, **Fixes #123151** — the live-cmdline half of both landed in #124965 (60e531cb52); this closes the record half @rhacius measured on the merged code.
- `gateway/status.py::get_running_pid_identity_strict` — when `gateway.pid` is absent beside a HELD lock, the lock's own record is validated against the live process (live PID, start-time agreement, live command line is a gateway's) instead of raising `active gateway lock has no PID metadata`. **Fixes #123430** (the `--replace` relaunch force-unlinks the old `gateway.pid`, gateway/run.py; the next `hermes update` died in its first second at `_pause_windows_gateways_for_update` until the operator rebuilt the PID file by hand — @nguyencuong102tg's recovery).

## Already fixed on main (no code here; recorded for the closes)

- #122495 — Windows `hermes update` pause-gate false negative on the inline-bootstrap gateway: fixed by #124965 (60e531cb52); reporter-side confirmation on the filing host by @yakold (CLI + Desktop paths). PRs #122619, #123131, #123276, #123169 are superseded by #124965.
- #123490 — PM relaunch `-c` wrapper invisible to `find_gateway_pids` / `_wait_for_gateway_ready`: fixed by 60e531cb52; `gateway_spawn_intent_subcommand` also resolves the bootstrap forms to `run` now. PR #123575 (control-socket fallback in the readiness poll) addresses a symptom the matcher fix removed.
- #123463 — strict identity rejects the live bootstrap-launched gateway: matcher half by 60e531cb52; the residual @sydamirrr traced (1 s dashboard poll deleting `gateway.pid` via the unscoped cleanup) is the first change in this PR.

## Not changed: #113206 (deliberate design)

`_apply_profile_override` skipping the sticky `active_profile` under a supervisor marker is the #74872 guard (b0acc558b1c) and applies to every child of the supervised gateway (kanban/relay/delegate workers inherit `HERMES_SUPERVISED_CHILD`), not only `gateway run`; narrowing it to `gateway run` as #113279 proposes would let the default gateway's own workers follow the sticky pointer into another profile — the credential-adoption class the guard exists for. Under the multiplex-only ruling (a20a88398f8) `gateway restart`/`stop` target the one host multiplexer and print its owner, so the "wrong unit restarted" symptom is designed away on migrated hosts. Left for a maintainer call; no `Fixes`.

## WHEN × WHERE

Process identity is the "storage identity" row of the profile-scope table: `(pid, start_time)` + canonical cmdline matchers, never argv substrings. Rows L6 (dashboard/status routers poll `resolve_gateway_liveness` → `get_running_pid_cached` → the unscoped cleanup) and the install/update path; topologies T4 (systemd `ExecStart=<repo>/.hermes/bin/hermes gateway run`, the launcher-script shape), T6 (launchd, same launcher), T10 (Windows task / updater `--replace` relaunch). Standalone T1 and the multiplexer T2/T3 both go through `get_running_pid` and the record writer.

## Validation

| Item | Test | origin/main (5912ed81ed) | head |
|---|---|---|---|
| #125610 / #123109 class | `tests/gateway/test_status.py::TestGatewayPidState::test_unscoped_live_identity_mismatch_never_unlinks_active_files` | FAIL (pid+lock unlinked) | pass |
| #124029 / #123151 record half | `tests/gateway/test_status.py::test_pid_record_names_the_entry_point_under_an_inline_launcher` | FAIL (`argv[0] == "-c"`, `_record_looks_like_gateway` False) | pass |
| #123430 | `tests/gateway/test_status.py::test_strict_gateway_identity_adopts_held_lock_when_pid_file_is_gone` | FAIL (`RuntimeError: active gateway lock has no PID metadata`) | pass; a recycled PID (start-time drift) is still refused |
| matcher premise | scratch probe feeding the REAL producers (`_launchers.runtime_command`, `_launcher_script`, `venv_sync.relaunch_command`, argv with `O'Brien, Inc`, restart-watcher control) through `_gateway_command_subcommand` in shlex / space-joined / list2cmdline forms | every Hermes form → `run`, watcher → `None`; only the record fallback (`["-c","gateway","run"]` → False) was red | record fallback green |

`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_status.py tests/gateway/test_gateway_inline_bootstrap_identity.py tests/gateway/test_gateway_command_line_matcher.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_windows.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_cmd_windows.py`: see the CI run; ruff / `check_no_tmp_literals` / `check_compat_pointers` / `git diff --check` / `audit_pr_attribution --fix` clean.

Not run: the `wine2e/**` live Windows gate for the #123430 atom (Linux host; the strict reader is exercised up to its Windows-only psutil tail).

## Infographic

DEGRADED: image generation unavailable in this lane (fal.ai balance exhausted at generation time); style picked was `demoscene-cracktro` / bento-grid.


## Review fixes

- **MAJOR — `gateway/status.py::get_running_pid` (unscoped branch) re-opened #89315**: fixed. The two rejections are distinct now — a SAME-home record the cmdline matcher rejects keeps both files (#125610 intent), while a live record whose `hermes_home` conflicts with the process home unlinks the poisoned `gateway.pid` only (`_cleanup_invalid_pid_path(unlink_lock=False)`); the held `gateway.lock` is never unlinked. Scoped polls keep #106406 (no unlink while a PID is live). `tests/hermes_cli/test_cross_profile_kill_refusal.py` is untouched and green again (it was the only red in the Python tests job); new invariant `tests/gateway/test_status.py::TestGatewayPidState::test_unscoped_live_cross_home_pid_file_is_unlinked_but_held_lock_stays` was red on the PR head. SIGTERM half re-verified: `stop_profile_gateway()` returns False and the other profile's process survives.
- **MINOR — `_record_argv` keys on `sys.modules['hermes_cli.main']`**: follow-up (see below). Under the published launcher `hermes_cli.main` is imported inside `python -c <script>`, so `__main__` is never `hermes_cli.main` there and that key cannot distinguish the launcher from an exec-form child.

## Reviewer follow-ups

- `gateway/status.py::_record_argv`: the `-c` → entry-module substitution keys on `sys.modules['hermes_cli.main']`, so a `runtime_command(code=...)` exec-form child that merely imported `hermes_cli.main` is recorded as `hermes_cli/main.py <args>`. Keying on `__main__` does not work (the launcher imports, not runs, `hermes_cli.main`); a correct key needs the launcher to stamp its own entry (e.g. an env/`sys` marker set by `_launcher_script`) — out of this PR's LOC budget.
