items.title: Served profiles no longer inherit the launch profile's logs, log ownership, slash gating, TTS credentials or skipped .env (#125974 #120151 #121705 #120481 #125530)

items.body:
Dashboard actions, sign-ins, model recommendations and the profile switcher now act on the profile the request names, and the gateway liveness check accepts an explicit `--profile default`.

## Per issue

- Fixes #120688 — `_profile_cli_args("default")` returned `[]`, so a hub action scoped to `profile=default` from a `-p worker serve` dashboard spawned a selector-less child that landed on `worker`'s home. `default` is now a real named target (`["-p", "default"]`), and unnamed gateway verbs from the default home name it too. Salvages #120689 by @beardthelion (tests trimmed to two invariants; the token-scrub assertion no longer holds since `host_gateway_child_env()` builds the `-p default gateway` env).
- Fixes #123616 — `_env_write_errors(http_passthrough=False)`, the learning-graph and plugins-hub catch-alls turned the scope's 404 into a 500; the same class in cron delivery-targets/blueprints, voice config, debug share, official skills and the non-Nous recommended default. Salvages #123617 by @jonpol01.
- Fixes #123980 — the Nous/MiniMax/xAI pollers looked the profile up by session id after the provider answered, so a cancel or the 15-minute sweep made `_profile_scope(None)` save the tokens into the launch profile; MiniMax and xAI had no locked cancel check. The pollers take `sess["profile"]` and check `cancelled` under the session lock (the Codex saver takes the scope before the lock, matching the others). Salvages #123982 by @jonpol01.
- Fixes #124283 — the `slug == "nous"` branch of `/api/model/recommended-default` returned before `_config_profile_scope(profile)`; now inside it, and an unknown profile is the scope's 404. Salvages #124284 by @jonpol01 (test fixture rewritten onto the hermetic home; the non-Nous passthrough came in via #123617).
- Fixes #125025 — `ProfileProvider` synced state→URL and URL→state in two effects, so `navigate("/skills?profile=beta")` (path AND param change) had the URL-writer run with the old state and rewrite `profile=alpha`. The URL param is adopted during render before any effect. Salvages #125026 by @Adolanium.
- Fixes #96712 — `shouldAdoptActiveProfile()` aligned the switcher to the machine-global sticky `active_profile` whenever it differed from the serving profile, so a dashboard hosted by a named profile (`hermes -p demo serve`) retargeted its banner, chat env and model to another agent on every load. Only the default-hosted machine dashboard aligns; `custom` never does. Salvages #96736 by @ipriyaaanshu (re-applied at the helper that replaced the inline condition).
- Fixes #100817 — `gateway/status.py::_command_line_belongs_to_profile` and its sibling `hermes_cli/gateway.py::_matches_current_profile` rejected any `-p/--profile` flag on the default-home branch, so a default gateway started with `--profile default` (hand-written launchd plist) showed as stopped. Only a flag naming ANOTHER profile disqualifies. Salvages #100888 by @Sahilvishnaliya (rebuilt on the `profile_flag_value()` matcher main uses now).
- #92520 (Hindsight settings written into the launch profile) is already fixed on main: the SPA sends `?profile=` for the `/api/memory` family since 6a3dcc39ab0 and the routes run in `scoped_to_thread(profile, …)` (76c063b3d97), so `provider.save_config(values, get_hermes_home())` lands in the selected profile's home. No change here; the parent closes it.

## WHEN × WHERE

L6 (dashboard routers / SPA scope) on T3 (dashboard hosted by a named profile) and T7 (pooled Desktop/dashboard `serve`); L5 (child processes: hub-action argv/env) on T3; the `--profile default` matcher is process identity on T6 (launchd) / T4.

## Validation

| Item | Red on origin/main | Green on head |
|---|---|---|
| #120688 | `test_hub_install_scoped_to_default_still_carries_the_selector`, `test_unnamed_lifecycle_verbs_from_default_home_always_name_default` both fail (argv `[]`) | pass; hub install from a `worker_alpha`-hosted dashboard with `profile=default` spawns `-p default` and pins `HERMES_HOME` to the default home |
| #123616 | `test_unknown_profile_is_the_scopes_404` 8/8 fail (500) | 8/8 pass (404 naming the profile) |
| #123980 | `test_dashboard_poller_saves_only_into_the_profile_the_login_started_in` 4/4 fail (saved into launch home / after cancel) | 4/4 pass: `coder` login saves into `coder`, cancelled login saves nowhere (both providers, cancel + expire) |
| #124283 | `test_nous_recommendation_reads_the_requested_profile` fails (`free_tier False` for the free profile) | passes: launch paid, `freebie` free, unknown 404 |
| #125025 | vitest `adopts ?profile= from a link that also changes the path` fails (settles on `alpha`) | passes; `/skills?profile=beta` ends on `beta` |
| #96712 | vitest `keeps a named-profile dashboard on its own profile` fails | passes; `demo`/`custom` hosts never adopt the sticky profile |
| #100817 | `test_command_line_belongs_to_profile_accepts_explicit_default` fails | passes; `-p coder` still rejected |

`web/`: `npx tsc -b` clean, `vitest run` 356/356. Python: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli tests/gateway` (see thread for the summary line), `ruff check`, `check_no_tmp_literals.py`, `check_compat_pointers.py`, `git diff --check` clean.

## Infographic

DEGRADED: not generated — `image_generate` refused with "Exhausted balance" at the image provider during this lane.


## Changed existing tests

Two pre-existing tests pinned the bare `["gateway", "restart"]` argv on the shared dashboard restart spawn site (`_restart_gateway_after` → `_spawn_gateway_restart` → `_gateway_subcommand(None, "restart")`). The #120688 fix deliberately makes that site emit `["-p", "default", "gateway", "restart"]` from the default home (`_own_profile_selector` names the default home `"default"`, `_profile_cli_args("default")` emits the selector), so a child can never re-read the sticky `active_profile` and restart another profile's gateway. Each assertion was updated to the new argv only; the tests' subjects are unchanged.

| Test | Old assertion | New assertion | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_dashboard_admin_endpoints.py::TestWebhookEndpoints::test_enable_platform_starts_gateway_restart` | `restart_calls == [(["gateway", "restart"], "gateway-restart")]` | `restart_calls == [(["-p", "default", "gateway", "restart"], "gateway-restart")]` | `POST /api/webhooks/enable` auto-restart now names the default home explicitly; the save-is-authoritative / `restart_started` + pid contract is untouched. |
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server.py::TestWebServerEndpoints::test_telegram_onboarding_apply_reports_restart_failure_after_save` | `subcommand == ["gateway", "restart"]` (inside the failing-spawn stub) | `subcommand == ["-p", "default", "gateway", "restart"]` | Telegram onboarding apply auto-restart, same spawn site; the "failed spawn is reported after the save, not raised" contract is untouched. |

`hermes -p default gateway restart` is accepted by `hermes_cli/gateway.py`: `_apply_profile_override` pins `HERMES_HOME` to the root and skips `active_profile`, `profile_lifecycle` and `_guard_named_profile_under_multiplexer` both pass `default` through (no exit 78, no second gateway), and the CLI's own multiplex refusal text prescribes exactly that argv as the host remedy. No other test under `tests/` asserts a bare `["gateway", ...]` argv produced by these spawn sites (remaining hits are mocks, hand-built argv, or `[-2:]` suffix checks that still hold).


## Behaviour change

Hub actions targeting the **default** profile from the machine (default-hosted) dashboard — skills install/update/uninstall, MCP install, toolset post-setup — now run with the same scrubbed, pinned environment every named-profile action gets (`_profile_cli_args("default")` → `["-p", "default"]` → `_profile_action_environment`'s named-target branch: `build_subprocess_env(scrub_secrets=True)`, dotenv/managed keys dropped, `HERMES_HOME` pinned to the default home) instead of the historical verbatim `os.environ` copy. Consequence: secrets that reach the dashboard *only* through its process environment (systemd `Environment=`, `op run`, a shell export that is not in `.env`) no longer reach those children; the child loads the default profile's own `.env` and secret sources at startup. This is deliberate and kept: one env contract for every hub target means the default profile cannot be the one target that silently inherits whatever the dashboard's supervisor had in its environment, and matches the documented scope rule (target profile's `.env` + secret sources). Gateway verbs are unaffected (`host_gateway_child_env`). Documented in `web-dashboard.md` § Managing multiple profiles.

## Review fixes

- `web_server_profiles.py::_profile_cli_args` → `web_server_gateway.py::_profile_action_environment` (default-target hub actions take the scrubbed/pinned branch; unstated behaviour change) → **kept the consistent env, stated under `## Behaviour change` above**, plus one docs paragraph in `website/docs/user-guide/features/web-dashboard.md` that hub actions run with the target profile's own secret scope, not the dashboard process environment.
- `web_routers/profiles.py::get_active_profile_endpoint::_or_default` (exception fallback `"default"` is exactly the `current` value that lets `shouldAdoptActiveProfile` adopt the sticky profile) → **fixed**: the `current` read's *failure* fallback is now `"custom"` (adoption-refusing); the empty-value case keeps `or "default"`, and `active` keeps `"default"` on failure — a `"custom"` there would itself trigger adoption of a non-existent profile when `current == "default"`. No existing test covers `_or_default`; verified with an off-tree probe (both raise → `{"active": "default", "current": "custom"}`; both empty → both `"default"`).

items.body:
After the package-manager takeover, `hermes update` now brings back a dashboard that was started by hand. If it cannot bring a dashboard back, the receipt books it as `failed` (receipt `partial`, exit 1) instead of `restarted` / `success`.

## Changes

| Issue | Root cause (origin/main) | Fix | From | E2E gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #124778 | `hermes_cli/main_dashboard.py::_respawn_dashboard_processes` replays the stopped dashboard's `/proc` argv verbatim: `[<old venv python>, ~/.local/bin/hermes, dashboard, …]`. The takeover has already rewritten that launcher into a shell shim, so the child dies with `SyntaxError`. Because `Popen` itself succeeded, the updater still prints `✓ restarted`. | A `python + hermes-launcher` argv is rebuilt on `_launchers.runtime_command`, the installation-bound launcher every other Hermes spawn uses (store Python + bootstrap). The checkout's own `hermes` entry is left unchanged. A child that exits within 1 s is reported as a failed restart. | #124797 (@liuhao1024); the launcher swap is ours | `DASHBOARD_GATES["n1"]`: #124778 entry removed |
| #109290 | `hermes_cli/update_inventory.py::match_runtime_outcomes` has no input for a failed respawn. The incarnation probe reads "pre-update pid gone" as `restarted`, and `update_cmd_fleet.py` drops the `unrecovered` PIDs from `_refresh_dashboard_after_update`. | `_refresh_dashboard_after_update` returns the PIDs it stopped and could not bring back. They read `failed` before the probe runs and set `restart.incomplete`, which gives receipt `partial` and exit 1. A failed respawn reports the caller's argv, so it matches the stopped PID's cmdline. | #109298 (@liuhao1024), ported onto the moved code | `FALSE_SUCCESS_GATE` removed |
| #123109 | Already fixed on origin/main by #124965 (`60e531cb52`, `inline_bootstrap_argv`): `_gateway_command_subcommand` reads the bootstrap launcher's argv. | None needed. The stale gate is removed. | #123131 is superseded by #124965 | `PID_FILE_GATE` removed; the cell passes on origin/main in both columns |

Unit tests added:
- 1 for receipt reconciliation.
- 2 for the respawn: the argv rebuild, and an instant death counted as a failure and reported with the caller's argv.

## Validation

E2E suite `tests/e2e/core/upgrade/handoff`, run locally under bwrap with the gates removed:

| Cell | n1 on origin/main | n1 on this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `test_update_exit_status_matches_what_came_back` | FAIL `the update exited 0 though the dashboard did not come back` | PASS |
| `test_dashboard_is_back_on_its_port` | FAIL `the respawned dashboard died parsing its launcher … SyntaxError` | PASS |
| `test_gateway_pid_file_and_status_find_the_relaunched_gateway` | PASS | PASS |
| all 7 cells | 5/7 | 7/7 |

- **Head column:** 7/7 on origin/main. The only red on this branch came from a cron change that has since been dropped (see below).
- **Why the N-1 gates come off now:** the dashboard respawn runs in HEAD's code even in the N-1 column, because `_finish_dashboard_update_cleanup` runs in the updated checkout.

**#113293 is not in this PR.** An update-lock deferral in `cron/scheduler_tick.py` (#111842's approach) made the head column red. A one-shot that comes due during an update more than `ONESHOT_GRACE_SECONDS` (120 s) long is retired as missed by `cron/jobs.py::_retire_expired_oneshot` before the first post-update tick (E2E: `the job due mid-update ran 0 times`, `cron job: null`). Deferring needs a grace policy for jobs that come due while an update holds the install; that is a product decision, so `CRON_GATES` is unchanged.

Fixes #124778
Fixes #109290
Fixes #123109

items.body:
`hermes update` works again on shallow, stale and partial-clone checkouts: a stale depth-1 install no longer times out downloading the whole history, a full clone stays a full clone, a `--depth` pre-fetch no longer triggers a false orphan-divergence reset, and git's partial-clone `should_include_obj` crash no longer blocks every update.

## What changed

| Issue | Root cause on `origin/main` | Fix | From | E2E cell |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #122353 | `hermes_cli/gitlock.py::fetch_full_commit_graph` always passed `--filter=tree:0`, and `git fetch --filter` writes `remote.origin.promisor`/`partialclonefilter`, which turns a full clone into a partial clone | the tag fetch reuses the clone's own filter: a partial clone repeats its filter, a full clone fetches unfiltered | #122430 (@dskwe), commits 1–2 | `test_partial_clone.py::…[full]`, gate removed |
| #124272 | git 2.53+ `index-pack --promisor` → `repack_local_links` BUG()s in pack-objects on a local object that leads to a promisor-missing one. The state stays in the repo, so every fetch in `update_cmd.py::_cmd_update_impl` and `update_cmd_check.py::fetch_compare_branch` dies | on exactly that crash signature, retry once with `-c remote.origin.promisor=` (per invocation, config untouched) | #124293 (@dskwe) | `test_shallow_install.py::test_second_update_after_the_unshallowing_update_succeeds`, gate removed |
| #123254 | `update_cmd.py::_cmd_update_impl` ran a plain `git fetch origin main` from a depth-1 clone: the server sends ~the whole history, which cannot finish inside the 300 s cap, and the unshallow only ran after a successful update | before the fetch, `gitlock.heal_shallow_history` unshallows a shallow checkout (commits only, 900 s budget, branch refspec included), through the same `fetch_full_commit_graph` | #123312 (@kokhlo) | `…::test_stale_depth1_install_updates_without_fetching_the_whole_history`, gate kept: N-1's pre-swap fetch (see below) |
| #123346 | a `git fetch --depth 1` pre-fetch grafts `origin/main`, `merge-base` fails, `_reconcile_diverged_checkout` resets as orphan divergence | the same pre-fetch heal unshallows the checkout before the pull. A grafted full clone already has its history locally, so it unshallows unfiltered and stays full | #123312 mechanism. #123476 / #123727 fix the same symptom after the fact (see below) | `…::test_depth1_prefetch_never_turns_shared_history_into_orphan_divergence`, gate removed |
| #124645 | `gitlock.py::prune_stale_shallow_grafts` drops grafts, but the remote-tracking reflog still names the old fetch tips, so the `--reflog` fail-safe walk fails and the prune rolls back every time | expire only the `refs/remotes/*` reflogs that name a dropped graft (HEAD and branch reflogs are never touched). The pre-fetch heal also unshallows before the pull | #124671 (@liuhao1024) | `…::test_passive_checks_do_not_push_the_next_update_into_orphan_divergence`, gate kept: N-1's check/pull code |

Our commits on top:
- `fetch_full_commit_graph` takes extra refspecs, and the heal is one line on top of it. There is one clone-mode rule: a partial clone keeps its filter, a full clone stays unfiltered, and only a depth-limited clone whose history is really missing (`_batch_missing_parents` on the shallow lines) unshallows as `tree:0`.
- Recovery wiring keeps the fetch's `network=True` cap and the check path's tracking refspec. The contributor branch predated both.
- The timeout text no longer claims "no response from the remote". There is no new classifier rule that would claim the opposite ("not a dead remote").
- Unit tests trimmed to two invariants per fix.

## Not taken, and why
- #122430 commit 3 (`-c remote.origin.promisor=true … --filter=tree:0` on every fetch) leaves a non-promisor repo with commits whose trees are missing. That is a corrupt repo for `gc`/`fsck`/history walks. Dropped.
- #123727 / #123476 (unshallow and re-test after `merge --ff-only` fails): once the pre-fetch heal lands, a shallow checkout never reaches the pull, so this second unshallow would only be defense-in-depth. #123476 also bundles unrelated shell-hook, terminal-notify and watchdog commits. The fixture of the #123727 unit test is reused for the heal's #123346 test.
- #125288 (print the git binary and repo on fetch failure) is a diagnostics change for #125138, not a fix for any issue here. It is left alone.

## Validation

Real `hermes update` over smart HTTP (`tests/e2e/core/upgrade/git/`), run locally:

| Cell | `origin/main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| partial_clone `[tree0]`, `[blobless]` | pass | pass |
| partial_clone `[full]` (#122353) | XFAIL | **pass** |
| shallow second update (#124272) | XFAIL | **pass** |
| shallow `--depth` pre-fetch (#123346) | XFAIL | **pass** |
| shallow stale depth-1 fetch size (#123254) | XFAIL | XFAIL (N-1 code), N-1 proof not obtained |
| shallow passive checks (#124645) | XFAIL | XFAIL (N-1 code), N-1 proof not obtained |

The last two cells fail inside N-1's own updater (the fetch and the check/pull run before the hand-off to HEAD), so they flip once a release carrying this fix becomes N-1. An N-1-override proof was attempted (`HERMES_E2E_N1_REF` = v2026.9.24 plus a hand port of the heal and the reflog-expiring prune, commit `6184ff9`). It did not apply: `scripts/run_tests.sh` does not forward `HERMES_E2E_N1_REF` (it is not in its env allowlist), so the run installed plain v2026.9.24 and only re-confirmed N-1 as red. Both gates stay.

Unit: `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_shallow_heal.py`, `test_tag_fetch_partial_clone.py`, `test_gitlock.py`, `test_shallow_graft_prune.py`, `test_shallow_boundary_repair.py`. `test_shallow_graft_prune.py::test_update_check_prunes_and_reports_count` fails identically on `origin/main` in a `.worktrees/` checkout (home-I/O guard on `.worktrees/manifest.json`), so it is unrelated.

Fixes #122353
Fixes #123254
Fixes #123346
Fixes #124272
Fixes #124645

Salvages #122430 and #124293 (@dskwe), #123312 (@kokhlo), #124671 (@liuhao1024), with authorship preserved. It supersedes #123727 (@Sahilvishnaliya) and #123476 (@WYSTAF), whose #123346 fix is covered by the pre-fetch heal.

## Infographic

Not generated: the image backend refused (account balance exhausted). Degraded, to be added.

items.body:
Kanban workers boot on store-Python / PM installs, unknown assignees leave a board trace, PR acceptance reads GitHub as the card's assignee profile, and a dead credential at worker startup exits terminal instead of burning the retry budget.

## Per issue

- Fixes #122299, fixes #122487, fixes #122500 — `hermes_cli/kanban_db_dispatch.py::_default_spawn` now pins the running install's root on the worker env's `PYTHONPATH` whenever the module argv (`sys.executable -m hermes_cli.main`) is chosen, via cron's existing `pin_hermes_tree_on_pythonpath` (#112729). Root cause in one sentence: `_resolve_hermes_argv`'s `find_spec("hermes_cli")` answers a question about the GATEWAY (where the launcher bootstrap injected the repo root into `sys.path`), while the worker env scrub strips Hermes-owned `PYTHONPATH` entries from the CHILD, so the bare interpreter died with `ModuleNotFoundError: hermes_cli`. `hermes_cli.main` → `hermes_bootstrap` → `activate_dependencies` then selects the committed PM dependency generation in the child, so a store Python with an empty `site-packages` boots too. A resolved shim path (`$HERMES_BIN`, `which hermes`) owns its imports and is left alone. Same class fixed in the Bot Chat delivery runner (`cron/scheduler_delivery.py`, module argv after `served_profile_child_env`). Salvages #122420 by @liuhao1024 (earliest; #125088 by @intellectronica reaches the same outcome by switching the argv to `-I -c <bootstrap>` and #123041 by @strokesws by republishing launchers — both superseded by the smaller pin, which keeps the argv shape `gateway/status.py`'s cmdline matchers recognise).
- Fixes #122422 — `_dispatch_lane_task` writes a per-task `skipped_nonspawnable` event `{"assignee": <name>}` when the assignee profile does not exist, so `hermes kanban show`/`tail` name the missing profile. Written once per card (only when the card's latest event is not already this skip), because unlike a respawn guard the condition never expires: one row per tick forever, or one per foreign home per tick on a shared board (#101015), would have been the noise. Salvages #122567 by @Finn763.
- Part of #101015 — the silent cross-home drop is now visible on the card (the event above). The remaining atom (a self-identity filter so the container that IS the assignee claims it) is a shared-board claim-policy question settled as an opt-in allowlist by 2d46af3fa2d (`kanban.dispatch_profiles`, #110995/#111004) rather than zero-config identity mapping; not changed here.
- Fixes #122689 — `hermes_cli/kanban_pr_acceptance.py::_api` runs `gh api` under `served_profile_child_env(target_home=<assignee home>, inherit_credentials=True)`: the assignee profile's own `GH_TOKEN`/`GH_CONFIG_DIR` (its `.env` + external sources), launch residue scrubbed. A 401/403/404 or a `null` GraphQL repository is classified `auth` naming the repository instead of a retryable `infra`. The assignee home is resolved exactly as the dispatcher resolves the worker's home (`resolve_profile_env`). Salvages #122714 by @dskwe (trimmed: the second commit's operation×status refusal ladder is not taken).
- Part of #122703 — a startup credential failure with `relogin_required` (revoked key, model access disabled) now exits `KANBAN_TERMINAL_PROVIDER_EXIT_CODE` (78) so the dispatcher blocks the card at once instead of charging the whole `failure_limit`; unknown startup failures keep exit 1; a turn result still takes precedence. Salvages #122716 by @Wenfengcheng. The pre-claim model probe half (#122893 by @strzhao, +735) is a new capability with a per-tick network cost and is left for a decision — not relabelled away, see `not_covered` in the lane report.

## WHEN × WHERE (profile-scope table)

- L5 (child processes) × T1/T2/T3/T4/T6: kanban worker + Bot Chat delivery runner — both spawn through `build_subprocess_env`/`served_profile_child_env`, never `os.environ.copy()`; the pin edits only the built child env.
- L5 × T2/T3/T7: `gh` acceptance child — `served_profile_child_env(target_home=B)`; B-only `.env` `GH_TOKEN` resolves, launch `GH_TOKEN`/`GH_CONFIG_DIR` residue absent.
- L3 (dispatcher ticker) × T2/T10: the skip event is idempotent across ticks and across homes sharing one `kanban.db`.

## Validation

| Item | Test | origin/main | this head |
|---|---|---|---|
| #122299/#122487/#122500 | `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_db.py::test_default_spawn_pins_repo_root_on_module_worker_pythonpath` (FakePopen; module argv → `PYTHONPATH[0]` == install root; shim argv → untouched) | 1 failed (`KeyError: 'PYTHONPATH'`) | 3 passed (with the two existing `_resolve_hermes_argv` tests) |
| #122422 / #101015 | `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_dispatch_unknown_assignee_event.py` (event named after one tick; exactly one after three ticks; dry-run writes none) | 2 failed | 2 passed |
| #122689 | `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_pr_acceptance.py::test_acceptance_runs_gh_as_the_assignee_profile` (ambient `GH_TOKEN=launch-token` + `GH_CONFIG_DIR` residue vs B's `.env` `GH_TOKEN=b-token`; fake `gh` dumps its env and returns `repository: null`) | 1 failed | 1 passed (file: 3 passed) |
| #122703 | `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_credential_startup_exit.py` (revoked→78 / quota→75 / unknown→1 × quiet × worker; turn result precedence) | 6 failed | 15 passed |

`ruff check` clean on touched files; `check_no_tmp_literals.py` clean; `audit_pr_attribution.py --fix`: all contributor emails mapped; `git diff --check` clean. Subset suite (kanban + single-query + cron bot-chat delivery files) run result is recorded in the lane report.

## Infographic

DEGRADED — `image_generate` refused (fal.ai balance exhausted: "User is locked. Reason: Exhausted balance"); style picked was `holo-tcg`. No image embedded.


## Review fixes

- MAJOR `kanban_pr_acceptance.py::_gh_env` (assignee with no own `GH_TOKEN`/`GH_CONFIG_DIR` fell through to the launch user's `~/.config/gh` because HOME/XDG stay the launch process's) → for a routed assignee home whose child env has none of `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_CONFIG_DIR`, `GH_CONFIG_DIR` is pinned to `<profile_home>/gh`; gh exits 4 ("authentication required"), which `_api` now classifies `auth` naming the profile. Popping `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` was not needed: gh consults `GH_CONFIG_DIR` first. Test: `test_kanban_pr_acceptance.py::test_assignee_without_own_gh_login_never_falls_through_to_ambient_login` (red → green).
- MINOR (a) `_assignee_profile_home` fail-open → profile resolution moved inside `collect_acceptance` (`assignee=` replaces `profile_home=`); an assigned card whose profile cannot be resolved raises `_GateAuthError` → `classification=auth` naming the profile, gh never spawned. Only unassigned cards keep the ambient env. Test: `test_assigned_card_with_unresolvable_profile_is_auth_not_ambient`.
- MINOR (b) docs → `kanban.md`: `GH_TOKEN` must live in the profile's `.env`/secret source; a shell/systemd export is scrubbed and never re-added.
- MINOR (c) Codex 200/non-JSON refresh body → `invalid_json_relogin=False` in `hermes_cli/auth_codex.py` (same as xAI), so the exit-78 startup gate cannot turn an edge misfire into a sticky terminal block. The 401–403 edge path (`_codex_refresh_failure_error`) is unchanged.
- MINOR (d) docs → `kanban.md` worker telemetry table gains the `skipped_nonspawnable {assignee}` row; the `gave_up` row notes that a startup relogin-required credential failure exits `78` (other startup failures `1`).

items.body:
Under a multiplexed gateway, cron now answers liveness, manual-run delivery, preflight routing, standalone-fallback retention and worker secret hydration by the job's OWNING profile — `hermes cron status/list` stop reporting a running scheduler as dead, `cronjob(action='run')` / `hermes -p X cron run` deliver through X's bot (or hand the run to the gateway that serves X), managed-scope `gateway.profile_routes` reach satellites, a retryable `send_path_degraded` rejection survives a doomed standalone fallback for post-reconnect redelivery, and external cron workers see plugin-registered secret sources.

## Changes (per issue)

- **Fixes #121881** — `hermes_cli/cron.py::_builtin_gateway_liveness` ends on "fresh ticker heartbeat in THIS home's store" after the own-home lock/pid probes, so the in-process `hermes serve` / Desktop ticker counts as a scheduler; `cron status` gains an in-process-ticker rung instead of the red "jobs will NOT fire" + `gateway install` hint. Salvages #121921 by @Bartok9 (cherry-picked, trimmed). Row L3 / topology T7.
- **Fixes #99631** — a named profile whose own heartbeat is fresh is reported as served even when the default-home multiplexer record predates `served_profiles` or excludes it; the earlier halves already landed (`named_profile_served_by_running_multiplexer` e7037175131, `gateway_state.json` pid fallback 52dbe0a7cd87 / #110271). #99659 by @686f6c61 is superseded: treating any default-home lock/pid as "alive for every profile" is over-broad under multiplex-only. Row L3 / T2.
- **Fixes #99579** — `cron status/list/create` name the inspected profile on every verdict and no longer assert a host-wide negative: `✗ No scheduler is serving profile 'X' — its cron jobs will NOT fire`, `Scheduled Jobs (profile: X)`, `No scheduled jobs in profile 'X'.` Profile-naming idea salvaged from #99613 by @webtecnica (Co-authored-by; its wrapper helper and unrelated kanban/script-validation scope were not taken). The `--profile` help atom landed separately in bd72c4205dc (`hermes -p <profile> <cmd>` in `hermes --help`). Row L3 / T3.
- **Fixes #124248** — `tools/cronjob_tools.py::_run_claimed_job` resolves `runner._adapters_for_profile(profile_name_for_home(get_hermes_home()))` (the same owner rule as `cron/scheduler_provider.py::tick_adapters_for`) instead of the launch profile's `runner.adapters`, failing closed when resolution fails. Salvages #116316 by @fabioaito (earliest; cherry-picked). #124254 by @liamdemafelix is the same one-line fix 7 days later plus a wrapper (superseded). Row L3 / T2.
- **Fixes #120330** — `tools/cronjob_tools.py::_action_run` (shared body behind `hermes -p X cron run` and out-of-gateway `cronjob(action='run')`) hands a primary-routed satellite's run to the serving gateway's ticker via `cron.jobs.trigger_job` when a gateway is alive, or fails fast BEFORE the agent turn naming the cause when it is not — mirroring the relay-fronted forward; `last_status` is never overwritten with `delivery_failed`. Detection reuses `cron/scheduler_preflight.py::_delivery_platform_routed_from_primary_gateway` so CLI and ticker cannot drift. Salvages #120387 by @DresvyanskiyDenis (the reporter). #120345 / #120902 by @holny and #120354 by @Finn763 POST to the satellite's `API_SERVER_PORT` (nothing listens there under multiplex; only the default profile's api_server is bound) and fall back to the doomed in-process run on forward failure — superseded. Row L6 / T3.
- **Fixes #125363** — `cron/scheduler_delivery.py` records the live lane's raw rejection on `_TargetDelivery.live_error` on BOTH arms (the unconfirmed-result branch and the exception arm the router's `RuntimeError` travels), and when standalone then fails for a reconnect-only rejection, `_deliver_standalone` hands the text to `gateway.delivery_ledger` as a failed row owned by the rejecting adapter's profile, which the existing post-reconnect sweep (`sweep_failed_for_runtime` → `_redeliver_failed_obligations_for_platform`) replays. `_TargetDelivery.where` now carries `thread_id` (the side finding). Salvages #125455 by @jayzhou2309 — its current head (4c40b7ea687) DOES populate the exception arm; the issue author's review predates that push. #125364 by @zengzheqing (credit for the report, forensic chain and thread_id finding) skips standalone entirely whenever the rejection is retryable, which would regress a token-holding primary from "delivers now" to "waits for reconnect" — superseded. Rows L3/L7 / T2–T3.
- **Fixes #121212** — `cron/scheduler_preflight.py::_primary_profile_routes_for_current_home` reads the primary home through `gateway.config_loader.read_yaml_layers` (user file + managed overlay, the loader `load_gateway_config()` itself uses) instead of `read_user_config_raw`; both consumers (the preflight rescue and the delivery-time `SharedRouteAdapters` fallback in `tick_adapters_for` / the `gateway/run.py` drain) go through this one helper, so both see managed-scope routes. Salvages #121595 by @ahisblessed (cherry-picked; its two new helpers and absent-user-file early return replaced by the gateway's own layered loader). Row L8 / T2, T4.
- **Fixes #121929** — `cron/scheduler.py::_run_external_worker_payload` runs `discover_plugins()` under the payload's `set_hermes_home_override(profile_home)` before `hydrate_profile_secret_sources()`, so the OWNING profile's plugin-registered secret sources are known to the worker. Salvages #121950 by @dyiapanis (cherry-picked, trimmed to one invariant). Rows L3/L5 / T2, T4.

Root cause, in one sentence: every one of these paths keyed on "this process / the launch profile / the raw user file" where the multiplex contract says "the job's owning profile, through the same loaders and resolvers the gateway ticker uses".

## Validation

| Item | Red on base (origin/main 5912ed81ed9) | Green on head |
|---|---|---|
| #121881 | `test_cron_satellite_diagnostics.py::test_desktop_serve_ticker_is_not_reported_as_no_gateway` fails at `_builtin_gateway_liveness() is True` (False with a 0 s-old heartbeat) | passes |
| #99631 / #99579 | `test_cron_satellite_diagnostics.py::test_named_profile_output_names_the_profile_and_trusts_its_own_ticker` fails (`No scheduled jobs.` without profile; served record excluding the profile → dead) | passes; existing missing/fresh/stale/disabled/excluded contract test unchanged |
| #124248 | probe + `test_cronjob_run_immediate.py::…delivers_through_owner_profile_adapters` / `…fails_instead_of_falling_back_when_owner_resolution_raises`: base uses launch adapters | owner adapters used, fail-closed on resolution error |
| #120330 | `test_cronjob_run_primary_routed.py` both tests fail on base (in-process run with `adapters=None`) | queued for the serving gateway / fails fast before the turn |
| #125363 | probe with the real `DeliveryRouter` + `SendResult(error='send_path_degraded', retryable=True)` + standalone stubbed to the BotFather failure: base → ledger empty (payload lost), failure line `telegram:-100` | head → `sweep_failed_for_runtime('telegram', profile='satellite')` claims the payload; line reads `telegram:-100:42`; `chat not found` still falls to standalone and queues nothing |
| #121212 | `test_preflight_managed_routes.py` 2 failed with base `scheduler_preflight.py` swapped in | 8 passed incl. existing user-file control |
| #121929 | `test_external_worker_secret_sources.py::test_worker_hydrates_owning_profile_plugin_secret_source` red (scope == {}) | green; launch home has no plugins, owning profile's plugin value reaches `current_secret_scope()` inside `run_one_job` |

A→B→A: the named-profile liveness, owner-adapter, routed-run and worker-hydration tests each stand up a launch home AND a distinct owning-profile home under `set_multiplex_active(True)` and assert the launch home's state is untouched (`os.environ` / launch adapters / launch plugins absent on the other side).

Attribution: `scripts/audit_pr_attribution.py --fix` mapped `d@yiapanis.co → @dyiapanis`. ruff, `check_no_tmp_literals`, `git diff --check` clean.

Not covered (re-dispatch input): the dashboard trigger surface `hermes_cli/web_routers/cron.py::_trigger_cron_job_sync → web_server_cron.py::_fire_cron_job_for_profile` still fires a primary-routed satellite's job with `adapters=None` in the serve process (T7 twin of #120330); `_forward_relay_fronted_run` shares the satellite-`API_SERVER_PORT` weakness under multiplex.

## Infographic

DEGRADED — style `hermes-patent-plate` was picked and the prompt built from its palette/elements/typography, but `image_generate` failed with `fal.ai: Exhausted balance` at publish time; no image embedded.



## Review fixes

- **MAJOR — `hermes_cli/cron.py::_builtin_gateway_liveness` trusted a bare-epoch heartbeat for ~200 s after its writer died (a killed serve/Desktop ticker read as alive, and `hermes -p X cron run` queued a routed run "for the gateway's next tick" with no ticker present).** Fixed: `cron/jobs.py::record_ticker_heartbeat` now stamps `<epoch> <pid>`; `get_ticker_heartbeat_age` parses the first field (legacy bare stamps still yield an age); new `cron/jobs.py::ticker_heartbeat_writer_alive` requires the stamped pid to be alive and treats a legacy bare stamp as NOT proof by itself. The heartbeat-only rung is now `fresh AND (named_profile_served_by_running_multiplexer() OR writer alive)` — the multiplexer pid gate is back for served named profiles (also covers a stale-code multiplexer still writing bare stamps), so only the in-process-ticker case relies on the heartbeat, and then only with a live writer. `cron status`'s in-process-ticker rung applies the same rule. Test: `tests/hermes_cli/test_cron_satellite_diagnostics.py::test_in_process_ticker_heartbeat_counts_only_while_its_writer_lives` (fresh stamp + dead pid → False; fresh bare stamp → False; fresh stamp + live pid → True) — red on the previous head, green now.
- **MINOR (a) — `tools/cronjob_tools.py::_hand_off_primary_routed_run` treated an unknown (`None`) liveness as alive.** Fixed: the hand-off is gated on `is True`; `None` returns an error naming the uncertainty (`Could not determine whether a gateway serves this profile; check hermes cron status and re-run.`) instead of "queued … runs and delivers it". Test: `tests/tools/test_cronjob_run_primary_routed.py::test_routed_run_without_a_serving_gateway_fails_before_the_turn` parametrized over `False`/`None`.
- **MINOR (b) — `_run_claimed_job` handed a credentialless shared-bot satellite the FULL primary adapter map while the ticker (`tick_adapters_for`) wraps it in `SharedRouteAdapters`.** Fixed: when `runner._is_shared_bot_satellite(profile)` the resolved map is wrapped in `SharedRouteAdapters(adapters, _primary_profile_routes_for_current_home())` — the same grant the ticker makes. Test: `tests/tools/test_cronjob_run_immediate.py::test_execute_job_now_grants_a_shared_bot_satellite_only_its_routed_targets` (routed target → primary adapter; unrouted target / target-less get → miss).
- **MINOR (c)** — follow-up, see below.

## Reviewer follow-ups

- `hermes_cli/web_server_cron.py::_fire_cron_job_for_profile` (dashboard trigger twin of #120330, reached via `hermes_cli/web_routers/cron.py::_trigger_cron_job_sync`) still fires a primary-routed satellite's job with `adapters=None` in the serve process; it needs the same hand-off / owner-adapter resolution as `_action_run`. Already listed under "Not covered" above; left for a follow-up PR.

items.title: cron under multiplex: liveness, manual-run delivery, managed routes, degraded-send retention and worker secrets follow the job's owning profile (#121881 #99579 #99631 #124248 #120330 #125363 #121212 #121929)

items.body:
Under a multiplexed gateway, every session-lifecycle path that used to fall back to the launch profile's home — spool replay at boot, torn-down `SessionDB` handles, session-isolated sandbox keys, shutdown notices, the cached agent's dead-session check, inbound attachment caching, peer-recovery fences and the tui_gateway child-run mirror — is now bound to the routed profile's own home. Sweep 6 lane `bleed-sessions`. Every fix binds via the turn's profile scope / the session record's home (`_profile_runtime_scope`, `set_hermes_home_override`, `_db_for_key(session_key)`, `db_path`-derived owner), never via env. Contributor commits are cherry-picked with authorship intact and trimmed to the salvage bar in follow-up commits. ## Per issue - **Fixes #123584** — `gateway/run.py::_recover_pending_flushes` replays each served profile's `profiles/

/pending_messages/` inside that profile's home so the spool lands in its own `state.db` (salvages #123585 by @Totoro-qaq). L1 / T2+T3. - **Fixes #123618** — `gateway/session_db_recovery.py::RecoverableHandleCache.get` and `gateway/platforms/api_server.py::_cached_session_db_locked` treat a handle whose registry generation was torn down (`_unserve_profile` → `close_all_under`) as absent and reopen through the registry, like `hermes_cli/goals.py::_registry_tore_down`; the API adapter's per-home cache was a third cache with the same bug and is fixed in the same PR (salvages #123619 by @Totoro-qaq). L6 / T3+T7. - **Fixes #123989** — `tools/terminal_tool.py::_resolve_container_task_id` branches 2 and 3 (session-isolated docker / `session:`) and the `_session_cwd` records are qualified with the routed profile via `_routed_home_task_key(profile_scoped=True)`, and `gateway/platforms/api_server.py::_derive_chat_session_id` namespaces named routed profiles (default/standalone ids and the launch profile's own `/p//` prefix unchanged). Salvages #124057 by @nabilaameena (mechanism + live docker repro) and #123991 by @liuhao1024 (id namespacing); #125125 is a different issue (#125124) and is left alone. L5 / T2+T3. Rollout note: session-isolated containers created under a routed profile before upgrade are not re-found under the qualified key (one fresh sandbox per routed session; old ones reaped). Header-less `/p//` conversations (Open WebUI-style, id derived from the first message) on a NON-launch profile derive a new id after upgrade, so each such existing conversation forks once into a fresh Hermes session; un-prefixed, `/p/default/` and `/p//` ids are byte-identical. - **Fixes #118233** — `gateway/run_shutdown.py::_notify_active_sessions_of_shutdown` now fans the stop/restart notice out to every served profile's home channel through that profile's own adapter under its scope, honouring its own `gateway_restart_notification`; the startup pass already fanned out (#118108) but its `_delivery_target_key` collapsed two bots' equal positive Telegram ids — the key is now per-profile for private Telegram chats only (salvages #118408 by @Wenfengcheng; the shutdown diagnosis was first in #107943 by @EloquentBrush0x, which no longer applies to main and is superseded). L7 / T2+T3. - **#120044 — already fixed on main** by 2e2fd696872 (#120103 salvaging #120045 by @jonpol01): `_run_secondary_profile_reconnect` calls `_schedule_planned_restart_replay()` + `_schedule_resume_pending_sessions(platform=)`; both regression tests pass at base. No change in this PR; parent closes. - **Fixes #118862** — `gateway/run_turn_runner.py::TurnRunner._cached_sid_is_dead` passes the session key and `gateway/session_lifecycle.py::_is_session_ended_in_db` resolves `_db_for_key(session_key)` instead of `_db_for_session_id` (which returned the launch store once routing moved the id off the index) (salvages #123406 by @Totoro-qaq). Since 54fb5a42e8e (#42422) a missing row counts as ended, so on current main the wrong-store read yields dead=True rather than the stale-agent symptom; the A→B→A test constructs the divergent state (routed row live but off-index) where base still answers from the launch store. L2 / T2+T3. - **Fixes #101134** — `gateway/run_inbound.py::rehome_inbound_media` moves adapter-cached attachments from the launch home's `cache/` into the active profile's cache at the in-scope preprocessing seam (`_prepare_inbound_message_text`, covers every adapter and the queued path), and `gateway/platforms/base.py::CachedMedia.path` is a host path translated to the agent-visible form at render time, so the note points at the mounted, populated directory. Slim redo (+135/-6 vs +480/-9) crediting #101369 by @JoaoMarcos44, whose base predates `run_inbound.py`. Legacy `/image_cache` layouts are not re-homed. L4 / T2+T3. - **Fixes #119121** — `hermes_state_gateway.py`: the `_PEER_BY_TUPLE_SQL` boundary row carries the same owner predicate as the candidate, both orphan-donor queries require the orphan's effective profile (`_ORPHAN_DONOR_PROFILE_FENCE_SQL`, NULL = store's own via `_own_profile_name()` from `db_path`), and `adopt_orphaned_gateway_session` refuses a cross-profile pair when an owner is derivable; unowned stores keep the historical behaviour (salvages #119122 by @beardthelion; tests trimmed 5 → 2). Store-level predicate; T2+T3 shared legacy `state.db`. - **Fixes #120212** — `tui_gateway/agent_callbacks.py` keys `_active_child_runs`/`_child_mirrors` on `(profile_home, child_key)`; `_child_run_active` takes the resolved home (required positional, no launch-profile default); `_mirror_subagent_to_child` resolves the watch window via `_find_live_session_by_key(child_key, parent_home)` instead of `_ANY_PROFILE` and binds nothing when the parent record is gone; `methods_session._resume_locate` checks `(ctx.profile_home, ctx.target)` (salvages #120282 by @liuhao1024, trimmed −`_UNRESOLVED_PROFILE` sentinel, −helper, −221-line test file; the PR's stale 1-arg test lambdas fixed). #120125 is the Desktop card dedup and is unrelated. L6 / T2+T7. ## Validation | Issue | Red on base (5912ed81ed9, source cp-swapped) | Green on head | |---|---|---| | #123584 | `tests/gateway/test_profile_spool_recovery.py` ImportError; probe of main's `_recover_pending` recovers 1 of 2, `work` spool file left | `::test_boot_recovery_replays_a_routed_profiles_spooled_backlog` passes (A launch + B routed both replayed, spool dirs empty) | | #123618 | `tests/gateway/test_session_db_handle_sharing.py` 4 passed / 2 failed (`…tore_down_is_reopened…`, `…api_server_profile_cache…`) | 6 passed | | #123989 | `tests/tools/test_docker_session_isolation.py::TestRoutedScopeQualification::test_colliding_session_id_is_isolated_per_routed_profile` FAIL (B reads A's cwd record); `tests/gateway/test_api_server.py::TestDeriveChatSessionId::test_routed_profile_namespaces_the_id_without_moving_default` FAIL | both pass; 59 passed in tests/tools trio | | #118233 | 3 FAILED: `test_multiplex_notice_egress_profile_adapter.py::test_shutdown_notice_reaches_every_served_profiles_home_channel`, `test_planned_restart_notice_multiplex.py::test_private_home_notices_reach_both_bots[success|failure]` | 12 passed in both files | | #120044 | n/a (already fixed) | `test_a_served_profiles_reconnect_replays_the_owed_notice`, `test_served_profile_reconnect_resumes_what_boot_deferred` pass at base | | #118862 | `tests/gateway/test_multiplex_session_db_profile_scope.py::test_cached_agent_dead_check_reads_the_routed_profile_store` FAIL (routed live session judged dead from launch store) | passes | | #101134 | probe: file in A/cache/documents, B/cache/documents empty, note hands agent an unmounted path; test ImportError | `test_routed_turn_rehomes_adapter_cached_attachments_a_b_a`, `test_cache_media_bytes_returns_host_path_and_translates_in_note` pass; 265 passed across media tests | | #119121 | `test_hermes_state.py::test_peer_fallback_reset_boundary_is_profile_fenced` FAIL; `test_orphan_gateway_session_repair.py::test_donor_must_share_the_orphans_profile` FAIL | both pass; orphan file 14/14 | | #120212 | `tests/tui_gateway/test_resume_child_run_profile_scope.py::test_lazy_resume_refuses_child_id_active_under_another_profile` FAIL (B's lazy resume of A's in-flight child accepted) | both tests pass; 43 passed across touched tui_gateway files + contracts 28 passed | All A→B→A cases run with two temp homes under `set_multiplex_active(True)`. `ruff`, `check_no_tmp_literals`, `check_compat_pointers`, `git diff --check`, `audit_pr_attribution --fix` clean. Known environmental red in this worktree (pre-exists on base): `tests/home_io_guard.py` trips on `.worktrees/manifest.json` / `.git/worktrees/*` probes for worktrees under `~/.hermes` (`test_grid_sweep_gateway_diagnostics::test_background_task_*`, parts of `test_session_db_ownership_teardown.py`, `test_agent_cache.py`) — unrelated to this change. ## Duplicate / superseded PRs (for the parent) - #107943 → superseded by #118408 + this PR (shutdown fan-out; does not apply to main). - #123991 complementary to #124057 — both salvaged here. - #125125 — not a fix for #123989; leave to its own review. - #120125 — Desktop card dedup, unrelated to #120212. ## Infographic DEGRADED: `image_generate` refused (fal.ai balance exhausted: "User is locked. Reason: Exhausted balance"). Style picked: `hermes-deco-chrome` (bento-grid); prompt built from the style file and ready to regenerate once billing is restored. ## Review fixes Independent-review findings on this PR (head 3720519199c): - **`tools/terminal_tool.py::record_session_cwd` vs `tui_gateway/methods_session.py::_create_session` (minor, fixed)** — `session.create` is a plain `@method`, so `_register_session_cwd` wrote the cwd record under the raw key while the scoped turn read `profile:

:` (miss until the first `cd`). `tui_gateway/session_workdir.py::_register_session_cwd` now binds the session's `profile_home` around the write, and `_task_env_overrides` is qualified with the same `_qualify_task_key` on write/clear/read (`register_task_env_overrides`, `clear_task_env_overrides`, `_has_isolation_overrides`, `resolve_task_overrides`; the isolation-override branch of `_resolve_container_task_id` returns the qualified key so the env cache and the override record agree) — closes the #123989 collision class for `docker_image`/`cwd` overrides too. Test: `tests/tui_gateway/test_session_cwd_profile_key.py::test_secondary_profile_session_cwd_is_found_inside_its_scope` (red on 3720519199c, green on head). - **`gateway/platforms/api_server.py::_derive_chat_session_id` (minor, fixed)** — `_resolve_request_profile` returns the served name even for the launch profile addressed via `/p//`, so prefixed and un-prefixed requests on the same launch profile derived different ids. The prefix is now skipped when the routed name is the process's launch profile (`_names_launch_profile`, compared against `get_routing_process_hermes_home()`). Rollout note for the remaining `/p//` fork is in the #123989 bullet above. Test: `tests/gateway/test_api_server.py::TestDeriveChatSessionId::test_launch_profile_prefix_keeps_the_unprefixed_id` (red on 3720519199c, green on head). - **`gateway/run_inbound.py::rehome_inbound_media` traversal/symlink cases** — reviewer confirmed safe; no change.

items.title: Multiplexed gateway: session lifecycle paths bind to the routed profile's home, not the launch profile (#123584 #123618 #123989 #118233 #118862 #101134 #119121 #120212)

items.body:
Desktop/TUI surfaces served by one pooled backend now act on the profile that OWNS the session or the rail selection instead of the backend's launch profile: `/save`, the interrupt hook, `/model` live sync, the exit resume hint, gateway-session resume, the new-chat slash palette, the error card's Open Logs, and the API-server card.

## Per issue

- Fixes #125241 — `tui_gateway/methods_session.py` `session.save` built `saved_dir` from `get_hermes_home()` (launch profile); it now uses the session's `profile_home` like `session.history`/`session.create`. Salvages #125242 by @jonpol01.
- Fixes #125063 — `tui_gateway/session_lifecycle.py::_interrupt_session_turn` dispatched `agent_loop_stopped` with no profile runtime scope; the dispatch is now inside `_session_profile_runtime_scope(session, hydrate_secrets=False)`, which covers every caller (`session.interrupt`, WS orphan reaper, idle reaper, lease takeover, compute-host close). Salvages #125073 by @dskwe (earliest; #125081 by @kokhlo is the same wrap → duplicate).
- Fixes #122655 — `tui_gateway/methods_slash.py::_mirror_slash_side_effects` ran `/model`'s `switch_model → resolve_runtime` credential read off-turn with no scope bound → `UnscopedSecretError` under multiplex; the mirror dispatch is wrapped in `_session_profile_runtime_scope(session)`. Salvages #122698 by @ahisblessed. (#125038 is a different bug — curator thread contextvars, #125032 — not salvaged here.)
- Fixes #125078 — `hermes_cli/main_tui_launch.py::_print_tui_exit_summary` now appends `-p <profile>` for non-`default`/`custom` profiles, matching `cli_session_mixin.py::_print_exit_summary`. Salvages #125079 by @dskwe.
- Fixes #125942 — `tui_gateway/server.py::_stored_session_runtime_overrides` read only top-level `model_config.provider` then `billing_provider`, ignoring the `gateway_runtime` route `gateway/run_turn.py` persists; it now uses the canonical `SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime` reader (nested `gateway_runtime` → top-level TUI keys, with a routable `billing_provider` filling a missing provider) that CLI `--resume` already uses. **CLI-visible precedence change:** a TUI-written row with top-level `base_url`/`api_mode` and no `provider` used to restore the endpoint alone (ambient provider); it now also restores the `billing_provider` that served it — the merge `tui_gateway/server.py` always did, now shared by `cli_model_switch_mixin.py::stored_session_route` (bare `auto`/`custom` buckets still contribute nothing). Slim redo of #125956 by @Wenfengcheng (its second reader inverted the precedence). #123799 and #121629 do not fix this.
- Fixes #124651 — Desktop `use-slash-completions.ts` sent `commands.catalog`/`complete.slash` with empty params for a draft, so `tui_gateway/methods_tools.py::_session_home_scope` scanned the launch home; the hook now passes the rail-selected `profile` when there is no `session_id`, and `commands.catalog`/`complete.slash`/`skills.reload` accept `profile` (contracts regenerated). Salvages #124845 by @chelsealong.
- Fixes #119080 — `apps/desktop/electron/fs-ipc.ts` `hermes:fs:logsRoot` resolved `readActiveDesktopProfile()`; the IPC now takes the owning profile and the error card passes the composer scope's profile (`default` → the home's own `logs/`). Sibling symptom (secondary-profile `gui.log` landing in the launch home) is a backend logging mechanism (`hermes_logging.py::_ProfileRoutingFileHandler`), tracked separately — not claimed here.
- Fixes #121125 — `hermes_cli/web_routers/messaging.py::_messaging_platform_payload` reported a served secondary's API server as disabled/needs-setup from its own never-configured config; a live `mirrored_from` entry from `gateway/status.py::shared_listener_mirror_platforms` now projects enabled+configured. Salvages #122165 by @Finn763.

## Cells (WHEN × WHERE)

L6 (RPC methods) and L2 (session end / interrupt hook) on T7 (Desktop pooled `serve`, several homes per process) and T2/T3 (multiplex gateway, default- or named-hosted). #125078 is the T1/T3 CLI entry-point twin of an already-fixed CLI path; #125942 is the T7 read path diverging from the canonical CLI reader.

## Validation

| Item | Test | Red on base (origin/main) | Green on head |
|---|---|---|---|
| #125241 | `tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py::test_session_save_lands_in_the_sessions_own_profile_a_b_a` | index 1 was `.hermes/sessions/saved`, expected `profiles/s6probe-work/sessions/saved` (A→B→A, `set_multiplex_active(True)`) | pass |
| #125063 | `tests/tui_gateway/test_interrupt_agent_loop_stopped_hook.py::test_interrupt_hook_observer_sees_the_sessions_profile_a_b_a` | `seen == [launch, routed, launch]` failed: observer saw launch home for B | pass |
| #122655 | `tests/tui_gateway/test_multi_profile_hosting_fail_closed.py::test_model_switch_mirror_binds_runtime_scope_under_multiplex` | `invoke(b) == ""` failed with "live session sync failed: Hermes could not read this profile's A_ONLY_TOKEN" | pass |
| #125078 | `tests/hermes_cli/test_exit_summary_resume_hint.py::TestTuiExitSummaryResumeHint::test_tui_hints_include_profile_flag_for_named_profile` | `hermes --tui --resume … -p dev` not in output | pass (7 passed) |
| #125942 | `tests/tui_gateway/test_resume_switched_provider_endpoint.py::test_resume_honors_gateway_runtime_over_first_call_billing_provider`, `::test_resume_prefers_gateway_runtime_over_stale_top_level_keys` | `('anthropic', None, None) == ('openai-codex', None, 'codex_responses')` | pass |
| #124651 | `tests/tui_gateway/test_protocol.py::test_sessionless_slash_palette_follows_profile_param` (A→B→A over `s6probe-a`/`s6probe-b`); vitest `use-slash-completions.test.tsx` "scopes a sessionless catalog and typed lookup to the routed profile" | `complete.slash` → error 4000 "profile: Extra inputs are not permitted"; hook never sent `{profile}` | pass / 6 passed |
| #119080 | vitest `apps/desktop/electron/fs-ipc.test.ts` "resolves the logs dir of the profile that owns the session" | received `…/profiles/launch-profile/logs`, expected `…/profiles/finex/logs` | 5 passed |
| #121125 | `tests/hermes_cli/test_served_profile_mirror_platforms.py::test_messaging_card_shows_mirrored_api_server_enabled_without_local_config` | `payload["enabled"] is True` failed | 5 passed |

Also: `ruff check` clean on all touched `.py`; `check_no_tmp_literals` clean; `git diff --check` clean; `audit_pr_attribution.py --fix` → all mapped; eslint 0 errors on touched TS files. `tests/tui_gateway/test_protocol.py::test_approval_for_a_ws_client_that_never_advertised_settles_the_queue_entry` is red on a pristine `origin/main` worktree in this host environment as well (not touched by this PR).

## Infographic

DEGRADED: image generation unavailable in this lane (fal.ai balance exhausted at generation time); style picked was `demoscene-cracktro` / bento-grid.

## Review fixes

Independent-review findings on this PR and what changed (all in the last commit):

- **MAJOR — `apps/desktop/electron/fs-ipc.ts::hermes:fs:logsRoot` joined the renderer-supplied `profile` (session-owner data; from the remote backend in remote mode) into `profiles/<name>` unvalidated, so `..`/absolute values escaped `profiles/`, were `ensureDir`'d and revealed.** Fixed: `localPluginsRoot` accepts an owner only when it is `default` or matches `DESKTOP_PROFILE_NAME_RE` (the same gate `local-skin.ts::localSkinProfileKey` and `main.ts` apply), else falls back to `readActiveDesktopProfile()` like an unnamed owner. Test: `fs-ipc.test.ts` "never leaves hermesHome for an owner that is not a profile name" (`../../x`, `/etc`, `a/b`, `Upper`, `.hidden`) — red on the previous head (`…/x/logs` outside the scratch home), 6 passed after.
- **MINOR (a) — `hermes_state_gateway.py::SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime` precedence change was undisclosed and untested for CLI `--resume`.** Kept the shared reader (one reader for both surfaces is the point of the #125942 fix; splitting the merge back into `server.py` would re-create the divergence), disclosed the CLI-visible change in the #125942 bullet above, and added `tests/hermes_cli/test_resume_model_restore.py::test_session_gateway_runtime_billing_provider_fills_top_level_route_without_provider` (merge + bare-bucket control).
- **MINOR (b) — `tui_gateway/methods_tools.py::commands.catalog` scoped only skill discovery; `_catalog_quick_commands` (`_load_cfg()`) and `_catalog_plugin_commands` ran against the LAUNCH profile.** All three loaders now run inside the one `_session_home_scope(..., profile=...)` block. `test_protocol.py::test_sessionless_slash_palette_follows_profile_param` now seeds a profile-only `quick_commands` entry per profile and asserts the palette carries only that profile's — red on the previous head (`set()` for quick commands), green after.
- **MINOR (c) — `commands.catalog` swallowed `ProfileUnavailableError` into `warning` and returned ok with `skills={}` while `complete.slash` returned 4064.** `_profile_scoped_rpc` re-raises `ProfileUnavailableError` out of the body so `rpc_dispatch` maps it to 4064; this also fixes `skills.reload`, which mapped the same error to its 5025 fail code. Negative case folded into the same test: `commands.catalog` and `skills.reload` with `profile: "../x"` → error 4064.

items.title: Desktop/TUI act on the session's owning profile, not the backend launch profile: /save, interrupt hook, /model sync, resume hint and route, slash palette, Open Logs, API-server card (8 issues, salvages 6 PRs)

items.body:
Under a multiplexed gateway / `hermes serve`, secondary profiles now get their own A2A enablement gate, Buzz config section, plugin message injector, freshly-rendered remote MCP headers, `profiles.describe` toolset snapshot and `tools.list`/`tools.show` read-back — every one bound to the served profile instead of the launch home.

Sweep 6 lane `bleed-plugins-tools` (multiplex/profile backlog, cluster: profile-local plugins/toolsets/MCP under multiplex). One PR, six fixed atoms, two premises found already correct on main.

## Per issue

- Fixes #122126 — `plugins/platforms/a2a/__init__.py::is_connected` read `A2A_PORT` via `os.getenv`, so the launch profile's port enabled an inbound `A2AAdapter` in every secondary (all falling back to 9900 → `bind_failed`). Now routed through `gateway.platforms._shared.env_is_connected("A2A_PORT")` (scoped `get_env_value`: fails closed under multiplex, environ IS the profile in T1); the client-tools gate `a2a/tools.py::_a2a_tools_available` switched to `get_scoped_secret` for the same class. Salvages #122128 by @JE4NVRG (its 3 seam-patching tests replaced by 2 invariants). L1 / T2,T3.
- Fixes #125985 — `plugins/platforms/buzz/adapter.py::_profile_buzz_extra` read only `gateway.platforms.buzz`; it now resolves the section through `gateway/config_loader.py::platform_section`, the same seam that feeds the plugin's YAML hook, so the documented top-level `platforms.buzz` shape passes `check_requirements` in a secondary profile. Salvages #126060 by @liuhao1024 (earliest). L1 / T2.
- Fixes #125102 — `gateway/run_inbound.py::_install_plugin_message_injector` published the injector on the launch home's `PluginManager` only. New `hermes_cli/plugins.py::publish_gateway_message_host` (twin of the existing `publish_tui_message_host`) stamps every known per-home manager and `get_plugin_manager()` attaches the published host to managers created later (profiles hot-added by a rescan); clearing is owner-conditional. Session routing was already correct on main. Salvages #125114 by @JoaoMarcos44 (earliest of three). L1/L3 / T2.
- Fixes #119092 — `tools/mcp_tool_discovery.py::_owner_scope_home` returned `None` whenever a scope was already bound, so the gateway's boot-time scope snapshot (taken before the profile's `secrets.command` answered) was trusted as-is and the header rendered as the literal `Bearer ${VAR}`; `MCPServerRunMixin.run` re-read config on every probe under the same frozen mapping, retrying the placeholder forever. Now the owner home is always returned so MCP rebuilds the owner scope fresh at connect and every reconnect; `mcp_tool_config._require_rendered_remote` fails closed (ValueError naming the `${VAR}`) instead of sending an unresolved url/header. Salvages #119097 by @JoaoMarcos44 (its connect-time re-render kept; alone it was a no-op for the bound-scope topology). L1/L3 / T2.
- Fixes #120726 — `tui_gateway/methods_profiles.py::_hermes_home_scope` bound only the `HERMES_HOME` override, so `_describe_toolsets → _xai_credentials_present → get_secret` raised `UnscopedSecretError` and `_try(..., set())` reported every toolset disabled. It now returns `_session_profile_runtime_scope` (home + secret + terminal, the `@_profile_scoped` composition) for describe, configure and create-time mirroring. Salvages #120734 by @angel12. L6 / T7.
- Fixes #117977 — `tui_gateway/methods_tools.py::_toolset_rows` / `tools.show` read a BUILT agent's toolsets only (unbuilt session → everything enabled) and resolved session-less calls unscoped. New `_session_toolsets(session)` answers `tools.list`, `tools.show` and `toolsets.list` from the live agent when built, else `_load_enabled_toolsets(platform)` / `_load_disabled_toolsets()` under `_session_profile_runtime_scope(session)` — the same read the build path uses and the `platform_toolsets.cli` key `profiles.configure` writes. No new RPC, no result-shape change. Salvages #118020 by @kokhlo. L6 / T7.
- #123483 and #117703 — **already correct on main**, no change in this PR: routed-profile plugin discovery runs lazily inside the turn/build scope (`hermes_cli/tools_config.py::_get_platform_tools → _get_plugin_toolset_keys → plugins.py::_nowait_plugin_set → discover_plugins()` on the per-home manager, `tools/registry.py` per-scope overlays) since 4e1b2e436c0 / 85020f2238d / 8be9c76f8c0. An A→B→A probe on 5912ed81ed shows B's plugin toolset validating and its tools reaching `get_tool_definitions` on both the gateway and `tui_gateway` build paths. PRs #117778 / #117804 add a `discover_plugins()` call that is a no-op on main; #124503 is about `mcp add --all-profiles` and unrelated. Left for the parent to close.

## Validation

| Item | Red on base (origin/main 5912ed81ed) | Green on head |
|---|---|---|
| #122126 | `tests/plugins/test_a2a_plugin.py::TestConnectionGateScope::test_secondary_profile_never_borrows_launch_env_port` — FAIL `(True, True) != (False, False)` (B borrowed launch `A2A_PORT`) | 2 passed; A→B→A two temp homes, multiplex active + T1 standalone case |
| #125985 | `tests/gateway/test_buzz_adapter.py::test_check_requirements_scoped_reads_toplevel_platforms_buzz` — FAIL (`extra={}`, `check_requirements=False`) | pass; A→B→A both shapes True, empty home False |
| #125102 | `probe_ab.py` (A→B→late-added→A, multiplex active): B `has_gateway_message_injector=False`; new pytest AttributeErrors (`publish_gateway_message_host` absent) | all True; 31 passed across the three injection test files |
| #119092 | `tests/tools/test_mcp_connect_secret_scope.py::test_connect_renders_remote_headers_under_the_owners_fresh_scope` + `::test_reconnect_…` — 2 FAIL (`header == 'Bearer ${EXAMPLE_TOKEN}'` at connect and on 2nd rebuild) | 6/6 pass |
| #120726 | `tests/tui_gateway/test_profiles_describe_secret_scope.py` — FAIL `assert set() == {'browser', ...}` (describe default→bot→bot→default, bot-only `XAI_API_KEY`, `os.environ` unchanged) | 1 passed |
| #117977 | `tests/tui_gateway/test_tools_readback_scope.py` — 2 FAIL (work session read back browser/computer_use/web…) | 2 passed; real handlers, two homes, A→B→A |

Per-lane suites (`scripts/run_tests.sh` on the touched dirs' files): a2a 155 passed; buzz 178 passed; injection 31 passed; mcp 829 passed / 6 red identical on pristine main (home-I/O guard tripping on `.worktrees/manifest.json`); tui_gateway profile/toolset files green, remaining reds reproduce on pristine main. `ruff`, `check_no_tmp_literals`, `check_compat_pointers`, `git diff --check`, `audit_pr_attribution --fix` clean.

## Duplicates (for the parent's close pass)

- #125282 (@lorenzozanee) and #125128 (@Eeshu-Yadav) → superseded by #125114 (same mechanism, later; #125128's extra `_plugin_home_scope` wrap is defense-in-depth past the reported failure).
- #126067 (@Tranquil-Flow) → superseded by #126060 (same `platform_section` mechanism, later, +129 LOC with a try/except around a call that cannot fail).
- #117778 (@tylerbrevard), #117804 (@JoaoMarcos44) → no-op on main (see #123483/#117703 above). #124503 (@Finn763) is unrelated to #123483.

## Not covered

- MCP stdio sibling of #119092: a stdio server's child env on respawn is still resolved under the run task's connect-time scope snapshot; the fresh owner scope is bound only around the remote-config refresh (small follow-up in `MCPServerRunMixin.run`).
- #123483 reporters measured on a build that already carried the lazy per-home mechanism; their trigger is unreproduced (hypothesis: tool execution on a worker thread that lost the home-override contextvar, or the #123386 parked-profile gate).

## Infographic

DEGRADED: image generation unavailable this run (fal.ai balance exhausted — `image_generate` returned `Exhausted balance`); style picked was `designers-republic` / bento-grid. To be regenerated by the parent.


## Review fixes

- MAJOR `tools/mcp_tool_discovery.py::_install_owner_secret_scope / _owner_secret_scope` (launch profile's env-only credentials dropped by the owner rebuild) → **fixed**. The rebuild now goes through a shared `_owner_secret_mapping(home)`: `launch_secret_scope(home)` when the owner home is the process/launch home (`_is_process_home`), so systemd `Environment=` / `op run` / Compose credentials that exist only in the frozen launch env keep rendering; `build_profile_secret_scope(home)` (own files only) for a served profile — same rule `kanban_db_dispatch` already applies. Test: `tests/tools/test_mcp_connect_secret_scope.py::test_launch_profile_env_only_credential_survives_the_owner_rebuild` (multiplex active, launch env `EXAMPLE_TOKEN=tok-from-systemd`, empty launch `.env`, connect + a second rebuild under `_owner_secret_scope`; red on the previous head with the exact `ValueError` from the reviewer's probe).
- MINOR (b) hydration re-run on every connect/reconnect → **fixed** inside the same helper: a home whose sources did not fully hydrate (`env_loader._APPLIED_HOMES` miss) is retried at most once per 30 s; a hydrated home stays the cheap cached read.
- MINOR (c) docs → **fixed**: `website/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference.md` (the "unset variable keeps its placeholder" rule now names the remote `url`/`headers` fail-closed exception and its error text) and `website/docs/developer-guide/multiplexing-gateway.md` (Failure modes: per-profile `${VAR}` fail-closed for remote MCP, launch-env survival, scoped A2A/Buzz gates).
- MINOR (a) `_connect_server` re-interpolates an already-rendered config → **follow-up** (below).

## Reviewer follow-ups

- `tools/mcp_tool_discovery.py::_connect_server` re-interpolates an already-rendered config (`_require_rendered_remote(name, _interpolate_env_vars(config))`). The raw (unrendered) server definition is not at hand at connect — `_load_mcp_config` renders at load and probes pass ad-hoc dicts — so re-rendering from the raw definition means threading it through discovery/probe callers (> 15 LOC). Idempotent today unless a secret VALUE itself contains a `${...}` token.
