items.body:
Editing a file in a cloned repository no longer runs that repository's own interpreter, TypeScript SDK, compiler plugins or build scripts. The user's own project, where Hermes was launched or where the session was opened, keeps full LSP diagnostics.

Fixes #125954. This salvages #125955 by @jonpol01: both of his commits (his own rebase onto main, `1f3b384906` and `482e5a1e54`) are kept unchanged with his authorship, and our follow-ups sit on top.

## What changes

From #125955 (@jonpol01):
- Language servers are denied by default in an untrusted workspace. Only servers that run no project code start there, with settings that keep them on Hermes's own tools:
  - pyright uses `VIRTUAL_ENV` or the Hermes-managed Python, never the checkout's `.venv`.
  - typescript-language-server's `tsserver.path` is pinned to Hermes's TypeScript.
  - svelte-language-server gets `isTrusted: false`.
  - bash, yaml, dockerfile, intelephense and clangd are unchanged.
- The `npx tsc` and `rustfmt` post-write lint fallbacks are skipped in an untrusted workspace, because they pick up the checkout's `node_modules/.bin/tsc` and `rust-toolchain.toml`.
- A new `lsp.trusted_workspaces` config key lists extra trusted directories. `hermes lsp status` marks the servers that only run in trusted workspaces.

Follow-ups (ours):
- **Trust follows the workspace the session was opened in**, not only the process cwd. The PR anchored on `os.getcwd()`. `hermes -w` sets `TERMINAL_CWD` without a `chdir`, the Desktop/TUI backend runs from the install tree or `$HOME` with the project bound as the session cwd, the gateway runs from `HERMES_HOME`, and cron binds a workdir per job. On all of these, the user's own repository lost pyright's venv, 19 other servers and the lint fallbacks. `operator_workspace_roots()` now also trusts the worktree of `resolve_agent_cwd()`. Only surfaces set that directory; the agent's `cd` does not move it.
- **Cron runs and Kanban workers get no automatic trust.** The `cronjob` tool lets the model choose a job's workdir, and `kanban_create` lets it choose a task's workspace. Both would otherwise anchor trust on a repo the agent cloned. These surfaces use `lsp.trusted_workspaces` only.
- **A repo at or above `$HOME` is never an anchor.** A dotfiles repository at home would otherwise trust every directory under it, including a tarball the agent extracts into `~/Downloads`.
- **Vue is removed from the allowlist.** `@vue/language-core` 2.2.x `require()`s the `vueCompilerOptions.plugins` listed in a project's tsconfig, resolved against the project root, so pinning `tsdk` was not enough.
- The lint gate checks only the linter's cwd, which is where `npx` and rustup resolve the toolchain. The `except Exception` wrapper is gone.
- Trust is computed once per spawn, and trust lookups take no lock. pyright shares one process only among trusted roots, so whichever root spawned first no longer decides the interpreter for the others. A client that started while its root was untrusted is still found and released after the root becomes trusted.
- Svelte goes back to the declarative registry form (`untrusted_init=`), the two path-list config keys share one parser, and the docs table is reworded ("run no project code").

## Validation

Real `pyright-langserver`. Each checkout ships a `.venv/bin/python` that records when it is executed. The "origin/main" column is the pre-PR behaviour: every repository's own interpreter runs.

| Scenario | origin/main | #125955 as submitted | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Agent edits a clone, CLI launched outside it | project python runs | not run | not run |
| `hermes -w` linked worktree (the user's own project) | runs | not run (lost venv) | runs |
| Desktop session opened in the project, backend cwd elsewhere | runs | not run (lost venv) | runs |
| `$HOME` is a dotfiles repo, agent-made dir below it | runs | **runs** | not run |
| Cron run whose workdir is a clone | runs | not run | not run |

- Tests: `tests/agent/lsp/` plus the file-operations, config, runtime-cwd, pm and Windows-subprocess test files: 35 files, 392 passed, 0 failed.
- The two trust tests were mutation-checked. Each of these changes turns them red: removing the session-cwd anchor, removing the `$HOME` exclusion, removing the cron gate, or removing the Kanban gate.
- ruff, the Windows footgun check and the compat-pointer check are clean.

items.body:
Gateway startup and `hermes doctor` now tell users when their config still asks for idle or daily session resets. Core stopped applying those resets in 1d5d059410, and until now nothing said so.

WHO/WHEN/WHY: A community plugin author reported on 2026-09-27 that his family's gateway conversations stopped resetting after the upgrade. Nobody in the house types `/new`, so context grew without bound and so did the bill. The docs say legacy `session_reset` settings are ignored, but a user whose config still carries them got no signal at all. Reset policy stays out of core. This PR only points those users at the opt-in catalog plugin, `hermes-session-reset-policy`, which reads the same block unchanged.

Changes:
- `hermes_cli/session_reset_retirement.py`: a small detector for `session_reset.mode` set to idle, daily or both. It checks the top level and the `gateway:` form the old loader accepted. The same module holds the "is the plugin enabled" check and the notice text.
- `gateway/run_startup.py`: one WARNING per served profile (multiplex included) at startup. Silent while the plugin is enabled.
- `hermes doctor`: new "Session Reset" section. Warns and adds a manual issue, or reports the policy as applied when the plugin is enabled.
- Docs: `sessions.md` and `messaging/index.md` name the warning and the plugin.
- The key is reported, never rewritten or dropped, because the plugin consumes it.

Live repro (isolated HOME + HERMES_HOME, `gateway run --force`, `session_reset: {mode: both}`):

| | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| gateway log | no mention of session_reset | `WARNING gateway.run: Profile default: session_reset.mode: both is no longer applied ... hermes plugins install hermes-session-reset-policy.` |
| `hermes doctor` | nothing | ⚠ same notice |
| plugin installed + enabled | n/a | no warning; doctor `✓ session_reset.mode: both is applied by the session reset plugin`; plugin logs `armed (pre_gateway_dispatch)` |
| multiplex, secondary profile `work` with `gateway.session_reset.mode: daily` | nothing | `Profile work: gateway.session_reset.mode: daily ... (move the block to top-level session_reset first)` |

Tests: `tests/gateway/test_retired_session_reset_notice.py` has 2 tests (3 cases). The first checks that startup warns and that the plugin silences it; it fails when the plugin gate is inverted. The second checks that only timed modes count, in both locations. Locally, `test_doctor.py` and `test_doctor_exit_status.py` show the same 41 environment failures on origin/main and on this branch, because the worktree's git dir sits under the real hermes home and trips the home-I/O guard. The failure sets are identical, and CI is the authority there.

Merge order: the notice names `hermes-session-reset-policy`. That name installs once the catalog entry lands, which waits on fastfinge/hermes-session-reset-policy#1 (a manifest `provides_hooks` line so `hermes plugins validate` passes). This PR should merge after the catalog entry.

The Qwen OAuth card on the Accounts page now shows the token expiry, the token preview and the credentials file path.

## What changed

| Card field (qwen-oauth, logged in) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `expires_at` | `None` | `2026-09-28T11:46:18.858000+00:00` (aware UTC ISO, same instant as the Qwen CLI `expiry_date`) |
| `token_preview` | `''` | `…ghijkl` |
| `source_label` | `Qwen CLI` | the path of `~/.qwen/oauth_creds.json` |

- `hermes_cli/web_routers/oauth.py:351-354`: the qwen-oauth row in `_PROVIDER_STATUS` reads `expires_at_ms`, `api_key` and `auth_file`, which are the keys `get_qwen_auth_status` returns (`hermes_cli/auth_qwen.py:143-146`).
- `hermes_cli/web_routers/oauth.py:332-334`: new `_epoch_ms_to_iso` converts the epoch-ms expiry into an aware UTC ISO string. That is the shape the nous card (`access_expires_at`) and the minimax card (`expires_at`) already send. It is also the type the clients declare: `web/src/lib/api.ts:2661` and `apps/desktop/src/types/hermes.ts:69` both use `expires_at?: string | null`. The web card parses it with `new Date(expiresAt)` (`web/src/components/OAuthProvidersCard.tsx:30-46`).
- The other rows in the same table (nous, openai-codex, minimax-oauth, xai-oauth; `hermes_cli/web_routers/oauth.py:342-361`) were checked against their getters (`hermes_cli/auth_nous.py:1176-1193`, `:1301-1345`; `hermes_cli/auth.py:2386-2397`). Each one reads keys its getter returns, so none of them changed.

Root cause: the qwen-oauth row read `expires_at`, `access_token` and `auth_store_path`, but `get_qwen_auth_status` returns `expires_at_ms`, `api_key` and `auth_file`. So all three card fields fell back to empty values.

## Verification

- Red on base: `tests/hermes_cli/test_web_oauth_dispatch.py::test_qwen_status_card_carries_the_getter_expiry_token_and_auth_file` failed with `E  +  where False = isinstance(None, str)`.

items.body:
The usage analytics daily chart now counts each session on the local calendar day it started, the same day `/insights` uses.

## What changed

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `daily[].day` in `/api/analytics/usage` | UTC calendar day: `date(started_at, 'unixepoch')` | Machine-local calendar day: `date(started_at, 'unixepoch', 'localtime')` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/analytics.py:87`) |
| Session at 02:00 IST on 2026-09-26 | counted on `2026-09-25` | counted on `2026-09-26` |
| Agreement with CLI `/insights` (`agent/insights.py:419-422`, `datetime.fromtimestamp`) | differs for sessions started between 00:00 and 05:30 IST | same day |

SQLite applies `'localtime'` per row, so each session uses the UTC offset in force at its own start time. A range that crosses a DST change is bucketed correctly. A single fixed offset for the whole range would not be.

Root cause: the daily query converted the epoch start time to a date without a zone modifier, so SQLite returned the UTC date, while both clients show the value as a local calendar date and `/insights` buckets by local day.

Refs #23982. Two older open PRs address the same issue, #62317 and #76764. Both edit `hermes_cli/web_server.py`, where this query no longer lives, and both use the `hermes_time` configured zone instead of the zone `/insights` uses. #76764 applies one offset to the whole range.

## Verification

- New tests in `tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server.py` (`TestNewEndpoints`), with `TZ` switched through `os.environ` + `time.tzset()` as in `tests/gateway/test_active_turn_recovery.py:560-574`:
  - `test_analytics_daily_buckets_use_local_day`: a session at 02:00 `Asia/Kolkata` on day D is counted on D.
  - `test_analytics_daily_buckets_follow_dst_offset_per_session`: sessions at 23:30 `America/New_York` on a January (EST) and a July (EDT) day each stay on their own day.
- Red on base: `AssertionError: assert {'2026-09-26': 1} == {'2026-09-27': 1}` and `assert {'2026-02-01'...026-08-01': 1} == {'2026-01-31'...026-07-31': 1}`.
- Green: `tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server.py`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_web_analytics_corrupt_store.py`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_dashboard_param_clamps.py`: 195 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed.
- E2E with real imports, fresh temp `HERMES_HOME`, `TZ=Asia/Kolkata`, session at 02:00 local on 2026-09-26 (`timestamp-recon/scripts/b4_probe_analytics_days.py`):
  - before: `analytics daily days=['2026-09-25'] sessions=[1]` / `insights day=2026-09-26 analytics matches insights: False`
  - after: `analytics daily days=['2026-09-26'] sessions=[1]` / `insights day=2026-09-26 analytics matches insights: True`
- Gates: `ruff check` on both touched files, `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all`, `git diff --check`: all clean.
- Not run: the full test suite, the desktop or web UI in a browser, and Windows (SQLite `'localtime'` uses the C library zone there too, but it was not exercised).

items.body:
After a gateway restart, a session interrupted shortly before a DST spring-forward is now auto-resumed instead of being treated as stale.

## What changed

`GatewayRunner._schedule_resume_pending_sessions` (`gateway/run_startup.py:590-592`) now checks marker freshness with `_is_fresh_gateway_interruption` (`gateway/run.py:1029`), which compares epoch seconds. It no longer subtracts naive local datetimes.

| Case (window 60 min) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Marker 01:50 local, boot 03:10 local on 2026-03-08 in America/New_York (20 real minutes) | measured as 80 min, session skipped | measured as 20 min, session auto-resumed |
| Marker carries a UTC offset | `TypeError: can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes` | compared exactly, session auto-resumed |
| `HERMES_AUTO_CONTINUE_FRESHNESS` set to 0 or below | every session with a marker skipped | gate disabled, as the docstring at `gateway/run.py:948` says |

Root cause: `last_resume_marked_at` / `updated_at` are naive local stamps written by the previous process (`gateway/session_lifecycle.py:21-23,211`), and naive subtraction ignores the UTC offset change between the write and the read. The per-turn path already reads the same field through the epoch helper (`gateway/run_turn_runner.py:1642`).

I also grepped `gateway/` for other code that subtracts a stored naive stamp from `datetime.now()`. `gateway/session_lifecycle.py:164-174` already uses epoch math. I left two cutoff sites unchanged: `SessionStore.list_sessions(active_minutes=...)` (`gateway/session.py:1274`) has no caller that passes `active_minutes`, and `prune_old_entries` (`gateway/session_lifecycle.py:230`) works in days, so a DST shift moves its cutoff by at most one hour.

## Verification

- New test `tests/gateway/test_restart_resume_pending.py::test_startup_auto_resume_freshness_survives_spring_forward`, parametrized over a naive local marker and an aware UTC marker. TZ is set to America/New_York with `time.tzset()`, as the neighbouring tests do.
  - On base `35272ce28b`: both cases fail. The naive case fails with `assert 0 == 1` and the aware case with `TypeError: can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes`.
  - With the fix: `2 tests passed`.
- Ran `scripts/run_tests.sh` on `tests/gateway/test_restart_resume_pending.py`, `test_platform_reconnect.py`, `test_restart_notice_replay.py` and `test_planned_restart_notice_multiplex.py` (every file that calls `_schedule_resume_pending_sessions`): 76 passed, 0 failed.
- E2E (`timestamp-recon/scripts/B5_auto_resume_dst_e2e.py`): one process uses a real `SessionStore` to write `sessions.json` with the marker at 01:50 local. A second process loads that file and runs the real scheduler at 03:10 local, with a fresh scratch `HERMES_HOME` and only the wall clock frozen.
  - Before: `real age s: 1200.0 | naive age s: 4800.0` → `scheduled auto-resume: 0`
  - After: `scheduled auto-resume: 1 | handle_message awaited: 1`
- Gates: `ruff check` on both touched files, `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all` and `git diff --check`, all clean.
- Not run: the full test suite, the rest of `tests/gateway/`, and a live gateway restart across a real DST transition.

On macOS under launchd, lines the gateway prints to stdout now reach `gateway.log` with a timestamp, so `hermes logs gateway --since` can filter them.

## What changed

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Gateway `print()` line in `gateway.log` (launchd and detached fallback) | `[whatsapp] Bridge started on port 3000` | `2026-09-28 15:20:01,434 [whatsapp] Bridge started on port 3000` |
| `hermes logs gateway --since 1h` on an old unstamped stdout line | kept, because the line cannot be dated (`hermes_cli/logs.py:80-86`) | new stdout lines carry a date and are filtered like handler lines |
| stdout line that already starts with `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS,mmm` | written as is | written as is (no second stamp) |
| Wrapper exit status | child's status, 78→0 for gateway argv, 128+N on signal | unchanged |
| Plist, log file names, detached fallback | `>> gateway.log 2>> gateway.error.log` | unchanged; no reinstall needed |

- `hermes_cli/stderr_timestamp.py`: the child now gets `stdout=PIPE` as well as `stderr=PIPE`. A daemon thread copies each stdout line, stamped with the existing `_write_timestamped_line`, to the wrapper's own fd 1, which is the file the caller chose (`gateway.log`). The wrapper waits at most 5 s for that thread after the child exits.
- Tests: `tests/hermes_cli/test_stderr_timestamp.py` (wrapper stamps stdout, keeps stderr in the error log, skips already-stamped lines, stamps a final line with no newline), `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_service.py` (macOS: a `print()` run through `launchd_program_arguments` + the wrapper arrives stamped in `gateway.log`), and `tests/hermes_cli/test_source_launcher_publication.py` (the launchd surface now strips the stamp before parsing the child's JSON receipt).

Root cause: the launchd shell appends the gateway's stdout to `gateway.log` (`hermes_cli/gateway_launchd.py:237,367`, detached fallback `:296-299`), the file the logging handler also writes (`hermes_logging.py:371`), and the wrapper stamped only stderr (`hermes_cli/stderr_timestamp.py:159` on base).

## Verification

- Red on base: `test_wrapper_timestamps_child_stdout_into_its_own_stdout` failed with `AssertionError: assert None ... fullmatch('\d{4}-... \[whatsapp\] Bridge started on port 3000', '[whatsapp] Bridge started on port 3000')`; `test_launchd_command_path_timestamps_gateway_stdout` failed with `'[whatsapp] Bridge started on port 3000\n' = read_text(...)`.
- Green: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_stderr_timestamp.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_service.py tests/hermes_cli/test_source_launcher_publication.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_external_supervisor.py tests/hermes_cli/test_doctor_command_install.py` → `5 files, 160 tests passed, 0 failed, 14 skipped`.
- E2E (macOS, fresh `HERMES_HOME`, real `launchd_program_arguments` osascript chain, stand-in child that calls `hermes_logging.setup_logging(mode='gateway')`, logs one record and prints one line):
  - Before: `gateway.log: '[whatsapp] Bridge started on port 3000' -> parsed ts: None`
  - After: `gateway.log: '2026-09-28 15:20:01,434 [whatsapp] Bridge started on port 3000' -> parsed ts: 2026-09-28 15:20:01`
  - A grandchild that holds the stdout pipe: before `exit 3 after 0.1s`, after `exit 3 after 5.1s` (exit code kept; bounded by the 5 s drain wait).
- Gates: `ruff check` on the 4 touched files, `python3 scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all`, `git diff --check`: all clean.
- Not run: a real `launchctl bootstrap` of an installed gateway service; the full test suite; Linux and Windows lanes (the new osascript test is `platforms("macos")`; the wrapper test is portable).
- Known change: a grandchild that inherited the gateway's stdout and outlives it now writes to a pipe whose reader (the wrapper) has exited, so its stdout writes fail (EPIPE) instead of landing in `gateway.log`. stderr already behaved this way. I found no gateway child that inherits stdout: the WhatsApp bridge, MCP stdio servers and terminal processes each get their own pipes or files.

The "Conversation started" line in the system prompt now shows the session's real start date when the session began in the other half of the DST year.

## What changed

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `TZ=Europe/London`, `HERMES_TIMEZONE=Europe/London`, today 2026-09-28 (BST), session id `20260115_003000_…` | `Conversation started: Wednesday, January 14, 2026 (Europe/London, BST, UTC+01:00)` | `Conversation started: Thursday, January 15, 2026 (Europe/London, BST, UTC+01:00)` |
| `spawn_tree.save` snapshot filename (`tui_gateway/methods_session.py:2371`), `finished_at=1768437000` | `20260115T003000.json` via deprecated `datetime.utcfromtimestamp` | `20260115T003000.json` via `datetime.fromtimestamp(..., timezone.utc)` |
| Hyperliquid `_format_timestamp_ms(1768437000123)` (`optional-skills/blockchain/hyperliquid/scripts/hyperliquid_client.py:174`) | `2026-01-15 00:30:00 UTC` via deprecated `utcfromtimestamp` | `2026-01-15 00:30:00 UTC` via `fromtimestamp(..., dt.timezone.utc)` |

- `agent/system_prompt.py:198`: `dt.replace(tzinfo=datetime.now().astimezone().tzinfo)` → `dt.astimezone()`.
- `tui_gateway/server.py:18`: also imports `timezone`. `tui_gateway/methods_session.py` has no imports of its own for these names; `bind_module` (`tui_gateway/method_ctx.py:78`) rebinds its functions onto `server.py`'s globals, so `timezone` has to exist there.
- `tests/agent/test_system_prompt.py`: `TestSessionStartLike::test_stamp_from_other_dst_half_keeps_its_own_offset`. Under `TZ=Europe/London` it checks a January 00:30 stamp read on a summer day and a July 00:30 stamp read on a winter day, so it fails on the old code whatever season the run happens in.

Root cause: `datetime.now().astimezone().tzinfo` is a fixed UTC offset for the current day, so attaching it to a naive stamp from the other DST half puts the stamp one hour off, which moves the date back a day for stamps between 00:00 and 01:00. `dt.astimezone()` uses the offset in force at the stamp, as `gateway/message_timestamps.py:34` already does.

Impact: only sessions whose id stamp falls within an hour of midnight and in the opposite DST half from the current day see a different date. For those sessions the first rebuild after this change produces a different "Conversation started" line, so their prompt-cache prefix is rebuilt once.

Related open PRs:
- #101811 also edits `_session_start_like` in `agent/system_prompt.py`, for a different reason. This change does not include its edit; whichever lands second will need a small rebase.
- #119970 fixes the same naive-plus-current-offset pattern in `cron/jobs.py:854` (with a DST-gap-aware helper). Not touched here.
- #79603 covers `datetime.utcnow()` in `gateway/platforms/bluebubbles.py`. Not touched here.

## Verification

- Red on base (35272ce28b): `AssertionError: assert '2026-01-14T23:30:00+00:00' == '2026-01-15T00:30:00+00:00'` in `test_stamp_from_other_dst_half_keeps_its_own_offset`.

items.body:
Cron execution, delivery and incident history now come back in time order across a DST fall-back or a timezone change.

Fixes #86520

## What changed

The cron stores write `hermes_time.now().isoformat()` (`cron/executions.py:190`, `cron/delivery_queue.py:195`, `cron/incidents.py:164`). That string carries the local UTC offset, which changes at DST and after a `timezone` config change. The queries sorted and compared the raw text. Every ORDER BY and the cursor comparison on these columns now use SQLite `julianday(col)`, which resolves any offset to the same instant. The raw text stays as the next sort key, so rows in the same millisecond keep their microsecond order.

Example (America/New_York, 2026-11-01): claim A at `01:50:00-04:00` (05:50Z), claim B at `01:10:00-05:00` (06:10Z, 20 minutes later).

| call | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `latest_execution(job)` / `list_jobs()[..]["latest_execution"]` | A (older) | B |
| `latest_executions([job])` | A | B |
| `list_executions(job_id=...)` order | A, B | B, A |
| `list_executions(before_claimed_at=B.claimed_at)` | `[]` | `[A]` |
| `delivery_queue.claim_next()` with A enqueued first | B | A (FIFO) |
| `incidents.list_incidents()` first row | A | B |
| timezone change: `+05:30` claim, then a claim 5 minutes later in `+00:00` → `latest_executions` | the `+05:30` claim | the later claim |

Call sites: `cron/executions.py:178` (prune), `:398` (cursor), `:407` (`list_executions`), `:436-446` (`latest_executions`); `cron/delivery_queue.py:60,69` (tombstone/prune), `:236` (pending claim order); `cron/incidents.py:268` (`list_incidents`).

The cursor in `list_executions` compares `(julianday(claimed_at), claimed_at) < (julianday(?), ?)`, the same key as its ORDER BY, so pages neither skip nor repeat rows.

`latest_executions()` now uses one `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY job_id ...)` window in place of a correlated per-row subquery. With `julianday()` in the ORDER BY, the index `idx_executions_job_claimed` no longer serves that subquery's `LIMIT 1`, so each row paid a sort: about 90 ms at 1000 rows and 800 ms at 3000 in a benchmark. The window form takes about 1 ms at 1000 rows and 3.5 ms at 3000. `ROW_NUMBER()` is already used in `hermes_state_sessions.py:1176` and `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:4459`.

No schema change and no data migration: stored values keep their offsets, and existing rows with mixed offsets order correctly as they are.

Root cause: offset-carrying ISO strings were ordered as TEXT, and text order differs from time order whenever two rows have different offsets.

This supersedes #86889 by zhao0112, which found the executions-ledger problem. That PR adds a `claimed_epoch` column with a backfill and moves storage to UTC for `cron/executions.py` only, and it no longer applies to the current `executions.py`. This PR covers all three stores (executions, delivery queue, incidents) and needs no schema migration.

## Verification

- Red on base 35272ce28b, 3 new tests failed:
  - `tests/cron/test_execution_ledger.py::test_history_orders_by_instant_across_dst_fall_back`: `AssertionError` on `latest_execution("dst-job")["id"] == later["id"]`
  - `tests/cron/test_delivery_queue.py::test_pending_deliveries_are_claimed_in_instant_order_across_dst_fall_back`: `assert 'exec-a-later' == 'exec-z-earlier'`
  - `tests/cron/test_cron_incidents.py::test_incidents_list_newest_instant_first_across_dst_fall_back`: `At index 0 diff: 'job-1_…' != 'job-2_…'`
- Green: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/cron/test_execution_ledger.py tests/cron/test_delivery_queue.py tests/cron/test_cron_incidents.py tests/cron/test_delivery_queue_retention_race.py tests/cron/test_cron_incidents_resolve.py`: 53 passed, 0 failed.
- SQLite probe (Python 3.11 and 3.12, SQLite 3.47.1): `julianday()` gives the same value for `06:10:00Z`, `11:40:00+05:30` and `01:10:00-05:00`, orders `01:50-04:00` before `01:10-05:00`, returns NULL for an unparseable string, and resolves to milliseconds (two stamps 1 µs apart compare equal, which is why the raw text is kept as the second key).
- E2E with real `cron.executions` / `cron.delivery_queue` / `cron.incidents` / `cron.jobs` against a fresh `HERMES_HOME`, only the wall clock pinned:
  - before: `latest_execution -> 2026-11-01T01:50:00-04:00 WRONG (older one)`, `delivery claim_next -> exec-a-second WRONG (not FIFO)`, `page before newest -> [] WRONG`, `tz change … latest_executions -> 2026-09-28T12:00:00+05:30 WRONG (older one)`
  - after: `latest_execution -> 2026-11-01T01:10:00-05:00 OK`, `delivery claim_next -> exec-z-first OK (FIFO)`, `page before newest -> ['2026-11-01T01:50:00-04:00'] OK`, `tz change … latest_executions -> 2026-09-28T06:35:00+00:00 OK`
- Query plans: `list_executions(job_id=...)` still searches `idx_executions_job_claimed (job_id=?)` and now adds `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY` over that job's rows. Terminal rows are capped at `MAX_TERMINAL_EXECUTIONS = 1000` (`cron/executions.py:29`). `list_executions()` without a job already scanned and sorted before this change.
- Gates: `ruff check` on the 6 touched files, `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all`, `git diff --check`: all clean.
- Not run: the full test suite, the rest of `tests/cron/`, and the dashboard or `hermes cron` CLI by hand.

Every console line the WhatsApp bridge writes to `bridge.log` now starts with a local-time stamp, and the JSON event lines that programs parse stay unchanged.

Fixes #97021

This salvages #97105 by @ygd58 (their commit is carried with authorship).

## What changed

| Line kind in `bridge.log` | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Lifecycle and warning lines (`console.log/warn/error`) | `⚠️  Connection closed (reason: 428). Reconnecting in 3s...` | `2026-09-28 15:27:46,818 ⚠️  Connection closed (reason: 428). Reconnecting in 3s...` |
| JSON event lines (pair events, `debug`, `poll_update_decode`, `ignored`) | `{"event":"ignored","reason":"allowlist_mismatch",...}` | byte-identical |
| Pino (Baileys logger) lines | `{"level":40,"time":...}` | byte-identical |
| Terminal QR block (`hermes whatsapp`) | printed through `console.log` | written straight to stdout, not stamped |

- Commit 1 (@ygd58): added a `timestampedLine()` helper and wrapped 12 of the bridge's console calls.
- Commit 2: replaces those 12 wraps with one `installConsoleStamps()` call at startup (`scripts/whatsapp-bridge/bridge.js:58`), so every console line is stamped, including the config summary, pairing-mode lines, the reconnect scheduler and version resolver messages, and inbound media download failures (`scripts/whatsapp-bridge/bridge_helpers.js:447`). The 12 call sites go back to plain console calls.
- The stamp is `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS,mmm` in local time (`formatLogStamp`, `scripts/whatsapp-bridge/bridge_helpers.js:733`), the same shape as the Python logs under `logs/`.
- JSON event lines go through `writeJsonLine()` (`scripts/whatsapp-bridge/bridge_helpers.js:754`), which writes to `process.stdout` directly. The dashboard pairing watcher runs `json.loads` on each stdout line of `bridge.js --pair-json` (`hermes_cli/web_routers/messaging.py:_watch_whatsapp_pairing`), so a stamped JSON line would be skipped and pairing would never see the QR or `connected` event.

Root cause: the adapter sends the bridge's stdout and stderr verbatim into `bridge.log` (`plugins/platforms/whatsapp/adapter.py:533-539`), and the bridge wrote its human-readable lines with bare `console.*` calls, so nothing in the chain added a time.

## Verification

- Red on the salvaged commit: `node --test scripts/whatsapp-bridge/bridge_helpers.timestamp.test.mjs` → `SyntaxError: The requested module './bridge_helpers.js' does not provide an export named 'formatLogStamp'` (fail 1).
- Green after commit 2: same command → `bridge_helpers.timestamp.test.mjs: all assertions passed`, pass 1, fail 0. The test checks that a wrapped `console.log` line carries a current local stamp with the text intact, that `console.warn` keeps multi-argument formatting on stderr, that a `writeJsonLine` event is written byte-for-byte without a stamp, and that an empty `console.log()` stays a bare newline.
- Neighbour tests still pass: `allowlist.test.mjs`, `bridge.reconnect.test.mjs`, `outbound_ids.test.mjs`, `owner_message_gate.test.mjs`.
- E2E: a node probe using the real `bridge_helpers.js` emitted each line kind. Its output was captured to a file the same way the adapter does, and also fed through the real `_watch_whatsapp_pairing` parser.
  - Before: `⚠️  Connection closed (reason: 428). Reconnecting in 3s...`; watcher `status=connected qr='QR-PAYLOAD'`.
  - After: `2026-09-28 15:27:46,818 ⚠️  Connection closed (reason: 428). Reconnecting in 3s...`; JSON and pino lines unchanged; watcher `status=connected qr='QR-PAYLOAD'`.
- Gates: `node --check` on `bridge.js` and `bridge_helpers.js`; `python3 scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all`; `git diff --check`.
- Not run: `bridge.native.test.mjs` fails to load without `node_modules` (`Cannot find package '@whiskeysockets/baileys'`), the same on base. The real bridge was not started against WhatsApp because its dependencies are not installed here.

## Pluggable, layered i18n across Core, TUI and Desktop — full language packs as plugins

**Bottom line:** any language can now be shipped as a plugin (`provides_locales` in `plugin.yaml` + YAML catalogs), overlaid per profile, or bundled; every user-facing string of the Python core (CLI, gateway platforms, approvals, tips), the Ink TUI and the Desktop app resolves through the catalog; and all 16 bundled locales carry full parity (**3,432 core keys + 1,250 TUI keys each**), verified by tests.

### What "pluggable" means here

Catalogs are **layered and partial**; resolution for `t(key)` / `i18n.catalog`:

```
plugin packs (last registered wins)  →  user overlay  <HERMES_HOME>/locales/<lang>[.tui|.desktop].yaml
  →  bundled  locales/<lang>[.tui].yaml  →  the same three layers for en  →  bare key
```

- **Plugin language pack** — manifest-only is enough:
  ```yaml
  provides_locales:
    - id: pl
      endonym: Polski
      rtl: false
  ```
  The plugin loader registers `locales/pl.yaml`, `pl.tui.yaml`, `pl.desktop.yaml` automatically; Python plugins can also call `ctx.register_locale(id, path_or_dict, surface=...)`. Packs may add languages Hermes never bundled (`pl`, `pt-br`, ...), and `display.language` / the Desktop and TUI language pickers accept them (`supported_languages()` = bundled ∪ overlay ∪ packs; `language_options()` carries endonym/rtl/source).
- **Per-profile overlay** — drop `<HERMES_HOME>/locales/<lang>.yaml` with only the keys you want to change; profile-scoped (A→B→A tested under one process).
- **Surfaces** — `core` (Python), `tui`, `desktop`. Renderers fetch their layer over JSON-RPC `i18n.languages` / `i18n.catalog {lang, surface}` and merge it over their bundled English; Desktop registers app locales dynamically (`host.i18n.registerAppLocale`, OpenRPC schema updated). Key sets for the TS surfaces are exported to `locales/_keys.tui.json` (1,250) and `locales/_keys.desktop.json` (4,878) on build.
- **Validation** — `hermes plugins validate <pack>` checks ids ↔ files, text-only leaves, unknown keys per surface, placeholder parity.
- **Reference pack** — https://github.com/teknium1/hermes-lang-pl (manifest-only, core + TUI + Desktop; v0.2.0 @ `3072a5f8adb` = full coverage: 3,426 core, 1,250 TUI, 4,862 desktop; `hermes plugins validate` passes).
- **Install scanner** — `locales/<lang>.yaml` in a pack steps the agent-config family down one level (the bundled `en.yaml` itself matched `updating: "... AGENTS.md"` at critical, making any faithful pack uninstallable); injection shapes keep full severity.

Docs: `website/docs/user-guide/features/language-packs.md`, developer-guide plugins § language packs, `agent/AGENTS.md` § i18n.

### String extraction (the bulk of the diff)

- **Core Python:** 3,113 hard-coded human-facing literals across 81 files wired through `t()` — display/turn explainers/status, the 387-tip catalog, CLI chat loops/REPL/slash commands/setup/doctor/profiles, session + skills-hub + cron CLIs, voice/dev/system commands, gateway base approval cards and all 12 platform adapters (shared approval-card keys so platforms cannot diverge). `locales/en.yaml`: 374 → **3,426** keys.
- **TUI (`ui-tui/`):** new i18n subsystem (`src/i18n/` runtime, loader over `i18n.catalog`, typed `en/*` siblings, `npm run i18n:keys` emitter) and ~1,200 literals wired: userMessages, every slash command reply, session/gateway/lib text, pickers, hubs, secure prompts, chat bits, billing/subscription/connection/journey overlays. Module-level English constants became lazy so a pack swap is observed (tests per table). `_keys.tui.json`: 81 → **1,250**.
- **Desktop (`apps/desktop/`):** dynamic `Locale` registry (bundled 16 + app-registered + backend packs), RPC synchroniser, plugin SDK entry, keys emitter.

Deliberately left literal (all lanes, same rule): model-facing text, RPC/tool/model/provider ids, slash names and flags, hotkey chords, env vars/paths/URLs, brand names, glyphs, log lines, agent-directed kanban wake messages.

### Bundled locales (Option A — full parity kept)

af, ar, de, es, fr, ga, hu, it, ja, ko, pt, ru, tr, uk, zh, zh-hant: each `locales/<lang>.yaml` = 3,426/3,426 keys and `locales/<lang>.tui.yaml` = 1,250/1,250 keys, 0 missing / 0 extra / 0 placeholder mismatches. Existing translations preserved byte-for-byte; 424 pre-existing English stubs in the old 374-key set translated. Comma-separated matcher lists keep the English tokens and append localized ones (and restore 3 that had dropped English tokens in fr/tr).

### Tests / verification

- `tests/agent/test_i18n.py` (parity + fallback, 37), `test_i18n_layers.py` (packs/overlay/profile scope, 22), `test_i18n_languages.py`, `test_i18n_tui_packs.py` (bundled TUI packs mirror `_keys.tui.json`; bundled layer served under overlay/packs), `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_validate_locales.py`, `tests/tui_gateway/test_i18n_methods.py`, `tests/gateway/test_platform_adapter_i18n.py`, per-lane wiring tests.
- Union sweep `scripts/run_tests.sh --paths tests/agent tests/hermes_cli tests/gateway tests/tools tests/tui_gateway tests/plugins`: **~35,000 passed**; the 45 failing files reproduce with identical pass/fail counts on `origin/main` (update/venv-holder/plugin-install/toolchain/network tests — environmental).
- `ui-tui`: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `i18n:keys:check` fresh, vitest 1611 passed / 1 failed (`textInputRedoShift` kitty CSI-u redo, pre-existing on main).
- `apps/desktop`: `tsc --noEmit` clean; vitest failures are all packaging/native-toolchain (`app-builder-lib`, `@novnc/novnc` not installed locally, real `uv`), none in i18n.

### Surfaced by CI on this branch (all fixed in-branch)

- **Install scanner vs. faithful packs** — `plugin_guard` scored our own `en.yaml` line `updating: "⚡ Updating AGENTS.md…"` as `agent_config_mod` (critical), so any complete language pack was uninstallable. `locales/*.yaml` inside a `provides_locales` plugin now steps the config-edit family down one level (caution, confirmable); injection shapes keep full weight. `tests/tools/test_plugin_guard.py::TestLanguagePackCatalogs`.
- **Fresh-source installer tail** — `hermes_cli.config` → `cli_output` now resolves text through `agent.i18n`, so `tests/scripts/test_fresh_source_install.py`'s minimal fixture tree carries the i18n kernel (`agent/{i18n,i18n_layers,i18n_languages}.py` + `locales/en.yaml`), not the agent runtime. Verified on a real 3.14 interpreter locally and in CI.
- **`display.language` validation** — refuses unknown ids with the live list (`tests/hermes_cli/test_config_display_language.py`); excluded from the e2e "any documented key accepts an arbitrary string" property alongside the other special-cased keys.
- Relay adapter (`gateway/relay/adapter.py`) prompt copy routed through `t()` (`platform.relay.*`, 5 keys × 17 catalogs); its dead import-bound `EA_HEADER_TEXT` copies dropped.
- Main's reworded uncompressed-context warning adopted in en + 16 locales; MDX pipe/template-literal escapes in docs; TUI import order; `utf-8-sig` on the pack validator (Windows footgun lint).
- **Builds never write the key exports** — the desktop build regenerated `locales/_keys.desktop.json` inside the checkout, so a `hermes update` that rebuilt the app left the tree dirty (Desktop update E2E caught it: `M locales/_keys.desktop.json`). `_keys.desktop.json` / `_keys.tui.json` are committed artifacts pinned to `en.ts` by `apps/desktop/scripts/i18n-keys.test.mjs` and `ui-tui` `i18n:keys:check`; the builds only read them.
- Three `origin/main` merges (65 + 67 + compat-layer removal #126164) with conflicts resolved in `cli_agent_setup_mixin.py`, `main_tui_launch.py`, `run_inbound.py`, `display.py`, `commands.py` — main's logic kept, string routed through `t()`.

### Behaviour notes

- Precedence puts plugin packs above the user overlay (a pack is something the user installed deliberately; the overlay still wins over bundled). `reset_language_cache()` on `config set display.language`, on pack (un)load, or overlay edit; catalogs cached per `(home, lang)`.
- `HERMES_LANGUAGE` env override and `display.language` unchanged in shape; unknown ids refused with the live list.
- No new `HERMES_*` env vars; no in-tree vendor packs; nothing written outside `HERMES_HOME`.

items.body:
Concurrent API requests on a brand-new session id no longer interleave their turns. The first turn on a session id without a row now takes the durable turn lease like every later turn does, so a second request waits and then sees the first turn's rows.

Fixes #125124. Salvage of #125125 by @jonpol01. Their three commits are cherry-picked with authorship kept; commit 2 also carries a `Co-authored-by` for @JoaoMarcos44, whose #125199 pointed out the post-admission read ordering.

## What changed

- `agent/turn_facade_lease.py::admit_durable_turn_lease` (@jonpol01):
  - A session id takes the lease whether or not its row exists.
  - The row is read once, after admission.
  - After a contended wait, the transcript is reloaded only when the row is not known to be missing, so an in-memory seed on a fresh id survives.
  - A failed row read is "unknown" rather than "exists", so it never promotes `_session_db_created`.
  - Background-review forks (`_persist_disabled`) still skip the lease.
- Follow-up (ours, `c894ebb75c`): after a wait, when the row state is unknown and the reload returns nothing, the caller's history is now kept. Before, input carried over from an interrupted earlier wait was appended before that check, so an empty reload looked non-empty and replaced the caller's history with the carried message alone.
- Tests (ours, `a550b94886`, `e7e4ffa24d`): the per-case row-state tests are folded into one parametrized table, and each production guard is checked by mutation:
  - Deleting the known-missing reload guard fails `absent-after-wait`.
  - Reverting the follow-up fails `unreadable-empty`.
  - The real-SQLite first-turn test detects the wait through `on_wait` rather than the status wording, and closes its DBs in a `finally`.

Root cause: `admit_durable_turn_lease` returned without a lease when `get_session()` found no row. Client-addressed ids (the `X-Hermes-Session-Id` header, the `/v1/runs` `session_id`, fingerprint-derived `api-<hash>` ids) are not unique to one process, so a second request could find the row the first turn had just created, take a lease nobody held, and run alongside it.

## Validation

| | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Two concurrent requests on a new `X-Hermes-Session-Id` (real `APIServerAdapter`, real `AIAgent`, real state.db, fake provider on loopback) | rows `user, user, assistant, assistant` (3/3 runs) | `user, assistant, user, assistant` (2/2 runs on this branch, 3/3 on #125125 head); the second request waits and sees the first turn |
| Header-less fingerprint-derived id | interleaved | serialized |
| Single first turn; delegate child while its parent holds the lease | no lease | completes without waiting; `session_turn_leases` empty afterwards |
| `tests/agent/test_cross_process_turn_lease.py` + `test_turn_facade_lease.py` | 4 of the new cases fail | 22 passed |

A wider run over the lease-related test files showed no failures unique to this branch. Every failure in those files also fails on origin/main at the same test IDs. Ruff, `check-windows-footguns.py --all` and `check_compat_pointers.py` are clean.

## Behaviour change

The first turn of every persisted session now takes the lease: CLI, cron, `-Q`, subagent children and the API server. That costs one acquire write and one release write per fresh session. When `turn_liveness` is configured, those first turns also get the watchdog and refresher.

## Not changed here

- The derived-id collision between different header-less clients (#7484).
- The API server's pre-admission history snapshot (#84235).
- Two effects of lease contention that this widening makes reachable on first turns:
  - A busy SQLite write lock (more than 0.5 s) shows up as "another process is using this session".
  - A crashed first turn on an id that never recurs leaves an expired lease row that no sweep removes.

  Both mechanisms already exist on main for later turns; each will get its own follow-up.

Supersedes #125125 and #125199.

Restart-safe cron jobs launched from a multi-profile gateway run their task again. They had been dying with `No module named 'ruamel'` before the worker acknowledged the job. If the worker's dependency environment cannot be activated, the worker now stops before that acknowledgement and the gateway reports the failure, instead of running on dependencies nothing holds.

This salvages #122936 by @ethernet8023, which is itself a salvage of #122290 by @123456hyu. All five original commits are cherry-picked with authorship preserved, and three commits of ours are on top. It covers both fixes andrexibiza asked for on #122936: the boot runs in the package prelude, and activation failures stop the worker. 123456hyu had already made both changes on #122290 (`dff16e12`). They are carried here without that commit's argv-substring gate and source-order test (AGENTS.md bans both), and 123456hyu is credited with `Co-authored-by`.

Closes #122222, closes #123400, closes #125269.

## Root cause

The restart-safe external worker is spawned as `sys.executable -m cron.scheduler --external-worker-file ...`. In multiplex mode the child env is scrubbed, which drops the committed PM generation's `site-packages`, and the spawning interpreter is PM's store Python, which owns no third-party packages. `-m cron.scheduler` runs `cron/__init__.py` first. Its first import, `cron.jobs` → `hermes_yaml` → `ruamel`, fails before the worker writes its ownership ack.

## Changes

From #122290 / #122936, unchanged:
- `cron/scheduler_worker_env.py`: pin the committed generation's `site-packages` on the worker's PYTHONPATH, after the checkout.
- `cron/worker_bootstrap.py`: the marked worker runs `pm.environments.activate_dependencies`, the same boot `hermes_bootstrap` performs. That call leases the generation for the process's lifetime and runs its `.pth` files.
- The `cron/AGENTS.md` contract and the contributor email mappings.

Ours:
- **Boot before `cron.jobs`.** #122936 called the boot from `cron/scheduler.py`. That code only runs after `cron/__init__.py` has already imported `cron.jobs`, so `ruamel` came from an unleased path (andrexibiza's first P1). The call now sits at the top of `cron/__init__.py`, under a private alias so the `cron.worker_bootstrap` submodule attribute is not shadowed.
- **Fail closed.** A genuine `activate_dependencies` failure now propagates. The worker exits before its ack, and `_launch_external_cron_worker` reports the dispatch failure with the worker's stderr. Previously the error was logged and the worker kept running on a generation the collector could delete mid-job (andrexibiza's second P1). PM's legitimate no-op cases (a venv, a wheel, Nix, nothing committed under a venv) still return normally.
- **Marker rename.** `HERMES_CRON_EXTERNAL_WORKER` becomes `_HERMES_CRON_WORKER_BOOT`. The old name differed by one underscore from `_HERMES_CRON_EXTERNAL_WORKER`, the owning execution id, which is read in the same worker.
- **Docs.** The docstrings and `cron/AGENTS.md` now describe the fail-closed boot.
- **Tests.** Three tests, each running a real subprocess:
  - The marked worker boots before `cron.jobs`, boots exactly once, and consumes the marker; unmarked importers are never booted. PM is stubbed in this test only.
  - With the real PM boot, the worker imports a sentinel module that exists only in the committed generation. When a newer generation is committed mid-job, the real collector keeps the worker's generation until the worker exits, then removes it.
  - With the real PM boot, a damaged selection (a committed venv without `site-packages`) makes the worker exit before `cron.jobs` is imported.

## Validation

**Real dispatch, live.** The probe drives the real `_launch_external_cron_worker` → spawn → ack → wait path. The parent is a PM-bootstrapped store Python 3.14, the generation is a real committed PM generation, and the job is a `no_agent` script job. The only stub is the Linux/systemd gate: dispatch mode is forced to `degraded`, the direct subprocess a managed gateway uses when it has no user D-Bus.

| multiplex worker env | `origin/main` | #122936 as-is | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| healthy generation | exits before ack (`No module named 'ruamel'`) | ack, script runs | ack, script runs, execution `completed` |
| damaged committed generation | not run | ack, job **runs on the unleased generation** | exits before ack; dispatch failure reported with PM's error |

On this head, single-profile runs give the same results as the multiplex rows.

**Mutation checks.** Each check reverts one part of the fix and runs the new tests against it:
- Restoring #122936's swallowed error fails the damaged-selection test.
- Removing the prelude boot fails all three new subprocess tests.
- Activating without a lease lets the collector delete the live worker's generation (`removed [g1]`).

**Suites.** `tests/cron/` + `tests/pm/` fail on the same tests as `origin/main` on the same macOS host (host-environment reds), with no new failures. ruff, `check-windows-footguns.py --all` and `check_compat_pointers.py` are clean.

**Follow-ups, not in this PR:**
- A shared PM helper for the checkout + committed site-packages PYTHONPATH recipe, which is also built in `activation_environment` and `cron/scheduler_script.py`.
- If PM commits a new generation mid-job, the worker's user-facing children still get the old generation's path.

## Credit

- @JoanDuarte: the original analysis (#122222).
- @webtecnica: the earliest fix (#122238).
- @123456hyu: the pin, the lease, and the prelude and fail-closed design (#122290).
- @ethernet8023: the consolidation and the PM-selection rework (#122936).
- @andrexibiza: the review that found both P1s.
- The duplicate cluster: #122719 by @aglowinthefield, #122685 by @etrisnanto, #122738 by @GabboAlarcon, #122382 by @Sakujakira. @ehz0ah's review of #122719 suggested the sentinel-plus-rotation test design used here.

## What does this PR do?

Fixes the #126338 wedge where a desktop runtime plugin whose `register()` fails (and whose rollback disposer also throws) can never be hot-reloaded again — every later reload dies re-running the previous incarnation's broken disposers, so file edits look inert until an app restart.

Root cause: both `unloadRuntimePlugin()` and `failRegistration()` ran the disposer list with a bare `forEach(dispose => dispose())` and only released the registration (`loaded.delete`) after the loop. A disposer with its own bug (the report: a `ReferenceError` inside the plugin's `stopDetailLoops`) aborted the loop mid-way, stranded the `delete`, and left the registration held. Every subsequent reload then hit `unloadRuntimePlugin(plugin.id)` first — which re-ran the SAME stale disposer list and threw again before the fresh `register()` could ever execute. The repeated stack traces carrying the old blob URL (the report's "cached blob" observation) are exactly those re-run disposers; each load already mints a fresh blob URL, so no stale module bytes were involved — the reload never got far enough to evaluate the new module.

The fix keeps the suggested shape from the issue:

- `unloadRuntimePlugin()` releases the record **before** running the disposers and wraps each disposer in its own `try/catch` (logged), so one bad cleanup can neither leak the remaining disposers nor hold the registration.
- `failRegistration()` reuses `unloadRuntimePlugin()` for its rollback instead of duplicating the bare loop, so the register-failure path is tolerant the same way.

## Related Issue

Fixes #126338

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/contrib/runtime-loader.ts` — `unloadRuntimePlugin()`: delete the registration first, then run each disposer in its own `try/catch` with an error log (was: bare `forEach` + delete that a throwing disposer could skip).
- `apps/desktop/src/contrib/runtime-loader.ts` — `failRegistration()`: rollback now goes through `unloadRuntimePlugin(plugin.id)` instead of its own bare `forEach` + `loaded.delete` (the disposer-list parameter is gone with it), so a throwing rollback disposer no longer escapes the failure handler.
- `apps/desktop/src/contrib/runtime-loader.test.ts` — two regression tests (see How to Test).

## How to Test

1. `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --project ui src/contrib/runtime-loader.test.ts` — all 32 tests pass, including the two new ones:
   - `a rollback disposer that throws cannot wedge the registry: the fixed source still reloads (#126338)` — loads v1 whose `register()` throws after `ctx.onDispose(() => { throw … })`, then loads a fixed v2 under the same id. Observed result: v2 registers and the row is `loaded`; on the pre-fix code the first assertion already fails (the row reports the rollback error instead of `register boom`) and the reload returns `null`.
   - `unloadRuntimePlugin releases the registration even when a disposer throws (#126338)` — a successfully loaded plugin with a throwing disposer; `unloadRuntimePlugin()` no longer throws and a reload registers fresh. Observed result: on the pre-fix code `unloadRuntimePlugin()` propagates `Error: dispose boom`; with the fix it passes and the reload reaches `status: 'loaded'`.
2. Both tests were verified red on the pre-fix source (via `git stash` of the loader change) and green with the fix.
3. Manual path from the issue: create a plugin whose `dispose` path throws and whose `register` fails, fix the file, save — the reload now evaluates the corrected bytes and the row recovers without an app restart.

## What does this PR do?

Toggling Settings → Appearance → Minimize to tray off and back on in one Linux session destroys the Electron `Tray` and then constructs another. `Tray.destroy()` drops the StatusNotifierItem object but leaves its D-Bus interfaces exported, so the second `new Tray()` cannot re-export them. The desktop app's dev renderer boots and renders again, instead of a blank page with `Cannot access 'IS_MAC' before initialization`.

## Root cause

`2ffa4977ba` made `combo.ts` import `keybindActionAllowedInEditableTarget` from `actions.ts`, but `actions.ts` already imported `IS_MAC` from `combo.ts`. This import cycle lets `actions.ts` build its `KEYBIND_ACTIONS` table before `combo.ts` has set `IS_MAC`, so module evaluation throws and `#root` stays empty.

## What changed

- `apps/desktop/src/lib/keybinds/actions.ts` now gets the platform from `isMacPlatform()` in `@/lib/platform`. That module has no imports of its own. `chords.ts` and other keybind code already use it.
- `actions.ts` no longer imports `combo.ts`, so the cycle is gone.
- The three platform-dependent defaults (`composer.voice`, `view.terminalCopy`, `view.terminalPaste`) are still resolved once, at module load, the same as before.

One file, +4/−5. No re-export shim: `IS_MAC` stays in `combo.ts` for its other importers.

## How verified

- **Live repro, before:** Vite dev server for `apps/desktop` on `origin/main`, loaded in headless Chromium. Page error: `Cannot access 'IS_MAC' before initialization`. `#root` has 0 children.
- **Live repro, after:** same setup with this change. No such error. `#root` renders. The only remaining errors come from `window.hermesDesktop` being absent, which is expected in a plain browser without the Electron preload.
- A static import-graph walk over `apps/desktop/src` finds no import cycle through `combo.ts` or `actions.ts`.
- `npm run typecheck` passes. `eslint` and `prettier --check` pass on the changed file.

Tests not run locally; CI runs them.

Codex web searches now stay a proper search card after a transcript refresh or reopen. Before this change they turned into a raw `[codex webSearch] {json}` note.

WHO: Codex app-server runtime users (Desktop, and any surface that reloads stored history).
WHEN: every Codex turn that runs its built-in web search, once the transcript is refreshed or reopened.
WHY: the live bubble for a `webSearch` item uses tool name `web_search` and id `codex_web_search_<itemId>`, but `CodexEventProjector` had no entry for `webSearch`, so the stored history held an opaque note instead of the tool call.

Changes
- `agent/transports/codex_event_projector.py`: new `webSearch` entry in `_TOOL_PROJECTIONS`. It stores a `web_search` tool call under the same id and args as the live bubble. The tool result is `{"provider": "codex"}` (plus `status` only when Codex sends one), so a later non-Codex turn can tell Codex ran the search.
- `agent/codex_runtime.py`: corrected the comment that said `webSearch` has no projector entry.
- One invariant test: the stored name and call id equal the live bridge's `_codex_item_to_tool_name` / `_stable_call_id`. It fails on main.

Validation
| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Codex `webSearch` item → projector → `SessionDB` → `/messages` display rows | 1 opaque `[codex webSearch]` row, no tool call | `web_search` tool call `codex_web_search_ws_abc`, same as the live card id |
| Desktop `toChatMessages` on those rows | raw JSON text bubble | one `web_search` tool card under the live id |
| codex/projector test files (41 files + `tests/agent/transports/`) | 68 pre-existing local failures | same 68, none new |

Credit
- Salvaged from #66995 by @h4ck200711, the first submitter of the `webSearch` projection. Their commit is cherry-picked with authorship kept. It was cut down to the projection only, rebuilt on the current `_TOOL_PROJECTIONS` table, and keeps the live `web_search` name so the existing Desktop search card and icon still apply. The MCP elicitation trust change from #66995 is not included here.
- This is the real cause behind #125917 by @helix4u, a client-side fix that re-attaches live tool cards after a text-only refresh. With the stored rows fixed, that client-side change is no longer needed.

## What

The checkout updater strategies (windows-handoff / posix-handoff, and their
manual-command path) reported a status with no `currentSha` whenever the
Python source probe could not attribute one — a probe-less checkout
(`readSourceUpdate` → null), or a probe status that predates the field. The
statusbar version badge and the command palette read
`status.currentSha` (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/122727,
part 3), so the commit showed nowhere on those installs.

`check()` in `updater/checkout.ts` now fills `currentSha` from the checkout's
own `install-stamp.json` commit — the same stamp the CLI's completion tail
publishes and the updater already trusts — whenever the probe did not supply
one. The probe's own value always wins; the stamp is a file read, not a new
git spawn.

**No update decision changed:** the stamped commit is display data only — it
never feeds the update-available decision, the handoff, or install
behaviour.

## Tests

New `electron/updater/checkout-current-sha.test.ts` (all four cases fail on
main):

- each handoff mechanism's status carries `currentSha` from the install
  stamp when the source probe never supplied one (the probe-less manual
  checkout)
- a probe status without `currentSha` (error shapes) is filled from the
  stamp; a probe status with its own `currentSha` is never overridden
- `readStampedCommit` handles absent and malformed stamps

Verification: `npm run check:lint` and
`vitest run --project electron electron/updater/` (144 passed) from
`apps/desktop` — updater tests live in the `electron` project per
`vitest.config.ts`.

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/122727

Other halves of that issue already landed in
https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/122737 (`display_version`
keeps `git.<sha>`; `version-status` treats `unknown` as missing). Open PRs
that *consume* `currentSha` but do not populate the checkout status:
https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/70954,
https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/42382,
https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/88326.

items.body:
When another writer holds the state.db write lock past the lease attempt's write patience (0.5s), a new turn no longer says "Another Hermes process is using this session". It also no longer sits out an extra poll second before retrying.

## Why

`acquire_session_turn_lease` handled a write-lock timeout the same way as a lease held by another turn. It called `on_wait`, so the agent announced another process on the session, even when the busy writer was a checkpoint or a different session's flush. It then slept a full poll interval, although the attempt had already spent its patience. Since #126309 (first-turn lease, #125124), this path also runs on first, delegate, cron and one-shot turns, which were not reached before.

## Change

- `hermes_state_compression.py`: a lock timeout retries at once. The poll interval moves into the retry's write patience, so the retry takes the lock the moment it frees up, and the failed-attempt cadence (and with it the `log_write_lock_holders` warning) stays at about one per 1.5s, as on main. It reports through a new `on_contended()` callback instead of `on_wait`. The retry sleep reuses `_sleep_before_write_retry`.
- `agent/turn_facade_lease.py`: `_on_contended` shows nothing, but the transcript still reloads after admission. The busy writer may have been the previous holder's final flush, and main already reloaded in that case through `on_wait`. "Session is free; loading the latest transcript..." now appears only after an announced wait.

## Verification

- Live, on a real SQLite state.db with a second connection holding `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`:

  | lock held | main | this PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | 0.3s | 0.26s, no notice | 0.40s, no notice |
  | 1.5s | 2.11s, `on_wait` fired | 1.52s, no `on_wait`, one `on_contended` |
  | 3.0s | 3.06s, `on_wait` fired | 3.04s, no `on_wait`, one `on_contended` |

- `tests/hermes_state/test_session_turn_lease.py`:
  - The existing lock-retry test now also asserts no `on_wait`, exactly one `on_contended`, and no poll-interval sleep.
  - A new test checks that a database locked for the whole wait times out without a lease-wait notice.
  - Both fail on main.
- `tests/agent/test_cross_process_turn_lease.py`: the reload test is parametrized over `on_wait` and `on_contended`. Both reload; only `on_wait` announces.
  - It fails if `_on_contended` stops requesting the reload.
  - It fails if the "Session is free" line is emitted unconditionally.
- The 3 lease test files pass 43/43. ruff is clean.

Review: `hermes-pr-review` 2c and three `/simplify-code` reviewers ran twice. The first round found that dropping the reload would lose a finishing holder's turn; this version fixes that. The second round found the unannounced "Session is free" line; also fixed.

  - Cherry-picked #109839 (@MaxFreedomPollard): the launch cwd beats a stale inherited `HERMES_CWD`.
  - On the local backend, the launcher now passes the launch dir (or `--worktree`) as `HERMES_TUI_CWD`, which the TUI sends on `session.create`. An absolute `terminal.cwd` no longer overrides it. Remote backends keep `terminal.cwd`.
- **Codex final reply renders twice** (#125951). The app-server bridge sends its final `agentMessage` down the interim path without setting `response_previewed`. `message.complete` now marks a final that matches an interim the client already received, so TUI and Desktop dedupe it.

## Desktop

- **"Chat out of date" after a tool-using turn** (#125975). A folded tool turn is addressed by its final row after live settle but by its first row after hydration, so the stale-send guard's tips never matched and the next send was refused. The tip now reads every durable row the bubble owns. This got worse after #125523.
- **Fallback-switch notice vanishes on refresh** (#126422). That notice exists only on the client, and every refresh path rebuilt from stored rows. Trailing client-local `system` rows (no `rowId`) are now carried across all three refresh paths.
- **Replayed preview typing ignores Stop** (#125408). The superseded handler's `finally` deleted the replay's abort controller. It now releases only the controller it owns.
- **Stuck "context compression in progress"** (#125479). Cherry-picked #125481 (@wdelarme): terminal compression stamps persist immediately instead of being dropped inside the persist window.
- **"Move to project" shows the session under both projects** (#125694). Cherry-picked #125804 (@Wenfengcheng): workspace-only sidebar refreshes are no longer discarded as unchanged.

Closes #126107
Closes #125951
Closes #125975
Closes #126422
Closes #125408
Closes #125479
Closes #125694
Refs #84015. The #121524 tool-row regression is fixed separately in #126479.

items.body:
Turn-lease rows left behind by turns that died without releasing (SIGKILL, crash, parent killed with children in flight) are now deleted once they are more than 24h past expiry.

## Why

Acquisition only reclaims the row of the conversation it is acquiring, so a row stays in `session_turn_leases` for good when nobody resumes that conversation. One real state.db had 4 such rows, 16 to 25 days past expiry, all from dead CLI processes. Since #126309 (first-turn lease, #125124), first turns also take the lease, so a crashed first turn now leaves a row too. The `idx_session_turn_leases_expires` index has existed since the lease landed (6e929a9694) but nothing read it.

## Change

`try_acquire_session_turn_lease` now runs `DELETE FROM session_turn_leases WHERE expires_at < now - 24h` inside its existing write transaction, through that index.

Startup maintenance is not the right home for this. The CLI path runs only one-time latched repairs, and the gateway path only runs when `sessions.auto_archive`/`auto_prune` are enabled (off by default). Acquisition runs on every surface.

The 24h grace keeps the deliberate starved-refresher recovery in `hermes_state_messages.py`: an expired row that a live writer still owns is renewed on its next fenced write. The grace is therefore also the longest a suspended holder can go unrefreshed and keep its lease. Past it, the next acquisition anywhere removes the row, and the holder's next write stops with `SessionTurnLeaseLostError`. That matches what already happens today when the same conversation is re-acquired.

## Verification

- On a copy of the real lease table (8 rows), one acquisition removed exactly the 4 rows expired 16 to 25 days ago. It kept the row expired 15.6h ago and the live rows.
- New test in `tests/hermes_state/test_session_turn_lease.py`:
  - A row expired just over 24h ago is swept.
  - Rows expired just under 24h ago and 10s ago are kept.
  - The 10s-expired row's live owner can still renew it on a fenced write.
  - It fails on main. It also fails with the grace changed to 36h, and fails if the grace is shortened.
- The file passes 20/20. ruff is clean.

Not included: the same sweep for `compression_locks`. That table has 0 rows in the real state.db, so the leak there is unproven.

Review: `hermes-pr-review` 2c and three `/simplify-code` reviewers found nothing material in the change. The re-review tightened the test so it pins the grace from both sides.

Author: @kshitijk4poor, follow-up to #126309.
items.title: fix(state): turn-lease rows left by dead holders are swept after 24h

items.body:
Hiding reasoning no longer hides tool activity. Each setting now controls only its own events: `display.show_reasoning` decides whether reasoning shows, and `display.tool_progress` decides whether tool rows show.

Salvages #125948 by @wyf9661. Their commit stays first, with authorship kept. Two commits on top remove the part of it that still tied the settings together, and fix the same coupling in the other direction.

## What was wrong

Two display settings reach the TUI and Desktop through `tui_gateway` (the Python backend that both apps talk to):

| Setting | Controls |
|---|---|
| `display.show_reasoning` | The model's thinking: streamed reasoning, the finished reasoning block, and the reference-model output of MoA (a mode where several models answer and one aggregates). |
| `display.tool_progress` | Tool rows: `terminal`, `read_file`, `search_files`, ... `off` hides them. |

#121524 (for #85110) made tool rows need **both** settings on. With `show_reasoning: false` or `/reasoning hide`, every ordinary tool row disappeared, even with an explicit `tool_progress: all`. Only card tools (`clarify`, `delegate_task`, file edits, ...) and failed calls were left. The gateway dropped the events, so no client could draw them. This change reached canary builds only.

`main` also had the reverse coupling, which predates #121524. `_on_tool_progress` returned early for every event when `tool_progress` was off. That dropped the finished reasoning block and the MoA events along with the tool events. For a model that streams no reasoning deltas, `tool_progress: off` hid all reasoning, even with `show_reasoning: true`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph main["main"]
    R1[show_reasoning] --> T1[tool rows]
    P1[tool_progress] --> T1
    P1 --> B1[reasoning block]
    R1 --> B1
  end
  subgraph pr["this PR"]
    R2[show_reasoning] --> B2[reasoning]
    P2[tool_progress] --> T2[tool rows]
  end
```

## What changes

| Commit | Change |
|---|---|
| `32244754a5` @wyf9661 (#125948) | Desktop gets its own tool-visibility store, `$showToolActivity`, fed by `display.tool_progress`. The three Desktop gates that read `$showReasoning` for tool rows now read it. On the gateway, an explicit `tool_progress` value restores tool rows while reasoning stays hidden. |
| `11fc8f1692` | Removes the rule that tools stay hidden when `show_reasoning` is off and no `tool_progress` key is written. That rule still read one setting from the other, and it relied on whether a key was present in config.yaml. The gateway gates `tool.start`, `tool.complete`, `tool.generating` and the subagent tool mirror on `_tool_progress_enabled` only. `_process_tool_chrome_enabled` and `_tool_progress_explicit` are deleted. On Desktop, `$showToolActivity` is a plain atom: only `false` or `"off"` hide rows, the same rule as the gateway's `_load_tool_progress_mode`. |
| `7d73f07047` | `tool_progress: off` now hides only `tool.output_risk` (the risk badge on a tool row). The reasoning block and the MoA events follow `show_reasoning`, which their handlers already check. |

This PR keeps these parts of #121524: reasoning deltas, finished blocks, MoA and subagent reasoning gated on `show_reasoning`; failed calls always emitted (`_tool_result_needs_user`); the card-tool set.

**Answer-only** (only the final response) is now `show_reasoning: false` plus `tool_progress: off`. `cli-config.yaml.example` says so.

## What the user sees

| show_reasoning | tool_progress | Tool rows: `main` | Tool rows: this PR | Reasoning: `main` | Reasoning: this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| true | all | shown | shown | shown | shown |
| **false** | **all** | **hidden** | **shown** | hidden | hidden |
| true | off | hidden | hidden | **finished block hidden** | **shown** |
| false | off | hidden | hidden | hidden | hidden |

In every row, card tools, todos, diffs and failed calls still show.

## Verification

**Live gateway probe.** A real `tui_gateway` ran over stdio with one real turn per row, on a Nous model with `reasoning_effort: medium`. Each run used a fresh temp `HERMES_HOME`. The turn had to call `terminal` and then `read_file`. The table counts the events that left the gateway.

| show_reasoning | tool_progress | `tool.start` on `main` | `tool.start` on this PR | finished reasoning block, `main` → this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| true | all | terminal, read_file | terminal, read_file | 1 → 1 |
| false | all | **none** | **terminal, read_file** | 0 → 0 |
| true | off | none | none | **0 → 1** |
| false | off | none | none | 0 → 0 |

**Live UI, this PR.** The same prompt ran with a fresh temp `HERMES_HOME` per run. The backend ran from this branch; the process list confirmed its python path and working directory.

| Surface | show_reasoning / tool_progress | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Ink TUI (`hermes --tui`) | true / all | `Tool calls (2)`: `Terminal("echo PROBE_OK")`, `Read File("hostname")` |
| Ink TUI | **false / all** | the same two rows, no reasoning block |
| Ink TUI | true / off | no tool rows. `agent.log` shows both tools ran |
| Ink TUI | false / off | no tool rows |
| Desktop (dev build, CDP DOM counts) | **false / all** | run summary "Explored hostname, ran 1 command"; expanded, 2 rows ("Ran PROBE_OK", "Read hostname"); 0 thinking disclosures |

The model gave no visible reasoning on this short prompt, so the UI runs do not show the reasoning half. The gateway probe above covers it (`reasoning.available`). Desktop `false / off` and `true / all` are covered by `tool-feed-chrome.test.tsx`, not by a live run.

The Ink TUI with reasoning hidden (`false / all`), after this PR:

![ink false/all](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5686a274-7e99-4b59-a0b7-880583ce4b2c)

Desktop with reasoning hidden (`false / all`), after this PR:

![desktop false/all](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1c84eb65-de09-4219-9198-5889ee191a95)

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

- `tests/tui_gateway/test_show_reasoning_display_gate.py`: 19 pass. `test_hidden_reasoning_keeps_tool_rows_when_tool_progress_is_on` and `test_subagent_tool_mirror_follows_tool_progress_not_reasoning` fail on `main`. `test_tool_progress_off_keeps_reasoning_blocks` fails on `11fc8f1692`, the commit before its fix. The test that encoded the regression (`test_hidden_reasoning_suppresses_nonessential_tool_chrome_without_effort_none`) is replaced. The card-tool, file-edit and failed-exit tests now run under `tool_progress: off`, which is where answer-only lives now.
- Desktop: `tool-activity.test.ts`, `use-hermes-config.test.ts` and `tool-feed-chrome.test.tsx` pass (19 tests). The case "keeps the execution flow while reasoning stays hidden" fails against #125948's store. `typecheck`, `eslint` and `prettier` are clean.
- `tests/tui_gateway/`: 653 pass. Two tests in `test_tui_gateway_server.py` (`test_model_options_preserves_canonical_custom_row_after_agent_init`, and the flaky `test_load_cfg_raw_sees_replacement_with_pinned_mtime_and_size`) fail the same way on `main` and are fixed separately. `test_subagent_lifecycle_bypasses_tool_progress_off` used `reasoning.available` as its example of an event that `tool_progress: off` drops. Since reasoning no longer follows `tool_progress`, it now uses `tool.output_risk`.

</details>

Refs #121524, #85110. Closes #125948 (salvaged here).

Two tests in tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py are red or flaky on `main` for reasons in the tests, not the code. Both now pass: the file goes from 653 passed / 2 failed to 655 passed.

| Test | What went wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `test_model_options_preserves_canonical_custom_row_after_agent_init` | It fails on any machine signed in to Claude Code or Anthropic OAuth. Since `4ec57d56a9`, `hermes_cli/inventory.py::_is_explicit` keeps the Anthropic row when `_anthropic_oauth_credentials_present()` is true. That helper reads the real `~/.claude/.credentials.json`, which the test does not isolate. CI has no such file, so CI passes. | Stub `_anthropic_oauth_credentials_present` to False, as `tests/hermes_cli/test_inventory.py` already does. Salvages #93665 by @EvenXieWF (authorship kept; their diff targeted the pre-move path). |
| `test_load_cfg_raw_sees_replacement_with_pinned_mtime_and_size` (flaky, about 1 run in 10) | The test rewrites the config in place with the same size and a pinned mtime. The only field of `utils.py::file_signature` left to differ is ctime. The kernel stamps ctime on a coarse clock of about 4 ms, so a rewrite in the same tick as the cached read looks unchanged, and the cache returns stale data. A probe of that sequence gave identical signatures in 1900 of 2000 runs. | Before the rewrite, wait on a condition (no sleep) until the file's ctime has moved past the cached one. The test still covers ctime: with ctime removed from `file_signature` it fails 3 of 3 runs. The same race in `tests/hermes_cli/test_config_cache_signature.py::_replace_pinning_mtime` gets the same fix. |

**Evidence:** the flaky test passed 18 of 20 runs before and 60 of 60 after. With the wait, the probe gave identical signatures in 0 of 2000 runs. `ruff` is clean.

Closes #93665 (salvaged here).

MoA surfaces in model pickers as a normal provider with a synthesized `default` preset even when the user never wrote a `moa:` block: `_moa_provider_row()` builds the row from `load_config()`, which merges `DEFAULT_CONFIG` presets for everyone. The shared row builder feeds both the CLI inventory (`build_models_payload()`) and the gateway interactive picker (`list_picker_providers()`), so the fix lands in the one place both consume.

```python
def _moa_provider_row(current_provider: str = "") -> dict | None:
    ...
    if not _raw_config_has_enabled_moa_preset():
        return None
```

The gate reuses the existing `_raw_config_has_enabled_moa_preset()` helper (raw `config.yaml` read, no `load_config()` merging), so the row now appears only when the user explicitly enabled a preset — or a legacy flat MoA config — in their own config.yaml. The explicit-only filter, unconfigured skeletons, and aux pickers already excluded MoA where they should; this closes the last default-on path.

Tests (proven red on main without the guard):
- `test_build_models_payload_hides_moa_without_raw_preset` — with `load_config()` returning the synthesized DEFAULT_CONFIG preset but a raw config of `{}`, the payload contains no `moa` row.
- Updated `test_build_models_payload_returns_expected_shape` and the unconfigured-skeleton/canonical-order tests to pin the opt-in contract (MoA excluded from canonical skeletons, kept when a raw preset exists).

## Summary

The stale-auxiliary-model warning banner (Model settings → Auxiliary models) had two problems reported in #66740:

1. **Too easy to miss.** `text-xs` amber-200 on a faint amber background — easy to overlook in dark mode and low-contrast in light mode.
2. **No way to acknowledge it.** A deliberate cross-provider pin (e.g. vision on the only provider that offers it) showed the warning on every settings visit.

Both fixes, in the shared `StaleAuxWarning` component:

- **Prominence with theme-aware contrast**: `text-sm` medium weight, `size-4` icon, stronger border (`amber-400/60`) and background (`amber-500/15`), and the app's warn-badge text pair `text-amber-600 dark:text-amber-300` (per the review feedback on #66771 and #40718) so light mode keeps its contrast.
- **"Don't show again"** on the persistent variant, backed by a per-profile fingerprint of the acknowledged configuration — main provider plus every slot's task/provider/model/base_url. Any slot edit, main switch, or endpoint repoint changes the fingerprint and re-arms the banner, so the silent-credit-burn protection is never lost. The post-switch notice stays undismissable: it announces a change that just happened.

Supersedes #66771 (kept its prominence improvements, swapped the unconditional `text-amber-50` for the theme-aware pair) and #117256 (kept its fingerprint dismissal design, rebased onto the current render, added the `base_url` dimension the review flagged). Thanks @kyssta-exe and @kokhlo!

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/66740

- `npx vitest run src/app/settings/model-settings.test.tsx src/app/settings/stale-aux-dismissal.test.ts` — 39 passed (dismiss/re-arm behaviour test proven red on main: no dismiss button exists there)
- `npx vitest run src/i18n/catalog-completeness.test.ts` — 20 passed
- `npm run typecheck` in apps/desktop — clean
