items.body:
Restores the #107692 fix: a secondary profile's routed cron fire no longer writes that profile's `.env` into the shared `os.environ`. The removed series goes back onto current `main` with its original authors kept, and the administrator-managed `.env` goes back into every profile secret scope.

This is the maintainer replacement for #126496. It carries @jonpol01's cherry-picks with authorship preserved, rebased onto current `main`.

## Root cause

#111187 landed the fix on 2026-09-15 (`cedf4a3d78`). A few hours later `23036e20a6` ("fix(ux): plain-language, actionable user-facing messages (core)", 234 files) deleted every piece of it along with its tests. The commit message doesn't mention the removal. `git show 23036e20a6` shows these definitions deleted: `set_multiplex_context`, `reset_multiplex_context`, `refresh_installed_secret_scope`, `_install_fire_secret_scope`, `_reset_fire_secret_scope`, `routed_profile_fire`, `source_supplied_names`, `launch_dotenv_keys` and `managed_dotenv_keys`. None of these names exist on `main` at `b9df1cccae`.

The desktop/dashboard backend and a standalone gateway (one that came up after the multiplex preflight refused) both tick every profile's cron in-process while the process-wide multiplex flag is off. Every isolation that keys on `is_multiplex_active()` therefore does nothing for a sibling profile's fire:

- the routed-dotenv guard
- `get_secret`'s fail-closed miss
- the subprocess scrub
- the launch-residue strip

So that profile's `.env` stays in `os.environ`, and the launch profile's later turns and child processes read it. Separately, `build_profile_secret_scope` lost the managed `.env` layer. Under multiplex semantics that means a managed-only credential is missing and a user's own value beats the managed one.

## What changes

- `agent/secret_scope.py`: adds `set_multiplex_context`, a context-local flag OR'd into `is_multiplex_active()`. Adds `refresh_installed_secret_scope`, and puts the managed `.env` back as the last layer in `build_profile_secret_scope`.
- `cron/scheduler_provider.py`: `_profile_cron_scope` marks a fire whose home is not the pinned launch home (`routed_profile_fire`).
- `cron/scheduler.py`: `_install_fire_secret_scope` / `_reset_fire_secret_scope` hydrate the profile's secret sources, then install the scope. For a routed fire they also install the multiplex context, for exactly that span. The external-worker handoff treats a routed fire as multiplexed.
- `hermes_cli/env_loader.py`: bookkeeping for loaded, managed and source-supplied key names.
- `hermes_cli/plugins.py`: after plugin discovery, secret sources are folded into the installed scope, and a removed plugin source is reconciled.
- `tools/environments/local.py`:
  - `strip_launch_profile_env` strips a wider set of launch residue and leaves managed keys alone;
  - adds `restore_managed_env`;
  - `build_subprocess_env(strip_launch_profile=True)` overlays the routed scope and then the managed keys before the scrub, only under multiplex semantics.
- Tests: the invariant set that `23036e20a6` deleted is back in `tests/cron/test_cron_multiplex_desktop_ticker_scope.py`, `tests/cron/test_cron_no_agent.py` and `tests/cron/test_restart_safe_worker.py`.

Rebase delta vs #126496: `main` changed `load_hermes_dotenv` for #125530 (launch-home loads still apply under multiplex). The conflict was comment-only and resolved by keeping `main`'s comment and guard and appending the restored note about the routed-fire context. The guard behaves as intended: inside a routed fire, both the target and the override resolve to the routed home, which is not the launch home, so the load is still skipped.

## Verification (cwd = worktree at the stated SHA, `scripts/run_tests.sh`)

- **Base `b9df1cccae` + restored tests only:** the 6 restored cases fail. These are `test_a_routed_profile_fire_runs_under_multiplex_semantics_for_exactly_its_scope`, `test_routed_fire_scope_carries_managed_env_authority[managed-only|managed-beats-user]`, `test_a_routed_profile_script_never_receives_a_launch_only_name`, `test_a_routed_profile_script_keeps_administrator_managed_values_over_its_own` and `test_launch_external_worker_treats_a_routed_fire_as_multiplexed`.
- **This branch, 42 related files** (secret scope, env loader, secret sources, subprocess-env guard, cron multiplex, `test_scheduler.py`, subprocess env, passthrough, local env, spawn-site child env, terminal scope, managed scope, plugins): 572 passed, 0 failed, 30 skipped.
- **Broader run, 205 files** (all of `tests/cron`, gateway multiplex/secret, `hermes_cli` secret/served, tools passthrough/MCP scope): 1920 passed, 0 failed, 12 skipped.
- `ruff check` on the changed files is clean.
- One follow-up commit (mine) changes the two restored script tests' shebang from `#!/bin/bash` to `#!/usr/bin/env bash`, as the "Windows footguns" lint requires.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/126496: @jonpol01's fix-forward. All 16 commits are carried with authorship preserved, rebased onto current `main`, with the `env_loader.py` conflict resolved.
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/109703: @kansha5845121-afk's earlier fix for the same leak, which snapshots and restores `os.environ` around a foreign tick. It isn't taken because a process-global snapshot/restore races with concurrent turns and still exposes the values during the fire. The invariant it pins (the parent `os.environ` is unchanged after a foreign fire) is covered by `test_a_routed_profile_fire_runs_under_multiplex_semantics_for_exactly_its_scope`.

Credit: @jonpol01 (original #107692 fix, restore series), @kshitijk4poor (#111187 refinements and managed-scope fix).

Fixes #126492
Refs #107692

## Auto-merge

Not armed. This changes the per-profile secret boundary and the subprocess env builders `build_subprocess_env` and `tools/environments/local.py`, which falls under the HITL system-level / security-boundary rule. It needs a human review. Reviewed head: `5c493a96165c0c2b4cc68108cf05494b4cb2cc3b`.

items.body:
Stops a busy backend from looking dead to the desktop. `gateway.ping` now gets an answer even while an earlier RPC is stuck in `dispatch()`.

## Root cause

`tui_gateway/ws.py::handle_ws` read one frame, awaited `asyncio.to_thread(server.dispatch, …)` for it, and only then read the next frame. Every inline handler (anything not in `_LONG_HANDLERS`) therefore held up the socket reader until it returned. When a handler got stuck behind a long preflight compaction (lock wait, GIL pressure, slow state.db), the client's `gateway.ping` frames sat unread. The desktop's 45s "no inbound frame" deadline (`apps/shared` `JsonRpcRequestChannel`, `heartbeatLiveness: 'any-inbound'`) then fired. It dropped the socket and the desktop restarted the backend, which killed the in-flight turn.

Earlier fixes treated this class one handler at a time: #50005 moved polled RPCs into `_LONG_HANDLERS`, and `_compress_session_history` snapshots outside `history_lock` "otherwise prompt.submit etc. block on the dispatcher loop". This PR closes the class for the heartbeat itself.

## Fix

- Non-ping frames go onto a bounded per-connection queue (256). A dispatcher task drains it through the same `server.dispatch` path, **one at a time, in arrival order**, so RPC ordering does not change.
- The reader answers `gateway.ping` directly. Its reply no longer waits on handler latency.
- A reply the dispatcher cannot send still ends the connection. The reader watches the dispatcher task.
- Disconnect teardown works as before: the in-flight handler and any frames read before the disconnect finish before `_close_sessions_for_transport` parks the transport's sessions. A cancelled connection (server shutdown) cancels the dispatcher right away, as the old cancelled await did.
- If the queue fills, the reader waits, which is the old serial behaviour.

No client, contract or UI change.

## Verification (pinned base `b9df1cccae`)

- New regression test `test_ws_ping_is_answered_while_an_earlier_rpc_blocks_dispatch`: **fails on base** (`gateway.ping went unanswered while dispatch was busy; sent ids=[]`) and passes with the fix.
- Guards: `test_ws_disconnect_teardown_waits_for_in_flight_dispatch` and `test_ws_failed_reply_from_dispatcher_ends_the_connection`.
- Real Starlette WebSocket probe (TestClient; one RPC blocked in `dispatch()` for 3s, then a ping):
  - base: `first reply id=r1 after 3.01s`, ping answered only afterwards
  - fix: `first reply id=heartbeat-1 after 0.00s`, then `r1`
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/`: 2218 passed, 6 failed. The 6 (`test_profiles_list_{ui_meta_cache,session_field_cache,canonical_session}`) fail identically with base `ws.py`, so this diff does not cause them.
- `uvx ruff check` clean; `check-windows-footguns --diff origin/main` clean.

## Scope

Fixes every heartbeat drop caused by a busy backend: long compaction (this report), silent long turns (maholler1's comment), and Bot Chat registry checks timing out behind a stuck handler (Apfelkringel's comment). Not covered: a genuinely slow network link (Ajar9715, a client-side deadline knob) and renderer timer throttling while the window is hidden (#123125, a separate client-side cause).

Trade-off: if a handler deadlocks, the socket now stays connected and requests time out on their own 30–45s deadlines. Before, the heartbeat dropped the socket and the desktop restarted the backend. The turn-liveness watchdog still covers wedged turns.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/108427 by @Sahilvishnaliya. It lowered the compaction activity status interval from 60s to 15s so status frames would refresh the any-inbound deadline. That only helps when the compaction status emitter is the thing writing. It also shows the compaction status line 4× as often and leaves every other stuck handler exposed. Credit for pinpointing the 60s-vs-45s gap during compaction; its code is not incorporated because the ping path no longer depends on turn output.

Fixes #108325

Auto-merge: backend-only transport change in `tui_gateway/ws.py` plus tests, with no UI, install, or platform surface. Reviewed head `64bdacb680f0fe7480b3752a9dd95f926c492d61`.

## Root cause

`_handle_session_messages` (`GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages` on the gateway API server) parsed `limit`, `offset` and `order` but never read `include_compacted`. It called `SessionDB.get_messages` with the default `include_compacted=False`, so REST clients only ever got the live transcript left after compaction. The dashboard router already accepts the flag (`hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py`). This change gives the gateway endpoint the same parameter.

## Behavior

- `include_compacted=true|1|yes|on` returns the display history, which adds the rows a context compaction archived. Rewind and undo rows are still left out, matching `SessionDB`'s display semantics.
- If the parameter is missing, false-ish or unrecognised, the endpoint returns the live transcript as before. Parsing goes through the existing `_coerce_request_bool` helper.
- The endpoint row in the API server docs now lists the parameter.

The hunk is kept small on purpose. #59661 edits the same `get_messages` call to add `include_ancestors`, which is a different feature and is not included here.

## Acceptance coverage

`tests/gateway/test_api_server_compaction_projection.py::test_messages_endpoint_honours_include_compacted` uses a real `SessionDB` in a temp `HERMES_HOME`. It runs a real `archive_and_compact` and makes real aiohttp requests to check that:
- the default response, `include_compacted=false` and `include_compacted=0` all return the same live transcript, with no archived turns;
- `include_compacted=true` returns every archived and carried turn exactly once, in chronological order.

items.body:
## Root cause

Every Desktop `SshConnection` for one scope, host and identity hashes to the same `ControlPath` (`controlSocketPath`). With `ControlMaster=auto`, a new attempt attaches to whatever master is already listening on that socket. `SshConnection.close()` then ran `ssh -O exit` unconditionally, which shuts the master down for every attached connection. When a stale bootstrap attempt closed late (timed out, superseded, or rolled back through `bootstrapSshConnectionInner`'s failure path, `rollbackSshBootstrapResult`, force cleanup, or `teardownSshConnection`), it killed the master its successor was using. The live backend's forward went down after "Remote Hermes backend is ready", which is the post-success "control master closed" in #97264.

## Fix

The rule lives in `SshConnection`, so every caller that closes a shared master is covered, not just the one call site:

- New `ssh-control-master-holders.ts`: a small holder registry, one per process, keyed by `ControlPath`, plus a pure decision function `controlMasterCloseAction(otherHolders)`.
- `open()` (mux only) claims the socket **before** dialing. A stale close that lands while a successor is still attaching sees that claim. A failed `open()` releases its claim.
- `close()` releases its claim. It runs `-O exit` and the socket-unlink fallback only when no other connection still holds the socket. Otherwise it logs `control master left running: N other connection(s) still use it` and marks itself closed.
- The registry can be injected (`opts.controlMasterHolders`) so tests stay isolated.
- No-mux (Windows) is unchanged. `_evictStaleMaster` is unchanged: it only runs after the current opener has shown with a real exec that the master is wedged.

## Scope: half of #97264

This PR covers only the half where a failed or stale attempt's close tears down the shared master. It does **not** change the hardcoded 45s ready timeout (`remote-lifecycle.ts` `DEFAULT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS`). That half is tracked in #94642, and open PR #94665 covers it. That is why this PR says `Refs #97264` and not `Fixes`.

Related but not included, because the root cause differs:
- #126006: mid-session tunnel drop leaves `backend.lock.json` pointing at a dead serve. It was reported on a Windows client, which runs mux-less, so `-O exit` never happens there. The bug is in lock/orphan reconciliation.
- #126380: the update lock is held by a `serve` that has exited while its orphaned builds keep running. Update-lock ownership, not SSH transport.

The diagnosis that a superseded attempt kills its successor's master came from the closed #97392 by @ALDRIN121. That PR gated one call site on `lease.isCurrent()`. This PR moves the rule into the transport so every close path follows it.

The failure is `pidIsOurDashboard recognizes an installer wrapper…` in `remote-lifecycle.test.ts`, and it fails the same way with `ssh-connection.ts` at origin/main, so it predates this change.

Not reproduced against a real slow SSH host. The tests use a scripted `ssh` that models the shared master's state.

items.body:
## Root cause

Desktop's managed SSH update (`apps/desktop/electron/managed-ssh-update.ts`) runs `hermes update --yes` on the remote with `HERMES_UPDATE_CORRELATION_ID=<uuid>`, for both POSIX and Windows. Its coordinator's `receipt()` then scans `<HERMES_HOME>/logs/update_receipts/update_*.json` and skips any file whose `correlation_id` isn't that uuid. The backend never read the variable: `UpdateReceipt` wrote only its own `update_id` (`hermes_cli/update_receipt.py`). No receipt could ever match, so Desktop reported "Update failed" and restored every profile, even after a successful update.

## Change

- `UpdateReceipt.__init__` records `correlation_id` from `HERMES_UPDATE_CORRELATION_ID`, or `null` when the variable is unset.
- `update_id` still holds the CLI's own id. pm sync receipts and the handoff/finish paths key on it, and the receipt filename uses it, so none of those change.
- `begin_update_receipt(previous=...)` carries the field through the interpreter handoff. If the pre-swap receipt came from an older updater that doesn't write the field, the new process fills it from the env var.

Desktop reads only `correlation_id`, `outcome`, `finished_at`, `started_at`, `pre_update`/`post_update` `sha`/`version`, and `stop_reason`. The backend already writes everything on that list except `correlation_id`.

The second cause reported on the issue (the stale-module purge evicting the in-flight receipt, #101690) no longer applies on main. `_purge_stale_hermes_modules` now stops for relaunch and no longer touches `sys.modules`.

## Tests

`tests/hermes_cli/test_update_receipt.py::TestLauncherCorrelation` uses a temp `HERMES_HOME` and runs Desktop's `receipt()` predicate against the written files. It covers:

- a direct run
- the handoff, where the post-swap process doesn't inherit the env var
- a legacy pre-swap receipt
- an unset env var, which gives `null`

## Validation

- `unset PYTHONPATH; uvx ruff check hermes_cli/update_receipt.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_receipt.py`: All checks passed
- RED on `origin/main`'s `update_receipt.py`: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_update_receipt.py -k LauncherCorrelation` gives 4 failed. GREEN with the fix: 4 passed.
- `test_update_receipt.py` has 28 passed and 1 failed. The failure is `test_cmd_update_boundary_finalizes_on_early_exit`, a `home_io_guard` "REAL hermes home" error from the local test-environment path. It fails the same way on unmodified main.
- `test_update_receipt_{scope,truthfulness,pm_embed,endpoint}`, `test_update_finish`, `test_update_finish_stamp`, `test_update_completion_routing`: all pass.
- `test_update_completion_process`: 6 failures from the same `home_io_guard` error, the same 6 as on unmodified main.

Not exercised against a live SSH remote.

## Residual

The POSIX launch never writes `.update_coordinator_ready.<id>`, so Desktop's `ready()` is always null there. Desktop's success verdict needs only the receipt, so this PR doesn't touch it.

## Credit

The `os.environ.get("HERMES_UPDATE_CORRELATION_ID")` approach was suggested by @LordMelkor on the issue (the author of #101691).

Fixes #101516

items.body:
## Root cause
`hermes_cli/source_check._branch_tip` reads `git ls-remote --exit-code` exit 2 as "branch deleted". `_check_branch` then switches the target to `main`, and `_heal_deleted_branch` rewrites the Desktop branch config to `main`. Exit 2 only means the remote has no such ref, which is also true for a branch that was never pushed. So a local-only branch lost its pin, and the next update moved the checkout to `main`. The same thing happened to the checked-out branch when no Desktop pin was set.

## Behavior
When the remote does not advertise a non-main branch, the branch is re-pinned to `main` only if one of these holds:
- no local `refs/heads/<branch>` exists, so there is nothing to lose (this is the existing behavior for a stale config), or
- the branch was once published (`refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` or `branch.<b>.merge`, which survives `fetch --prune`) **and** `git cherry origin/main <branch>` (falling back to local `main`) shows no unmerged commits. Rebase-merged commits count as merged.

In every other case the pin stays. The status comes back as `error: "branch-local-only"` with `localOnly: true` and a message. Because it is an error, Desktop's apply path refuses instead of handing off `hermes update`. If the merge state can't be determined, the pin stays. Embedded (`HERMES_REVISION`) installs have no local refs and keep the old behavior.

## Tests (real temp git repos, bare remote, no mocks)
- `test_never_pushed_branch_keeps_its_pin[desktop|current]`: the pin and the Desktop config stay unchanged.
- `test_deleted_remote_branch_heals_only_when_its_commits_are_in_main[fast-forward|rebase|unmerged]`: the branch is pushed with `-u`, deleted upstream and pruned. Fast-forward and rebase merges heal to `main`; unmerged work keeps the pin.

## Validation
- `uvx ruff check hermes_cli/source_check.py tests/hermes_cli/test_source_check.py` → All checks passed
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_source_check.py` → 40 passed
- Before the fix (source reverted, new tests kept): 3 failed (`never_pushed[desktop]`, `never_pushed[current]`, `unmerged`), 2 passed (the heal cases)
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_parked_branch_guard.py`: 7 tests fail identically on clean `main` (home-io guard in this environment). This PR does not cause them.

## Residual
A branch that was squash-merged upstream has a different patch-id, so it keeps its pin and reports `branch-local-only` instead of healing. The user has to switch it by hand. That is the safe direction.

Based on the diagnosis in #105053 by @0xalydev and #105055 by @kokhlo. Both patched the Electron `resolveHealedBranch`, which has since moved into `hermes_cli/source_check.py`.

Fixes #105042

items.body:
## Root cause

On Windows the desktop hard-codes `%SystemRoot%\System32\OpenSSH\ssh.exe` in three places: `effectiveSshConfigFingerprint`, the `hermes:ssh-config:resolve` IPC handler and the SSH terminal spawn in `terminal-ipc.ts`. Meanwhile `SshConnection` spawns a bare `ssh` from PATH. If the in-box OpenSSH is missing or broken (#103288: after component-store corruption, every native `ssh.exe` exits 255), there was no way to point the app at a working client. On top of that, the failing boot-time `ssh -G` probe was classified as a transient remote failure, so the renderer retried it every ~2s and the user never got to the UI.

## Change

- **`electron/ssh-binary.ts`**: new pure `resolveSshBinary({ platform, override, env, fs })`, which is now the only place the ssh binary is chosen:
  - **Windows order:** `desktop.ssh_path` (used verbatim) → System32 OpenSSH → Git for Windows `usr\bin\ssh.exe` → bare `ssh`.
  - **Git candidates** come from the existing `windowsGitCandidates` list that `resolveGitBinary` uses (Hermes PortableGit, UGit, Program Files, per-user install).
  - **Every other platform** gets bare `ssh`, with no filesystem probes.
- **Where the override lives:** in `desktop.ssh_path` in `config.yaml`, not in a new `HERMES_*` env var (AGENTS.md rule). The app reads it with the same pre-window reader that handles `desktop.electron_flags` (`readDesktopLaunchConfig`). That reader accepts plain, single-quoted and YAML double-quoted Windows paths. The key is registered in `DEFAULT_CONFIG` and documented in `desktop.md`.
- **Call sites:** the resolver is wired into all ssh spawns: the `-G` probe, `ssh-config:resolve`, SSH terminals (injected as `sshBinary` into `registerTerminalIpc`) and `SshConnection`. `SshConnection` gets a new `sshBinary` option that `runSsh` and the no-mux tunnel child use; it defaults to `'ssh'`.
- **Boot loop:** a failed `ssh -G` now throws a tagged `ssh-client-failed` error that names the binary (plus a `desktop.ssh_path` hint on Windows). `runHermesStart` latches it the same way it latches SSH auth / host-key failures and marks it non-retryable, so boot stops on the failure overlay instead of looping.

## Acceptance coverage

- Override → System32 → Git → bare ordering; non-Windows returns `ssh` without touching fs; custom SystemRoot; PortableGit preferred over system Git; UGit/LOCALAPPDATA candidate mapping (`ssh-binary.test.ts`, platform passed as data, fs injected).
- `desktop.ssh_path` parsing, including the YAML double-quote escapes (`renderer-heap-flags.test.ts`).
- `ssh -G` failure is tagged, latched and not auto-retried; ordinary remote faults still retry; the hint is Windows-only (`backend-start-failure.test.ts`).
- `SshConnection` spawns the injected binary for open + exec and bare `ssh` by default (`ssh-connection.test.ts`).

## Validation

```
npm ci                                  # worktree root: ok
cd apps/desktop && npm run typecheck    # exit 0
npx vitest run electron/ssh-binary.test.ts electron/backend-start-failure.test.ts \
  electron/renderer-heap-flags.test.ts electron/ssh-connection.test.ts
# Test Files 4 passed (4) / Tests 117 passed (117)
npx eslint <changed electron files>     # clean
uvx ruff check hermes_cli/config_defaults.py   # All checks passed!
```

Not reproduced on a real Windows host with broken OpenSSH (no Windows hardware here). That path is covered only by the injected-fs unit tests and needs Windows review.

## Behaviour notes / residual

- On Windows, `SshConnection` now spawns the same resolved absolute path as the `-G` probe (usually System32 OpenSSH) instead of whatever `ssh` comes first on PATH. The probe and the connection now use the same client. A user who relied on a different `ssh` being first on PATH should set `desktop.ssh_path`.
- `desktop.ssh_path` is read at launch, so changing it needs an app restart.
- The `ssh -G` latch applies on all platforms (it only fires for a local-client failure). A `-G` timeout, e.g. the stdin hang in #118983, now latches too instead of looping. #118983's root cause is separate and not addressed here.
- There's no Settings UI field for `ssh_path` yet; it's set through `config.yaml`.

Fixes #103288

The diagnosis builds on #103289 by @SZWzz (closed unmerged). This PR takes a different approach: an existence-ordered resolver plus a config key, instead of `ssh -V` health probes and an env var.

## Root cause

The busy-queue is in-memory only, and the sole retire of the accept-time user row
(`_replace_queued_user_row_for_turn`'s `deactivate_message`) runs only in the drain path.
A backend restart discards the queue with nothing left to retire the accept-time row, so the
row stays active and the next cold resume's `repair_alternation` glues the never-run prompt
into the previous turn's user message.

## What changes

- `_write_submit_user_row` accepts `display_metadata`; the busy-queue accept stamps
  `display_metadata._queued_prompt` (`QUEUED_PROMPT_METADATA_KEY`) on the accept-time row.
- The drain's re-placement writes an unmarked replacement for the DISPATCHING envelope only;
  still-queued envelopes keep the marker, so still-marked after a restart == never drained.
- `reopen_session` deactivates still-marked rows on cold resume — the same retire the drain
  uses, deactivated never deleted, and `repair_alternation` is untouched (the projection
  cannot know whether a row ran; per the issue author's invariant comment).
- Rows that DID drain are unmarked and survive the reopen untouched.

## Sequencing with #123533

Both PRs retire via `deactivate_message` on different triggers (in-process discard vs cold
reopen). Verified combined: both branches merged together pass the full queued-prompt suite
(13 tests, no double-deactivate).

## Tests (all on `origin/main` vs with-fix)

- `test_restart_retires_the_never_drained_accept_row` — red on main, green with fix. Now
  also asserts the RAW row sequence — order/roles/active state — per the review thread, not
  just the count: `[user A active, user B inactive(marked), assistant A active]`.
- `test_resume_does_not_retire_drained_or_plain_rows` — green both (guard).
- `test_restart_between_drains_retires_only_the_later_prompt` — red on main, green with
  fix; two queued prompts, first drains, restart retires only the second.
- Sibling suites green: `test_queued_prompt_persistence.py` (7), reopen consumers
  `test_oneshot_resume.py` + `test_stranded_session_adoption.py` (31), combined with
  PR #123533's branch (13).

Fixes #125577

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/125595 (rebased onto current
main + the raw-sequence assertion from the review thread; authorship kept). Thanks @dskwe!

Co-authored-by: Yuan Li <dskwelmcy@163.com>

Based on #120778 by @kvnloo. This reuses its idea of building the `-ot` selector from the recurrent block indices, and also sizes the selector to the spill.

## Root cause
`spill_overrides()` (context_policy.py:251-252) sends any spilled hybrid `-ot blk\.\d+\.ffn_.*\.weight=CPU`. That pattern matches every block's FFN, including the full-attention blocks, so it is all-or-nothing. It ignores how many bytes the plan actually has to take off the GPU (`WindowDecision.spill_bytes`).

## Change
- `gguf.py`: while reading the tensor table, record FFN weight bytes per block (`ffn_block_bytes`). This uses the same `blk\.N\.ffn_.*\.weight` selection the override targets. `profile_from_gguf` copies it onto `ModelProfile`.
- `context_policy.recurrent_spill_blocks(profile, spill_bytes)`: a pure function that picks the fewest recurrent (`n_head_kv==0`) blocks, lowest index first, whose FFN bytes cover `spill_bytes`. It falls back to every recurrent block when sizes are unknown or `spill_bytes` is None. If all recurrent FFNs together still fall short, it lists all of them and fit spills the rest. It never selects a full-attention block.
- `spill_overrides(profile, spill_bytes=None)` emits `blk\.(i|j|…)\.ffn_.*\.weight=CPU`, and `launch_args` passes `decision.spill_bytes`. The MoE and dense paths are unchanged.

## Tests (synthetic metadata; deterministic)
- Interleaved qwen35-style layout (every 4th block full attention): 250 MiB of spill moves blocks 0,1,2. A 301 MiB spill adds block 4 and skips full-attention block 3. `blk.1` does not match `blk.10`–`15`. An oversized spill moves every recurrent block and no full-attention block.
- No FFN sizes, or one recurrent block missing a size: every recurrent block, nothing else.
- `launch_args` sizes the selector from the decision. UMA gets no `-ot`.
- End to end: a hand-written GGUF v3 (qwen35, 12 blocks, `full_attention_interval=4`) → `read_gguf_header` → `profile_from_gguf` → `spill_overrides` moves exactly [0,1,2,4,5]. `attn_norm` is not counted.

## Validation
- `uvx ruff check` on the 5 touched files: all checks passed.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_context_policy.py tests/hermes_cli/test_local_runtime_gguf.py`: 30 passed. With the source files reverted to main, the new tests fail (ImportError / FAILED).
- Every test file that references `local_runtime` (46 files): 695 passed, 51 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is `test_load_progress.py::test_loading_events_build_snapshot_and_terminal_clears`, which is flaky: it failed 1 of 3 isolated reruns on this branch and passed on main. That module doesn't touch spill placement.

## Not covered
No GPU was available here, so there is no tok/s or RSS measurement of the new placement. The overhead calibration part of #113329 is also untouched: `RUNTIME_OVERHEAD_BYTES` (:32) and the non-MTP `ub_logits_bytes` term (:277-286), reported as an overestimate for large-vocab models. Changing those constants needs a measured allocation receipt, especially since the non-MTP launch still passes `-b 2048 -ub 2048`.

Refs #113329

items.body:
## Root cause

`recoverManagedSshScopes` (`apps/desktop/electron/managed-ssh-update.ts`) called `completeRecovery()` only when **every** scope restored. `ManagedConnectionUpdateGate.assertCanDial` / `assertCanMutate` throw whenever a durable journal record exists for the connection. So one scope that never restores (for example, its restore target is gone) kept the record forever: every launch logged "left 1 scope(s) pending; will retry next launch", and the connection could not be dialed, edited, or removed. `runManagedSshUpdate` had the same all-or-nothing condition, so a restore failure right after a successful update fenced the connection until relaunch.

## Behavior

Recovery is now bounded once the remote install marker is positively clear, meaning the mutator is gone and the fence has nothing left to protect:

- New pure decision function `managedSshRecoveryDisposition` → `complete | retry | abandon`.
  - All scopes restored → `complete`, which works as before.
  - The correlated remote exit code is 0 → `abandon` right away. A receipt is not required, because some backends exit 0 without writing one (#101516). A receipt that reports a non-success outcome still blocks this. This is the reported case: `.update_exit_code.<correlation>` → 0.
  - Otherwise `retry`, until `MAX_MANAGED_SSH_RECOVERY_ATTEMPTS` (3) failed attempts, then `abandon`.
- `abandon` clears the journal record. The gate stops fencing and the connection can be dialed, edited, and removed again. The unrestored profiles are logged (`[ssh-update] durable recovery for X stopped after N attempt(s); connection released with M scope(s) not restored (...)`). A scope that is not restored is just a stopped service, and the next ordinary dial starts it again.
- The failed-attempt count is saved as an optional `attempts` field on the existing journal record. Older Desktop builds ignore unknown record fields, so downgrading does not turn the journal "malformed". No new phase value was added, for the same reason.
- `runManagedSshUpdate` uses the same decision: after a proven-successful update (exit 0 plus a success receipt), it clears the journal even if a scope fails to restore. The failure is still reported in `scopes`, with outcome `restore-failed`.
- `waitForManagedRemoteClearance` now returns the clearing observation, so recovery can read the exit code and receipt.
- Clearance that cannot be proven (marker live, malformed, or unreachable) stays fenced as before, because a mutator may still be running.

No user "abandon recovery" action was added. There is no existing UI surface for durable managed-SSH recovery state, and this PR does not create one.

## Acceptance coverage (vitest, `electron/managed-ssh-update.test.ts`)

- Disposition table: complete / retry / abandon-at-max / abandon-on-success / custom max.
- A scope that never restores: the first relaunch retries and records attempt 1, and the connection stays fenced. At the max attempt the connection is released for dial and mutate.
- A correlated exit 0 (with a success receipt, or with no receipt) ends recovery on the first failed restore. A failed receipt keeps it fenced.
- `runManagedSshUpdate`: a successful update with one stuck scope clears the journal. A failed update with one stuck scope keeps it.
- The existing test "inactive SSH crash recovery keeps ordinary dials fenced until positive clearance" is unchanged apart from the new return shape.

## Validation

- `npm ci` (worktree root) → exit 0
- `cd apps/desktop && npm run typecheck` → exit 0
- `npx vitest run --project electron electron/managed-ssh-update.test.ts` → 33 passed
- `npx eslint electron/managed-ssh-update.ts electron/managed-ssh-update.test.ts electron/main.ts` → clean. `prettier --check` → clean.
- Repro against `origin/main`'s `managed-ssh-update.ts` (temporary probe; 10 recovery runs with one stuck scope): `assertCanDial` still throws "SSH connection "homelab" is paused while its managed update is in progress." With this branch, the connection is released at attempt 3, or on the first attempt when the exit code is 0.
- Full `vitest run --project electron`: 309 files pass. 13 files fail (signing, native deps, uninstall sandbox, i18n keys, updater preflight). None of them import `managed-ssh-update` or `main`, and this PR does not touch them.

## Residual

- While a non-success update is still under the attempt bound, the connection stays fenced until the next launch, so the 30 s refresh errors continue until the bound is reached. Users now have to wait out at most 3 launches, not forever.
- A clearance that can never be proven (for example, the host is gone permanently) still fences dial, edit, and removal. That is deliberate for safety and needs a separate user-facing recovery affordance.

Fixes #107827


## macOS remotes in "Update all instances" (#124617)

The POSIX drain stops the Desktop-owned serve only through a pidfd, so the signal is bound to the verified process. Darwin has no equivalent, so `terminateOwnedDashboardForUpdate` deliberately refuses there (`DARWIN_UNAVAILABLE`) instead of accepting a PID-reuse window. The update lifecycle still cancelled every forward, hit the refusal, and reported the row as a failed update on every attempt ("Update fan-out failed: Could not safely drain every managed SSH scope ..."), so a macOS remote with a live serve never updated.

This PR keeps that safety limit. Right after scope capture, and before any forward or serve is touched, the new `managedSshDrainBlocker` detects a live Desktop-owned Darwin serve. The update then returns a structured refusal with `skipReason: 'darwin-drain-unsupported'`. `managedSshUpdateAllRow` reports that connection as a **skipped** row with a clear per-remote message, and Settings shows it as an informational toast instead of an error. A macOS remote with no live Desktop serve needs no drain, so it still updates. Other rows are unaffected, because each row was already independent. No Darwin self-shutdown path was added: there is no authenticated one to reuse.

Related: #124839 fixes the separate problem that the probe's non-zero exit hides the specific refusal message. This PR does not reuse its code and does not depend on it.

- Regression tests: `a live Desktop-owned serve on a macOS remote is a per-row skip, not a batch failure (#124617)` and `macOS remotes with no live serve and Linux remotes still update`. Both fail when the source change is reverted (2 failed / 33 passed) and pass with it.
- `npm run typecheck` → exit 0. `npx vitest run electron/managed-ssh-update.test.ts src/app/settings` → 54 files, 454 tests passed. eslint and prettier → clean.

Fixes #124617

## What does this PR do?

The N1X performance reference currently depends on the exact driver-reported GPU name. A renamed N1X falls back to the generic estimate, while a different device with the matching name can receive the N1X reference. Use PCI vendor/device identity as the primary key, retaining the current name fallback only when a usable PCI ID is unavailable.

Recognize N1X with vendor `0x10DE` and device range `0x2E00–0x2E3F`. A valid conflicting ID takes precedence over the name. This uses the full N1X family range; it does not add benchmark evidence for every SKU. The existing 21.9 tok/s reference, Windows/CUDA/model/quant/MTP eligibility and memory-fit rules are unchanged.

## Related Issue

Follow-up to #112107.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hardware.py`: add `pci.device_id` to the existing memory/name query, parse it with `int(value, 16)`, and retain the packed integer from the same adapter row. Keep the original single-query failure behavior; nonnumeric PCI values such as `N/A` leave identity unavailable without discarding memory data.
- `estimator.py`: carry one optional PCI integer in `HardwareBudget`.
- `hermes_platform/host/products.py` and `catalog.py`: match the vendor/device range and resolve it to the existing calibration key. Keep the calibration table and recommendation flow intact. No regex or separate 32-bit validation is needed.
- Add two parameterized regression tests (19 cases); update existing memory-probe fixtures for the additional identity field.

## How to Test

Run the canonical isolated runner on Windows:

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_local_n1x_pci_identity.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_unified_pool_quirk.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_local_launch_budget.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_local_recommendation.py -j 4 --tb=short
```

Validated on native Windows / Python 3.14.7: **101 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped** (19 new cases and 82 existing cases; the skip is an existing Linux-only WSL test). Ruff 0.15.10 and `git diff --check` passed.

The new cases cover renamed/empty names, range endpoints, the supplied N1X allowlist IDs, N1 exclusion, wrong vendors, unavailable/malformed IDs, negative/oversized integers, preserving memory data when PCI identity is `N/A`, quoted CSV names and keeping identity tied to the same adapter as the memory reading. They run the production parsing, budget and recommendation code with simulated driver responses at the subprocess boundary.

These are functional regressions, not performance measurements. Physical N1X validation and a full-project test run have not been performed.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contributing guide and applicable development instructions.
- [x] Conventional commit; only changes related to this fix.
- [x] Searched existing PRs for N1X/PCI detection fixes.
- [x] Added regression coverage and ran focused tests on Windows.
- [ ] Full test suite run.
- [ ] Physical N1X validation.
- [x] Updated relevant docstrings; no configuration, tool-schema or workflow changes.
- [x] Considered cross-platform behavior; the existing Windows-only calibration gate remains in place.

items.body:
## Root cause

Under a container terminal backend (`docker`, `modal`, ...), `terminal.cwd` is a path inside the sandbox, e.g. `/workspace`. Two readers handle it differently:

- `_terminal_task_cwd` uses it as-is, so the terminal tool gets `/workspace`.
- `_completion_cwd`, which sets the session workspace, runs `os.path.isdir` on it. The host has no `/workspace`, so it fell back to the gateway's own cwd. For the desktop that is `$HOME`.

`_stage_session_file_attachment` then treated every file under `$HOME` as "inside the workspace" and returned it without copying it into the bind-mounted `attachments/` dir. The agent got a relative host ref that does not exist in the container. The issue's corrected diagnosis (comment 2) is right. The desktop `setTerminalBackend` theory from the original report is not.

## Changes

- `tui_gateway/session_workdir.py`
  - `_completion_cwd` keeps an absolute container cwd without host validation when the bound backend is non-local, as `_terminal_task_cwd` already does.
  - New `_sandbox_workspace_cwd` covers two sources the `isdir` check used to drop: a config-only backend (in-process desktop gateway with no `TERMINAL_ENV` bridge) and a named profile's own container `terminal.cwd`.
  - A `terminal.cwd` that exists on the host is still validated and kept (the `docker_mount_cwd_to_workspace` source). Local backends behave as before.
  - `_session_is_local_backend` now reads the effective backend (env or config). Without this, a config-only docker session's `/workspace` would be "healed" up to `/` and saved.
- `tools/credential_files.py`: `map_cache_path_to_container` also matches through a symlinked `HERMES_HOME`. `@file:` expansion passes resolved paths, but the mount roots keep the configured spelling. A symlinked `~/.hermes` (dotfiles setups, or macOS `/var` → `/private/var`) therefore sent an already-staged attachment's host path to the agent. I reproduced this on main. It is one plausible cause of the 2026-09-22 comment (staged paste, host path in the prompt). I could not confirm that commenter's setup.

Once the workspace is the container path, host files fall outside it. `file.attach` stages them into `attachments/`, and the `📎` block shows `/root/.hermes/attachments/<name>`.

## Acceptance / tests

`tests/tui_gateway/test_container_backend_workdir.py` calls the real functions with a temp `HERMES_HOME` and a docker backend config:
- container cwd from config only or from the env bridge → the session workspace, the same value as `_terminal_task_cwd`, and not healed
- local backend with a missing cwd → still falls back; docker with a host-dir cwd → still the host dir
- named docker profile → its own container cwd, even when the client sends an inherited workspace
- end to end: a file under the launch dir → staged into `<HERMES_HOME>/attachments`, absolute ref, and `preprocess_context_references` shows `/root/.hermes/attachments/report.pdf`

`tests/tools/test_credential_files.py::test_symlinked_home_maps_resolved_path`: a resolved staged path under a symlinked home maps to the container path.

## Validation

- `uvx ruff check` (touched files): All checks passed
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_container_backend_workdir.py tests/tools/test_credential_files.py`: 51 passed. With the two source files reverted to `origin/main`: 5 failed (4 new gateway tests, plus the symlink test)
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` on all 13 test files that exercise the touched helpers (includes `test_tui_gateway_server.py`, `test_context_references.py`, `test_complete_path_at_filter.py`, ...): 795 passed, 0 failed, 4 skipped

## Not covered

A binary `@file:` ref typed by hand to a host file outside the mounted dirs still shows its host path in the `📎` stub. One example: a workspace file under `docker_mount_cwd_to_workspace`, which is visible as `/workspace/...` but rendered with its host path. Fixing that needs the workspace-mount mapping in `_agent_visible_path`, so this PR does not close the issue.

#119363 (@MuhammadUsamaMX) takes a different approach: it copies into `attachments/` by basename inside `_agent_visible_path`. It does not touch the `_completion_cwd` root cause, it overwrites same-named files, and it treats ssh as a mount. Nothing from it is reused here.

Refs #103147

items.body:
## Root cause

Covers holes 1 and 3 of #103738. Hole 2 (matching bare or unprefixed provider names) is #124290 by @jonpol01, and this PR doesn't touch that code.

- **Hole 1:** `tui_gateway/server.py::_make_agent` builds `AIAgent` from `resolve_runtime_provider` but drops `runtime["request_overrides"]`, which is where the resolver puts a custom entry's `extra_body`. The CLI, cron and the messaging gateway all pass it. Without it, the body only arrives through `agent_init._merge_custom_provider_extra_body`, which matches `custom`/`custom:*` alone. `hermes -z` (`hermes_cli/oneshot.py`) and ACP (`acp_adapter/session.py`) drop it the same way.
- **Hole 3:** aux requests only read `auxiliary.<task>.extra_body` (default `{}`). They never read the destination entry's `extra_body`, even though the main agent sends it on every request to that endpoint. Aux calls already inherit the entry's `extra_headers` (#109595), and the docs say the entry's `extra_body` "follows the provider everywhere", so this is a gap, not an intentional design choice.

With a proxy that needs a body field (`user`), `hermes chat` works, but Desktop/TUI and smart-approval get a 400.

## Behavior

- `_make_agent`, oneshot and ACP now pass `request_overrides=runtime.get("request_overrides")`. ACP skips it when an explicit `base_url` points at a different endpoint.
- `_build_call_kwargs`, which primary, same-provider-retry and fallback requests all go through, now puts the destination entry's `extra_body` underneath the task/caller body. It uses the agent's own matcher (`_custom_provider_extra_body_for_agent`). Each destination gets only its own entry's body. A fallback to OpenRouter or to another entry never inherits the primary's. Keys from `auxiliary.<task>.extra_body` and from the caller win.
- Invariants: the agent receives the body once, at construction, so the prompt cache isn't touched mid-conversation. The runtime and config are resolved inside the build's existing profile scope, so profile scope is unchanged.

## Acceptance coverage (behavioral)

- `tests/tui_gateway/test_custom_provider_session_persistence.py::TestMakeAgentForwardsProviderRequestBody`: runs the real resolver against a patched config, and `_make_agent` hands `{"extra_body": {"user": ...}}` to AIAgent.
- `tests/agent/test_auxiliary_named_custom_providers.py::TestAuxInheritsCustomProviderExtraBody`: `call_llm(task="approval")` with an empty task `extra_body` sends the inherited `user`. This holds with and without a live `main_runtime`, and the check reads kwargs from the real OpenAI SDK `create`. Task/caller keys win. OpenRouter, a different entry and a stray custom URL don't inherit.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_oneshot_fallback.py::test_run_agent_forwards_resolved_request_overrides` and `tests/acp_adapter/test_session_reasoning_config.py::test_acp_agent_receives_custom_provider_request_body`: covers the sibling build sites, plus ACP's base_url guard.

## Validation

- `uvx ruff check <8 changed files>`: all checks passed.
- Red on `origin/main` b9df1ccc (source reverted, new tests kept): 7 failed (`KeyError: 'request_overrides'` / `'user'` / `'extra_body'`).
- Green: `scripts/run_tests.sh` on the 4 touched test files, 71 passed.
- Wider run: `scripts/run_tests.sh` on 62 files (`tests/agent/test_auxiliary*.py`, fast compression lane, switch-model request overrides, provider fallback, `tests/tools/test_approval_smart*`, tui_gateway server/make_agent/custom-provider files, `tests/acp_adapter/test_session*`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_oneshot*`): 1277 passed, 0 failed. Python 3.14, macOS.

## Residual / notes

- If an aux task pins a different model on the same endpoint, and the entry has `model:` without that model in its catalog, it doesn't inherit. That matches the main agent's per-model rule.
- Aux labels that use a bare entry name (`provider: my-proxy`) start inheriting once #124290 widens the shared matcher. This PR calls that matcher and doesn't fork it.
- #83398 (@justinh20, service tier) also adds a `request_overrides=` kwarg to `_make_agent`. Whichever lands second needs to merge the two dicts.

Refs #103738

items.body:
## Root cause

`sessions.auto_archive` archives a whole compression lineage through `set_session_archived`. When that chat later resumed and compressed, `_publish_child_session_row` inserted the new tip with the default `archived=0` under a root that was still `archived=1`. `list_sessions_rich` admits a lineage by its root's flag (`s.archived = 0` on admitted roots), so the live chat stayed hidden from the sidebar. `unarchive_recoverable_session` only handles `ws_orphan_reap`/`agent_close` tips, so nothing cleared it.

The store could not tell a sweep archive from a deliberate one, and a deliberate archive has to survive re-activation (#89325 / #89341 cover that as a separate feature). So the fix records where the archive came from.

## Change

- New column `sessions.auto_archived INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`. `_reconcile_columns` adds it, and the schema-history event is recorded as seq 30.
- `archive_stale_sessions` archives through `_auto_archive_lineage`, which sets `auto_archived=1` only on rows it hides. Rows that were already archived keep their provenance, so a manually archived ancestor is never relabelled.
- `set_session_archived` (sidebar, API, TUI, `hermes sessions archive`, transfer donor) always clears `auto_archived`, so it counts as a deliberate archive.
- `_unarchive_auto_archived_lineage(conn, sid)` un-hides the lineage only if every archived row came from the sweep. It runs:
  - in `publish_compression_child`'s transaction, after the parent is closed with `compression`, and only when the parent was archived;
  - in `reopen_session` (CLI/TUI `/resume`, oneshot resume, gateway stale-route recovery).
- Compression children inherit the parent's `archived`/`auto_archived`, so a manually archived lineage stays uniformly archived. Before, a lineage with mixed flags gave the sweep an `archived=0` tip that it could relabel.
- Docs: `developer-guide/session-storage.md` and `user-guide/sessions.md`.

## Validation

- `uvx ruff check hermes_state_sessions.py hermes_state_compression.py hermes_state_maintenance.py hermes_state_common.py hermes_cli/session_schema_history.py tests/hermes_state/test_auto_archived_lineage_reactivation.py`: All checks passed.
- Behavioural probe using a real `SessionDB` in tmp_path. Steps: root→tip lineage, run the sweep, compress tip→tip2, then run the sidebar query.
  - Clean `origin/main`: `AssertionError: []` (chat hidden).
  - With the fix: passes, and the sidebar shows `tip2`.
- New `tests/hermes_state/test_auto_archived_lineage_reactivation.py` (6 tests):
  - sweep then compression un-hides the chat;
  - a manual archive stays hidden through compression and a later sweep;
  - a manual archive after the sweep overrides it;
  - the sweep does not relabel a manually archived ancestor (legacy mixed lineage);
  - `reopen_session` un-hides an auto archive but not a manual one;
  - unarchiving clears the provenance.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh <new test> tests/hermes_cli/test_session_schema_history.py tests/hermes_state/test_pinned_archived_sidebar.py tests/hermes_state/test_canonical_title_guard.py`: 23 passed.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_state tests/hermes_cli/test_session_schema_history.py tests/hermes_cli/test_session_recovery_lost_and_found.py tests/hermes_cli/test_session_system_prompt_dedup.py tests/agent/test_compression_rotation_state.py tests/agent/test_compression_concurrent_fork.py`: 1477 passed, 64 failed. Re-running the 19 failing files on clean main gives the same 64 failures. They are environment-dependent tests (auto-vacuum holder gates, cross-VM FS, sqlite3 CLI salvage, repair loops) and none are caused by this change.

## Not covered

- Lineages the sweep archived **before** this change have `auto_archived=0`. They are treated as deliberate and stay hidden until you unarchive them once. There is no way to recover their provenance.
- If an auto-archived tip that never ended gets more messages but never compresses or resumes, it stays hidden until one of those happens. Un-hiding on every inbound message is the broader #89325 / #89341 feature.
- `export`/`import` round-trips carry `archived` but not `auto_archived`, so an imported sweep archive is treated as deliberate.

Fixes #117713

items.body:
## Root cause

`apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/inline-preview-directive.tsx`:

- `intentScript` sliced every prompt to `MAX_INTENT_LENGTH` (500) inside the frame, and `intentFromMessage` sliced it again in the parent. A JSON payload over 500 chars reached the agent as invalid JSON.
- `InlineHtmlFrame` dropped any intent that arrived within `INTENT_THROTTLE_MS` (1s) of the previous one, without queuing it or telling anyone.
- `send()` returned `true` once `postMessage` ran. The frame had no way to know whether an intent was delivered, dropped, or turned away because no visible composer surface existed (`requestComposerSubmit` returning `false`).

## Behavior after this change

- The parent is the only authority. The frame posts the full prompt with a per-call `id`. The pure gate `evaluateIntent()` either accepts it (trimmed, never truncated) or rejects it with a reason: `too_long` (+`maxLength`), `throttled` (+`retryAfterMs`), or `invalid`.
- Accepted intents go through `requestComposerSubmit` exactly as before. A `false` return becomes `undelivered`.
- The parent posts `{ type: 'hermes-inline-preview-intent-ack', token, id, ack }` back to `event.source`. `window.hermes.send()` now returns a `Promise<IntentAck>` and resolves `undelivered` if no ack arrives within 5s. `window.hermes.maxLength` exposes the cap.
- The 500-char cap and the 1 msg/s throttle are unchanged. The code documents the cap as "a sentence, not a payload dump", so I didn't raise it. Over-cap input is now rejected visibly instead of corrupted.
- Security posture is unchanged. Messages without this mount's token are still ignored with no reply. The ack goes only to the source that proved it holds the token. It carries status and nothing from the app. `'*'` is required because the sandboxed frame's origin is opaque. The frame only accepts acks where `e.source === parent` and the token matches. There is no new UI and no sandbox change.
- `data-hermes-send` keeps working. The declarative path ignores the ack.
- Docs: the talk-back paragraph in `website/docs/developer-guide/desktop-plugin-sdk.md` now documents the ack.

## Scope

This covers findings 2 and 3 of #118973: truncation, silent throttle drops, and the missing delivery ack. **Finding 1 is not addressed**: the side preview pane (`persist:hermes-preview` webview) still has no bridge, because adding one is a feature decision. For that reason the commit uses a neutral reference and does not say `Fixes`.

Related: #126638 (@MrB0req) routes intents to the owning session's composer instead of `'active'`. It's a different fix in the same handler, so expect a small textual conflict around the `requestComposerSubmit` call. The two changes are compatible.

## Validation (worktree, after `npm ci` at the root)

- `cd apps/desktop && npm run typecheck` → exit 0
- `npx vitest run src/components/assistant-ui/inline-preview-directive.test.ts` → 26/26 passed
- `npx vitest run src/components/assistant-ui/ src/app/chat/composer/` → 164 files, 1234 tests passed
- `npx eslint` + `npx prettier --check` on both changed files → clean
- Before/after probe: the new test file run against the `origin/main` source → 11 failures. These include the frame-script test showing a 3200-char prompt posted truncated, plus the missing gate and ack. All pass with the fix.

New tests execute the injected frame script against a fake parent. They check that the full prompt is posted, that `send()` resolves with the matching ack, that acks with a wrong token or a non-parent source are ignored (timeout → `undelivered`), and that an empty prompt resolves `invalid`. They also cover the pure gate: accept, at-cap, over-length reject, throttle with retry hint, invalid, hostile id, and foreign messages ignored.

Covers the truncation, throttle, and delivery-ack findings of #118973.

items.body:
A multiplexed gateway or Desktop `serve` backend no longer lets launch-profile state bleed into the profiles it serves: each served profile's agent logs into its own `agent.log`, a root gateway's log rollover hands the file back to the worker uid that owned it, slash gating (`allow_admin_from`) is read from the profile whose bot received the command, a command TTS/STT provider gets the served profile's own `env_passthrough` credential, and the launch home's `.env` still loads under multiplex so `fallback_providers` keys are visible.

## Per issue

- Fixes #125974 — `agent/agent_init.py::_setup_logging` passed `run_agent._hermes_home` (frozen at first import) so `setup_logging` never adopted a routed home and every profile's records landed in the launch profile's `agent.log`. Now `setup_logging(hermes_home=get_hermes_home())` honours the active override. Salvages #126005 by @Tranquil-Flow (trimmed: the `FileNotFoundError` fallback chain and 3 of 5 tests dropped — a served home exists by construction). L1/L2 · T7.
- Fixes #120151 — `hermes_logging.py::_ManagedRotatingFileHandler.doRollover` let the stdlib rollover create the new `agent.log` as the rotating process's uid (root gateway) and a worker on another uid could never reopen it. Now stats before, chowns back as root and restores the mode after, best-effort. Salvages #124764 by @WYSTAF (only its logging commit; the two helpers are inlined into `doRollover`, 4 tests → 2). L3 · T5.
- Fixes #121705 — every `policy_for_source(self.config, source)` caller (`run_busy::_check_slash_access`, `/whoami`, catalog, `/approvals`, `/login`, `_resume_caller_is_admin`) read the launch profile's `GatewayConfig`, so a platform configured only in a secondary profile had no `PlatformConfig` and came back unrestricted. New `gateway/slash_access.py::policy_for_runner_source(runner, source)` resolves the **bot-owning (transport) profile's** cached config — the owner `RoutingIdentity.authorization_home` already names — and fails closed (floor only) when a served profile's config is not cached. Salvages #121722 by @MohamadKanso (the 50-line mixin helper became a 14-line function in the topical module; the "gated launch + ungated routed ⇒ fail closed" rule is dropped: each profile's own config governs its own bots). L6 · T2/T3. #121731 by @0xGr1mm is a later duplicate.
- Fixes #120481 — `tools/tts_command_provider.py::run_command_provider` read `os.environ.get(key)` for `env_passthrough`, the launch profile's `.env` under multiplex; now `resolve_passthrough_value(key, os.environ.get(key))` like the terminal/code-execution spawns. Covers speech, voice-note transcription and the warm/release hooks (all spawn through it). Salvages #120482 by @jonpol01 as-is. L5 · T2.
- Fixes #125530 — `hermes_cli/env_loader.py::load_hermes_dotenv` returned `[]` whenever multiplex was active and *any* home override was set, including the launch profile's own scoped bodies (which bind an override naming the launch home), so the launch `.env` (e.g. a `fallback_providers` `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`) never reached the process env and `run_agent` logged "No .env file found". The guard now skips only a load whose target is a *foreign* home (`home_path != _process_hermes_home()`, the same identity `_reapply_terminal_config_bridge` uses). Salvages #125572 by @dskwe (helper inlined; its test rewrote the live process home's `.env` and is replaced by a two-temp-home A→B→A test). #125535 by @flowioo is earlier but drops the guard for foreign homes too (a routed `.env` would enter `os.environ`), so it is superseded, not salvaged. L6/L8 · T7. A served profile that is not the launch profile still does not see the launch home's key — that is the profile isolation boundary, not this bug.
- #120018 — already fixed on main by d9199d8e8d1a (`_ProfileRoutingFileHandler.emit` binds the record's home; `agent/redact.py::_redact_enabled` is per-home). No change here.
- #119985 — already fixed on main by bb3011a2022b (`plugins/video_gen/openrouter::_credentials` via `resolve_runtime_provider`). No change here.

## Validation

Targeted files run with the 9 touched source files swapped to their `origin/main` copies (base) vs head; everything else in those files green on both.

| Item | Test | base | head |
|---|---|---|---|
| #125974 | `tests/agent/test_setup_logging_profile_scope.py::test_routes_agent_records_to_profile_scope` (A then B under override; witness only in B) | FAIL | pass |
| #120151 | `tests/test_hermes_logging.py::TestRolloverPreservesLogOwnership::test_rollover_hands_the_new_file_back_to_the_previous_owner` | FAIL | pass |
| #121705 | `tests/gateway/test_slash_access_dispatch.py::test_secondary_profile_slash_policy_uses_its_own_config`, `::test_missing_secondary_profile_config_fails_closed` | FAIL | pass |
| #120481 | `tests/tools/test_tts_command_providers.py::TestCommandTtsEnv::test_env_passthrough_forwards_the_served_profiles_value` | FAIL | pass |
| #125530 | `tests/gateway/test_multiplex_credential_isolation.py::test_launch_home_dotenv_still_loads_under_multiplex` (launch→routed→launch on two temp homes under `set_multiplex_active(True)`) | FAIL | pass |

5 files / 85 tests green on head; the same 5 files on base: 79 pass, exactly the 6 new invariants fail. `ruff`, `check_no_tmp_literals`, `check_compat_pointers`, `git diff --check`, `audit_pr_attribution --fix` clean.

Changed assertion in an inherited test (`test_secondary_profile_slash_policy_uses_its_own_config`, pinned-identity case): #121722 asserted a turn with `transport=primary, runtime=beta` is gated by beta's config; this PR asserts it follows the primary's (bot-owning) config, because `allow_admin_from` lives in `platforms.<name>.extra` of the profile that owns the bot and a routed turn must not weaken or borrow another profile's per-bot policy.

## Infographic

DEGRADED: image generation was unavailable during this lane (fal.ai balance exhausted); style picked was `nous-mission-patch`. No image embedded.



## Changed existing tests

- `tests/agent/test_skip_background_review.py::test_persistence_failure_error_fallback_is_pinned_and_leaves_final_response_empty` — fixture only, no assertion changed. It pointed `HERMES_HOME` at a named profile dir (`<tmp>/.hermes/profiles/research`) that never existed and built an `AIAgent` inside it; that only worked because `setup_logging()` used run_agent's import-time home. With this PR the agent logs under the ACTIVE home, and `mkdir_under_hermes_home()` refuses to materialize a missing named profile by design (`load_config()` → `ensure_hermes_home()` and `SessionDB` already refuse the same home, #94590), so the test now creates the profile dir first. Tolerating a missing routed home in `setup_logging()` alone would carve an exception into that contract without changing reachability (config load refuses first).
- CI red #2 (`tests/e2e/core/tenancy/test_two_tenant_gateway.py`) was a real regression from the #125530 guard: a launch-home-targeted `load_hermes_dotenv()` inside a FOREIGN routed turn ran `_reapply_terminal_config_bridge(launch)`, whose config reads follow the override, so the routed profile's `terminal.cwd` was bridged into the shared `TERMINAL_CWD`. Fixed in product code (both the target and the active home must be the launch home) with a red/green regression test `test_launch_home_load_inside_foreign_turn_keeps_routed_cwd_out_of_process_env`.


## Review fixes

- MAJOR `tools/tts_tool_lifecycle.py::_signal_user_tts_provider` — the warm/release command hook thread was a bare `threading.Thread`, so under the multiplexer `resolve_passthrough_value()` raised `UnscopedSecretError` and the best-effort hook swallowed it at debug level (every `warm_command`/`release_command` with a non-empty `env_passthrough` silently never ran). Fixed: the thread target is wrapped with `ctx_bound` (`copy_context().run`), the seam the keep-warm timer already uses. Regression test `tests/tools/test_tts_lifecycle_leases.py::test_command_hook_thread_resolves_passthrough_under_the_callers_scope` (red on the PR head: `[UnscopedSecretError(...)] != ['tok-work']`; green after).
- MINOR (b) docs — `website/docs/user-guide/multi-profile-gateways.md` "What is isolated per profile" table gains a slash-command gating row: the bot-owning profile's own `allow_admin_from`/`user_allowed_commands` govern its bots, and a served profile with no cached config is gated with an empty admin list and no user commands (only the `/help`/`/whoami` floor runs).

## Reviewer follow-ups

- MINOR (a) `agent/agent_init.py::_setup_logging` raising `FileNotFoundError` for a deleted/missing named profile home — deliberately NOT caught. Reachability check: every production path that builds an agent under a named-profile override already refuses the same home earlier with the same error — `tui_gateway/compute_host.py::_build_server_session` opens `acquire(<profile_home>/state.db)` (→ `SessionDB._open_writer` → `mkdir_under_hermes_home`) before `_make_agent`; every unguarded `load_config()` runs `ensure_hermes_home()` → `assert_named_profile_home_live()`; the CLI's `-p <name>` refuses via `profile_exists()` in `hermes_cli/profiles.py`. A fallback to the process home in `_setup_logging` alone would not change reachability and would re-create the #125974 bleed for exactly that case (a deleted profile's records landing in the launch profile's `agent.log`), so the fixture change in `tests/agent/test_skip_background_review.py` stands as the correct fix.

items.body:
Dashboard actions, sign-ins, model recommendations and the profile switcher now act on the profile the request names, and the gateway liveness check accepts an explicit `--profile default`.

## Per issue

- Fixes #120688 — `_profile_cli_args("default")` returned `[]`, so a hub action scoped to `profile=default` from a `-p worker serve` dashboard spawned a selector-less child that landed on `worker`'s home. `default` is now a real named target (`["-p", "default"]`), and unnamed gateway verbs from the default home name it too. Salvages #120689 by @beardthelion (tests trimmed to two invariants; the token-scrub assertion no longer holds since `host_gateway_child_env()` builds the `-p default gateway` env).
- Fixes #123616 — `_env_write_errors(http_passthrough=False)`, the learning-graph and plugins-hub catch-alls turned the scope's 404 into a 500; the same class in cron delivery-targets/blueprints, voice config, debug share, official skills and the non-Nous recommended default. Salvages #123617 by @jonpol01.
- Fixes #123980 — the Nous/MiniMax/xAI pollers looked the profile up by session id after the provider answered, so a cancel or the 15-minute sweep made `_profile_scope(None)` save the tokens into the launch profile; MiniMax and xAI had no locked cancel check. The pollers take `sess["profile"]` and check `cancelled` under the session lock (the Codex saver takes the scope before the lock, matching the others). Salvages #123982 by @jonpol01.
- Fixes #124283 — the `slug == "nous"` branch of `/api/model/recommended-default` returned before `_config_profile_scope(profile)`; now inside it, and an unknown profile is the scope's 404. Salvages #124284 by @jonpol01 (test fixture rewritten onto the hermetic home; the non-Nous passthrough came in via #123617).
- Fixes #125025 — `ProfileProvider` synced state→URL and URL→state in two effects, so `navigate("/skills?profile=beta")` (path AND param change) had the URL-writer run with the old state and rewrite `profile=alpha`. The URL param is adopted during render before any effect. Salvages #125026 by @Adolanium.
- Fixes #96712 — `shouldAdoptActiveProfile()` aligned the switcher to the machine-global sticky `active_profile` whenever it differed from the serving profile, so a dashboard hosted by a named profile (`hermes -p demo serve`) retargeted its banner, chat env and model to another agent on every load. Only the default-hosted machine dashboard aligns; `custom` never does. Salvages #96736 by @ipriyaaanshu (re-applied at the helper that replaced the inline condition).
- Fixes #100817 — `gateway/status.py::_command_line_belongs_to_profile` and its sibling `hermes_cli/gateway.py::_matches_current_profile` rejected any `-p/--profile` flag on the default-home branch, so a default gateway started with `--profile default` (hand-written launchd plist) showed as stopped. Only a flag naming ANOTHER profile disqualifies. Salvages #100888 by @Sahilvishnaliya (rebuilt on the `profile_flag_value()` matcher main uses now).
- #92520 (Hindsight settings written into the launch profile) is already fixed on main: the SPA sends `?profile=` for the `/api/memory` family since 6a3dcc39ab0 and the routes run in `scoped_to_thread(profile, …)` (76c063b3d97), so `provider.save_config(values, get_hermes_home())` lands in the selected profile's home. No change here; the parent closes it.

## WHEN × WHERE

L6 (dashboard routers / SPA scope) on T3 (dashboard hosted by a named profile) and T7 (pooled Desktop/dashboard `serve`); L5 (child processes: hub-action argv/env) on T3; the `--profile default` matcher is process identity on T6 (launchd) / T4.

## Validation

| Item | Red on origin/main | Green on head |
|---|---|---|
| #120688 | `test_hub_install_scoped_to_default_still_carries_the_selector`, `test_unnamed_lifecycle_verbs_from_default_home_always_name_default` both fail (argv `[]`) | pass; hub install from a `worker_alpha`-hosted dashboard with `profile=default` spawns `-p default` and pins `HERMES_HOME` to the default home |
| #123616 | `test_unknown_profile_is_the_scopes_404` 8/8 fail (500) | 8/8 pass (404 naming the profile) |
| #123980 | `test_dashboard_poller_saves_only_into_the_profile_the_login_started_in` 4/4 fail (saved into launch home / after cancel) | 4/4 pass: `coder` login saves into `coder`, cancelled login saves nowhere (both providers, cancel + expire) |
| #124283 | `test_nous_recommendation_reads_the_requested_profile` fails (`free_tier False` for the free profile) | passes: launch paid, `freebie` free, unknown 404 |
| #125025 | vitest `adopts ?profile= from a link that also changes the path` fails (settles on `alpha`) | passes; `/skills?profile=beta` ends on `beta` |
| #96712 | vitest `keeps a named-profile dashboard on its own profile` fails | passes; `demo`/`custom` hosts never adopt the sticky profile |
| #100817 | `test_command_line_belongs_to_profile_accepts_explicit_default` fails | passes; `-p coder` still rejected |

`web/`: `npx tsc -b` clean, `vitest run` 356/356. Python: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli tests/gateway` (see thread for the summary line), `ruff check`, `check_no_tmp_literals.py`, `check_compat_pointers.py`, `git diff --check` clean.

## Infographic

DEGRADED: not generated — `image_generate` refused with "Exhausted balance" at the image provider during this lane.


## Changed existing tests

Two pre-existing tests pinned the bare `["gateway", "restart"]` argv on the shared dashboard restart spawn site (`_restart_gateway_after` → `_spawn_gateway_restart` → `_gateway_subcommand(None, "restart")`). The #120688 fix deliberately makes that site emit `["-p", "default", "gateway", "restart"]` from the default home (`_own_profile_selector` names the default home `"default"`, `_profile_cli_args("default")` emits the selector), so a child can never re-read the sticky `active_profile` and restart another profile's gateway. Each assertion was updated to the new argv only; the tests' subjects are unchanged.

| Test | Old assertion | New assertion | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_dashboard_admin_endpoints.py::TestWebhookEndpoints::test_enable_platform_starts_gateway_restart` | `restart_calls == [(["gateway", "restart"], "gateway-restart")]` | `restart_calls == [(["-p", "default", "gateway", "restart"], "gateway-restart")]` | `POST /api/webhooks/enable` auto-restart now names the default home explicitly; the save-is-authoritative / `restart_started` + pid contract is untouched. |
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server.py::TestWebServerEndpoints::test_telegram_onboarding_apply_reports_restart_failure_after_save` | `subcommand == ["gateway", "restart"]` (inside the failing-spawn stub) | `subcommand == ["-p", "default", "gateway", "restart"]` | Telegram onboarding apply auto-restart, same spawn site; the "failed spawn is reported after the save, not raised" contract is untouched. |

`hermes -p default gateway restart` is accepted by `hermes_cli/gateway.py`: `_apply_profile_override` pins `HERMES_HOME` to the root and skips `active_profile`, `profile_lifecycle` and `_guard_named_profile_under_multiplexer` both pass `default` through (no exit 78, no second gateway), and the CLI's own multiplex refusal text prescribes exactly that argv as the host remedy. No other test under `tests/` asserts a bare `["gateway", ...]` argv produced by these spawn sites (remaining hits are mocks, hand-built argv, or `[-2:]` suffix checks that still hold).


## Behaviour change

Hub actions targeting the **default** profile from the machine (default-hosted) dashboard — skills install/update/uninstall, MCP install, toolset post-setup — now run with the same scrubbed, pinned environment every named-profile action gets (`_profile_cli_args("default")` → `["-p", "default"]` → `_profile_action_environment`'s named-target branch: `build_subprocess_env(scrub_secrets=True)`, dotenv/managed keys dropped, `HERMES_HOME` pinned to the default home) instead of the historical verbatim `os.environ` copy. Consequence: secrets that reach the dashboard *only* through its process environment (systemd `Environment=`, `op run`, a shell export that is not in `.env`) no longer reach those children; the child loads the default profile's own `.env` and secret sources at startup. This is deliberate and kept: one env contract for every hub target means the default profile cannot be the one target that silently inherits whatever the dashboard's supervisor had in its environment, and matches the documented scope rule (target profile's `.env` + secret sources). Gateway verbs are unaffected (`host_gateway_child_env`). Documented in `web-dashboard.md` § Managing multiple profiles.

## Review fixes

- `web_server_profiles.py::_profile_cli_args` → `web_server_gateway.py::_profile_action_environment` (default-target hub actions take the scrubbed/pinned branch; unstated behaviour change) → **kept the consistent env, stated under `## Behaviour change` above**, plus one docs paragraph in `website/docs/user-guide/features/web-dashboard.md` that hub actions run with the target profile's own secret scope, not the dashboard process environment.
- `web_routers/profiles.py::get_active_profile_endpoint::_or_default` (exception fallback `"default"` is exactly the `current` value that lets `shouldAdoptActiveProfile` adopt the sticky profile) → **fixed**: the `current` read's *failure* fallback is now `"custom"` (adoption-refusing); the empty-value case keeps `or "default"`, and `active` keeps `"default"` on failure — a `"custom"` there would itself trigger adoption of a non-existent profile when `current == "default"`. No existing test covers `_or_default`; verified with an off-tree probe (both raise → `{"active": "default", "current": "custom"}`; both empty → both `"default"`).

items.body:
After the package-manager takeover, `hermes update` now brings back a dashboard that was started by hand. If it cannot bring a dashboard back, the receipt books it as `failed` (receipt `partial`, exit 1) instead of `restarted` / `success`.

## Changes

| Issue | Root cause (origin/main) | Fix | From | E2E gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #124778 | `hermes_cli/main_dashboard.py::_respawn_dashboard_processes` replays the stopped dashboard's `/proc` argv verbatim: `[<old venv python>, ~/.local/bin/hermes, dashboard, …]`. The takeover has already rewritten that launcher into a shell shim, so the child dies with `SyntaxError`. Because `Popen` itself succeeded, the updater still prints `✓ restarted`. | A `python + hermes-launcher` argv is rebuilt on `_launchers.runtime_command`, the installation-bound launcher every other Hermes spawn uses (store Python + bootstrap). The checkout's own `hermes` entry is left unchanged. A child that exits within 1 s is reported as a failed restart. | #124797 (@liuhao1024); the launcher swap is ours | `DASHBOARD_GATES["n1"]`: #124778 entry removed |
| #109290 | `hermes_cli/update_inventory.py::match_runtime_outcomes` has no input for a failed respawn. The incarnation probe reads "pre-update pid gone" as `restarted`, and `update_cmd_fleet.py` drops the `unrecovered` PIDs from `_refresh_dashboard_after_update`. | `_refresh_dashboard_after_update` returns the PIDs it stopped and could not bring back. They read `failed` before the probe runs and set `restart.incomplete`, which gives receipt `partial` and exit 1. A failed respawn reports the caller's argv, so it matches the stopped PID's cmdline. | #109298 (@liuhao1024), ported onto the moved code | `FALSE_SUCCESS_GATE` removed |
| #123109 | Already fixed on origin/main by #124965 (`60e531cb52`, `inline_bootstrap_argv`): `_gateway_command_subcommand` reads the bootstrap launcher's argv. | None needed. The stale gate is removed. | #123131 is superseded by #124965 | `PID_FILE_GATE` removed; the cell passes on origin/main in both columns |

Unit tests added:
- 1 for receipt reconciliation.
- 2 for the respawn: the argv rebuild, and an instant death counted as a failure and reported with the caller's argv.

## Validation

E2E suite `tests/e2e/core/upgrade/handoff`, run locally under bwrap with the gates removed:

| Cell | n1 on origin/main | n1 on this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `test_update_exit_status_matches_what_came_back` | FAIL `the update exited 0 though the dashboard did not come back` | PASS |
| `test_dashboard_is_back_on_its_port` | FAIL `the respawned dashboard died parsing its launcher … SyntaxError` | PASS |
| `test_gateway_pid_file_and_status_find_the_relaunched_gateway` | PASS | PASS |
| all 7 cells | 5/7 | 7/7 |

- **Head column:** 7/7 on origin/main. The only red on this branch came from a cron change that has since been dropped (see below).
- **Why the N-1 gates come off now:** the dashboard respawn runs in HEAD's code even in the N-1 column, because `_finish_dashboard_update_cleanup` runs in the updated checkout.

**#113293 is not in this PR.** An update-lock deferral in `cron/scheduler_tick.py` (#111842's approach) made the head column red. A one-shot that comes due during an update more than `ONESHOT_GRACE_SECONDS` (120 s) long is retired as missed by `cron/jobs.py::_retire_expired_oneshot` before the first post-update tick (E2E: `the job due mid-update ran 0 times`, `cron job: null`). Deferring needs a grace policy for jobs that come due while an update holds the install; that is a product decision, so `CRON_GATES` is unchanged.

Fixes #124778
Fixes #109290
Fixes #123109
