## Summary
- Fold the count into the Desktop context meter: once a session has compacted, the meter reads `… 38% ◈ 2` (the Codicon `layers` glyph the sidebar already puts on compression-continuation rows), and the meter's panel shows `Compressions: N` beside `N% Full`. The meter stays unchanged at zero so fresh sessions carry no noise; the panel shows zero explicitly.
- Project the existing canonical `usage.compressions` field (published by `tui_gateway/server.py::_get_usage`): no new backend counter, DB schema, or lineage traversal. This covers the default in-place compaction path that a lineage-derived count would miss (`compression.in_place` defaults to true — same session id, no parent link).
- Authoritative-snapshot semantics throughout: `session.info`/`session.resume`/create usage merges into the addressed `ClientSessionState` (including focused secondary tiles) and clears a stale count when the snapshot omits `compressions`; a cold session switch drops the previous session's live-only count immediately; background `session.usage` ticks cannot overwrite the focused session. Zero is real data; missing stays hidden.

Supersedes #38258, #109376:
- @Xipong's #109376 is the better core approach and this PR carries that commit (plus the `gaoanze888` review fixes: per-tile projection, omission clearing, accessible name).
- @sweetcornna's #38258 proposed a lineage-derived `compress_count`; as the sweeper review on that PR notes, a lineage count is zero on the default in-place compaction path, so this PR uses the canonical live `usage.compressions` instead. The `SessionInfo`/sidebar-history portion of that proposal is deliberately out of scope here.

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/38246 (acceptance: live count surfaced in the status bar's context meter with no-command parity to the CLI/TUI `🗜️ N`; tracked across cold switches and focused tiles; zero rendered explicitly in the panel). A durable lifetime count across restarts is live-runtime state by design and remains the backend's accounting.

## Tests
- RED on base for the three new behavior tests (`applyRuntimeInfo` background usage projection, focused-omission clearing, cold-switch clearing) — 3 failed with the implementation reverted, 132 passed.
- GREEN: `npx vitest run src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/utils.test.ts src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/usage.test.tsx src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/index.test.tsx` — 280 passed; `src/app/shell/context-usage-panel.test.tsx` covers the meter/panel contract (count only after a compaction in the meter; zero shown in the panel; nothing invented when usage omits it).
- `npm run typecheck` (renderer + electron + e2e) — 0 errors.
- ESLint on all touched files — 0 errors (2 pre-existing hook-dependency warnings elsewhere in the files).
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py -k 'compression_count or compress_helper or usage_ticker'` — 8 passed.

items.body: Salvages #120664 and #120686 by @Sonnenwerk (stacked). Their net diff didn't cherry-pick cleanly, so it's replayed and reworked here with `Co-authored-by`. Log search used to filter lines out, so you lost the context around a match. Now `LogTail` searches in place: - matches are highlighted, and the active one scrolls into view - a `3/6` counter with up/down buttons steps through them - Enter, Shift+Enter and ⌘G / ⇧⌘G move between matches; Esc clears - key handling and labels come from the ⌘F find bar, so both behave the same The Command Center system log and the MCP log pane both use it. The original PRs added a separate Command Center log view; that fork is gone, and there is one log component again. Other changes: - **Following the live log.** Clearing a search now returns the pane to following the tail. Before, it stayed parked at the last match and stopped following new lines, the bug @Enough1122 flagged in review. A regression test covers it. - **Severity marks.** WARNING, ERROR and CRITICAL lines get a thin gutter bar. The level is read from the log format's level column, so an INFO line that mentions "ERROR" isn't marked. INFO lines get no icon. - **Jump buttons.** Top and bottom buttons sit next to copy and show on hover. - **Breadcrumb header.** Command Center sections use the same breadcrumb header as Settings (the author's change, kept). The section descriptions it replaced are removed from every locale. - **Translations.** Every locale has the new strings. items.body: Salvages #121385 by @Sonnenwerk, reworked with `Co-authored-by`. Messaging gets a status filter next to its search. Only tones that some platform is currently in get a tab (Errors, Needs attention, Connected, Inactive), and the filter disappears when every platform is in the same state. Picking a tab moves the detail pane into the filter. A platform that drops out because you just toggled it stays open, so the pane doesn't jump away mid-edit. Messaging and the gateway menu now read platform state through one classifier (`lib/platform-status.ts`). Before, they disagreed on unknown states (warn on the Messaging page, muted in the menu), so the same bot could show two tones. The shared rule: an enabled platform that isn't connected or failed is waiting on something, so it shows warn. What changed from the original PR: - dropped the `status:` / `sort:` search syntax and its hint line; the filter tabs cover the same need without new syntax to learn - dropped sorting; the filter already groups platforms by status - replaced the duplicate `stateTone` / `statusFilterTone` switches with the one classifier - all locales carry the filter labels Supersedes #121385 ## Screenshots The real `MessagingView` with stubbed platform data (2 connected, 2 needs attention, 1 error, 3 off), after clicking **Needs attention**.

items.body:
Salvage of #126307 by @100yenadmin (Eva), implementing #126265.

Context engines and plugins currently have no stable id for a message. A row id changes when compaction or a row-addressed rewrite re-inserts the row, list position changes on every merge, and the content hash changes on every edit. So a plugin cannot tell "the message I saw last turn" apart from a new one. With this stack, every persisted message carries a durable `message_uid` that survives restore, compaction copies, rewrites, export/import and branch copies. A consecutive-user merge records which uids it folded in (`_absorbed_message_uids`). Each tool call and its result share a per-occurrence uid (`_tool_call_uids` on the assistant row, `_tool_call_uid` on the result). None of these fields reach provider requests. Schema v30 → v31.

WHO / WHEN / WHY: Eva filed #126265 and opened #126307 on 2026-09-28. The 6 feature commits are hers and are cherry-picked with authorship kept. The follow-up commits are mine, from a review that found one startup blocker, two identity mismatches, and a set of cleanups.

## Salvage commits on top of Eva's work

- **Bounded legacy backfill (blocker).** The v31 migration minted uids for every legacy row in a single UPDATE at open. On an 837k-row / 4.8 GB store that took 261 s, and a second process trying to write gave up with `database is locked` after 120 s. The backfill now runs in 2,000-id autocommit chunks: each open spends about 1 s after its first chunk and resumes from a cursor in `state_meta`. New stores are marked done at creation.
- **TUI submit row and model-switch marker.** These rows were written to the DB with one uid while the live dict carried none, or a different one. `append_message` now takes the caller's uid and returns it, so both sides match.
- **Branch and seed copies.** TUI branch, lazy seed and CLI `/branch` wrote fresh uids while the child session kept the parent's live dicts. All three now write the uid the live history keeps. Tool-call uid maps are copied only where the copy also carries `tool_calls`.
- **Tool-call uid pairing (from review, including @andrexibiza's two threads on #126307).**
  - Folding two assistant turns that reuse a provider id (llama.cpp-style ids) keeps a uid for each occurrence instead of only the later one. When one response repeats an id, those calls share one uid, which every result carries. Before a fold appends the next turn's uid, that shared uid is copied into each of the row's own positions so every call stays lined up with its uid.
  - A merge that discards the later turn's text (text next to image content is never joined) no longer records that row as absorbed.
  - Rewriting a stored row no longer loses uids: a restored fold keeps its longer list, a dict that lost its map keeps the stored uids for the calls it still names, and a call the dict dropped doesn't get its uid back.
  - Chunked branch/seed copies pair a result with a call from an earlier chunk.
  - A non-dict uid map on either turn of a fold is ignored instead of raising.
- **Gateway replay keeps identity on plain rows** (Eva's follow-up, cherry-picked with her authorship). `_build_replay_entry` rebuilt plain user/assistant rows without `message_uid` or the merge witness; it now copies both on every role. Tool-call uid maps stay with the rows that still carry their calls.
- **Performance.**
  - The flush path now memoizes each assistant's call index, so pairing a result with its call no longer recomputes it per result. With 160 parallel results: 430 ms → 4 ms.
  - Restore builds that index only for results without a stored uid (an older build's rows).
  - The token-estimate cache key skips persistence-only fields.
- **Cleanups.**
  - One uid reader/stamper and one identity-field copier in `agent/message_metadata.py`, replacing two duplicate helper pairs and four copied blocks.
  - One restore decoder.
  - The four columns recorded as a single schema-history event.
  - The backfill cursor removed once done.
  - Rewind uses the shared helpers.
  - The uid read/write helpers moved into `hermes_state_identity.py`, keeping `hermes_state_messages.py` under 2,000 lines.
  - Three tests dropped that pass without the feature. One added that pairs a result with the assistant that named its call rather than the nearest one; it catches two mutations the existing tests missed.
- **Docs.** Session-storage (v31 row) and context-engine-plugin docs describe the bounded backfill and branch behaviour.

## Behaviour

- New rows get a uid at insert (trigger plus stamping). Legacy rows get one over later opens of any Hermes process. On the 837k-row store that took 85 opens, each about 1.5 s (3.5 s worst). Until then, older rows restore without a uid, as the docs note.
- Opening once the backfill is finished: 0.36 s (main: 0.54 s). During the backfill, a concurrent writer waited at most 1.41 s (p99 1.09 s over 440 attempts). Result: 0 rows without a uid, 0 duplicate uids.
- A v30 (main) build can open, append to, compact and replace in a v31 store, including one that is partly backfilled.
- None of the identity fields reach a provider request. Checked on the chat_completions, anthropic, bedrock and responses converters and on context-engine `select_context` output.

## Known limits (not changed here)

- A branch taken after in-place compaction duplicates the live tail in the child. The duplicate itself already happens on main (the display/live reconcile anchors on the summary row); with this stack the two copies share a uid. The docs already say uids are not unique per row.
- Tool-call uids on legacy rows copied by CLI `/branch` are minted on the copy, so they differ from the live dicts.
- The stored `tool_call_uid` column is kept. It can be derived from the preceding assistant row, but keeping it avoids a restore-time walk.

## Verification

- Uid, context-engine, sequence-repair, TUI submit-row, branch-command and schema-history test files: 127 passed on the rebased head. Each review fix has a test that fails when the old code is put back.
- Live E2E through the real CLI (`chat -q --oneshot` with two tool calls, then `--resume`): every row gets a distinct uid, resumed rows keep theirs, tool results carry the uid their call was given, and `HERMES_DUMP_REQUESTS` shows no identity field in the provider request.
- tests/hermes_state, tests/tui_gateway, tests/acp_adapter and tests/agent, plus targeted hermes_cli/gateway files, run with `scripts/run_tests.sh` on this branch and on main: no failure occurs only on this branch. The failures are local (sqlite `.recover`, holder gates, repair harness) and none are caused by this stack.
- `ty` on the touched files, compared with main: the only new diagnostics are two more `set_meta` calls on the schema mixin (the same pattern main already flags three times) and one `record_absorbed_message` call inside a `micro_compaction` block where main already reports six errors on that `Optional` narrowing.
- Backfill E2E on a copy of a real 837k-row store, with a concurrent writer thread (numbers above).

Closes #126265. Supersedes #126307; Eva's commits are kept as authored.

Persistent Modal sandboxes no longer lose their filesystem after 30 idle days: the snapshot is retained until Hermes deletes it, and the SDK pin moves to a version that has the knob.

## Changes
- `tools/environments/modal.py::ModalEnvironment.cleanup` passes `snapshot_filesystem(ttl=None)`. On modal ≥ 1.5 the default is `ttl=2592000` (30 days), after which the snapshot image is gone and the next session silently restarts from the base image.
- `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock`: `modal==1.3.4` → `modal==1.5.5` (+ its `synchronicity` dep). 1.3.4 has no `ttl` parameter at all (legacy `SandboxSnapshotFs` RPC), so the kwarg needs the bump to exist on every install; the venvs already on 1.5.x were sending the 30-day default.
- Dead code removed: `_modal.Mount.from_local_file(...)` credential-mount block. `modal.Mount` left the public API in modal 1.0, so that line raised `AttributeError` into the surrounding `except` on every sandbox start and mounted nothing. The `FileSyncManager` created right after already uploads the same credential, skills and cache files (`iter_sync_files`), so nothing is lost. The test fake stops exporting a `Mount` the real SDK does not have.
- Docs: `configuration.md` Modal persistence paragraph states the retention.

## Root cause
Modal added a default snapshot TTL in SDK 1.5; our call site predates it and never opted out.

## Validation
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/tools/test_modal_snapshot_isolation.py::test_persistent_cleanup_snapshots_without_expiry` | red on `origin/main` (`snapshot_calls == []`, the fake swallowed the kwarg-less call), green on head |
| Modal test files (6) + `tests/tools/environments` | 55 passed |
| `python -m pm.build_env --source . --check-lock` | resolves clean |
| `inspect.signature(modal.Sandbox.snapshot_filesystem)` on 1.5.5 | `(self, timeout: int = 55, *, ttl: int | None = 2592000)`; docstring: "Pass `ttl=None` to retain the image indefinitely" |
| Rest of our Modal surface on 1.5.5 (`App.lookup.aio`, `Image.from_registry/from_id`, `Sandbox.create.aio`, `exec.aio`, `terminate.aio`) | present, signatures compatible |

No Modal credentials on the dev box, so no live sandbox round-trip in this PR; the fix is the vendor-documented kwarg, proven at the SDK boundary.

items.body:
Fresh Vercel sandboxes start from a managed container image (`vercel/sandbox/universal:latest`) instead of the `runtime` preset Vercel deprecated, with a config migration so existing installs follow along and legacy pins keep working.

## Changes
- New `terminal.vercel_image` (default `vercel/sandbox/universal:latest`: Ubuntu, Node 24, Python 3.14). Accepts any Vercel managed image or a project VCR repository[:tag|@digest].
- `terminal.vercel_runtime` default `node24` → `""`. A pinned runtime (`node24|node22|python3.13`) still works, overrides the image and logs a deprecation warning; the two are never sent together (Vercel rejects that).
- Snapshot restores send neither `runtime` nor `image`: the snapshot carries its filesystem, and Vercel refuses `runtime` with a snapshot source. Persisted sandboxes are unaffected by the default change.
- `_migrate_to_49`: drops `terminal.vercel_runtime: node24` (the template default, never a choice) from config.yaml AND the `TERMINAL_VERCEL_RUNTIME=node24` mirror the setup wizard wrote to `.env`; `node22`/`python3.13` pins survive. `_config_version` 48 → 49.
- Surfaces: `TERMINAL_VERCEL_IMAGE` bridged like its siblings (`cli_config_load`, `config.py`, `gateway/run.py`, `terminal_tool.py`), setup wizard prompts for the image (and warns when a legacy runtime pin will override it), dashboard config gets an image field and a clearable legacy-runtime select, `hermes status`/`hermes config` show the effective image. Docs updated (`configuration.md`, `tools.md`).

## Vendor basis
- [Runtimes](https://vercel.com/docs/sandbox/concepts/runtimes): "Since August 7th, runtimes are deprecated and we recommend using Images for new sandboxes… sandboxes that specify neither `runtime` nor `image` use the `vercel/sandbox/universal:latest` managed image."
- [Images](https://vercel.com/docs/sandbox/concepts/images): `vercel/sandbox/universal:latest` = Node.js LTS (24), Python (3.14), coding agents, utilities.
- Python SDK 0.7.2 (our pin) `Sandbox.create` docstring: `runtime` "Mutually exclusive with `image` and unavailable when `source` is a snapshot"; `image` "Vercel Container Registry image… a bare repository name resolves to the `latest` tag."

## Validation
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/tools/test_vercel_sandbox_environment.py::TestImageSelection` (fresh → image only; legacy pin → runtime only; restore → neither) | green on head; the `runtime`/`image` keys did not exist on base |
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_config_migration_49_vercel_image.py` (seeded default dropped from config.yaml + .env, user pin survives, merged default resolves) | green |
| Vercel suite + terminal requirements + setup/status/doctor/cli_init + config env/migration suites | 184 passed, 0 failed |
| Real-import chain probe (temp `HERMES_HOME` → `_mirror_config_to_env` → `terminal_tool._get_env_config` → backend factory kwargs) | default: `{'runtime': None, 'image': 'vercel/sandbox/universal:latest'}`; with `TERMINAL_VERCEL_RUNTIME=python3.13`: runtime carried, image dropped in `__init__` |

No Vercel credentials on the dev box, so no live sandbox round-trip in this PR; behaviour follows the vendor docs and the pinned SDK's own contract.

## Follow-up context
Found while verifying vendor docs for #121169 (Bot Screen in the sandbox).

Salvages #121396 by @ajbmachon, with tests from #102987 by @shorehefei-ship-it and credit to #98523 by @salch-cred. The two gateway commits from #121396 are cherry-picked, so authorship is kept (the Desktop busy-turn deferral hunk from that PR is left out; it is a separate change). One commit on top.

The change watcher fingerprinted `sessions.changed` on the raw `state.db` / WAL mtime. The gateway heartbeat and the session activity stamp (`last_activity_at`) write to that same file about once a minute with no session change, so every write broadcast `sessions.changed` and the Desktop Sessions panel refreshed on its own every ~25–60s.

#121396 replaces the mtime with a blake2b digest of the session columns Desktop renders, read only when the DB/WAL mtime moved, so an idle pass is still just a stat. Its column list still included `last_activity_at` and `last_activity_description`, which the activity heartbeat restamps, so the refresh kept firing. This PR removes them from the digest. Creating, renaming, deleting, pinning or archiving a session, or a new message landing (`message_count`), still moves it.

What changed from the original PRs:

- `last_activity_at` / `last_activity_description` are no longer hashed. Desktop doesn't render either field from the list, and liveness comes from `session.active_list`.
- The probe opens through `_connect_tracked_db` + `read_only_db_uri`, the read-only connect other live `state.db` readers use, instead of a raw `sqlite3.connect`.
- If a read fails after a good one (locked or busy store), the last digest is kept and the next pass tries again, instead of flipping to the mtime signature and back (two false broadcasts). #102987 handled this case the same way.
- #102987's `SUM(...)`-based fingerprint is dropped (swapping two titles of equal length doesn't change it), and so is its `chat/index.tsx` hunk: it conflicts with main's `isRouteSessionMismatch` options API and isn't needed once the heartbeat broadcasts stop.
- Nothing from #98523 is used. Its `max(updated_at)` probe always throws because `sessions` has no `updated_at` column, so it falls back to mtime.

Tests (`tests/tui_gateway/test_change_watcher.py`, `test_change_watcher_sessions.py`):

- Three heartbeat windows (a `gateway_heartbeats` write plus a `last_activity_at` stamp each) broadcast nothing. On origin/main this fails, and it also fails on #121396 as submitted.
- A new session row, a rename, a `message_count` bump and a delete each broadcast.
- A store that becomes unreadable after a good read doesn't broadcast. This fails on origin/main and on #121396.
- On origin/main: 3 failed / 25 passed. On this branch: 28 passed (`scripts/run_tests.sh`), and `ruff check` is clean.

Supersedes #121396
Supersedes #102987
Supersedes #98523
Fixes #98005

Salvages #76838 by @webtecnica. Their commit is cherry-picked with the test file conflict resolved onto the current mock setup, so authorship is kept. One commit on top removes the refocus effect and extends the test.

In Settings → Gateway with SSH mode, an empty saved host, and aliases in `~/.ssh/config`, picking "Custom (enter manually)…" did nothing the first time. The host Select's controlled value fell back to the Custom sentinel whenever the saved host wasn't one of the aliases, so it was already `__custom__` before the click. Radix only calls `onValueChange` when the value changes, so `selectHost` never ran and the text input never mounted. It only worked after picking an alias first and then Custom. The trigger also showed "Custom (enter manually)…" as its value instead of the placeholder.

The fix is @webtecnica's: the Select's value falls back to `''` instead of the sentinel. The trigger shows the placeholder, and the first Custom pick goes from `''` to `__custom__`, which fires the callback and mounts the input.

What changed from the original PR:
- Re-applied on the current `gateway-settings.tsx`. The file was refactored since the PR opened, which is why it conflicted; the SSH host logic itself had not changed.
- Dropped the `requestAnimationFrame` refocus effect and the input ref. The issue came from the input never rendering, not from a focus race. Once it mounts, the existing `autoFocus` focuses it, and the test passes without the effect.
- Ported the regression test to the current hoisted store mocks. It also types into the field, then clears it and blurs to check that it goes back to the dropdown.
- No styling changes.

Tests:
- `npx vitest run src/app/settings/gateway-settings.test.tsx -t Custom` with `origin/main`'s `gateway-settings.tsx`: fails, no textbox after the first Custom click.
- `npx vitest run src/app/settings/gateway-settings.test.tsx` on this branch: 15 passed.

Supersedes #76838
Fixes #76825

Salvages #125917 by @helix4u. Their two commits are cherry-picked as-is, so authorship is kept. No rework commit on top: the change applies cleanly to current main and does not clash with anything that landed since.

A completed tool card disappeared from Desktop chat and Bot Chat tiles once the transcript refreshed. When the newest stored page brought the final assistant reply without the turn's tool rows, the refresh took that page as the whole window, and the live tool card went with it. The Discord reporter hit this on KoboldCPP. It doesn't depend on the provider: any text-only page that carries the final reply triggers it.

#126409 was merged as the real fix and #125917 was closed. That PR fixed only the Codex `webSearch` projector, so Codex searches now get stored as `web_search` tool rows. Nothing on the Desktop side changed, and a refresh page without the tool rows still clobbers the live card for every other runtime. The three regression tests below fail on current main, which already includes #126409.

The fix follows the "Merge, don't clobber" rule in `apps/desktop/AGENTS.md`. After `graftRefreshedTailOntoBackfill` builds the refreshed window, completed live tool parts from the settled turn are carried onto the refreshed final reply, but only when:

- the durable user row and the final assistant row ids match the live turn,
- the final reply text is unchanged,
- the refreshed turn doesn't already have a tool part with that `toolCallId`.

Durable rows still win when the page has them. The standard runtime emits `tool.start` with the stored `tool_call_id`, and #126409 made Codex search rows use the live id too. So when the page has the tool row, the live copy is skipped and nothing renders twice. The same reply text on a different durable row doesn't inherit the tools.

What changed from the original PR
- Nothing. Rebased onto current main with no conflicts.

Tests (`apps/desktop`, `npx vitest run --project ui`)
- On main with only the test changes: `completed-reply-refresh.test.tsx` + `use-session-tile-delegate.test.ts` give 3 failed / 32 passed. The new cases (text-only refresh for active chat and tile, Bot Chat tile final-reply refresh) all end with `expected [] to match object [{ toolCallId: … }]`.
- This branch: those two files plus `transcript-backfill.test.ts`, `folded-tool-turn-refresh.test.tsx` and the `use-background-sync` suites give 6 files, 117/117 passed.
- `npx tsc -p . --noEmit` and eslint on the touched files: clean.

Supersedes #125917

items.body:
If a Hermes.app that an earlier `hermes update` installed is later removed, `hermes update` now puts it back and says so. Finder, the Dock and Spotlight can find Hermes again.

**Who / when / why:** Found on 2026-09-28 while working out why Hermes had disappeared from Spotlight on a maintainer's Mac. A test had deleted `/Applications/Hermes.app`; the test side is fixed in a companion PR. Every `hermes update` after that skipped the missing copy without a word, so nothing ever brought the app back. The skip goes back to 032cf8438f (#113933, @teknium1, 2026-09-17), which refreshes only bundles that still exist. That was reasonable at the time: the ownership stamp that marks a copy as this checkout's lives inside the bundle, so it disappears along with the bundle.

**Changes**
- `hermes_cli/main_desktop.py`
  - `_refresh_installed_desktop_apps` records which installed copies the update keeps current, in `desktop-installed-apps.json` under the default Hermes root. Only the checkout that owns installed apps writes this file, never one running off macOS or from a dev worktree. A copy that failed to reinstall stays recorded, so the next update tries again. If the record can't be written, the update prints a warning and carries on.
  - A restored copy prints `✓ Reinstalled the Desktop app at … it had been removed, so Finder, the Dock and Spotlight could not find Hermes`.
  - When no owned copy is left, `_installed_desktop_apps` counts a recorded path that is now missing as installed, so the update rebuilds the Desktop app for it. A copy the user moved from `/Applications` to `~/Applications` (or back) keeps its stamp, so the update finds it there and doesn't install a second one.
  - `_install_rebuilt_macos_bundles` installs into missing paths as well as stale ones, using the same stage-and-swap with `ditto`, so the signature is preserved. `_install_rebuilt_desktop_app` now takes the candidate list from its caller rather than computing it a second time.
- `hermes_cli/gui_uninstall.py`: `desktop_install_record()` is the one place the record's path is defined. `uninstall_gui` deletes the record wherever the uninstall runs from, including a profile, since the installed apps are machine-wide. So `hermes uninstall` in any mode deletes it, including the in-app uninstall, which runs `hermes uninstall`, and the app stays uninstalled.
- Docs: `getting-started/updating.md` step 6.

**Validation**

| | before (origin/main) | after |
|---|---|---|
| Real rebuilt bundle, install path in a temp dir, copy deleted, then the update tail runs | nothing printed, app stays missing, update wouldn't even rebuild for it | `✓ Reinstalled …`, app present, `codesign --verify --deep --strict` passes |
| `uninstall_gui` then update | — | app stays gone, record removed |
| Copy moved to the other Applications folder, then update | — | no second copy is installed |

- Tests: one existing test flipped (a missing candidate path is now installed) and one new invariant test (macOS): a moved copy isn't doubled, a deleted copy comes back every time, and nothing comes back after a GUI uninstall run from a profile home. Both fail on origin/main. A mutation that stops uninstall from removing the record makes the new test fail.
- Local run of the 82 test files that reference the touched symbols (first revision): the same 38 environment failures as origin/main, no new failures, +1 pass. The touched test files were re-run on this revision: all pass, except one launchd-plist test that also fails on origin/main on this machine.
- Review: 4-angle review plus the reuse/quality/efficiency passes. I applied the moved-copy, profile-uninstall, stale-record, record-write-failure, `read_json_or_empty` reuse and single-computation findings.

**Known edge:** a user who drags an update-installed Hermes.app to the Trash by hand, instead of running `hermes uninstall`, gets it back on the next update. From inside the updater that looks exactly like the app being deleted by accident, which is the case this PR fixes.

A test that runs the real GUI uninstall or update swap can no longer delete or overwrite the developer's own installed Hermes desktop app. The test now fails and says so.

**Who / when / why:** On 2026-09-26, during review of #122553 (commit 954d90f15f by @dskwe, 2026-09-25), its `test_uninstall_gui_keeps_userdata_dir_when_told_to` called the real `uninstall_gui()` and stubbed only the userData dir. On macOS, `packaged_gui_app_paths()` returns the real `/Applications/Hermes.app`, and tests keep `HOME` intact, so the test deleted a maintainer's installed app. The open app started failing lazy chunk loads two minutes later, and Hermes was gone from Spotlight. That test was trimmed before it merged. Nothing stops the next one.

**Changes**
- `tests/conftest.py` captures `packaged_gui_app_paths()` at import time, before any test can patch `sys.platform`, `HOME` or `XDG_*`. The captured paths are `/Applications/Hermes.app` and `~/Applications/Hermes.app` on macOS, the desktop entry and icons on Linux, and `Programs\Hermes` on Windows.
- `tests/home_io_guard.py` fails the test on any delete, rename, replace, `chmod`, `utime` or write-mode `open` / `os.open` inside those paths, whether the path matches as written or only after resolving symlinks. Reads stay allowed, because update paths probe the installed app. Calls that don't delete or write pay nothing extra. The refusal uses `pytest.fail` rather than `AssertionError`: `gui_uninstall._remove_path` catches `Exception`, so an assertion would have been logged as a warning and the test would have passed.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_real_home_tripwire.py`: one invariant test. Reading is allowed; `rmtree`, `unlink`, replace, an in-place write, and an `rmtree` through a symlinked parent are all refused.

**Validation**

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| #122553's destructive test, run on a Mac with `/Applications/Hermes.app` installed | app deleted, test passes | test fails with `TEST BUG: changing the REAL installed Hermes desktop app: /Applications/Hermes.app`; app intact (`codesign --verify --deep` OK) |

- Local run of `test_real_home_tripwire.py`, `test_linux_desktop_entry.py`, `test_gui_uninstall.py` and `test_desktop_install_after_update.py`: 100 passed, 2 skipped. The only failure in that run was #122553's planted destructive test, which is the intended result.
- Review: I applied the in-place write and resolved-path findings. I kept `refuse()` for home-root I/O as it was, since changing it is out of scope.

items.body:
Rebuilding Hermes Desktop no longer mangles output paths containing an apostrophe (`C:\Users\r'y'z` → `C:\Users\ryz`, EPERM), and no longer needs the `cross-env` bin to be installed.

Fixes #103010. Also fixes #110121.

Root cause: the desktop `builder` npm script was `cross-env NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=16384 node scripts/run-electron-builder.mjs`. `cross-env@10.1.0` strips every bare `'` from the arguments it forwards, on every platform. The rebuild passes its staging directory as `-c.directories.output=<path>`, so a profile path containing `'` reached electron-builder without it. The same prefix is also why a rebuild failed whenever the cross-env bin was missing (#110121).

## Changes
- `apps/desktop/package.json`: `builder` is now plain `node scripts/run-electron-builder.mjs`. `cross-env` is still a devDependency for the `dev:*` scripts.
- `apps/desktop/scripts/run-electron-builder.mjs`: the wrapper already spawns every child itself (native-deps staging, packaging-tool preparation, the strict builder, electron-builder). It now sets the heap flag on those children:
  - The flag is appended to any inherited `NODE_OPTIONS` without re-tokenizing it, so quoted preload paths survive.
  - It goes last, so 16384 still takes effect even when a smaller heap is inherited, as it did under cross-env.
- Behaviour differences from cross-env:
  - An inherited `NODE_OPTIONS` (for example a `--require` hook) now reaches the build children; cross-env used to replace it.
  - The release path (`scripts/bundles/desktop.py` → `run-electron-builder.mjs --prepared`) never went through cross-env. It now also gets the 16384 heap on electron-builder.

## Validation
| Check | Before (origin/main) | After |
|---|---|---|
| `npm run builder -- --dir --publish never "-c.directories.output=/Users/r'y'z/…"`, argv as received | `/Users/ryz/…` | `/Users/r'y'z/…`, verbatim through npm → wrapper → strict builder child |
| Heap on each child, with inherited `NODE_OPTIONS="--import=<probe> --max-old-space-size=4096"` | 16384 (inherited value dropped) | `--max-old-space-size=4096 --max-old-space-size=16384`, V8 `heap_size_limit` = 16480 MB; inherited preload kept |
| `vitest --project electron scripts/` | 6 failures (macOS-host environment) | the same failures, plus 2 new tests passing; neither new test passes on origin/main |

## Credit
- The approach and first commit come from @teknium1's #110142, cherry-picked to keep authorship and re-applied onto the prepared-packaging wrapper that has since landed on main.
- @liuhao1024 first fixed #103010 in #103035 (bypassing `npm run` from Python).
- @Ryfferty traced the stripping to cross-env and confirmed the fix end-to-end on the affected Windows machine.

items.body:
## What

Adds Claude Sonnet 5.5 (`claude-sonnet-5-5`), which Anthropic released on 2026-09-28, and fixes the one request shape that breaks on it.

**WHO / WHEN / WHY:** Anthropic launched Sonnet 5.5 on 2026-09-28 ([announcement](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-sonnet-5-5), [model page](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/sonnet-5-5/overview), [migration guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/sonnet-5-5/migration-guide)). As of this PR no open PR or issue covered it. It is already live on OpenRouter and on Nous Portal as `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`.

## Changes

| Surface | Change |
|---|---|
| `hermes_cli/models_catalog_static.py` | `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` added to `OPENROUTER_MODELS`; the `nous` list derives from it. `claude-sonnet-5-5` added to native `anthropic`, and `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5` to `bedrock`. The Bedrock default at `[0]` is unchanged. |
| `website/static/api/model-catalog.json` | Regenerated with `scripts/build_model_catalog.py` |
| `agent/usage_pricing.py` | Sonnet 5 and 5.5 share one native Anthropic row: $2 / $10, cache read $0.20, 5m cache write $2.50 (the migration guide says "the same prices as Claude Sonnet 5"). Main's Sonnet 5 comment said the $2/$10 intro price reverts to $3/$15 after 2026-08-31; Anthropic's [pricing page](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing) still lists $2/$10, so that stale instruction is removed. |
| `agent/anthropic_adapter.py` | Reasoning-off requests now send `thinking: {"type": "between_tools"}` to Sonnet 5.5 on anthropic.com. See below. |

These already resolve correctly through the existing `claude-sonnet-5` prefix entries, so they needed no change: 1M context (native + Bedrock), 128K max output, the adaptive-thinking / xhigh / no-sampling-params gates, and the 180s reasoning stale-timeout floor.

## Thinking-off breaking change

On Sonnet 5.5, `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` returns HTTP 400. The lowest setting is now `between_tools`, which turns off up-front thinking. It takes no other thinking field and returns 400 at `xhigh`/`max` effort. The disable path therefore sends it with no other fields and no `output_config`, so the API default effort of `high` applies.

Without this change, every path that turns reasoning off would 400 on native Anthropic: title generation, the compression fast lane, and `/reasoning none`. Opus 5.5 hit the same class of bug in #120069.

Relays behave differently. Live probe of Nous Portal `/v1/messages` with `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` on 2026-09-28:

| `thinking` sent | Portal response |
|---|---|
| omitted | 200 |
| `adaptive` | 200 |
| `disabled` | 400 "Reasoning is mandatory for this endpoint and cannot be disabled." |
| `between_tools` | 400 "Invalid Anthropic Messages API request" |

So on endpoints outside anthropic.com, the Sonnet 5.5 family keeps the mandatory-thinking omission. That includes Bedrock via the AnthropicBedrock SDK, which passes the `bedrock-runtime` URL, and Azure; neither was verified for `between_tools`. Omitting the field never 400s; the cost is that thinking stays on. `_accepts_thinking_disable` now returns False for this family, and `base_url` is keyword-only on `_thinking_kwargs`, so no caller gets the native shape by default.

## Verification

- `tests/agent/test_anthropic_thinking_disable.py`: Sonnet 5.5 gets `between_tools` (bare, even when xhigh is requested) on `None` / api.anthropic.com, and the omission on Portal and Bedrock; `claude-sonnet-5` still gets `disabled`. Mutation check: removing the third-party guard fails exactly the Portal and Bedrock rows.
- `tests/agent/test_usage_pricing.py`: Sonnet 5.5 rates equal Sonnet 5 rates (relationship test, not a snapshot).
- Targeted suite (75 files: every `tests/agent/test_anthropic*`, transports, model-switch, catalog, pricing, metadata, bedrock, auxiliary): 1393 passed, 42 failed. All 42 failures are identical by name on `origin/main` (re-run on the merge-base). After the follow-up commit, the touched files pass 434/434. Ruff is clean.
- Live, through Portal `/v1/messages` with this adapter's real kwargs: reasoning off → 200; high → 200 (adaptive + summarized); xhigh with a tool → 200 with `tool_use`. Also live through Portal `chat_completions` via `AIAgent` with reasoning off: returned `TEST-OK anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`.
- **Not live-tested on native anthropic.com** (no Anthropic key available). The `between_tools` shape there comes from the vendor's migration guide.

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- **Forced `tool_choice`** (`any`/`tool`) also returns 400 on Sonnet 5.5, as on Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1. No in-tree caller forces tool choice on the Anthropic path; auxiliary pass-through is the only route. #123690 adds the generic guard; Sonnet 5.5 belongs in its `_NO_FORCED_TOOL_CHOICE_CLAUDE_SUBSTRINGS`, but not in the mandatory-thinking set, since it accepts `between_tools`. I've commented there.
- Bedrock pricing is not added: AWS has not published a Sonnet 5.5 SKU rate that I could verify, so cost shows unknown there instead of a guessed number.
- OpenRouter's chat-completions path sends `reasoning: {enabled: false}` for reasoning-off. Whether OpenRouter maps that to Anthropic's `disabled` (which would 400) is unverified; there's no OpenRouter key here. Portal on chat-completions was verified: reasoning off returns 200.
- #121016 (Opus 5.5 → mandatory set) touches the adjacent tuple in `anthropic_adapter.py`. It composes with this PR (Opus 5.5 has no `between_tools`), and whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase.

items.body:
Every Hermes surface now asks the shared-metrics question once per profile, with the same three answers, and a "no" finally sticks.

## Changes

- **`hermes setup`**: the offer runs at the end of every flow (Quick, Full, Blank Slate, Portal, `--quick`), from `_record_setup_completed`, which all of them already call.
- **`hermes` / `hermes --tui`**: one offer before an interactive chat on a profile with no answer. It is skipped for `-q`/`--oneshot`, piped or JSON output, spawned actions (`HERMES_NONINTERACTIVE`), Desktop-hosted panes, safe mode and managed installs.
- **Web dashboard**: a banner for the profile being managed, backed by a new `GET/PUT /api/shared-metrics/consent` router (profile-scoped, writes under `config_write_scope`). The dashboard's Chat tab spawns the TUI directly, so the banner is that surface's offer.
- **Desktop**: unchanged. Its composer strip already existed and now reads the same `decided` definition.
- **Answer persistence fix**: `save_consent()` writes both keys straight into config.yaml. A CLI "no" equals the shipped defaults, so `save_config` used to strip it and every surface kept asking, the Desktop strip included. `decided` now has one definition (`consent_state`), shared by the RPC, the CLI and the router.
- **Docs**: `relay-shared-metrics.md` gets a per-surface table and the default/Esc semantics.

"No thanks" is the terminal default, so Enter never opts anyone in. Esc in the terminal and the ✕ on the banner leave the question open.

## Validation

| Check | origin/main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `hermes setup telemetry` → "No", then the wizard's `save_config` | `telemetry.shared_metrics` absent from config.yaml (undecided, asked again) | `{enabled: false, send: false}` (decided) |
| `hermes chat` on an undecided profile (tmux PTY) | no offer | offer shown; ↑ + Enter writes `enabled: true, send: false` |
| same, Esc | n/a | chat opens, nothing written |
| same, Enter | n/a | `enabled: false, send: false` written |
| `hermes --tui` | no offer | offer before Ink starts; "Send to Nous" writes `true/true` |
| `hermes setup --quick` (existing install) | no offer | offer after the summary; Enter writes `false/false` |
| Dashboard (Playwright, real `hermes dashboard`) | no banner | banner shown; "Local only" click → `true/false` in config.yaml, banner gone after reload |

Tests: 2 new invariants in `tests/hermes_cli/test_setup_telemetry.py`. The persistence one is red on `origin/main`. Shared-metrics / setup / RPC suites: 61 passed. Web vitest: 356 passed, `tsc -b` clean.

Terminal offer as captured:

```
Help improve Hermes?
Shared metrics are bounded counters: activity, outcomes, error classes, model routes,
token totals, feature use and coarse machine facts. Never prompts, files, paths,
setting values or error text. Collection stays on this machine; sending to Nous is
a separate choice, and data from before you opt in is never sent.
Details: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/relay-shared-metrics
Change it any time: hermes setup telemetry
  ↑↓ navigate  ENTER/SPACE select  ESC cancel
   (○) Collect and send to Nous
   (○) Collect locally only
 → (●) No thanks
```

The messaging gateway is not a surface for this question: chat participants are not necessarily the install owner.

## Infographic

![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aac47a2/U3IcVxBY8OghTNZ8w9bxU_tKL3uwJz.png)

items.body:
A Bot Chat DM that was already handed to a live teammate no longer reads as "not delivered" when its background delivery runner cannot boot — the sender gets the same "ambiguous, do not resend" outcome (same delivery id) instead of a repair hint that invites a duplicate.

Lands #123070 as well: its two commits (@jervaise, @OutThisLife) are the first two here with authorship intact, since #123070's CI could not start on its current head. Based on the failure-contract case @Neomail2 reported and prototyped on #123070 (their commit is cherry-picked here with authorship preserved), narrowed to the one case where the outcome is actually unknown.

## Changes

- **Live-admitted DM stays ambiguous on a boot failure.** When `_start_delivery` has already pinned `<dm>.live.json` and told the model "Durably queued… Do NOT resend", a runner whose `hermes_bootstrap` import fails now prints the existing ambiguous payload (shared with `_run_delivery` via `_live_outcome_unknown`). Without an intent nothing was handed over, so the plain `run \`hermes pm repair\`` failure stays and a resend remains correct.
- **Only `--run-delivery` boots.** Malformed argv exits 2 before any Hermes import; the stdlib reply waiter stays off bootstrap as in #123070.
- **A Windows relaunch never adds a second outcome.** `hermes_bootstrap` relaunches onto the store interpreter with `subprocess.call` on Windows and exits with the child's status; the child (the same runner) already printed its result. The relaunch now raises `RelaunchExit` (a `SystemExit` subclass — exit code and every existing handler unchanged) and the runner skips its report for it.
- One stdlib-only argv splitter (`_runner_argv`) serves `_delivery_main` and the boot-failure report; one helper names the intent file (4 hand-written joins before).

## Validation

| Case (store CPython 3.14.7, `-I`, no PYTHONPATH) | #123070 head | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| healthy delivery | delivered, exit 0 | delivered, exit 0 |
| boot failure, no live intent | repair hint, exit 1 | repair hint, exit 1, stdout empty |
| boot failure, live intent pinned | repair hint only (reads as "NOT delivered") | ambiguous JSON, same delivery id, "Do not resend" |
| relaunched child already printed its outcome | — | child's line only, no second JSON |
| malformed argv | bootstrap runs first | exit 2, no bootstrap |

- `scripts/run_tests.sh` on the bot suites: 136 passed, 0 failed. `tests/pm/` + bootstrap-consuming `tests/hermes_cli/` files: the same 42 macOS-local failures with and without the `hermes_bootstrap.py` change.
- The new test fails on #123070's head; dropping the intent-file condition turns the existing no-intent test red.
- The Windows relaunch branch is covered by code reading and a simulated relaunch on macOS, not a real Windows run.

items.body:
## Root cause

`_notif_claim_turn` gated only on `running`, so a background-completion,
async-delegation, or kanban event arriving on an idle session whose
`_turn_cancel_requested` latch is set (set by **Stop** in
`tui_gateway/session_lifecycle.py`) claimed the session and started a new
model turn the user had just cancelled. The goal-continuation path in
`prompt_turn.py::_run_post_turn_followups` had the same gap. `session_auto_continue.py`
already refuses while the latch is set — the notification pollers were the asymmetry.

## What changes

- `_notif_claim_turn` also refuses when `_turn_cancel_requested` is set; callers
  keep their existing refuse handling (events requeued, kanban buffered), so the
  completion stays queued and is delivered after the user's next prompt clears the latch.
- `_run_post_turn_followups` holds a `/goal` continuation under the same latch.
- Bot-live delivery (`_poll_bot_live_delivery_once`) is deliberately **exempt**: a
  delivery is a person's message, not an automatic turn, and only a local prompt
  clears the latch — gating it would park the sender until the next prompt. Commented in code.

## Tests

- `test_notification_poller_starts_no_turn_after_stop` — completion arriving on a
  stopped idle session starts no turn and is requeued. Red on `origin/main`, green with the fix.
- `test_goal_continuation_starts_no_turn_after_stop` — goal continuation held after Stop.
- Sibling suites (notification turn release, heartbeat tick, kanban poller, loop
  command/loop noise, heartbeat wakes): 41 passed.

Fixes #124347

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/124356 (rebased onto current main;
cherry-picked verbatim, authorship kept). Thanks @zanzipanzi!

Co-authored-by: Herman Bohdanov <zanzipanzi@gmail.com>

items.body:
Desktop cron takes over again once a gateway that was live at backend start goes away, without racing a live gateway on any path.

## Root cause
29ca3f2770 (#122943, the #52202 stand-down) added a one-shot early return to `_start_desktop_cron_ticker`: if `_check_gateway_running(HERMES_HOME)` was true when the Desktop backend started, the function returned and started no ticker. It runs once, on the `desktop-cron-ticker` thread from the backend lifespan, so when that gateway later stopped or crashed nothing ticked cron for any profile until Desktop restarted (#126822). The multiplex path already had a per-tick `profile_gate`; the early return made it unreachable.

## Fix (`hermes_cli/web_server.py`)
- One ownership predicate `_gateway_owns_cron(name, home)`: the profile's own gateway is running, or a named profile is served by the live default multiplexer.
- Multiplex path: startup probe removed; the per-tick `profile_gate` stands down while a gateway owns a store and resumes when it stops.
- Built-in fail-open path (enumeration failure / empty served set): ticks this backend's own store through the same multiplex loop behind the same `profile_gate`. It was the reason for #52202's stand-down, and it is now gated every tick instead of never started. A gated-out store is not ticked or heartbeated, so Desktop never marks the gateway's store healthy or clears its tick error.
- External provider: it can't be gated per tick, so its `start()` is deferred. It re-probes once per interval, honours `stop_event`, and starts after the gateway is gone.
- #52202 still holds: no path ticks while a live gateway owns the store.

## Acceptance coverage
| Requirement | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Gateway live at start, dies later → Desktop ticks | `test_gated_ticker_resumes_after_the_gateway_stops`, `test_fail_open_ticker_uses_the_same_profile_gate`, `test_external_provider_starts_once_the_gateway_is_gone`; live repro below |
| Never double-fire with a live gateway (#52202) | same tests assert gate is False while live and again when a gateway returns; `test_gated_out_fail_open_tick_leaves_the_gateway_store_status_alone` (real built-in loop) |
| Satellite served by the multiplexer | `test_fail_open_ticker_yields_to_the_multiplexer_serving_this_profile` |
| Shutdown never hangs in the wait | `test_external_provider_waits_while_gateway_owns_cron` |

## Checks (run from the worktree, base `b9df1cccaec26a910e5f0d1d77f52a71641e3d98`)
- RED on base: new tests against base `web_server.py` → **5 failed** (4 in `test_desktop_cron_ticker_gateway_standdown.py`, 1 in `test_desktop_cron_ticker_profiles.py`).
- GREEN: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_desktop_cron_ticker_gateway_standdown.py tests/hermes_cli/test_desktop_cron_ticker_profiles.py tests/cron/test_cron_multiplex_desktop_ticker_scope.py tests/cron/test_scheduler_provider.py tests/plugins/test_chronos_cron.py` → **65 passed, 0 failed**.
- Live repro: real `_start_desktop_cron_ticker` and real `InProcessCronScheduler` over a temp `HERMES_HOME`, with only the gateway probe and the tick body stubbed. Interval 0.05s; gateway live 1s → dead 1s → live 1s. Ticks per phase:
  | path | base | this PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | multiplex | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 20 / 0 |
  | fail-open | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 20 / 0 |
- `ruff check` clean; `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py` clean.

## Out of scope (known gaps)
- Once an external provider has started, nothing gates it. The Chronos identity-rejection fallback's ungated built-in ticker is tracked separately in #126907 and needs a provider-contract change.
- The default gateway's `served_profiles` can lag behind newly created profiles. That behaviour is already on main and not changed here.

## Supersedes
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/125541 by @AhmetArif0: the gated-path restructure and the stand-down regression test (commit cherry-picked, authorship kept).
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/126872 by @liuhao1024: the re-probing wait, used here for external providers (`Co-authored-by` on the fail-open commit).
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/126903 by @unsupportedpastels: the per-tick gating of every fail-open path and the shared ownership predicate (both commits cherry-picked with `-x`, authorship kept). This PR carries #126903's head as-is, rebased on current main.

Fixes #126822

## Auto-merge
Backend-only cron-ticker gating in `hermes_cli/web_server.py` plus tests. It changes no install/update/launch path, no Desktop UI and no platform code. Rebase auto-merge is armed on reviewed head `709cc4083645d579d4d6fe219f9678ca19fff755`.

items.body:
Desktop finds a healthy Hermes install outside `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` through the `hermes` launcher that install published, and no longer drops to the first-run setup choice. The launcher is looked up at its fixed location, so it doesn't matter that a Finder/Dock launch leaves `~/.local/bin` off PATH.

## Root cause
- The original report: the old "existing `hermes` on PATH" rung searched only `process.env.PATH`. A GUI-launched app gets launchd's short PATH, which has no `~/.local/bin`, so the lookup came back empty and nothing was logged.
- On current main it's worse. The PM rework (3d12e86ef1) removed that rung entirely. `resolveHermesBackend()` now accepts only `HERMES_DESKTOP_HERMES` or `$HERMES_HOME/hermes-agent`. Any other install (`install.sh --dir`, a `setup-hermes.sh` clone) ends at `bootstrap-needed`, and Desktop offers to install a second copy. @rafpigna confirmed this on Linux in [the issue](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/73014) after the 2026-09-28 update.

## Change
- New rung 5, after `ACTIVE_HERMES_ROOT` and before `bootstrap-needed`: `userLauncherInstallRoot()` looks for the published launcher in its user-bin directory (`~/.local/bin` and `$HERMES_HOME/bin` on POSIX; the Windows Hermes home `bin` on Windows) and runs `--version` to read the `Install directory:` it reports. That root must be a Hermes source tree. It is then resolved through `resolveSourceInstallationBackend`, the same validated path the canonical install uses: exact launcher identity check, then a `--version` probe.
- `HERMES_DESKTOP_IGNORE_EXISTING=1` and bootstrap repair requests skip the new rung. A miss is now logged instead of passing silently.
- `resolveInstallationLauncher` and the new rung share the user-bin launcher list and the `--version` install-directory probe (`launcherInstallDirectory`). PATH is still never trusted as installation identity.

## Acceptance coverage
- `electron/user-launcher-install.test.ts` (new):
  - POSIX: `HOME` has a `~/.local/bin/hermes` launcher that reports a clone at `~/src/hermes-agent`, and `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`. The rung finds the root, and `resolveSourceInstallationBackend` returns a command backend for that launcher.
  - Cross-platform: a launcher that reports a directory that isn't a Hermes source tree is ignored.
- Red on base b9df1cccae: `TypeError: userLauncherInstallRoot is not a function` (2 failed). Green with the fix.

## Checks run (macOS, `apps/desktop`)
- `npx vitest run electron/user-launcher-install.test.ts electron/update-prerequisites.test.ts electron/backend-resolution.test.ts electron/first-run-setup-gate.test.ts electron/first-run-setup-main-process.test.ts`: 19 passed, 1 skipped.
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json --noEmit`: clean. `npx eslint` on the touched files: clean.
- `npx vitest run --project electron`: 2985 passed, 17 failed. All 17 fail the same way on base b9df1cccae with this diff removed. They are local-environment tests (a PM fixture needs Python 3.14, mac signing/native toolchains, i18n keys), not caused by this diff.
- Not run here: the Windows `.cmd`/`.exe` launcher path and a real Finder launch of a packaged build.

## Supersedes
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/73118 by @JonthanaHanh. It extended `findOnPath('hermes')` with `~/.local/bin` and logged the miss, but the rung it patched no longer exists on main. This PR carries its two ideas into the current resolver: find the launcher at `~/.local/bin` without depending on PATH, and log a failed discovery. Credited as co-author. Its `buildDesktopBackendPath` change isn't needed, because the backend is launched by absolute launcher path.

Fixes #73014

## Auto-merge
Not armed. This changes how Desktop resolves the local runtime at boot (a system-level, install/launch happy-path change, labelled `area/install-update`), so it needs human review. Reviewed head: cd72951e2ef6e366efaa9320753520620ece2ca8.

items.body:
Restores the #107692 fix: a secondary profile's routed cron fire no longer writes that profile's `.env` into the shared `os.environ`. The removed series goes back onto current `main` with its original authors kept, and the administrator-managed `.env` goes back into every profile secret scope.

This is the maintainer replacement for #126496. It carries @jonpol01's cherry-picks with authorship preserved, rebased onto current `main`.

## Root cause

#111187 landed the fix on 2026-09-15 (`cedf4a3d78`). A few hours later `23036e20a6` ("fix(ux): plain-language, actionable user-facing messages (core)", 234 files) deleted every piece of it along with its tests. The commit message doesn't mention the removal. `git show 23036e20a6` shows these definitions deleted: `set_multiplex_context`, `reset_multiplex_context`, `refresh_installed_secret_scope`, `_install_fire_secret_scope`, `_reset_fire_secret_scope`, `routed_profile_fire`, `source_supplied_names`, `launch_dotenv_keys` and `managed_dotenv_keys`. None of these names exist on `main` at `b9df1cccae`.

The desktop/dashboard backend and a standalone gateway (one that came up after the multiplex preflight refused) both tick every profile's cron in-process while the process-wide multiplex flag is off. Every isolation that keys on `is_multiplex_active()` therefore does nothing for a sibling profile's fire:

- the routed-dotenv guard
- `get_secret`'s fail-closed miss
- the subprocess scrub
- the launch-residue strip

So that profile's `.env` stays in `os.environ`, and the launch profile's later turns and child processes read it. Separately, `build_profile_secret_scope` lost the managed `.env` layer. Under multiplex semantics that means a managed-only credential is missing and a user's own value beats the managed one.

## What changes

- `agent/secret_scope.py`: adds `set_multiplex_context`, a context-local flag OR'd into `is_multiplex_active()`. Adds `refresh_installed_secret_scope`, and puts the managed `.env` back as the last layer in `build_profile_secret_scope`.
- `cron/scheduler_provider.py`: `_profile_cron_scope` marks a fire whose home is not the pinned launch home (`routed_profile_fire`).
- `cron/scheduler.py`: `_install_fire_secret_scope` / `_reset_fire_secret_scope` hydrate the profile's secret sources, then install the scope. For a routed fire they also install the multiplex context, for exactly that span. The external-worker handoff treats a routed fire as multiplexed.
- `hermes_cli/env_loader.py`: bookkeeping for loaded, managed and source-supplied key names.
- `hermes_cli/plugins.py`: after plugin discovery, secret sources are folded into the installed scope, and a removed plugin source is reconciled.
- `tools/environments/local.py`:
  - `strip_launch_profile_env` strips a wider set of launch residue and leaves managed keys alone;
  - adds `restore_managed_env`;
  - `build_subprocess_env(strip_launch_profile=True)` overlays the routed scope and then the managed keys before the scrub, only under multiplex semantics.
- Tests: the invariant set that `23036e20a6` deleted is back in `tests/cron/test_cron_multiplex_desktop_ticker_scope.py`, `tests/cron/test_cron_no_agent.py` and `tests/cron/test_restart_safe_worker.py`.

Rebase delta vs #126496: `main` changed `load_hermes_dotenv` for #125530 (launch-home loads still apply under multiplex). The conflict was comment-only and resolved by keeping `main`'s comment and guard and appending the restored note about the routed-fire context. The guard behaves as intended: inside a routed fire, both the target and the override resolve to the routed home, which is not the launch home, so the load is still skipped.

## Verification (cwd = worktree at the stated SHA, `scripts/run_tests.sh`)

- **Base `b9df1cccae` + restored tests only:** the 6 restored cases fail. These are `test_a_routed_profile_fire_runs_under_multiplex_semantics_for_exactly_its_scope`, `test_routed_fire_scope_carries_managed_env_authority[managed-only|managed-beats-user]`, `test_a_routed_profile_script_never_receives_a_launch_only_name`, `test_a_routed_profile_script_keeps_administrator_managed_values_over_its_own` and `test_launch_external_worker_treats_a_routed_fire_as_multiplexed`.
- **This branch, 42 related files** (secret scope, env loader, secret sources, subprocess-env guard, cron multiplex, `test_scheduler.py`, subprocess env, passthrough, local env, spawn-site child env, terminal scope, managed scope, plugins): 572 passed, 0 failed, 30 skipped.
- **Broader run, 205 files** (all of `tests/cron`, gateway multiplex/secret, `hermes_cli` secret/served, tools passthrough/MCP scope): 1920 passed, 0 failed, 12 skipped.
- `ruff check` on the changed files is clean.
- One follow-up commit (mine) changes the two restored script tests' shebang from `#!/bin/bash` to `#!/usr/bin/env bash`, as the "Windows footguns" lint requires.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/126496: @jonpol01's fix-forward. All 16 commits are carried with authorship preserved, rebased onto current `main`, with the `env_loader.py` conflict resolved.
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/109703: @kansha5845121-afk's earlier fix for the same leak, which snapshots and restores `os.environ` around a foreign tick. It isn't taken because a process-global snapshot/restore races with concurrent turns and still exposes the values during the fire. The invariant it pins (the parent `os.environ` is unchanged after a foreign fire) is covered by `test_a_routed_profile_fire_runs_under_multiplex_semantics_for_exactly_its_scope`.

items.body:
Stops a busy backend from looking dead to the desktop. `gateway.ping` now gets an answer even while an earlier RPC is stuck in `dispatch()`.

## Root cause

`tui_gateway/ws.py::handle_ws` read one frame, awaited `asyncio.to_thread(server.dispatch, …)` for it, and only then read the next frame. Every inline handler (anything not in `_LONG_HANDLERS`) therefore held up the socket reader until it returned. When a handler got stuck behind a long preflight compaction (lock wait, GIL pressure, slow state.db), the client's `gateway.ping` frames sat unread. The desktop's 45s "no inbound frame" deadline (`apps/shared` `JsonRpcRequestChannel`, `heartbeatLiveness: 'any-inbound'`) then fired. It dropped the socket and the desktop restarted the backend, which killed the in-flight turn.

Earlier fixes treated this class one handler at a time: #50005 moved polled RPCs into `_LONG_HANDLERS`, and `_compress_session_history` snapshots outside `history_lock` "otherwise prompt.submit etc. block on the dispatcher loop". This PR closes the class for the heartbeat itself.

## Fix

- Non-ping frames go onto a bounded per-connection queue (256). A dispatcher task drains it through the same `server.dispatch` path, **one at a time, in arrival order**, so RPC ordering does not change.
- The reader answers `gateway.ping` directly. Its reply no longer waits on handler latency.
- A reply the dispatcher cannot send still ends the connection. The reader watches the dispatcher task.
- Disconnect teardown works as before: the in-flight handler and any frames read before the disconnect finish before `_close_sessions_for_transport` parks the transport's sessions. A cancelled connection (server shutdown) cancels the dispatcher right away, as the old cancelled await did.
- If the queue fills, the reader waits, which is the old serial behaviour.

No client, contract or UI change.

## Verification (pinned base `b9df1cccae`)

- New regression test `test_ws_ping_is_answered_while_an_earlier_rpc_blocks_dispatch`: **fails on base** (`gateway.ping went unanswered while dispatch was busy; sent ids=[]`) and passes with the fix.
- Guards: `test_ws_disconnect_teardown_waits_for_in_flight_dispatch` and `test_ws_failed_reply_from_dispatcher_ends_the_connection`.
- Real Starlette WebSocket probe (TestClient; one RPC blocked in `dispatch()` for 3s, then a ping):
  - base: `first reply id=r1 after 3.01s`, ping answered only afterwards
  - fix: `first reply id=heartbeat-1 after 0.00s`, then `r1`
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/`: 2218 passed, 6 failed. The 6 (`test_profiles_list_{ui_meta_cache,session_field_cache,canonical_session}`) fail identically with base `ws.py`, so this diff does not cause them.
- `uvx ruff check` clean; `check-windows-footguns --diff origin/main` clean.

## Scope

Fixes every heartbeat drop caused by a busy backend: long compaction (this report), silent long turns (maholler1's comment), and Bot Chat registry checks timing out behind a stuck handler (Apfelkringel's comment). Not covered: a genuinely slow network link (Ajar9715, a client-side deadline knob) and renderer timer throttling while the window is hidden (#123125, a separate client-side cause).

Trade-off: if a handler deadlocks, the socket now stays connected and requests time out on their own 30–45s deadlines. Before, the heartbeat dropped the socket and the desktop restarted the backend. The turn-liveness watchdog still covers wedged turns.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/108427 by @Sahilvishnaliya. It lowered the compaction activity status interval from 60s to 15s so status frames would refresh the any-inbound deadline. That only helps when the compaction status emitter is the thing writing. It also shows the compaction status line 4× as often and leaves every other stuck handler exposed. Credit for pinpointing the 60s-vs-45s gap during compaction; its code is not incorporated because the ping path no longer depends on turn output.

Fixes #108325

Auto-merge: backend-only transport change in `tui_gateway/ws.py` plus tests, with no UI, install, or platform surface. Reviewed head `64bdacb680f0fe7480b3752a9dd95f926c492d61`.

## Root cause

`_handle_session_messages` (`GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages` on the gateway API server) parsed `limit`, `offset` and `order` but never read `include_compacted`. It called `SessionDB.get_messages` with the default `include_compacted=False`, so REST clients only ever got the live transcript left after compaction. The dashboard router already accepts the flag (`hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py`). This change gives the gateway endpoint the same parameter.

## Behavior

- `include_compacted=true|1|yes|on` returns the display history, which adds the rows a context compaction archived. Rewind and undo rows are still left out, matching `SessionDB`'s display semantics.
- If the parameter is missing, false-ish or unrecognised, the endpoint returns the live transcript as before. Parsing goes through the existing `_coerce_request_bool` helper.
- The endpoint row in the API server docs now lists the parameter.

The hunk is kept small on purpose. #59661 edits the same `get_messages` call to add `include_ancestors`, which is a different feature and is not included here.

## Acceptance coverage

`tests/gateway/test_api_server_compaction_projection.py::test_messages_endpoint_honours_include_compacted` uses a real `SessionDB` in a temp `HERMES_HOME`. It runs a real `archive_and_compact` and makes real aiohttp requests to check that:
- the default response, `include_compacted=false` and `include_compacted=0` all return the same live transcript, with no archived turns;
- `include_compacted=true` returns every archived and carried turn exactly once, in chronological order.

items.body:
## Root cause

Every Desktop `SshConnection` for one scope, host and identity hashes to the same `ControlPath` (`controlSocketPath`). With `ControlMaster=auto`, a new attempt attaches to whatever master is already listening on that socket. `SshConnection.close()` then ran `ssh -O exit` unconditionally, which shuts the master down for every attached connection. When a stale bootstrap attempt closed late (timed out, superseded, or rolled back through `bootstrapSshConnectionInner`'s failure path, `rollbackSshBootstrapResult`, force cleanup, or `teardownSshConnection`), it killed the master its successor was using. The live backend's forward went down after "Remote Hermes backend is ready", which is the post-success "control master closed" in #97264.

## Fix

The rule lives in `SshConnection`, so every caller that closes a shared master is covered, not just the one call site:

- New `ssh-control-master-holders.ts`: a small holder registry, one per process, keyed by `ControlPath`, plus a pure decision function `controlMasterCloseAction(otherHolders)`.
- `open()` (mux only) claims the socket **before** dialing. A stale close that lands while a successor is still attaching sees that claim. A failed `open()` releases its claim.
- `close()` releases its claim. It runs `-O exit` and the socket-unlink fallback only when no other connection still holds the socket. Otherwise it logs `control master left running: N other connection(s) still use it` and marks itself closed.
- The registry can be injected (`opts.controlMasterHolders`) so tests stay isolated.
- No-mux (Windows) is unchanged. `_evictStaleMaster` is unchanged: it only runs after the current opener has shown with a real exec that the master is wedged.

## Scope: half of #97264

This PR covers only the half where a failed or stale attempt's close tears down the shared master. It does **not** change the hardcoded 45s ready timeout (`remote-lifecycle.ts` `DEFAULT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS`). That half is tracked in #94642, and open PR #94665 covers it. That is why this PR says `Refs #97264` and not `Fixes`.

Related but not included, because the root cause differs:
- #126006: mid-session tunnel drop leaves `backend.lock.json` pointing at a dead serve. It was reported on a Windows client, which runs mux-less, so `-O exit` never happens there. The bug is in lock/orphan reconciliation.
- #126380: the update lock is held by a `serve` that has exited while its orphaned builds keep running. Update-lock ownership, not SSH transport.

The diagnosis that a superseded attempt kills its successor's master came from the closed #97392 by @ALDRIN121. That PR gated one call site on `lease.isCurrent()`. This PR moves the rule into the transport so every close path follows it.

## Validation (worktree at origin/main b9df1ccc + this commit)

- `cd apps/desktop && npm run typecheck`: exit 0.
- `npx vitest run --project electron electron/ssh-connection.test.ts electron/ssh-control-master-holders.test.ts`: 88/88 passed.
- `npx vitest run --project electron electron/ssh-*.test.ts electron/managed-ssh-update.test.ts electron/remote-lifecycle.test.ts`: 232 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `pidIsOurDashboard recognizes an installer wrapper…` in `remote-lifecycle.test.ts`, and it fails the same way with `ssh-connection.ts` at origin/main, so it predates this change.
- Behavioral probe: with `ssh-connection.ts` reverted to origin/main, the three new #97264 tests fail: stale close under a live successor, failed newer attempt under a live older connection, stale close while the successor is still dialing. With the fix, all pass.
- `eslint` and `prettier --check` are clean on the changed files.

Not reproduced against a real slow SSH host. The tests use a scripted `ssh` that models the shared master's state.

items.body:
## Root cause

Desktop's managed SSH update (`apps/desktop/electron/managed-ssh-update.ts`) runs `hermes update --yes` on the remote with `HERMES_UPDATE_CORRELATION_ID=<uuid>`, for both POSIX and Windows. Its coordinator's `receipt()` then scans `<HERMES_HOME>/logs/update_receipts/update_*.json` and skips any file whose `correlation_id` isn't that uuid. The backend never read the variable: `UpdateReceipt` wrote only its own `update_id` (`hermes_cli/update_receipt.py`). No receipt could ever match, so Desktop reported "Update failed" and restored every profile, even after a successful update.

## Change

- `UpdateReceipt.__init__` records `correlation_id` from `HERMES_UPDATE_CORRELATION_ID`, or `null` when the variable is unset.
- `update_id` still holds the CLI's own id. pm sync receipts and the handoff/finish paths key on it, and the receipt filename uses it, so none of those change.
- `begin_update_receipt(previous=...)` carries the field through the interpreter handoff. If the pre-swap receipt came from an older updater that doesn't write the field, the new process fills it from the env var.

Desktop reads only `correlation_id`, `outcome`, `finished_at`, `started_at`, `pre_update`/`post_update` `sha`/`version`, and `stop_reason`. The backend already writes everything on that list except `correlation_id`.

The second cause reported on the issue (the stale-module purge evicting the in-flight receipt, #101690) no longer applies on main. `_purge_stale_hermes_modules` now stops for relaunch and no longer touches `sys.modules`.

## Tests

`tests/hermes_cli/test_update_receipt.py::TestLauncherCorrelation` uses a temp `HERMES_HOME` and runs Desktop's `receipt()` predicate against the written files. It covers:

- a direct run
- the handoff, where the post-swap process doesn't inherit the env var
- a legacy pre-swap receipt
- an unset env var, which gives `null`

## Validation

- `unset PYTHONPATH; uvx ruff check hermes_cli/update_receipt.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_receipt.py`: All checks passed
- RED on `origin/main`'s `update_receipt.py`: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_update_receipt.py -k LauncherCorrelation` gives 4 failed. GREEN with the fix: 4 passed.
- `test_update_receipt.py` has 28 passed and 1 failed. The failure is `test_cmd_update_boundary_finalizes_on_early_exit`, a `home_io_guard` "REAL hermes home" error from the local test-environment path. It fails the same way on unmodified main.
- `test_update_receipt_{scope,truthfulness,pm_embed,endpoint}`, `test_update_finish`, `test_update_finish_stamp`, `test_update_completion_routing`: all pass.
- `test_update_completion_process`: 6 failures from the same `home_io_guard` error, the same 6 as on unmodified main.

Not exercised against a live SSH remote.

## Residual

The POSIX launch never writes `.update_coordinator_ready.<id>`, so Desktop's `ready()` is always null there. Desktop's success verdict needs only the receipt, so this PR doesn't touch it.

## Credit

The `os.environ.get("HERMES_UPDATE_CORRELATION_ID")` approach was suggested by @LordMelkor on the issue (the author of #101691).

Fixes #101516

items.body:
## Root cause
`hermes_cli/source_check._branch_tip` reads `git ls-remote --exit-code` exit 2 as "branch deleted". `_check_branch` then switches the target to `main`, and `_heal_deleted_branch` rewrites the Desktop branch config to `main`. Exit 2 only means the remote has no such ref, which is also true for a branch that was never pushed. So a local-only branch lost its pin, and the next update moved the checkout to `main`. The same thing happened to the checked-out branch when no Desktop pin was set.

## Behavior
When the remote does not advertise a non-main branch, the branch is re-pinned to `main` only if one of these holds:
- no local `refs/heads/<branch>` exists, so there is nothing to lose (this is the existing behavior for a stale config), or
- the branch was once published (`refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` or `branch.<b>.merge`, which survives `fetch --prune`) **and** `git cherry origin/main <branch>` (falling back to local `main`) shows no unmerged commits. Rebase-merged commits count as merged.

In every other case the pin stays. The status comes back as `error: "branch-local-only"` with `localOnly: true` and a message. Because it is an error, Desktop's apply path refuses instead of handing off `hermes update`. If the merge state can't be determined, the pin stays. Embedded (`HERMES_REVISION`) installs have no local refs and keep the old behavior.

## Tests (real temp git repos, bare remote, no mocks)
- `test_never_pushed_branch_keeps_its_pin[desktop|current]`: the pin and the Desktop config stay unchanged.
- `test_deleted_remote_branch_heals_only_when_its_commits_are_in_main[fast-forward|rebase|unmerged]`: the branch is pushed with `-u`, deleted upstream and pruned. Fast-forward and rebase merges heal to `main`; unmerged work keeps the pin.

## Validation
- `uvx ruff check hermes_cli/source_check.py tests/hermes_cli/test_source_check.py` → All checks passed
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_source_check.py` → 40 passed
- Before the fix (source reverted, new tests kept): 3 failed (`never_pushed[desktop]`, `never_pushed[current]`, `unmerged`), 2 passed (the heal cases)
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_parked_branch_guard.py`: 7 tests fail identically on clean `main` (home-io guard in this environment). This PR does not cause them.

## Residual
A branch that was squash-merged upstream has a different patch-id, so it keeps its pin and reports `branch-local-only` instead of healing. The user has to switch it by hand. That is the safe direction.

Based on the diagnosis in #105053 by @0xalydev and #105055 by @kokhlo. Both patched the Electron `resolveHealedBranch`, which has since moved into `hermes_cli/source_check.py`.

Fixes #105042
