items.body:
## Root cause

On Windows the desktop hard-codes `%SystemRoot%\System32\OpenSSH\ssh.exe` in three places: `effectiveSshConfigFingerprint`, the `hermes:ssh-config:resolve` IPC handler and the SSH terminal spawn in `terminal-ipc.ts`. Meanwhile `SshConnection` spawns a bare `ssh` from PATH. If the in-box OpenSSH is missing or broken (#103288: after component-store corruption, every native `ssh.exe` exits 255), there was no way to point the app at a working client. On top of that, the failing boot-time `ssh -G` probe was classified as a transient remote failure, so the renderer retried it every ~2s and the user never got to the UI.

## Change

- **`electron/ssh-binary.ts`**: new pure `resolveSshBinary({ platform, override, env, fs })`, which is now the only place the ssh binary is chosen:
  - **Windows order:** `desktop.ssh_path` (used verbatim) → System32 OpenSSH → Git for Windows `usr\bin\ssh.exe` → bare `ssh`.
  - **Git candidates** come from the existing `windowsGitCandidates` list that `resolveGitBinary` uses (Hermes PortableGit, UGit, Program Files, per-user install).
  - **Every other platform** gets bare `ssh`, with no filesystem probes.
- **Where the override lives:** in `desktop.ssh_path` in `config.yaml`, not in a new `HERMES_*` env var (AGENTS.md rule). The app reads it with the same pre-window reader that handles `desktop.electron_flags` (`readDesktopLaunchConfig`). That reader accepts plain, single-quoted and YAML double-quoted Windows paths. The key is registered in `DEFAULT_CONFIG` and documented in `desktop.md`.
- **Call sites:** the resolver is wired into all ssh spawns: the `-G` probe, `ssh-config:resolve`, SSH terminals (injected as `sshBinary` into `registerTerminalIpc`) and `SshConnection`. `SshConnection` gets a new `sshBinary` option that `runSsh` and the no-mux tunnel child use; it defaults to `'ssh'`.
- **Boot loop:** a failed `ssh -G` now throws a tagged `ssh-client-failed` error that names the binary (plus a `desktop.ssh_path` hint on Windows). `runHermesStart` latches it the same way it latches SSH auth / host-key failures and marks it non-retryable, so boot stops on the failure overlay instead of looping.

## Acceptance coverage

- Override → System32 → Git → bare ordering; non-Windows returns `ssh` without touching fs; custom SystemRoot; PortableGit preferred over system Git; UGit/LOCALAPPDATA candidate mapping (`ssh-binary.test.ts`, platform passed as data, fs injected).
- `desktop.ssh_path` parsing, including the YAML double-quote escapes (`renderer-heap-flags.test.ts`).
- `ssh -G` failure is tagged, latched and not auto-retried; ordinary remote faults still retry; the hint is Windows-only (`backend-start-failure.test.ts`).
- `SshConnection` spawns the injected binary for open + exec and bare `ssh` by default (`ssh-connection.test.ts`).

## Validation

```
npm ci                                  # worktree root: ok
cd apps/desktop && npm run typecheck    # exit 0
npx vitest run electron/ssh-binary.test.ts electron/backend-start-failure.test.ts \
  electron/renderer-heap-flags.test.ts electron/ssh-connection.test.ts
# Test Files 4 passed (4) / Tests 117 passed (117)
npx eslint <changed electron files>     # clean
uvx ruff check hermes_cli/config_defaults.py   # All checks passed!
```

Not reproduced on a real Windows host with broken OpenSSH (no Windows hardware here). That path is covered only by the injected-fs unit tests and needs Windows review.

## Behaviour notes / residual

- On Windows, `SshConnection` now spawns the same resolved absolute path as the `-G` probe (usually System32 OpenSSH) instead of whatever `ssh` comes first on PATH. The probe and the connection now use the same client. A user who relied on a different `ssh` being first on PATH should set `desktop.ssh_path`.
- `desktop.ssh_path` is read at launch, so changing it needs an app restart.
- The `ssh -G` latch applies on all platforms (it only fires for a local-client failure). A `-G` timeout, e.g. the stdin hang in #118983, now latches too instead of looping. #118983's root cause is separate and not addressed here.
- There's no Settings UI field for `ssh_path` yet; it's set through `config.yaml`.

Fixes #103288

The diagnosis builds on #103289 by @SZWzz (closed unmerged). This PR takes a different approach: an existence-ordered resolver plus a config key, instead of `ssh -V` health probes and an env var.

items.body:
## Root cause

The busy-queue is in-memory only, and the sole retire of the accept-time user row
(`_replace_queued_user_row_for_turn`'s `deactivate_message`) runs only in the drain path.
A backend restart discards the queue with nothing left to retire the accept-time row, so the
row stays active and the next cold resume's `repair_alternation` glues the never-run prompt
into the previous turn's user message.

## What changes

- `_write_submit_user_row` accepts `display_metadata`; the busy-queue accept stamps
  `display_metadata._queued_prompt` (`QUEUED_PROMPT_METADATA_KEY`) on the accept-time row.
- The drain's re-placement writes an unmarked replacement for the DISPATCHING envelope only;
  still-queued envelopes keep the marker, so still-marked after a restart == never drained.
- `reopen_session` deactivates still-marked rows on cold resume — the same retire the drain
  uses, deactivated never deleted, and `repair_alternation` is untouched (the projection
  cannot know whether a row ran; per the issue author's invariant comment).
- Rows that DID drain are unmarked and survive the reopen untouched.

## Sequencing with #123533

Both PRs retire via `deactivate_message` on different triggers (in-process discard vs cold
reopen). Verified combined: both branches merged together pass the full queued-prompt suite
(13 tests, no double-deactivate).

## Tests (all on `origin/main` vs with-fix)

- `test_restart_retires_the_never_drained_accept_row` — red on main, green with fix. Now
  also asserts the RAW row sequence — order/roles/active state — per the review thread, not
  just the count: `[user A active, user B inactive(marked), assistant A active]`.
- `test_resume_does_not_retire_drained_or_plain_rows` — green both (guard).
- `test_restart_between_drains_retires_only_the_later_prompt` — red on main, green with
  fix; two queued prompts, first drains, restart retires only the second.
- Sibling suites green: `test_queued_prompt_persistence.py` (7), reopen consumers
  `test_oneshot_resume.py` + `test_stranded_session_adoption.py` (31), combined with
  PR #123533's branch (13).

Fixes #125577

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/125595 (rebased onto current
main + the raw-sequence assertion from the review thread; authorship kept). Thanks @dskwe!

items.body:
Based on #120778 by @kvnloo. This reuses its idea of building the `-ot` selector from the recurrent block indices, and also sizes the selector to the spill.

## Root cause
`spill_overrides()` (context_policy.py:251-252) sends any spilled hybrid `-ot blk\.\d+\.ffn_.*\.weight=CPU`. That pattern matches every block's FFN, including the full-attention blocks, so it is all-or-nothing. It ignores how many bytes the plan actually has to take off the GPU (`WindowDecision.spill_bytes`).

## Change
- `gguf.py`: while reading the tensor table, record FFN weight bytes per block (`ffn_block_bytes`). This uses the same `blk\.N\.ffn_.*\.weight` selection the override targets. `profile_from_gguf` copies it onto `ModelProfile`.
- `context_policy.recurrent_spill_blocks(profile, spill_bytes)`: a pure function that picks the fewest recurrent (`n_head_kv==0`) blocks, lowest index first, whose FFN bytes cover `spill_bytes`. It falls back to every recurrent block when sizes are unknown or `spill_bytes` is None. If all recurrent FFNs together still fall short, it lists all of them and fit spills the rest. It never selects a full-attention block.
- `spill_overrides(profile, spill_bytes=None)` emits `blk\.(i|j|…)\.ffn_.*\.weight=CPU`, and `launch_args` passes `decision.spill_bytes`. The MoE and dense paths are unchanged.

## Tests (synthetic metadata; deterministic)
- Interleaved qwen35-style layout (every 4th block full attention): 250 MiB of spill moves blocks 0,1,2. A 301 MiB spill adds block 4 and skips full-attention block 3. `blk.1` does not match `blk.10`–`15`. An oversized spill moves every recurrent block and no full-attention block.
- No FFN sizes, or one recurrent block missing a size: every recurrent block, nothing else.
- `launch_args` sizes the selector from the decision. UMA gets no `-ot`.
- End to end: a hand-written GGUF v3 (qwen35, 12 blocks, `full_attention_interval=4`) → `read_gguf_header` → `profile_from_gguf` → `spill_overrides` moves exactly [0,1,2,4,5]. `attn_norm` is not counted.

## Validation
- `uvx ruff check` on the 5 touched files: all checks passed.

items.body:
## Root cause

`recoverManagedSshScopes` (`apps/desktop/electron/managed-ssh-update.ts`) called `completeRecovery()` only when **every** scope restored. `ManagedConnectionUpdateGate.assertCanDial` / `assertCanMutate` throw whenever a durable journal record exists for the connection. So one scope that never restores (for example, its restore target is gone) kept the record forever: every launch logged "left 1 scope(s) pending; will retry next launch", and the connection could not be dialed, edited, or removed. `runManagedSshUpdate` had the same all-or-nothing condition, so a restore failure right after a successful update fenced the connection until relaunch.

## Behavior

Recovery is now bounded once the remote install marker is positively clear, meaning the mutator is gone and the fence has nothing left to protect:

- New pure decision function `managedSshRecoveryDisposition` → `complete | retry | abandon`.
  - All scopes restored → `complete`, which works as before.
  - The correlated remote exit code is 0 → `abandon` right away. A receipt is not required, because some backends exit 0 without writing one (#101516). A receipt that reports a non-success outcome still blocks this. This is the reported case: `.update_exit_code.<correlation>` → 0.
  - Otherwise `retry`, until `MAX_MANAGED_SSH_RECOVERY_ATTEMPTS` (3) failed attempts, then `abandon`.
- `abandon` clears the journal record. The gate stops fencing and the connection can be dialed, edited, and removed again. The unrestored profiles are logged (`[ssh-update] durable recovery for X stopped after N attempt(s); connection released with M scope(s) not restored (...)`). A scope that is not restored is just a stopped service, and the next ordinary dial starts it again.
- The failed-attempt count is saved as an optional `attempts` field on the existing journal record. Older Desktop builds ignore unknown record fields, so downgrading does not turn the journal "malformed". No new phase value was added, for the same reason.
- `runManagedSshUpdate` uses the same decision: after a proven-successful update (exit 0 plus a success receipt), it clears the journal even if a scope fails to restore. The failure is still reported in `scopes`, with outcome `restore-failed`.
- `waitForManagedRemoteClearance` now returns the clearing observation, so recovery can read the exit code and receipt.
- Clearance that cannot be proven (marker live, malformed, or unreachable) stays fenced as before, because a mutator may still be running.

No user "abandon recovery" action was added. There is no existing UI surface for durable managed-SSH recovery state, and this PR does not create one.

## Acceptance coverage (vitest, `electron/managed-ssh-update.test.ts`)

- Disposition table: complete / retry / abandon-at-max / abandon-on-success / custom max.
- A scope that never restores: the first relaunch retries and records attempt 1, and the connection stays fenced. At the max attempt the connection is released for dial and mutate.
- A correlated exit 0 (with a success receipt, or with no receipt) ends recovery on the first failed restore. A failed receipt keeps it fenced.
- `runManagedSshUpdate`: a successful update with one stuck scope clears the journal. A failed update with one stuck scope keeps it.
- The existing test "inactive SSH crash recovery keeps ordinary dials fenced until positive clearance" is unchanged apart from the new return shape.

## Validation

- `npm ci` (worktree root) → exit 0
- `cd apps/desktop && npm run typecheck` → exit 0
- `npx vitest run --project electron electron/managed-ssh-update.test.ts` → 33 passed
- `npx eslint electron/managed-ssh-update.ts electron/managed-ssh-update.test.ts electron/main.ts` → clean. `prettier --check` → clean.
- Repro against `origin/main`'s `managed-ssh-update.ts` (temporary probe; 10 recovery runs with one stuck scope): `assertCanDial` still throws "SSH connection "homelab" is paused while its managed update is in progress." With this branch, the connection is released at attempt 3, or on the first attempt when the exit code is 0.
- Full `vitest run --project electron`: 309 files pass. 13 files fail (signing, native deps, uninstall sandbox, i18n keys, updater preflight). None of them import `managed-ssh-update` or `main`, and this PR does not touch them.

## Residual

- While a non-success update is still under the attempt bound, the connection stays fenced until the next launch, so the 30 s refresh errors continue until the bound is reached. Users now have to wait out at most 3 launches, not forever.
- A clearance that can never be proven (for example, the host is gone permanently) still fences dial, edit, and removal. That is deliberate for safety and needs a separate user-facing recovery affordance.

Fixes #107827


## macOS remotes in "Update all instances" (#124617)

The POSIX drain stops the Desktop-owned serve only through a pidfd, so the signal is bound to the verified process. Darwin has no equivalent, so `terminateOwnedDashboardForUpdate` deliberately refuses there (`DARWIN_UNAVAILABLE`) instead of accepting a PID-reuse window. The update lifecycle still cancelled every forward, hit the refusal, and reported the row as a failed update on every attempt ("Update fan-out failed: Could not safely drain every managed SSH scope ..."), so a macOS remote with a live serve never updated.

This PR keeps that safety limit. Right after scope capture, and before any forward or serve is touched, the new `managedSshDrainBlocker` detects a live Desktop-owned Darwin serve. The update then returns a structured refusal with `skipReason: 'darwin-drain-unsupported'`. `managedSshUpdateAllRow` reports that connection as a **skipped** row with a clear per-remote message, and Settings shows it as an informational toast instead of an error. A macOS remote with no live Desktop serve needs no drain, so it still updates. Other rows are unaffected, because each row was already independent. No Darwin self-shutdown path was added: there is no authenticated one to reuse.

Related: #124839 fixes the separate problem that the probe's non-zero exit hides the specific refusal message. This PR does not reuse its code and does not depend on it.

- Regression tests: `a live Desktop-owned serve on a macOS remote is a per-row skip, not a batch failure (#124617)` and `macOS remotes with no live serve and Linux remotes still update`. Both fail when the source change is reverted (2 failed / 33 passed) and pass with it.
- `npm run typecheck` → exit 0. `npx vitest run electron/managed-ssh-update.test.ts src/app/settings` → 54 files, 454 tests passed. eslint and prettier → clean.

Fixes #124617

## What does this PR do?

The N1X performance reference currently depends on the exact driver-reported GPU name. A renamed N1X falls back to the generic estimate, while a different device with the matching name can receive the N1X reference. Use PCI vendor/device identity as the primary key, retaining the current name fallback only when a usable PCI ID is unavailable.

Recognize N1X with vendor `0x10DE` and device range `0x2E00–0x2E3F`. A valid conflicting ID takes precedence over the name. This uses the full N1X family range; it does not add benchmark evidence for every SKU. The existing 21.9 tok/s reference, Windows/CUDA/model/quant/MTP eligibility and memory-fit rules are unchanged.

## Related Issue

Follow-up to #112107.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hardware.py`: add `pci.device_id` to the existing memory/name query, parse it with `int(value, 16)`, and retain the packed integer from the same adapter row. Keep the original single-query failure behavior; nonnumeric PCI values such as `N/A` leave identity unavailable without discarding memory data.
- `estimator.py`: carry one optional PCI integer in `HardwareBudget`.
- `hermes_platform/host/products.py` and `catalog.py`: match the vendor/device range and resolve it to the existing calibration key. Keep the calibration table and recommendation flow intact. No regex or separate 32-bit validation is needed.
- Add two parameterized regression tests (19 cases); update existing memory-probe fixtures for the additional identity field.

## How to Test

Run the canonical isolated runner on Windows:

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_local_n1x_pci_identity.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_unified_pool_quirk.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_local_launch_budget.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_local_recommendation.py -j 4 --tb=short
```

Validated on native Windows / Python 3.14.7: **101 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped** (19 new cases and 82 existing cases; the skip is an existing Linux-only WSL test). Ruff 0.15.10 and `git diff --check` passed.

The new cases cover renamed/empty names, range endpoints, the supplied N1X allowlist IDs, N1 exclusion, wrong vendors, unavailable/malformed IDs, negative/oversized integers, preserving memory data when PCI identity is `N/A`, quoted CSV names and keeping identity tied to the same adapter as the memory reading. They run the production parsing, budget and recommendation code with simulated driver responses at the subprocess boundary.

These are functional regressions, not performance measurements. Physical N1X validation and a full-project test run have not been performed.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contributing guide and applicable development instructions.
- [x] Conventional commit; only changes related to this fix.
- [x] Searched existing PRs for N1X/PCI detection fixes.
- [x] Added regression coverage and ran focused tests on Windows.
- [ ] Full test suite run.
- [ ] Physical N1X validation.
- [x] Updated relevant docstrings; no configuration, tool-schema or workflow changes.
- [x] Considered cross-platform behavior; the existing Windows-only calibration gate remains in place.

items.body:
## Root cause

Under a container terminal backend (`docker`, `modal`, ...), `terminal.cwd` is a path inside the sandbox, e.g. `/workspace`. Two readers handle it differently:

- `_terminal_task_cwd` uses it as-is, so the terminal tool gets `/workspace`.
- `_completion_cwd`, which sets the session workspace, runs `os.path.isdir` on it. The host has no `/workspace`, so it fell back to the gateway's own cwd. For the desktop that is `$HOME`.

`_stage_session_file_attachment` then treated every file under `$HOME` as "inside the workspace" and returned it without copying it into the bind-mounted `attachments/` dir. The agent got a relative host ref that does not exist in the container. The issue's corrected diagnosis (comment 2) is right. The desktop `setTerminalBackend` theory from the original report is not.

## Changes

- `tui_gateway/session_workdir.py`
  - `_completion_cwd` keeps an absolute container cwd without host validation when the bound backend is non-local, as `_terminal_task_cwd` already does.
  - New `_sandbox_workspace_cwd` covers two sources the `isdir` check used to drop: a config-only backend (in-process desktop gateway with no `TERMINAL_ENV` bridge) and a named profile's own container `terminal.cwd`.
  - A `terminal.cwd` that exists on the host is still validated and kept (the `docker_mount_cwd_to_workspace` source). Local backends behave as before.
  - `_session_is_local_backend` now reads the effective backend (env or config). Without this, a config-only docker session's `/workspace` would be "healed" up to `/` and saved.
- `tools/credential_files.py`: `map_cache_path_to_container` also matches through a symlinked `HERMES_HOME`. `@file:` expansion passes resolved paths, but the mount roots keep the configured spelling. A symlinked `~/.hermes` (dotfiles setups, or macOS `/var` → `/private/var`) therefore sent an already-staged attachment's host path to the agent. I reproduced this on main. It is one plausible cause of the 2026-09-22 comment (staged paste, host path in the prompt). I could not confirm that commenter's setup.

Once the workspace is the container path, host files fall outside it. `file.attach` stages them into `attachments/`, and the `📎` block shows `/root/.hermes/attachments/<name>`.

## Acceptance / tests

`tests/tui_gateway/test_container_backend_workdir.py` calls the real functions with a temp `HERMES_HOME` and a docker backend config:
- container cwd from config only or from the env bridge → the session workspace, the same value as `_terminal_task_cwd`, and not healed
- local backend with a missing cwd → still falls back; docker with a host-dir cwd → still the host dir
- named docker profile → its own container cwd, even when the client sends an inherited workspace
- end to end: a file under the launch dir → staged into `<HERMES_HOME>/attachments`, absolute ref, and `preprocess_context_references` shows `/root/.hermes/attachments/report.pdf`

`tests/tools/test_credential_files.py::test_symlinked_home_maps_resolved_path`: a resolved staged path under a symlinked home maps to the container path.

## Validation

- `uvx ruff check` (touched files): All checks passed
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_container_backend_workdir.py tests/tools/test_credential_files.py`: 51 passed. With the two source files reverted to `origin/main`: 5 failed (4 new gateway tests, plus the symlink test)
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` on all 13 test files that exercise the touched helpers (includes `test_tui_gateway_server.py`, `test_context_references.py`, `test_complete_path_at_filter.py`, ...): 795 passed, 0 failed, 4 skipped

## Not covered

A binary `@file:` ref typed by hand to a host file outside the mounted dirs still shows its host path in the `📎` stub. One example: a workspace file under `docker_mount_cwd_to_workspace`, which is visible as `/workspace/...` but rendered with its host path. Fixing that needs the workspace-mount mapping in `_agent_visible_path`, so this PR does not close the issue.

#119363 (@MuhammadUsamaMX) takes a different approach: it copies into `attachments/` by basename inside `_agent_visible_path`. It does not touch the `_completion_cwd` root cause, it overwrites same-named files, and it treats ssh as a mount. Nothing from it is reused here.

Refs #103147

items.body:
## Root cause

Covers holes 1 and 3 of #103738. Hole 2 (matching bare or unprefixed provider names) is #124290 by @jonpol01, and this PR doesn't touch that code.

- **Hole 1:** `tui_gateway/server.py::_make_agent` builds `AIAgent` from `resolve_runtime_provider` but drops `runtime["request_overrides"]`, which is where the resolver puts a custom entry's `extra_body`. The CLI, cron and the messaging gateway all pass it. Without it, the body only arrives through `agent_init._merge_custom_provider_extra_body`, which matches `custom`/`custom:*` alone. `hermes -z` (`hermes_cli/oneshot.py`) and ACP (`acp_adapter/session.py`) drop it the same way.
- **Hole 3:** aux requests only read `auxiliary.<task>.extra_body` (default `{}`). They never read the destination entry's `extra_body`, even though the main agent sends it on every request to that endpoint. Aux calls already inherit the entry's `extra_headers` (#109595), and the docs say the entry's `extra_body` "follows the provider everywhere", so this is a gap, not an intentional design choice.

With a proxy that needs a body field (`user`), `hermes chat` works, but Desktop/TUI and smart-approval get a 400.

## Behavior

- `_make_agent`, oneshot and ACP now pass `request_overrides=runtime.get("request_overrides")`. ACP skips it when an explicit `base_url` points at a different endpoint.
- `_build_call_kwargs`, which primary, same-provider-retry and fallback requests all go through, now puts the destination entry's `extra_body` underneath the task/caller body. It uses the agent's own matcher (`_custom_provider_extra_body_for_agent`). Each destination gets only its own entry's body. A fallback to OpenRouter or to another entry never inherits the primary's. Keys from `auxiliary.<task>.extra_body` and from the caller win.
- Invariants: the agent receives the body once, at construction, so the prompt cache isn't touched mid-conversation. The runtime and config are resolved inside the build's existing profile scope, so profile scope is unchanged.

## Acceptance coverage (behavioral)

- `tests/tui_gateway/test_custom_provider_session_persistence.py::TestMakeAgentForwardsProviderRequestBody`: runs the real resolver against a patched config, and `_make_agent` hands `{"extra_body": {"user": ...}}` to AIAgent.
- `tests/agent/test_auxiliary_named_custom_providers.py::TestAuxInheritsCustomProviderExtraBody`: `call_llm(task="approval")` with an empty task `extra_body` sends the inherited `user`. This holds with and without a live `main_runtime`, and the check reads kwargs from the real OpenAI SDK `create`. Task/caller keys win. OpenRouter, a different entry and a stray custom URL don't inherit.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_oneshot_fallback.py::test_run_agent_forwards_resolved_request_overrides` and `tests/acp_adapter/test_session_reasoning_config.py::test_acp_agent_receives_custom_provider_request_body`: covers the sibling build sites, plus ACP's base_url guard.

## Validation

- `uvx ruff check <8 changed files>`: all checks passed.
- Red on `origin/main` b9df1ccc (source reverted, new tests kept): 7 failed (`KeyError: 'request_overrides'` / `'user'` / `'extra_body'`).
- Green: `scripts/run_tests.sh` on the 4 touched test files, 71 passed.
- Wider run: `scripts/run_tests.sh` on 62 files (`tests/agent/test_auxiliary*.py`, fast compression lane, switch-model request overrides, provider fallback, `tests/tools/test_approval_smart*`, tui_gateway server/make_agent/custom-provider files, `tests/acp_adapter/test_session*`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_oneshot*`): 1277 passed, 0 failed. Python 3.14, macOS.

## Residual / notes

- If an aux task pins a different model on the same endpoint, and the entry has `model:` without that model in its catalog, it doesn't inherit. That matches the main agent's per-model rule.
- Aux labels that use a bare entry name (`provider: my-proxy`) start inheriting once #124290 widens the shared matcher. This PR calls that matcher and doesn't fork it.
- #83398 (@justinh20, service tier) also adds a `request_overrides=` kwarg to `_make_agent`. Whichever lands second needs to merge the two dicts.

Refs #103738

items.body:
## Root cause

`sessions.auto_archive` archives a whole compression lineage through `set_session_archived`. When that chat later resumed and compressed, `_publish_child_session_row` inserted the new tip with the default `archived=0` under a root that was still `archived=1`. `list_sessions_rich` admits a lineage by its root's flag (`s.archived = 0` on admitted roots), so the live chat stayed hidden from the sidebar. `unarchive_recoverable_session` only handles `ws_orphan_reap`/`agent_close` tips, so nothing cleared it.

The store could not tell a sweep archive from a deliberate one, and a deliberate archive has to survive re-activation (#89325 / #89341 cover that as a separate feature). So the fix records where the archive came from.

## Change

- New column `sessions.auto_archived INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`. `_reconcile_columns` adds it, and the schema-history event is recorded as seq 30.
- `archive_stale_sessions` archives through `_auto_archive_lineage`, which sets `auto_archived=1` only on rows it hides. Rows that were already archived keep their provenance, so a manually archived ancestor is never relabelled.
- `set_session_archived` (sidebar, API, TUI, `hermes sessions archive`, transfer donor) always clears `auto_archived`, so it counts as a deliberate archive.
- `_unarchive_auto_archived_lineage(conn, sid)` un-hides the lineage only if every archived row came from the sweep. It runs:
  - in `publish_compression_child`'s transaction, after the parent is closed with `compression`, and only when the parent was archived;
  - in `reopen_session` (CLI/TUI `/resume`, oneshot resume, gateway stale-route recovery).
- Compression children inherit the parent's `archived`/`auto_archived`, so a manually archived lineage stays uniformly archived. Before, a lineage with mixed flags gave the sweep an `archived=0` tip that it could relabel.
- Docs: `developer-guide/session-storage.md` and `user-guide/sessions.md`.

## Validation

- `uvx ruff check hermes_state_sessions.py hermes_state_compression.py hermes_state_maintenance.py hermes_state_common.py hermes_cli/session_schema_history.py tests/hermes_state/test_auto_archived_lineage_reactivation.py`: All checks passed.
- Behavioural probe using a real `SessionDB` in tmp_path. Steps: root→tip lineage, run the sweep, compress tip→tip2, then run the sidebar query.
  - Clean `origin/main`: `AssertionError: []` (chat hidden).
  - With the fix: passes, and the sidebar shows `tip2`.
- New `tests/hermes_state/test_auto_archived_lineage_reactivation.py` (6 tests):
  - sweep then compression un-hides the chat;
  - a manual archive stays hidden through compression and a later sweep;
  - a manual archive after the sweep overrides it;
  - the sweep does not relabel a manually archived ancestor (legacy mixed lineage);
  - `reopen_session` un-hides an auto archive but not a manual one;
  - unarchiving clears the provenance.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh <new test> tests/hermes_cli/test_session_schema_history.py tests/hermes_state/test_pinned_archived_sidebar.py tests/hermes_state/test_canonical_title_guard.py`: 23 passed.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_state tests/hermes_cli/test_session_schema_history.py tests/hermes_cli/test_session_recovery_lost_and_found.py tests/hermes_cli/test_session_system_prompt_dedup.py tests/agent/test_compression_rotation_state.py tests/agent/test_compression_concurrent_fork.py`: 1477 passed, 64 failed. Re-running the 19 failing files on clean main gives the same 64 failures. They are environment-dependent tests (auto-vacuum holder gates, cross-VM FS, sqlite3 CLI salvage, repair loops) and none are caused by this change.

## Not covered

- Lineages the sweep archived **before** this change have `auto_archived=0`. They are treated as deliberate and stay hidden until you unarchive them once. There is no way to recover their provenance.
- If an auto-archived tip that never ended gets more messages but never compresses or resumes, it stays hidden until one of those happens. Un-hiding on every inbound message is the broader #89325 / #89341 feature.
- `export`/`import` round-trips carry `archived` but not `auto_archived`, so an imported sweep archive is treated as deliberate.

Fixes #117713

items.body:
## Root cause

`apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/inline-preview-directive.tsx`:

- `intentScript` sliced every prompt to `MAX_INTENT_LENGTH` (500) inside the frame, and `intentFromMessage` sliced it again in the parent. A JSON payload over 500 chars reached the agent as invalid JSON.
- `InlineHtmlFrame` dropped any intent that arrived within `INTENT_THROTTLE_MS` (1s) of the previous one, without queuing it or telling anyone.
- `send()` returned `true` once `postMessage` ran. The frame had no way to know whether an intent was delivered, dropped, or turned away because no visible composer surface existed (`requestComposerSubmit` returning `false`).

## Behavior after this change

- The parent is the only authority. The frame posts the full prompt with a per-call `id`. The pure gate `evaluateIntent()` either accepts it (trimmed, never truncated) or rejects it with a reason: `too_long` (+`maxLength`), `throttled` (+`retryAfterMs`), or `invalid`.
- Accepted intents go through `requestComposerSubmit` exactly as before. A `false` return becomes `undelivered`.
- The parent posts `{ type: 'hermes-inline-preview-intent-ack', token, id, ack }` back to `event.source`. `window.hermes.send()` now returns a `Promise<IntentAck>` and resolves `undelivered` if no ack arrives within 5s. `window.hermes.maxLength` exposes the cap.
- The 500-char cap and the 1 msg/s throttle are unchanged. The code documents the cap as "a sentence, not a payload dump", so I didn't raise it. Over-cap input is now rejected visibly instead of corrupted.
- Security posture is unchanged. Messages without this mount's token are still ignored with no reply. The ack goes only to the source that proved it holds the token. It carries status and nothing from the app. `'*'` is required because the sandboxed frame's origin is opaque. The frame only accepts acks where `e.source === parent` and the token matches. There is no new UI and no sandbox change.
- `data-hermes-send` keeps working. The declarative path ignores the ack.
- Docs: the talk-back paragraph in `website/docs/developer-guide/desktop-plugin-sdk.md` now documents the ack.

For that reason the commit uses a neutral reference and does not say `Fixes`.

Related: #126638 (@MrB0req) routes intents to the owning session's composer instead of `'active'`. It's a different fix in the same handler, so expect a small textual conflict around the `requestComposerSubmit` call. The two changes are compatible.

They check that the full prompt is posted, that `send()` resolves with the matching ack, that acks with a wrong token or a non-parent source are ignored (timeout → `undelivered`), and that an empty prompt resolves `invalid`. items.body:
## Summary

If you send a correction while a **regenerated** turn is streaming, the Desktop view drops the partial reply and your correction. Only the post-correction answer stays on screen, attached straight under the original prompt.

## Root cause

`appendMidTurnUserMessage` seals the live bubble and appends the correction. It is the same seal Stop uses: `finalizeUserInterruptedMessages` marks the row settled and marks its open tool calls interrupted. But it left the regenerate's `pendingBranchGroup` armed, so the next assistant row (seeded by `mutateStream`, `newAssistantFromCompletion` or the interim path) joined the branch group too.

`useRuntimeMessageRepository` parents every branch-group member to the group's user row. That made the post-correction reply a **sibling** of the sealed partial, so the head branch became `question → new answer`. `applyBranchVisibility` then synced that back into the store and marked the partial `hidden`.

## Fix

The correction ends the branch group: `appendMidTurnUserMessage` clears `pendingBranchGroup`. The main composer's `redirectPrompt` and the session tiles' `steerPrompt` both go through this helper. The sealed partial keeps its group (it is the regenerated variant), and output after the correction chains under the correction.

## Routing notes (#119015 / #119686)

- The routing hypothesis was that the runtime adapter sync deletes the live row (`incremental-external-store-runtime.ts` `deleteMessage`). That does not reproduce on current main. The runtime only deletes ids the store no longer has, plus its own always-empty optimistic placeholder.
- A plain (non-regenerated) redirect already keeps the partial on main: the correction seals the bubble with the same helper Stop uses. `steer-arrival-order.test.tsx` covers this, and I confirmed it with a full store → repository → runtime probe.
- The only current-main path I could reproduce where a redirect drops the partial is the regenerate one fixed here. So this PR **does not** close #119015; it covers its regenerate half. The reporter's build (`ddde715b`) already had the sealing code, and I could not reproduce their exact plain-turn case.
- Not touched: queue-mode honour (#125983), and the #119686 tool-narration symptom inside a regenerated turn. Branch variants assume a single assistant row per variant, which is a separate design issue.

## Validation

- New test in `use-message-stream/steer-arrival-order.test.tsx`. It drives the real stream reducer and the real `redirectPrompt`, then projects the store through `useRuntimeMessageRepository` and `IncrementalExternalStoreRuntimeCore` and asserts what is rendered.
  - base `7154128f`: **fails** (rendered `[question, short answer]`; the partial and the correction are missing)
  - with fix: **passes** (`[question, partial, correction, short answer]` mid-turn and after completion)
- `cd apps/desktop && npm run typecheck`: clean
- `npx eslint` on touched files: clean
- `npx vitest run src/app/session src/app/chat src/lib/incremental-external-store-runtime.test.ts src/lib/incremental-runtime-adapter-notify.test.ts`: 254 files / 2354 tests passed

Covers the regenerate half of #119015. Related: #119686, #121597.

items.body:
## Root cause

`hermes update` plans a restart for every profile home from `_profile_homes()`, including a `profiles/<name>` that is a symlink to a separate Hermes install (its own checkout, venv and LaunchAgent). The restart phase leaves that gateway alone, which is correct. The post-restart fleet matrix already marks it `external` (#117449, via `_gateway_code_root` vs `_updater_code_root`). But `match_runtime_outcomes` has no such outcome. The planned gateway therefore ends `unaccounted`, `report_unaccounted_runtimes` returns True, and every update exits 1. On macOS the Desktop hand-off then fails both of its attempts.

## Fix

- `update_cmd_fleet._verify_fleet_after_update` passes `external_gateway_pids` to `match_runtime_outcomes`. These are the pids of fleet rows the probe already classified as `external`.
- `match_runtime_outcomes`: a gateway that no restart bookkeeping mentions (not relaunched, killed, failed or name-matched) and whose planned pid is in that set gets the outcome `external`. It fails closed: no fleet row, an unresolvable code root, or a different pid all still give `unaccounted`. Serve/dashboard runtimes never use this evidence.
- `report_unaccounted_runtimes` lists `external` rows under an informational `ℹ Left to their own install` block. They don't count toward the exit-1 tripwire.

The new parameter is an optional keyword argument, so the frozen compat surface (`tests/compat/old_updater_surface.json`) is unchanged.

## Acceptance coverage

`tests/hermes_cli/test_update_external_profile_reconciliation.py`:
- Uses a real temp `HERMES_HOME` with its own gateway, plus `profiles/work` symlinked to another install whose gateway's pid-guarded `gateway_state.json` argv resolves to a separate fake code root. The test runs the real `_verify_fleet_after_update`, and `collect_fleet_versions` runs for real. With the fix: receipt `success`, outcomes `{default: restarted, work: external}`, no "never touched" block. **On `origin/main` this raises `SystemExit: 1` with `✗ gateway [work] pid 4242 — planned mechanism: launchd`.**
- If the root's own gateway is also missed, the update still exits 1 (`default: unaccounted`), so an external profile can't hide a real miss.
- Fail-closed unit cases: with no evidence, or evidence for a different pid, the outcome is still `unaccounted`. Serve runtimes never become `external`.

## Validation

```
unset PYTHONPATH; uvx ruff check hermes_cli/update_inventory.py hermes_cli/update_cmd_fleet.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_external_profile_reconciliation.py
→ All checks passed!

scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_update_external_profile_reconciliation.py   # on origin/main, before the fix
→ 4 failed (2 integration: SystemExit 1 / work=unaccounted; 2 unit: new kwarg)

scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_update_external_profile_reconciliation.py tests/hermes_cli/test_restart_plan_reconciliation.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_inventory.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_scoped_reconciliation.py tests/hermes_cli/test_windows_update_restart_reconciliation.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_external_checkout.py tests/hermes_cli/test_manual_serve_deferral.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_fleet_check_fail_closed.py tests/hermes_cli/test_fleet_matrix_self_restart_pending.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_fleet_completion.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plan_reconciliation_windows_live.py
→ 11 files, 158 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped

scripts/run_tests.sh tests/test_old_updater_compat_surface.py
→ 570 passed
```

Not exercised: a live two-install macOS host. The regression test drives the real verify/reconcile path with the fleet probe's inputs stubbed at the socket and live-pid layer.

## Related

- #110333 / #110345 / #110256: same exit path, different triggers (sticky-profile root label, hash-suffixed units). They don't overlap with this change.
- The reporter's workaround in #120240 does the same `_code_root_for_path` vs `_updater_code_root` classification inside `match_runtime_outcomes`. This PR reuses the fleet probe's existing classification of the same live pid instead of adding a second probe.

Fixes #120240

items.body:
## Root cause
When a turn's stored rows end in a tool round with `content = ''` and `tool_calls` set, and no prose row follows, `toChatMessages` hydrates that turn as a text-less assistant shell (a prose row would fold into it). `preserveLocalPendingTurnMessages` pairs the settled live bubble (`assistant-stream-*`, `pending: false`) with that shell by ordinal, then drops it: `localPendingSupersedes` only accepts **live-tail** authoritative rows, and a committed shell is not one. The answer the user just watched stream is removed at end of turn, right as the completion chime plays.

## Fix
New `settledReplyOverEmptyShell(local, authoritative)`, checked only at the ordinal-pairing call site in `preserveLocalPendingTurnMessages`. It keeps the local row (the shell still supplies turn state and row identity through `withAuthoritativeTurnState`) only when all of these hold:
- the local row is a settled assistant (`pending !== true`), not interim, not errored, and has answer text (a local row with only tool/reasoning parts doesn't count)
- the authoritative row is a committed assistant (not live-tail), not errored, and has no answer text

`localPendingSupersedes` is unchanged, so resume reconciliation keeps its stricter live-only rule. Once a prose row commits for the turn, hydration folds it into the tool round, the authoritative row now has text, and it wins. No duplicate.

## Tests
New `streamed-reply-survives-sync.test.ts`, 6 cases:
- the reporter's shape built from real `SessionMessage` rows through `toChatMessages` (user 196700, assistant 196701 `content=''` + `tool_calls`, a tool result): the streamed reply survives
- row identity carried from the shell onto the kept reply
- a committed prose row folded into the tool round: the result equals `next` (no duplicate, no resurrection)
- interim narration, a tool-only local row, and an errored shell: none of them displace the authoritative row

## Validation (in worktree)
- `npx vitest run src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/streamed-reply-survives-sync.test.ts` with only `utils.ts` reverted to `origin/main`: **2 failed, 4 passed** (the two keep-the-reply cases fail as expected; the four guard cases already pass on main)
- same file with the fix: 6/6 passed
- `npx vitest run <all 8 test files that use preserveLocalPendingTurnMessages or use-session-actions/utils> src/app/session`: **89 files, 1101 tests passed**
- `cd apps/desktop && npm run typecheck`: passed
- prettier and eslint on both files: clean

## Notes / residual
- This fixes the renderer dropping the reply. It does **not** explain why the store committed the turn's prose as `content=''`. After a restart the reply is still missing, because the store never had it. If that turns out to be a backend persistence bug, it's a separate root cause.
- #126834 (open) calls `preserveLocalPendingTurnMessages` from transcript backfill but doesn't touch this predicate, so no conflict.

Based on #123065 by @kvnloo: same call-site approach and the interim/tool-only guards. This version adds a factored helper, errored-shell and no-duplicate-after-fold coverage, and a regression built on real hydration.

Fixes #123047

items.body:
## Root cause

`preview.read` / `preview.act` / `terminal.read` / `window.read` / `tour` are window-owned bridges: since #114981 only the Desktop window showing the requesting session answers, and every other window returns `'ignore'` (`server-requests.ts::previewSessionRoute`) and stays silent. That silence is correct when another window owns the request. It is wrong when **no** attached window shows the session (the user is on a different chat): nobody answers, the agent waits out the whole 30–45 s deadline, and `read_pane` reports the generic `No preview tab is open, or the read timed out.`

A renderer-only fix (answer the refusal from the non-hosting window) would bring #113348 back. The gateway's `resolve_response` settles on the first frame, so a bystander window's refusal would beat the owner's real answer. One window cannot know whether another window hosts the session. The gateway does know who is attached, so the count happens there.

## Behavior

- **Renderer** (`server-requests.ts`): on `'ignore'`, and when a replayed request's one-turn `'retry'` still finds no host, the window calls `request.decline(...)` instead of staying silent.
- **Shared channel** (`json-rpc-channel.ts`): `ServerRequest.decline` sends JSON-RPC error `4404` (`JSON_RPC_SESSION_NOT_SHOWN`), but only when the backend's `client.capabilities` result said `declines_not_shown: true`. An older backend settles on the first error, so against one the decline is a no-op and behavior matches today's.
- **Gateway** (`server_requests.py`): a `4404` frame counts as a vote from the transport it arrived on (`rpc_dispatch.dispatch` now passes the transport). It does not settle the request. The request stays open for the owner and settles only when every live, advertised WS client attached to the session (`session_transports._session_answering_clients`) has declined. It then resolves right away with `{"success": false, "error": "No Hermes Desktop window is showing this chat, so its preview, terminal and tour are out of reach. Ask the user to open this chat in the Desktop app, then retry."}`. The tools pass that JSON straight through (`passthrough_json`), which is the same `{success:false,error}` shape as the explicit `previewAct` / `tour` refusals from #114981.
- Repeat declines from the same window count once. A decline with no known transport (the `request.answer` proxy, a compute-host relay) is not counted, so the wait continues as before.

## Acceptance coverage

| Test | Before (origin/main source) | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_protocol.py::test_window_owned_request_refuses_at_once_when_no_window_shows_the_session`: 2 windows both decline, so `preview.read` returns the refusal in under 2 s, not after 30 s. A repeated decline from window 1 does not settle the request. | FAILED | passed |
| `test_protocol.py::test_window_owned_request_decline_does_not_beat_the_owner_window`: a bystander declines, an unattributed decline arrives, the request stays open, and the owner's answer is the result (#113348 guard). | FAILED | passed |
| `test_protocol.py::test_client_capabilities_advertises_counting_not_shown_declines` | FAILED | passed |
| `server-requests.test.ts`: `preview.act`, the pane reads and `tour` decline in a window showing another session. A replayed request declines only after the retry turn. A window hosting the session in a tile answers and does not decline. | 4 failed | 17/17 passed |
| `json-rpc-channel.test.ts::sends a not-shown decline only to a backend that advertised counting it` | failed | 13/13 passed |

## Validation (worktree, real output)

- `npm ci` at the root: added 1330 packages
- `cd apps/desktop && npm run typecheck`: exit 0
- `cd apps/shared && npx tsc -p . --noEmit`: exit 0
- `npx vitest run src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event/` (desktop): 11 files, 48 tests passed
- `cd apps/shared && npx vitest run src/json-rpc-channel.test.ts`: 13 passed
- `npx eslint` on the 4 touched TS files: 0 problems. `prettier` applied to the desktop files. The shared files keep their existing line width (running prettier would reformat untouched lines).
- `scripts/gen_gateway_contracts.py`: regenerated `gateway-contract.generated.ts` / `.openrpc.json` (+`declines_not_shown?: boolean`)
- `uvx ruff check` on the touched Python files: All checks passed
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_protocol.py tests/tui_gateway/contracts tests/tui_gateway/test_compute_host_phase1.py …`: 107 passed
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway`: 2222 passed, 6 failed. The 6 failures are in `test_profiles_list_{ui_meta_cache,session_field_cache,canonical_session}.py` and fail the same way on clean origin/main (checked by reverting this diff: 24 passed, 6 failed).

Not reproduced in a live multi-window Electron rig. The proof is the gateway-level two-window fanout test and the renderer dispatcher tests.

## Residual

- A client that answers `-32601` (no handler), such as a dashboard `/chat` tab, still settles a window-owned request at once with the old generic message, as it does today. This PR does not change that.
- A compute-host child owns its requests. Declines relayed to it carry no transport and are not counted, so those sessions still wait out the deadline.

Fixes #119333

items.body:
## Root cause
#121377 made the pre-main launcher (`electron/wslg-launch.ts`) pass `--ozone-platform=wayland` on every local Wayland session so amdgpu stops crashing on XWayland (#83578). On the NVIDIA proprietary driver (615.71.09, RTX 4060, KDE Wayland) the GPU process dies under Wayland ozone with the bundled Electron 40 Chromium (`error_code=1002`, `GPU process isn't usable`). `--ozone-platform=x11` launches fine. The `linux-nvidia-egl-fallback.ts` comment saying 615 is fine is about the #40077 ANGLE EGL probe, not about Wayland ozone.

## Behavior
- If `/proc/driver/nvidia/version` exists (the proprietary kernel module is loaded; not nouveau, not WSL's dxg) and the user set no ozone platform, the automatic default becomes `x11` instead of `wayland`. This puts NVIDIA back on the XWayland path it used before #121377.
- `ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT=auto` counts as no preference.
- User choices still win: `--ozone-platform=…` on argv or in `desktop.electron_flags`, and an `x11`/`wayland` hint from argv, `electron_flags` or `ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT`. NVIDIA users who have Wayland working can keep it with `ozone_platform_hint: wayland`.
- Non-NVIDIA sessions, WSLg, and remote displays behave as before, so the #83578 amdgpu fix is untouched.
- The detection lives in `entry.ts` and is passed into the pure `wslgLaunchArgs()` as a boolean.

## Validation (worktree, `apps/desktop`)
- `npx vitest run electron/wslg-launch.test.ts electron/wslg-launch-process.test.ts electron/linux-nvidia-egl-fallback.test.ts scripts/bundle-electron-main.test.mjs`: 26 passed. The bundled-entry test (5 tests) also passes when run on its own.
- RED: the new test run against `origin/main`'s `wslg-launch.ts` fails with `expected [ '.', '--ozone-platform=wayland' ] to deeply equal [ '.', '--ozone-platform=x11' ]`. It passes with this change.
- `npm run typecheck`: clean. `eslint` and `prettier --check` on the touched files: clean.
- Not reproduced on hardware (no NVIDIA/Wayland box). This rests on the single report, where x11 works and wayland crashes on 615.

## Auto-merge
Off. This changes the Linux launch command.

Fixes #126013

items.body:
## Root cause

`PreviewPane`'s guest-creation effect (`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/right-rail/preview-pane.tsx`) had `target.url` in its dependency array, so every external URL change ran `host.replaceChildren()`, nulled `webviewRef`, and rebuilt the `<webview>` from scratch — dropping the guest's JS state, form data, scroll position, and injected engine handles (`window.__hermesActHolder`), and detaching annotate/console state keyed to the old instance. An in-page navigation steered the same guest fine; only session-driven URL changes tore it down.

## Fix

- The guest-creation effect drops `target.url` from its deps and reads the live address through a `targetUrlRef` mirror, so the guest is created once per preview kind.
- A new steering effect, on `target.url` change, calls `webview.loadURL()` on the live guest instead of rebuilding it — preserving the instance and everything it holds.
- Per-page state resets explicitly around the load so nothing bleeds across pages: annotate (loopRef increment + `teardownAnnotateOverlay` + empty session), console (`consoleState.reset()`), history flags, load error, loading state. Skipped when the guest already shows the address (an in-page navigation arrived first).
- Error paths that previously closed over `target.url` (module-mime load error, `noteBrowserPage`, `did-fail-load`) now read `liveUrlRef.current` so they report the URL actually loaded.

## Coverage

- #120265 — webview instance reused across URL navigations via `loadURL`; JS state/cookies/form data/scroll/refs survive; annotate and console state reset cleanly around the load.

## Checks run

- `npx vitest run src/app/chat/right-rail/preview-pane.test.tsx --maxWorkers=2` — 26 passed (26), including the new regression test asserting the SAME guest node survives a `target.url` change, `loadURL` was called (not a src swap or rebuild), and the address bar tracks the new URL.
- Red on base: same test file against `origin/main`'s `preview-pane.tsx` — 1 failed (the new test), 25 passed. Restored afterwards.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/120303 (approved base — this branch is that commit rebased onto current `main`; authorship preserved: finn763)
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/120379 (closed/unresolvable duplicate)

Thanks @Finn763 for the original fix and regression test.

## Root cause
`useComposerSubmit` auto-skips a parked clarify card (`skipClarifyRequest` → `clarify.respond {answer: ''}`) and a parked connection card (`skipConnectionRequest` → `connection.respond {settled_by: 'continue'}`) for **any** non-empty draft. `/btw` (and `/bg` / `/background`) never speak into the blocked turn — they fork a side question / separate session — yet sending one resolved the pending card with an empty answer.

## Fix
- `isSideTaskSlashCommand(text)` in `lib/desktop-slash-commands.ts`: resolves the command through the slash registry (aliases + catalog) and returns true for side-task actions `btw` and `background` (`/btw`, `/bg`, `/background`, any case, bare or with args).
- `use-composer-submit.ts`: both auto-skips are bypassed for side-task commands. With attachments the draft is not routed as a slash command, so it keeps the ordinary-message behavior. Other slash commands (e.g. `/status`) and plain replies still skip the card as before.
- Test: fixed a `TS2352` cast in the contributor's gateway mock so desktop typecheck passes.

## Validation (in worktree, `apps/desktop`)
- `npx vitest run --project ui src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-submit.test.tsx src/lib/desktop-slash-commands.test.ts src/store/connection-request.test.ts` → **77 passed**.
- Red check: the same composer suite with `use-composer-submit.ts` restored from `origin/main` → **10 failed**. Each of the 5 side-task drafts × the clarify and connection cards fails: the clarify gets `{answer: ''}`, or the connection gets `settled_by: 'continue'`.
- `npm run typecheck` → exit 0, no TS errors.
- `npx eslint` + `npx prettier --check` on the 3 changed files → clean.
- Not run: a live Desktop manual check.

Supersedes #126220. Based on #126220 by @charan-rathore: the two cherry-picked commits keep their authorship, and the follow-up commit carries a co-author trailer. This PR adds the `/bg`/`/background` siblings, resolves commands through the registry instead of a regex, adds the attachment guard, and fixes the typecheck.

Fixes #126188

items.body:
## Root cause

Every desktop terminal tab stays mounted by design, so all xterm instances that share font/theme/DPR share one WebGL glyph atlas (@xterm/addon-webgl 0.19.0, pinned; the upstream sibling-notification fix in xtermjs/xterm.js#6055 is only in the 0.20.0-beta line). `clearTextureAtlas()` on one instance wipes the shared texture and rebuilds only the caller's render model; sibling terminals keep per-cell texture coordinates into the wiped atlas and render garbled glyphs until a resize forces a full rebuild. Separately, after a `webglcontextlost` the addon was disposed (DOM renderer takes over) but no repaint was forced, so the viewport could stay black while the buffer was intact.

## Fix

- `terminals.ts`: a `registerWebglRefresh` registry (unregister on dispose) and a coalesced single-rAF `redrawAllTerminals(skipTerm?)` with two-phase ordering — ALL atlas clears before ANY refresh, so no terminal rebuilds against an atlas that a later clear wipes.
- Every atlas-mutating call site fans out: theme change and tab activation for both the user terminal (`use-terminal-session.ts`) and the agent mirror (`use-agent-terminal.ts`), plus the live font change (`use-terminal-font.ts`).
- `webgl.onContextLoss` (both hooks): after disposing the dead addon, force a fit + full-row repaint so the DOM renderer shows the buffered output instead of a black canvas.
- Remaining `clearTextureAtlas` paths (the fan-out clear in the registry and the live font change) are wrapped so a half-dead GL context cannot abort the repaint path.
- `terminals.ts` subscribes to the main process's `hermes:power-resume` broadcast (powerMonitor `resume`/`unlock-screen`) and rebuilds every registered terminal: macOS can evict glyph textures on wake without firing `webglcontextlost`.

## Coverage

- #76102 — sibling garbling after shared-atlas clear (theme change, tab activation, font change) and the macOS resume-eviction variant: fully covered.
- #98273 — context-loss repaint (fit + `term.refresh(0, rows-1)` on both hooks). The reporter's exact Windows trigger is unconfirmed (custom skin, stock-theme repro still outstanding); tracked there rather than auto-closed.

## Checks run

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/app/right-sidebar/terminal/ --project ui` — 78 tests, all new/changed tests pass on this branch; all new tests fail on base (red-on-base proven by checking out base sources with the new test files). Two pre-existing tests in `terminals.test.ts` (`restores user tabs…`, `persists user tabs…`) time out on this machine both on base and on this branch — local first-import slowness, unrelated to this change.
- `npx tsc -p . --noEmit` — see PR checks.
- `npx eslint src/app/right-sidebar/terminal/` — see PR checks.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/76463
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/107808

Thanks @thatssoheil for the registry + two-phase fan-out design and tests, and @salch-cred for the context-loss repaint and the atlas-clear guards.

Fixes #76102

## Root cause

The Desktop voice conversation runs its own full-duplex barge monitor (`lib/voice-barge-in.ts` → `use-voice-conversation.ts` `submitCapturedUtterance`). Over speakers, Hermes' own TTS bleeds into the mic and trips the playback-phase trigger. The captured audio is transcribed and submitted as the next user turn, with no check against the reply that was playing. The interruption latch also stays set, so the model gets told "the user interrupted your previous spoken reply" when nobody spoke. The CLI fixed the same loop with `tools/voice_mode_transcript.is_tts_echo`. The renderer never got that check.

## Fix

- `apps/desktop/src/lib/voice-tts-echo.ts`: a pure TS port of `is_tts_echo`. It includes a faithful `difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, a, b).ratio()` port (autojunk included, compared by code point), the 0.6 threshold, and `MIN_FRAGMENT_LENGTH_FOR_ECHO = 10` with the transcript-sized sliding window for fragments of long replies.
- `use-voice-conversation.ts`: when the barge trips, the hook records the text of the reply being spoken, but only if playback is audible (`$voicePlayback.status === 'speaking'`). It records it before playback is cut, because the reply is consumed by the time STT returns. This matches the CLI's playback-phase-only rule. In `submitCapturedUtterance`, after the stop-phrase check, a matching transcript counts as silence: nothing is submitted, `takeVoicePlaybackInterrupted()` clears the "user interrupted" latch, and the loop resumes listening. Generation-phase trips (no audio playing) and genuine interjections are unchanged.

No conflict with #80996. That PR applies the same guard to the TUI gateway listener and touches only `tui_gateway/server.py` and its test.

## Scope / residual (why this says "Covers", not "Fixes")

Covers the TTS-echo half of #126708. Not addressed:
- The client-direct STT path (`voice-client-direct.ts`) still skips the `is_whisper_hallucination` filter.
- The Desktop renderer still doesn't read `voice.barge_in` (only `barge_in_threshold_multiplier`).
- An echo still cuts playback when it trips, as in the CLI. We only know it was an echo after STT returns. If the reply was still being generated, the in-flight turn has already been interrupted too.

## Validation (worktree, `apps/desktop`, `unset PYTHONPATH`)

- Regression test: the new `use-voice-conversation.test.tsx` case "drops a playback-phase capture that is a fragment of the reply being spoken" **fails on origin/main's hook** (1 failed / 10 passed). With the fix, all pass. Two sibling cases check that a genuine playback-phase interjection and a generation-phase trip still submit.
- `voice-tts-echo.test.ts` mirrors every case in `tests/tools/test_voice_tts_echo_guard.py::TestIsTtsEcho`, plus CPython reference ratios, including the autojunk case.
- Differential check (not committed): 600 random cases generated with CPython `difflib` and `is_tts_echo`. The random strings were up to 400 chars, so autojunk ran. The TS ratio matched to 1e-12 and the echo verdict matched on 600/600.
- `npx vitest run src/lib/voice src/app/chat/composer`: 83 files, 607 tests passed.
- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- `npx eslint` on the 4 files: 0 errors. The one warning (`react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` on the drive effect) is pre-existing.
- `npx prettier --check`: clean.

Covers #126708 (echo half).
items.title: fix(desktop): drop voice-conversation barge captures that echo the spoken reply

items.body:
Streaming into a long chat gets slower as the transcript grows. Settled messages already don't re-render per chunk on main (a new render-count test pins that at 0 for 8, 42 and 1602 messages), but two row selectors still scan the whole transcript on every thread notify — `runtimeUserOrdinal` in `user-message.tsx` and `interAgentSender` in `assistant-message.tsx` — so per-chunk cost is mounted rows × transcript length.

This builds one id→index and id→user-ordinal map per `thread.messages` array (WeakMap keyed by array identity) and shares it across rows. Results are identical (last-occurrence index, first-occurrence ordinal).

Measured in jsdom through the real pipeline (`useRuntimeMessageRepository` → `useIncrementalExternalStoreRuntime` → `<Thread />`), 10 chunks × 3 runs:

| history | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 20 turns | 4.8–8.3 ms/chunk | 5.5 ms/chunk |
| 400 turns | 38.4–45.1 ms/chunk | 29.4–30.6 ms/chunk |

Neither selector appears in the CPU profile afterwards. The rest of the per-chunk time is assistant-ui's per-subscriber machinery plus the O(N) `list.tsx` signatures and `timeline.tsx` layout loop, which this doesn't touch — so the issue stays open.

Covers the per-row transcript-scan part of #126486. Prior art: #69151 by @frizikk.

Tests: `stream-settled-renders.test.tsx` (settled roots/text parts re-render 0× per chunk, live tail does render — guards the property; passes on main too) and `thread-message-index.test.ts`. `npm run typecheck`, eslint, prettier clean; vitest 291 passed across `assistant-ui/thread/`, `runtime-repository`, `incremental-external-store-runtime`. Not yet measured with `npm run perf -- stream-history --spawn --prod`.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Stops a supervisor's stop signal from being logged and handled as an adapter crash when it reaches a managed child process (the WhatsApp bridge, the Photon sidecar) before the gateway's stop flow calls that adapter's `disconnect()`.

Both children run in their own session (`start_new_session=True`), so an ordinary signal to the gateway's process group never reaches them. A container-wide stop can still reach them: s6-overlay's stage 3 (the Hermes image's PID 1) SIGTERMs every process. Plain `docker stop` signals only the container's main process, so whether a child sees it depends on the init/supervisor. The child then exits with -15 while `_shutting_down` (WhatsApp) is still False or `_inbound_running` (Photon) is still True, and the adapter reports a retryable fatal error in the middle of shutdown.

The fix is @liuhao1024's #127067 cherry-picked with authorship intact. The classification also checks the runner's `_stop_requested_by_signal`, which the signal handler sets before it schedules `stop()`. This PR adds the same check to Photon's `_supervise_sidecar()`, the only other adapter that makes this exit-means-crash decision about a child in its own session.

A -15 exit while the gateway keeps running is still a retryable fatal error, so the reconnect watcher restarts the child. Examples: another Hermes process's `_kill_port_process` / `_kill_stale_bridge_by_pidfile`, or someone running `kill` by hand.

## What this changes on current main

Deterministic ordering reproduction (not a live Docker/s6 restart): a real `GatewayRunner`, a real `WhatsAppAdapter` and the real signal handler, with a real child process killed with SIGTERM before the adapter's `disconnect()` runs:

| Scenario | main | #127065 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Container stop (gateway + bridge both signalled) | ERROR "exited unexpectedly (code -15)", fatal handler runs, whatsapp queued for reconnect during shutdown | clean "exited during shutdown" | clean "exited during shutdown" |
| Bridge SIGTERMed while the gateway keeps running | retryable fatal, queued for reconnect ✅ | **not reported, never queued**: poll loop logs `Poll error` every 5 s and WhatsApp stays down | retryable fatal, queued for reconnect ✅ |

On current main this race does not change the process exit code. An unplanned SIGTERM already exits 1 on purpose (`_resolve_gateway_exit_verdict`, so the service manager restarts the gateway), and the fatal path queues the platform instead of setting `_exit_with_failure`. The problem this fixes is the wrong ERROR/fatal classification, the fatal-handler teardown, and the "retrying" platform status written during a normal stop. The crash loop in the issue was reported on v0.16.0 and does not reproduce on main.

## Related Issue

Fixes #127047
Salvages #127067

Supersedes #127065. Its approach, treating -15 as never fatal, is not adopted: a bridge SIGTERMed while the gateway is still running would never be queued for reconnect (second row above). Thanks @dskwe for the diagnosis, and @allissonbrito for the report and logs.

## Changes Made

- `plugins/platforms/whatsapp/adapter.py`: `_check_managed_bridge_exit()` also treats `{0, -2, -15}` as intentional when the runner flags a signal-driven stop (#127067, @liuhao1024).
- `plugins/platforms/photon/adapter.py`: `_supervise_sidecar()` skips the `SIDECAR_CRASHED` fatal when the runner flags a signal-driven stop.
- WhatsApp comment corrected: the bridge runs in its own session, not the gateway's process group.
- Tests: WhatsApp race window is not fatal and the no-flag SIGTERM stays fatal (#127067). Photon has the same pair, parametrized.

## How to Test

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_whatsapp_connect.py tests/gateway/test_runner_fatal_adapter.py tests/plugins/platforms/`: 203 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed (main: 198 passed, 4 skipped). Ruff clean on all changed files.
- RED check: with both adapters reverted to `origin/main`, the new race-window tests fail (WhatsApp sigterm/sigint, Photon gateway-stopping). The "stays fatal" cases pass on both.

## What does this PR do?

Fixes Windows source-install setup when the account path contains an apostrophe. The installer obtains a Python `-c` bootstrap from the installation launcher and invokes it through Windows PowerShell. Python's `repr()` chooses double quotes for a path containing `'`, and Windows PowerShell's native argument handoff removes those embedded quotes. Python then receives invalid source and setup exits with `SyntaxError`.

`runtime_command()` now writes its inline string values as single-quoted Python literals, encoding embedded quote characters as `\x27` and `\x22` on Windows. The module bootstrap remains visible in the process command line, preserving Hermes's gateway and updater process-identity checks. POSIX command construction is unchanged.

## Related Issue

No public issue filed. The regression test reproduces the failing Windows installer path with a synthetic apostrophe-containing account directory.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/_launchers.py`: construct Windows inline Python string literals that survive PowerShell's native argv handoff without hiding the bootstrap from process inspection.
- `tests/scripts/install/test_install_ps1_execution_policy.py`: exercise the real installer invocation through Windows PowerShell with a synthetic apostrophe path in both the install root and Hermes home.

## How to Test

1. On unmodified `main`, the new Windows test reproduces the installer's `SyntaxError` after `sys.path.insert(0, C:\\...user's-home...)` loses its quotes.
2. Run `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/scripts/install/test_install_ps1_execution_policy.py -j 4`. Both tests pass with this change.
3. Run the focused neighboring launcher and holder-classifier checks in `tests/hermes_cli/test_source_launcher_publication.py` and `tests/hermes_cli/test_venv_holder_classifier.py`. All three selected tests pass. The Windows process-identity probe still recognizes a `gateway run` command with an apostrophe in its root.

items.body:
fix(wake): recover transient capture read failures and fall back to blocking reads when read_available stalls

## Root cause

Two independent bugs in the local-capture read loop of `tools/wake_word.py`, both reported on Windows:

- **#118001**: a single `stream.read` exception fell through to `failed = True`, permanently disarming wake detection until the user toggled it. Real microphone stacks (USB disconnect, device sleep, driver reset) throw transient read errors all the time.
- **#118552**: on some Windows DirectSound devices, `read_available` never advances even while audio flows. The poll guard introduced for #117096 then spins forever below `frame_length` and no audio is ever read.

## Fix

- `_run` catches a read error, closes the failed capture, and calls a new `_recover_capture` with a bounded whole-arm retry budget (0.5s / 1s / 2s) — reusing `_open_capture` so the owner and engine are kept, resetting the engine and silence counters on reopen. Exhausting the budget (or a stop during it) is the only path that arms `on_failure`.
- `_Capture.read` abandons the `read_available` poll guard after `_READ_STALL_FALLBACK_SECONDS` of starvation (warn once per capture, `_skip_available_poll`), falling back to the blocking read; a truly wedged blocking read is released by `_halt_thread` aborting the stream.
- `_halt_thread` keeps `self._cap` (armed by `_run` and re-armed on every recovery) so a wedged blocking read in the *current* capture is aborted when `pause()`/`stop()` joins out. `_open_capture` also closes the capture on a failed stream start.

## Coverage

- **#118001**: `tests/tools/test_wake_word_stream_recovery.py` — transient read failure recovers with the same device/engine; recovery is bounded and cancellable (read/open/cancel/external modes).
- **#118552**: `tests/tools/test_wake_word.py` — starved `read_available` falls back to blocking reads and warns once; starved-AND-wedged read is released by `pause()`'s abort (`#117096` guarantee preserved).
- **Composition**: new test proves that after recovery reopens the microphone, a reader wedged in the *recovered* capture is still released by `pause()` (the halt hook follows the recovered capture — this was a gap when composing the two PRs; fixed here).

## Checks

- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tools/test_wake_word.py tests/tools/test_wake_word_stream_recovery.py` — 74 passed, 0 failed, 4 skipped (platform skips).
- The composition test is red on the composed contributor commits without the `self._cap` re-arm fix (verified by checking out the pre-fix `tools/wake_word.py`).

Windows DirectSound behaviour itself cannot be exercised on macOS; the stream-mock tests above are the detection net, and final e2e confirmation needs a Windows host (#118560's How-to-Test).

## Supersedes

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/118011
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/118560

Thanks @Wenfengcheng and @liuhao1024 — both commits are cherry-picked verbatim (rebase-merged onto main) so authorship is preserved.

Co-authored-by: liuhao1024 <sunsky.lau@gmail.com>
```

## Root cause

`website/docs/user-guide/desktop.md` promises Review-pane diffs scoped to **Uncommitted, Branch, or Last turn**, but the renderer hardcodes `'uncommitted'` (`src/store/review.ts`: `review.list(cwd, 'uncommitted', null)` and the diff read the same). The Electron side fully implements `branch`/`lastTurn` — no renderer caller ever reached them, so the documented scopes were dead.

## What changes

- **Scope selector** in the Review pane header (`Uncommitted / Branch / Last turn`), backed by a persisted `$reviewScope` atom.
- `$reviewTurnBase` captures HEAD per repo cwd at turn start (driven off `$sessionStates`, so pinned tile worktrees and background sessions get their own baseline), **LRU-capped at 8 entries** with a documented race note and cwd-normalization contract.
- The selected scope + last-turn baseRef thread through **both** read paths (list + diff).
- **Mutations gated**: stage/unstage/revert and the commit/PR ship bar apply to Uncommitted only; outside that scope the ship bar shows a read-only note (new `readOnlyScope` string in all five locales) instead of vanishing.
- `desktop.md` reconciled with the shipped behavior (Last-turn / read-only semantics spelled out).

## Acceptance coverage

| Requirement (issue #84347) | Covered |
|---|---|
| Scope selector in the renderer (option 2 chosen over amending docs) | Yes — picker in pane header |
| Thread selected scope through list and diff reads, incl. per-cwd last-turn baseline | Yes — `reviewReadParams()` threads scope+baseRef into both paths |
| Gate stage/unstage/revert + commit bar to uncommitted | Yes — early return + read-only note |
| Reconcile `desktop.md` | Yes |

## Tests (real results)

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --project ui src/store/review.test.ts src/app/right-sidebar/review/index.test.tsx src/app/right-sidebar/review/ship-bar.test.tsx`
  - On `origin/main` + this branch's new test files: **6 failed / 29 passed** (selector, gating, ship-bar note absent on main) — log: `$RUN/builds/logs/84347-on-main.log`
  - With the fix: **green** (44/45 in the first log — the 1 failure was a stale pre-rebase transform from a killed run; fresh single-file rerun after cache clear: **3/3 green**, `/tmp/shipbar-rerun.log`) — log: `$RUN/builds/logs/84347-with-fix.log`

Typecheck skipped per the UI rule (visible Desktop UI change); before/after harness shots captured (`$RUN/shots/84347-before.png` / `-after.png`).

Fixes #84347

Thanks @Chukwuebuka-2003 — both commits are yours, cherry-picked with authorship preserved.

## What

`hermes dump`, `hermes debug share` and the gateway `/debug` report no longer print a `fallback_providers` entry's credentials.

## Why

- `_config_overrides` rendered `fallback_providers` as `str(fallbacks)`, which included each entry's `api_key` and any credential in its `base_url`.
- `_capture_dump()` returned the dump without redacting it. Upload-time redaction only ran on the log snapshots.

## How

- From #126132 (jonpol01): the dump is force-redacted with strict URL-credential redaction, both at the source (`dump.py`) and again at the upload boundary (`_capture_dump`, which honours `--no-redact`). GCS `X-Goog-Signature` and Azure SAS `sig` now count as URL credentials. Docs updated.
- From #126168 (JoaoMarcos44): the canonicalizer fix so `X-Amz-Signature` is masked, and a test proving the upload boundary redacts the dump on its own.
- New: `api_key` is masked by field before the entries are turned into text. Text redaction alone missed three `api_key` values that `resolve_entry_api_key` still passes to the provider: an unquoted numeric key (a YAML int), a mapping, and a key containing `***`, which the redactor treats as already masked.

## Tests

- The new shape tests fail with the `dump.py` change reverted, and the boundary test fails with the `_capture_dump` redaction reverted.
