items.body:
New installs of the Hermes desktop app now open in a window sized to the screen, at 110% zoom, so text is readable on first launch without pressing Cmd+ several times. ## The problem Every new install opened in the same fixed window, 1220×800 pixels, at 90% zoom. On a large monitor that is a small box in the middle of the screen. At 90% the app's 13-px body text renders at 11.7 px and its smallest 9-px text at 8.1 px. That is below Apple's guidance (13 pt body text, 10 pt minimum) and below the Windows 11 body size. Users fixed it by pressing Cmd+ (zoom in) again and again. Earlier builds used about 91%. Commit `4a9754b3c3` rounded it to 90%, one of the fixed choices in the Settings zoom menu, so the menu would show a selected option. It had no readability reason. ## Before / after | Before (Window on a 27-inch display, drawn to scale) | After (Window on a 27-inch display, drawn to scale) | |:---:|:---:| | ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0158f3c4-734a-4b90-8e9b-de2608265297) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6c44c09b-d8d8-4082-9537-f6e4d7ad47c0) | | Before (Heading text at actual pixels) | After (Heading text at actual pixels) | |:---:|:---:| | ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff3eddd4-b40f-4ac4-826f-e03f6dcf2112) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eee31008-3701-4091-ba22-ff5123aface0) | ## What the user experiences The "work area" is the screen minus the menu bar or taskbar. | Situation | Before | After | |---|---|---| | New install, 27" monitor (work area 3008×1692) | 1220×800 box, 90% | 1600×1000, centred, 110% | | New install, 14" laptop (work area 1470×919) | 1220×800, 90% | 1220×800 (the minimum size), 110% | | New install, small screen (work area 1280×752) | 1220×752, 90% | 1220×752 (capped to the screen height), 110% | | Existing install | Its saved size and zoom | Unchanged. Saved size and zoom always win. First launch has always saved the zoom, so existing installs stay at 90% until the user changes it. | | Cmd+0 or View → Actual Size, any install | Resets to 90% | Resets to 110% | ## What changes A new install has no `window-state.json` (saved window size and position) and no `zoom-state.json` (saved zoom). Both live in Electron's per-app data folder ("userData"). This PR changes only what the app does when they are missing. **Window size.** A new function, `firstLaunchSize(workArea)` in `electron/window-state.ts`, computes the first size from the primary display's work area. It has no side effects, so it is easy to reason about in isolation. - width = 75% of the work area, clamped to 1220–1600 - height = 80% of the work area, clamped to 800–1000 - then capped at the work area itself; the cap wins over the 1220/800 minimum on small screens No position is set, so Electron centres the window. **Zoom.** `DEFAULT_ZOOM_LEVEL` in `electron/zoom.ts` is now the existing 110% choice from Settings → Appearance → UI Scale. It applies when `zoom-state.json` is missing, and to Cmd+0 / View → Actual Size. ```mermaid flowchart TD L[App launch: createWindow] --> W{window-state.json saved?} W -- yes --> S[computeWindowOptions with the saved size and position] W -- no --> F["firstLaunchSize(primary display work area)
(before: fixed 1220×800)"] F --> S S --> BW[Window opens] BW --> Z{zoom-state.json saved?} Z -- yes --> ZS[Apply the saved zoom] Z -- no --> ZD["Apply 110% and save it
(before: 90%)"] K[Cmd+0 or View → Actual Size] --> ZR["Reset to 110%
(before: 90%)"] ``` | File | Change | |---|---| | `apps/desktop/electron/window-state.ts` | New `firstLaunchSize`. The fixed `DEFAULT_WIDTH` / `DEFAULT_HEIGHT` and the "no saved size" branch of `computeWindowOptions` are deleted; it now always receives a size. | | `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` | The main window, and a new extra window opened when no other window exists to offset it from (`nextInstanceBounds`), use `readWindowState() ?? firstLaunchSize(screen.getPrimaryDisplay().workArea)`. | | `apps/desktop/electron/zoom.ts` | `DEFAULT_ZOOM_LEVEL` = 110%. | | `apps/desktop/src/store/zoom.ts` | The Settings zoom control's first-paint value is 110, matching the main process. | ## What this deliberately does not do - **No migration for existing installs.** Moving untouched 90% installs to 110% belongs with the planned cleanup of the desktop's single-setting JSON files. - **No onboarding window sizing.** The first-run guide's own window size is a later change that reuses `firstLaunchSize`. ## Live verification Fresh userData each time. Electron stores zoom as a level where zoom = 1.2^level, so level 0.5228 is 110%. `devicePixelRatio` is the display's scale factor times the zoom (Retina is 2). | Host | Work area | Window | Zoom | Observed at | |---|---|---|---|---| | macOS, `origin/main` (before) | 3008×1692 | 1220×800 | `devicePixelRatio` 1.8 = 2 × 0.9 | `39faafb616` | | macOS, this PR | 3008×1692 | 1600×1000 at x=704 (centred) | level 0.5228 = 110%; `devicePixelRatio` 2.2 = 2 × 1.1 | `29827817fb` | | Windows 11 on Arm, this PR | 1646×1029 at 175% scale | 1236×824 at x=205, y=102 | level 0.5228; `devicePixelRatio` 1.925 = 1.75 × 1.1 | `29827817fb` | On Windows the formula gives 1235×823. The 1-point difference is most likely rounding to whole physical pixels at 175% scale; it was not investigated further. ## Side effect: a test-harness fix Not part of the feature. The update E2E suite pins the window at 1280×860 but not the zoom, so it now runs at 110%. At that zoom the page is 1163.6 CSS pixels wide, and the browser reports its width (`innerWidth`) rounded to 1164. The harness's `waitForInteractive` treated a full-screen overlay as blocking only when the overlay was at least `innerWidth` wide. The 1163.6-pixel startup overlay ("Starting Hermes…") stopped counting, so the test declared the app ready too early. The check now allows 1 pixel of rounding (`7eab48b8a9`, verified by CI only). ## Checks No new tests, by the maintainer's rule for this series; the one existing test that used the deleted constants is removed. Final-tree CI passed, including the Linux first-run update E2E.

Hermes can now tell "a free-tier account exists on this machine" apart from "this conversation runs on the free tier", and creating the free-tier account no longer changes which provider the user picked. ## Background: the Nous free tier When `HERMES_GUEST_ONBOARDING=1` is set, Hermes creates an anonymous Nous account at first launch. This PR calls that step **the mint**. The account gives two things: free connectors (hosted integrations such as Gmail), and free inference on one model, `nous/welcome`, served by a separate Nous server, the **welcome host**. A user can have this account AND their own provider key, for example OpenRouter. Then the account still exists for connectors, but the user's key does the inference. So there are two separate facts: - **Account fact:** a free-tier account is on disk and the free tier is switched on. - **Route fact:** this conversation's inference actually goes to the free tier. To pick a provider, Hermes runs `resolve_provider("auto")`. It walks a fixed order: explicit settings and keys first, then a sign-in, then a free-tier step, which applies only when nothing the user chose is present. ## The problem Both facts were called `free_tier`, and several screens read the account fact when they meant the route fact. A user with the free-tier account and their own OpenRouter key saw the CLI banner name the free model (`welcome · Nous Research`), although OpenRouter did the inference. `/status` and the messaging gateway's startup message could also say "free tier". The old desktop onboarding guide switched to its free-tier copy and forced minimal reasoning. Separately, the mint wrote `active_provider: nous` into `auth.json` when it found no other provider. `active_provider` is the field a real sign-in writes; it records a user choice. The write was not needed, because the free-tier step in `resolve_provider("auto")` already gives the same answer. And the write stayed in `auth.json` after the user added their own key. ## Before / after | Before (CLI banner with an OpenRouter key and a free-tier account) | After (CLI banner with an OpenRouter key and a free-tier account) | |:---:|:---:| | ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/261b43c0-d13e-41e7-bf16-706c92919e2f) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6597a158-ccc7-4423-b70a-f602f1ac4424) | ## What the user experiences | Situation | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Fresh install, nothing configured | Free tier does the inference; the banner names the free model | Same | | Free-tier account + own OpenRouter key: CLI banner | `welcome · Nous Research` (wrong) | `no model configured — run /model or hermes setup` (see the note below) | | Same: CLI `/status`, gateway `/status`, gateway startup message | Can say "free tier" | No free-tier line | | Same: old desktop onboarding guide | Free-tier copy, minimal reasoning | Normal copy and reasoning | | Desktop billing page | Free-tier view when the account exists | Same (it reads the account fact, now under its own name) | | `auth.json` after the mint | `active_provider: nous` | No `active_provider` | **Note on the banner.** With an OpenRouter key and no `model` in `config.yaml`, the banner now says "no model configured". A new chat would still go to OpenRouter: in that run, `setup.runtime_check` resolved OpenRouter with a default model (`z-ai/glm-5.2`). The test key was fake, so no OpenRouter chat was sent. Every install without the free tier already shows this same line. Making the banner show the resolved model for every provider is a separate change. ## What changes **The mint stops writing `active_provider`.** This is the one write-path change. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Boot as Startup (free_tier_bootstrap) participant Anon as anon_auth.ensure_portal_identity participant Portal as Nous account service participant Store as auth.json Boot->>Anon: create the free-tier account if missing Anon->>Portal: POST /api/anonymous/create Portal-->>Anon: anonymous credential Anon->>Store: providers.nous = free-tier account Note over Anon,Store: Before: also active_provider = "nous"
when nothing else was configured.
After: no active_provider write. Boot->>Boot: resolve_provider("auto") → "nous" through the free-tier step ``` - The `carries_inference` parameter is removed from `ensure_portal_identity` and the functions under it. - The two places that replace a dead free-tier credential (in `auth_nous` and `managed_tool_gateway`) now write nothing to `active_provider` either. - Picking up a real sign-in that another Hermes profile on this machine already saved still writes `active_provider`, because that is a sign-in. **One name per fact.** The desktop app talks to the Python backend over JSON-RPC (named request/response methods). These fields change: | Method or event | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `setup.status`, and the `setup.ready` event sent once at startup | `free_tier` (account) | `free_tier_account` and `free_tier_route` | | `setup.runtime_check` (checks the route a new chat would use) | `free_tier` (route) | `free_tier_route` | | `billing.state` | `free_tier` (account) | `free_tier_account` | In Python (`hermes_cli/anon_auth.py`): - `guest_carries_inference()` returned the account fact despite its name. It is renamed `has_free_tier_account()`. - New `free_tier_route()`: the account exists AND `resolve_provider("auto") == "nous"`. The banner, CLI `/status`, gateway `/status` and the gateway startup message use it. Three of them already did this check inline; the banner did not. ```mermaid flowchart LR HA["has_free_tier_account()"] --> BL[billing.state] HA --> FR["free_tier_route()"] RP["resolve_provider('auto')"] --> FR FR --> SURF[CLI banner · /status · gateway startup message] REC[Startup record] --> SS[setup.status / setup.ready] SS --> KO[Old onboarding kickoff reads the route] ``` The startup record's route is its account fact AND its resolved provider being `nous`. When the desktop asks `setup.status` about a named profile, such as the onboarding setup profile, the route is computed live for that profile. The Nous login status keeps its own `free_tier` flag: inside one provider's status it can only mean "this login is the free-tier account". The model inventory's `free_tier` means the Nous plan tier, a different fact, and is not touched. ## Contracts When the mint fails, the backend returns `error_code`, `retryable` and `retry_after`. The declared shapes of `setup.status`, `free_tier.status` and `free_tier.provision` did not list these fields, and those shapes reject fields they do not list. They are declared now. The generated TypeScript and OpenRPC contract files are regenerated. ## What this deliberately does not do - **No banner change for other providers** (see the note above). - **No cleanup of old writes.** Installs that an earlier build already minted keep their `active_provider: nous`. Every explicit user choice still ranks above it. - **No rename of the login-status flag**, for the reason above. ## One decision for reviewers The old onboarding kickoff asks `setup.status` about the setup profile. Before, it read the launch profile's account fact. Now it reads the route computed live for the setup profile. So if the setup profile's inference is not the free tier, the guide no longer uses free-tier copy or minimal reasoning. That kickoff is deleted later in the onboarding rebuild; reverting this reader is a one-line change. ## Live verification Summary: on `main` the mint writes `active_provider: nous` and the banner names the free model even when OpenRouter does the inference; on this PR neither happens, and free inference still works when nothing else is configured. Method: real code and a real mint against the Nous account service, one process per scenario. Each run used a clean environment (`env -i`), a fake `HOME`, a temporary `HERMES_HOME` and its own shared-credentials folder, with `HERMES_GUEST_ONBOARDING=1`. Observed at `fed2ac2c35` (this PR) and `39faafb616` (`origin/main`). "Route" and "Account" are the values the backend returned for each fact; on `main` the account fact is the old `free_tier` key. | Scenario | Tree | `active_provider` in `auth.json` | Provider used | Banner model line | Route | Account | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | S1: nothing configured | main | `nous` | nous | free model | true | true | | | this PR | none | nous | free model | true | true | | S2: OpenRouter key before first launch | main | none | openrouter | free model (wrong) | false | true | | | this PR | none | openrouter | none | false | true | | S2b: key added after S1's first launch | main | `nous` (left by the mint) | openrouter | free model (wrong) | false | true | | | this PR | none | openrouter | none | false | true | | S3: `nous.guest: false` (free tier off) | both | none | none | none | false | false | Each run called `setup.status`, `setup.runtime_check`, `billing.state` and `free_tier.status` through the backend's real request handler. On this PR, in the S1 home, a real chat turn (`hermes -z "Reply with exactly one word: pong"`) answered `pong`, and `auth.json` still had no `active_provider` afterwards. The banner captures above came from a later run. The Nous account service had started rate-limiting new anonymous accounts, so `main`'s capture used a copy of this PR's S1 home with `active_provider: nous` added: the exact state `main`'s mint writes (row S1). ## Checks No new tests, by the maintainer's rule for this series. Existing tests change only where a rename or the removed write breaks them; one lifecycle test now asserts that the mint leaves `active_provider` unset and that `resolve_provider("auto")` still answers `nous`. - The shebang lint was red on `apps/desktop/electron/remote-lifecycle.test.ts:813` (`#!/bin/bash`, already on `main`). This PR carries @teknium1's one-line fix from #127265 as a cherry-picked commit, author kept. - CI for the current head (`438bf1e67a`) is running.

Source installs whose `~/.local/bin/hermes` was written by the May–July 2026 installer now converge on the current `.hermes/bin/hermes` forwarder on update, instead of running the retired `venv` forever.

Salvage of #123734 by @helix4u (cherry-picked, authorship preserved), plus one test follow-up.

**Who / when / why:** `scripts/install.sh` wrote `exec "$INSTALL_DIR/venv/bin/hermes" "$@"` into the user bin from 043a118d41 (May 6) until a7d5147cf1 (Jul 28). `_owns_launcher` recognises `venv/bin/python` and `<root>/hermes` wrappers but not that console-script form, so `_publish_conveniences` treated it as a user's file and skipped it on every update. Normal shells were rescued by the store-Python relaunch; shells with `HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS=1` fail with `No module named 'pydantic_core._pydantic_core'` (field report on #123734).

## Changes
- `hermes_cli/_launchers.py`: add `<root>/venv/bin/hermes` to the exact-token ownership set (@helix4u). Still root-bound exact tokens: other checkouts, comment mentions, `<root>-2/…` and `venv/bin/hermes-foo` stay untouched.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_source_launcher_publication.py`: the boot-migration test is parametrized over both legacy wrapper shapes (@helix4u); the follow-up folds the "another checkout's `venv/bin/hermes` is never adopted" case into that test's existing foreign wrapper and drops a standalone test that duplicated it, called the private `_publish_conveniences`, and asserted an mtime-derived flag right after writing the file (flaky on coarse-timestamp filesystems).

## Validation
| Check | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Real-import probe, exact install.sh wrapper | left as is | rewritten to `.hermes/bin/hermes` |
| Foreign wrappers (other checkout / comment / prefix sibling / `hermes-foo`) | untouched | untouched |
| `…legacy_conveniences[venv-console-script]` | fails | passes |
| Mutation: loose `endswith("venv/bin/hermes")` match | — | both cases fail (foreign wrapper adopted) |
| `test_source_launcher_publication.py` | — | 22 passed, 9 skipped (macOS) |

`scripts/install.sh` history has no `.venv/bin/hermes`, `venv/bin/hermes-acp` or `venv/bin/hermes-agent` wrappers, so no other legacy form is missing. `/usr/local/bin` wrappers of this shape come only from root FHS installs, which root updates.

Related: #76421. Earlier broader attempt: #76518 by @spfcraze (pre-PM update path, conflicts with current main).

Closes #123734

items.body:
## Outcome

A plugin calling the retired `tools.lazy_deps.install_specs` during agent construction no longer starts the full update takeover (PM sync + Desktop rebuild + relaunch loop) — it now gets a catchable `ImportError`, while the historical on-disk updaters still hand off to the takeover child. Part of #122326, salvage of #122341 by @Wenfengcheng (cherry-picked to preserve authorship).

## Root cause

Since 6a5a6a05d2 the `install_specs` shim unconditionally called `stop_for_relaunch()`, which is only meaningful inside an already-running historical updater. The community Hindsight plugin still calls it at runtime, turning every `hermes serve`/Desktop agent construction into a complete update + Desktop rebuild (#122326).

## Changes

- `tools/lazy_deps.install_specs` hands off to `stop_for_relaunch()` only inside a genuinely historical updater call stack, otherwise raises `ImportError` (matching sibling `ensure()`); decision is made from the caller stack, never argv (an in-process `/update` still shows `serve`/`gateway` in argv).
- `hermes_cli/_old_updater.in_historical_update()`: new shared predicate extracting the exact frame matcher `_historical_context` already used (module, function name, and `pre_update_version` in `co_varnames`), so the shim and the context detector cannot drift. This also fixes the salvaged matcher's gap: the CURRENT updater's `cmd_update` frames (version on `opts`, not a local) would also have handed off and exited the process mid-`hermes update`.
- `install_specs` accepts the `constraints`/`dry_run` kwargs historical updaters pass, so they reach the handoff instead of dying on `TypeError`.
- Tests collapsed to the real invariants (29 cases → 5): runtime/lookalike refusal (including a current-updater-shaped frame) and the historical handoff — now exercised through a nested helper so the frame walk itself is proven (a `getframe(1)`-only implementation fails the suite).

## Verification

Base `ea114c3e98` (fresh `origin/main`), macOS, canonical runner:

- Before: real-import probe of the base shim → takeover child spawned (`SystemExit`) on a plain runtime call; all 13 salvaged runtime tests red.
- After: runtime call → `ImportError`, zero child calls; current-updater-shaped frame (`hermes_cli.update_cmd`/`_cmd_update_impl`, no `pre_update_version` local) → `ImportError`, no takeover; historical frame through a nested helper → `SystemExit(0)` handoff with the correct request dict.
- Touched + sibling suites (`tests/tools/test_lazy_deps_runtime.py`, `test_old_updater_shims.py`, `test_old_updater_additional_shims.py`, `test_old_updater_takeover.py`, `test_old_updater_compat_surface.py`, `test_audit_old_updater_imports.py`, `pm/test_no_lazy_deps.py`, `test_update_lock.py`): **680 passed**, 0 new failures. The 39 pre-existing `test_old_updater_shims.py` failures are byte-identical on base and head (macOS `home_io_guard` TMPDIR-scratch trips), verified by failing-test-ID diff.
- Mutation check: replacing the frame walk with a single-caller check turns the nested-handoff tests red.

## Credit

Based on #122341 by @Wenfengcheng (commit 46ef6cce, author preserved); follow-up tightening in 4d3e393d. Also verified independently by @whyyagswhy on Linux at the original head.

items.body:
`hermes update` and an installer rerun now get a partial clone past git 2.53+'s `should_include_obj` pack-objects crash, including installs already stuck before fetch. The inert `-c remote.origin.promisor=` retry is replaced by marking the unmarked packs.

## Why

git 2.53+ `index-pack --promisor` hands every object outside the promisor packs to pack-objects, which BUG()s on the missing objects they lead to. A partial clone with packs lacking a `.promisor` marker keeps crashing fetches. Those packs come from filtered fetches that turned a full or depth-1 clone partial, and from checkouts that lost their markers (#123324).

The retry merged in #126150 (fc6144e3c1, from #124293) runs `git -c remote.origin.promisor= fetch`. git registers promisor remotes additively, so the repo's own `true` still wins. GIT_TRACE on 2.50 and 2.55 shows `index-pack --promisor` and `filter tree:0` under the override. The retry only passes when the crashed fetch already stored the pack; when it has to transfer again, it crashes again. That matches a Windows report where this exact command still crashed.

#126150's depth-1 heal (010618c767) also converts a depth-1 full clone to `tree:0` without marking its old pack. With git 2.55 every later fetch then crashed.

## Changes

- `gitlock.fetch_with_partial_clone_recovery`: on the crash, mark every pack that has no `.promisor` marker and retry the same fetch once. No config change, no refetch; the clone stays partial. If it still crashes, the updater points at the new docs section.
- Mark after conversion: `fetch_full_commit_graph` (depth-1 `tree:0` unshallow) and `worktree_ops._deepen_shallow_repo` (`--filter=blob:none`, bfd9cef389) mark the clone's old packs. git writes the partial-clone config before it fetches, so marking also runs when that fetch fails.
- Installers (`install.sh`, `install.ps1`): on an existing checkout whose origin is a promisor remote, mark the unmarked packs before fetching. The fetch runs in the installed code, so a stuck install can't pull an updater fix; the web-served installer is the path that reaches it.
- Docs: `getting-started/updating.md` gets the manual marker commands (POSIX and PowerShell). It also covers the missing-object backfill for checkouts that were already turned into full clones by hand, where `gc` fails with `bad tree object`.
- Review follow-up: `_deepen_shallow_repo` marks in its `finally` with no extra git call; installers warn instead of aborting when a marker can't be written; the docs commands follow `HERMES_HOME` and feed missing IDs through `fetch --stdin`.
- Includes #127149 by @foxion37 (cherry-picked, authorship kept): the recognizer also matches git 2.55's `fetch-pack: invalid index-pack output` wording.

## Validation

Real git 2.55 (Homebrew bottle) against local smart-transport fixtures:

| Scenario | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| depth-1 full install → `fetch_full_commit_graph` → 3 upstream moves + fetch | 3/3 fetches crash | 3/3 pass |
| stuck install (tree:0, markers lost) → `install.sh` `stage_repository` rerun | `git fetch failed` | updates to origin/main |
| updater recovery when upstream moves between crash and retry | retry crashes | retry passes |

- After marking: fetch, `fsck --connectivity-only`, `gc --aggressive --prune=now` and `stash apply` are all clean.
- Turning the promisor off and refetching main instead leaves objects that only release tags reach missing: `rev-list --all` / `gc` fail with `bad tree object`. That's why this PR doesn't do what #123403 does.
- Unit tests: 4 changed or new (recovery marks and retries the same argv, depth-1 conversion leaves no unmarked pack, blobless deepen leaves no unmarked pack, installer rerun marks and fetches). All four fail on origin/main and pass here.
- Update and installer test files (25): the failures on this branch are a subset of the failures on origin/main in the same local setup (home-I/O guard for checkouts under `~/.hermes`).

Fixes #123324
Refs #124272 (the promisor retry did not work), #125138

Supersedes #123403 and #123417 (@JoaoMarcos44). Salvages #127149 (@foxion37).

items.body:
If `~/.hermes/active_profile` names a deleted profile, `hermes profile use default` and `hermes uninstall` work again instead of exiting at startup. Every other command still refuses, and the error now names the command that gets you out.

Salvage of #127441 by @helix4u. Their commit is cherry-picked, so authorship is preserved. Two follow-ups are added on top, plus a docs commit.

## Changes

- **helix4u's fix.** When the sticky selector points at a missing profile, `profile list`, `profile use default` and `uninstall` run in the default home with a warning. `chat` and every other command, an explicit `-p <missing>`, and `uninstall --data` still exit 1.
- **Follow-up: stricter uninstall check.**
  - The guard checked for the literal string `--data`, but argparse accepts abbreviations. So `hermes uninstall --dat` got past it and removed the default root's data.
  - `--full` was allowed outright. In the default root, a full uninstall also deletes every other profile under `profiles/`.
  - The uninstall argv is now parsed with the real `uninstall` subparser, with its output silenced. It passes only when neither `data` nor `full` comes out true.
  - `uninstall --help` passes too, so the help prints once instead of help followed by an error.
  - The predicate lives in `hermes_cli/main_profile_recovery.py` instead of growing `main.py`.
- **Follow-up: clearer error.** The error used to say `Create it with: hermes profile create <name>`, which fails the same way. It now says `Switch back with: hermes profile use default`. An explicit `-p` keeps the old wording.
- **Docs.** `user-guide/profiles.md` describes what still runs in this state. It also notes that the plain interactive `hermes uninstall` menu still offers a full wipe of the default profile, behind its own confirmation prompts. `--full` is refused because it wipes without asking.

## Validation

Live run through the real entry point, with a temp HOME where `active_profile=ray` and `profiles/ray` is gone:

| command | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `profile use default` | exit 1 | exit 0, sticky cleared |
| `profile list`, `uninstall --yes --dry-run`, `uninstall --gui-summary`, `uninstall --help` | exit 1 | exit 0 |
| `uninstall --dat` / `--fu` / `--full` / `--data`, `chat` | exit 1 | exit 1, new hint |
| `-p ray uninstall` | exit 1 | exit 1, unchanged hint |

After recovery, switching between profiles works again: default → work → default.

`tests/hermes_cli/test_apply_profile_override.py`: 30 passed. Checked that the tests catch the bugs:
- The allow cases fail on origin/main.
- The abbreviated and `--full` block cases fail on helix4u's commit alone.
- The hint assertion fails without the last code commit.
- Reverting the `--help` handling fails its two cases.

items.body:
An unfinished update's final stage (product builds + maintenance) no longer starts another copy of itself when the update lock can't protect it.

Salvage of #123046 by @helix4u (cherry-picked; authorship preserved), plus a widening commit, a test and a comment cleanup.

## Changes
- `fix(update): prevent recursive source completion` (@helix4u, #123046): `prepare_launch` returns early when this process is the checkout's own `hermes_cli/source_completion.py`.
- `fix(update): hermes update's own tail no longer starts a second tail`: the same exemption covers `hermes_cli/update_completion.py`, `hermes update`'s own tail. Both scripts go through one identity check, `_is_tail_script` (exact script name plus resolved parent directory, compared against the process's own `argv[0]`, which the processes a tail spawns do not inherit).
- `test(update)`: a script with the same name outside the checkout still gets the repair.
- `refactor(update)`: one comment explains the exemption; the existing lock-ancestry comment now describes what it still covers (processes an update spawns).

## Why
Both tails import `hermes_cli.main` while the `source-completion-pending` marker is armed, so they run `prepare_launch` again. On main, the lock-ancestry check stops that only while the owning lock claim is live and writable. It misses three cases:
- a lock marker that can't be written (full disk, read-only home)
- a claim older than the 20-minute ceiling (a long product build)
- a tail run with no lock holder (installer / Desktop)

## Validation
Real process-chain probe (actual `subprocess` spawns, real `UpdateLock`), depth of nested final stages:

| Case | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| lock normal | 1 | 1 |
| lock unwritable | recursed to probe cap (6) | 1 |
| lock older than 20 min | recursed to probe cap (6) | 1 |
| no lock holder | 2 | 1 |
| `hermes update` tail, unwritable or stale lock | 1 extra tail, marker cleared early | 0 extra, marker kept |

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_launch_completion.py`: 22 passed. The parametrized test fails on main for both scripts. Dropping `update_completion.py` from the set fails its row. A name-only identity check fails the negative test.

Does not address #123340 (a supervised gateway retrying the unfinished stage on every restart). That is a separate fix.

The Desktop HUD's per-turn note ("this"/"here" means the app behind the HUD; `read_window_below` identifies it) fires again on default installs, where tool search defers the desktop tools.

**Who / when / why:** #97979 (@teknium1, merged 2026-09-02, `7e310f5037`) put the desktop GUI tools on the default `tool_search` defer list, a deliberate −49% cut in desktop schema size. `hud_surface_note()` (@OutThisLife's `e24bac49fa`, 2026-08-08) gates on `agent.valid_tool_names`, which lists only direct tools. With `read_window_below` behind the `tool_call` bridge, the note has been withheld on every HUD turn since. Found while reviewing #127285 and #127317, which fix it by un-deferring all 11 tools (+~2.5k tokens per Desktop session). This PR keeps the deferral.

- `agent/prompt_builder.py::hud_surface_note` takes the session's deferred-but-callable names and counts them as available. When a tool the note names (`read_window_below`, `computer_use`) is deferred, one sentence is added telling the model to call it through the `tool_call` bridge, because a direct call to a deferred name is rejected as an unknown tool.
- `tui_gateway/session_notifications.py::_hud_surface_note` passes `agent/tool_executor._tool_search_scoped_names(agent)`, only when the bridge is present. This is the same cached per-agent set that `tool_call` dispatch validates against, so the note never names a tool the session can't reach.
- Sessions without tool search get byte-identical note text (tool search off: 861 chars, unchanged).

**Validation**

| | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Real Desktop agent (`_load_enabled_toolsets("desktop")`, default config) | `read_window_below` deferred, HUD note **0 chars** | note **961 chars**, ends "Call read_window_below and computer_use through the tool_call bridge" |
| `tool_search.enabled: off` | 861 chars | 861 chars, identical |

- Tests: `tests/tui_gateway/test_hud_surface_note.py`, `test_voice_live_delegation.py`, `tests/agent/test_prompt_builder.py` → 74 passed, 1 skipped.
- 2 new tests:
  - A routing test that uses real toolset resolution and the real defer list. It goes red when `session_notifications.py` is reverted to main (`assert 'read_window_below' in ''`).
  - A unit test for the bridge sentence.

Refs #127095, #88006.

items.body:
## Outcome

Historical updaters from every release window now hand off to the takeover child again — including the 2026-07-26..08-16 window that af26acab73's `pre_update_version` check accidentally rejected — while current-tree updater frames still never do.

## Problem

The `in_historical_update()` gate added in af26acab73 (#127672) distinguished historical from current updater frames by requiring `pre_update_version` in `co_varnames`. History audit shows `_cmd_update_impl` only declared that local between 2026-08-16 and 2026-09-03; updaters before and after do not. For the 07-26..08-16 window (where `install_specs` first became reachable from the update path), a runtime `install_specs` call inside the updater would raise `ImportError` instead of handing off — the old update would print "Install failed" and continue on the pre-swap interpreter, exactly what the shim exists to prevent.

## Change

Invert the gate — detect the CURRENT updater instead of enumerating historical ones:

- `hermes_cli.update_cmd._cmd_update_impl` and `hermes_cli.main.cmd_update` declare a `_hermes_current_updater_frame = True` sentinel local; no historical on-disk version contains that name.
- `hermes_cli._old_updater.in_historical_update()` hands off on entrypoint match unless the sentinel is in the frame's `co_varnames`.
- Tests: the current-updater lookalike row mirrors the real sentinel-carrying frame; a new handoff row covers the version-less historical window.

## Verification

Base ea7c6a133 (fresh origin/main), macOS:

- Live probes (real imports, temp HERMES_HOME): runtime call → `ImportError`, 0 child spawns; current updater frame (sentinel) → `ImportError`, 0 child spawns; historical frame with `pre_update_version` → `SystemExit(0)` handoff; historical frame without it (07-26..08-16 shape) → `SystemExit(0)` handoff (regression fixed).
- Tests: all 6 lazy-deps/handoff tests pass; sibling suites (update_receipt, old_updater_additional_shims, old_updater_takeover, old_updater_compat_surface, pm/no_lazy_deps) 663 passed with 1 pre-existing environmental failure (`test_cmd_update_boundary_finalizes_on_early_exit` — `home_io_guard` TMPDIR trip, verified failing identically on clean origin/main).
- Mutation check: removing the sentinel check turns the current-updater refusal test red.
- `ruff check` and `git diff --check` clean.

A gateway started by systemd, launchd, s6 or the Windows task no longer re-runs an unfinished source-update tail on every start. That loop filled the disk in #123340. The tail is left to `hermes update`, and the start prints one line saying so.

Salvage of #123364 by @liuhao1024 (both commits cherry-picked; authorship preserved). Our follow-ups are on top.

## Changes
- `fix(update): keep supervised launches off the pending completion tail` and `fix(update): narrow the supervised-child exemption to the sticky tail` (@liuhao1024, #123364). When a process carries the `HERMES_SUPERVISED_CHILD` or `HERMES_S6_SUPERVISED_CHILD` launcher marker, its dependencies are current, and `source-completion-pending` exists, `prepare_launch` skips the tail and keeps the marker. Out-of-date dependencies still sync, run the tail once and relaunch, as before. `INVOCATION_ID` is deliberately not read, because systemd exports it to every descendant.
- `test(update)`: the marker off-value table (`0`/`false` still repay the tail) is folded into the supervised-launch test, so it checks behaviour instead of the private parser. Two tests in total.
- `fix(update)` + `refactor(update)`: a supervised start that leaves the tail owed prints `hermes: a source update is unfinished; run \`hermes update\` from a shell to finish it` to stderr. It prints once, in the process that boots, not in a parent that relaunches. Without it, a headless host running only the gateway would carry the unfinished tail (product builds, skills sync, config migration) with nothing telling the operator.

## Validation
Live probe: five restarts of `gateway run` in fresh interpreters, with a real spawn of a completion tail that keeps failing.

| Case | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `HERMES_SUPERVISED_CHILD=1`, deps current, marker pending | 5 tails | 0 tails, marker kept, 1 notice per start |
| `HERMES_SUPERVISED_CHILD=0` or unset | 5 tails | 5 tails (unchanged) |
| supervised, stale deps, no marker | 1 sync + 5 tails | 1 sync + 1 tail |

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_launch_completion.py`: 27 passed. Each of these breaks at least one test: main's condition, a presence-only marker parse (`0` counted as supervised), and removing the notice.
- The symbol-mapped suite (59 files) fails exactly the same test IDs on this branch and on main. Those failures come from local setup, not this change.

Not addressed here, same as the issue's other suggestions: a terminal `source-completion-failed` marker, disk or environment-count caps, and Dashboard Update refusal while a supervised gateway runs.

Fixes #123340.

## What

`hermes debug share` (paste.rs/dpaste and `--nous`), gateway `/debug`, the dashboard debug share and desktop `diagnostics.share_nous` no longer upload credential values from URLs in the logs, such as `?token=`, `?api_key=`, `?access_token=` and the password in `user:pass@host`.

## Why

- Log lines keep full URLs because log-time redaction deliberately leaves web URLs alone, so magic links and OAuth callbacks still work in tool flows. For example, Firecrawl logs every URL it scrapes at INFO.
- `_redact_log_text` runs `redact_sensitive_text(force=True)` on the copy being uploaded, but only `_capture_dump` (#127207) turned on `redact_url_credentials`. The log snapshots and the desktop error context and extra files were left in default URL mode.

## How

From #127426 (@Froraut): `_redact_log_text` now defaults `redact_url_credentials` to `True`. Every caller is on an upload path, and this is the same strict policy already used by compaction, cron, the kanban notifier and the connector payload. Parameter names, hosts and paths stay readable. Log files on disk and log-time redaction are unchanged, and `--no-redact` still turns redaction off.

Trade-off: the strict pass matches on parameter name, so uploaded logs also mask the values of `session=`, `code=`, `key=`, `sig=`/`signature=` and similar parameters.

## Tests

- `test_redaction_masks_url_credentials` fails with `main`'s `debug.py` (1 failed, 53 passed) and passes with the fix.
- Focused suites (`test_debug`, `test_dump_*`, `test_diagnostics_share_nous`, `test_redact`, `test_dashboard_admin_endpoints`, `test_sanitiser_escalation`, `test_compaction_redaction_boundaries`): 355 passed, 0 failed. ruff is clean.

items.body:
A live gateway that lost `gateway.pid` is now covered end to end by a real lock-holding process: the updater's strict discovery maps it, and every ambiguous state still fails closed.

Salvage of #122188 by @jquesnelle, cherry-picked so the commit stays authored by him. The `gateway/status.py` half of #122188 landed separately in #126133 (54684326), which left main covered only by a monkeypatched unit test; this carries over his live test file, which is what main is missing.

## Changes

- `tests/gateway/test_status_strict_identity_live.py` (from #122188): a child process takes `gateway.lock` through the real `acquire_gateway_runtime_lock` (flock on POSIX, msvcrt on Windows) and writes its PID file. Covers:
  - missing `gateway.pid` → identity resolves from the lock, equal to the identity with the PID file present
  - `find_profile_gateway_processes(strict=True)` maps the profile with no `gateway.pid` (the `hermes update` Windows pause path)
  - a PID file that disagrees with the lock → `identities disagree` (untested on main before this)
  - a garbled lock with no PID file → `malformed`
  - a lock held by a non-gateway process → `does not identify a live gateway`
- Follow-up commit (ours), test robustness only:
  - handshake read is bounded and stderr is captured, so a stuck or crashed child fails with a reason instead of hanging the worker
  - the holder blocks on stdin instead of `sleep(120)`, so it exits when pytest dies
  - `if not acquire…: sys.exit()` instead of `assert` (stripped under `-O`)
  - teardown kills the launcher tree plus the self-reported interpreter PID (Windows venv launcher) and reaps via `communicate()`; no more unclosed-pipe ResourceWarnings
  - discovery test pins `_get_default_hermes_home` / `_get_profiles_root` like `test_control_socket_windows_live.py` and compares resolved paths
  - one class-scoped holder with per-test restore of `gateway.pid` / `gateway.lock` (5 spawns → 2)
  - `utf-8-sig` read for the windows-footguns lane
- Second follow-up (review round): the holder is killed via the `psutil.Process` captured at spawn (a recycled PID is refused, not killed), `psutil.Error` is tolerated so one AccessDenied can't strand the tree, handshake bounded at 20s.

Five tests instead of the usual two: the two positive cases pin the fix; the three fail-closed cases (disagree, garbled, non-gateway holder) are the reason to keep a live file at all, since only a real holder proves the lock record the gateway actually writes is what gets validated.

## Validation

| | result |
|---|---|
| This file on current main (macOS, 3 runs) | 5 passed |
| With 54684326's `status.py` hunk reverted | 4 failed, 1 passed (the disagree case predates the fix, as expected) |
| With the PID-agreement check removed from `status.py` | disagree test fails |
| `tests/gateway/test_status.py` + `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway.py` + this file | 121 passed; 4 launchd/systemd failures identical on main on this host |
| `ruff`, `check-windows-footguns.py`, `check_subprocess_stdin.py` | clean |

No production code changes.

items.body:
The `clarify` tool now has one input shape and one result shape on every surface, so the model can always tell an answer, a skip, a cancel, a timeout and an undelivered question apart. Linear: NS-1007 (P03 of the onboarding rewrite map NS-973). | Before (desktop, one question) | After (desktop, one question) | |:---:|:---:| | ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df370ac1-9fd3-4cd7-967c-49b84a9322f6) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da45582e-db75-44fd-ba32-e94a89075181) | | Before (desktop, 1 of 3 answered) | After (desktop, 1 of 3 answered) | |:---:|:---:| | ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/998d7af5-14ef-4c9b-b1d4-0808afd75085) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/749cda08-176b-41ac-bfb3-e97dff80f7a9) | ## Background: the clarify tool `clarify` is the tool the agent calls to ask the user questions and wait for the reply. Five surfaces answer it: the CLI panel, the Ink TUI (`hermes --tui`), the desktop app's question card, messaging adapters (Telegram, Discord, Slack, …), and the no-user modes `-q` / `-z`. Each surface gives the tool a Python **callback**. The TUI and desktop reach the backend over `tui_gateway` JSON-RPC: the backend opens a `clarify` server request, and the client answers each question with `clarify.lock`. ## The problem There were two input shapes (a single top-level `question`, or a `questions` batch) and each surface ended the wait in its own way. The model could not tell these outcomes apart: | What happened | What the model got before | |---|---| | User skipped a question | `""` (TUI/desktop) — the same value as a timeout | | Wait timed out | CLI: `"The user did not provide a response within the time limit. Use your best judgement…"` as the user's answer. TUI/desktop: `""`. Messaging: `"[user did not respond within 60m]"` | | User pressed Ctrl+C | `"The user cancelled. Use your best judgement to proceed."` as the answer | | Question never shown | `[clarify prompt could not be delivered…]` as the answer | Sentences that read like the user's words went into `user_response`, and the context compressor had to recognise them by string prefix. The desktop also had two cards (single and batch). The batch card kept Confirm disabled until every question had an answer, so a user could not skip one question and send the rest. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Before A1[single question] --> S1[CLI / TUI / desktop / messaging
each with its own sentinel text] A2[questions batch] --> S1 S1 --> R1["user_response: '' or prose
(skip = timeout = cancel)"] end subgraph After B1["questions: [...] only"] --> S2[every surface, one callback contract] S2 --> R2["status per question +
one outcome + notice"] end ``` ## What changes **Model contract.** The only input is `questions: [{question, choices?, multi_select?}]` (1–5 questions). A wrong shape, such as the old top-level `question`, is a tool error that names the right shape; in the live runs a model recovered on its next call. The result is always: ```json {"responses": [ {"question": "Which colour?", "choices_offered": ["Blue","Red"], "status": "answered", "user_response": "Blue"}, {"question": "Which size?", "choices_offered": null, "status": "skipped", "user_response": null}, {"question": "Any notes?", "choices_offered": null, "status": "unanswered", "user_response": null}], "outcome": "timed_out", "notice": "…written by the surface: why the wait ended"} ``` - `status`: `answered`, `skipped` (the user sent this question empty), or `unanswered` (the wait ended before the user answered it). - `outcome`: `submitted`, `cancelled` (Skip, Esc, Ctrl+C, a new message, session end), `timed_out`, or `undelivered` (no surface could show it). **Callback contract** (every surface): `callback(questions) -> {"answers": {qid: raw | None}, "outcome", "notice"?}`. `None` means skipped; a missing id means unanswered. **Wire (TUI and desktop).** `clarify.lock` with `answer: null` skips a question. A response without `answers` cancels. `tui_gateway/server_requests.py` settles every ending with one mapping: ```mermaid flowchart TD W[open clarify request] -->|last clarify.lock| S[submitted + locked answers] W -->|response with answers| S W -->|response without answers| C[cancelled + locked answers] W -->|interrupt / session close / shutdown| C W -->|deadline| T[timed_out + locked answers] W -->|no client answered| U[undelivered] ``` **Surfaces** | Surface | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Desktop | Two cards. The single card had keyboard control; the batch card had none, and Confirm stayed disabled until every question had an answer | One card for 1–5 questions, with the keyboard control moved in: arrows, letters and digits, auto-advance to the next unanswered question, Enter picks and then confirms. Confirm enables at one answer; blank questions are sent as skipped. The settled card shows **Skipped** or **No answer** | | Ink TUI | Single and batch prompts; `multi_select` ignored | One prompt. Multi-select works: Space or a digit toggles, Enter locks, and typed Other text is added to the picks. An empty submit skips; Esc cancels | | CLI | Single panel plus batch panel; timeout and Ctrl+C sent prose | The batch panel only. Enter on an empty field skips; Ctrl+C returns `cancelled` and keeps the locked answers | | Messaging | One card per question; timeout prose | Each question card has a line "Reply "skip" to skip this question." (in all 17 locales). Timeout and delivery failure map to `timed_out` and `undelivered` | | `-q` / `-z` | Prose sentinel | `undelivered` + a no-user notice | | Desktop bots room card | Single branch through `request.answer` | Same contract: `clarify.lock` per question, ≥1 answer enables | Also: the tool-row preview shows the first question (it was blank). A multi-select answer that is not a JSON array counts as one typed answer; before, a messaging "Other" reply on a multi-select card made the whole call fail. ## What this deliberately does not do - **No back-compat.** The old shape, sentinel strings, dict choices and bare-string questions are gone from code, tests and docs. Old sessions keep working because the error tells the model the right shape. - **The timeout stays.** Removing it (pause instead of timeout) is #127708. - **One-string prompts** (sudo, secret capture, MCP setup) still collapse skip, timeout and cancel into `""`. That is #127708 too. - **Inline agent tools skip the shared argument repair** (`coerce_tool_args`), so clarify does not repair a JSON-string `questions`. That was already true before this PR; the stacked follow-up PR fixes it for every inline tool. ## Decisions reviewers should weigh 1. **Input leniency is cut.** Bare-string question items and dict-shaped choices now return errors instead of being converted. This follows the codebase convention: shared type repair runs in one place, and everything else gets a tool error that gives the shape. 2. **Desktop picks are staged until Confirm.** So on a timeout, picks the user did not confirm come back `unanswered`. The CLI and TUI lock each answer as it is picked, so they return partial answers. 3. **A one-question card needs two steps** (pick, then Enter or Confirm). The old single card sent on the first click. ## How to test ```bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_clarify_tool.py tests/tui_gateway/ tests/gateway/test_clarify_card_retire_on_timeout.py tests/gateway/test_clarify_delivery_fallback.py tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_clarify_batch.py tests/agent/test_context_compressor.py tests/agent/test_i18n.py cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/components/assistant-ui/clarify src/plugins/hermes-bots src/store/clarify.test.ts cd ui-tui && npx vitest run src/lib/text.test.ts src/__tests__/createGatewayEventHandler.test.ts ``` No new tests were added; existing tests were changed only where the contract change broke them. ## Live verification Observed on the tree committed as `d7ef458d5a`, rebased without conflicts to `92f3738c68`. Every run used a throwaway `HOME`/`HERMES_HOME`/`HERMES_SHARED_AUTH_DIR`, except the real-model rows, which read the existing Nous login in place. A scripted OpenAI-compatible fake model (`tests/fakes/fake_llm_provider.py`) sent the same clarify calls to every surface, and the table shows the result each surface returned to the model. | # | Scenario | CLI | Ink TUI | Desktop | Telegram (real gateway + adapter vs stand-in) | `-q` / `-z` | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | S1 | 1 question, answered | answered · submitted | — | answered · submitted (↓ then Enter, Enter) | answered · submitted (button) | unanswered · undelivered + notice | | S2 | 3 questions, some skipped | answered, answered, skipped · submitted | answered, answered, skipped · submitted | answered, skipped, skipped · submitted | answered, skipped (`skip`), answered · submitted | unanswered ×3 · undelivered | | S3 | multi-select + Other text | `["Cheese","Basil"]` | `["Cheese","Basil","Ham"]` | `["Cheese","Basil","Ham"]` | typed `1, 3` → `["Cheese","Basil"]`; Other → `["extra ham"]` | — | | S5 | cancel after one pick | Ctrl+C → answered, unanswered · cancelled | Esc → answered, unanswered · cancelled | Skip → cancelled; composer message → cancelled | — | — | | S6 | timeout after one pick | answered, unanswered · timed_out | answered, unanswered · timed_out | unanswered ×2 · timed_out (picks are staged) | answered, unanswered · timed_out + notice | — | | S7 | undelivered | — | — | — | send failures → undelivered + notice | see S1 | | S8 | reload mid-question | — | — | card restored and answerable | — | — | | S9 | old top-level shape | tool error naming the shape → next call answered | — | — | — | — | | S10 | desktop keys | — | — | letters, digits, arrows, Enter pick/confirm, auto-advance, focus moves to the open-ended field | — | — | **Real models** (branch code, Nous provider, clarify toolset only, a scripted user who answers question 1, skips question 2 and leaves question 3 unanswered). "Reads it right" means the final plan uses only the answered value and names the other two as assumptions. | Model | Calls | Shape | Outcome given | Reads it right | |---|---|---|---|---| | openai/gpt-5.6-terra | 1 | `questions[3]` | timed_out, cancelled | yes (one run put its own "Other" in `choices`) | | anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5 | 1 | `questions[3]` | timed_out, submitted | yes | | google/gemini-3.8-flash | 1 | `questions[3]` | timed_out | yes | | deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash | 1 | `questions[3]` | timed_out | yes | | moonshotai/kimi-k3 | 1 | `questions[3]` | timed_out | yes | | z-ai/glm-5.3 | 1 | `questions[3]` | timed_out | yes | | nous/welcome (free tier, fresh guest) | 1 | `questions[3]` | timed_out | yes | | qwen/qwen3.8-flash | not run: Nous Portal returned HTTP 429 (rate limit) | | | | | local model | not run: no local server on the test machine | | | | Not shown by this evidence: Discord and Slack adapters (same gateway path as Telegram, not driven), and CI on the final tree (pending at the time of writing).

items.body:
Inline agent tools (clarify, todo_list, memory, session_search and the rest) now get the same argument repair as every other tool, so a model that sends a JSON-encoded string for an array parameter no longer gets an error.

Independent of #127760 (clarify contract); either can merge first.

## The problem

`model_tools.handle_function_call` runs `tools/arg_coercion.py::coerce_tool_args` on every tool call. This is the codebase's one place for repairing argument types: it turns `"42"` into `42`, `"true"` into `true`, a JSON string into an array or object, and a single value into a one-item list. It uses the tool's schema and changes a value only when the fix has one clear answer.

Agent-level "inline" tools never reach `handle_function_call`. `agent/tool_executor.py::_resolve_sequential_dispatch` (sequential path) and `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py::invoke_tool` (concurrent path) both call `INLINE_TOOL_EXECUTORS` directly. So these tools got no repair:

- `clarify` rejected a `questions` array sent as a JSON string.
- `todo_list` handled the same mistake with its own `json.loads` block.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  M[model tool call] --> D{inline tool?}
  D -- no --> H[handle_function_call] --> C[coerce_tool_args] --> R[registry tool]
  D -- yes, before --> I[INLINE_TOOL_EXECUTORS] --> T[tool gets raw args]
  D -- yes, after --> I2[INLINE_TOOL_EXECUTORS] --> C2[coerce_tool_args] --> T2[tool]
```

## What changes

- Every entry in `INLINE_TOOL_EXECUTORS` is wrapped to run `coerce_tool_args(name, args)` first. Both dispatch paths read that one table, so one wrapper covers both.
- `tools/todo_tool.py` no longer parses a JSON string by hand. Its schema declares `todos` as an array, so the shared repair covers it.
- One existing todo test called `todo_tool` directly, which skips dispatch. It now calls the dispatch table. No new tests.

## Not in scope

- Memory-provider tools on the concurrent path have no registry schema, so the repair has nothing to act on there. That is the same as before.

## How to test

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_todo_tool_type_coercion.py tests/agent/ tests/tools/test_clarify_tool.py
```

items.body:
`hermes config check` now reports saved `platform_toolsets` names that no longer resolve, and bundled platform plugins that are disabled while their required credentials are configured. It judges both the way the runtime does.

Salvage of #127392 by @helix4u. Their commit is cherry-picked, so authorship is preserved. Two follow-up commits fix what review found before landing.

## Changes

- **Stale toolset names:** `config check` and `hermes config migrate` now share one resolver, `toolset_validation.saved_toolset_resolver`. Before this, migrate warned about MCP server names and plugin-platform bundles (it even suggested `'hermes-teams'` for `'hermes-teams'`). The new check accepts them.
  - A configured MCP server counts as known even when it has `enabled: false`. It is inactive, not a typo.
  - `known_plugin_toolsets` no longer counts as proof that a toolset exists. It records what a platform was offered at save time, so it hid toolsets from uninstalled plugins, which is exactly the stale case this check exists for.
  - Plugin-provided names and the platform-manifest scan are only consulted for names the cheaper checks cannot place. A clean config never runs plugin discovery.
- **Disabled platforms:** `plugins.disabled` is read through the runtime's own reader. A non-list value, which the runtime ignores, is no longer reported as disabling a platform. Required credentials come from `_platform_manifest_env_entries(optional=False)`, so optional vars never count.
- **Crash fix:** a malformed `mcp_servers` (for example a list) no longer crashes the command.
- **Dropped check:** the original PR also checked the top-level `toolsets` key. The CLI resolves toolsets from `--toolsets` or `platform_toolsets` and reads the top-level key only for the legacy kanban opt-in, so that check is gone.
- **Not included:** the original PR's Desktop fixture-shebang commit. It is byte-identical to #127265, which is still open.

## Validation

| Case (real `hermes config check`, temp `HERMES_HOME`) | Original #127392 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `platform_toolsets.cli` lists a removed name | reported | reported |
| toolset of an uninstalled plugin, remembered in `known_plugin_toolsets` | silent | reported |
| MCP server with `enabled: false` listed in `platform_toolsets` | "unknown toolset … did you mean 'hermes-cli'?" | silent |
| `mcp_servers: [a]` | `AttributeError` traceback | runs |
| `plugins.disabled: platforms/telegram` (string) with token | "disabled" (runtime still loads it) | silent |
| `plugins.disabled: [platforms/telegram]` with token | reported | reported |
| fresh config | silent | silent, no plugin discovery |

- Tests: 2 invariant tests in `tests/hermes_cli/test_config_check_diagnostics.py`, red on the original commit and green here.
  - Test 1 asserts that `config check` and migrate report the same names across A→B→A homes. Mutating migrate back to bare `validate_toolset` turns it red.
  - Test 2 uses a synthetic platform manifest rather than Telegram's.
- The 34 test files that reference `platform_toolsets`, `_platform_manifest_env_entries` or `migrate_config` give identical results on this branch and on `origin/main`: 852 passed, 17 failed and 8 errors on both, and the failures are the same set.
- `ruff check` on the touched files, and the Windows footgun checker, are clean.

## Known limits

- `platform_toolsets.cli: [no_mcp]` on its own is still not reported. `validate_platform_toolsets` counts `no_mcp` as a valid toolset.
- When the config names something the cheaper checks cannot place, migrate now runs plugin discovery. It stays inside the existing best-effort `try/except` and under the profile's own plugin scope.

## Credit (post-merge sweep)

Earlier PRs fixed parts of the migrate-side false positives that this resolver now covers. They were closed as resolved, with credit:
- #107104 (@kokhlo): plugin-platform `hermes-<platform>` bundles. This was the first submitted fix.
- #109844 (@prasta1): plugin toolsets judged before plugin discovery.
- #126333 (@686f6c61): the self-referential hint.
- #106715 (@a692570): MCP server names. The `mcp-<server>` half lands as a follow-up.

items.body:
The gateway's first-contact note now fires only in direct messages, and its "offered" flag is saved in the same profile it is read from.

Linear: NS-1009 (P05 of the onboarding rewrite map NS-973).

## Background: the first-contact note

On the first message a profile ever receives through the messaging gateway, Hermes adds a one-shot note to that user message: a plain intro, or (when `onboarding.profile_build` is `ask`) an opt-in offer to build a user profile in the profile's `USER.md`. A flag, `onboarding.seen.profile_build_offered` in `config.yaml`, makes the offer fire once. Under **multiplex** one gateway process serves several profiles; each inbound message runs inside its routed profile's scope (`gateway/run_adapters.py::_make_default_profile_message_handler`).

## The problem

1. **Group chats.** `_hmwa_first_contact_notes` (`gateway/run_turn.py`) had no chat-type check, so the note could fire on a group's first message and ask the model to save a group member's facts into the owner's `USER.md`.
2. **Flag written to the wrong profile.** The flag was read from the routed profile (`_load_gateway_config()` → `_gateway_config_home()`), but written to `gateway.run._hermes_home / "config.yaml"`, a module constant bound to the launch profile. Under multiplex the routed profile never got marked, so its offer could repeat, and the launch profile was marked instead.

## What changes

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Where the note fires | First message of any chat | First message in a DM (`chat_type == "dm"`) on a messaging platform (not local or webhook) |
| Where the flag is written | Launch profile's `config.yaml` | `_gateway_config_home() / "config.yaml"`, the routed profile, the same file it is read from |
| Docs (`configuration.md`) | "the very first gateway message ever … at most once" | "a profile's first direct message through the gateway (never in a group chat) … at most once per profile" |

The one-time "no home channel" prompt keeps its exact condition; it now reads it from the same `human_platform` check.

## Checked and left alone (the issue listed them)

- **Built-in commands run outside the routed profile scope:** not the case. `_hm_cmd_*` runs inside `_handle_message`, which the adapter handler already wraps in the routed profile scope.
- **Hyphenated built-in names break the `getattr` lookup:** no name in `_HM_CANONICAL_COMMANDS` has a hyphen, so there is nothing to fix.
- **First contact per install vs per profile:** it is already per profile; `has_any_sessions()` reads the active profile's own `state.db` (`gateway/session_persistence.py::_db`).

## Proof

Code reading only, by decision: no new tests and no live run for this change. `SessionSource.chat_type` defaults to `"dm"`, so existing tests that build a source without it keep the old path. CI on this head is pending.

items.body:
## What this PR does

Two places in the desktop app used long `if` chains that tested one name after another:

- The first picks the custom widget a tool call shows in the chat. We call that widget a **tool card**: for example the question card for `clarify`, or the image for `image_generate`. A tool with no card shows the **plain tool row**, the small expandable line every other tool call gets.
- The second reacts to **bridge events**: one-way messages from the agent that tell the desktop app to do something, such as show a tip bubble or apply a layout.

This PR replaces each chain with a lookup table: one row per name, and one lookup. Nothing the user sees changes.

This is cleanup before the desktop onboarding rewrite ([NS-1008](https://linear.app/nousresearch/issue/NS-1008)). Later onboarding work adds two new tool cards (`setup_choose`, `start_chat`) and hooks into the `layout.apply` bridge event. After this PR, each new card or event is one new row in a table. The repo rule in the root `AGENTS.md` asks for the same shape: no `if` chain of 4 or more branches keyed on a name.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Before
    A1[tool call] --> B1{delegate_task?} -->|no| C1{image_generate?} -->|no| D1{clarify?} -->|no| E1{manage_catalog?} -->|no| F1{manage_connections?}
  end
  subgraph After
    A2[tool call] --> B2{name is a key in TOOL_CARDS?} -->|yes| C2[that row's card]
    B2 -->|no| D2[plain tool row]
  end
```

## Table 1: tool cards (`components/assistant-ui/thread/message-parts.tsx`)

| Tool name | Card it shows (unchanged) |
|---|---|
| `clarify` | The question card. A question the turn stopped on, never answered, shows the plain tool row. |
| `delegate_task` | The list of subagents it started. A failed call shows the plain tool row. |
| `image_generate` | The generated image. A failed call shows the plain tool row. |
| `manage_catalog` | The plugin/skill install card. |
| `manage_connections` | The card that sets up local MCP servers (tool servers the agent can run) when the call adds one; otherwise the card for hosted connectors such as Gmail. |

Three name checks stay in front of the table, because each needs more than a name: `todo` tools (drawn in their own panel), a `terminal` call that messages another agent (drawn as a short notice), and `react_to_message` (the emoji lands on the message bubble instead). Everything after the table is unchanged.

## Table 2: bridge events (`gateway-event/desktop-bridge.ts`)

Each handler body and its comments moved into its row unchanged.

| Event | Sent by | What the app does (unchanged) |
|---|---|---|
| `agent.terminal.output` | a background process | streams output into the agent's read-only terminal tab |
| `terminal.close` | `close_terminal` tool | closes that tab; the process keeps running |
| `tip.show` | `show_tip` tool | shows a tip bubble (active chat only) |
| `pane.reveal` | `focus_pane` tool | opens or focuses a pane (active chat only) |
| `layout.apply` | `apply_layout` tool | applies a layout preset (active chat only) |
| `message.reaction` | `react_to_message` tool | paints the emoji on the message now |

The lookup checks `Object.hasOwn` first (the same guard `tools-list.tsx` uses). Without it, an event whose name matches a built-in object property, such as `toString`, would find that property and run it as a handler.

## One list of card names, checked by the compiler

`lib/tool-render-class.ts` already kept a list of card tools. Two other parts of the chat read it: the step that folds finished tool calls into a one-line summary, and the step that limits how much of a long chat is kept on screen. Both leave card tools out. So that list and the old `if` chain had to agree, and nothing checked that they did.

Now that list exports its names as a TypeScript type, `CardToolName`, and `TOOL_CARDS` is typed `Record<CardToolName, FC>` (a map from every card name to a React component). A card name added in one place and not the other fails the type check (`tsc`).

One code move: `manage_connections` joined that list from a separate check inside `isCardTool`. `isCardTool` returns the same result for every name, so behaviour is unchanged.

## What this does not do

- No visible change.
- No new tests: behaviour is identical, and the compiler now enforces that the two lists agree.
- No new comments: handler comments moved with their code, word for word.
- It does not touch the card components themselves. Other onboarding issues own those.
- It does not merge the "draw nothing" checks in the chat with `SILENT_TOOL_NAMES`, a second list in `lib/tool-render-class.ts` of tools that draw nothing. That list's comment says a failed `todo` call still draws a row, but the chat hides every `todo` call. Making them agree changes behaviour, so it is left for a follow-up.

## Live verification

The same scripted run was driven over the Chrome DevTools Protocol (a remote-control port on the desktop app) against two builds: **before** = `main` at `914d4fcaf5` (this branch's base), **after** = this branch at `41536274d4`. Each run used a throwaway home directory and a fake model server that answers each test message with one scripted tool call, so both builds saw the same calls in the same order. Tool search was turned off in that sandbox so the desktop tools are called directly.

| Step | What the fake model called | Observed (both builds) | Before vs after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Seeded history | one past call of every card kind, written straight into the session database | clarify row, subagent card, generated image, failed image as a plain row, catalog and connections rows | identical |
| `apply_layout` / `focus_pane` | `layout.apply`, `pane.reveal` | Review, Files and Terminal panes open | identical |
| Background command, then `close_terminal` | `agent.terminal.output`, `terminal.close` | the command's terminal tab appears | identical |
| `react_to_message` | `message.reaction` | 👍 lands on the user's message | identical |
| `show_tip` | `tip.show` | tip bubble points at the composer | identical |
| plain `terminal` call | none (not a card) | plain tool row | identical |
| `clarify` | none (live card) | question card with choices, Skip, and Confirm | identical structure (see below) |

The page structure (every element's `data-slot` marker, in order) and the text of the chat were compared after each step: 8 of 10 steps match exactly. The other two are artifacts of the test drive, not of this change: the first message of the before-run went out before its backend was ready, and in the after-run the collapsed `Show Tip` row had been expanded (the same plain row in both builds; `show_tip` is not a card, so this PR does not touch its path). The drive did not check whether `close_terminal` removed the tab; that tab was still listed afterwards in both builds.

This covers the rendering and event paths. Live cards that need a signed-in portal (the connector card) or the setup profile (the catalog install card) were only seen as history rows.

<!-- before-and-after:start -->
| Before (Seeded history: every card kind) | After (Seeded history: every card kind) |
|:---:|:---:|
| ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/906f77d4-e02a-433c-bbb2-5740fac1f106) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1eee0486-44a4-4334-a1a8-321dec21c20e) |

| Before (Live run: reaction, tip, clarify card) | After (Live run: reaction, tip, clarify card) |
|:---:|:---:|
| ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d255b15-637f-4e18-a44e-f4d7e4aceaf8) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e6cd49f7-60b8-4532-ace5-1a340036b68d) |

<!-- before-and-after:end -->

## Checks

- `tsc -p .` and `eslint` on the three changed files: clean.
- CI: pending at the time of writing.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

A checkpoint of a directory that contains a nested git repository stores that repository as a gitlink (a commit reference), not its files. On main, `/rollback` then reports success while the nested repository's uncommitted work stays overwritten (#127073).

This salvages @dskwe's #127077 (Yuan Li's three original commits are kept with their authorship) and finishes the fix:

- A full rollback, or a selection that touches a gitlink (the gitlink itself, a file below it, or a parent directory), is refused before any file, index, ref or pre-rollback snapshot changes. The error names the uncaptured repositories.
- Selections that don't touch a gitlink still restore, **including Git pathspecs** (`*.txt`, `:(glob)…`, `:(exclude)tool`). Git resolves the selection against a throwaway index first, so a wildcard that would reach a gitlink is refused, and one that doesn't behaves as it does on main. (#127077's current head rejects all pathspecs, which removes the `*.txt` recovery that works on main.)
- The guard selects by the path **recorded in the checkpoint**, normalised without touching the filesystem. It no longer follows today's symlinks: a captured `notes.txt` that has since become a symlink into a nested repo is recoverable again. A recorded gitlink replaced by an unrelated symlink is still refused. Resolved-path confinement is unchanged in `_validate_file_path`.
- **Checkpoint-time disclosure:** a checkpoint that stores a gitlink gets `[nested git repos not captured: tool]` added to its message (first three paths, then `+N`). Every `/rollback` listing already shows that message, so no contract or locale changes are needed.
- `rollback.list` (TUI/Desktop) read a `message` key that the manager calls `reason`, so those listings never showed a checkpoint's description. It's now mapped from `reason`, which also makes the new label visible there.
- Components are split with the platform's `Path`, so `packages/nested` and `packages\nested` both refuse on Windows. This covers the Windows path-normalisation finding in the latest review of #127077.

## Related Issue

Fixes #127073. The issue asks that nested repos either be captured or that "the checkpoint and rollback say plainly that the nested repo was **not** captured". This PR does the second: the checkpoint is labelled when it's taken, and rollback refuses. Capturing nested repositories' files is left as a possible follow-up feature.

Supersedes #127077 with credit. Thanks @dskwe for the fix, @andrexibiza for the review rounds, and @Froraut for the report and macOS testing.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `tools/checkpoint_manager.py`: gitlink guard in `_restore`, using a lexical scope check and then Git's own selection through a disposable index; NUL-safe tree parsing.
- `tests/tools/test_checkpoint_gitlinks.py` (new) and `tests/tools/test_checkpoint_manager.py`: real-Git contracts. Refusals are non-mutating (working files, store refs, index and ledger compared byte-for-byte) across full, safe and scoped restores, wildcard and magic pathspecs, and a deleted nested repo. Also covered: unrelated recovery, unusual and non-UTF-8 filenames, inspection failure, symlink replacement both ways, and a gitlink below an ordinary directory in every spelling.
- `tools/checkpoint_manager.py` `_take`: labels checkpoints containing gitlinks (shared `_gitlink_paths` parse).
- `tui_gateway/methods_tools.py`: `rollback.list` maps `message` from the checkpoint `reason`; test in `tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py`.
- `website/docs/user-guide/checkpoints-and-rollback.md`: documents the gitlink limitation, the label and the refusal.

## How to Test

1. Create `work/tool` as a committed git repo, add `work/notes.txt`, take a checkpoint of `work`, then edit `tool/main.py` and `notes.txt`.
2. `/rollback` lists the checkpoint as `… [nested git repos not captured: tool]`. `/rollback 1` refuses and names `tool`. On main it reports success and `tool/main.py` stays overwritten.
3. `/rollback 1 notes.txt` restores `notes.txt` and leaves `tool/` untouched.
4. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_checkpoint_gitlinks.py tests/tools/test_checkpoint_manager.py`

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs (#127077 is salvaged here; #127435 does not detect gitlinks; #127516 has no implementation)
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass: the checkpoint, rollback and TUI-contract suites (55 files, 1732 passed, 25 skipped) on Linux, not the full suite
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu (Linux 6.8), system Git

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example`: N/A
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md`: N/A
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered: Windows separator cases are parametrised to run on Windows; symlink tests skip on Windows. Native Windows/macOS execution is left to CI.
- [x] Tool descriptions/schemas: N/A (no schema change)

Co-authored-by: Yuan Li <dskwelmcy@163.com>
Co-authored-by: FroRaut <79215537+Froraut@users.noreply.github.com>
