## Summary

#99859: long-lived processes freeze `sys.modules` at boot. After `hermes update`, the code-skew watchdog (979c7baeef) retired stale backends — but only SSH-isolated ones — while Desktop-owned local `hermes serve` backends (which the updater equally never restarts) kept serving stale modules, and only the picker endpoint refused.

Two focused increments:

1. **Widen the self-heal (R1):** `start_code_skew_watchdog` is now also wired for Desktop-owned local backends (`is_desktop_owned_backend()`), not just `ssh_isolated` clients — both have the "updater never restarts me" property; the Desktop's ownership ledger drives the reconnect-respawn on new code.
2. **Centralize the skew refusal (R2):** `POST /api/model/set` and the tui_gateway `model.options` / `model.save_key` JSON-RPCs now refuse with the same "restart required" message `GET /api/model/options` and the gateway `/model` switch already return (new error code 5098, existing i18n key `gateway.model.err_skew`), so no model-mutating path can hand a stale-module string to a provider.

R3 (deleted-profile eviction) is partially covered on main by tombstones (7e34522454); R4 (Bots UI provisioning through `create_profile`) is deliberately out of scope here.

## Test plan

- [x] Green on this branch (rebased): `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_cli/test_code_skew.py tests/tui_gateway/test_model_rpc_skew_guard.py tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_skew_exit.py` → 19 passed, 0 failed (incl. new: stale `model.set` returns 503 and skips the assignment apply; stale `model.options`/`model.save_key` answer 5098 without reaching the payload build; fresh paths unchanged)
- [x] Red equivalents verified against origin/main sources by construction: the guard calls and the 5098 branch do not exist there.

## Limitations

- The watchdog widening trusts `is_desktop_owned_backend()` process identity the same way the existing cron-ticker path does.
- Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/100216 (stale since 2026-09-01, conflicting, predates the watchdog).

items.body:
## Root cause

One typed message could be persisted into two sessions, and a single turn's rows could split across a parent and its continuation session, in two related ways:

1. **Off-turn writes used a stale `session_key` (#123545).** The submit path wrote the user row under `session['session_key']` while the turn's own rows flush under `agent.session_id`, and the two diverge for the whole of a turn that begins after a compression rotation moved the agent onto the continuation (`session_key` is re-anchored only at turn end). One message then landed as user rows in two sessions, and tool rows split across them.
2. **The busy-queue envelope held a dead row id across an in-place compaction (#123675).** `archive_and_compact`'s concurrent-append path deactivates the accept-time row and clones it to a fresh id, but the drain's `deactivate_message` and the merge's `set_user_message_content` addressed the dead original — leaving the queued prompt active twice after the drain, or a text-only merge a silent no-op.

## What changes

Combines #123635 and #123676 (their queue hunks overlap; the two fixes compose — owner-session addressing AND live-row re-resolution):

- `_submit_row_target_key` picks the session the turn will actually write (`agent.session_id` or `session_key`, recorded once on the staged dict) and every off-turn writer is addressed by it: `_write_submit_user_row`, the @-expansion rewrite, the queue merge/drain, `_append_model_switch_marker`, `message.react` newest_role, `session.history`, and the out-of-band probe.
- Model-switch durable rows no longer accumulate across switches: superseded markers are deactivated by `display_kind` (the durable counterpart of the in-memory strip), leaving one live row.
- New `SessionDB.resolve_active_row_id(row_id)`: the row itself while active, else the single clone with same role/content/timestamp, `None` when ambiguous. The drain deactivate and the merge update both re-resolve through it; the envelope's staged row is dropped when no live row remains.
- The transcript read addresses the rotated tip (continuation) after a rotation.

## Acceptance coverage per issue

- #123545: one typed message persists as a user row in exactly one session; a turn's rows never split across parent/child after a rotation; off-turn writers target the live session; model-switch rows don't accumulate — `tests/tui_gateway/test_submit_row_session_target.py` (9 tests) drives the real `publish_compression_child` rotation against a real SessionDB.
- #123675: a queued prompt is active exactly once after an in-place compaction + drain; a text-only merge updates the live clone — `tests/tui_gateway/test_queued_prompt_persistence.py` (2 new tests, real SessionDB + real `_handle_busy_submit`/`_drain_queued_prompt`).

## Tests run

- `HERMES_PYTHON=$RUN/test-venv/bin/python bash scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tui_gateway/test_submit_row_session_target.py tests/tui_gateway/test_queued_prompt_persistence.py` — on main: RED (11 failed across both files); with fix: **18/18 green**.
- Same runner for queue/submit-adjacent suites (`test_tui_gateway_queue_on_busy.py`, `test_submit_time_user_row.py`, `test_model_switch_marker_role.py`, `test_busy_compression_demotion.py`, `test_message_metadata.py`, `test_message_sequence_repair.py`, `test_merged_user_override.py`, `hermes_state/test_message_uid.py`, `agent/test_context_engine_message_uid.py`) — **all green (135 tests)**.
- The one failure seen in the huge `test_tui_gateway_server.py` file (`test_profile_scoped_agent_build_starts_mcp_discovery_in_profile_home`, an `agent_ready` Event 5s wait) reproduces identically on pristine `origin/main` under this machine's load — a pre-existing timing flake, not touched by this diff. This branch's modified test in that file passes.

Fixes #123545
Fixes #123675

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/123635 (Thanks @Halldrix — all 9 commits cherry-picked with authorship kept)
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/123676 (Thanks @Totoro-qaq — the composed commit is co-authored)

Notes for review:
- Composes with (does not collide with) #126999's queued-row restart retire: that PR's `_queued_prompt` display_metadata marker and this PR's owner-key/row-id re-resolution touch adjacent hunks of `_persist_queued_user_row`/`_replace_queued_user_row_for_turn` and should be merged in one coordinated pass.
- The model-switch deactivation interacts with the #65891 in-memory strip as documented in the code comments.

items.body:
## Root cause

Both speech-text normalizers handle Markdown/URLs/symbols but have no pass
for identifier-dense tokens — `apps/desktop/src/lib/speech-text.ts`
(`sanitizeTextForSpeech`) and `tools/tts_text_normalize.py`
(`prepare_spoken_text`). A filename like `peyton-sample-20260922.wav` reaches
the TTS engine verbatim and is read character by character
("peyton dash sample dash two zero two six..."), so clean synthesized audio
sounds corrupted (#119207).

## Fix

One identifier-to-speech pass, mirrored token-for-token in both normalizers:

- `tools/tts_text_normalize.py` — `prune_identifier_tokens_for_tts`,
  wired into `prepare_spoken_text` after the symbols pass (gateway auto-TTS,
  voice-mode streaming, explicit TTS calls).
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/speech-text.ts` — `pruneIdentifierTokens` in
  `sanitizeTextForSpeech`, after code fences/links/URLs/MEDIA: tokens are
  consumed (Read Aloud, auto-speak replies).

Detection: filename-with-extension tokens, hex-hash runs and
`sha256:…`-prefixed digests, UUIDs, dense model/version IDs
(`meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct`, `v2.1.0-beta.3`), and filesystem
paths. Matched tokens become **silence** — never a hardcoded English
placeholder word, per the #86602 lesson (the reply may be in any language).
Ordinary prose, email addresses, dates (`2026/06/02`), ratios (`3:2`) and
short hyphenated words (`COVID-19`, `well-known`) pass verbatim.

Also fixes a pre-existing `smooth_whitespace_for_tts` bug the new corpus
surfaced: `user@example.com` was spoken as "user@example. com" because the
punctuation-spacing pass split any punctuation-followed-by-letter pair; it
now only splits when the punctuation is not glued to a word character.

## Coverage per requirement (#119207)

- Identifier pass in `speech-text.ts`: corpus tests fail on base (filenames
  spoken verbatim), pass with the fix.
- Same identifier policy in `tts_text_normalize.py`: same corpus, pytest.
- Both normalizers agree on the same tokens: one shared corpus
  (`tests/fixtures/identifier_speech_corpus.json`) asserted by both
  `tests/tools/test_tts_identifier_speech.py` and
  `apps/desktop/src/lib/speech-text.identifier-corpus.test.ts`.
- Normal replies no longer sound corrupted: prose around replaced tokens is
  asserted to survive ("Saved ... and ...").

## Checks run

- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tools/test_tts_identifier_speech.py tests/tools/test_tts_text_normalize.py tests/tools/test_tts_prepare_spoken.py` — 25 passed
- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/lib/speech-text.identifier-corpus.test.ts src/lib/speech-text.test.ts` — 36 passed
- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/lib/voice-playback.routing.test.ts src/lib/voice-playback.same-turn.test.ts` — 9 passed (downstream consumers)
- Red on base: corpus test against `origin/main`'s `speech-text.ts` — 2 failed / 2 passed; with the fix, 4 passed.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/119212

Thanks @KoNit-K — the desktop-half normalization approach and its test
corpus (filenames, paths, UUIDs, dense identifiers, ordinary-prose control)
are reused here; this PR extends the policy to the gateway/CLI normalizer
that #119212 left untouched and replaces the spoken labels with silence so
non-English voices are never handed English placeholder words.

Fixes #119207

## Root cause

The original misclassification (a 401 from `POST /api/auth/ws-ticket` reported as "Could not reach the remote Hermes gateway") was the fetch layer never attaching `err.statusCode`; that hole is **already fixed on main** by #95701 (shared `httpStatusError` in `api-transport.ts:183-191`, used by `fetchJson`, `fetchPublicJson`, and the OAuth-session fetch), and `gatewayTicketFailure` (`connection-config.ts`) classifies 401/403 → `needsOauthLogin`/`isReauthRequired` with sign-in copy. #96449/#98656 (the hand-rolled duplicates of that fix) were correctly rejected/withdrawn.

The **still-live defect** (djmango's fleet evidence in #98647): every non-auth mint failure — timeout, `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`, DNS failure, 502 — was wrapped in one undifferentiated sentence (`remote-oauth-ticket.ts:38` passed a static string as `transportMessage`), so ~1,100 log lines across three different upstream causes all read identically and the diagnostic cost stayed high even after the auth/transport split was fixed.

## What changed

- `connection-config.ts` — new exported `gatewayTicketTransportMessage(error)`: names the actual transport failure class in user-facing copy — timeout/unreachable/DNS → "timed out or the host could not be resolved… check your network/VPN path", `ECONNREFUSED` → "connection was refused… the gateway process is likely down", anything else keeps the legacy one-liner.
- `remote-oauth-ticket.ts` — `resolveRemoteOauthTicket` passes `gatewayTicketTransportMessage(error)` instead of the static sentence. Auth classification is untouched: 401/403 still route to the sign-in copy with `needsOauthLogin`/`isReauthRequired` (covered by the existing parametrized test).
- `remote-oauth-ticket.test.ts` — behavioural test: timeout/DNS/refused/ambiguous/500 produce the expected distinct copy, and none of the transport classes ever read as an auth failure (`isReauthRequiredError` false, no `needsOauthLogin` tag).

Refs #98647 (the primary requirement — 401 misreported as "could not reach" — is already met on main by #95701; this PR closes the remaining live sub-defect from the issue thread. #96449 was rejected as a duplicate of #95701, so nothing is superseded here.)

## Tests actually run

- `vitest run --project electron electron/remote-oauth-ticket.test.ts electron/connection-config.test.ts` — pass
- `npm run check:lint` — pass

Off (hitl): user-facing error-copy change in the remote-gateway auth path; per the sweep rules for auth-cluster PRs.

items.body:
The desktop main process holds several module-level registries; #58485 reported its V8 heap climbing to the ~4GB ceiling over about an hour of normal use. The renderer-side leak fixes from the #77311 series never touched the main process, and a survey of the registries named in that issue shows most are bounded on current main — but one provably is not.

## Root cause

`remoteOwnerBySessionId` (main.ts, from #85834) memoizes which remote profile owns a session id when a `/api/sessions/:id` read arrives with no profile hint. The memo **only ever inserts**: the 30s TTL makes an entry stale but never removes it, and there is no delete call anywhere. A long-lived main process therefore keeps one Map entry per session id it has ever resolved — and session ids churn through normal use, so the map grows without bound for the life of the process.

## What changes

- The memo moves to `electron/remote-owner-cache.ts` as a pure, injectable cache (`limit` / `now` / `ttlMs`) with FIFO eviction past 500 entries — the same shape as the existing `titleCache` bound.
- `main.ts` wires `remoteOwnerProfileForSession` through it; behaviour (30s TTL, hint-less resolution, sweep across configured remotes) is otherwise unchanged.

Survey of the other registries named in the issue (all bounded on current main, no change needed): `titleCache` (500 FIFO), `hermesLog` (300), `recentFileReveals` (self-pruning), `renderTitleQueue` (drained by 2 concurrent 8s-timeout jobs), `sshConnections` (full lifecycle on teardown/close), and the baseUrl-keyed `gatewayAuthProvidersCache` / `_nativeTokens` (one entry per configured remote). `fetchJson` buffers one response at a time with no retained references after `JSON.parse` — a transient buffer, not retention.

## Acceptance coverage

- "Identify and fix the main-process heap retention" — one provable unbounded path fixed; a full attribution (heap-snapshot diff of the remaining growth) still needs a live long-run session and is not claimed here.
- "Verify the fix on macOS Apple Silicon" — not exercised live in this PR; the fix is platform-neutral main-process logic.
- "Add regression/leak coverage" — unit tests cover the FIFO bound and TTL behaviour.

## Tests

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 electron/remote-owner-cache.test.ts` → **1 file, 3 passed**.
- Red on main: `remote-owner-cache.ts` does not exist on `origin/main`, so the test file fails to import there.
- `npx tsc -p . --noEmit` (apps/desktop) → clean (exit 0).

## Not exercised live

The 1-hour heap ceiling reproduction needs a long interactive session on macOS; this PR fixes the provable unbounded path and bounds it, but does not claim the whole OOM is closed — the remaining gap (if any) needs the in-band heap sampler the issue's fix plan describes.

Refs #58485

## Root cause

Switching models mid-session could drop the next user prompt. The model-switch `[System:...]` marker is persisted as `role=user` on purpose (#48338). When alternation repair merges that marker with the following plain user row, `_merge_consecutive_users` kept the marker's `display_kind` and its `_row_id` — hiding the merged pair from every user-turn index and burying the plain row's durable id. `_resolve_truncate_row_id` read only the repaired durable view, so the absorbed row id could never resolve: `prompt.submit` failed closed with 4018 ("refusing truncation without fallback") and the user's input was silently dropped.

## What changes (combining #94500 + #99955)

- **Merge side (#94500, rebased):** when a display-marker user row merges with a plain user row, the merged pair drops the display classification and carries the plain row's `_row_id` (the marker's own id is retired onto `_absorbed_row_ids`), keeping the pair addressable for rewind/submit. The persist marker is popped — reclassifying stales the row even when the merged bytes reproduce the persisted content. Scope note: when BOTH rows carry `display_kind` (two consecutive markers) the pair keeps the first marker's classification — no plain row is swallowed there.
- **Resolver side (#99955):** `_resolve_truncate_row_id` now loads the durable transcript with `repair_alternation=False` for identity lookups. Repair merges any user;user run (marker runs, or an interrupted turn + resend) into its first row, so the repaired view cannot see absorbed ids; reading the physical rows resolves rows that are genuinely present.

## Acceptance coverage per issue

- Marker-merged rows keep the plain row's addressable identity (`test_repair_marker_user_merge_keeps_plain_row_addressable`, `test_repair_plain_user_then_marker_stays_addressable`).
- `prompt.submit` with `truncate_before_row_id` resolves after a marker merge instead of 4018 (`test_prompt_submit_resolves_row_id_absorbed_into_marker_merge`).
- The broader swallowed-id family — dual markers, and a plain-user merge with NO marker at all — resolves via the un-repaired transcript (`test_prompt_submit_resolves_row_id_swallowed_by_marker_merge`, `test_prompt_submit_resolves_row_id_swallowed_by_plain_user_merge`).

## Tests run

- On `origin/main`: all 5 new tests RED — including the exact 4018 "refusing truncation without fallback" from the report (`pytest ... -q`, 5 failed in 88.42s).
- With this branch: all 5 GREEN (5 passed in 51.55s); full `tests/agent/test_message_sequence_repair.py` suite 61/61 green; the gateway server file's `row_id or truncate or marker or repair or rewind` selection 35/35 green (the 2 selection-mode failures seen once were cross-test pollution in the huge file, reproduced as passing in isolation on both main and this branch).

Fixes #94486

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/94500 (Thanks @liuhao1024 — both commits cherry-picked with authorship kept)
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/99955 (Thanks @zengzheqing — resolver change + tests folded in as a co-authored commit)
Also supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/112908 (heavier resolver-signature variant made redundant by #99955's minimal read-side fix)

Notes for review: the issue's optional fail-open floor (skip truncation and submit as a plain append when the target still doesn't resolve) is deliberately NOT included — heliangwjq offered to PR it separately and it changes the fail-closed contract #82959 established; that is a maintainer call.

items.body:
## What

Adds OpenAI **Ultrafast** as a `/fast` tier for GPT-6 Astra, and prices responses at the tier OpenAI actually served them at.

**WHO / WHEN / WHY:** At DevDay 2026 (2026-09-29) OpenAI launched Ultrafast, a `service_tier: "ultrafast"` request field ([guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/ultrafast-mode), [pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing?latest-pricing=ultrafast), [Codex speed docs](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/speed)).
- It is broadly available for GPT-6 Astra in the API, and in Codex on Pro 500 and Enterprise plans.
- It is billed at **6x Standard**: $60 / $300, cached $6, cache write $75, and 2x/1.5x again above 272K.
- GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast is announced as "coming soon" with no published rate yet.

Hermes had no way to request the tier. If it had been requested through `request_overrides`, cost would have shown Standard, one-sixth of the real bill.

Companion to #128248 (GPT-6.1 Sol). The two PRs don't touch the same files.

## Changes

| Surface | Change |
|---|---|
| `agent/fast_mode.py` | One tier table: `parse_service_tier`, `STATIC_TIERS`, `service_tier_word`. The CLI (`cli_config_load`), gateway (`run_config_loaders`) and TUI (`server._load_service_tier`) config loaders used three hand-copied parsers; all three now call this one. |
| `hermes_cli/models.py`, `models_catalog_static.py` | `model_supports_ultrafast` covers `gpt-6-astra` (vendor prefix and `-900k` alias stripped). `resolve_fast_mode_overrides(tier="ultrafast")` returns `{"service_tier": "ultrafast"}` only for Ultrafast models on the existing first-party route gate (api.openai.com / chatgpt.com). Any other model gets **nothing**, never a silent switch to Priority, which is a different paid tier. |
| CLI / gateway / TUI | `/fast ultrafast` works on all three. The gateway picker shows the choice only when the model supports it; a typed `ultrafast` on an unsupported model is refused with a clear message. Every place that attaches a static tier (`_resolve_turn_agent_config` on CLI and gateway, TUI `config.set fast`, TUI `session.info`) now passes the tier through instead of hard-coding `priority`. The TUI slash command and Desktop settings toggle recognise the new value. |
| Pricing (`usage_pricing`, `turn_usage`, `aux_accounting`, `codex_runtime`) | OpenAI reports the served tier on the response, not inside `usage`. `with_served_service_tier` folds it into `raw_usage`, and the Codex stream assembler now keeps `service_tier` from the terminal frame. A response served at `ultrafast` prices from a published `_OPENAI_ULTRAFAST_PRICING` row. A request that asked for Ultrafast but was served at `default` bills at Standard. A served-ultrafast model with no published rate reports unknown instead of guessing. |
| `locales/*` | 4 new keys in all 17 locales. The option lists in usage/description strings now mention `ultrafast`. |

## Verification

- New `tests/agent/test_openai_ultrafast.py`, 9 relationship tests:
  - all three config loaders agree on every tier word;
  - the tier is gated by model and route (6 Sol gets none; OpenRouter gets none);
  - CLI and gateway turn routes send `ultrafast`;
  - the CLI refuses it on 6 Sol;
  - served ultrafast costs exactly 6x Standard, below and above 272K;
  - requested-but-served-default costs Standard;
  - unpublished models report unknown;
  - the Codex assembler keeps the served tier.
- Mutation checks: removing the pricing branch fails 3 tests; dropping `tier=` at the CLI attach site fails 1; dropping `service_tier` from the assembler fails 1.
- Existing fast-mode, pricing, i18n-parity, codex-transport, TUI-server and gateway suites (26 files): 1150 passed, 39 failed. All 39 fail identically on `upstream/main` (home-IO guard in this local checkout). Ruff is clean, and `tsc --noEmit` + eslint are clean for `ui-tui`.
- **Live, Codex OAuth, real `AIAgent`** with `gpt-6-astra` and `/fast ultrafast` overrides: the wire request carried `service_tier: ultrafast`, the backend accepted it, and it reported **served `default`** because this account isn't on Pro 500. The run returned `PASS`. That's the exact case the served-tier pricing handles.
- **Not live-tested:** a response actually served at `ultrafast` (needs a Pro 500 account or an API key), and the direct API path (no OpenAI key here).

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- **Fast mode (Priority, 2x) is still priced at Standard for OpenAI.** This is pre-existing. The served-tier plumbing here makes adding those rows a data-only change; left out so this PR stays about Ultrafast.
- GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast: add `gpt-6.1-sol` to `_OPENAI_ULTRAFAST_MODELS`, plus its pricing row, once OpenAI publishes the rate.
- The Desktop settings toggle stays binary (fast/normal). It now shows "on" for an ultrafast config instead of "off"; there's no dedicated Desktop control yet.

items.body:
## Root cause

`touchPoolBackend` (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts) refreshes `entry.lastActiveAt` on every renderer keepalive — and `lastActiveAt` is the **only** clock both the idle reaper and LRU eviction read. The keepalive proves the chat is *open*, not that anything *streamed*, so the pinned tier (every backend whose profile chat was ever opened) was exempt from both `maxBackends` and the idle reaper indefinitely: N open chats held N ~120 MB `hermes serve` children until app quit. The reporter's machine: 62 profiles → 126 serve processes / 7.5 GB, all parented to the live Hermes.exe (not orphans) (#105239). A maintainer retest on 2026-09-29 confirmed the defect class persists post-#118246 for what still pools per-profile (isolated mode, unscopable mutating REST requests): "the pinned tier still has no cap in the code".

## What changed

- `touchPoolBackend` stamps `entry.lastStreamedAt` when the renderer reports an active prompt turn (`activeTurn: true` — the existing #104871 turn-lease signal). A turn leasing the backend IS streamed activity; the bare keepalive touch only refreshes `lastActiveAt`, as before.
- `pool-retire.ts`: `PoolRetireEntry` gains `lastStreamedAt`; `retireIdle` accepts an optional idle-eligibility override so the reaper can key on the streamed clock. **Every other safeguard is unchanged**: `activeTurn` veto (never reap mid-stream), identity checks, admission permit, backend proof probe.
- `startPoolIdleReaper` retires a local child whose last streamed turn is older than `POOL_PINNED_IDLE_MS` (default 60 min; `HERMES_DESKTOP_POOL_PINNED_IDLE_MS` override; floor `POOL_LIMITS_MIN.idleMs`) even while keepalive-fresh. Entries without the stamp (spawned before this change, or never streamed) keep the legacy `lastActiveAt` clock — no behavior change for them.
- Teardown stays invisible: re-focusing the chat re-ensures via the idempotent `ensureBackend`/`ensureRegistryBackend` pool-entry reuse (the issue's requirement 3, already met on main).

This implements the reporter's option 2 (pinned idle TTL keyed on streamed activity, "reap after 60 min with no streamed token") rather than option 1 (hard `maxPinnedBackends`), because it composes with the existing admission machinery and never kills a backend a user is actively reading/writing toward; overflow LRU-by-`lastStreamedAt` remains possible as a follow-up if fleets still grow.

## Acceptance coverage (#105239)

- "Idle reaper eventually retires a backend whose chat is open but has had no activity for hours" — met: keepalive-fresh + stream-idle > 60 min → retired through the retirer (probe-proven, mid-stream safe).
- "maxBackends (or a second pinned-tier cap) bounds total resident backends" — bounded in time rather than count: the pinned tier now drains to zero within `POOL_PINNED_IDLE_MS` of inactivity instead of persisting until quit. A count-based `maxPinnedBackends` (option 1) is a heavier design choice this PR does not make.
- "Killing hours-idle backends must never be user-observable" — unchanged (idempotent re-ensure) and asserted by the existing pool-retire tests' admission/identity cases.

## Tests

- `npx vitest run --project electron electron/pool-retire.test.ts electron/pool-limits.test.ts electron/pool-stop.test.ts electron/pool-touch-scope.test.ts electron/pool-spawn-coordinator.test.ts` → 41 passed. New case: keepalive-fresh entries with a 2h-stale `lastStreamedAt` retire; 5-min-stale ones do not; a mid-turn entry is vetoed by the retirer even when the override says eligible.
- `npm run check:lint` → exit 0.
- Fail-first: on `origin/main`, `retireIdle` takes no eligibility override and `PoolRetireEntry` has no `lastStreamedAt`, so the new test does not compile/run on base — the regression it pins (pinned tier never reaped) is the base behavior by construction (reaper keys solely on keepalive-refreshed `lastActiveAt`).

Refs #105239 (the memory-footprint half is fixed by the TTL; a count-based pinned cap or rail badge remains open design space)

items.body:
## Root cause

Desktop/TUI `command.dispatch` runs skills through `_dispatch_skill` in `tui_gateway/methods_tools.py`, which built a single-skill invocation from `(name, arg)` with no stacked handling: on `/skill-a /skill-b do XYZ` the extra `/skill-b` token stayed in the prompt as plain instruction text. The CLI (`cli.py`) and the messaging gateway (`gateway/run_inbound.py`) both route through `split_stacked_skill_commands` + `build_stacked_skill_invocation_message`; the TUI gateway had zero references to either, so the Desktop was the only surface without stacked-skill parity (#74705).

## Fix

Inside `_dispatch_skill`, after the `key in cmds` gate, split the remaining leading skill tokens with `split_stacked_skill_commands(arg)` (up to 5, non-skill/repeated tokens stop the stack and stay in the instruction). Extra keys build one `build_stacked_skill_invocation_message` with a loading notice and the `_skill_scaffold_projection` display payload the UIs render; the single-skill fallback now receives the post-split instruction. The current `_dispatch_skill` body shape (`contextlib.suppress` + `_tools_mod` + the `_session_home_scope` bound by `command.dispatch`) is preserved, so the dispatch stays scoped to the session's profile home.

## Coverage

- #74705: stacked `/skill` tokens load every skill over the remaining instruction on Desktop/TUI, with CLI/gateway parity.

## Checks run

- `pytest tests/tui_gateway/test_protocol.py -k stacked` — 2 passed (both new tests fail on `origin/main`: `KeyError: 'notice'` — no stacked expansion on base).
- Red-on-base proven by swapping `origin/main:tui_gateway/methods_tools.py` into the worktree and rerunning the same tests.
- Two new tests use two real skills under a temp `HERMES_HOME` and dispatch through `command.dispatch`, asserting both bodies land in `message`, the typed invocation in `display`, and that an unknown `/token` stays instruction text.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/74876

Thanks @lifeFedorovAlexey — this adapts #74876's approach (same helpers, same split semantics) into the restructured `_dispatch_skill` on current main, which the original diff predated.

Fixes #74705

items.body:
## Root cause

`tui_gateway/slash_worker.py:100` — `/prompt` and `/compose` (and `/blueprint`) park their
composed prompt on the one-shot `_pending_agent_seed`, which only the **interactive REPL
loop** consumes (`cli.py` main loop). The persistent slash worker that Desktop/TUI
`slash.exec` routes these commands to has no REPL loop, so the composed prompt was
silently dropped: `/prompt` on Desktop returned `(no output)` and the user's composed
text vanished (#107800). Worse, `tui_gateway/methods_slash.py:220` registered a live
`prompt` entry that answered with a raw **system-prompt dump** instead of ever composing
— a repurposing a maintainer flagged as deliberate in
[#107800 (comment)](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/107800#issuecomment-),
which this PR removes in favour of the compose flow (no replacement viewer is added;
that trade-off is called out for sign-off).

## What changed

- **`tui_gateway/slash_worker.py`** — `_run` keeps its existing `str` return; after each
  command it harvests `cli._pending_agent_seed` (resetting it, keeping the one-shot
  contract) onto `cli._harvested_seed`, cleared at the top of every run so a stale seed
  can never re-send. `main()` replies with the output plus a `seed` field.
- **`tui_gateway/server.py`** — `_SlashWorker.run` keeps its existing `str` return; the
  seed rides back on the reply's `seed` field and is retrieved via `pop_seed()` (old
  workers that don't reply a seed get `""` — no break).
- **`tui_gateway/methods_tools.py`** — after `worker.run(cmd)`, `slash.exec` pops the
  seed; when the worker harvested one it returns `{"type": "send", "message": seed}` — a
  dispatch both clients already handle
  (`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/slash.ts:307`,
  `ui-tui/src/app/createSlashHandler.ts:157`).
- **`tui_gateway/methods_slash.py`** — removed the live system-prompt viewer:
  `_format_live_prompt_output`, the `"prompt"` entry in `_LIVE_SLASH_OUTPUT`,
  `_mirror_prompt`, and `"prompt"` from `_MUTATES_WHILE_RUNNING`. `/prompt` in the CLI
  is compose-only (`hermes_cli/commands.py:95`), so the viewer answered a question the
  command no longer asks, and it shadowed the compose flow from the gateway.
- **`hermes_cli/cli_commands_mixin.py`** — `_compose_in_editor` no longer falls back to
  `shell=True` with the raw `$EDITOR` unquoted when the argv invocation fails (#81364).
  An unargv-splittable (`ValueError`) or unrunnable (`OSError`) editor, or a nonzero
  editor exit (which may leave abandoned buffer text), cancels the compose cleanly.

The seed is carried **out of band** rather than changing `_run`/`run` to a dict/tuple:
both string return shapes are contracts main's callers and test fakes rely on, and the
`{type: "send"}` dispatch is an existing `SlashExecResult` shape.

Two tests on main asserted the live `/prompt` viewer this PR intentionally removes and
were updated minimally (the PR's intentional behavior change, per its own removal of
the viewer): `test_slash_exec_r7_read_commands_use_metadata_mirror_flag_on` drops its
`prompt` case, and `test_mirror_slash_side_effects_rejects_mutating_commands_while_running`
drops its `/prompt` row (`/prompt` no longer mirrors or mutates live agent state — it is
compose-only now).

No desktop/TUI client change is needed — both already handle `{type: "send"}`.
`/refine` live routing is **deliberately not in this PR**: it overlaps
[#127241](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/127241), which already implements it.

## Known limitation (unchanged by this PR)

The slash worker is headless (pipes, no tty), so terminal `$EDITOR`s (vim/nano) fail
there and the compose is cancelled with the existing `editor_failed` message; GUI
editors (`code --wait`) work. Same as before the fix, except the failure is now reported
instead of silently dropping the prompt.

## Acceptance coverage

- Worker harvests `_pending_agent_seed` and resets it (one-shot preserved)
- `slash.exec` with a seeded worker → `{"type": "send", "message": <seed>}`; plain
  output path unchanged (no `type` key, mirrors/warnings intact)
- Compose cancels on: unargv-splittable editor, unrunnable editor, nonzero editor exit —
  never through a shell
- Empty-buffer cancel and header-stripping behaviour preserved

## Tests run (all green)

- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tui_gateway/test_slash_prompt_compose_seed.py` — new
  (5 tests), proven RED on base first
- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_cli/test_prompt_compose_command.py` — extended
  (2 new tests), proven RED on base first
- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tui_gateway/test_slash_worker_skill_refuse.py`,
  `test_slash_worker_ansi.py`, `test_slash_worker_provider.py`, `test_protocol.py` —
  all pass **unmodified from main** (the string contracts are preserved)
- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py -k "slash_exec_r7_read_commands_use_metadata_mirror_flag_on or mirror_slash_side_effects_rejects_mutating_commands_while_running or slash_exec_concurrent_first_use_spawns_single_worker"`
- `tests/tui_gateway/test_slash_review_owner.py`, `tests/tui_gateway/test_slash_worker_sys_path.py`,
  `tests/tui_gateway/test_slash_worker_mcp_discovery.py`
- 3 pre-existing failures in `tests/agent/test_background_review.py`
  (`test_live_turn_waits_for_review_exit…`, `…acknowledgement_times_out`,
  `test_stale_review_cleanup…`) reproduce identically on clean `origin/main` — timing-sensitive
  live-turn tests unrelated to this diff (verified on a separate clean worktree).

## Supersedes

- [#107803](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/107803) (KoNit-K) — same
  seed-harvest + `{type:"send"}` routing, adapted to current main
- [#115149](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/115149) (JPeetz) — same
  approach; hunks adapted and verified against current file shapes
- [#81366](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/81366) (Adolanium) — the
  `$EDITOR` shell-fallback removal + tests, applied nearly verbatim

Credit: `@KoNit-K`, `@JPeetz`, `@Adolanium` (Co-authored-by trailers on the respective
commits, with their actual commit emails).

Fixes #107800
Fixes #81364

items.body:
## Root cause

`cli.py:211` — `from prompt_toolkit.patch_stdout import patch_stdout` was the one
unguarded top-level prompt_toolkit import (its neighbours at 213 and 219 already use
try/except, so the guard was the intended pattern). A partial/broken prompt_toolkit
install — e.g. the reporter's stale venv that has the package but not every submodule —
crashed the import: `ModuleNotFoundError`/`ImportError` at import time, taking down
`hermes` and every `tui_gateway.slash_worker` child (which imports `cli` at module
scope, `tui_gateway/slash_worker.py:27`), i.e. every gateway session (#96075).

## What changed

`cli.py` — the import is guarded with an `ImportError` fallback to
`contextlib.nullcontext as patch_stdout`. The only use site is
`with patch_stdout():` (cli.py:1476), a drop-in for a null context manager, so the
interactive path is unchanged when prompt_toolkit is healthy. This mirrors the in-repo
precedent in `agent/display.py:897` (guarded `from prompt_toolkit.patch_stdout import
StdoutProxy`).

Note the CLI's TUI mixins still import prompt_toolkit unguarded; a *fully* missing
prompt_toolkit therefore still fails on the interactive path — by design, since the
reporter's case (and the routing fix plan) is the *partial* install, where only the
fragile submodule import needed the guard to keep headless paths (slash worker) alive.

## Acceptance coverage

- `import cli` succeeds with a `sys.meta_path` blocker raising ImportError only for
  `prompt_toolkit.patch_stdout`
- `cli.patch_stdout is contextlib.nullcontext` and `cli.HermesCLI` stays callable under
  the blocker
- (Proven RED on base: both tests fail with the import error before the fix.)

## Tests run (all green)

- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_import_without_patch_stdout.py`
  — new (2 subprocess tests), proven RED on base first
- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_cli/test_prompt_compose_command.py` — smoke,
  no regression
- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tui_gateway/test_slash_worker_sys_path.py` — the
  slash-worker import-chain path, no regression

## Auto-merge

Backend import-robustness only: no visible UI change, no install/update/launch path,
no system-level behaviour, no markdown/transcript processing, no auth/secrets/config
keys. The change is a two-line guarded import with a nullcontext fallback whose only
use site is a context manager. Reviewed full head SHA:
`3c8663f4f2396c6e1d22243184d02e1521c0517e` (`bb/cli-guard-prompt-toolkit-import`).

Fixes #96075

items.body:
## Summary

If you send a correction while a **regenerated** turn is streaming, the Desktop view drops the partial reply and your correction. Only the post-correction answer stays on screen, attached straight under the original prompt.

## Root cause

`appendMidTurnUserMessage` seals the live bubble and appends the correction. It is the same seal Stop uses: `finalizeUserInterruptedMessages` marks the row settled and marks its open tool calls interrupted. But it left the regenerate's `pendingBranchGroup` armed, so the next assistant row (seeded by `mutateStream`, `newAssistantFromCompletion` or the interim path) joined the branch group too.

`useRuntimeMessageRepository` parents every branch-group member to the group's user row. That made the post-correction reply a **sibling** of the sealed partial, so the head branch became `question → new answer`. `applyBranchVisibility` then synced that back into the store and marked the partial `hidden`.

## Fix

The correction ends the branch group: `appendMidTurnUserMessage` clears `pendingBranchGroup`. The main composer's `redirectPrompt` and the session tiles' `steerPrompt` both go through this helper. The sealed partial keeps its group (it is the regenerated variant), and output after the correction chains under the correction.

## Routing notes (#119015 / #119686)

- The routing hypothesis was that the runtime adapter sync deletes the live row (`incremental-external-store-runtime.ts` `deleteMessage`). That does not reproduce on current main. The runtime only deletes ids the store no longer has, plus its own always-empty optimistic placeholder.
- A plain (non-regenerated) redirect already keeps the partial on main: the correction seals the bubble with the same helper Stop uses. `steer-arrival-order.test.tsx` covers this, and I confirmed it with a full store → repository → runtime probe.
- The only current-main path I could reproduce where a redirect drops the partial is the regenerate one fixed here. So this PR **does not** close #119015; it covers its regenerate half. The reporter's build (`ddde715b`) already had the sealing code, and I could not reproduce their exact plain-turn case.
- Not touched: queue-mode honour (#125983), and the #119686 tool-narration symptom inside a regenerated turn. Branch variants assume a single assistant row per variant, which is a separate design issue.

## Validation

- New test in `use-message-stream/steer-arrival-order.test.tsx`. It drives the real stream reducer and the real `redirectPrompt`, then projects the store through `useRuntimeMessageRepository` and `IncrementalExternalStoreRuntimeCore` and asserts what is rendered.

items.body:
## Root cause

`hermes update` plans a restart for every profile home from `_profile_homes()`, including a `profiles/<name>` that is a symlink to a separate Hermes install (its own checkout, venv and LaunchAgent). The restart phase leaves that gateway alone, which is correct. The post-restart fleet matrix already marks it `external` (#117449, via `_gateway_code_root` vs `_updater_code_root`). But `match_runtime_outcomes` has no such outcome. The planned gateway therefore ends `unaccounted`, `report_unaccounted_runtimes` returns True, and every update exits 1. On macOS the Desktop hand-off then fails both of its attempts.

## Fix

- `update_cmd_fleet._verify_fleet_after_update` passes `external_gateway_pids` to `match_runtime_outcomes`. These are the pids of fleet rows the probe already classified as `external`.
- `match_runtime_outcomes`: a gateway that no restart bookkeeping mentions (not relaunched, killed, failed or name-matched) and whose planned pid is in that set gets the outcome `external`. It fails closed: no fleet row, an unresolvable code root, or a different pid all still give `unaccounted`. Serve/dashboard runtimes never use this evidence.
- `report_unaccounted_runtimes` lists `external` rows under an informational `ℹ Left to their own install` block. They don't count toward the exit-1 tripwire.

The new parameter is an optional keyword argument, so the frozen compat surface (`tests/compat/old_updater_surface.json`) is unchanged.

## Acceptance coverage

`tests/hermes_cli/test_update_external_profile_reconciliation.py`:
- Uses a real temp `HERMES_HOME` with its own gateway, plus `profiles/work` symlinked to another install whose gateway's pid-guarded `gateway_state.json` argv resolves to a separate fake code root. The test runs the real `_verify_fleet_after_update`, and `collect_fleet_versions` runs for real. With the fix: receipt `success`, outcomes `{default: restarted, work: external}`, no "never touched" block. **On `origin/main` this raises `SystemExit: 1` with `✗ gateway [work] pid 4242 — planned mechanism: launchd`.**
- If the root's own gateway is also missed, the update still exits 1 (`default: unaccounted`), so an external profile can't hide a real miss.
- Fail-closed unit cases: with no evidence, or evidence for a different pid, the outcome is still `unaccounted`. Serve runtimes never become `external`.

## Validation

```
unset PYTHONPATH; uvx ruff check hermes_cli/update_inventory.py hermes_cli/update_cmd_fleet.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_external_profile_reconciliation.py
→ All checks passed!

scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_update_external_profile_reconciliation.py   # on origin/main, before the fix
→ 4 failed (2 integration: SystemExit 1 / work=unaccounted; 2 unit: new kwarg)

scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_update_external_profile_reconciliation.py tests/hermes_cli/test_restart_plan_reconciliation.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_inventory.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_scoped_reconciliation.py tests/hermes_cli/test_windows_update_restart_reconciliation.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_external_checkout.py tests/hermes_cli/test_manual_serve_deferral.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_fleet_check_fail_closed.py tests/hermes_cli/test_fleet_matrix_self_restart_pending.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_fleet_completion.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plan_reconciliation_windows_live.py
→ 11 files, 158 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped

scripts/run_tests.sh tests/test_old_updater_compat_surface.py
→ 570 passed
```

Not exercised: a live two-install macOS host. The regression test drives the real verify/reconcile path with the fleet probe's inputs stubbed at the socket and live-pid layer.

## Related

- #110333 / #110345 / #110256: same exit path, different triggers (sticky-profile root label, hash-suffixed units). They don't overlap with this change.
- The reporter's workaround in #120240 does the same `_code_root_for_path` vs `_updater_code_root` classification inside `match_runtime_outcomes`. This PR reuses the fleet probe's existing classification of the same live pid instead of adding a second probe.

Fixes #120240

items.body:
## Root cause
When a turn's stored rows end in a tool round with `content = ''` and `tool_calls` set, and no prose row follows, `toChatMessages` hydrates that turn as a text-less assistant shell (a prose row would fold into it). `preserveLocalPendingTurnMessages` pairs the settled live bubble (`assistant-stream-*`, `pending: false`) with that shell by ordinal, then drops it: `localPendingSupersedes` only accepts **live-tail** authoritative rows, and a committed shell is not one. The answer the user just watched stream is removed at end of turn, right as the completion chime plays.

## Fix
New `settledReplyOverEmptyShell(local, authoritative)`, checked only at the ordinal-pairing call site in `preserveLocalPendingTurnMessages`. It keeps the local row (the shell still supplies turn state and row identity through `withAuthoritativeTurnState`) only when all of these hold:
- the local row is a settled assistant (`pending !== true`), not interim, not errored, and has answer text (a local row with only tool/reasoning parts doesn't count)
- the authoritative row is a committed assistant (not live-tail), not errored, and has no answer text

`localPendingSupersedes` is unchanged, so resume reconciliation keeps its stricter live-only rule. Once a prose row commits for the turn, hydration folds it into the tool round, the authoritative row now has text, and it wins. No duplicate.

## Tests
New `streamed-reply-survives-sync.test.ts`, 6 cases:
- the reporter's shape built from real `SessionMessage` rows through `toChatMessages` (user 196700, assistant 196701 `content=''` + `tool_calls`, a tool result): the streamed reply survives
- row identity carried from the shell onto the kept reply
- a committed prose row folded into the tool round: the result equals `next` (no duplicate, no resurrection)
- interim narration, a tool-only local row, and an errored shell: none of them displace the authoritative row

## Validation (in worktree)
- `npx vitest run src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/streamed-reply-survives-sync.test.ts` with only `utils.ts` reverted to `origin/main`: **2 failed, 4 passed** (the two keep-the-reply cases fail as expected; the four guard cases already pass on main)
- same file with the fix: 6/6 passed
- `npx vitest run <all 8 test files that use preserveLocalPendingTurnMessages or use-session-actions/utils> src/app/session`: **89 files, 1101 tests passed**
- `cd apps/desktop && npm run typecheck`: passed
- prettier and eslint on both files: clean

## Notes / residual
- This fixes the renderer dropping the reply. It does **not** explain why the store committed the turn's prose as `content=''`. After a restart the reply is still missing, because the store never had it. If that turns out to be a backend persistence bug, it's a separate root cause.
- #126834 (open) calls `preserveLocalPendingTurnMessages` from transcript backfill but doesn't touch this predicate, so no conflict.

Based on #123065 by @kvnloo: same call-site approach and the interim/tool-only guards. This version adds a factored helper, errored-shell and no-duplicate-after-fold coverage, and a regression built on real hydration.

Fixes #123047

items.body:
## Root cause

`preview.read` / `preview.act` / `terminal.read` / `window.read` / `tour` are window-owned bridges: since #114981 only the Desktop window showing the requesting session answers, and every other window returns `'ignore'` (`server-requests.ts::previewSessionRoute`) and stays silent. That silence is correct when another window owns the request. It is wrong when **no** attached window shows the session (the user is on a different chat): nobody answers, the agent waits out the whole 30–45 s deadline, and `read_pane` reports the generic `No preview tab is open, or the read timed out.`

A renderer-only fix (answer the refusal from the non-hosting window) would bring #113348 back. The gateway's `resolve_response` settles on the first frame, so a bystander window's refusal would beat the owner's real answer. One window cannot know whether another window hosts the session. The gateway does know who is attached, so the count happens there.

## Behavior

- **Renderer** (`server-requests.ts`): on `'ignore'`, and when a replayed request's one-turn `'retry'` still finds no host, the window calls `request.decline(...)` instead of staying silent.
- **Shared channel** (`json-rpc-channel.ts`): `ServerRequest.decline` sends JSON-RPC error `4404` (`JSON_RPC_SESSION_NOT_SHOWN`), but only when the backend's `client.capabilities` result said `declines_not_shown: true`. An older backend settles on the first error, so against one the decline is a no-op and behavior matches today's.
- **Gateway** (`server_requests.py`): a `4404` frame counts as a vote from the transport it arrived on (`rpc_dispatch.dispatch` now passes the transport). It does not settle the request. The request stays open for the owner and settles only when every live, advertised WS client attached to the session (`session_transports._session_answering_clients`) has declined. It then resolves right away with `{"success": false, "error": "No Hermes Desktop window is showing this chat, so its preview, terminal and tour are out of reach. Ask the user to open this chat in the Desktop app, then retry."}`. The tools pass that JSON straight through (`passthrough_json`), which is the same `{success:false,error}` shape as the explicit `previewAct` / `tour` refusals from #114981.
- Repeat declines from the same window count once. A decline with no known transport (the `request.answer` proxy, a compute-host relay) is not counted, so the wait continues as before.

## Acceptance coverage

| Test | Before (origin/main source) | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_protocol.py::test_window_owned_request_refuses_at_once_when_no_window_shows_the_session`: 2 windows both decline, so `preview.read` returns the refusal in under 2 s, not after 30 s. A repeated decline from window 1 does not settle the request. | FAILED | passed |
| `test_protocol.py::test_window_owned_request_decline_does_not_beat_the_owner_window`: a bystander declines, an unattributed decline arrives, the request stays open, and the owner's answer is the result (#113348 guard). | FAILED | passed |
| `test_protocol.py::test_client_capabilities_advertises_counting_not_shown_declines` | FAILED | passed |
| `server-requests.test.ts`: `preview.act`, the pane reads and `tour` decline in a window showing another session. A replayed request declines only after the retry turn. A window hosting the session in a tile answers and does not decline. | 4 failed | 17/17 passed |
| `json-rpc-channel.test.ts::sends a not-shown decline only to a backend that advertised counting it` | failed | 13/13 passed |

## Validation (worktree, real output)

- `npm ci` at the root: added 1330 packages
- `cd apps/desktop && npm run typecheck`: exit 0
- `cd apps/shared && npx tsc -p . --noEmit`: exit 0
- `npx vitest run src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event/` (desktop): 11 files, 48 tests passed
- `cd apps/shared && npx vitest run src/json-rpc-channel.test.ts`: 13 passed
- `npx eslint` on the 4 touched TS files: 0 problems. `prettier` applied to the desktop files. The shared files keep their existing line width (running prettier would reformat untouched lines).
- `scripts/gen_gateway_contracts.py`: regenerated `gateway-contract.generated.ts` / `.openrpc.json` (+`declines_not_shown?: boolean`)
- `uvx ruff check` on the touched Python files: All checks passed
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_protocol.py tests/tui_gateway/contracts tests/tui_gateway/test_compute_host_phase1.py …`: 107 passed
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway`: 2222 passed, 6 failed. The 6 failures are in `test_profiles_list_{ui_meta_cache,session_field_cache,canonical_session}.py` and fail the same way on clean origin/main (checked by reverting this diff: 24 passed, 6 failed).

Not reproduced in a live multi-window Electron rig. The proof is the gateway-level two-window fanout test and the renderer dispatcher tests.

## Residual

- A client that answers `-32601` (no handler), such as a dashboard `/chat` tab, still settles a window-owned request at once with the old generic message, as it does today. This PR does not change that.
- A compute-host child owns its requests. Declines relayed to it carry no transport and are not counted, so those sessions still wait out the deadline.

Fixes #119333

items.body:
## Root cause
#121377 made the pre-main launcher (`electron/wslg-launch.ts`) pass `--ozone-platform=wayland` on every local Wayland session so amdgpu stops crashing on XWayland (#83578). On the NVIDIA proprietary driver (615.71.09, RTX 4060, KDE Wayland) the GPU process dies under Wayland ozone with the bundled Electron 40 Chromium (`error_code=1002`, `GPU process isn't usable`). `--ozone-platform=x11` launches fine. The `linux-nvidia-egl-fallback.ts` comment saying 615 is fine is about the #40077 ANGLE EGL probe, not about Wayland ozone.

## Behavior
- If `/proc/driver/nvidia/version` exists (the proprietary kernel module is loaded; not nouveau, not WSL's dxg) and the user set no ozone platform, the automatic default becomes `x11` instead of `wayland`. This puts NVIDIA back on the XWayland path it used before #121377.
- `ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT=auto` counts as no preference.
- User choices still win: `--ozone-platform=…` on argv or in `desktop.electron_flags`, and an `x11`/`wayland` hint from argv, `electron_flags` or `ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT`. NVIDIA users who have Wayland working can keep it with `ozone_platform_hint: wayland`.
- Non-NVIDIA sessions, WSLg, and remote displays behave as before, so the #83578 amdgpu fix is untouched.
- The detection lives in `entry.ts` and is passed into the pure `wslgLaunchArgs()` as a boolean.

## Validation (worktree, `apps/desktop`)
- `npx vitest run electron/wslg-launch.test.ts electron/wslg-launch-process.test.ts electron/linux-nvidia-egl-fallback.test.ts scripts/bundle-electron-main.test.mjs`: 26 passed. The bundled-entry test (5 tests) also passes when run on its own.
- RED: the new test run against `origin/main`'s `wslg-launch.ts` fails with `expected [ '.', '--ozone-platform=wayland' ] to deeply equal [ '.', '--ozone-platform=x11' ]`. It passes with this change.
- `npm run typecheck`: clean. `eslint` and `prettier --check` on the touched files: clean.
- Not reproduced on hardware (no NVIDIA/Wayland box). This rests on the single report, where x11 works and wayland crashes on 615.

## Auto-merge
Off. This changes the Linux launch command.

Fixes #126013

items.body:
## Root cause

`PreviewPane`'s guest-creation effect (`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/right-rail/preview-pane.tsx`) had `target.url` in its dependency array, so every external URL change ran `host.replaceChildren()`, nulled `webviewRef`, and rebuilt the `<webview>` from scratch — dropping the guest's JS state, form data, scroll position, and injected engine handles (`window.__hermesActHolder`), and detaching annotate/console state keyed to the old instance. An in-page navigation steered the same guest fine; only session-driven URL changes tore it down.

## Fix

- The guest-creation effect drops `target.url` from its deps and reads the live address through a `targetUrlRef` mirror, so the guest is created once per preview kind.
- A new steering effect, on `target.url` change, calls `webview.loadURL()` on the live guest instead of rebuilding it — preserving the instance and everything it holds.
- Per-page state resets explicitly around the load so nothing bleeds across pages: annotate (loopRef increment + `teardownAnnotateOverlay` + empty session), console (`consoleState.reset()`), history flags, load error, loading state. Skipped when the guest already shows the address (an in-page navigation arrived first).
- Error paths that previously closed over `target.url` (module-mime load error, `noteBrowserPage`, `did-fail-load`) now read `liveUrlRef.current` so they report the URL actually loaded.

## Coverage

- #120265 — webview instance reused across URL navigations via `loadURL`; JS state/cookies/form data/scroll/refs survive; annotate and console state reset cleanly around the load.

## Checks run

- `npx vitest run src/app/chat/right-rail/preview-pane.test.tsx --maxWorkers=2` — 26 passed (26), including the new regression test asserting the SAME guest node survives a `target.url` change, `loadURL` was called (not a src swap or rebuild), and the address bar tracks the new URL.
- Red on base: same test file against `origin/main`'s `preview-pane.tsx` — 1 failed (the new test), 25 passed. Restored afterwards.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/120303 (approved base — this branch is that commit rebased onto current `main`; authorship preserved: finn763)
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/120379 (closed/unresolvable duplicate)

Thanks @Finn763 for the original fix and regression test.

Fixes #120265

## Root cause
`useComposerSubmit` auto-skips a parked clarify card (`skipClarifyRequest` → `clarify.respond {answer: ''}`) and a parked connection card (`skipConnectionRequest` → `connection.respond {settled_by: 'continue'}`) for **any** non-empty draft. `/btw` (and `/bg` / `/background`) never speak into the blocked turn — they fork a side question / separate session — yet sending one resolved the pending card with an empty answer.

## Fix
- `isSideTaskSlashCommand(text)` in `lib/desktop-slash-commands.ts`: resolves the command through the slash registry (aliases + catalog) and returns true for side-task actions `btw` and `background` (`/btw`, `/bg`, `/background`, any case, bare or with args).
- `use-composer-submit.ts`: both auto-skips are bypassed for side-task commands. With attachments the draft is not routed as a slash command, so it keeps the ordinary-message behavior. Other slash commands (e.g. `/status`) and plain replies still skip the card as before.
- Test: fixed a `TS2352` cast in the contributor's gateway mock so desktop typecheck passes.

## Validation (in worktree, `apps/desktop`)
- `npx vitest run --project ui src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-submit.test.tsx src/lib/desktop-slash-commands.test.ts src/store/connection-request.test.ts` → **77 passed**.
- Red check: the same composer suite with `use-composer-submit.ts` restored from `origin/main` → **10 failed**. Each of the 5 side-task drafts × the clarify and connection cards fails: the clarify gets `{answer: ''}`, or the connection gets `settled_by: 'continue'`.
- `npm run typecheck` → exit 0, no TS errors.
- `npx eslint` + `npx prettier --check` on the 3 changed files → clean.
- Not run: a live Desktop manual check.

Supersedes #126220. Based on #126220 by @charan-rathore: the two cherry-picked commits keep their authorship, and the follow-up commit carries a co-author trailer. This PR adds the `/bg`/`/background` siblings, resolves commands through the registry instead of a regex, adds the attachment guard, and fixes the typecheck.

Fixes #126188

items.body:
## Root cause

Every desktop terminal tab stays mounted by design, so all xterm instances that share font/theme/DPR share one WebGL glyph atlas (@xterm/addon-webgl 0.19.0, pinned; the upstream sibling-notification fix in xtermjs/xterm.js#6055 is only in the 0.20.0-beta line). `clearTextureAtlas()` on one instance wipes the shared texture and rebuilds only the caller's render model; sibling terminals keep per-cell texture coordinates into the wiped atlas and render garbled glyphs until a resize forces a full rebuild. Separately, after a `webglcontextlost` the addon was disposed (DOM renderer takes over) but no repaint was forced, so the viewport could stay black while the buffer was intact.

## Fix

- `terminals.ts`: a `registerWebglRefresh` registry (unregister on dispose) and a coalesced single-rAF `redrawAllTerminals(skipTerm?)` with two-phase ordering — ALL atlas clears before ANY refresh, so no terminal rebuilds against an atlas that a later clear wipes.
- Every atlas-mutating call site fans out: theme change and tab activation for both the user terminal (`use-terminal-session.ts`) and the agent mirror (`use-agent-terminal.ts`), plus the live font change (`use-terminal-font.ts`).
- `webgl.onContextLoss` (both hooks): after disposing the dead addon, force a fit + full-row repaint so the DOM renderer shows the buffered output instead of a black canvas.
- Remaining `clearTextureAtlas` paths (the fan-out clear in the registry and the live font change) are wrapped so a half-dead GL context cannot abort the repaint path.
- `terminals.ts` subscribes to the main process's `hermes:power-resume` broadcast (powerMonitor `resume`/`unlock-screen`) and rebuilds every registered terminal: macOS can evict glyph textures on wake without firing `webglcontextlost`.

## Coverage

- #76102 — sibling garbling after shared-atlas clear (theme change, tab activation, font change) and the macOS resume-eviction variant: fully covered.
- #98273 — context-loss repaint (fit + `term.refresh(0, rows-1)` on both hooks). The reporter's exact Windows trigger is unconfirmed (custom skin, stock-theme repro still outstanding); tracked there rather than auto-closed.

## Checks run

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/app/right-sidebar/terminal/ --project ui` — 78 tests, all new/changed tests pass on this branch; all new tests fail on base (red-on-base proven by checking out base sources with the new test files). Two pre-existing tests in `terminals.test.ts` (`restores user tabs…`, `persists user tabs…`) time out on this machine both on base and on this branch — local first-import slowness, unrelated to this change.
- `npx tsc -p . --noEmit` — see PR checks.
- `npx eslint src/app/right-sidebar/terminal/` — see PR checks.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/76463
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/107808

Thanks @thatssoheil for the registry + two-phase fan-out design and tests, and @salch-cred for the context-loss repaint and the atlas-clear guards.

Fixes #76102

items.body:
## Root cause

The Desktop voice conversation runs its own full-duplex barge monitor (`lib/voice-barge-in.ts` → `use-voice-conversation.ts` `submitCapturedUtterance`). Over speakers, Hermes' own TTS bleeds into the mic and trips the playback-phase trigger. The captured audio is transcribed and submitted as the next user turn, with no check against the reply that was playing. The interruption latch also stays set, so the model gets told "the user interrupted your previous spoken reply" when nobody spoke. The CLI fixed the same loop with `tools/voice_mode_transcript.is_tts_echo`. The renderer never got that check.

## Fix

- `apps/desktop/src/lib/voice-tts-echo.ts`: a pure TS port of `is_tts_echo`. It includes a faithful `difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, a, b).ratio()` port (autojunk included, compared by code point), the 0.6 threshold, and `MIN_FRAGMENT_LENGTH_FOR_ECHO = 10` with the transcript-sized sliding window for fragments of long replies.
- `use-voice-conversation.ts`: when the barge trips, the hook records the text of the reply being spoken, but only if playback is audible (`$voicePlayback.status === 'speaking'`). It records it before playback is cut, because the reply is consumed by the time STT returns. This matches the CLI's playback-phase-only rule. In `submitCapturedUtterance`, after the stop-phrase check, a matching transcript counts as silence: nothing is submitted, `takeVoicePlaybackInterrupted()` clears the "user interrupted" latch, and the loop resumes listening. Generation-phase trips (no audio playing) and genuine interjections are unchanged.

No conflict with #80996. That PR applies the same guard to the TUI gateway listener and touches only `tui_gateway/server.py` and its test.

## Scope / residual (why this says "Covers", not "Fixes")

Covers the TTS-echo half of #126708. Not addressed:
- The client-direct STT path (`voice-client-direct.ts`) still skips the `is_whisper_hallucination` filter.
- The Desktop renderer still doesn't read `voice.barge_in` (only `barge_in_threshold_multiplier`).
- An echo still cuts playback when it trips, as in the CLI. We only know it was an echo after STT returns. If the reply was still being generated, the in-flight turn has already been interrupted too.

## Validation (worktree, `apps/desktop`, `unset PYTHONPATH`)

- Regression test: the new `use-voice-conversation.test.tsx` case "drops a playback-phase capture that is a fragment of the reply being spoken" **fails on origin/main's hook** (1 failed / 10 passed). With the fix, all pass. Two sibling cases check that a genuine playback-phase interjection and a generation-phase trip still submit.
- `voice-tts-echo.test.ts` mirrors every case in `tests/tools/test_voice_tts_echo_guard.py::TestIsTtsEcho`, plus CPython reference ratios, including the autojunk case.
- Differential check (not committed): 600 random cases generated with CPython `difflib` and `is_tts_echo`. The random strings were up to 400 chars, so autojunk ran. The TS ratio matched to 1e-12 and the echo verdict matched on 600/600.
- `npx vitest run src/lib/voice src/app/chat/composer`: 83 files, 607 tests passed.
- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- `npx eslint` on the 4 files: 0 errors. The one warning (`react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` on the drive effect) is pre-existing.
- `npx prettier --check`: clean.

Covers #126708 (echo half).

items.body:
Streaming into a long chat gets slower as the transcript grows. Settled messages already don't re-render per chunk on main (a new render-count test pins that at 0 for 8, 42 and 1602 messages), but two row selectors still scan the whole transcript on every thread notify — `runtimeUserOrdinal` in `user-message.tsx` and `interAgentSender` in `assistant-message.tsx` — so per-chunk cost is mounted rows × transcript length.

This builds one id→index and id→user-ordinal map per `thread.messages` array (WeakMap keyed by array identity) and shares it across rows. Results are identical (last-occurrence index, first-occurrence ordinal).

Measured in jsdom through the real pipeline (`useRuntimeMessageRepository` → `useIncrementalExternalStoreRuntime` → `<Thread />`), 10 chunks × 3 runs:

| history | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 20 turns | 4.8–8.3 ms/chunk | 5.5 ms/chunk |
| 400 turns | 38.4–45.1 ms/chunk | 29.4–30.6 ms/chunk |

Neither selector appears in the CPU profile afterwards. The rest of the per-chunk time is assistant-ui's per-subscriber machinery plus the O(N) `list.tsx` signatures and `timeline.tsx` layout loop, which this doesn't touch — so the issue stays open.

Covers the per-row transcript-scan part of #126486. Prior art: #69151 by @frizikk.

Tests: `stream-settled-renders.test.tsx` (settled roots/text parts re-render 0× per chunk, live tail does render — guards the property; passes on main too) and `thread-message-index.test.ts`. `npm run typecheck`, eslint, prettier clean; vitest 291 passed across `assistant-ui/thread/`, `runtime-repository`, `incremental-external-store-runtime`. Not yet measured with `npm run perf -- stream-history --spawn --prod`.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Stops a supervisor's stop signal from being logged and handled as an adapter crash when it reaches a managed child process (the WhatsApp bridge, the Photon sidecar) before the gateway's stop flow calls that adapter's `disconnect()`.

Both children run in their own session (`start_new_session=True`), so an ordinary signal to the gateway's process group never reaches them. A container-wide stop can still reach them: s6-overlay's stage 3 (the Hermes image's PID 1) SIGTERMs every process. Plain `docker stop` signals only the container's main process, so whether a child sees it depends on the init/supervisor. The child then exits with -15 while `_shutting_down` (WhatsApp) is still False or `_inbound_running` (Photon) is still True, and the adapter reports a retryable fatal error in the middle of shutdown.

The fix is @liuhao1024's #127067 cherry-picked with authorship intact. The classification also checks the runner's `_stop_requested_by_signal`, which the signal handler sets before it schedules `stop()`. This PR adds the same check to Photon's `_supervise_sidecar()`, the only other adapter that makes this exit-means-crash decision about a child in its own session.

A -15 exit while the gateway keeps running is still a retryable fatal error, so the reconnect watcher restarts the child. Examples: another Hermes process's `_kill_port_process` / `_kill_stale_bridge_by_pidfile`, or someone running `kill` by hand.

## What this changes on current main

Deterministic ordering reproduction (not a live Docker/s6 restart): a real `GatewayRunner`, a real `WhatsAppAdapter` and the real signal handler, with a real child process killed with SIGTERM before the adapter's `disconnect()` runs:

| Scenario | main | #127065 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Container stop (gateway + bridge both signalled) | ERROR "exited unexpectedly (code -15)", fatal handler runs, whatsapp queued for reconnect during shutdown | clean "exited during shutdown" | clean "exited during shutdown" |
| Bridge SIGTERMed while the gateway keeps running | retryable fatal, queued for reconnect ✅ | **not reported, never queued**: poll loop logs `Poll error` every 5 s and WhatsApp stays down | retryable fatal, queued for reconnect ✅ |

On current main this race does not change the process exit code. An unplanned SIGTERM already exits 1 on purpose (`_resolve_gateway_exit_verdict`, so the service manager restarts the gateway), and the fatal path queues the platform instead of setting `_exit_with_failure`. The problem this fixes is the wrong ERROR/fatal classification, the fatal-handler teardown, and the "retrying" platform status written during a normal stop. The crash loop in the issue was reported on v0.16.0 and does not reproduce on main.

## Related Issue

Fixes #127047
Salvages #127067

Supersedes #127065. Its approach, treating -15 as never fatal, is not adopted: a bridge SIGTERMed while the gateway is still running would never be queued for reconnect (second row above). Thanks @dskwe for the diagnosis, and @allissonbrito for the report and logs.

## Changes Made

- `plugins/platforms/whatsapp/adapter.py`: `_check_managed_bridge_exit()` also treats `{0, -2, -15}` as intentional when the runner flags a signal-driven stop (#127067, @liuhao1024).
- `plugins/platforms/photon/adapter.py`: `_supervise_sidecar()` skips the `SIDECAR_CRASHED` fatal when the runner flags a signal-driven stop.
- WhatsApp comment corrected: the bridge runs in its own session, not the gateway's process group.
- Tests: WhatsApp race window is not fatal and the no-flag SIGTERM stays fatal (#127067). Photon has the same pair, parametrized.

## How to Test

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_whatsapp_connect.py tests/gateway/test_runner_fatal_adapter.py tests/plugins/platforms/`: 203 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed (main: 198 passed, 4 skipped). Ruff clean on all changed files.
- RED check: with both adapters reverted to `origin/main`, the new race-window tests fail (WhatsApp sigterm/sigint, Photon gateway-stopping). The "stays fatal" cases pass on both.

## What does this PR do?

Fixes Windows source-install setup when the account path contains an apostrophe. The installer obtains a Python `-c` bootstrap from the installation launcher and invokes it through Windows PowerShell. Python's `repr()` chooses double quotes for a path containing `'`, and Windows PowerShell's native argument handoff removes those embedded quotes. Python then receives invalid source and setup exits with `SyntaxError`.

`runtime_command()` now writes its inline string values as single-quoted Python literals, encoding embedded quote characters as `\x27` and `\x22` on Windows. The module bootstrap remains visible in the process command line, preserving Hermes's gateway and updater process-identity checks. POSIX command construction is unchanged.

## Related Issue

No public issue filed. The regression test reproduces the failing Windows installer path with a synthetic apostrophe-containing account directory.

- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

- `hermes_cli/_launchers.py`: construct Windows inline Python string literals that survive PowerShell's native argv handoff without hiding the bootstrap from process inspection.

All three selected tests pass. The Windows process-identity probe still recognizes a `gateway run` command with an apostrophe in its root.

fix(wake): recover transient capture read failures and fall back to blocking reads when read_available stalls

## Root cause

Two independent bugs in the local-capture read loop of `tools/wake_word.py`, both reported on Windows:

- **#118001**: a single `stream.read` exception fell through to `failed = True`, permanently disarming wake detection until the user toggled it. Real microphone stacks (USB disconnect, device sleep, driver reset) throw transient read errors all the time.
- **#118552**: on some Windows DirectSound devices, `read_available` never advances even while audio flows. The poll guard introduced for #117096 then spins forever below `frame_length` and no audio is ever read.

## Fix

- `_run` catches a read error, closes the failed capture, and calls a new `_recover_capture` with a bounded whole-arm retry budget (0.5s / 1s / 2s) — reusing `_open_capture` so the owner and engine are kept, resetting the engine and silence counters on reopen. Exhausting the budget (or a stop during it) is the only path that arms `on_failure`.
- `_Capture.read` abandons the `read_available` poll guard after `_READ_STALL_FALLBACK_SECONDS` of starvation (warn once per capture, `_skip_available_poll`), falling back to the blocking read; a truly wedged blocking read is released by `_halt_thread` aborting the stream.
- `_halt_thread` keeps `self._cap` (armed by `_run` and re-armed on every recovery) so a wedged blocking read in the *current* capture is aborted when `pause()`/`stop()` joins out. `_open_capture` also closes the capture on a failed stream start.

## Coverage

- **#118001**: `tests/tools/test_wake_word_stream_recovery.py` — transient read failure recovers with the same device/engine; recovery is bounded and cancellable (read/open/cancel/external modes).
- **#118552**: `tests/tools/test_wake_word.py` — starved `read_available` falls back to blocking reads and warns once; starved-AND-wedged read is released by `pause()`'s abort (`#117096` guarantee preserved).
- **Composition**: new test proves that after recovery reopens the microphone, a reader wedged in the *recovered* capture is still released by `pause()` (the halt hook follows the recovered capture — this was a gap when composing the two PRs; fixed here).

## Checks

- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tools/test_wake_word.py tests/tools/test_wake_word_stream_recovery.py` — 74 passed, 0 failed, 4 skipped (platform skips).
- The composition test is red on the composed contributor commits without the `self._cap` re-arm fix (verified by checking out the pre-fix `tools/wake_word.py`).

Windows DirectSound behaviour itself cannot be exercised on macOS; the stream-mock tests above are the detection net, and final e2e confirmation needs a Windows host (#118560's How-to-Test).

## Supersedes

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/118011
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/118560

Thanks @Wenfengcheng and @liuhao1024 — both commits are cherry-picked verbatim (rebase-merged onto main) so authorship is preserved.

## Root cause

`website/docs/user-guide/desktop.md` promises Review-pane diffs scoped to **Uncommitted, Branch, or Last turn**, but the renderer hardcodes `'uncommitted'` (`src/store/review.ts`: `review.list(cwd, 'uncommitted', null)` and the diff read the same).
