## What

A console-less parent (the `pythonw` desktop backend, detached daemons) allocates a **visible console window for every bare `subprocess` spawn of a console-subsystem child**. On Windows startup that means ~7-8 flashing console windows (#117781), and the GPU statusbar paints **two more every 5 seconds** via `nvidia-smi` (#101895).

## Root cause

`hermes_cli._subprocess_compat.windows_hide_flags()` (CREATE_NO_WINDOW) exists and is the established pattern, but a dozen spawn sites never threaded it through.

## Changes

- `gitlock.py`: tasklist/pgrep process probe (now one shared spawn), `_git_stdout_lines`, both `_batch_missing_parents` git spawns, `repair_broken_shallow_boundaries` rev-list probe, `prune_stale_grafts` reflog expire, `fetch_full_commit_graph` — all carry `creationflags=windows_hide_flags()`.
- `gateway.py` `_windows_scheduled_task_state`: the scheduled-task PowerShell probe hides its window.
- `update_cmd.py`: `_git_run` (the updater's central git runner, ~26 call sites) and `_no_prompt_git_kwargs()` (network fetch/pull) carry the flags — layered, not duplicated, when both apply.
- `update_cmd_git.py`: `_GIT_TEXT_KW` shared kwargs and its `_git_run` runner hide every plumbing spawn; `update_cmd_check.py` `_git` too.
- `_subprocess_compat.py` safe-directory `git config` probes.
- **Statusbar consolidation (#101895 + #120262)**: `hardware.py` gains `_cached_nvidia_gpu_query()` — ONE nvidia-smi spawn (hidden) per 4s TTL window shared by `_nvidia_vram()`, the `/api/local-models/hardware` endpoint, and `bootstrap._detect_gpu_vendor()` — instead of two bare spawns per 5s poll. Failures are cached too, so a missing smi doesn't respawn per poll.
- `system-resources-statusbar.tsx`: polling pauses while `document.hidden` and resumes on `visibilitychange`.

## Acceptance coverage

- #117781 — all four files' sites + siblings covered. **Fixes #117781**
- #101895 — hide flags + single spawn per poll. **Fixes #101895**
- #120262 — one spawn per poll window + visibility-paused polling. [Refs #120262](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/120262) — poll-interval backoff for foreground games not included.

## Tests (all run on this Mac, Darwin)

Python — `HERMES_PYTHON=<test-venv>/bin/python bash scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/test_windows_subprocess_no_window_flags.py`:
- on `origin/main` (current): **11 failed, 4 passed, 3 skipped** — every new wiring test red.
- with this branch: **15 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped** (the 3 `platforms('windows')` tests skip on darwin and run on the Windows lane).

JS — `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/app/shell/system-resources-statusbar.test.tsx`:
- on `origin/main`: **2 failed, 1 passed** (poll fires while hidden / no resume on visible).
- with this branch: **3 passed**.

## Not exercised live

The console-hiding itself is a Windows-only behaviour — the `creationflags` wiring is unit-proven (helper stubbed to CREATE_NO_WINDOW, asserting each site threads it into `subprocess.run`), but that **zero consoles actually paint needs a Windows 11 check**, ideally watching a `pythonw`-style console-less backend startup and a 5s statusbar poll. VRAM/name parsing from the consolidated query should also be eyeballed on a real NVIDIA Windows box.

Supersedes #117805, #117833, #102047, #120285. Thanks @JoaoMarcos44, @Finn763, @monerostar, @szzhoujiarui — the site inventories and the cached-query design came from your PRs.

items.body:
## What

All four `shell: true` call sites in the desktop main process pass the executable path **unquoted** to the shell. On Windows that shell is cmd.exe, which truncates the command line at the first space: an install under `C:\Users\John Doe\...` makes every probe and backend launch run `C:\Users\John` — so the desktop ignores a perfectly working hermes install and offers the installer instead (#74064).

## Root cause

No quoting helper existed; `resolveHermesBackend` still marks `.cmd` shims for shell execution (`shell: shellForProbe`), and each site passes `command` straight through.

## Changes

- New `windowsShellCommand(command, shell)` in `electron/windows-child-options.ts`: wraps the executable in double quotes when the shell will interpret the line (cmd.exe `/s` semantics keep the quoted command intact); already-quoted commands and non-Windows platforms pass through unchanged. Arguments stay in the separate array — only the executable token is quoted.
- Applied at the four shell-delegating sites:
  - `backend-probes.ts` `verifyHermesCli` — the `--version` probe,
  - `backend-serve-support.ts` — the `serve --help` probe,
  - `main.ts` — both `spawnOwnedBackend` call sites (primary backend start + per-profile pool start), quoted only when `backend.shell` is truthy.

## Acceptance coverage

**Fixes #74064** — all five requirements: version probe quotes, serve probe quotes, both backend spawn sites quote, regression test with a spaced fixture path, direct execution and non-Windows commands unchanged.

## Tests (run on this Mac, Darwin)

`cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 electron/windows-child-options.test.ts electron/backend-probes.test.ts electron/backend-serve-support.test.ts`
- with this branch: **30 passed (3 files)**.
- on `origin/main` (pristine extraction + the new tests): the 4 new `windowsShellCommand` unit tests fail (helper absent); the behavioral premise was also verified directly — an unquoted spaced path through `shell: true` exits 127 (shell truncates at the space) on POSIX just as on cmd.exe, and the quoted form exits 0.

`npx tsc -p . --noEmit` — exit 0.

## Not exercised live

The cmd.exe `/s` quote semantics are Windows-specific. The helper's quoting logic is unit-proven and the truncation failure mode reproduces identically on POSIX sh, but **a Windows run with a spaced-path `.cmd` fixture install needs a check on a Windows host** (probe succeeds + backend launches from a spaced user-profile path).

Supersedes #74073. Thanks @dk3yyyy — the helper design and test cases come from your PR; the sites moved since (serve probe now in `backend-serve-support.ts`, both spawns via `spawnOwnedBackend`), so it is re-applied at the current locations.

## Root cause

`setPermissionCheckHandler` hand-rolled its permission allow-list with two `as any` casts and an unanswered `/* todo: is this needed? */`, while the async request handler already delegates to a typed `isMediaCapturePermission` helper — the exact inconsistency #78223 asks to remove. The casts existed because Electron's check-handler `permission` union predates the capture permission strings Chromium actually sends at runtime (`audioCapture`, `videoCapture`, `automatic-fullscreen`).

## What changes

- Extract the predicate into `apps/desktop/electron/media-capture-permission.ts` with widened `MediaCapturePermissionString` / `MediaCapturePermissionDetails` types that document exactly which runtime strings the Electron unions don't admit (and why widening is needed).
- Both session hooks now delegate to the one shared predicate; the check handler passes `undefined` details (Chromium gives it no mediaTypes metadata), which allow-lists the same strings it allowed before: `media`, `automatic-fullscreen`, `audioCapture`, `videoCapture` — plus `fullscreen`, which the old hand-rolled body accidentally denied on the check handler while the request handler allowed it.
- The `as any` casts and the todo are gone; the docstring covers the Windows empty-`mediaTypes` rationale the todo was asking about.

Policy is unchanged for every string the old handler saw; the only behavior delta is that `'fullscreen'` now resolves the same way on both handlers (allowed), matching `isMediaCapturePermission`'s documented contract.

## Acceptance coverage per issue

- #78283 requirement 1 (remove `as any` casts in the check handler): done — handler body is one typed call.
- Requirement 2 (resolve the todo by validating runtime behavior): the todo is replaced by the helper's docstring documenting the Windows empty-`mediaTypes` behavior and the macOS TCC backstop; runtime validation on Windows is noted below.
- Requirement 3 (reuse/reconcile with `isMediaCapturePermission`): both handlers now share the one extracted predicate.

Fixes #78223
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/78233 (same extraction idea, but that PR adds a `mediaType === 'video' → false` denial the request handler doesn't have — re-introducing the inter-handler disagreement — and carries unrelated patch files. Thanks @iborazzi for the direction.)

## Tests

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run electron/media-capture-permission.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` — 6/6 pass (shared-predicate cases: check-handler shape without metadata, Windows empty-mediaTypes shape, one-policy invariant across both handlers, denials).
- `cd apps/desktop && npx tsc -p . --noEmit` — exit 0.

## Not exercised live

The runtime permission flow (getUserMedia capture on Windows, where Chromium consults the check handler in place of the request handler) needs a Windows session to confirm end-to-end; the pure predicate is fully unit-tested and the handler wiring is a one-line delegation with unchanged policy for previously-handled strings.

items.body:
## Root cause

`hermes update`'s macOS re-sign and swap path resolved signing policy with two bugs:

1. **Electron Framework lost its entitlements on local re-sign** (#85620): `_desktop_macos_local_codesign` gated the inherit entitlement plist on `bundle.suffix == ".app" and "Helper" in bundle.name`, so `Electron Framework.framework` was signed with `--options runtime` but **no** `allow-jit` / `allow-unsigned-executable-memory` — hardened runtime then traps V8 (`SIGTRAP` in `Isolate::Initialize`) on the next self-updated launch.
2. **A failed configured identity had one blanket fallback** (#121857, #123748): the except branch of `_desktop_macos_relaunchable_fixup` went straight from a failed `desktop.macos_signing_identity` attempt to the legacy `codesign --deep --sign -` (cdhash-only DR, entitlements stripped) — resetting TCC grants every rebuild — and neither the fixup nor `_install_rebuilt_macos_bundles` ever checked whether the bundle being replaced was **publisher-signed** (Team ID), so a `hermes update` could silently swap a Developer-ID installation for an ad-hoc/local build, invalidating the cdhash-bound keychain ACLs safeStorage credentials live under.

## What changes

- **Nested bundles all take the inherit entitlements** during inside-out local re-sign — frameworks included (`allow-jit` is what V8 needs under the hardened runtime). (#85607's minimal fix.)
- **Configured-identity failure is now policy-aware** instead of blanket ad-hoc:
  - over a **publisher-signed (Team ID)** replace-target: **refuse** — keep the installed bundle, name the remedy (`--setup-tcc-identity` / `desktop.macos_signing_identity`), never fall back to ad-hoc (#123748's no-downgrade requirement);
  - over a **locally-signed/ad-hoc** target: retry the same inside-out signer with `identity="-"` (identifier-pinned DR, entitlements kept — one TCC re-prompt instead of a full reset) before the legacy cdhash-only sign (#121857).
- **`_macos_signature_summary` + `_macos_signing_downgrade_error`**: pre-swap verification of Team ID, bundle identifier, and strict signature state; a publisher-signed install is never replaced by a local/unknown-identity or unverifiable rebuild — the swap is refused and reported instead. Ad-hoc→ad-hoc (local development) is untouched.
- **`_promote_staged_desktop_app` no longer discards a refused fixup**: a staging whose signature could not be established is discarded and the previous-app-kept error path fires, so the live bundle is never swapped for an unsigned build.
- Refusal messages name the next action (publisher identity / signing setting / bundle id / `codesign -vvv`), matching the running-app message style.

## Acceptance coverage

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/85620 — framework entitlements: `test_desktop_macos_local_codesign_preserves_framework_entitlements` (fails on main: framework signed with `--requirements` instead of `--entitlements inherit`). **Fixes.**
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/121857 — pinned-ad-hoc retry on identity failure: `test_relaunchable_fixup_failed_identity_uses_pinned_adhoc_before_legacy` (fails on main: only the configured identity is tried, then legacy), `test_relaunchable_fixup_legacy_when_pinned_adhoc_also_fails` (legacy still last resort). **Fixes.**
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/123748 — no-downgrade + pre-swap verification: `test_publisher_signed_install_is_never_replaced_by_local_build`, `test_team_id_mismatch_refuses_swap`, `test_bundle_identifier_mismatch_refuses_swap`, `test_unverifiable_rebuilt_refuses_swap`, `test_matching_publisher_signing_swaps`, `test_adhoc_installed_still_swaps`, `test_relaunchable_fixup_configured_identity_failure_never_falls_back_to_adhoc`, `test_promote_staged_desktop_app_refuses_an_unsigned_staging`. **Partial** — reqs 2–3 (verify-before-swap, never silently downgrade) are covered; req 1 (CI notarized release channel for git installs) is separate release-engineering work; req 4 (keychain ACL rotation on cdhash change) is tracked separately in https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/91115.

## Test evidence (real runs, macOS host)

Red on `origin/main` (branch tests applied to a detached `origin/main` worktree):
`scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_cli/test_gui_command.py tests/hermes_cli/test_desktop_install_after_update.py` → **11 failed** (5 in test_gui_command: framework entitlements, both pinned-adhoc fallback tests, publisher-target refusal, promotion refusal; 6 in test_desktop_install_after_update: the whole downgrade-guard matrix), 61 passed.

Green with the fix (branch @ ffe27f461a7):
`scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_cli/test_gui_command.py tests/hermes_cli/test_desktop_install_after_update.py` → **83 passed, 0 failed, 14 skipped**.

## Limitations

- Runtime signing behavior is exercised through the real fixup/promotion functions with codesign stubbed at the process boundary; no real Developer-ID signing or notarization happens in tests (no credentials on CI).
- The SSH-locked-keychain scenario (#121857's trigger) is simulated by a failing configured identity, not a real locked login keychain.
- #123748's req 1 and req 4 are explicitly out of scope here (see above).

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/91207 — Thanks @ryrenz (framework entitlements fix + its regression test, cherry-picked)
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/121958 — Thanks @686f6c61 (pinned-ad-hoc retry + fallback tests, cherry-picked)
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/123769 — Thanks @dskwe (signature summary, downgrade guard, promotion refusal + test matrix, cherry-picked)

The three conflicted on the same except branch; this PR reconciles them: publisher-signed target → hard refusal (#123769's policy), locally-signed target → identifier-pinned ad-hoc retry (#121958's policy), with #91207's entitlement fix underneath.

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/85620
Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/121857

items.body:
## Root cause

The backend persists segments while a turn runs. Switching away mid-stream and back hydrates the store's flat mid-turn partial next to the still-streaming local copy — and that partial need not be a byte prefix of the streamed text (tool-call interleaving, different separators around folded tool rounds, reference lines). `localPendingSupersedes` only accepted a local row over the authoritative row when the store text was empty or a strict byte prefix, so the stale store row won and the pre-switch streamed content was dropped on hydrate (#80151).

`preserveLocalPendingTurnMessages` already widens this pairing for a *settled* local final over an empty committed tool shell (#123047, merged as #127038). This is the divergent-partial direction: a still-**pending** local stream meeting a **committed** same-turn partial whose flat text is not a prefix.

## What changes

In `localPendingSupersedes`, a still-pending local stream row may claim a committed same-turn row only with same-turn proof:

- **shared tool-call ids** — every tool-call id the committed row names also streams locally (call ids are unique to the turn), and the committed text is one of the stream's own folded text segments (or a prefix of one — a mid-segment flush); or
- **folded strict prefix** — the streamed answer, with reference lines stripped and separators folded away, strictly extends the committed text.

Guards kept: the streamed copy must cover the committed text (never trade a committed partial for a shorter local row); an empty-text committed row is never claimable (empty prose carries no identity, #114543); interim narration and settled rows are unchanged; the different-turn-at-same-ordinal protection (a resent prompt answered earlier) still refuses.

## Acceptance coverage

- #80151 requirement 1 (switching away mid-stream and back preserves pre-switch content) — `keeps a pending streamed reply when the store holds a same-turn partial whose flat text is not a byte prefix`
- #80151 requirement 2 (hydrate/resume retains the live pending stream over a stale persisted row with divergent tails) — `keeps a pending streamed reply over a committed same-turn partial proven by shared tool-call ids`
- Negative guards — `does not let a pending stream claim a different turn's committed answer at the same ordinal`, `does not trade a committed partial for a pending stream that is behind its text`

Requirement 3 of #80151 (flushing queued deltas client-side at session switch) is deliberately **not** implemented here — it is a separate backend/gateway flush change, out of scope for this merge-guard fix.

## Tests

- Red on `origin/main` (fd0b98f6256): `streamed-reply-survives-sync.test.ts` → **2 failed / 8 passed** (the two #80151 positive shapes fail; all #123047 shell tests pass on main via #127038).
- Green with fix: **10 passed (10)**.
- Regression: the full `use-session-actions` suite (utils.test.ts, resume-empty-prose-pairing.test.ts, streamed-reply-survives-sync.test.ts — 144 tests) was green in an earlier iteration of the same logic; the merged files rerun green here.

Fixes #80151

Thanks @kvnloo — the test harness and the guard shape here build directly on your #123065.

items.body:
## Root cause

The cold-start navigation restore in `use-desktop-integrations` ran in peer instance windows too — its only exclusions were `isHudWindow() || isBrowserWindow()`. A `?peer=1` window (Ctrl+Shift+N / New Window) therefore restored the profile's remembered last-session route (`getRememberedRoute`, written continuously by the primary window) and booted into the same chat as Window 1, instead of the blank fresh-draft route (#74948).

The source-restoration path in `connections.ts` already excludes `isPeerInstanceWindow()`; the route-restore gate was missing the same exclusion.

## What changes

Add `isPeerInstanceWindow()` to the restore effect's early-return gate in `use-desktop-integrations.ts`, mirroring `connections.ts`. A peer window skips remembered-route/remembered-session restore and stays on the fresh draft.

Product note (flagged for the reviewer): the plain `isPeerInstanceWindow()` gate means an explicit "Open profile in new window" (`profileWindow=1`) also boots onto the fresh draft. The profile override still applies to boot **profile selection** — only the remembered-**route** restore is skipped. The verdict named this as a product call; the alternative (`isPeerInstanceWindow() && !windowProfileOverride()`) is a one-line change if the reviewer prefers profile windows to restore their remembered route.

The second #74948 requirement (closing Window 2 must not orphan Window 1's stream) is a separate WS-subscription-routing issue and needs reproduction before any fix; not addressed here.

## Tests

- Red on `origin/main` (fd0b98f6256): new test `peer instance windows (#74948) > does not restore the primary window's remembered session into a peer window` fails — `navigate` is called once with the remembered session route while the same fixture correctly restores it in the adjacent main-window tests.
- Green with fix: full `use-desktop-integrations.test.tsx` — 38 passed (38), including the adjacent main-window restore tests still passing (gate does not affect them).

Fixes #74948

items.body:
## Root cause

Four reports, one pipeline: the build freshness machinery that guards `hermes update`'s desktop rebuild treats noise and self-inflicted changes as genuine input changes, and the completion tails that run it are not serialized.

1. **OS file-manager metadata is hashed as a build input.** `scripts/build/freshness.mjs`'s tree hash skipped generated build dirs but not `.DS_Store`, AppleDouble `._*` sidecars, `.localized`, `Thumbs.db` or `Desktop.ini`. Finder or Explorer touching the checkout mid-build flips the source hash and `recordProduct` throws `Build inputs changed during compilation` — the update is marked failed for a cosmetic file (#122632, #122803).
2. **The build's own stamp rewrite trips its own guard.** `write-build-stamp.mjs` rewrites `builtAt` on every build, and the desktop stamp is a hashed *prepared* input. A second build racing the first (or a restamp landing between `bundleElectronMain` and the receipt) kills or mis-certifies the build with a difference the build machinery itself made (#123308).
3. **`withProduct`'s single `rmSync` races Finder.** Removing the `.dist-*` scratch dir can hit `ENOTEMPTY` when Finder drops a `.DS_Store` into it mid-removal, aborting an otherwise-clean product build (#122803).
4. **Stacked source completions race.** A gateway restarted while `hermes update` still runs (launchd `KeepAlive`, a second `hermes` launch) reaches the same completion tail through `venv_sync`, and two tails build the same output directories concurrently and race on `install-stamp.json`, leaving a mixed desktop build and a permanent "Restart to finish update" banner (#123376).

## What changes

- `scripts/build/freshness.mjs`: an `osMetadata` skip (.DS_Store, `._*`, `.localized`, Thumbs.db, Desktop.ini) applied inside `treeHash`, so it covers **every** hashed tree — source, output and prepared directories. Desktop stamps hash their *provenance identity* (commit/payload/tag) instead of raw bytes, with the `builtAt` clock recorded separately as `stampClock` — the clock the output actually baked, passed from `bundleElectronMain`, not re-read from disk. The mid-compile guard (`recordProduct`) ignores the clock while still failing on real provenance changes; the pre-build gate (`productCurrent`) still sees it so packaging can't ship a bundle whose copied stamp disagrees with the baked main. Missing/unparsable stamps fall back to a stable whole-file hash instead of throwing.
- `scripts/build/frontend-common.mjs`: `rmTree` retries `ENOTEMPTY` removals a bounded number of times (5 × 50 ms) so the Finder race can't abort the update receipt; non-`ENOTEMPTY` errors propagate immediately.
- `hermes_cli/source_completion.py`: `complete_source_checkout` claims the shared `UpdateLock` (same marker the Tauri updater and Electron read), so stacked completions serialize. A tail whose orchestrator already holds the lock (venv_sync's interrupted-update finish, the updater's completion child) runs under its parent's claim via the existing handoff-pid/ancestor path; only a genuinely concurrent update hits the refusal.
- `scripts/build/desktop.mjs` + `apps/desktop/scripts/bundle-electron-main.mjs`: thread the baked stamp clock from the bundle step to the receipt.
- `scripts/build/README.md`: documents the skip sets and the clock semantics.

## Acceptance coverage

- **#122632** — `.DS_Store`/`._*`/`.localized` (and Thumbs.db/Desktop.ini) written into any hashed tree no longer flips `productCurrent`; a real source change still does. Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/122632
- **#122803** — the hash flip and the `ENOTEMPTY` scratch-dir race are both absorbed; real changes still fail closed. Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/122803
- **#123308** — restamps no longer trip the mid-compile guard or the pre-build gate for clock-only differences; provenance changes still do; the receipt records the baked clock. Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/123308
- **#123376** — concurrent completion tails serialize on the shared update lock instead of racing on `install-stamp.json`. Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/123376

## Tests (real runs; red first)

Red on `origin/main` @ `fd0b98f625`, with this branch's new test files copied over:

```
npx vitest run tests-js/freshness-metadata.test.mjs --maxWorkers=1
  → 1 failed: web/src/._main.ts: expected false to be true (AppleDouble sidecar flips productCurrent)
npx vitest run tests-js/frontend-common.test.mjs --maxWorkers=1
  → 3 failed: rmTree is not a function
scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_cli/test_source_completion_stamp.py
  → 7 passed, 2 failed (the new lock-holding / refuse-to-stack tests)
```

Green on this branch @ `3f1f2daf4e0`:

```
npx vitest run tests-js/freshness-metadata.test.mjs tests-js/frontend-common.test.mjs --maxWorkers=1
  → 4 passed
npx vitest run tests-js/desktop-builder.test.mjs --maxWorkers=1
  → 11 passed, 1 failed — 'native preparation stages…' times out at its default 5 s; it fails identically on main @ fd0b98f625 (npm staging under load), pre-existing
scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_cli/test_source_completion_stamp.py
  → 9 passed
```

Pre-existing on main, not caused by this diff (verified by running the same files on `fd0b98f625`): two `product-builders` tests assert an unprefixed `/var/folders` TMPDIR path that macOS reports as `/private/var/folders`, and several 30 s-timeout build tests flake under CI-level load.

## Limitations

- Thumbs.db/Desktop.ini skipping is filename logic and OS-independent, but it was only exercised on macOS here.
- The `UpdateLock` refusal path surfaces as a `RuntimeError` ("an update is still running") to the restart that raced it; recovery is relaunching after the update exits, which venv_sync already prints.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/122636 — the `macMetadata` skip in `treeHash` is taken from this PR (cherry-picked); extended to Windows metadata and all prepared trees. Thanks @PRATHAMESH75.
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/125734 — byte-identical to #122636. Thanks @MwC-Trexx.
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/123078 — the `rmTree` `ENOTEMPTY` bounded retry is taken from this PR; its narrower `.DS_Store`-only hash exclusion is subsumed. Thanks @dlshumway.
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/123377 — the stamp-identity hashing and clock split are taken from this PR (cherry-picked whole). Thanks @Halldrix.

items.title: fix(build,update): OS metadata, stamp-clock races and stacked completions break the desktop freshness pipeline

items.body:
## Root cause

The `.hermes-update-in-progress` marker gates every update acquire and every
Desktop boot, and its owner is judged alive by a bare `kill(pid, 0)` /
`os.kill(pid, 0)` probe. Two defects stack:

1. **The Rust reader never self-healed.** `live_marker_owner` in
   `apps/bootstrap-installer/src-tauri/src/update.rs` returned `None` for a
   stale marker (dead pid, past ceiling, unparseable) but left the file on
   disk — unlike its Python twin `read_live_update`
   (`hermes_cli/update_lock.py`), which unlinks. A crashed updater whose
   `Drop` never ran therefore left every later acquire refusing
   "Another Hermes update is already running" until the 20-minute age
   ceiling expired.
2. **`kill(pid, 0)` false-positives on zombies.** A process that exited but
   whose parent has not reaped it answers signal 0 like a live one, on every
   POSIX platform. A crashed updater lingering unreaped kept its marker
   "live" for the full 20-minute ceiling in all three readers (Rust
   installer, Python CLI gate, Electron boot gate).

## What changes

- **Rust** (`update.rs`, cherry-picked from #77885, authorship kept):
  `live_marker_owner` now `remove_file`s a marker judged stale (dead pid,
  past-ceiling, unparseable pid line), mirroring `read_live_update`.
  `pid_is_alive` returns `false` for pid 0 (`kill(0,0)` always succeeds — a
  marker corrupted to "0" read as alive forever) and consults the process
  state on Linux (`/proc/<pid>/stat`, state `Z`) and macOS (`ps -o stat=`),
  failing open to the signal-0 verdict when the state can't be read.
- **Python** (`hermes_cli/_early_recovery.py`): new `_process_state(pid)`
  probe (Linux `/proc`, macOS `ps`), and `_pid_is_running` treats a zombie as
  dead. `read_live_update` in `update_lock.py` already unlinked stale
  markers — it inherits the zombie-awareness through `_pid_alive`, so a
  zombie-owned marker now self-heals in seconds instead of 20 minutes.
- **Electron** (`apps/desktop/electron/update-marker.ts`): new
  `posixProcessState(pid)` export (same probes, fail-open to the signal-0
  verdict), and `readLiveUpdateMarker` unlinks a marker whose owner answers
  signal 0 but is a zombie. The probe is injectable for tests.

The lock contract is preserved: a live foreign owner still blocks, and a
marker pre-written with our own pid is still reported for adoption
(#74761 handoff), never deleted.

## Acceptance coverage per issue

- **Fixes #77259** — the Tauri updater wedge: stale-marker unlink-on-read +
  zombie-aware pid hardening in the Rust reader, with the dead-pid /
  past-ceiling / malformed / live-foreign / own-live regression tests the
  issue asks for.
- #120635 (partial) — the stale-marker boot-gate self-heal now works when
  the owner is dead-but-unreaped in all three readers (the macOS
  `kill(0)` false-positive window); surfacing of the handoff result after
  gate-clear already exists on main (`main.ts` `readAndConsumeHandoffResult`
  after `waitForUpdateToFinish`). The PATH-warning and gateway-restart
  surfacing asks are separate UX work, not covered here.
- #125932 (partial) — the "wedge for up to 20 min" half: a dead or zombie
  updater clears in seconds on every reader, and the Python gate unlinks
  stale markers explicitly. The marker-owner-identity claim (gateway pid as
  owner) could not be reproduced — every in-tree writer writes its own pid
  — and the bundle-skew git-storm half is tracked in #125243.
- #109795 (partial) — the dead/zombie-owner liveness half only. The full
  JSON-marker schema (run_id, step, heartbeat) is a larger cross-language
  change deliberately not attempted here.

## Test evidence (macOS arm64; Linux zombie branches exercised by CI)

Red on `origin/main` (new tests copied onto a clean main checkout):

- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_cli/test_early_recovery.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_lock.py`
  → **4 failed** (3 zombie/state-probe tests, 1 zombie-owned-marker self-heal), 28 passed.
- `npx vitest run electron/update-marker.test.ts` (apps/desktop) →
  **2 failed** (zombie marker stays live; `posixProcessState` does not exist), 18 passed.
- `cargo test --manifest-path apps/bootstrap-installer/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --lib update`
  → 29 passed, 0 failed — the 9 new tests do not exist on main.

Green with this branch (same commands):

- Python → **46 passed, 0 failed**.
- Electron → **20 passed, 0 failed**.
- Rust → **38 passed, 0 failed** (includes all 9 new tests:
  `live_marker_owner_removes_stale_marker_with_dead_pid`,
  `live_marker_owner_removes_marker_past_the_age_ceiling`,
  `live_marker_owner_removes_malformed_marker`,
  `live_marker_owner_keeps_live_foreign_marker`,
  `live_marker_owner_keeps_own_live_marker`,
  `pid_is_alive_false_for_unusable_pid`,
  `pid_is_alive_false_for_pid_zero`,
  `pid_is_alive_false_for_zombie`, `pid_is_alive_true_for_self`).

## Limitations

- The Linux `/proc` zombie branch is compile-gated and exercised by CI's
  Linux lane; the macOS `ps` branch was verified locally (tests above).
- The few-seconds `kill(0)` false-positive window for a *just-exited* pid
  (not yet zombie, entry still in the table) is inherent to pid probing
  without start-time checks and matches the Python side's behavior.
- Windows `pid_is_alive` is untouched (Win32 handle API, no zombie state).

Supersedes #77885 — thanks @webtecnica for the Rust fix and tests, which
this PR carries forward with the Python and Electron parity work.

items.body:
## Root cause

Two defects on the pop-out renderer boundary:

1. **#101198** — after popping the Browser out, the live webview registries (`activePreviewScriptRunner` / `activePreviewInput` / `activePreviewNav`) exist only in the pop-out renderer, while the chat window still passes the active-session gate for `preview.act` / `preview.read` (`server-requests.ts` `WINDOW_OWNED_REQUESTS`). The chat window's handlers ran the local engine with no live webview and answered `NOTHING_OPEN` / empty.
2. **#103245** — Comment Mode's flush rode the renderer-local composer CustomEvent bus, which cannot cross windows, and nothing recorded the originating chat on the popped tab. The batch was delivered nowhere and the pins were cleared anyway.

## Fix

One shared cross-window relay, so the codebase grows a single mechanism for the pop-out boundary:

- **`hermes:window:relay`** (electron/main.ts + preload) — main relays opaque payloads between Hermes renderer windows. Packaged builds load renderers over `file://`, where BroadcastChannel origin semantics must not be trusted; BroadcastChannel stays as a dev/test fallback.
- **#101198 leg** — new `preview-popout-bridge.ts`: the chat window's `previewAct`/`previewRead` handlers forward the action/read to the pop-out when this window has no live surface and answer with its result; a silent pop-out falls back to the legacy local answer (empty read / `NOTHING_OPEN`). The pop-out installs a responder in `browser-popout-shell.tsx` and only serves requests when it is the browser window.
- **#103245 leg** — `store/preview.ts` pins the exact chat/group composer destination at pop-out time (`capturePreviewAnnotateDestination`, nearest-group + workspace-owner resolution); the pop-out's flush hands the batch (prompt + numbered crops) to that exact surface over the relay, ACK-correlated, and fails closed — pins are retained with a warning when the destination is gone or does not ACK. Never auto-sends: it populates the draft and focuses the composer.

## Coverage

- #101198: chat window with no live surface forwards act/read; local surface still runs locally; no pop-out answering keeps the legacy answer.
- #103245: destination pinned at pop-out (multi-pane nearest-group + workspace-owner fallback, fail-closed when ambiguous); delivery only to the pinned window/surface; ACK retention on failure; docked (non-popped) flush path unchanged.

## Checks run

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/app/chat/right-rail/preview-popout-bridge.test.ts src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event/server-requests.test.ts src/lib/preview-annotate/handoff.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` — 29 passed
- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/lib/preview-annotate/ src/store/preview.test.ts src/app/chat/composer/focus.test.ts src/plugins/hermes-bots/group-chat-view.test.ts src/plugins/hermes-bots/group-chat-view.render.test.tsx src/app/chat/right-rail/preview-pane.test.tsx --maxWorkers=2` — 141 passed
- Red on base proven: the new `server-requests` forwarding tests were run against `origin/main`'s `server-requests.ts` — 3 of 4 fail there.

## Supersedes

items.body:
## Root cause

`minimize-to-tray.ts`'s shared `hide()` calls `win.hide()` without releasing keyboard focus. On Windows a hidden Chromium window emits no `blur` and keeps the UI thread's `hwndFocus`, so keys and screen readers (NVDA) stay trapped in the invisible page after a tray hide.

## What changes

- In the shared `hide()` path (both entry points funnel through it: the deferred minimize handler from #119252 and close-to-tray/Alt+F4), `win.blur()` is called on `win32` **before** `win.hide()` — once hidden, the blur no longer takes.

## Acceptance coverage per issue

Issue #126570 requirements:
- no app window owns keyboard focus after a tray hide → `win.blur()` before `win.hide()` on win32
- both hide entry points covered → single shared `hide()` is the choke point
- screen readers not trapped → follows from focus release; needs on-Windows verification with the report's GetGUIThreadInfo probe

## Tests run (real results)

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run electron/minimize-to-tray.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` **on origin/main** (fix reverted, test kept): **1 failed** — `Windows tray hide releases keyboard focus before hiding (#126570)` fails (`focused` stays true)
- Same command **with the fix**: **1 file, 6 tests passed**
- `cd apps/desktop && npx tsc -p . --noEmit`: **exit 0**

The test fake models the Win32 reality (hide does not release focus; only explicit blur does), so the regression test proves ordering: blur fires exactly once, before hide.

## Not exercised live

Actual focus release (`GetGUIThreadInfo`'s `hwndFocus == null`) needs verification on real Windows with NVDA, for both the minimize-to-tray and close-to-tray paths.

Fixes #126570

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/126697 (Thanks @Yicheng-Mark) — its branch is pre-da77a7e2e8 and re-lands the already-merged deferred-hide/restore-re-activate hunks; this PR carries only the blur-before-hide delta on current main.

items.body:
## Root cause

`drive_preview` / `annotate_preview` bridge onto a `preview.act` JSON-RPC server request with a flat 45s deadline (`tui_gateway/agent_callbacks.py`: `_ask("preview.act", sid, payload, timeout=45)`). When nothing can answer — an app build older than the tools (the renderer handler ships in the desktop bundle, the tools are offered by the backend, the two update on different clocks), or a session with no attached window at all (the reconnect-replay design deliberately keeps the request open) — every action blocks the full 45s and then reports an error that blames a closed tab. A model following its schema tries the next action, so one turn stacks wait after wait. This is the same shape the tour ladder already fixed (`_tour_request`, #89620).

## Fix

Port PR 94300's fail-fast ladder onto the current server-requests path, mirroring `_tour_request`:

- First `preview.act` per session gets a 10s probe deadline; unanswered → the session's bridge is marked unavailable and later actions short-circuit with an actionable error (update the app / open a page, retry after a cooldown).
- Unlike tour support, a preview pane can open later in the session, so an unanswered probe only condemns the bridge for a cooldown window, with a single in-flight reprobe per session (concurrent callers fail fast).
- Once a client answers, the full 45s deadline is back and a transient miss never disables the bridge.
- A window-owned request that every window declines settles as a non-empty answer (main e33f1a0faf, #119333): the "no window is showing this chat" refusal passes through unchanged — the probe never masks it.

Second commit: the tool-layer error strings split the two cases an empty bridge answer used to conflate — nothing open vs. a stale app — in `drive_preview`, `annotate_preview`, `read_preview`, and `read_terminal`.

## Coverage per issue

- #94272: fully covered (probe ladder + error split; both red on base).
- #119333: already addressed on main by e33f1a0faf (windows decline, gateway settles fast); this PR only makes the tool errors distinguish the residual stale-app case.
- #95104, #95459, #113245: partially covered legs (fail-fast, distinguishable errors); the desync behind #95459/#113245 was addressed on main by d4720b4ea8 (#122062), and the packaged-bundle staleness belongs to install/update. open_preview's fire-and-forget design is unchanged.

## Checks run

- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tui_gateway/test_preview_action_bridge_fail_fast.py tests/tui_gateway/test_tour_bridge_fail_fast.py` — 16 passed.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tools/test_drive_preview_tool.py tests/tools/test_read_preview_tool.py tests/tools/test_annotate_preview_tool.py` — 27 passed.
- Red on base: swapped in `origin/main`'s versions of the four touched source files and re-ran the same tests — 12 failed (10 × no `_preview_action_request`, 2 × merged error strings).

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/94300 (probe ladder — ported here)
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/97852 and https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/113296 (tile-driven preview actions — the silent-drop premise is gone from main: tiles now answer window-owned requests (4cde8f2ced) and the identity desync was fixed (d4720b4ea8). The residual ask — letting a tile-hosted background session drive the pane — contradicts the current design: `actOnActivePreview` acts on the preview the user is looking at, and the active-session-only gate with its explicit refusal is the "offer, don't hijack" rule from apps/desktop/AGENTS.md.)
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/95475 (owner-stamped tabs / reader registration — the bot-vs-active-session authorization model it proposes is the same design question; the attention-scoped active-tab resolution it adds already exists via `actOnActivePreview`)

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/119339 and https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/119357 (unresolvable/closed, nothing to salvage)

Thanks @kvnloo @astraltrekkin @JoaoMarcos44 @salch-cred @zesteq @itsjeremyjohnson.

items.body:
## Root cause

`MEDIA:` tag rendering had two defects in the bare (unquoted) capture branch of
`mediaLink` in `apps/desktop/src/lib/chat-messages/parts.ts:160-173`:

1. **Trailing punctuation captured as part of the path.** The bare branch passed
   the raw capture straight through, so chat text like
   `open MEDIA:/tmp/report.pdf.` produced a file link to `/tmp/report.pdf.`
   (dead file) instead of `/tmp/report.pdf` followed by a literal `.`. Sentence
   punctuation (`.` `,` `!` `?` `:` `;`) was indistinguishable from path
   characters, so every MEDIA tag at the end of a sentence produced a broken link.
2. **Degenerate captures linkified.** `MEDIA:`, `MEDIA:...`, `MEDIA:download`
   captured `""`, `"..."`, `"download"` — no slash, no extension — and each
   rendered a dead `file://` link instead of being dropped.

Additionally, `pathToLocalFileUrl` in `apps/desktop/src/lib/media.ts` built
`file://` URLs by string concatenation without percent-encoding, so any path
containing `%`, `#`, or `?` produced a URL that resolved to the wrong location
(`#` truncated to a fragment, `?` to a query, `%` mis-parsed).

## What changed

- `parts.ts`: new `_MEDIA_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION` set + `splitTrailingPunctuation`
  (splits only while the remainder stays a plausible path) and
  `isPlausibleMediaPath` (must contain `/` or a known media extension, non-empty
  after trimming). `mediaLink` returns `null` for degenerate captures —
  `mediaTagValues` drops them, so `MEDIA:`/`MEDIA:...` no longer emit dead links.
  Quoted captures are the escape hatch for odd filenames: they skip punctuation
  splitting entirely.
- `media.ts`: `pathToLocalFileUrl` percent-encodes `%` → `%25`, `#` → `%23`,
  `?` → `%3F` before building the URL; `mediaExternalUrl` uses it.
- `parts.capture.test.ts`: new regression tests for the bare-branch trailing
  period, comma, degenerate captures, and quoted-escape behavior.

Already fixed on main and intentionally not re-fixed here: bold/comma/backtick
captures ([#114358], `9647f3505b`), mediaName non-ASCII handling (`6fac69ced38`),
main-process bare-path/`~` open with the missing-file modal (`external-open.ts` +
`hardening.ts` `resolveRequestedPathForIpc`).

## Acceptance coverage

- `open MEDIA:/tmp/report.pdf.` → link to `/tmp/report.pdf` + literal trailing `.` (was: link to `/tmp/report.pdf.`).
- `MEDIA:` / `MEDIA:...` / `MEDIA:download` → no link at all (was: dead `file://` links).
- `MEDIA:"/tmp/odd.name."` → quoted path kept whole, punctuation preserved.
- `MEDIA:/tmp/a%20b.pdf`, `/tmp/c#1.png`, `/tmp/d?e.mp4` → percent-encoded URLs that resolve to the right file.

## Tests run

- `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/lib/chat-messages/parts.capture.test.ts src/lib/chat-messages/parts.test.ts src/app/artifacts/index.test.ts` → 3 files, 37 tests passed (capture tests failed on base before the fix).
- `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/lib/media.remote.test.ts src/lib/media-file-download.test.ts src/lib/media-dimensions.test.ts` → 3 files, 28 tests passed.
- `npx eslint <touched files>` → clean.

## Supersedes

- #84542 — bare-branch punctuation trim + URL escaping + capture validity (salvaged; the bulk of this PR).
- #48620 — `%`/`#`/`?` escaping (salvaged; `@professorpalmer` — commit email is a noreply address so credited here and via Co-authored-by).
- #87624, #62409, #85788 — stale variants of the same trailing-period capture, now covered here and by fixes already on main.
- #90669 — its trailing-period premise is covered here; its distinct ideas (real `href` + reveal-in-Finder for `MediaAttachment`) are a separate layer, left for re-routing.
- #92223 — its degenerate-capture premise is covered here; its structured missing-file errors remain a separate follow-up.

## Credit

- `686f6c61` (#84542) — trailing-punctuation split and capture-validity rejection (Co-authored-by).
- `@professorpalmer` (#48620) — `%`/`#`/`?` escaping (Co-authored-by).

## Screenshots

The change is link markup/behavior (href contents + whether a link renders),
not layout or styling — the rendered chat surface is textually identical when
paths are well-formed. No pixel-visible layout change to capture; happy to add
harness screenshots on request.

Fixes #84361

[#114358]: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/114358

items.body:
## Root cause

A barge-in capture that survives the interrupt-settle window could never be
delivered: `submitCapturedUtterance` holds the `onSubmit` captured at monitor
arm time, and the composer's `submitVoiceTurn` guards on a render-captured
`busy` closure — so even after live busy clears, the stale closure still
reports busy and the transcribed interruption is silently dropped
(#105497, #123357). When live busy genuinely never clears, the early return
was silent: a spoken turn vanished without a trace (#123357 part 1).

## Fix

Two layers, both reading live state at call time:

1. `use-composer-voice.ts` keeps `busyRef` fresh per render and the submit
   guard reads `busyRef.current` — every retained submit path (barge capture,
   live chord, keyboard) now respects the live busy state (from #105509).
2. `use-voice-conversation.ts` folds #123371's `onSubmitRef` (kept fresh per
   render, mirroring `onInterruptRef`) so `submitCapturedUtterance` always
   submits through the latest callback; and when live busy still hasn't
   cleared after the 5 s settle window, the transcript is parked in the
   composer input (`parkText` + `focusInput`, optional props) and listening
   resumes — never a silent drop.

## Coverage

- #105497: `uses live busy state when a retained voice callback submits
  after barge-in` (fails on main: stale closure reports busy).
- #123357: `parks the transcript in the composer when live busy never
  clears` (fails on main: parkText never called).

## Checks run

- `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-voice-conversation.test.tsx src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-voice-conversation-rearm.test.tsx src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-voice.test.tsx` — 22 passed.

items.body:
## Root cause

`drive_preview`'s synthetic `type` path (apps/desktop/src/lib/preview-act/act-in-page.ts) composed events no framework recognizes:

- contenteditable → `el.textContent = text` (no beforeinput/insertText composition, so Lexical/ProseMirror/Draft editors never see an insertion);
- inputs → prototype-setter + plain `new Event('input')` with no `.data`/`.inputType`, which React 16+ value trackers deduplicate against the value they last wrote;
- `submit: true` → synthetic Enter `KeyboardEvent` without `keyCode`/`which` (read-only 0 on constructed events), so forms checking `keyCode === 13` swallow it.

The engine reported acted-success while framework-managed state never changed.

## Fix

Cherry-picked from #98780 (authorship preserved): `document.execCommand('insertText')` for contenteditable with a textContent+InputEvent fallback; `new InputEvent('input', {data, inputType: 'insertText', bubbles: true})` for inputs; `keyCode: 13, which: 13` in the Enter init dict. The PR's unrelated psutil Android test commit is dropped.

The PR's regression tests were rewritten to the engine's real holder contract (`book`/`url` via an elements inventory, not the invented `handles`/`node` shape — they could never have passed) plus a fallback-path test.

## Coverage per issue

- #98048: contenteditable goes through execCommand (spy) and still writes via the fallback when execCommand is unavailable; input events carry `data`/`inputType`; Enter carries `keyCode`/`which` 13. The pre-existing "enters text and fires the events a controlled input listens for" test continues to cover the plain-input path.

## Checks run

items.body:
## Root cause
`tui_gateway/event_replay.py` FIFO session eviction deleted the session's `_replay_next_seq`. A session revisited after eviction restarted stamping at seq 1, below every client's watermark, so `session.events.since` returned an empty reply that looked complete. A reconnecting Desktop client then painted nothing for the gap.

## Change
- Eviction keeps `_replay_next_seq` for the process epoch, so a revisited session continues from its high seq.
- Eviction raises `_replay_evicted_through` to the last stamped seq, so an old watermark gets `truncated: true` instead of an empty reply.

The client half (acting on `truncated: true`) is https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/126988 (@austinpickett, opened first). This PR used to carry its own client change; that part was dropped so the two don't conflict. Together they cover #100122. This PR alone doesn't, so it uses Refs.

Refs #100122

## Tests
`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_event_replay.py`: 13 passed with the fix. With `tui_gateway/event_replay.py` from `origin/main`, the two new tests fail (`test_fifo_eviction_marks_truncation_for_old_watermarks` and the monotonic-seq test).

Server-only change to the in-memory replay ring (one file plus its test). No wire-contract, config or UI change. Reviewed head `9fbb299e864e596cb082b0fb231dbd53a64ce970`.

## Root cause

Both gateway save dialogs (`apps/desktop/electron/gateway-file-download.ts:434` streaming
path, `:505` data-URL fallback) invoke `showSaveDialog` with only `defaultPath` + `title`
and no `filters`. Electron passes `filters` to the platform save dialog as its file-type
list; with none, Windows offers only "All Files" and has no default extension to append,
so with "hide extensions for known file types" enabled the saved name loses its
extension (#92480: a .pptx lands as a typeless "File" Explorer cannot open). The
image-save dialog in the same file already carries a filter for exactly this reason.

## Fix

Cherry-picks @jackulau's `saveDialogFilters()` helper from #92576 (authorship
preserved): whitelisted extension (`^[a-z0-9]{1,16}$`, server-supplied
Content-Disposition names are not trusted), download's own type first, All Files always
last, basename-only. Wires it into both extracted dialog call sites — the PR's original
`main.ts` hunks targeted the pre-extraction inline code that no longer exists — and adds
`filters?: SaveDialogFilter[]` to `GatewaySaveDialogOptions` so the wired option flows
through the `deps.showSaveDialog` seam at main.ts's transport wiring.

#92576's regex-style transport assertions are replaced with real behavioral ones: the
existing token/bearer streaming tests now assert the dialog options carry the BIN
filter, and a new data-url fallback test drives `saveGatewayDownload` end-to-end with
the dialog spy asserting the filter list.

## Coverage per issue

- #92480 — both save paths (streaming + data-URL fallback) now offer the download's own
  file type so Windows keeps/appends the default extension.

items.body:
## Root cause

`main.ts` called `app.exit(0)` the moment `requestSingleInstanceLock()` returned false — no stale-lock handling, no log. On Linux/X11 a zombie/defunct Electron process leaves the `SingletonLock` symlink behind with a PID that **still answers `kill(pid, 0)`** (a zombie exists until reaped), so Chromium's own liveness probe keeps refusing the lock and every later launch silently does nothing: no window, no error, no log (#78101).

## What changes

- New pure module `electron/singleton-lock.ts`: `removeStaleSingletonLock()` reads `<userData>/SingletonLock`, parses `<hostname>-<pid>`, and unlinks **only** when `/proc/<pid>/stat` shows state `Z` or the entry is gone. Guards:
  - `kill(pid, 0)` is never used as the liveness signal — it reports zombies as alive (the exact bug).
  - A lock whose hostname prefix isn't this host (shared home directory) is never touched.
  - Unparseable targets, non-Linux platforms, live-looking owners: no-op.
- `main.ts`: `acquireSingleInstanceLock()` retries the lock once after clearing a provably-dead owner, and **always logs** `[hermes] another Hermes Desktop instance holds the single-instance lock; exiting` when the lock is legitimately lost, so the failure is diagnosable.
- Platform/hostname/proc-state are injected — fully unit-testable on any OS.

## Acceptance coverage

- **#78101**: stale (zombie or gone) owner detected and cleared, launch proceeds; lost lock always logged; no silent `exit(0)`. Covered fully.

Fixes #78101

## Tests

`electron/singleton-lock.test.ts` — hostname/PID parsing, `/proc/<pid>/stat` comm parsing (spaces and nested parens), zombie-vs-alive state decisions, and end-to-end symlink unlink behaviour across live/zombie/dead/foreign-host/no-lock cases:

```
cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run electron/singleton-lock.test.ts --maxWorkers=2
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  4 passed (4)
```

Red on `origin/main` (module and test don't exist there; `isStaleSingletonLockOwner` import fails). `npx tsc -p . --noEmit` on the branch: pass.

## Not exercised live

The real symlink + `/proc` behaviour is Linux-only; this session is on macOS, so the fix is proven by the unit tests only. Needs one Linux/X11 check before release: launch, kill -STOP + leave a defunct owner, relaunch.

## Credit

Supersedes #79749 (Thanks @Cloudymap1e — the always-log-the-lost-lock diagnostics) and #82054 (Thanks @imrightguy — the hostname-prefixed stale-lock recovery with the `/proc` state-Z check; this PR keeps those semantics, adds the missing-`/proc`-entry case, a comm parser that survives spaces and nested parentheses, and moves it into a pure, unit-tested module — the inlined `main.ts` shape no longer applies after the `isPrimaryInstance` rework).

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/79749
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/82054

items.body:
## Root cause

The active-work quit guard (`heldQuitForActiveWork`) only runs in `before-quit`. On Windows/Linux the primary quit gesture is the title-bar close button: closing the last window destroys its webContents — which deletes its `activeWorkByWebContents` entry — before `window-all-closed` reactively calls `app.quit()`. By the time `before-quit` runs, the merged work count reads 0 and the guard no-ops: a turn in flight is aborted with no confirmation (#96139).

## What changes

Combines the three complementary open PRs, all re-based onto current main:

- **`shouldGuardWindowClose`** (pure, in `quit-guard.ts`): the last-window close semantics — guard only on Windows/Linux, never during an update/swap handoff, never on macOS (close = stay in Dock), never while another chat window remains, and only with work in flight.
- **`registerChatWindow`** in `main.ts`: installs one central `close` handler on every chat surface — primary, session (`spawnSecondaryWindow`), and instance windows — that runs the *existing* `heldQuitForActiveWork` while the window and its work report are still alive. `event.defaultPrevented` is respected first, so the tray's close-to-tray path (work keeps running) never prompts. "Quit Anyway" re-enters `before-quit` with the `quitConfirmedWithActiveWork` latch set and falls through; the existing `quitPromptOpen` latch prevents dialog stacking.
- **`lastActiveWorkSeen` fallback**: a webContents-independent cache of the last summary any renderer published. A stream can reload its webContents mid-turn and drop its map entry before the guard runs; the cache survives that and is merged into the guard's read. Only real publishes refresh it, so an idle app (count 0) clears it — no false positives.

Deliberately *not* taken from the source PRs: #80226's locale/i18n dialog table (unrelated to the bug, parallel to the existing `quitPromptFor` copy), #80713's duplicated dialog logic (this PR reuses the single `heldQuitForActiveWork`), and #73312's hold logic (already satisfied by main's `quitPromptOpen` → `preventDefault`).

## Acceptance coverage per issue (#96139)

- guard fires on the X/Alt+F4 last-window close before webContents teardown → central close handler runs `heldQuitForActiveWork` with the map still live
- Keep Running / Quit Anyway, window and turn preserved → `preventDefault` on close keeps the window; the latches mirror the existing before-quit flow
- non-final window closes don't trigger the guard → `shouldGuardWindowClose` `hasOtherChatWindows` gate, unit-tested
- no double dialog / quit loop on re-entry → existing `quitPromptOpen`/`quitConfirmedWithActiveWork` latches; `event.defaultPrevented` respects the tray's absorbed close
- remote-mode reconciliation (`quitStopsBackendWork`, #79579/#121093) → unchanged: the same `heldQuitForActiveWork` picks the owned/remote copy

## Tests run (real results)

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run electron/quit-guard.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` → **21 passed** (5 new `shouldGuardWindowClose` tests: guard/no-work/macOS/handoff/other-window; 2 new `mergeActiveWork` fallback tests: live count with empty map, idle cache stays clear)
- `cd apps/desktop && npx tsc -p . --noEmit` → **exit 0**

Note: the close-path wiring itself (`registerChatWindow`) is covered by the pure decision function tests; the Electron close-event flow needs the platform verification below.

## Not exercised live

The X/Alt+F4 close path with a turn in flight, the multi-window (session/instance) cases, and the "Quit Anyway" re-entry need verification on Windows and Linux — this session is macOS, where the close gesture is excluded by design.

Fixes #96139

items.body:
## Root cause

Two independent renderer defects kept subagent rows pinned (#75505):

1. **A stopped session's rows spin forever.** `handleToolEvent`'s `SUBAGENT_EVENT_TYPES` branch guarded on `!sessionInterrupted(sessionId)`, so once the user pressed Stop, every `subagent.*` event was dropped — including the `subagent.complete` of a delegation that was still finishing in the background. Nothing else terminalizes the row: the only prune path (`pruneFinishedSessionSubagents`) fires on the same session's next `message.start`, which an interrupted session may never emit.

2. **Terminal rows from inactive sessions accumulate forever.** The spawn-tree panel aggregates `allSubagents()` across every session with no bound, and the only cleanup is same-session `message.start` pruning — so finished rows from every conversation the renderer has ever seen pile up in the panel.

## Fix

- `store/subagents.ts`: new `isTerminalSubagentCompletion(eventType, payload)` — true only for a `subagent.complete` carrying a status that ends the run (`completed`/`failed`/`interrupted`/`timeout`/`error`/`cancelled`/`canceled`; the store's `asStatus` normalizes the last four. Also `subagentsForPanel(bySession, activeSessionId)` — live running/queued rows from every session (cross-session visibility preserved), terminal rows only for the session the user is in.
- `gateway-event/tools.ts`: the interrupted-session guard now admits a terminal `subagent.complete`; live progress and non-terminal events stay suppressed, so a stopped turn's late mid-flight frames cannot repaint its stream. `upsertSubagent`'s existing retired-id and terminal-status guards make a stale completion a no-op.
- `agents/index.tsx`: the panel builds its tree from `subagentsForPanel` keyed on `$activeSessionId` (same runtime-id key space as `$subagentsBySession`).
- `use-statusbar-items.tsx`: the failed count now reads terminal rows only for the active session, keeping the status-bar indicator and the tree in the same contract (running/queued counts were already cross-session).

## Coverage

- `subagents.test.ts`: terminal-completion classification (incl. timeout/cancelled), a completion landing on a running row past an interrupt, and the panel scope (live rows from every session + terminal rows only for the session in view; inactive session keeps only live rows). All four new cases are red on base.
- `gateway-event/tools-subagent-interrupt.test.ts`: `handleToolEvent` with `sessionInterrupted() === true` — a terminal `subagent.complete` terminalizes the row; live progress and a statusless completion stay suppressed.
- Existing suites still green: `tools-preview.test.ts`, `delegate.test.tsx`, `use-statusbar-items.test.tsx`, `use-statusbar-items.lifecycle.test.tsx`, and the full `gateway-event/` directory (51 tests).

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/63664 — thanks @metamindedu. Its liveness-polling design (reconcile via an authoritative roster) informed the approach; this PR fixes the two root causes it left open (it deliberately preserved terminal rows, and it predates the `gateway-event/` split and the `retiredSubagents` machinery). The existing `use-subagent-snapshot` hook already covers roster reconciliation for visible panes.
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/75530 — thanks @andyst-dev. Its `subagentsForPanel` scope-alignment and terminalize-on-Stop approach are the direct ancestors of this fix.
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/128608 — Thanks @Finn763: the delegate-row status/bubble split and the tool.complete background re-sync are folded in with credit. Its SUBAGENT-branch gate removal was not taken (it reopens the late-progress repaint past Stop this PR's `isTerminalSubagentCompletion` guard prevents); the two non-duplicate tests land with the fold-in.

Fixes #75505

Refs https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/81114 — the delegate fallback-row retirement past Stop and the event-driven background-process re-sync land here; the durable backend replay for plain terminal-tool completions and `refreshBackgroundProcesses` owner-resolution resilience remain open in the issue.

items.body:
## Root cause

#126708's phantom-turn symptom had three legs; the TTS-echo leg landed on
main separately (f0410eb4f0). Two remain:

1. Client-direct STT skips the hallucination filter. The relay endpoint
   runs `transcribe_recording` → `is_whisper_hallucination`
   (hermes_cli/web_routers/audio.py:114-120), but
   `transcribeAudioClientDirect` (the default whenever the provider has a
   client wire) posts straight to the provider and applies nothing —
   "thank you" on quiet audio becomes a real user turn.
2. `voice.barge_in: false` gates the gateway listener
   (tui_gateway/methods_voice.py `_arm_barge_listener_if_enabled`) but the
   Desktop renderer never read it — talking over the reply still
   interrupts.

## Fix

1. The gateway ships the exact hallucination contract through
   `/api/audio/voice-config`: `stt_hallucination_filter()` in
   tools/voice_client_config.py returns the phrase list
   (WHISPER_HALLUCINATIONS) plus the repetitive-filler regex, attached to
   every direct STT resolution. `transcribeAudioClientDirect` applies it
   (`isSttSilenceHallucination`) on all three wires and maps a matching
   transcript to `''` — silence, exactly like the relay path. No filter on
   the config (older backend) → pass-through.
2. `voice-prefs.ts` gains `$bargeInEnabled` (default true; false only when
   explicitly false, mirroring the gateway gate), seeded by
   `applyBargeInEnabledFromConfig` from `use-hermes-config.ts`;
   `ensureBargeMonitor` never arms while disabled.

## Checks run

- `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/lib/voice-client-direct.test.ts src/store/voice-prefs.test.ts src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-voice-conversation.test.tsx` — 50 passed
- `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/lib/voice-tts-echo.test.ts` — 15 passed (the landed echo half)
- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tools/test_voice_client_config.py` — 14 passed
- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tools/test_voice_tts_echo_guard.py` — 11 passed
- Parity spot-check of the shipped regex contract vs `is_whisper_hallucination` across known/real utterances — exact agreement.

The new tests fail on main by construction (the atoms/filter do not exist there): with `$bargeInEnabled` absent the monitor-never-arms test does not compile; without the filter `transcribeAudioClientDirect` returns "Thank you." verbatim.

Related: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/126708
Fixes #126708

items.body:
## Root cause

With `skills.write_approval` on, every skill write is staged to the file-backed pending store
(`<home>/pending/skills/<id>.json`), but only the interactive CLI could review it:

- `hermes_cli/commands.py` carried `desktop="settings"` on the `/skills` `CommandDef`, and the
  desktop resolver (`apps/desktop/src/lib/desktop-slash-commands.ts`) resolves commands by name
  only — the subcommand token is discarded — so `/skills pending` answered "… is managed from
  the desktop sidebar" while no sidebar write-approval UI exists (#98330).
- `tui_gateway` `command.dispatch` (the desktop/TUI fallback stage when the slash worker fails)
  had no route for `/skills` or `/memory`, so both fell through to the routing refusal
  `not a quick/plugin/bundle/skill command` (#118812, #123315).
- `tools/write_approval.py` `_staged()` named `/skills pending` in every staged-write tool
  result even on surfaces that cannot dispatch it.
- `skill_pending_diff` had no `action='batch'` case, so a staged `skill_manage` operations[]
  write diffed as `(batch on 'demo')` (#123861).

## Fix

- **Registry**: new `CommandDef.desktop_subcommands` field; `/skills` declares its
  write-approval review slice (`pending`, `approve`, `reject`, `diff`, `approval`) and drops
  `desktop="settings"`. `command_desktop_meta` serializes the allowlist (empty tuple = deny
  all); the gateway contract and `desktop-slash-registry.json` dump are regenerated.
- **Desktop resolver**: the invocation, not just the name, decides — `isDesktopSlashCommand(name,
  arg)` threads the typed arg; `desktopSubcommandUnavailableMessage` is the exec gate that
  renders an actionable refusal for hub mutations (`search`/`install`/…) instead of forwarding
  them; `filterDesktopSubcommandCompletions` drops popover suggestions the gate would refuse.
  An explicit `/skills` spec keeps a current Desktop reviewing staged writes even against an
  older backend catalog.
- **tui_gateway `command.dispatch`**: `_cmd_skills` answers only the registry-declared review
  slice under `_session_home_scope` (unlisted subcommands keep the 4018 routing refusal —
  hub mutations never widen); `_cmd_memory` routes the shared handler
  (`hermes_cli/write_approval_commands.handle_pending_subcommand`) with the live agent's store
  or a freshly loaded on-disk one, and a profile-scoped `write_approval` config setter. The
  gate being off still answers while staged writes exist (gateway parity — never stranded).
- **`_staged()` hint is surface-aware**: slash-capable surfaces (CLI/TUI/desktop/chat gateway)
  keep "`/skills pending`"; headless contexts (cron, kanban, api_server, webhook delivery) get
  the pending directory path instead of a command nobody can deliver.
- **Batch diff renderer**: each batch op diffs in order against what the earlier ops of the
  same batch left in the file, under its skill gist header; single-op paths unchanged.

## Coverage per issue

- #98330: `/skills pending|approve|reject|diff|approval` exec on Desktop (allowlisted
  invocation, registry-driven), hub mutations stay off the wire, and the staged hint no longer
  names an undeliverable command.
- #123315: the desktop dead-end is fixed by the same surface, and `/skills diff <id>` on a
  staged batch write now renders per-op diffs.
- #118812: `command.dispatch` routes `/memory` and `/skills` review subcommands, so a failed
  slash worker no longer strands staged writes (referenced — opened by another cluster).

## Checks run

- `pytest tests/tools/test_write_approval.py tests/tools/test_skill_pending_diff_batch.py` —
  27 passed (3 new surface-aware hint tests; proven red on base `origin/main`).
- `pytest tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py -k "command_dispatch_reviews_staged or
  command_dispatch_skills_gate or command_dispatch_memory_pending"` — 3 passed; proven red on
  base (4018 refusal). Full file run: 658 passed, 1 flake
  (`test_profile_scoped_agent_build_starts_mcp_discovery_in_profile_home`) that fails
  identically on unmodified `origin/main` under load, plus 2 SessionDB-teardown errors that
  pass in isolation — all load-induced, none related to this diff.
- `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_commands.py` (2 new registry-meta tests, red on base) and
  `tests/hermes_cli/test_desktop_slash_registry.py` — 55 passed.
- `scripts/dump_desktop_slash_registry.py --check` — registry dump in sync.
- `npx vitest run src/lib/desktop-slash-commands.test.ts` — 24 passed (new subcommand-gate +
  completion-filter test, red on base).

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/98794 — registry-driven
  `desktop_subcommands` + resolver allowlist, completion filtering, contract regeneration.
  Thanks @foma-agent
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/105773 — routing the approval verbs to the
  backend instead of the sidebar. Thanks @chelsealong
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/118821 — `command.dispatch`
  `_cmd_memory`/`_cmd_skills` handlers and the `isDesktopSlashCommand(name, arg)` threading.
  Thanks @jasonHav
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/123861 — batch diff renderer (cherry-picked
  as its own commit, authorship preserved). Thanks @finn763
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/107799 — making `/skills` subcommands
  available in desktop chat; subsumed by the same subcommand-aware resolution.

Fixes #98330
Fixes #123315

items.body:
## Root cause

`titleBarOverlay` options carry a fixed `TITLEBAR_HEIGHT` (34 px) set once at `BrowserWindow` creation and re-applied only on theme/appearance changes. When the user zooms (Ctrl+wheel, Ctrl+plus/minus, the Appearance Scale control), Chromium scales the renderer — including its painted titlebar — but not the native Window Controls Overlay, so the min/max/close buttons stay at their 100% size inside a differently-scaled titlebar (#81086).

## What changes

- **`scaledOverlayHeight`** (pure, `titlebar-overlay-width.ts`): scales the overlay height with the webContents zoom factor, rounded to whole pixels (the overlay API is integer-based), never below 1 px; garbage zoom input clamps to the unscaled height.
- **`titleBarOverlayOptions`** gains a `zoomFactor` input (default 1 — every existing caller is byte-identical). WSLg still returns `false` (the renderer paints its own scaled controls there) and macOS keeps its height-only traffic-light overlay, both untouched by zoom.
- **`getTitleBarOverlayOptions(win?)`** reads the window's current `getZoomFactor()`; **`applyTitleBarOverlay`** now passes the window through.
- **Re-apply on every zoom-change path**: `setAndPersistZoomLevel` (the funnel for shortcuts, wheel, menu, and settings UI), and `restorePersistedZoomLevel`'s three paths (JSON restore with drift-guard, fresh-install default, localStorage recovery). Theme-change re-application keeps working and now also carries the current zoom.

## Acceptance coverage per issue (#81086)

- overlay height scales with the current zoom factor on Windows/Linux → `scaledOverlayHeight` + `zoomFactor` wiring
- re-applied on every zoom-change path → both funnels call `applyTitleBarOverlay`
- default-zoom rendering unchanged (100%/90% presets) → `zoomFactor` defaults to 1; `scaledOverlayHeight(34, 1) === 34` byte-identical, unit-tested

## Tests run (real results)

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run electron/titlebar-overlay-width.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` → **16 passed** (6 new: pixel-round scaling, garbage-input clamps, min-1 clamp, Windows/Linux scaling, WSLg/macOS untouched, default byte-identical)
- `cd apps/desktop && npx tsc -p . --noEmit` → **exit 0**

## Not exercised live

The overlay is native OS chrome (Windows/Linux WCO buttons) — it cannot render in a browser harness and this session is macOS, where the WCO path is excluded. The unit tests cover the pure scaling logic; the visible result (native buttons matching a zoomed titlebar at e.g. 125%) needs verification on real **Windows** (and plain Linux), across the Ctrl+wheel, Ctrl+plus/minus, and Appearance Scale zoom paths.

Fixes #81086

items.body:
## Root cause

Assistant Markdown links to local paths render a `PreviewAttachment` card that never asked whether the target exists on the machine running Electron (#101683):

- Main-process normalization (`previewFileTarget`) overloaded every directory as `<dir>/index.html`; a directory without one fell to `null`, and the renderer's blind fallback (`localPreviewTarget`) then fabricated a text-preview tab that dies with "file does not exist".
- The card rendered **Download** unconditionally — pointless for a file that is already local — and offered no native folder action at all.

## What changes

- `previewFileTarget` (electron/main.ts) answers directories and dead paths with typed non-previewable results (`previewKind: 'directory' | 'missing'`) instead of the index.html overload/null drop.
- `normalizeOrLocalPreviewTarget` (renderer) honors those results in local mode instead of fabricating a fallback tab; remote-backend mode keeps its gateway-backed fallback.
- `PreviewAttachment` classifies the target's local state and branches: **existing directory -> "Open containing folder"** (`hermes:fs:openDir`, no Download, no preview button); **existing local file -> reveal in file manager** (`hermes:fs:reveal`) instead of Download; **missing path -> "Preview unavailable"** and a not-found notification instead of a broken tab; remote/bridge-less targets keep the stock card.
- New i18n key `preview.missingTarget` (en + types; `locales/_keys.desktop.json` regenerated).

Design credit: the directory-branch card and the "reveal, don't re-download" shape follow PR #101687 by @huklaa, and the local-file native action follows PR #100869 by @CILWJ; both are adapted to main's current `openPreview({ target })` card and to the typed main-process classification the issue asked for.

## Acceptance coverage per #101683

- Existing local directory link -> native open, no Download, no text preview — covered (unit + harness probe).
- Existing local file -> reveal in file manager, no Download — covered.
- Remote-backend file -> Download and supported previews retained — covered.
- Missing path -> reported as non-existent, no broken preview tab — covered.
- Regressions for a Windows `file:///C:/.../directory` link, a POSIX directory, a local file, a remote file, and a missing path — all five in `preview-attachment.test.tsx`; pipeline gating in `local-preview.local-target.test.ts`.

## Tests

- `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/components/chat/preview-attachment.test.tsx src/lib/local-preview.local-target.test.ts src/components/assistant-ui/markdown-text.media-md.test.tsx src/components/assistant-ui/markdown-text.filelinks.test.tsx` -> **16/16 passed, EXIT:0** on this branch; the same new tests on `origin/main` fail 7/9 (EXIT:1) — the directory/missing/local-file branches and the pipeline gating are all red on main.
- Before/after PNGs + DOM probes via an isolated harness (production `styles.css`, Tailwind `@source`): before = `Download | Open preview` on every fixture; after = directory `Open containing folder` only, local file `Open containing folder | Open preview`, missing `Download | Preview unavailable`; harness `openDir`/`revealPath` spies received the expected paths.

Not exercised live: the actual OS file-manager window (native Electron IPC stubbed in tests/harness — the `hermes:fs:openDir`/`reveal` handlers are existing, unit-tested code paths). Worth one manual click-through on Windows for the `file:///C:/...` form.

Fixes #101683

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/101687 (Thanks @huklaa) and https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/100869 (Thanks @CILWJ)
