items.body:
## Summary

Prevent partial config payloads from silently deleting unrelated settings. `atomic_config_write()` now rejects omitted mapping keys, including nested omissions under unchanged top-level keys. Intentional full-state deletion uses the explicit `atomic_config_replace()` API.

The underlying ruamel round-trip writer remains unchanged: comments and formatting are preserved, and deliberate deletion still works. Intentional replacement callers (config saves/set/unset, provider changes, credential cleanup, doctor migration, profile channel stripping, and TUI saves) use the replacement path.

## Priority

**P1** — a partial write can silently erase model routing, MCP servers, plugins, and other configuration while leaving valid YAML behind.

## Root cause and behavior

The public writer's docstring described a merge, but the underlying writer deletes omitted keys recursively. Existing read guards catch unreadable files, not incomplete payloads.

| Path | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 99-key config followed by a partial `skills` payload | Silently becomes a one-key file | Refused; original configuration remains intact |
| Same top-level keys with omitted nested siblings | Nested settings silently deleted | Refused |
| Intentional profile-channel stripping | Deliberately removes channel state | Still works through explicit replacement |
| Config set/unset | Full-state write | Full-state replacement, retaining main's telemetry wrapper |

## Provenance and integration

Salvages #125152

Fixes #125107

Cherry-picked JoaoMarcos44's `cec5fe37c74c13d9313c16f4fb9163f571fe1290`, preserving original authorship and adding a `Co-authored-by` trailer. Resolved the current-main conflict by passing `atomic_config_replace` through `recording_raw_config_write`, rather than removing main's telemetry wrapper. Restored the existing executable bit on `scripts/check_config_yaml_writers.py`.

Thanks to @33hodl for the original report and competing #125109. Its top-level bulk-drop threshold catches the reported large wipe but misses nested omissions and rejects a supported profile-channel prune. No implementation from #125109 was reused. The closed merge-semantics alternative #127196 was reviewed but not incorporated.

## Verification

At head `93854b1291329ce4a84052a051f26ed149957b34`:

- Canonical runner: **263 passed, 0 failed, 12 platform skips** across the seven suites below.
- `scripts/check_config_yaml_writers.py`: passed (1,830 files).
- `git diff main...HEAD --check`: passed.
- Live temporary-file probes: partial writes are refused with the original file intact; deliberate profile channel stripping succeeds.
- Regression sensitivity: disabling the omission guard made both the top-level and nested-omission tests fail; restoring it made them pass.

```bash
HERMES_PYTHON=/path/to/test/python bash scripts/run_tests.sh \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_config.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_profile_clone_channels.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_config_yaml_comment_preservation.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_model_provider_persistence.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_doctor.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_credential_lifecycle.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_config_unversioned_migration.py -q
```

Earlier direct-pytest runs inherited the host environment and failed. Those are superseded by the successful canonical, clean-environment, per-file run above. Hosted CI has not yet been verified.

## Compatibility and scope

External callers intentionally deleting mapping keys must use `atomic_config_replace`; an incomplete mapping write now raises instead of silently deleting settings. This does not change permission or authentication policy.

This patch does not redesign sequence replacement or stale-snapshot/concurrent-write behavior. The guard walks mappings; it does not inspect mappings inside supplied lists. Sequence values retain the existing writer semantics, so this is not a guarantee against every possible deletion inside sequences.

items.body:
Windows desktop release builds now calculate the native package version from the same admitted timestamp as the rest of the build.

## What does this PR do?

The desktop builder constructs an environment with the immutable release epoch, but the subprocess calculating the Windows native version inherited the runner's environment instead. With no epoch there, the subprocess received `NaN` and rejected the version. Passing the admitted build environment to that subprocess fixes the failure without changing the version policy.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Native-version subprocess can miss `HERMES_RELEASE_EPOCH` and reject the build. | It reads the release epoch from the prepared build environment and derives the native version. |

## Related Issue

No linked issue.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `scripts/bundles/desktop.py`: pass the prepared environment through the native-version capture call.
- `tests/scripts/test_desktop_preparation.py`: check subprocess environment propagation with an absent parent epoch.

## How to Test

1. Run `HERMES_TEST_FILE_RETRIES=0 scripts/run_tests.sh tests/scripts/test_desktop_preparation.py -q` — 9 passed on Linux.
2. Run `ruff check scripts/bundles/desktop.py tests/scripts/test_desktop_preparation.py` — passed.
3. Invoke the real Node native-quad calculation with an explicit admitted epoch; it returned `2026.5761.123.0`, matching an independent UTC calculation. A signed Windows package build was not run here.

The new test failed before the fix (`capture()` had no environment argument) and passed afterward.

items.body:
The desktop's bundle-skew version probe no longer piles up `git` processes on treeless (`tree:0`) checkouts. It also no longer lazy-fetches from origin or leaves orphans behind after a restart. In an idle 5-minute window on a real treeless checkout, main started a median of 121 probe-owned git processes and left 20 running after quit. This branch leaves none. Fixes #125243.

## Why

`detectRendererSkew` runs on every `hermes:version` call: at startup, on each window focus, after update checks, and from About. Each call spawned `git merge-base` + `git rev-list --count <stamp>..HEAD -- <runtime paths>` through `main.ts::runGit`. That function had no timeout, did no coalescing and did not set `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH`. On a `tree:0` clone the path-limited `rev-list` lazily fetches the trees in the range from origin, one fetch at a time, so each probe runs for minutes. Overlapping calls stacked up, and the whole `rev-list → fetch → remote-https / index-pack` tree was reparented to PID 1 when the app quit.

## What changed

- **Coalesced and cached probe** (salvaged from #126186 by @dreamfarer-space, authorship kept). `createBundleSkewChecker` shares one in-flight check per checkout and caches the answer, failures included, for 30 s. It skips the check while the update gate is closed. Both git calls run with `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, a 5 s timeout and a non-interactive environment. They go through the existing `execGit`, whose timeout now kills the whole tree: a POSIX process group, or `taskkill /T /F` on Windows, which covers the no-console Python host.
- **Treeless-clone regression test** (salvaged from #123039 by @mheals). A real `--filter=tree:0` clone runs the probe and asserts that `objects/pack` is unchanged. It fails when `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH` is removed.
- **`runGit` deleted.** The skew probe was its only caller. Its spawn-failure path (`describeGitSpawnFailure`, `GIT_UNUSABLE`) had no other producer, and nothing in the renderer read the `git-unusable` error, so that path is gone too. The `hermes:updates:check` handler now always reports `check-failed` on error, which is what it already did in practice. The `updates.gitUnusable` locale string was already unused before this PR; I left it alone.
- **Quit cleanup** (the idea from #125861 by @chelsealong, credited as co-author). Timed `execGit` children lead their own process group, so nothing reached one still running at quit. `execGit` now tracks them, and `will-quit` kills every live tree: a group SIGKILL on POSIX, or one batched synchronous `taskkill` on Windows. On Windows a root that has already exited is skipped, because its pid may already belong to another process.

- **Treeless checkouts keep the warning** (the fix proposed by @Froraut on #123039, credited as co-author). With lazy fetch off, the path-limited walk fails on a `tree:0` checkout as soon as an update moves more than one commit, because only the checked-out endpoints have local trees. The probe now falls back to `git diff --quiet <stamp> HEAD -- <runtime paths>`. Ancestry is already proven at that point, so a differing diff means the renderer predates runtime changes. On a real `tree:0` clone of this repo it takes 45 ms and adds no packs. If the stamp's tree is missing too, git exits 128 and the probe stays quiet, as before. The count is `null` in that case; the renderer does not read it.
- **In-app relaunch reaps too.** `app.exit()` skips `will-quit`, so `exitAfterBackendShutdown` kills the timed git trees as well. That function is the exit path for About's Restart, the bundle-swap relaunch and the GPU relaunches.

Side effects worth knowing:
- Every `execGit` call with a timeout now runs in its own process group on POSIX: `git-worktree-ops` (30 s), `git-review-ops` (30 s) and the plugin-install `--version` probe (5 s). They get no controlling TTY, so a credential prompt fails fast instead of blocking. Ctrl-C in a dev terminal no longer reaches them, but quit and relaunch now kill them explicitly.
- On Windows, if the root git/Python host has already exited while a descendant still holds the pipes, the timeout skips `taskkill`: `/T` cannot walk a tree from a dead root, and the pid may already have been reused. Closing that gap needs a Job Object, which is out of scope here.
- The `updates.gitUnusable` locale string had no consumer on main before this PR (the `git-unusable` path had no live producer), so it is left for a separate cleanup.

## Measurement

The real Electron app ran from this branch and from its base (`b8a8be185d`). The build stamp was baked into the dev main bundle the way packaged builds carry it, pointing 150 first-parent commits behind HEAD. `HERMES_DESKTOP_HERMES_ROOT` pointed at a fresh copy-on-write copy of a `--filter=tree:0` clone of this repo from GitHub for each run, so the network lazy fetches are real. Same machine (macOS, Apple Git 2.50), 300 s per run, `ps` sampled every second. Each figure is the median of 3 runs. The churn rows for this branch were measured on the final stack (`b54ee68a3f`, identical to this PR's head before a clean rebase onto current main). The idle rows were measured one commit earlier (`cf2f24e0b1`); the last commit only changes what happens at quit. "Probe-owned" means a `merge-base`/`rev-list` process and every git process it spawned.

| scenario | build | probe-owned git processes | max concurrent | git CPU (s) | alive at quit | alive 30 s after quit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| idle (startup calls only) | base | 121 | 21 | 4.13 | 20 | 20 |
| idle (startup calls only) | this branch | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| focus churn (one `getVersion` every 15 s) | base | 498 | 92 | 18.58 | 88 | 81 |
| focus churn (one `getVersion` every 15 s) | this branch | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

- Under churn, base started 23 `rev-list` probes for 20 focus calls (from a `git` wrapper on `PATH`). This branch started 10, one per 30 s cache window. Each one fails in well under a second on the missing tree, so the 1 s sampler never catches it.
- Git CPU is a lower bound. Processes that live less than a second between samples are missed on both sides, and the base cost is mostly network wait rather than CPU.
- Packs added to the clone per run: base 7–25, this branch 1–2. The branch's packs come from git processes outside the probe tree (the backend's own git calls), which this PR does not touch.

## Tests

- `npx vitest run --project electron`: every failure also fails on base (machine-local: sqlite `SQLITE_BUSY`, POSIX sandbox, signing and native-deps tests). No failures in `bundle-skew`, `no-console-git` or `select-runnable-binary`.
- New or changed: coalescing, cache and update-gate (`bundle-skew.test.ts`); no packs added on a real `tree:0` clone; a timed-out command reaps a real grandchild that owns a TCP listener; quit kills a running timed command with its descendants (fails when the kill is a no-op).
- `tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json`, eslint, prettier and `check-windows-footguns.py --all` are clean. The main-process boot smoke passes on the final head.
- Not run: native Windows. The `taskkill` paths are covered by the Windows branch of the process-tree test, but no Windows lane runs the electron suite yet (#127369).

Supersedes #126186, #124590, #126058, #125861 and the desktop half of #123039. Windows: #126186's author ran its process-tree tests on a Windows Server 2025 runner (50 passed, 1 skipped): https://github.com/dreamfarer-space/hermes-agent/actions/runs/36399665200

items.body:
The running-work arc (`.arc-border`, on working sidebar rows, the HUD composer and the Nous provider row) now travels a 240% layer instead of a 300% one, with the same look. The saving is small, and this PR says how small.

Who, when, why: @royhemi's attribution on #89732 (2026-09-11) named `.arc-border::before` as about half of the visible-idle cost and pointed at its 300% × 300% masked layer, about 9× the ring's visible area. Tracker #127647 (wave 1) asked for that layer to shrink without changing the look, measured before and after.

## What changed
- `.arc-border::before` is 240% × 240% of its host (5.76× the host's area, was 9×). It still overhangs the host by 0.2 at the end of each cycle.
- Its gradient is one period of the old one, repeated. The old gradient repeated every 40% of its line, and each cycle travelled exactly one period, so only that period was ever visible. The period in pixels, the stop profile, the speed and the direction are unchanged.
- The keyframes travel 1.2 of the host per cycle, as before: 50% of the new layer, so the period, travel and stops (18.75 / 25 / 31.25 / 43.75 / 50%) are exact numbers.

## Look: pixel comparison
Headless Chrome, with the old and new rules on identical hosts: 3 host sizes (232 × 26, 431.5 × 52.3, 674 × 68), 4 device scales (1, 2, 2.2, 3), and 10 points of the cycle, including its last frame.
| comparison | worst max channel diff | pixels over 8/255 |
|---|---:|---:|
| old vs new at the same point of travel | 2/255 | 0 |
| static (`animation: none`, the reduced-motion ring) | 1/255 | 0 |
| new, first frame vs last frame (seam) | 2/255 | 0 |
| control: old frame vs a different old frame | 32/255 | up to 1,096 |

The one difference: a newly mounted arc starts a quarter of a cycle further on in its loop. Arcs mount whenever work starts, so no two ever shared a phase anyway.

## Cost: measured
Machine: Apple M3 (Mac15,12), macOS 26.3.1, Electron 40.10.2, dev renderer build, isolated instance (own `HERMES_HOME`, user-data dir and HOME). Scenario: three sessions working with no tokens arriving, so three sidebar-row arcs run. Per-process CPU-time deltas from `SystemInfo.getProcessInfo`, 20 s settle, 45 s windows (20 s windows for the attribution rows), states interleaved, median of 3–5. The machine was shared with other sessions' work (load average 6–70), so read the rows against each other, not as absolutes.

Window viewed, this PR's exact rules against the old ones, injected into the same running instance and interleaved:
| state | renderer | GPU process | style recalcs/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| old rules (300% layer) | 10.4% | 10.6% | 76 |
| this PR (240% layer) | 9.2% | 9.4% | 79 |
| arc animation off | 2.1% | 0.8% | 2 |

Rep by rep: the new rules were cheaper in two of three reps and more expensive in the first, so read this as roughly 1 point each off renderer and GPU, not a firm number.

Attribution from an earlier run on the same instance setup: as shipped 12.5% / 12.4%; one 10 px square animating `transform` instead of the arcs 8.5% / 8.3%; the arcs with the mask dropped 12.4% / 8.7% (this changes the look, so this PR does not do it).

Window covered by other apps (median of 5, an earlier 220% variant of this change): old 5.9% / 1.6%, new 5.1% / 1.5%, arc off 1.9% / 1.0%. That is no measurable difference.

So the saving is about a point of a core each on renderer and GPU with the window viewed, and nothing measurable when covered. The layer size was not the main term. The floor is the 10 px square: any running animation, even a 10 px square, keeps the frame loop running at about 17% of a core on this machine. Most of what an arc costs is that it runs at all, which is the policy question in #127647 and not something this PR changes.

## Checks
- `prettier --check src/styles.css`: clean.
- CSS only. No test reads stylesheets, and none is added.

Base: main. This PR is independent of #127719 (the hidden-window pause list and idle lint gate). The two touch different rules in `styles.css` and do not conflict.

Refs #89732, #127647.

items.body:
In a seeded Desktop chat whose provider reuses tool-call ids, a finished turn now renders once instead of twice.

Linear: NS-1029 (B2)

## Problem

What the user saw: in the setup chat, after the "Quick tour please" turn, the reply "That's the shape of it. / Know what you'd like it to make?" showed twice. A stale live row "Reading tool details · 1 tool 1 step" stayed under the stored "Ran 1 command, used 3 tools" fold. The provider gave every tool call the id `call_0`.

The stale live bubble stays because two checks fail. Each check alone keeps the duplicate on screen.

- **Backend: `tui_gateway/session_workdir.py::_persist_branch_seed`.** This function writes the seed rows to the database. It never copies the new row ids back onto the live history dicts. So every turn receipt in a seeded session came back with `complete=false`, and the renderer never saw a complete durable turn. `tui_gateway/methods_session.py::_persist_branch` (branch create and `session.branch`) has the same gap. Its copied live dicts also kept the parent's `_row_id`.
- **Renderer: `apps/desktop/src/lib/chat-messages/tool-parts.ts::withUniqueToolCallIds`.** This function used one seen-set for the whole transcript. So a second `call_0` in a later message got a new name. The stored fold then carried the new id, the live bubble carried the raw `call_0`, and the id check in `durableFoldCoversLiveResponse` (`use-session-actions/utils.ts`) did not match.

## What changes

- `_persist_branch_seed` keeps the live history dicts. After the batch write, it calls the existing `agent.transcript_repair.sync_flushed_message_markers(live, seed)` under `history_lock`. The agent flush does the same step after its own write. The step copies `_DB_PERSISTED_MARKER`, `_row_id`, the row snapshot, the timestamp and the identity fields onto the live dicts.
- `_persist_branch` calls the same sync, but only after the copy and the title write succeed. If either write fails, the compensation delete and the first-submit fallback still see clean dicts. The live dicts now get the child's row ids, not the parent's.
- `withUniqueToolCallIds` makes one seen-set for each message. A reused id keeps its raw value across messages. Only a duplicate inside one message gets a new name. This matches the per-message key space of assistant-ui and the existing `withUniqueToolCallIdsWithinMessage`.

`append_messages_batch` already stamps these fields on the row dicts it receives, so its signature and other callers do not change.

Known edge cases with reused ids (not changed here):
- An earlier stored `call_0` part that never got a result can now claim a new live `call_0` event. Before, only the first `call_0` in the transcript could.
- `coalesceToolOnlyAssistants` can drop a call with the same id as a call in the message just before it. This needs hydration to split a turn into a separate tool-only message, which is rare.
- `committedFoldsOfLocalTurn` can now count folds from every turn that uses `call_0`. A settled interim bubble whose text exactly matches an earlier turn's text can stay hidden until its own turn is stored.

B3 (`findToolPartIndex` merges parts that share a reused id) is a separate bug and is not fixed here.

## Proof

Observed at `674cb86e30`. Live Desktop run in an isolated sandbox (`env -i`, temp `HOME`, `HERMES_HOME` and `HERMES_SHARED_AUTH_DIR`, CDP port 9333). A fake model gave every tool call the id `call_0`. The model saw the same requests in the same order as the repro on `main`.

| Step | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| "That's the shape of it." after the tour turn | 2 | 1 |
| Stale "Reading tool details" row | 1 | 0 |

- After each card commit (look, connectors, layout), every assistant message showed once.
- During the tour turn, the settled stream bubble showed for about 8 s. Then the stored fold "Ran 1 command, used 3 tools" replaced it, and no copy stayed.
- An isolated script against a real `SessionDB` confirmed the backend step. The seed live dicts got row ids 1 and 2 with the persisted marker set. The branch live dicts got the child's row ids 5 and 6, not the parent's 3 and 4.
- Checks: ruff on both Python files, `import tui_gateway.server`, prettier and eslint on `tool-parts.ts`, and `tsc -p . --noEmit` in `apps/desktop`.

Gaps:
- The run used only the reuse-ids mode. It did not repeat the unique-ids control run.
- The portal refused a new free-tier identity (`anon_rate_limited`). The run used a throwaway anonymous identity from the repro sandbox, copied into its own auth dir.
- No test suites ran locally. CI runs them.

items.body:
In the desktop app, a tool call that reuses an earlier call's id now gets its own row, so a finished row is no longer overwritten while the turn streams.

Linear: NS-1029 (B3)

## The problem

**What the user saw.** Some providers reuse one tool call id for every call (llama.cpp sends a constant id; `deterministic_call_id` repeats across turns). In onboarding, the name turn loads `hermes-agent` (success), then tries `hermes-setup` (fails). While the reply streamed, the chat showed only one red row, "Failed to load skill: hermes-setup". The successful "Loaded skill: hermes-agent" row was gone. The correct rows came back only after the turn settled.

**Root cause.** `apps/desktop/src/lib/chat-messages/tool-parts.ts::findToolPartIndex` matched a live `tool.start` / `tool.complete` to the first part with the same `toolCallId`, even when that part already had a result. So the second call's events took over the first call's finished row and wrote their name, args and result into it.

A second path had the same bug class. `apps/desktop/src/store/tool-diffs.ts` kept inline diffs keyed only by `payload.tool_id`, and `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/tool/fallback.tsx::ToolEntry` preferred that side diff over the part's own diff. With a reused id, the first row showed the newest patch's diff. The fix above makes this visible, because the second call now gets its own row.

## What changes

- `tool-parts.ts::findToolPartIndex`: the stable-id match claims only a part that has no result yet. A completion that finds no open part matches the last same-id part only when it carries no result or the same result (a replayed completion). Otherwise the call gets a new row.
- `fallback.tsx::ToolEntry`: the row reads its diff only from its own result (`inlineDiffFromResult(toolResultRecord(part))`). `upsertToolPart` already writes `inline_diff` into `toolResultMetadata` on every live completion, and cold hydration never filled the side store.
- `gateway-event/tools.ts`: the `recordToolDiff` call is removed.
- `store/tool-diffs.ts` and its test are deleted. `inline-edit-persistence.test.tsx` loses two assertions about the deleted store.

No new tests. CI runs vitest.

## Proof

Observed at `b0859c33bead053b6d29d9db7e45282277655c95` in the live desktop app (isolated `HOME` / `HERMES_HOME` under `/tmp/lane0/ns1029-B3/`, CDP port 9333). A fake model in reuse-ids mode gave every tool call the id `call_0`. On the name turn it called `skill_view hermes-agent` (success), then `skill_view hermes-setup` (fails), then streamed a long reply.

- Before: midstream, the chat showed one red row, "Failed to load skill: hermes-setup", and no hermes-agent row.
- After: from t+1.0s, through the streaming text, and after the turn settled, the group header read "Loaded skill: hermes-agent, failed to load skill: hermes-setup, 1 tool call failed". Expanded, it showed two separate rows: "Loaded skill: hermes-agent" and "Failed to load skill: hermes-setup".
- The live midstream view now matches the settled view.

Checks: `eslint`, `prettier --check` on the changed files, and `tsc --noEmit -p apps/desktop` pass.

Both screenshots show the same moment, midstream. The after build collapses the two rows into one group header, so the two views do not look alike row for row.

## What does this PR do?

Main's `Python tests / Run tests` is red on one test: `tests/tui_gateway/test_show_reasoning_display_gate.py::test_gateway_lifecycle_set_covers_desktop_card_tools` fails with `CARD_TOOL_NAMES not found in tool-render-class.ts`.

#127828 changed `CARD_TOOL_NAMES` in `apps/desktop/src/lib/tool-render-class.ts` from `new Set([...])` to `[...] as const`. The test finds that list with a regex that only matches `new Set([`. The gateway's `_TOOL_LIFECYCLE_UI_TOOLS` still covers every desktop card name, so this is a stale test parser, not a product bug.

#127828 merged green because it only touched `apps/`, so the classifier skipped the Python lane and the one test that reads that file never ran.

## Related Issue

No issue filed. Regression from #127828.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Changes Made

- `tests/tui_gateway/test_show_reasoning_display_gate.py`: the parser accepts both `new Set([...])` and `[...] as const`, and fails on an empty list instead of passing a vacuous subset check.
- `scripts/ci/classify_changes.py`: `tool-render-class.ts` joins `_PY_RELEVANT_CONTRACT_FILES`, so an edit to it runs the Python lane.
- `tests/ci/test_classify_changes.py`: one classifier case for the new entry.

The TypeScript is unchanged; the `as const` tuple types #127828's card table.

4. The new classifier case fails against the old classifier, and feeding #127828's file list to the classifier now yields `python=true`.

## What does this PR do?

Some models escape `patch` arguments one extra time on the wire ("escape drift"), so a real line break arrives as the two characters `\n`. The escape-drift guard in `tools/fuzzy_match.py` already caught drifted quotes and doubled backslashes, but not this case: the edit went through with `success: true` and wrote a literal `\n` into the file instead of a line break.

For example, with this file:
```python
def greet():
    print("hi")
```
a drifted call sends `old_string` as `def greet():\n    print("hi")` on one line. Before, a loose match could still apply it and the file became the single broken line `def greet():\n    print("hello")`. Now the call is rejected with an escape-drift error asking the model to resend with real line breaks.

**How the check works:** for each matched region of the file, if the region has real line breaks and `old_string` contains **more** literal `\n` than that region, the extra ones are drift, and the call is rejected. `old_string` is copied from the file, so a normal edit has the same count even when the code legitimately contains `"\n"`, and is unaffected. The literal must also be in `new_string`, since that's what would be written in place of the line break.

- **Counts, not presence:** an earlier version only fired when the region had no literal `\n` at all, so a block that also contained a legitimate `"\n"` masked the drift and was still corrupted.
- **Per match:** regions are compared one at a time; joining them multiplied the file-side count under `replace_all`.
- **`\n` only, not `\r`:** a literal `\r` is already converted back to a real carriage return by `_maybe_unescape_new_string` whenever the region has one, so guarding it only rejected good edits (it made the existing `test_carriage_return_in_new_string_unescaped` fail).

**Known limitation:** if only `new_string` is escaped, it can't be told apart from a normal edit that adds a `"\n"` to the code, so it isn't caught.

## Related Issue

Fixes #

## Type of Change

- [x] :bug: Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] :sparkles: New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] :lock: Security fix
- [ ] :pencil: Documentation update
- [ ] :white_check_mark: Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] :recycle: Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] :dart: New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `tools/fuzzy_match.py`
  - New `_detect_newline_literal_drift(content, matches, old_string, new_string)`: compares literal `\n` counts between `old_string` and each matched region individually; wired into `_detect_escape_drift()`.
- `tests/tools/test_fuzzy_match.py`
  - `test_carriage_return_in_new_string_unescaped` (existing): now uses real line breaks. Its old form sent a literal `\n` next to the `\r` and only asserted `"replaced\r" in new`, so it passed while the file received a literal backslash + n.
  - New `TestNewlineLiteralDrift` (4 tests): drifted call rejected; code that really contains `"\n"` still applies; drift next to a legitimate `"\n"` rejected; drift under `replace_all` rejected. Each rejection also checks the content is unchanged.

## How to Test

1. Create a file with `def greet():` and `    print("hi")` on two lines.
2. Call `patch` with `old_string` `def greet():\n    print("hi")` and `new_string` `def greet():\n    print("hello")`, both with a literal `\n`.
   - **Before:** the edit succeeds and the file becomes one broken line.
   - **After:** the call is rejected with an escape-drift error and the file is unchanged.
3. Patch a file that really contains `print("hi\n")` with a correct `old_string`: the edit applies normally.
4. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_fuzzy_match.py -k "TestNewlineLiteralDrift or test_carriage_return_in_new_string_unescaped"`

Results: all 5 pass. On the original commit (`098833743e`) the mixed case and the `\r` test fail; on v0.21.1 three of the new tests fail.

- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)

items.body:
The first terminal command in a fresh desktop, gateway or newly routed profile session now runs at once, instead of waiting for the tirith security scanner to download.

Linear: NS-1029 (side-2)

## Problem

What the user saw: in a fresh desktop setup session, the user clicks "Quick tour". Hermes says "One moment." and then shows "Running python3 -m http.server 18931 --bind 127.0.0.1" with a spinner. The spinner never stops. The user must press Stop and send again before the tour runs.

Root cause: `tools/tirith_security.py::_resolve_tirith_path`. The CLI starts the tirith install in a background thread at startup. Desktop serve, the gateway and a newly routed profile never run that startup step. For them, the first `check_command_security` call claimed the install and ran `pm.ensure("tirith")` inline. So the first terminal command waited for the PM worker, the runtime toolchain and the tirith download before it could run.

## What changes

- `_resolve_tirith_path` no longer installs inline. A cold scan starts the same background install as CLI startup, through a new `_start_background_install` helper. `ensure_installed` uses the same helper.
- A new `_install_in_flight()` helper returns the live install thread for this profile home. `missing_is_expected()` uses it.
- `check_command_security` does not spawn the missing default `tirith` binary while this home's install thread is alive. So a scan during the download never counts as a crash and never opens the circuit breaker.
  - With `tirith_fail_open: true` (the default), the command is allowed at once with the summary "tirith installing".
  - With `tirith_fail_open: false`, the scan waits for the install (the old behaviour) and then scans with the real binary.
- `tests/tools/test_tirith_security.py` and `tests/pm/test_security_consumers.py::test_tirith_failed_cold_scans_make_one_attempt_then_explicit_can_retry` now join the background install thread before they assert. The install no longer runs inline, so these tests must wait for it.

## Proof

Observed at e83fe55449 (before the rebase). The rebase onto `main` (now e031ff02e7) had no conflicts and did not change the code.

- Rig: the desktop app from this branch, under `env -i` with a fake HOME and a fresh `HERMES_HOME` and `HERMES_SHARED_AUTH_DIR`. A fake onboarding model replayed the setup flow (name, theme, connectors, layout Basic, then "Quick tour").
- Before (same base, without this change): the terminal call never returned. After 12.05 s the Stop step cancelled it: "[Tool execution cancelled — terminal was abandoned: explicit stop requested]".
- After: the terminal result ("Background process started") came 138 ms after the call. The same turn then ran `tool_describe`, `gui_tour` targets and `gui_tour` start, and finished with its final text. No Stop button showed at any sample from 3 s to 15 s after the click.
- The background install wrote the tirith binary about 11 s after the terminal result. So the command did not wait for the download.
- Breaker check (in process, download held open): before the second commit, 3 fail-open scans returned "tirith unavailable" and then the breaker opened. With fail-closed, 3 commands were blocked and then the breaker allowed commands unscanned. After the fix, 5 fail-open scans returned "tirith installing" with 0 crashes. Fail-closed waited 1.01 s for the download and then ran real scans. The breaker stayed closed in both cases.

Out of scope: the after image shows "That's the shape of it." twice. This branch does not have the separate NS-1029 rendering fixes.

<!-- before-and-after:start -->
| Before (Desktop onboarding: Quick tour turn) | After (Desktop onboarding: Quick tour turn) |
|:---:|:---:|
| ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ba308074-4413-44b2-8489-d946573812ae) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/987bfb6f-ea77-4ff8-af2d-c73b6a2f94d2) |

## What does this PR do?

A flavored (canary/commit) desktop release build now stages its rendered icon set for the packaging window only, so the checkout is clean when the build ends and the source custody check passes.

**Root cause:** electron-builder resolves all packaging artwork from the workspace (`icon: 'assets/icon'`, the `assets/icon.ico` extraResource, the MSIX logos `before-build.mjs` stages from `assets/appx`, and the exe identity stamp), so `_build_prepared` copied the flavored render over `apps/desktop/assets/` and never restored it — harmless while those paths were gitignored, fatal once #122022 committed them, after which `require_source` refused that build at the check sitting right after the copy and every later build in the tree at the first check.

## Related Issue

No issue — reported directly.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `scripts/bundles/desktop.py`: new `flavored_assets()` context manager holds the render at its workspace path for the packaging block and restores the admitted files afterwards, finished or failed.
- `scripts/bundles/desktop.py::_build_prepared`: the packaging block (build stamp, desktop product build, native version capture, electron-builder) runs inside it; the trailing `require_source` moved after it and now asserts the build handed the checkout back.
- `tests/scripts/test_desktop_preparation.py`: invariant test — the render is live in the packaging window, the custody check correctly refuses there, and the admitted files are back with render-only additions removed, on both the success and the failure path.

## How to Test

1. From a clean checkout whose `HEAD` equals the tag: `python scripts/bundles/desktop.py --tag=<canary tag>` (unchanged release flow, see `apps/desktop/BUILDING.md`).
2. After it finishes, `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` prints nothing.
3. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/scripts/test_desktop_preparation.py`

**Live repro:** replaying the real sequence (flavored render → copy → `require_source`) against a clean worktree reproduces the reported error with exactly the 15 icon paths; with the fix, the same replay leaves `git status --porcelain` empty and `require_source` passing.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| custody check inside the packaging window | passes, then the copy dirties the tree | still refuses, as designed |
| that build's post-copy check | `ValueError: desktop builds require a clean source checkout…` (15 paths) | passes |
| later build in the same tree | fails at the first check, permanently | clean checkout, builds normally |
| `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/scripts/test_desktop_preparation.py` | 1 failed (new test red on base) | 10 passed |

## Checklist

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(desktop):`)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) — #122022 is the change that made these paths tracked, and no open PR fixes the resulting build failure
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] `scripts/run_tests.sh` on the mirrored dirs (`tests/scripts/test_desktop_preparation.py`, `test_desktop_cli_wrapper.py`, `test_desktop_build_cache.py`): 34 passed, 2 skipped; plus `ruff check`, `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all`, `scripts/check_subprocess_stdin.py` clean. Full suite left to CI.
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (proven red on base, then green)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: NixOS (Linux) — the flavored render, the staging window and the custody check exercised end to end with the real functions

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Documentation: N/A — no user-visible behaviour, command or config key changes; the release flow in `apps/desktop/BUILDING.md` is unchanged
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example`: N/A
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md`: N/A

# Keep native Wayland fullscreen windows painting

## Root cause

On native Wayland (Hyprland and other wlroots compositors), a fullscreen
chat window is misclassified as occluded by Chromium and background-throttled
at idle. The stream-throttle controller on main only unthrottles while
turns are in flight, and nothing invalidates the stuck surface, so after a
few idle minutes the page stops painting and goes white until the user
leaves fullscreen.

## What changes

From #121020 (kvnloo), adapted onto current main:

- `createStreamThrottle` takes a `keepFullscreenPainting` option; the fleet
  stays unthrottled while any registered window is fullscreen, and the
  trailing throttle re-arms when the last window leaves fullscreen or
  closes.
- main.ts scopes the option to native Wayland only
  (`linuxOzoneBackend() === 'wayland'`), reusing the same Ozone resolver as
  the rest of Desktop, so X11/XWayland, macOS and Windows keep the normal
  idle-throttling contract.

## Acceptance coverage

- #94865: fullscreen windows keep painting (fleet unthrottled while any
  window is fullscreen on native Wayland) ✓; no manual reload, no renderer
  state discarded (no reload involved — throttling policy only) ✓; idle
  throttling preserved for non-fullscreen windows and re-armed on
  leave/close ✓.

## Tests run

- `npx vitest run electron/stream-throttle.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` —
  **10/10 pass** on this branch; on origin/main (impl reverted) the new
  lifetime tests fail red (3 failures).

Not exercised live: actual painting behavior on a Hyprland host (this is a
macOS dev machine). The reporter of #94865 volunteered a Hyprland machine —
a Linux run should confirm before merge.

Supersedes #121020 (its draft status and main.ts conflicts are resolved
here) and #94949 (the watchdog treated the stuck-surface symptom; the
root-cause unthrottle makes it unnecessary, and carrying both would double
nudge surfaces). Thanks @kvnloo and @Finn763.

Fixes #94865

## What

Quick Entry's **Send to** dropdown options are unreadable under dark themes on Windows/Chromium. The closed `<select>` already paints theme-aware text, but the native `<option>` popup had no explicit foreground/background pair, so a themed foreground landed on an OS-provided popup surface with too little contrast.

Every built-in and dynamic option now paints the existing elevated-surface and primary-text theme tokens explicitly (`apps/desktop/src/app/quick-entry/quick-entry-app.tsx`). The select stays native, because a custom popup gets clipped by the compact Quick Entry window.

This is @Nagisa-3000's fix from https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/121510, cherry-picked with their authorship after they closed that PR. It was reviewed and verified there: the regression test fails on the pre-fix code and passes with it.

Fixes #77429

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/121510 (closed by its author) and the earlier https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/121505 / https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/77430.

## Tests

- `npx vitest run src/app/quick-entry/quick-entry-app.test.tsx`: 1/1 passed on this branch (rebased on current `main`).

## Review

This is a visible UI change, so auto-merge is off. There's no harness screenshot, because the bug is in the OS-drawn native option popup, which a browser harness doesn't render the way Windows Chromium does.

Thanks @Nagisa-3000!

# Guarantee an exit path for a fullscreened preview pane

## Root cause

A preview `<webview>` guest that HTML5-fullscreens itself owns all input:
the guest is its own out-of-process webContents, so the host renderer can't
see into it, the macOS-only Close menu item and the HUD's ⌘W aren't
reachable, and on Wayland there is no xdotool/wmctrl to break out from a
terminal. A guest page that swallows Esc (or never offers an exit) locks the
whole display.

## What changes

Three layers, all routed before the guest sees the key or fully outside it:

- **`before-input-event` on every webview guest**: Esc exits the host
  window's fullscreen (gated on the fullscreen state so normal-mode panes
  keep passing Esc to the page — video players use it), Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+W
  closes the pane via the existing close-preview channel. Electron fires
  this per-webContents, so it works even while the guest holds focus.
- **`hermes://close-preview` deep link**, handled in the main process:
  restores and focuses the window, exits fullscreen, closes the pane. Works
  when the GUI cannot hear anything because it's handled entirely in main.
- **`hermes desktop --close-preview`** CLI flag forwarded to the packaged
  exe, riding the single-instance argv — a second invocation from a
  terminal or SSH session unlocks the running app.

The permission handlers keep auto-allowing 'fullscreen'/'automatic-fullscreen':
the exit paths are the fix, and scoping the grant would just break legitimate
video fullscreen.

## Acceptance coverage

- #97213: reachable exit while a fullscreen pane holds input focus ✓
  (guest-level key interception); CLI/deep-link command to close/exit when
  input-locked ✓ (`--close-preview` + `hermes://close-preview`); panes open
  contained by default ✓ (already the norm — the fullscreen came from the
  guest page's own request).

## Tests run

- `npx vitest run electron/preview-guest-escape.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` —
  **7/7 pass** (pure routing decision + flag parsing; the module is new so
  origin/main has nothing to run red — the wiring is main-process only).
- `bash scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_cli/test_gui_command.py` —
  **69 passed, 0 failed**; the close-preview forwarding test fails red on
  origin/main.

Not exercised live: a real fullscreened webview guest (needs a Linux/Wayland
or any desktop run); the interception logic is the pure function
`previewGuestInputAction`, unit-tested hermetically.

Fixes #97213

## Root cause

Two catalog fetch paths, one bad budget model:

- `website/src/pages/skills/index.tsx` fetched `skills.json` (~50 MB raw, served via
  CDN) with a bare `fetch` — no abort path at all. A silently hung connection
  (polluted DNS, TLS reset) left the page on "Loading the catalog…" forever, and a
  failed load fell through to the misleading "No skills found" empty state with
  no retry.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/capabilities/catalog/catalog-data.ts` used
  `AbortSignal.timeout(60_000)` — a *total-time* budget. The skills snapshot is
  10.9 MB gzip; anything under ~181 KB/s aborts mid-transfer, and Chromium
  renders our own abort as "The user aborted a request."

## Fix

Both surfaces now bound *inactivity*, not total transfer time: the body is read
as a stream and every non-empty chunk re-arms the deadline (45s website, 60s
desktop). A slow-but-alive download finishes; a stalled one aborts and is
reported as a stall/timeout, never as user cancellation. The website gains a
dedicated load-error card with a Retry button (replacing the hero's inline
error note and the "No skills found" fall-through) and aborts in-flight fetches
on unmount/retry.

Deliberately unchanged (per the issues' own scoping): automatic retry/backoff
policy, download progress UI, and any payload slimming — manual Retry stays.

## Coverage per issue

- #97861: the issue's expected behavior is an OR (load, or clear error + retry,
  or system proxy). This delivers the stall abort + retryable error card on the
  website gallery, the surface still live via the Bot Mode picker embed and the
  docs site.
- #123838: the desktop Discover catalog no longer aborts a progressing transfer
  at 60s total and no longer surfaces "The user aborted a request." for its own
  timeout.

## Checks run (real commands + results)

- Red on base: with `catalog-data.ts` reverted to origin/main, the new
  `catalog-download.test.ts` fails 8/8 (progressing downloads aborted, stall
  reported as cancellation, timer leaks).
- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 --no-file-parallelism
  src/app/capabilities/catalog/catalog-download.test.ts
  src/app/capabilities/catalog/catalog-data.test.ts` — 15 passed.
- Website has no local test setup; the page file parses clean under the TSX
  parser (0 diagnostics) and full `tsc`/build runs in CI.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/97996 — Thanks @liuhao1024
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/123872 — Thanks @funky-xamarin

Both commits are cherry-picked verbatim (authorship preserved) with a trivial
rebase over hero-copy drift on the website page.

Fixes #97861
Fixes #123838


## Screenshots

Website skills page (`website/src/pages/skills/index.tsx` mounted directly in a Docusaurus-free harness, catalog fetch stubbed to fail), before/after at the same load state:

**Before (current `main`):** the failed load leaves the hero's tiny inline error note and an empty "No skills found" grid — no retry:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OutThisLife/hermes-agent/38026c31c9e381320efbaba04a1df1f917b95cba/pr-128192/before.png

**After (PR head):** a dedicated "Couldn't load the catalog" error card with a Retry button:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OutThisLife/hermes-agent/31bd5f3d2c753bb63de2570a8748deefbb6bdc7d/pr-128192/after.png

## What

Clarify choices could disappear without anyone noticing, in two places:

- **Tool (#73152).** A `choices` list whose entries were all blank quietly became an open-ended question (`tools/clarify_tool.py::_normalize_questions`, `... or None`). The model never learned its options were gone, and Desktop showed a free-text card for what was meant to be a choice prompt.
- **Desktop (#124127).** `normalizeChoices` (`apps/desktop/src/store/clarify.ts`) dropped any choice over 200 characters or containing a newline, while `choices_offered` still reported it as shown. Users picked among missing options, and the agent never knew.

## Change

- The tool now returns an error for both cases instead of degrading silently:
  - a non-empty `choices` list with no surviving label names the question;
  - a choice over `MAX_CHOICE_CHARS` (8000, also declared as `maxLength` in the schema) names its position and the limit.

  An omitted or empty `choices` list stays open-ended, which is still the documented way to ask free-text.
- Desktop's filter matches that contract: choices up to 8000 characters (measured without the `(Recommended)` label) and newlines are kept. Long option text wraps in the card instead of vanishing.

This is rebuilt on top of #127760's `questions[]` refactor, which left both paths as they were.

## Tests

- `tests/tools/test_clarify_tool.py`: 4 new tests (all-blank rejected, empty list stays open-ended, over-limit rejected, long multi-line choice kept). The all-blank and over-limit tests fail on `main` and pass here. The file passes in full, along with `tests/tools/test_clarify_gateway.py`.
- `apps/desktop/src/store/clarify.test.ts`: 20/20.

items.body:
## Root cause

`stopVoicePlayback()` reached only the newest playback through a single module-level
`currentStop` slot (`apps/desktop/src/lib/voice-playback.ts:23` at base, 7 writer sites).
When two playbacks overlap — `startSpeechStream` resolves its gateway URL/TTS config
asynchronously and only then calls `stopVoicePlayback()`, so a barge-in plus a next-turn
open can cross that gap — the overwritten session is never stopped: its WebSocket stays
open, its AudioContext keeps scheduling buffers, its `done` never settles (leaking the
150 ms feed timer in `use-voice-conversation` that clears after `await session.done`),
and its queued audio resurfaces audibly turns later (#91991).

## Fix

- Every live playback registers an idempotent stop in a `liveStops` set: client-direct
  sessions, streaming sessions (WebSocket close + AudioContext close), and data-URL
  audio elements. Each stop unregisters itself on settle, so the set self-cleans.
- `stopVoicePlayback()` drains the whole set, not just the newest slot, then clears it.
- Stale-start guard: if the voice-playback sequence advanced during `startSpeechStream`'s
  async discovery, it returns `null` instead of resurrecting stopped playback.
- Sequence-scoped settle: a session's completion only writes the idle state when no newer
  playback started since, so a settled session cannot stomp a newer turn's state.

## Coverage

- Fixes #91991 — interrupted/overlapping speech sessions are fully torn down on barge-in.

## Checks run

- `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/lib/voice-playback.test.ts` — 6/6 pass
  (2 of these fail on base: the stale-start and sequence-scoped-settle tests).
- `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-voice-conversation-boundary.test.tsx src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-voice-conversation.test.tsx` — 12/12 pass.
- Red-on-base proven by checking out base `voice-playback.ts` alongside the new tests:
  2 failed / 4 passed; branch passes 6/6.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/92334 — same three-part design
  (liveStops registry, stale-start guard, sequence-scoped completion), re-authored onto
  current main's voice-playback.ts (the PR's head predates the sentence-queue fallback,
  edge-TTS interim flushes and id-rewrite work, so hunks were re-authored rather than
  cherry-picked) and extended to all seven `currentStop` writer sites. Thanks @Finn763.

Fixes #91991

items.body:
After the onboarding tour, the composer status stack no longer shows a stray preview row for the app's own page.

Linear: NS-1029 (B4)

## Problem

After the tour turn, a globe row "127.0.0.1:5174" appeared above the composer. In a packaged build the row reads "index.html". The row is the app's own page, not something the agent made.

Root cause: `apps/desktop/src/lib/tour/engine.ts::runTourEngine` returns the app's own `location.href` as `url` for the `gui_tour` action `targets`. `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/tool/fallback-model/index.ts::toolPreviewTarget` treats a top-level `url` in a result as a deliverable preview. Two paths record it:

- The live `tool.complete` handler (`app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event/tools.ts`). Its frames name the real tool, `gui_tour`.
- The tool row, when it mounts (`components/assistant-ui/tool/fallback.tsx`). A bridged `tool_call` reaches this path under another name. A labelled call renders through `components/assistant-ui/connector-tool.tsx::ConnectorExecution`, one row per inner call, and that row's `toolName` is the label title ("Gui Tour"). An unlabelled part keeps `toolName: 'tool_call'` with the real tool in `args.name` or in a one-entry `args.calls`.

So a guard on the tool name never saw `gui_tour` on the row path. I observed this in the live renderer: the preview atom write came from the `fallback.tsx` effect.

## What changes

- `toolPreviewTarget` returns no target for tools that only look at a page: `gui_tour`, `drive_preview`, `annotate_preview`, and `desktop_preview` unless its action is `open`. The file-read tools stay in the same set.
- `ConnectorExecution` passes each row's real tool name as `innerToolName`. For a `tool_call` entry this is the label's name. For any other tool it is the part's own tool. `buildToolView` uses this name for the preview check only. The row title does not change.
- `toolPreviewTarget` unwraps a one-call `tool_call` (legacy `name` form or a one-entry `calls`) to the inner tool and its arguments.

## Proof (observed at 075a544529)

I ran the dev app from this branch in an isolated home with a scripted model. The flow starts a background `python3 -m http.server`, then runs the tour turn twice. I hooked the preview atom to catch any write that holds `5174`.

- With every tool call id set to `call_0`: after the tour turn, the status stack held only the metrics row. The preview atom stayed `{}` and caught no write.
- The same held after a renderer reload, and after I expanded the tool groups so the "Gui Tour" rows mounted.
- Control with unique tool call ids: same result.
- `desktop_preview` with action `open` still gives its url as a preview target.

Before: origin/main, same flow with every id set to `call_0`. After: this branch, same flow.

<!-- before-and-after:start -->
| Before (Desktop) | After (Desktop) |
|:---:|:---:|
| ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8a43ed4d-727b-4da9-895b-151f65b83cee) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01124f9e-c76e-4b5e-ac2b-769975e5151b) |

<!-- before-and-after:end -->

items.body:
## Root cause

`drive_preview type` clears the target field with a select-all chord before typing. `selectAll()` in `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/right-rail/preview-drive.ts` hardcoded `['control', 'meta']` — both modifiers held simultaneously. No OS treats Ctrl+Cmd+A (macOS) or Ctrl+Win+A (Windows/Linux) as select-all, so native select-all never fired, the pre-type clear silently no-op'd, and typed text appended to the existing value (a 9.99 price field became 19999.99) while the tool still reported success. Compounded by controlled React inputs that re-render on focus (money/date/number masks) and throw the selection away even when the chord is correct.

## Fix

Cherry-picked from #103785 (thanks @YTminiboss) and rebased onto current main, plus the exact-modifier test assertions from #98325 (thanks @guillaumehussong):

- `selectAll()` sends one platform-correct modifier: `['meta']` on macOS, `['control']` elsewhere (same `isMacPlatform()` helper shape as #98325).
- After the focus click, settle so a re-render commits, then select-all and **verify** via `document.activeElement` that the field actually emptied.
- If select-all silently failed, clear deterministically with End + N Backspaces instead of typing over stale content.
- If real keystrokes cannot empty a masked field at all, fall back to setting the value through the input's native prototype setter with input/change events.
- Fail closed: never type into a field that could not be emptied, so the driver can never silently corrupt a value.
- Thread `typeText`'s character count out through the type path so an interrupted type reports how many characters landed instead of claiming none did.

## Coverage

- #98324 — platform-correct chord + verify-and-fallback layers (fixes).
- #98325 — its narrower per-platform modifier assertions folded into the suite (superseded).

Fixes #98324

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/103785 — the complete fix this PR carries forward (thanks @YTminiboss)
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/98325 — its platform-native chord and test assertions folded in (thanks @guillaumehussong)

## Checks run

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/app/chat/right-rail/preview-act.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` — 26/26 pass
- Red on base proven: with `origin/main`'s `preview-act.ts`/`preview-drive.ts` checked out, the new "Command+A on macOS and Control+A elsewhere" test fails (`expected { keyCode: 'a', … } to match object { modifiers: ['meta'] }` — main sends `['control','meta']`)
- `cd apps/desktop && npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` — clean

items.body:
## Root cause

Two layers in `apps/desktop/src/plugins/radio/plugin.js`:

1. The external `pause` event listener called `stop()` unconditionally —
   clearing `src`, calling `load()`, removing the element, advancing the
   generation — so any external media controller (macOS media keys, Fluid
   Voice pausing audio to hear the microphone) destroyed the stream it might
   resume.
2. But preserving the stream is not enough: the reporter's own identical
   experiment still failed the real Fluid Voice reproduction. Fluid Voice
   delivers the transcript into the focused editable field via macOS
   Accessibility APIs — a guarded paste (⌘V) in Chromium/Electron — and emits
   **no media-session resume signal** afterwards. Radio could stay
   non-destructively paused forever with nothing to tell it dictation ended.

## Fix

- External `pause` is now non-destructive: `status.set('paused')`, the
  element and its `src` survive (`stop()` → `status.set('paused')` in the
  external listener, credit to #108115 for the one-liner and survival test).
- The player tracks `playGeneration` — the generation that last reached
  `playing` — so it knows whether the paused element is the live stream.
- `resume()` resumes that intact element with a plain `element.play()`;
  it returns false when the stream is not intact (fresh start, the plugin's
  own destructive Pause, a stop from another window).
- On dictation completion — a `paste` event targeting a text field or
  contenteditable (the composer) — the plugin resumes the preserved stream.
  Never on window focus: that would override an intentional pause.
- The plugin's own Pause stays destructive by design: `toggle()` from `live`
  runs `stop()`, so a paste never resurrects a stream the user paused, and
  Play afterwards is a full reconnect.

## Coverage per requirement (#108113)

- External pause preserves the stream: survival test (status `paused`,
  same element, same `src`, later `playing` → `live`).
- Auto-resume after dictation: paste into a textarea while externally
  paused → same element resumes, status `live`, no teardown/reconnect.
- Plugin Pause stays destructive: after `toggle()` from `live` the element
  is gone, a paste does not resume, and Play creates a fresh element.
- Real-macOS Fluid Voice verification remains platform acceptance evidence
  the reporter can now run: dictate with the Option key, confirm insertion,
  radio resumes. The unit tests cover the renderer-visible contract.

## Checks run

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/contrib/radio-plugin.test.ts` — 5 passed
- Red on base: same suite with `origin/main`'s plugin.js — 2 failed (survival + dictation-resume), 3 passed
- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/contrib/radio-plugin.test.ts src/contrib/radio-artist-links.test.ts` — full radio suite green

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/108115

Thanks @kokhlo — the non-destructive external pause and the stream-survival
test are taken verbatim from #108115.

Fixes #108113
items.title: fix(desktop/radio): keep the stream alive across an external pause and resume it when dictation lands

items.body:
## Root cause

Vercel's WAF denies some residential IP ranges (e.g. Spamhaus-listed ones) for
the entire `hermes-agent.nousresearch.com` domain. The Bot Mode Skills Hub
picker (`apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/skills-hub.tsx`) hardcodes that
origin for its iframe with no fallback, so users on a flagged range get a
permanent 403 block page instead of the picker. Nothing in the repo or docs
mentioned the mirror or the workaround.

## Fix

- Re-land the surviving half of closed #118206 (its Capabilities-picker target
  was deleted by the native catalog): before each browse session the plugin
  HEAD-probes the primary picker URL and falls back to the equivalent GitHub
  Pages deployment (`https://nousresearch.github.io/hermes-agent/docs/skills?embed=picker`)
  when the probe is refused, fails, or hangs.
- The probe carries an `AbortSignal.timeout(8s)` deadline (the open review note
  on #118206) so a hanging connection cannot delay the fallback.
- Picker installs are accepted from either trusted origin, still gated on our
  own frame's `contentWindow` (the source check from #86243 stays).
- New FAQ troubleshooting entry: what the 403 is, that the picker self-heals
  via Pages, and to report affected ranges to the maintainers.

The Vercel-side action (WAF mitigation rules for the reporter's range) is a
deployment task outside this repo and still needs a maintainer answer on the
issue.

## Checks run (real commands + results)

- Red on base: with `skills-hub.tsx` reverted to origin/main, the four new
  tests fail (no fallback on refused/failed/hung probe; fallback-origin install
  rejected).
- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism
  src/plugins/hermes-bots/skills-hub-picker.test.tsx` — 12 passed (4 new
  fallback tests + 8 pre-existing pick-security tests, fetch stubbed).

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/118206 — Thanks @KoNit-K
  (closed; half its diff targeted a file since deleted. The skills-hub half is
  re-landed here with credit.)

Fixes #118203

items.body:
`main` fails the JS & TS checks on every desktop PR. This PR fixes the four failing tests in `clarify-hydration.test.tsx`. It changes no product code.

## The problem

Since #127760, a clarify request has one shape: `questions: [{question, choices?, multi_select?}]`. The desktop clarify handler (`server-requests.ts`) reads only `questions`.

Three later commits (`cc931d239c`, `adb1cbde32`, `73688014f7`) added tests that send the old shape: a top-level `choices` and `question`. The handler gets an empty list and returns at once. So it stores no card, `requestId` is `undefined`, and the hydrated part keeps `args: {}`. These four tests fail:

- hydrates an already-pending sparse clarify row from the live request
- keeps a live clarify card through a spurious message.complete
- keeps a live clarify card through a spurious error
- keeps a live clarify card through a stale session.info running=false snapshot (#83319)

The product code in those commits already works with the new shape. `restorePendingClarifyToolCall` gets its args from `pendingClarifyToolPayload`, which sends `questions`.

## What changes

- The four `clarifyRequest(...)` calls send `questions: [{ choices, qid: 'q0', question }]`.
- The re-arm test expects `args: { questions: [...] }`.
- Prettier reflowed one `act(...)` line in the same file.

## How to test

```bash
cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/clarify-hydration.test.tsx
```

The tests were not run on the author's machine. CI runs them.

items.body:
## Root cause

Four failed sessions ([#125830](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/125830)): the agent does not know it owns a screen. When the user says "open chrome in screen 20", the model has never been told what "screen 20" is — nothing in the system prompt, tool descriptions, or session context names the Bot Screen, its display number, or the lease state — so it falls back to launching Chrome on the user's own display through the terminal. And even when a session happens to know, terminal children inherit the **seat** environment: `_make_run_env` never merges the bot desktop's published `DISPLAY`/`XAUTHORITY`/`DBUS`, so GUI apps open on the user's display anyway.

## What changes

**Terminal env half** (from #125835, kept): while this profile's Bot Desktop is running, `_make_run_env` merges `published_env()` — the pure read, no activity stamp (a plain `ls` must not keep the screen alive past `idle_stop_minutes`) — so `DISPLAY`/`XAUTHORITY`/`DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` route children to the bot screen, and `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is dropped (an X11 desktop; a leaked Wayland socket flips GTK/Chromium backends). A user who wants their own seat still can: an inline `DISPLAY=:0 cmd` prefix wins, since bash applies it after this env.

**Model-context half** (new):
- `agent/prompt_builder.py`: the environment-hints block gains one line — "Bot Screen: … RUNNING on display :N (you hold it / a human holds it…)" — naming the screen, the display, and the lease state, exactly the facts "screen N" / ":N" / "your screen" need to resolve. Local backends only: a sandboxed terminal cannot open windows on the gateway host. Pure reads, never raises, drops out entirely when no screen runs.
- `tui_gateway/methods_display_watch.py`: the runtime-file watcher (which already detects a screen start/stop from any process) now also stages the same sentence as a one-shot per-turn note on every live session of that profile — the system prompt is byte-stable and only rebuilt at compaction, so a screen started mid-session would otherwise stay unknown for the rest of the conversation. The note rides the existing `_gateway_turn_context_notes` channel behind the cached prefix, and another profile's sessions are never told.

## Acceptance coverage

- "screen N" / ":N" / "your screen" resolves to the bot screen — the hint line names it and its display directly. **Covered** (prompt line; the routing itself is behavioural and needs the reporter's babysit-style check below).
- GUI apps the agent launches from terminal open on the bot screen — **covered** by the env merge + `test_local_env_bot_desktop.py` (kept from #125835).
- Display introspection targets the bot display — **covered by the same env merge** (`xrandr`/`xdotool`/`wmctrl` read `DISPLAY` from the child env).
- Screen existence/display/lease reach the model — **covered**: prompt hints (rebuilt at compaction) + per-turn notes (immediately on start/stop).

## Tests

All on the Linux-and-macOS-runnable surface (pure functions + file-driven watcher; no X server needed):

- `tests/agent/test_prompt_builder.py` — running screen names display + holder (**red on main**, green with fix); human-held wording (**red on main**); stopped screen leaves no hint; remote backend never sees a host screen.
- `tests/tui_gateway/test_display_watch.py::test_screen_start_and_stop_reach_the_models_turn_notes` — a start/stop made by another process stages the note on that profile's live agent and not on another profile's (**red on main**, green with fix).
- `tests/tools/test_local_env_bot_desktop.py` (from #125835, kept): env merge, snapshot precedence, stopped-screen passthrough, no activity stamp. Green.

One pre-existing timing-sensitive failure, `TestContextFileReadTimeout::test_slow_hermes_md_is_skipped_and_agents_md_still_loads`, fails identically on `origin/main` on this loaded machine — unrelated to this change.

## Not exercised live

The end-to-end "model actually resolves screen 20" behaviour and the lease-note delivery in a real `hermes serve` session need a Linux gateway with a running Bot Desktop; the pure wiring is what this PR unit-proves.

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/125830
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/125835 (keeps its env-merge commit and tests, adds the missing model-context half). Thanks @liuhao1024.

items.body:
## What

Adds GPT-6.1 Sol (`gpt-6.1-sol`, plus `-pro`), which OpenAI released on 2026-09-29, and fixes the one request shape that breaks on it: turning reasoning off.

**WHO / WHEN / WHY:** OpenAI announced GPT-6.1 Sol on 2026-09-29 ([announcement](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-1-sol/), [model page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.1-sol)). No open PR or issue covered it when this was opened. It follows the shape of #126842 (Sonnet 5.5), but 6.1 Sol needs more surfaces: none of the existing `gpt-6-sol` keys match it, because `gpt-6-sol` is not a substring of `gpt-6.1-sol`.

Where it's available, probed live on 2026-09-29:

| Route | Status |
|---|---|
| OpenRouter `/api/v1/models` | `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` and `openai/gpt-6.1-sol-pro`, 1.05M context |
| Direct OpenAI API | model page says `gpt-6.1-sol`, 1.05M context / 128K output |
| Nous Portal `/v1/models` | `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` and `-pro` (missing at the first probe; listed a few hours later) |
| Codex OAuth (our account) | missing from the live catalog; a direct request returns 400 "not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account" |

## Changes

| Surface | Change |
|---|---|
| `hermes_cli/models_catalog_static.py` | `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` and `-pro` added to `OPENROUTER_MODELS`. The `nous` list derives from it; the Portal now serves both. `gpt-6.1-sol` and `-pro` added to the `openai-api` picker. |
| `website/static/api/model-catalog.json` | Regenerated with `scripts/build_model_catalog.py` |
| `agent/model_metadata.py` | 1,050,000 in `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_LENGTHS`; 272K in `_CODEX_OAUTH_CONTEXT_FALLBACK`, so if Codex discovery surfaces it later, the context isn't over-promised at 1.05M. It is **not** added to the `-900k` opt-in because nothing has been verified above 272K. |
| `agent/auxiliary_client.py` | Added to the 272K compaction auto-raise family list. This only has an effect on the `openai-codex` route. |
| `agent/usage_pricing.py` | $2 / $10, cached input $0.10 (5% of input; 6 Sol is 10%), cache write $2.50. Above 272K: 2x input and cache, 1.5x output. `-pro` is aliased to the base row. |
| `agent/reasoning_effort.py` | `gpt-6.1-sol*` uses Astra's `low..max` effort ladder but not Astra's account gating, so it stays in the static catalogs. |
| `plugins/model-providers/openrouter/__init__.py` | Reasoning-off is omitted when the OpenAI ladder has no `none`. See below. |

`codex_models.py` is deliberately unchanged. The Codex backend rejects the slug for this account, and listing it would add a dead picker entry (#52492). Live discovery will pick it up once the account has access.

## Reasoning-off breaking change

GPT-6 Sol accepts `reasoning.effort: none`. GPT-6.1 Sol doesn't. Live via OpenRouter on 2026-09-29, both `reasoning: {enabled: false}` and `{effort: "none"}` return:

> 400 Unsupported value: 'none' is not supported with the 'gpt-6.1-sol-2026-09-29' model. Supported values are: 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'xhigh', and 'max'.

Before this PR:
- Direct API (Responses): `gpt-6.1-sol` fell through to the legacy ladder (`none..xhigh`). Reasoning-off sent `none` (400), and `max` was clamped down to `xhigh`.
- OpenRouter: the live catalog lists `none` as supported with `mandatory: false`, so the profile forwarded the disable (400). This affected `/reasoning none` on the main loop. Aux lanes already recover through `auxiliary_reasoning_floor`.

After this PR:
- Direct API: reasoning-off drops the field (with the existing once-per-model warning), and `max` passes through.
- OpenRouter: the disable is omitted whenever `codex_supported_efforts` for an `openai/` slug has no `none`. The OpenAI ladder overrides a wrong catalog entry. `gpt-6-sol` still sends its disable.

## Verification

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gpt6_tiers_registration.py`: 3 new relationship tests covering the effort ladder (Astra's, but not Astra-gated), the OpenRouter disable omission (6.1 omits, 6 keeps), and context/pricing parity with the tier (`-pro` is the base row; cached rate = input/20; not `-900k`-eligible). Mutation check: reverting the OpenRouter guard fails exactly 1 test, and reverting the ladder prefix fails 2.
- Targeted suite (57 files: codex models, catalog, pricing, metadata, reasoning effort, provider profiles, model-provider plugins, codex transports, model switch, aux reasoning floor): 1023 passed, 10 failed. All 10 fail identically on `upstream/main` (home-IO guard, local env). Ruff is clean.
- Real-import E2E from the worktree: `openai-api` picker leads with `gpt-6.1-sol`; context is 1.05M on `openai` and 272K on `openai-codex`; pricing resolves from `openai-api`; `_resolve_reasoning` gives `(None, False)` for off, `low` for minimal, `max` for max/ultra.
- Live, OpenRouter: the patched profile's reasoning-off kwargs (`extra_body: {}`) no longer return the 400. The request gets past parameter validation and hits a 403 account-policy block on our OpenRouter key, the same block every `openai/*` request returns on that key.
- **Live, Nous Portal, real `AIAgent`** with `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` + terminal tool: ran `echo HELLO-61` and replied `HELLO-61` / `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` (2 API calls, cost $0.0101). Passes with reasoning off too.
- **Not live-tested:** direct OpenAI API (no key here) and OpenRouter (our key is policy-blocked by OpenAI; the `none` 400 above came back before that block).

## Notes / follow-ups

- `/model gpt` version-sorts, so on a route that has both it now resolves to `gpt-6.1-sol` ahead of `gpt-6-astra`. That's the existing "newer version wins" rule. Astra is account-gated and absent from static lists, so on most routes this only replaces `gpt-6-sol`.
- Ultrafast for 6.1 Sol is announced but has no published rate yet. The `/fast ultrafast` tier lands in #128307; 6.1 Sol joins its model set once OpenAI publishes the rate.
- Codex OAuth: once the account catalog lists it, probe the real ceiling before adding it to the `-900k` opt-in.

## Root cause

A Desktop assistant start times out with the generic /model / `hermes setup` hints while the real
cause is auth-store lock contention: `CredentialPool._refresh_entry` legitimately holds the
cross-process `_auth_store_lock` across its OAuth refresh POST (single-use-token safety — the
sync → POST → write-back atomicity is pinned by tests/agent/test_credential_pool_anthropic_refresh_race.py),
but two aggravators made a slow token endpoint fatal for other processes (#124533):

1. `_refresh_pending_entries` chained N holds back-to-back, so a waiter with the shorter
   `AUTH_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 15s` timeout starved behind the whole chain of 20s+ holds.
2. The timeout error named neither the lock file nor the holder, and the user-facing init
   failure message appended the misleading "check /model or run hermes setup" copy.

## What changes

- `_refresh_pending_entries` spaces consecutive holds by 0.5s so a waiter's 50ms poll cadence
  can interleave; the lock-across-POST contract itself is deliberately unchanged (test-pinned,
  maintainer decision per the issue's investigating comment).
- `_file_lock` stamps the holder pid into the lock file on acquire and clears it on release;
  a timing-out waiter names the lock file and, when the pid is live, the probable holder
  (stale pids from dead processes are probed and stay silent). Permanent lock failures
  (flock-unsupported filesystem, ENOSYS) propagate immediately instead of burning the deadline.
- `agent_init_failed_message` recognizes auth-lock timeout prefixes and gives the
  contention-appropriate copy (wait / exit the other process) instead of the credential hints.

Thanks @liuhao1024 — the first commit is his #124933 rebased onto current main (his authorship
kept); this PR supersedes that PR by adding the sweep-spacing half.

## Acceptance coverage

#124533:
- Requirement 3 (timeout names lock file + likely holder, no misleading hints): covered by the
  cherry-picked commit (tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_lock_timeout_diagnosis.py,
  tests/tui_gateway/test_user_messages.py).
- Requirement 2-adjacent mitigation (bound aggregate holds via spacing): covered by the new
  tests/agent/test_credential_pool_refresh_sweep_spacing.py — a waiter window ≥ 0.4s must
  exist between consecutive holds of a 3-entry sweep.
- Requirements 1 and 4 (move the POST outside the lock; capture the dashboard holder path):
  **not** done — moving the POST outside the lock is a deliberate single-use-token tradeoff the
  existing race test pins; that redesign stays a maintainer decision. The spacing mitigation is
  the safe part of the verdict's plan.

## Tests run (real results)

- `bash scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/agent/test_credential_pool_refresh_sweep_spacing.py` on
  plain origin/main: **1 failed** (back-to-back holds starve the waiter); with the fix: **1 passed**.
- `bash scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2` over tests/agent/test_credential_pool_refresh_sweep_spacing.py,
  tests/agent/test_credential_pool_anthropic_refresh_race.py,
  tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_lock_timeout_diagnosis.py, tests/tui_gateway/test_user_messages.py
  on this branch: **4 files, 13 tests passed, 0 failed** — the pinned lock-across-POST contract
  is untouched and still green.

Refs #124533

Co-authored-by: liuhao1024 <sunsky.lau@gmail.com>
