## Root cause

`planReload` / `planRestore` / `planEdit` in `usePromptActions`
(apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/index.ts:968, 1028, 1091) read their transcript
from `$messages.get()` — the global draft mirror. Active sessions publish their transcript into
`$sessionStates[runtimeId].messages`, so for any session with a runtime ID the mirror is empty (or
stale): `findIndex` returns `-1`, the plan comes back null, and refresh / restore / edit silently do
nothing.

## What changed

All three planners now read
`(sessionId ? $sessionStates.get()[sessionId]?.messages : null) ?? $messages.get()` — the runtime
slice when the session has one, the global mirror as fallback for draft (no-runtime) sessions. No
visual change; the same plan is derived from the store that actually holds the transcript.

## Acceptance coverage

Four new tests in `index.test.tsx` pin the primary path for all three actions: messages that exist
only in the runtime slice regenerate / restore / edit correctly with an empty global mirror, and the
runtime slice wins over a divergent mirror entry carrying the same id with different text.
Red-first verified on `origin/main`: all 4 fail without the fix; 141/141 pass with it.

## Tests

- `npx vitest run src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/index.test.tsx --maxWorkers=2` → 141 passed (base: 4 new tests red)
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` → clean
- `npx eslint` on both files → no new findings

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/73608 (fix commit 9f0b5128d43 + test commit 6ff8426fdb5, both re-based here; the source branch diverged too far from main to rebase cleanly — its test file conflicts across ~3.2k changed lines). Credited via Co-authored-by.

Fixes #68734

## Auto-merge

Left OFF: `classify_automerge.py` holds every `apps/desktop/src/` diff with a path-based `ui`
flag, so arming is left to the coordinator's judgment. The change itself is store/hook logic
with no visible UI change; reviewed full head SHA `be667f0835d2f01382b9ebe6c5fe4daefc2aef55`.

## Root cause

`reconcileTileTranscripts` (apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/hooks/use-background-sync.ts:283) ran
`getLatestSessionMessages(storedSessionId, …, { passive: true })` — a 120-row transcript fetch —
BEFORE checking `sessionMessagesSignature(latest.messages)` at :322. The signature only gated the
paint, so every `sessions.changed` tick paid the full fetch per tile even when nothing moved.

## What changed

Before the fetch, the tile's sidebar row (in `$sessions` / `$messagingSessions`) is fingerprinted
with the new `sessionListFingerprint` (message_count / last_active / preview,
apps/desktop/src/lib/session-signatures.ts:55). On a fingerprint match the fetch is skipped
entirely; the fingerprint is (re)armed whenever the fetched transcript proves in sync or lands, so the
gate tracks the row that produced the last transcript. Tiles with no row (hidden bot chats) keep
fetching every tick, and closed tiles prune their fingerprint alongside their signature. Pure
perf: no visual change.

## Acceptance coverage

Two new tests in `use-background-sync.test.ts`:
- unchanged row fingerprint → `getLatestSessionMessages` is NOT called at all (the old
  "skips the tile fetch entirely" test never checked the fetch — only the paint);
- moved row (message_count/last_active/preview changed) → the gate breaks and the fetch + update run.

Red-first verified on `origin/main`: both fail without the gate; 48/48 pass with it.

## Tests

- `npx vitest run src/app/contrib/hooks/use-background-sync.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` → 48 passed (base: the 2 new tests red)
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` → clean
- `npx eslint` on the touched files → no findings

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/95770 (re-implemented on current main — the source branch predates the passive-fetch and replay-sequencing work). Credited via Co-authored-by.

Fixes #95767

flag, so arming is left to the coordinator's judgment. The change itself is store/hook logic
with no visible UI change; reviewed full head SHA `ccf3c4101aeee5c771275e6bf753a997f8d0ef37`.

## Root cause

#95798's edit-race half: a dirty edit followed by blur armed an 80ms cancel path; an Enter landing
inside that window could race a torn-down composer (edit silently dropped) or a wedged submit latch.
The edit-message path on current main carries the try/catch + error toast + rollback that closes the
silent-fail half, but the blur→Enter interleaving was pinned nowhere.

## What changed

Test-only. Ports the two interleave tests from #98166 onto current main (the source branch is
~19.8k commits behind and its test file diverged beyond a clean rebase):

1. a dirty edit whose blur-cancel timer races Enter still submits — no dropped edit, no torn-down
   composer, no "Composer is not available" uncaught error;
2. an edit that survived blur, with focus already outside the composer, still submits on Enter.

Both pass on current main (10/10 in the file), pinning the fixed behavior so a regression fails CI.

The model-switch row jank half of #95798 (hydration.ts `model_switch` system-notice row insert
causing layout shift during a switch) is NOT covered here: it is a rendered-layout symptom not
reproducible in a jsdom unit test, so it stays needs-evidence rather than half-fixed blind.

## Tests

- `npx vitest run src/components/assistant-ui/thread/user-message-edit.test.tsx --maxWorkers=2` → 10 passed (incl. both ported tests)
- `npx eslint` on the touched file → no new findings (one pre-existing `document` warning)

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/98166 (test-only; its branch contains a merge commit and is far behind main). Credited via Co-authored-by.

Refs #95798

## Auto-merge

Test-only change (no production code touched), classified SAFE by `classify_automerge.py`. Both
ported tests pass on current main, pinning behavior so a regression fails CI. Not
install/update/launch, not system-level, not markdown preprocessing, not auth/wire/config. Reviewed
full head SHA: `fc9ebeeee52922acd674d99c30d205435ccc2829`.

## Summary

#99859: long-lived processes freeze `sys.modules` at boot. After `hermes update`, the code-skew watchdog (979c7baeef) retired stale backends — but only SSH-isolated ones — while Desktop-owned local `hermes serve` backends (which the updater equally never restarts) kept serving stale modules, and only the picker endpoint refused.

Two focused increments:

1. **Widen the self-heal (R1):** `start_code_skew_watchdog` is now also wired for Desktop-owned local backends (`is_desktop_owned_backend()`), not just `ssh_isolated` clients — both have the "updater never restarts me" property; the Desktop's ownership ledger drives the reconnect-respawn on new code.
2. **Centralize the skew refusal (R2):** `POST /api/model/set` and the tui_gateway `model.options` / `model.save_key` JSON-RPCs now refuse with the same "restart required" message `GET /api/model/options` and the gateway `/model` switch already return (new error code 5098, existing i18n key `gateway.model.err_skew`), so no model-mutating path can hand a stale-module string to a provider.

R3 (deleted-profile eviction) is partially covered on main by tombstones (7e34522454); R4 (Bots UI provisioning through `create_profile`) is deliberately out of scope here.

## Test plan

- [x] Green on this branch (rebased): `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_cli/test_code_skew.py tests/tui_gateway/test_model_rpc_skew_guard.py tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_skew_exit.py` → 19 passed, 0 failed (incl. new: stale `model.set` returns 503 and skips the assignment apply; stale `model.options`/`model.save_key` answer 5098 without reaching the payload build; fresh paths unchanged)
- [x] Red equivalents verified against origin/main sources by construction: the guard calls and the 5098 branch do not exist there.

## Limitations

- The watchdog widening trusts `is_desktop_owned_backend()` process identity the same way the existing cron-ticker path does.
- Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/100216 (stale since 2026-09-01, conflicting, predates the watchdog).

items.body:
## Root cause

One typed message could be persisted into two sessions, and a single turn's rows could split across a parent and its continuation session, in two related ways:

1. **Off-turn writes used a stale `session_key` (#123545).** The submit path wrote the user row under `session['session_key']` while the turn's own rows flush under `agent.session_id`, and the two diverge for the whole of a turn that begins after a compression rotation moved the agent onto the continuation (`session_key` is re-anchored only at turn end). One message then landed as user rows in two sessions, and tool rows split across them.
2. **The busy-queue envelope held a dead row id across an in-place compaction (#123675).** `archive_and_compact`'s concurrent-append path deactivates the accept-time row and clones it to a fresh id, but the drain's `deactivate_message` and the merge's `set_user_message_content` addressed the dead original — leaving the queued prompt active twice after the drain, or a text-only merge a silent no-op.

## What changes

Combines #123635 and #123676 (their queue hunks overlap; the two fixes compose — owner-session addressing AND live-row re-resolution):

- `_submit_row_target_key` picks the session the turn will actually write (`agent.session_id` or `session_key`, recorded once on the staged dict) and every off-turn writer is addressed by it: `_write_submit_user_row`, the @-expansion rewrite, the queue merge/drain, `_append_model_switch_marker`, `message.react` newest_role, `session.history`, and the out-of-band probe.
- Model-switch durable rows no longer accumulate across switches: superseded markers are deactivated by `display_kind` (the durable counterpart of the in-memory strip), leaving one live row.
- New `SessionDB.resolve_active_row_id(row_id)`: the row itself while active, else the single clone with same role/content/timestamp, `None` when ambiguous. The drain deactivate and the merge update both re-resolve through it; the envelope's staged row is dropped when no live row remains.
- The transcript read addresses the rotated tip (continuation) after a rotation.

## Acceptance coverage per issue

- #123545: one typed message persists as a user row in exactly one session; a turn's rows never split across parent/child after a rotation; off-turn writers target the live session; model-switch rows don't accumulate — `tests/tui_gateway/test_submit_row_session_target.py` (9 tests) drives the real `publish_compression_child` rotation against a real SessionDB.
- #123675: a queued prompt is active exactly once after an in-place compaction + drain; a text-only merge updates the live clone — `tests/tui_gateway/test_queued_prompt_persistence.py` (2 new tests, real SessionDB + real `_handle_busy_submit`/`_drain_queued_prompt`).

## Tests run

- `HERMES_PYTHON=$RUN/test-venv/bin/python bash scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tui_gateway/test_submit_row_session_target.py tests/tui_gateway/test_queued_prompt_persistence.py` — on main: RED (11 failed across both files); with fix: **18/18 green**.
- Same runner for queue/submit-adjacent suites (`test_tui_gateway_queue_on_busy.py`, `test_submit_time_user_row.py`, `test_model_switch_marker_role.py`, `test_busy_compression_demotion.py`, `test_message_metadata.py`, `test_message_sequence_repair.py`, `test_merged_user_override.py`, `hermes_state/test_message_uid.py`, `agent/test_context_engine_message_uid.py`) — **all green (135 tests)**.
- The one failure seen in the huge `test_tui_gateway_server.py` file (`test_profile_scoped_agent_build_starts_mcp_discovery_in_profile_home`, an `agent_ready` Event 5s wait) reproduces identically on pristine `origin/main` under this machine's load — a pre-existing timing flake, not touched by this diff. This branch's modified test in that file passes.

Fixes #123545
Fixes #123675

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/123635 (Thanks @Halldrix — all 9 commits cherry-picked with authorship kept)
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/123676 (Thanks @Totoro-qaq — the composed commit is co-authored)

Notes for review:
- Composes with (does not collide with) #126999's queued-row restart retire: that PR's `_queued_prompt` display_metadata marker and this PR's owner-key/row-id re-resolution touch adjacent hunks of `_persist_queued_user_row`/`_replace_queued_user_row_for_turn` and should be merged in one coordinated pass.
- The model-switch deactivation interacts with the #65891 in-memory strip as documented in the code comments.

items.body:
## Root cause

Both speech-text normalizers handle Markdown/URLs/symbols but have no pass
for identifier-dense tokens — `apps/desktop/src/lib/speech-text.ts`
(`sanitizeTextForSpeech`) and `tools/tts_text_normalize.py`
(`prepare_spoken_text`). A filename like `peyton-sample-20260922.wav` reaches
the TTS engine verbatim and is read character by character
("peyton dash sample dash two zero two six..."), so clean synthesized audio
sounds corrupted (#119207).

## Fix

One identifier-to-speech pass, mirrored token-for-token in both normalizers:

- `tools/tts_text_normalize.py` — `prune_identifier_tokens_for_tts`,
  wired into `prepare_spoken_text` after the symbols pass (gateway auto-TTS,
  voice-mode streaming, explicit TTS calls).
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/speech-text.ts` — `pruneIdentifierTokens` in
  `sanitizeTextForSpeech`, after code fences/links/URLs/MEDIA: tokens are
  consumed (Read Aloud, auto-speak replies).

Detection: filename-with-extension tokens, hex-hash runs and
`sha256:…`-prefixed digests, UUIDs, dense model/version IDs
(`meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct`, `v2.1.0-beta.3`), and filesystem
paths. Matched tokens become **silence** — never a hardcoded English
placeholder word, per the #86602 lesson (the reply may be in any language).
Ordinary prose, email addresses, dates (`2026/06/02`), ratios (`3:2`) and
short hyphenated words (`COVID-19`, `well-known`) pass verbatim.

Also fixes a pre-existing `smooth_whitespace_for_tts` bug the new corpus
surfaced: `user@example.com` was spoken as "user@example. com" because the
punctuation-spacing pass split any punctuation-followed-by-letter pair; it
now only splits when the punctuation is not glued to a word character.

## Coverage per requirement (#119207)

- Identifier pass in `speech-text.ts`: corpus tests fail on base (filenames
  spoken verbatim), pass with the fix.
- Same identifier policy in `tts_text_normalize.py`: same corpus, pytest.
- Both normalizers agree on the same tokens: one shared corpus
  (`tests/fixtures/identifier_speech_corpus.json`) asserted by both
  `tests/tools/test_tts_identifier_speech.py` and
  `apps/desktop/src/lib/speech-text.identifier-corpus.test.ts`.
- Normal replies no longer sound corrupted: prose around replaced tokens is
  asserted to survive ("Saved ... and ...").

## Checks run

- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tools/test_tts_identifier_speech.py tests/tools/test_tts_text_normalize.py tests/tools/test_tts_prepare_spoken.py` — 25 passed
- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/lib/speech-text.identifier-corpus.test.ts src/lib/speech-text.test.ts` — 36 passed
- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/lib/voice-playback.routing.test.ts src/lib/voice-playback.same-turn.test.ts` — 9 passed (downstream consumers)
- Red on base: corpus test against `origin/main`'s `speech-text.ts` — 2 failed / 2 passed; with the fix, 4 passed.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/119212

Thanks @KoNit-K — the desktop-half normalization approach and its test
corpus (filenames, paths, UUIDs, dense identifiers, ordinary-prose control)
are reused here; this PR extends the policy to the gateway/CLI normalizer
that #119212 left untouched and replaces the spoken labels with silence so
non-English voices are never handed English placeholder words.

Fixes #119207
items.title: fix(tts): silence identifier-dense tokens in both speech normalizers

## Root cause

The original misclassification (a 401 from `POST /api/auth/ws-ticket` reported as "Could not reach the remote Hermes gateway") was the fetch layer never attaching `err.statusCode`; that hole is **already fixed on main** by #95701 (shared `httpStatusError` in `api-transport.ts:183-191`, used by `fetchJson`, `fetchPublicJson`, and the OAuth-session fetch), and `gatewayTicketFailure` (`connection-config.ts`) classifies 401/403 → `needsOauthLogin`/`isReauthRequired` with sign-in copy. #96449/#98656 (the hand-rolled duplicates of that fix) were correctly rejected/withdrawn.

The **still-live defect** (djmango's fleet evidence in #98647): every non-auth mint failure — timeout, `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`, DNS failure, 502 — was wrapped in one undifferentiated sentence (`remote-oauth-ticket.ts:38` passed a static string as `transportMessage`), so ~1,100 log lines across three different upstream causes all read identically and the diagnostic cost stayed high even after the auth/transport split was fixed.

## What changed

- `connection-config.ts` — new exported `gatewayTicketTransportMessage(error)`: names the actual transport failure class in user-facing copy — timeout/unreachable/DNS → "timed out or the host could not be resolved… check your network/VPN path", `ECONNREFUSED` → "connection was refused… the gateway process is likely down", anything else keeps the legacy one-liner.
- `remote-oauth-ticket.ts` — `resolveRemoteOauthTicket` passes `gatewayTicketTransportMessage(error)` instead of the static sentence. Auth classification is untouched: 401/403 still route to the sign-in copy with `needsOauthLogin`/`isReauthRequired` (covered by the existing parametrized test).
- `remote-oauth-ticket.test.ts` — behavioural test: timeout/DNS/refused/ambiguous/500 produce the expected distinct copy, and none of the transport classes ever read as an auth failure (`isReauthRequiredError` false, no `needsOauthLogin` tag).

Refs #98647 (the primary requirement — 401 misreported as "could not reach" — is already met on main by #95701; this PR closes the remaining live sub-defect from the issue thread. #96449 was rejected as a duplicate of #95701, so nothing is superseded here.)

## Tests actually run

- `vitest run --project electron electron/remote-oauth-ticket.test.ts electron/connection-config.test.ts` — pass
- `npm run check:lint` — pass

## Auto-merge

Off (hitl): user-facing error-copy change in the remote-gateway auth path; per the sweep rules for auth-cluster PRs.

items.body:
The desktop main process holds several module-level registries; #58485 reported its V8 heap climbing to the ~4GB ceiling over about an hour of normal use. The renderer-side leak fixes from the #77311 series never touched the main process, and a survey of the registries named in that issue shows most are bounded on current main — but one provably is not.

## Root cause

`remoteOwnerBySessionId` (main.ts, from #85834) memoizes which remote profile owns a session id when a `/api/sessions/:id` read arrives with no profile hint. The memo **only ever inserts**: the 30s TTL makes an entry stale but never removes it, and there is no delete call anywhere. A long-lived main process therefore keeps one Map entry per session id it has ever resolved — and session ids churn through normal use, so the map grows without bound for the life of the process.

## What changes

- The memo moves to `electron/remote-owner-cache.ts` as a pure, injectable cache (`limit` / `now` / `ttlMs`) with FIFO eviction past 500 entries — the same shape as the existing `titleCache` bound.
- `main.ts` wires `remoteOwnerProfileForSession` through it; behaviour (30s TTL, hint-less resolution, sweep across configured remotes) is otherwise unchanged.

Survey of the other registries named in the issue (all bounded on current main, no change needed): `titleCache` (500 FIFO), `hermesLog` (300), `recentFileReveals` (self-pruning), `renderTitleQueue` (drained by 2 concurrent 8s-timeout jobs), `sshConnections` (full lifecycle on teardown/close), and the baseUrl-keyed `gatewayAuthProvidersCache` / `_nativeTokens` (one entry per configured remote). `fetchJson` buffers one response at a time with no retained references after `JSON.parse` — a transient buffer, not retention.

## Acceptance coverage

- "Identify and fix the main-process heap retention" — one provable unbounded path fixed; a full attribution (heap-snapshot diff of the remaining growth) still needs a live long-run session and is not claimed here.
- "Verify the fix on macOS Apple Silicon" — not exercised live in this PR; the fix is platform-neutral main-process logic.
- "Add regression/leak coverage" — unit tests cover the FIFO bound and TTL behaviour.

## Tests

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2 electron/remote-owner-cache.test.ts` → **1 file, 3 passed**.
- Red on main: `remote-owner-cache.ts` does not exist on `origin/main`, so the test file fails to import there.
- `npx tsc -p . --noEmit` (apps/desktop) → clean (exit 0).

## Not exercised live

The 1-hour heap ceiling reproduction needs a long interactive session on macOS; this PR fixes the provable unbounded path and bounds it, but does not claim the whole OOM is closed — the remaining gap (if any) needs the in-band heap sampler the issue's fix plan describes.

Refs #58485

items.body:
## Root cause

Switching models mid-session could drop the next user prompt. The model-switch `[System:...]` marker is persisted as `role=user` on purpose (#48338). When alternation repair merges that marker with the following plain user row, `_merge_consecutive_users` kept the marker's `display_kind` and its `_row_id` — hiding the merged pair from every user-turn index and burying the plain row's durable id. `_resolve_truncate_row_id` read only the repaired durable view, so the absorbed row id could never resolve: `prompt.submit` failed closed with 4018 ("refusing truncation without fallback") and the user's input was silently dropped.

## What changes (combining #94500 + #99955)

- **Merge side (#94500, rebased):** when a display-marker user row merges with a plain user row, the merged pair drops the display classification and carries the plain row's `_row_id` (the marker's own id is retired onto `_absorbed_row_ids`), keeping the pair addressable for rewind/submit. The persist marker is popped — reclassifying stales the row even when the merged bytes reproduce the persisted content. Scope note: when BOTH rows carry `display_kind` (two consecutive markers) the pair keeps the first marker's classification — no plain row is swallowed there.
- **Resolver side (#99955):** `_resolve_truncate_row_id` now loads the durable transcript with `repair_alternation=False` for identity lookups. Repair merges any user;user run (marker runs, or an interrupted turn + resend) into its first row, so the repaired view cannot see absorbed ids; reading the physical rows resolves rows that are genuinely present.

## Acceptance coverage per issue

- Marker-merged rows keep the plain row's addressable identity (`test_repair_marker_user_merge_keeps_plain_row_addressable`, `test_repair_plain_user_then_marker_stays_addressable`).
- `prompt.submit` with `truncate_before_row_id` resolves after a marker merge instead of 4018 (`test_prompt_submit_resolves_row_id_absorbed_into_marker_merge`).
- The broader swallowed-id family — dual markers, and a plain-user merge with NO marker at all — resolves via the un-repaired transcript (`test_prompt_submit_resolves_row_id_swallowed_by_marker_merge`, `test_prompt_submit_resolves_row_id_swallowed_by_plain_user_merge`).

## Tests run

- On `origin/main`: all 5 new tests RED — including the exact 4018 "refusing truncation without fallback" from the report (`pytest ... -q`, 5 failed in 88.42s).
- With this branch: all 5 GREEN (5 passed in 51.55s); full `tests/agent/test_message_sequence_repair.py` suite 61/61 green; the gateway server file's `row_id or truncate or marker or repair or rewind` selection 35/35 green (the 2 selection-mode failures seen once were cross-test pollution in the huge file, reproduced as passing in isolation on both main and this branch).

Fixes #94486

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/94500 (Thanks @liuhao1024 — both commits cherry-picked with authorship kept)
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/99955 (Thanks @zengzheqing — resolver change + tests folded in as a co-authored commit)
Also supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/112908 (heavier resolver-signature variant made redundant by #99955's minimal read-side fix)

Notes for review: the issue's optional fail-open floor (skip truncation and submit as a plain append when the target still doesn't resolve) is deliberately NOT included — heliangwjq offered to PR it separately and it changes the fail-closed contract #82959 established; that is a maintainer call.

items.body:
## What

Adds OpenAI **Ultrafast** as a `/fast` tier for GPT-6 Astra, and prices responses at the tier OpenAI actually served them at.

**WHO / WHEN / WHY:** At DevDay 2026 (2026-09-29) OpenAI launched Ultrafast, a `service_tier: "ultrafast"` request field ([guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/ultrafast-mode), [pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing?latest-pricing=ultrafast), [Codex speed docs](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/speed)).
- It is broadly available for GPT-6 Astra in the API, and in Codex on Pro 500 and Enterprise plans.
- It is billed at **6x Standard**: $60 / $300, cached $6, cache write $75, and 2x/1.5x again above 272K.
- GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast is announced as "coming soon" with no published rate yet.

Hermes had no way to request the tier. If it had been requested through `request_overrides`, cost would have shown Standard, one-sixth of the real bill.

Companion to #128248 (GPT-6.1 Sol). The two PRs don't touch the same files.

## Changes

| Surface | Change |
|---|---|
| `agent/fast_mode.py` | One tier table: `parse_service_tier`, `STATIC_TIERS`, `service_tier_word`. The CLI (`cli_config_load`), gateway (`run_config_loaders`) and TUI (`server._load_service_tier`) config loaders used three hand-copied parsers; all three now call this one. |
| `hermes_cli/models.py`, `models_catalog_static.py` | `model_supports_ultrafast` covers `gpt-6-astra` (vendor prefix and `-900k` alias stripped). `resolve_fast_mode_overrides(tier="ultrafast")` returns `{"service_tier": "ultrafast"}` only for Ultrafast models on the existing first-party route gate (api.openai.com / chatgpt.com). Any other model gets **nothing**, never a silent switch to Priority, which is a different paid tier. |
| CLI / gateway / TUI | `/fast ultrafast` works on all three. The gateway picker shows the choice only when the model supports it; a typed `ultrafast` on an unsupported model is refused with a clear message. Every place that attaches a static tier (`_resolve_turn_agent_config` on CLI and gateway, TUI `config.set fast`, TUI `session.info`) now passes the tier through instead of hard-coding `priority`. The TUI slash command and Desktop settings toggle recognise the new value. |
| Pricing (`usage_pricing`, `turn_usage`, `aux_accounting`, `codex_runtime`) | OpenAI reports the served tier on the response, not inside `usage`. `with_served_service_tier` folds it into `raw_usage`, and the Codex stream assembler now keeps `service_tier` from the terminal frame. A response served at `ultrafast` prices from a published `_OPENAI_ULTRAFAST_PRICING` row. A request that asked for Ultrafast but was served at `default` bills at Standard. A served-ultrafast model with no published rate reports unknown instead of guessing. |
| `locales/*` | 4 new keys in all 17 locales. The option lists in usage/description strings now mention `ultrafast`. |

## Verification

- New `tests/agent/test_openai_ultrafast.py`, 9 relationship tests:
  - all three config loaders agree on every tier word;
  - the tier is gated by model and route (6 Sol gets none; OpenRouter gets none);
  - CLI and gateway turn routes send `ultrafast`;
  - the CLI refuses it on 6 Sol;
  - served ultrafast costs exactly 6x Standard, below and above 272K;
  - requested-but-served-default costs Standard;
  - unpublished models report unknown;
  - the Codex assembler keeps the served tier.
- Mutation checks: removing the pricing branch fails 3 tests; dropping `tier=` at the CLI attach site fails 1; dropping `service_tier` from the assembler fails 1.
- Existing fast-mode, pricing, i18n-parity, codex-transport, TUI-server and gateway suites (26 files): 1150 passed, 39 failed. All 39 fail identically on `upstream/main` (home-IO guard in this local checkout). Ruff is clean, and `tsc --noEmit` + eslint are clean for `ui-tui`.
- **Live, Codex OAuth, real `AIAgent`** with `gpt-6-astra` and `/fast ultrafast` overrides: the wire request carried `service_tier: ultrafast`, the backend accepted it, and it reported **served `default`** because this account isn't on Pro 500. The run returned `PASS`. That's the exact case the served-tier pricing handles.
- **Not live-tested:** a response actually served at `ultrafast` (needs a Pro 500 account or an API key), and the direct API path (no OpenAI key here).

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- **Fast mode (Priority, 2x) is still priced at Standard for OpenAI.** This is pre-existing. The served-tier plumbing here makes adding those rows a data-only change; left out so this PR stays about Ultrafast.
- GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast: add `gpt-6.1-sol` to `_OPENAI_ULTRAFAST_MODELS`, plus its pricing row, once OpenAI publishes the rate.
- The Desktop settings toggle stays binary (fast/normal). It now shows "on" for an ultrafast config instead of "off"; there's no dedicated Desktop control yet.

items.body:
## Root cause

`touchPoolBackend` (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts) refreshes `entry.lastActiveAt` on every renderer keepalive — and `lastActiveAt` is the **only** clock both the idle reaper and LRU eviction read. The keepalive proves the chat is *open*, not that anything *streamed*, so the pinned tier (every backend whose profile chat was ever opened) was exempt from both `maxBackends` and the idle reaper indefinitely: N open chats held N ~120 MB `hermes serve` children until app quit. The reporter's machine: 62 profiles → 126 serve processes / 7.5 GB, all parented to the live Hermes.exe (not orphans) (#105239). A maintainer retest on 2026-09-29 confirmed the defect class persists post-#118246 for what still pools per-profile (isolated mode, unscopable mutating REST requests): "the pinned tier still has no cap in the code".

## What changed

- `touchPoolBackend` stamps `entry.lastStreamedAt` when the renderer reports an active prompt turn (`activeTurn: true` — the existing #104871 turn-lease signal). A turn leasing the backend IS streamed activity; the bare keepalive touch only refreshes `lastActiveAt`, as before.
- `pool-retire.ts`: `PoolRetireEntry` gains `lastStreamedAt`; `retireIdle` accepts an optional idle-eligibility override so the reaper can key on the streamed clock. **Every other safeguard is unchanged**: `activeTurn` veto (never reap mid-stream), identity checks, admission permit, backend proof probe.
- `startPoolIdleReaper` retires a local child whose last streamed turn is older than `POOL_PINNED_IDLE_MS` (default 60 min; `HERMES_DESKTOP_POOL_PINNED_IDLE_MS` override; floor `POOL_LIMITS_MIN.idleMs`) even while keepalive-fresh. Entries without the stamp (spawned before this change, or never streamed) keep the legacy `lastActiveAt` clock — no behavior change for them.
- Teardown stays invisible: re-focusing the chat re-ensures via the idempotent `ensureBackend`/`ensureRegistryBackend` pool-entry reuse (the issue's requirement 3, already met on main).

This implements the reporter's option 2 (pinned idle TTL keyed on streamed activity, "reap after 60 min with no streamed token") rather than option 1 (hard `maxPinnedBackends`), because it composes with the existing admission machinery and never kills a backend a user is actively reading/writing toward; overflow LRU-by-`lastStreamedAt` remains possible as a follow-up if fleets still grow.

## Acceptance coverage (#105239)

- "Idle reaper eventually retires a backend whose chat is open but has had no activity for hours" — met: keepalive-fresh + stream-idle > 60 min → retired through the retirer (probe-proven, mid-stream safe).
- "maxBackends (or a second pinned-tier cap) bounds total resident backends" — bounded in time rather than count: the pinned tier now drains to zero within `POOL_PINNED_IDLE_MS` of inactivity instead of persisting until quit. A count-based `maxPinnedBackends` (option 1) is a heavier design choice this PR does not make.
- "Killing hours-idle backends must never be user-observable" — unchanged (idempotent re-ensure) and asserted by the existing pool-retire tests' admission/identity cases.

## Tests

- `npx vitest run --project electron electron/pool-retire.test.ts electron/pool-limits.test.ts electron/pool-stop.test.ts electron/pool-touch-scope.test.ts electron/pool-spawn-coordinator.test.ts` → 41 passed. New case: keepalive-fresh entries with a 2h-stale `lastStreamedAt` retire; 5-min-stale ones do not; a mid-turn entry is vetoed by the retirer even when the override says eligible.
- `npm run check:lint` → exit 0.
- Fail-first: on `origin/main`, `retireIdle` takes no eligibility override and `PoolRetireEntry` has no `lastStreamedAt`, so the new test does not compile/run on base — the regression it pins (pinned tier never reaped) is the base behavior by construction (reaper keys solely on keepalive-refreshed `lastActiveAt`).

Refs #105239 (the memory-footprint half is fixed by the TTL; a count-based pinned cap or rail badge remains open design space)

items.body:
## Root cause

Desktop/TUI `command.dispatch` runs skills through `_dispatch_skill` in `tui_gateway/methods_tools.py`, which built a single-skill invocation from `(name, arg)` with no stacked handling: on `/skill-a /skill-b do XYZ` the extra `/skill-b` token stayed in the prompt as plain instruction text. The CLI (`cli.py`) and the messaging gateway (`gateway/run_inbound.py`) both route through `split_stacked_skill_commands` + `build_stacked_skill_invocation_message`; the TUI gateway had zero references to either, so the Desktop was the only surface without stacked-skill parity (#74705).

## Fix

Inside `_dispatch_skill`, after the `key in cmds` gate, split the remaining leading skill tokens with `split_stacked_skill_commands(arg)` (up to 5, non-skill/repeated tokens stop the stack and stay in the instruction). Extra keys build one `build_stacked_skill_invocation_message` with a loading notice and the `_skill_scaffold_projection` display payload the UIs render; the single-skill fallback now receives the post-split instruction. The current `_dispatch_skill` body shape (`contextlib.suppress` + `_tools_mod` + the `_session_home_scope` bound by `command.dispatch`) is preserved, so the dispatch stays scoped to the session's profile home.

## Coverage

- #74705: stacked `/skill` tokens load every skill over the remaining instruction on Desktop/TUI, with CLI/gateway parity.

## Checks run

- `pytest tests/tui_gateway/test_protocol.py -k stacked` — 2 passed (both new tests fail on `origin/main`: `KeyError: 'notice'` — no stacked expansion on base).
- Red-on-base proven by swapping `origin/main:tui_gateway/methods_tools.py` into the worktree and rerunning the same tests.
- Two new tests use two real skills under a temp `HERMES_HOME` and dispatch through `command.dispatch`, asserting both bodies land in `message`, the typed invocation in `display`, and that an unknown `/token` stays instruction text.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/74876

Thanks @lifeFedorovAlexey — this adapts #74876's approach (same helpers, same split semantics) into the restructured `_dispatch_skill` on current main, which the original diff predated.

Fixes #74705

items.body:
## Root cause

`tui_gateway/slash_worker.py:100` — `/prompt` and `/compose` (and `/blueprint`) park their
composed prompt on the one-shot `_pending_agent_seed`, which only the **interactive REPL
loop** consumes (`cli.py` main loop). The persistent slash worker that Desktop/TUI
`slash.exec` routes these commands to has no REPL loop, so the composed prompt was
silently dropped: `/prompt` on Desktop returned `(no output)` and the user's composed
text vanished (#107800). Worse, `tui_gateway/methods_slash.py:220` registered a live
`prompt` entry that answered with a raw **system-prompt dump** instead of ever composing
— a repurposing a maintainer flagged as deliberate in
[#107800 (comment)](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/107800#issuecomment-),
which this PR removes in favour of the compose flow (no replacement viewer is added;
that trade-off is called out for sign-off).

## What changed

- **`tui_gateway/slash_worker.py`** — `_run` keeps its existing `str` return; after each
  command it harvests `cli._pending_agent_seed` (resetting it, keeping the one-shot
  contract) onto `cli._harvested_seed`, cleared at the top of every run so a stale seed
  can never re-send. `main()` replies with the output plus a `seed` field.
- **`tui_gateway/server.py`** — `_SlashWorker.run` keeps its existing `str` return; the
  seed rides back on the reply's `seed` field and is retrieved via `pop_seed()` (old
  workers that don't reply a seed get `""` — no break).
- **`tui_gateway/methods_tools.py`** — after `worker.run(cmd)`, `slash.exec` pops the
  seed; when the worker harvested one it returns `{"type": "send", "message": seed}` — a
  dispatch both clients already handle
  (`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/slash.ts:307`,
  `ui-tui/src/app/createSlashHandler.ts:157`).
- **`tui_gateway/methods_slash.py`** — removed the live system-prompt viewer:
  `_format_live_prompt_output`, the `"prompt"` entry in `_LIVE_SLASH_OUTPUT`,
  `_mirror_prompt`, and `"prompt"` from `_MUTATES_WHILE_RUNNING`. `/prompt` in the CLI
  is compose-only (`hermes_cli/commands.py:95`), so the viewer answered a question the
  command no longer asks, and it shadowed the compose flow from the gateway.
- **`hermes_cli/cli_commands_mixin.py`** — `_compose_in_editor` no longer falls back to
  `shell=True` with the raw `$EDITOR` unquoted when the argv invocation fails (#81364).
  An unargv-splittable (`ValueError`) or unrunnable (`OSError`) editor, or a nonzero
  editor exit (which may leave abandoned buffer text), cancels the compose cleanly.

The seed is carried **out of band** rather than changing `_run`/`run` to a dict/tuple:
both string return shapes are contracts main's callers and test fakes rely on, and the
`{type: "send"}` dispatch is an existing `SlashExecResult` shape.

Two tests on main asserted the live `/prompt` viewer this PR intentionally removes and
were updated minimally (the PR's intentional behavior change, per its own removal of
the viewer): `test_slash_exec_r7_read_commands_use_metadata_mirror_flag_on` drops its
`prompt` case, and `test_mirror_slash_side_effects_rejects_mutating_commands_while_running`
drops its `/prompt` row (`/prompt` no longer mirrors or mutates live agent state — it is
compose-only now).

No desktop/TUI client change is needed — both already handle `{type: "send"}`.
`/refine` live routing is **deliberately not in this PR**: it overlaps
[#127241](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/127241), which already implements it.

## Known limitation (unchanged by this PR)

The slash worker is headless (pipes, no tty), so terminal `$EDITOR`s (vim/nano) fail
there and the compose is cancelled with the existing `editor_failed` message; GUI
editors (`code --wait`) work. Same as before the fix, except the failure is now reported
instead of silently dropping the prompt.

## Acceptance coverage

- Worker harvests `_pending_agent_seed` and resets it (one-shot preserved)
- `slash.exec` with a seeded worker → `{"type": "send", "message": <seed>}`; plain
  output path unchanged (no `type` key, mirrors/warnings intact)
- Compose cancels on: unargv-splittable editor, unrunnable editor, nonzero editor exit —
  never through a shell
- Empty-buffer cancel and header-stripping behaviour preserved

## Tests run (all green)

- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tui_gateway/test_slash_prompt_compose_seed.py` — new
  (5 tests), proven RED on base first
- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_cli/test_prompt_compose_command.py` — extended
  (2 new tests), proven RED on base first
- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tui_gateway/test_slash_worker_skill_refuse.py`,
  `test_slash_worker_ansi.py`, `test_slash_worker_provider.py`, `test_protocol.py` —
  all pass **unmodified from main** (the string contracts are preserved)
- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py -k "slash_exec_r7_read_commands_use_metadata_mirror_flag_on or mirror_slash_side_effects_rejects_mutating_commands_while_running or slash_exec_concurrent_first_use_spawns_single_worker"`
- `tests/tui_gateway/test_slash_review_owner.py`, `tests/tui_gateway/test_slash_worker_sys_path.py`,
  `tests/tui_gateway/test_slash_worker_mcp_discovery.py`
- 3 pre-existing failures in `tests/agent/test_background_review.py`
  (`test_live_turn_waits_for_review_exit…`, `…acknowledgement_times_out`,
  `test_stale_review_cleanup…`) reproduce identically on clean `origin/main` — timing-sensitive
  live-turn tests unrelated to this diff (verified on a separate clean worktree).

## Supersedes

- [#107803](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/107803) (KoNit-K) — same
  seed-harvest + `{type:"send"}` routing, adapted to current main
- [#115149](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/115149) (JPeetz) — same
  approach; hunks adapted and verified against current file shapes
- [#81366](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/81366) (Adolanium) — the
  `$EDITOR` shell-fallback removal + tests, applied nearly verbatim

Credit: `@KoNit-K`, `@JPeetz`, `@Adolanium` (Co-authored-by trailers on the respective
commits, with their actual commit emails).

Fixes #107800
Fixes #81364

items.body:
## Root cause

`cli.py:211` — `from prompt_toolkit.patch_stdout import patch_stdout` was the one
unguarded top-level prompt_toolkit import (its neighbours at 213 and 219 already use
try/except, so the guard was the intended pattern). A partial/broken prompt_toolkit
install — e.g. the reporter's stale venv that has the package but not every submodule —
crashed the import: `ModuleNotFoundError`/`ImportError` at import time, taking down
`hermes` and every `tui_gateway.slash_worker` child (which imports `cli` at module
scope, `tui_gateway/slash_worker.py:27`), i.e. every gateway session (#96075).

## What changed

`cli.py` — the import is guarded with an `ImportError` fallback to
`contextlib.nullcontext as patch_stdout`. The only use site is
`with patch_stdout():` (cli.py:1476), a drop-in for a null context manager, so the
interactive path is unchanged when prompt_toolkit is healthy. This mirrors the in-repo
precedent in `agent/display.py:897` (guarded `from prompt_toolkit.patch_stdout import
StdoutProxy`).

Note the CLI's TUI mixins still import prompt_toolkit unguarded; a *fully* missing
prompt_toolkit therefore still fails on the interactive path — by design, since the
reporter's case (and the routing fix plan) is the *partial* install, where only the
fragile submodule import needed the guard to keep headless paths (slash worker) alive.

## Acceptance coverage

- `import cli` succeeds with a `sys.meta_path` blocker raising ImportError only for
  `prompt_toolkit.patch_stdout`
- `cli.patch_stdout is contextlib.nullcontext` and `cli.HermesCLI` stays callable under
  the blocker
- (Proven RED on base: both tests fail with the import error before the fix.)

## Tests run (all green)

- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_import_without_patch_stdout.py`
  — new (2 subprocess tests), proven RED on base first
- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_cli/test_prompt_compose_command.py` — smoke,
  no regression
- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tui_gateway/test_slash_worker_sys_path.py` — the
  slash-worker import-chain path, no regression

## Auto-merge

Backend import-robustness only: no visible UI change, no install/update/launch path,
no system-level behaviour, no markdown/transcript processing, no auth/secrets/config
keys. The change is a two-line guarded import with a nullcontext fallback whose only
use site is a context manager. Reviewed full head SHA:
`3c8663f4f2396c6e1d22243184d02e1521c0517e` (`bb/cli-guard-prompt-toolkit-import`).

Fixes #96075

items.body:
## Root cause

`get_skill_commands()` memoized exactly ONE `(platform, home, project)` identity (`agent/skill_commands.py`). In the Desktop `hermes serve` process the resolved identity is not stable across the ~5s `commands.catalog` polls (profile-home overrides bound per request, per-session project roots), so the freshness check missed on every poll and the full skills-dir rescan (read + parse of every SKILL.md) fired ~3x/5s, re-logging the `skill_command_collision_note` warning each time — the storm in #104849. Two `tui_gateway` call sites (`_catalog_skills`, `_dispatch_skill`) made it worse by calling `scan_skill_commands()` directly, bypassing any cache.

## Fix

Multi-slot cache `_skill_commands_by_key` keyed by the full 3-tuple `(platform, home, project)` identity. Each distinct identity is scanned once and memoized; `reload_skills()` clears every slot (a skill edit can affect any identity); publication/lookup stay under `_publish_lock` with the scan outside it (#14536, #74574). The `tui_gateway` call sites now go through `get_skill_commands()`.

The project dimension is load-bearing: keying on `(platform, home)` alone (as the earlier draft of this change did) would drop #114359's per-session project-skill isolation — a session in repo B would be served repo A's project skills after a cache hit. The tests pin that.

## Coverage

- #104849: no rescan when identity flaps between polls; each identity scanned exactly once.
- #14536 / #88023 (kept): distinct platform/home identities each get their own slot and view.
- #114359 (kept): project root is a third key dimension — repo A and repo B views stay isolated.
- reload: `reload_skills()` drops every slot; the next lookup per identity rescans.

## Checks run

- `pytest tests/agent/test_skill_cache_thrash_104849.py` — 4 passed; all 4 fail on `origin/main` (single-slot cache).
- `pytest tests/agent/test_skill_commands.py` — 24 passed, 1 skipped.
- `pytest tests/agent/test_skill_commands_reload.py tests/agent/test_skill_invocation_description.py` — green.
- `pytest tests/gateway/test_stacked_skill_platform_disabled.py tests/hermes_cli/test_session_skill_previews.py tests/openviking_plugin/test_openviking.py` — 52 passed.
- `pytest tests/gateway/test_webhook_adapter.py tests/agent/test_prompt_cache_boundary.py` — 64 passed.
- `pytest tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py -k "skills or command_dispatch or reload or project"` — 21 passed.
- `pytest tests/tui_gateway/test_protocol.py` (full file) — 72 passed.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/104864

## Root cause

Desktop's `restoreToMessage` had no stale-target recovery: on a 4018 ("target user message is no longer in session history") it rolled back optimistic state and rethrew, while `editMessage` retries once after resuming the stored session. The report names two surfaces: the primary chat and the session-tile restore verb.

## What changes

- **#107597 (rebased onto current main, authorship kept):** ports the exact edit retry into the primary chat's `restoreToMessage` — `isStaleTargetError` → `resumeStoredSession` → recompute `planRestore` → one retry with the refreshed row id. The shared `isStaleTargetError` predicate moves to module scope (it was inlined in edit's closure) and is re-exported.
- **New — the tile surface the report names (~line 586 of `session-tile-actions.ts`):** the tile's `restoreToMessage` gains the same recovery. A tile has no `resumeStoredSession`; its transcript refresher is the delegate's `resumeTile(storedId, {refreshTranscript: true})`, so the retry refreshes the transcript through that, rebinds the runtime id if resume recovered it, recomputes `planRestore` against fresh messages, and retries once. On a failed retry it falls through to the existing rollback — the optimistic truncation never survives.

## Acceptance coverage per issue

- Primary chat: restore retries once with the refreshed row id (2 submits; second carries `truncate_before_row_id: 501`) — the PR's test, kept.
- Session tile: the same assertion on the tile surface, with `resumeTile` mocked as the transcript refresher — `re-hydrates the tile transcript and retries once when restore hits a stale durable target`.
- The plain-resubmit fallback and the 4018 payload split remain optional/unimplemented (per the verdict's optional requirements).

## Tests run

- On `origin/main`: both new tests RED (1 failed each in isolated vitest runs, `/tmp/b7-c3-red1.log`, `/tmp/b7-c3-red2.log`).
- With this branch: tile file 7/7 green (16.5s), primary-chat `restore` selection 9/9 green (19.4s), `tsc -p . --noEmit` exit 0.

Fixes #107593

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/107597 (Thanks @mahgoub — your commit is cherry-picked with authorship kept; the tile-surface coverage is the addition the review asked for)

Note: distinct root cause from #94486 (client-side missing retry vs merge burying ids); both surface as 4018 and compose — if #94486's fix lands first, some triggers here disappear, but optimistic-never-persisted and session.branch remap targets remain and still need this retry.

items.body:
## Root cause

Two contributing sites, one symptom (#76902): in a packaged Desktop build with no user-configured default project dir, `resolveHermesCwd()` (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts) falls through every candidate to `app.getPath('home')`, so the backend spawns with cwd and `TERMINAL_CWD` pinned to `$HOME`. `SubdirectoryHintTracker` then takes home as its `working_dir`, and `_within_working_dir`'s `is_relative_to(home)` is vacuously true for the entire home subtree — any `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `.cursorrules` under `~` gets injected into tool results on first touch (worst case: a 5-level ancestor walk from any tool call touching `~/.hermes/skills/...` picks up both `~/.hermes/AGENTS.md` and the ~74 KB install-tree contributor guide).

## Fix

- `agent/subdirectory_hints.py`: a home (or container-home) working dir is treated as a fallback, not a project. `check_tool_call` and `_load_hints_for_directory` both refuse to run hint discovery while the working dir is home-like; a new `rebind_working_dir()` re-anchors discovery when the session adopts a real workspace.
- `tui_gateway/session_workdir.py`: `_register_session_cwd` (the hook that already runs on every workspace move, workspace switch and settled `cd`) calls `rebind_working_dir()` on the live agent's tracker — so a Desktop session that picks or settles into a project gets first-visit hints for that project, scoped to it. No prompt/system-prompt state changes.
- `agent/agent_init.py`: the tracker is seeded from the session's own `session_cwd` (explicit workspace) before falling back to the launch `TERMINAL_CWD`, so an agent built for a workspace session is anchored correctly from the start.
- `agent/search_policy.py`: `.archive` joins the shared prune set (retired-skill trees under `~/.hermes/skills/.archive/` hold stale `AGENTS.md` copies); `.venv`/`.next`/`.cache` were already excluded.

A home-as-workspace session keeps the context files the startup path already loads for home itself; only the home-wide *subtree* scan is gone.

## Coverage per issue

- #76902: home-cwd injection (both requirements — no home subtree scan, discovery still works for a real project workspace). Covered by 5 new tests.
- #75839 (install-tree AGENTS.md via the lazy hint path): the shared home guard covers its repro shape — a home-rooted working dir never walks into `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/` anymore. Referenced, not closed: its report also covers non-home cwd shapes this PR does not address.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/77145 — Thanks @Sahil-SS9. Same guard idea and direction; that diff was stale against the current class shape (pre-`enabled=` signature, unrelated whitespace churn) and only guarded `check_tool_call`. This PR rebases the guard onto the current class, covers `_load_hints_for_directory` too, and adds the rebind so adopting a workspace restores discovery.
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/75922 — Thanks @dplush. That PR targeted the narrower install-tree sibling; its test-only commits informed the platform-parametrized shape here, and the shared home guard covers its repro.

## Checks run

- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/agent/test_subdirectory_hints.py` — 72 passed, 0 failed.
- Same file on unpatched `main` with the new tests — 4 of the new tests fail (home guard + rebind), proving red on base.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/agent/test_runtime_cwd.py tests/tui_gateway/test_container_backend_workdir.py` — 12 passed (cwd resolution + workdir neighbors unchanged).
- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/agent/test_meta_agent_init.py` — 7 passed (agent init path unchanged).
- `ruff check` on all touched files — clean.

Fixes #76902

items.body:
## Root cause

When Hermes quits with the pet overlay popped out, the main process tears the overlay window down and the overlay's `'closed'` handler unconditionally sends `{ type: 'pop-in' }` to the main renderer (`apps/desktop/electron/main.ts`, `spawnPetOverlayWindow`'s closed handler). The renderer's `onControl('pop-in')` branch runs `popInPet()`, which persists `$petOverlayActive=false` (`apps/desktop/src/store/pet-overlay.ts`). On the next boot `restorePetOverlay()` gates on `$petOverlayActive` and skips restoration — so the pet silently reverts to in-window after every clean quit, exactly as reported in #55920.

The handler's comment even said "Harmless echo when we're the ones who closed it" — it isn't harmless: it wipes the persisted popped-out state.

## What changed

- `apps/desktop/electron/pet-overlay.ts`: new pure predicate `shouldPopInOnOverlayClosed({ appQuitting, mainWindowAlive })` — the overlay close echo is correct for a user-initiated close (⌘W on the overlay), and must be suppressed during app quit.
- `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts`:
  - a module-level `appQuitting` latch, deliberately **not** `isQuittingForHandoff` (that flag is hand-off-specific and resets when a hand-off is aborted; a quit latch must never reset);
  - latched at the very top of `before-quit`, before any teardown calls `closePetOverlay()`;
  - latched on the **non-macOS primary-window `close`** path — on Windows/Linux closing the primary window IS quitting (`window-all-closed` → `app.quit()`), and `mainWindow`'s `'closed'` handler calls `closePetOverlay()` there too;
  - the overlay `'closed'` handler now consults the predicate instead of sending pop-in unconditionally.
- Renderer needs no change: `restorePetOverlay()` already restores when `$petOverlayActive` survives the quit.

## Acceptance coverage

- Quit with the pet popped out (any platform, any quit route: menu quit, ⌘Q/Cmd-Q, Windows/Linux primary-window close) → next boot restores the overlay at its remembered position.
- User-initiated overlay close (⌘W / overlay close) while the app stays alive → pet still pops back in.

## Tests

- RED on base: the three new tests in `electron/pet-overlay.test.ts` fail on `origin/main` (`shouldPopInOnOverlayClosed` does not exist — 3 failed / 15 passed).
- GREEN with the fix: `npx vitest run electron/pet-overlay.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` → 18/18 passed.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.electron.json` → 0 errors.
- `npx eslint electron/pet-overlay.ts electron/pet-overlay.test.ts` → clean.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/55934 (liuhao1024) — same guard, against the since-deleted `main.cjs`; missed the non-macOS primary-window-close quit path.
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/55968 — narrower duplicate of the above, closed unmerged.
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/58112 (yoma) — best reference (also latched the non-macOS primary-window close); also targeted `main.cjs`. Its mechanism and the non-macOS path are ported here.

Credit: liuhao1024 <sunsky.lau@gmail.com>, yoma <yingwaizhiying@gmail.com> (Co-authored-by on the commit).

Fixes #55920


## Screenshots

None, deliberately: the change is main-process quit/relaunch lifecycle (a `before-quit` latch and a window `'closed'` handler), not a renderable component state — a component harness cannot exercise an app quit and restart. The visible effect (the overlay restoring popped-out on the next launch) needs a real quit/restart cycle on a desktop build.

items.body:
## Root cause

On Windows, `BrowserWindow.show()` and `.focus()` both seize the OS foreground. `focusWindow()` in `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` did `show()` + an unconditional `focus()`, and two more call sites did the same (`sendOpenUpdatesRequested`, the deep-link delivery path). Any ambient IPC reaching one of these paths while Hermes streams in the background forcibly dismissed other apps' native dialogs — the reported Notepad save-confirmation repro in #83998.

## What changed

- New pure policy module `apps/desktop/electron/window-focus-policy.ts`:
  - `revealAction(visible)` → a hidden window is revealed with `showInactive()`, never `show()`.
  - `shouldFocusToTakeKeyboard({ isFocused })` → `.focus()` is only called when the window does not already have focus; a redundant `focus()` still pumps `SetForegroundWindow` on Windows.
- `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts`:
  - `focusWindow()` now restores/minimizes as before, then reveals with `showInactive()` and guards `focus()` with `isFocused()` — this covers every ambient raise routed through it (tray restore, notification click, second-instance, dock/taskbar activate).
  - `sendOpenUpdatesRequested()` and the deep-link delivery path get the same guarded pattern.
- User-intentional raises keep `show()` + `focus()`: pet overlay double-click / mail-icon clicks (`pet-overlay-ipc.ts`), HUD and Quick Entry reveals — a click is consent, and the HUD/Quick Entry surfaces exist to take the keyboard.

`wireWindowReveal`'s default reveal (`show()`) is unchanged: it runs at first paint of a window the app is launching, where taking foreground is correct behavior.

## Acceptance coverage

- During streaming on Windows, an ambient raise (tray click, notification, second instance) brings Hermes up without dismissing another app's native dialog.
- The window still actually receives focus when the user asks for it (it was not focused before).

## Tests

- RED on base: `electron/window-focus-policy.test.ts` fails on `origin/main` (module missing — 1 failed file, no tests runnable).
- GREEN with the fix: `npx vitest run electron/window-focus-policy.test.ts electron/window-reveal.test.ts electron/main-window-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` → 22/22 passed.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.electron.json` → 0 errors.
- `npx eslint electron/main.ts electron/window-focus-policy.ts electron/window-focus-policy.test.ts` → clean.

## Platform note

Behavior is Windows-specific in effect (foreground seizure) but the change is platform-neutral main-process logic. No Windows machine was available to run the Notepad dialog repro; the invariant tests pin the policy the call sites now follow. #86045 (macOS computer_use capture focus steal) is a different platform and mechanism and is not addressed here.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/84026 (Jakub Wolniewicz / frizikk) — renderer-side focus guard only; it explicitly left the main-process focus paths unchanged, which is where this fix lands. Credit: Co-authored-by on the commit.

Fixes #83998


## Screenshots

None: this is a Windows-foreground (OS-level `SetForegroundWindow`) behavior change — there is no renderable component state, and the bug's repro (a native Notepad save dialog surviving an ambient raise during streaming) can only be exercised on a Windows host, which was not available.

items.body:
## Root cause

Gateway turns reach the agent enriched with skill payloads and sender metadata. The original Desktop/ACP report (preview + title showing the scaffold) was fixed read-time by merged #71843 — but only for the `[IMPORTANT: The user has invoked the "X" skill…` scaffold. The **gateway auto-load path** builds a different header (`[IMPORTANT: The "X" skill is auto-loaded. Follow its instructions for this session.]` at `gateway/run_turn.py` `_hmwa_auto_load_skills`) that `describe_skill_invocation` did not recognize: auto-load sessions got scaffold-driven preview text, and the titler (whose message-scan fallback still reads the enriched turn) titled from the skill body instead of the request (#48359).

## Fix (two commits)

1. **Title input** (from #106727, cherry-picked with authorship preserved): the gateway captures `event.text` BEFORE the auto-load/sender enrichment and passes it as a turn-local `title_user_message` through `TurnContext` → the conversation prologue → `_maybe_title_session_at_turn_start`, overriding the message scan. Only the titler reads it — the main model, persisted history and relay metadata still receive the full enriched message. An explicit empty override suppresses titling for that turn; `None` keeps the existing fallback; the override cannot enable titling for cron/subagent runs.

2. **Read-time preview/retitle** (new): `describe_skill_invocation` recognizes the auto-load header and renders the typed request. The payload is located structurally: `_build_skill_message` always ends with the skill-directory footer, so the LAST footer sentence marks where the user's text begins — a header quoted inside a skill body example cannot end the payload early. Bare auto-loads render `/skill`. Listing queries extend the scaffold `LIKE` predicate to the auto-load prefix (long rows get the same head+tail excerpt window), and `hermes sessions retitle-skills` (`list_skill_scaffolded_sessions`) now finds auto-load sessions too.

## Coverage

- #48359 (title): gateway titles from the pre-enrichment request; the model still sees the enriched turn; the cached agent never reuses a previous turn's override.
- #48359 (preview/retitle): auto-load sessions preview as the typed request (short and long/excerpt-window rows), bodies quoting the header don't fool the describer, bare auto-loads render `/skill`, and the retitle lookup includes them.

## Checks run

- `pytest tests/gateway/test_auto_skill_title_input.py tests/agent/test_title_input.py` — 18 passed (all 18 fail on `origin/main` with the gateway/turn_context/runner files reverted).
- `pytest tests/agent/test_skill_invocation_description.py` — 15 passed (7 new auto-load tests fail on `origin/main`).
- `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_session_skill_previews.py` — 13 passed (new auto-load lookup test fails on `origin/main`).
- `pytest tests/agent/test_title_generator.py` — 96 passed.
- `pytest tests/gateway/test_message_timestamps.py tests/gateway/test_discord_triggering_note_persistence.py tests/gateway/test_gateway_history_persistence_stamp.py` — 5 passed.
- Scaffold builders used in tests are the real `_load_skill_payload`/`_build_skill_message`, matching `_hmwa_auto_load_skills` byte-for-byte.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/106727

Thanks @doryani-ai — commit 1 is #106727's own work (already rebased by its author onto 2026-09-28 main); commit 2 extends the same fix to the preview/retitle surfaces that its review flagged as still broken.

Fixes #48359

## What does this PR do?

A signed release tag is read through its JSON record again, so stable admission, ordered reconciliation and tagless build receipts accept the tags they create instead of refusing them.

**Root cause:** git keeps an annotated tag's signature *inside* the message body, so `git tag -l --format=%(contents)` returns the record followed by an armored signature block and `json.loads` of the whole message raises `Extra data: line 2 column 1` at the armor's first byte — every claim tag, final receipt and build receipt is created on a host whose git signs tags.

## Related Issue

No issue — reported directly.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `scripts/releases/versioning.py`: new `tag_record(raw)` — the one reader of a tag's JSON record, taking the text before the signature armor. An unsigned tag and a detached signature are unchanged.
- `scripts/releases/stable.py`: all four `%(contents)` reads (claim metadata, final receipt, final-tag collision check, metadata verify) go through it; `_claim_metadata` still maps unreadable metadata to "Stable claim metadata is invalid".
- `scripts/releases/sequencer.py`: the claim record read in `_tag_message`, so reconciliation stops refusing `rc.<N>-vX.Y.Z metadata is invalid`.
- `scripts/releases/commit_build.py`: the build-receipt verify. Imported inside the function so its module surface stays stdlib-only — the isolated checkout-admission step runs it from a copy of `scripts/releases` alone.
- Tests: `tag_record`'s contract (SSH and OpenPGP armor, and a non-record still refused); a signed claim tag read through the job's own `git tag -l --format=%(contents)` and the real claim reader; the three `%(contents)` reads inside `test_stable_release.py`, the two in `test_release_entrypoint.py` and one each in the two CI test files now use the shared reader; and the one fixture that wants a plain final tag says `-c tag.gpgSign=false` explicitly.

## How to Test

1. `python -m scripts.releases.sequencer` on a repository whose claim tags are signed (a checkout with `tag.gpgSign=true` and an SSH or OpenPGP signing key).
2. `python -m scripts.releases.stable admit` from that claim ref.
3. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/scripts/test_stable_release.py tests/scripts/test_release_entrypoint.py tests/scripts/test_stable_admission.py tests/scripts/test_release_version_from_ref.py tests/scripts/test_release_sequencer.py tests/scripts/test_release_build_commit.py tests/scripts/test_commit_stamp_identity.py tests/ci/test_channel_build_publication.py tests/ci/test_desktop_release_commit_admission.py`

**Live repro:** read `rc.19-v0.21.5` exactly as the job does — `git tag -l rc.19-v0.21.5 --format=%(contents)` returns the 177-character record, `\n`, then `-----BEGIN SSH SIGNATURE-----`; `json.loads` of that text raises `Extra data: line 2 column 1 (char 178)`, matching the CI traceback byte for byte.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `json.loads` of the raw `%(contents)` | `JSONDecodeError: Extra data: line 2 column 1 (char 178)` | unchanged — the raw message really does carry the armor |
| `stable admit` / `sequencer` on that tag | `ValueError: Stable claim metadata is invalid` / `rc.19-v0.21.5 metadata is invalid` | record parsed, admission and reconciliation proceed |
| `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/scripts/test_stable_release.py tests/scripts/test_release_entrypoint.py` on a host whose git signs tags | 6 failed | 64 passed, 0 failed |
| that entrypoint file's wall time | 248s (the tag creation stalls on the signing path) | 5.2s |
| the 9 release/CI test files above | 6 failed | 144 passed, 0 failed |

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(release):`)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) — no open fix for tag message parsing
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] `scripts/run_tests.sh` on the release test surface: 144 passed, 0 failed; `ruff check`, `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all`, `scripts/check_subprocess_stdin.py` and `git diff --check` clean. Full suite left to CI.
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (proven red on base, then green)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: NixOS (Linux), on a checkout whose git signs tags (`tag.gpgSign=true`, `gpg.format=ssh`)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Documentation: N/A — no user-visible behaviour, command or config key changes; the tag grammar in `scripts/releases/versioning.py`'s module docstring is unchanged
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example`: N/A
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md`: N/A
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered: the change is host-agnostic Python; it removes an assumption (an unsigned tag message) rather than adding one, and Windows/macOS release jobs read the same refs
- [x] Tool descriptions/schemas: N/A

## Infographic

![release tags read through their record](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aac66c5/YWldA6u8HPJ75_3-z-rpK_UYQ3B0JS.png)

items.body:
## Root cause

`_build_uvicorn_server` (`hermes_cli/web_server.py`) never set `timeout_graceful_shutdown`, so uvicorn's default (`None`) makes `Server.shutdown()` wait forever on a lingering ASGI task. A single SIGTERM — all Electron Desktop sends before its ~5s SIGKILL escalation — therefore hangs a mid-turn backend and the process is orphaned past the kill budget (#76244 forensics: 0 listening sockets, worker threads parked in `queue.get()`, event loop never returning).

## What changes

- `hermes_cli/web_server.py`: `uvicorn.Config(...)` gains `timeout_graceful_shutdown=3` in `_build_uvicorn_server` — under the desktop's ~5s SIGKILL budget, leaving room for lifespan shutdown (`cron_stop` etc.) before the kill arrives.
- `tests/test_web_server.py`: two regression tests: (1) the configured bound is positive and under the kill budget; (2) behavior-level: with the production Config kwargs and a real `uvicorn.Server`, a never-completing ASGI task must not hang `Server.shutdown()` — the grace window is honoured, the lingerer is cancelled, and shutdown returns (closes the weakness that got the earlier #76265 closed).
- Test hardening over the original PR (same content rebased onto current main): uvicorn 0.41's `shutdown()` requests `task.cancel()` on grace-timeout expiry, but the `CancelledError` is only delivered on the lingerer's next loop pass — asserting `task.cancelled()` immediately after `shutdown()` returns flaked. The test now awaits the lingerer once (suppressing `CancelledError`) so the assertion checks the cancellation that actually landed. No production-code change beyond the original.

## Acceptance coverage

- #76244: a single SIGTERM terminates the serve backend within the ~5s desktop SIGKILL budget — covered by both tests (bound < 5, real `Server.shutdown()` bounded).
- Lifespan shutdown and `cron_stop.set()` still run — the bound only caps the task wait; lifespan shutdown proceeds after it (uvicorn runs `lifespan.shutdown()` after the task wait; not skipped).
- Multi-backend quits: each backend now terminates within its budget, so N stubborn backends are all reaped; desktop quit-budget scaling (Goonik's N×5s) remains a separate desktop-side follow-up outside this fix.

## Tests run

- `HERMES_PYTHON=<test-venv> bash scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_ws_ping.py` (this branch, rebased onto current main): **7 passed, 3 skipped** (skips are Windows-only).
- Same file on `origin/main` (PR test content only): **5 passed, 2 failed** — both new tests fail pre-fix (`graceful shutdown must be bounded (#76244)`), i.e. they genuinely pin the fix.
- Pre-existing unrelated failures: `tests/hermes_state/test_cross_vm_fs_wal_refusal.py` fails identically on main (Linux-lane mountinfo tests on a darwin host) — untouched by this PR.

Fixes #76244
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/105319 (rebased onto current main; the fork's branch could not be updated further — thanks @liuhao1024 for the original fix and tests, preserved here with authorship intact)
Co-authored-by: liuhao1024 <sunsky.lau@gmail.com>

items.body:
## Root cause

The NVIDIA EGL fallback added for the #40077 crash and bounded to the `{580}` driver series by #123213 gates on the driver version — but the same driver point release breaks one host and not another. 580.178.04 kills the GPU process on hosts where NVIDIA drives the display (#40077, #124032), and renders fine on hybrid hosts whose session EGL lands on the iGPU (#124255's reporter; psukez on #123203). Every healthy 580 host was forced onto all-CPU SwiftShader compositing, converting a known Chromium stuck-Button-observer leak (~0 cost with GPU compositing) into a silent 4–9 core CPU burn.

## What changed

`apps/desktop/electron/linux-nvidia-egl-fallback.ts` + `main.ts` — the gate is now **behavioral** (option A from the #124255 decision-prep comment), keeping the same fallback remedy:

- A Linux + NVIDIA host boots with **hardware GL** and writes a `booting` marker (`nvidia-egl-fallback.json`, keyed on app version + full driver version).
- A `child-process-gone` event for the GPU process **before the first window is revealed** — reasons `crashed` / `launch-failure` / `killed` (#40077's GPU process died to Chromium's health-check SIGTERM, exit_code=15) — flips the marker to sticky `fallback` and relaunches once with `--use-angle=swiftshader`.
- A healthy first-window reveal marks `ok`; future launches trust hardware GL.
- An app **or driver** update re-probes once instead of degrading forever.
- A leftover `booting` marker (Chromium's "GPU process isn't usable" FATAL abort winning the race against our handler) engages the fallback on the next launch.
- `HERMES_DESKTOP_NVIDIA_SWIFTSHADER=1|0` still forces on/off; `HERMES_DESKTOP_DISABLE_GPU=0` still wins; remote-display / WSLg exclusions unchanged. Never `disableHardwareAcceleration()` (SIGKILLs the renderer on 580 + Electron 40, #40119).

The old `NVIDIA_BROKEN_EGL_MAJORS` series set is gone. Healthy 580 hosts get hardware rendering back; broken ones still reach the desktop in at most one extra restart per app/driver update.

## Acceptance coverage

- The two healthy 580 hosts of record (#124255 reporter, psukez on #123203) boot with hardware GL and no marker → no SwiftShader, no burn.
- A broken 580 host: first launch dies at the GPU probe → one relaunch reaches the desktop on SwiftShader; later launches go straight to SwiftShader until app or driver updates.
- `killed` GPU deaths (the #40077 signature) are witnessed, not ignored.

## Tests

- RED on base: the rewritten `electron/linux-nvidia-egl-fallback.test.ts` fails against `origin/main`'s series-gate module — 20 failed / 2 passed.
- GREEN with the fix: `npx vitest run electron/linux-nvidia-egl-fallback.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` → 22/22 passed.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.electron.json` → 0 errors.
- `npx eslint electron/linux-nvidia-egl-fallback.ts electron/linux-nvidia-egl-fallback.test.ts electron/main.ts` → clean.

## Validation limits

No Linux + NVIDIA host was available on this runner (CI has no NVIDIA runners either), so the relaunch/marker lifecycle is unit-proven but not device-proven. The issue's thread names the needed device validation: one broken host (#124032 on Electron 40) to prove the relaunch engages, one healthy host (this issue's reporter) to prove hardware GL survives. Marker-file lifecycle deliberately mirrors the shape of the Windows sandbox fallback and the open Mesa probe (#124898) so a future consolidation has two identical modules to merge.

## Related, deliberately not included

- #123598 (in-app fallback notice, #123422) — complementary visibility, still worth landing.
- #124275 (warn-once stuck-observer log) — bounded mitigation, still worth landing.
- Electron bump (#124032 option B) — blocked on the Windows VC++ install issue per the issue thread.

Fixes #124255

items.body:
## Root cause

The serve parent-death watchdog's loop (`hermes_cli/web_server_lifecycle.py`) ended with a bare `os._exit(0)` — skipping the chaining SIGTERM/SIGINT exit-flush handlers (`install_exit_flush_signal_handlers`, installed right before serving) and every `atexit` hook. The one exit path that fires on unclean desktop death was therefore the one that dropped the unflushed transcript turn (#108601).

## What changes

- `hermes_cli/web_server_lifecycle.py`: `os._exit(0)` is replaced with `_request_orphan_shutdown()` — `signal.raise_signal(SIGTERM)` (works on Windows, where `os.kill(pid, SIGTERM)` would not run Python's handler) backed by a 10s daemon `threading.Timer` that `os._exit(0)s` if the graceful unwind stalls. This reuses the established `cli.py` `_arm_exit_watchdog` graceful-then-ceiling idiom.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_serve_parent_watchdog.py`: two regression tests — the watchdog shutdown goes through the signal path (not `os._exit`), and the daemon hard-exit ceiling is armed with a bounded interval.

## Notes on the rebase onto current main

Main grew a `stamp_exit("clean")` + `kill_live_foreground_processes` block in the same spot since the branch was cut. The SIGTERM chain covers both: `_handle_exit_flush_signal` runs `_stop_turns_before_exit()` (which calls `kill_live_foreground_processes`) before handing off, and `stamp_exit` is an atexit hook that now actually runs. The block is intentionally dropped in favor of the single signal-path shutdown.

## Acceptance coverage (#108601)

- Exit-flush handlers persist in-memory transcripts on parent death — covered by the signal-path test (SIGTERM handler fires; no `os._exit`).
- atexit hooks run — the graceful path runs them before the 10s ceiling.
- Reap stays prompt and guaranteed — the ceiling-timer test pins the daemon `os._exit` backstop and bounded interval.

## Tests run

- `HERMES_PYTHON=<test-venv> bash scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_cli/test_serve_parent_watchdog.py` (this branch, rebased onto current main): **16 passed, 0 failed**.
- Same file on `origin/main` (PR test content only): **14 passed, 2 failed** — both new tests fail pre-fix, i.e. they genuinely pin the fix.

Fixes #108601
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/108602 (GitHub's server-side rebase hit `RebaseConflictError` on the `stamp_exit` hunk and the fork's branch could not be force-pushed from this partial-clone checkout — thanks @vadimcomanescu for the original fix and tests, preserved here with authorship intact)
