items.body:
Flavored desktop builds now write their install stamp while the checkout is still clean, so one-off commit builds are stamped `dirty: false` and channel builds no longer abort.

## Root cause

A flavored build (a one-off commit build, canary, or preview channel) copies its own icons over the committed files in `apps/desktop/assets/` before packaging. The install stamp was written after that copy. `write-build-stamp.mjs` runs `git status --porcelain -uno` (`apps/desktop/scripts/write-build-stamp.mjs:59`), saw the modified tracked files, and reported the checkout as dirty. The CI driver ran it inside the `flavored_assets(...)` block (`scripts/bundles/desktop.py:124-125` on main). The source build ran it after the `cpSync` of the icons (`apps/desktop/scripts/build.mjs`, `buildSourceDesktop`).

## Symptoms

- One-off commit builds got a stamp with `dirty: true`. The Windows smoke then refused the package: `stamp.dirty: true != false` (`tests/install/e2e-assets/bundle-smoke-metadata.mjs:45`). Evidence: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/36743495163
- Channel builds failed outright in `write-build-stamp.mjs:96` with `Channel build identity does not match clean checkout HEAD`. All four native legs failed in "Build and package". Evidence: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/36753381711

## Change

- `scripts/bundles/desktop.py`: the stamp step now runs before the `with flavored_assets(...)` block. The `require_source(repo, request.commit)` call just before it has already proven the checkout is clean.
- `apps/desktop/scripts/build.mjs`: the stamp step now runs before the icon `cpSync` in `buildSourceDesktop()`.

`write-build-stamp.mjs` reads no artwork. The stamp content is the same as before, except that `dirty` is now correct.

| Build | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| One-off commit build | stamp `dirty: true`, Windows smoke refuses it | stamp `dirty: false`, smoke accepts it |
| Channel build (canary, preview) | "Build and package" fails with `Channel build identity does not match clean checkout HEAD` | stamp written, build continues |
| Default-brand build (no `--icons`) | no copy, stamp clean | unchanged |

## Testing

New test: `apps/desktop/scripts/build.test.mjs`. It gives `buildSourceDesktop` a temp source tree with a committed `apps/desktop/assets/icon.ico` and a separate icons tree with a different `icon.ico`. A fake `run` reads the asset file when the `write-build-stamp.mjs` step is invoked. The test asserts that the stamp step saw the committed bytes and that the flavored icon is in place afterwards.

With `build.mjs` reverted to main (red):

```
 FAIL  |electron| scripts/build.test.mjs > the install stamp is written while the committed assets are still in place
AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal:
Expected: "committed icon"
Received: "flavored icon"
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed (1)
```

With this branch (green):

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

Files run:

- `apps/desktop/scripts/build.test.mjs`, `write-build-stamp.test.mjs`, `commit-stamp-identity.test.mjs` (vitest): 3 files, 11 tests passed.
- `tests/scripts/test_desktop_preparation.py` (pytest): 10 passed.
- `ruff check scripts/bundles/desktop.py`: clean. `eslint` on the new test file: clean.

The Python driver has no test for this order. The same ordering rule applies there, and the CI run below is the evidence for it.

## Not verified

No full native build was run locally. The live evidence is CI run https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/36756600176, built from the same fix on another branch, which got win32-x64 through "Build and package".

This PR touches no workflow YAML.

`release.py --channel NAME --branding stable --build-commit SHA` now works before any stable release has published through the channel pipeline.

## What was wrong

`--branding stable` (added in #129319) makes a new channel copy its app identity (name, icon, package ID) from the stable channel's record on R2, `releases/channels/stable.json`. It refused when that record had no published release.

In production that record does not exist:

| Record | HTTP |
|---|---|
| `releases/channels/onboarding-v1-preview.json` (a channel created today) | 200 |
| `releases/channels/stable.json` | 404 |
| `releases/channels/canary.json` | 404 |

Channel records are public (installed apps read them), so the 404 means "never created". The channel pipeline reached `main` after the last stable release: the `v2026.9.24` tag has no `apps/desktop/product-identity.cjs`. Every `v0.21.5` attempt through the new pipeline has failed since, so no stable record was ever written.

Result: every stable-branded channel build fails at the allocation step. The first real dispatch did: run [36750895255](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/36750895255), `ChannelError: Stable branding copies the published stable channel identity; none is published`.

## The change

In `scripts/releases/channels.py` `ChannelPublisher._stable_identity`:

| Stable record on R2 | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Does not exist | refuse | `product_identity()` |
| Exists, no head | refuse | refuse (unchanged) |
| Exists, has a head | copy its identity | copy its identity (unchanged) |

`product_identity()` (`scripts/releases/channel_releases.py`) is the identity `channel_publish` already requires every stable release to carry (`scripts/releases/channel_publish.py:50`). So the first stable release through the pipeline will write this same identity into `stable.json`. From then on the record exists and the old rule applies again, so this path stops running without a follow-up change.

What it returns today:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `displayName` | `Hermes Agent` |
| `appId` | `com.nousresearch.hermes-bundled` |
| `msixAppIdWithOrg` | `NousResearch.HermesBundled` |

These match the stable row of the table in #129319.

`product_identity()` runs `apps/desktop/product-identity.cjs` with node. The allocation step only set up node for disposable receivers, so `.github/workflows/desktop-bundled-release.yml` now also runs the "Set up native identity reader" step when `inputs.branding == 'stable'`. This touches a workflow file, so the PR needs the `ci-reviewed` label.

## One thing this does not do

Current stable users run `v2026.9.24`, which is packaged as `Hermes` / `com.nousresearch.hermes` by the older system. A stable-branded channel build carries the new pipeline's identity (`Hermes Agent`, `HermesBundled`), so it does not install over their current app. That is true with or without this change: the identity it would have copied from `stable.json` is the same one. It installs as the regular app that the first new-pipeline stable release will ship.

## How it was tested

- `tests/scripts/test_release_channels.py::test_stable_branded_channel_reuses_the_published_stable_identity` now asserts both halves: no stable record gives the product identity and reserves no preview token; a stable record with no head still refuses.
- Red on the unchanged `channels.py`: `ChannelError: Stable branding copies the published stable channel identity; none is published`. Green with the change.
- `tests/scripts/test_release_channels.py`, `tests/scripts/test_release_channel_build.py`, `tests/scripts/test_dispatch_log.py`: 34 passed.
- `product_identity("v0.0.0")` run for real from the repo root (node + `product-identity.cjs`): returns the values in the table above. A canary-shaped tag would return `com.nousresearch.hermes-bundled-canary`, which is why the fallback passes a fixed non-canary tag.
- `ruff check` clean on the touched Python; the workflow YAML parses.

## Not verified

- No workflow dispatch with this change. The allocation step always runs `main`'s code (`scripts/releases/commit_build.py:48-53`), so the first real check is the first stable-branded dispatch after merge.
- The `setup-pm` node step was not run for this path. It is the same step disposable receivers already use before calling `product_identity()`.

items.body:
Desktop can create sessions again against a backend older than #122899, such as a Hermes Cloud backend behind a Desktop that updates from main (#128971).

Salvage of #128972 by @dskwe. Their two commits are cherry-picked with authorship preserved; one follow-up commit is ours.

**Who / when / why:** Desktop builds from main send `cwd_explicit` on `session.create`. The field was added to the contract in #122899 (2026-09-25). No released backend declares the field (v0.21.3, v0.21.4 and v0.21.5 all lack it), and since v0.21.3 they validate params strictly and reject the whole create with code 4000, so every new chat fails with "invalid params for session.create: cwd_explicit: Extra inputs are not permitted". The reporter's backend is a remote Cloud instance, so `hermes update` on their machine can't fix it.

## Changes
- (@dskwe) On that specific rejection, `session.create` is resent once without `cwd_explicit`. `cwd` is kept, and both new-chat call sites go through the retry.

Inside the packaged desktop app, the agent can now run `hermes` from its terminal. Before this change, every call failed.

**Why it failed:** bare `hermes` resolved to `<payload>\venv\Scripts\hermes.exe`. CI builds that venv. Its Windows redirector reads `pyvenv.cfg` `home`, and that value still points at the CI path, so the call stops with `did not find executable at C:\a\hermes-agent\...`. The working launcher is `<payload>\bin\<cliName>.exe` (for example `hermes-onboarding-v1-preview.exe`), and it was never on the agent's PATH. (Handoff 2026-09-30, section B, row 16.)

## What changes

- `pm/environments.py::activate_dependencies`: in a sealed payload, the payload's launcher dir (read from the manifest's `runtime.commands`) goes first on PATH. On Windows, the shipped venv's `Scripts` dir is no longer added at all. New small helpers: `payload_command_dir`, `cli_command_name`. `payload_venv` and `store_root` now share one manifest reader.
- `tools/environments/local.py::_resolve_hermes_bin_dir`: in a sealed payload, it returns that launcher dir first, so terminal and cron children get the working `hermes` whatever the PATH order is.
- `apps/desktop/scripts/write-build-stamp.mjs::stageDesktopLaunchers`: it now copies the canonical launchers to their qualified names instead of renaming them. So `<payload>/bin` holds both `hermes.exe` and `hermes-<channel>.exe`. Only the qualified names are published (MSIX aliases and `~/.local/bin` links both read the manifest), so side-by-side installs still never shadow each other.
- `hermes_cli/plugins_cmd_install.py`: the "plugin already exists" hint uses the real command name (`hermes-<channel> plugins update X` on a channel build).
- `side-by-side-launchers.test.mjs`: I updated this test on purpose. The canonical files now stay in the payload.

Source and dev installs do not change, because they have no payload manifest. On macOS and Linux bundles, the payload's `bin` now goes first on PATH, and the venv `bin` stays second.

## Checks

- Ran: `scripts/run_tests.sh` on `tests/pm/test_runtime_selection.py`, `test_runtime.py`, `test_store_extensions.py`, `test_uv_cache.py`, `test_environment_build.py`, `tests/tools/environments/test_local_path_completion.py`, `tests/tools/test_local_env_blocklist.py`, `tests/test_managed_runtime_resolution.py`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins_cmd.py`. The first chat after setup now connects the picked apps, installs the picked plugins, and delivers a small finished result within about 5 minutes instead of surveying the whole machine first.

## What changes

- **New `first-task` skill.** `start_chat` adds it to the end of the task chat's first message. The message holds the user's ask, then the "What setup learned" block, then the skill with the picked app and plugin ids. No system prompt changes. The history view cuts the message before the skill, so no surface shows it.
- **Rules in the skill:** connect and install the picks first, in one step. Show work within 1 minute and a finished result within 5. Do not survey the machine: the setup facts are the survey. Cut a big ask to a first slice and say so. Offer three options only when the ask is vague. Run machine setup as 2 or 3 short choice cards, then install a few apps first.
- **Fork card from picks and scan.** The backend fills the fork card when it shows, so the earlier picks are known. It leads with two first tasks, such as "A daily brief from Linear and Slack", "Install a few apps for this Spark", or "A cheat sheet page for Figma". Then it shows "I have something in mind", "Help me set up this <machine>" and "Let's figure it out together". The machine-first "Something else" step and the "automate" and "skip" rows are gone. "Figure it out" now hands off at once, and the task chat asks.
- **Handoff message.** The template now asks only for the user's ask. "Call me <name>" and the install and plan paragraphs are gone. `start_chat` no longer adds "Start from this; look at my computer again only when the task needs more."
- **Folded block in the desktop app.** "What setup learned about me" shows as a small closed disclosure under the first message. The model still gets the full text.
- **`initiate-setup` SKILL.md** keeps only the setup beats: 20.5 KB down to 10 KB. Every task-chat rule now lives in `first-task`.

The Desktop install card now installs several plugins at once without refusals, can turn on a plugin that is already on disk, stops blocking the turn when a row fails, and each card shows only its own install.

These are bugs B1, B3 and B17 from the recorded Windows run (run17, 30 Sep).

## What changes

- **Parallel enables (B1).** The card runs each approved row on its own thread. Each thread read the config version first and committed much later, so every commit after the first failed with "Plugin configuration changed since this selection was read; retry." A lock per Hermes home (`hermes_cli/plugins_cmd.py::_set_plugin_enabled`) now covers the read-then-enable step, so enables in one process wait their turn. The version check in PM stays. It still refuses an edit from another process.
- **Install or enable (B3).** A refused enable leaves the plugin on disk. "Try again" then ran a full install, which failed with "already exists". A catalog install (no force) now checks for a plugin on disk that has its catalog record and is not enabled. If it finds one, it skips the download and runs the same enable and live load that a normal install ends with (`plugins_cmd_install.py::_catalog_install_on_disk`). This covers the card, `manage_catalog install`, and the Plugins tab.
- **A failed row no longer blocks the turn (B17).** A failed catalog row now counts as done (`tools/connectors/contract.py::resolves`). The operation settles when every row is installed, skipped or failed, so the model gets the reason at once and does not wait 300 s. When the operation settles, a failed row stays failed and keeps its reason (it no longer turns into "Not installed"). "Try again" still works while another row keeps the card open. This applies to catalog rows only. Connector and MCP rows behave as before.
- **One card, one operation (renderer).** Models reuse tool call ids (`call_0`). Cards looked up their operation by session and call id, so an old card redrew a newer install. When `connection.request` arrives, the tool row now records the op id, and the card draws only that operation. Settled install cards are kept, so each card stays on its own row. The held-click seq is keyed by op id, so the "Installing…" that should not show is gone.
- **Try again on a settled card.** A failed plugin row on a settled card keeps "Try again". It runs the host install through `plugins.manage`, which now enables a plugin that is already on disk. The row then shows the result.
- The `manage_catalog` description now says that failed rows end the wait and that install turns on a plugin that is installed but not enabled.

## Checks

- `scripts/run_tests.sh` on single files: `tests/tools/test_connectors_{catalog,operation,contract,mcp,managed}.py`, `tests/tools/test_connector_local_batches.py`, `tests/tui_gateway/test_connector_operation_{e2e,rpc}.py`, `tests/pm/test_worker_publication.py`, the `tests/hermes_cli` plugin files (catalog, packs, update, known issues, hub perf, relay cutover, dashboard routes), `tests/tui_gateway/test_plugins_manage_install.py`, `tests/agent/test_run_agent.py`. All pass.
- I updated two tests in `tests/tools/test_connectors_catalog.py` on purpose, because failed rows now settle the operation.
- A/B for the lock with a scratch test that was not committed: three concurrent `_set_plugin_enabled` calls against a real PM worker. Without the lock, two fail with the run17 error. With the lock, all three land.
- Scratch check (not committed) for install-or-enable: a catalog plugin on disk and not enabled gets enabled with no clone. Once it is enabled, a second install takes the normal path again.
- Desktop: `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint` and `prettier --check` on the changed files. `vitest` passes on `catalog-install-tool`, `connector-tool`, `mcp-setup-tool`, `message-parts-connectors`, `connection-request`, `use-composer-submit`, `input-requests` and `catalog-install`.
- Not done: a live Desktop run and a Windows bundle run. Sid will live test the bundle.

items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #129254

Surface post-acknowledgement worker failures: record the worker's exit cause, preserve its stderr diagnostic, retire the matching fire claim, and invoke the job's existing failure-notification lane.

The execution ledger deliberately remains `unknown`: an acknowledged worker may already have performed side effects. The job records an error. This does not automatically retry or claim to identify/prevent the reporter's initiating startup crash.

## Root cause

After a worker adopts its execution and dies, the parent recovers its row to terminal `unknown`, then returns without recording the job outcome. The fire claim and empty job error survive. Separately, the payload cleanup unlinks stderr before Python prints an escaping exception, so an outer traceback wrapper cannot preserve that diagnostic.

## Fix

- Carry forward the targeted dead-owner terminalizer and observed exit status from #128616; never terminalize a live worker.
- Read the existing bounded/redacted stderr tail after a lost worker exits. Keep exceptional captures until that read; successful workers still clean up their own captures.
- Project a recovered unknown run onto the job through the existing incident/failure-delivery path. Hold its fire-owner fence through notification and bookkeeping so an already-recorded run, replay, or newer fire is not overwritten.
- Preserve diagnostics when a concurrent recovery sweep wins the ledger transition first.
- Keep new outcome logic in `cron/scheduler_worker_failure.py`; normal worker completion and unrelated waiter-error semantics remain unchanged.

## Prior work and credit

- [#128616](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/128616), @Finn763: cherry-picked `d3f3571f8c6f4d2f188e90151d8f8393f049a573` with `-x`, retaining the original author. Its exit-evidence/claim fix is the base; this adds failure delivery and closes its payload-exception stderr gap.
- [#120391](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/120391), @DresvyanskiyDenis: recovery projection and failure-delivery approach, hand-ported with verified `Co-authored-by: Denis Dresvyanskiy <dresvyanskiydenis@gmail.com>`. This version holds the fire fence over the side effect and adds worker diagnostics.
- [#129256](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/129256), @dskwe, with @ehz0ah's reviews: identified the post-ack stderr unlink ordering and, at `e322e76`, records a worker-side traceback and releases the owner-fenced claim when `run_one_job` raises. This PR reaches the same claim/cause outcome from the parent, so it also covers a hard worker exit and sends the job's failure notice. No code copied. One deliberate difference: the ledger stays `unknown` rather than `failed`, because `run_one_job` may already have had side effects before it raised.
- [#126355](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/126355), @dahux-net: managed-store relaunch fixes that are a plausible *initiating* cause of this crash class. Separate mechanism, not superseded here.
- [#120347](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/120347), [#108806](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/108806), and closed [#108920](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/108920): broader recovery projections reviewed, not incorporated. Their periodic/restart scope remains separate; #120347 also failed the already-recorded-success cross-test.
- [#124847](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/124847) and [#124855](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/124855) address bootstrap re-exec in #124827; [#127931](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/127931) addresses dead fire-owner identity. These are not proven causes of this report and are not superseded by touching the same file.
- Pre-ack proposal [#109294](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/109294) and existing merged work [#113219](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/113219), [#124013](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/124013) (carrying [#123432](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/123432)), [#116689](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/116689), [#126344](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/126344), and [#106733](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/106733) informed the comparison. Existing redaction, atomic acknowledgement, dependency activation, pre-ack notices, and claim-reclaim behavior are retained.

## Test plan

Canonical runner, with `HERMES_PYTHON=/home/mark/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python`:

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/cron/ --file-retries 0 -j 8` on base `7239625ae1b`: baseline 1,411 passed / 3 skipped; this branch 1,422 passed / 3 skipped; no failures.
- Two new invariant test functions (eleven cases): real child death and payload exception through the shared claimed-job entry, direct and builtin execution creation, concurrent recovery on both wait-return and timeout branches, repeat/new-owner fencing, and refusal to terminalize a live worker.
- RED checks: restoring main production files makes all four core failure-visibility cases fail; restoring #128616 production also makes all four fail. Restored the committed fix and reran the suite.
- Separate cross-PR harness executes the real module entry, including #129256's wrapper: 4/4 cases fail on main and each open candidate (including #129256 at `e322e76` and #126355); 4/4 pass on this branch. This is controlled fault injection, not reproduction of the reporter's unknown crash cause.
- #120391's two behavioral tests pass on the final salvage, including preserving a run the worker recorded before dying.
- `python3 scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all`: passed.
- `python -m ruff check cron/scheduler.py cron/executions.py cron/scheduler_worker_failure.py tests/cron/test_restart_safe_worker.py tests/cron/test_restart_safe_worker_death_evidence.py`: passed.
- `git diff --check origin/main..HEAD`: passed; contributor author-email mapping check passed.

## Scope and risk

No real Telegram delivery, native Windows/macOS runtime run, or hosted CI is claimed yet. Notification tests exercise the existing delivery boundary without sending messages.

This covers the surviving parent observing its worker's death, as in the report. If the gateway itself has already died, it cannot project or notify the failure here; broader periodic recovery remains separate. A failed worker may leave its stderr capture if no parent survives. No interpreter-selection, lazy-install policy, schema, or automatic retry changes. Rollback is reverting the four implementation commits.

## What

`apps/desktop/src/i18n/zh-hant.ts` was **4419 lines** on main. This splits the Traditional Chinese override table into the same 11 topic files as the source PR, leaving `zh-hant.ts` as the composing `defineLocale` file (**177 lines**) with the export name `zhHant` unchanged.

| New file | Top-level keys owned |
| --- | --- |
| `zh-hant_artifacts.ts` | artifacts, artifactCard, artifactPreview, preview |
| `zh-hant_assistant.ts` | assistant |
| `zh-hant_boot.ts` | boot, remoteDisplayBanner, updates, guidedGreeting, install, onboarding |
| `zh-hant_capabilities.ts` | skills, starmap, agents |
| `zh-hant_chat.ts` | composer, statusStack, prompts, desktop, tips |
| `zh-hant_chrome.ts` | fileMenu, titlebar, sidebar, shell, rightSidebar, zones, contextMenu |
| `zh-hant_command_center.ts` | commandCenter, messaging, profiles, cron |
| `zh-hant_common.ts` | common, billingBlock, ui |
| `zh-hant_connectors.ts` | sessionImport |
| `zh-hant_diagnostics.ts` | notifications, sendDiagnostics, errors |

- `zh-hant` is a sparse override, so siblings carry `satisfies Pick<TranslationOverrides, …>` and the composition keeps the original top-level key order. **No re-export shim.**
- Naming follows the root `AGENTS.md` `<stem>_<topic>` rule with the locale id `zh-hant` as the stem, matching the `zh_<topic>` split exactly.
- `defineFieldCopy` moves with its only use site (`fieldLabels`/`fieldDescriptions` under `settings`) into `zh-hant_settings.ts`.

## Why rebuilt, not merged

Main added six top-level keys to `zh-hant.ts` after the source PR branched (3663 → 4419 lines): `externalOpenFailed`, `sharedMetrics`, `intro`, `catalog`, `modelAssignment`, `interfaceMode`. None of them falls inside a topic boundary of the split scheme, so they stay inline in the composing file at their original positions — exactly how the sibling `en`/`zh` split PRs treat keys outside their scheme. The 41 mapped keys moved to the same topics with the same filenames as the source PR.

## Evidence

**Flattened dictionary equality** (two separate bundles via the repo's own esbuild alias map — one importing the pristine `origin/main` blob, one the new composition): **4950 leaf paths on both; key sets and order element-wise identical; differing values 0** (functions compared by type, arrays/objects by deep serialization).

**Key set**: `npm run i18n:keys` in apps/desktop rewrites `locales/_keys.desktop.json` **byte-identical (no diff)** — the catalog surface is unchanged.

**tsc / lint / tests** (all on the split tree):

- eslint on all 12 touched files → 0 errors/warnings (one import-order fix applied for `perfectionist/sort-imports`).

- `vitest run --project ui src/i18n src/app/settings` → **64 files, 496 tests passed** (includes catalog-completeness, registry, runtime, languages, profile-locale and both zh-hant consumer suites).

## Notes

- `zh-hant_connectors.ts` holds only `sessionImport` (zh-hant also lacks `webhooks`, `freeTier`, `keybinds`, `findInPage`), so this PR shares the topic taxonomy with the `zh` split but not an identical key set.
- No in-repo document references the old monolith path, so no docs changes.

items.body:
## What

Markdown links to local files whose paths contain spaces rendered as `label [blocked]` instead of the preview card (#102782).

Root cause, two halves:

- `apps/desktop/src/lib/markdown-preprocess.ts:220` — `FILE_LINK_RE`'s target char class `[^)\s]*` cannot cross a literal space, so CommonMark angle-bracket destinations (`[notes](<~/My Notes/todo with spaces.md>)`) never matched and fell through to rehype-harden, which blocks them.
- `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` (`previewFileTarget`) — markdown hrefs are percent-encoded (`/my%20notes/x.md`), so the raw resolved path missed on disk and the preview 404'd even though the decoded file exists.

## Fix

- `FILE_LINK_RE` now alternates two branches: the original plain-path branch, and an angle-bracket branch matching `<…>` destinations that may contain spaces. `routeFileLinksToPreview` already strips the surrounding `<>`, so no renderer change beyond the regex was needed. The doc comment above the regex is updated to describe both branches.
- `previewFileTarget` retries the percent-decoded path (`decodedPathIfMissing`) when the raw path misses — **before** main's directory/missing classification, so a decoded target is typed by what it actually is (file vs directory), keeping the typed `missing` result for genuinely dead links intact.

## Conflict resolution vs #102797

Cherry-picked from #102797 (authorship kept) and rebased onto current main, which changed `previewFileTarget` since that PR branched: it now also retries HOME-relative attachment candidates (#115609) and returns a typed `{previewKind: 'directory' | 'missing'}` result instead of `null` (#101683). The contributor's retry slotted in at the old `return null` site, which no longer exists; resolved by moving the decoded-path retry **above** the directory/missing classification (and extending it to directories) so main's typed-result behaviour is preserved and the PR's intent — spaces-in-path links opening in the preview rail — still holds.

## Tests

- `markdown-text.filelinks.test.tsx` — angle-bracket link with spaces routes to the preview card (no `[blocked]`): **red on base, green on the fix**. Percent-encoded link routes through the same pipeline.
- Neighbours green: `markdown-preprocess.file-preview.test.ts` (8), `markdown-preprocess.autolink.test.ts`, `markdown-preprocess.citation.test.ts`, `markdown-text.linklabels.test.tsx`, `markdown-preprocess.fences.test.ts` — 68 passed total.
- `tsc --noEmit -p .` clean on apps/desktop; eslint on touched files clean (2 pre-existing `no-restricted-globals` warnings in the test file's older cases).

Fixes #102782
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/102797
Thanks @kokhlo

items.body:
## What

The Logs pane (⌘K → Toggle logs) had two defects (#77794):

- Log text couldn't be selected or copied — the pane's `<pre>` didn't opt into the app's `data-selectable-text='true'` escape hatch from the global body `user-select: none`.
- The pane never followed the tail: it refetches every 5s but had no stick-to-bottom scroll management, so new lines rendered below the fold with no way to keep them in view short of manual scrolling.

## Fix

Cherry-picked from #77801 (authorship kept) and rebased onto current main:

- `data-selectable-text="true"` on the `<pre>`, the same opt-in the rest of the app's selectable surfaces use.
- Stick-to-bottom with a `shouldStickRef` gate and a 48px threshold: on each data change, a cancellable `requestAnimationFrame` scrolls to the bottom **only when the user is already within 48px of the bottom**; a deliberate scroll-up flips the gate off and subsequent refetches leave the user's position alone — mirroring the pattern the preview console uses (`isNearConsoleBottom`/`CONSOLE_BOTTOM_THRESHOLD`).

The only conflict was the `react` import line (main added `useMemo` for a neighbouring pane); resolved by keeping both imports. No other hunks conflicted.

## Tests

New `src/app/contrib/panes.logs.test.tsx` (jsdom has no layout, so the `<pre>`'s scroll geometry is stubbed and rAF is driven from a controllable queue):

- selects into text selection: `data-selectable-text="true"` present — **red on base**.
- sticks to the bottom across a refetch while the user is at the bottom (`scrollTo({top: scrollHeight})` fired) — **red on base**.
- does NOT scroll when the user has scrolled up past the threshold (the no-yank contract) — passes on base (base never scrolls) and on the fix.
- Neighbours green: `panes.test.tsx`, `log-tail.test.tsx`, `latest-actions.test.ts`, `surfaces.test.tsx`.
- `tsc --noEmit -p .` clean on apps/desktop; eslint clean on both touched files.

Fixes #77794
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/77801
Thanks @JonthanaHanh

items.body:
Setup cards now tell the model the name the user saw, the apps card no longer shows a dead end, and the intro no longer shows the name card mid-motion.

**1. The pick's name reaches the model.** The accent card showed "Ultraviolet". The result held only `#8a2be2`, so the model guessed "BlueViolet". Now the card sends the label of each picked row next to its id. The backend passes it through for the lists it cannot name itself (accent, theme, layout, connectors, plugins). Rows the backend fills (tour, fork, machine_use) were named already, and the backend's names still win. The tool description gained one clause: say the label, never the id. The skill says the same. The contract `SetupChooseResult` gains `label?: string | string[]`, and the generated files are regenerated.

**2. An empty apps or plugins list shows no card.** Without a Nous identity, connectors are off. The apps card then said "This list isn't available right now. Reply in chat instead." Now `setup_choose kind:"connectors"` checks before it sends a card:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[connectors card] --> B{connectors_available}
  B -- yes --> C[show card]
  B -- no --> D{config on, no identity, free tier on}
  D -- yes --> E[one ensure_portal_identity attempt] --> F{available now}
  F -- yes --> C
  F -- no --> G[no_answer + notice + next]
  D -- no --> G
```

An empty plugins list (`onboarding_entries()` returns nothing) returns `no_answer` the same way. The skill tells the model to say one line: connecting apps needs a Nous account, which is free, and it can be set up later. Then it goes on to plugins.

*Why the check is in the backend:* the renderer's `connectors.list` (account owner) calls the same gate, `connectors_available()`, in the setup profile's scope. The tool runs in the setup session's turn, so it gets the same answer, and it gets it before any card is sent. So no card flashes, and the model gets a reason it can say. A check in the renderer could only take down a card that was already on screen.

*Guest sign-up on demand:* the attempt uses the existing mint path, `ensure_portal_identity(explicit=True)` without `force`. So the mint memo's cooldown (Retry-After) still applies, and a second card in the cooldown does not reach the portal. The memo is kept per profile, so the boot failures of the launch profile do not block this one attempt in the setup profile. The docstring's list of callers now names this one. The renderer reads a cached `unavailable` connector catalog again when the card mounts, so a guest minted by the card is not hidden by the prefetch from the start of setup.

**3. The intro holds the thread.** The backend prelude writes the first row and the name card while the intro copy is still typing. The copy's cover uses `--ui-chat-surface-background`, and that colour is `transparent` under glass, so the card showed through. `$introHoldsThread` (true only in the `playing` stage) hides the thread under the copy. The thread shows when the spring settles. With reduced motion it shows at once, because that path goes straight to `landed`. The backend prelude is unchanged.

**Live repro:** backend only, `env -i`, a temporary `HERMES_HOME`, and a local stand-in portal. `setup_choose_tool` is called directly with a stub card callback.
- Before (`origin/onboarding/next`): accent `{"outcome":"submitted","picked":"#8a2be2"}`. The connectors card was shown with no identity.
- After, with no free tier (own key): accent `{"outcome":"submitted","picked":"#8a2be2","label":"Ultraviolet"}`. Connectors return `{"outcome":"no_answer","picked":null,"notice":"Connecting apps needs a Nous account (free) ...","next":"Send card plugins: ..."}`, and the callback is never called.
- After, with the free tier on and the portal returning 429: one portal hit, then `no_answer`. A second call in the cooldown makes 0 more hits.
- After, with the free tier on and the portal minting: one hit, the identity becomes `anonymous`, and the connectors card is shown.
- Empty plugins list: `no_answer` with the notice and `next` for layout. No card.

Checks: ruff, `check-windows-footguns.py --all`, `check_no_tmp_literals.py`, `git diff --check`, `tsc -p apps/desktop`, and eslint on the changed TS files all pass. The contract generator and `generate-skill-docs.py` were run, and their output is committed.

**Not verified:** no Electron run (lane rule). I did not see the intro hold or the card's label round trip in a live window. I did not run the setup session's turn scope under multiplex (A→B→A). No test suite was run.

items.body:
A first-run user who hits the free tier's capacity pause now gets a clear card within a second, and a retry that outlives the 15-minute guest token renews it instead of telling the user that signing-in is switched off.

**Live repro:** backend-only desktop setup chat (`hermes_cli.main serve` + WebSocket kickoff) in an `env -i` temp home, against a local stub for the portal and the welcome host (all other https egress blocked by a dead proxy).
- Before (`fe50fc8b60`): 429 `retry_after=25`, then the token expires during the wait → `403 invalid jwt` on the same token → "Using Hermes without signing in is switched off right now" (`free_tier_disabled`). The wait's `status.update` arrives at turn end (t=32.8 s, not t=7.8 s) and says "attempt 2/3" while the thinking line says "attempt 1/3". 429 `retry_after=1069` → "retrying in 600s", silent. `session.resume` says `z-ai/glm-5.2`, no provider. The prelude's `setup_choose` args have no `options`.
- After (this branch): the same 25 s wait ends with a new token (`POST anonymous/token`, new jti) and a 200 reply. A revoked token (`403 invalid jwt` with no expiry) heals the same way. `status.update` "The free model is busy. Retrying in 25s (attempt 2/3)" arrives when the wait starts, and every line says 2/3. `retry_after=1069` ends the turn 0.6 s after the 429 with the `free_tier_at_capacity` card ("…or try again in about 18 minutes", sign-in button, Retry). `session.resume` says `nous/welcome` via `nous`. Both prelude cards carry `"options": []`.

## What was wrong

Lab run `20260930-201200`: the welcome host answered `429 at_capacity, retry_after: 1069`. Hermes waited 600 s (the Retry-After cap), retried inside the same pause, waited 469 s, and sent the third attempt on a guest JWT (a short-lived signed token, 15 minutes here) that had expired during the wait. The host answered `403 {"error": "invalid jwt"}`. Any plain 403 from the welcome host is read as "the free tier is switched off", so that is what the user saw, after 18 minutes of a thinking line.

## What changes

| Bug | Root cause | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Expired token read as "switched off" | The key is only refreshed before an iteration (`turn_iteration_prep.py`), never between retries; `welcome_route_refusal` maps every welcome-host 403 to `tier_disabled` | `interruptible_backoff_sleep` adopts a fresh key after each wait. A 403 that says `invalid jwt` is a new route kind, `session_expired`, which the existing one-shot route heal (`_recover_welcome_tier`) fixes by re-exchanging the guest credential. If that fails, the copy says Hermes could not renew the connection and the card is the retryable outage card |
| 2. Up to 18 silent minutes | `compute_error_backoff` sleeps `min(retry_after, 600)` on every surface | On desktop and TUI a cooldown longer than 60 s ends the attempt cycle at once: fallback first, else the terminal result with the reset time. For the free tier that is the existing at-capacity card with its sign-in button (the setup chat keeps Skip). Cron, messaging platforms and `hermes chat -q` keep the long wait |
| 3. Status lines late and misnumbered | Rate-limit statuses always went to the end-of-turn buffer; the three lines used `retry_count` and `retry_count + 1` | A wait over 60 s, or any rate-limit wait on desktop/TUI, emits its status when it starts. Every line names the attempt that runs after the wait |
| 4. Resume reports the silent default | Lazy session info used the configured default; the agent build later pins `nous/welcome` | `_session_default_route` reports the pinned route when the profile routes to the free tier (resume, create, lazy fallback info, live identity) |
| 5. Prelude calls lack `options` | `initiate_setup_prelude` built the cards before #129344 made `options` required | Name card: the suggested-name row or `[]`. Accent card: `[]` |

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[429 with retry_after] --> B{desktop or TUI and retry_after > 60 s?}
  B -- yes --> C[fallback, else card: busy, reopens in N min, sign in]
  B -- no --> D[wait, status shown now]
  D --> E[adopt a fresh key if the old one is near expiry]
  E --> F[retry]
  F -- 403 invalid jwt --> G[re-exchange the guest credential once, retry]
  G -- fails --> H[card: could not renew, Retry]
```

## For the reviewer

- The 60 s live cap also applies to paid providers on desktop/TUI. An Anthropic 429 with `Retry-After: 171` now ends the turn with "resets in ~3 min, send /retry" instead of waiting 171 s. It also takes precedence over `fallback.min_switch_reset_seconds` on those surfaces. Say if you want the cap limited to the free tier.
- Waits over 60 s now announce their status when they start on every surface, including messaging platforms (where the existing noise filter still applies).
- No new tests (lane rule). Proof is the live runs above, plus a direct check that `cli`/`cron`/`telegram` still wait 600 s for `retry_after=1069`.

items.body:
On desktop and TUI, a rate limit from a paid provider waits out its `Retry-After` again; only the free Nous tier still ends the turn at once.

## What changed

#129396 made desktop and TUI stop retrying when a provider's cooldown (the wait the provider asks for in `Retry-After` or a `retry_after` body field) is longer than 60 s. The turn then ends and shows the reset time.

That fits the **free tier** (the no-sign-in Nous route on the welcome host). Its pause covers the whole service, so an early retry only gets the same 429.

It does not fit **paid providers** (paid Nous, Anthropic, OpenRouter, and others). Their limit reopens on time. Before this fix, a 429 with `Retry-After: 75` ended the turn with "wait a minute and send /retry" instead of retrying after 75 s. It also broke `fallback.min_switch_reset_seconds`: the turn ended instead of waiting on the primary.

The fix adds one condition to `cooldown_outlasts_live_wait`: the call must go to the welcome host. It uses the existing routing check `hermes_cli.anon_auth.route_is_welcome_host(agent.base_url)`. That check reads the endpoint the call actually used, not profile state, so a paid pool key next to a guest profile is not treated as free tier.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[429 with cooldown over 60 s on desktop or TUI] --> B{Call went to the welcome host?}
  B -- yes, free tier --> C[End the turn now: fallback, else the at-capacity card]
  B -- no, any other provider --> D[Announce the wait now, sleep Retry-After, retry]
```

| Case (desktop, cooldown over 60 s) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Free tier, `retry_after` 1069 | Turn ends, at-capacity card | Same |
| Paid provider, `Retry-After` 75 | Turn ends, "wait a minute and send /retry" | Wait status shows at once, retry after 75 s, reply arrives |
| Paid provider, cooldown under 60 s | Waits | Same |

Kept from #129396: a rate-limit wait on a live surface is announced when it starts, not only at the end of the turn.

Also removed: `retry_utils.retry_wait_cap`. Nothing called it.

Docs: `website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md` now says that the 60 s cutoff applies only to the free tier.

**Live repro:** real `hermes serve` backend over WebSocket, `env -i` temp home, local stubs only. An egress guard (dead HTTPS proxy) blocks real hosts.
- Before, paid-shaped stub, 429 `Retry-After: 75`: at +4.46 s `❌ Rate limited after 1 attempt … (resets in ~1m)`, then `message.complete status=error` ("custom is rate-limiting requests right now … send /retry"). The stub got 1 request.

items.body:
The 32-core runner pool is backed up behind the slow CI lanes. The four E2E suites, the two Windows E2E jobs, the Docker image build and the Nix flake check account for about 120 of the ~140 larger-runner minutes each PR push spends, and they fired on nearly every PR (66–98% of the last 200 merged PRs).

On a pull request, each slow lane now runs only when the diff touches that suite, its harness, or the code it guards, or when the PR carries the `run-e2e` label. Every push to `main` still runs all of them, and a stable-release run still forces every lane on.

## Lanes

| Lane | What starts it on a PR | Last 200 merged PRs (before) |
|---|---|---|
| `e2e` + Windows E2E | `tests/e2e/`, the shared test harness, `hermes_state*` | 4% (66%) |
| `e2e-upgrade` + Windows install/update | updater, installer, `pm/`, dependency manifests, the upgrade suites | 6% (66%) |
| Desktop core E2E | its specs and harness, `electron/backend-*`, `apps/shared/src`, session/transcript stores, packaging | 13% (98%) |
| Desktop update E2E | its specs, the Electron updater, `scripts/desktop-update/`, `install.sh`, `hermes_cli/update_*` | 6% (98%) |
| Docker / Nix | their own files, dependency manifests, `pm/`, `tests/docker/` | 2% (98%) |

Replayed over those 200 PRs with measured job times, the modelled 32-core cost of one push per PR drops from about 120 to about 10 runner-minutes.

## Changes

- `scripts/ci/classify_changes.py`: the path lists live in one table (`_E2E_LANES`, `_DOCKER_PATHS`, `_NIX_LANE_PATHS`). The classifier reads the `run-e2e` label from the API, because a rerun replays the original event payload. The fail-open contract now names these lanes as its one deliberate exception.
- `ci.yaml`, `tests.yml`, `tests-os.yml`: each lane's answer is passed to the job it gates. Called with no inputs, those jobs still run.
- `label-rerun.yml`: adding `run-e2e` cancels and reruns the head commit's CI, Docker and Nix runs.

## Tests

- `tests/ci/test_classify_changes.py`, 95 tests, green. New tests check that:
  - the label turns every slow lane on and changes nothing else;
  - every path in the lane tables still matches a tracked file, so a rename cannot quietly stop a lane from running on PRs;
  - no job gates on, or passes on, a detect output that detect does not declare.
- Four deliberate sabotages each turned the suite red: nix always on, label ignored, a dead path prefix, an undeclared output passed through `with:`.
- actionlint passes on every workflow this PR edits.

This PR edits `.github/`, so the classifier turns every lane on and its own CI runs the full suite.

## Known gaps

- On a rerun, Docker and Nix may not see the label. Those workflows grant only `contents: read`, and I have not confirmed that token can read a PR's labels. Adding the permission means changing the stable-release caller too. The four E2E suites pick up the label through `ci.yaml`.
- On a fork PR the label's rerun job cannot rerun anything, because the token is read-only. `ci-reviewed` already has the same limit. A maintainer clicking "Re-run all jobs" gets a run that sees the label.
- An E2E regression the path lists miss now first shows up as a red `main`, and nothing alerts anyone when that happens.

The task chat that setup opens now starts from what setup learned, and it talks before it builds.

## What changes for the user

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| What the task chat knows | Only what the setup model chose to write. The scan never reached it. | The model's message, plus a block the backend adds: the user's picks and a plain summary of the scan. |
| First turn | Plans and builds at once, pushed toward "one HTML page". | Says what it took from setup, asks one plain-text question with 2 to 4 concrete directions, offers to connect the apps they need, and builds after a pick or "go". |

## How

- `tools/setup_choose_tool.py::_remember` records the name, apps, plugins and layout picks into the setup conversation's card facts (`setup-cards/<session>.json`). The scripted opening goes through the same tool, so the name is recorded too.
- `host_facts.py::_learned` turns the interpreted scan into plain first-person lines (machine, RAM, apps in use, runs agents, level). `setup_cards` stores them beside the fork rows. Only interpreted fields go in, no raw scan values or private strings.
- `tui_gateway/start_chat.py`: when the caller is the setup profile, it reads those card facts in the setup profile's scope and appends the "What setup learned about me" block under the model's message. The model's message stays first. Other profiles get no block.
- `templates/handoff.md` and the SKILL.md handoff lines: the plan now asks the task chat to talk first. The "one HTML page" push is gone. These rules stay: no mock data, no routing around connectors, ask before sending, deleting or scheduling. The "I use:" line is gone, because the block carries the exact picks. The install/connect step now runs after the user picks a direction, not before the first reply. SKILL.md is 20.5 KB. Skill docs are regenerated.

## Before / after: the task chat's first user message

**Before.** This is the real message from the play-onboarding run (`start_chat` call in the setup session, read-only):

```text
Figure out what to automate for me by looking at my machine and setup, propose the top candidates, and build the first one as a working result.

Call me sid. You're figuring out the automation from my machine because I don't know what to pick.

I use: gmail, googlecalendar, linear.

Plan briefly, then build: scaffold, research, first artifact. Use real data only from connected apps and find their tools with tool_search; tools already signed in on this computer, like a logged-in gh, are fair to use, and say so in one line. Never route around a connector: no IMAP client, app password or other way into the same account; if I decline one, that app is out of this build. Ask before sending, deleting or scheduling anything, and set up no recurring job unless I asked. Make the result something I can open: one HTML page if the idea allows it. Make this first version finishable with no account I have not connected: web research with the browser visible to me, scripts, a small app, a file-based tracker, a generated page. If the idea needs an account, build the no-account core first and offer the connection next.

As you start, tell me in one short sentence that you'll ask for permissions as you go and I can say no or redirect you. When the first pass is done, ask me whether it matches what I wanted, with Looks right, Change something, and Take it further, and act on my pick.
```

**After.** The backend path ran in an `env -i` temp home. `setup_choose_tool` got stubbed card replies, the same picks as the run. `record_cards` got that run's collected facts. Then `start_chat` ran from a setup-profile session. Session creation and `prompt.submit` were stubbed, so no agent started and no endpoint was called. The lead paragraph is the new template filled by hand for the same ask. The block under it is the real backend output.

```text
Figure out what to automate for me by looking at my machine and setup, propose the top candidates, and build the first one as a working result.

Call me sid. You're figuring out the automation from my machine because I don't know what to pick.

Talk with me before you build. In your first reply, say in two or three plain lines what you take from what setup learned, then ask me in plain text, not a card, one short question with two to four concrete directions drawn from my apps and this computer, like: Should I start with A, B or C? Or tell me more about what you want. Name the apps each direction needs and offer to connect them. Build only after I pick one or say go; then plan briefly and build. Use real data only from connected apps and find their tools with `tool_search`; tools already signed in on this computer, like a logged-in gh, are fair to use, and say so in one line. Never route around a connector: no IMAP client, app password or other way into the same account; if I decline one, that app is out of this build. Ask before sending, deleting or scheduling anything, and set up no recurring job unless I asked. Never use mock or sample data. Make this first version finishable with no account I have not connected: web research with the browser visible to me, scripts, a small app, a file-based tracker, a generated page. If the idea needs an account, build the no-account core first and offer the connection next.

When you start building, tell me in one short sentence that you'll ask for permissions as you go and I can say no or redirect you. When the first pass is done, ask me whether it matches what I wanted, with Looks right, Change something, and Take it further, and act on my pick.

What setup learned about me:
- Name: sid
- Apps I picked: Gmail, Google Calendar, Linear
- Plugins I picked: Blender
- Layout: Basic
- This Mac: Apple M4 Pro, darwin 24.6.0, arm64, 24 GB RAM.
- Apps I use on it: Discord, Obsidian, Slack, Spotify, Steam, Teams, Zoom.
- I already run AI agents here.
- I am a power user, a developer.
Start from this; look at my computer again only when the task needs more.
```

With the setup-profile marker removed, the same call adds no block.

## Checks

ruff on the touched .py files, `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all`, `scripts/check_no_tmp_literals.py`, `git diff --check`, `website/scripts/generate-skill-docs.py`. No tool schema or gateway contract changed.

## Not verified

- A live model run of the new template. I did not check that a real task chat asks first and offers directions.
- The desktop UI render of the longer first message.

The local-setup offer from #121969 now works on top of the new onboarding (`onboarding/next`). A machine that can run a local model hears about it at three moments, and none of them lands inside setup.

## What the user sees

| Moment | When | Checked live |
|---|---|---|
| Tour model stop | The quick tour's "Model picker" step adds "This computer can run one locally". | yes |
| Handoff tour, last step | After `start_chat`, the handoff tour ends on the model pill: "This machine can run models locally. Qwen3.6 35B-A3B fits your hardware…" | yes |
| Card above the composer | After the first **finished task** in the task chat. It does not show on the setup chat's turns or on the task chat's opening question. | yes |
| "Run locally" row | At the top of the model menu, until local models are set up. **Show me** opens it. | yes |

## What changed from #121969

The first two commits are #121969, cherry-picked with authorship kept. Conflicts were resolved in favour of both sides: the locale files, and `signpost.ts` (its header comment was dropped to match the trimmed file on this branch). The third commit fits the offer to the new flow:

- **Setup chat turns do not count.** The setup chat's closing words after `start_chat` are not a finished task.
- **The task chat's opening turn does not count.** Since #129419, the task chat speaks first and asks which direction to take. The card waits for the next completed turn. If the task is concrete and the first turn already builds, the card comes one turn later. That is the tradeoff.
- **"The guide will not start" now reads `onboarding.state`.** The intro film and its `intro-reveal` store are gone (#126139).
- **The `gui_tour` model stop reads the same eligibility** as the card and the menu row. The old `localSetupEligible` helper is gone.
- **Skip still retires the tutorial tips.** The offer arms, and its card waits for a finished task. Before, Skip also retired the old local-setup tip, which this PR deletes.

## Verification

- `tsc -p apps/desktop` is clean. eslint on the changed files is clean.
- vitest, one file at a time: `components/tips/*` (32), `lib/tips/*` (4) and `i18n/*` (76) all pass. No new tests.
- Live on the Mac, in a dev app with a sandbox home, OpenRouter and DeepSeek V4 Flash. This Mac fits no catalog model, so a renderer stub held eligibility at "fits Qwen3.6 35B-A3B". Two full onboarding runs:
  - **Run 1 (quick tour, "I have something in mind"):** the tour model stop had the local line. After handoff the offer was `armed`, and the opening question was consumed. The card appeared after the next finished turn (a habit-board HTML build). **Show me** set `accepted` and opened the menu with the row on top.
  - **Run 2 (tour skipped, "Help me set up this Mac"):** the handoff tour started by itself and ended on the model-pill step.
- Not checked: a real qualifying machine (the RTX Spark leg was dropped). In run 1 the handoff tour did not start by itself, and I found no cause. Run 2 showed it with debug logs on the same code.

items.body:
Flavored desktop builds now write their install stamp while the checkout is still clean, so one-off commit builds are stamped `dirty: false` and channel builds no longer abort.

## Root cause

A flavored build (a one-off commit build, canary, or preview channel) copies its own icons over the committed files in `apps/desktop/assets/` before packaging. The install stamp was written after that copy. `write-build-stamp.mjs` runs `git status --porcelain -uno` (`apps/desktop/scripts/write-build-stamp.mjs:59`), saw the modified tracked files, and reported the checkout as dirty. The CI driver ran it inside the `flavored_assets(...)` block (`scripts/bundles/desktop.py:124-125` on main). The source build ran it after the `cpSync` of the icons (`apps/desktop/scripts/build.mjs`, `buildSourceDesktop`).

## Symptoms

- One-off commit builds got a stamp with `dirty: true`. The Windows smoke then refused the package: `stamp.dirty: true != false` (`tests/install/e2e-assets/bundle-smoke-metadata.mjs:45`). Evidence: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/36743495163
- Channel builds failed outright in `write-build-stamp.mjs:96` with `Channel build identity does not match clean checkout HEAD`. All four native legs failed in "Build and package". Evidence: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/36753381711

## Change

- `scripts/bundles/desktop.py`: the stamp step now runs before the `with flavored_assets(...)` block. The `require_source(repo, request.commit)` call just before it has already proven the checkout is clean.
- `apps/desktop/scripts/build.mjs`: the stamp step now runs before the icon `cpSync` in `buildSourceDesktop()`.

`write-build-stamp.mjs` reads no artwork. The stamp content is the same as before, except that `dirty` is now correct.

| Build | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| One-off commit build | stamp `dirty: true`, Windows smoke refuses it | stamp `dirty: false`, smoke accepts it |
| Channel build (canary, preview) | "Build and package" fails with `Channel build identity does not match clean checkout HEAD` | stamp written, build continues |
| Default-brand build (no `--icons`) | no copy, stamp clean | unchanged |

## Testing

New test: `apps/desktop/scripts/build.test.mjs`. It gives `buildSourceDesktop` a temp source tree with a committed `apps/desktop/assets/icon.ico` and a separate icons tree with a different `icon.ico`. A fake `run` reads the asset file when the `write-build-stamp.mjs` step is invoked. The test asserts that the stamp step saw the committed bytes and that the flavored icon is in place afterwards.

With `build.mjs` reverted to main (red):

```
 FAIL  |electron| scripts/build.test.mjs > the install stamp is written while the committed assets are still in place
AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal:
Expected: "committed icon"
Received: "flavored icon"
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed (1)
```

With this branch (green):

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

Files run:

- `apps/desktop/scripts/build.test.mjs`, `write-build-stamp.test.mjs`, `commit-stamp-identity.test.mjs` (vitest): 3 files, 11 tests passed.
- `tests/scripts/test_desktop_preparation.py` (pytest): 10 passed.
- `ruff check scripts/bundles/desktop.py`: clean. `eslint` on the new test file: clean.

The Python driver has no test for this order. The same ordering rule applies there, and the CI run below is the evidence for it.

## Not verified

No full native build was run locally. The live evidence is CI run https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/36756600176, built from the same fix on another branch, which got win32-x64 through "Build and package".

This PR touches no workflow YAML.

`release.py --channel NAME --branding stable --build-commit SHA` now works before any stable release has published through the channel pipeline.

## What was wrong

`--branding stable` (added in #129319) makes a new channel copy its app identity (name, icon, package ID) from the stable channel's record on R2, `releases/channels/stable.json`. It refused when that record had no published release.

In production that record does not exist:

| Record | HTTP |
|---|---|
| `releases/channels/onboarding-v1-preview.json` (a channel created today) | 200 |
| `releases/channels/stable.json` | 404 |
| `releases/channels/canary.json` | 404 |

Channel records are public (installed apps read them), so the 404 means "never created". The channel pipeline reached `main` after the last stable release: the `v2026.9.24` tag has no `apps/desktop/product-identity.cjs`. Every `v0.21.5` attempt through the new pipeline has failed since, so no stable record was ever written.

Result: every stable-branded channel build fails at the allocation step. The first real dispatch did: run [36750895255](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/36750895255), `ChannelError: Stable branding copies the published stable channel identity; none is published`.

## The change

In `scripts/releases/channels.py` `ChannelPublisher._stable_identity`:

| Stable record on R2 | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Does not exist | refuse | `product_identity()` |
| Exists, no head | refuse | refuse (unchanged) |
| Exists, has a head | copy its identity | copy its identity (unchanged) |

`product_identity()` (`scripts/releases/channel_releases.py`) is the identity `channel_publish` already requires every stable release to carry (`scripts/releases/channel_publish.py:50`). So the first stable release through the pipeline will write this same identity into `stable.json`. From then on the record exists and the old rule applies again, so this path stops running without a follow-up change.

What it returns today:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `displayName` | `Hermes Agent` |
| `appId` | `com.nousresearch.hermes-bundled` |
| `msixAppIdWithOrg` | `NousResearch.HermesBundled` |

These match the stable row of the table in #129319.

`product_identity()` runs `apps/desktop/product-identity.cjs` with node. The allocation step only set up node for disposable receivers, so `.github/workflows/desktop-bundled-release.yml` now also runs the "Set up native identity reader" step when `inputs.branding == 'stable'`. This touches a workflow file, so the PR needs the `ci-reviewed` label.

## One thing this does not do

Current stable users run `v2026.9.24`, which is packaged as `Hermes` / `com.nousresearch.hermes` by the older system. A stable-branded channel build carries the new pipeline's identity (`Hermes Agent`, `HermesBundled`), so it does not install over their current app. That is true with or without this change: the identity it would have copied from `stable.json` is the same one. It installs as the regular app that the first new-pipeline stable release will ship.

## How it was tested

- `tests/scripts/test_release_channels.py::test_stable_branded_channel_reuses_the_published_stable_identity` now asserts both halves: no stable record gives the product identity and reserves no preview token; a stable record with no head still refuses.
- Red on the unchanged `channels.py`: `ChannelError: Stable branding copies the published stable channel identity; none is published`. Green with the change.
- `tests/scripts/test_release_channels.py`, `tests/scripts/test_release_channel_build.py`, `tests/scripts/test_dispatch_log.py`: 34 passed.
- `product_identity("v0.0.0")` run for real from the repo root (node + `product-identity.cjs`): returns the values in the table above. A canary-shaped tag would return `com.nousresearch.hermes-bundled-canary`, which is why the fallback passes a fixed non-canary tag.
- `ruff check` clean on the touched Python; the workflow YAML parses.

## Not verified

- No workflow dispatch with this change. The allocation step always runs `main`'s code (`scripts/releases/commit_build.py:48-53`), so the first real check is the first stable-branded dispatch after merge.
- The `setup-pm` node step was not run for this path. It is the same step disposable receivers already use before calling `product_identity()`.

items.body:
Desktop can create sessions again against a backend older than #122899, such as a Hermes Cloud backend behind a Desktop that updates from main (#128971).

Salvage of #128972 by @dskwe. Their two commits are cherry-picked with authorship preserved; one follow-up commit is ours.

**Who / when / why:** Desktop builds from main send `cwd_explicit` on `session.create`. The field was added to the contract in #122899 (2026-09-25). No released backend declares the field (v0.21.3, v0.21.4 and v0.21.5 all lack it), and since v0.21.3 they validate params strictly and reject the whole create with code 4000, so every new chat fails with "invalid params for session.create: cwd_explicit: Extra inputs are not permitted". The reporter's backend is a remote Cloud instance, so `hermes update` on their machine can't fix it.

## Changes
- (@dskwe) On that specific rejection, `session.create` is resent once without `cwd_explicit`. `cwd` is kept, and both new-chat call sites go through the retry.
- (follow-up) The retry fires only on the real rejection: the flag was sent and the error starts with `invalid params for session.create: cwd_explicit:`. Before this commit, any error text mentioning the field triggered a resend. The match deliberately doesn't use `isOutOfSyncRpcParams`: v0.21.3 rejects without the "out of sync" suffix, which only arrived in v0.21.4.
- (follow-up) The helper moves out of the 3.2k-line hook into the sibling `use-session-actions/session-create-request.ts`. That module also owns the route/transport choice the two call sites had duplicated.
- (follow-up) Two invariant tests covering both message wordings and both transports. Each guard was mutation-checked and turned a test red: the broad matcher, no retry, requiring the suffix, dropping the flag-was-sent guard, and matching any field.

## Validation
| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `handle_request` on a pre-#122899 backend, desktop params | 4000 rejection, handler never runs | resend without flag accepted (1 handler call, no duplicate session) |
| `validate_params` at the v0.21.3 tag | rejects (bare wording) | resend accepted |
| Current backend | accepted | accepted on the first call, no resend |

`electron/no-console-git.test.ts` no longer fails at random with "Unexpected end of JSON input".

**Who / when / why:** the hanging-tree fixture's grandchild writes `pids.json` with a plain `writeFileSync` while the test polls `existsSync` → `JSON.parse`. The race came in with our own #127983 (commit `4daeec7f2c`, 2026-09-29), which rewrote the fixture around the existence-then-parse read added in `c42db5415f` (2026-09-28).

Inside the packaged desktop app, the agent can now run `hermes` from its terminal. Before this change, every call failed.

**Why it failed:** bare `hermes` resolved to `<payload>\venv\Scripts\hermes.exe`. CI builds that venv. Its Windows redirector reads `pyvenv.cfg` `home`, and that value still points at the CI path, so the call stops with `did not find executable at C:\a\hermes-agent\...`. The working launcher is `<payload>\bin\<cliName>.exe` (for example `hermes-onboarding-v1-preview.exe`), and it was never on the agent's PATH. (Handoff 2026-09-30, section B, row 16.)

## What changes

- `pm/environments.py::activate_dependencies`: in a sealed payload, the payload's launcher dir (read from the manifest's `runtime.commands`) goes first on PATH. On Windows, the shipped venv's `Scripts` dir is no longer added at all. New small helpers: `payload_command_dir`, `cli_command_name`. `payload_venv` and `store_root` now share one manifest reader.
- `tools/environments/local.py::_resolve_hermes_bin_dir`: in a sealed payload, it returns that launcher dir first, so terminal and cron children get the working `hermes` whatever the PATH order is.
- `apps/desktop/scripts/write-build-stamp.mjs::stageDesktopLaunchers`: it now copies the canonical launchers to their qualified names instead of renaming them. So `<payload>/bin` holds both `hermes.exe` and `hermes-<channel>.exe`. Only the qualified names are published (MSIX aliases and `~/.local/bin` links both read the manifest), so side-by-side installs still never shadow each other.
- `hermes_cli/plugins_cmd_install.py`: the "plugin already exists" hint uses the real command name (`hermes-<channel> plugins update X` on a channel build).
- `side-by-side-launchers.test.mjs`: I updated this test on purpose. The canonical files now stay in the payload.

Source and dev installs do not change, because they have no payload manifest. On macOS and Linux bundles, the payload's `bin` now goes first on PATH, and the venv `bin` stays second.

## Checks

- Ran: `scripts/run_tests.sh` on `tests/pm/test_runtime_selection.py`, `test_runtime.py`, `test_store_extensions.py`, `test_uv_cache.py`, `test_environment_build.py`, `tests/tools/environments/test_local_path_completion.py`, `tests/tools/test_local_env_blocklist.py`, `tests/test_managed_runtime_resolution.py`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins_cmd.py`. The first chat after setup now connects the picked apps, installs the picked plugins, and delivers a small finished result within about 5 minutes instead of surveying the whole machine first.

## What changes

- **New `first-task` skill.** `start_chat` adds it to the end of the task chat's first message. The message holds the user's ask, then the "What setup learned" block, then the skill with the picked app and plugin ids. No system prompt changes. The history view cuts the message before the skill, so no surface shows it.
- **Rules in the skill:** connect and install the picks first, in one step. Show work within 1 minute and a finished result within 5. Do not survey the machine: the setup facts are the survey. Cut a big ask to a first slice and say so. Offer three options only when the ask is vague. Run machine setup as 2 or 3 short choice cards, then install a few apps first.
- **Fork card from picks and scan.** The backend fills the fork card when it shows, so the earlier picks are known. It leads with two first tasks, such as "A daily brief from Linear and Slack", "Install a few apps for this Spark", or "A cheat sheet page for Figma". Then it shows "I have something in mind", "Help me set up this <machine>" and "Let's figure it out together". The machine-first "Something else" step and the "automate" and "skip" rows are gone. "Figure it out" now hands off at once, and the task chat asks.
- **Handoff message.** The template now asks only for the user's ask. "Call me <name>" and the install and plan paragraphs are gone. `start_chat` no longer adds "Start from this; look at my computer again only when the task needs more."
- **Folded block in the desktop app.** "What setup learned about me" shows as a small closed disclosure under the first message. The model still gets the full text.
- **`initiate-setup` SKILL.md** keeps only the setup beats: 20.5 KB down to 10 KB. Every task-chat rule now lives in `first-task`.

The Desktop install card now installs several plugins at once without refusals, can turn on a plugin that is already on disk, stops blocking the turn when a row fails, and each card shows only its own install.

These are bugs B1, B3 and B17 from the recorded Windows run (run17, 30 Sep).

## What changes

- **Parallel enables (B1).** The card runs each approved row on its own thread. Each thread read the config version first and committed much later, so every commit after the first failed with "Plugin configuration changed since this selection was read; retry." A lock per Hermes home (`hermes_cli/plugins_cmd.py::_set_plugin_enabled`) now covers the read-then-enable step, so enables in one process wait their turn. The version check in PM stays. It still refuses an edit from another process.
- **Install or enable (B3).** A refused enable leaves the plugin on disk. "Try again" then ran a full install, which failed with "already exists". A catalog install (no force) now checks for a plugin on disk that has its catalog record and is not enabled. If it finds one, it skips the download and runs the same enable and live load that a normal install ends with (`plugins_cmd_install.py::_catalog_install_on_disk`). This covers the card, `manage_catalog install`, and the Plugins tab.
- **A failed row no longer blocks the turn (B17).** A failed catalog row now counts as done (`tools/connectors/contract.py::resolves`). The operation settles when every row is installed, skipped or failed, so the model gets the reason at once and does not wait 300 s. When the operation settles, a failed row stays failed and keeps its reason (it no longer turns into "Not installed"). "Try again" still works while another row keeps the card open. This applies to catalog rows only. Connector and MCP rows behave as before.
- **One card, one operation (renderer).** Models reuse tool call ids (`call_0`). Cards looked up their operation by session and call id, so an old card redrew a newer install. When `connection.request` arrives, the tool row now records the op id, and the card draws only that operation. Settled install cards are kept, so each card stays on its own row. The held-click seq is keyed by op id, so the "Installing…" that should not show is gone.
- **Try again on a settled card.** A failed plugin row on a settled card keeps "Try again". It runs the host install through `plugins.manage`, which now enables a plugin that is already on disk. The row then shows the result.
- The `manage_catalog` description now says that failed rows end the wait and that install turns on a plugin that is installed but not enabled.

## Checks

- `scripts/run_tests.sh` on single files: `tests/tools/test_connectors_{catalog,operation,contract,mcp,managed}.py`, `tests/tools/test_connector_local_batches.py`, `tests/tui_gateway/test_connector_operation_{e2e,rpc}.py`, `tests/pm/test_worker_publication.py`, the `tests/hermes_cli` plugin files (catalog, packs, update, known issues, hub perf, relay cutover, dashboard routes), `tests/tui_gateway/test_plugins_manage_install.py`, `tests/agent/test_run_agent.py`. All pass.
- I updated two tests in `tests/tools/test_connectors_catalog.py` on purpose, because failed rows now settle the operation.
- A/B for the lock with a scratch test that was not committed: three concurrent `_set_plugin_enabled` calls against a real PM worker. Without the lock, two fail with the run17 error. With the lock, all three land.
- Scratch check (not committed) for install-or-enable: a catalog plugin on disk and not enabled gets enabled with no clone. Once it is enabled, a second install takes the normal path again.
- Desktop: `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint` and `prettier --check` on the changed files. `vitest` passes on `catalog-install-tool`, `connector-tool`, `mcp-setup-tool`, `message-parts-connectors`, `connection-request`, `use-composer-submit`, `input-requests` and `catalog-install`.
- Not done: a live Desktop run and a Windows bundle run. Sid will live test the bundle.
