## What does this PR do?

Adds `plugin-catalog/letsfg.yaml`, a community catalog entry for the LetsFG plugin. LetsFG searches and books flights and hotels. Someone from the Hermes team asked us on X for a plugin, so here it is.

The plugin is a portable Agent Plugins v1 package (`plugin.json` + `mcp.json` + `skills/letsfg/`), in the `integrations/hermes` folder of our public repo. It points at our hosted MCP server (`https://letsfg.co/mcp`, Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + DCR, PKCE S256). It bundles a workflow skill that covers how the search, shortlist and booking tools fit together, how to show the server's text cards in a chat, and the booking rules: book only the offer the traveller chose, one booking per trip, never invent traveller details, card details never in the chat.

- Repo: https://github.com/LetsFG/LetsFG (owner-submitted; I maintain the LetsFG org). Folder: [`integrations/hermes`](https://github.com/LetsFG/LetsFG/tree/3a309f60e2e0a52082728a277f319148fa60bff1/integrations/hermes)
- Releases: https://github.com/LetsFG/LetsFG/releases (latest `v2026.5.101`)
- Pinned SHA: `3a309f60e2e0a52082728a277f319148fa60bff1`, `subdir: integrations/hermes`
- No Python, hooks, env vars or self-update code. The folder is 8 files: manifests, the skill, README, licence and two images.

**Booking is real, so the entry says so.** A booking holds the price on the card saved on the user's LetsFG account. The hold is captured only once the airline or hotel confirms, and released if the booking fails. By default each booking is approved from an e-mail before anything is held, and card details are only ever entered on letsfg.co. The description carries this as a disclosure, like other hosted-only entries.

**Auth note.** Portable `mcp.json` remote entries can't declare `auth: oauth`, so the README asks users to run `hermes mcp add letsfg --url https://letsfg.co/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300` once. The config entry overrides the package entry of the same name, and the plugin still supplies the skill. `--connect-timeout 300` is there because `mcp add` bounds the browser sign-in by `connect_timeout` (30 s by default). That's enough for a one-tap guest connect but too short for a returning user's e-mail sign-in. `hermes mcp login` uses `login_connect_timeout` (about 315 s), so `mcp add` giving the same window may be worth a look on your side.

We also have #126200 open for `optional-mcps/letsfg`, which gives OAuth plus default tool exclusions with no manual step. Happy to keep whichever you prefer, or both.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (plugin catalog entry)

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/letsfg.yaml` (new)

## How to Test

All run on 2026-09-29 against `main` (`ea114c3e`), Windows 11:

1. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` → `OK: 350 file(s) valid`
2. The catalog CI step by hand: full clone of `LetsFG/LetsFG`, `git checkout --detach 3a309f60…`, then `hermes plugins validate --install-deps <clone>/integrations/hermes`: portable manifest ✓, manifest fields ✓, security scan: safe. No JS files, so the self-updater gate has nothing to match.
3. `hermes plugins install LetsFG/LetsFG/integrations/hermes --ref 3a309f60e2e0a52082728a277f319148fa60bff1 --enable` in a fresh `HERMES_HOME`. Result: `enabled  git pinned@3a309f60  1.0.0  letsfg`, only the folder's 8 files come down, and the skill registers as `agent-plugin-letsfg-…:letsfg`.
4. `hermes mcp add letsfg --url https://letsfg.co/mcp --auth oauth --connect-timeout 300`: DCR registers a loopback client, the consent completes, and 29 tools are listed. Then, through Hermes's own plugin discovery plus `discover_mcp_tools` and `handle_function_call` (no LLM in the loop), the skill loads, the 29 `mcp__letsfg__*` tools register, and tool calls work. One real search, WAW→LIS, returned 266 offers, and `present_flight_options` returned its text card.

# Add the Qdrant memory provider to the plugin catalog

## What does this PR do?

Adds one file: `plugin-catalog/qdrant.yaml`, an entry for the standalone
`hermes-qdrant-memory` repo — a `kind: exclusive` memory provider plugin that
stores Hermes turns in a self-hosted Qdrant server, embeds them on-device, and
recalls them by dense cosine search with session-scoped payload filtering.

The problem it solves: Hermes users who run their own infrastructure need a
memory backend whose content never leaves the machine they control, without
shipping vectors to a hosted embedding API.

Scope: the entry file only. No core code changes.

## Related Issue

N/A — catalog entry submission, no upstream issue (not a bug fix).

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/qdrant.yaml` — new catalog entry:
  - **Repo:** https://github.com/kuehnberger/hermes-qdrant-memory
  - **SHA:** `26540540975ef3297bd5d2b19b637c3099f5e8a3`
  - **Version:** `0.1.5`
  - **Category:** memory · **Tier:** community · **Maintainer:** `kuehnberger` (repo owner)
  - `image:` is a 2:1 `raw.githubusercontent.com` banner pinned to the same commit.

### What this plugin does

- Stores each Hermes turn as a single Qdrant point (`user: … assistant: …`) —
  no LLM summarization, so recall is quote-faithful and cheap.
- Embedding is local and on-device: `fastembed` (ONNX, CPU-only) by default at
  384 dims (~287 MB peak RSS vs 2,191 MB for sentence-transformers);
  `sentence-transformers` remains selectable on GPU hosts. Both backends
  produce identical vectors (cosine 1.0000), so switching needs no re-embedding.
- Recall is session-scoped via a `session_id` payload filter — a new profile
  starts with empty recall.
- Registers 5 agent tools: `qdrant_search`, `qdrant_upsert`, `qdrant_recall`,
  `qdrant_collect` (read-only), `qdrant_prepare`.
- A circuit breaker (5 consecutive I/O failures, 120 s cooldown) degrades to
  "no new memories" instead of crashing.
- Honest availability surface: `is_available()` (config only),
  `check_backend()` (real probe), `unavailable_reason()` (user-facing
  diagnosis) distinguish misconfiguration from a dead server.
- **Progress display** (`0.1.1`): optional `status_callback` events during
  memory operations — the CLI/TUI shows `💾 qdrant — stored (127,778 points)`
  after each turn and `💾 qdrant — recalled 3 memories` after each retrieval,
  configurable via `memory.qdrant.progress` (`off` / `minimal` / `verbose`).
- **Observability** (`0.1.2`): `hermes memory status` prints the provider
  config block plus **last store/recall timestamps and counts**, so a fresh
  process can answer "is this working, and when did it last store?" without a
  live connection; prefetch drops near-duplicate hits (word-level Jaccard
  >=0.72 / containment >=0.86); unknown `memory.qdrant` config keys warn
  instead of being silently ignored.
- **Declaration-parity tests**: `plugin.yaml provides_tools` <-> `tool_schemas`
  <-> `handle_tool_call` dispatch asserted mechanically in both directions
  (catalog rule 6).
- Deliberately not implemented (documented in README/CHANGELOG): local embedded
  Qdrant mode, gRPC, collection pruning/TTL, LLM extraction, hybrid RRF + INT8.

## Disclosure

The provider talks only to the Qdrant server named by `url` (default
`http://localhost:6333`); memories live there and are read back.
`QDRANT_API_KEY` is needed only for Qdrant Cloud, is read through the Hermes
secret scope, and is never written to `config.yaml` or logged. The sole
outbound request is the embedding model's weights from `huggingface.co` on
first use; embedding then runs on-device and no memory content is sent to any
third party. Runtime config lives in `<HERMES_HOME>/qdrant.json`, created 0600
at `os.open` time (not chmod-ed after the write) and outside the plugin
directory. Both statements became true only in `0.1.5` (`265405409`,
teknium1's review items 1 and 2); at earlier pins the key reached
`qdrant.json`/`config.yaml` in plaintext and the file was briefly world-readable
at the default umask — see "Known gap" below. Local embedded Qdrant mode is not
supported — a reachable server over REST is required.

## Known issues

- Windows on ARM is unsupported: `grpcio`, pulled in by `qdrant-client`, has no
  `win_arm64` wheel. Linux and macOS on x86_64/arm64 and Windows x86_64 are
  supported.
- Local embedded Qdrant mode is not supported — the provider is REST-only and
  requires a reachable server.

## How to Test

```bash
# 1. Start a Qdrant server
docker run -p 6333:6333 qdrant/qdrant

# 2. Install from the catalog (after merge)
hermes plugins install qdrant

# 3. Configure and activate
hermes memory setup qdrant

# 4. Verify
hermes memory status          # shows active provider and diagnosis
# then in a session, ask the agent something from earlier — recall works:
#   💾 qdrant — stored (N points)
#   💾 qdrant — recalled N memories
```

Or validate a clone without installing anything:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/kuehnberger/hermes-qdrant-memory
cd hermes-qdrant-memory && git checkout 26540540975ef3297bd5d2b19b637c3099f5e8a3
hermes plugins validate .
```

Tester reports: the repo has a `tester-report` issue template (host OS, python
version, install command, `hermes plugins validate` output, recall round-trip).

## Verification

Run locally against the pinned SHA and against branch head:

- **Structural gate** — `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` on this entry:
  `OK: 1 file(s) valid`; whole directory: `OK: 350 file(s) valid`.
- **Pinned-source gate** — the entry's SHA checked out detached and run through
  `hermes plugins validate --install-deps`: passes, exit 0.
- **Self-updater gate** — the grep the catalog CI runs returns empty (the
  plugin ships no `.js`/`.ts` files at all).
- **Test suite** — 115 tests pass at the pinned SHA (8 skipped: live tests need a scratch Qdrant), including a mutation-checked
  stored-vector parity test proving existing 127k vectors need no re-embedding.
- **CI on the plugin repo** — lint (whole-tree ruff) + pytest 3.11/3.12/3.13/3.14
  green, against a scratch Qdrant service.
- **No network calls** except the one-time Hugging Face model download.

### One validator warning, and why it is expected

`hermes plugins validate` prints:

```
⚠ provides_tools declares qdrant_collect, qdrant_prepare, qdrant_recall,
  qdrant_search, qdrant_upsert but register() did not register them
```

This is expected for every memory-provider plugin, not specific to this entry.
The capability probe runs `register()` in a scratch child process and records
what it registers. A memory provider registers itself with
`ctx.register_memory_provider(...)`; its tools reach the agent later through
`MemoryManager.add_provider()` → `provider.get_tool_schemas()`, so no
`register_tool()` call is ever made. Verified by running the same validator on
the merged, reviewer-approved `entropicmem` entry at its pinned SHA
(`7e02412`): it emits the same warning (plus the same shape for hooks) and
still exits 0. The check is `report.warn(...)`, not `report.add(…, False)`,
so it is non-fatal by design.

The declared list is still correct and worth keeping: the admission rule
requires the catalog list to match the manifest, and the manifest list is what
the plugin list, the catalog card, and `hermes plugins` read to name the
plugin's tools. It is verified mechanically in both directions by
declaration-parity tests inside the plugin repo.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [ ] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) — deviation: all six commits on this catalog branch are plain `Add …` / `Bump … pin to 0.1.x` headlines (the newest, `Bump qdrant plugin catalog pin to 0.1.5`, carries no body either). Left as-is rather than force-pushing a branch that has been up for review. The plugin repo's own commits do follow the convention — the pinned SHA `265405409` is `fix: honor teknium1's review — …`.
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate — `qdrant` was unclaimed in the catalog at submission time (checked again 2026-10-01)
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this entry (`gh pr diff --name-only` = `plugin-catalog/qdrant.yaml`)
- [x] The plugin's own suite passes (`pytest`, 115 tests at the pinned SHA) — N/A for core's `pytest tests/`, since this PR changes no core code
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (the plugin ships declaration-parity, stored-vector parity, tree-rule and docs-honesty gates)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu (WSL2) — Windows 11 and macOS validation is exactly what the `tester-report` template is for

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation — plugin README/CHANGELOG at the pinned SHA
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` — or N/A, this entry adds no core config key
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` — or N/A, no architecture change
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact — Windows-on-ARM limitation stated in `known_issues`

### Entry-specific gates

- [x] Repo is public and clonable at the pinned SHA
- [x] `image:` is a 2:1 `raw.githubusercontent.com` URL pinned to the entry SHA
- [x] `capabilities.provides_tools` mirrors `plugin.yaml` exactly (5 tools)
- [x] `known_issues` documents real constraints
- [x] `Disclosure —` block in `description` covers data location, network egress, and non-features
- [x] Dependency floors have upper bounds: `qdrant-client>=1.10.0,<2`, `fastembed>=0.4.0,<1`, `sentence-transformers>=2.7.0,<7`
- [x] No self-updating code; updates via `hermes plugins update` only
- [x] Name `qdrant` is unclaimed in the catalog
- [x] Submitted by the repository owner (rule 5)

## Known gap, stated plainly

The venv-re-sync fix (`0fd8559`), the bounded `fastembed` floor and the
`dimension()` measurement fix (`fdaf86e`), and the `api_key` secret-flag fix
from teknium1's PR #1 (`728cd17`) all landed after the earlier pin, as did the
0.1.5 review response (`2654054`): `save_config()` no longer persists `api_key`
(and scrubs legacy keys), `qdrant.json` is created `0600` at open time, the
model-supplied `limit` is clamped, URL credentials are stripped from the system
prompt, and `_setup.py`'s stale claims are fixed. All of it is in the pinned
SHA — the entry was re-pinned to `2654054` in the same PR, so nothing here
needs a follow-up bump.

One residual constraint is upstream and cannot be fixed in this plugin:
`pm.workspace.members_stamp()` hashes every file in a plugin member dir and
`_MEMBER_EXCLUDE` does not cover gitignored state, so running the plugin's own
pytest suite inside an installed copy still moves the dependency stamp. It is
declared in `known_issues` rather than left unmentioned.

The desktop session list no longer reads every message row of every session when `state.db` carries planner stats older than `idx_messages_session_id`. On the test store below, one list call drops from 521 MB of page reads to 5.6 MB.

Reported by @Lutkovtime in #119403 (2026-09-22) as 416 MB → 2 MB per query on a live store. This PR is the fix for the index-choice half of that report.

## What changes

- `hermes_state_common._sql_freshest_of`: the per-session `MAX(timestamp)` subquery names `INDEXED BY idx_messages_session`.
- A new builder, `hermes_state_common._sql_preview_raw(session_id_expr)`, produces the preview column with the same hint. Four session listings use it:
  - the sidebar (`list_sessions_rich`);
  - session_search's recent browse (`list_recent_sessions_bounded`, correlated on `tip.id`);
  - the telegram unlinked listing;
  - the export select.

  Before this PR these were four hand-copied subqueries that differed only in whitespace. Review found the fourth one (the bounded browse) after the first commit.
- One regression test, `tests/hermes_state/test_session_list_index_choice.py`, parametrized over the sidebar, session_search and telegram readers.
  - It seeds a `sqlite_stat1` with no row for `idx_messages_session_id`.
  - It traces every statement the reader runs, and checks that both the preview (`m`) and last-active (`_act_m`) searches run, each only through `idx_messages_session`.
  - All three cases fail on `origin/main` and when the hint is dropped from the builder.

## Why the planner picked the wrong index

- `idx_messages_session_id (session_id, id)` came in with #76877 (`8f91e249e4`, 2026-08-02; salvage of #76237 by @spfcraze).
- A `sqlite_stat1` written before that index existed has no row for it. SQLite then assumes the index is selective and prefers it over `idx_messages_session (session_id, timestamp)`.
- Every correlated subquery then walks the table pages of all of a session's messages.
- I confirmed this on SQLite 3.46 and 3.51: with the stale stats, dropping `idx_messages_session_id` inside a transaction sends the plan back to `COVERING INDEX idx_messages_session`.
- #122283 (`f27bde1fdd`, 2026-09-25) added a timestamp-window predicate to the last-active subquery, which incidentally moved that subquery back onto the covering index. The preview subquery still flips.

Hermes never runs `ANALYZE` itself. So on a store with no `sqlite_stat1` at all, the planner already picks the right index, and this PR changes nothing there.

`INDEXED BY` turns a missing index into a `no such index` error instead of a slow plan, so this change assumes `idx_messages_session` exists.

- It has been in `SCHEMA_SQL` since the first schema (`440c244cac`).
- No `hermes_state*.py` path drops it.
- The `sqlite_master` de-dup repair keeps one row per name.

The residual case is a hand-built or partially recovered `state.db`. Read-only opens run no schema init, so such a file would now fail listing instead of listing slowly. I judged a per-connection probe with a `NOT INDEXED` fallback, which `_legacy_display_page` uses for the newer index, not worth two variants of every listing query. Say if you want it.

## Measurements

- Store: generated through the real `SessionDB`, 515 sessions, 125,145 messages (~3 KB each), 1.17 GB.
- Call: `list_sessions_rich(limit=40, order_by_last_active=True, include_pinned=True, compact_rows=True)`, which is the desktop sidebar shape.
- Method: the call's exact statements, captured with `set_trace_callback` and replayed through `sqlite3 .stats on`. The figure is SQLite page-cache misses × 4 KB, one fresh process per run, median of 3. The three runs were identical to within 3 pages.

| planner stats | before #122283 | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| stale (no row for `idx_messages_session_id`) | 1033 MB | 521 MB | 5.6 MB |
| none (fresh store) | 5.6 MB | 5.6 MB | 5.6 MB (no change) |

This is a per-query cost. #126752 already stopped idle `sessions.changed` ticks, which were what made this query run repeatedly at idle. I did not re-measure idle `serve` CPU for this PR. The change moves page reads per list call, not a poll rate.

## Not in this PR

The reporter's other half is still open: the preview and last-active columns are computed for every listable session before `LIMIT`. #98566 (@qiqikuaidianpao) moves them after `LIMIT`. It is complementary to this change and needs a salvage onto the decomposed `hermes_state_sessions.py`.

## Tests

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_state/ tests/tools/test_session_search.py tests/hermes_cli/test_session_{export,system_prompt_dedup,detail_malformed_db,recovery}.py tests/hermes_cli/test_sessions_export_md_cli.py tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server.py tests/agent/test_insights.py`: 1680 passed, 68 failed.
- The same 68 fail on `origin/main` in the same tree layout, identical test IDs. They are holder-scan, repair, cross-VM filesystem and home-I/O-guard tests that fail on this machine; an earlier run without `test_web_server.py` had the same 55 on both sides.
- Live smoke on a second generated store (200 sessions, 30k messages, stale stats): the sidebar list reads 125.4 MB on base and 2.0 MB on head. `list_recent_sessions_bounded`, the telegram unlinked listing and the export rich-row reads all return non-empty previews on head.
- The new test has 3 cases. All fail on `origin/main`, all fail with the hint removed from `_sql_preview_raw`, and all pass here.
- The page-read numbers above were taken on the first commit. The second commit only moves the same SQL into one builder, so the sidebar plan is unchanged; the new test checks it.

Refs #119403, #127647

`hermes config migrate`, `hermes update` and `hermes config check` no longer report a configured MCP server's `mcp-<server>` toolset name as an unknown toolset.

Follow-up to #127782. That PR taught the shared `saved_toolset_resolver` about bare MCP server names but not the prefixed alias. MCP tools register under `mcp-<server>` only after MCP discovery, and these commands run without discovery.

- An `mcp-<name>` with no matching server is still reported.
- The rule comes from #106715 by @a692570, which covered both halves on the migrate path. The commit is authored by them, adapted onto the resolver that landed in #127782. Commit 1 maps their email.

items.body:
## Root cause

On Linux (Mesa/Wayland, several AMD iGPU generations), the bundled Chromium 144 GPU child can fail initialization with `error_code=1002` in three distinct ways, and `main` has no Linux recovery for any of them — the only `child-process-gone` ladder is Windows-gated:

1. A FATAL `GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.` SIGTRAP abort — a 100% crash loop on the affected hosts (#86073, #121954).
2. A silent sub-zygote init-retry loop: ~350–650% CPU, no `--type=gpu-process` child ever exists, no crash fires, and it survives restart, update and cache clears (#124843).
3. `HERMES_DESKTOP_DISABLE_GPU=1` only disables compositing — it never spawn-blocks the GPU process, so one still spawns and dies with 1002 on AMD/Mesa (#97616).

## What changes

- Keeps @Finn763's software ladder from #124898 (per-version marker, one-shot `--disable-gpu` relaunch, reveal/quit marker hygiene) and @dskwe's Linux extension of the #38216 `--no-sandbox` two-strike ladder from #126771, with authorship preserved.
- Coalesces the two `child-process-gone` handlers into one bounded decision (`linuxGpuChildDeathPath`): the sandbox signature (SIGTERM/exit 143) is tried first — on that host `--disable-gpu` still crashes, so software fallback would waste the one shot — and the software ladder takes the relapse after a `--no-sandbox` boot died again. One death produces exactly one relaunch; Windows keeps its existing fast path unchanged.
- Adds the #124843 silent-retry catch: `LINUX_GPU_SILENT_RETRY_GRACE_S` after the main window reveals, a boot with no GPU child in `app.getAppMetrics()` engages the same sticky software fallback for the next launch — the event-driven ladder can never see this manifestation because no `child-process-gone` fires.
- `HERMES_DESKTOP_DISABLE_GPU` now also appends `--disable-gpu` so the GPU child is fully spawn-blocked; remote-display detections keep their long-standing compositing-only behavior.

Fixes #86073
Fixes #124843
Refs #97616 — the `--disable-gpu` spawn-block is in; the intermittent launcher-vs-direct-binary race is not root-caused here and still needs a strace from a failing `hermes desktop` launch on Linux.
Refs #121954 — the recovery ladder bounds the FATAL crash loop; the systemd transient-scope hypothesis from that thread remains untested (the A/B the reporter could not run).

## Tests

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run electron/linux-gpu-fallback.test.ts electron/windows-sandbox-fallback.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` — 43/43 pass on this branch. Red proof: on the pre-coalescing cherry-picked tree (both source PRs applied as-is) 8 of the new tests fail, and on `origin/main` the module does not exist at all.
- `cd apps/desktop && npx tsc -p . --noEmit` — clean.

## Not exercised live

Authored and unit-tested on macOS. The decision functions are pure and platform-parameterized; the Electron integration (`child-process-gone`, `app.getAppMetrics`, `app.relaunch`, marker writes) is typechecked only here. Before merge this needs one real launch on an affected Linux host — ideally the #124843 silent-retry host (watch the fallback engage after the grace window) and one #86073/#121954 sandbox-signature host (watch the single `--no-sandbox` relaunch, then the software relapse) — with `~/.hermes/logs/desktop.log` attached to the issue threads. The durable fix for the underlying Chromium 144 failures remains the Electron bump tracked in #124032.

Supersedes #124898 (thanks @Finn763 — the marker/relaunch machinery is kept verbatim)
Supersedes #126771 (thanks @dskwe — the Linux sandbox-ladder gates are kept verbatim)

Co-authored-by: Finn763 <165816600+finn763@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Yuan Li <dskwelmcy@163.com>

## What does this PR do?

Adds `plugin-catalog/wiki-ref.yaml`, a community entry for **wiki-ref**: `@wiki:<title>` context references. Writing `@wiki:Alan_Turing` (or `@wiki:"Washington, D.C."`) in a message attaches the lead section of that Wikipedia article to the turn, `@wiki:Berlin#History` attaches one section of it, and typing `@wiki:` in the TUI or Desktop composer suggests article titles through `complete.path`.

It is built only on the plugin context-reference API (`ctx.register_context_reference`, #26193, shipped in #84937), which no catalog entry uses yet. Submitted by the owner (rule 5): I maintain `EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs`.

- Repo: https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs, subdir `wiki-ref`, release tag [`wiki-ref-v1.1.0`](https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/releases/tag/wiki-ref-v1.1.0) (rule 3)
- Pinned SHA: `0154f6bfaafc837cc4af78742e6db7c087d5b5a7` (1.1.0). First pinned at `e0395d4` (1.0.0), re-pinned to `4a5a257` to add the card, to `3cc4835` for 1.0.1 and to `0154f6b` for 1.1.0 (see Updates). The plugin's CI is green on all four: [e0395d4](https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/actions/runs/36607278067), [4a5a257](https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/actions/runs/36610548819), [3cc4835](https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/actions/runs/36637557550), [0154f6b](https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/actions/runs/36766709247)
- Category `web`: it pulls web content into the turn and registers no tools.

**Footprint** (also in the entry's `Disclosure —` sentence and the README's "Security and footprint" section):
- `register()` only calls `ctx.register_context_reference(...)`: no tools, hooks, middleware or commands.
- Network: HTTPS GET to `https://<language>.wikipedia.org/w/api.php` only. Redirects are followed only on the same HTTPS host; responses over 2 MiB are refused. The referenced title and the typed autocomplete prefix leave the machine, with a descriptive User-Agent as Wikimedia's API etiquette asks. A `#Section` reference is still one request to the same host: the article's plain text comes back and the section is cut locally, so the section name does not leave the machine.
- No API key, no dependencies, no files written, no subprocess, no self-update code. The only environment variables involved are the standard proxy ones `urllib` honours.
- Each reference is time-bounded (`timeout_seconds`, default 10; autocomplete 3 s). Requests run on a plugin-owned thread pool with an overall deadline: `preprocess_context_references` runs `asyncio.run()`, whose shutdown joins the loop's default executor, so a request parked there would hold the turn past the timeout. A test covers this through the sync wrapper.
- Settings (`language`, `max_chars`, `timeout_seconds`) come from `config_schema` and are read per reference. An unusable value becomes a context warning on that reference rather than a silent fallback.

## Related Issue

Uses the extension point from #26193 (shipped in #84937). Not a fix.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality): new catalog entry

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/wiki-ref.yaml` (new). All `capabilities` lists are empty, matching what the plugin registers at the pinned SHA.

## How to Test

1. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` → `OK: 350 file(s) valid`
2. Clone the repo at the pinned SHA → `hermes plugins validate --install-deps wiki-ref`: every check passes, security scan `safe`; the self-updater grep finds nothing.
3. `hermes plugins install wiki-ref --enable` with this branch's catalog → installed from `catalog:community`, pinned `1.1.0 @ 0154f6bf`, with only `plugin.yaml`, `__init__.py` and `README.md` in the plugin directory; `hermes plugins search wiki-ref` lists it under `web`.
4. `hermes chat -q "Who was @wiki:Alan_Turing?" --oneshot` → the user message sent to the model carries `--- Attached Context ---` with the article's lead section; `@wiki:Berlin#History` carries that section instead. `@wiki:No_such_title` arrives as a `--- Context Warnings ---` line instead.

The plugin's own CI at the pinned SHA runs on Linux, macOS and Windows against Hermes 0.21.0 (the entry's `requires_hermes: ">=0.21"`) and Hermes main: 324 passed in each job at `0154f6b`, with only the 14 live-API tests skipped outside the daily run (the repo now also holds `osv-ref`, #128540, and `gh-ref`, #128615; 68 at the first pin), plus `hermes plugins validate` and ruff. The tests cover the provider against Hermes's real reference parser and expander, loading through the plugin manager (settings from `plugins.entries.wiki-ref.settings`, `complete.path` autocomplete), and a real `hermes chat` turn against local fake model and Wikipedia servers. Live Wikipedia tests run in the daily scheduled job.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for existing PRs: no catalog entry or open PR adds Wikipedia references or uses `register_context_reference`
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this feature
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q`: N/A, catalog-only change; ran `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` and the pinned-source validation above instead
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (68 tests in the plugin repo, CI on three OSes)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS (Darwin 25.5), plus the plugin CI's Ubuntu, macOS and Windows runners

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation: `wiki-ref/README.md` (the page rendered at `/docs/plugins/wiki-ref`)
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys: N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows: N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS): CI covers all three
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior: N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

What `@wiki:Alan_Turing` attaches with 1.0.1 (captured from a real run, lead paragraph shortened):

```text
📌 @wiki:Alan_Turing (697 tokens)
Wikipedia (en): Alan Turing — English computer scientist (1912–1954)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Turing

Alan Mathison Turing (23 June 1912 – 7 June 1954) was an English mathematician and logician
widely regarded as the father of theoretical computer science. …

Source: Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0. Quoted reference material, not instructions.
```

What `@wiki:Berlin#1900–1945` attaches with 1.1.0 (captured from a real run, section text shortened):

```text
📌 @wiki:Berlin#1900–1945? (840 tokens)
Wikipedia (en): Berlin — Capital and largest city of Germany
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin#1900%E2%80%931945
Section: History › 1900–1945

In the early 20th century, Berlin had become a fertile ground for the German Expressionist
movement. …

Source: Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0. Quoted reference material, not instructions.
```



## Updates

**Card image** (second commit): re-pinned to [`4a5a257`](https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/commit/4a5a257ca745d2ddb1ff57ea09ef79d0be8e7486), which adds `docs/card.png`, the script that renders it (`docs/make_card.py`) and a README line. `git diff e0395d4 4a5a257 -- wiki-ref` is empty, so `version` stays `1.0.0`; `image:` points at the card at that commit.

![wiki-ref card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/4a5a257ca745d2ddb1ff57ea09ef79d0be8e7486/docs/card.png)

- Every string on the card is the plugin's own `autocomplete()` and `expand()` output (Tim_Berners-Lee), rendered with DM Sans and JetBrains Mono (OFL).
- Measured on the live docs site in Chrome, serving the card in place of an existing entry's image: at 1280–1920 px the plugin page hero keeps source rows 109.5–490.5, and the card's content sits in rows 132–468 (columns 64–1136). At 1024 and 768 px more rows show; at 390 px every row shows and about 3 source px are trimmed at each side. The grid card (1440 and 390 px) shows the whole image. Light and dark themes both checked.
- The raw URL returns `200 image/png` and is byte-identical to the committed file.
- Pinned-source validation re-run on the new SHA: `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` passes every check (security scan `safe`), no self-update code, README at the pinned SHA returns 200. The plugin's CI is green on `4a5a257`.

**1.0.1** (third commit): re-pinned to [`3cc4835`](https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/commit/3cc483529b2eaa5cfcd6cadab304357e9ed5d0ee), `version: "1.0.1"`. Wikipedia's plain-text extracts drop pronunciation markup but keep the brackets and spaces around it, so the attached lead read `Alan Mathison Turing (; 23 June 1912 – …`, `Gauss ( ; German: Gauß; …`, `Kurt Gödel ( GUR-dəl; German: [ˈkʊʁt ˈɡøːdl̩] ; April 28, …`. 1.0.1 removes the shapes seen in real extracts (an emptied first field, `(US also ;`, a leading space inside a bracket, a space between `]` and `;`, runs of spaces) and leaves ordinary text such as `printf()` or French `mot ; mot` alone.

- `git diff 4a5a257 3cc4835 -- wiki-ref`: `__init__.py` (+`clean_extract()`, version), `plugin.yaml` (version), `README.md` (the captured example now reads `Alan Mathison Turing (23 June 1912 – 7 June 1954)`). Nothing else in the plugin changed; `docs/card.png` is byte-identical, so `image:` only moves to the new SHA.
- Tests: the openings of ten real English Wikipedia extracts (Turing, Gauss, Newton, Euler, Tchaikovsky, Gödel, Sartre, Descartes, Wrocław, Curie) as fixtures, ordinary-text cases that must not change, and a live check that the Alan Turing lead no longer contains `(;`. Each rule, the call in `render_article()` and three over-broad variants (any space before `;`, dropping `()`, collapsing newlines) were mutated in turn; each mutant made a test fail.
- The plugin's CI is green on `3cc4835`: [run](https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/actions/runs/36637557550). Pinned-source validation re-run on the new SHA: `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` passes every check (security scan `safe`), no self-update code, README at the pinned SHA returns 200 and shows the cleaned example; `hermes plugins install wiki-ref --enable` from this branch records `sha: 3cc48352…` and `plugins search` shows `1.0.1 @ 3cc48352`; the card URL returns `200 image/png`, byte-identical to the file.

**1.1.0** (fourth commit): re-pinned to [`0154f6b`](https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/commit/0154f6bfaafc837cc4af78742e6db7c087d5b5a7), `version: "1.1.0"`. A `#Section` part used to be ignored with a note (`section links are not supported; attached the lead section`). Now `@wiki:Title#Section` attaches that section with its subsections, the heading path (`Section: History › 1900–1945`) and a link to the anchor.

- Same host and still one request: without `exintro` and with `exsectionformat=wiki`, TextExtracts returns the article's plain text with `== Heading ==` lines, and the section is cut locally, so the section name never leaves the machine. Checked on real answers: Berlin 74 kB, United States 95 kB and World War II 86 kB come back whole, well under the 2 MiB cap.
- Headings match regardless of case and underscores (`@wiki:Alan_Turing#early_life_and_education`). An unknown section attaches nothing; the warning suggests the heading that starts with or contains what was typed, else the closest spelling, and lists the sections: `no section 'early life' in 'Alan Turing' on en.wikipedia.org; did you mean 'Early life and education'? Sections: …`. A section with no text in the extract (Notes, References) is reported rather than attached empty.
- Autocomplete stays quiet once a `#` is typed: Wikipedia answers `Berlin#Hi` with titles such as `Berlin High School`, and picking one would replace the section being typed.
- Hermes's parser keeps `#Section` in a bare value and inside quotes (`@wiki:"New York City#Early history"`) on both 0.21.0 and main, but ends a quoted value at the closing quote, so `@wiki:"New York City"#History` loses the section. The README says so and a test pins it.
- `git diff 3cc4835 0154f6b -- wiki-ref`: `__init__.py`, `plugin.yaml` (version, description), `README.md`. `docs/card.png` is byte-identical (sha256 `129ce048…`), so `image:` only moves to the new SHA; the catalog description mentions sections and keeps its disclosure.
- Tests: section cutting on a fixture trimmed from the real Berlin answer, heading paths, case and underscore matching, exact-over-folded precedence, the suggestions, empty sections, truncation, autocomplete after `#`, the parser round trip, a section through Hermes's expander, a real `hermes chat` turn against the fake Wikipedia server, and live checks that every `==` line of three real articles has the heading shape the cutting relies on. 18 mutants (each rule and branch of the change) were applied one at a time; each made a test fail.
- The plugin's CI is green on `0154f6b`: [run](https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/actions/runs/36766709247), 324 passed in each of the six jobs. Pinned-source validation re-run on the new SHA: `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` passes every check (security scan `safe`), no self-update code, README at the pinned SHA returns 200; `hermes plugins install wiki-ref --enable` from this branch records `sha: 0154f6bf…`, and `plugins search` shows `1.1.0` under `web`; the card URL returns `200 image/png`, byte-identical to the file.

## What it does

**hermes-anilist** tracks anime for Hermes Desktop. A status-bar chip names the next episode of your own
list with a countdown; its popover is the airing feed, sectioned by local day. A workspace tab holds the
season browser and a **My list** view, and each show gets a page: the next episode, a month calendar of
its air dates, an episode table, tracking controls, and a one-click alert. Alerts are cron jobs that
survive closing Hermes, and an optional daily digest carries what airs from your list. Two agent tools —
`anilist_list` and `anilist_show` — let the model read the list you actually track and answer about one
show, plus a bundled skill that teaches when to reach for them.

- Repo: https://github.com/BatataBF/hermes-anilist (MIT), pinned at
  `0081dfd7b45a469eef1ec35d3d0797318694c640` — the `v0.9.0` release commit plus a documentation-only
  commit on top of it. `git diff v0.9.0..<pin>` touches no file the plugin runs; the two commits differ
  only in `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and this entry's own local copy.
- One package: root `plugin.yaml` + `__init__.py` + `tools.py` (the two tools), `dashboard/plugin_api.py`
  (the only AniList client — routes, cache, rate budget, normalization) and `desktop/plugin.js`.
- `requires_hermes: >=0.21`; category `desktop`; 2 declared tools, 0 hooks, 0 middleware, no required env.
- The desktop half registers its chip, palette commands and panes only while its own backend answers on
  the **active connection**, so a device pointed at a host without the plugin shows nothing at all. It
  uses only the plugin SDK — no prototype patching, no `eval`/`new Function`, no script injection.

## Disclosures

- **No credential is required to install or to read.** The AniList token is optional, appears only after
  the user signs in from the pane, and lives in the profile's `.env`. The renderer never holds it: it
  only ever travels *to* the backend, and answers carry public data plus a `connected` flag.
- **One outbound host: AniList.** `graphql.anilist.co` only, through a single HTTP client and cache
  shared by the pane and the tools, inside AniList's ~30 req/min budget. No telemetry, no other endpoint.
- **No self-updater.** Updates arrive only through a new pin here plus `hermes plugins update hermes-anilist`.
- **No `tools.override`, no LLM access, no shell.** `hermes plugins validate` reports `safe`.

## Verification

Replayed this PR's own checks:

- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` → **`OK: 1 file(s) valid`**.
- Cloned the plugin and `checkout --detach` at the pin (what `pinned-source-validate` does):
  `hermes plugins validate` → **`Validation passed`** — `security scan — safe`,
  `desktop surface — stays inside the plugin SDK surface`, `declared tools — matches registrations`.
- Self-updater gate (`releases/latest|raw.githubusercontent.com` next to `writeTextFile|renamePath|writeFile(`)
  → **no hits**.
- `hermes plugins doctor --ci` → OK, 2 tools / 0 hooks.
- The plugin repo's CI runs the same validator on every push: **green** on this commit
  (`hermes plugins validate`, plus the backend suite — 104 tests — and the desktop half's checks).

## Screenshots

The status-bar chip and its popover, from the app itself:

![The chip and its popover: the airing feed sectioned by local day, a row's hover action, and the two doors out](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BatataBF/hermes-anilist/0081dfd7b45a469eef1ec35d3d0797318694c640/docs/screenshots/popover-upcoming.png)

The season browser, and a show page:

![The Catalog tab: a season and year with the search box above and starred rows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BatataBF/hermes-anilist/0081dfd7b45a469eef1ec35d3d0797318694c640/docs/screenshots/workspace-catalog.png)

![A show's page: the next episode card, the calendar of air dates and the episode list](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BatataBF/hermes-anilist/0081dfd7b45a469eef1ec35d3d0797318694c640/docs/screenshots/workspace-show-page.png)

items.body:
## Root cause

Three stacked, individually deliberate denials crippled the Bot Mode Skills Hub
embed (`#91612`; the two other embeds named in the original report were since
deleted by the native catalog):

1. `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/skills-hub.tsx` — iframe sandbox
   omitted popups and had no `allow="clipboard-write"`, so external links and
   the Copy controls did nothing.
2. `apps/desktop/electron/window-open-policy.ts` — the CVE-2026-70608 handler
   denies every `window.open`/`target=_blank` with no trusted-origin delegation
   to the audited `openExternalUrl`.
3. `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` — `installMediaPermissions` refuses
   `clipboard-sanitized-write` for every origin.

Additionally no `will-frame-navigate` guard exists, so the hub frame can
self-navigate off the picker URL into the un-embeddable docs site (macOS data
point in the issue: `/docs/skills?embed=picker` → `/docs` →
`/docs/getting-started/installation`), after which its links are dead too.

## Fix

All carve-outs are gated on the EXACT hub origins (Vercel docs site + the
GitHub Pages mirror) via a new `hub-iframe-policy.ts` — an opaque sandboxed
frame (origin `'null'`, i.e. artifact previews) never qualifies.

- **iframe**: `allow="clipboard-write"` +
  `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox"`.
- **window-open policy**: `{action:'deny'}` stays unconditional (CVE-2026-70608
  posture preserved, comment block kept). New optional
  `TrustedWindowOpenOptions {getOpenerOrigin, openExternalUrl}`: a hub-origin
  opener plus an http/https/mailto URL delegates to the audited `openExternalUrl`
  as a side effect of the deny — a window is never created from this path, and
  non-hub openers trigger no side effect at all. Throwing probes/observers/
  openers cannot change the decision.
- **permissions**: `clipboard-sanitized-write` granted to hub origins only
  (request and check handlers); clipboard reads stay denied everywhere.
- **frame pinning (new vs both source PRs)**: `will-frame-navigate` in the main
  window denies a hub frame's escape off the picker URL and reloads it onto the
  picker; main-frame and non-hub-frame navigations are untouched.

## Security review note (please verify)

The maintainer should confirm (a) the `openExternalUrl` side effect is gated on
`getOpenerOrigin()` returning EXACTLY a hub origin and the URL scheme being
http/https/mailto (both asserted by tests), and (b) the deny envelope never
becomes allow (asserted for every test case, including throwing callbacks).

## Checks run (real commands + results)

- Red on base (policy): with `window-open-policy.ts` reverted to origin/main,
  `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism
  electron/window-open-policy.test.ts` fails 3/12 (the delegation cases — on
  base there is no trusted path at all).
- Red on base (component): with `skills-hub.tsx` reverted to origin/main, the
  picker suite fails the new sandbox/allow posture test 1/13.
- Green: `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism
  electron/window-open-policy.test.ts` — 12 passed.
- Green: `npx vitest run --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism
  src/plugins/hermes-bots/skills-hub-picker.test.tsx` — 13 passed (fetch
  stubbed; no source-text reading anywhere).
- `npx tsc --noEmit --ignoreConfig --strict electron/hub-iframe-policy.ts
  electron/window-open-policy.ts` — clean.

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/97945 — Thanks
  @sylvesterkaczmarek (the exact-origin/scheme predicate design and the
  permission-handler wiring are theirs; two of its three iframe call sites were
  deleted on base by the native catalog, and its source-regex test is replaced
  by component-behavior assertions).
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/116223 — Thanks @lepkov
  (its `allow="clipboard-write"` idea is folded in; its only target file was
  deleted on base).

Fixes #91612

items.body:
## Summary

On macOS, when the agent opens a file via a tool call (`open <file>` / `open -a <App> <file>`), the command returns exit 0 and genuinely opens the document — but the window lands **behind** the maximised Hermes window, so the user sees nothing while the agent reports success. Root cause: the tool shell runs as a child process of the Electron app, and macOS does not let a non-frontmost process hand activation to another app, so the implicit activation that normally accompanies `open` is silently ignored. `osascript … activate` alone is also unreliable — it returns 0 while focus lands elsewhere.

This PR appends a **verified raise-ladder** to file-opening `open` invocations instead of trusting the exit code:

- **`tools/terminal_tool_macos_open.py`** (new) — `_transform_macos_open_command()`, a pure deterministic string rewrite (no subprocess at transform time) gated to Darwin, that detects only file-opening `open` forms and appends a ladder: check `frontmost` → `osascript activate` → `lsappinfo setfront` → re-issue `open -a` → unminimise + activate, then settle ~0.8 s, re-check, and re-assert once to absorb a queued activation from another app. Each rung is verified before escalating. The not-front branch gets one extra activate + 0.4 s, and the tool output reports from the **final observed frontmost state** — naming the app that actually holds focus when another app wins the race, so a focus race can no longer read as plain success.
- **`tools/environments/base.py`** — `_prepare_command()` applies the transform before the existing sudo transform (they compose; `_prepare_command` is the single funnel every terminal backend routes through, so all sibling call paths are covered). No-op on Linux/Windows.
- **`tests/tools/test_terminal_macos_open.py`** — 24 regression tests passing the platform as data (`system="Darwin"` / `system="Linux"`) covering the transform matrix, no-op flags (`-R -e -t -f -W -n -g -h -b -D`), non-`open` commands, compound commands, and the final-outcome reporting.

## What is not exercised live

The ladder and its outcome reporting were validated as a pure decision-logic rewrite (transform matrix + unit tests) on this Mac. The **actual raise behaviour against the live macOS window server** — maximised Hermes, `open -a Preview <pdf>` through the terminal tool, confirming the Preview window lands frontmost — needs a real desktop session and is not covered by these tests; a ladder rung returning 0 is not a pass on its own. That live verification remains open for this issue.

## Tests

- Red on `origin/main`: `PYTHONPATH=<main-archive> pytest tests/tools/test_terminal_macos_open.py` → collection error, `ModuleNotFoundError: tools.terminal_tool_macos_open` (exit 2).
- With fix: `HERMES_PYTHON=<run>/test-venv/bin/python bash scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tools/test_terminal_macos_open.py` → **24/24 passed** (exit 0).
- Sibling regression: same runner, `tests/tools/test_terminal_tool.py tests/tools/test_base_environment.py` → **33/33 passed** (exit 0).

Fixes #95261

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/95286 (based on its raise-ladder approach; thanks @Jackal991 — its commit is cherry-picked here with authorship kept).

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

`activate` now only activates an interactive shell, and `scripts/run-in-hermes-env CMD...` runs one command in the dev environment.

Before, `activate` did two jobs. Humans sourced it to get a reversible environment, a `hermes` function and a prompt prefix. Scripts sourced it too (through `hermes_ensure_activated`), which is why it carries a `--` argument guard, why `run_tests.sh` switches off `errexit` around it, and why a script had to tolerate a prompt and shell functions it never wanted.

|  | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Interactive shell | `source ./activate` | `source ./activate` |
| Repo Python script | shebang → `scripts/_hermes-python` → sources `activate` → `python3` | shebang → `scripts/run-in-hermes-env python3 <script>` |
| `scripts/run_tests.sh` | sources `activate` into its own shell | re-executes itself under `run-in-hermes-env` unless the inherited env is current |
| Any other command | source `activate` first | `scripts/run-in-hermes-env CMD...` |
| Env → shell syntax | inline Python inside `activate` | `python -m pm.environments --format sh` |

There is no compatibility layer. `scripts/_hermes-python` and `hermes_ensure_activated` are deleted.

fish support was split out of this PR and is stacked on top of it in the next PR (`ethie/activate-fish`).

## Related Issue

None.

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [x] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

One behavior change rides along, stated under "One decision" below: the runner's staleness now includes the test environment.

## Changes Made

- `scripts/_activation.sh`: now the shared library (`hermes_sync`, `hermes_bootstrap_python`, `hermes_compose_env`, `hermes_apply_env`, `hermes_activation_current`, `hermes_ensure_env`). It holds the MSYS path fix-up that used to live in `activate`.
- `activate`: shrinks to the interactive part. It sources the library, snapshots the keys it will change, applies the env, defines `hermes` and the prompt hook, and defines `deactivate`. It unsets the library functions from the user's shell when it finishes.
- `scripts/run-in-hermes-env`: renamed from `scripts/_hermes-python`, now runs any command instead of only `python3`. The 9 Python scripts that used the old shebang point at it.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh`: replaces "source `activate --`" with a re-exec under the runner. `__HERMES_TESTS_REEXEC` stops a loop if the runner cannot produce a current env. The `HERMES_PYTHON` path for the Nix devShell and minimal CI lanes is unchanged.
- `pm/environments.py`: `--format json|sh` (default `json`, so `activate.ps1` is unaffected).
- Docs: `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `website/docs/reference/package-management.md`.

## One decision

A plain `hermes pm install` does not build the test environment, and the runner now treats that install as stale.

- Before: only `run_tests.sh` checked for the test environment, so scripts ran against an install without it.
- After: every environment the library composes includes it, so one consumer cannot be current while another is stale.
- Cost: one extra sync after a plain install.
- Revert: drop the `.test-environment` clause in `hermes_activation_current`.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/pm/test_activate_scripts.py tests/pm/test_activation_runtime.py tests/pm/test_environment_script.py tests/pm/test_activation_setup.py tests/scripts/test_run_in_hermes_env.py tests/scripts/test_activation_guard.py tests/scripts/test_bash_shebangs.py`
2. `scripts/run-in-hermes-env bash -c 'echo $__HERMES_ACTIVATED'` from any directory.

Tests are split along the same seams:

- `tests/pm/activation_support.py`: shared fixtures, previously imported out of another test module.
- `test_activate_scripts.py` and `test_activation_runtime.py`: bash and PowerShell activation.
- `test_environment_script.py`: env-script quoting.
- `tests/scripts/test_run_in_hermes_env.py`: the runner's staleness. It replaces `test_hermes_python_prologue.py` and adds three tests: arguments and exit status pass through, a failed sync runs nothing, no command is a usage error.

| Result | Count |
| --- | --- |
| Passed | 28 |
| Skipped (Windows-only activation tests) | 8 |
| Failed | 0 |

Removing the `.test-environment` clause from `hermes_activation_current` turns `test_install_that_skipped_the_test_environment_is_stale` red (15 pass, 1 fail in `test_run_in_hermes_env.py`), so that test does detect the change.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — ran the seven files above through `scripts/run_tests.sh`, not the full suite
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: NixOS (Linux x86\_64), bash

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [ ] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — the MSYS path fix-up moved verbatim into `hermes_apply_env`, but the 8 Windows-only tests did not run here; macOS not run
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

```
=== Summary: 7 files, 28 tests passed, 0 failed, 8 skipped (100% complete) ===
```

## Infographic

![activate stops doing two jobs](https://files.catbox.moe/da8a5y.png)

Submitted by the repository owner (rule 5). Companion to #128222 (`healthrelay`), but independent of it.

**What it is:** a portable Agent Plugins v1 package of ten skills (setup, weekly review, concerns check, nutrition review, energy target, labs review, module management, and three for the opt-in GLP-1 monitoring module) that drive a separately installed `health-insights` command line tool (`pipx install git+https://github.com/mwdearing/hermes-health-insights`). The plugin itself contains no executable, no MCP entry and no dependencies. The tool computes trends and rule-based findings from a self-hosted HealthRelay / Health Bridge receiver database; the agent only explains the output.

- Repo: https://github.com/mwdearing/hermes-health-insights, pinned to `a4df1055e5153e9f0fd4eb0a668332b120e2788a` (0.3.1) (see the entry's `sha`)

- No self-updating code, no hooks, no registered tools (the capabilities block is empty and matches).
- Personal integrations (medication counts, push command, local-model wording) are off by default; without a model configured a fixed template writes summaries.

**Checks run at the pinned SHA**
- `hermes plugins validate` passes (portable manifest, manifest fields, security scan: safe).
- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` passes with the entry added (350 files valid).
- `hermes plugins install mwdearing/hermes-health-insights --no-enable` from GitHub works; `pip install` of the CLI from the same repo works in a clean venv; the repository's 458 tests pass there.

**Disclosure (also in the entry description):** it handles sensitive health data, so it is meant for a local model or one the user trusts with that data. Informational only, not medical advice.

**Update (0.2.0):** adds an opt-in modules system (all modules off by default, `health-insights modules list|enable|disable|info|report`) and a GLP-1 monitoring module with three skills. Findings are worded as information, never advise on medication, and are linted for that in the test suite. Still no executable, hooks, tools or MCP entries in the plugin.

items.body:
## Root cause

Task-scoped process queries filtered on the collapsed **container key** (`session.task_id`) instead of the raw spawning owner (`owner_task_id`). The container key is shared across turns and delegate children, so a delegate child's own background work was invisible under its raw `sa-...` id: empty `process_list` results, missed reaps, ownerless PIDs.

Most of the query surface (list / snapshot / kill_all / completion-wait) was already fixed on `main` by 529d683d6a3. Two gaps remained:

1. `has_active_processes()` still matched the container key alone — a delegate child's running background process answered `False` where the (already-fixed) list/snapshot paths saw it.
2. `wsl[.exe]`-launched spawns recorded the short-lived launcher's host PID with no indication that the real workers live on the Linux side and outlive the launcher.

## Fix

- `has_active_processes()` now matches `owner_task_id`, consistent with the sibling query paths fixed on main (`running_owned_by`, kill/wait sweeps all key on the raw spawning owner).
- Spawns routed through a `wsl` / `wsl.exe` launcher are stamped with a durable `wsl_chain` marker:
  - persisted in the crash-recovery checkpoint (`_CHECKPOINT_FIELDS`),
  - set at registration time via a first-token check that tolerates Windows path forms (`C:\...\wsl.exe`) and quoting,
  - surfaced in `process_list` entries as `wsl_chain: true` plus a `wsl_note` pointing at `wsl -e ps` / `wsl --list --running`, so the recorded host PID is never mistaken for the Linux-side workers.

## Tests

`unset PYTHONPATH; scripts/run_tests.sh -j 1 tests/tools/test_process_registry_owner_chain_120546.py` — run twice (pre-rebase and post-rebase onto `origin/main`):

```
=== Summary: 1 files, 8 tests passed, 0 failed ===
```

8/8 covering: ownership-chain matching for `has_active_processes` (delegate-child raw id vs container key), WSL launcher detection across command spellings (`wsl`, `wsl.exe`, quoted, absolute Windows path, `cmd /c wsl ...` negatives), checkpoint round-trip of `wsl_chain`, and `process_list` surfacing of the `wsl_note`.

## System-level note

⚠️ The WSL portion is a **Windows/WSL system-level** change and needs maintainer review on that platform — please do not auto-merge. The host-side detection is unit-tested, but the Linux-side worker lifecycle (guest PID tree capture, durable WSL-side reaping) is explicitly out of scope here: the launcher exiting still moves the session to `_finished`, and guest-side PIDs are not captured. That larger follow-up is tracked in https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/120546, which stays open.

## Supersedes

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/120574 — Thanks @finn763 for the original report, reproduction, and the ownership-chain diagnosis; this carries that work forward (original commit d60225d5a2, authorship preserved via rebase-merge).

The memory-provider setup UI now lists a provider's Python dependencies from the same declaration PM installs from, so an authored `pyproject.toml` shows up instead of an empty or stale list.

## Root cause

The REST transcript projection `hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py::_project_for_display` lagged the gateway projection (`tui_gateway/session_history.py`) in two ways:

1. **Untyped scaffold rows ship as visible user rows (#109921).** A `[System: …]` role=user row persisted without a `display_kind` (e.g. the stream-timeout nudge the turn-truncation path appends) reached Desktop's transcript prefetch as a visible user row. Desktop addresses visible user rows by durable row id for rewind/regenerate, but the gateway truncation resolver refuses scaffold rows fail-closed — so a retry targeting one dead-ends every time (`refusing truncation without fallback`). The gateway's own projection drops these rows.
2. **Stored steer rows ship marker-wrapped (#121978, mechanism 2 — diagnosed in the issue thread).** `session.resume`'s projection unwraps a `role=user` `display_kind=steer` row to the user's own words; the REST projection did not, so the persisted row never paired with the optimistic plain-text copy Desktop holds — the mid-turn correction rendered twice (marker-wrapped from REST + plain optimistic) and reordered below later tool work on refresh.

## What changes

- `_is_untyped_scaffold_notice` + a `display_kind="hidden"` branch in `_project_for_display` (cherry-picked from #109922, authorship kept): rows are hidden, never dropped, so pagination offsets and "Show earlier" stay stable; typed notices (`model_switch`, …) keep flowing as timeline rows. Grafted around main's newer read-side failed-turn typing (`untyped_failed_turn_display_kind`) and tool-call-label wiring added since the PR was opened.
- A steer-unwrap branch: for `role=user` `display_kind=steer` rows, `display_content = _extract_steer_text_from_message(message)` (same shape as the compaction display branch); `content` untouched for export/inspection consumers. Rows without a resolvable marker fall through unchanged.

## Acceptance coverage

- #109921: GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages no longer ships untyped `[System:` user rows as visible/addressable; typed notices keep flowing; rows kept (offsets stable). Fully covered → Fixes #109921.
- #121978: the REST projection now unwraps steer rows (mechanism 2). Mechanism 1 — optimistic-row re-anchoring between folded tool rounds — is NOT in this PR (it lives in #121990's renderer changes); the issue is only partially covered here → partial, tracked at https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/121978.

## Tests

- `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_sessions_rest_scaffold_notices.py` — on `origin/main` (7cadfaa668): **2 failed** (scaffold-hide + steer-unwrap, the two root causes); with this branch: **4 passed** in 16.7s.
- `pytest tests/gateway/test_api_server_compaction_projection.py` — 14 passed (main's new include_compacted suite on the same projection).
- `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_session_messages_inline_images.py tests/hermes_cli/test_session_message_page_owner.py tests/hermes_cli/test_history_commentary_display.py` — 29 passed.
- `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_session_timeline.py` — 6 passed.

## Supersedes & credit

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/109922 — thanks @jahfaliabdulrahman-dev (commit f7b1d6e4bc7 cherry-picked, authorship kept, grafted onto main's current projection). #121990 remains the home for mechanism 1 (optimistic re-anchoring) and is noted as the complementary renderer-side fix; thanks @Xipong for the mechanism-2 diagnosis in the issue thread.

items.body:
## Root cause

The Electron `hermes:api` ipcMain.handle transport logs a full "Error occurred in handler" stack for EVERY rejected invoke, with no opt-out. Desktop's session resolution is a deliberate probe ladder (`resolveStoredSession`: cache -> active backend -> each other profile), so a cross-profile 404 is a normal rung outcome the renderer already handles — but each one printed a multi-line stack into the launching terminal (the reporter's ~30 traces per boot).

## What changes

- New `apps/desktop/electron/api-expected-404.ts` sentinel seam (`HERMES_API_EXPECTED_404`): the main-process handler RESOLVES an expected 404 with a sentinel instead of rejecting, so Electron's per-rejection stack log is bypassed for that one case.
- `preload.ts` unwraps the sentinel and rethrows it as an ordinary `Error` carrying the identical `404: <body>` message — the renderer contract is unchanged; only Electron's logging is bypassed.
- The 404 check is narrow (a 404 word-boundary match on the `fetchJson` error message shape) and runs BEFORE `formatApiRequestFailure`, so every other handler failure still rejects, still persists its full stack to desktop.log, and still prints.

Rebased onto the grown `hermes:api` handler (registry-pinned dispatch, profile rename/delete gate, `formatApiRequestFailure`): the sentinel return sits inside the existing catch, ahead of the failure logging, so profile-deletion and rename gating are preserved untouched.

## Acceptance coverage (#79265)

- Expected 404 from the session probe ladder no longer prints an ipcMain "Error occurred in handler" stack trace
- Every other `hermes:api` handler failure still logs in full (the sentinel is the only bypassed case; non-404 failures still hit `rememberLog(formatApiRequestFailure(...))`)
- 5 unit tests on the sentinel seam: narrow-sentinel discrimination (backend payloads can't be mistaken for one), unwrap rethrows the identical message, non-sentinel pass-through

## Tests

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run electron/api-expected-404.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` on the rebased branch: **5 passed, 0 failed**.
- Sibling suites on the same tree: `session-pin-sync` + `gateway-switch` **40 passed** (probe consumers unchanged); the PR's test file against pristine `origin/main`: **red** (`Cannot find module './api-expected-404'`).
- `npx tsc -p . --noEmit`: **exit 0**.

## Supersedes

- Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/79266 — the contributor's single commit cherry-picked with authorship kept; the branch had drifted (a merge of an old main plus unrelated in-flight commits), so the server-side rebase hit conflicts and a replacement branch was opened per the landing policy. Thanks @hernanda-git.

Fixes #79265

## Root cause

The titlebar's left hide/show button stayed pane-bound (`toggleSidebarOpen`)
while commit 0c208aa7ec made the right button positional (`toggleRightSide`,
resolving the physically-right column from the live tree). After the "Swap the
session and file browser sides" flip the sessions pane sits physically right,
so both edge buttons acted on the sessions column and the physically-left file
tree was unreachable from the titlebar — contradicting the titlebar's own
"POSITIONAL toggles" contract in `titlebar-controls.tsx`.

## Fix

Add `toggleLeftSide()` as the exact mirror of `toggleRightSide()`:

- resolve the outermost root-row column left of main from the live tree
  (`leftSideGroup()`), fold/unfold it through the tree's zone minimize so it
  round-trips like the rail chevron;
- reopen a side-collapsed column through its owner store (sidebar or files,
  whichever owns the physical side) so the persisted flags stay truthful;
- fall back to the semantic sidebar branch when no leaf column lives left of
  main (main leftmost, or a nested split);
- the titlebar button and its open-state indicator now read a new
  `$leftSideOpen` computed atom derived from the same resolution (falling back
  to `$sidebarOpen` when there is no left column).

`⌘B` keeps its pane-bound meaning (`view.toggleSidebar`); only the titlebar
button changes.

## Coverage

- Fixes #66357 — after the swap, the left button folds the physically-left
  column (the file tree) and the right button the physically-right one (the
  sessions sidebar); both columns are reachable again; the swap button itself
  already round-tripped (covered by the existing
  `layout-flipped-sides.test.ts`).

## Checks

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/store/right-side-toggle.test.ts src/store/layout-flipped-sides.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` — 13 passed
  (the 6 new left-side tests fail on base: `toggleLeftSide`/`$leftSideOpen`
  do not exist there, and the base button folds the sessions pane after a flip)
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/desktop` — clean

Fixes #66357

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds `plugin-catalog/osv-ref.yaml`, a community entry for **osv-ref**: `@cve:`, `@ghsa:` and `@osv:` context references. Writing `@cve:CVE-2024-3651` (or `@ghsa:GHSA-jjg7-2v4v-x38h`, `@osv:RUSTSEC-2023-0064`) in a message attaches that vulnerability record from [OSV.dev](https://osv.dev) to the turn: summary, aliases, severity, affected packages with version ranges and fixed versions, details and references.

A CVE record in OSV usually carries only upstream git commit ranges; the package names and fixed versions live on its GHSA / PYSEC / RUSTSEC / ... aliases. The plugin reads up to four alias records in parallel and merges their package data, each line tagged with the record it came from. So `@cve:CVE-2024-3651` arrives with `PyPI idna: < 3.7 (fixed in 3.7)`, which is what a coding agent needs when it is asked to fix a dependency advisory.

Built on the plugin context-reference API (`ctx.register_context_reference`, #26193, shipped in #84937), like `wiki-ref` (#128257, same repo). Submitted by the owner (rule 5): I maintain `EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs`.

- Repo: https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs, subdir `osv-ref`, release tag [`osv-ref-v1.0.0`](https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/releases/tag/osv-ref-v1.0.0) (rule 3; same plugin code as the pinned SHA)
- Pinned SHA: `43ab2b75e660db5edcfe2f215776294c45408b40` (1.0.0). First pinned at `bb7e1f9` (the release commit), re-pinned in the second commit to add the card; `git diff bb7e1f9 43ab2b7 -- osv-ref` is empty. The plugin's CI is green on both: [bb7e1f9](https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/actions/runs/36636659406), [43ab2b7](https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/actions/runs/36638026843)
- Category `web`: it pulls web records into the turn and registers no tools.

**Footprint** (also in the entry's `Disclosure —` sentence and the README's "Security and footprint" section):
- `register()` only calls `ctx.register_context_reference(...)` three times (`cve`, `ghsa`, `osv`): no tools, hooks, middleware or commands.
- Network: HTTPS GET to `https://api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/<id>` only, one request for the referenced id and at most four for its aliases. Ids are checked against a strict pattern before any request and percent-encoded, so a reference cannot change the request path. Redirects are followed only on the same HTTPS host; responses over 8 MiB are refused. No API key: OSV's API is keyless.
- No dependencies, no files written, no subprocess, no self-update code, no background work. Autocomplete sends nothing (OSV has no search-by-prefix API). The only environment variables involved are the standard proxy ones `urllib` honours.
- Each reference, alias lookups included, is bounded by `timeout_seconds` (default 10) plus about a second. Requests run on a plugin-owned thread pool, for the same reason as in `wiki-ref`: `preprocess_context_references` runs `asyncio.run()`, whose shutdown joins the loop's default executor. A test covers this through the sync wrapper.
- Settings (`max_chars`, `timeout_seconds`) come from `config_schema` and are read per reference. An unusable value becomes a context warning on that reference rather than a silent fallback.
- An id OSV does not have, a network failure or a timeout attaches nothing and becomes a `--- Context Warnings ---` line. When OSV's 404 names another id (unreviewed GHSA advisories: `Vulnerability not found, but the following aliases were: CVE-2024-3094`), the warning quotes it.

## Related Issue

Uses the extension point from #26193 (shipped in #84937). Not a fix.

Related entries, different mechanism: `shodan`'s `shodan_cve` is a tool the model calls, backed by Shodan CVEDB (CVSS, EPSS, KEV, affected CPEs); osv-ref is a reference the user writes, backed by OSV's package-level data (ecosystem, version ranges, fixed versions). They complement each other. Hermes core's `tools/osv_check.py` also queries OSV, but only to block `MAL-*` malware advisories before an MCP `npx`/`uvx` launch; osv-ref is a user-facing lookup of any record.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality): new catalog entry

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/osv-ref.yaml` (new), in two commits: the entry pinned at the release commit, then the re-pin that adds `image:`. All `capabilities` lists are empty, matching what the plugin registers at the pinned SHA.

## How to Test

1. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` → `OK: 350 file(s) valid`
2. Clone the repo at the pinned SHA → `hermes plugins validate --install-deps osv-ref`: every check passes, security scan `safe`; the self-updater grep finds nothing; `osv-ref/README.md` at the pinned SHA (the docs page source) returns 200. Also run at the first pin `bb7e1f9`, same result.
3. `hermes plugins install osv-ref --enable` with this branch's catalog → `.hermes-catalog.json` records `sha: 43ab2b75…`, `plugins list` shows `catalog:community@43ab2b75`, the plugin directory holds only `plugin.yaml`, `__init__.py` and `README.md`; `hermes plugins search osv-ref` lists it under `web` as `1.0.0 @ 43ab2b75`.
4. With that catalog-installed plugin, `hermes chat -q "Does @cve:cve-2024-3651 affect idna 3.6?" --oneshot` (local fake model, real `api.osv.dev`) → the user message sent to the model carries the block shown below under `--- Attached Context ---`. An unknown id such as `@ghsa:GHSA-aaaa-bbbb-cccc` arrives as a `--- Context Warnings ---` line instead (covered by the plugin's end-to-end test).

The plugin's own CI runs on Linux, macOS and Windows against Hermes 0.21.0 (the entry's `requires_hermes: ">=0.21"`, checked out at its release tag so the version gate is exercised) and Hermes main: 194 passed in each job at `43ab2b7` (178 at `bb7e1f9`), plus `hermes plugins validate` for each plugin and ruff. The tests cover the providers against Hermes's real reference parser and expander, loading through the plugin manager next to `wiki-ref` (settings from `plugins.entries.osv-ref.settings`, `complete.path`), and real `hermes chat` turns against local fake model and OSV servers. Live OSV tests run in the daily scheduled job. Each safety and correctness property (the id pattern, percent-encoding, the same-host redirect rule, the 8 MiB cap, the trickle deadline, the plugin-owned executor, the timeout, the alias cap and shared deadline, the settings checks, 404 handling, output caps) was mutated in turn; each of the 33 mutants made a test fail.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for existing PRs: no catalog entry or open PR adds CVE / GHSA / OSV references; searched `osv`, `cve`, `ghsa`, `vulnerability`, `advisory`
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this feature
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q`: N/A, catalog-only change; ran `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` and the pinned-source validation above instead
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (194 tests in the plugin repo at the pinned SHA, 106 of them osv-ref unit tests, CI on three OSes)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS (Darwin 25.5), plus the plugin CI's Ubuntu, macOS and Windows runners

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation: `osv-ref/README.md` (the page rendered at `/docs/plugins/osv-ref`)
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys: N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows: N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS): CI covers all three
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior: N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

What `@cve:CVE-2024-3651` attaches (captured from a real run, details and reference list shortened):

```text
📌 @cve:CVE-2024-3651 (631 tokens)
OSV: CVE-2024-3651 — Denial of Service via Quadratic Complexity in kjd/idna
https://osv.dev/vulnerability/CVE-2024-3651
Aliases: GHSA-jjg7-2v4v-x38h, PYSEC-2024-60
Published 2024-07-07 · Modified 2026-09-08
Severity: CVSS_V3 CVSS:3.0/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H [CVE-2024-3651]
Severity: CVSS_V3 CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H [GHSA-jjg7-2v4v-x38h]
Severity: CVSS_V4 CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N [GHSA-jjg7-2v4v-x38h]
Severity: CVSS_V3 CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H [PYSEC-2024-60]
Severity label: MODERATE [GHSA-jjg7-2v4v-x38h]
Weaknesses: CWE-1333, CWE-400

Affected packages:
- PyPI idna: < 3.7 (fixed in 3.7) [GHSA-jjg7-2v4v-x38h]
- PyPI idna: >= 0.1, < 3.7 (fixed in 3.7) [PYSEC-2024-60]

Details:
A vulnerability was identified in the kjd/idna library, specifically within the `idna.encode()`
function, affecting version 3.6. …

References:
- ADVISORY https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-3651
- ADVISORY https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jjg7-2v4v-x38h
- FIX https://github.com/kjd/idna/commit/1d365e17e10d72d0b7876316fc7b9ca0eebdd38d
…
(+5 more on the OSV page)

```

**Card** (second commit): `image:` points at `docs/osv-ref-card.png` at the pinned SHA.

![osv-ref card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/43ab2b75e660db5edcfe2f215776294c45408b40/docs/osv-ref-card.png)
