## Problem

Closes #79833 — with Inline Embeds set to "Always", an X/Twitter card that auto-loads in one session keeps painting over the whole UI after switching to another session, the Artifacts view, or Settings. It also survives a renderer reload (Ctrl+R).

## Root cause

Keep-alive tabs stay **mounted** when inactive and are hidden with `visibility: hidden` (not `display: none`) so their layout box — and with it the scroll position — survives a tab round-trip (`pane-shell/tree/renderer/tree-group.tsx`). But CSS `visibility` is inherited-*and-overridable*: Twitter's embed script renders its card into a sandbox element with an **inline** `visibility: visible` (`platform.twitter.com/widgets.js`), which CSS then lets paint through the hidden pane over the active view. It returned after Ctrl+R because the tab layout and the embed mode ("always") are persisted, so the embed re-auto-loads.

Plain-iframe embeds (YouTube, Spotify, maps) do not set inline `visibility`, which is why only the X/Twitter card was affected.

## Fix

One pane-level CSS rule — every descendant of a `[data-pane-hidden]` pane follows the pane's visibility (`visibility: inherit !important`). An author `!important` rule beats the widget's inline non-important style. The fix does not require additional unmounting: the embed stays mounted and renders exactly as before when its tab is active (no re-fetch, no flicker), and scroll preservation is untouched.

## Verification

- New "hidden pane painting contract" tests in `pane-visibility.test.ts` validate the rule against the **live stylesheet** (extracted by an anchored regex, so removal/rename fails loudly): a `visibility: visible` descendant inside a hidden pane computes `hidden`; an element outside is unaffected.
- Real-Chromium (Electron 40) probes: with the rule, a widget-style card inside a hidden pane computes `hidden`; without the rule it computes `visible` (bug mechanism reproduced); cards outside hidden panes stay `visible`.
- Full desktop UI suite: 4525 tests passed (480 files, 2 skipped); `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Notes

- **Open question:** a widget that set `visibility: visible` on elements *inside* a shadow root (rather than on the host, which is what Twitter's script does) would not be covered — CSS cannot select into shadow roots. No known provider (Twitter/Instagram/TikTok, all checked) does this; if one appears, the follow-up is gating widget embeds on pane visibility in `social-embed.tsx`.
- **Open question:** the rule cannot win against a widget that set inline `visibility: visible !important`; today's widget scripts use plain inline styles.

items.body: ## Description In Hermes Desktop, sending a message that combines an image or file attachment with a slash command (e.g. `/moa `) silently degraded: the command was **not executed**, the user received **no indication**, and the command text was delivered to the model as ordinary prose processed by the current base model. I traced the root cause to two layers: 1. Desktop skipped slash command dispatch whenever `attachments.length > 0` across all three submission paths (`use-prompt-actions/index.ts`, `use-composer-submit.ts`, `session-tile-actions.ts`). Instead of notifying the user of the conflict, the draft silently fell through to `submitPromptText`. 2. Gateway `MessageEvent.is_command()` only checked `lstrip().startswith("/")`, which failed when Desktop prepended attachment reference tags like `@image:` or `@file:` to the payload. ### Fix Details - **Desktop UI**: Restructured the slash command check in `use-prompt-actions/index.ts`, `use-composer-submit.ts`, and `session-tile-actions.ts`. When a slash command is submitted alongside attachments, I now trigger an explicit warning toast (`slashCommandIgnoredTitle` / `slashCommandIgnoredBody`) rather than silently routing to plain prompt submission. - **i18n**: Added missing translation strings for the warning toast in `types.ts`, `en.ts`, `ar.ts`, `ja.ts`, `zh.ts`, and `zh-hant.ts`. - **Gateway**: Added a private `_command_text()` helper in `gateway/platforms/base.py` that strips Desktop attachment-ref tags (`@image:`, `@file:`, `@url:`) before command matching, and updated `is_command()`, `get_command()`, and `get_command_args()` to use it consistently. - **Tests**: Added unit test coverage in `tests/gateway/test_platform_base.py` verifying `is_command()` and `get_command()` with various attachment-ref prefixes (including Windows paths containing spaces). Fixes #81798 Related: #79765 --- ## Environment Info - **OS**: Windows 11 - **Python**: 3.11.15 - **Hermes Version**: v0.20.0 (`main` branch) --- ## How to Reproduce & Verify ### 1. Minimal Reproducer (Python / Gateway) I created a reproducer script that verifies the Gateway payload parsing: ```python from gateway.platforms.base import MessageEvent # Desktop payload with image attachment ref prepended before slash command payload = "@image:C:\\Users\\User\\Pictures\\test.png\n\n/moa Explain this" event = MessageEvent(text=payload) assert event.is_command() is True assert event.get_command() == "moa" assert event.get_command_args() == "Explain this" print("OK") ``` ### 2. Manual Verification (Hermes Desktop UI) 1. Launch Hermes Desktop (`npm run dev` in `apps/desktop`). 2. Attach an image using the paperclip icon. 3. Type `/moa Explain this image` into the composer and press Enter. 4. **Expected**: A warning toast appears (`Command not sent — Slash commands cannot be combined with attachments...`) and the prompt is not silently sent to the base model. 5. **Control**: Remove the attachment and type `/moa Explain this image` — the MoA command executes as expected. ### 3. Automated Tests ```bash python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_platform_base.py::TestMessageEventIsCommand tests/gateway/test_platform_base.py::TestMessageEventGetCommand -v ``` All 10 tests pass clean. ### Screenshots - **With attachment**: command is blocked and warning toast is displayed. - **Without attachment (control)**: slash command executes normally. --- ## What platforms tested - **Windows 11** (primary Desktop target — Windows path handling, C:\\Users\\... refs) - **Linux** (gateway unit tests via pytest; path-agnostic cases) - macOS: not directly tested — changes are path-agnostic string handling, no platform-specific APIs introduced ## Known limitations (tracked as follow-up) - **Inline palette refs vs gateway**: Desktop now detects commands after any ref kind (folder/line/terminal) and blocks the attachment+command combo. The gateway-side ref strip still covers the wire kinds that can actually reach it from Desktop (image/file/url). Aligning the gateway regex with every palette kind, and reconciling the "Desktop blocks vs gateway executes" semantics for mixed-version clients, is a separate design change — intentionally kept out of this PR to keep the fix narrow. - **Ref and command on the same line** (command eaten by the ref pattern): not produced by the real composer format (buildContextText always joins refs and text with newlines), so it is out of scope here.

## Summary

Fixes #88842: a numeric profile id (DB row id or falsy sentinel) handed to `normalize_profile_name()` was silently `str()`'d into a real profile name — `0` became `"0"`, passed validation, and bootstrapped `profiles/0/` (a phantom profile with `state.db`/skills but no `config.yaml` on desktop first launch).

## What does this PR do?

Stops the Hermes Desktop app from spamming a console stack trace for every missing-file preview read at startup.

**Problem:** When the desktop app restores persisted state (preview tabs, pane shares, session transcripts), the renderer re-probes every file reference. References to files that no longer exist — deleted, moved, or cleared from `/tmp` on reboot — caused the `hermes:readFileText` / `hermes:readFileDataUrl` / `hermes:readFileDataUrlForAttach` IPC handlers to **reject** with `ENOENT`. Electron logs every rejected `ipcMain.handle` handler with a full stack trace, so a single stale `/tmp` reference produced 12+ noisy error blocks per launch — even though the renderer already handled the rejection gracefully as "preview unavailable".

**Fix (whole bug class, not just the symptom):**
- **Main process** (`electron/hardening.ts`, `electron/main.ts`): added `isMissingFileError()` (classifies `ENOENT`/`ENOTDIR`). All three preview-read handlers now return a structured `{ ok: false, error, message, path }` result instead of rejecting when the file is simply not on disk. All other errors still reject as before.
- **Renderer** (`src/lib/desktop-fs.ts`, `src/global.d.ts`): new `HermesReadFileErrorResult` type + `isReadFileErrorResult()` guard. The facade (`readDesktopFileText`, `readDesktopFileDataUrl`, `readDesktopFileDataUrlLocalFirst`) converts the structured result back into a thrown error, so every existing `try/catch` caller behaves identically to a rejection.
- **Raw bridge callers**: all 7 call sites that use `window.hermesDesktop.readFileText/readFileDataUrl` directly (inline preview directive, directive image, media resolution, generated image, file preview fallback, attach utils, runtime plugin loader) now guard the union result — showing "unavailable" / returning null / falling into their existing catch.

## Related Issue

Fixes #92222

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/electron/hardening.ts` — `isMissingFileError()` classifier + export
- `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` — wrap `hermes:readFileText`, `hermes:readFileDataUrl`, `hermes:readFileDataUrlForAttach` to return `{ok:false,...}` on missing files instead of rejecting
- `apps/desktop/src/global.d.ts` — `HermesReadFileErrorResult` interface; read methods return the union type
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/desktop-fs.ts` — `isReadFileErrorResult()` guard; wrappers throw on error result (preserving existing caller behavior)
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/media.ts`, `src/components/assistant-ui/inline-preview-directive.tsx`, `src/components/assistant-ui/directive-text.tsx`, `src/components/chat/generated-image-result.tsx`, `src/app/chat/right-rail/preview-file.tsx`, `src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/utils.ts`, `src/contrib/runtime-loader.ts` — guard the structured error result at raw bridge call sites
- `apps/desktop/electron/hardening.test.ts` — regression test for `isMissingFileError` classification
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/desktop-fs.test.ts` — regression test for facade converting `{ok:false}` into a thrown error

## How to Test

1. Open a preview tab pointing at a file, then delete it (or reference a path under `/tmp` and reboot, which clears it).
2. Restart the desktop app (`hermes gui`).
3. **Before:** 12+ `Error occurred in handler for 'hermes:readFileText'` … `ENOENT` stack-trace blocks in the console.
4. **After:** clean startup; the stale preview shows "preview unavailable" silently with no stack traces.
5. Run the desktop test suites: `vitest run --project ui --project electron` (7013 tests pass).

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)

```
Error occurred in handler for 'hermes:readFileText': Error: Text preview failed: file does not exist.
    at ipcPathError (…/electron-main.mjs:5137:17)

  code: 'ENOENT'
```

## What does this PR do?

`/init` resolved its project directory via `os.getcwd()` — the process launch directory — on all three dispatch surfaces (CLI, gateway, TUI/desktop). On the desktop app the process launches from the home directory, so `/init` scanned the HOME and merge-updated the home directory's `AGENTS.md` even though the session was attached to a project workspace (and its terminal commands ran in the right directory).

This PR makes `/init` target the session's ACTIVE directory:

1. **The terminal tool's per-session cwd record** (`tools.terminal_tool.get_session_cwd`) — seeded when a workspace attaches to the session (desktop project picker, `project_create`/`project_switch`, gateway `terminal.cwd`) and updated after every completed command, so it tracks `cd`. Keyed by `session_key`; dispatch sites pass it so multi-session hosts consult the right record.
2. **`agent.runtime_cwd.resolve_agent_cwd()`** — the codebase's canonical ladder (session contextvar → `TERMINAL_CWD` → process cwd), already used by the system prompt and tool surfaces.

A record for a deleted directory (removed project, linked worktree) falls through to the ladder on every surface — the guard lives in `build_init_prompt_for_cwd()`, so no dispatch site can hand a truthy-but-dead `cwd` straight through. An explicit `cwd` still wins while it exists (tests pass it directly).

## Related Issue

Fixes #96376

Related (sibling, distinct): #76902

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/init_command.py` — new `_resolve_session_cwd()` (record → `resolve_agent_cwd()` ladder); `build_init_prompt_for_cwd()` gains a `session_key` param and uses the resolver instead of `os.getcwd()`; an explicit `cwd` that no longer exists falls through to that resolver
- `hermes_cli/cli_commands_mixin.py` — CLI `/init` passes `session_key=""` (single-session CLI's `"default"` record; previous behavior preserved when no record exists)
- `gateway/run_inbound.py` — gateway `/init` (`_hm_cmd_init`) passes `session_key=_quick_key or self._session_key_for_source(source)`
- `tui_gateway/methods_tools.py` — TUI/desktop `/init` becomes a dedicated `_cmd_init` handler (replacing the generic `_prompt_builtin` factory): the session's live cwd record when it still exists, else the session's attached workspace (`_session_cwd`), else the builder's ladder
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_init_command.py` — 5 regression tests (session record, stale-record fallback, explicit-cwd precedence, ambient session key, stale explicit `cwd` fall-through)
- `tests/tui_gateway/test_init_targets_session_cwd.py` — new: drives the real `command.dispatch` handler for `/init` (live record, and a stale record falling through to the session workspace)

## How to Test

1. Attach a project workspace to a desktop session (project picker) while the process cwd is elsewhere (e.g. home dir — the default on desktop).
2. Run `/init` in that session.
3. The injected prompt now says `for the project at: <project>` and reads the project's `AGENTS.md` for merge, not the home directory's.
4. `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_init_command.py tests/tui_gateway/test_init_targets_session_cwd.py -q` — 13 passed (6 pre-existing + 5 builder regressions + 2 TUI/desktop dispatches).

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — targeted suites re-run on this rebase onto current `main`: `test_init_command.py` + `test_init_targets_session_cwd.py` (13 passed), and the other `command.dispatch` consumers `test_goal_dispatch.py` + `test_compress_lock_skip.py` + `test_composite_carrier_rewind.py` (90 passed)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11 (native, desktop app repro + pytest on the patched tree)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — docstrings on the resolver + `build_init_prompt_for_cwd`
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A (no config keys)
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — resolution uses the existing platform-agnostic session-cwd machinery; `os.path` paths only
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A (no model-tool changes; `/init` has no engine)

## Screenshots / Logs

Repro evidence is in the issue: session `20260827_212218_17afe7` — session row recorded `cwd = C:\Users\funky\AppDev\infinite-jukebox` while the injected `/init` prompt targeted `C:\Users\funky` (home dir). After this patch the resolver returns the session record first.

## Summary

- route Star Map node hits through a registered context-menu handle
- keep the app shell fallback menu on empty starfield
- preserve link, editable, terminal, Radix, and generic app menu paths
- add focused JSDOM regressions for both node hits and empty-canvas misses

## Root cause

`AppContextMenu` listens during capture and stopped propagation for the canvas before the Star Map React handler could perform node hit-testing. A canvas-wide `data-context-menu-skip` opt-out restores the node menu, but also removes the documented shell fallback from empty starfield.

The Star Map now registers a node-hit-aware handle with the app coordinator. A node hit opens `NodeContextMenu` and consumes the gesture; a miss continues through the existing DOM resolver to `shellSections()`.

## Validation

Initial implementation validation on head `dcf81836ac934668ad2fb99ab03a46336e64ca8a`:

- `vitest run --project ui src/app/context-menu/app-context-menu.test.tsx src/app/starmap` — 49 tests passed across 4 files

Follow-up `82d2385052bc9f9967221ca5f740541e53d1db83`:

## Root cause

`_dashboard_sanitize_desktop_env` (#52945) stopped Desktop-spawned **agent-shell** backends from serving the Electron renderer, but the Desktop-spawned **dashboard/serve** backend kept inheriting `HERMES_DESKTOP=1` plus `HERMES_WEB_DIST` pointing at `app.asar`. Opening that backend's loopback port in a normal browser rendered the full Desktop app without its IPC (#101748) — a replay of the original #52945 gap on a path the earlier fix didn't cover.

## What Changes

- New `electron/dashboard-web-dist.ts`: `resolveDashboardWebDist()` finds the standalone web SPA bundle (packaged `extraResources` dashboard-web-dist first, then the build tree) **without** touching `resolveWebDist()`'s renderer behaviour.
- Both backend spawn sites in `main.ts` point the child's `HERMES_WEB_DIST` at the standalone dashboard bundle, so a browser client hitting the desktop-spawned port gets the SPA, not the Electron renderer.
- Desktop's own `BrowserWindow` load path is untouched (it loads the renderer from disk).
- Regression tests in `electron/dashboard-web-dist.test.ts` cover the resolution order and that Desktop's renderer resolution is unaffected.

Salvages and supersedes #44556 (the original fix predates the TS Electron migration — thanks @dontcallmejames). Rebased over current main; authorship preserved.

Fixes #101748
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/44556

## Tests

```
cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run electron/dashboard-web-dist.test.ts --maxWorkers=2
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  4 passed (4)
```

Red on `origin/main` (`electron/dashboard-web-dist.ts` doesn't exist there; the suite can't even import). `npx tsc -p . --noEmit` on the branch: pass.

## Review note

With this change the desktop-spawned backend no longer serves **any** Electron renderer. The report's own A/B check (env-stripped second instance served the SPA fine from the same binary) already proves the standalone bundle works; `BrowserWindow`/HUD/session windows all load via `file://` (`buildSessionWindowUrl`), not from the backend. The legacy `dashboard --no-open` runtime fallback distinguished by `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN` is worth a spot-check in review (see routing notes) — no consumer found that needs the renderer from the loopback port.

## Not exercised live

Serving behaviour is platform-neutral (env + served dist) but the end-to-end loopback check was done from the report, not re-run in this session; the ready-sentinel and token handshake at `GET /` are covered by the existing startup suite which stays green.

## What does this PR do?

A remote-client hop can percent-encode an `/api/fs` path on top of HTTP's own query decoding, so a non-ASCII (CJK) filename reaches the gateway as a literal `%E5%8D%8A...` string. `_fs_path` never percent-decodes a plain path, the stat fails, and the dashboard file preview returns `404 {"detail":"File not found"}` even though the file exists (#103425).

`_fs_path` now resolves the verbatim path first and only falls back to one `unquote` retry when that path does not exist on disk:

- filenames that genuinely contain `%XX` sequences keep resolving verbatim (the fallback only fires when the literal path is missing and the decoded form exists);
- write-text opts out of the fallback so creating a literal-percent filename can never silently overwrite its decoded sibling.

## Related Issue

Fixes #103425

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/web_server_files.py`: extracted path candidate resolution into `_resolve_fs_candidate`; `_fs_path` gained a decode-retry fallback (verbatim path wins whenever it exists) behind a `decode_fallback` switch.
- `hermes_cli/web_routers/files.py`: `fs_write_text` passes `decode_fallback=False` to keep literal-percent write semantics.

items.body:
## What

The safe-sync "recreated" path in `_safe_sync_slash_commands` (`plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py`) deleted a command before re-upserting it when a non-patchable field changed. A 429 landing between the delete and the upsert aborts the sync (`_run_post_connect_initialization` records `retry_after_until` and returns), leaving the command deleted until a later fully-clean sync. On reconnect-heavy deployments the safe sync never completes cleanly, so commands like ``/model`` silently vanish from the slash picker.

Fix: drop the delete entirely and upsert alone. Discord's create endpoint overwrites same-name commands ("Returns 201 if a command with the same name does not already exist, or a 200 if it does"), so the lone upsert recreates the command while keeping it available even when a mid-sync 429 aborts the run. It also saves one mutation in Discord's small per-application command-management bucket.

The obsolete-commands delete-first loop is intentionally untouched: an upsert pushing the live total over 100 fails with 30032 (breaks ALL slash commands), so an app at the cap must shrink before creating.

## Verification

- RED: both new regression tests fail on unmodified `upstream/main` (`fail-without-fix`: `delete` awaited once; call sequence `['delete:21', 'upsert']`).
- GREEN: focused files `tests/gateway/test_discord_connect.py` + `tests/gateway/test_discord_sync_limit.py` → 16 passed (pre- and post-rebase onto current main).
- Nearby: `tests/gateway/ -k discord` → 378 passed, 1 skipped, 4 pre-existing batch-order failures in `test_discord_send.py`/`test_send_multiple_images.py` (identical on a clean tree under the same batch run).
- `git rev-list --left-right --count upstream/main...HEAD` = `0 1` (one focused commit).

## Tests

- `test_safe_sync_recreated_upserts_without_delete` — recreated path performs exactly one upsert and no delete/edit.
- `test_safe_sync_recreated_survives_rate_limit_between_mutations` — a 429 raised by the upsert never leaves the command deleted (only mutation attempted is the upsert).

Fixes #104399

Competitor note: #104461 implements the same ordering swap but keeps a redundant trailing `delete_global_command(old_id)` in a bare `except Exception: pass` — the overwrite already replaced the old command, the extra delete consumes another scarce rate-limit slot, and if Discord preserves the id on same-name overwrite it would remove the just-upserted command with the failure silently swallowed. This PR drops the delete entirely and adds regression coverage.

Auto-published by Moonsong via Path B automated pipeline.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Keeps a background secondary gateway alive across a transient WebSocket disconnect when its only remaining owner is an active-turn lease.

After a routed `prompt.submit` ACK, the per-request lease is released but the whole-turn lease must remain. Previously, the secondary's `closed`/`error` callback released that last lease, synchronously disposed the route, and set `wantOpen = false` before reconnect could be scheduled. The background session then received neither replayed outage events nor subsequent completion unless another consumer rescued the route.

Move orphaned-turn cleanup to actual secondary disposal. Transport reconnect retains the existing route and JSON-RPC replay state; explicit disposal disables reconnect and pending material-edit redial before releasing leases. Normal authoritative settlement remains unchanged.

## Related Issue

Fixes #105983

Duplicate searches covered issues and open/closed PRs using desktop reconnect, secondary gateway, turn lease, and narrower mechanism terms. Adjacent changes inspected:
- #93662 bounds primary reconnect IPC waits; it does not preserve a secondary's sole turn lease.
- #88070 handles failed primary remote boot and SSH/HTTP self-healing.
- #95084 reconciles transcript/composer state after reconnect and probes pooled remotes.
- Open #99178 changes reconnect backoff/service proof and backend sibling retirement; its gateway diff still releases turn leases on socket closure.
- Open #104871 reports whole-turn activity to the local backend pool for eviction; it does not change this disconnect teardown.

No exact competing fix found; mechanism searches repeated before publication.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/store/gateway.ts`: preserve active-turn leases on transport close/error; release them at actual disposal with reentrancy protection and cancelled pending redial.
- `apps/desktop/src/store/gateway-background-reconnect.test.ts`: exercise the real request router, registry, HermesGateway and JSON-RPC client through an asynchronous mock WebSocket. Two parameterized behavior contracts cover automatic reconnect/event replay/foreground isolation, plus explicit close/removal/prune/permanent missing-connection cleanup and same-session reuse.
- `apps/desktop/src/store/session-request-router.test.ts`: replace the old immediate-disconnect-release expectation with retention until explicit route close. Existing terminal ACK, authoritative settlement and pruning tests remain exercised.

No real remote gateway or model calls; no app/backend restart. Existing backoff policy is unchanged: this is ownership-lifetime repair, not a new retry-budget policy. Explicit teardown and permanent missing-connection failures stop retries, and authoritative session settlement releases an unpinned recovered route.

## How to Test

1. Submit on a non-selected registered remote without prewarming, selecting, or relay-pinning its gateway. Let `prompt.submit` ACK while the turn runs.
2. Drop the remote WebSocket, produce an event during the outage, and allow automatic reconnect. The outage event must replay and later completion must reach the background fan-in without changing the foreground gateway.
3. Explicitly close/remove/prune during reconnect (or remove the connection before the next lookup). There must be no later redial. Reusing the same session/route must acquire a fresh lease and settle normally.

Executed from the repository root with independently installed worktree dependencies:

```bash
NODE_ENV=development npm ci --include=dev
NODE_ENV=test NODE_OPTIONS='--max-old-space-size=8192 --localstorage-file=/tmp/hermes-h2-final-focused.json' npm --workspace apps/desktop exec -- vitest run --project ui src/store/gateway src/store/session-request-router.test.ts
NODE_ENV=test npm --workspace apps/desktop run typecheck
NODE_ENV=test npm --workspace apps/desktop exec -- eslint src/store/gateway.ts src/store/gateway-background-reconnect.test.ts src/store/session-request-router.test.ts --max-warnings 0
NODE_ENV=production NODE_OPTIONS='--max-old-space-size=8192' npm --workspace apps/desktop run build
NODE_ENV=test NODE_OPTIONS='--max-old-space-size=8192 --localstorage-file=/tmp/hermes-h2-final-full-storage.json' npm --workspace apps/desktop run test:ui
git diff --check HEAD^ HEAD
```

items.title: fix(desktop): retain background turn leases across reconnect

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #89696. When the main pane switches to a warm-cached session while another session is still streaming, the streaming session's live answer shows up inside the session just opened. It's display-only: both transcripts persist correctly. It stays on screen until the user switches away and back, or the other stream finishes.

### Root cause

`resumeSession` moves the selection to the target at entry. The target's warm runtime only gets bound after the owner-resolve / gateway-swap awaits (`resolveStoredSession`, then `ensureGatewayProfile` / `ensureGatewayAgent` / `openGatewayFor*`). Cold targets clear the foreground at entry. The warm branch skipped that clear (`if (!takeWarmCache()) { setActiveSessionId(null) ... }`), so for the whole await window **the previous chat's runtime stayed `$activeSessionId`**:

- `PRIMARY_SESSION_VIEW.$messages` reads the active runtime's `$sessionStates` slice.
- `syncSessionStateToView` / `flushPendingViewState` admit only `activeSessionIdRef.current`.

So each delta from the still-streaming turn kept painting under the new session's route. `resetViewSync()` at entry drops a pending frame, but the next delta stages a new one right away because its runtime is still active.

A re-entrant resume of the same target inside that window (route self-heal, reconnect `gatewayBecameOpen`, a repeated click) makes it worse. It sees `resumedSameSelectedSession === true` and snapshots `$messages` (still the other chat's live view) as the target's own local pending turn (`resumeStartMessages`). `preserveLocalPendingTurnMessages` then grafts the other chat's optimistic prompt and streaming reply into the **target's cache**. At that point the leak survives the original resume's rebind.

The window is only as long as the awaits, so it's short on a single local backend and long with pooled profiles or remote connections: dial, spawn, `gatewaySwitch` mutex, a `getSession` REST lookup. That matches the report, where the leak appears and then "goes away when I switch back".

### Why this shape

The comment the warm branch relied on ("A warm-cached target keeps its transcript — the cached fast-path repaints it this same tick") dates from before the gateway-swap and owner-resolve awaits sat between entry and the fast path (#71254, f7bf740640, the #89206 routing work). The fast path no longer repaints in the same tick, so the premise behind skipping the clear stopped holding.

- **Detach at entry unless the foreground already is the target.** The foreground stays bound only when it is this session's own warm runtime, i.e. a genuine same-session re-resume. Every other entry nulls `$activeSessionId` exactly like the cold path. The foreground stops being "whatever ran last" and becomes something explicitly owned.
- **Warm switches stay instant, without loosening #73646.** A target whose cache already carries persisted-display provenance for its listed owner paints at entry, display-only, through `setMessages` (the draft atom `PRIMARY_SESSION_VIEW` falls back to while unbound). The fast path re-proves provenance against the resolved owner before binding, as before. An unproven cache (possibly a compressed runtime tail) still holds the loader until REST authority lands, so the flicker guard is unchanged.
- **No new state and no new events.** The change reuses `takeWarmCache` (belongs-to validated), the existing provenance helpers, and the cold path's own clear.

A background turn keeps streaming into its own slice and cache entry. Its sidebar working state and unread dot are unaffected. The only change is that it never owns the foreground while the user is looking at a different chat.

## Related Issue

Fixes #89696

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/index.ts`
  - Clear the foreground at resume entry unless the warm target's runtime already is `activeSessionIdRef.current`.
  - Display-only entry paint for a warm target whose cache is persisted-display authority for its listed owner.
  - Updated the stale "cached fast-path repaints it this same tick" comment.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions.test.tsx`: new `WarmSwitchHarness` wiring the **real** `useSessionStateCache` to `useSessionActions`. The leak lives in the seam between resume's foreground binding and the cache's view gate, so the fake-cache `ResumeHarness` can't see it. Three cases:
  - `stops painting the outgoing live turn while the warm target waits on its gateway`
  - `never grafts the outgoing chat's pending turn into a warm target re-resumed mid-switch`
  - `paints a proven warm target at entry, never the outgoing live turn`

## How to Test

Repro (before the fix):

1. Open chat **B** so it's warm-cached, then open chat **A**.
2. Send a prompt in **A** that streams for a while.
3. While **A** streams, click **B** in the sidebar. The effect is easiest to see with a profile/remote-routed B, where the gateway swap takes a moment.
4. **B**'s route shows **A**'s live answer and keeps growing with **A**'s deltas.

Regression proof: all three new cases fail on current `main` for exactly those reasons, and pass with the fix:

```
# main (fix reverted)
× stops painting the outgoing live turn …        expected 'rt-A' not to be 'rt-A'
× never grafts the outgoing chat's pending turn … B's cache contains 'A live prompt' / 'A streaming reply'
× paints a proven warm target at entry …         pane shows A's transcript, not B's
# this branch
✓ 3 passed
```

Verification on this branch, rebased onto current `main`:

```
npx vitest run src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions.test.tsx   # 115 passed
npx vitest run src/app/session                                      # 70 files, 968 passed
npx vitest run src/app/chat                                         # 157 files, 1153 passed
npx vitest run src/components src/lib src/hooks src/contrib src/sdk src/api src/i18n src/themes src/types src/debug src/test src/*.test.ts
                                                                    # 368 files, 3008 passed
npx vitest run src/plugins                                          # 84 files, 767 passed
npx tsc -p . --noEmit                                               # 0 errors
npx eslint <changed files>                                          # 0 errors
npx prettier --check <changed files>                                # clean
```

Two unrelated results, reproduced identically with this diff reverted:

- `src/store/voice-prefs.test.ts`: 2 failures that already fail on `main`.
- `src/app/settings/custom-endpoints-settings.test.tsx`: 1 flake under full-directory load. It passes 5/5 in isolation, with and without this diff.

## What does this PR do?

Configured provider rows use durable inventory identities such as `custom:openrouter`, but that slug is only a user-config identity — it does not prove which upstream actually serves the row. Pricing dispatch previously missed all `custom:*` rows; the initial fix then proved too broad because a config key may shadow a canonical provider name while pointing at an arbitrary proxy.

This revision resolves pricing for custom rows from their **actual endpoint identity** instead of trusting the slug suffix:

- `custom:openrouter` on the real `openrouter.ai` endpoint reuses OpenRouter pricing.
- `custom:vercel` on the real Vercel AI Gateway endpoint resolves to canonical `ai-gateway` pricing.
- A row named `custom:openrouter` that points at an arbitrary proxy remains unpriced.
- Unknown, suffixless, and lookalike-host custom providers fail closed.

The same resolved pricing identity is used by live pricing, cached-only reads, and picker prewarm cache scope.

## Related Issue

Fixes #120757

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/models_pricing.py`
  - add `resolve_pricing_provider()` as the shared pricing-identity resolver;
  - require endpoint evidence for `custom:*` rows;
  - canonicalize the inferred provider before pricing fetch/cache lookup;
  - use the same resolver in `pricing_cache_scope()`.
- `hermes_cli/inventory.py`
  - pass each custom row's `api_url` into pricing lookup;
  - include the same endpoint evidence in prewarm single-flight cache scope.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_inventory_pricing.py`
  - cover real OpenRouter upstream reuse;
  - cover Vercel → `ai-gateway` canonicalization;
  - cover canonical-named arbitrary proxies;
  - reject lookalike hosts such as `openrouter.ai.attacker.invalid`;
  - cover cached-only, `_apply_pricing()`, and prewarm-scope behavior.

## How to Test

- [x] `HERMES_PYTHON=/Users/blockkonit./miniforge3/bin/python scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_inventory_pricing.py -q` — **19 passed**
- [x] `python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_aggregator_overlap_twin_upstream.py tests/hermes_cli/test_user_providers_model_switch.py -q` — **19 passed**
- [x] `python -m ruff check hermes_cli/models_pricing.py hermes_cli/inventory.py tests/hermes_cli/test_inventory_pricing.py` — passed
- [x] `git diff --check` — passed
- [ ] `tests/acp_adapter/test_named_provider_catalogs.py` — not run locally because the environment lacks the `acp` package; collection stops with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'acp'`.

## Evidence

RED → GREEN while tightening the invariant:

- Initial endpoint-identity regressions: **4 failed, 11 passed** — exposed missing `base_url` propagation and `_apply_pricing()` endpoint context.
- Prewarm identity regression: **1 failed, 15 passed** — exposed `pricing_cache_scope()` not receiving the custom row endpoint.
- Lookalike-host safety regression: **1 failed, 16 passed** — exposed that broad URL substring inference was insufficient as a pricing trust boundary.
- Final focused pricing suite: **19 passed**.

## Review follow-up

The review correctly identified that the earlier suffix-only handling left alias cases such as `custom:vercel` unresolved. The follow-up commit `de9a3622cf1911063c1d28c72e054fff7accb9d6` addresses that case while preserving a stricter invariant: a `custom:<name>` slug does not inherit canonical pricing unless its concrete endpoint proves the upstream provider. This avoids leaking canonical prices into a user-defined proxy that merely shadows a canonical config key.

The branch was not rebased or history-rewritten for this follow-up.

## What does this PR do?

The Linux minimize-to-tray probe treats a healthy StatusNotifier host as missing. dbus-native 0.15 defaults `plainValues` to true, so `IsStatusNotifierHostRegistered` arrives as the boolean `true`. The probe only accepted the older `{ value: true }` wrapper, so `value.value` was undefined and the setting always reported that no tray was available.

Accept both shapes. A missing or false flag still fails the probe.

items.body:
## Summary

Add the community God’s Eye View Desktop integration, maintained by cygnostik / ProDyn, pinned to [v0.1.1](https://github.com/cygnostik/Hermes-Plugin-Gods-Eye-View/releases/tag/v0.1.1) at `6a02e2822edb21fc34062906de6947272226dc23`. Only `plugin-catalog/gods-eye-view.yaml` changes in this PR. Media and README resolve from that same pin; the interface screenshot is identified as a historical v0.1.0 capture.

This release addresses the requested SDK migration: the Desktop bundle imports `SandboxedFrame` from `@hermes/plugin-sdk`, keeps its default opaque-origin sandbox, and removes the raw Electron webview, shared preview partition, private preload IPC, readiness probe and scripted provider-settings click. Backend `/status` reports engine state without claiming globe rendering. Provider Settings directs the user to GEV’s own settings chip. Hermes >=0.21.5 is required.

## Runtime and trust boundaries

- Windows/macOS with a local companion backend; Git, supported Node 24/26 and a separately installed official GEV checkout are required. GEV is not bundled, forked or automatically downloaded.
- Starts/stops GEV’s local Node server on loopback. Configuration remains profile-scoped outside the replaceable plugin directory. No model-facing tools, hooks, middleware or required environment variables are declared.
- On explicit request, Update engine updates that separate checkout from GitHub/npm after clean-checkout verification: fast-forward Git, `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, then explicit execution of `node_modules/esbuild/install.js`. This external engine is mutable executable code outside the catalog pin. The plugin does not self-update.
- Only on explicit opt-in, the compatibility bridge copies matching Hermes API keys into GEV’s own key store. No ambient key copying or OAuth subscription reuse occurs. Provider authentication, feed freshness and imagery rights remain upstream responsibilities.
- Backend source and controls are unchanged from the reviewed pin, including the nonblocking unused raw `POST /keys` endpoint. Start/Stop, Reload, Focus/restore, update confirmation and bridge opt-in remain covered by tests. No same-origin, popup or microphone privileges are added to the frame. Open in browser uses the SDK explicitly.

## Verification

- Local macOS: 32 backend tests (including the real Node/HTTP lifecycle fixture), 14 frontend tests, syntax and diff checks pass. A fresh npm lockfile install was used; five migration regressions fail against the original v0.1.0 bundle.
- [CI on the exact release commit](https://github.com/cygnostik/Hermes-Plugin-Gods-Eye-View/actions/runs/36849702609) runs the Windows/macOS matrix. Final outcome is recorded in the follow-up review comment.
- Plugin admission validation passes: isolated registration, declared capabilities, Desktop SDK surface, scanner `safe`, no warnings. Plugin Doctor has no findings. The current upstream Desktop lint and catalog structural validator also pass.

# plugin-catalog: add `hermes-workflows` (community, automation)

Submitted by the plugin repository owner (rule 5).

## What it is

`workflow` tool for Hermes Agent: the calling agent owns a JSON graph of agent
nodes, fan-outs and gates; a background runner executes it with fingerprint
replay-skip resume, fan-out quorum, per-node retries, cooperative steer, and
typed failure events (`error_class` + `attempts` on every `node.failed` — the
parent never infers from exit code + prose). Ships a desktop DAG view (SDK
surface only), an inline `::workflow{id}` transcript card, and the authoring
skill with measured budget recipes. Children are spawned through the stock quiet
one-shot CLI (`hermes chat --query-file … -Q --max-turns N`).

Repo: https://github.com/jacobhausler/hermes-workflows — README with
screenshots, `AGENTS.md` (agent front door: install / operate / contribute),
`INSTALL.md`.

## Catalog rules, checked at the pinned SHA

| Rule | Evidence |
|---|---|
| 2 — exact pin | `sha` = `88b1c095902f57f3d87417f0f9b86e4ceb2fb4a5`, the 40-char commit of tag `v1.1.2` (release https://github.com/jacobhausler/hermes-workflows/releases/tag/v1.1.2); `image`/`screenshots` are raw URLs pinned to the same SHA |
| 3 — no self-updater | No update checks and no remote fetches anywhere: zero `fetch(` in `desktop/plugin.js`, zero `urlopen` outside `tests/`; the plugin never loads code it did not ship |
| 6 — capabilities match | `provides_tools: [workflow]`; no hooks; no middleware; `requires_env: []` — the runner's `HERMES_WF_STEER_*` vars are plugin-internal IPC set by the runner for its own children, never user-provided (`docs/manifest-decisions.md`) |
| 7 — install scanner | `hermes plugins validate .` → `Validation passed.`, local security scan `caution`: one `system_passwd_access` finding at `tests/test_lane_recover_8edcc9bf.py:145`; validation exits 0 |
| 8 — desktop surface | `desktop/plugin.js` imports only `@hermes/plugin-sdk` / `react`; gate resumes use `host.composer.submit(ownerSessionId, text)` (visible) or SDK `insertText`; no app DOM reach or private composer events |
| 9 — dependencies | None. Stdlib-only Python; no `python_dependencies`, no `pyproject.toml` |

## Disclosure (what the plugin actually does at runtime)

Each `workflow run` starts a detached `wf.py run <id>` process, independent of
the originating session and gateway; disabling the plugin does not stop an
already-running process. It continues until a graph boundary or `workflow stop`
(subject to host process shutdown), and interrupted runs need an explicit
resume. Each agent node launches an operator-configured `hermes chat
--query-file … --oneshot -Q …` child (the launcher comes only from plugin
settings / `HERMES_WF_HERMES_BIN`, never from tool arguments), with optional
routing/budget flags and a copy of the runner environment plus workflow IPC
variables. A graph-authored gate `wait.until_argv` executes a fixed argv
command without a shell directly in the runner, outside Hermes tool approval.
Run state is stored under `$HERMES_HOME/workflows/`. The plugin registers no
cron and opens no sockets or credential-store reads of its own; however,
run/amend may issue one provider liveness request per distinct explicitly
routed model through Hermes' core auxiliary client, child agents may make
provider/tool calls with the inherited environment, the Desktop half uses the
Hermes plugin REST API, and gate commands inherit the runner environment.
Stop live runs before disabling. Clause-by-clause `file:line` evidence:
[`docs/catalog/disclosure-check.md`](disclosure-check.md).

## `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.4"` — measured, not guessed

The spawn contract needs every flag the plugin passes (`--query-file -Q
--source --create-if-missing --max-turns --run-budget --provider --reasoning
--toolsets`) in `hermes_cli/_parser.py` and the `HERMES_QUIET_TURN_REPORT_FILE`
turn-report contract in `hermes_cli/quiet_single_query.py`. Walking published
tags newest → older: `v2026.9.24` PASS, `v2026.9.21` PASS, `v2026.9.14` FAIL
(flags present, turn report absent). `v2026.9.21` is `pyproject.toml` version
`0.21.4`.

## Test evidence (verified on the published pin)

- Published tag `v1.1.2` resolves to `88b1c095902f57f3d87417f0f9b86e4ceb2fb4a5`. The squash-merged Git tree exactly matches the tested release branch tree.
- Final serial suite: TOTAL 106 FAIL 0. The first complete local attempt exposed a claim-fixture teardown race; its failed ledger is retained, the fixture now waits for the killed runner to release ownership, and all original claim assertions remain.
- Desktop ESM parse passed; `hermes plugins validate .` passed with the one local scanner caution disclosed above; `scripts/make_public.py` published 198 files with 0 scrub hits; `scripts/graph_check.py` matched 1947 nodes and 3903 edges.
- CI on final release head `cd0b902eb8ba7120aa11f4e0c0c955d6bda9d6c3`: completed-success, using the pinned Hermes commit and graphify extractor in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: https://github.com/jacobhausler/hermes-workflows/actions/runs/36800401993
- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py --json plugin-catalog/hermes-workflows.yaml` passed locally on this exact catalog entry.

## Relationship to a patched core

None required. Stock Hermes records a child that dies on its turn cap as
`error_class: unknown` (partial output and log preserved). Open PR #121041 adds
`turn_exit_reason` to the quiet turn report; with it the same death is typed
`cap_exhausted`. The plugin reads the field if present and says `unknown` if not —
nothing auto-patches anyone's core, and `status` reports which tier a failed
child ran under (`turn_report: typed|untyped`). If #121041 merges, the
distinction disappears.

fix(desktop): scope Bot Screen display.* to the bot backend profile

Problem
- Bot Mode -> Open Screen showed the SAME desktop for every bot: each pane
  attached to the launch display (:20) instead of that profile's own
  bot-desktop/rfb.sock (e.g. home-ops on :21).
- Root cause: display.* handlers are @_profile_scoped, so without an
  explicit `profile` param the gateway answers for the LAUNCH home.
  displayRequest() called host.requestProfile(route, method, params) with
  raw params, and dedicated/secondary dials (requestGatewayForAgent, and
  requestGatewayForProfile with scopeProfile=false) forward params
  unchanged - only shared-primary routes inject `profile`. The ticket was
  therefore always minted for the launch home.

Change (apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/screen-connection.ts)
- displayRequest(), the single choke point every Bot Screen RPC flows
  through (status, observe, start, stop, thumbnail, install, lease
  acquire/release), now always sends `profile`: the route's backend
  target (targetProfile || profile; bare profile name for legacy
  string routes). Caller params are preserved; the route owns the
  identity and is never overridden by a caller param.

RED -> GREEN
- screen-connection.test.ts: 2 new tests RED before (params forwarded
  with no `profile`), GREEN after (6 passed).
- Neighbors: screen-install-retention, screen-isolation,
  cross-connection-bots, sdk/profile-routing - 70 passed, 5 files.
- screen-pane-lifecycle / screen-pane-status-events do not run in this
  environment: @novnc/novnc is absent from node_modules machine-wide and
  fails identically on pristine base (import-resolution, untouched file).

Notes
- Remote-CUA PRs #104080/#103653 are feats in the computer_use transport
  area, unrelated to this attachment bug.
- Open PR #121691 (Fixes #121690) only cites this issue in its duplicate

Closes #120966

Background processes armed with a heartbeat no longer lose the lines they printed before the heartbeat was armed: the first heartbeat carries everything since spawn.

## Root cause
`ProcessRegistry.arm_heartbeat` reset `_heartbeat_total_at_last` to the *current* `total_output_chars`. The terminal tool arms the heartbeat only after its spawn bookkeeping, so a fast-starting process (`echo first; …`) had already written its first lines, and they were in no heartbeat at all (the spawn result carries no output either). On CI the gap is wide enough to fire: `tests/tools/test_process_heartbeat.py` read beats `['', '', 'second\n', '']` and lost `first`.

## Changes
- `tools/process_registry.py::ProcessRegistry.arm_heartbeat` — keep the spawn baseline (field default `0`); only the interval clock resets at arm time.
- `tests/tools/test_process_heartbeat.py` — one invariant test: arm after `first` is already in the buffer, the first heartbeat must carry it (red on base, green fixed).

## Validation
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Probe: 0.3 s gap between `spawn_local` and `arm_heartbeat`, base | beats `['', '', 'second\n']` → **FAIL (first lost)** — the CI signature |
| Same probe, fixed | beats `['first\n', '', 'second\n']` → PASS |
| New test with fix reverted (base `process_registry.py`) | FAILED (sabotage red) |
| `tests/tools/test_process_heartbeat.py` ×5 consecutive | 3 passed ×5 |
| `tests/tools/test_process_registry*.py`, `test_completed_process_results.py` | 114 passed (1 pre-existing host-only redaction failure, identical on pristine `origin/main`) |

CI evidence: main run [36033989953](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/36033989953) (`⚠ FLAKY`, `assert joined.count("first") == 1` → 0).

Flaky Test Scout (Sep 25).

## What does this PR do?

Gives the desktop app a proper macOS 26 icon and drops the brand ring from every icon output.

**macOS 26.** The system clips every app icon to its own squircle and shows legacy `.icns` art inside a glass plate, so our ringed tile picked up a grey rim and a pinched ring at the corners (#40937, #73195; #42946 moved the art onto Apple's 824-on-1024 grid, which fixed the size but not the shape). This ships the dual artwork Apple expects:

- `apps/desktop/assets/icon.icon` — an Icon Composer package that the **system** masks: the girl (light/dark variants, + the commit-flavour badge) and a grayscale **mono** layer for Clear light/dark and Tinted light/dark. In mono the parts of the girl that are black in light mode become a near-black frosted Liquid Glass ink (`0.13` @ 90%) and her white parts stay white — one image, each pixel painted once, so translucent materials never stack. The art layer hides under `tinted`; the mono layer shows only there.
- `apps/desktop/assets/icon.icns` — still generated for macOS ≤ 15 (and still on the 824 grid, like Apple's own 26-era `.icns`).

**No ring, anywhere.** Next to macOS 26's own icons the flat plate + girl reads better than the ringed tile, so `BORDER_ENABLED = False` turns the ring off in every output — tiles, favicons, appx logos, the layered icon. The ring code (including the fitted Apple mask curve: arc + cubic easing, R = 214 px on the 824 grid, smoothing 0.645, rms 0.32 px against macOS 26.6.2's own render) stays one flag away; a unit test keeps its geometry honest. Without a ring the girl's lowest nodes are dragged past the tile edge so the outline crops her instead of leaving a gap. Mac targets use a 1.06× girl (between `main`'s 1.12× and the original layers' 1.0×), identical for the `.icns` and the layers.

**Packaging.** electron-builder 27.0.0-alpha.6 compiles a `.icon` given as `mac.icon` into `Contents/Resources/Assets.car` — only with actool ≥ 26, and it replaces the bundled `icon.icns` with actool's 256 px fallback. `scripts/mac-icon.cjs` selects the package only when that actool is present (a dev Mac on Xcode 16 keeps building what it always built), the darwin release job selects Xcode 26 via `DEVELOPER_DIR` and asserts the actool version so CI can't silently ship the fallback, and `after-pack` restores our full 16…1024 `.icns`.

Two actool facts learned the hard way, both pinned by tests: a layer with a fixed `image-name` **and** `image-name-specializations` compiles only the fixed image (dark mode showed a black girl on the dark fill); and `appearance: "tinted"` is the single mono annotation behind all four Clear/Tinted styles.

## Related Issue

Fixes #40937
Fixes #73195

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `scripts/generate_icons.py` — `BORDER_ENABLED` / `EDGE_OVERSHOOT`; Apple mask curve (`mac_mask_outline`, `offset_inward`) kept; the `icon.icon` target (manifest, `art-*.png`, `mono.png` via `icon_mono_image`); `portrait_layer()` extracted so tiles and layers share girl placement; mac girl box 1.06×, layered box derived from it in plate coordinates.
- All generated icon outputs (40 targets) — regenerated without the ring; `apps/desktop/assets/icon.icon/**` added.
- `apps/desktop/scripts/mac-icon.cjs` (+ test) — `mac.icon` resolution by host actool version.
- `apps/desktop/electron-builder.config.cjs` — `mac.icon: macIconResource(__dirname)`.
- `apps/desktop/scripts/after-pack.mjs` (+ test) — restore `assets/icon.icns` over actool's fallback.
- `.github/workflows/desktop-bundled-release.yml` — darwin: select newest `/Applications/Xcode_26*.app`, fail if actool < 26.
- `apps/bootstrap-installer/src-tauri/icons/icon.icon/**` + `tauri.conf.json` `bundle.icon` — Tauri's bundler compiles the same package (unbranded) into the installer's `Assets.car`; `.github/workflows/bootstrap-installer-build.yml` selects Xcode 26 and asserts `Assets.car` + `CFBundleIconName` in the built `.app` (Tauri only logs when actool is too old).
- **DMG volume icon** — `assets/dmg-volume.png` (hand-made drive-with-the-girl artwork; volume icons have no appearance variants) → `apps/desktop/packaging/dmg-volume.icns` (kept out of the app bundle next to the DMG background) → `dmg.icon`. The default would have been actool's 256 px fallback icns once `mac.icon` is the package, and dmgbuild's `badgeIcon` can only paste onto the stock removable-drive icon. Tauri has no volume-icon option, so `scripts/bundles/set_dmg_volume_icon.sh` sets the same `.VolumeIcon.icns` on the bootstrap DMG before signing and the verify step checks it. Both DMGs render the identical volume icon on macOS 26.6.2.
- `tests/scripts/test_icon_flavors.py`, `tests/scripts/test_icon_generation_exit.py` — manifest contract (no fixed `image-name`, dark specialization, mono layer wiring), mono materials, girl reaches the plate edge, ringless tile geometry, mask-offset geometry, flavours recolour only the fill.

## How to Test

1. `SSL_CERT_FILE=… scripts/run_tests.sh tests/scripts/test_icon_flavors.py tests/scripts/test_icon_generation_exit.py` → 32 passed; `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --project electron scripts/mac-icon.test.mjs scripts/after-pack.test.mjs` → 6 passed; `npx vitest run tests-js/generate-icons.test.mjs` → 2 passed; `node scripts/generate-icons.mjs --check` → all 40 targets.
2. On a macOS 26 machine with Xcode 26: `cp -R apps/desktop/assets/icon.icon /tmp/Icon.icon && actool /tmp/Icon.icon --compile /tmp/out --output-format human-readable-text --notices --warnings --output-partial-info-plist /tmp/out/partial.plist --app-icon Icon --enable-on-demand-resources NO --development-region en --target-device mac --minimum-deployment-target 26.0 --platform macosx` → `Assets.car` + `Icon.icns`, no warnings.
3. Drop that `Assets.car` into any `.app` with `CFBundleIconName=Icon`, add it to the Dock, and cycle System Settings → Appearance → Icon & widget style through Default / Dark / Clear / Tinted (`defaults write -g AppleIconAppearanceTheme Regular|RegularDark|ClearLight|ClearDark|TintedLight|TintedDark` does the same headlessly).

Verified on macOS 26.6.2 / actool 27.0 with electron-builder's exact actool invocation; the committed package is pixel-identical to the bundle reviewed in the live Dock across all six styles. Legacy `.icns` render checked against Calculator/Safari on the same grid.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate

- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: generator + tests on NixOS; rendering on macOS 26.6.2 (M1)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — generator docstring lists the new outputs
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A

- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — Linux/Windows packaging untouched (their icons just lose the ring); non-mac hosts always resolve the legacy `.icns`
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

All icon renders below are macOS 26.6.2's own (IconServices, the same call the Dock uses), captured under each of the six icon styles; only the wallpaper and Dock pill are composited. Columns: Finder as rendered by that system · **Shipping** (`main`'s `.icns`) · three candidates, of which **NoRing** is what this PR ships (New = same layers with the ring, Frost = ring + mono).

![Six macOS 26 icon styles: Finder, shipping icon, and the candidates on a Dock](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethernet8023/hermes-pr-assets/main/pr-122976/macos26-six-appearances.png)

### Installer DMG volume icon (mounted, macOS 26.6.2)

Left: desktop DMG (`dmg.icon` → `packaging/dmg-volume.icns`, built with the same `dmgbuild` binary electron-builder downloads). Right: bootstrap DMG after `set_dmg_volume_icon.sh`. Same artwork on a light and a dark desktop — volume icons have no appearance variants.

| Light desktop | Dark desktop |

| ![DMG volume icon on a light desktop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethernet8023/hermes-pr-assets/main/pr-122976/dmg-volume-light.png) | ![DMG volume icon on a dark desktop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethernet8023/hermes-pr-assets/main/pr-122976/dmg-volume-dark.png) |

## What does this PR do?

When Nous retires a `:free` route, the provider answers HTTP 404 with a deterministic body like:

```
This model is no longer free. To continue using the paid variant, switch to 'meituan/longcat-2.0'.
```

`_status_404` ran this message through `_404_RULES` (billing → policy block → model-not-found) and nothing matched — the wording is neither the free-tier/billing vocabulary (`not available on the free tier`, `requires available credits`, …) nor the model-not-found vocabulary (`no such model`, `does not exist`, …). The verdict fell through to `_V_UNKNOWN`, i.e. `code: unknown`, `retryable: true`, which makes the retry loop burn retries on a slug that can never succeed again while the provider keeps 404-ing (#123180).

This PR adds the `is no longer free` wording to `_MODEL_NOT_FOUND_PATTERNS`, so a retired free route classifies as `model_not_found`: non-retryable, `should_fallback` armed — the same recovery the classifier already gives the structurally identical OpenRouter "no endpoints found that support tool use" 404 (#58446).

Why `model_not_found` and not `billing`: the free-tier billing wordings reject because of the *account's* tier/balance, so rotating a credential can help. A retired free route is a model-lifecycle change — the slug is dead for every credential — so the right move is falling back to a different model, not rotating or retrying.

## Related Issue

Fixes #123180

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/error_classifier.py`: added `"is no longer free"` to `_MODEL_NOT_FOUND_PATTERNS` with a comment distinguishing it from the free-tier billing wordings (4 lines).
- `tests/agent/test_error_classifier.py`: added `test_404_retired_free_route_is_model_not_found` next to the existing Nous 404 billing tests, using the provider's observed wording; asserts `model_not_found` + non-retryable + fallback armed.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/agent/test_error_classifier.py -k test_404_retired_free_route -q` — before the fix this fails with `unknown` + `retryable=True` (exact symptom from the issue); after the fix it should pass.

4. `ruff check agent/error_classifier.py tests/agent/test_error_classifier.py` — Observed result: All checks passed.

items.body:
## Problem

`resolve_persist_behavior()` treats every `--provider`-scoped model switch as exploratory — it returns `False` **before** `model.persist_switch_by_default` is ever read — so the flag is silently ignored whenever a provider is passed. That is exactly the shape the Desktop picker sends (`/model <name> --provider custom:...`).

For **twin provider pairs** — two `custom_providers` entries sharing one `base_url` with different API keys (multi-account / multi-tenant setups behind one gateway) — this silently flips tenants:

1. `hermes /model agnes-3.0-flash --provider custom:family-xizhao` (explicit pick, key B)
2. `resolve_persist_behavior(..., explicit_provider="custom:family-xizhao")` → `False`, nothing is written
3. the next chat re-derives the provider from the shared `base_url`; the scan order deterministically returns **one fixed twin**, so the request is served with key A even though key B was picked
4. wire proof in #123150: the request dump shows the snowflake key on a call that was picked as xizhao

No error, no banner — wrong credentials/quotas/billing on the call. The bare-model path already respects the flag; only the provider-scoped path bypasses it, so `persist_switch_by_default` semantics differ between surfaces.

## Fix (option A from the issue discussion)

Read `model.persist_switch_by_default` **before** the `explicit_provider` bail-out:

- `--session` / `--once` remain the explicit opt-outs (checked first, unchanged),
- `--global` still persists (unchanged),
- **without** the flag, provider picks stay exploratory exactly as today (#101287 / #90235 rationale preserved for genuinely different backends),
- **with** the flag, a provider pick persists like any other switch.

This is the minimal change from the three options in #123150. Option B (persist only same-`base_url` picks) is a narrower follow-up if maintainers prefer that blast radius; option C (keep semantics, surface it in the banner) is independent. If the reporter prefers to land their own PR for this, I'm happy to close mine.

## Root cause

On every cold start Desktop reads `spawn-ledger.json` and `spawnOrAttach()` picks the newest record unconditionally. The ledger survives the process it describes, so after any shutdown the newest record points at a dead PID — the app dials a port nobody listens on and burns the wait budget before falling through (or, on a squatted port, all of it) before spawning its own backend. The report's 45–60 s cold-start hang is exactly this dial-then-timeout loop against dead records.

## What changes

- `spawnOrAttach()` takes an optional `isPidAlive` probe and filters dead-PID records out **before** any network I/O, deciding `spawn` instead.
- The attach fallback rung in `attachToHostBackend()` skips dead PIDs too, so a stale record never costs a live one.
- `main.ts` wires the real probe (`isPidAliveWindows`, the same `process.kill(pid, 0)` pattern the spawn gate uses).
- Absent the probe the behaviour is exactly today's (dependency-injected, hot path unchanged for live PIDs).

PID reuse stays guarded by the existing boundary: a reused PID still fails the HTTP probe + session-token handshake, which is why this check is deliberately PID-only (rationale in the source comment; the reporter's `create_time` suggestion is deferred — no stdlib way to read another PID's start time, and the handshake already blocks impostors).

## Acceptance coverage

- **#123586**: dead-PID records never attach and never get dialled — covered fully. The report's secondary "Repair acts destructively against a live backend" observation is **not** covered here and should be tracked separately.

Fixes #123586

## Tests

- `a record whose pid is dead decides spawn instead of attach` / `a dead pid is skipped before any network probe runs` / `a dead newest record falls through to a live older one` / `a live pid still attaches` — all in `electron/backend-discovery.test.ts`.
- Red on `origin/main` (3 failures before any network probe ordering assertions), green with the change:

```
cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run electron/backend-discovery.test.ts electron/backend-health.test.ts electron/primary-backend-startup.test.ts --maxWorkers=2
Test Files  3 passed (3)
Tests  49 passed (49)
```

- `npx tsc -p . --noEmit` on the branch: pass.

## Not exercised live

The real PID-liveness semantics (`process.kill(pid, 0)` on Windows where the report came from) are unit-tested via the injected probe; the end-to-end cold-start timing was not measured on Windows in this session — the report's Windows repro is the natural post-merge check.

## Summary

Fixes #123988.

Allocates session file attachments atomically via `target.open("xb")` within the shared profile attachment directory to eliminate race conditions between concurrent uploads with the same sanitized filename, and ensures partial/interrupted uploads are unlinked on error.

## Problem

`_stage_session_file_attachment` previously checked `target.exists()` before writing via `target.write_bytes()`. In a shared profile namespace, concurrent uploads with identical sanitized names could observe the same non-existing filename, leading to the latter upload silently overwriting the earlier one. Furthermore, if a write failed mid-stream, partially written files were left behind.

## Changes

1. **Atomic Allocation (`tui_gateway/prompt_attachments.py`)**:
   - Use `target.open("xb")` inside a loop that increments `-<counter>` on `FileExistsError`.
   - Protect write operations with `try...except BaseException:` to clean up (`target.unlink(missing_ok=True)`) any partially written destination on failure.
2. **Regression Tests (`tests/tui_gateway/test_file_attachment_allocation.py`)**:
   - Verify concurrent uploads with identical filenames across both same-session and multi-session scenarios preserve distinct paths and exact bytes.
   - Verify failed writes remove only their partial upload without impacting concurrent successful uploads.

## What

Adds `plugin-catalog/openltm.yaml` — OpenLTM as a Hermes memory provider.

OpenLTM gives a Hermes agent durable long-term memory in a local SQLite database:
FTS5 full-text search with optional sqlite-vec vector recall, importance-weighted
decay, a queryable memory graph, and automatic capture.

## Automatic capture

Capture is a declarative rule engine rather than ad-hoc keyword lists. One ordered
rule table classifies each turn as a correction, constraint, preference, decision,
or agent-discovered fact, and distils it into a single self-contained declarative
sentence (speech markers stripped, negations preserved). Constraints are evaluated
before preferences so a rule like "Always use Bun, never npm" is stored as a
constraint (importance 4), not downgraded to a soft preference.

Named guards keep noise out: `is_transient_operational()` rejects runtime
notifications, and `is_read_only_memory_request()` rejects messages that are only
read-only OpenLTM bookkeeping. A *mixed* message still passes, so a constraint
stated alongside "call openltm_context" is kept.

`eval` time aside, capture policy is verified by 33 stdlib `unittest` tests that
need no third-party package and no Hermes runtime.

## Security notes for the reviewer

- **Secret redaction on every write.** The write path scrubs API keys, tokens, JWTs,
  private keys and connection strings before any database insert or dedup check.
- **No self-updating code** (catalog rule 3). The plugin contains no fetch, no git
  operations, and no remote loader. The only network egress is the optional
  embedding providers (Gemini / OpenAI / Ollama), which are disabled by default and
  require the operator to configure them.
- **No required environment variables** — `requires_env` is empty; it runs with zero
  configuration.
- **All data stays local** in `~/.hermes/openltm.db`. No cloud, no telemetry.
- **Declared capabilities match the pinned commit** (catalog rule 6): 8
  `openltm_*` tools and 7 hooks, all cross-checked against the plugin source by an
  automated validator.

## Admission checklist

| Requirement | Status |
|---|---|
| Owner-submitted | this PR is from the plugin repo's owner |
| Public, cloneable repo | https://github.com/RohiRIK/OpenLtm |
| Released (real tags) | yes, `v2.14.2` and later |
| Exact 40-hex SHA pin | yes |
| Passing validation | entry validated against `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` rules |
| Not self-updating | yes |

## Install

```bash
hermes plugins install openltm
```

Docs: https://github.com/RohiRIK/OpenLtm/blob/main/docs/10-hermes-plugin.md

items.body:
## Root cause

A cron run is finalised by `cron/scheduler.py::_finalize_cron_session`, which calls `SessionDB.end_session(...)` inside a `try/except` that only `logger.debug`s on failure. When the run is killed by the inactivity watchdog (or crashes on a provider/connection error), no code runs at all — the session row keeps `ended_at` NULL while no agent owns it. The desktop's orphan reap stamps it later, sometimes hours after.

Both desktop Cron surfaces rendered every run row as a clickable tile that resumed it as a normal desktop chat:

- `src/app/chat/sidebar/cron-jobs-section.tsx` → `onOpenRun(run.id)` → `onResumeSession`
- `src/app/cron/index.tsx` (`CronJobRuns`) → `onOpenSession?.(run.id)`

Neither consulted liveness or `source`, so clicking (or auto-restoring) such a run resumed it as a writable chat and the composer routed the user's messages into a dead `source='cron'` session, where the cron agent executed unrelated desktop work under the cron identity.

## Behaviour

Opening a cron run is now gated on the run being **live** (`is_active` — the scheduler's agent is still executing it) or **properly closed** (`ended_at` set). This needs no backend change: the runs endpoint already computes `is_active` as `ended_at IS NULL` **and** `last_active` inside a 300 s window (`hermes_cli/web_routers/cron.py`), so a zombie (never closed, not running) is distinguishable from a live run — and a backend that omits the flag fails safe (read as zombie → view-only).

- **Zombie run** → still opens, so the failed run's output stays one click away, but it is latched read-only *before* the route flips. `use-prompt-actions/submit.ts` now refuses the send with the existing read-only explanation ("This chat is open as a read-only transcript — sending is disabled"), exactly as the #94724 no-owner path already does. No user message can be routed into the dead session, and starting a fresh chat is the way forward.
- **Live / closed run** → unchanged, fully writable.
- The latch lives in its own `$readOnlyCronRuns` set: the #94724 owner-recovery latch is cleared by a successful live resume, which would evaporate this guard the moment the transcript painted. `isStoredTranscriptReadOnly` reports both, so every write path gets one answer.
- One policy owner (`openCronRun` / `isResumableCronRun` in `src/app/cron/open-cron-run.ts`) serves both surfaces, so they cannot drift.
- The latch is honoured on every desktop write path, not only the primary chat: the tile delegate's `submitToSession` (open in split / new tab) previously refused sends only for synthetic `read-only:` runtime ids, so moving a latched run's transcript into a tile reopened the write path. It now reads `isStoredTranscriptReadOnly` too — the same answer `submit` gets.

Reuses the existing read-only stored-transcript machinery from #94724 rather than inventing a second "view-only" concept.

## Acceptance coverage

- `src/app/cron/open-cron-run.test.ts` — policy truth table (live, closed, zombie, older-backend fail-safe) and the latch-before-open ordering.
- `src/app/chat/sidebar/cron-jobs-section.test.tsx` — renders the real sidebar run peek: zombie click → `onOpenRun` called **and** session latched read-only; closed click → not latched; live click → not latched; rendering alone latches nothing; script-only output rows stay non-clickable.
- `src/store/read-only-transcript.test.ts` — the cron latch blocks `isStoredTranscriptReadOnly` and survives a live resume clearing the owner-recovery latch.
- `src/app/contrib/hooks/use-session-tile-delegate.test.ts` — a tile submit into a latched cron run is refused (no `prompt.submit` on any gateway, read-only notice shown).

## Validation (all run in a fresh worktree off `origin/main` @ ddb56d0)

```
$ cd apps/desktop && unset PYTHONPATH && npm run typecheck
typecheck exit=0

$ npx vitest run --project ui src/app/chat/sidebar/cron-jobs-section.test.tsx \
    src/app/cron/open-cron-run.test.ts src/store/read-only-transcript.test.ts
Test Files  3 passed (3)
     Tests  19 passed (19)

$ npx vitest run --project ui src/app/cron src/app/chat/sidebar \
    src/store/read-only-transcript.test.ts src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions
Test Files  58 passed (58)
     Tests  638 passed (638)

$ npx eslint <changed files>       # clean
$ npx prettier --check <changed files>   # all files use Prettier code style
```

Behavioural probe (repro before / pass after), by reverting only the click handler:

```
# onClick={() => onOpenRun(run.id)}   (pre-fix)
     × opens a never-closed run (ended_at NULL, not live) READ-ONLY
AssertionError: expected false to be true
 Test Files  1 failed (1)   Tests  1 failed | 4 passed (5)

# onClick={() => openCronRun(run, onOpenRun)}   (post-fix)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  5 passed (5)
```

## Issue reference

Refs #88443 — the desktop half (requirement 2: "the desktop sidebar should not allow resuming a cron session that was never properly closed … at minimum, clicking a cron run should open it read-only, not route new messages to it"). This does **not** claim the scheduler-side guarantee (requirement 1: booking `end_reason`/`ended_at` when the process is killed) — that close is inherently best-effort for a watchdog kill, so it is left to the cron owner's judgement instead of being closed by a `Fixes` keyword.

Not covered here (deliberately out of scope, say the word and I'll fold it in): the guard is client-side and in-memory, so a *restored* route/tab that already points at a zombie run is resumed writable again after an app restart. Closing that needs the gate at the resume boundary (resolve the row there and refuse a live resume of a never-closed cron run), which is a larger change to `use-session-actions`.
