items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Re-pins `plugin-catalog/telegram_dashboard_probe.yaml` from `v0.6.0` to [`v0.9.2`](https://github.com/bablobanov/hermes-agent-telegram-dashboard/releases/tag/v0.9.2). It closes both nits left in the review of #122408, gives the entry a card title and a screenshot gallery, and adds to the disclosure what 0.8.x and 0.9.0 read. I'm the author and maintainer of the plugin repo. (Opened for 0.7.0 on 2026-09-28, updated to 0.8.2, 0.9.0 and then 0.9.2 on 2026-10-01, before any review, so the maintainers look at one re-pin rather than four. 0.9.2 is a correctness fix: 0.9.0 showed the time to a limit's reset in whole days from two days on, cut down, so up to almost a day earlier than the real reset (`2d` for two days and 23 hours); 0.9.2 shows it to the minute under a day and to the hour from a day on, never earlier. It reads nothing new.)

Commits: [`v0.6.0...v0.9.2`](https://github.com/bablobanov/hermes-agent-telegram-dashboard/compare/v0.6.0...v0.9.2) (`a409e9a..d60eafc`, 56 commits).

**The two nits from #122408** (closed in 0.7.0):

- *"`_edit_text` is a private adapter method — fall back to `edit_message` first."* Every tick the plugin now reads the verb off the live adapter by signature, never by version number: the public `edit_message` when `inspect.signature` shows a parameter named `parse_mode` (positional-or-keyword or keyword-only; `**kwargs` does not count, since a verb that swallowed the keyword would send the markup as plain text and report success), else the adapter's `_edit_text`, else plain text through the public `edit_message`. On every engine I could check, main at `a3b56cac95` included, `edit_message` takes no parse mode (`plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py:3912`), so today the HTML form still goes through `_edit_text` (`:3892`); the day the public verb takes a `parse_mode`, the plugin uses it from the next tick, without a release. The delivery record names the verb in use (`html_verb`), and a refused HTML edit falls back to a plain edit in the same tick. A `parse_mode` parameter on the public `edit_message` would let the plugin drop the private call entirely; that is an engine change and not part of this PR.
- *"`links.py` is dead code."* Removed with its test.

Also new: the five properties the review checked by hand (no bot-token read in plugin mode, no listening socket, the drift command as argv without a shell, state only under `plugin-data/`, the one task through `ctx.spawn_task`) are now tests in the plugin repo (`tests/test_invariants.py`); 0.9.0 adds four more for what it reads, below.

**What 0.8.x and 0.9.0 read that 0.6.0 did not**, now in the disclosure:

- *External limit sources* (0.8.0, opt-in): up to four `limits_sources` from the config, each asked with one GET to `http` on loopback only (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `::1`), no proxy from the environment, no redirect, 64 KB at most, at most once per `limits_refresh_seconds`. A source may name an environment variable whose value is sent as `Authorization: Bearer`; bot-token variables (`TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `HERMES_DASHBOARD_BOT_TOKEN`, any `*_BOT_TOKEN`) are refused. Without `limits_sources` nothing is asked
- *Gemini refusals from the engine's log* (0.8.1, words of 0.8.2): Google reports Gemini quota only to a project with billing enabled, so the Gemini line shows the last HTTP 429 the engine logged. Every tick the plugin reads the tail of `HERMES_HOME/logs/errors.log` (the last 256 KB; the whole file, up to 4 MB, until the first successful read) and keeps four fields of the newest Gemini 429: the time, the `limit`, the retry and the `model`. The rest of the message never reaches the record or the screen, no other log is read, and nothing goes to the network
- *Failed sends from the same log* (0.9.0): the same tail is also read for the engine's own `Failed to send Telegram message` ERROR lines; only their time is kept
- *The cron line* (0.9.0): every tick `HERMES_HOME/cron/jobs.json` is read for each job's id, name, enabled flag, state, times, status and failure streak (never `prompt`, `script`, `deliver`, `skills` or the model), the ticker's marker files (`ticker_heartbeat`, `ticker_last_success`, `ticker_last_error`) for their epoch, and `HERMES_HOME/cron/executions.db` is opened read-only (`sqlite3` with `mode=ro` in the URI and `PRAGMA query_only`, in a worker under the tick's deadline, closed after the query) for the `job_id`, `status`, `delivery_outcome`, `claimed_at` and `finished_at` columns of failed or undelivered runs, never the `error` column and never `state.db`. The engine's error texts (`last_error`, `last_delivery_error`, the ticker's) are reduced to the kind of the error in a word and never reach the screen or the plugin's record. The rules are the engine's own (`hermes cron status`): a `last_status` outside `ok`/`delivery_failed`/`delivery_queued` is a failed run, a `last_delivery_error` an undelivered result, a heartbeat older than 200 s a dead ticker, a `next_run_at` more than 15 min in the past an overdue job
- *Whether the connected channel is deaf* (0.9.0), in a sentence of its own in the disclosure because one part of it is not the engine's public API: every tick the plugin reads the public property `send_path_degraded` of the connected Telegram adapter (`BasePlatformAdapter`, since 0.21.1; the Telegram adapter overrides it), and, as a capability and not a contract, four private attributes of the live adapter object (`_updates_received_total`, `_polling_generation`, `_polling_last_progress_monotonic`, `_polling_generation_started_monotonic`), read as attributes, with nothing called on the adapter (a test reads the plugin's source to pin that). An adapter without them shows `Telegram traffic: no data` with the reason and never raises; a public snapshot of the polling state on the adapter would turn the capability into a contract, which is an engine change and not part of this PR

0.9.1 and 0.9.2 read nothing beyond this: the `paused_at` stamp 0.9.1 reads is one of a job's times, and 0.9.2 reads the same fields as the engine's ticker reads them (`is_job_runnable`). The disclosure now also names the enabled flag, which 0.9.0 already read.

What the entry changes:

| key | v0.6.0 | v0.9.2 |
|---|---|---|
| `sha` | `a409e9a7e0…` | `d60eafca56…` (tag `v0.9.2`) |
| `version` | `"0.6.0"` | `"0.9.2"` |
| `title` | none | `Telegram Dashboard` |
| `description` | a long feature list, then the disclosure | a two-sentence summary, then the maintainer's disclosure word for word, our 0.8.2 sentence about errors.log extended with the failed-send lines, and the sentences above added after the Kimi Code one |
| `image` | `docs/social-preview.jpg` at the old sha | the same file at `682e20b` (tag `v0.7.0`) |
| `screenshots` | none | 4 PNGs at `682e20b`: the pinned screen healthy, with its details open, with a config-drift warning, and under the stale banner |

`image` and `screenshots` stay pinned at the `v0.7.0` commit: `docs/` has not changed since, and the files at `682e20b` are byte-identical to the ones at `v0.9.2`. The screenshots are the plugin's own demo states (`python -m telegram_dashboard --demo 14`, `15`, `16`) sent as a test message; the Hermes release dates in them are upstream's real ones, every other number is made up. They were taken on 0.7.0: 0.9.0 adds a `Cron` line to the top block (`Cron ✓ N jobs` after `Drift`), four sources to the coverage count in the details (`sources 10/10` where they show `6/6`: the Gemini log, the cron jobs, the cron history and the Telegram traffic), and lines about Gemini refusals, cron, the Telegram traffic and the dashboard's own version to the open details.

Everything else the disclosure describes is unchanged: the same hosts, the same writes (the plugin's record under `HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/`, which gains two keys, `cron_cache` and `traffic_cache`), the same optional `drift_command` subprocess; no hook, no tool, no new setting; the plugin still never reads the Telegram bot token itself.

Gate evidence (run for `v0.9.2` on 2026-10-01; Hermes v0.21.5 in a scratch venv, plugin folder exported from the tagged commit with `git archive`, 28 files = `SHA256SUMS`):

- `hermes plugins validate plugin/telegram_dashboard_probe` → 13 checks passed, `security scan — safe`, `Validation passed.`; `--json` → `"ok": true`, `"warnings": []` (Hermes 0.21.3: its 10 checks passed, `"ok": true`, `"warnings": []`)
- `python scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` (from main at `a3b56cac95`) on the entry → `OK: 1 file(s) valid`; with the whole `plugin-catalog/` → `OK: 349 file(s) valid`
- `plugin.yaml` at the pinned sha, the `image` and the four `screenshots` URLs return 200; the image files are byte-identical to the tagged ones

Other evidence: 0.9.2 runs on the author's live gateway (Hermes 0.21.3) since 2026-10-01; its delivery record shows `html_verb: _edit_text`, `screen_format: html`, `cron_cache` and `traffic_cache`, and the installed folder matches the tag's `SHA256SUMS`. Its limits read `⚠️ Claude 24% (3h8m) · 95% (4d6h)` and `Codex 34% (5d19h)`, where the code of 0.9.0 gives `95% (4d)` and `Codex 34% (5d)` for the same data. The first tick of 0.9.0 said `Cron ⚠️ 1 of 23 failing`: one job's result from 2026-09-27 had not reached one of its chats, which `hermes cron list` confirms and the screen of 0.8.2 did not show. The repo's CI at the pinned sha runs tests on Python 3.11-3.13 (705 passed), ruff, `mypy --strict`, and the manifest job (28 files).

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality): the entry is re-pinned to a new plugin release

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/telegram_dashboard_probe.yaml`: `sha`, `version`, `title`, `description` (the summary before the disclosure, the sentences above added to it), `image` re-pinned, `screenshots` added

## How to Test

1. `hermes plugins install telegram_dashboard_probe` installs 0.9.2 from the pinned sha (over 0.6.0: `hermes plugins update telegram_dashboard_probe`)
2. Restart the gateway; the pinned message keeps being edited every period
3. The delivery record under `HERMES_HOME/plugin-data/` shows `html_verb: _edit_text` on today's engines; the open details of the message carry `Cron N active · M paused · ticker HH:MM`, `Telegram last update seen …`, `Telegram send errors: …`, `Gemini refusals seen by Hermes: …` and, last, `Dashboard 0.9.2`

## Checklist

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide and the catalog README
- [x] My commit message follows Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains only this catalog entry
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q`: N/A, no engine code changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: validation on Windows 10; the plugin itself runs on a Linux gateway

feat(plugin-catalog): add minimax-search (community, web)

Adds a catalog entry for the MiniMax Token Plan web search plugin.

**What it does:** registers a web search provider named `minimax` that queries
`POST https://api.minimax.io/v1/coding_plan/search` with `{"q": <query>}` and maps
`organic[]` (title / link / snippet / date) onto the shared `web_search` row shape.
Search-only — the vendor returns snippets, never page bodies, so extraction is
unchanged and continues to use `web.backend` / `extract_backend`.

**Why it's useful:** SearXNG and other metasearch backends depend on third-party
engines (Brave, Google, Startpage, DuckDuckGo) that rate-limit or CAPTCHA
datacenter IPs. This provider goes straight to the vendor with a keyed request, so
it does not inherit those upstream blocks.

**Credential:** requires a MiniMax **Token Plan** key (`sk-cp-…`). Ordinary
MiniMax model API keys are rejected by the search endpoint — `is_available()`
reports the provider as unavailable rather than failing at call time, and
`get_setup_schema()` points at the Token Plan key page.

**Scope:** search backend only. No tools, hooks, or middleware are registered,
and `capabilities` declares exactly that (`requires_env: MINIMAX_API_KEY`).
SHA is pinned to the initial commit; `version` is a cosmetic label for it.

Plugin repo (author-owned): https://github.com/pdonizete/hermes-minimax-search

Re-pins `bot-forge` from v0.12.0 to **v0.15.0** (`58493c3236f4eec75395718765c3ad0a11f4e8af`, tagged [v0.15.0](https://github.com/BkashJEE/hermes-bot-forge/releases/tag/v0.15.0)). Follows #121190, which listed v0.12.0.

This PR previously proposed v0.13.0; it has been re-pointed rather than stacking a second bump of the same file, so there is one entry to review instead of two.

### A blocked Bot tells the user instead of waiting to be asked

`check_agents` gathers what needs the user; that is a pull. This adds the push: when a Bot journals a `blocked` or `failed` entry it sends one plain-text email, and a `digest` action sends the whole waiting queue on a schedule. It reuses Hermes' existing `EMAIL_SMTP_HOST` / `EMAIL_ADDRESS` / `EMAIL_PASSWORD`, so there is **no new credential and nothing to sign up for**, and it is skipped in silence when those are unset.

"An agent with email" is usually where this goes wrong, so the scope is deliberately narrow:

- **Outbound only.** Nothing reads a mailbox or accepts a reply.
- **The recipient is resolved from config alone** — never from a tool argument, a persona, or any text a model produced. There is no tool for mailing an arbitrary address, by design, so a Bot cannot be talked into contacting a third party and two Bots cannot start a reply loop.
- Rate limited per Bot, secret-scanned before sending, `Auto-Submitted: auto-generated`, and a failed send can never break a turn, a journal write or a routine.

### Acknowledgement reactions that fit the work

A Bot reacts to the user's own message as the turn runs. The reaction now reads the message — 🔧 a fix, 🔎 research, ✍️ writing, 📊 numbers, ⏳ scheduling, 📋 a review, 🛠️ something to build, 💬 a question — and the ending says what happened: 🚀 shipped, 📝 written, 📈 numbers, 🗓️ scheduled, 💡 found out, 🧹 cleaned up, with ✅ as the fallback and ✋ / ⚠️ taking precedence when the user is needed or something is blocked.

Three fixes behind that, all found by running it on a real machine rather than a fixture:

- **A profile running both the plugin and its `bot-forge-marks` companion appeared never to react.** Both registered the same turn hooks, and Hermes treats a second identical emoji on a message as a tapback toggle — so the reaction was placed and immediately cleared. The plugin now stands down when the companion is beside it.
- **A Bot could have the hook installed and enabled and still stay silent**, because Hermes' own `message_reactions` setting was never switched on and an unset value reads as off. Creation now sets both, and the plugin adopts every live profile on load — including Bots made through Hermes' New Agent dialog, which never heard of this plugin. `adopt_bots: false` switches that off.
- The numbers rule never matched a percentage: its pattern ended in a word boundary directly after `%`, which is already a non-word character.

### The workspace survey, corrected against a real machine

v0.12.0's survey was validated on a clean fixture. Against ten configured roots and thirty near-identical checkouts: one crowded root drained the whole scan budget; a directory with almost no words matched anything it shared one with; nested copies appeared several times. Each root now gets its own share of the cap, a place needs real vocabulary and two shared terms, duplicates collapse to the shallowest path, and the job's terms are widened with related ones before places are searched (job side only — never the corpus, never the duplicate guard).

139 tests pass on the pinned commit ([CI](https://github.com/BkashJEE/hermes-bot-forge/actions/workflows/tests.yml)); `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` passes on this entry. `image:` points at the repo's social-preview card at the same pinned SHA.

items.body:
Third-party plugins can run in a per-profile plugin host process instead of inside Hermes (`plugins.isolation: host`), without any change to the plugins; the default stays `in_process`, so nothing changes for existing installs.

This is the Hermes side of the shared-pool design: one tenant's plugin Python never runs in the same interpreter as another tenant's data, plugins stay tenant-unaware (same `ctx`, no new API), and the catalog, MCP and every plugin surface keep working.

## What changes

- **`plugins.isolation: host`** (new config key, default `in_process`; optional `plugins.host.launcher` argv prefix for a sandbox runner). Under `host`, every non-bundled plugin is imported by a host process started on demand per profile, with only that profile's environment and secrets (`served_profile_child_env`). Under the multiplex gateway that means one host per profile.
- **Same `ctx` over a pipe.** The host gives plugins a `RemotePluginContext`; Hermes registers matching proxies: tools, hooks, slash/CLI commands, skills, and provider objects as subclasses of the ABC Hermes checks (image/video gen, web search, browser, TTS/STT, memory, context engine, cron). Re-entrant: a handler can call `ctx.dispatch_tool` / `ctx.get_config` / `ctx.llm` back into Hermes while Hermes waits on it.
- **Every user-code import path is routed or refused:** general plugins (`plugins_loader`), memory / context-engine / cron providers (`load_instance`), model-provider profiles (credential-free extraction cached by file fingerprint, overridden methods run by name in the host), dashboard plugin APIs (ASGI bridge through the host). `plugins/plugin_loader.load_plugin_module` refuses any other in-process import of user code under `host`.
- **What cannot cross is one table** (`HOST_UNSUPPORTED_CTX_METHODS`: platform adapters, approval transports, platform handlers). Those plugins fail with the reason instead of loading. The same table drives a static audit shown by `hermes plugins validate` / `hermes plugins show`, and `evals/plugin_isolation/audit_catalog.py` re-measures the catalog.
- **Crashes stay contained.** A plugin that kills its host costs the call in flight a tool error; Hermes restarts the host and reloads its plugins (3 restarts / 10 min, the plugin that was loading when the host died is skipped).
- **Operator lock for shared deployments.** `plugins.isolation` is profile config, so a profile can set it back to `in_process`. Pin it in the managed scope (`/etc/hermes/config.yaml`): the isolation reader goes through the managed overlay, so the pin wins over every profile's own config and `hermes config set` refuses to change it. Documented in the plugins page, pinned by a test. Pair it with an isolated terminal backend so the agent cannot reach the operator's files either.
- **Windows:** the model-provider extraction child now gets `USERPROFILE` (Windows ignores `HOME` for `Path.home()`); without it every user model-provider plugin was dropped under `host` (reported by @Enough1122). The host's cross-platform tests now carry `platforms("any")` so the Windows and macOS lanes actually run them.
- Docs: `user-guide/features/plugins.md` section, `plugins/AGENTS.md` invariants.

## Catalog coverage (audit at each entry's pinned SHA)

**299 / 348 catalog plugins run in the host unchanged** (241 Python + 58 portable). The 49 that need `in_process`:

| reason | plugins |
|---|---|
| gateway platform adapters (`register_platform` / kind `platform`) | 18 |
| monkeypatch a Hermes module | 13 |
| model-provider builds its own SDK client (`create_client`) | 11 |
| streaming dashboard endpoints (SSE / websocket) | 6 |
| platform handlers / direct registry mutation | 3 + 2 + 1 |

For the pool these route to a silo; nothing about them changes in `in_process` mode.

## Validation

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_host.py` (5 tests: out-of-process tool/hook/provider/nested ctx + crash restart; import-path refusal + audit; model-provider data local, overrides in host; async plugin code keeps the caller's session + awaitable facades; hosted memory provider live attributes, schema in host, survives a host SIGKILL) | pass; the 2 review tests fail on the pre-fix head |
| Real catalog plugins under `host` (command-tray tools + hooks, web-serply, aihubmix + hopper model providers, agentplaybooks-memory memory provider, usage-stats dashboard API) | identical output to `in_process`; 0 plugin modules in the Hermes interpreter; 1 host process |
| Real `hermes chat -Q` turn (loopback fake provider → `tool_call` → `command_tray_list`) | same tool result in `host` and `in_process`, host pid logged |
| Multiplex: 2 profiles in one Hermes process | 2 host pids, profile A's host sees only A's secret, B's only B's |
| Crash: plugin `os._exit(3)` in a tool | one tool error, host auto-restarted, next call served by a new pid |
| Dashboard API across profiles (launch, `?profile=workerb` without the plugin, `?profile=workerc` with it) | 200 from A's host / 404 / 200 from C's own host with C's home; both `Set-Cookie` headers survive |
| Memory provider loaded 20× | host holds only the live instance (released refs return `LookupError`) |
| `tests/hermes_cli`, `tests/plugins`, `tests/providers` | see comment below |
| Windows model-provider plugin under `host` (real `windows-latest`, wine2e lane) | red on the pre-fix head (`profile extraction exited 1: hermes: Could not determine home directory`), green with the `USERPROFILE` fix |
| Managed pin vs profile config (real loader + host, `HERMES_MANAGED_DIR`) | profile says `in_process`, managed says `host` → plugin runs in the host, 0 plugin modules in Hermes; `hermes config set plugins.isolation in_process` refused naming the admin file; control without the pin → in-process. The new test goes red when `isolation_mode()` is switched to a raw profile-file read |

**Live repro:** before, `plugins.isolation` did not exist and every user plugin's module loaded into the Hermes interpreter (`sys.modules` held `hermes_plugins.command_tray`, `_hermes_user_provider_*_aihubmix`, `hermes_dashboard_plugin_usage-stats`); after, under `host` the same list is empty and every call above is served by the host pid.

## Independent review

A delegated review found 8 defects on the first head; all are fixed in `fix: plugin host review findings`: async `ctx` facades not awaitable; async handlers' callbacks losing the caller's session (fell back to the host creator's context); category providers dead after a host restart (and stale object ids after one); per-call instance leak in the host; base-class attribute defaults frozen on the Hermes-side proxy; user `config_schema.py` executed in the dashboard process; dashboard API resolved from the launch profile for every `?profile=`; `platform_actions` coroutines run on a private loop. Plus the lows: bounded worker pool deadlock under nested callbacks, racy/late channel-close restart, repeated response headers, model-provider cache name collision.

## Not covered

- Platform adapters and approval transports stay in-process (they hand live gateway objects across). Streaming dashboard endpoints are buffered-only in the host.
- A model-provider plugin that reads a non-secret setting from the environment at import time gets its default in the cached profile data (the extraction is credential-free by design, so no secret lands in the cache).
- The sandbox itself (filesystem / network confinement of the host) is the deployment's `plugins.host.launcher`; this PR provides the process boundary and the hook.

## Infographic

![plugin host](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aac485a/D0j1bGSryJvq0HY7FNOT-_mksfgrZp.png)

Adds `evalroute` to the community catalog (tier: community, category: tools).

**Repo:** https://github.com/keppy/hermes-plugin-evalroute — pinned at `684c6a871787870519b41b8cef0a152334fbf8ee` (tag `v0.3.3`).

## What it does

Routes a task to a (model, reasoning effort) arm before the session starts. `/route <task>` classifies the task into one of nine lanes from a YAML route table and prints a route card: the model, the effort, the escalation option, and the row's provenance verbatim (`priors` / `observed` / `measured`). Three lanes are measured (10 tasks × 3 samples × 4–5 arms each, McNemar-stamped via gonogo); the rest are marked priors. `/rate pass|fail` after the work labels the outcome so the table's own data grows. `hermes evalroute install-routes` writes the effort column into `agent.reasoning_overrides`.

Same author as the `gonogo` entry already in the catalog; evalroute uses gonogo for the statistical stamps on measured rows (optional import, degrades to "unverified").

## Why each hook exists

- **`pre_llm_call`** — first-turn sniff on cli/tui/desktop only. If the task's keyword signal is strong and the session's model differs from the lane's pick, it injects one advisory line suggesting `/route`. It also flags an unrated route left pending by a previous session (turn caps) so the user doesn't re-route a continuation. Advisory context only; never blocks, never switches the model, silent on gateway platforms and subagents.
- **`pre_command`** — observes `/model` and `/reasoning` after a route and appends a switch record to the plugin's local labels file. Diagnostics only: the README and code say explicitly these are not attributed to a route as fact.
- **`post_llm_call`** — records the last-seen model in process memory for the `/rate` confirmation line. Nothing persisted; no response bodies or conversation content are ever logged.

## Paid paths, stated plainly

Strong keyword classification is local file math. Weak-signal classification (0–1 hits) makes one `ctx.llm.complete_structured` call on the host's own model and auth — it consumes tokens and the manifest, tool schema and README say so. The vendored evalroute harness and Hermes shim make paid provider calls only when the user runs them deliberately from a separate venv; nothing paid runs on import, install or as a side effect of a route. `requires_env: []` — the plugin owns no credentials.

## Checks run at the pin (fresh `git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.3.3`)

- `pytest`: 142 passed (isolated `HERMES_HOME` fixture; no test touches a live ledger)
- `hermes plugins validate .`: passed (manifest, capability probe, declared tools/hooks match registrations, security scan)
- `hermes plugins doctor --ci .`: OK — 1 tool, 3 hooks
- `hermes plugins compat .`: no deprecated imports
- `python scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/`: OK, 350 files
- `plugin.yaml` and `pyproject.toml` both `0.3.3`; sha from `git rev-parse v0.3.3^{commit}`
- secret scan of the clone (vendored run logs included): clean
- route-table numbers reproduced by running the vendored harness `report` + `routes_from_report.py` over the shipped `examples/artifacts/*/runs.jsonl`

Dependency: `pyyaml>=6,<7` only (already in the Hermes venv).

items.body:
## Root cause

`session.events.since` returns `truncated: true` when the replay ring evicted events between the client's watermark and its oldest retained seq. `JsonRpcGatewayClient.fetchSessionReplay` (`apps/shared/src/json-rpc-gateway.ts`) never read the flag. It dispatched the retained tail as though it were the complete gap, so a reconnect after eviction painted streamed output missing its prefix, tool state or terminal event.

## Behavior

On a truncated reply, the client now:
- dispatches none of the partial tail.
- advances the session watermark to the server head (`latest_seq`, or the highest tail seq). This stops the next reconnect from asking for the same evicted window again.
- emits a client-local `session.replay_truncated` event for that session before releasing the replay barrier. Desktop's lifecycle handler treats it like `sessions.changed`: it re-reads which turns are still running (ending a turn whose terminal event was evicted and closing its spinning tool rows), then reloads the open transcript and tiles. Without this, the reconnect backstop (#94779) waits for an idle transition that never arrives when the evicted window held the turn's final event.
- resolves the session replay barrier `true`, the same path a backend-epoch change takes, so history reads waiting on `pendingSessionReplay` go ahead.
- still dispatches parked live frames newer than the head. Frames at or below the head fall inside the skipped window.

## Acceptance coverage

New vitest `never dispatches a truncated replay tail; history reads proceed after fresh parked frames` in `apps/shared/src/json-rpc-gateway-replay.test.ts`. The test answers the reconnect replay with `truncated: true` and checks four things: the tail (699/700) is not dispatched, the parked duplicate 700 is dropped, the post-head live frame 701 dispatches, and the barrier resolves `true` only after that; the reload signal fires for `s1` at seq 700 before the post-head frame.

New desktop vitest in `use-background-sync.test.ts`: a live turn, a reconnect and a truncated replay whose backend no longer lists the turn. Nothing reloads before the event; after it, running turns are re-fetched, the session goes idle and the transcript reloads.

## Validation (worktree, after `npm ci` at root)

- Red on unpatched source: `cd apps/shared && npx vitest run src/json-rpc-gateway-replay.test.ts` → 1 failed / 13 passed (`seen` got `[3, 699, 700, 701]`).
- Green: `npx vitest run --environment jsdom src/json-rpc-gateway-replay.test.ts src/json-rpc-gateway-connect.test.ts src/json-rpc-channel.test.ts` → 28/28 passed. (`--environment jsdom` is there because the connect test needs `CloseEvent`, which the node environment lacks.)
- `cd apps/shared && npm run typecheck` → clean. `npx eslint` on both files → clean.
- `cd apps/desktop && npm run typecheck` → clean.
- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/store/gateway src/app/contrib/hooks/use-background-sync` → 16 files / 181 tests passed.

## Scope

Refs #100122. This PR is only the client half (item 1 of the report). Item 2 is the server-side FIFO session-eviction seq reset in `tui_gateway/event_replay.py`, and #124587 by @dskwe covers it. The two are compatible: once #124587 lands, a returning evicted session answers with `truncated: true`, and this change turns that into a resync. #120064 (flag truncation when the watermark is ahead of the ring) is also server-only and feeds the same client path.

items.body:
## Root cause
`RealProfileConsentDialog` (added in ada7213cca, "first-open consent prompt for real-profile browsing") opens when the config is loaded, `browser.use_real_profile` is off, the user has not opted out, and this pane holds the claim. It never checked which machine the backend runs on. "Enable" sends `saveHermesConfigRecord({ browser: { use_real_profile: true } }, writeScope)` to the **connected** backend. Over a remote/SSH/cloud connection, that sets the flag on the remote host. There, "your default browser's profile" means the remote machine's browser, which is often missing on a headless box, so the browser tools unregister. The copy also claims "Nothing leaves this computer", which is false in that case. "Not now" only mutes the prompt for the current app run, so after an operator resets the flag the prompt comes back with the next Browser tab. That matches the flag-flipping-back pattern in the issue.

## Behavior
- New pure gate `shouldOfferRealProfilePrompt()`. It returns true only when the live resolved `$connection` has `mode === 'local'`, the same resolver sibling surfaces use (`plugins-tab`, `session-actions-menu`, `about-settings`). `mode` is only ever `local` or `remote`; `cloud` resolves to `remote`.
- If the connection is not resolved yet, the gate fails closed.
- The existing gates are unchanged (config loaded, feature off, not dismissed or muted, claim).
- Remote users can still opt in on purpose from the Capabilities → Tools → Browser toggle, which makes the target backend explicit.
- **Visible UI change:** on remote backends the dialog no longer appears.

I chose "skip on remote" over "ask the backend for its state". The feature was built around the local user's own browser (see the copy and the commit intent). The backend status endpoint has no field saying whether real-profile mode is usable, so the second option would need new API surface.

Adjacent: #103069 (@Zeus-Deus) names the target browser/profile in this dialog. It does not gate on remote, so it does not overlap this fix.

## Validation (worktree, after `npm ci` at the root)
- `cd apps/desktop && npm run typecheck`: clean
- `npx vitest run src/app/chat/right-rail/real-profile-consent-dialog.test.tsx`: 12/12 passed. New: gate unit tests (local offers; remote ssh/url/cloud never; unresolved fails closed; existing gates kept) and a component test (remote: no dialog, no save).
- Behavioral probe: with the pre-fix component, both remote tests **fail** (the dialog renders for a remote connection). With the fix they pass.
- `npx eslint` and `npx prettier --check` on both files: clean

Fixes #119398

items.body:
## Root cause

`watchPreviewFile` and `watchDirectory` (the disk-plugin door) in `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` use raw `fs.watch`. On Windows, `ReadDirectoryChangesW` can flood one handle with `rename` events. The report measured about 180k events/s on `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\desktop-plugins`, one core pinned (mostly kernel time), and CPU back to 0% as soon as the `FSWatcher` was closed. The existing 120ms debounce only covers the IPC dispatch. libuv still runs the JS listener once per event.

## Fix

New pure module `electron/watch-storm-breaker.ts` (`guardedWatch`). It wraps the watcher creation and counts events in fixed 1s windows. Once a window goes over 1000 events, it:
- closes the `FSWatcher` (the operation the report showed recovers the CPU),
- drops any events still queued,
- switches to a 5s poll of a cheap snapshot and reports a change only when the snapshot differs.

Snapshots:
- `watchDirectory`: sorted `readdir` names. This matches the 5s readdir poll that c14ae3796e3 replaced with the watch.
- `watchPreviewFile`: `mtimeMs:size` of the target file.

A snapshot error (target removed) counts as a change and does not throw. `close()` clears the poll and is idempotent, so the existing registry, owner-destroyed teardown, and `closePreviewWatchers` behave as before.

The breaker is armed on **win32 only**, and the platform is passed in as data (`process.platform`). On macOS and Linux, events go straight through with no counting. The storm is Windows-specific, and on other platforms a legitimate burst would demote a watch to 5s polling for the rest of its life. No new env vars. It logs one `console.warn` when it trips.

Creation errors (#73524, #109154) are a separate class and not touched here.

## Validation (worktree from current origin/main)

- `npm ci` at the root: exit 0
- `cd apps/desktop && npm run typecheck`: clean
- `npx vitest run --project electron electron/watch-storm-breaker.test.ts electron/preview-file-watch.test.ts`: 2 files, 14 tests passed. The breaker suite uses fake timers and an injected watcher. It covers: forwarding under the threshold, window reset, a win32 storm closing the watcher once and dropping further events, poll-on-change-only, the same storm untouched on darwin, close idempotence with zero timers left, and a vanished target.
- `npx vitest run --project electron` (full): 18 failures in 13 files. The same 18 fail on clean main without this change (failure lists diffed: identical).
- eslint and prettier are clean on the touched files.

## Not verified

I could not reproduce the Windows IOCP storm on macOS. The breaker logic is unit-tested, but nobody has confirmed on real Windows that it trips and that CPU recovers. **Hold for Windows review.** The 1000 events/1s threshold is a judgment call: the report's storm is about 180× that rate.

Fixes #118974

items.body:
## Root cause

Two related durability gaps in how interrupted and failed turns are persisted:

**#124373 (stopped marker):** the Stop paths finalize interrupted rows with no stopped
metadata — `handle_api_interrupt` persists the partial assistant row with bare content (no
`display_metadata`), and `finalizeUserInterruptedMessages` only marks tool calls — so
hydration has nothing to render a stopped marker from, live or after reload.

**#124379 (failed-turn card):** `_close_durable_failed_turn` persists only the generic notice
text and `display_kind` on the failed-turn boundary row — no error text, no structured
`error_surface` — so after a restart hydration can only rebuild the note, not the card.

## What changes (PRs #124348 + #124355 rebased together — same author, same hydration files, paired per review)

- Backend: `handle_api_interrupt` stamps `display_metadata.interrupted` on the partial
  assistant row; `_close_durable_failed_turn` attaches the capped error text (2000 chars)
  and the `error_surface` descriptor (via `build_error_surface_from_result`) as
  `display_metadata` on the boundary row.
- Desktop: `interrupted` on `ChatMessage`; hydration restores both flags from
  `display_metadata` (verified `_project_for_display` in `hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py`
  passes `display_metadata` through untouched); a new `StoppedNotice` renders
  "Response stopped" under a stopped reply (i18n: en/de/es/fr — the repo's complete-locale
  set; ja/ru/zh/zh-hant/ar are `defineLocale` overlays that fall back to English by design).
- `finalizeStoppedMessages` flags the live reply on Stop (redirect finalize keeps the old
  behavior); failed-turn hydration rebuilds the error card from the boundary row, and
  reconciliation keeps exactly one card when the refresh already rebuilt it.
- Conflict with main's #120978 attachment-error fold resolved: the persisted-tail-error
  dedupe now runs after (and distinct from) the attachment fold.

## Tests (all run with `--maxWorkers=2` / `-j 2` under the shared test env)

Red on `origin/main` / green with fix:
- JS (6 red on main → 161 passed in 4 files): `chat-messages.test.ts` (stopped flag
  hydration, failed-card redraw, degraded bogus-layer case, one-card reconciliation),
  `assistant-message.test.tsx` (marker renders, finished reply unmarked),
  `rewind.test.ts` (stop vs redirect finalize).
- Python (2 red on main → 7 passed in 2 files): `test_turn_api_call_interrupt.py`
  (`display_metadata.interrupted` on the persisted partial row),
  `test_failed_turn_closure.py` (boundary keeps error + `error_surface`, durable after flush).

Fixes #124373
Fixes #124379

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/124348 and
https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/124355 (both rebased onto current main and
paired to resolve their shared hydration conflicts; authorship kept). Thanks @Adolanium!

Follow-up to the catalogued plugin (owner-submitted pin bump, catalog rules 4 and 5).

Pin: b7ab470b51a2915e19e4df52bb80cd5973c1b0ca -> 3d691dadfdd515083237337c4a9747389a18ca4a
Version: 1.0.5 -> 1.0.6
Release: https://github.com/soyelmismo/hermes-antigravity-subscription/releases/tag/v1.0.6

Commits adopted in range (`v1.0.5..v1.0.6`):

• `3d691da` release: v1.0.6
• `139238d` fix(prompt): use HEADLESS INFERENCE MODE framing in preamble to avoid prompt injection trigger (soyelmismo/hermes-antigravity-subscription#16)
• `e433510` fix: strip --effort for Claude models (soyelmismo/hermes-antigravity-subscription#15), strengthen preamble identity override (soyelmismo/hermes-antigravity-subscription#16)
• `8e04c3f` docs: update README with context window limits, tool pruning, env vars, and pytest command
• `c9dd72d` docs: polish AGENTS.md and SKILL.md for stop-slop compliance
• `ebd846d` docs: add AGENTS.md and hermes-catalog-release skill

### Root Cause / Motivation

1. `agy` rejects `--effort` for Claude models:
   `error: invalid model selection (--model "claude-sonnet-4-6" --effort "medium"): --effort is not supported for model "claude-sonnet-4-6"`
   The persistent worker exited at startup, surfacing as `BrokenPipeError` in Hermes. After three failed attempts, Hermes dropped to the fallback provider.

2. On tool-using turns, models like `claude-sonnet-4-6` and `gemini-3.6-flash` prioritized `agy`'s embedded system persona over the plugin's tool instructions and attempted native tool calls (`RunCommand`), which headless mode soft-denied.

### Changes in v1.0.6

1. **Claude `--effort` suppression (`models.py`, `__init__.py`)**
   - Added `_NO_EFFORT_MODEL_PREFIXES = ("claude",)` in `models.py`. Claude models resolve to bare model IDs with `effort=None`, so `client.py` never appends `--effort`.
   - `supported_reasoning_efforts()` returns `()` for Claude models, preventing the Hermes `/model` picker from offering invalid effort flags.

2. **Headless mode preamble framing (`prompt.py`)**
   - Reframed the prompt preamble to declare `HEADLESS INFERENCE MODE` and state that native tools are disabled at the transport layer.
   - Verified empirically against `agy`: `claude-sonnet-4-6` emits clean `<tool_call>` blocks instead of native tool calls.

3. **Documentation (`README.md`)**
   - Added model compatibility matrix documenting `<tool_call>` compliance across tested models.
   - Added directory naming note regarding plugin backup directories in `~/.hermes/plugins/`.

### Validation

• Plugin repo CI: 185 passed, 1 skipped against `HERMES_REF v2026.9.21`.
• `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/antigravity-subscription-directsdk.yaml` passed (1 file valid).
• `hermes plugins validate /root/.hermes/plugins/antigravity-subscription-directsdk` passed (safe, declared capabilities match).
• Manifest version 1.0.6 matches git tag `v1.0.6` and catalog entry.

## Root cause

YouTube inline embeds fail with **error 153** in the packaged app because the Referer stamp was wired only to the unused `persist:hermes-embed` session partition, while chat embeds are plain iframes in the default session. The packaged renderer loads via `file://` (null origin), so no Referer is sent — and on Electron ≥ ~17 `webRequest.onBeforeSendHeaders` **Referer mutation is silently dropped** (electron/electron#21374), so default-session stamping alone is inert. YouTube requires a Referer **plus a matching `origin` param** (verified empirically against a packaged Linux build on Electron 40.10.2).

## What changes

Two layers, from the only empirically verified working direction plus a belt-and-braces composition:

1. **Loopback HTTP renderer origin** (salvaged from #63492, authorship preserved): `electron/renderer-server.ts` + `renderer-url.ts` serve the packaged renderer over loopback HTTP, giving the window a real `http://127.0.0.1` origin so the browser sends a Referer YouTube accepts. `createWindow`/window loads are wired for it (the async-launcher trap from the issue thread is handled). The YouTube embed component now always passes the `origin` param (it previously dropped it when `location.origin === 'null'` — the exact packaged case).
2. **Composed Referer stamp** (salvaged from #106620, credited): Electron allows a single `onBeforeSendHeaders` listener per webRequest hook — `installRemoteHeaderRules` already owns the default-session slot, so a separate stamp listener was silently discarded. The stamp is now composed into that shared listener (`stampEmbedRefererHeaders` / `withEmbedRefererStamp` in `remote-ws-headers.ts`) as defense-in-depth, with remote-gateway header rules unchanged.

## Acceptance coverage

| Requirement (issue #106596) | Covered |
|---|---|
| YouTube embeds play in the packaged app (error 153 gone) | Loopback origin = the empirically verified fix; **packaged-build validation on Windows/macOS/Linux still needed before merge** (HITL) |
| A Referer/origin YouTube accepts reaches the request on modern Electron | Loopback HTTP origin + always-on `origin` param; stamp composed for belt-and-braces |
| Stamp survives the single-listener-per-hook slot | Composed into `installRemoteHeaderRules`' existing listener, not a second registration |
| No regression to remote-gateway header rules | `remote-ws-headers.test.ts` green |

## Tests (real results)

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --project electron electron/embed-referer.test.ts electron/renderer-server.test.ts electron/renderer-url.test.ts electron/remote-ws-headers.test.ts` — **26/26 green** with the fix; on current `origin/main` + the branch's `embed-referer.test.ts`: **9 failed / 1 passed** (red proof). Logs: `$RUN/builds/logs/106596-with-fix.log`, `$RUN/builds/logs/106596-on-main.log`.
- Typecheck: `cd apps/desktop && npx tsc -p . --noEmit` — **exit code 0** (clean; first attempt hit a 420s timeout under heavy machine load, the completed run is recorded as `builds/logs/106596-tsc.log`).

Fixes #106596
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/63492
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/106620

Thanks @ugoenyioha (loopback renderer direction, cherry-picked with authorship) and @kokhlo (stamp composition helper, cherry-picked as commit 2 with a Co-authored-by trailer). Credit also to @pitalgoras for the packaged-build Electron-40 verification that settled the direction (Referer mutation inert; loopback works; Referer + origin required) and for identifying the async `createWindow` packaging trap.

items.body:
## Root cause

Two Windows window-chrome bugs compound in #94319:

1. `chatWindowSurfaceOptions()` passed `backgroundMaterial` on Windows whenever glass was *supported* — including `'none'` when glass was inactive (intensity 0) — which Electron treats as a translucent-window opt-in (`WS_EX_LAYERED`), disabling the native caption maximize button (`SC_MAXIMIZE`), the restore-down glyph, and thick-frame edge resize.
2. `window-state.json` could recover stale fullscreen-as-normal bounds verbatim (normal bounds ≈ whole work area with `isMaximized=false`, e.g. after a DPI/display transition), leaving the window with no meaningful restore-down size.

## What changes

- **`windowBackgroundMaterialOptions()`** (new helper in `electron/translucency.ts`): returns the native Windows backdrop only when glass is actually active — omitting `backgroundMaterial` entirely otherwise, so an inactive-glass window is never created layered. `chatWindowSurfaceOptions()` now spreads this helper instead of its inline ternary. Construction-time omission is deliberately different from the runtime reset path, which explicitly sends `'none'` when clearing an already-created window.
- **Stale-fullscreen recovery** (`electron/window-state.ts`): `computeWindowOptions` gains a `platform` parameter (defaulting to `process.platform`, keeping it a pure function testable with the platform as data). On `win32` only, a saved normal-bounds snapshot that covers ≥90% of a work area's dimensions and starts near that work area's origin is treated as the stuck-fullscreen shape and recovered to a centered 80% windowed size. Deliberate near-fullscreen layouts on macOS/Linux and genuinely maximized saves are untouched.

## Acceptance coverage per issue

Issue #94319 requirements:
- restore-down glyph + sane windowed restore for stale fullscreen-as-normal bounds → covered by the stale-fullscreen recovery + tests
- native caption maximize button / titlebar double-click actually maximizes (no layered/translucent window) → covered by omitting `backgroundMaterial` when glass is inactive
- window stays resizable (WS_THICKFRAME drag edges) → un-layering the window restores the thick frame
- no regression for active Windows glass windows → `windowBackgroundMaterialOptions` passes the material only for active glass; covered by `translucency.test.ts`

## Tests run (real results)

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run electron/translucency.test.ts electron/window-state.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` → **2 files, 97 tests passed** (includes the new `windowBackgroundMaterialOptions` describe block and four new `computeWindowOptions` platform-scoped tests)
- `cd apps/desktop && npx tsc -p . --noEmit` → **exit 0**

One contributor test's expected clamped position (`computeWindowOptions does not shrink a large normal window away from the work-area origin`) was re-baselined: current main clamps a trusted saved position inside its work area (`240,120` → `180,90` for a 1740×950 window on a 1920×1040 work area), and this change preserves that behavior — the assertion now states the clamped values.

## Not exercised live

Both fixes change Windows OS-level window behavior (`WS_EX_LAYERED`, `SC_MAXIMIZE`, thick-frame styles). Unit tests cover the pure logic on this Mac (macOS); the caption maximize button, restore-down glyph, and edge-drag resize need verification on real Windows 11 with glass off, and that active glass windows keep their material.

Fixes #94319

## Root cause

Three at-rest secret surfaces were world-readable under the documented `HERMES_HOME_MODE=0701` traversal hatch (#77486):

1. The Chromium debug-profile user-data dir and media-cache dirs were created with bare `os.makedirs(..., exist_ok=True)` inheriting the umask (0755), and cache files landed 0644 — so `Cookies`, `Login Data`, screenshots and inbound media were readable by every other local account.
2. The same for the gateway's inbound-media caches and the vision/computer-use capture caches (a screen capture is as sensitive as the screen it came from).
3. Deleting a session left its journaled in-flight turn tail (user prompt + tool calls) in localStorage to age out on its own — no purge on either delete surface.

(connection.json safeStorage/0600 and the journal retention bounds are already on main; this PR covers the remaining two gaps.)

## What changes

- `launch_chrome_debug`'s user-data dir and media caches, the gateway's five media caches, and the vision/computer-use caches are now created owner-only (`makedirs(mode=0o700)` at creation — no post-chmod window — no post-hoc chmod window) and reconciled via the house `hermes_cli.config._secure_dir`/`_secure_file` policy helpers, which keep the managed/NixOS group-share carve-out and `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID` ownership. Cache files are written 0600 via `os.open`.
- `purgeInFlightTurnJournals` purges (and drops a pending throttled write for) every id a delete holds, wired into both delete surfaces: sidebar `removeSession` and Settings permanent delete.

## Acceptance coverage per issue

- #77486 browser-profile ACLs requirement: `_ensure_chrome_debug_data_dir` (0700 at creation + legacy reconcile) — adopted from #77579.
- #77486 journal-purge requirement: `purgeInFlightTurnJournals` + wiring on both delete surfaces — adopted from #77584.
- connection.json / safeStorage items: already on main (`7e151bd9d3`, `4c8e3265`), no work needed.

Fixes #77486
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/77579 (thanks @ZHJay — the `_ensure_chrome_debug_data_dir` shape is yours)
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/77584 (thanks @ZHJay — the purge-on-delete wiring and journal tests are yours)

## Tests (real runs)

Red on `origin/main` (`fd0b98f625`), then green with this branch:

- Python: `HERMES_PYTHON=$RUN/test-venv/bin/python bash scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_cli/test_browser_connect_media_permissions.py` — **on main: 13 failed** (dirs 0755, files 0644); **with fix: 13 passed**.
- JS: `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/lib/inflight-turn-journal.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` — **on main: 3 failed** (`purgeInFlightTurnJournals` missing); **with fix: 42/42 passed**.

## Notes for reviewers

- The journal redaction design question (redacting secrets in tool args vs. treating localStorage as a bounded, profile-protected store) is left as the documented decision it was in routing — this PR fixes purge-on-delete and dir/file modes only.
- Managed/NixOS installs keep the group-share carve-out via the policy helpers; unmanaged local installs get owner-only everywhere.

## Root cause

`createBackendSessionForSend` (and the fork path) released `creatingSessionRef` in a `finally` via `window.setTimeout(0)` — a macrotask — before HashRouter's render caught up to the created stored id. `use-route-resume`'s `stuckOnRoutedSession` self-heal then saw the stale pre-create route with the guard already down and resumed the OLD session over the new one: after creating a new session and sending the first message, the view jumped back to the old session's transcript (#66057).

## What changes

Port of #66610 (closed by its author for backlog-throttling, not superseded) onto current main:

- Hold `creatingSessionRef` until `routedSessionId` + selection both agree on the created stored id (`armPendingCreatedSession` + release effect).
- Recovery paths: release on navigate throw; release when the user diverts to a different session than the pending one; a 3s safety timeout that retries the navigation once, then releases so `use-route-resume` can self-heal a stuck route.
- `use-route-resume`'s suppression is scoped to the active pending-create hold only (`selectionMovedAheadOfRoute` requires `creatingSessionRef.current`), so a genuine route/selection mismatch after the timeout can still self-heal.
- New `routedSessionId` option threaded through `wiring.tsx` and the session-actions harnesses.

## Acceptance coverage

- #66057 requirement 1 (stay on the new session, show its streaming response) — guard hold until route catch-up.
- #66057 requirement 2 (self-heal must not fire while the created session's route has not caught up) — `selectionMovedAheadOfRoute` suppression, hold-scoped.
- #66057 requirement 3 (recovery: navigate failure, user diversion, safety timeout) — all three, one test each.

## Tests

- Red on `origin/main` (fd0b98f6256): the four `creatingSessionRef hold (#66057)` tests in `use-session-actions.test.tsx` all fail (setTimeout(0) releases the guard one tick after create; navigate throws propagate).
- Green with fix: full `use-session-actions.test.tsx` + `use-route-resume.test.tsx` suites pass.
- `routedSessionId: null` added to every existing `useSessionActions` test harness so the new required option typechecks.

Fixes #66057

Credit: Stan Shih (@stantheman0128) — this is his #66610 (with the four deterministic tests from stantheman0128's repro comment), ported onto current main by the Hermes triage build worker.

Co-authored-by: Stan Shih <stanshih888@gmail.com>

## Root cause

`"context"` sits in `_ISOLATED_SESSION_READ_COMMANDS`, so `_live_slash_command_output` returns `None` for any session that does not use a compute host, and the command falls through to the `_SlashWorker` subprocess whose `HermesCLI` never builds an `AIAgent` — its `/context` prints `(._.) No active agent -- send a message first.` for **every** local Desktop/TUI session, active or idle (#81251). `/refine` had no live entry at all, so it hit the same worker fallthrough and answered "Nothing to refine yet" on completed sessions whose in-memory agent cache was absent (#83455).

## What changes

**`/context`, answered in-process for local sessions** (gateway half of #114419):
- New `_CONTEXT_LOCAL_IN_PROCESS` pre-gate branch in `tui_gateway/methods_slash.py`: `/context` on a local session is served by `_format_live_context_output` — agentless or live-agent alike — instead of falling through to the worker.
- With a live agent, the output now carries the full Cursor-style breakdown via the desktop gauge's engine (`agent.context_breakdown.compute_session_context_breakdown`; `/context all` expands per-skill/per-toolset details), with the session cwd bound (`_set_session_context`) so workspace pinning keys on the session, not the backend process.
- Without an agent, the persisted-state view (message counts, model, provider, context usage) — the formatter never required an agent, only the routing gate did.
- `tools`/`help` keep their existing routing (they read `session["agent"]`; serving them agentless would answer worse), and compute-host live routing is unchanged. The race-spawn probe in `test_tui_gateway_server.py` moves from `/context` to an unregistered command, since `/context` no longer reaches the worker.

**`/refine`, run on the live session** (from #109934):
- `_format_live_refine_output` dispatches the background memory/skill review on the session's live agent with `explicit=True` (so unattended-review gates don't swallow it), reading the **persisted transcript** (`get_messages_as_conversation`) when the in-memory history is empty — the reattached/cold-cache case — and falling back to the locked in-memory history mid-conversation.
- Compute-host sessions run it through a new **idle-gated** `slash.refine` control route (`host_supervisor.MUTATOR_ROUTE_TABLE` + the compute-host `_control_ack` branch), mirroring how `slash.model` already crosses that boundary.
- `review_skills` is set from the agent's real toolset (`skill_manage` present).

## Acceptance coverage

| Requirement | Covered |
|---|---|
| #81251: `/context` on a local session with messages returns a breakdown, not "No active agent" | Yes — in-process for ALL local sessions |
| Persisted-state formatter serves local sessions; compute-host live routing unchanged | Yes — guard test pins the compute-host route |
| tools/help keep existing routing | Yes — guard test |
| #83455: `/refine` on a completed session runs the review, not "Nothing to refine yet" | Yes |
| Cold-cache/reattached session falls back to the persisted transcript | Yes — state.db first, in-memory fallback |
| Compute-host sessions can run `/refine` (idle-gated) | Yes — `slash.refine` route |

## Tests (real results)

- `HERMES_PYTHON=$RUN/test-venv/bin/python bash scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tui_gateway/test_context_local_slash.py tests/tui_gateway/test_slash_refine_live.py tests/tui_gateway/test_compute_host_phase1.py`
  - On `origin/main` + the two new test files: **6 failed / 2 passed** (both refine tests red; 4 of 6 context tests red — the 2 passing are the routing guards that pin unchanged behavior) — log: `$RUN/builds/logs/81251-on-main.log`
  - With the fix: **16/16 passed** (includes all 8 pre-existing phase1 tests) — log: `$RUN/builds/logs/81251-with-fix.log`
- Backend-only change: no visible UI, no tsc/lint scope.

Fixes #81251
Fixes #83455

## Root cause

`ImageLightbox` (`apps/desktop/src/components/chat/zoomable-image.tsx`) hard-codes the
image to `max-h-[calc(100vh-12rem)] object-contain` with no zoom, so an oversized image
(e.g. a 2160x13552 screenshot) opens at ~6% scale with no way to see it at original size.

## Fix

- Reuse the shared `useZoomPan` hook (already powering the diagram/artifact viewer) for
  the lightbox image: non-passive native wheel zoom toward the cursor, drag pan,
  two-finger pinch, pointercancel cleanup, and a `moved` flag so only a clean click
  dismisses the lightbox (download action bar and click-to-close preserved).
- Add a zoom control bar (zoom out / percentage / zoom in, i18n'd in en/ar/ja/zh/zh-hant)
  mounted through the dialog's `chrome` slot. Two real defects surfaced while landing it:
  - The lightbox img mounts inside the dialog portal one commit after the open flag flips,
    so a `useZoomPan` effect keyed on `[enabled]` captured a null ref and never attached
    the wheel listener. The hook now tracks the surface node as state (callback ref), so
    the listener attaches on mount.
  - The bar rendered outside `DialogContent`, i.e. outside the dialog portal, where the
    open modal dialog hides it from the a11y tree and react-remove-scroll strips pointer
    events in a real browser. Moving it into the `chrome` slot keeps it interactive.
- Test expectations use the shared hook's step (BUTTON_STEP 1.25 → 125%/80%), and
  `locales/_keys.desktop.json` is regenerated for the new keys.

## Coverage per issue

- #99066 — tall/high-res images can now be viewed near original size: wheel/pinch zoom
  to 8x, drag pan, percentage readout; download and clean-click-to-close preserved.

## Checks run

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --config vitest.config.ts --maxWorkers=2 src/components/chat/zoomable-image.test.tsx src/components/ui/zoomable.test.tsx scripts/i18n-keys.test.mjs` — 14 passed
- Red on base (main's `zoomable-image.tsx` + `use-zoom-pan.ts` with the new tests): 5 of 11 fail (wheel zoom, zoom buttons, pan-after-zoom, pinch, pointercancel).

## Supersedes

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/72588 — Thanks @EvanProgramming: this
  carries that PR's zoom/pan/pinch implementation and i18n (commits cherry-picked with
  authorship preserved), hand-merged onto main's evolved store-based lightbox.
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/99084 — Thanks @salch-cred: the
  zoom/pan/pinch approach covers the full-size legibility case its Fit/Full Size toggle
  addressed. Its unrelated `tests/hermes_cli/test_psutil_android.py` file is not carried.

Fixes #99066


## Screenshots

Isolated harness (real `ImageLightbox` under the app's real `ThemeProvider`, dark mode, tall 420×1600 image, 1000×800):

**Before — `main`: the lightbox is fit-only (max-height 608px, `cursor: zoom-out`), no zoom/pan/controls; the dialog shell also paints a themed background box behind the image:**

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OutThisLife/hermes-agent/5d7376bfaa33dc910d91d4a3bdd8a212cffdde15/pr-127247/before.png)

**After — PR head: wheel-zoomed to 177% (`scale(1.77156)`), drag-panned up so the image bottom moves above the shell's bottom edge, with the zoom bar (−, 177% readout, +) over a clean dark overlay — the exposed strip below the image shows only the scrim, no stray shell box:**

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OutThisLife/hermes-agent/bfa1c17978a6ad3517f39567a7c360580bd153b3/pr-127247/after.png)

Numeric gate (per shot): dark body `color(srgb 0.051 0.063 0.081)` (luma ≈ 16), app font stack active (not serif default); before: img 160×608, no zoom controls in DOM, shell bg `color(srgb 0.086 0.095 0.112 / 0.96)` — after: img 283×1077 at `translate(0,-264px) scale(1.77156)` with `grab` cursor, shell bg `rgba(0,0,0,0)` (`data-variant="media-lightbox"`), zoom bar bg `oklab(0.172 -0.002 -0.011 / 0.85)`. `document.elementsFromPoint` on the exposed strip (y≈685) returns overlay-only with no shell paint; fixed-region pixel delta 113,748 px, and the exposed strip that used to paint the stray box now averages 11/255 (dark scrim) vs 102/255 on `main`. A follow-up commit (`a22497be296`) makes the shell genuinely transparent: styles.css painted every `[data-slot='dialog-content']` with the themed elevated background (the stray box), tailwind-merge couldn't drop the base `shadow-nous`, and the plain `bg-transparent`/`shadow-none` utilities lost the specificity fight — fixed with a `data-variant='media-lightbox'` opt-out + `!` utilities, regression-tested.

## Summary

Adds **groq-provider** to the catalog: Groq as a first-class model provider (`kind: model-provider`, provider id `groq`). Today Groq is reachable only as a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint; in-tree Groq profiles were closed under the third-party integration policy (#75160). Measured on 2026-09-29 against Groq's live API with Hermes v2026.9.24 and main:

| | Custom endpoint → `api.groq.com` | groq-provider |
|---|---|---|
| `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, `-20b` | Every turn fails. The custom profile sends `reasoning_effort: "default"` (`"none"` when reasoning is off) and Groq returns 400 `` `reasoning_effort` must be one of `low`, `medium`, or `high` ``. Reproduced with reasoning unset, `none`, `low` and `high` | Answers; the level goes out as `low`/`medium`/`high` |
| `/model` list | All 11 `/models` rows, including whisper ×2 (no chat endpoint), orpheus ×2 (text-to-speech), prompt-guard ×2 (512-token classifier) and allam-2-7b (4,096-token window; Hermes refuses anything under 64K) | The 4 models Hermes can run |

Two commits:
- `add groq-provider`, pinned to `f12f178`, version 1.0.0.
- `catalog card`: the pin moves to `b5be038`, which only adds `docs/card.png` (outside the plugin directory), and `image` points at it. It stays inside the plugin page hero's visible band (rows 110–490); I checked this on the live site at six widths in both themes, plus the grid card.

## Disclosure / footprint

- One file, `__init__.py`. At import it calls `register_provider(GroqProfile(...))` (the `kind: model-provider` contract) and nothing else: no tools, hooks, commands or threads. It imports only `providers` and `providers.base`.
- It overrides two documented `ProviderProfile` hooks:
  - `build_api_kwargs_extras` puts a top-level `reasoning_effort` for the model families whose values were checked live (`openai/gpt-oss-*`: low/medium/high; `qwen/qwen3.8-*`: none/low/medium/high). A level the model does not take goes to the nearest weaker one it does; a level below the model's lowest (`minimal`, or off on gpt-oss, which always reasons) goes to that lowest one. This is Hermes' own `clamp_effort` rule. The field is left out when reasoning is unset and for every other model, since Groq rejects it on models without reasoning.
  - `fetch_models` calls the base fetch unchanged (`open_credentialed_url`, Bearer) and drops the ids Hermes cannot run.
- Network happens only through Hermes' own client, to `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1` (or the configured `model.base_url`), with `GROQ_API_KEY`, which Hermes resolves. The plugin opens no connections, reads and writes no files and starts no processes.
- Naming: the catalog key is `groq-provider`, per the README's Names rule; the plugin is not affiliated with Groq and its README says so. The provider id is `groq`, the id core already maps (`PROVIDER_TO_MODELS_DEV`, `doctor_live`, `billing_links`).

## Verification

- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` (ruamel.yaml 0.18.17): OK at both commits.
- Replay of the catalog CI's pinned-source step at `f12f178` and at `b5be038`, using Hermes main at `c2f3192929`: clone and checkout OK, `plugin.yaml` found at the subdir, `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` passes with a safe security scan, the self-updater gate is OK, and the subdir README is present and identical to the root one.
- The README URL from `readme_url()` returns 200 with identical bytes at both pins. The pinned `image` URL returns 200 `image/png`, and its bytes match the committed file (sha256).
- Install by name from this branch's catalog records `sha: b5be038…` and installs files identical to the repo's `groq-provider/`. `plugins search groq` lists it under models as `1.0.0 @ b5be0388`.
- Plugin repo CI, 8/8 at each pin ([run 36513408586](https://github.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-groq-provider/actions/runs/36513408586) for `f12f178`, [run 36513822626](https://github.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-groq-provider/actions/runs/36513822626) for `b5be038`):
  - unit jobs on Linux/macOS/Windows × py3.11/3.14: 38 passed each;
  - end-to-end on Hermes v2026.9.24 and main: 46 passed each, and `plugins validate` passes.
- The end-to-end tests patch nothing on the host side. Each check runs in a fresh interpreter with the plugin installed at `$HERMES_HOME/plugins/groq-provider`:
  - provider discovery loads it, and `list_available_providers()` shows Groq as authenticated;
  - `fetch_models` against a server replaying Groq's recorded `/models` response returns the 4 runnable ids;
  - real `hermes chat` turns against `FakeLLMServer` record the wire body for six model/effort cases, and none carries the generic `extra_body.reasoning`.
- Mutation: 11/11 mutants killed. They cover the per-model mapping, the gpt-oss floor, the never-escalate rule, unknown levels, the checked-families-only rule, the model filter (whisper and allam), the override itself, and top-level placement.
- Live, with a free Groq key:
  - through the plugin, `hermes chat --oneshot` answered on gpt-oss-120b and qwen3.8-27b with reasoning unset, `none`, `low` and `high` (main), and on gpt-oss-120b with reasoning unset, `none` and `high` (v2026.9.24);
  - the copy installed by name from GitHub at `b5be038` answered on main at `c2f3192929`, and its picker listed the 4 runnable models from the live API;
  - the same model through a custom endpoint returned the 400 on both versions.

## Scope note

- Groq's free plan allows 8,000 tokens per minute per model (its rate-limit headers). A Hermes request with tools is 10.7K–11.7K tokens with one toolset and about 18.8K with the defaults, so free-plan agent turns get a 413 that Hermes words as "grown too large to send". The README says this. The plugin does not reclassify that 413, because compression is still the right answer when a long tool-less chat crosses the limit; #124104 (open) addresses the classification in core.
- Reasoning values are sent only for the families checked live; any other model runs at Groq's default.
- The model filter works on ids (`whisper`, `orpheus`, `prompt-guard`, `allam`) because the base `fetch_models` returns ids only. Each exclusion matches Groq's own `/models` metadata (a non-text output modality, or `context_window` below 64K); the tests assert this against the recorded response.
- `qwen/qwen3.8-27b` lists image input, but vision is not declared yet: it has not been tried live.

## Related

- #124103 (open, P3) fixes gpt-oss-120b/20b in the core custom profile. The plugin does not depend on it and works the same either way. That PR does not cover `openai/gpt-oss-safeguard-20b` (same 400) or the model list.

In-tree Workers AI providers were closed under the third-party integration policy (#58084, #53105), and #108691 is open. Measured on 2026-09-29 against Cloudflare's live API on the Workers Free plan, with Hermes v2026.9.24 and main:

| | Without the plugin | With it |
|---|---|---|
| `model.provider: cloudflare-workers-ai` (the models.dev id) | `Unknown provider 'cloudflare-workers-ai'` | `workers-ai`, listed in `hermes model` |
| `/model` list through a custom endpoint | `[]`: Cloudflare's OpenAI-compatible `/models` answers 405 | The 16 Workers AI models with function calling and 64K+ context |
| Context window through a custom endpoint | gpt-oss-120b resolves to 256,000 (Cloudflare: 128,000); the host is a custom endpoint, so the 405 probe falls to the default | Cloudflare's values, from the profile's `get_model_context_length` |
| qwen3.8-27b with `reasoning_effort: high` | The turn fails: 400 `Unexpected reasoning effort high. Supported types are xhigh (default), medium, and low` | Sent as `medium`, one request |
| A Workers Paid model on a Free account (Cloudflare 403) | "custom rejected your API key … Update it in Settings" | "Cloudflare Workers AI rejected the request and retrying won't help. Pick another model", plus Cloudflare's "not available on the Workers Free plan" |

The plugin uses its own variable names, so a Pages token in `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (used by the publish-site and cloudflare-temporary-deploy skills) is never sent to Workers AI.

It overrides four documented `ProviderProfile` hooks:

  - `get_model_context_length`, needed because the host is treated as a custom endpoint, whose lookup never reaches the declarations;
  - `build_api_kwargs_extras`, a top-level `reasoning_effort` from each model's `supported_efforts`, using Hermes' `clamp_effort` rule; models without listed levels get no field;
  - `classify_api_error`, which maps only a 403 whose text contains "is not available on the workers free plan" to `model_entitlement`.
- Chat requests go through Hermes' own client to the configured URL with `CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_AI_API_TOKEN`. The plugin reads and writes no files and starts no processes.
- Naming: the catalog key is `cloudflare-workers-ai-provider`, per the Names rule; the plugin is not affiliated with Cloudflare, and its README says so. The provider id is `workers-ai`, because the models.dev id `cloudflare-workers-ai` resolves in `providers.py` to a def whose `api` is the unexpanded `${CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID}` template.

## Verification

- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` (ruamel.yaml 0.18.17): OK at both commits.
- Replay of the catalog CI's pinned-source step at `5cb8a79` and `f6821d0`, using Hermes main at `39faafb616`: clone and checkout OK, `plugin.yaml` found at the subdir, `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` passes with a safe security scan, the self-updater gate is OK, and the subdir README is present and identical to the root one.

- Plugin repo CI, 8/8 at each pin ([run 36519708522](https://github.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-cloudflare-workers-ai-provider/actions/runs/36519708522) for `5cb8a79`, [run 36519863346](https://github.com/AhmetArif0/hermes-cloudflare-workers-ai-provider/actions/runs/36519863346) for `f6821d0`):
  - unit jobs on Linux/macOS/Windows × py3.11/3.14: 43 passed each;
  - end-to-end on Hermes v2026.9.24 and main: 51 passed each, and `plugins validate` passes.
- The end-to-end tests patch nothing on the host side. Each runs in a fresh interpreter with the plugin installed at `$HERMES_HOME/plugins/cloudflare-workers-ai-provider` and the two variables in `.env`:
  - discovery gives the registry row (`base_url_env_var`), an authenticated picker row and the 16 models;

- Live, on the Workers Free plan:

## What does this PR do?

For `no_agent` (script-only) cron jobs, a script failure is recorded correctly — `last_status="error"`,
`failure_streak += 1`, `last_error` set — but the **next successful run resets both in the same pass**
(`cron/jobs.py::_record_run_outcome`), and nothing durable records that a failure happened. A silent
watchdog-style script that fails every Nth tick collapses to a single visible tick: the job self-heals
its own status, and any monitor sampling `jobs.json` later (dashboards, health checks, daily
summaries, `cron list`) reports green forever (#118354 — reproduced on a real fleet, where three real
overnight failures were invisible to a Daily All-Clear monitor).

Fix (the issue's option 1, generalized to the whole class so agent-run jobs heal the same way):

- Every failed run stamps `job["last_failure"] = {at, detail}` — latest failure wins. A later success
  does **not** clear it; `last_status`/`failure_streak` keep describing *current* health while
  `last_failure` preserves the recency evidence. The recency window stays the consumer's call.
- `create_job` seeds `last_failure: None` so the schema is explicit and persisted.
- `hermes cron list` prints a warning line for the stamp — `⚠ Last failure at <at>: <detail>` —
  marked "recovered since" (yellow) when `last_status` is healthy, red when the current status is
  still the failure. While `last_status` reports the failure it is redundant-but-consistent; after
  recovery it is the only job-level trace left.
- Delivery failures keep their own sticky `last_delivery_error` channel; the stamp's `detail` falls
  back to the explicit `status` (e.g. `blocked_config`) when `error` is absent.

Mirrors the existing `last_fire_error` stamp shape (`{at, detail}`) and its tested overwrite semantics.

## Related Issue

Fixes #118354

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `cron/jobs.py`: stamp in `_record_run_outcome`; seed the key in `create_job`.
- `hermes_cli/cron.py`: `_job_warnings` line for the stamp.
- `tests/cron/test_last_failure_stamp.py` (new): stamp written on failure; the healing success resets
  `last_status`/`failure_streak` but keeps the stamp; latest failure wins; success without prior
  failure leaves no stamp; status-fallback detail; delivery-failure separation.

## How to Test

1. `python -m pytest tests/cron/test_last_failure_stamp.py tests/cron/test_fire_forward_failure_stamp.py tests/cron/test_jobs.py -q`
2. End to end: create a `no_agent` script job that exits 1, let it fire, watch `jobs.json` show
   `last_status=error` + `last_failure` set; let a successful tick fire; `last_status` returns to `ok`
   and `failure_streak` to 0, while `last_failure` still names the failure — `hermes cron list` shows
   it with "recovered since".

## Checklist

### Code
- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix
- [x] I've run `pytest` on the touched cron suites (126 cron tests + 28 CLI tests pass)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11 x64 (pure-Python path; cron store behavior is
  platform-neutral)

### Documentation & Housekeeping
- [x] New job-record key documented in docstrings; no config keys added
