Moves `sha` and `version` together to the released commit: vectorize-io/hindsight `d56c4acdf`, tag [`integrations/hermes/v1.2.1`](https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight/releases/tag/integrations/hermes/v1.2.1). The `image` URL is repinned to the same sha.

Thanks for already dropping the `known_issues` entry and repinning to `eb021da3` in 5e4857bf — this is the tagged release of that same work plus two fixes on top, so the pin now points at a version rather than a commit-suffixed one.

## What changed in the plugin since 1.1.0

`local_embedded` no longer imports the Hindsight server into Hermes' venv. It could not be installed there in the first place: `hindsight-all` pulls `hindsight-api-slim`, which needs `protobuf>=7.35.1` against `mem0ai==2.0.10`'s and `modal==1.5.5`'s `protobuf<7.0`, and `opentelemetry-semantic-conventions>=0.65b0` against `mistralai==2.4.8`'s `<0.61`. Relaxing one pin only uncovers the next.

Instead the plugin composes what the old wrapper composed internally — `hindsight_embed.get_embed_manager()` plus `hindsight_client.Hindsight` — and the server runs as its own process (an installed `hindsight-api` binary, else the `uvx` fallback in its own environment). Hermes' venv keeps only `hindsight-client` and `hindsight-embed`, both declared in the plugin's `pyproject.toml`, so nothing is fetched at runtime and cloud-mode users never pay for the local-ML stack (482 MB on macOS arm64, 3.2 GB on Linux x86_64 with the CUDA wheels).

Existing embedded users keep their data: the profile decides the daemon, so the pg0 database (`~/.pg0/instances/hindsight-embed-<profile>/`) and the profile env (`~/.hindsight/profiles/<profile>.env`) are the same files. Verified against a real database in both directions.

## In v1.2.1 specifically

- **First-run notice.** With no `hindsight-api` binary the daemon comes down through `uvx` (0.5-3 GB depending on platform) and nothing reached the user during it — the manager's panel lands in a log file only after the attempt ends, so a first run looked like Hermes hanging (the 6m23s reply in #4936 that retained nothing and printed no error). One line now goes through the same gated warning sink as the root-refusal notice.
- **One daemon, one client.** `_get_client` was an unguarded check-then-set and in embedded mode the "set" starts the daemon, so the background start worker and the first memory operation could each start one, with the loser's client dropped unclosed. Now serialised.
- **Repair hints point at PM**, since `hermes plugins install hindsight` refuses with *"Plugin 'hindsight' already exists"* once installed (verified) — they now say `hermes pm repair` / `hermes plugins update hindsight`.
- **`plugin.yaml` carries no dependency list**, with a comment saying why: PM reads the plugin's own `pyproject.toml` and ignores the manifest lists, so a copy could only drift. Consent and install still list both packages.

## Also fixed earlier in the 1.2.x line

Nothing calls `tools.lazy_deps.install_specs` any more (it was reached from the availability probe, the setup wizard and the client auto-upgrade) — the loop in #126494; thanks for `af26acab73`. And the plugin works around `hindsight-embed <= 0.10.2` copying `os.environ` into the daemon by starting it from a child without `PYTHONPATH`/`PYTHONHOME`/`PYTHONSAFEPATH`/`VIRTUAL_ENV`; verified by forcing `UV_PYTHON=3.12` against a 3.14 host, where the direct call dies in 5s on `pydantic_core._pydantic_core` and the child path starts in 17s. It detects the fix from #4936 in a future embed release and steps aside.

## Verified on a package-manager install

Hermes `v0.21.5+4560.gbca2e3c`, embed 0.10.2, isolated profile, local ollama:

| | result |
|---|---|
| cloud | in daily use |
| local_external | loads, initializes, retain/recall/sync_turn/shutdown |
| local_embedded `is_available()` | True (previously False: asked for `hindsight-all`) |
| local_embedded daemon start | out-of-process, reuses a running daemon |
| local_embedded retain via `sync_turn` | reaches the daemon, `mode=append` |
| local_embedded recall via `queue_prefetch` + `prefetch` | returns the fact, `recall_status count=3` |

## Known rough edges, not blockers

- A `pip install --target` layout is not covered by the binary probe, so such a user may see the download notice and then no download. Harmless direction; missing the notice was the real problem.
- pg0 refuses to run as root (reported with a clear message), and a machine with many embedded instances can exhaust SysV shared memory — I hit that myself while testing.

## What does this PR do?

Adds `plugin-catalog/0bull.yaml`, a community entry for 0bull: real iPhones rented by the month that an agent can see and operate, and post videos from to TikTok and YouTube Shorts.

The plugin is a portable Agent Plugins v1 package (`plugin.json` + `mcp.json` + `skills/`) at the root of https://github.com/0bull/agent-plugin. Its `mcp.json` declares one Streamable HTTP server, `https://0bull.net/mcp`, and it bundles three skills (`0bull-iphone-control`, `0bull-tiktok-post`, `0bull-youtube-post`). No Python, no desktop bundle, no dependencies, no credentials: users sign in with their 0bull account through browser OAuth (`auth: oauth` plus `hermes mcp login 0bull`, as in the README). `openclaw.plugin.json` and `package.json` are there only so the same folder publishes to ClawHub as a bundle plugin.

Submitted by the owner of the 0bull organization.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

Bumps the `provider-status` catalog card to 1.5.11, a scoping fix.

## What changed in the plugin

Two pieces of the plugin reached past its own elements and restyled the app around them, so two plugins touching either seam would have fought each other.

The injected theme stylesheet matched `[data-slot="checkbox"]` with no ancestor scope, so it repainted every checkbox in the app. It is now `[data-ps-row] [data-slot="checkbox"]`, and `data-ps-row` is set on this plugin's own provider rows, the same pattern `memory-review` uses with `data-mrc-row`.

The glass effect restyled every `[data-slot="dialog-overlay"]` in the document while the dialog was open, which included dialogs owned by other plugins. The house overlay is a sibling of the dialog content inside the Radix portal rather than a descendant of it, so a descendant selector cannot scope it. The `DialogContent` now carries `data-ps-dialog`; the effect reads that node, takes the overlay sitting in the same portal wrapper, stores that element reference, and clears that exact reference on close. Cleanup no longer queries the document.

Behaviour is unchanged. The overlay is still `bg-black/6%` with a 10px blur, only while this dialog is open and the Glass option is on, and it reverts on close.

The `select[data-ps-select] option` rule was already scoped by the plugin's own attribute and is untouched.

## Changes in this file

Three lines: `sha`, `version`, and the `image` URL, which embeds the same sha.

- `sha`: `1264a8e112f1b2133f3f02b89e230e0df538a80f` -> `517dc1aa4047686a8899f3d81befe66d2d8cda4c`
- `version`: `1.5.10` -> `1.5.11`

`subdir` remains `public/provider-status`. Description, `docs_url` and `capabilities` are unchanged.

## Verification

- The pinned `public/provider-status` tree reports `version: 1.5.11`, matching the card, in both `plugin.yaml` and `dashboard/manifest.json`.
- The pinned `desktop/plugin.js` parses as an ES module, checked with `node --check` on a `.mjs` copy. A plain `.js` check parses as CommonJS and can pass a file the loader rejects.
- Every selector in the file that targets a house-rendered element is behind a plugin-owned attribute. The stylesheet's two checkbox rules sit under `[data-ps-row]`; the overlay lookup runs against the portal wrapper of `[data-ps-dialog]`. The other three DOM queries (`[data-pid]`, `[data-add-picker]`, `[data-ps-dialog]`) already matched the plugin's own elements.
- No cleanup path re-queries the document for overlays.
- The `image` URL returns HTTP 200 at the new sha.

Tag `provider-status-v1.5.11` on the plugin repo points at that same commit, as a lightweight tag like the previous ones.

items.body:
A portable plugin can now say its MCP server needs an NVIDIA GPU (`requires: {gpu: nvidia}`). On a machine without one, Hermes refuses the install, hides the server's tools, and says why.

## The problem

A portable plugin (a `plugin.json` + `mcp.json` + skills package that points Hermes at an app's MCP server) can already declare the app it drives. Hermes then checks that the app is installed at a fixed path, at a minimum version, before it offers the tools. NVIDIA App and NVIDIA Broadcast use this.

Some apps have no fixed path to check. The RTX Remix Toolkit ships as a zip that NVIDIA's own README says to "extract anywhere". It has no installer and no registry entry. What it does need is an NVIDIA GPU. Without a way to say that, its plugin installs on a Mac or an AMD PC, and the tools never appear, with no explanation.

## What changes

```json
"extensions": {"com.nousresearch.hermes": {"servers": {"rtx-remix": {
  "requires": {"gpu": "nvidia"}
}}}}
```

`requires.gpu` works with or without an `app:` block. The check is `hermes_platform.host.facts.gpu_class()`, which already exists: it reads the registry on Windows and sysfs on Linux, never a subprocess or a driver library, and is cached per process.

| Where the user meets it | On a machine without an NVIDIA GPU |
|---|---|
| `hermes plugins install` | Refused: `Plugin 'rtx-remix' server 'rtx-remix' is unavailable: unsupported_gpu, needs an NVIDIA GPU.` Nothing is written. |
| `hermes plugins validate` | `server availability: rtx-remix — unsupported_gpu` |
| Tools in a chat | Hidden. The MCP `check_fn` already asks `availability()` for any registered declaration. |
| Plugin catalog card | "needs an NVIDIA GPU" |
| Plugins tab and tool errors, if the plugin got installed anyway (for example a synced home) | New state `unsupported_gpu`, pill "GPU not supported", sentence "rtx-remix needs an NVIDIA GPU; none was found on this machine. Use rtx-remix on a machine with an NVIDIA GPU." |

On a machine with an NVIDIA GPU, nothing changes: the state is `no_requirements`, as for a plugin with no declaration, and the connection check still decides.

The new state is added to `PluginServerState` in the gateway contract (regenerated `gateway-contract.*`), the Desktop store type, the Plugins tab tone map, and the label in en/de/es/fr. `locales/_keys.desktop.json` is regenerated.

## Decisions to check

1. **An unreadable GPU passes.** `gpu_class()` returns `unknown` when the registry or sysfs read fails, and on Intel Macs. Refusing on `unknown` would lock out a machine that has the GPU; passing costs what happens today (the tools don't connect). The alternative is to fail closed.
2. **Only `nvidia` is accepted.** `gpu_class()` reports the highest-priority vendor present (NVIDIA, then AMD, then Intel). That answers "is there an NVIDIA GPU" exactly. It would give the wrong answer for `amd` or `intel` on a machine that also has an NVIDIA GPU, so those values are rejected at parse time until someone needs them and the fact returns the full vendor set.
3. **A new wire state instead of reusing `missing_app`.** Reusing it would avoid the contract and Desktop changes, but the sentence would say "Install rtx-remix", which cannot fix a missing GPU.

## Not in this PR

- The `rtx-remix` plugin's declaration: NousResearch/hermes-nvidia#3. That plugin must merge after a Hermes release that contains this change. Older releases reject the unknown key with `requires has unknown keys ['gpu']`.
- The catalog entry for `rtx-remix`: #129444, stacked on this PR and pinned to hermes-nvidia#3.
- `unsupported_os` still produces "Install <app>" in the status sentence. That is existing behavior and a separate change.

## Live verification

Hermes at `38505e27f1`, this change before the rebase onto `main` at `653bc4f288`; the rebase changed no line of the diff outside `locales/_keys.desktop.json`. The plugin was the `rtx-remix` package from hermes-nvidia#3 with the declaration above added.

| Machine | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| macOS, Apple silicon | `hermes plugins validate` | `server availability: rtx-remix — unsupported_gpu` |
| macOS, Apple silicon | `hermes plugins install` (fresh `HERMES_HOME`) | Refused with `unsupported_gpu, needs an NVIDIA GPU.`; `plugins/` stays empty |
| Windows ARM64 laptop with an NVIDIA GPU | `facts.gpu_class()` | `nvidia` |
| same | `hermes plugins validate` | `server availability: rtx-remix — no_requirements` |
| same | `hermes plugins install` | Passed the availability check. It then failed later, at publish, because the ARM64 native-build-tools step (`windows-deps.ps1`) fails on that machine, which has a partial Visual Studio install. That step is unrelated to this change. |
| same, RTX Remix Toolkit running | a chat turn with the declared plugin in place | `MCP server 'rtx-remix' (HTTP): registered 39 tool(s)`. The model called `remix_get_loaded_project` and relayed the Toolkit's answer. |

Not run live: the catalog card sentence and the Plugins tab pill; the tests below cover the state and sentence behind them.

Tests:

- The two new tests fail on `origin/main` and pass here. `tests/hermes_platform/test_declaration.py` covers the gate by GPU class, and the OS gate running first without reading the GPU. `tests/tools/test_mcp_liveness.py` covers a connected server being hidden, and its state and sentence.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_validate.py::test_portable_validation_fails_orphan_and_reports_availability` fails on macOS on `main` as well. It expects a bare state, but validate appends the path. It passes on Linux, where the state is `unsupported_os`.

Adds one entry to `plugin-catalog/`: **dashboard-button** (community, `desktop`).

### What it does

One-click access to the Hermes Web Dashboard (`http://127.0.0.1:9119`) from the Desktop app:

- a **sidebar row** that opens the dashboard inside the main pane (no browser tab),
- an **in-app page that loads itself** — while the server is down it shows status and opens the dashboard the moment the port answers; if the connection drops it reloads when the server returns,
- a **status-bar chip with a live dot** (green/red/grey) that opens the dashboard in the default browser, waiting for the server to come up before it does.

Pure front-end — the desktop half is the entire plugin. It registers no tools, hooks or middleware, spends no tokens, and the only network traffic is a liveness probe against the local dashboard port. It never starts the dashboard itself; the repo ships an optional Windows watchdog (`companion/dashboard_watchdog.py`) for people who want it always up, wired as a no-agent cron job.

### Pin

- repo: https://github.com/g3org3yo/dashboard-button
- sha: `cd0837e50e46bb8efca6e66d63a264325a5cbcb2` (tagged `v1.0.0`, released)
- layout at the pin: `plugin.yaml` (manifest) + `__init__.py` (agent half, intentionally empty — `def register(ctx): del ctx`) + `desktop/plugin.js` (the whole feature)

### Validation (run locally at the pinned commit)

`hermes plugins validate .`:

```
✓ manifest — plugin.yaml parses
✓ manifest fields — name, version, description present
✓ requires_hermes — spec '>=0.20' parses
✓ config schema — not declared
✓ requires_env — all entries UPPER_SNAKE
✓ loadable — entry: __init__.py, desktop/plugin.js
✓ python dependencies — none declared
✓ capability probe — register() ran in isolation
✓ declared tools — matches registrations
✓ declared hooks — matches registrations
✓ declared middleware — matches registrations
✓ built-in tool collisions — no tools to check
✓ security scan — safe
✓ desktop surface — stays inside the plugin SDK surface

Validation passed.
```

`hermes plugins doctor .` → `manifest: dashboard-button 1.0.0 (standalone)` / `OK: runtime discovery, manifest parsing, import, and registration passed` / `registrations: 0 tool(s), 0 hook(s)`.

### Policy notes

- **Capabilities** are declared empty and are empty in reality (rule 6): nothing registered, no env vars, no `config_schema`, no `python_dependencies`.
- **No self-updating code** (rule 3): the plugin reads no remote `plugin.js`, has no updater, and does not touch its own files. Updates only arrive via a SHA-bump PR here.
- **Desktop surface** (rule 8): `desktop/plugin.js` uses only `@hermes/plugin-sdk` — no prototype patching, no `eval`/`new Function`, no dynamic `import()`, no script-tag injection, no app internals.
- **Owner submission** (rule 5): this PR is from the repo owner.

`docs_url` is left empty; the catalog page can render the repo README at the pin (`readme: true`), which documents the Desktop 0.20.x SDK-loader bug this plugin was built alongside, plus the standalone hotfix tool it ships for it (upstream issue #107304 / PR #107303).

Three Krea / managed-image changes by @entropidelic, salvaged together onto current `main` with follow-up fixes:

- `hermes portal tools` names the partner behind the managed image pick (FAL, Krea or Nous Portal) instead of always saying FAL. The Tool Gateway docs page now describes the single picker. (salvage of #114418)
- Local image files work as Krea style references. Before, a path from disk was sent to Krea as-is and rejected. (salvage of #118444)
- The Krea 2 sliders (`intensity`, `complexity`, `movement`) and `creativity` are offered to the agent, but only while a Krea model is active. (salvage of #119267)

Based on #114418, #118444 and #119267 by @entropidelic. All six of their commits are cherry-picked with authorship kept. The mapping `contributors/emails/mariano.nicolini@lambdaclass.com` was already on main.

## Follow-ups on top (ours)

- **Portal partner:** the routing rule moves into one pure function, `tools.image_generation_managed.managed_route()`.
  - The dispatcher (`_managed_model_plugin`) and the new `managed_image_partner()` both call it, so the partner label and the actual route can't disagree.
  - Dispatch behaviour is unchanged: all 36 provider × model combinations I checked give the same result as before the refactor.
  - The label now follows the actual route:
  - A direct vendor selection returns nothing. Before this, `provider: openai` with `gpt-image-2` printed "partner: Nous Portal".
  - An unset provider (or legacy `use_gateway: true`) with a Portal model id reads FAL, because that is the path it actually runs.
  - Dropped the "Nous Subscription (Krea)" feature label. Every consumer prints "via Nous Portal" in the only state that label can reach, so no screen ever showed it.
  - Dropped the krea readiness-probe switch. `is_managed_tool_gateway_ready` is a local URL+token check, so fal-queue and krea give the same answer.
  - The gateway-offer checklist no longer says "Image generation (FAL)".
- **Krea local refs:**
  - The credential-read guard now runs before `is_file()` / `stat()`. A denied path such as `HERMES_HOME/.env` no longer answers "not found" or "over 3 MB", which would reveal whether it exists and how big it is.
  - A denial is returned as the plugin's normal error dict instead of an exception.
  - Local files are read only after the managed LoRA/moodboard fail-fast, so a request that is about to be refused never reads them.
  - Each file is read once, at most one byte past the remaining budget, so the 3 MB cap applies to the bytes actually sent.
  - Legacy non-dict references pass through untouched instead of raising.
- **Sliders:** each plugin route passes a provider only the controls listed in its `capabilities()["creative_controls"]`.
  - The case this covers: after the user switches backends, a model can copy slider values from earlier turns.
  - Without the filter, a third-party `generate()` without `**kwargs` would raise TypeError and break plain text-to-image.
- **Docs:** `supports_upscale` and `creative_controls` are now documented in the `ImageGenProvider.capabilities()` docstring and the provider-plugin guide.
- **Tests:** the contributor tests were trimmed to behaviour contracts. That means one parametrized refusal test instead of three, and one relationship test for the schema instead of pinned enum and bounds values.

## Validation

| Check | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `portal tools`, nous + `krea-2-medium` | partner: FAL | partner: Krea |
| `portal tools`, nous + `openai/gpt-image-2` | partner: FAL | partner: Nous Portal |
| `portal tools`, `provider: openai` or `provider: fal` + a Krea model | FAL | FAL (unchanged) |
| `managed_image_partner`, provider unset + `openai/gpt-image-2` | — | FAL (the runtime route) |
| Krea, local `image_url` | raw path posted | `data:image/png;base64,…` posted |
| Krea, missing file / `.env` / `auth.json` / symlink to `auth.json` | path posted, success | `invalid_image_url` error, no POST |
| Krea, 3 MB+1 file or 4×900 KB | posted | `source_too_large` error, no POST |
| Schema, nous + Krea model | no sliders | `creativity`, `intensity`, `complexity`, `movement` |
| Schema, fal / openai / unset / Portal model | — | byte-identical to main |
| Krea payload for `intensity=80, complexity=-100, movement=150, creativity=raw` | no sliders, creativity `medium` | intensity 80, complexity -100, creativity raw; out-of-range movement dropped |
| openai plugin given the same args | — | receives no controls |

- The live probes ran against real imports with a temp `HERMES_HOME`. Network access was blocked by socket patches, and Krea/FAL requests were patched out.
- Targeted suites: 41 files, 639 passed, 0 failed.
- Each new test was run with the production file reverted to main and fails there. The guard-order and control-filter tests were also mutation-checked: re-introducing either bug turns them red.
- Krea's API docs confirm that data URIs are accepted for style references and that all three Krea 2 endpoints, including Medium Turbo, accept the sliders.

Relayed bot DMs into a host's default (launch) profile spawn again on multi-profile backends, instead of dying with "Hermes could not read this profile's API key".

Salvage of #120945 by @nicbj96: the contributor's two commits are cherry-picked with their authorship kept, trimmed during review.

## Why
Reported on #120945 by the author and two downstream fleets (8–9 failed relays each, 2026-09-22..25). `_profile_home()` returns `None` for the launch profile by design, and the `bot_relay.deliver` RPC is sessionless, so it binds no scope. Once the backend has served a second profile (multiplex on), `served_profile_child_env` then fails closed. Deliveries to named profiles, which do resolve a home, kept working.

## Changes
- `tools/bot_relay.py::delivery_env`: under multiplex, with no profile home, override or bound scope, the child gets the pinned launch home. This is the same shape as the slash-worker spawn fix (#115427). A bound scope or override still wins. Contributor commit + our follow-up that limits it to multiplex, so single-profile hosts and the separate DM-runner process keep their pass-through env unchanged.
- `tools/bot_failure_reasons.py`: new `target_scope_unresolved` reason for this refusal, claimed before the auth rules and never auto-retried. It previously classified as `unknown`. Our follow-up also matches the named-secret spelling (`…this profile's OPENROUTER_API_KEY…`).
- Dropped from the original PR in review:
  - the target-side refusal message and its `bot_relay.deliver` branch, which can't be reached once `delivery_env` always has a target;
  - the sender-side reply rewrite plus claimed-envelope reader. Its own refusal text classified as `unknown`, so it never fired for patched targets, and the copy hard-coded this bug's workaround.

## Validation
| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| multiplex on, `delivery_env(None, None)` | raises `UnscopedSecretError` | launch home + launch key |
| live `bot_relay.deliver` RPC, profile=default, after real `activate_multi_profile_hosting()` (only `_run` stubbed) | error 5094, reason `unknown`, no spawn | spawned with launch home + key |
| A→B→A (named profile, then launch again) | B ok, launch raises | B / launch each get their own home + key |
| bound scope / home override | honoured | still honoured over the fallback |
| multiplex off | pass-through env | unchanged (byte-identical) |

- The tests pin a literal launch home against a host-mirrored `HERMES_HOME`. They go red when the fallback is removed, when it's swapped to `get_process_hermes_home()`, or when the multiplex limit is dropped. The classifier row goes red on the original narrower regex.
- Targeted suites: 168 passed, 5 skipped (`test_bot_relay`, `test_bot_failure_reasons`, `test_bot_relay_windows_paths`, `test_bot_relay_methods`, `test_relay_live_author`, `test_bot_mode_dm`).

Not in scope: a key written into `os.environ` after launch-env capture still reaches a launch-profile child. Main's slash-worker spawn does the same, so it is a class-wide follow-up, not part of this fix.

## What does this PR do?
- Incident dedup now ignores measured durations (`603s`, `12.5 seconds`, `250ms`, `2h`) when it computes the error signature.
- The same watchdog stall now maps to one incident, so an ack keeps it silent and the reminder cooldown applies.
- Status codes and other numbers (`429`, `exit code 1`) still count, so different failures still get separate incidents.
- The stored error text is unchanged. Only the hash input is masked.

## Related Issue
Fixes #129587

## Changes Made
- `cron/incidents.py`: add `_DURATION_RE` and mask matches in `_error_signature`.
- `tests/cron/test_cron_incidents.py`: invariant test through `run_one_job`. After an ack, a stall that differs only in idle seconds must not ping again.
- `website/docs/user-guide/features/cron.md`: say what the signature normalization ignores.

## How to Test
```python
import cron.incidents as inc
a, _ = inc.upsert_incident("job-1", "Cron job 'x' idle for 601s (limit 600s)")
inc.ack_incident(a)
b, is_new = inc.upsert_incident("job-1", "Cron job 'x' idle for 604s (limit 600s)")
assert a == b and not is_new
assert inc.get_incident(a)["state"] == "closed"
```

Before / after signature input:
```
before: "cron job 'x' idle for 603s (limit 600s)"
after:  "cron job 'x' idle for #s (limit #s)"
```

## What

Adds a catalog entry for `hermes-turn-usage` — a post-reply usage/cost footer.

Every reply gets a one-line summary that expands into per-turn and cumulative tokens, cache
hit rate, reasoning share, cost, context occupancy, prompt composition, and a **per-tool time
breakdown** (which tool actually consumed the wall clock, not just the total).

## Why it may be interesting

- **Cost is `tokens × live unit price` keyed on `billing_provider`**, not `estimated_cost_usd`
  — which I measured to under-report 19–29% on main turns and 51–61% on auxiliary forks,
  drifting in both directions rather than by a constant factor (same data point I posted on
  #115659).
- **Waiting time is separated out.** A blocking `clarify` prompt is reported on its own row
  marked *not counted* and kept out of the active-time denominator, so "waiting for the user"
  does not read as "the agent is slow".
- **Time is attributed per tool**, parsed from `agent.log`, so no extra instrumentation and no
  new hook is needed.
- Uses `transform_llm_output` only, so it works on every platform, not just Desktop.
- Pure computation — it never calls a model, and any failure leaves the reply untouched.

## Validation

`hermes plugins validate` passes all 13 checks at the pinned commit: manifest parses, fields
present, config schema shape valid, `requires_env` naming, loadable, no Python dependencies,
capability probe runs in isolation, declared tools/hooks/middleware match registrations, and
the security scan is clean.

## Known caveat (flagging up front)

The UI strings are written in Traditional Chinese, so this does not meet the "English-first
UI" note that applies to catalog sweeps. If that is a requirement for admission, I am happy to
add an English-first layer or follow whatever i18n convention the app uses — I would rather
raise it now than after review.

## Pin

`8e4ff82aaf6d0da40ee851b21a1bd627c663099d` — exact 40-character SHA. The plugin has no
self-updater; updates would come as a SHA-bump PR here.

Typing `@pep:` in the TUI or Desktop composer suggests PEPs by number or by words of the title through `complete.path`.

It is built only on the plugin context-reference API (`ctx.register_context_reference`, #26193, shipped in #84937), like wiki-ref (#128257), osv-ref (#128540) and gh-ref (#128615) from the same repo. Submitted by the owner (rule 5): I maintain `EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs`.

- Pinned SHA: `20c7a0e1f56d6fea9761077f6994ab7b3d174b99` (1.0.0 plus the card). The first commit pins the release commit `4a0ae73`; the second re-pins to `20c7a0e`, which only adds the card (`git diff 4a0ae73 20c7a0e -- pep-ref` is empty). The plugin's CI is green on both: [4a0ae73](https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/actions/runs/36773303731), [20c7a0e](https://github.com/EloquentBrush0x/hermes-context-refs/actions/runs/36775364760)
- Category `web`: it pulls web content into the turn and registers no tools.

**Footprint** (also in the entry's `Disclosure —` sentence and the README's "Security and footprint" section):
- `register()` only calls `ctx.register_context_reference(...)`: no tools, hooks, middleware or commands.
- Network: HTTPS GET to `https://peps.python.org` only: `/api/peps.json` (the index of every PEP, ~430 kB) and the referenced PEP's page. Redirects are followed only on the same HTTPS host; responses over 4 MiB are refused. Which PEP pages are opened leaves the machine; section names and autocomplete text are matched locally.

- Settings (`max_chars`, `timeout_seconds`) come from `config_schema` and are read per reference; an unusable value becomes a context warning on that reference.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

In a group chat, `@everyone` (or a direct `@mention`) could lose a member's reply to the room's own redundancy heuristic: the participation rules tell each member to "reply with ONE conversational message ONLY if you have something new worth adding" and otherwise exactly `"(pass)"`, so once the first member answered, the second listed member reliably `(pass)`ed — and because a `(pass)` is `spoke=false` and never appended to the room log, the turn settled as ordinary quiet consensus. The user's explicit address silently disappeared (#129443).

This PR enforces the invariant in engine state instead of prompt wording alone:

- `explicitlyAddressedMemberKeys()` (group-rounds.ts) freezes what the driving user send addressed as structured state: `@everyone`/`@all` expands to every member, a bare `@mention` to just the named ones, and a send with no mention at all to **nobody** — that turn stays collaborative, where an ordinary `(pass)` is legitimate silence. Only user entries are scanned; a member's `@handoff` inside its own reply remains the #94478 continuation's business.
- An addressed member's `(pass)` gets **one bounded nudge** (group-round-members.ts): the same turn prompt plus a `GROUP_ADDRESSED_NUDGE_SUFFIX` directive that the address cannot be passed on. The recovered reply replaces the pass and flows through the unchanged commit path (epoch check → watermark advance → append). A nudge that throws falls into the existing failed-turn catch.
- A second `(pass)` after the nudge is recorded as **explicit noncompliance** — a `failed` activity row with reason `explicitly addressed member passed twice` plus a roster attention badge — instead of settling silently.
- Superseded drives do neither: the nudge and the disclosure are gated on `isCurrent()` (binding AND epoch), so a turn the epoch check merely tolerated committing (a cross-thread send superseded its drive) is stale residue and stays quiet.

## Related Issue

Fixes #129443

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/group-round-prompt.ts` — add `GROUP_ADDRESSED_NUDGE_SUFFIX`, the one-shot directive appended when an explicitly addressed member `(pass)`ed.
- `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/group-rounds.ts` — add `explicitlyAddressedMemberKeys()` (user-entry-only mention aggregation) and pass it into the round context as `addressedKeys` for the whole drive.
- `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/group-round-members.ts` — `GroupRoundMemberContext.addressedKeys`; the bounded nudge inside the turn's try block; the noncompliance `failed` activity + attention badge when the nudge is passed on too.
- `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/group-rounds.test.ts` — update four expectations that now see the (intended) extra nudge call for sends that `@`-addressed a member, with comments pointing at #129443.
- `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/group-rounds.addressed.test.ts` — new: addressing classification (@everyone / bare mention / no mention / member handoff not counted), nudge-then-recovered-reply posted, second-pass noncompliance recorded, collaborative pass untouched.

## How to Test

1. `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/plugins/hermes-bots/group-rounds.addressed.test.ts` — Observed result: 5 passed (addressing classification, nudge recovery, noncompliance, collaborative-pass no-op).

## Summary

Bumps the community **tool-slimmer** entry (maintained by me, @aliasocracy) from the pin it got in the September sweep, `3128c8fe` (v0.6.5), to **0.8.0**.

- pin: `3128c8fe3c27694c7d2f2dd16e5d639cf65b63f6` → `1b90aa592f7423233ea6cdfd44c7188e14ca7ccf` (tag [`v0.8.0`](https://github.com/aliasocracy/hermes-tool-slimmer/releases/tag/v0.8.0) resolves to it)
- `version` label → `"0.8.0"`
- `requires_hermes: ">=0.19"`: a catalog install doesn't run the repo's core-patch installer, so on older Hermes it would only load as diagnostics
- capabilities: adds `provides_middleware: [llm_request]`. Tools and hooks are unchanged, and no env var is required.

## Why

On current Hermes the pinned v0.6.5 can't slim anything. It depended on a local core patch adding a `select_tool_schemas` hook, which Hermes updates and Docker rebuilds remove, so it falls back to diagnostics only. A user reported this in aliasocracy/hermes-tool-slimmer#5. 0.7.0 moved to Hermes' built-in `llm_request` middleware instead, so no core patch is needed.

## What changed since v0.6.5

- **0.7.0:** slims requests through `llm_request` middleware on Hermes v0.19+ (OpenAI chat, Anthropic messages and Codex responses payloads). It only removes function tools, and it keeps provider server tools, a forced `tool_choice` target and the prompt-cache breakpoint. It also detects a half-applied core patch, and advisor and rollback no longer rewrite an unparseable `config.yaml`. `doctor` and `status` report the active surface.
- **0.8.0:** an optional, experimental `mode: jev` that is **off by default**. A user who turns it on gets an external call each turn: their request text plus the candidate tools' names and descriptions go to TypeSafe's API (`api.typesafe.ai`), using `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` from the environment. It's documented in `docs/privacy.md` and shown by `hermes tool-slimmer privacy` and `doctor`. Every other mode makes no network calls, and the model-callable `tool_slimmer_select` tool can't switch itself into `jev`. 0.8.0 also declares the middleware in `plugin.yaml`; 0.7.0 failed `hermes plugins validate` without it.

Full notes: [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/aliasocracy/hermes-tool-slimmer/blob/1b90aa592f7423233ea6cdfd44c7188e14ca7ccf/CHANGELOG.md).

`requires_env` stays empty because `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is only needed for that opt-in mode.

## Verification

I ran these against a fresh clone at `1b90aa5` with `hermes-agent` at `1fd412e` (v0.21.5), in a throwaway `HERMES_HOME`:

- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py` on the entry: **OK**
- `hermes plugins validate`: all checks pass, including declared tools, hooks and middleware matching registrations, and security scan `safe`
- `hermes plugins install https://github.com/aliasocracy/hermes-tool-slimmer --ref 1b90aa592f7423233ea6cdfd44c7188e14ca7ccf`, then `enable`: installs and enables 0.8.0, and `hermes tool-slimmer doctor` reports `ok: true` with surface `llm_request_middleware`
- For comparison, `hermes plugins install tool-slimmer` today installs `3128c8fe` (v0.6.5)
- No self-updater: the shipped code has no `releases/latest`, `raw.githubusercontent.com` or `git pull`. The only package installs are in the manual installer script, which installs the local checkout.
- Tests: 185 passed, ruff and mypy clean, and the wheel and sdist asset checks pass. The repo's own CI on the pinned commit: [passing](https://github.com/aliasocracy/hermes-tool-slimmer/actions/runs/36798681876)

## Disclosure

I prepared the plugin changes behind this bump, and this PR, with Claude Code (Anthropic) working in my session. I reviewed the changes and the verification above, and I'm submitting this as the plugin's owner.

## What does this PR do?

Adds `plugin-catalog/cloudflare-sandbox.yaml`, a terminal environment provider that runs Hermes' `terminal`, file tools and `execute_code` in Cloudflare Containers. I own and maintain the plugin repository (catalog rule 5).

Each workspace is a Cloudflare Container managed by a Durable Object. Idle workspaces are saved to a filesystem snapshot and restored on the next command. The user deploys the bundled Worker to their own Cloudflare account. The plugin talks only to that Worker (`HERMES_CF_ENDPOINT`) with a bearer token (`HERMES_CF_TOKEN`).

The plugin registers no tools, hooks or middleware. It has no Python dependencies and does not update itself. It keeps Hermes' dangerous-command approval on (`skip_container_guards = False`), and it does not copy host env vars, skills or credentials into the container.

items.body:
## What

On macOS, user keyboard shortcuts bound to native **Window → Move & Resize** commands are ignored in Hermes Desktop. The green window button still tiles because AppKit handles that path directly, but the menu commands have no owner in the app.

Root cause in `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` (`buildApplicationMenu()`): the top-level Window menu is pushed with a `label` but no `role`, so macOS never registers it as the application's standard Window menu and AppKit doesn't attach its Move & Resize commands (or user shortcuts) to it. The neighbouring Help menu does carry `role: 'help'` — the omission is specific to Window. Re-proved on current `origin/main` (`grep -rn windowMenu` still matches nothing; the inline template entry is unchanged).

## Fix

Assign Electron's `windowMenu` role to the macOS Window menu, extracted into `apps/desktop/electron/window-menu.ts`:

- macOS: `{ label: 'Window', role: 'windowMenu', submenu: [minimize, zoom, front] }` — the role makes AppKit register it as the standard Window menu, restoring Move & Resize commands and user shortcuts, while the explicit submenu keeps the existing entries.
- Other platforms: unchanged `{ label: 'Window', submenu: [minimize, close] }` — no role, no behavior change.

This is the contributor's fix, cherry-picked with their authorship kept, plus the import-order fix-up re-resolved on current main (the `window-focus-policy` import moved between the hunks; the perfectionist sort order is now `window-focus-policy → window-menu → window-open-policy`, eslint-verified clean).

## Screenshots

None — a native macOS menu lives in the system menu bar, which this harness can't screenshot. The behavior is covered by `electron/window-menu.test.ts` (role assertion) and needs a manual macOS check on the Window menu after launch.

## Tests

- `npx vitest run electron/window-menu.test.ts` — 2 passed: macOS template carries `role: 'windowMenu'` with the minimize/zoom/front submenu intact; non-macOS keeps the explicit cross-platform menu. (The test file itself is new in this PR, so it can't fail on base — the file under test doesn't exist there; the role absence on base is the grep evidence above.)
- `npx eslint` on the three touched files: clean (one pre-existing padding-line warning in `main.ts` at ~15403 also fires on clean `origin/main`).
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .`: clean.

Fixes #103105
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/103107
Thanks @victorjmilagres

## What

The official `default` skin (Classic Hermes — gold/navy) was invisible on desktop: `backend-sync.ts` special-cased `name === 'default'` to skip theme registration, `context.tsx` kept `default` in `RETIRED_SKINS` (so `skinPref` silently fell back to `nous`), and `use-skin-command.ts` aliased `default → nous`. The palette only appeared by accident when the skin was forked to a non-`default` name (#76579).

Root cause on main: `apps/desktop/src/themes/backend-sync.ts:94-97` ("we never register a converted theme under `default`"), `apps/desktop/src/themes/context.tsx:53` (`RETIRED_SKINS` includes `'default'`), `apps/desktop/src/themes/use-skin-command.ts:8` (`ALIASES.default = 'nous'`).

## Fix

Cherry-picked from #76743 (rebased by W4A onto current main, authorship preserved):

- Register the converted `default` skin in `$backendThemes` with label **Classic Hermes** instead of skipping it.
- Drop `default` from `RETIRED_SKINS` so `skinPref`/`setTheme` keep the `default` identity instead of remapping to `nous`; the legacy `gold`/`hermes` aliases now point at `default` so old muscle memory reaches the real palette.
- Regression tests: registration + label + pending apply, provider resolves and keeps `default` (static imports — the dynamic ones deadlocked under vitest's module runner), `setTheme('default')` paints the classic gold palette, and the default-named CSS-keying test updated to post-#76579 semantics (the classic default registers as its own palette carrying its `customCSS`; the separate built-in CSS store stays empty for it).
- Our additions: fix eslint `padding-line-between-statements` warnings in the touched files.

Boot default remains `nous` (`DEFAULT_SKIN_NAME`) — unchanged and intended.

## Tests

- `npx vitest run src/themes --maxWorkers=2` → 10 files / **124 passed** at the fix head.
- On base (`origin/main`) the same suite runs 122 tests and asserts the pre-#76579 semantics (`never registers default in the backend store`, default-named CSS keyed under `nous`), so the rewritten assertions are red on base by construction.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` clean; `npx eslint` on the touched files clean (after the blank-line fix).

## Screenshots

Dark theme, Settings → Appearance theme grid. The classic `default` skin is seeded the way the real app does it (`window.hermesDesktop.localSkin`, the electron preload's sanitized `display.skin`). The Classic Hermes card sits in the grid exactly like its neighbours — same swatch size (216×80), label style (13px/500) and active selection ring; its swatch paints the classic gold on navy (`#1a1a2e` / `#FFBF00`):

| Before (main: classic palette unregistered — 11 cards, no Classic Hermes) | After (fix: registered, selectable, gold ring on select) |

Selecting it paints the classic gold/navy palette (`data-hermes-theme=default`, `--theme-accent-soft: #433826`); on main the same stored pick silently normalizes to `nous`.

items.body:
## What

Two related defects in the Mermaid/Zoomable path (#110336):

1. **Overlay opens huge diagrams at 100%.** `ZoomPanViewer` reset to the identity transform on every open — no fit computation anywhere in the path — so a 4758×1671 SVG opened in a 90vw/85vh overlay showing an off-canvas corner that looks exactly like a failed render. Aggravating: the reporter's fit scale (~0.24) sat below `MIN_SCALE = 0.25`, so even ~15 manual zoom-out steps clamped just above fitting — the diagram could never fully fit interactively either.
2. **Inline preview rendered at intrinsic width.** Mermaid emits an inline `style="max-width: 4758px"` on the SVG, which beats the container's width caps (`max-w-full` inline, `max-w-[85vw]` overlay), so the inline preview was a clipped sliver.

Root cause on main: `apps/desktop/src/components/ui/zoomable.tsx:74-78` (`reset()` on open), `apps/desktop/src/components/ui/use-zoom-pan.ts` (`MIN_SCALE = 0.25`, reset = identity), `apps/desktop/src/lib/svg-image.ts` (`normalizeSvgSize` left the inline pixel max-width in place).

## Fix

Cherry-picked from #110353 (rebased by W4A onto current main, authorship preserved):

- `useZoomPan.fit()`: computes `scale = min(stageW/contentW, stageH/contentH, 1)` — **never upscale** — from live DOM geometry, clamped through the scale bounds. Exposes node setters instead of object refs so portal-mounted stages subscribe correctly.
- Overlay fits on open and re-fits on later geometry changes (async mermaid render, dialog/window resize) while the view is still the fitted one; any manual zoom/pan opts out until reset. Reset and macOS smart-zoom return to the fitted view, not the broken 100%.
- `MIN_SCALE` 0.25 → 0.05 so fitted giant diagrams stay reachable by wheel/buttons.
- `normalizeSvgSize`: rewrites a pixel inline `max-width` to `100%` (relative values untouched) so the container caps govern again — the inline preview gets the accepted fit-to-pane behaviour with its existing expand affordance.

- The fit insets content from the stage edges: 32px on the sides, and 64px top and bottom, which also clears the floating toolbar. Otherwise wide diagrams landed about 4px from the overlay edges.

## Tests

- `zoomable-fit.test.tsx` (5) + `svg-image-inline-cap.test.ts` (2) + neighbouring `zoomable.test.tsx` (1) → 3 files / **8 passed** at the fix head (`--maxWorkers=2`).
- Both new suites do not exist on base (no fit logic exists there), red-on-base by construction; the contributor mutation-verified the fit logic (fit-noop, `MIN_SCALE = 0.25`, reset-without-reflag each turn the suite red).
- W4A's rebase fix: queries the Zoomable trigger by role after main dropped the native `title=` (getByTitle → getByRole).
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` clean; `npx eslint` on the touched files clean.

## Screenshots

Dark theme, zoom overlay opened on the reporter's exact ERD from #110336 (4665×1671 viewBox), a wide 3600×900 SVG image (same `normalizeSvgSize` pipeline), and a small flowchart that must NOT change:

| Case | Before (main: opens at 100%, off-canvas / clipped) | After (fit on open, centred, no upscale) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Large Mermaid ERD | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OutThisLife/hermes-agent/543f426fed0d0ed0ab18f19aed47f1851e9a2e29/mermaid-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/b78cbee64609e5b5532760b068e33091d335d582/mermaid-after2.png) |
| Wide SVG image | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OutThisLife/hermes-agent/543f426fed0d0ed0ab18f19aed47f1851e9a2e29/wide-svg-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/b78cbee64609e5b5532760b068e33091d335d582/wide-svg-after2.png) |
| Small flowchart (ordinary case, unchanged) | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OutThisLife/hermes-agent/543f426fed0d0ed0ab18f19aed47f1851e9a2e29/small-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/b78cbee64609e5b5532760b068e33091d335d582/small-after2.png) |

Measured in the harness: on main the ERD overlay content renders 4665px wide inside a 1150px stage (stage effectively empty — the "diagram failed to render" look); after the fix it fits at 1150×412 inside the 1150×678 stage, centred with sensible padding, and the small diagram keeps its natural 582×174 size (no upscale).

## Supersedes

Fixes #110336

Thanks @kokhlo 🙏

items.body:
## Root cause

Follow-up to #128304. The merged fix taught `_resolve_truncate_row_id` to read the UN-repaired durable transcript for identity, but the mapping back onto the live list still assumed the two lists share user ordinals. They do not, always: a cold resume/reload materializes `session["history"]` with `repair_alternation=True` (`server._load_resume_transcript`), so the live list is the REPAIRED projection of the physical rows — a durable `user;user` run (interrupted turn + resend, or a model-switch marker run) arrives already merged, one live carrier carrying the first row's `_row_id` with the absorbed ids retired onto `_absorbed_row_ids`.

For consecutive plain rows 303/304 the un-repaired DB read finds 304 as user ordinal 2, but the live list has only user ordinals 0/1, so the same-ordinal guard returned `None` and `prompt.submit` still failed closed with 4018. The plain-user regression in #128304 constructed the repaired view but fed `live` from the verbatim rows, so it could not catch this.

## What changes

- `_resolve_truncate_row_id` (tui_gateway/methods_prompt.py) now, when the same-ordinal mapping fails, maps the durable target onto the merge survivor that owns it — the live user turn whose own `_row_id` or `_absorbed_row_ids` names the target — gated on the carrier holding the target's text (`_merge_carrier_holds_target_text`: repair joins a run with `"\n\n"`, so the target's sanitized text is the carrier's content or a whole `\n\n`-delimited part of it).
- Resolving to the carrier's own index would cut the whole merged pair away, losing the unanswered earlier half. The resolver therefore returns the physical durable prefix (the un-repaired rows strictly before the target) and `_truncate_history_for_submit` cuts from that, so targeting the absorbed row retains the carrier's earlier half — 303 stays when the client targets 304. `_resolve_truncation_ordinal` threads the prefix through as a fourth tuple element; every other cut path is unchanged.
- The regression test now feeds `live` from the repaired history with stamps kept, exactly the shape production resume installs, and asserts 303 survives the cut.

## Acceptance coverage

- `test_prompt_submit_resolves_row_id_swallowed_by_plain_user_merge` (reworked per the review finding): repaired live carrier at 303, target 304 → resolves (no 4018), and the cut retains 303's row (`replaced[0][1]` keeps its content).
- The marker-merge and absorbed-into-marker regressions from #128304 still pass unchanged (they exercise the stamp-heal and same-ordinal paths this change leaves alone).

## Tests run

- On `origin/main`: reworked regression RED — exact 4018 `refusing truncation without fallback` (`bash scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 --file-timeout 1200 tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py -k plain_user_merge`: 1 failed).
- With this branch: `tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py` full file 667/667 green and `tests/agent/test_message_sequence_repair.py` 61/61 green (same runner, `-j 2`).

Fixes #94486

Thanks @JoaoMarcos44 for the review finding on #128304 that this follows up on.

Carries @686f6c61's #76120 unchanged (their commits and authorship), on a branch in this repo. GitHub would not start CI for the fork PR: every push ended in a zero-job "workflow file issue" run, even though the merge commit builds cleanly.

Supersedes #76120, credit @686f6c61.

---

## What does this PR do?

With two or more terminal tabs open in Desktop, pressing Cmd/Ctrl+L once inserted one `>_ selection` pill **per mounted tab**. Every `TerminalInstance` stays mounted when inactive, and each `useTerminalSession` registered its own window-level capture keydown for the add-selection shortcut without checking `active`. `readSelection()` falls back to `window.getSelection()`, so a selection anywhere (chat, preview, or the active terminal) fired every listener.

## Fix

- Register the global Cmd/Ctrl+L listener only while the session is `active`.
- Add `shouldOwnAddSelectionShortcut()` as a pure helper used by the listener path, with unit tests for the active/inactive and empty-selection cases.

Inactive tabs no longer insert duplicate attachments. Clear-screen when there is no selection is unchanged (listener returns without preventDefault when there is no text).

## Related Issue

Fixes #76116

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Tests

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/app/right-sidebar/terminal/use-terminal-session.ts` — gate listener on `active`
- `apps/desktop/src/app/right-sidebar/terminal/selection.ts` — `shouldOwnAddSelectionShortcut`
- `apps/desktop/src/app/right-sidebar/terminal/selection.test.ts` — regression coverage

## How to Test

```bash
cd apps/desktop
npx vitest run src/app/right-sidebar/terminal/selection.test.ts
```

Manual:

1. Open Desktop with 2+ terminal tabs.
2. Select text in chat or a terminal.
3. Press Cmd+L (macOS) or Ctrl+L (Windows/Linux) once.
4. Expect exactly one selection pill in the composer.

Docker vitest: **2/2 passed**.

## Checklist

- [x] Conventional Commits
- [x] Focused PR, no open competing fix for #76116
- [x] Tests added
- [x] Linux (Docker Node 22)

## Notes

I chose gating on `active` over hoisting the listener to `TerminalWorkspace` so the change stays local to the session hook. Happy to hoist later if maintainers prefer a single owner for the chat/preview race with `preview-file.tsx`.

items.body:
The welcome chat now opens on a slow cold first boot. Before, it gave up after 30 s and the app opened the normal chat.

## Why

A tester's Windows ARM64 first boot took 51 s to start listening. Then `onboarding.ensure_setup_profile` answered late because the backend was still busy. The kickoff stopped at the 30 s request default. The gate also had a 45 s wall-clock deadline. The user never saw the welcome chat.

## What changes

- The kickoff is now an explicit state machine: `waiting-backend` -> `preparing` -> `opening` -> `started`, or `off` / `failed` (`apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/onboarding-kickoff-machine.ts`).
- The kickoff waits while the state is known: the gateway is open or reconnecting, a call is in flight, or a profile dial timed out while main still spawns that backend. There is no wall-clock deadline.
- The kickoff fails only when it cannot wait: an RPC error response, the primary backend process exits, or a result it does not expect.
- A dropped connection retries the preparing step once. The steps in it are idempotent.
- `onboarding.ensure_setup_profile`, `setup.status` and `onboarding.ensure_setup_session` have no request deadline now. `setup.status` dials the setup profile in the foreground. This skips the background redial cooldown.
- The gate's 45 s deadline is gone. The existing `starting` view stays up for the whole wait. The fallback (`abandonGuide` / `record_failed_start`) still runs on a real failure.
- Each transition logs a `[setup] kickoff <from> -> <to> (<detail>)` line to the renderer console and to desktop.log.

## Checks

- Ran: `tsc -p . --noEmit`, eslint and prettier on the three changed files, `git diff --check`.
- Ran: a scratch vitest harness (deleted, not committed) that drives the machine. It covers: waiting with no deadline, backend exit during a wait and during a call, one transient retry, an RPC error as fatal, and repeated dial timeouts that keep waiting.
- Not ran: a live cold-boot run on the Mac. The dev port was held by another session. Live testers drive this next.
- Not changed: `session.resume` and `config.set` in the opening step keep their own 30 s defaults.

items.body:
## What

Rehydrating a Desktop session painted a persisted `reasoning_details` value straight into the transcript's **Thought** block. SQLite hands `reasoning_details` back to the history surface as a string, and the hydration fallback at `apps/desktop/src/lib/chat-messages/hydration.ts` treated any such string as human-readable reasoning:

```ts
const rawReasoning =
  message.reasoning ||
  message.reasoning_content ||
  (typeof message.reasoning_details === 'string' ? message.reasoning_details : '')
```

Two failure shapes result, both shown in the screenshots:

- **Opaque replay carrier** (the `claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` `.native_assistant` envelope from #126588): the Thought block shows the cryptographic thinking signature, the native `text` blocks, and the same public answer again inside `projection`.
- **Decodable envelope** (reasoning-details carrying `reasoning.summary` / `reasoning.text` blocks): the Thought block shows the serialized JSON instead of the readable reasoning prose.

The stored carrier is required for signed replay and is left untouched — this is a display-only fix.

## Fix

One decoder, `reasoningTextFromDetails()` in `apps/desktop/src/lib/chat-messages/parts.ts`, now guards the fallback:

- plain persisted reasoning strings render unchanged;
- a serialized or already-decoded structured envelope is walked for readable prose only: top-level `summary` / `thinking` / `content` / `text` fields, plus nested `reasoning.summary` / `reasoning.text` / `thinking` blocks inside provider-native carriers;
- `signature`, `projection`, `data` and other opaque replay fields never render; a carrier with no readable reasoning yields no reasoning part at all;
- a malformed JSON envelope is replay metadata, not display text, and yields no reasoning part;
- canonical `reasoning` / `reasoning_content` keep precedence when set, and `display_reasoning` is untouched.

This supersedes and merges two contributor PRs that each fixed half of the same fallback:

- #116508 (LordMelkor) decoded serialized/decoded envelopes into readable prose and returned nothing for opaque-only or malformed data.
- #126594 (686f6c61) recognized provider-native nested carriers and kept their signatures/projections out of the Thought block.

They are complementary halves of the same bug; each test suite failed against the other's base. The merged decoder keeps both behaviors, and the interaction test locks them together.

## Screenshots

Dark theme, hydrated session history carrying (a) an opaque DirectSDK reasoning carrier and (b) a decodable reasoning-details envelope:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OutThisLife/hermes-agent/7197e0506bdc607a40928216576d8f5eed3118cb/before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OutThisLife/hermes-agent/7197e0506bdc607a40928216576d8f5eed3118cb/after.png) |

Before: the first assistant turn shows a Thought block with the raw carrier JSON — signature, native text and the answer repeated in `projection`; the second shows the envelope's serialized JSON. After: no Thought block for the opaque carrier, readable reasoning prose for the decodable envelope, and the ordinary answers unchanged.

## Tests

- `apps/desktop/src/lib/chat-messages/reasoning-details.test.ts` — decoded/serialized envelope extraction, opaque-field exclusion, malformed-envelope suppression, canonical-field precedence, and the opaque-carrier + decodable-envelope interaction (red on base: the merged test file fails 5/5 on the pre-fix fallback).
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/chat-messages.test.ts` — the #126588 opaque `.native_assistant` carrier produces no Thought part and no signature/native-type leakage; a `reasoning.summary` plus nested non-empty `thinking` still renders, without the signature.
- `npx vitest run src/lib/chat-messages/ --maxWorkers=2`: 36 passed (7 files). Neighbours (`chat-messages.test.ts`, `markdown-preprocess.test.ts`): 117 passed. `npm run typecheck`: exit 0. eslint on touched files: clean.

Fixes #126588
Refs #116508

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/116508
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/126594

Thanks @LordMelkor and @686f6c61 — this PR carries both fixes forward together.

items.body:
One Skip on a setup card no longer breaks the rest of onboarding, and words typed in the chat box are no longer saved as picks.

## Why

The provider names every model-written tool call `call_0`. The desktop remembered each setup card's request by call id alone. After the apps card was skipped, every later card with `call_0` showed that old "Skipped" answer instead of its picker. Composer text also answered a waiting card as a pick, so "hey" was saved as a plugin and a complaint was saved as the layout.

## What changes

- **Unique call ids (agent).** When a new tool call reuses an id that is already in this session's history, the agent renames the new call (`call_0` -> `call_0_d2`, then `_d3`). This happens before the call is stored or run, so the tool result, the history and the desktop all see the new id. Ids already in history never change, so the prompt cache holds. Unique ids are not touched. It extends the existing within-turn rename (`uniquify_tool_call_ids`), same `_d<n>` shape.
- **Card binding (desktop).** A card remembers its request by session, message and call id, so a reused id cannot show another card's answer.
- **Typed text (setup_choose).** On a card with fixed rows (apps, plugins, layout, theme, accent, tour, fork, machine_use, a question with options), composer text counts as a pick only when it names a row by id or label (any case). Otherwise the card returns `{outcome: "typed", said: "<words>"}`, no card facts are written, and `next` tells the model to reply and send the card again. The name card (free text) still takes typed text as the answer. The settled card shows the typed words.
- On the fork card (and first-task cards after it), `next` lets typed words that name a task count as the first task, and the fork handoff is still attached, as the setup skill already describes.
- Contract: `SetupChooseResult.said`. Skill text and tool docs updated.

## Checks

Ran:

items.body:
## What

#38072 finding 3 (axe `nested-interactive`, serious): the sidebar session row's reorder grabber — a dnd-kit activator carrying `role="button"` + `tabIndex=0`, kept focusable for keyboard reorder (#83617) — rendered **inside** the row's primary button (`SidebarRowBody` in `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/session-row.tsx:433`). Every session row was a button containing a focusable button: confusing keyboard and screen-reader behavior, and an ambiguous tab order in a repeated list. The same nesting existed in the card (Inbox) variant's header line.

## The fix

- The row **body is now a plain div** (`SidebarRowCluster`) carrying the exact same gesture handlers — resume, modifier-clicks (⇧ pin / ⌘ tab / ⌥ archive), middle-click, drag-on-press. Every click still bubbles to the same resolver, so pointer users keep click-anywhere-on-the-row.
- The **title is the row's real button** (the app's `RowButton`), matching the idiom project/group rows already use in this sidebar. It has no `onClick` of its own — the click bubbles to the body div's resolver, and Enter/Space on the focused title activate natively.
- The **grabber keeps its full dnd-kit handle semantics as a sibling** — keyboard reorder (Space on the focused grabber) is unchanged, as is the ⋯ trigger (already a sibling in flat rows via the shell's actions column; a sibling in card rows too now).
- Gateway/project rows already render the grabber inside plain div clusters — verified, unchanged.

`cursor-pointer` is carried explicitly on the body div (it no longer earns it from the base layer's interactive-control rule). The screenshot pair is pixel-identical: this is a semantics-only change.

## Screenshots (dark theme, real `SidebarSessionRow` in a `ReorderableList`)

| Before (main) | After (this PR) |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OutThisLife/hermes-agent/d6904c720e874b1b95917fe416807dd6dd9cc9d1/before-sidebar.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OutThisLife/hermes-agent/COMMIT2/after-sidebar.png) |

DOM probe of the same harness: before, `grabberInsideButton: true` (the violation); after, `role="button"`, `tabIndex=0`, `grabberInsideButton: false` — the handle's semantics survive, the nesting is gone.

## Tests

- `session-row.test.tsx` gains "renders the grabber outside any button, with the title as the row button": red on base (grabber nested inside the body `<button>`), green on the fix. Existing tests prove the behaviours that must not regress: Space still arms a keyboard reorder from the grabber, Space still passes through to the ⋯ control, rename-dialog presses still don't lift the row, a body press still lifts it.
- Neighbours green: `session-row-rename-drag`, `session-row-actions`, `chat-sidebar.integration`, `gateway-groups-drag`, `virtual-session-list`, `sessions-section-new-session-drag` (41 tests). `tsc --noEmit` + eslint clean on touched files.

Fixes the finding-3 scope of #38072 (findings #4/#5/#6 are covered by #93836/#93838/#93848; findings #1/#2 are already fixed on main)
Refs #38072
Thanks @elchic00, who claimed this finding in the audit thread and never got a PR up — the claim expired; this carries the audit's fix direction.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

An exhausted Codex pool row is skipped by the proactive refresh chain, so by the time the selection-path quota probe runs, its access token has usually expired. Since #89415, `_codex_quota_restored_upstream` refreshes it first. It spends the single-use refresh token `RT0`, adopts the rotated pair `RT1` into the pool and writes it to disk (`agent/credential_pool.py:1953-1963` on `1ce2cfb7fa`).

When the probe then reports the quota restored, `_available_entries` clears the cooldown with `self._adopt(entry, persist=False, **_MARK_OK)` (`agent/credential_pool.py:2122`). That `entry` is the loop's own pre-probe copy, which still holds `RT0`. `_adopt` replaces the row by id, so the pool row goes back to `RT0` and the expired access token:

1. The same `select()` sees an expired access token and refreshes the row again with `RT0`.
2. The token endpoint rejects the spent token with `refresh_token_reused`, and the row can go DEAD.

This happens in one process with one pool. No second instance or shared auth file is involved. It is reachable whenever a Codex usage-limit cooldown outlives the access token and the quota probe reports restored, for example after a top-up, a plan upgrade or an early reset.

The fix re-reads the row by id just before the cooldown clear, so `_MARK_OK` is applied to the row the probe left in the pool. If nothing rotated, the lookup returns an identical row and the behavior is unchanged.

## Related Issue

No upstream issue filed. Related open PRs:

- #96414 changes the same block of `_available_entries` to stop a false-positive probe from hot-looping a 429. It still clears the cooldown on the pre-probe copy.
- #127024 re-reads a Codex `manual:*` row's own pool record before refreshing it, to handle a rotation by another pool instance. It does not cover `device_code` rows, and it does not stop the in-memory row from being rolled back to `RT0`.
- #72690 (open since 2026-07-27, merge conflicts since 2026-07-30) is a broader rewrite of the probe's token refresh. It also covers this rollback: it refreshes the row before probing and re-syncs it from the auth store before the cooldown clear. This PR is the one-line version of that part, mergeable on current main. If #72690 lands, this change becomes redundant and can be closed.
- #114399 changes what the probe counts as restored. It does not touch the cooldown clear.

Search: `gh pr list -R NousResearch/hermes-agent --state open --search` with "quota probe refresh_token", "_codex_quota_restored_upstream", "codex quota restored", "refresh_token_reused codex pool", "codex probe stale" and "credential_pool codex quota".

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/credential_pool.py`: in `_available_entries`, clear the cooldown on the live pool row (`self._find` by id) instead of on the loop's pre-probe copy.
- `tests/agent/test_credential_pool_codex_quota_probe_rotation.py`: one regression test. The setup is an exhausted `openai-codex` row (429 `usage_limit_reached`, reset days out) with an expired access token. The token endpoint is single-use (`rt-N` mints `rt-(N+1)`, and a spent token is refused). The probe is stubbed to return restored. After `select()`, only `rt-0` has been sent and the selected entry, the pool row and the persisted row all hold `rt-1`. A forced refresh then sends `rt-1`, never `rt-0` again.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_credential_pool_codex_quota_probe_rotation.py`
2. Before the fix: 1 failed. `select()` sends `['rt-0', 'rt-0']`, replaying the spent token.
3. After the fix: 1 passed. Together with every `tests/agent/test_credential_pool*.py` file and `tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_codex_quota_probe.py`: 25 files, 181 passed.

## Checklist

- [x] Conventional commit message
- [x] Searched existing PRs
- [x] Only changes related to this fix
- [x] Added regression tests (red before, green after)
- [x] Tested on macOS (Darwin, Python 3.14, PM-built test env)

items.body:
## Root cause

Two defects strand Desktop on a dead session when a compression lineage runs deeper than the forward chain-walk bound (real lineages run ~180 deep):

1. **Search remapped hits from the lineage root.** `search_sessions` resolved each hit via `tip(compression_root(hit))`, but `get_compression_chain` is defensively bounded (100 hops on main), so a root-started walk truncated to a stale mid id that was itself still `end_reason=compression`. Resuming that id re-derives a stale branch — or fails outright. The CLI already resumes from the matched id (`_resume_follow_tip`) and reaches the live tip.
2. **Desktop `resolveTargetSessionId` resumed without `omit_messages`** — the only `session.resume` call site missing it. A full-lineage response then exceeds `max_resume_messages` in `assert_resume_safe` and the resume fails ("Resume failed"). Every other desktop resume already passes `omit_messages: true`, and only the resolved tip `session_id` is consumed here.

## What changes

- `hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py`: `lineage_tip()` resolves from the **matched id** instead of the lineage root; dedupe stays keyed by lineage root, so result grouping is unchanged.
- `hermes_state_compression.py`: the chain-walk bound is named (`_CHAIN_CAP`) and raised 100 → 1000 (the `seen` set already guards cycles) so root-based tip walks also terminate at the live tip.
- `apps/desktop/.../resolve-target-session.ts`: `omit_messages: true` on the bare resume, matching the contract of every other desktop resume call site.
- Tests: a 179-deep simulated lineage whose fake walks the real `_CHAIN_CAP` from the start id — the resume id must be the live tip (`s178`), with lineage bookkeeping still keyed by the root (`s000`). Red against the old root-started capped walk (which truncated to `s100`).

Supersedes #125054, which is CI-red only because its `omit_messages` addition was not reflected in the exact-args assertion at `resolve-target-session.test.ts:38`; that expectation is updated here. The unpushed strengthening commit from the source branch is included as well. Thanks @dskwe for the investigation, the fix, and the deep-lineage test.

## Acceptance coverage

- Opening/searching a mid-lineage session id lands on the live tip (parity with `hermes chat --resume <mid>`): `lineage_tip(raw_sid)` + raised cap.
- Search-hit resume ids are the tip forwarded from the matched id, not a truncated walk: `test_deep_lineage_search_resolves_tip_from_matched_id` (red on main, green with the fix).
- Desktop resume of a deep lineage no longer fails on `max_resume_messages`: `omit_messages: true` at the single bare call site.
- Lineages deeper than 100 hops resolve to the true tip: `_CHAIN_CAP = 1000`, covered by the same test.

## Tests run

- `bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_session_search.py` — 4 passed (deep-lineage tip test is red on `origin/main`, green here).
- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/resolve-target-session.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` — 8 passed.
- `cd apps/desktop && npx tsc -p . --noEmit` — clean.

Fixes #125041

items.body:
## Root cause

Desktop Review used a generation only after a list request started. A repository switch could queue a debounced refresh without invalidating the old request, allowing that request's `catch` or `finally` to clear the new repository's files or loading state. Selection reconciliation was path-only, so an older list or same-path diff could overwrite newer user intent.

The related `openReviewForPath()` path could be overtaken by an already-pending debounce: its direct list request became stale, returned before selecting the requested file, and the later request had no record of that target.

## What changes

- Invalidate active list ownership as soon as a refresh is scheduled.
- Let a direct refresh absorb a redundant pending debounce.
- Bind list success, error, loading cleanup, and selection reconciliation to both the list generation and repository cwd.
- Give Review selection/diff requests their own generation and cwd ownership, including same-path reselections.
- Stop `openReviewForPath()` when its direct refresh no longer owns the requested repository.
- Preserve current main's originating composer target while applying the ownership checks.

Supersedes #76721, which went CI-red after main's js05 low-value test purge (`51766a72a3`) removed the `pushChanges` test while the branch still imported the symbol — `unused-imports/no-unused-imports` at `review.test.ts:28`. This branch rebases the same two commits onto current main, drops the now-unused import, and re-adds the `clearReviewSelection` import the ownership test needs. Thanks @embwl0x for the original investigation, fix, and regression suite.

## Regression coverage

The deferred-promise tests cover:

- an old repository rejection during the new repository's debounce gap;
- an older list response trying to clear a newer direct selection;
- an older `finally` racing a genuinely newer in-flight refresh;
- a pending debounce overtaking `openReviewForPath()`;
- two same-path diff requests resolving in reverse order;
- the current-main composer target surviving the direct file-open path.

## Tests run

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/store/review.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` — 46 passed.
- `cd apps/desktop && npx eslint src/store/review.ts src/store/review.test.ts` — clean (the exact check that was red on #76721).
- `cd apps/desktop && npx tsc -p . --noEmit` — clean.

Fixes #76532
