![Cloud File Manager for Hermes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electricsheephq/hermes-cloud-file-manager/b367ff4f4411e1216a0e7b1599e32ca6c7887679/docs/media/banner.png) ## What does this PR do? Adds **Cloud File Manager** (`hermes-cloud-file-manager`) to the plugin catalog. It is a desktop + gateway plugin for people whose Hermes agent runs on **another machine**: a VPS, a home server, or a hosted agent. When the agent is remote, its files live on that machine, not yours. Today, getting a file to the agent means a terminal, `scp`, or pasting its contents into the chat. Cloud File Manager puts the agent's working folders one click away in Hermes Desktop: - **Cloud Files** in the sidebar: browse the agent's folders, search by name or glob, create folders, and upload files or whole folders by drag-and-drop. Large files go up in chunks with automatic retries, and a name clash keeps both files. Uploads never overwrite anything. - **Cloud** in the chat **+** menu: tick files that are already on the agent's machine and drop their *locations* into your message. The agent opens them in place with its own tools. Nothing is uploaded again, and nothing is inlined into the context. - **Google Drive** (new in 0.2.0), for agents whose `google-workspace` skill is signed in to Drive: browse or search the agent's own Drive and **Import to Cloud Files**, or use **+ → Google Drive** in a chat to import picked files and insert their locations. Google Docs and Slides arrive as PDF, Sheets as CSV. It is read-only toward Drive, and the plugin never reads the Google token. - **Read and edit Markdown** (new in 0.3.0): open a report, `AGENTS.md` or any `.md`/`.txt` file. It opens **read-only and rendered**. **Edit** is a deliberate step, **Changes** shows a line diff, and only **Save** in the **Review & save** dialog writes the file. There is no autosave, closing never saves, and if the agent changed the file after you opened it, Save is refused until you compare. ![Upload, find, hand off, import, edit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electricsheephq/hermes-cloud-file-manager/b367ff4f4411e1216a0e7b1599e32ca6c7887679/docs/media/features.png) | Browse and upload | Upload a whole folder | |---|---| | ![The Cloud Files page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electricsheephq/hermes-cloud-file-manager/b367ff4f4411e1216a0e7b1599e32ca6c7887679/docs/media/screenshot-page.png) | ![Uploading a folder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electricsheephq/hermes-cloud-file-manager/b367ff4f4411e1216a0e7b1599e32ca6c7887679/docs/media/screenshot-upload.png) | | **+ → Cloud: pick files on the agent's machine** | **The agent opens them where they are** | | ![Picking files for a chat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electricsheephq/hermes-cloud-file-manager/b367ff4f4411e1216a0e7b1599e32ca6c7887679/docs/media/screenshot-picker.png) | ![The agent reads the inserted locations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electricsheephq/hermes-cloud-file-manager/b367ff4f4411e1216a0e7b1599e32ca6c7887679/docs/media/screenshot-chat.png) | | **Google Drive as a source** | **+ → Google Drive in a chat** | | ![Browsing the agent's Google Drive](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electricsheephq/hermes-cloud-file-manager/b367ff4f4411e1216a0e7b1599e32ca6c7887679/docs/media/screenshot-drive-page.png) | ![Picking Drive files to import](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electricsheephq/hermes-cloud-file-manager/b367ff4f4411e1216a0e7b1599e32ca6c7887679/docs/media/screenshot-drive-picker.png) | | **A report, rendered read-only** | **Review the diff, then Save** | | ![A Markdown report in the rendered view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electricsheephq/hermes-cloud-file-manager/b367ff4f4411e1216a0e7b1599e32ca6c7887679/docs/media/screenshot-editor-view.png) | ![The Review & save dialog with a line diff](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electricsheephq/hermes-cloud-file-manager/b367ff4f4411e1216a0e7b1599e32ca6c7887679/docs/media/screenshot-editor-review.png) | The repository owner submits this entry (admission rule 5). It is pinned to the `v0.3.4` release commit `b367ff4f4411e1216a0e7b1599e32ca6c7887679`. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR D["Hermes Desktop
(desktop half: plugin.js)"] -- "ctx.rest → /api/plugins/hermes-cloud-file-manager/*
gateway's own auth (token or sign-in)" --> G["Agent's gateway
(gateway half: dashboard/plugin_api.py)"] G -- "confined list / search / mkdir / chunked upload
read + explicit save of .md / .txt" --> F[("Agent's working folders
terminal.cwd or settings.roots")] A["The agent"] -- "opens the inserted paths
with its own file tools" --> F GD[("Agent's Google Drive")] -- "read-only list / search / download
via the agent's own google-workspace skill" --> G ``` - **One package, two halves.** Desktop's **Install from Git** installs the gateway half into the connected agent and the desktop half on your computer. Its routes run under the gateway's existing dashboard auth. The plugin adds no login or tokens of its own. - **Uploads are a plain JSON chunk protocol** (4 MiB chunks that halve behind strict proxies, two files in flight, resume by offset). They work through token remotes and sign-in remotes, where `ctx.rest` multipart cannot. - **The batch is pinned to the agent it started on.** Switching agents pauses it, so files never land on the wrong machine. - **Google Drive runs the agent's own `google-workspace` skill** as a subprocess with a fixed argument list, only when its sign-in check reports Drive access. The scripts come from a fixed place (the agent's own copy, then the one bundled with Hermes) and run with a minimal environment, so they never see the gateway's provider keys or tokens. Imports land in `uploads/drive/` and keep both files on a name clash. The source is hidden for agents without it. - **The editor saves only on an explicit Save.** The save carries the sha256 of the version you opened. The gateway refuses it if the file changed since, and otherwise replaces the file atomically (temp file, fsync, rename), keeping its mode. Apart from that temp file, it never creates, renames or deletes files. - **The roots match the agent's own working folder** (`terminal.cwd`, else the gateway user's home), so the inserted paths are the ones the agent already uses. ## Install 1. In Hermes Desktop, open **Capabilities → Plugins → Install from Git**, enter `https://github.com/electricsheephq/hermes-cloud-file-manager`, then **Review repository → Install**. 2. **Restart the agent's gateway** once. Hermes mounts plugin APIs at startup. 3. In **Capabilities → Plugins → Cloud File Manager**, switch on **Desktop**. CLI alternative on the gateway machine: `hermes plugins install electricsheephq/hermes-cloud-file-manager`, then `hermes plugins enable hermes-cloud-file-manager`, then restart. The sidebar row and **+ → Cloud** appear only for agents that have the gateway half, so installing the desktop half is harmless for your other agents. ## Type of Change - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) ## Changes Made `plugin-catalog/hermes-cloud-file-manager.yaml`: - exact 40-char `sha`, quoted `version: "0.3.4"`, `category: desktop`, `tier: community`, `maintainer: 100yenadmin`; - a description with a `Disclosure —` sentence; - a 2:1 banner and 6 screenshots on raw.githubusercontent.com, pinned to the same sha; - empty capabilities, matching reality. ## How to Test **Automated** 1. `hermes plugins validate `: validation passes, including the security scan ("safe"), the desktop surface lint, and loadable. 2. `python scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/hermes-cloud-file-manager.yaml`: OK. **Manual walkthrough (about 5 minutes; any remote or local gateway)** 1. Install as above, then restart the gateway, then switch on **Desktop**. **Cloud Files** appears in the sidebar. 2. Drag a folder with a few files onto the page. The drawer shows per-file progress, and the folder structure appears on the agent's machine, byte-identical. 3. Upload a file with the same name again. It arrives as `name (1).ext`, and the original is untouched. 4. **Search files** for one of them. It is found across folders. 5. In a chat, choose **+ → Cloud**, tick two files in different folders, and choose **Insert locations**. Ask the agent "what are these files?" It opens them where they are. 6. Optional, for an agent whose `google-workspace` skill is signed in to Drive: switch the page's source to **Google Drive**, tick a Google Doc and choose **Import to Cloud Files**. A PDF appears in `uploads/drive/`. 7. Double-click a scratch `.md` file. It opens rendered. Choose **Edit**, change a line, then **Close**: it asks before discarding, and the file is unchanged. Edit again, choose **Review & save**, check the diff and **Save**. The file on the agent's machine now has your change. **Proven by the plugin's maintainer:** - token and sign-in remotes; - a 50-file nested folder, 6×30 MiB files and a 740 MB batch, all byte-identical; - a 101 MiB file refused before anything was sent; - the real Install-from-Git path on a fresh gateway and a fresh Desktop; - real Google Drive on a real local agent in Hermes Desktop: the Drive root listed, and a Google Doc imported as a valid PDF; - the editor on a loopback gateway and a Desktop dev build: - Save verified on disk (bytes and mode, no temp left); - Close and Cancel discard nothing without asking; - an outside edit is caught as a conflict; - CRLF and BOM files round-trip. The plugin's CI runs the backend on Ubuntu and macOS against pinned upstream and fork Hermes builds, the desktop tests, and both desktop loaders' import scanners. ## Security model - **Every path is confined to the shown folders.** Traversal, non-portable names and links that leave the folders are refused. - **The agent's Hermes home (settings, API keys, sessions) is never listed, read or written,** even when it sits inside a shown folder. It is matched by file identity and canonical path, including case and Unicode variants on macOS. The one exception is a working folder set inside it: `roots`, `terminal.cwd`, or the `workspace/` folder the plugin creates when the working folder would be the home itself. - **Uploads never overwrite, rename or delete** an existing file. There is no delete route. The plugin removes only what it created itself: its `.cfm-*` temp files (stale after 24 hours, or from an aborted upload), a Drive import's staging folder, and the empty placeholder it makes to reserve a new file's name when publishing that file fails. - **Only the editor's explicit Save overwrites,** and only an existing `.md`, `.markdown` or `.txt` file of at most 1 MiB that is unchanged since you opened it. Links, hard links, mount points and non-regular files are refused, and saves run one at a time. - **Its only network use is Google Drive, read-only,** through the agent's own `google-workspace` skill. Browsing and imports run when you ask; while Desktop is open, it also re-checks the Drive sign-in about once a minute. The plugin never reads the Google token and never installs packages; if the skill's libraries are missing, Drive simply stays hidden. - **No self-updating code, no `python_dependencies`.** The desktop bundle imports only `@hermes/plugin-sdk`, `react` and `react/jsx-runtime`. Full policy: [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/electricsheephq/hermes-cloud-file-manager/blob/b367ff4f4411e1216a0e7b1599e32ca6c7887679/SECURITY.md). ## Compatibility Hermes **0.21.5 or newer**, with its Desktop (`requires_hermes: ">=0.21.5"`). It needs an agent whose terminal runs locally on the gateway machine (`terminal.backend: local`, the default). For Docker, SSH or other sandboxed backends, the tab explains why it can't show the files instead of showing the wrong ones. Adds `openai-compatible`, an image_gen provider for GPT Image through self-hosted or reseller gateways: [CLIProxyAPI](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI), [New API](https://github.com/QuantumNous/new-api), or any OpenAI Images-compatible server.

**Why a plugin instead of the bundled `openai` image provider:** gateway-specific behavior. It reports requested vs returned size (these gateways often resize), returns actionable `auth_error` / `rate_limited` / `io_error` categories instead of one generic error, sends gateway-defined model names verbatim, and keeps image routing separate from `OPENAI_BASE_URL` so chat, auxiliary, TTS and memory routing are untouched.

**Network behavior:** `base_url` must be HTTPS. Plain HTTP is accepted only when every resolved address is loopback, RFC 1918, `100.64.0.0/10` or IPv6 ULA; public, link-local, unresolvable and mixed answers are refused. Remote source images are fetched over HTTPS only, without redirects, with private addresses refused and a 50 MB cap. No self-updater; no telemetry.

## Root cause

The reporter's desktop.log (macOS Desktop, 2026-09-24) holds 229 copies of the same error, each one collapsing a whole reply into the raw-Markdown fallback panel:

```
[error-boundary:markdown-render] Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: file:///Applications/Hermes.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar.unpacked/dist/assets/shiki-block-Dcm1B2nM.js
    at Lazy (<anonymous>)
    at Suspense (<anonymous>)
```

The shiki code-block renderer is loaded through a React.lazy dynamic import of ./shiki-block (shiki-highlighter.tsx), the single seam that keeps the multi-MB shiki bundle out of the entry chunk. When that chunk is missing or fails to fetch in a packaged app (asar/asar.unpacked path drift, an install mid-update), the rejected import re-throws at render time — **past Suspense, which only covers the pending state** — to the nearest boundary. For chat messages that boundary is markdown-render (markdown-text.tsx), whose fallback is HugeTextFallback: the entire reply degraded to a bordered raw-Markdown monospace panel because one fenced code block couldn't load its highlighter. Same symptom class as #93479 (the diff path, fixed for syntax-diff) and #109643.

## What changes

- **shiki-chunk-boundary.tsx** (new): a block-local error boundary that degrades a **failed chunk load** — and only that failure class — to the plain preformatted code path the app already renders before highlight lands (PlainShiki). Same re-throw pattern as MessageRenderBoundary: any other render error (a real shiki render bug) is re-thrown, so the markdown-render boundary keeps its exact job and logging for genuine throws.
- **shiki-highlighter.tsx**: the lazy factory retries the dynamic import **once** for a chunk-load error (some fetch failures are transient); LazyShiki wraps the Suspense in the new boundary. The rest of the message keeps rendering through Streamdown.
- The boundary logs one console.warn per caught block (with the error), so a broken install stays diagnosable in desktop.log without the reporter's 229-error storm.

The visible-UI change is confined to the failure path: a reply that previously collapsed into the HugeTextFallback raw-Markdown panel now renders its prose rich (headings, lists, emphasis) and shows each affected fence as a plain, unhighlighted code card — same output as the pre-highlight Suspense fallback, i.e. monospace with the card chrome and copy button, just without token colors. The happy path is untouched.

## Acceptance coverage

- shiki-highlighter.test.tsx mocks the lazy chunk import to reject with the reporter's exact chunk-load error and asserts, through the real MarkdownTextContent pipeline (Streamdown + the markdown-render boundary), that prose still renders rich (an h1 is present, no raw fence markers) and the code block shows as plain text in the code card — with no HugeTextFallback panel. A second test proves a genuine render error still propagates to markdown-render.

## Tests run

- `npx vitest run --project ui --maxWorkers=2 src/components/chat/shiki-highlighter.test.tsx` — 2 passed (with fix)
- Same command against origin/main's shiki-highlighter.tsx — 1 failed (the whole message hit HugeTextFallback; RED on main, GREEN with fix)
- Neighbor suites unaffected: shiki-block.test.tsx, diff-lines.test.tsx, markdown-text.artifacts.test.tsx — 9 passed
- `npm run typecheck` — 0 errors; `npm run check:lint` — 0 errors (pre-existing warnings only)

Fixes #95995

Thanks @skyeyesec333 for capturing the desktop.log line that pinned the root cause.

## What does this PR do?

Approval and clarify prompts in the CLI, the TUI and the Desktop app no longer time out. A prompt stays up until it's answered, the turn is interrupted (Ctrl+C / Stop), or the session closes. Nothing runs while it waits, so this is still fail-closed.

Messaging platforms (Telegram, Discord, Slack, …), ACP editors and approval transport plugins keep `approvals.timeout` and `agent.clarify_timeout`. Those surfaces need a deadline: a push notification can sit unseen and platform buttons expire.

One PR rather than one per surface: the TUI and Desktop share the `tui_gateway` backend, and all three surfaces read the same approval resolver. Each surface binds one switch around its turn.

## How it works

- `tools/approval_context.py`: `set_prompts_wait_for_answer()` / `reset_prompts_wait_for_answer()` bind a per-turn ContextVar. `approval_wait_seconds()` is the one resolver for the built-in approval window. It returns the platform-safe maximum (`agent.deadline.MAX_SAFE_TIMEOUT_S`) when the switch is bound, else `approvals.timeout`. Its readers:
  - the gateway-queue poll loop (`approval_gateway_wait._poll_event`), which serves TUI/Desktop approvals
  - the CLI prompt (`approval_prompt.prompt_dangerous_approval`)
  - the human-wait ceiling (`approval_human_wait.human_wait_ceiling`), and through it the authorization-gate lock bound in `agent/tool_executor.py`
- `tools/approval_human_wait.py`: a human-wait window records its ceiling when its waiters enter it. The batch-deadline loop can read `human_wait_seconds()` from a context that never saw the binding, and it still excludes an unbounded prompt in full. Messaging windows stay clamped as before (#79719).
- CLI: `cli_chat_turn_mixin` binds the switch around `run_conversation`. The approval and clarify panels in `cli_modal_mixin` drop their own `approvals.timeout` / `clarify_timeout` deadlines, and the hint row hides the countdown. The now-unreachable timeout copy is removed from every locale.
- TUI + Desktop: `tui_gateway/prompt_turn.py` binds the switch in `_prepare_turn_input` and resets it in teardown. `_clarify_block` sends its `clarify` server request with no deadline (`_clarify_timeout_seconds` is gone).
- Desktop: a Bot Mode group turn blocked on the user's clarify/approval answer pushes its runaway hard cap out instead of expiring the card under the room. The offline toast and the Settings → Safety description no longer promise an approval timeout (all desktop locales). The `approval.respond` deadline comments now describe what that deadline actually bounds: the answer's round trip.
- Docs: `security.md`, `configuration.md` (Clarify), `acp.md`, and the `config_defaults.py` comments describe `approvals.timeout` / `agent.clarify_timeout` as the messaging-platform deadlines.

## Supersedes

- #128662: TUI notice for a timed-out approval. TUI approvals no longer time out.
- #71372: preserve TUI clarify drafts on timeout. TUI clarify no longer times out.
- #25865: unify the clarify timeout key across CLI and gateway. The CLI no longer has a clarify timeout.
- #13088 (CLI half only): the CLI approval panel no longer reads a timeout. The ACP half of that PR is unrelated to this change.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_approval_prompts_wait_for_answer.py`: an attended approval outlives `approvals.timeout: 1` while an unbound (messaging) wait in the same process still times out. An attended human-wait window keeps counting when read from an unbound context.
2. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_approval_ui.py tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_clarify_batch.py`: the CLI panels stay up past a 1s `approvals.timeout` / `agent.clarify_timeout` and resolve when answered.
3. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py -k "approval_session_key or clarify_callback"`: a TUI/Desktop turn's approval window is unbounded inside the turn and back to the config value after it. Clarify requests go out with no deadline.
4. `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/plugins/hermes-bots/group-turns.test.ts`: a member blocked on an approval past the 3 h hard cap still delivers its reply. Red on `main`, green here.
5. Manual: set `approvals.timeout: 5` and `agent.clarify_timeout: 5`, then trigger a dangerous command and a clarify in `hermes`, `hermes --tui` and the Desktop app. Wait past 5s. The prompts stay up and still resolve when answered.

Supersedes #103406 by @ericmaddox, with the same commit and authorship. The fork PR's `CI` workflow kept failing to start (zero-job `startup_failure`), so this runs it from a branch on the main repo.

## What does this PR do?

Passes `--session <name>` alongside `--cdp <ws_url>` in `tools/browser_tool_session.py:_run_browser_command()`.

When interacting with a browser over CDP (e.g. via `/browser connect` or cloud CDP sessions), omitting `--session` caused `agent-browser` CLI invocations to run statelessly without maintaining a persistent session daemon. Consequently, the accessibility ref map (`@e1`, `@e2`, `@e4`, etc.) produced during `browser_snapshot` / `browser_navigate` was not stored across subsequent commands. Actions referencing snapshot refs (such as `browser_click("@e4")` or `browser_type("@e4", text)`) fell back to raw CSS selector resolution in Playwright and failed with:
`locator.click: Unsupported token "@e4" while parsing css selector "@e4". Did you mean to CSS.escape it?`

Passing `--session` binds the CLI invocations to the session daemon, which persists the ref map across calls and resolves accessibility snapshot refs as expected.

## Related Issue

Fixes #103285

(#103280 is a different symptom, a `browser_vision` screenshot timeout, so this PR doesn't close it.)

- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

- [ ] 📝 Documentation update

- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- **`tools/browser_tool_session.py`**: Updated `_run_browser_command` to include `--session session_info["session_name"]` in `backend_args` for both CDP and local sessions.
- **`tests/tools/test_browser_cdp_override.py`**: Added `TestCdpSessionCommandArgs` asserting both `--session` and `--cdp` are passed to `agent-browser` for CDP commands.

1. Start Chromium with remote debugging port: `chrome --remote-debugging-port=9222 --headless=new`.
2. Connect Hermes to the CDP endpoint: `export BROWSER_CDP_URL="http://127.0.0.1:9222"`.
3. Run `browser_navigate("https://example.com")` and note ref IDs (e.g. `@e1`).
4. Run `browser_click("@e1")`.
5. Verify `browser_click` succeeds with `{"success": true, "clicked": "@e1"}` instead of raising a Playwright CSS parser error.
6. Run unit test suite: `pytest tests/tools/test_browser_cdp_override.py -v`.

## What does this PR do?

Fixes the residual `WinError 32` from #130244: deleting a profile served by the multiplexed gateway still failed on `logs/.__agent.lock`, `logs/.__errors.lock` and `mcp-stderr.log`, because those handles are held by the **gateway process**, not the deleting process. The landed #113363 fix (`release_profile_log_handlers` in `delete_profile`) releases only the deleting process's copies — `_unserve_profile`, the gateway-side teardown that `delete_profile` triggers through the `rescan-profiles` control verb, released session DB and memory-store handles but never released this process's routed log handlers or the profile's scoped MCP servers (whose cached `mcp-stderr.log` stderr handle `shutdown_mcp_servers(scope=...)` closes).

The fix teaches `_unserve_profile` the same two releases `delete_profile` already performs for the deleting process:

- `shutdown_mcp_servers(scope=hermes_home_key(home))` — scoped, so a still-served sibling's servers are untouched; this also closes the cached `mcp-stderr.log` parent handle for exactly that scope.
- `release_profile_log_handlers(home)` — per-home (`_ProfileRoutingFileHandler.release_profile` pops and closes only the deleted home's handlers), leaving sibling profiles' routing intact.

This also covers the rename path and the `unserve-profile` control verb, which go through the same `_unserve_profile`: on Windows the old name's directory cannot be moved while this process holds its routed log files open either, and a re-serve rebuilds routing/MCP via `_after_profiles_added`.

## Related Issue

Fixes #130244

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/run_profile_reconcile.py` — `_unserve_profile`: after the existing session/memory handle releases, shut down the profile's scoped MCP servers and release this process's routed log handlers for its home (docstring updated to name the second-holder problem).
- `tests/gateway/test_multiplex_hot_serve.py` — regression test `test_unserve_releases_gateway_held_log_and_mcp_handles`: enables real profile log routing across three homes, emits records to open per-home handlers, spies `shutdown_mcp_servers`, deletes one profile through the real `reconcile_served_profiles` path, and asserts the deleted home's handlers are closed/forgotten while the sibling's keep working.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/gateway/test_multiplex_hot_serve.py::test_unserve_releases_gateway_held_log_and_mcp_handles -q`
   Observed result: 1 passed.
2. Fail-before check: reverting only `gateway/run_profile_reconcile.py` (keeping the test) makes step 1 fail with the deleted home still present in the routers' `_profile_handlers` — Observed result: 1 failed, restored → 1 passed.
3. Full related suites: `pytest tests/gateway/test_multiplex_hot_serve.py tests/test_hermes_logging.py tests/gateway/test_profile_identity_purge.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_multiplex_lifecycle.py tests/gateway/test_profile_signature_during_connect.py tests/tools/test_mcp_multiplex_connection_keys.py tests/tools/test_mcp_initial_connect_shutdown.py tests/tools/test_mcp_stderr_lifecycle.py tests/tools/test_mcp_reconcile_with_config.py -q` — Observed result: all passed (82 passed, 7 skipped across the files).
4. On Windows, the reporter's scenario (delete a gateway-served profile from the Desktop UI) should now succeed without the `hermes gateway restart` workaround: the gateway releases `.__agent.lock` / `.__errors.lock` / `mcp-stderr.log` during the rescan the delete waits on.

items.body:
The Discord title-retry rename recovery merged in #129020 no longer runs a full `SessionDB.get_session` on every turn in a Hermes-created Discord thread, and it moved out of the turn runner into the Discord auto-thread lane module. No case that recovered before stops recovering.

Follow-up to #129020 (salvage of #127673 by @anpicasso, fixes #127667). Same behaviour, different shape.

Why: the merged recovery block sits inline in `TurnRunner._attach_session_title_callback`. It pushes `gateway/run_turn_runner.py` past the 2,000-line cap, and every native in-thread Discord turn (user-created threads included, for the life of the session) calls `get_session`. That call drains queued token counts (can wait up to 5 s) and joins the full system prompt just to read `origin_json`.

Changes
- `GatewayTopicThreadsMixin._recover_discord_auto_thread_source` in `gateway/run_topics.py`, next to `_is_discord_auto_thread_lane`; the turn runner now calls it in one line (`run_turn_runner.py` is back to its pre-fix 2,001 lines).
- Reads the opening source from the routing entry (`SessionEntry.origin`, an already-parsed `SessionSource` that survives restarts). Threads Hermes auto-created never touch the DB on this path.
- Falls back to the session row only when the entry's origin isn't this thread's auto-thread opening. That covers an entry rebuilt from an unmarked event after the routing index was lost: the row keeps the opening origin until that entry's first peer refresh, so it still recovers exactly as on main. User-created threads pay that read, as they do on main today.
- The row comes from `SessionStore._db_for_key(session_key)`, the store that owns the key's rows whatever profile scope is active. There's no blanket `suppress(Exception)`: missing rows are checked explicitly, malformed rows get a narrow parse guard, and a DB failure reaches the caller's logged handler.
- Tests (2, through the real predicate and recovery):
  - recovery contract, parametrised over routing entry / rebuilt-entry fallback: live message id and transport owner kept, markers recovered;
  - negative contract: another thread, a user-created thread, or an unreadable session row never lends markers.

  This replaces the five recovery tests from #129020. The broken-DB case no longer applies on the common path; on the fallback path the read stays inside `suppress`.

Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/gateway/test_session_title_rename_lane.py` | 9 passed |
| Mutations | row fallback disabled → the rebuilt-entry case fails; thread-id check dropped → the other-thread case fails; helper made a no-op → both recovery cases fail |
| E2E, real `SessionStore` + `SessionDB` in a temp `HERMES_HOME` | recovered after a store reload; after deleting `gateway_routing` + `sessions/`, recovered via the row fallback, both on the event that rebuilt the entry and on a later event; another thread, a relay event and a user-created thread get nothing |

## What does this PR do?

Adds `rtk-rewrite-docker` to the plugin catalog. It is a community plugin that rewrites `terminal` commands through RTK (rtk-ai/rtk), like the existing `rtk-rewrite` entry, with one difference: a backend gate.

The existing hook rewrites on the Hermes host, but the rewritten command runs on the terminal backend. On a Docker backend without `rtk`, this gives `rtk: command not found`. In one real Docker-backed profile, 52 of 839 terminal results had this error. 31 exited 127. 16 exited 0 with incomplete output.

This plugin rewrites only for backends that a profile opts in to (`plugins.entries.rtk-rewrite-docker.settings.backends`, default `[local]`). It reads the backend from the per-profile terminal policy, not from `os.environ`, so it also works when one process serves several profiles. If the backend is unknown, it does not rewrite. The repo also has an optional `container/Containerfile` that adds a pinned, checksum-verified RTK binary to an image.

The name is `rtk-rewrite-docker` because the key `rtk-rewrite` is taken by another plugin (kerrz2020).

## Related Issue

N/A (new catalog entry)

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/rtk-rewrite-docker.yaml`: new entry, pinned to `929c8f5f86fc544a523f94a92f95a57d4c0d7d40`.

## How to Test

1. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/rtk-rewrite-docker.yaml` gives `OK: 1 file(s) valid`.
2. `hermes plugins validate <clone at the pinned SHA>` passes all checks: manifest, config schema, capability probe, declared hooks (`pre_tool_call`) match registrations. The security scan gives `caution` with two `echo_pipe_exec` findings (README.md:81 and ci.yml:43). Both are a documented `echo "<sha256>  file" | sha256sum -c` checksum check. No finding is in plugin code.
3. The repo CI passes at the pinned SHA: 50 tests (unit, dispatch against a pinned Hermes commit, RTK integration).

Admission policy notes:
- Owner submission (rule 5). I own the repo.
- No self-updater (rule 3). The plugin downloads nothing. The RTK download happens only when a user builds the optional container image.
- No Python dependencies and no `pyproject.toml`.
- Declared capabilities match: hooks `pre_tool_call`, no tools, no env vars.
- Disclosure: every terminal command is passed to the `rtk` binary on the host `PATH`. The plugin fails open.

## Checklist

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this entry
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu (Linux 7.0), Hermes 0.21.5
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation, or N/A (README lives in the plugin repo)

## What does this PR do?

Adds **Hermes Agent Builder** to the community Desktop plugin catalog. The plugin helps someone turn a recurring job into a reusable specialist: describe the task, answer tailored questions, add reference files, edit instructions and capabilities, compare two versions on the same task, try a model-only conversation, then save a separate native bot profile and open its Bot Chat.

The entry appears only in the **BOTS** section. Each saved bot has its own selected tools and skills; an explicit empty tool selection remains empty. Hermes's mandatory core skill stays enabled. The builder uses the existing Desktop SDK, plugin API namespace, model facade, and native profile/session APIs.

This is a catalog admission request for an implemented standalone plugin. The implementation stays in its own repository, and this PR changes only one catalog YAML file.

- [Source and installation guide](https://github.com/itsflownium/hermes-agent-builder/tree/6ed39da7c7054587cbe2a42e60c3e9cbe4969cf6)
- [69-second workflow demo](https://github.com/itsflownium/hermes-agent-builder/blob/6ed39da7c7054587cbe2a42e60c3e9cbe4969cf6/docs/demo.mp4)
- [Validation details](https://github.com/itsflownium/hermes-agent-builder/blob/6ed39da7c7054587cbe2a42e60c3e9cbe4969cf6/VALIDATION.md)

![Hermes Agent Builder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/itsflownium/hermes-agent-builder/6ed39da7c7054587cbe2a42e60c3e9cbe4969cf6/docs/banner.png)

## Related Issue

New catalog submission; no existing Agent Builder issue or PR was found. [Bot Forge](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/plugin-catalog/bot-forge.yaml) already covers conversational bot creation. This plugin offers a guided visual workspace with reference material, editable capabilities, version comparisons, and a trial before saving. It does not claim the general agent-builder concept is new.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature: community plugin catalog admission

## Changes Made

- Adds `plugin-catalog/hermes-agent-builder.yaml`, pinned to full commit `6ed39da7c7054587cbe2a42e60c3e9cbe4969cf6`.
- Declares the registered `agent_builder` tool, with no hooks, middleware, required environment secrets, or additional Python dependencies.
- Includes pinned banner/screenshots, the original logo, README, maintainer, platform targets, and a Windows testing limitation.

The plugin saves drafts in profile-scoped storage. Saving creates a separate profile with fresh memory/history and native credential inheritance; messaging channels are not cloned and MCP servers are disabled until configured. Opening the conversational Builder creates its own companion profile and copies/enables this same plugin in that profile. Model-only trials do not execute connected tools. Model calls are bounded; stopping the frontend wait does not cancel an already-running backend request.

## How to Test

1. Clone the plugin repository, check out the exact pin above, and run `hermes plugins validate <checkout>`.
2. Install that checkout with `python install.py --enable` in a Hermes environment. Enable the separate Desktop component in **Capabilities → Plugins**, and reconnect the backend once if necessary. An existing configured Hermes model is required.
3. Select **BOTS → Agent Builder**. Use `examples/launch-brief.md` to build a release-writing specialist, answer the interview, and review instructions and capabilities.
4. Refine the blueprint, compare both versions using the same prompt, and try a task. Then save the specialist and choose **Open in Bot Mode**.
5. Verify the separate native profile, canonical Bot Chat, and selected tools/skills. Include an empty tool selection to verify conversation-only behavior.

## Validation and Platform Limits

- Catalog structural validation: all 350 entry/blocklist files passed.
- Native plugin validation at the source snapshot passed, including isolated capability registration, security scan (`safe`), and Desktop SDK surface checks.
- Desktop module parsed successfully as ESM.
- All 12 backend tests passed: profile isolation, stale-response protection, malformed suggestions, failure/timeouts, version comparisons, publish lifecycle, portable installer paths, and exact native capability resolution.
- Real model interviews/builds/trials, native profile saving, and a canonical hidden Bot Chat were exercised on macOS with Hermes Desktop `0.21.5+4477`.
- Windows is a platform target; its native Desktop runtime has **not** been exercised. That limitation is in the catalog entry and plugin documentation.
- The demo records the actual plugin UI in an isolated demo shell and replays real model responses to shorten waits. Native profile saving was verified separately; those boundaries are labeled in the film.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contribution and catalog admission guides.
- [x] Searched existing issues, PRs, and the current catalog.
- [x] Conventional commit; one focused catalog change.
- [x] Full reachable source SHA; declared capabilities match registration.
- [x] No remote self-updater or renderer access outside the Desktop SDK.
- [x] macOS validation and Windows limitations documented.
- [ ] Maintainer admission review and GitHub CI.

The full Hermes core test suite was not run for this metadata-only submission; the catalog validator and plugin-specific checks above cover the changed surface.

## What this adds

A community catalog entry for **hermes-worker-monitor** 0.2.1, a worker-only fork of
`mr-3mm3/hermes-monitor` (MIT), pinned to the exact 40-hex commit `cd7db41c04e5594324a8fa08e12d77681a17d6fb`
(tag `v0.2.1-fork`).

The footer item appears without a switch flip: the desktop half ships
`defaultEnabled: true`. It can still be turned off in Capabilities, Plugins.

## Why a fork

Upstream's second footer item is provider quota usage, and that item is the only reason
the plugin reaches outside the machine. The fork removes it and everything that supported
it:

- the provider fan-out that loads every credential pool
- the `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` lookup in the environment and in `.env` files
- the DeepSeek balance call, the only outbound HTTP call in the repository
- the Anthropic OAuth refresh path, which can rewrite `auth.json`
- the clone of a private Hermes fetcher used to work around an internal signature

## What is left

One route, `GET /summary`, on the local backend. It opens `kanban.db`, and each profile's
`state.db` for worker activity, read-only, with a fallback to the root `state.db` for a
default-profile card that has no profile directory. No writes anywhere, no network egress,
no credential read.

The payload carries counts only:

- board groups: `blocked`, `waiting`, `running`, `queued`, `scheduled`, `review`, `done_today`
- workers: the count of active, stalled, and looping running cards

Card identifiers, titles, assignees, and tool arguments never leave the backend. Arguments
stay hashed inside it for stall and loop detection.

## What it looks like

One footer strip, right aligned: cards that stopped and need a person come first in red,
then `waiting`, `running` (with a state dot: green active, amber stalled, red looping),
`queued`, `scheduled`, `review`, `done today`. A group with no cards is left out.
The core Kanban counter stays to its left and is untouched.

Hover any count for the breakdown (`10 running: 8 active, 2 stalled. Click for the board`).
Click any count to open the Kanban board page inside the app. There is no dropdown menu.

## Checks

- `hermes plugins validate` passes: manifest, capability probe, security scan, and the
  desktop surface check (all UI stays inside the plugin SDK surface).
- 20 offline tests pass. They cover the group mapping, the stall and loop thresholds, the
  read-only connection, the default-profile store fallback, the credential-free module
  guard, and a guard that fails if an em dash returns to a shipped file.
- `node --check desktop/plugin.js` is clean.
- No install-time code, and no third-party dependency. The Python half imports only the
  standard library and the `fastapi` Hermes already provides.

## Disclosure for review

The entry pins an exact SHA and the package never fetches, downloads, or replaces its own
files. Updates come as a SHA bump in a new pull request.

The four handlers take an optional `profile` query parameter and scope the write to `body.profile or profile`. The body still wins when both are given, matching `toggle_skill`. The docstrings give the reason.

The quota-probe rotation regression from #130084 now lives in the Codex quota-probe suite and runs the real probe, instead of a separate 97-line file with its own copies of the helpers.

**WHO / WHEN / WHY:** #130084 (@100yenadmin, merged 2026-10-01) fixed the pool rolling a Codex row back to its spent refresh token after the quota probe rotated it. Its regression test is the restored-quota twin of `test_pool_selection_refreshes_expired_token_before_probe` (the still-exhausted case), but it shipped as a standalone file that re-implemented that suite's JWT builder, exhausted-row writer and fake token endpoint, stubbed the probe out, and asserted on the private `pool._find`. Found during a post-merge review of #130084.

## Changes

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_codex_quota_probe.py`: new `test_pool_selection_keeps_probe_rotated_tokens_when_quota_restored`, next to its twin. It reuses `_expired_jwt_pool_store`, `_fake_refresh` and the expiry-aware usage stub, so the probe really runs and must use the rotated bearer.
- `_fake_refresh` also patches `hermes_cli.auth.refresh_codex_oauth_pure`. The pool's own refresh path reads it there; without it, a replayed refresh in this scenario goes to the real token endpoint.
- `tests/agent/test_credential_pool_codex_quota_probe_rotation.py`: deleted.

No production code changes.

## Validation

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Gives dispatcher-spawned Kanban workers an in-process `kanban_schedule` tool so they can park their own card in `scheduled` again.

Since the worker CLI fence (`b578261584`), a worker can no longer run `hermes kanban schedule` from its terminal, and there was no tool equivalent, so workers lost the ability to schedule. This keeps the fence and restores the capability through a tool, the same way `kanban_block` / `kanban_request_review` work. `scheduled` keeps its existing meaning: the card stays parked until something outside the worker unblocks it. No timer is added.

### Prior work and credit

- The tool itself is @fangliquanflq's commit from #108566, cherry-picked onto current `main` with authorship preserved.
- The second commit adds the integration that current `main` needs so the new tool gets the same guards as the other lifecycle tools.
- Reported in #108554.

## Related Issue

Fixes #108554
Supersedes #108566 (includes its commit unchanged)

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

**`feat(kanban): add in-process schedule tool`** (@fangliquanflq)
- `tools/kanban_tools.py`: `kanban_schedule` handler, behind `_worker_guard` and passing `expected_run_id`, so a worker can only park its own run. Reason is validated and redacted.

**`fix(kanban): gate kanban_schedule like the other lifecycle tools`**
- `tools/kanban_tools.py`: added to `_RUN_LIFECYCLE_TOOLS`, so a worker with an unbound or malformed `HERMES_KANBAN_RUN_ID` is refused instead of skipping the run-ownership check.
- `tools/kanban_tools.py`: `goal_mode` tasks are refused. The goal loop treats `scheduled` as terminal like `blocked`, so parking would bypass the completion judge (same reasoning as #38696).
- `agent/kanban_stop.py`: added to `_TERMINAL_KANBAN_TOOLS`, so a worker that schedules its card isn't nudged to call `kanban_complete`/`kanban_block` (both of which would then fail).
- `agent/transports/hermes_tools_mcp_server.py`: added to `EXPOSED_TOOLS`, so Codex app-server workers can call it.
- `cron/AGENTS.md`: listed with the worker toolset.

## How to Test

items.body:
Quick Entry, and any background send to a stored session tile, now goes through when the only unsynced rows are this window's own turn residue. Before this fix it silently dropped the prompt.

Fixes #130031

## What happened
#128450 changed the main composer's stale-send check to `transcriptRefreshIfBehind`, which blocks a send only when a different view has advanced the transcript (`competingView`). The tile path (`SessionTileDelegate.submitToSession`, which Quick Entry uses through `resumeTile`) still called `refreshIfTranscriptStale`. That path blocked the send on any non-null refresh, including this window's own server-side residue, so the Quick Entry prompt never reached `prompt.submit`.

## Change
- `apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/hooks/use-session-tile-delegate.ts`: `submitToSession` now calls `transcriptRefreshIfBehind`.
  - On `competingView` it still refuses, keeping the accepted-identity return `{ runtimeSessionId, storedSessionId: null }` from a928f049f8.
  - Otherwise it grafts the refreshed rows into the cached session state and proceeds to `prompt.submit`.
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/stale-transcript-guard.ts`: removed the now-unused `refreshIfTranscriptStale` export, which has no remaining callers. The `transcriptRefreshIfBehind` doc now stands on its own and states the null contract: null when current or when the read fails.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/hooks/use-session-tile-delegate.test.ts`: new test "grafts same-window residue and still submits the Quick Entry prompt". It asserts the grafted rows (`rowId` `[1, 2]`) and the `prompt.submit` call.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/transcript-backfill.stale-guard-loop.test.ts`: comment updated. Only a `competingView` surplus refuses a send; own residue is grafted and the send goes ahead.

## Credit
- @JoaoMarcos44 found the primary-vs-tile mismatch and wrote the fix and test in #130035, opened 05:26Z on 2026-10-01 (first submitter). The fix lands as commit 2d1e2ee8c2, authored by JoaoMarcos44.
  - It is a hand rebuild, not a cherry-pick. #130035's merge-base predates a928f049f8, so a bare `return` would have reverted the accepted-identity refusal contract. The test hunk applied as-is.
- @kokhlo independently opened #130042 for the same bug nine minutes later and closed it in favour of #130035.
- Follow-up commits by @kshitijk4poor: removed the dead export, rewrote the doc so it stands alone, and tightened the test assertion.

## Verification
- vitest (`apps/desktop`): ran `use-session-tile-delegate.test.ts`, `transcript-backfill.stale-guard-loop.test.ts`, `stale-transcript-guard.test.ts` and `submit-view-binding.test.ts` on the rebased head. 4 files, 44/44 pass.
- Red on base: with the base delegate, the new test fails. `prompt.submit` is never called; the mock saw 4 calls and none were `prompt.submit`. The peer-window refusal (#65047) passes on both base and head.
- Mutation: each change below turned at least one test red.
  - Gating on `refresh` instead of `refresh?.competingView` → residue test red.
  - Dropping the graft → residue test red.
  - Never refusing → peer-window refusal test red.
- `git diff --check` is clean. The change is TS-only, so no Python lint applies.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- The refusal branch in `submit.ts` still logs nothing when it blocks a send. That is left as a possible small follow-up.

fix(desktop,gateway): retry a lost branch create idempotently

## Root cause

`forkBranch`'s catch path only called `notifyError` and returned false — no
retry affordance, and `session.create` had no idempotency key, so a
backend-restart mid-RPC either lost the branch silently or risked a duplicate
child on manual re-branch (first create committed, response lost).

## What changes

- `session.create` gains an `idempotency_key` param (OpenRPC contract +
  generated TS regenerated via `scripts/gen_gateway_contracts.py`); the
  tui_gateway keeps a TTL registry in `server.py` (published through
  `bind_module`) and dedupes a retried create whose key was already committed —
  the retry returns the original child instead of duplicating.
- The desktop's branch-failure notification gains a Retry action that
  re-invokes `forkBranch` with the original arguments (same
  `idempotency_key`), adapted to main's `notifyError` options-object shape and
  main's current `forkBranch` signature (`sourceSessionId, parentStoredId,
  cwd, profile, ownerRoute` + key last).

## Acceptance coverage (#65410)

- Branch failure surfaces a persistent, actionable notification — the error
  toast already persists (duration 0) on main; this adds the Retry action.
- Retry re-invokes the branch with the original payload — desktop test.
- A retried `session.create` must not duplicate the child when the first
  create committed but the response was lost — backend dedupe tests.

## Tests (all real runs)

- `HERMES_PYTHON=… bash scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 --file-timeout 1200
  tests/tui_gateway/test_protocol.py` — 75 passed at head `8f0ff52f9f`
  (72 pre-existing + 3 new idempotency tests). Red on `origin/main`
  (`40e4af42b8e`, test file copied in): the same 3 tests FAIL
  (`test_session_create_idempotency_key_dedupes_retry`,
  `…_creates_distinct_sessions`, `…_expires_with_session`).
- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2
  src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions.test.tsx -t 'branchStoredSession
  failure retry'` — 3/3 passed (retry action surfaced, SAME idempotency key
  reused on retry, readableError normalization).

Fixes #65410

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/65411

Thanks @jinglun010-cpu — both commits (retry notification + idempotent create)
are theirs, ported onto current main's split `tui_gateway/methods_session.py`
and current `forkBranch` signature.

fix(desktop): show the branch fork button in session tiles

## Root cause

Session tiles never received `onBranchInNewChat`: `session-tile.tsx` passed
~20 `ChatView` props but not the branch callback, so `Thread` computed
`hasBranchInNewChat=false` and the GitFork button was deterministically absent
in every tile — matching the reporter's "random sessions, reopen fixes it"
(reopen renders the same session in the primary pane, where the button
exists).

## What changes

- `session-tile.tsx` passes `onBranchInNewChat={actions.branchInNewChat}`.
- `use-session-tile-delegate.ts` grows a `branchMessage(runtimeId, messageId)`
  delegate: the tile's branch resolves the clicked message against the tile's
  OWN live transcript (a fresh child's parent row ids are invalid), and fails
  closed when the tile's live state disappeared (stale action guard) instead
  of falling through to the foreground session.
- `use-session-actions` gains `branchLoadedSession({ messages, runtimeId,
  storedSessionId, … })` — a loaded-transcript branch entry point shared by the
  main chat and tiles, so a clicked message id is resolved against the exact
  message array that rendered the action bar.

## Acceptance coverage (#81846)

- Every assistant message in every session (incl. session tiles/split panes)
  shows the fork button in its hover action bar — delegate tests + visual
  harness (below).
- The clicked earlier reply is preserved as the branch boundary (no dropped
  question/history) — `branches a tile from the live message array that
  rendered the clicked action`.

## Tests (all real runs)

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --maxWorkers=2
  src/app/contrib/hooks/use-session-tile-delegate.test.ts
  src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions.test.tsx
  src/app/chat/session-tile-actions.test.ts
  src/app/chat/session-tile-attachments.test.tsx` — 157/157 passed at head
  `1b904f3dbc`. Red on `origin/main` (`40e4af42b8e`, test files copied in): 3
  failed (`branches a tile from the live message array…`, `does not branch
  when the clicked tile no longer has live state`, `branches a loaded tile
  transcript through the clicked message`).

## Visual harness (per the UI rule)

Isolated Vite harness mounting the production `Thread` with a complete
`ThreadMessage` fixture, `onBranchInNewChat` unwired (before) vs wired
(after); production Tailwind + `styles.css` imported, body font sans-serif.

  54×26. `shots/81846-before.png`
- After: action bar renders 4 buttons, first icon `tabler-git-fork`; bar box
  74×26; clicking it invokes the callback with `assistant-1`. No page
  errors in either shot. `shots/81846-after.png`

Fixes #81846

Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/82120

Thanks @embwl0x — both commits (tile branch restore + stale-action guard) are
theirs, rebased onto current main (3 conflicts resolved; the PR's
read-durable-projection intent in use-session-actions was subsumed by main's
branch_whole rewrite — kept HEAD there, kept the tile delegate wiring).

items.body:
## Root cause

Preview tabs in the right rail were window-global: `preview.ts` keyed its tab list per-profile only, so two conversations in the same profile shared one drawer — a file or artifact opened in one chat stayed visible above the composer in every other chat, and the same file could stack duplicate tabs because file ids were keyed by raw URL.

## Fix

Cherry-picked from #87288 (authorship preserved), rebased onto main's per-profile scoping:

- Every preview tab records the session that opened it (`sessionId` stamped at open); the drawer renders only the focused session's tabs plus an explicit pinned set. Switching conversations swaps the drawer; switching back restores it. Hidden tabs stay alive — their panes leave the layout tree without firing close.
- Pin-to-workspace escape hatch: pinned tabs render in every session. The pin toggle rides the zone tab menu (`tabMenuPrefix`) — main's pane mirror has no strip-tools slot, so this replaces the PR's strip-glyph placement; design point for review.
- File tab ids are canonicalized (`file://` stripped) and session-scoped, so the same file dedupes across entry points while two conversations can open it independently.
- Reuse semantics hardened (from #87288's second commit): a pinned file row reused from another session keeps its owner's id; the singleton Browser re-owns to the session that navigates it; the rail selection follows the row's final id.
- Deleting a session prunes its tabs (pins survive). Ownerless draft tabs are adopted — and rekeyed — when a session appears. Legacy unscoped tabs migrate to pinned on load.

Rebase adaptations against current main:

- `openPreview` keeps main's single-argument signature (main dropped `PreviewRecordSource`); render-mode resolution stays with `withRenderMode`.
- The PR's `preview-strip-tools.tsx` module was dropped: main moved the console/DevTools toggles into `preview-browser-bar.tsx` and removed the strip-tools revision machinery the module depended on.
- `$focusedStoredSessionId` moved to `session-focus.ts` (re-exported from `session-states.ts`): the new `preview.ts` import of it plus `session-states.ts` importing `setPreviewScope` back formed a module load cycle that crashed with a TDZ error. Its inputs are leaf stores, so the derivation is cycle-free there.
- The Browser re-own test asserts the minted `url:browser-` id prefix instead of the PR's fixed `url:browser` id (main mints unique browser ids).

## Coverage

- #73890 (preview-tab scope requirement): fixed — per-session buckets with pin-to-workspace, the exact design from the issue's Aug-15 comment. The issue's Artifacts-pane and focused-session-fallback items are separate follow-ups (see #73940's direction).

## Checks

- `npx vitest run src/store/preview.test.ts src/app/chat/preview-tile.test.ts src/app/chat/close-tab.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` — 64 passed (21 new session-scoping tests).
- `npx vitest run src/store/preview-tabs-scope.test.ts src/store/session-sidebar-focus.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` — 4 passed (existing per-profile scoping unchanged).
- `npx tsc -p apps/desktop --noEmit` — clean.

New tests are red on base: on `origin/main` the session-scoping block fails (no `sessionId`/`pinned` on `PreviewTab`, `openPreview` ignores the focused session).

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/87288 — thanks @DavidMetcalfe
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/73940 — thanks @Johnny-xuan
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/73947 — thanks @Johnny-xuan

items.body:
## Root cause

`message.reaction` desktop-bridge events mutated the visible transcript with no
session-scope gate, in two halves:

- **Renderer** — `handleDesktopBridgeEvent`'s `message.reaction` branch called
  `setMessages` on the visible transcript whenever `payload.row_id` was a
  number. Every sibling UI-mutating branch (`tip.show`, `pane.reveal`,
  `layout.apply`) gates on `isActiveEvent`; this one did not. A background
  session's event stamped its `row_id`/`reactions` onto the foreground's
  optimistic bubble via the `findLastIndex` fallback, and the reaction overlays
  (`$agentReactions` keyed by bare DB row id, `$localReactions`) were never
  wiped across profile/gateway switches — a foreign DB's coincidental row id
  could repaint after a swap.
- **Emitter** — `emit_desktop_bridge_event` routed session-scoped events by
  window id only, so a reaction fired from one session could land in whatever
  window was focused, with no session tag to gate on.

## What changes

- Renderer: add `isActiveEvent &&` to the `message.reaction` gate (the same gate
  every sibling branch uses), and wipe the live reaction overlays when the
  row-id space changes — on a profile swap (change-guarded) and in
  `wipeSessionListsForGatewaySwitch()`.
- Emitter: route session-scoped bridge events by `HERMES_SESSION_ID` with the
  window id as fallback, so the renderer's `isActiveEvent` gate has a correct
  tag to evaluate.
- The owning background session still paints its reaction from the persisted
  write on its next load — nothing is lost, only the cross-session repaint is.

## Acceptance coverage

- #118748 requirement 1 (background event must not mutate the visible
  transcript — `isActiveEvent` gate): covered by
  `desktop-bridge.reaction.test.ts` "a background session event never mutates
  the visible transcript or the overlay" + the emitter's session-id routing.
- requirement 2 (findLastIndex fallback must not stamp a background session's
  row): covered by "an active event stamps row id and reactions onto the
  optimistic bubble" / "an active event matches the byRowId leg" — the same
  legs now only run for the active session.
- requirement 3 (overlays wiped on profile swap / connection switch):
  covered by `reactions-local.test.ts` "a profile swap clears the overlay so a
  foreign row id cannot repaint", "a same-profile set is not a swap", "a
  connection switch wipes the overlays along with the rest of the outgoing
  transcript".

Fixes #118748

## Tests (real results)

Red on pristine `origin/main` (b9f6ab279d) with only the new test files copied

items.body:
## Root cause

Quick Entry's submit was fire-and-forget: `main.ts` hid the window before validating or delivering, dropped the text when no primary window existed, and sent a one-way `webContents.send` with no success/failure acknowledgement. The New-session target made it worse — `startFreshSessionDraft()` and `submitText()` ran back-to-back, so the submit snapshotted route refs before React Router committed `/new`, and the drift guard classified the just-created session as foreign.

## What changes

- Acked submit contract: the renderer sends `hermes:quick-entry:submit` and waits for an explicit ack from the main process (preload + IPC round-trip), so the draft is retained until delivery is acknowledged instead of vanishing into a one-way send.
- `lib/quick-entry-submission.ts` centralizes the submit outcome: accepted runtime session id, stored-session binding, timeout-as-unknown semantics, and late relay-outcome reconciliation inside the capture window.
- Atomic new-session submit: create the session, then submit to its runtime id, independent of Router commit timing. The bridge keeps the new-session submit route-neutral and commits the fresh route (flushSync, from #107773) before the submit snapshots route refs, so the drift guard no longer aborts the just-created session.
- `useSessionTileDelegate` gains `resumeTile` + `submitToSession` so a picked session is resumed and submitted through the routed profile gateway, reporting the accepted runtime and its stored binding — refusals (e.g. read-only tile, peer-window transcript drift) never report delivery.
- Drift pins are scoped to their owning request, so a stale classification from one submit can't poison the next.

Geometry: not touched here. The double-shadow macOS capsule from the report is already fixed on main by 13b9feea33 (`hasShadow: !IS_MAC`); the remaining reveal-vs-no-reveal contract is a maintainer product call this PR deliberately leaves to them — the floor this PR guarantees is that the draft is retained until the ack arrives.

## Acceptance coverage per issue (#85590)

- Defined submit contract — acked, draft retained until acknowledged. Covered in `store/quick-entry.test.ts` and `lib/quick-entry-submission.test.ts`.
- New-session submit is atomic, independent of Router commit timing. Covered in `use-quick-entry-bridge.test.ts` and `session-context-drift.test.ts`.
- Regression coverage for the IPC ack round-trip and the atomic new-session integration. Covered across the five test files listed below.
- Geometry — already fixed on main by 13b9feea33; not re-litigated here.

## Tests

- `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/store/quick-entry.test.ts src/app/contrib/hooks/use-quick-entry-bridge.test.ts src/app/contrib/hooks/use-session-tile-delegate.test.ts src/app/session/hooks/session-context-drift.test.ts src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/index.test.tsx --maxWorkers=2` — 5 files, 216/216 passed, on the branch rebased onto current `origin/main` (local run; no CI wait).
- The full-file `use-session-tile-delegate.test.ts` run previously failed in `submitToSession > returns the accepted runtime and its stored binding` because a leftover `mockResolvedValueOnce` on `getLatestSessionMessages` leaked from an earlier describe; the suite now resets that mock in its `beforeEach` (same pattern as the #65047 describe).

Fixes #85590
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/89920
Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/107773

Thanks @LeonardoLGDS (acked-submit + atomic-create foundation, commits cherry-picked with authorship kept) and @mdenil (flushSync route-commit fix, folded into the bridge).

items.body: ## Root cause Every ```mermaid fence rendered its diagram synchronously on mount: the mermaid runtime was imported and ran parse/layout in the same task as the transcript's first paint, and remounting a message re-ran the whole render. A transcript with several diagrams stalled the main thread on each one (#98951). ## What changes Supersedes #98986 (LikelyLucid) with #98967's (kokhlo) nextPaint seam folded in. - New `embeds/mermaid-render-cache.ts`: a dependency-injected render cache — identical in-flight renders are **deduplicated** (observer-counted cancellation: a remount that leaves zero observers aborts before the render mutex), completed SVGs are cached per `(source, theme)` in an LRU bounded at `maxEntries`, **failed renders never enter the cache** (a transient parse error retries on the next mount), rendering is serialized through a mutex with a task yield between CPU-heavy renders, and the mermaid import is retryable after a transient chunk failure (`createRetryableLoader`). - The embed renders each mounted SVG in an `` resource, so two copies of the same diagram share one render but keep isolated defs/ids. - The first uncached render is **deferred one paint** (`nextPaint`: rAF, timer fallback) so the source fallback paints before the mermaid runtime is imported and parsed. This replaces #98986's `requestIdleCallback` deferral, which never fires under the jsdom test setup's inert stub — the component test times out on main (see red control) and passes here. - Registry comment updated; no new dependencies, no config, no API changes. ## Tests Red on `origin/main` (branch tests copied onto a clean main worktree, `--testTimeout 8000`): `reuses one render while isolating each mounted SVG in an image resource` **times out — the diagram never renders** (`requestIdleCallback` never fires in jsdom); the cache module does not exist there (`/tmp/vitest-98951-red.log`). Green on this branch (`apps/desktop`, `--maxWorkers=2`): ``` ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/components/assistant-ui/embeds/mermaid-render-cache.test.ts src/components/assistant-ui/embeds/mermaid-embed.test.tsx → Test Files 2 passed (2), Tests 13 passed (13) ``` Cache coverage: in-flight sharing, per-theme keys, serialization, failure eviction, LRU bound, cancellation + immediate-remount restart, task yield between renders, retryable loader, nextPaint one-frame admission and timer fallback. Typecheck: `npx tsc -p . --noEmit` exit 0. Fixes #98951 Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/98986 Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/98967 Thanks @LikelyLucid (the render cache and image-resource isolation are your #98986 commit, cherry-picked with authorship intact) and @kokhlo (the nextPaint seam and its tests come from your #98967).

items.body: ## What Wide markdown forced sideways panning in chat (#70451). Fenced code in tool bodies, user bubbles and bot group rooms grew horizontal scrollbars. The group room was worst: it clipped both edges with no scroll affordance at all. - **Fences wrap.** Tool-body (`CompactMarkdown`) fences, user-bubble fences and group-room `pre` soft-wrap inside their box. The compact fence's inner `code` drops its inline-pill styling, so wrapped lines read as one block instead of per-line stripes. - **Prose stays in the column.** `min-w-0` on the markdown container, and huge plain-text fallbacks soft-wrap. - **Tables keep content-sized columns.** Cells already wrap at word boundaries. A genuinely unbreakable token (a 300-character run, a long URL) scrolls inside the table's own card, the way code cards already do, rather than squeezing every column letter by letter. Compact-table headers stay on one line (`OTHER` used to break as `OT/HE/R`). - **Code cards are unchanged:** they keep their in-card overlay scroller. ## Design call for review The issue suggests "tables: wrap cells". I tried forcing that two ways: - `table-fixed` makes every table equal columns, so short label columns get as wide as description columns and identifiers break mid-word even when there's room. - Auto layout with `overflow-wrap: anywhere` starves the short columns (`Metri/c`, `seco/nd_r/ow`). Both looked worse on ordinary tables than today's. So only the pathological token scrolls, and only inside its card; the transcript never scrolls sideways. Say the word if you'd rather force wrapping. ## Screenshots Dark theme, 720px column, the same fixture before and after: an assistant message with a long token, a wide table and a code fence; a user bubble with a long fence; and a tool body with a compact table and a long fence. | Before | After | |---|---| | | | ## Tests - New and updated regression tests: `markdown-text.overflow.test.tsx`, `compact-markdown.overflow.test.tsx`, `user-message-text.test.tsx`, `group-chat-view.wrap.test.tsx`. They fail on the base (`47310227c2`) and pass here. - `vitest src/components/assistant-ui src/components/chat` plus the group-room test: 92 files and 676 tests, all green. eslint is clean. - `e2e/markdown-overflow.spec.ts` (ported from #70520) pins the containment contract: the root never scrolls sideways, and tables and code scroll inside their own cards. It needs the built app, so it runs in CI. Fixes #70451 Supersedes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/70520, https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/70561, https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/101560, https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/103357 Thanks @yuexiongHNU, @FalconOrtiz and @networthexplained. Each is credited with `Co-authored-by`.
