## What does this PR do?

Adds **Hermes Agent Builder** to the community Desktop plugin catalog. The plugin helps someone turn a recurring job into a reusable specialist: describe the task, answer tailored questions, add reference files, edit instructions and capabilities, compare two versions on the same task, try a model-only conversation, then save a separate native bot profile and open its Bot Chat.

The entry appears only in the **BOTS** section. Each saved bot has its own selected tools and skills; an explicit empty tool selection remains empty. Hermes's mandatory core skill stays enabled. The builder uses the existing Desktop SDK, plugin API namespace, model facade, and native profile/session APIs.

This is a catalog admission request for an implemented standalone plugin. The implementation stays in its own repository, and this PR changes only one catalog YAML file.

- [Source and installation guide](https://github.com/itsflownium/hermes-agent-builder/tree/6ed39da7c7054587cbe2a42e60c3e9cbe4969cf6)
- [69-second workflow demo](https://github.com/itsflownium/hermes-agent-builder/blob/6ed39da7c7054587cbe2a42e60c3e9cbe4969cf6/docs/demo.mp4)
- [Validation details](https://github.com/itsflownium/hermes-agent-builder/blob/6ed39da7c7054587cbe2a42e60c3e9cbe4969cf6/VALIDATION.md)

![Hermes Agent Builder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/itsflownium/hermes-agent-builder/6ed39da7c7054587cbe2a42e60c3e9cbe4969cf6/docs/banner.png)

## Related Issue

New catalog submission; no existing Agent Builder issue or PR was found. [Bot Forge](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/plugin-catalog/bot-forge.yaml) already covers conversational bot creation. This plugin offers a guided visual workspace with reference material, editable capabilities, version comparisons, and a trial before saving. It does not claim the general agent-builder concept is new.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature: community plugin catalog admission

## Changes Made

- Adds `plugin-catalog/hermes-agent-builder.yaml`, pinned to full commit `6ed39da7c7054587cbe2a42e60c3e9cbe4969cf6`.
- Declares the registered `agent_builder` tool, with no hooks, middleware, required environment secrets, or additional Python dependencies.
- Includes pinned banner/screenshots, the original logo, README, maintainer, platform targets, and a Windows testing limitation.

The plugin saves drafts in profile-scoped storage. Saving creates a separate profile with fresh memory/history and native credential inheritance; messaging channels are not cloned and MCP servers are disabled until configured. Opening the conversational Builder creates its own companion profile and copies/enables this same plugin in that profile. Model-only trials do not execute connected tools. Model calls are bounded; stopping the frontend wait does not cancel an already-running backend request.

## How to Test

1. Clone the plugin repository, check out the exact pin above, and run `hermes plugins validate <checkout>`.
2. Install that checkout with `python install.py --enable` in a Hermes environment. Enable the separate Desktop component in **Capabilities → Plugins**, and reconnect the backend once if necessary. An existing configured Hermes model is required.
3. Select **BOTS → Agent Builder**. Use `examples/launch-brief.md` to build a release-writing specialist, answer the interview, and review instructions and capabilities.
4. Refine the blueprint, compare both versions using the same prompt, and try a task. Then save the specialist and choose **Open in Bot Mode**.
5. Verify the separate native profile, canonical Bot Chat, and selected tools/skills. Include an empty tool selection to verify conversation-only behavior.

## Validation and Platform Limits

- Catalog structural validation: all 350 entry/blocklist files passed.
- Native plugin validation at the source snapshot passed, including isolated capability registration, security scan (`safe`), and Desktop SDK surface checks.
- Desktop module parsed successfully as ESM.
- All 12 backend tests passed: profile isolation, stale-response protection, malformed suggestions, failure/timeouts, version comparisons, publish lifecycle, portable installer paths, and exact native capability resolution.
- Real model interviews/builds/trials, native profile saving, and a canonical hidden Bot Chat were exercised on macOS with Hermes Desktop `0.21.5+4477`.
- Windows is a platform target; its native Desktop runtime has **not** been exercised. That limitation is in the catalog entry and plugin documentation.
- The demo records the actual plugin UI in an isolated demo shell and replays real model responses to shorten waits. Native profile saving was verified separately; those boundaries are labeled in the film.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contribution and catalog admission guides.
- [x] Searched existing issues, PRs, and the current catalog.
- [x] Conventional commit; one focused catalog change.
- [x] Full reachable source SHA; declared capabilities match registration.
- [x] No remote self-updater or renderer access outside the Desktop SDK.
- [x] macOS validation and Windows limitations documented.
- [ ] Maintainer admission review and GitHub CI.

The full Hermes core test suite was not run for this metadata-only submission; the catalog validator and plugin-specific checks above cover the changed surface.

## What this adds

A community catalog entry for **hermes-worker-monitor** 0.2.1, a worker-only fork of
`mr-3mm3/hermes-monitor` (MIT), pinned to the exact 40-hex commit `cd7db41c04e5594324a8fa08e12d77681a17d6fb`
(tag `v0.2.1-fork`).

The footer item appears without a switch flip: the desktop half ships
`defaultEnabled: true`. It can still be turned off in Capabilities, Plugins.

## Why a fork

Upstream's second footer item is provider quota usage, and that item is the only reason
the plugin reaches outside the machine. The fork removes it and everything that supported
it:

- the provider fan-out that loads every credential pool
- the `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` lookup in the environment and in `.env` files
- the DeepSeek balance call, the only outbound HTTP call in the repository
- the Anthropic OAuth refresh path, which can rewrite `auth.json`
- the clone of a private Hermes fetcher used to work around an internal signature

## What is left

One route, `GET /summary`, on the local backend. It opens `kanban.db`, and each profile's
`state.db` for worker activity, read-only, with a fallback to the root `state.db` for a
default-profile card that has no profile directory. No writes anywhere, no network egress,
no credential read.

The payload carries counts only:

- board groups: `blocked`, `waiting`, `running`, `queued`, `scheduled`, `review`, `done_today`
- workers: the count of active, stalled, and looping running cards

Card identifiers, titles, assignees, and tool arguments never leave the backend. Arguments
stay hashed inside it for stall and loop detection.

## What it looks like

One footer strip, right aligned: cards that stopped and need a person come first in red,
then `waiting`, `running` (with a state dot: green active, amber stalled, red looping),
`queued`, `scheduled`, `review`, `done today`. A group with no cards is left out.
The core Kanban counter stays to its left and is untouched.

Hover any count for the breakdown (`10 running: 8 active, 2 stalled. Click for the board`).
Click any count to open the Kanban board page inside the app. There is no dropdown menu.

## Checks

- `hermes plugins validate` passes: manifest, capability probe, security scan, and the
  desktop surface check (all UI stays inside the plugin SDK surface).
- 20 offline tests pass. They cover the group mapping, the stall and loop thresholds, the
  read-only connection, the default-profile store fallback, the credential-free module
  guard, and a guard that fails if an em dash returns to a shipped file.
- `node --check desktop/plugin.js` is clean.
- No install-time code, and no third-party dependency. The Python half imports only the
  standard library and the `fastapi` Hermes already provides.

## Disclosure for review

The entry pins an exact SHA and the package never fetches, downloads, or replaces its own

## What does this PR do?

The four handlers take an optional `profile` query parameter and scope the write to `body.profile or profile`. The body still wins when both are given, matching `toggle_skill`. The docstrings give the reason.

Other surfaces: the local Desktop is unaffected (these requests count as unscopable mutations there and go to a pooled per-profile backend); the TUI `learning.*` RPCs run inside the profile's own process; `hermes journey` binds the profile through `-p`. A sweep of every mutating dashboard route with `?profile=b` found no other route writing to the launch profile's home.

#118275 (merged) is the audit that listed `/api/learning/*` as already scoped; only its reads were. This is not a security issue: the caller is the same authorized dashboard operator, and the bug is the wrong target profile, not a widened permission.

The quota-probe rotation regression from #130084 now lives in the Codex quota-probe suite and runs the real probe, instead of a separate 97-line file with its own copies of the helpers.

**WHO / WHEN / WHY:** #130084 (@100yenadmin, merged 2026-10-01) fixed the pool rolling a Codex row back to its spent refresh token after the quota probe rotated it. Its regression test is the restored-quota twin of `test_pool_selection_refreshes_expired_token_before_probe` (the still-exhausted case), but it shipped as a standalone file that re-implemented that suite's JWT builder, exhausted-row writer and fake token endpoint, stubbed the probe out, and asserted on the private `pool._find`. Found during a post-merge review of #130084.

## Changes

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_codex_quota_probe.py`: new `test_pool_selection_keeps_probe_rotated_tokens_when_quota_restored`, next to its twin. It reuses `_expired_jwt_pool_store`, `_fake_refresh` and the expiry-aware usage stub, so the probe really runs and must use the rotated bearer.
- `_fake_refresh` also patches `hermes_cli.auth.refresh_codex_oauth_pure`. The pool's own refresh path reads it there; without it, a replayed refresh in this scenario goes to the real token endpoint.
- `tests/agent/test_credential_pool_codex_quota_probe_rotation.py`: deleted.

No production code changes.

## Validation

| | pre-#130084 `credential_pool.py` | main |
|---|---|---|
| new test | fails: `['rf-old', 'rf-old'] == ['rf-old']` (spent token replayed) | passes |
| `test_auth_codex_quota_probe.py` | n/a | 9 passed |

## Summary
- The preview pane treated every non-loopback http(s) URL as unloadable, so `preview.open` reported success while the pane stayed blank and a later read timed out with "No preview tab answered".
- Public http(s) pages now resolve to a navigable preview target. Loopback `0.0.0.0` is still rewritten to `127.0.0.1`.

## Test plan
- [x] `vitest run electron/preview-url-target.test.ts` (public https URL, loopback rewrite, non-http rejection)
- [ ] In Desktop, ask Hermes to open a normal website in the in-app browser and confirm the pane navigates, then that a read returns page text

---

Fixes #129757

Supersedes #129758 (@dskwe — same diagnosis and the same hunk, filed first) and #130191 (@zuturn — renderer-side fallback for the same symptom). Maintainer note: the loopback allowlist in `previewUrlTarget()` only became load-bearing when 1fb569aa23 (#101683) made the main-process answer authoritative in local mode; before that, public URLs fell through to the renderer's `localPreviewTarget`. Main is the one resolver now, so it has to classify http(s) itself — which this PR does. `c5637b22da` adds the scheme-boundary matrix from the #129758 review thread (plain `http://`, LAN host, `data:`, `javascript:`).

Update ClinePass to 1.2.3 to address the catalog-policy review. The plugin uses its registered `ProviderProfile` for model discovery:

```diff
- Write curated and live IDs into Hermes private _PROVIDER_MODELS dictionaries
- Temporarily replace providers.list_providers during import
+ Supply the curated catalog through fallback_models
+ Return pass and free model IDs through fetch_models()
```

The catalog pins [fba50fb34b1691d609da0351979d5121ff18aad8](https://github.com/Adolanium/hermes-clinepass/commit/fba50fb34b1691d609da0351979d5121ff18aad8), with package and manifest versions aligned at 1.2.3. Free models retain their exact gateway IDs. Hermes owns picker and validator integration. After a failed live refresh, discovery returns to the curated fallback; the plugin no longer preserves learned models by modifying core state. Tests and README reflect that behavior.

Only `plugin-catalog/clinepass.yaml` changes in Hermes. Capability declarations remain unchanged. The source commit is on `release/catalog-1.2.3-20261001`; the plugin default branch is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before: both live/free refresh regression tests fail against the old plugin because discovered IDs persist in Hermes' private static catalog.
- After: all 23 plugin tests pass on Windows with Python 3.13 against real Hermes imports at this PR's base state. Fresh-process tests cover three import orders, curated validation, live pass/free picker and validation, failed refresh fallback, and unchanged core catalog/discovery functions.

No paid inference requests were made. Network responses in catalog regression tests are fixtures. These results cover the new source commit; prior exact-pin installation and scanner results are not claimed for this revision. Upstream admission CI and maintainer review are still required.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way; revert the catalog pin to roll back.

**Blast Radius:** new or updated ClinePass catalog installations. Rotating free and newly advertised pass models require an available live catalog after a failed refresh; the curated pass list remains available offline.

Since the worker CLI fence (`b578261584`), a worker can no longer run `hermes kanban schedule` from its terminal, and there was no tool equivalent, so workers lost the ability to schedule. This keeps the fence and restores the capability through a tool, the same way `kanban_block` / `kanban_request_review` work. `scheduled` keeps its existing meaning: the card stays parked until something outside the worker unblocks it. No timer is added.

### Prior work and credit

- The tool itself is @fangliquanflq's commit from #108566, cherry-picked onto current `main` with authorship preserved.
- The second commit adds the integration that current `main` needs so the new tool gets the same guards as the other lifecycle tools.
- Reported in #108554.

## Related Issue

Fixes #108554
Supersedes #108566 (includes its commit unchanged)

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

**`feat(kanban): add in-process schedule tool`** (@fangliquanflq)
- `tools/kanban_tools.py`: `kanban_schedule` handler, behind `_worker_guard` and passing `expected_run_id`, so a worker can only park its own run. Reason is validated and redacted.

**`fix(kanban): gate kanban_schedule like the other lifecycle tools`**
- `tools/kanban_tools.py`: added to `_RUN_LIFECYCLE_TOOLS`, so a worker with an unbound or malformed `HERMES_KANBAN_RUN_ID` is refused instead of skipping the run-ownership check.
- `tools/kanban_tools.py`: `goal_mode` tasks are refused. The goal loop treats `scheduled` as terminal like `blocked`, so parking would bypass the completion judge (same reasoning as #38696).
- `agent/kanban_stop.py`: added to `_TERMINAL_KANBAN_TOOLS`, so a worker that schedules its card isn't nudged to call `kanban_complete`/`kanban_block` (both of which would then fail).
- `agent/transports/hermes_tools_mcp_server.py`: added to `EXPOSED_TOOLS`, so Codex app-server workers can call it.
- `cron/AGENTS.md`: listed with the worker toolset.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_kanban_tools.py tests/agent/test_kanban_stop.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_review_surfaces.py tests/agent/transports/test_hermes_tools_mcp_server.py tests/tools/test_kanban_descendant_scope.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_block_kinds.py tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_db.py tests/hermes_cli/test_goals.py`
2. New/extended tests: unbound and malformed run ID refusal, goal-mode refusal, no stop nudge after `kanban_schedule`, presence in `EXPOSED_TOOLS`.
3. With only the first commit's production code, those 5 tests fail; with both commits they pass.

Local results on this branch (rebased on `a3b56cac95`): **171 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped** across those 8 files. `ruff check` clean on touched files, `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all` clean, `scripts/audit_pr_attribution.py` reports all emails mapped.

- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)

items.body:
Quick Entry, and any background send to a stored session tile, now goes through when the only unsynced rows are this window's own turn residue. Before this fix it silently dropped the prompt.

Fixes #130031

## What happened
#128450 changed the main composer's stale-send check to `transcriptRefreshIfBehind`, which blocks a send only when a different view has advanced the transcript (`competingView`). The tile path (`SessionTileDelegate.submitToSession`, which Quick Entry uses through `resumeTile`) still called `refreshIfTranscriptStale`. That path blocked the send on any non-null refresh, including this window's own server-side residue, so the Quick Entry prompt never reached `prompt.submit`.

## Change
- `apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/hooks/use-session-tile-delegate.ts`: `submitToSession` now calls `transcriptRefreshIfBehind`.
  - On `competingView` it still refuses, keeping the accepted-identity return `{ runtimeSessionId, storedSessionId: null }` from a928f049f8.
  - Otherwise it grafts the refreshed rows into the cached session state and proceeds to `prompt.submit`.
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/stale-transcript-guard.ts`: removed the now-unused `refreshIfTranscriptStale` export, which has no remaining callers. The `transcriptRefreshIfBehind` doc now stands on its own and states the null contract: null when current or when the read fails.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/hooks/use-session-tile-delegate.test.ts`: new test "grafts same-window residue and still submits the Quick Entry prompt". It asserts the grafted rows (`rowId` `[1, 2]`) and the `prompt.submit` call.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/transcript-backfill.stale-guard-loop.test.ts`: comment updated. Only a `competingView` surplus refuses a send; own residue is grafted and the send goes ahead.

## Credit
- @JoaoMarcos44 found the primary-vs-tile mismatch and wrote the fix and test in #130035, opened 05:26Z on 2026-10-01 (first submitter). The fix lands as commit 2d1e2ee8c2, authored by JoaoMarcos44.
  - It is a hand rebuild, not a cherry-pick. #130035's merge-base predates a928f049f8, so a bare `return` would have reverted the accepted-identity refusal contract. The test hunk applied as-is.
- @kokhlo independently opened #130042 for the same bug nine minutes later and closed it in favour of #130035.
- Follow-up commits by @kshitijk4poor: removed the dead export, rewrote the doc so it stands alone, and tightened the test assertion.

## Verification
- vitest (`apps/desktop`): ran `use-session-tile-delegate.test.ts`, `transcript-backfill.stale-guard-loop.test.ts`, `stale-transcript-guard.test.ts` and `submit-view-binding.test.ts` on the rebased head. 4 files, 44/44 pass.
- Red on base: with the base delegate, the new test fails. `prompt.submit` is never called; the mock saw 4 calls and none were `prompt.submit`. The peer-window refusal (#65047) passes on both base and head.
- Mutation: each change below turned at least one test red.
  - Gating on `refresh` instead of `refresh?.competingView` → residue test red.
  - Dropping the graft → residue test red.
  - Never refusing → peer-window refusal test red.
- `git diff --check` is clean. The change is TS-only, so no Python lint applies.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- The refusal branch in `submit.ts` still logs nothing when it blocks a send. That is left as a possible small follow-up.

items.body:
On messaging platforms, a short reply to a long assistant answer no longer blocks compaction of the long tool loop it starts: the oversized in-progress turn splits again and the request survives in the task snapshot.

Salvages #129081 (no linked issue; close it after merge)

## What happened
The oversized-active-turn split (#80449) only fires when the turn-opening request is at most `_ACTIVE_TASK_MAX_CHARS`. The gateway prepends `[Replying to: "<quoted message>"]` to replies, so a two-line reply quoting a ~2K-char answer measured as a long request. The split never fired, the compress window collapsed to nothing, and each automatic pass became a structural no-op (300 s backoff) while the turn kept growing; `/compress` hit the same empty window. The over-cap task snapshot also elided from the head, keeping the quote and dropping the request.

## Change
- `agent/context_compressor.py`
  - `_authored_request_text()` measures what the user wrote: it strips the in-flight replay header, then one leading gateway reply pointer (optionally behind the Discord triggering note). The split gate in `_find_tail_cut_by_tokens` uses it; the whole-row token guard is unchanged.
  - `_latest_user_task_snapshot` uses the same text when a row exceeds the cap, so the request is kept instead of the quote.
  - `_restated_request_text()` holds the replay-header peel shared by `_authored_request_text` and `_reappend_inflight_user_task`; the reappend path still keeps the reply pointer.
  - A quote whose closing delimiter cannot be found is stripped only partly, so the request looks longer and the conservative anchor is kept. Authored text is never removed.
- `tests/agent/test_split_turn_compaction.py`
  - Reply-pointer split, parametrized over reply / own-reply / Discord-note pointers built with the real `GatewayRunner._prepend_inbound_reply_context`; also asserts the over-cap snapshot keeps the request.
  - A restated reply keeps splitting over three compactions.
  - `_oversized_active_turn` takes `request` and `groups` so both tests share it.

## Credit
- @ruizanthony (Anthony Ruiz) found and fixed this in #129081. Commit ccaf61b3b6 is cherry-picked with `-x` and keeps his authorship (code plus the reply-pointer and restated-reply tests).
- Follow-up commits by @kshitijk4poor: trim the salvaged tests to two, add the snapshot assertion, and extract the shared replay-header helper.

## Verification
- `tests/agent/test_split_turn_compaction.py`, `test_context_compressor.py`, `test_context_compressor_task_heading.py`, `test_context_compressor_structural_backoff.py`: 294 passed on the rebased head.
- Red on base: with the base `agent/context_compressor.py`, all 4 kept test cases fail.
- Probe (real import, 64-row turn): base `reply`/`own-reply`/`discord-note`/`restated-reply` → split=False cut=2/64, snapshot keeps request=False; head → split=True cut=46/64, snapshot keeps request=True. Neighbouring cases behave the same on both: a plain request splits, and a 1500-char authored request keeps the anchor.
- Mutation: reverting the split-gate hunk alone turns 4 cases red; reverting the snapshot hunk alone turns the 3 parametrized cases red at the snapshot assertion.
- ruff F401/F811/F821 clean, `git diff --check` clean, Windows footgun check clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- A user who types a leading `[Replying to: "..."]\n\n` by hand gets that prefix left out of the size gate. The whole-row token guard still bounds the row, so the worst case is a split whose snapshot drops the typed quote.
- #130194 (summary language keyed on user turns) is not included. It edits byte-pinned summarizer wording and removes the "do not translate or switch to English" guard, and the GLM behaviour it targets can't be reproduced offline. It needs a maintainer call.
- #127330 is already fixed on main by fdbcdef914 and 31447bda5e (its #108647 closed 2026-09-19), and it conflicts with main.

items.body:
An auxiliary endpoint or OpenRouter mirror on the same hostname but a different scheme (`http://`) or port no longer receives the main `model.api_key` or an `OPENAI_BASE_URL`-bound `OPENAI_API_KEY`. The key goes only to the exact origin it was configured for.

Fixes #126104
Fixes #126218

## What happened
When an auxiliary `custom` endpoint had no key of its own, it inherited the main key if its hostname matched the main `base_url`. Scheme and port were not compared, so `http://gw.example.com` or `gw.example.com:8443` got the key in plaintext or on a different service. A keyless live runtime (or one using a key_cmd) also paired its own `base_url` with the `api_key` from config.yaml, and the client cache kept serving a key borrowed earlier after the main runtime's key changed. `_resolve_openrouter_runtime` had the same hostname-only check for an `OPENAI_BASE_URL`-bound `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

## Change
- `agent/auxiliary_client.py`
  - `_read_main_api_key_if_same_host` is now `_read_main_api_key_if_same_origin`. It compares `base_url_origin` (scheme, host, port) and takes the anchor endpoint and the key from one source: the live main runtime if set, otherwise config.yaml. Origins are compared before any key is read.
  - `_client_cache_key` gains `_borrowed_main_credential_key`, so a keyless `custom` client is cached against the main credential it borrowed. A later runtime with a different key gets a fresh client.
- `hermes_cli/runtime_provider_backends.py`: when `OPENAI_BASE_URL` binds an `OPENAI_API_KEY`, the key goes only to that origin. A bound URL with an invalid port matches nothing.
- Tests:
  - `tests/agent/test_auxiliary_client.py`: two parametrized invariant tests, one for the key the client build borrows (a real config.yaml task route) and one for the key the cache serves.
  - `tests/hermes_cli/test_runtime_provider_resolution.py`: three origin rows added to the existing OpenRouter-mirror parametrization (`http://`, `:8443`, `:443`).
  - `tests/agent/test_auxiliary_ollama_local_provider.py`: updated for the helper rename.
- Docs: `OPENAI_API_KEY` row in the environment-variables reference and the configuration guide, in English and zh-Hans.

## Credit
- John Paul Soliva (@jonpol01) reported both issues and wrote both fixes. From #126108, 6 commits were cherry-picked with authorship kept: 8abb258561, 5ccf26f976, ad3de0cf6f, d1d322c14e, f1611a1bb3, 392ac46179. From #126222, 2 commits: c9fce52528, e2a64b8323. @jonpol01 was the first to submit a fix for this bug (2026-09-28).
- @vanscodex opened #127663 a day later with an overlapping origin-match fix. It covers a subset of #126108, and the live-runtime anchor case still leaks with it.
- @kshitijk4poor added 3 review commits:
  - the helper rename, with origins compared before the key is read
  - test parametrizations folded into existing tests
  - a redundant key normalization removed

## Verification
- On the head rebased onto current main:
  - `test_auxiliary_client`, `test_runtime_provider_resolution`, `test_auxiliary_ollama_local_provider`, `test_async_httpx_del_neuter`: 343 passed, 2 failed.
  - `test_auxiliary_client_cache_eviction`, `test_auxiliary_client_cache_follows_credential`, `test_auxiliary_runtime_cache_key`, `test_auxiliary_transient_retry`: 14 passed.
  - `test_model_alias_credentials`: 56 passed.
- Neither failure comes from this stack. Both also fail on main:
  - `test_qwen_oauth_auto_fallthrough_on_auth_failure` fails on main.
  - `TestAuxUnhealthyCache::test_ttl_expiry_evicts` is a timing flake with a 10 ms TTL. It passes alone on this head and also fails on main under load.
- Red on base: the new aux tests fail on the base files (9 failed). The http and `:8443` OpenRouter-mirror rows fail on the base `runtime_provider_backends.py`.
- Repro script (real config.yaml and imports, client creation stubbed), 13 cases:
  - On main: 6 leaks. `http://` and `:8443` get MAINKEY, a keyless live runtime gets MAINKEY, the cache serves the stale LIVEA key, and the OpenRouter mirror on `http://` and on `:8443` gets BOUNDKEY.
  - On head: all 13 cases OK. Same-origin, `:443` and uppercase-host inheritance are unchanged.
- Mutation: reverting each behaviour commit turned its tests red (9, 2, 5, 3 and 2 failures). No commit lacked a test that catches its removal.
- Checks: ruff F401/F811/F821 adds no new findings, and `git diff --check` is clean. The Windows-footgun check reports 4 hits in these files; main reports the same 4.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- Cron has the same hostname-only binding. It is tracked separately in #126300, also by @jonpol01, and is not in this PR.
- One edge case changes: a live runtime with a whitespace-only api_key and no base_url now falls back to config.yaml, which then pairs config's key with config's own base_url. No test covers it, and `set_runtime_main` can't produce that state.

A web page open in the operator's browser can no longer drive `hermes proxy` and spend the attached subscription credential, while SDK, `curl` and LAN clients keep working.

Fixes #126118
Closes #126121
Closes #126202

## What happened
`create_app` had no request gate, so every request went straight to `handle_proxy` and got the operator's credential attached. A foreign `Host` (DNS rebinding), a foreign `Origin`, or a cross-site `Sec-Fetch-Site` GET was forwarded upstream with the credential.

## Change
- `hermes_cli/proxy/server.py`: new `local_only` middleware backed by `_local_request_error`.
  - Loopback or specific-IP bind: accepts only its own Host names (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, the bound IP), and an `Origin` only when its host and port match the Host.
  - Wildcard bind (`0.0.0.0` / `::`): accepts any Host name, because LAN exposure is an explicit opt-in. It refuses every request a page makes (any `Origin`, or a `Sec-Fetch-Site` other than `none`), since a rebound page is same-origin with its Host.
  - `Sec-Fetch-Site` is checked so that Origin-less browser GETs are refused too. Malformed Host or Origin values fail closed. Refusals return 403 with code `host_not_allowed` / `origin_not_allowed`.
  - `create_app(adapter, bound_host=...)` derives the bind policy once. `run_server` passes its bind host.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_proxy.py`: one parametrized test with 17 rows (allowed and refused cases on loopback, specific-IP and wildcard binds). Each row asserts the exact status and whether the request reached upstream.
- `website/docs/.../subscription-proxy.md` (EN + zh-Hans): describe the Host and Origin checks and what a wildcard bind refuses.

## Credit
- @jonpol01 reported #126118 and wrote the fix in #126121, which was submitted first. Four commits were cherry-picked with `-x` and keep their authorship: 3cf3870cfc, 4ffa98773f, 5ce7aac4d7, 72bf4e9c34 (Host/Origin gate, zh-Hans docs, wildcard refusal, Sec-Fetch-Site plus host:port Origin compare).
- @JoaoMarcos44 opened the overlapping #126202. Its parsed host+port Origin comparison had already been adopted in #126121 (Co-authored-by kept on that commit). Its userinfo-in-Host, Origin-with-path and specific-IP rows are folded into the parametrized test in a follow-up commit, with Co-authored-by.
- @kshitijk4poor added a follow-up that computes the bind policy once, pins the refusal status to 403, and moves the Sec-Fetch-Site sets into module constants.

## Verification
- `test_proxy.py`, `test_proxy_off_loop.py`, `test_iron_proxy_cli.py`, `test_sse_done.py`: 55 passed on the rebased head.
- Red on base: with the base `server.py`, the parametrized test fails 17/17 (hostile rows are forwarded, and allowed rows fail on the missing `bound_host` kwarg).
- Live probe against a fake upstream (19 rows): base has 9 hostile requests forwarded with the credential, head has 0. The 10 benign rows return 200 on both.
- Mutation: reverting each behaviour commit turns its own kept rows red (17, 6 and 3 rows). Changing the refusal status to 400 fails all 10 refused rows.
- ruff F401/F811/F821 shows no new findings, `git diff --check` is clean, and the Windows-footguns check is clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- #126805 (token auth and bind guard for the same proxy, #126757) complements this change and touches the same `create_app`, so expect a small text conflict whichever lands second.

items.body:
A chat pinned before it was compressed now keeps its newest part: `hermes sessions prune`, stale auto-archive and the orphan sweep leave the whole pinned conversation alone.

Fixes #126432

## What happened
The pin is lineage-wide, but `publish_compression_child` wrote the new segment row without the parent's `pinned` flag. The prune filter, `archive_stale_sessions` and `sweep_orphaned_sessions` all check the pin per row. So after one compression, the newest segment of a pinned chat showed up as an ordinary unpinned candidate: prune deleted it, auto-archive archived the chat, and the orphan sweep closed its open tip.

## Change
- `hermes_state_compression.py`: a compression child takes the parent's `pinned` value, the same way it already took `archived`/`auto_archived`.
- `hermes_state_maintenance.py`: a new `_not_pinned_sql(alias)` predicate spares pinned rows plus the unpinned continuations below a pinned segment (`_PINNED_TAIL_SQL`, which follows continuation edges only, so real branches stay eligible). This covers stores written before the producer fix. The prune filter, `archive_stale_sessions` and `sweep_orphaned_sessions(exclude_pinned=True)` all use it. `count_prune_matches` gains a keyword-only `pinned_only` that counts the rows carrying the pin itself.
- `hermes_cli/sessions_cmd.py`: the "N pinned sessions also match" note makes a single `pinned_only` count, so it no longer counts the protected unpinned continuations as pinned.
- Tests: `tests/hermes_state/test_pinned_lineage.py` (new, 2 tests): a pin follows the chat through compression and bulk cleanup spares it; the orphan sweep spares the open tip of a pinned chat. The `FakeDB` in `tests/hermes_cli/test_sessions_delete.py` honours `pinned_only`.

## Credit
- John Paul Soliva (@jonpol01), the issue author and first submitter (#126434). Three commits cherry-picked with authorship kept: 4c854e6199 (the producer inherits the pin, and the selectors honour the pinned tail), 72ed7953f5 (orphan sweep) and 9ca695fb65 (invariant tests).
- @JoaoMarcos44 (#126510, #126566, #126645) was first with the orphan-sweep hunk and is `Co-authored-by` on the sweep commit and the follow-up.
- Follow-ups by @kshitijk4poor: the pinned-only count for the CLI note, and folding the predicate into one helper.

## Verification
- On the rebased head: test_pinned_lineage + test_sweep_orphaned_sessions + test_prune_activity_recency + hermes_cli/test_prune_spares_pinned: 35 passed. hermes_cli/test_sessions_delete + test_pinned_archived_sidebar + test_auto_archived_lineage_reactivation + test_orphan_sweep_cross_backend: 21 passed.
- Red on base: both new tests fail with the base production files.
- Real-`SessionDB` probe on a legacy split store (pinned `keep`, unpinned continuation `keep-2`). Base: `keep-2` is a prune candidate, auto-archive archives the pinned chat, and the orphan sweep reaps `keep-2`. Head: only the unrelated chat is a candidate or archived, the sweep reaps nothing, `--include-pinned` / `exclude_pinned=False` still opt in, and a real marker-carrying branch under a pinned row stays a candidate.
- Mutation: reverting each behaviour commit's hunk (producer, prune/archive selector, orphan sweep, CLI note) turns at least one kept test red. None of the commits is toothless.
- ruff (F401/F811/F821) clean, `git diff --check` clean, Windows footgun check clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- #89698 (@Archiloss) and #99090 (@salch-cred) are older producer-only pin-inheritance PRs against the pre-split `hermes_state.py`. This PR covers the pinned part of both. Closing them with credit is left to you. #99090 also inherits `hidden`, which this PR does not touch.
- When `whole_lineages=True`, the pinned-tail CTE appears twice in one statement. That path is a cold CLI/maintenance one.

items.body:
An A2A adapter bound to a non-loopback address with a bearer token and no `A2A_TRUSTED_PEERS` now refuses dispatch (403) instead of trusting every authenticated peer; loopback binds keep working as before.

Fixes #126756

## What happened
`A2ASecurityContext.is_trusted_peer` returned `True` whenever the trusted-peer allow-list was empty (`... or not self.trusted_peers`). That made the allow-list fail open: any peer holding a valid token on a `0.0.0.0` / LAN / `::` bind was treated as trusted.

## Change
- `plugins/platforms/a2a/security.py`: adds `is_loopback_bind()`, which classifies the resolved bind host with `agent.proxy_bypass.is_loopback_host`, so it covers `127.0.0.2`, `0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1` and `localhost`. Adds `dispatch_fails_closed()`, which is true for a network-exposed bind with no allow-list, no allow-all and token auth. `is_trusted_peer` returns `False` in that case. Otherwise it keeps the existing behaviour: allow-all, no-token localhost mode, an empty allow-list on loopback, or allow-list membership.
- `plugins/platforms/a2a/adapter.py`: `connect()` logs the misconfiguration once at startup, instead of on every refused request.
- `plugins/platforms/a2a/README.md`: the `A2A_TRUSTED_PEERS` row now documents that a non-loopback bind with a token requires it (or `A2A_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true`).
- `tests/plugins/test_a2a_plugin.py`: one new test (non-loopback bind + empty allow-list → refused). `test_no_allowlist_trusts_authenticated` is renamed to `test_loopback_bind_no_allowlist_trusts_authenticated` and pins `A2A_HOST=127.0.0.1` (loopback backward compatibility). One added assert in `test_localhost_trusts_all` covers a no-token localhost peer with an allow-list configured.
- `contributors/emails/953639086@qq.com`: maps JerryLiu369 for attribution.

## Credit
- @JerryLiu369 wrote the core fix in #130310 (bind-aware fail-closed using a real loopback check). Commit 26a8dca575 was cherry-picked with `-x`, and authorship is kept.
- @liuhao1024 was the first to submit a fix, in #126775. The README hunk comes from that PR, and they are credited as `Co-authored-by` on the follow-up commits.
- @Sahilvishnaliya wrote the first bind-aware design, in #127608. Credited as `Co-authored-by`.
- @kshitijk4poor added the follow-ups: deduplicating the loopback branch, restoring the no-token localhost short-circuit, logging once at connect, reusing `is_loopback_host`, and trimming the tests.
- Issue reported by @aniruddhaadak80.

## Verification
- `tests/plugins/test_a2a_plugin.py`, `tests/plugins/test_a2a_phase23.py`, `tests/plugins/test_a2a_tools_gate.py`, `tests/tools/test_a2a_reason_roundtrip.py` on the rebased head: 146 passed, 1 skipped (Linux-only), 17 deselected by repo markers.
- Red on base: `test_non_loopback_bind_empty_allowlist_fails_closed` fails against the base `security.py`. The localhost-with-allow-list assert fails against the pre-follow-up contributor head.
- Probe (13 cases over bind host, token mode, allow-list and allow-all): base 3 FAIL (token + `0.0.0.0` / `10.0.0.5` / peer-token + `::` with no allow-list were trusted); head 0 FAIL.
- Mutation: reverting the contributor fix, or restoring only the base `is_trusted_peer` body, turns the new fail-closed test red. The refactor commits are behaviour-neutral, which an exhaustive truth table over the five inputs confirmed.
- ruff (F401/F811/F821) clean and `git diff --check` clean. `check-windows-footguns.py` passes on the touched source files; its 3 test-file hits are on pre-existing lines this PR does not touch.
- Reviewed over 3 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- Behaviour change: a token-protected adapter bound to a non-loopback address with no allow-list now returns 403 to every peer until `A2A_TRUSTED_PEERS` or `A2A_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true` is set. The startup log names the fix.

items.body:
Running `python -m gateway.cgroup_cleanup` from inside the gateway (for example from the agent's terminal tool) no longer SIGKILLs the live gateway. `ExecStopPost` still reaps orphans after a real stop.

Fixes #126845

## What happened
`gateway/cgroup_cleanup.py` `main()` called `reap_cgroup()` with no guard. That SIGKILLed every PID in the caller's cgroup. The systemd unit's `ExecStopPost` is meant to run it after the gateway exits. Any process inside the running gateway's cgroup could also run it, for example a terminal-tool child or a shell, and it then killed the gateway that was still serving.

## Change
- `gateway/cgroup_cleanup.py`
  - `main()` refuses with exit 1 unless its parent is systemd (`/proc/<ppid>/comm == "systemd"`). There is no PID-1 shortcut because the gateway or `tini` can be PID 1 in containers. An unreadable `comm` refuses.
  - `reap_cgroup()` refuses and returns `None` when a live gateway runtime (`gateway run` / in-process `gateway restart`, via `looks_like_gateway_runtime_command_line`) is still in the cgroup. This covers explicit `reap_cgroup(path)` calls too. `main()` maps the refusal to exit 1. The unit's `ExecStopPost=-…` prefix means a non-zero exit cannot fail a stop.
  - An empty cgroup returns 0 before importing `gateway.status`. The kill loop reads the PIDs again after the guard, so PIDs that exit during the check are not signalled and orphans spawned during it are still reaped.
- `tests/gateway/test_cgroup_cleanup.py`: adds 3 tests: a PID-1 parent that is not systemd is refused; a live gateway in the cgroup is refused for `run` and `restart` (parametrized, also asserts `main() == 1` and that the orphans-only path still kills just the orphan from a fresh read).
- `contributors/emails/jcjc81@users.noreply.github.com`: contributor mapping.

## Credit
- @jcjc81 reported #126845 and opened #126846, the first fix submitted (2026-09-28). Their 3 commits are cherry-picked with `-x`, authorship kept: the non-systemd-parent refusal, the live-gateway guard without PID-1 trust, and the runtime (`run|restart`) matcher. Their empty CI-retrigger commit is skipped. @ehz0ah approved #126846.
- @JoaoMarcos44 opened #126927 later the same day with an equivalent live-gateway guard. They are credited as `Co-authored-by` on the fix commit.
- Follow-up commits by @kshitijk4poor: test trim to 3 invariants, a non-zero exit on refusal, a single guarded read with an early empty-cgroup return, and the fresh kill read.

## Verification
- `tests/gateway/test_cgroup_cleanup.py`, `test_systemd_stop_mark.py`, `test_gateway_command_line_matcher.py`, `test_agent_cache_pressure.py` on the rebased head: 122 passed, 2 skipped (`test_cgroup_cleanup.py` alone: 5 passed).
- Red on base: the 3 new tests fail against the base `cgroup_cleanup.py`: the PID-1 test and the live-gateway test for both `run` and `restart`.
- Probe, with the stubbed cgroup, `/proc` and `kill`: on base, a live gateway in the cgroup was SIGKILLed (`killed=[888, 777]`). On head, the same case is refused (`rc=1, killed=[]`), and the orphans-only post-stop reap still kills just the orphan (`killed=[888]`).
- Mutations: disabling the live-gateway guard turns both guard tests red. Restoring the stale kill list turns the fresh-read assertion red (`[777] == [888]`).
- ruff (F401/F811/F821), `git diff --check`, and `check-windows-footguns.py --all`: clean.
- Reviewed over 3 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- #127528 is a later copy of #126846, and #127524 is a later copy of #126927. Both can be closed as duplicates.
- Out of scope, left as a follow-up: the `gateway restart` fallback that takes over a systemd-managed gateway (#126474 / #126578), and the short `force_after` stop timeouts on the other service-manager paths.

items.body:
`hermes gateway restart` now refuses to kill and respawn a gateway that systemd runs under a non-canonical unit name (such as a pre-convention `hermes.service`), and prints the unit's own `systemctl` restart command instead.

Fixes #126474
Closes #126578

## What happened
The restart path checks only the canonical unit names. A gateway that is the MainPID of a legacy `hermes.service` therefore fell through to the manual fallback. That fallback stopped the live gateway (with SIGKILL after the 5s window) and started an unsupervised replacement in the caller's shell cgroup, while the unit's `Restart=` kept failing against the lock the orphan now held.

## Change
- `hermes_cli/gateway.py`: new `_refuse_restart_of_service_managed_gateway(pid)`, called in `_cmd_restart` just before the stop + `run_gateway` fallback.
  - It reuses the dashboard's MainPID-verified lookup (`main_dashboard._get_systemd_service_for_pid`). A bare `.service` cgroup, for example a caller started from `cron.service`, does not count as ownership.
  - When a unit owns the gateway, it exits 1 and prints a restart hint that matches the unit's scope: `systemctl --user restart <unit>` for user units, `sudo systemctl restart <unit>` for system units, and both when the scope is unknown. It also points to `hermes gateway migrate-legacy`.
  - Plain manually-run gateways restart exactly as before.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_restart_external_supervisor.py`:
  - One new test, parametrized over system, user and unknown cgroup scope. It asserts no stop, no spawn, exit 1 and the exact hint lines.
  - The `restart_calls` fixture now stubs the systemd owner lookup, so existing tests stay hermetic on Linux CI.

## Credit
- @Finn763 wrote the fix and the original test in #126578 (first and only submitter for #126474). Their commit was cherry-picked with `-x` and authorship kept: `fix(gateway): refuse restart fallback when gateway is service-managed under any unit name`.
- Follow-up commits by @kshitijk4poor:
  - dropped a `try/except Exception` around callees that already handle their own OSError/systemctl errors
  - inlined the single-use owner-lookup wrapper
  - scoped the hint to user/system units and table-drove it
  - parametrized the test and made the fixture hermetic
- Issue reported by @KimSpecht.

## Verification
- `test_gateway_restart_external_supervisor.py` + `test_gateway.py`: 39 passed, 9 skipped.
- Adjacent restart/update suites: `test_gateway_host_verbs`, `test_gateway_multiplex_lifecycle`, `test_gateway_restart_no_unit_linger`, `test_spawn_gateway_restart_reap`, `test_update_serve_generation_recovery`, `test_update_stale_dashboard`, `test_gateway_restart_loop`, `test_update_gateway_restart_fallback`. Results: 28 passed / 2 skipped and 406 passed / 3 skipped.
- Red on base: with the new test file run against `origin/main`'s `gateway.py`, all 3 cases of `test_service_managed_gateway_refuses_fallback_takeover` fail (3 failed, 5 passed). On head, all of them pass.
- Probe (real `_get_systemd_service_for_pid` / `_unit_main_pid_is` / scope parsing, with only `/proc` cgroup entries and `systemctl show` stubbed):
  - On base, a gateway that is MainPID of a system `hermes.service` or of a user-scope legacy unit is stopped and respawned (bug fires).
  - On head, both are refused with the scoped hint.
  - The caller-in-`cron.service`, session-scope and no-`/proc` cases restart unchanged.
- Mutation: reverting the contributor commit turns the new test red. The try/except removal is behaviour-neutral, as expected.
- `ruff` adds no new F401/F811/F821 (the 2 pre-existing re-export hits at `gateway.py:69` are unchanged), `git diff --check` is clean, and the Windows footgun check is clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- Out of scope, tracked as a follow-up: the other 5s `force_after` stop sites (`_cmd_start`, `_restart_all`, `systemd_status`, `gateway_launchd.launchd_stop`), and the general case where a fallback replacement is spawned in the caller's cgroup. This PR fixes the takeover only on the restart path for service-managed gateways.
- Not exercised on a live Linux systemd host. The probe and tests stub `/proc` and `systemctl`.

items.body:
A second `gateway.standalone: true` profile now starts beside a live standalone gateway instead of being refused with exit 75 ("starting beside" followed by "Refusing" 2 ms later).

Fixes #128600

## What happened
A standalone profile that loses the host lock re-checks the owner through `host_gateway()`, and it only consulted `standalone_attach_decision` when that call returned an owner. `host_gateway()` returns None when the owner's rendezvous record is missing, or when the record fails the 2 s `createTime` liveness check. On WSL a wall-clock resync shifts psutil's absolute create time, so the check fails for a gateway that is still alive. With no owner returned, the profile went straight to `_refuse_second_host_gateway` and exited 75.

## Change
- `gateway/run.py` (`_claim_host_gateway_role`): the standalone branch that runs after a lost lock now calls `standalone_attach_decision` even when the host probe returns no owner. Profile discovery then decides START or REFUSE, so a missing or unprovable record no longer counts as a refusal. Removed an unreachable trailing refusal from that block.
- `gateway/host_rendezvous.py`: new host records also store `startTime`, the process-start fingerprint from `gateway.status` (boot-relative /proc start ticks on Linux/WSL). Liveness checks prefer it, so a clock resync no longer makes a live owner look like a recycled PID. Records without `startTime`, written by older versions, keep the `createTime` check. The fingerprint is used by `record_is_stale`, `liveness_is_proven` and `discard_dead_record`, which means `_owner_is_standalone`, `host_attach.decide` and the dead-record sweep all benefit.
- `tests/gateway/test_host_gateway_lock_refusal.py`: added a test for a lost lock with an empty host probe and a standalone owner (expects START).
- `tests/gateway/test_host_rendezvous.py`: added a test that a live host record survives a +5 s `createTime` drift and is still rejected on PID reuse. It runs on POSIX with real process data.

## Credit
- @dskwe (Yuan Li) — #128602, the first fix submitted for this issue. Its two commits (run.py fix + lock-loss test) were applied with authorship and author dates kept. The PR's original commit objects could not be fetched, so they were applied from the PR diff, and each message records the original SHA (7167be14e488, ae1773274aae).
- @JoaoMarcos44 — #129035, the process-identity fix in `host_rendezvous.py` plus the drift test. Cherry-picked with `-x` (3a9043b3dc8d), authorship kept.
- Follow-up commits by kshitijk4poor: switched the drift test to real POSIX process data (`dataclasses.replace` instead of patching a private helper), tightened the lock-loss test's call assertion, dropped the unreachable refusal in run.py, and dropped a redundant assert.

## Verification
- Rebased onto current main. Tests: `test_host_rendezvous.py` 9 passed; `test_host_attach_standalone.py` 4 passed, 5 skipped; `test_host_gateway_lock_refusal.py` 6 passed. One case, `test_second_host_gateway_is_refused_with_75_…`, timed out in the full-file run on a loaded machine and passed when rerun alone; it is unchanged by this PR. Gate rounds also ran these mirror files green: `test_host_topology.py`, `test_owner_liveness_drift.py`, `test_host_attach_lifecycle.py`, `test_host_gateway_profile_env.py`, `test_multiplex_host_topology_reporting.py`.
- Red on base: the new lock-loss test fails with run.py at base (SystemExit 75, "owner unknown (its record is gone)"). The drift test fails with host_rendezvous.py at base (`record_is_stale` → True).
- Live probe (real imports; the host lock is held by another process, and the owner is a live standalone profile): base REFUSED exit 75 for both "+5 s createTime drift" and "record missing"; head STARTED for both. Benign cases are unchanged on both: a no-drift standalone owner STARTED, and a multiplexer still serving the profile REFUSED 75 with and without a record. A legacy record with no `startTime` and an exact `createTime` still reads as live.
- Mutation: reverting either behaviour commit turns its new test red. The test-only commits have nothing to mutate.
- ruff F401/F811/F821 clean (no delta vs main), `git diff --check` clean, Windows footgun check clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- #118726 (@billshoap, opened 2026-09-22) targets the same refusal in `_claim_host_gateway_role` with a different approach: when the socket path can't answer, it falls back to the owner's `gateway_state.json`. This PR covers both of its symptoms (a missing or unprovable record, and boot-time drift), so it is likely superseded. It predates #128602, so first-submitter credit for the symptom may belong there. Decide before closing it.
- `gateway/run.py` is over 6000 lines. The edit here is net-neutral. A possible follow-up is moving the standalone lock-loss branch into `gateway/host_attach.py`.

items.body:
When rotation compaction adopts a durable parent that grew past the in-memory transcript, the current user prompt now appears once in the compression child instead of twice.

Fixes #125888

## What happened
`_adopt_grown_durable_parent` flushes the turn's unpersisted prompt to the parent and then re-reads it, but `lease.watermark` stayed at the value captured when the lease was acquired. At publish time every parent row above that watermark, including the flushed prompt the compressor had already kept in the handoff tail, was cloned into the child as concurrent foreign tail, so the prompt showed up twice.

## Change
- `agent/conversation_compression.py`: the adopted snapshot is loaded with `include_row_ids=True`. The row ids are popped from the messages in a single pass, and `lease.watermark` is moved up to the newest adopted row. It never moves down, and it is left alone when the watermark is `None` or the snapshot has no ids. The watermark comes from the snapshot rows themselves rather than a fresh `MAX(id)` read, so a row committed after the snapshot read is still cloned once.
- `hermes_state_compression.py`: the `publish_compression_child` docstring now defines `watermark` as the parent's highest row already represented in the handoff. That is either the start watermark or the newest row of an adopted snapshot.
- `tests/agent/test_compression_adoption_preserves_live_tail.py`: two regressions.
  - Adopted snapshot rows are not re-cloned as foreign tail.

`hermes profile export` no longer packs credential stores such as `.op.env`, `npmrc`, `mcp-tokens/`, `vault/`, platform pairing and session stores, `home/.git-credentials`, `honcho.json`, `mem0.json` or browser profiles (or Hermes' backup copies of them), and a profile distribution can no longer plant or replace those stores on install.

Fixes #126114

## What happened
The named export filtered out only `auth.json`, `.env` and the desktop bot dir (`_EXPORT_CREDENTIAL_FILES`). Any other credential store in the profile home, and Hermes' own `.bak-*`/`.corrupt` copies of `auth.json`, `.env` and `config.yaml`, went into the archive. The distribution installer applied the same narrow notion of "private", so an archive could write a nested store, or replace a store's parent directory with a file.

## Change
- `hermes_cli/profiles.py`: adds `PROFILE_CREDENTIAL_PATHS` plus case-insensitive `profile_path_is_private` / `profile_path_contains_private_store` predicates covering nested stores and Hermes' recovery copies. The named export prunes them in `copytree`. Secret redaction now also runs on `config.yaml.*` siblings that are not Hermes backups.
- `hermes_cli/profile_distribution.py`: one predicate, `_is_installer_owned_path`, decides what an install never writes. A directory that contains a store is merged per entry instead of being replaced whole. A shipped file that would replace a store's ancestor directory is refused before anything is written.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_profile_export_credentials.py`: a named-export invariant test, plus a distribution plant/replace test parametrized over declared-owned and legacy installs. It covers file-over-store-dir and the merge of a store-ancestor directory.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_profile_export_special_files.py`: browser profile state is now expected to stay out of the export.
- Docs: `profile-commands.md`, `profile-distributions.md` (en + zh-Hans) list what stays out.

## Credit
- John Paul Soliva (@jonpol01) reported #126114 and wrote #126116. His 7 commits are cherry-picked with `-x` and he stays the author: fb8ce7a999, 0a24aeaaf5, 395959f4ae, 10a3b017c5, 2bd63066f4, 6e44670c62, a3ebec0fce. He was the first to submit a fix.
- @JoaoMarcos44 is kept as `Co-authored-by` on the commits from 395959f4ae and 2bd63066f4. He also submitted #126214 for the same issue.
- @ehz0ah reviewed #126116 and caught three gaps that were fixed before salvage (honcho.json, file-over-store-dir, the Teams pipeline store).
- Two follow-up commits by @kshitijk4poor: one test commit that pins the store-ancestor merge and names the issue's stores, and one refactor that merges the two installer predicates into one.

## Verification
- Rebased on current main. `test_profile_export_credentials.py`, `test_profile_export_special_files.py`, `test_profile_distribution.py`, `test_profile_export_default_path.py`: 72 passed, 1 skipped. `test_profiles.py`: 103 passed, 6 skipped.
- Red on base: `test_named_export_ships_no_credential_store_or_copy_of_one` and both `test_distribution_can_neither_plant_nor_replace_a_store` params fail with the base `profiles.py` / `profile_distribution.py`.
- Probe (real `export_profile` / `install_distribution` in a sandboxed HERMES_HOME): base leaks 15 of 16 seeded stores, plants 3 and lets a file replace a store directory. Head leaks 0, plants 0, refuses the replacement, and ships all benign neighbours (config, SOUL, skills, memories, `platforms/keep.json`, workspace).
- Mutation: reverting each of the contributor commits turns the 3 tests red. Removing case-folding, the store-ancestor refusal, the nested private check in the export ignore, the `config.yaml.` redaction prefix or the store-ancestor merge clause turns at least one test red.
- `ruff` adds no new F401/F811/F821. `git diff --check` is clean. `check-windows-footguns.py --all` is clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

- Root-level `.env.local`-style siblings that Hermes does not create are still exported. That is outside the issue's scope.
- `_STORE_COPY_RE` repeats the `config.yaml` backup patterns from `hermes_cli/config_backups.py::_LEGACY_SIBLING_GLOBS`. A shared constant would be a small follow-up.
- #35601 is older and overlaps this class, but it is a larger, different design that also covers SQLite export safety, so it is left open.

items.body:
Recurring cron jobs now get rescheduled and show as `scheduled` again once croniter imports successfully after a transient ImportError. Before this, they stayed stuck with no next run until the gateway restarted.

Fixes #127182

## What happened
`cron/jobs.py` stored a single failed `import croniter` as `HAS_CRONITER = False` and kept it for the life of the process. After that, `compute_next_run()` returned None for every cron job, so the due-scan recovery path had nothing it could re-arm. Each job stayed enabled with `next_run_at=None` and `state=error`. `cron/scheduler.py`'s `_cron_interval_minutes` cached None the same way.

## Change
- `cron/jobs.py`
  - A failed croniter import leaves `HAS_CRONITER` as None, so a later call tries the import again.
  - Retries are spaced at most once every 60s (monotonic `_croniter_retry_at`). A package that is really missing therefore doesn't re-run the import finder on every due-scan tick while `_jobs_lock` is held.
  - Explicit True/False overrides still take precedence, and a successful import is still cached.
  - The import warning now logs `sys.executable`, which makes a scheduler running under the wrong interpreter easy to spot.
  - `_recover_missing_next_run`: when a recurring (cron/interval) job is re-armed after an `error` state, its state is set back to `scheduled` in the same persist. Without this, `hermes cron list` kept reporting a job that was healthy and due as broken. One-shot jobs are not touched. Docstring updated.
- `cron/scheduler.py` `_cron_interval_minutes`: a None result caused by a failed croniter import is no longer cached, so the in-flight allowance recovers once the import works. A None from a malformed expression (croniter loaded, expression invalid) is still cached.
- `tests/cron/test_jobs.py`: the regression test from the cherry-picked commit (`TestMarkJobRun::test_transient_croniter_import_error_not_latched`) was extended to cover:
  - the outage leaving the job in error
  - the 60s backoff window
  - recovery to `state == "scheduled"` once the import works again
  - the scheduler cadence cache skipping an import-failure None

## Credit
- @liuhao1024 (#127195) was the first to submit the core fix: re-probe instead of latching, plus the regression test. Their commit bb48a7b48f was cherry-picked with `-x` and they remain its author.
- @itsflownium (#127202) contributed the idea of resetting the re-armed job from `error` to `scheduled`. That follow-up commit includes `Co-authored-by: itsflownium`.
- @JerryLiu369 (#129719) independently found the same fix.
- The follow-up commits (state reset, retry backoff, scheduler cadence cache) are by kshitijk4poor.

## Verification
- On the rebased head, `tests/cron/test_jobs.py` + `tests/cron/test_scheduler.py`: 206 passed. Earlier gate rounds also ran `test_inflight_stale_guard.py`, `test_recurring_wedge_selfheal.py` and `test_cron_multiplex_inflight_release.py`, and they passed.
- Red on base: the kept test fails against the current `cron/jobs.py` ("a transient ImportError was latched"). With only the cherry-pick applied it fails with `'error' == 'scheduled'`. With the backoff gate reverted it fails inside the backoff window. With the always-cache scheduler restored it fails with "import-failure None was cached".
- Probe (forced import failure in-process, then recovery):
  - base: `after recovery tick: error None` → BUG_FIRES
  - head: `after recovery tick: scheduled 2026-09-29T08:30:00+00:00` → "cron job due again"
  - Both: interval jobs still due, successful import still cached, False override still honoured.
- Mutation: reverting either behaviour commit (the contributor's or the follow-up) turns the kept test red.
- Lint: ruff F401/F811/F821 shows no new findings vs main. `git diff --check` is clean. `check-windows-footguns.py` is clean on `cron/jobs.py` and `cron/scheduler.py`.
- Reviewed over 3 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

items.body:
Switching connection or profile while a preview Save or a project creation is still in flight no longer overwrites a file on the newly selected connection, profile or local device.

Fixes #127659
Fixes #127676

## What happened
`writeDesktopFileText` routes each call through the window's current connection, and both of its callers await before writing. In the preview editor, Save validated the file on connection A and then, if the user switched mid-await, wrote the draft to the same path on B. `createProject` sent the RPC to the captured gateway A, then wrote `IDEA.md` and updated the sidebar/store for whatever owner was current, so A's idea could replace B's `IDEA.md` at the same path.

## Change
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/right-rail/preview-file.tsx`: Edit records a scope key (desktop FS cache key + REST request connection). Save checks it before the disk re-read and again right before the write, which also covers the Overwrite path. On mismatch the save fails with "Switch back to the original connection and profile to save this draft." and the draft is kept.
- `apps/desktop/src/store/projects.ts`: new `stillOnWritableProjectOwner` predicate (active gateway + live active profile; the All profiles view filter does not change the write owner). `createProject` returns `null` without writing `IDEA.md` or touching the store when the owner changed during the RPC, and shows an info toast if the project was created on the previous owner. A missing-RPC error that arrives after an owner switch no longer marks the new owner's backend stale. `activeProjectsContext` reuses the same predicate.
- i18n: `preview.saveScopeChanged` and `sidebar.projects.createdInPreviousContext` in en/de/es/fr/ja/ru/zh/types, and in the split `ar_*` / `zh-hant_*` locale files.
- Tests: `preview-file-save-scope.test.tsx` (new, it.each over connection / profile / local / API route, real temp files) and `projects.test.ts` (createProject owner-switch it.each for connection and profile, plus an owner-switch case in the existing missing-RPC test). The projects tests now use the shared `@/test/deferred` helper.
- `locales/_keys.desktop.json`: regenerated (`npm run i18n:keys`) for the two new strings.

## Credit
- @Froraut (FroRaut) reported both issues and wrote both fixes: #127662 (preview save scope) and #127677 (project IDEA.md owner). Both were cherry-picked with `-x` (d92993cabc03, f968d4ca8d57) and keep FroRaut's authorship. The `ar.ts` / `zh-hant.ts` conflicts were resolved by moving the new keys into the split locale files that main now uses.
- Follow-up commits by kshitijk4poor: a test for the missing-RPC owner guard, a single owner predicate and a live edit scope key, test cleanup (removed unused temp-file scaffolding, replaced a hedged assertion), reuse of the shared deferred helper, and the regenerated locale key catalog.

## Verification
- Rebased onto current main with no conflicts. vitest on the rebased head: `preview-file-save-scope.test.tsx`, `store/projects.test.ts`, `preview-file.test.tsx` and `i18n/catalog-completeness.test.ts` ran 4 files, 84/84 passed.
- Red on base: with `preview-file.tsx` and `projects.ts` at base, the save-scope test fails 4/4 (`expected 'draft for origin' to be 'unrelated valuable contents'`) and createProject fails on 2 cases (new connection, new profile).
- Probe (the head test fixtures run against a base tree and the head tree): on base, save-scope fails 4/4 and createProject fails 3 of 7 (new connection, new profile, missing-RPC after an owner switch). On head, save-scope passes 4/4 and createProject passes 7/7. The same-owner create paths pass on both.
- Mutation: reverting the preview fix turns the 4 save-scope cases red. Reverting the projects fix, or forcing the post-RPC owner check off, turns the 2 owner-switch cases red. Forcing the missing-RPC guard to `true` turns the extended missing-RPC test red.
- `git diff --check` clean. The Windows footgun check is clean. No Python files changed, so ruff does not apply.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- Neighbouring open PRs also edit `apps/desktop/src/store/projects.ts`. #129788 (@Froraut, opened 2026-10-01) adds a broader route-epoch fence across project reads, mutations and dialogs, including stale create completions. #129276 (@sy0u1ti) fences optimistic rollbacks for update, folder and delete, and leaves create/IDEA unchanged. Neither one duplicates this PR, but expect textual conflicts in `projects.ts` with whichever lands second.
- Other desktop-fs mutators (rename/delete dialogs) were not audited for the same pattern.

items.body:
Write/terminal tool calls carrying a truncated context-compression marker are now refused before they run, and long interactive turns keep going when the user sends corrections or answers clarify cards while the model works.

Fixes #128000
Refs #127260

## What happened
The dispatch guard only recognized a compression marker when its full first sentence was present, so a marker cut by a later boundary (`⟪HERMES-CONTEXT-COMPRESSION: 1,800 of`) slipped into effectful tool arguments. Separately, the redirect/rebuilt restart cap counted every restart for the whole turn, so a turn ended as `redirect_restart_limit_exceeded` on the (`max_retries` + 1)th mid-turn message even when the model had answered in between.

## Change
- `agent/compression_marker.py`: new `_COMPRESSION_MARKER_ARTIFACT_RE` matches the marker prefix plus its first rendered count; the count fragment is shared with `_COMPRESSION_MARKER_RE` as `_MARKER_COUNT_RE`. The bare prefix and the literal template still do not match, so source and docs that mention them stay editable.
- `agent/tool_dispatch_helpers.py`: `_context_pruned_argument_paths` uses the artifact regex. Read-only tools may still quote markers.
- `agent/turn_iteration_prep.py`: `apply_retry_restarts` resets `restart_count` when a response arrives, so the cap now bounds restarts since the last response. Back-to-back cancelled requests still end the turn at `max_retries` + 1.
- `agent/conversation_loop.py`: updated the `_LoopState.restart_count` comment (no code change).
- Tests: the existing dispatch-guard test also covers the template and the three cut-short marker forms; a new `test_response_between_restarts_resets_the_bound` (parametrized over both restart flags); `test_restart_refunds_are_bounded_per_turn` is renamed to `test_back_to_back_restart_refunds_are_bounded`.

## Credit
- @JoaoMarcos44 wrote the partial-marker guard in #127613. Commit cherry-picked with authorship kept.
- @Froraut wrote the restart-cap reset in #128682. Commit cherry-picked with authorship kept; their run_agent end-to-end test was folded into a unit-level invariant test.
- Follow-up commits by @kshitijk4poor: docstring/comment wording, the shared count fragment, and test folding.
- Related: #128004 (@dskwe, opened earlier) addresses #128000 differently with a separate `agent.redirect_restart_limit` config knob. Not included here; see Maintainer notes.

## Verification
- On the rebased head: `test_tool_call_guardrail_runtime.py`, `test_turn_iteration_prep.py`, `test_tool_dispatch_helpers.py`, `test_compression_marker.py`: 60 passed. Related marker consumers (`test_pre_compress_memory_context_handoff.py`, `lsp/test_reporter.py`, `test_trajectory_compressor.py`, `test_truncated_tool_call_boost.py`): 34 passed.
- Red on base: with the behaviour files reverted, the cut-short marker assertions fail and both params of `test_response_between_restarts_resets_the_bound` fail.
- Probe, base vs head: cut-short markers in `write_file` args were allowed on base and are blocked (`['$.c']`) on head. The field-report sequence (redirect, response, redirect, response, redirect, redirect) gave `break:4 redirect_restart_limit_exceeded` on base and continues on head. These are unchanged between base and head: bare prefix, template, prefix+word, `read_file` quotes, and four back-to-back redirect/rebuilt restarts (still break at 4).
- Mutation: reverting either contributor commit turns its kept test red.
- ruff F401/F811/F821: no new findings vs main. `git diff --check` clean. Windows-footguns check clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- The reset also relaxes the rebuilt-for-fallback cap when responses land between stalls (B, resp, B, resp, B, B, B, B now breaks on the 4th back-to-back B). `max_iterations` still bounds it.
- #128004 adds a separate `agent.redirect_restart_limit` knob. This PR fixes #128000 without new config; #128004 can be taken on top or closed as superseded.
- #129895 (opened 2026-10-01) gives the rebuilt restart its own counter sized by fallback-chain depth. It is complementary, but it edits the same function and the renamed test, so whichever lands second needs a rebase.
- #127260 stays open: the token-insertion and BOM parts are not addressed here.

items.body:
`kanban gc`, archiving and task completion no longer delete a scratch dir or linked worktree while another non-terminal task, on this board or another board, still points at it.

Fixes #126508

## What happened
Cleanup ran `rmtree` on a task's `workspace_path` as soon as that one task went terminal. It never checked whether other tasks shared the path. A ready or running task that shared the directory lost its files, and so did a task on a named board, since the guard only looked at the current board.

## Change
- `hermes_cli/kanban_db_workspace.py`
  - `_workspace_in_use_by_other` compares resolved paths against live tasks on the current board, then on each sibling board DB (opened read-only). It returns `"shared"`, `"unknown"` or `None`. If the board list or a sibling DB cannot be read, it returns `"unknown"` and the dir is kept, so failures never lead to a delete.
  - `_defer_shared_workspace_cleanup` logs the reason and records a `workspace_cleanup_deferred_shared` event (`path`, `reason`). `_defer_shared_worktree_cleanup` runs that check only for real linked worktrees.
  - `_cleanup_workspace` and `_try_cleanup_parent_workspaces` check containment / linked-worktree first and run the sharing check just before removing anything. tmux and parent cleanup still run on the normal path.
  - `_is_linked_worktree_checkout` now uses a single `rev-parse --git-dir --git-common-dir` call. The `_git_dir` helper had no callers left and is removed. A shared `_TERMINAL_STATUSES_SQL` constant now feeds the active-children and live-path queries.
- `hermes_cli/kanban_ops.py`: `_cmd_gc` runs the same guard before it removes a scratch dir or worktree. Most of the diff is re-indentation into the `with conn` block.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_gc_retention.py`: 2 tests.
  - `gc` keeps a scratch dir that a live task still uses, and records the deferred event.
  - Cleanup keeps the scratch dir when a named board has a live user, and also when the boards directory cannot be listed.

## Credit
- @686f6c61 wrote the fix in #126513 and submitted it first. Their commit (`fix(kanban): keep a scratch dir another live task still uses`) is cherry-picked with authorship kept.
- Follow-up commits by @kshitijk4poor: tighten the guard order, harden the tests, return a fail-closed `"unknown"` reason, reuse existing helpers, and use one git call for the linked-worktree check.
- #126617 by @JoaoMarcos44 addressed the same bug. Its per-gc snapshot was not adopted, and its board-discovery path deleted the dir on failure instead of keeping it.

## Verification
- On the rebased head: `test_kanban_gc_retention.py`, `test_kanban_worktree_teardown.py`, `test_kanban_swarm.py` and `test_kanban_db.py` give 82 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is `test_infrastructure_spawn_refusal_never_charges_the_card`, and it fails the same way on main.
- Both new tests fail when run against the main versions of `kanban_db_workspace.py` and `kanban_ops.py`.
- Probe (real import, isolated HOME):
  - Main: the shared dir is deleted in the same-board gc, cross-board, board-listing-failure and deferred-parent cases.
  - Head: the shared dir is kept in all 5 shared cases, and unshared or all-terminal dirs are still removed.
- Mutation checks:
  - Reverting the contributor fix turns both tests red.
  - Reverting only the gc path turns the gc test red.
  - Changing the board listing to delete on failure turns the board-listing test red.
- ruff F401/F811/F821, `git diff --check` and `check-windows-footguns.py --all` are clean.
- Reviewed over 4 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- `gc` scans the sibling boards once per candidate row, which is O(rows × boards). This is fine at current board counts; a per-run snapshot (the approach in #126617) could be a follow-up.
- Producer-side path sharing, where decompose children inherit a root's workspace (#103303 / #103325), is out of scope here.

items.body:
`/snapshot restore` no longer signs you out of OAuth providers by rolling a rotated single-use refresh token back to the spent one, no longer writes a corrupt snapshot `auth.json` over the live one, and says so when a restore was incomplete instead of claiming the snapshot does not exist.

Refs #127010

## What happened
`restore_quick_snapshot` copied the snapshot's `auth.json` over the live file with `shutil.copy2`. OAuth providers such as Codex rotate single-use refresh tokens, so the restored file held an already-spent grant and the next refresh failed; a malformed snapshot `auth.json` was also published verbatim, and the function still returned success as long as any other file was restored.

## Change
- `hermes_cli/backup_restore.py`, `hermes_cli/auth_oauth_grants.py`: `auth.json` is restored through a merge under the auth-store lock. Static entries (API keys, config-like rows) come from the snapshot; live OAuth grants (provider tokens and OAuth credential-pool rows) keep the live generation. An unreadable or invalid snapshot `auth.json` is refused and the live file is left untouched.
- `hermes_cli/backup.py`:
  - `restore_quick_snapshot` returns False when `auth.json` was listed in the snapshot but was refused, skipped, missing from the snapshot dir, or escaped the home directory, even if other files were restored.
  - A root-profile `auth.json` alias is trusted only when the home is not the root itself and the target stays under the root.
- `hermes_cli/cli_commands_mixin.py`: when the restore returns False for a snapshot that exists, `/snapshot restore` prints the new `snapshot.restore_incomplete` message ("Snapshot {id} was not fully restored; some files were refused (see logs)") instead of "Snapshot not found".
- `locales/*.yaml`: `snapshot.restore_incomplete` added to the 17 catalogs that carry `snapshot.not_found`.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_snapshot_restore_oauth.py`: two tests.
  - A rotated Codex grant survives a restore while static auth is restored.
  - A refused `auth.json` makes the restore and the CLI report incomplete, with the live file byte-identical. The test covers two cases: a corrupt snapshot `auth.json`, and one listed in the manifest but missing from the snapshot dir.
- `contributors/emails/`: map for Lion-Leporidae.

## Credit
- @JoaoMarcos44 was the first to submit this fix, in #127063. Commit 303ca2e738 (OAuth-preserving merge, `_restore_auth_json`, trusted root-auth alias) is cherry-picked with `-x` and keeps its authorship and its `Co-authored-by: FroRaut` trailer. @Froraut reported #127010.
- @Lion-Leporidae wrote the follow-ups in #128351. Commits 9e15369ff6 (propagate a refused auth restore as failure) and 8d43b16d66 (fail closed for skipped or missing auth and tighten the root alias) are cherry-picked with `-x` and keep their authorship.
- Commits by @kshitijk4poor: trim the salvaged tests from 17+ cases to two, the CLI "not fully restored" message and its locale keys, and test coverage for the missing-auth fail-closed path.

## Verification
