The Desktop preview drawer shows only the focused session's tabs again, plus pinned ones (#73890). This version fixes the regressions that got #128552 reverted.

Re-lands #128552 (reverted in #130852). Fixes #73890.

## What changed

The original commits are cherry-picked with authorship kept: @DavidMetcalfe's from #87288, plus the follow-ups. They add:

- per-session tab ownership (`sessionId`)
- a drawer showing the focused session's tabs plus pinned tabs
- pin/unpin from the zone tab menu
- session-scoped file tab ids
- pruning a session's tabs when the session is deleted
- adopting a fresh draft's tabs when that draft's first send gives it a stored id (no longer on any focus change; see F1 below)
- migrating legacy unscoped tabs to pinned
- moving `$focusedStoredSessionId` to `session-focus.ts` to break the TDZ cycle

On top of that, `3ef4d29031f` fixes what the review of #128552 found:

| Review finding | Fix |
|---|---|
| **M1** Strip "+" minted an ownerless Browser. It was invisible, then adopted by the wrong session on the next switch. | `newBrowserTab` stamps the focused session as owner. |
| **M2** Restore deduped `url` tabs per bucket, so every Browser collapsed to one. Pop-out couldn't find a non-last Browser. | `parseTabList` keeps every row as stored. File tab ids are identity only: lookups match a file by canonical path among the tabs its owner can see, so ids never need a rekey. |
| **M3** An agent `preview.open` from a side tile was stamped with the focused session. A tile's `preview.close` couldn't reach its own tabs. | `openPreview(target, { owner })`. The routing hook maps the event's runtime id to its stored id and uses it to open and close (`closeAgentPreview`). |
| **M4** Auto-compression rotated the stored id and the old tip's tabs vanished. | `rekeyPreviewTabsSession(old, new)` runs at both rotation sites (`handleTransition` and the state cache), the same pattern drafts, queues and journals use. |
| `preview.close` with no url wiped every session's tabs and pins. | It closes only that session's own unpinned tabs. |
| A URL open in session B navigated session A's Browser. | Browser reuse only picks among the tabs the owner can see. |
| `markPreviewTabMissing`'s real caller passes `target.url` and never matched. | It resolves by id, url or canonical path. Main's test stays as it was; #128552 had rewritten it. |
| Each session didn't remember its front tab. Booting with null focus reset the persisted selection. | Each session remembers its front tab. Boot checks the selection against all tabs. |

The new pin/unpin labels are translated in every locale.

An independent review of this branch found more; each is fixed in its own commit:

| Review finding | Fix |
|---|---|
| **F1** Any null → id focus change adopted every ownerless tab, so a fresh draft's file / "+" Browser tabs were taken by the next side tile or sidebar-clicked session, and the draft's drawer came back empty. | The focus listener is gone. `adoptDraftPreviewTabs(storedId)` runs where the draft's first send assigns its stored id, beside the composer draft hand-over (`4130b2c21c6`). An agent `open_preview` that lands before the stored id is noted against the runtime that opened it (the event's own runtime, memory-only) and handed over only when THAT runtime's stored id binds in its session state (`handleTransition` / `ensureSessionState`), never on a selection change. A fresh draft has no runtime, so its tabs carry no note. |
| **F2** `rekey(A,B)` then `rekey(B,A)` made the alias map cyclic, and the `latestSessionId` walk hung `$visiblePreviewTabs`. | Both ends resolve to their tips first, and a rekey that resolves to the same tip is ignored. The map stays acyclic. |
| **F3** `read_preview` / `drive_preview` read every session's tabs: with no visible selection the `tabs[0]` fallback gave the agent another session's hidden tab, and the multi-tab meta listed hidden tabs' labels and URLs. | Reader, input, nav, script runner, `drive_preview` and `tour` resolve the requester's tab with `resolveActivePreviewTab(previewTabsFor(owner))` (own tabs plus pins). The owner is the requesting runtime's stored id; a session id that does not resolve reads the ownerless/draft view, never the focused session's. Requests forwarded to a popped-out Browser carry the requester's tab ids, and a pop-out showing another session's tab stays silent. |
| **F4** A tab opened inside the rotation alias window was stamped with the rotated-away id and orphaned after relaunch. | Opens, the strip "+" and unpin stamp the resolved tip. A deleted conversation is pruned by any of its ids. |
| **F5** `session-states.ts` re-exported the moved focus atoms as a compat shim. | Every importer reads `@/store/session-focus`; the shim is deleted. |
| **F8** Dead `$focusedStoredSessionId` stub in the `close-tab.test.ts` mock. | Removed; the file is back to main. |
| **F9** No-url `close_preview` did one tab-list write per tab. | One filtered write and one selection fix-up. |

A second review pass found more, fixed in `fix(desktop): scope every agent preview tool to the requesting session`:

| Review finding | Fix |
|---|---|
| **N1** `drive_preview` and `tour` still acted on the focused session's tab (runner/nav/input looked up the focused tabs, `tabs[0]` fallback). | `previewAct` / `tour` resolve the requesting runtime's stored id and pass it to `actOnActivePreview` / `runPreviewTour`; runner, nav and input resolve the tab among that owner's tabs. |
| **N2** Pending agent tabs were adopted by whichever stored id got selected while their runtime was active, so resuming X handed them to X. | Adoption happens when that runtime's stored id binds (null → id in its session state). `openPreview` records the event's runtime, not `$activeSessionId`. |
| **N3** An unresolved requester id fell back to the focused session. | It reads the ownerless/draft view (`null`). |
| **N4** Pop-out bridge requests carried no owner. | Requests carry the requester's visible tab ids; the pop-out answers only for its own tab when listed. |
| **N5** Runtime notes leaked on close/prune/profile drop; draft adoption took tabs pending for a live runtime. | Notes are dropped with their tabs; draft adoption skips them. |
| **N6** Change-detector `writes === 1` assertion; alias-cycle regression would hang. | Assertion dropped (final state kept); the alias walk is bounded by the map size, so a cycle fails the test instead of hanging. |

A third review pass approved `99f6d637b7a` with follow-ups, fixed in `fix(desktop): third-review follow-ups for per-session preview tabs`:

| Review finding | Fix |
|---|---|
| **R1** `previewTabIdsVisibleTo` (pop-out bridge scope) read only the profile in view, so a background session in another profile got no answer from its popped-out Browser (`read_preview` timed out). | It reads every profile bucket. A background bucket counts only when the requester has a tab of its own there, so one profile's pins never answer for another profile's session. |
| **R2** When the selection already named a stored id its runtime had not bound yet, the drawer showed the runtime's pending tab but the agent view did not, so `drive_preview` returned NOTHING_OPEN. | Agent tools pass a `PreviewOwner` of `{ runtimeId, sessionId }` from `previewOwnerFor`. `previewTabsFor` / `tabsVisibleTo` include tabs pending for that runtime, locally and through the pop-out bridge. |
| **R3** A runtime that died before binding a stored id left its tab ownerless and pending for good. Draft adoption skipped it. | `dropSessionState` / `clearAllSessionStates` drop that runtime's pending notes (`forgetPendingRuntimeTabs`), so the next draft's first send adopts the tab. |
| **R4** During a cold resume, the selection moves to S a few statements before the old runtime R unbinds. In that window R's pending tab joined S's drawer. | The drawer's pending-tab clause skips a selection that is a listed session (one being resumed). An unlisted id can only be the runtime's own stored id arriving, so main's `keeps the tab when the stored session id arrives afterwards` stays green. |
| **R5** The `server-requests.test.ts` pop-out mocks dropped the owner arg. | They forward it, and the tests assert the owner reaches the bridge (`toHaveBeenCalledWith(payload, { runtimeId: 'session-a', sessionId: 'stored-a' })`). |

Swapping the source files back to `d2d0da05abd` makes 8 tests fail: `scopes a pop-out request to a background profile session's tabs` (R1), `drives the tab its runtime opened before the selection named its stored id` (R2), `lets the next draft adopt a tab whose runtime died before its stored id bound` (R3), `keeps a runtime's pre-stored-id tab out of a session resumed while that runtime is still active` (R4), and the 4 tests whose owner-forwarding assertions R5 added (pop-out act, pop-out read, local-read fallback, tour). No `vi.mock` of `session-focus`, `preview` or `session-states` is missing an export the new code imports: the full UI vitest project is green (1172 files, 10446 tests).

Known behaviour, unchanged by this PR's follow-ups:

- **F6** Upgrading users' legacy (pre-scoping) Browser tabs migrate to pinned, so they stay shared across sessions until unpinned. That matches main, where every tab is shared.
- **F7** Rolling back to main reads the new storage format. Reopening a file on main can then add a second, unscoped copy, which becomes a legacy pinned tab after re-upgrading.

## Invariants

| # | Invariant | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | A file preview opened in A is absent from B and back on return to A. Hidden tabs stay alive (no close). | Unit: `shows only the focused session tabs plus pinned ones, keeping hidden tabs alive`, `does not create panes for another session tabs`. Live: steps 1–4 below. |
| T2 | Strip "+" Browser belongs to the focused session, is visible at once, and is never adopted elsewhere. | `owns a strip "+" Browser by the focused session, never adopting it elsewhere`: red on #128552 head and on main. Live: step 3. |
| T3 | Relaunch restores every Browser of every session and every pin. Pop-out of a non-last Browser works. | `restores every Browser tab of every session and every pin on relaunch` (fresh module load from storage): red on #128552. `pops out a Browser tab that is not the last one persisted`: red on #128552, green on main (regression guard). Live: steps 5–7. |
| T4 | Agent open/close from a side-tile session targets that session's tabs. | Hook tests on the real `usePreviewRouting`: `honors an open from an open tile session…` (tab owned by `stored-tile`) and `closes only the tile session tabs when its agent closes without a url`. Both red on #128552. |
| T5 | Tabs survive auto-compression rotation. | `carries the conversation preview tabs onto the new tip when compression rotates it` (state cache) and `keeps a conversation tabs visible across a compression tip rotation`. Both red on #128552. |
| T6 | No-url close closes only the active session's tabs. A URL open in B never takes A's Browser. | `agent close without a url closes only that session own tabs`, `agent close by url reaches only the tabs that session can see`, `never navigates another session Browser for a URL open`. All red on #128552. |
| T7 | Pins show everywhere. Deleting a session prunes its unpinned tabs. Legacy tabs migrate to pinned. Per-profile scoping unchanged. | `renders only the focused session previews, pinning spans sessions`, `prunes a deleted session tabs but keeps its pins`, `migrates legacy unscoped tabs to pinned and keeps their ids`. `preview-tabs-scope.test.ts` and `session-sidebar-focus.test.ts` are unchanged and green. |
| T9 | A fresh draft's tabs stay in the draft when a tile or an existing session takes focus, and become the draft's own on its first send. An agent tab opened before the stored id goes to that runtime's session only. | `keeps a draft tabs in the draft until that draft itself gets its stored id`, `hands an agent tab opened before the stored id to that runtime only`: both red on `0134528ad60`. Main's `keeps the tab when the stored session id arrives afterwards` stays unchanged and green. Live: steps 8–11. |
| T10 | Rotation alias cycles can't hang the drawer. Tabs opened during the alias window are owned by the tip. | `survives a rotation that points back at an earlier tip` hangs on `0134528ad60`. `stamps a tab opened under a rotated-away id with the new tip, so it outlives a relaunch` and `prunes a deleted conversation by any of its ids` fail there. |
| T11 | The agent's preview reader/driver/tour sees only the requesting session's tabs, including through a pop-out. | `never answers with, or lists, another session hidden tab` (`preview-reader.test.ts`): red on `0134528ad60`. `drives the requesting session's page, not the focused tile's`, `runs a preview tour against the requesting session's tabs`, `reads no tab for a requester whose stored id is not bound yet, never the focused one` (`server-requests.test.ts`) and `answers only for the session whose tab the pop-out shows` (`preview-popout-bridge.test.ts`): red on `2a2a978db24`. |
| T12 | A pre-stored-id agent tab goes to the runtime that opened it, when that runtime's id binds. | `records the agent event's runtime, not whichever runtime is active`, `hands an agent tab opened before the stored id to that runtime only` (`preview.test.ts`): red on `2a2a978db24`. `hands a runtime's pre-stored-id preview tabs over when its stored id binds, even on a no-op update` (`use-session-state-cache.test.tsx`): red without the state-cache hook. |
| T8 | No main test rewritten to pass. No TDZ cycle. | See the changed assertions below. `tsc` is clean and the full UI vitest project is green; the suites that import the moved focus atom load without a TDZ error. |

Swapping the source files back to #128552's head makes 16 of these tests fail. Two of them are main's own tests that #128552 had rewritten: `opens the pane and fronts the new tab` and `tombstones a confirmed-missing tab in place without closing it`. Swapping back to main makes 22 feature tests fail.

### Changed existing assertions

Two existing assertions changed:

- `preview-open.test.tsx` › `honors an open from an open tile session even when main holds focus`: it used to assert `$previewTarget` is the tile's file. It now asserts that the tab exists and belongs to `stored-tile`. That is the point of #73890: a tile's preview lands in the tile's drawer, not in the focused one.
- Test mocks and imports follow `$focusedStoredSessionId` / `$focusedSessionIsTile` to `session-focus.ts`, where they now live (no assertion changed):
  - `model-picker-overlay`, `use-statusbar-items` and `sdk/profile-routing` stub the atom on the `session-focus` mock instead of `session-states`.
  - `sdk/open-session-refresh-in-place` and `wrong-session-closeout` import it from `session-focus`.
  - `session-states.test.ts`: two assertions read the atom from the module that defines it instead of `states.$focusedStoredSessionId`. Same values.
  - `session-sidebar-focus.test.ts` imports the atom from `session-focus` and loads `session-states` for the primary-follow wiring its last case asserts, which the old import pulled in implicitly.

## Live evidence

The live run used the production `npm run build` with Electron (headless ozone) and the mock inference backend, driven by a throwaway Playwright spec (not committed):

1. In session A, the agent's reply links a local HTML file. "Preview" opens it, and the tab is stored as owned by A.
2. A new session B opens with no preview tab, and A's tab is still in storage.
3. In B, `Ctrl+Shift+L` opens a Browser and the strip "+" adds a second. Both are visible and owned by B.
4. Back in A, `session-a-demo.html` returns and B's Browsers are absent.
5. After relaunch, all 3 tabs are restored (ids identical).
6. B shows both Browser tabs.
7. A shows its file.

A second run, after the review follow-ups, repeats steps 1–7 and adds the F1 case:

8. `Ctrl+N` gives a fresh draft with an empty drawer. `Ctrl+Shift+L` opens a Browser, stored with no owner.
9. Clicking session A in the sidebar shows only `session-a-demo.html`. The draft's Browser is still ownerless (not adopted).
10. `Ctrl+N` back to a draft: the Browser is still there.
11. The draft's first message creates session C, and the Browser is now stored as owned by C. A still shows only its file. After relaunch every tab is restored.

Steps 1–11 were re-run green after the second review pass's fixes, and again after the third pass's.

The Files pane isn't mounted in the e2e sandbox's default layout, so the live F1 case uses the draft's Browser tab. A file opened in a draft goes through the same ownerless-tab path, which the unit test covers.

## Infographic

![preview tabs](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aacb049/_5v5TAuDwdubBElgCyv4C_G0fYWwbe.png)

## Credit

- @DavidMetcalfe: original implementation (#87288 → #128552), commits cherry-picked with authorship.
- @Johnny-xuan: the session-scoping direction in #73940, #73947 and #73948 (co-author).

## Fourth review

Head `382c9b8bbb4`. Every row's test fails with that commit's source files swapped back to `f5f54a2b6c9` and passes after the fix.

| Finding | Fix | Test | Red on `f5f54a2b6c9` |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P1:** a profile-X tile's `preview.read` returned profile Y's pinned page | The requester's owner now includes its profile, using `previewScopeForRuntime`, the same lookup the rail scope uses. Agent tools (read, act, nav, input, script, tour, pop-out bridge ids, open reuse, close) only count pins from that profile's bucket. Own tabs count in any bucket. The human UI path is unchanged. | `server-requests.test.ts` › never answers a tile of another profile with the viewed profile's pinned page; `preview.test.ts` › authorizes only the requester's own profile pins for a pop-out | read returned `PROFILE_Y_PRIVATE_TEXT`; bridge ids included Y's pin |
| **P2:** Pin to workspace never turned into Unpin | `previewTabMenuPrefix` reads the pin state when the menu renders and again on select, not when the pane registers | `preview-tab-pin-menu.test.tsx` (pin → unpin → pin through the real menu callback) | second menu still said `Pin to workspace` |
| **P2:** deleting profile X's session while Y was on screen left X's tabs | `prunePreviewTabsForSession` prunes every profile bucket and persists the result. Pins survive. | `preview.test.ts` › prunes a deleted session's tabs from its own profile while another profile is on screen | X's unpinned tab was still in storage |
| **P2:** pending runtimes shared one ownerless pool | An ownerless tab is now either a runtime's pending tab, owned only by that runtime, or a true draft tab, owned only by the draft on screen. This applies to reads, open reuse and closes. | `preview.test.ts` › keeps one pending runtime's Browser out of another pending runtime's reads, opens and closes | B saw A's tab, reused or navigated it, and closed it |
| **Regression:** A→B→A destroyed A's live Browser guest | When a session leaves the screen, its page tabs leave the layout tree but keep their contribution, so the keep-alive host stays mounted while hidden: `inert`, `aria-hidden`, no pointer events. The same guest re-docks when the session comes back. `parked-panes.ts` keeps parked panes out of adoption. Retention is capped by `HIDDEN_LIVE_PREVIEW_LIMIT = 8`: past that, the page hidden longest unmounts and reloads from its saved row. | `preview-tile.test.ts` › keeps a hidden session's live page mounted and re-docks the same body; › unmounts only the longest-hidden live page past the cap | the contribution was disposed when the session switched |

**Live runs in real Electron:**
- Playwright tabs spec, kept in scratch (2/2 passed): the original relaunch, adoption and isolation flow, plus a new A→B→A case.
  - Guest id 3 before, while hidden and after. Same node, input `UNSAVED_B` and JS marker `alive` kept. While the other session was shown, the host was inert and aria-hidden.
  - The real tab menu went `Pin to workspace` → `Unpin from workspace` → `Pin to workspace`.
- The reviewer's native harness, re-run:
  - Guest id 2 → 2 with the same node, `UNSAVED_A` and `alive` kept.
  - Pin menu went Pin → Unpin → Pin.
  - `CROSS_PROFILE_READ` returned `''`, and the bridge ids held only X's own tab.
  - The same-profile control read still returned Y's page.

**Changed assertions:** in `server-requests.test.ts`, `sessionAOwner` and the tour owner assertion now expect `profile: 'default'`. These tests were added by this PR. The owner now carries the requester's profile on purpose; that is the P1 fix.

**Gates:**
- `check:lint`: 0 errors.
- Full `vitest --project ui`: 1173 files and 10453 tests passed. No electron files changed.
- prettier, `git diff --check`, `check_no_tmp_literals` and attribution audit all clean.

## Fifth review

Head before: `382c9b8bbb4`; new head `442ea4a150c`. Each fix test below fails when that commit's source files are swapped back in (`git show 382c9b8bbb4:<path>`) and passes after the fix. The keep-alive behaviour test fails on `f5f54a2b6c9`, the head before keep-alive.

| Finding | Fix | Test | Red on base |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P2-1:** mouse back/forward on A navigated B's hidden Browser | **Renderer:** a keep-alive host that goes hidden now blurs any focused element inside it (`keep-alive-panes.tsx`). Before, `inert` left an inert hidden guest as `activeElement`. The preview pane reports its guest's on-screen state to main over `hermes:preview-guest-hidden`, using `usePaneVisible`, so this covers parked sessions, inactive tabs and collapsed sides. **Main:** `commandFocusedGuest` moved to `electron/preview-guest-offscreen.ts` and now skips any guest reported hidden, so the gesture falls through to the renderer's visible pane. It is the only main-side focused-guest path: `getFocusedWebContents` is used nowhere else, and zoom, devtools and print act on the window. | `keep-alive-panes.test.tsx` › releases focus held inside a live body when its host is hidden; `preview-pane.test.tsx` › tells main when its guest leaves the screen and when it returns; `electron/preview-guest-offscreen.test.ts` › leaves a focused guest its host reported hidden untouched (plus visible, only-the-embedder and app-chrome controls) | focus stayed on the hidden input; the hidden report was never sent; with the 382c9b8 `commandFocusedGuest` body, `goBack` ran on the hidden guest |
| **P2-2:** hidden sessions kept playing audio | `parked-panes.ts` is now an atom. While its tab is parked, a preview pane mutes its guest with `webview.setAudioMuted(true)`. On return it unmutes only if it did the muting, so a page the user had already muted stays muted. Inactive tabs in the visible session keep playing, as background tabs do in a browser. | `preview-pane.test.tsx` › mutes a hidden session's page and restores its sound on return; › never unmutes a page that was already muted before its session left (control, green on base) | `setAudioMuted` was never called |
| **P3-1:** a fresh draft's drawer showed another runtime's pending tab | `tabVisibleTo` no longer counts a pending tab as an ownerless draft tab. A pending tab shows only while its own runtime is on screen; a true draft tab stays in the draft. | `preview.test.ts` › keeps a runtime's pending tab out of a fresh draft's drawer | the draft drawer listed the other runtime's tab |
| **P3-2:** shape | Own commit: ownership, pending-runtime and owner-resolution logic moved to `src/store/preview-ownership.ts` (200 lines). `preview.ts` went from 1465 to 1316 lines. The bucket writers (adopt, rekey, prune) stay in `preview.ts` because they need its storage. `bucketTabsFor` now takes the viewed bucket as a parameter, so the sibling never imports `preview.ts` (no import cycle). There is no re-export shim; the 12 `PreviewOwner` importers and `session-states.ts` were updated. Behaviour is unchanged: the full ui suite is green after the move. | The 4th-round test `preview-tile.test.ts` › keeps a hidden session's live page mounted and re-docks the same body compared the registration object's identity. It is replaced by `preview-tile-live-body.test.tsx`, which renders the layout tree and checks that A's body element stays connected and inert while B is shown, and is the same node, with the same input value, mounted once and never disconnected, when A returns. | on `f5f54a2b6c9`, A's body was disconnected when the session switched |

**Why the renderer pushes visibility to main:** focused-guest gestures are handled synchronously in main, and only the renderer's layout tree knows which `<webview>` is on screen. Main accepts a report only from the guest's own embedder (`guest.hostWebContents === event.sender`) and forgets it when the guest is destroyed. Fixing the renderer alone is not enough. In the live run, `getFocusedWebContents()` still returned B's guest (id 3) after the switch and the blur. The main-side guard is what stops the gesture.

**Audio and throttling:** Chromium still reports a muted guest's stream as audible: `isCurrentlyAudible()` stays true, which is what drives Chrome's muted-speaker tab icon. The live check therefore asserts `isAudioMuted()`, which is what the user hears. A CSS-hidden webview still counts as visible to Chromium. Electron has no API that marks a guest hidden without detaching it, and detaching destroys the guest, losing its state. So timers and rendering are not throttled.

**Live runs, real Electron, full-app Playwright spec (4/4 passed on the final build; spec kept in scratch):**
- **A→B→A:** same guest id 3 and node, `UNSAVED_B` and `alive` kept. Pin went Pin → Unpin → Pin. The relaunch, adoption and isolation flow is unchanged.
- **P2-1, keys:** typed `b1` into B's guest, switched to A by hash route (no click), then typed `LEAK`. `activeElement` was not inside the hidden host and the hidden input stayed `b1`.
- **P2-1, gestures:** B's guest was focused on `PAGE2` and still `getFocusedWebContents()` id 3 on A. On A, `app-command browser-backward` left it on `PAGE2` with marker `alive`. Control: back on B with the guest focused, the same command went to `PAGE1`. On base, the reviewer's receipt `R5B_AFTER_BACK_ON_A` shows `PAGE1`.
- **P2-2:** B was playing an oscillator. On A, `isAudioMuted()` was true and the AudioContext was still `running`, so state is preserved. Back on B, it was unmuted and audible. A page muted before leaving was still muted on return. On base, the reviewer's receipt `AUDIO_HIDDEN` shows `muted:false, audible:true`.

**Changed assertions:** only the 4th-round identity test above. It was added by this PR, not taken from main, and is replaced by a behavioural test.

**Gates:**
- `check:lint`: 0 errors (245 warnings, same as the previous round).
- Full `vitest --project ui`: 1174 files / 10458 tests passed.
- `vitest --project electron`: 3280 passed, 11 failed. All 11 failures come from the test host, not this change: the 8 known ones (bundle-electron-main, channel-build-version, source-backend, checkout-source) plus backend-probes-runtime (pip-less python venv) and mac-sign ×2 (need HERMES_PYTHON, which the gate unsets); `electron/preview-guest-offscreen.test.ts` is green.
- prettier, `git diff --check`, `check_no_tmp_literals`, `check-windows-footguns` and `audit_pr_attribution --fix` all clean.



## Sixth review

Independent review of `382c9b8bbb4..442ea4a150c`: **approve**, no P1/P2. Verified live in real Electron (fresh build + composite on `origin/main`): the hidden-guest IPC can't be spoofed by a guest or another window, and it never gets stuck on the visible page (back/forward still worked on B after 4 route round trips, sidebar clicks, tab switches, crash/reload hidden and visible). Mute on park works through rapid switches and LRU eviction. The 11 Electron-vitest failures are identical on a pristine `origin/main` worktree.

| Finding | Fix | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P3: a guest that attaches after its session is already hidden was never reported to main or muted | the pane feeds the guest's `dom-ready` to `usePreviewGuestOffscreen`, which re-reports and re-mutes for the attached id | `preview-pane.test.tsx › reports and mutes a guest that attaches while its session is already hidden`: fails on `442ea4a150c`, passes now. Full UI vitest 1174 files / 10459 tests; `check:lint` 0 errors; live spec 4/4 on a fresh build |
| P3: the earlier Ctrl+R live claim proved nothing (base run gave the same result) | claim removed from the fifth-review receipts | — |

items.title: fix(desktop): scope preview tabs to the session that opened them (re-land #128552)

items.body:
Launching a source checkout that already finished installing its current commit no longer rebuilds it: only stale dependencies re-sync, and a leftover marker from a previous install is discharged. An unfinished update at the same commit is still retried. A Windows update that the watchdog killed after it finished now counts as success instead of a failure or a re-run.

Supersedes #123863 and #127198.

## What changes

- **Same-commit launch (#123314, salvage #123863 by @Finn763):** if `install-stamp.json` names a clean HEAD (recorded clean, still clean), the last install/update already built this tree. A stale venv (a pristine `HERMES_HOME`) only re-syncs dependencies, and a `source-completion-pending` marker armed **before** that stamp (a preserved home after a reinstall) is discharged. Neither runs the tail again (Node deps, TUI/web builds, maintenance) for the same SHA.
- **A same-commit update that failed is still owed (review M1, @unsupportedpastels):** `hermes update` at an unchanged commit re-arms the marker before its tail. A marker armed **after** the stamp is that newer debt, so the launch retries it exactly as before. Local edits since the stamp also void the shortcut.
- **Adoption stamps are not evidence (blocker raised by @Enough1122 on #123863):** boot-time adoption of an unstamped blessed checkout stamps HEAD but builds nothing. It now writes `adoptedAt`, the completed-tree check ignores such stamps, and the next real completion rewrites the stamp without the field. Without this, adoption would silently clear a pending marker whose tail never ran.
- **Windows exit 124 after completion (#96205, salvage #127198 by @OutThisLife, with @Finn763):** if `hermes update` printed `✓ Update complete!` and the hand-off's idle watchdog then killed its silent restart phase (exit 124), the hand-off now treats the update as done. It verifies, restores the gateway fleet and relaunches. Before, it reported failure, and legacy installs re-ran the whole update. Any failure line after the banner keeps the failure: `Update not complete`, `Update incomplete — …`, `✗ <unit> failed to come back after restart`, `verification incomplete`.

Not taken from #127198, because none of it is reachable on current main:
- The posix.sh and Rust bootstrap-installer remaps. Only the Windows hand-off watchdog produces exit 124; posix.sh has no watchdog and `hermes update` never exits 124.
- The chunk-check commits, which already landed in #130729.

The retry-state helper and its self-test arm are replaced by one end-to-end test through the real hand-off.

## Validation

| Case | before | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Real `prepare_launch`, stamped clean checkout, pristine `HERMES_HOME` (real PM sync + real tail) | `origin/main`: full tail: Node deps, TUI + web builds, 58 skills synced, "Update complete!", **25.0 s** (minutes on Windows) | dependencies only, **6.7 s**, no tail |
| Same, then a marker armed after the stamp (same-commit update died) | previous head `c3b46e5`: **0.3 s**, marker cleared, tail never runs (M1) | "finishing an interrupted source update…", full tail, **21.0 s**, marker cleared |
| Same, then a marker armed before a fresh stamp (preserved home) | `origin/main`: tail runs again | **0.8 s**, marker cleared, no tail |
| Unstamped blessed root + pending marker, tail fails twice | (new invariant) | adoption stamps `adoptedAt`, tail still runs on both launches (red without the adoption fix) |
| Windows hand-off, update prints banner then parks silent past a 3 s ceiling (`windows-latest`, real `windows.ps1`) | `origin/main` + the PR's test (scratch branch): **exit 124**, update reported failed ([run 36938077040](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/36938077040)) | PR tree `dea1e0c` + the test step (scratch branch): **exit 0**, `gateway start --all` ran, receipt `ok` ([run 36967263416](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/36967263416), 10/10) |
| …banner followed by `✗ <unit> failed to come back after restart` / `Update incomplete — …` / stall mid-update | 124 | 124 (unchanged) |

Unit tests: the M1 marker-age case and the edited-tree case fail on the previous head and pass here.

Linux: `tests/hermes_cli/` + `tests/scripts/`, ruff, Windows-footgun and `/tmp` checks are clean, and attribution is mapped.

Not in scope: `hermes update` at an unchanged commit still rebuilds the desktop app (the #130729 follow-up); this PR changes launch, not the update command.

- @Finn763: #123863 (cherry-picked with authorship) and the hoisting review on #127198.
- @OutThisLife: #127198 (cherry-picked with authorship).
- @Enough1122: the adoption blocker on #123863.
- @unsupportedpastels: review of this PR (same-commit failed tail, post-banner failure lines, dirty tree).
- @salch-cred: #96221 raised the Rust retry gate; dropped here as unreachable on current main.

Fixes #123314. Fixes #96205.

The Desktop YouTube embed host answers a malformed request path with a 404 instead of throwing an uncaught `TypeError: Invalid URL` in the main process.

Follow-up to #130975 (loopback YouTube player host).

## Change

- `apps/desktop/electron/embed-host.ts::youtubeWrapperFor` now rejects targets `URL` can't parse (`//`, `//[`) and returns `null`, so the request handler sends a 404. Before, `new URL('//', origin)` threw inside the `http.createServer` callback. That surfaced as an uncaught main-process exception, which `crash-forensics` logs as a crash, and the socket was never answered. Any local process that can reach the port can trigger it, and the Host check runs first, so a correct Host header is all it takes.
- Test: `//` and `//[` are added to the existing "serves nothing" list, plus one live-listener request.

While testing #130909 for #130895 on native Windows, the ordinary-message timestamp test raised `OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument` for epoch `1.0`.

The timestamp itself is valid. In a timezone west of UTC, it falls on December 31, 1969 locally. Starting from an aware UTC datetime avoids the failing naive-local conversion and still renders the system's local time.

Review also identified the sibling failure for timezone-less ISO strings and existing bracketed prefixes. I reproduced it through the actual gateway history builder, including prefix cleanup with timestamp injection disabled.

### Changes
- Numeric formatting starts from aware UTC when `tz=None`.
- Successful string conversions keep their existing behavior. Only Windows naive-local `EINVAL` failures use a bounded `mktime` recovery for the first Unix day, checked by a localtime round trip and preserving microseconds.
- Platform conversion/range failures yield an unparsed timestamp or an omitted prefix instead of aborting replay. Message content and the existing metadata fallback are retained; this is not general negative-epoch rendering support.
- Added regressions for ISO/human prefixes, injection on/off, observed-group context, unsupported values, and existing timezone/DST behavior.

Only `gateway/message_timestamps.py` and its existing test file change. No dependencies, configuration, or prefix-regex changes. Explicit timezone interpretation remains unchanged. This does not replace #130909 or either compression fallback PR.

### Validation at `9b00fce8cceda8649a6ae5a6e4d1630a8c599a9e`
- Native Windows 11/Python 3.11.15, canonical runner: 56 passed across six focused files, including 36 timestamp cases.
- Negative control with the previous production code restored: 21 regression failures. Restoring the extension returned all 56 to passing.
- `scripts/ci/list_os_marked_tests.py windows` selects the file; canonical `-m platforms`: 22 passed.
- Native helper probes on Python 3.11.15 and 3.14.7 passed in system Central time, UTC, and UTC+8, including fractional epochs and modern DST fold/gap comparisons against the old implementation.
- Ruff and `git diff --check`: passed.
- The full repository suite was not run locally. Hosted CI still needs to run before merge.

Historical validation: the initial numeric fix was tested with #130909 and main (`7817bf522af`); the four focused suites passed all 28 tests, including its original epoch-1 fixture. That is not a claim that the new extension was retested with #130909.

Related to #130895 and #130909; this PR does not close the two-part issue.

`hermes status` now prints a one-screen summary by default; `hermes status --full` shows every section as before.

Salvage of #130857 by @PhoeniXAbhisheK (commit cherry-picked, authorship preserved), reworked on top to be the default and to read canonical sources.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                 ☤ Hermes Agent Status                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Model:        deepseek-v4.1-flash
  Provider:     OpenRouter
  Providers:    Nous Portal, OpenRouter, GitHub Copilot, Z.AI / GLM, ChatGPT or Codex Subscription, Anthropic
  Gateway:      ✗ stopped
  Platforms:    Telegram
  Jobs:         0

  Run 'hermes status --full' for every section
```

## Changes

- **Default is the summary**: model, active provider, connected providers, gateway, platforms, jobs. No key values are printed.
- **`--full`** prints the old full report; `--all` is an alias (it never changed the output before). `--deep` implies `--full`. Hermes Console keeps the full report since it accepts no flags.
- **Canonical sources, no re-derivation:**
  - Providers row = `list_authenticated_providers`, the list the `/model` picker offers (cached catalogs only, no custom-endpoint probes). Honours `model_catalog.excluded_providers`, credential pools and plugin providers for free.
  - Platforms row = `GatewayConfig.get_connected_platforms()`, the gateway's own decision about which adapters to start (it also rejects placeholder tokens).
- **Full Messaging Platforms section fixed**: plugin rows used `check_fn`, a passive "SDK importable" probe that returns True for every bundled plugin, so a fresh install showed Discord, Slack, Matrix, Teams, WhatsApp and ~9 more as `✓ configured` with no credentials. They now use the same gateway verdict as the summary.
- Docs: `cli-commands.md`, plus the pages that point at a full-only line (`Serves:`, `Manager:`, slot usage, Tool Gateway section) now say `hermes status --full`.

Compared with #130857's original +332/−13, this PR is +153/−43 against main. The contributor's 100-line registry walk is replaced by the picker call, 8 tests are cut to 2 invariants, and the nested fail-soft guards are reduced to one per summary row.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `hermes status` (real CLI, scratch home with OpenRouter/GLM/Telegram keys + placeholder `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`) | summary above; placeholder Discord omitted; 0 key values in output |
| `hermes status --full` / `--all` | 130 lines, every section; plugin rows marked configured: only Telegram (main: 14 with no tokens) |
| `hermes status --help` | `--full, --all` / `--deep (implies --full)` |
| Wall time, summary vs `--full` | 2.3 s vs 2.4 s |
| New tests on `origin/main` source | both FAIL (no summary; Discord plugin row `configured` via `check_fn`) |
| New tests on branch | pass |
| `test_status*`, `test_jobs_json_utf8_bom`, `test_status_report_contract`, `test_console_engine`, `test_estop`, `test_gateway_multiplex_served_record`, `test_status_bar_git_branch` | 67 passed |

Existing tests that exercise the full report now pass `full=True` instead of `all=False` (12 call sites, assertions unchanged), because the default output changed.

Root cause of the platform rows: `_render_platforms` asked `check_fn` (dependency probe) the question only `is_connected` / the gateway config can answer, the same mistake `hermes gateway setup` and gateway enablement already fixed (#31116).

Plugin authors now get one complete catalog submission guide whose rules are identical to the README reviewers enforce, and CI fails if the two ever drift.

Before this, the catalog page's "Submitting" section was a stale 5-point summary. It omitted rules 6–10, and it listed a "Released (real tags)" requirement that nothing enforces. Several criteria reviewers apply on every PR were written nowhere public.

## Changes

- **`plugin-catalog/README.md`**: rules 11–15 write down criteria reviewers already apply:
  - 11: credentials stay with their owner (vendor-login reads disclosed; OAuth refresh or impersonation needs a maintainer ruling)
  - 12: approvals and unattended runs are respected (no auto-approve, no YOLO-inheriting children, no hangs under cron or the gateway)

items.body:
## What

Normalize provider-minted tool-call ids **once, when the turn is minted**, if a turn has two or more parallel calls whose ids all start with a known provider prefix (`chatcmpl-tool-`). The new ids are deterministic (`call_` + sha256 prefix), and composite `call_id|response_item_id` halves are preserved.

Fixes #130363

## Why mint time only

The ids are rewritten in `validate_tool_calls`, and the final batch is re-checked after dedup, before the assistant message is built and before any tool runs. Both the stored assistant row and the tool results read their id from the same objects, so a call and its result always match. Nothing rewrites stored history, summaries, prefill or Responses replay. Earlier attempts that did rewrite at replay time each surfaced new call/result pairing regressions.

## Changes

- `normalize_provider_tool_call_ids` in `agent/message_sanitization.py`, called beside `_uniquify_tool_call_ids` in `agent/turn_tool_validation.py` (commit by @dskwe from #130366, cherry-picked with provenance).
- Decide eligibility by the effective id (stripped; a blank `call_id` falls back to `id`) and re-check the final batch after dedup/capping in `run_tool_round`, so a batch that only becomes all-provider after filtering is still normalized before it is staged.
- Rewrite the call half of `id` and `call_id` separately, so a composite `id` keeps its response-item half when `call_id` is bare.
- Write `call_id` through `provider_data` for the transport `ToolCall` type, where it is a read-only property, so Responses-transport batches don't raise `AttributeError` and `id`/`call_id` stay in agreement.
- Hash with `surrogatepass`, so a lone surrogate in a provider id neither crashes validation nor collapses two distinct ids onto one digest.
- Integration tests through real `validate_tool_calls` (with duplicate repair), `run_tool_round` filtering up to staging, assistant-row serialization and both transports (synthetic responses; tool results are built from the same call objects, no live provider):
  - an all-provider batch is rewritten to distinct, byte-stable ids that match their results;
  - single, mixed and ordinary batches are left untouched;
  - response-item halves survive for distinct and duplicate ids;
  - through `run_tool_round` to the Chat Completions wire: plain, padded, blank `call_id` and mixed-until-dedup batches never send all-`chatcmpl-tool-` ids, and results match their calls;
  - real `ResponsesApiTransport` and `ChatCompletionsTransport` output validates, with matching stored/result ids and preserved response-item ids;
  - surrogate ids don't crash and stay distinct.

## Not in scope

Sessions that are already wedged are not repaired. Their stored ids are unchanged, so they still need a new session or a one-time DB fix.

## Tests

29 related suites plus `tests/agent/transports`: 1125 passed on main. 1140 passed on this branch: the same 1125, plus 2 from @dskwe and 13 new. Ruff, the Windows footgun scan and the attribution audit are clean. There was no live provider probe; the provider behavior rests on @prasta1's bisect.

Thanks to @prasta1 for the precise bisect and the mint-time design, and to @dskwe for the implementation.

## Add Ando platform plugin

Connect a Hermes agent through Ando’s existing Invite members > Agent flow, using its own identity. The plugin receives authorized inbox work and Realtime wakeups, recovers context, and sends replies through Ando’s existing message tools. Durable execution claims prevent a competing receiver from taking over unfinished work.

This adds one community/platform entry maintained by Ando-Corporation, pinned to public commit `32d4c6bce36382b9f6367c0874784a57d671d99e`. The public repository is MIT licensed and has [v0.2.0-beta.5](https://github.com/Ando-Corporation/hermes-ando/releases/tag/v0.2.0-beta.5). It exports only the connector; no Ando monorepo history, credentials, or user data is included.

## Validation

- Clean isolated profile: installed the initial public beta through Hermes’s plugin manager, then upgraded through the plugin manager to the exact submitted SHA. Discovery and `hermes ando` CLI loading worked. The prior beta was live-tested; this authorization delta is tested against actual Hermes lifecycle APIs, not claimed as a fresh live model pilot. All 29 manifest hashes match. Upgrade preserved the private connection and delivery database.
- Current upstream validator at `be5e9f72c6`: all 14 plugin checks pass, including isolated registration, dependency declarations, security scan, and no core override; no warnings. `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` passes.
- 52 connector tests pass against Hermes `38d3dbce4adbb9074a34214eb330237a129e5904`, with actual Hermes session/background-turn contract tests. Coverage includes pagination, frozen uncertain-send retry, interrupted generation, identity isolation, invitation/reconnect failures, disabled tool preferences, claim conflicts and thread context.
- Live pilot in the user-selected Sara Tester Ando workspace, using only synthetic messages and actual `gpt-6.1-sol` generation: invitation redemption, offline startup request, idle DM, context followup, channel mention, original-thread reply, restart recovery, browser-closed operation, and durable claim conflicts for competing and legacy callers.
- The original beta posted a thread reply at channel level. This SHA fixes that boundary using the source message’s thread root and retains acknowledgement of inaccessible rows before source reads. Direct API readback confirms the corrected generated reply belongs to the original thread.

Sanitized live IDs: root `0c8321fa-eb98-411d-a977-17cfa89781cc`; corrected request `8a533fa3-6c23-4796-8068-b46b68050d2b`; corrected threaded reply `e16294b8-dd98-41b3-941b-2719675d618d`; final-beta threaded reply `50fe1bdf-6113-407b-aea0-d2e32ceddd73`; restart response `81e8cf24-455b-4c00-8d26-65d3620514bd`. No secret or private message dump is attached.

## Environment and limits

Runtime tested on macOS arm64, Python 3.14.7, mcp 2.0.0, httpx2 2.7.0, httpx 0.28.1, websockets 15.0.1. Live MCP reports version 2.6.0 and deployed SHA `b75cf4b36863e3ff0e8545b4267604e25182042b`. Artifact source provenance is clean committed Ando `4146134159d2f95021f5fc034367a565a20f0d0f`, recorded with file hashes in release-manifest.json.

Linux is declared as supported but was not run in this pilot. This user-selected workspace pilot does not establish external-company customer validation. Expired/revoked credentials, multi-page live history, uncertain live sends, and interrupted live generation retain automated coverage or remain live release-matrix followups; they are not claimed as live-verified here. The original source routing fix merged. The authorization source fix is [Ando PR #14012](https://github.com/Ando-Corporation/ando/pull/14012); the [public export PR](https://github.com/Ando-Corporation/hermes-ando/pull/2) includes both corrections. Their review/CI is tracked separately. This is a beta admission request, not a production certification.

## Catalog review correction

Installer-only local sender authorization is now the invitation default, including existing profiles with no explicit list. `role_authorized` requires an explicit local grant; `ANDO_ALLOWED_USERS` and `ANDO_ALLOW_ALL_USERS` are registered. Explicit local widening and conversation restrictions are documented. Credential-mode normalization retains deduplication with private allowlists. Security regressions verify unknown agents never enter a host turn, unchecked sources do not delegate authorization, and explicit operator opt-ins work. The stale README publication status is fixed.

Healthy cron runs already executing in an isolated systemd scope can hold the restart after-turn wait for the full cap even though they survive the gateway restart.

Only restart wait accounting and scoped-worker bookkeeping; no timeout/config-key, subprocess launch, interruption or durable-delivery policy changes. Degraded workers remain awaited. Not in scope: embedded Kanban drain (#103961), stop-phase timeout budget (#129957).

## What does this PR do?

Bumps the `web-search-plus` catalog pin from `6751abc` (v4.3.1) to `c8a67fd` (v4.3.3).

This rebases #130204 onto current main: its base predates 811a1c01fc (disclosure line) and 00e17daa01 (v4.3.1 pin), which landed from main's side and caused the conflict. With the disclosure already on main, the remaining delta of the original PR is exactly this 2-line pin bump — the rebased entry file is byte-identical to the original PR's target state.

4.3.2 and 4.3.3 are security hardening releases: stricter extract URL validation, same-origin-only redirects in the HTTP client for provider API calls, response size limits, no provider error text passed to the model, and punycode conversion for internationalized hostnames.

## Related Issue

Rebases #130204 (original PR by @robbyczgw-cla, the plugin maintainer). No separate issue — this is a plugin-catalog pin bump.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/web-search-plus.yaml`: `sha` `6751abc…` → `c8a67fd…` (verified: the pinned sha is the exact commit of the upstream `v4.3.3` tag)
- `plugin-catalog/web-search-plus.yaml`: `version` `"4.3.1"` → `"4.3.3"` (cosmetic label; capabilities unchanged)

## How to Test

1. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` → OK: 350 file(s) valid (matches the CI structural gate's invocation)
2. `gh api repos/robbyczgw-cla/hermes-web-search-plus/git/ref/tags/v4.3.3` → `c8a67fd7ed7fb649355d918053069ce785e0b341`, identical to the pinned sha (pinned-source-validate reachability)
3. Upstream range v4.3.1...v4.3.3 touches `plugin.yaml` only to bump its own `version:` line — no manifest/schema change, so `hermes plugins validate` at the pinned commit keeps passing as it did for 4.3.1

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)

## What does this PR do?

Adds one catalog entry, `plugin-catalog/aichipmunk.yaml`.

[Pacific-Cloud-Solutions/hermes-plugins](https://github.com/Pacific-Cloud-Solutions/hermes-plugins)
(MIT) pairs this machine's Hermes bots with the **AI Chipmunk** mobile app, from inside Hermes
Desktop: pick a bot, get the host the phone can reach, the profile name, and that profile's
`API_SERVER_KEY` as a scannable code. It replaces the terminal-only `hermes bots pair` flow, which
could not ship to customers.

A bot *is* a Hermes profile. The plugin contributes three surfaces and **no tools or hooks**: a
`hermes aichipmunk` CLI command for headless users (`--json` for machine-readable output), a
desktop page with a sidebar row, ⌘K command and status chip, and a dashboard API at
`/api/plugins/aichipmunk/` (`GET /state`, `POST /pair`, `POST /use-tailscale`) that the desktop
page reads. No core files are touched, so an update cannot overwrite it.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| **repo** | [Pacific-Cloud-Solutions/hermes-plugins](https://github.com/Pacific-Cloud-Solutions/hermes-plugins) |
| **pinned sha** | `d565d7698a28f4364f819446e5f7ae2b67c57352` |
| **release** | tagged — `aichipmunk-v0.1.0` |
| **tier / category** | community / platform |
| **capabilities** | 0 tool(s), 0 hook(s), no requires_env |
| **platforms** | all |

Install name and manifest name match: `hermes plugins install aichipmunk` then
`hermes plugins enable aichipmunk`.

## Disclosures

- **It changes one setting and restarts one service.** The desktop page's *Use Tailscale* action
  runs `hermes -p <profile> config set platforms.api_server.host <address>` for the profile that
  owns the API server, then restarts that gateway. It never edits a config file directly, and it
  refuses without an explicit confirmation because the restart drains in-flight runs.
- **It reads a credential, and the pairing code is that credential.** `API_SERVER_KEY` is read
  from the target profile's own secret scope at pairing time, because the API server authenticates
  per profile (`/p/<profile>/`). It is rendered locally as a QR code and never transmitted by the
  plugin. The README states the consequence plainly: while the code is on screen, treat a
  screenshot of it like the key itself.
- **No egress of its own.** The only outbound calls are the ones it visibly needs: the `tailscale`
  CLI (`status`, `serve status`, `serve --bg`) and the `hermes` CLI for the config write and the
  gateway restart. No telemetry, no analytics, no third-party hosts, no update checks.
- **It reads the local Hermes tree**, at a fixed set of locations: profile directories, their
  `config.yaml`, their `.env` secret scope, and the API server's bind. There is no caller-supplied
  path and no arbitrary file reader.
- **The desktop half stays inside the plugin SDK.** `desktop/plugin.js` imports only
  `@hermes/plugin-sdk`, `react` and `react/jsx-runtime` — no prototype patching, no `eval`/`new
  Function`, no dynamic `import()`, no reaching into app internals. `hermes plugins validate`
  confirms this on the desktop-surface check.
- **No self-updater**, and no bundled third-party code. Updates reach users only as a SHA-bump PR
  plus `hermes plugins update aichipmunk`.
- **Tailscale is how the phone reaches these bots.** The API server stays on a loopback bind
  and `tailscale serve` carries that port onto the tailnet, so the phone must be signed in to the
  same tailnet as this machine. There is no second, local-network address: the plugin reports
  what the current setup actually allows rather than implying an address works.
- **It reports rather than guesses.** When the API server's bind and the `tailscale serve` handler
  disagree — which is the state that breaks a phone that used to connect — the page says so
  instead of offering an address that cannot answer. Every address it hands over is one it has
  probed or whose Serve handler it has verified.

## How to Test

1. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/aichipmunk.yaml` — `OK: 1 file(s) valid`.
2. Clone `https://github.com/Pacific-Cloud-Solutions/hermes-plugins` and check out `d565d7698a28f4364f819446e5f7ae2b67c57352`.
3. `hermes plugins validate` on that checkout — passed here (manifest, capability probe, security scan **safe**, declared tools match `register()`).

Verified locally before filing:

- Structural validator: `OK: 1 file(s) valid`
- `hermes plugins validate` on the pinned checkout: `Validation passed.` Security scan **safe**. Declared tools match `register()`.

## Related Issue

No issue. Catalog submissions are a PR that adds one entry file. I maintain
`Pacific-Cloud-Solutions/hermes-plugins`.

## Type of Change

- [ ]  🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x]  ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ]  🔒 Security fix
- [ ]  📝 Documentation update
- [ ]  ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ]  ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ]  🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/aichipmunk.yaml` — one new entry, pinned to `d565d7698a28f4364f819446e5f7ae2b67c57352`.

## Checklist

- [x]  I am the owner/maintainer of the submitted plugin repository
- [x]  The plugin repository is public and tagged — public, tagged `aichipmunk-v0.1.0` at the pinned commit
- [x]  The pinned SHA is reachable on `main`

## What does this PR do?

`hermes plugins update` refuses to move a pinned plugin and tells the user to run `hermes plugins install <source> --force --ref <new-commit>` (the docs say the same). That force reinstall published a bare clone over the plugin directory: git-ignored and untracked files (plugin state, a local config) were deleted, and tracked edits were lost with no copy. `update` on an unpinned plugin keeps exactly those files (#124261), so a pinned plugin had no update path that kept them.

Now, when `--force` replaces an install whose recorded source is the same as the new one, `_install_plugin_core` treats it as the update it is, using the same pieces `update` uses:

1. user files are carried into the staged tree with `_carry_user_files`, classified by `_local_changes` (untracked/ignored in a git checkout; the no-git rules for a subdirectory install);
2. edits to tracked files are copied to `~/.hermes/plugins-backup/<name>-<sha8>/` before publication, with a notice.

What stays the same: the new revision's tracked files win, plugin code is never resurrected from the old tree, a reinstall from a different source still starts clean, and callers that pass their own `before_swap` (`_reclone_plugin_update`) are untouched. `hermes plugins remove` + `install` remains the way to reset a plugin.

Builds on #122007 (landed via #124261), which made `update` keep the user's files; this is the same bug class on the reinstall path.

## Related Issue

Fixes #131126

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/plugins_cmd_install.py::_install_plugin_core`: a forced reinstall of the same recorded source carries user files and backs up tracked edits (reusing `_local_changes`, `_carry_user_files`, `_stash_local_files`). The `prior` record lookup moved up so both checks share it.
- `hermes_cli/subcommands/plugins.py`: `install --force` help no longer says it removes the existing plugin.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_install_ref.py`: one invariant test, three rows.
- Docs: `website/docs/user-guide/features/plugins.md`, the pinned-install paragraph that documents `--force --ref` now says what a forced reinstall keeps and how to reset a plugin. The zh-Hans mirror of that page has no pinned-install paragraph, so there is nothing to mirror.

Surfaces: every install path goes through `_install_plugin_core`, so this covers `hermes plugins install` (CLI), `install <catalog-name> --force --ref`, the dashboard/Desktop install (Pin to commit), TUI `plugins.manage`, and plugin packs.

## How to Test

`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_install_ref.py -k force_reinstall_of_the_same_source`

Real git, `file://` repos, real worker publication. `test_force_reinstall_of_the_same_source_keeps_the_users_files`: install, add a git-ignored `data/state.json`, an untracked `settings.local.yaml`, and an edit to tracked `marker.txt`; then force reinstall.

- `[pinned-new-ref]` (move the pin with `--force --ref`) and `[unpinned-reinstall]`: the new revision's `marker.txt` is live, both user files survive, and `plugins-backup/demo-*` holds the edited `marker.txt`.
  - Red on `main` (`5bba024d8d`): `data/state.json` does not exist (`assert False is True`), both rows.
- `[other-source]`: the same plugin name from another repository starts clean; nothing is carried or backed up.
  - Red with the source check removed: `data/state.json` is carried into the other plugin.
- Red with the backup step removed: `assert [] == ['edited']`.
- Green with the fix. Related files `test_plugin_install_ref.py test_plugins_cmd.py test_plugins_cmd_catalog.py test_plugin_update_transaction.py test_plugin_update_recovery.py`: 116 passed. `test_dashboard_plugin_routes_secret_scope.py test_plugin_catalog_known_issues.py test_plugin_dependency_consent.py test_plugin_install_manifest_version.py test_plugin_packs.py test_plugins_hub_perf_guard.py test_web_plugins_catalog.py tests/pm/test_install_default_closure.py tests/pm/test_install_extra.py tests/tools/test_plugin_guard.py tests/tui_gateway/test_plugins_manage_install.py tests/tui_gateway/test_plugins_manage_late_activation.py`: 131 passed. Ruff clean. Python 3.14.

## Notes for review

- Same fail-closed rules as `update`: a user-owned symlink in a git checkout's untracked set, or a file whose path became a directory in the new revision, stops the reinstall before publication with the existing message, and the installed plugin is left as it was. Before this change `--force` replaced the tree regardless; `remove` + `install` still does.
- Carried files are merged before the security scan, so the one scan admits the final tree (the `before_swap` contract).
- The backup is written just before publication; if publication then fails, the live plugin is unchanged and the copy is left behind (same as `update`).
- A subdirectory (no-git) install carries user-state files with the no-git rules, but tracked-edit backup needs git. Our open #126774 adds the revision-compare backup for no-git updates; it touches other functions and does not conflict.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass. I ran only the related files listed above via `scripts/run_tests.sh`, not the full suite.
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

## Compared with #132309

#132309 (opened 2026-10-03) changes the same function for the same issue with the same helpers (`_local_changes`, `_carry_user_files`, `_stash_local_files`). Read side by side at its head `023ee83e91`:

| | this PR | #132309 |
|---|---|---|
| Same-source `--force` carries untracked/ignored files | yes | yes |
| Tracked edits copied to `plugins-backup/` | yes, just before publication | yes, before the manifest-pinned check and the security scan, so a refused or rejected reinstall still writes a backup copy |
| Symlinked plugin directory | left to the existing replace path (`not target.is_symlink()`) | treated as a same-source update (`target.exists()`) |
| Notice to the user about the backup | console line naming the backup path | `logger.warning` only |
| Regression test | one invariant test, three rows (pin move, unpinned reinstall, other source starts clean), red on `main` | none |
| `install --force` help text, plugins.md | updated | unchanged |

No case covered there is missing here, so nothing was ported.

## Summary

Updates the existing Nerve community plugin catalog entry from **v0.3.0** to the new stable **v0.3.1** maintenance release.

- bumps the exact release pin from `b9e78dd5e00cf1117c563cada4d563a56f66e609` to `3de7d94982b7a2cb87c829e4b2366ced927d8fed`
- updates the catalog version label from `0.3.0` to `0.3.1`
- leaves the declared tool/hook capability surface unchanged

## Nerve v0.3.1

This stable maintenance/hardening release includes:

- configuration and context-engine correctness fixes
- multiplexed-gateway / profile-secret context propagation hardening
- stale Definition-of-Done re-evaluation against current workspace state
- deterministic retry-loop suppression while preserving transient retries
- task-relative progress and environment-thrash recovery hardening
- conservative Shared Context setup behavior: OFF by default until HermesContextBus has a public distribution path
- public-source path hygiene
- the opt-in ask-only Action Gate mode, where BLOCK verdicts escalate to human approval rather than becoming classifier-owned hard stops, together with action-specific approval-key and registration hardening

## Release verification

The published `v0.3.1` tag resolves exactly to:

`3de7d94982b7a2cb87c829e4b2366ced927d8fed`

Release:
https://github.com/keeltrace/hermes-nerve/releases/tag/v0.3.1

The release is published as stable/non-prerelease. The catalog pin therefore points at the exact reviewed and qualified release commit rather than a moving branch.

## Scope

This is intentionally a catalog-only update. It does **not** include Nerve's separate 0.3.2 feature tracks such as Deep Research Kit, block-review judge, or public HermesContextBus packaging.

## Attribution

Nerve v0.3.1's published release notes preserve contributor attribution, including work and reports from @jcrabapple, @colibrishin, @omarabdo516, and @HiroKws, alongside maintainer integration/release engineering.

## AI assistance disclosure

AI coding/review agents assisted with parts of Nerve's implementation, validation, and release workflow. Human-visible issue/PR authorship is preserved in the upstream release attribution.

Right-clicking inside a Desktop pane now opens the menu for what you clicked (Paste in the composer, Copy on selected text, Copy URL on links, image actions on images) instead of the tab-strip zone menu. Empty pane space keeps the zone menu and gains New session / Settings / Update Hermes.

Salvage of #129402 by @unsupportedpastels, which builds on #127999 by Yuan Li (@dskwe). All four contributor commits are cherry-picked with authorship intact. One small cleanup commit is ours.

Fixes #127313
Fixes #127997

## Changes

- `app-context-menu.tsx`: only the pane-body wrapper (`data-zone-body`) counts as a fallback menu. Explicit Radix menus on rows, tabs and the status bar still own the whole gesture. Inside a pane, a text selection claims the gesture only when it intersects the clicked element, so a stale selection elsewhere can't take over the zone menu. (@unsupportedpastels, on top of @dskwe's edit-target ordering)
- `tree-group.tsx` + new `shell-menu-items.tsx`: the pane-body zone menu adds New session / Settings / Update Hermes, using the same items and labels as the app-chrome fallback. Tab menus are unchanged.
- Our commit: `shellSections` calls `renderActionItem` directly. The old code declared an `Item` component inside the render function, which created a new component type and remounted the rows on every render. The `tree-group.tsx` file doc comment goes back above its imports.

Root cause: ad2d4822e1 made the whole pane body a Radix context-menu trigger, and `AppContextMenu` returned early for any trigger before it resolved editables, links, images or selections.

## Validation

| Check | Before (origin/main) | After (this branch) |
|---|---|---|
| Live Electron (built app, mock backend, real right-clicks): empty composer | zone menu (Reload / Close… / Hide tabs) | Cut / Copy / Paste / Select all |
| Live: selected transcript reply | zone menu | Copy |
| Live: empty pane space, no selection | zone menu | zone menu + New session / Settings / Update Hermes |
| Live: empty pane space with a selection elsewhere | zone menu | zone menu + app commands (selection doesn't take over) |
| Live: tab right-click | tab menu | tab menu |
| vitest (context-menu, tree-group, actions-menu, statusbar, session-actions, starmap) | new invariant tests red (2 failed) | 71/71 passed |
| `npm run typecheck`, eslint on touched files, windows-footguns, attribution audit | | clean |

Not covered: packaged Electron on native Windows/macOS, and the OS clipboard itself. The live pass ran headless Electron on Linux. Clipboard execution in the renderer is a separate mechanism (#127752 / #128347), still open.

## Credit

- #127999 by Yuan Li (@dskwe): edit targets take priority over pane menus, plus the original regression test (cherry-picked).
- #129402 by @unsupportedpastels: ownership scoping, the selection-intersection rule, the pane fallback app commands, and the React/Radix ownership tests (cherry-picked).
- #127324 (@dskwe), #127333 (@salch-cred / @creditlabsonarc-rgb) and #129399 (@herovivian-collab) worked on the same regression and pointed out the clicked-target containment requirement.

On the messaging gateway, `/fast` and `/fast ultrafast` now check the route the session's next turn will actually use. A session `/model` pick (e.g. GPT-6 Astra on the ChatGPT subscription) is no longer rejected because of the config default model.

Fixes #118761. Salvages #65028 (@Willhong) with authorship kept. Supersedes #11165 (@Junass1), #116559 (@HelpMePleasepls) and #118763 (@KoNit-K). Credit to @GodsBoy for the rebased diagnosis, which showed that #128307's Ultrafast gate reads the default too.

## Changes
- `gateway/slash_commands_model.py::_handle_fast_command` resolves the session route through `_resolve_session_agent_runtime`, the same resolver the turn uses (session `/model` override, channel override, a persisted override rehydrated after a restart). It then gates both Priority and Ultrafast with `resolve_fast_mode_overrides(model, provider=, base_url=)`, the turn's own gate in `_resolve_turn_agent_config`.
- The source is normalized with `_normalize_source_for_session_key`, as `/model` and `/reasoning` already do (#30479). The session tier override now lands under the key the next turn reads, so it isn't dropped on Telegram DM topics.
- Route resolution runs off the event loop because it can refresh an OAuth token, just like the turn does. If there is no usable route at all, the configured model is judged on its own, as before.

## Behaviour
| Default (anthropic) | Session `/model` | Command | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| claude-sonnet-4-6 | gpt-6-astra @ openai-codex | `/fast status` | "only available for OpenAI models…" | status shown |
| claude-sonnet-4-6 | gpt-6-astra @ openai-codex | `/fast ultrafast` | "only available for OpenAI models…" | ULTRAFAST (this session only) |
| claude-opus-5-5 | gpt-6-astra @ openai-codex | `/fast ultrafast` | "Ultrafast is only available for GPT-6 Astra (current model: claude-opus-5-5)" | ULTRAFAST |
| claude-opus-5-5 | openai/gpt-5.4 @ openrouter | `/fast fast` | accepted "FAST", but the turn never sends it | refused |
| either | none (control) | `/fast status`, `/fast ultrafast` | unchanged | unchanged |
| claude-sonnet-4-6 | Astra, gateway restarted, no turn yet | `/fast status` | refused | status shown (persisted override rehydrated) |

**Live repro:** a real `python -m gateway.run` with a fake platform plugin (tests/e2e chaos harness) in a throwaway HERMES_HOME, with fake Anthropic/OpenRouter keys and a fake far-future Codex JWT. There was no inference; every message is `/model` or `/fast`. Every row above was observed on origin/main and then on this branch.

**Tests:** two invariants on the real fast-mode tables. (1) Both gate directions, plus the turn's `request_overrides` carrying the accepted tier. (2) The tier override is stored under the topic-recovered key. 3/3 red on origin/main; with only the salvaged commit, 2 are still red (proxy route, topic key). `tests/gateway/` passes in full.

## Not changed
- The CLI `/fast` already reads the live agent's model. The TUI/Desktop path (`tui_gateway/server.py::_fast_tier_applies`) is already route-aware.
- A session `/fast` tier stays in memory across a gateway restart, as it did before.

## What does this PR do?

Adds a catalog entry for **sidebar-cycle**, a Desktop-only plugin that steps through the left sidebar's session rows **in on-screen order**, one row per key press, wrapping from the last row to the first (and back).

- Shortcuts: `Ctrl+Cmd+]` / `Ctrl+Cmd+[` (rebindable in Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts as *Next/Previous sidebar session (wraps)*)
- `requires_hermes: '>=0.21.5'`; category `desktop`; no Python half, tools, hooks, middleware or env vars

Why it exists: the built-in `session.next` / `session.prev` walk sessions by recency and open the switcher HUD on repeated presses while Ctrl is held. This plugin follows the sidebar exactly as laid out (pins, date groups, manual drag order, filters).

## Hermes surfaces used

Only `@hermes/plugin-sdk`:

- `SESSION_ROW_AREAS.leading` — a zero-size marker per session row; walking the markers in document order gives the sidebar's render order
- `host.state.focusedStoredSessionId` — the current session
- `host.openSession(id)` — navigation
- `KEYBINDS_AREA` — the two rebindable actions

It does not query, click or restyle the app's own markup. The one `document.querySelectorAll` call selects the plugin's own `data-sidebar-cycle-id` markers. For the virtualized Recents list it calls `scrollIntoView` on its own marker to render more rows before deciding to wrap.

## Disclosures

None: no network calls, no reads outside the renderer, no shell commands, no background processes, no stored credentials, no telemetry.

No screenshots: the plugin adds no visible UI (keybinds only).

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

- `plugin-catalog/sidebar-cycle.yaml` (new entry, the only file in this PR)

## How to Test

1. `hermes plugins validate <checkout at the pinned sha>` → `Validation passed` (`desktop surface — stays inside the plugin SDK surface`)
2. `python scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/sidebar-cycle.yaml` → `OK: 1 file(s) valid`
3. Install, enable, reload desktop plugins, then press `Ctrl+Cmd+]` / `Ctrl+Cmd+[` in the sidebar: it moves one row at a time, crosses the pinned/Recents sections and wraps at both ends, including on a long, virtualized Recents list.
