items.body:
Opted-in `-900k` models on a custom `codex_responses` endpoint are now capped by that endpoint's own catalog `max_context_window`. A Codex catalog probe that finds nothing is no longer repeated on every context resolution.

This follows up on andrexibiza's review of #128288 (thread r4147463985). #116329 (teknium1) kept that route probe-free; #121751 later made gateway catalogs reachable but did not update this caller.

Changes:
- **Negative cache.** A probe that finds no catalog (endpoint down, non-200, or a body without a Codex catalog) is remembered for 300s instead of being retried on every resolution (agent init, `/status`, aux routing, `@`-reference turns). Each miss could cost two GETs with a (5, 10)s timeout.
  - The tuple shape is unchanged: the entry is stamped so the existing TTL check expires it.
  - It never overwrites a fresh catalog stored by a concurrent probe.
  - The max cache is left alone, so an observed cap survives an outage (#130686).
  - A refreshed token is a new fingerprint and probes immediately.
- **Route cap.** For an opted-in `-900k` variant, the custom route asks its own catalog, at its own URL and with its own key, for `max_context_window`, and caps the static bump with it.
  - The proxy's `context_window` is still never trusted.
  - Plain slugs make no request.
  - The slug lookup is the same exact-then-case-insensitive match the native path uses, now a module-level helper.

Validation:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Local HTTP stub, Codex-shaped catalog (`max_context_window` 600000) | `-900k` → 600000 with 1 GET to the stub; base slug → 272000 with no GET |
| Local HTTP stub, OpenAI-shaped `/models`, 3 resolutions | 900000 (no cap available), 2 GETs in total (both client_version URLs once) |
| Mutations | cap removed → 900000 ≠ 600000; negative cache removed → 6 GETs instead of ≤ 2 |
| Related test files (model_metadata*, codex models/headers/host binding, gpt6 tiers, astra, read-dedup) | no failures beyond those already failing on main |
| Review | hermes-pr-review 2c + three simplify-code reviewers, two rounds |

Known cost: a hung custom gateway can take up to about 30s on the first `-900k` resolution, then once per 5 minutes. These are the same timeouts as the native probe, and the chat traffic goes to that gateway anyway.

GPT-family sessions whose toolset has no terminal/execute_code/read_file/search_files are no longer told to use those tools, so they stop refusing plain arithmetic as "prohibited mental computation".

Salvage of #106548 by @chelsealong (authorship preserved), rebased onto current main. Fixes #106506.

## Changes
- `agent/prompt_builder.py::execution_guidance_text(valid_tool_names)`: each `<mandatory_tool_use>` / `<act_dont_ask>` line that names terminal, execute_code, read_file or search_files is dropped when none of its tools are in the session's toolset. `None` (toolset unknown) and a full toolset return the guidance byte-identical to today.
- `agent/system_prompt.py`: passes `agent.valid_tool_names`. The toolset is fixed per session, so the system prompt stays cache-stable.
- The web_search filtering in the original PR is gone: main's guidance no longer names a web tool (#39797).

Root cause: `OPENAI_MODEL_EXECUTION_GUIDANCE` was injected unconditionally and its docstring called it "toolset-neutral", but six lines name specific local tools.

items.body:
A single `invalid_encrypted_content` rejection on the Responses/Codex route no longer turns encrypted-reasoning replay off for the rest of the session: the stale blobs are stripped once and reasoning minted afterwards keeps carrying across turns. A route that does trip the kill switch no longer takes it along to the next route after a `/model` switch, fallback or primary restore.

Includes a salvage of #61552 by @necoweb3 (authorship preserved, reapplied on current main).

## Changes
- `agent/turn_recovery.py::_recover_stale_codex_reasoning`: the first rejection strips stale `codex_reasoning_items` and keeps replay on. A repeat rejection (the route cannot round-trip its own fresh blobs) disables replay for the session, same as main does today on the first.
- The strip now also applies to `api_messages`, the copy the retry is rebuilt from. Main's kill switch hid that this copy still carried the rejected blob, so the retry would have resent it.
- `run_agent.py::_disable_codex_reasoning_replay(keep_replay=...)` and `_codex_reasoning_replay_rejected` session state in `agent/agent_init.py`.
- `agent/turn_recovery.py::reset_codex_reasoning_replay`, called at the three route changes: `switch_model` (`_resolve_switch_destination`), `try_activate_fallback`, `restore_primary_runtime`. Both flags join `_SWITCH_SNAPSHOT_FIELDS` so a failed switch rolls them back (#61552).
- Docs: `developer-guide/provider-runtime.md` recovery bullet.

Root cause: the recovery treated "this blob is stale" (a rotated sealing key, a resumed session after a re-login) as "this route can never replay", and set a session-wide kill switch that nothing re-enabled.

## Validation
Live loopback probe: a real `AIAgent` (`codex_responses`, custom base_url) drives 3 user turns against a `/v1/responses` stub that seals blobs to a key epoch and honours `include`.

| Scenario | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Key rotates once (req 3) | 1×400, then every later request `include=false`, 0 blobs replayed (turns 2–3 lose continuity) | 1×400, retry clean, then requests replay 1→2→3→4 fresh blobs with `include` on |
| Route rejects every replay | 1×400, replay off | 2×400, replay off (bounded: one extra request) |
| Route A rejects every replay, then `/model` switch to healthy route B | B: 5/5 requests `include=false`, 0 blobs | B: `include` on, replays 1→2→3 fresh blobs |

| Tests | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `test_codex_token_expired_replay_recovery::test_token_expired_strips_cached_reasoning_once_before_the_credential_path` | fail | pass |
| e2e `test_openai_responses::test_rejected_encrypted_replay_is_stripped_and_primary_retried[http_400]` (real hermes process, fake Responses server) | fail | pass |
| `test_primary_runtime_restore::test_reasoning_replay_verdict_does_not_follow_the_session_to_another_route` (fallback activation + restore) | fail | pass |
| test files touching turn_recovery / codex_reasoning_items / session state / switch_model / fallback / restore + `tests/e2e/core/providers/` | — | 193 files, 4472 passed, 0 failed |

Changed existing assertions: the 401 test previously asserted `_codex_reasoning_replay_enabled is False` after the FIRST strip. That assertion encoded the behaviour this PR changes; it now asserts replay stays on after the first strip and turns off after a second rejection in a later turn. The e2e case gains a fourth scripted response so the retry's fresh blob must replay on the next call. The test's fake agent also forwards `**kwargs` to the real `_disable_codex_reasoning_replay`.

Related: #119336 / #119344 report the same session-wide strip on a third-party Responses relay and propose a durable per-issuer deny list. This PR goes the other way: a rotated key is recoverable, and only a route that rejects its own fresh blobs loses replay.

items.body:
Catalog admission now refuses plugins that replace Hermes core or Desktop internals at runtime, so two listed plugins can no longer silently break each other by patching the same seam.

Policy (Teknium): a listed plugin extends Hermes only through public surfaces (hooks, middleware, provider profiles and the other `register_*` APIs, Desktop SDK slots and routes). If the hook it needs is missing, the author asks for the seam.

## Changes

- **New `no core override` check** (`hermes_cli/plugin_validate_core_override.py`, wired into `validate_plugin_dir` after the security scan). It does a static taint pass over the code Hermes actually loads: the import closure of `__init__.py` and `dashboard/*.py`.
  - **Core values:** Hermes modules (plus `hermes_plugins.*`) and attribute chains off them. They are reached by import, `importlib.import_module` / `sys.modules` lookups (literal, module constant, or f-string head), `getattr`, iteration, or a plugin helper that returns one, including through an import alias.
  - **Rebinds:**
    - attribute assignment or deletion on a core value;
    - `setattr` / `delattr`;
    - writes into `sys.modules` or a core module's tables;
    - `mock.patch` outside tests;
    - passing a core value to a helper that `setattr`s its parameter.
  - **Not judged:** tests, benchmarks and CI/smoke scripts outside the import closure.
- **Desktop lint: new `app DOM reach` rule.** It flags document-level queries of the app's own `data-slot` / `data-tour` / `data-sidebar` / `data-testid` markup, and `document.body` childList/subtree MutationObservers, used to restyle, hide, click or rewrite core UI. Element-scoped queries inside the plugin's own subtree still pass.
- **Desktop lint bug fixed.** The comment stripper did not skip string literals, so any string holding `/*` (a glob like `'**/*.md'`) opened a fake comment. That blinded every rule up to the next `*/`, and vault-view evaded the lint this way. Strings are now matched first and kept.
- **Docs:** README rule 9, the plugin-catalog user guide and the plugin developer guide's compatibility contract.

## Validation

Every pinned tree on disk was checked: the 121 entries in open catalog PRs, the 349 listed catalog entries (one repo returns 404), and humalike. That is 466 trees, with zero crashes.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Python trees flagged | 0 | 17 (hand-verified, all real rebinds) |
| Desktop trees with new findings | n/a | 7 (hand-verified) |
| Previously reported Desktop findings that disappear | n/a | 0 |
| Benchmark/CI-script false positives (cashew, hermes-lcm-x, yantrikdb, …) | n/a | 0 after scoping to the import closure |

Flagged in open PRs: model-picker (`AIAgent._replace_primary_openai_client`), codex-account-switch (`tui_gateway.server` request handler), hermes-zh (34 gateway/CLI rebinds), clinepass (`list_providers`, `_PROVIDER_MODELS`), humalike, plus the Desktop entries t3-code-theme, provider-status and vault-view. All of them already carry a request-changes review citing this policy.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds `plugin-catalog/hermes-dreaming.yaml`: a community, skill-only entry for
[itpartypattaya/hermes-dreaming](https://github.com/itpartypattaya/hermes-dreaming), submitted by the repository
owner.

`hermes-dreaming` is nightly, deterministic memory consolidation in the spirit of OpenClaw dreaming. A stdlib Python
pass corroborates candidate facts with human messages on distinct days, scores them, matches them against
`MEMORY.md` / `USER.md` (duplicates, conflicting numbers, stale entries), quarantines secrets and prompt-injection, and
hands the agent a compact JSON only when there is work — a memory file close to its char limit counts as work, since
the limit gates writes silently. The agent applies the few proposals through the regular `memory` tool (at most six
changes a night, `replace` only with a verbatim anchor the script provides) and reports in a few lines. Every item
gets an outcome: written, rejected (a reject list matched by text), or quiet for a cooldown that starts only when the
agent actually answered. Fact sources: the holographic store, a SQLite or JSONL export, or none.

It is complementary to the existing memory entries: it is not a memory provider and registers nothing; it reviews
what the built-in memory and the holographic store already hold. No catalog entry mentions dreaming or nightly
consolidation of built-in memory. Several open core PRs propose a native dreaming plugin (#64281, #9225); this
entry changes nothing in core and can coexist with or give way to such a plugin.

## Package

Portable Agent Plugins v1 package at the repository root: `plugin.json` + `skills/dreaming/` (`SKILL.md`, `scripts/`,
`references/`, `examples/`). No Python is imported by the loader. The primary install is the plugin itself
(`hermes plugins install itpartypattaya/hermes-dreaming && hermes plugins enable hermes-dreaming`): the cron jobs
are bound to the plugin's own skill and both gates run the plugin's copy of `dream.py`, so the jobs execute exactly
the catalog-pinned code. Hermes runs cron scripts only from `~/.hermes/scripts/`, so `scripts/install.py` copies the
two pre-check gates there (and `--check` verifies the copies later); this is the one manual step. Nothing in the
package modifies Hermes core.

### Changes after review (2.1.0)

- **No core patching:** `scripts/patch_cron_memory.py` and the core-patch section of `references/cron-memory.md` are
  removed (the README line and its tests with them). The skill requires Hermes ≥ 0.21, where cron sessions get memory
  natively; `install.py --check` only reads `cron/scheduler.py` to tell an older core apart and suggests upgrading.
- **Jobs run the reviewed copy:** `install_cron.py` no longer requires a separate `hermes skills install`. It binds the
  jobs to the plugin's own skill and both gates prefer `plugins/hermes-dreaming/skills/dreaming/scripts/dream.py` over
  any `skills/*/dreaming`. One detail: on 0.21.5 and current `main` a portable plugin's skill is registered as
  `agent-plugin-<slug>-<sha256(key)[:8]>:dreaming` (`hermes_cli/plugins_manifest.py` `_portable_skill_namespace`), so
  `hermes-dreaming:dreaming` does not resolve through `skill_view`. The installer therefore reads the qualified name
  from the plugin registry (`list_plugin_skill_metadata` + `find_plugin_skill` under `plugins/hermes-dreaming/`)
  instead of hard-coding it — checked in an isolated `HERMES_HOME` (in-process, no CLI install):
  `agent-plugin-hermes-dreaming-7bb971ab:dreaming` → `skill_view` success. A regular skill install is used only when
  the plugin is absent.
- **`allow_memory` dropped** from the installer and the examples.

### Follow-up (2.1.1)

A second-opinion review of 2.1.0 turned up the upgrade path and a few edges, fixed before re-review:

- **Existing jobs are checked, not silently kept.** A job that loads another skill than this install
  provides (a 2.0 job on a regular `dreaming`, or a plugin reinstalled under another name) is now an
  error with a hint; `install_cron.py --rebind` updates its skill in place. (`--force` only ever added
  a second job.) `install.py --check` reads `cron/jobs.json` and reports the same, which also catches a
  plugin disabled or removed after the jobs were created.
- **The plugin's skill is matched by its exact `SKILL.md`**, not by any file under the plugin
  directory; two registered names for it, or a registry the current interpreter cannot import, are
  reported as such.
- **The gates hand their home to `dream.py`** (`--hermes-home` for the nightly pass, a re-pointed
  module for extraction), so a gate installed into a non-default home without `HERMES_HOME` no longer
  reads `~/.hermes`. Done without writing `os.environ`: `skills_guard` stays **safe** with the same two
  informational findings as before (`allowed_tools_field`, `python_subprocess`).
- Tests now run the real registry lookup against a stand-in registry instead of replacing the function
  under test.

## Disclosure

- **Network:** none.
- **LLM calls:** none from the scripts. The only model turn is the agent in the user's own cron session.
- **Reads:** `~/.hermes/state.db` (sessions and messages, `mode=ro`), the fact store (`mode=ro`, or a JSONL file),
  `memories/MEMORY.md` and `USER.md`.
- **Writes (scripts):** `~/.hermes/cache/dream*.json` (cooldowns, reject list, loss-guard snapshot, extraction
  cursor; 0600) and `~/.hermes/memories/DREAMS.md` (diary). `install.py` additionally copies two gates into
  `~/.hermes/scripts/` and seeds `~/.hermes/dreaming.json` if absent.
- **Writes (agent):** memory entries through the `memory` tool; in the optional extraction job, candidate facts
  through `fact_store`. Nothing is ever deleted from the fact store.
- **Processes:** the nightly gate runs `dream.py` with the same interpreter (argument list, no shell, 600 s timeout).
- **Capabilities:** no tools, hooks, middleware, slash commands or env vars. No credentials are read.
- **Updates:** no self-updater; new versions arrive only through a SHA-bump PR.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/hermes-dreaming.yaml` — new entry, pinned to `dd43dfb0fa5ff80a82c4b5ec340bfbcd5a0f3a71`, category `memory`, tier `community`.

## How to Test

1. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/hermes-dreaming.yaml` → `OK`.
2. Clone the repo at the pinned SHA and run `hermes plugins validate <dir>` → portable manifest OK, security scan
   **safe**, validation passed. The portable loader lists the skill `dreaming`; `skills_guard` on
   `skills/dreaming` (community source) → safe, install allowed.
3. `hermes plugins install itpartypattaya/hermes-dreaming && hermes plugins enable hermes-dreaming`, then
   `python3 ~/.hermes/plugins/hermes-dreaming/skills/dreaming/scripts/install.py --check` and
   `install_cron.py --dry-run` — the planned jobs name the plugin's skill.
4. `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` in the repo — 255 stdlib tests, synthetic data, no network.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this entry
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` — N/A, catalog entry only; the plugin's own tests pass
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Debian 12 (Hermes 0.21.5) and Windows 10 (tests)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Relevant documentation — the plugin's README renders at the pinned SHA
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered — stdlib only; the installer is Python, not shell

## For New Skills

- [x] SKILL.md follows the standard format (`description` ≤ 60 chars, When to Use → Verification)
- [x] No external dependencies (stdlib only)
- [x] End-to-end on Hermes 0.21.5 (Debian 12): `hermes chat -q "Use the dreaming skill to show what tonight's memory dream would propose. Read only: do not change memory, the fact store or any state files." -t skills,terminal`, skill not preloaded, run against a live install with 75 facts (regular-skill install, version 2.0.0 — the pass itself is unchanged in 2.1.0). The agent called `skill_view("dreaming")`, ran `python3 <skill_dir>/scripts/dream.py --dry-run` through `terminal` (`${HERMES_SKILL_DIR}` resolved) and answered correctly (75 facts, 235 human messages, nothing to propose, memory 59 % / 64 % full). Two tool calls, 20 s; checksums of the memory files and of the state files were identical before and after.

Note: `tools/skill_linter.py` reports one advisory finding — `metadata.hermes.{tags, related_skills}` is missing.
This is deliberate: Agent Plugins v1 requires `metadata` to be a flat string map, so a nested `metadata.hermes`
block would make the portable loader skip the skill. Tags are declared at the top level, which Hermes also reads.

The skill has run nightly in production since June 2026 on a family assistant (Hermes 0.18 → 0.21.5).

## Screenshots / Logs

![banner](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/itpartypattaya/hermes-dreaming/dd43dfb0fa5ff80a82c4b5ec340bfbcd5a0f3a71/docs/banner.png)

```text
✓ portable manifest — plugin.json parses (Agent Plugins v1)
✓ manifest fields — name present
✓ security scan — safe

Validation passed.
```

This reverts three Desktop PRs from Oct 1 that regressed upgraded users. Remote backends connect again, renderer settings (theme, layout, composer model…) come back, stock users keep the Nous theme, and preview tabs behave as before.

## What's reverted and why

- **#127201** (restore YouTube embeds): it moved the packaged renderer from `file://` to `http://127.0.0.1:47891`, which caused two problems.
  - Remote backends bound to a specific IP (including the Tailscale setup in `desktop.md`) now refuse the renderer WebSocket with 4403 `origin_mismatch`. Reported in #130277, #130535, #130710, #130730.
  - localStorage is per-origin and nothing migrated it, so every upgraded user lost all renderer settings (#130635). Reverting puts the renderer back on the `file://` origin, where pre-upgrade settings still live.
  - Commits reverted: `d428df2a65f`, `9abeb829df5`, `587e673e2a2`.
- **#130015** (classic default skin): un-retiring `default` repaints stock users Classic gold on gateway connect, because the stock config is `display.skin: "default"`, and the gold is cached for later launches. Commits reverted: `743d3a4119e`, `d753222ee79`, `c356d1df829`, `ac6079b3293`, `aeff051a182`.
- **#128552** (scope preview tabs per session): four regressions, each reproduced with a probe.
  - The strip's "+" Browser tab is invisible and gets adopted by the wrong session.
  - On restore, every Browser tab collapses to one, which breaks pop-out.
  - An agent `preview.open` from a tile lands in the focused session's drawer.
  - Tabs disappear after auto-compression.
  - Commits reverted: `b3e896246f8`, `824e107cb72`, `310c7ae9e55`, `cb9cb968eed`, `572e4f4fad3`.

## How

- `git revert` of each PR's commits, newest first, on `origin/main`.
- Conflicts were all formatting churn from `973b27f5c82` (`npm run fix` on merge) except one hunk in `main.ts::createWindow`. All were resolved to the pre-PR side, and Prettier is clean on every touched file.
- After the revert, every file these PRs touched is byte-identical to its pre-PR state, except:
  - `electron/main.ts`: keeps later unrelated commits (`986192cd1d8`, `3ae62879c32`, `4d2dfe52617`, `65db662577a`/`0bc5d9688b5`).
  - `use-session-actions/index.ts`: keeps #128547's branch-retry commits.
  - `session-states.ts`: keeps #130300's steer guard.
  - `i18n/{en,ja,zh}.ts`: keeps the approval-copy lines, which #130826 reverts separately.
- No conflict with #130826 (`git merge-tree` clean).

- When an author ships a compliant version, drop their file from this PR and land their SHA bump instead.

SMS, email and both WeCom adapters now deliver long replies and oversized cron output in full, instead of failing (SMS), cutting it at 4000 chars with a footer that points to a file on the gateway host (email, WeCom), or silently dropping the tail (WeCom).

This finishes the class #130727 fixed for the relay: the router only hands the full payload to adapters that declare `splits_long_messages`, and these four adapters didn't.

## Changes

- **SMS:** `send()` called `truncate_message()` without a limit, so it chunked at the 4096 default. Twilio rejects any `Body` over 1600 chars (code 21617), so every reply over 1600 chars failed outright, not just cron output. It now chunks at `MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH` (1600) and declares `splits_long_messages`. `sms.md` already promised 1600-char splitting; now that's true.
- **Email:** one email carries the whole body, so the adapter declares `splits_long_messages`. Cron output arrives as a single complete email.
- **WeCom AI Bot:** `send()` queues one markdown message per 4000-char chunk, so each chunk draws its own token from the adapter's 30 msgs/min per-chat bucket (errcode 846607). Every chunk goes on the cached reply `req_id`, the same as every other send in that chat (group chats cannot send proactively, errcode 600039). `_send_inner` is unchanged.
- **WeCom callback (self-built app):** `message/send` keeps only the first **2048 bytes** of `text.content` and drops the rest ([vendor docs](https://developer.work.weixin.qq.com/document/path/90236): 最长不超过2048个字节，超过将截断). The old code sliced at 2048 *chars*, so CJK replies lost everything past about 680 characters. It now chunks by UTF-8 bytes at 2048.
- Both WeCom paths stop at the first failed chunk and return its error, matching SMS and every other chunking adapter.
- Docs: `wecom.md` and `wecom-callback.md` (en + zh-Hans) now describe the per-message limits and splitting.

## Independent review: two findings, both fixed here

The integration review reproduced two failures on `fc4f658a`. Both are class bugs that predate this PR, but this PR made them routine, so they are fixed here as separate commits:

- **A split send that fails partway was re-sent whole.** The new chunk loops returned a plain failure after earlier chunks had landed, so `_send_with_retry` retried or sent the 3500-char plain-text fallback and reported success: the head arrived twice and the tail never did. The three loops now share `gateway.platforms.helpers.send_chunks()`, which sets the existing `partial_overflow` contract (the one Telegram and Discord already use). On the cron path, the router used to raise a bare `RuntimeError` that dropped it, and the live lane then re-sent the whole payload through the standalone sender. That affected Telegram and Discord partials on main too. The router now raises `PartialDeliveryError` and the live lane records `delivered N of M chunks, then failed` instead of falling back.
- **A cron send that outlasted the 60s wait was killed partway and re-sent.** `_live_send_text` used `future.cancel()` to mean "never started", but a `run_coroutine_threadsafe` future stays PENDING until done, so `cancel()` returns True mid-send and cancels it (probed directly: `cancel() -> True`, log `['started', 'cancelled mid-flight']`). A paced 55-chunk WeCom payload arrived as 25 chunks and was reported failed. The send now records its own start under a lock and is abandoned only when it never began.

`tests/cron/test_scheduler.py::TestDeliverResultTimeoutCancelsFuture` is **rewritten**: it faked "in flight" with a mocked `cancel()` returning False, which is exactly the assumption that does not hold. It now drives a real event loop and keeps its contract (an in-flight timeout produces no duplicate), plus the wedged-loop case it never covered (a send that never started falls back to standalone and never goes out late).

| Reviewer's probe (real `_live_send_text`, real router and adapters, real clock and token bucket) | `fc4f658a` | this head |
|---|---|---|
| 55-chunk WeCom cron payload | 25 chunks, reported failed, standalone fallback | in flight at 60s; **all 55 delivered by 120s, each once**, no fallback |
| SMS, chunk 3 gets a 503, via `_send_with_retry` | success; paragraph 0 twice; tail missing | honest failure; paragraph 0 once; nothing re-sent |
| WeCom callback, same | success; paragraph 0 twice | honest failure; paragraph 0 once |
| WeCom AI Bot, same | success; paragraph 0 twice | honest failure; paragraph 0 once |

Each new test fails against the PR's previous head and passes here. The scheduler A/B gave the old file only the now-configurable timeout so the guard itself is what is measured: the in-flight and partial tests are red, and the wedged-loop control is green on both.

## Validation

**Live repro:** the real `DeliveryRouter.deliver()` and real adapter `send()` with a 33,538-char cron payload (35,778 bytes, CJK mixed in). SMS and the WeCom callback go over real HTTP to local stubs enforcing the vendor behaviour (Twilio 400/21617 above 1600 chars; WeCom keeps 2048 bytes). Email and the WeCom AI Bot are captured at the SMTP message / WS frame boundary.

| Target | `origin/main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| SMS | delivery **fails**: Twilio 400, *body exceeds the 1600 character limit* | 23 messages, max 1469 chars, last section delivered |
| WeCom callback | 1 message, 1908 chars; tail and footer gone | 18 messages, every one ≤ 2048 bytes (pure-CJK 6,000 chars: 9 chunks, max 2040 bytes) |
| Email | 4,000 chars + `[truncated, full output saved to <gateway path>]` | 1 email, 33,538 chars |
| WeCom AI Bot | 4,000 chars + footer | 9 reply frames on the cached req_id, max 3976 chars |

**Regression pass:**

- Short messages: wire output on all four adapters is **byte-identical to `origin/main`** (markdown stripping on SMS, threading headers on email, an empty WeCom send).
- SMS: when Twilio rejects chunk 3 of a 12,000-char reply, the send stops there and returns Twilio's error. Nothing after chunk 3 is sent, and the cron lane gets a failure it can report.
- WeCom callback: a stale access token on chunk 1 (40001) is refreshed once and every chunk is delivered.
- WeCom AI Bot: a code fence split across chunks is closed and reopened with its language tag. With the bucket cut to 3 tokens, chunks 4 to 6 wait for the next window and all six deliver. On the first version of this PR, 4 chunks drew 1 token; the WeCom test now asserts one token per chunk and was red on that head.
- Email: a 120,000-char body goes out as one email, still threaded (`In-Reply-To`, `Re:` subject).
- `splits_long_messages` has one reader (`DeliveryRouter._cap_oversized_output`). The standalone cron/`send_message` path already chunks by the registry `max_message_length` before calling these senders.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway tests/cron tests/tools tests/plugins tests/e2e/core/delivery`: **22,040 passed** across 2,029 files. 4 failures in unrelated files are identical with the adapter files reverted to `origin/main` (missing optional extras and a host-only worktree shim), and they pass on this PR's CI.

- 4 new tests, one per adapter, each through `DeliveryRouter._cap_oversized_output` → `send()`. All four are red on `origin/main` (source files swapped back) and green here.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` on every test file referencing these adapters, plus `tests/e2e/core/delivery/` and `tests/plugins/`: **2249 passed, 0 failed** (169 files).
- ruff, windows-footgun and no-tmp checks clean; `audit_pr_attribution.py` clean.

**Not covered:** table-aware splitting. `truncate_message` is fence-aware but can split inside a markdown table, and WeCom then renders the continuation rows as literal pipes (#107443's AWS section). That applies to every chunking adapter, so it belongs in the shared splitter as its own change. A partial send now stops with an honest failure instead of duplicating, but it does not resume the undelivered tail; resuming is #124295's scope.

## Credit

Slim redo of the community fixes for this cluster. Every author is a `Co-authored-by` on the commit for their adapter:

- SMS: @PhilipAD (#46972, the earliest; the 1600 cap), @jackjin1997 (#62752, the flag), @euisuh (#67734), @Froraut (#128062)
- Email: @petrakersten (#53264, the earliest), @liuhao1024 (#62000)
- WeCom: @luyao618 (#19751, the earliest), @briandevans (#19811), @LeonSGP43 (#20006), @TaoMasterCoder (#94835, both adapters and the #107443 report)

Fixes #62751, fixes #61990, fixes #19689, fixes #107443.

![SMS, email and WeCom deliver long output without truncation](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aacac31/DtjjFYKBMhHXP3BLEafLN_hZtuJlIf.png)

## What does this PR do?

Adds the official [Linkup](https://www.linkup.so) plugin to the plugin catalog as a community entry, pinned to the full commit SHA of release [v1.0.0](https://github.com/LinkupPlatform/linkup-hermes-plugin/releases/tag/v1.0.0) (`6a1909656b96f5e951bb6a332ea252501f4fb686`).

Submitted by the plugin's author, a member of the Linkup team. The repository lives in the [LinkupPlatform](https://github.com/LinkupPlatform) org.

The plugin provides:

- **Tools:** `linkup_search` (live, cited web search at `flash`/`fast`/`standard`/`deep` depths, with sourced-answer and structured output), `linkup_fetch` (URL to Markdown, JS rendering, PDFs), and `linkup_research` / `linkup_research_status` (async deep research).
- **A `linkup` web backend** for the built-in `web_search` / `web_extract`.
- **A `/linkup` slash command, a `hermes linkup` CLI, and two bundled skills.**

It needs `LINKUP_API_KEY`, has no Python dependencies (standard library only), and has no self-updater.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (catalog entry only; no Hermes code changes)

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/linkup.yaml`: the new entry. Capabilities match what the plugin registers at the pinned commit.
- `contributors/emails/shaurya@linkup.so`: maps the commit author email to `shauryajain21` for the Contributor Attribution Check.

## How to Test

1. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/`: passes (351 files valid).
2. Clone `https://github.com/LinkupPlatform/linkup-hermes-plugin` at the pinned SHA and run `hermes plugins validate --install-deps .`: all checks pass, security scan `safe`, no symlinks, and the SHA is reachable from `main`.
3. `hermes plugins install LinkupPlatform/linkup-hermes-plugin --enable` on a clean `HERMES_HOME`: installs and runs a live search.

Also verified with end-to-end agent sessions on Hermes v0.21.5 (macOS), with Claude as the model:

- search with citations
- full-page fetch of a 270k-character page
- Linkup as the `web_search` / `web_extract` backend
- a complete `linkup_research` → `linkup_research_status` run

The plugin repo's own CI runs unit tests on Python 3.11–3.14 plus `hermes plugins validate` and `doctor`.

## Checklist

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide (third-party integrations ship as standalone plugins)
- [x] Commit message follows Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched existing PRs; this isn't a duplicate
- [x] This PR contains only the catalog entry and the contributor email mapping
- [x] Tested on macOS 26
- [x] Documentation: N/A (the README at the pinned SHA documents install, tools, settings, and commands)

`hermes -w`, kanban and subagent worktrees, and the delegation recovery hint work again in repositories whose own git config carries an `includeIf`, such as actions/checkout checkouts, without letting a repository-defined filter run.

#130661 hardened every automatic git call against repo-controlled clean/smudge/process filters. It refused any repo with a repo-local `includeIf`, because a conditional include can match at spawn time (`onbranch:` on the new branch, `gitdir:.git/worktrees/` during `worktree add`) when it didn't at discovery. actions/checkout writes exactly such includes for its credential helper, so inside CI checkouts Hermes stopped making worktrees: `hermes -w` failed with "could not read the repository's filter config".

## Changes
- `hermes_cli/_subprocess_compat.py::noninteractive_repo_git_env`:
  - One discovery probe (`--includes --show-origin -z`) lists the filter keys and the include paths with their origin file.
  - Every `includeIf` target is read directly with `git config --file`, whatever its condition, and the filter commands it defines are neutralized next to the others.
  - Relative origins are resolved against the worktree top level (git prints them that way); relative include paths against the file that names them, as git does.
  - Still refused: an include nested inside an include target, a non-regular target (FIFO, device, directory), more than 16 targets, a non-file origin, or a probe that fails. A missing target is skipped, as git skips it. Targets are read once each.
- `tests/security/test_gitspawn_config_injection.py`: the `onbranch:` and `gitdir:worktrees` include rows now expect the worktree to be created with the filter not firing; new rows for a nested include (refused), the actions/checkout credential include (allowed) and an include flood (refused); discovery from a subdirectory must match discovery from the top level.

## Validation
- Security test file + worktree, subagent worktree, kanban teardown and recovery-diagnostics tests: 87 passed, 6 skipped (Linux-only).
- Red on #130661's code: the `onbranch_include` and `gitdir_include` rows fail (repo refused). Mutation: skipping the target read lets the filter run during `worktree add` and un-refuses the nested include; resolving origins against cwd fails the subdirectory check; removing the target cap fails `include_flood`.
- Real-git probes on the real function: relative, absolute and `~/` paths, values with spaces and newlines, case variants, includes declared in an included file, symlinked targets, `hasconfig:` conditions and `process` filters are all neutralized; a FIFO target is refused in about 2 s rather than hanging.
- A repo built like an actions/checkout clone: refused before, hardened env returned after.

Cost: no extra spawn when a repo has no `includeIf`; one spawn per distinct include target plus one top-level lookup otherwise (two extra in the actions/checkout case).

Follow-up to #130661 (decision on its refusal trade-off).

items.body:
The WhatsApp Cloud adapter now ignores signed webhooks addressed to a different phone number or WhatsApp Business Account, so another number's messages on the same Meta app no longer reach this profile.

Closes #129851

**Behaviour change:** if `WHATSAPP_CLOUD_WABA_ID` is set, inbound webhooks are now filtered by it. A webhook whose `entry.id` does not equal the configured WABA ID gets HTTP 200 and is dropped. Before this change the docs and setup wizard called the field "analytics only" and nothing read it on inbound. Operators who put a different ID in that field (a Business-portfolio ID or the App ID) will stop receiving messages after upgrading. The dropped message logs a WARNING that shows the incoming and configured IDs, so the mismatch can be traced. If `WHATSAPP_CLOUD_WABA_ID` is unset, only the phone number ID is checked.

## What happened
`X-Hub-Signature-256` proves a webhook came from the Meta app, not that it belongs to this adapter. One app (and one WABA subscription) can serve several phone numbers. `_dispatch_payload` ingested every signed `messages` change without comparing `metadata.phone_number_id` or `entry.id` to the configured identity, so a sibling number's traffic was treated as this profile's inbound messages, media downloads included.

## Change
- `gateway/platforms/whatsapp_cloud.py`: new `_webhook_identity_matches(entry_id, metadata)`. `metadata.phone_number_id` must equal `WHATSAPP_CLOUD_PHONE_NUMBER_ID`, and `entry.id` must equal `WHATSAPP_CLOUD_WABA_ID` when that is set. `_dispatch_payload` runs the check after HMAC verification and before contact parsing, dedup, media download and `_ingest_message`. On a mismatch it skips the change. The log is a WARNING when the change carries messages and a DEBUG for status-only changes (sibling numbers' delivery receipts), and it lists the incoming and configured IDs. A non-dict `value` is skipped. The module docstring now says what `_WABA_ID` does.
- `hermes_cli/setup_whatsapp_cloud.py`: the WABA help text and the STEP 4 header now say that the WABA ID binds inbound webhooks. They no longer say "for analytics".
- `website/docs/reference/environment-variables.md`, `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/whatsapp-cloud.md`: `WHATSAPP_CLOUD_WABA_ID` rows rewritten to match.
- `tests/gateway/test_whatsapp_cloud.py`: one parametrized `TestWebhookDispatch::test_signed_webhook_bound_to_configured_identity` with 5 rows. Three rows (foreign WABA, foreign phone, both foreign) are dropped. Two rows (matching, WABA unset) are dispatched. All rows go through the real HMAC path. Existing fixtures were moved to the adapter's configured phone number ID, so the existing dispatch tests still cover the accept path.

## Credit
- @Froraut first submitted this fix in #129851 (draft) and wrote the identity gate, setup and docs wording, and the original tests. Their commit is cherry-picked with authorship kept: `fix(whatsapp): bind cloud webhooks to configured identity`.
- @sy0u1ti opened #129267 (2026-09-30) independently. It applies the same `phone_number_id` filter without the WABA check. This PR covers that behaviour (phone filter before dedup, media and interactive resolution).
- kshitijk4poor added two follow-up commits. The first puts incoming and configured IDs in the drop log, uses WARNING vs DEBUG, skips non-dict `value`, removes a dead branch and fixes the stale wizard header and docstring. The second folds the new tests into `TestWebhookDispatch` with the existing helpers.

## Verification
- `tests/gateway/test_whatsapp_cloud.py`, `tests/gateway/test_whatsapp_cloud_allowed_users.py`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_whatsapp_cloud_setup.py`: 71 passed on the rebased head.
- Red on base: with the pre-fix `whatsapp_cloud.py`, `TestWebhookDispatch` has 3 failures (the three foreign-identity rows) and 5 passes. With the fix it has 8 passes.
- Probe (signed payloads for (WABA, phone) = (W1,999), (W9,111), (W1,111), adapter configured W1/111): base ingests all three, head ingests only (W1,111). With no WABA configured, head ingests (W9,111) and (W1,111) and still drops phone 999.
- Mutation: putting back the contributor commit's parent version of `whatsapp_cloud.py` turns all foreign-identity cases red.
- Ruff F401/F811/F821, `git diff --check` and `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py` are clean on the touched files.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- #129267 (sy0u1ti) overlaps on the phone-number filter and was opened about a day before #129851. This PR keeps #129851's code because it also covers the WABA check. #129267 adds one more regression case: a foreign-recipient interactive tap must not consume this number's pending clarify prompt. This PR handles that case too, because the gate runs before `_ingest_message`, but the case is not pinned by a test here.
- The WARNING vs DEBUG log level has no test.

A webhook subscription update that races a delete or disable (CLI or dashboard) no longer restores the route. Moving a subscription to another profile now gives it a new HMAC secret, so senders using the old secret must be reconfigured.

Salvage of #129804 (no linked issue; #129804 is closed after merge).

## What happened
The CLI (`hermes webhook subscribe/remove`) and the dashboard `/api/webhooks` endpoints each loaded the whole `webhook_subscriptions.json`, edited a local copy and atomically replaced the file. The atomic replace prevented torn JSON, but nothing serialized the read/modify/write. A stale writer could therefore republish a route that a concurrent delete had removed, or re-enable one that a concurrent disable had turned off. Separately, `--route-profile` rebinding kept the existing secret, so a sender holding the old profile's secret could still authenticate events that now run under the new profile.

## Change
- `hermes_cli/webhook.py`:
  - All subscription mutations go through `_mutate_subscriptions`, which holds a per-store lock (a thread lock plus a cross-process file lock) for the full read/modify/write.
  - `_replace_subscription` compare-and-swaps a same-route update against the snapshot it was based on, so a concurrent delete or disable wins. It also owns the "explicit `enabled: false` survives a re-post" rule and returns the published route.
  - Rebinding a route to a different profile rotates the secret in the same atomic replacement. Explicitly passing the old secret on a rebind is rejected.
  - Reads (`_load_subscriptions`) are lock-free, because writers always publish via atomic rename. The dead `_save_subscriptions` / revision-snapshot helpers are removed.
- `hermes_cli/web_routers/ops.py`: dashboard create, delete and enable/disable use the same transaction helpers. Create builds its summary from the published route.
- `gateway/platforms/webhook.py`: `_reload_dynamic_routes` checks `(st_mtime_ns, st_size, st_ino)` instead of mtime alone, so an atomic same-size rewrite with a restored mtime is still picked up (new inode). It reads without the CLI writer lock, so a pre-auth POST never blocks on it. An unparseable or non-object file keeps the last good routes and is parsed once rather than on every POST. A transient read error is retried, and a missing file clears dynamic routes as before. Non-object route entries are skipped individually.
- `hermes_cli/subcommands/webhook.py`, `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/webhooks.md`: document secret rotation on rebind, the serialized mutations and the stat-gated reload.
- Tests: `tests/hermes_cli/test_webhook_cli.py` (stale update vs delete/disable, rebind rotates the secret without a mixed record, inode-only reload change, torn file keeps the last good routes, store file mode). `tests/hermes_cli/test_dashboard_admin_endpoints.py` (a disabled route stays disabled after re-POST).

## Credit
- @Froraut (FroRaut) wrote the core fix in #129804 and was the first to submit this shape (transactional mutations, CAS on stale updates, secret rotation on rebind, dashboard routed through the same boundary). Commit `fix(webhook): transact subscription mutations` was cherry-picked with authorship kept.
- @kshitijk4poor wrote 3 follow-up commits: the stat-gated, lock-free gateway reload that replaces the per-POST lock and hash, keep-last-good on unreadable files, lock-free CLI reads, moving the disable rule into the CAS helper, and two test pins.

## Verification
- Rebased head:
  - `test_webhook_cli.py`, `gateway/test_webhook_dynamic_routes.py`, `gateway/test_webhook_adapter.py`, `test_dashboard_admin_endpoints.py`: 109 passed.
  - `test_web_routers_destructive_profile_scope.py`, `gateway/test_webhook_integration.py`: 36 passed.
- Red on base: both kept CLI tests fail with the base production files. The dashboard re-POST test fails on base (`KeyError 'enabled'`).
- Probe:
  - Base: rebind keeps the old secret, and a stale update resurrects a deleted route.
  - Head: neither happens. Benign updates work on both.
  - Head also passes every reload-gate check: restored-mtime same-size swap detected, torn file keeps last good, non-object entry filtered, missing file clears, recreate loads.
- Mutation, each turning a kept test red:
  - Dropping `st_ino` from the stat key.
  - Removing the disable rule from `_replace_subscription`.
  - Using the PR-head gateway reload (lock + hash), which wipes routes on a torn file.
- ruff F401/F811/F821: no new hits. `git diff --check` is clean. The Windows footgun check is clean on the 4 touched source files. In the test files it reports 2 new ASCII-only `write_text` calls without `encoding=`, matching the existing style there.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- Behaviour change, kept on purpose: moving an existing webhook subscription to another profile (`--route-profile`) rotates its secret. Senders configured with the old secret will get 401 until they are updated with the new one, which `subscribe` prints. Passing a different `--secret` on the rebind sets an operator-chosen value instead. The alternative was to keep the secret unless asked to rotate. That would not break current senders, but it leaves the old profile's secret valid for the new profile, so rotation was kept.
- Overlapping open PRs, not closed by this one: #120964 (serializes registry writes, including plugin writers and desktop/web UI changes; wider scope), #129687 (same author; refuses to overwrite an unreadable store, so the CLI read-error path still returns `{}` here, as it does on main), #126420 (skips non-object routes; the gateway part overlaps the per-entry filter here).

items.body:
Revoking a paired Matrix user now takes effect immediately for invites and approval reactions, with no gateway restart. Discord's live allowlist is purged on revoke too.

Matrix invites and approval reactions now follow the same authorization as messages (MATRIX_ALLOW_ALL_USERS honored; GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS no longer overrides MATRIX_ALLOWED_USERS); revoke also purges Discord's live allowlist.

## What happened
Matrix invites and approval reactions were authorized against an allowlist snapshot taken when the adapter was built, not the gateway's live, profile-aware check. A paired user was never recognized there. A user whose ID had been mirrored into the snapshot kept passing after `hermes pairing revoke`, because the revoke purge did not touch `_allowed_user_ids` / `allowed_users`.

## Change
- `plugins/platforms/matrix/adapter.py`: `_is_authorized_user` asks the gateway's injected authorization callback when one is wired, and treats any non-`True` verdict as a deny. The construction-time snapshot remains only as the fallback for unwired adapters. This method gates `_on_invite`, startup invite replay and `_validate_matrix_prompt_reactor`. The callback applies its own `chat_type` default, so the call passes only `chat_id`.
- `gateway/pairing.py`: `_sync_live_adapter_allowlist_remove` also purges `_allowed_user_ids` and `extra["allowed_users"]`. Live `set` snapshots are updated in place, so objects holding a reference to the set lose the revoked user too: Discord's approval/component views and `VoiceReceiver`. Lists, strings and `None` are still rebound as before.
- `tests/gateway/test_pairing_allowlist_bypass.py`: adds two tests. The first checks that a revoked Matrix user is denied for messages and approval reactions on the same adapter instance. The second checks that the live snapshot, plus a held reference to it, loses the revoked user.

## Credit
- @Froraut wrote the fix and both tests in #129773. Their commit `fix(matrix): apply pairing revocations live` is cherry-picked with authorship kept.
- @kshitijk4poor added two follow-ups: the in-place set purge for objects that hold the set, and dropping the hardcoded `"group"` chat_type. The second also removes a tautological assertion and an unused fixture from the new test.

## Verification
- Head tests: test_pairing_allowlist_bypass, test_matrix_approval_reaction_fail_closed, test_matrix_pending_invite_auth, test_matrix_dm_invite_recording, test_matrix, gateway + hermes_cli test_pairing, test_matrix_exec_approval, test_adapter_authz_secret_scope, test_adapter_settings_scoped_precedence and test_adapter_connect_classification: 226 passed, 0 failed.
- Red on base: both new tests fail with the base `gateway/pairing.py` + `plugins/platforms/matrix/adapter.py`.
- Probe, run against the real `GatewayRunner._make_adapter_auth_check`, `PairingStore` and `MatrixAdapter._on_invite`:
  - Base: the paired user is denied by the adapter while the runner allows them, and the snapshot is stale after revoke.
  - Head: the paired user's DM and group invites are joined. After revoke the paired user is denied immediately, the owner is still allowed, and a stranger or empty sender stays denied.
  - DM and group verdicts match across 7 allowlist configurations.
- Mutation: reverting `gateway/pairing.py` reddens the snapshot-purge test. Reverting `plugins/platforms/matrix/adapter.py` reddens the live message/approval test. Reverting the in-place set update reddens the held-reference assertion.
- ruff F401/F811/F821 shows no new findings, `git diff --check` is clean, and check-windows-footguns is clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- Behaviour change for operators: `MATRIX_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true` now admits invites and reactions from anyone. `GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true` with a non-empty `MATRIX_ALLOWED_USERS` no longer admits unlisted inviters or reactors. Matrix messages were already gated this way.

It is unconfirmed whether the dashboard and the gateway share a process.

items.body:
Desktop no longer forwards configured remote-gateway headers (Authorization, Cloudflare Access, custom proxy secrets) to a redirect target outside that gateway's origin and path.

Salvages #129625 (GHSA-f9c2-hmjp-45jw). No linked issue.

## What happened
The default-session `onBeforeSendHeaders` listener only ever added the configured gateway headers. Chromium keeps app-set headers across redirects (it drops only `Cookie`), so a 3xx from inside the gateway's scope carried those secrets to whatever origin it pointed at (public counterpart of GHSA-f9c2-hmjp-45jw).

## Change
- `apps/desktop/electron/remote-ws-headers.ts`
  - `applyRemoteRequestHeaders` records, per webRequest `details.id`, the lower-cased header names it injected. When a later hop of the same request falls outside every configured scope, those names are removed. In-scope hops re-apply the configured values and drop differently-cased stale copies.
  - Requests that never received injected headers pass through unchanged, even if they carry the same header name and value (e.g. an IdP's own `Authorization`).
  - `attachRemoteRequestHeaderListener` clears the per-request entry on `webRequest.onCompleted` / `onErrorOccurred`. No other desktop code registers those hooks, so no existing listener is replaced.
- `apps/desktop/electron/remote-ws-headers.test.ts`: the existing scoped-headers test now covers redirect hops (off-host, same host outside the path, and a second gateway), unrelated requests with the same name and value, and reuse of an id after completion. Still one test.

## Credit
- @Froraut wrote the fix in #129625 (first submitter). Commit `13e0275f74` is a hand rebuild of their `e469a8ec71` with their authorship kept: the strip/re-apply logic and the unit test. Their live-Electron fixture and test (+222 lines) were left out.
- `49feaae4c4` (kshitijk4poor) on top: keys the strip on request id instead of on header values, so an unrelated request that happens to carry the same value is left alone, and adds the completion/error cleanup.

## Verification
- vitest `electron/remote-ws-headers.test.ts`: 7/7 passed on head. With origin/main's `remote-ws-headers.ts` it fails 1 of 7 (redirect hop keeps the headers).
- Probe (drives the real listener with request ids). On origin/main the off-host redirect, the same-host-outside-path redirect and the cross-gateway hop all keep `CF-Access-Client-Secret` / `Authorization`. On head all three drop them. Unrelated requests (other token, same value, no headers) are unchanged on both, and the other gateway still gets its own header.
- Mutation (gate rounds): the test fails if the strip is keyed by value (contributor's original approach, same-value unrelated request), if the `onCompleted` cleanup is removed, or if the source is reverted to before the fix.
- `git diff --check` clean. No Python touched.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- The request-id keying relies on Electron's documented contract that `details.id` stays the same across the redirect hops of one request. That is per the Electron docs and has not been confirmed in a live Electron run yet. If an id did change across a hop, the failure mode is a missed strip on that hop, i.e. the behaviour before this PR. Nothing else breaks, because untracked requests just get the old pass-through.
- Rebased over 47c3a6c5e8 (revert of the YouTube embed Referer composition). The listener is installed directly again, without the `withEmbedRefererStamp` wrapper, and the `id?` field the earlier revision added to `EmbedRequestDetails` was dropped because that type no longer exists.
- Known small gap: the `onErrorOccurred` cleanup is not covered by the test. If it were removed, failed or cancelled requests would leave a small entry in the per-session map.
- Not covered here: whether Chromium fires `onCompleted`/`onErrorOccurred` for WebSocket upgrades and for OAuth hops that end on a custom-scheme redirect. If it doesn't, the per-session map leaks slowly, one small set per injected request. The `mcp-oauth-callback-ipc.ts` redirect path was not audited.

## What was wrong

On the opt-in `codex_app_server` runtime, `turn/start` carried only the thread id and input. Hermes' reasoning effort and `/fast` never reached the codex thread: codex kept its own defaults whatever Hermes showed. Three users reproduced this on #65599.

## What changed

Salvage of #65599 by @agarg21 (opened 2026-07-16). Their commit keeps them as author. They were also first to forward the model on every turn; that part landed separately via #130735 (salvaged from the later #83269), so this PR carries the rest.

1. **Their change, adapted to current main:** `turn/start` now carries `effort` and `serviceTier` alongside the model.
2. **Effort is clamped to what the model accepts.** Hermes has levels the backend does not. Live on codex-cli 0.147 with ChatGPT auth, a raw `ultra` fails the turn with 400 "Unsupported value". The effort now goes through the Responses transport's `_resolve_reasoning` (`ultra` becomes `xhigh`, disabled reasoning becomes `none` where accepted). It is sent only when Hermes has an explicit reasoning setting; otherwise codex's own default applies.
   - **Ultra is codex's own mode where the model can take it** (from #130965 by @Froraut, co-author). Live on codex-cli 0.147, `effort: "ultra"` runs on gpt-5.6-sol and gpt-5.6-luna (their ladders reach `max`) and fails with 400 "'max' is not supported" on gpt-5.5. So `ultra` is sent verbatim to models whose ladder reaches `max`, and clamped as before everywhere else. A named custom provider and `provider: openai` keep the clamp, since only ChatGPT-subscription `openai-codex` was live-tested. The same rule drives the labels: Desktop's `reasoning_effort_wire` and the CLI/gateway `/reasoning` status show "ultra" there instead of "ultra (sends max on this route)".
3. **The tier is the one Hermes would request on its own Responses path, sent only when it changes.**
   - It comes from `fast_mode.effective_request_overrides(agent)`: a static `/fast` tier pinned per model and route, or an open `auto`/`cold` window. OpenAI's `priority` goes out as codex's `fast`. A tier codex has no word for (`ultrafast`) is not sent, and `auto`/`cold` are never sent as raw strings.
   - The session remembers what its thread last received. A new thread keeps codex's configured tier until Hermes selects one. A resumed thread is treated as unknown, so its first turn sends Hermes' tier even when that is a clearing null. This matters because CLI `/fast` rebuilds the agent, and `/fast off` has to reach a thread that still carries fast.
4. Docs row in the app-server runtime guide.
5. **Refactor from review:** the turn settings are resolved inside the turn's failure handler, so an error there still closes the session and offers the fallback. The effort clamp reuses `classify_responses_route`, and the codex tier names live in `fast_mode.CODEX_TIER_WORDS`.

## Behaviour now

Live E2E, real Codex login, `gpt-5.5`:

| Hermes setting | Sent on `turn/start` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Reasoning off | `effort: none` | 0 reasoning tokens |
| Effort `ultra` with `/fast` | `effort: xhigh`, `serviceTier: fast` | completes |
| Effort `ultra`, `gpt-5.6-sol` (real AIAgent → real app-server) | `effort: ultra` (main: no effort) | completes |
| Nothing set | neither field | codex default (26 reasoning tokens) |
| `/fast`, then resume, then `/fast off`, then another turn | `fast`, then `null`, then omitted | all complete |

## Tests

- 21 related test files: 409 passed. The 8 failures fail on main too. After the Ultra commit: 62 symbol-mapped files, every failure also fails on `origin/main`.
- Each follow-up has a test that fails when only that fix is reverted: the `ultra` clamp, sending the tier only on a change, and the null on a resumed thread.
- Reviewed with hermes-pr-review 2c and three separate simplify-code reviewers, in three rounds; the Ultra commit had its own 2c + simplify round and a re-gate.

Closes #65599.

items.body:
X and Instagram embeds in the desktop app now render in sandboxed cross-origin iframes, so the vendors' widget scripts no longer run in the window that holds the desktop preload bridge.

Closes #129637

## What happened
`social-embed.tsx` appended `platform.twitter.com/widgets.js` and `www.instagram.com/embed.js` to the main renderer document. That document exposes `window.hermesDesktop` (terminal, files, backend API), so anyone who served or intercepted those scripts could drive the bridge, including `terminal.start` / `terminal.write`. This is the public counterpart of advisory GHSA-5rwg-hf29-9hm8 (CWE-829).

## Change
- `embeds/social-embed.tsx`: rewritten. X loads `platform.twitter.com/embed/Tweet.html?id=…&theme=…&dnt=true` and Instagram loads its existing embed URL, each in an `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin">`. The frame is always cross-origin, so `allow-same-origin` grants nothing from the app. Top navigation, popups, forms and modals are dropped. Height follows `message` events only when `event.source` is that iframe's `contentWindow` and `event.origin` exactly matches the provider. `reportedHeight` reads only a finite positive number. Nothing is injected into the app document any more.
- `embeds/url-embed.tsx`: `SocialEmbedRenderer` is keyed by `descriptor.id`, so a reused slot starts at the new embed's default height instead of carrying over the previous one. The comment now describes the iframe path.
- `embeds/embed-size.ts`: new `EMBED_DEFAULT_H` (320). `social-embed.tsx`, `embed-consent.tsx` and `url-embed.tsx` use it in place of three copies of the literal.
- `embeds/escape-html.ts`: deleted (no importers left).
- `embeds/providers/instagram.ts`, `providers/types.ts`: comment updates only.
- `embeds/social-embed.test.tsx`: new file. It checks that X, Instagram post and Instagram reel each render a sandboxed iframe and add no `<script>` to the document. It also checks that height messages with a foreign origin or a foreign `source` are ignored, and that a valid one is applied.

## Credit
- @Froraut found and reported the issue and wrote the fix in #129637. Their commit `fix(desktop): render X and Instagram embeds in isolated iframes` is a hand rebuild of c863c8949f onto current main, with authorship kept. The only conflict was the `url-embed.tsx` comment, where main has since reverted the autoplay prop. Main's signature was kept.
- kshitijk4poor added three follow-up commits: the test trim, the positive control for the resize test, and the per-descriptor key with the shared default height.

## Verification
- vitest on the rebased head (private copy, root vitest): `social-embed.test.tsx` + `providers/detect.test.ts` gave 27/27 passed. The whole `embeds/` directory gave 5 files, 44/44 passed.
- Red on base: `social-embed.test.tsx` passes 0/4 on main's source, which injects `<script>` and renders no iframe.
- Probe, base vs head: on base, `widgets.js` / `embed.js` are injected into the app document. On head, no scripts are injected and the iframes are sandboxed. A message from a foreign origin leaves the height unchanged (320px / 450px), and valid messages resize to 613px / 777px. YouTube, TikTok and Spotify descriptors are identical on base and head.
- Mutations: reverting the contributor commit turns 4/4 tests red. Dropping the source check, the origin check or the sandbox attribute turns 1, 1 and 3 tests red. Removing the message listener turns 1 red (the positive control).
- `git diff --check` is clean on the rebased head. eslint and prettier were clean on the touched files in the fold round. No Python files are touched.
- Reviewed over 1 gate round plus a fold round (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- Resize protocol: X's embed iframe (`platform.twitter.com/embed/Tweet.html`, bundle `embed.Tweet.*.js`) posts `{"twttr.embed": {method: "twttr.private.<key>", params: [{...details}]}}` to `window.parent` with targetOrigin `"*"` and no handshake. I confirmed this by reading the current bundle. That is the shape `reportedHeight` parses for `twttr.private.resize`, and Instagram's `{"type":"MEASURE","details":{height}}` is handled the same way. A live Electron run was not possible. If X stops sending resize, tweets stay at the 320px placeholder; nothing breaks.
- The `key={descriptor.id}` remount has no dedicated test, because there is no `url-embed` test harness.
- The Instagram reel iframe has no `allow=` attribute (autoplay/encrypted-media), unlike `frame-embed.tsx`. No playback breakage has been observed.

items.body:
## What this changes

YouTube embeds play in the packaged Desktop app. YouTube refuses with error 153 unless the page embedding the player has an http(s) origin matching the player's `origin` param. The packaged renderer is a `file://` page, and modern Electron drops a stamped Referer header.

The renderer stays on `file://`. A loopback host in the main process (`electron/embed-host.ts`) serves one small wrapper page per video, and only that page gets the http origin: the chat iframes the wrapper, and the wrapper iframes the player. The host starts lazily on the first embed, on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port. It serves only `/youtube/<11-char id>` with numeric `start`/`rel`/`modestbranding`, answers only its own Host header, and sends `default-src 'none'; frame-src https://www.youtube-nocookie.com`.

This replaces [#127201](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/127201), which moved the whole renderer onto loopback and was reverted in [#130852](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/130852): settings reset on update and remote backends rejected the new origin. With only the embed moving, neither can happen.

## Side effects

- **Existing state:** none. The renderer origin, localStorage, settings and backend connections are untouched.
- **Version skew:** a new renderer bundle on an older main process has no `getEmbedHostOrigin`, so it embeds directly as it does today. An old renderer never calls the new handler.
- **Dev and web renderers:** they already have an http origin and keep the direct embed. Covered by the component test.
- **Failure:** if the host can't start, the embed falls back to today's direct iframe.
- **Rewritten assertions:** none.

## Test plan

- [x] Real Electron 40.10.2 running the production `embed-host` module, with a `file://` page against live YouTube, on `M7lc1UVf-VE` and `9MVqxnIb98Y` (the reporter's video):
  - Direct iframe, as on `main` today: "Video player configuration error" (153).
  - Through the host: **playing**. Player state 1, with the clock advancing to 2.1s and 2.2s.
- [x] `npx vitest run src/components/assistant-ui/embeds electron/embed-host.test.ts electron/embed-referer.test.ts`: 50 passed.
- [x] `npx tsc -p . --noEmit` and `npx tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json --noEmit`: clean. ESLint and Prettier on the touched files: clean.
- [ ] Packaged build on macOS, Windows and Linux: a pasted YouTube link plays inline.

Fixes #106596

Thanks @pitalgoras for the Electron 40 packaged-build findings in #127201 (Referer mutation is inert; YouTube needs an http origin plus a matching `origin` param), which pointed here.

items.body:
Desktop users can now pick the Classic Hermes gold-on-navy look in Settings › Appearance, and a stock install (`display.skin: default`) still paints Nous: Classic only appears when someone picks it.

Re-lands #130015 (reverted in #130852). Fixes #76579. Credit to @686f6c61 for the original feature (#76743); this commit carries their `Co-authored-by`.

## What changed

- **`classic` built-in theme** (`apps/desktop/src/themes/presets.ts`), labelled **Classic Hermes**. The palette goes through the same `skinToDesktopTheme` converter a backend skin takes, using the CLI `default` skin colors (`hermes_cli/skin_engine.py`), so it paints the same colors as the reverted PR. As a built-in it resolves on the very first frame, works offline, and shows in the grid whatever skin the gateway reports.
- **`default` stays retired → Nous** for boot, backend sync and `setTheme`. That was the reverted PR's mistake: it un-retired and registered `default`, and because stock config ships `display.skin: default`, every user without a pick was repainted gold on gateway connect, and the gold was cached.
- **`/skin` aliases** (`use-skin-command.ts`): `gold` and `hermes` → `classic`, since those names only ever meant the gold look. `default` → `nous`, unchanged: it is the stock config value, and Desktop reads "default" as the Desktop default everywhere else. Typing `/skin classic` or `/skin classic hermes` also works.
- **Write-back:** none. Desktop never writes a theme pick to `display.skin` (the renderer has no `config.set` path for skins), so a Classic pick stays Desktop-local like every other Desktop theme. The CLI/TUI skin keeps its own setting.
- **Stale cache from the reverted build is purged.** The #130015 build cached the CLI `default` skin as "Classic Hermes" under `hermes-desktop-backend-themes-v1`, which would have shown a second, broken Classic card. `backend-sync.ts::readCached` now drops every retired name (`default`, `gold`, `nous-light`; `RETIRED_SKINS` moved to `presets.ts` so the store and the provider share it) as well as built-in names, and writes the cleaned map back on first launch. `ingestBackendSkin` uses the same rule, so it never registers a retired name.
- **Classic follows light/dark.** Light uses the CLI `default` skin's `light_colors` ladder (`#F5F5F5` surface, goldenrod accent, which the converter's AA pass deepens to `#825d02`), with one change: the ink is a deeper brown, `#2B2109`. The CLI's `#5C4718` left Desktop's 74% secondary text at 4.2:1 and its 54% tertiary text at 2.7:1. With the deeper ink they are 6.5:1 and 3.5:1, which matches Nous Light; body text is 12.3:1. Dark is unchanged gold on navy (body 14.2:1, tertiary 5.5:1).
- **Docs** (`website/docs/user-guide/features/skins.md`, new "On the Desktop app" section): on Desktop, `default` and `/skin default` mean Nous, and a CLI/TUI or config switch to `default` moves a Desktop pick back to Nous. The gold look is the separate `classic` theme (`/skin classic`, `gold`, `hermes`). `classic` is a reserved Desktop theme name, like `mono` and `slate`.
- The description now reads "Gold on navy, the CLI's original look", and the `as DesktopTheme` cast is gone.
- No test that exists on main was edited or deleted. `never registers default in the backend store` is unchanged and passes. One test added by this PR, "a Classic pick paints gold/navy", now sets dark mode explicitly, because Classic has a light variant.

## Invariants

| # | Invariant | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | A stock user with no pick, and `display.skin` set to `default` or unset, gets Nous on first boot, after connect/reconnect, and after a relaunch | `classic-skin.test.tsx` "a stock user (…) paints Nous…" (both cases). Green on base, and **red against the reverted #130015 code** (`Expected "nous" / Received "default"`). The existing `never registers default…` test is unchanged and green. Live: probe states `s1_firstBoot`, `s1_relaunch` and `s1_unset` are all `painted: nous` with `localSkin: default` |
| S2 | An explicit Classic pick paints gold/navy and survives connect, reconnect and relaunch | `classic-skin.test.tsx` "a Classic pick paints gold/navy…": red on base (no `classic` theme), green on head. Live: `s2_afterPick` / `s2_relaunch` = `painted: classic`, `--theme-background-seed: #1a1a2e`, `--theme-primary: #ffbf00`, `display.skin` still `default` |
| S3 | Picking Nous after Classic works and persists | Same test, last step. Live: `s3_afterNousPick` / `s3_relaunch` = `painted: nous`, stored `nous` |
| S4 | CLI/TUI skin behaviour unchanged | No Python, `ui-tui` or skin-engine changes. The diff is limited to `apps/desktop/src/themes/` |
| S5 | `/skin` aliases resolve sensibly | `classic-skin.test.tsx` "/skin gold and /skin hermes select Classic; /skin default stays … Nous": red on base, green on head |
| S6 | Custom and forked backend skins register and apply as on main | All existing `backend-sync.test.ts` and `context.test.tsx` cases pass unchanged (themes dir: 11 files / 129 tests). One edge, now documented: a user skin file named exactly `classic` follows the same rule as `mono`/`slate`. The Desktop palette wins and its `customCSS` still applies |
| S7 | A Desktop that ran the reverted #130015 build shows exactly ONE Classic Hermes card and one `/skin list` row, and the stale `default` entry is removed from storage | `classic-skin.test.tsx` "a cache left by the reverted #130015 build…", seeded with that build's exact cache shape: **red on the previous head 2a226d0b547** (`expected ['classic','default'] to deeply equal ['classic']`), green now. Live, same seed: before the fix there were 2 Classic cards and the cache kept `default`; after, 1 card and the cache was `[]` on boot |
| S8 | Classic in Light mode paints a light surface, and both modes stay readable | `classic-skin.test.tsx` "Classic follows the light/dark toggle…" checks fg/bg ≥ 4.5 and accent/sidebar ≥ 4.5 in each mode: red on 2a226d0b547 (light mode rendered `dark`), green now. Live: Light gives `mode: light`, bg `#f5f5f5`, fg `#2b2109`, primary `#825d02`. Dark gives bg `#1a1a2e`, fg `#fff8dc`, primary `#ffbf00`. Before the fix, Light painted navy (`mode: dark`) |

## Live evidence

Built the desktop (`npm run build`) and drove it with a throwaway Playwright spec on `e2e/fixtures.ts` (`createSandbox` + `launchDesktop`). The sandbox `HERMES_HOME` was configured with a mock provider and `display.skin: default`; `HERMES_*`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` and `XDG_SESSION_TYPE` were unset. Flow: first boot → relaunch → pick Classic in Appearance › Theme → relaunch → pick Nous → relaunch, plus a second sandbox with no `display.skin`. Every step was checked after the gateway reported ready. All seven assertions passed; screenshots show Nous before the pick and gold-on-navy chrome after it and after the relaunch. The spec was deleted before commit.

Review-fix pass (head de19c1e45e7). Same harness, but the renderer runs with `--ozone-platform=headless` and the sandbox has `display.skin: default`. Launch 1 seeds the #130015 cache shape (`{default: {label: 'Classic Hermes', …}}`) into localStorage. Launch 2 opens Appearance › Theme, then Classic is picked, then the run relaunches into Light and into Dark. On the fixed build: one `Classic Hermes` card, cache `[]` after boot, Light paints `#f5f5f5`/`#2b2109` and Dark paints `#1a1a2e`/`#fff8dc`. On a build of 2a226d0b547 with the same seed: two Classic cards, cache `['default']`, and Light painted navy.

## Validation

- `npx vitest run src/themes src/lib`: 181 files / 1868 tests pass. After the review fixes, `npx vitest run src/themes` gives 11 files / 129 tests. Full desktop vitest shows only the known host-environmental electron/scripts failures (plus `mac-sign`, which needs `HERMES_PYTHON`).
- `npm run check:lint`: 0 errors. `prettier --check` is clean on touched files, and `git diff --check` is clean.
- `scripts/check_no_tmp_literals.py apps/desktop/src/themes` and `scripts/audit_pr_attribution.py --fix` are clean.

![Classic Hermes: opt-in only](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aacafc5/cobzrvEsj5IVyVRsMnLzp_3vxlHICo.png)
