items.body:
A partial-clone install checkout keeps git's own lazy-fetch pack fold between updates again (follow-up to #131679).

## What changed

- `hermes_cli/gitlock.py`: `_TREE0_MAINTENANCE_OFF` swaps `maintenance.auto=false` for `maintenance.commit-graph.enabled=false`. `gc.writeCommitGraph=false` and `fetch.writeCommitGraph=false` stay.
- `_restore_auto_maintenance`: an install that already has `maintenance.auto=false` from #131679 (merged 4e3fcd5) has exactly that value unset on its next `hermes update` / `hermes update --check`.
- `scripts/install.sh`, `scripts/install.ps1`: the same key swap (CRLF preserved).
- `website/docs/getting-started/updating.md`: the key list.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gitlock.py`: one invariant. Starting from `maintenance.auto=false`, a clone carrying the keys never leaves more lazy-fetch packs than a stock-config clone does.

Root cause: #127711's loop needs a commit-graph write. `maintenance.auto=false` stopped it, but it also stopped the post-fetch `gc --auto` that git ≤ 2.53 runs after every lazy fetch, and nothing calls `--check` automatically (I checked the banner prefetch and Desktop). So packs piled up until a manual update.

## Validation

Live, real `clear_git_debris()` (worktree imports), real tree:0 clone with a changed-path (Bloom) commit-graph, starting from `maintenance.auto=false`, then 100 more lazy fetches with stock git:

| git | updater fold | packs after 100 lazy fetches: main | this PR | commit-graph writes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.53.0 | 122 → 1 | 101 | **1** | 0 |
| 2.55.0 (built from tarball) | 322 → 1 | 101 | 101 | 0 |

Stock 2.55 maintenance doesn't fold lazy-fetch packs at all, with or without these keys, so on 2.55 the updater's fold remains the only one (unchanged). With only the new key set, stock `git gc --auto` still does 0 commit-graph writes on both versions. The #127711 loop (123 → 31 packs, 30 `git maintenance` children) stays closed.

| | 2.53.0 | 2.55.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_gitlock.py`, this PR | 15 passed | 15 passed |
| same, `gitlock.py` swapped to main's | **1 failed** (`assert 5 <= 1`) | 15 passed (no stock fold to lose) |

ruff, `check_no_tmp_literals`, `check-windows-footguns --all`, `bash -n install.sh`, `check_doc_links` are all clean. `install.ps1` is a one-token change to the key list, not run on Windows.

## Earlier-cut migration (folds #131741, review point from @Godhet)

Nothing records who wrote a `maintenance.auto=false`, so it is migrated only under the fingerprint both earlier Hermes cuts left: `maintenance.auto=false` together with `fetch.writeCommitGraph=false`, and no `maintenance.commit-graph.enabled`. The first pass writes that key, so the migration runs once. An operator's own lone `maintenance.auto=false` is never touched (@ethernet8023's commit and test, cherry-picked from #131741).

The same migration removes the `gc.auto=0` that 73c17151f61 (Sep 29) persisted. 6880ffc1afa stopped writing it but never removed it, and `gc --auto` with `gc.auto=0` skips every heuristic, so **on main the update's fold is a no-op for every checkout configured Sep 29 to Oct 2**. #131741's fingerprint also required `gc.writeCommitGraph=false`, which only the Oct 2 cut wrote.

Real `clear_git_debris()`, treeless clone with 203 lazy-fetch packs; git 2.53.0 and 2.55.0 identical:

| checkout keys | main | #131741 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sep 29 cut (`maintenance.auto=false`, `gc.auto=0`, `fetch.writeCommitGraph=false`) | 203 → **203**, keys kept | 203 → **203**, keys kept | 203 → 1, both migrated |
| Oct 2 cut (+ `gc.writeCommitGraph=false`) | 203 → 1, `maintenance.auto=false` kept | 203 → 1, migrated | 203 → 1, migrated |
| operator's own lone `maintenance.auto=false` | 203 → 1, kept | 203 → 1, kept | 203 → 1, **kept** |

`tests/hermes_cli/test_gitlock.py`: 17 passed on 2.53.0 and 2.55.0. `test_a_checkout_the_first_cut_configured_folds_on_update` fails with main's and #131741's `gitlock.py` on both versions (`assert 5 == 1`). `test_an_operators_own_maintenance_auto_false_is_never_erased` fails with this PR's first commit (the unconditional unset).

## What does this PR do?

Replaces the `ci-reviewed` label gate with `.github/CODEOWNERS`, and deletes the machinery that existed to support the label.

The gate had three parts: classify which paths are sensitive, check for a label, and (in `label-rerun.yml`) wait for the CI run to finish and rerun failed jobs when the label was added. CODEOWNERS replaces all three for path-based review: GitHub requests the reviewer and enforces the approval, with no label, no classification, and no rerun.

### What moves to CODEOWNERS (`@NousResearch/hermes-agent-core`)

CI and the autofix job execute these, or they decide what users install or run. Patterns without a leading slash match at any depth.

| Group | Paths |
|---|---|
| What CI runs | `.github/` (workflows, composite actions, CODEOWNERS itself), `scripts/ci/` (the scripts the workflows call), `eslint.config.*`, `.prettierrc` |
| MCP catalog | `optional-mcps/`, `hermes_cli/mcp_catalog.py` |
| Runs at install or interpreter startup | `setup.py`, `setup.cfg`, `sitecustomize.py`, `usercustomize.py`, `*.pth` |
| Dependency manifests, pins, images | `pyproject.toml`, `package.json`, `uv.lock` (incl. `pm/uv.lock`), `*package-lock.json` (incl. `nix/node-gyp-11-4-0-package-lock.json`), `flake.lock`, `pm/lock.json`, `*Dockerfile` (3 tracked) |
| Supply-chain config | `.npmrc` (holds the 14-day `min-release-age` npm quarantine), `pm/artifact-mirror.json` (where PM fetches artifacts from) |
| Installers | `scripts/install.sh`, `scripts/install.ps1`, `scripts/install.cmd`, `scripts/gen-bootstrap-pins.py` (generates the pins the installers carry) |
| Trust model, third-party pins | `SECURITY.md`, `plugin-catalog/` (each entry pins a third-party repo by sha) |

An earlier revision of this PR left `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `flake.lock` and `package*.json` out on the assumption that the `main` ruleset's required-reviewers rule covers them. They are listed here so they request review on their own and do not depend on the ruleset.

### What this does NOT replace: content scanning

CODEOWNERS matches paths, not diff content. The supply-chain scan's content patterns (base64 decode + `exec`/`eval`, obfuscated `subprocess` commands) can fire in any `.py` file, so they cannot be owned. They used to be overridable with the label; there is no override now. The scan fails on its own again, the way it did before #68833 routed it through the label gate. The patterns are narrow by design, so a false positive should mean fixing the pattern. If you would rather keep an override for these, that is a follow-up and not something CODEOWNERS can provide.

The scan's `.pth` and install-hook path checks are dropped, since CODEOWNERS owns those paths now.

## Changes made

- Add `.github/CODEOWNERS` (every pattern matches at least one tracked file, except the `setup.cfg`, `sitecustomize.py`, `usercustomize.py` and `*.pth` guards, which match none today).
- Delete `review-labels.yml`, `scripts/ci/emit_review_status.py`, `tests/ci/test_emit_review_status.py`.
- `label-rerun.yml`: drop the `rerun-review-labels` job. The `run-e2e` rerun job stays.
- `ci.yaml`: drop the `review-labels` job, its `needs` entry, and the `ci_review`, `ci_review_files`, `mcp_catalog` detect outputs.
- `classify_changes.py`, `detect-changes/action.yml`: drop the same three outputs and their path lists.
- `required_results.py`: `review-labels` is no longer a PR-only job.
- `supply-chain-audit.yml`: scan reports and fails on its own; drop `critical_findings` plumbing and the `ci-reviewed` override.
- `lockfile-diff.yml`: the comment text now points at a core review instead of the label.

## How to test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/ci/` (22 files, 320 passed, 0 failed).
2. `actionlint` on the touched workflows reports only pre-existing findings (`if: false` at `ci.yaml:194`, two SC2034 in `lint.yml`).
3. This PR touches `.github/`, so it should itself request a `hermes-agent-core` review.

### One decision for reviewers

`plugin-catalog/` matches 354 tracked files, and community plugin PRs touch it often, so each of those PRs now waits on core review. Reverting is deleting the `/plugin-catalog/` line.

I did not run the changed workflows on Actions; CI on this PR is the first real run of the new `supply-chain-audit.yml` shape.

## What does this PR do?

Adds Sigrex to the MCP catalog and re-pins the existing `sigrex` plugin entry to v1.0.4.

- **MCP catalog entry.** Sigrex ships a remote MCP server at `https://mcp.sigrex.io` (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, Client ID Metadata Document). The entry gives users a supported sign-in path: Connect in Desktop, `hermes mcp install sigrex` in the terminal, or "connect Sigrex" in chat.
- **Why it's needed.** The `sigrex` plugin declares the same server in its `mcp.json`, but Hermes does not run OAuth for a server that comes from a portable plugin, so that entry stays unconnected (401). The catalog entry writes `auth: oauth` to `mcp_servers`, which Hermes does sign in to. A user's own `sigrex` entry takes precedence over the plugin's, and the plugin keeps providing the skill.
- **Plugin re-pin.** v1.0.4 documents the connect step for Hermes in the README, a new `after-install.md` and the bundled skill. No change to `mcp.json`, no Python, no executables.

## What does this PR do?

Restoring a Hermes window that minimize-to-tray hid no longer leaves it dead to mouse and keyboard on Windows when the restore does not come from the tray (relaunch, deep link, notification click).

## Related Issue

Fixes #127349

Overlaps #127350, which calls `focus()` only. That variant stays dead on real hardware (table below).

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/electron/minimize-to-tray.ts`: when the `restore` or `show` handler releases a window that the tray hid, it now runs `show()` then `focus()` on Windows. The call is deferred with `setImmediate`, as the hide already is. `released()` now returns whether the window was tray-hidden, so windows the tray never hid and the tray's own `restoreHidden()` path (which already releases first) are unchanged.
- `apps/desktop/electron/minimize-to-tray.test.ts`: 2 tests. An OS-driven restore of a tray-hidden window activates it (red on base), and a window the tray never hid is left alone.

Root cause: `focusWindow()` (used by `second-instance` and others) calls `restore()`, which paints the window but does not make it the OS foreground window. Electron reports `isFocused() === true` and fires `focus`, so the guarded `focus()` is skipped. Only the tray path ran `show()` + `focus()`.

## How to Test

Real Electron 40 (arm64) on Windows 11 arm64. Probe: real `minimize-to-tray.ts` + the real `focusWindow` and `ensureMainWindow`. Window options match the chat window (`titleBarStyle: 'hidden'`, `titleBarOverlay`, `focusOnNavigation: false`). Each cycle: minimize (tray hides it), restore, then a real `SendInput` click and key press. A page counter and a textarea show if the input arrived. The foreground lock timeout was set to 0 for the run, so the result is not caused by Windows foreground rules. It was restored afterwards.

| Restore path | Code | Cycles with live input |
|---|---|---|
| relaunch (`focusWindow`) | base | 0 / 3 |
| relaunch | #127350 (`focus()` in handlers) | 0 / 4 |
| relaunch | `restore()` + `focus()` forced | 0 / 3 |
| relaunch | `setSkipTaskbar(false)` first | 0 / 3 |
| relaunch | `restore()` + `show()` + `focus()` | 3 / 3 |
| relaunch | this PR | 4 / 4 |
| tray (`restore()`) | this PR | 4 / 4 |

On every dead cycle, Electron reported `focus` and `isFocused()` true, but `GetForegroundWindow()` was another app's window. The baseline click before the first minimize always worked.

Unit: `vitest run --project electron electron/minimize-to-tray.test.ts` (9 pass; the new activation test fails with the source change reverted), `tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json --noEmit`, `eslint` on both files.

## Notes for review

- Not run: a packaged build, the `mica` backdrop variant, and a restore with the foreground lock timeout at its default.
- Separate bug, not in this PR: `shouldFocusToTakeKeyboard` destructures `isFocused` from the window and throws `Object has been destroyed` (#131732 fixes it). It does not change these results: the table's last rows pass with and without it.
- `restoreHidden()` stays the only place that restores every hidden window. This change activates one window at a time, as the OS restores it.

## Checklist

Adds `plugin-catalog/agent-mail-gateway.yaml`, submitted by the repository owner.

**What it does:** a portable Agent Plugins v1 package that ships one skill, `agent-mail`. It teaches an agent how to use its own mailbox through [Agent Mail Gateway](https://github.com/dominikamann/agent-mail-gateway), a self-hosted email gateway (IMAP/SMTP behind per-agent API keys, sender/recipient allow lists, HTML-to-Markdown, calendar invites): checking and reading mail, replying in-thread, attachments, creating/moving/cancelling invites without duplicates, what each error code means, and rules for treating email content as data rather than instructions.

**Hermes surfaces used:** portable package with `plugin.json` + `skills/agent-mail/SKILL.md` only. No Python, no hooks, no middleware, no `mcp.json`.

**Pin:** `d4d857c3d6e13ef1f522971fe6b1fd7e8e7d89d5` (tag v0.1.2), `subdir: integrations/hermes/agent-mail-gateway`. `hermes plugins validate` at that commit: portable manifest ✓, manifest fields ✓, security scan: safe.

**Disclosure (rule 13):**
- The plugin itself makes no network calls, runs no commands, starts no processes and stores no credentials.
- The skill refers to tools of an MCP server the user configures separately in `mcp_servers` (their own self-hosted gateway URL and their own API key from the profile's `.env`); setup is documented in [docs/hermes.md](https://github.com/dominikamann/agent-mail-gateway/blob/main/docs/hermes.md).
- No telemetry. No self-updating code.

Duplicate and misordered replies keep coming back because the core e2e suite exercises each transition once, while the bug reports involve specific combinations of turn shape and timing. This PR forces those combinations, makes the transcript oracle stricter about ordering, and fixes the duplicate the new tests found on main.

### Fix: a tool turn that completes during the switch-back hydrate rendered its reply twice

Repro: switch away from a chat while a tool turn is still answering, then switch back. If `message.complete` arrives while the switch-back history page is still loading, the answer paints twice (sometimes frozen on its first chunk, sometimes healing at the next refresh). The new `switch-back-race` tool-turn case was red on main for this. The same mechanism shows up in four places, each matching on text that history's folded tool bubble never has:

- `appendLiveSessionProjection` stood the stale activate snapshot down only for a tool-free reply. It now stands down when the committed bubble ends in a reply covering the snapshot. A mid-turn commit ends on a tool, so a running turn still projects.
- `overlayConcurrentMessageChanges` only added and replaced rows. A page composed from the older baseline could bring back a live row the store had already retired into the committed reply. Such a row now stays retired.
- The same overlay dropped the settled live reply only when the page had a message with the same words. It now matches the reply's stored row (`final_assistant_row_id` → `sourceRowId`) first, then a folded bubble's answer text (the text after its last tool).
- When the page still carried the reply's streaming copy under the same id, the overlay replaced it in place without that check. The check now runs first and drops the stale copy.

Four `utils.test.ts` cases fail on main and pass here. The switch-back race passed 16/16 locally (`--repeat-each 4`).

### The oracle now also checks order between checkpoints

At each checkpoint, the oracle already required every stored message to render exactly once and in stored order. Its in-page sampler also failed any frame where a message appeared twice.

The sampler now also fails any frame where:
- a reply renders above its own prompt;
- two messages swap places compared with an earlier frame.

So a wrong order that corrects itself before the final check still fails. Reasoning is left out, because live and history place the thinking block differently. This applies to every spec that uses `assertTranscriptOracle`.

A steer that lands at a tool boundary is stored as its own user row, wrapped in the out-of-band marker the model sees. The oracle now compares that row by the user's own words, which is what the app shows. Rows the backend writes itself (`process_complete`, `model_switch` and the other notice kinds hydration draws as notices) are skipped, since they aren't messages.

### New scenarios: `reply-settle-paths.spec.ts`

- **An answer repeated as the final reply.** The model answers beside a housekeeping tool, then sends an empty follow-up. The backend reuses the answer as the final reply, so the same text arrives as `message.interim` and again as `message.complete`.
  - Plain: must render once.
  - With a `review.summary` row delivered before that turn's `message.complete`, the order #131626 reports. The test routes the socket and holds that one frame until the row has been delivered. It renders once on main, so this shape does not reproduce #131626. It stays as a guard.
- **A steer at every point of a tool turn:**
  - while reasoning;
  - while the narration before a tool streams;
  - while the tool runs (the steered command finishes in the background and its notification turn is checked too);
  - while the answer after it streams;
  - two steers back to back.
- **A finished two-tool turn, then reload and switch-back.**

### `switch-back-race.spec.ts`

Both orders ("reply completes first" and "switch-back hydrate resolves first") now also run with a tool turn (#128809).

### Harness

`provider.scriptPrompt(label, needle, steps)` scripts requests that carry no turn marker, such as the background review fork.

A Windows update no longer fails with `[WinError 5] Access is denied` when a running Hermes process still has the replaced Python runtime's DLLs mapped: the held tree is set aside and deleted later, and the update completes.

Reported in Discord support (Windows 11, Desktop install): `hermes update` failed twice in source preparation deleting `.previous-python-*/DLLs/libcrypto-3-x64.dll`, then again deleting a `.displaced-*` tree after a rollback. Each time the new runtime was already published (or the old one already restored); only the garbage cleanup failed, and it failed the whole update.

## Changes

- `pm/install.py::_discard_entry` owns every cleanup that runs after a publish or restore has finished: the displaced `.previous-*` entry (publish and settle arms), the restored-over `.displaced-*` tree, and the `fetch-*` archives. When the delete fails it renames the tree to `.reclaim-<uuid>` (Windows allows renaming a tree with mapped images) and logs a warning instead of raising.
  - The `.previous-<entry>` slot is free again, so the next publish of the same entry is not blocked by a still-held leftover.
  - A half-deleted tree can never be picked up by a later restore.
- `_reclaim_set_aside` deletes `.reclaim-*` trees whose hold is gone (single attempt, no retry sleep). It runs at the start of every install under the store lock, and from `hermes pm gc`.
- An interrupted restore's `.displaced-*` tree (never set aside) is still left alone by gc.
- Restore and verify failures are still fatal. Only cleanup of trees that are already garbage became best-effort. A rollback whose own cleanup is held now re-raises the error that caused the rollback, so the cleanup error no longer hides it.

Root cause: `_remove_entry` raises after ~2 s of retries, and all four post-commit cleanup sites called it as if a failed delete meant a failed install.

## Validation

| Check | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| **Live Windows** (`windows-latest`, runs 37070065756 / 37070071146, real `LoadLibraryW` of a DLL inside the live entry, reinstall over it; `wine2e/pm-held-red` vs `wine2e/pm-held-green`) | `InstallError: faketool: install failed: [WinError 5] Access is denied: …\.previous-faketool-1.0-win32-x64\DLLs\held.dll` | pass: install succeeds while the DLL stays mapped, the tree is set aside, and `hermes pm gc` removes it after `FreeLibrary` (run 37070071146) |
| `test_held_replaced_entry_does_not_fail_reinstall_and_is_reclaimed` (publish arm, two reinstalls while held, gc after release) | FAIL `PermissionError` | pass |
| `test_held_displacement_does_not_fail_restore_and_gc_spares_interrupted_one` (restore arm + gc selectivity) | FAIL `PermissionError` | pass |
| `tests/pm/test_pm_core.py`, `tests/pm/test_recovery.py` (rebased on main after #128955) | | 46 passed, 2 skipped (host-marked) |

The windows-only test runs on the PR's Windows lane. The two cross-platform tests model the hold by patching `_remove_entry`, because Linux can't hold a file the way Windows does.

## Credit

Consolidates the proposals for #124807, with authorship preserved:
- #124819 by @janviernine: best-effort `.previous-*` cleanup on both arms (earliest). Its commit is cherry-picked here.
- #128955 by @helix4u was merged to main while this PR was in CI. It added the `.displaced-*` restore arm with a `.restored` sidecar marker for gc. This PR replaces that marker with the set-aside rename, so the four cleanup sites share one mechanism. Its gc selectivity contract (an interrupted restore's displacement is never reclaimed) is kept and still tested.
- #124858 by @dskwe: the same publish-arm fix. It is superseded, and its review findings (leaked orphan, settle arm, `fetch-*` arm) are addressed here.

Review findings from @Enough1122 on #124819/#124858 (version-bump orphan unreachable by gc, restore arm still fatal, `fetch-*` arm) are all covered by this change.

Not handled: a `.displaced-*` tree that a main build since #128955 marked with `.restored` is no longer reclaimed by gc. That window is hours and only affects main-channel Windows installs that hit a held restore, so there is no compatibility code for it.

Fixes #124807

AMD and Intel GPU machines now get the Vulkan llama.cpp build from `backend: auto`, and a discrete AMD/Intel card is sized from its own memory instead of system RAM.

Reported in Discord (RX 9060 XT 16 GB, Windows, Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_M): Hermes spawned `runtimes/llamacpp/b10679/cpu/llama-server.exe` and failed with `unable to allocate CPU buffer` (11.8 GiB). Forcing `local_runtime.backend: vulkan` downloaded the Vulkan build, and the model still failed to load: the planner priced the card as "unified memory" equal to system RAM and handed it a 147,456-token window with every layer resident on a 16 GB card.

## Changes

- `bootstrap.py::_detect_gpu_vendor` falls back to `hermes_platform.host.facts.gpu_class()` when nvidia-smi doesn't answer (registry/sysfs, no subprocess), so `select_backend` reaches its existing AMD/Intel → Vulkan branch. (Cherry-picked from #129750 by @skyecon.)
- `hardware.py::probe_budget`: when no NVIDIA device answers and the configured engine is Vulkan or HIP, ask that engine which device it will use. A discrete card is budgeted from its own memory, with system RAM as spill space (`uma=False`). An integrated GPU, a CPU/Metal engine, or a failed probe keeps the RAM-as-unified budget, same as before.
- New `local_runtime/devices.py`: a bounded child process (`python -I`, stdlib only, 20 s deadline, hidden console) loads the engine's `ggml` library and reads `ggml_backend_dev_type` / `ggml_backend_dev_memory`. That device type is ggml's own integrated-vs-discrete call (Vulkan takes it from `VkPhysicalDeviceType`). The probe result is cached per engine binary, since the hardware endpoint polls every few seconds.
- `hardware.py::_configured_engine`: both engine probes read `local_runtime.backend` through `load_config_readonly()`. They used to call `get_config_value(key, "auto")`, which is the `hermes config get` printer with signature `(key, *, as_json, raw)`. The TypeError was swallowed by `suppress(Exception)`, so the probes returned None every time. Main's CUDA `--list-devices` pool fallback has been dead since it landed (bdb52ce7117).
- `endpoint.py::_boot_in_flight`: the CLI's on-demand boot now checks for the engine of the *configured* backend instead of `auto`. With `backend: vulkan` and only the Vulkan build installed, `hermes chat` used to print "The local model server isn't running" and never boot.
- **One engine identity for the shared server** (`bootstrap.py::serving_engine`): the managed server is one per process and serves every profile it hosts, so budgets now price the engine it runs or is booting and fall back to `local_runtime.backend` only when no server is up. The on-demand kick and the Local Models job/refresh threads carry the caller's contextvars (`spawn_context_thread`). Before, a named profile on Vulkan booted on demand from a default profile set to CPU was sized at 262,144 tokens from system RAM.
- **Quickstart prices after installing the engine** (`local_models.py::_repriced_quickstart`): the job re-picks right after the engine install, before any bytes are committed, and updates the job's `target`/`model_id` (what Desktop renders). The POST contract is unchanged.
- **Vulkan/HIP launches subtract other programs' VRAM** (`hardware.py::launch_budget`): a fresh device probe at launch time (the polled view stays cached), the same contract `nvidia-smi` serves on NVIDIA.
- Docs: `local-models.md` says what `auto` prefers (with the platform's pinned fallbacks) and how each GPU kind is sized.

## Why ask the engine for the device type

`llama-server --list-devices` (#109336's source) prints a size but doesn't say integrated or discrete. Counting an iGPU as discrete double-counts memory: the 129750 reporter's Intel N100 shows `11821 MiB` of a 16 GB machine's shared RAM, which would land as VRAM *and* spill. llama.cpp itself puts layers only on discrete devices when one exists and falls back to an iGPU otherwise (`src/llama.cpp`, "add integrated GPUs only if no discrete GPUs were found"). The budget uses the same rule, read from the same device enum (`ggml-backend.h`: CPU, GPU, IGPU, ACCEL, which is identical at b10679 and b10964).

## Validation

**Live run on real hardware.** A real Hermes home, the managed Vulkan b10964 engine installed through PM, and the catalog's `Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_M` (16.5 GB) on an RTX 3090 24 GB. NVIDIA's management and compute surfaces were hidden at the OS level (`bwrap`: `nvidia-smi`, `libcuda`, `/proc/driver/nvidia`) while the Vulkan driver stayed available, so the box looks like a non-NVIDIA discrete GPU to Hermes. The server was booted the way Desktop's backend does it (`ensure_local_runtime(load_config())`), then a real `hermes chat -q` ran against it. One run each:

| | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `probe_budget` | `uma=True`, 50.1 GiB (system RAM) | `uma=False`, 22.1 GiB (the card), RAM as spill |
| planned window (presets.ini) | 262,144 + batch 4096 / ubatch 2048 | 98,304 |
| model load | 18.2 s | 9.6 s |
| decode | 3.79 tok/s | 9.91 tok/s |
| `hermes chat` alone (no Desktop boot), `backend: vulkan` | "The local model server isn't running" | boots on demand, answers |
| DRM vendor ID presented as AMD (0x1002): `_detect_gpu_vendor()` | `None` (so `auto` picks the CPU build) | `amd` (so `auto` picks Vulkan) |

On 24 GB, main's oversized plan didn't crash: llama.cpp's fitter pushed part of the model off the card and decode ran 2.6x slower. On the reporter's 16 GB card the same overestimate (a 147K window there) is more than the fitter can absorb, and the load fails. That matches @wonine's RX 9070 XT run on #109336 (`ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory` before; 3.0 to 11.7 tok/s on IQ4_XS).

The live run is what found the dead config read (commit `cef368d8e6f`). Before it, the device probe answered but `probe_budget` still returned the RAM budget. The unit test had patched the whole probe function, so it passed anyway. The test now reads a real `config.yaml`.

**Windows (real runner, `wine2e/` lane, run 37079630701).** On `windows-latest` with the official b10964 Windows Vulkan zip, sha-verified, `ggml-base.dll` and `ggml.dll` load through `ctypes` plus `os.add_dll_directory`, and `ggml_backend_load` runs `ggml-vulkan.dll`. The runner has no GPU (`ggml_backend_init returned NULL`), so the child exits rc=0 with `[]` in 0.11 to 0.23 s and the budget falls back cleanly. The registry vendor read returns `none` there, as it should.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_auto_vendor_detection_uses_host_gpu_class` | red on main, green here |
| `test_vulkan_device_type_decides_discrete_vs_unified` (real config read; GPU → card memory, IGPU → RAM-as-unified) | red on the previous PR head, green here |
| `test_boot_in_flight_real_gate` (configured backend gates the CLI boot) | red on base, green here |
| 33 local-runtime test files (`run_tests.sh`, scratch HOME for the worktree home-I/O guard) | 295 passed, 62 skipped, 0 failed |
| `test_boot_prices_the_engine_it_serves` | red on the previous PR head, green here |
| `test_quickstart_prices_after_installing_the_engine` | red on the previous PR head, green here |
| `test_launch_budget_reads_free_memory_on_a_vulkan_card` | red on the previous PR head, green here |
| ruff, windows-footguns, subprocess-stdin, no-tmp, profile-scope patterns, doc links | clean |

**Not covered:** no AMD or Intel GPU was available, so the discrete verdict has come only from NVIDIA hardware under Vulkan, and on Windows only the no-GPU path ran. A reporter or contributor with an RX card is the remaining proof.

### Independent review round (all on the same 3090 with NVIDIA hidden, real Vulkan engine)

| Probe | previous head `0a0c9cf` | this head |
|---|---|---|
| Named profile `backend: vulkan`, default profile `backend: cpu`, on-demand boot thread | window 262,144 (RAM budget) | 98,304 (card budget), same as a direct boot |
| Real quickstart POST, empty engine store, real Vulkan engine install | downloads Qwen3.6 35B-A3B (picked from 50 GiB RAM) | switches to Qwen3.8 27B (picked from the card) before the download |
| `launch_budget` with another process holding 3.7 / 5.4 / 16.2 GB of VRAM | `None` (capacity plan, 98,304) | 18.8 / 17.1 / 6.7 GiB usable; window narrows to the 64K floor |

The Vulkan driver's free count includes other processes (16.2 GB held elsewhere read as 8.2 GB free of 26.0). On this card the 27B doesn't fit fully even at the 64K floor once others hold 3.7 GB or more, so decode was the same on both heads in those runs; the launch-budget change brings Vulkan in line with the NVIDIA contract rather than being a measured speedup here. Not covered: real AMD/Intel silicon, native Windows GPU inference, HIP, multi-GPU.

## Credit and related

- #129750 (@skyecon): vendor fallback, cherry-picked.
- #109336 (@mbeattietex1-star): discrete Vulkan budget, cherry-picked; its `--list-devices` source is replaced in the follow-up commit.
- #115076 (@Belaquaa): the ggml device-type probe, adapted (co-author), and the "price after installing the engine" quickstart leg, re-implemented inside the job so the POST contract and Desktop stay unchanged. Its device pinning is left out: llama.cpp already skips iGPUs when a discrete card exists.
- Superseded for the same symptom: #100749, #104281 (vendor detection); related #105796, #102562 (Linux sysfs AMD budget). Issues: #100740, #105710.
- Not in scope here: posture of spilled launches (mmproj offload, q8 KV when spilled; @wonine's second comment on #109336), and #123677 (HIP archive missing rocBLAS).

items.body:
## Summary

The Nous Portal enforces a cumulative replayed-reasoning budget: replaying stored
`reasoning_details` on every request wedges long sessions with a non-retryable 400 once the
replayed total crosses the budget. Drop the Portal from the replay allowlist so the wire copy
strips `reasoning_details` on that route, exactly like every other non-replaying
chat-completions route. Stored history keeps the field, so a later switch to a route that
genuinely replays it (OpenRouter, #129037) still receives it.

## Fixes #118182

- #118182 — long Nous Portal sessions wedge with a non-retryable 400 once replayed
  reasoning_details pass the route's cumulative budget.

## Root cause

`agent/transports/chat_completions.py:271` — `_route_replays_reasoning_details` allowlisted
both `openrouter.ai` and `nousresearch.com` (added in #70233 for multi-turn reasoning
continuity). For a Portal base URL this makes `convert_messages` keep
`reasoning_details` on the wire copy of every stored assistant message. The Portal meters
replayed reasoning cumulatively, so a long session builds an ever-growing replayed payload
until the route rejects it with a non-retryable 400 and the session wedges. The continuity
the allowlist intended is exactly what the Portal's budget forbids.

## Tests

Red on base (branch base 98cceaef2b) / green after (this PR):

```
unset PYTHONPATH && scripts/run_tests.sh \
  tests/agent/test_provider_history_parity.py \
  tests/agent/transports/test_chat_completions_reasoning_details_replay.py \
  tests/agent/test_iteration_summary_reasoning_details.py \
  tests/e2e/core/providers/test_chat_reasoning_variants.py
```

- **Red on base**: `tests/agent/test_provider_history_parity.py::test_nous_portal_strips_replayed_reasoning_details_from_wire`
  failed with `reasoning_details` present on the wire for `inference-api.nousresearch.com/v1` (1 failed, 3 passed).
- **Green after**: 10 passed, 4 skipped (the 4 e2e cells are Linux-gated; the file collects and imports cleanly on macOS).
- New contracts in `tests/agent/test_provider_history_parity.py`:
  - Portal base URL (prod + stg subdomain) strips `reasoning_details` from the wire copy; stored history untouched.
  - Substring lookalike hosts (`nousresearch.com.evil.io`) never matched the allowlist and still strip.
  - OpenRouter (#129037 sibling) keeps replaying `reasoning_details` unchanged.
  - A profile declaring `native_reasoning_details_type` still receives its carrier on the Portal route (profile contract intact).
- `tests/agent/transports/test_chat_completions_reasoning_details_replay.py` updated from the #70233 contract
  (OpenRouter/Nous keep) to the #118182 contract (OpenRouter keeps, Nous strips, durable history untouched).
- `tests/e2e/core/providers/test_chat_reasoning_variants.py::test_long_session_does_not_wedge_on_replayed_reasoning_budget`:
  the #118182 repro cell. Its `KNOWN` xfail gate is removed and the cell now asserts the fixed behavior —
  8 turns each minting ~1 KB of reasoning against a 4 KB budget route: zero route rejections, zero
  `reasoning_details` on the wire, every turn answered, state.db keeps all blocks for a switch back.
  (Linux-gated; runs in CI.)
- Wider blast check: full `tests/agent/transports/` dir — 19 files, 406 tests, 0 failed.

## Side effects

- **Fresh-install / local-backend users**: CI and this PR's tests run on a fresh install with a
  local backend and test fixtures; the change only alters the wire copy for hosts matching
  `nousresearch.com`. Users on the real Portal stop sending replayed reasoning — that is the
  fix; users on OpenRouter see no change (`openrouter.ai` branch untouched). Users on other
  strict/lenient routes see no change (they already stripped).
- **Multi-turn reasoning continuity on the Portal is lost by design**: the Portal's own budget
  made replay infeasible; before this fix the "continuity" manifested as a wedged session.
  Continuity on OpenRouter and on profile-declared native carriers is preserved (tested).
- **Cache stability**: stripping happens in `convert_messages` on every request identically, so
  the wire copy of a given history is stable across turns of a conversation — no mid-conversation
  mutation, no prompt-cache invalidation. Stored history is never modified (asserted in tests).
- **Anthropic Messages path untouched**: the Portal's Anthropic-thinking replay
  (`anthropic_thinking_policy` / `_is_nous_portal_endpoint`) is a separate contract and unchanged.
- **The three reverted-PR failure mode (green in CI, broken for real users)**: this change
  cannot 400 newly — it removes a field from outgoing request bodies on one host family; strict
  schema providers reject unknown fields, and this only ever removes one. The one behavioral risk
  is a Portal model that *requires* reasoning replay to function (none known; the Portal's budget
  400 makes replay impossible for long sessions anyway).

## Self-review

- **Secretly a feature?** No — it removes the Portal from an allowlist; no new surface, no new
  config, no new env vars.
- **Secretly broader?** The allowlist change is host-scoped (`base_url_host_matches` — exact
  host or subdomain, not substring). OpenRouter replay, profile-native carriers, thought
  signatures, and the Anthropic path are all untouched and covered by existing + new tests.

## Risk

`triage risk`: **0.30** (kind `bug`, surfaces `code` + `tests`, critical none). An initial
draft included a comment-only edit to `agent/turn_context.py` which scored agent-core 0.80;
that comment was dropped to keep the diff code-path minimal — the same why is documented in
the `_route_replays_reasoning_details` docstring.


## Supersedes

- #118185 (KoNit-K, "fix(transports): cap Portal reasoning replay", opened Sep 21 from a fork)
  — gets the diagnosis right (cumulative Portal replay budget, non-retryable 400) and correctly
  strips only the wire copy while keeping durable history. But its fix — replay only the newest
  assistant turn's `reasoning_details` — is a turn-count heuristic, not a budget bound: a single
  turn whose reasoning exceeds the budget still wedges the session non-retryably (the e2e mints
  ~1 KB/turn against a 4 KB budget; one 5 KB turn would still cross). It also keeps the Portal
  in `_route_replays_reasoning_details`, so the Linux e2e cell
  (`test_long_session_does_not_wedge_on_replayed_reasoning_budget`) fails: its precondition
  asserts the budget WAS crossed (route rejections observed), and the cap keeps every request
  under budget — no fork runs the Linux lane, so this was never caught. This PR strips the field
  on the Portal wire entirely (stored history keeps it), which makes the budget unreachable and
  keeps continuity on routes that genuinely replay it.

items.body:
## Summary

On Windows, a custom TTS/STT command provider (`tts.providers.<name>` with a `command:`) spawns
its shell with `shell=True` and `creationflags=CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` only. `shell=True` routes
through `cmd.exe` — a console-subsystem shim — so every provider run allocates a **visible console
window flash** when Hermes runs from a windowless host (pythonw gateway, TUI, Desktop). STT shares
the exact runner (`tools/transcription_command.py`, `tools/tts_tool_lifecycle.py` re-export
`run_command_provider`), so command-based STT providers flash too.

Same bug class one code path later: `terminate_command_process_tree()` shells out to `taskkill`
(the idle-timeout kill) with no creationflags — a second console flash from the same feature.

## Fixes #101585

## Root cause

- `tools/tts_command_provider.py:152-155` (base): the Popen branch passed only
  `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP`, missing `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`, unlike the shared helper at
  `hermes_cli/_subprocess_compat.py:206` (`windows_detach_flags_without_breakaway`).
- `tools/tts_command_provider.py:101-106` (base): the `taskkill` subprocess.run had no
  creationflags at all.

## What changed

- `run_command_provider()` now uses the shared bundle
  `windows_detach_flags_without_breakaway()` (`CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP | CREATE_NO_WINDOW`,
  0 elsewhere) instead of hand-rolled flags. The branch composition is extracted into a pure
  `provider_popen_group_kwargs(os_name)` helper (platform-as-data, DI-testable).
  `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` is deliberately **not** included: the provider child is
  foreground-owned and killed by us on idle timeout, so job-teardown propagation must keep
  working (the breakaway flag exists for the post-update gateway watcher, a different consumer).
- `terminate_command_process_tree()`'s `taskkill` run now passes
  `creationflags=windows_hide_flags()`.
- POSIX behavior is byte-identical: `start_new_session=True` as before.
- Test-only drive-by in the same file: one pre-existing `read_text(encoding="utf-8")`
  flagged by `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py` when it now runs on this changed file —
  switched to the repo-policy `utf-8-sig` (reads BOM'd and BOM-less alike; assertion
  value unchanged, the written fixture is BOM-less UTF-8).

## Tests

Red on base (3 failed: the pure-contract tests, helper absent / bundle missing
`CREATE_NO_WINDOW`), green after — commands run from the worktree root with
`unset PYTHONPATH`:

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_tts_command_providers.py`
  - base: `1 files, 33 tests passed, 3 failed, 2 skipped`
  - after fix: `1 files, 36 tests passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped` (the 2 skipped are the
    `platforms("windows")`/`platforms("posix")` spawn-site tests, run for real on their
    host lanes in CI per the repo's platform-gating policy)
- Pure contract (every host): nt branch returns exactly
  `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP | CREATE_NO_WINDOW` and matches
  `windows_detach_flags_without_breakaway()`; posix branch returns `{"start_new_session": True}`.
- Spawn site, `platforms("windows")`: fake `Popen` kwargs carry `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` and
  `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP`, no `start_new_session`.
- Spawn site, `platforms("posix")`: `start_new_session=True`, no `creationflags`.
- Idle kill, `platforms("windows")`: the `taskkill` run carries `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`.
- Sibling suites that exercise the runner:
  `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_transcription_command_providers.py tests/tools/test_tts_lifecycle_leases.py` — green.
  `tests/tools/test_transcription_tools.py` has one pre-existing failure on base
  (`test_config_device_and_compute_type_passed_to_whisper`, verified red on origin/main
  before applying this fix) — untouched by this change, noted not fixed.
- Required gate for subprocess changes: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_subprocess_text_encoding.py` — green.
- `uvx ruff check` on both changed files — clean.
- `python scripts/check-windows-footguns.py tools/tts_command_provider.py tests/tools/test_tts_command_providers.py` — clean.

## Side effects

- **Who runs this code without a Windows CI lane?** Native-Windows users running Hermes from a
  windowless host (pythonw gateway, TUI, Electron Desktop) with a `command:`-type TTS or STT
  provider. The change adds a creationflag bit; on Windows the spawn itself is otherwise
  untouched. Users who *wanted* the console window (nobody does; it's a flash) lose nothing.
- **Does the flag change process-tree semantics?** `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` is preserved, so
  the idle-timeout tree kill (`taskkill /T` via the new group) behaves identically.
  `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` gives the child its own hidden console that descendants inherit — the
  repo's documented A/B-verified behavior (see `_subprocess_compat.py`, commits for #54220/#56747);
  it does not detach the child (no DETACHED_PROCESS, no breakaway). POSIX paths are unchanged.
- **Remote backends?** None: the command provider only ever spawns on the host running Hermes;
  no env var, config, or surface change.
- **Prompt-cache / tool-schema impact?** None: no tool schemas, prompts, or config keys change.
- **What if `windows_detach_flags_without_breakaway()` returns 0 (non-Windows)?** The nt branch
  is only taken when `os.name == "nt"`, so 0 cannot reach a real Windows spawn; on POSIX the
  helper is never consulted.
- **Prompt-injection risk from provider commands?** Unchanged: the command still runs as
  user-configured, with the same secret-scrubbed env and `env_passthrough` allowlist.

## Self-review

Not secretly a feature: no new surface, no schema change, no new env var or config key —
one flag bit on an existing spawn plus one on an existing kill, both through the established
shared helpers. Not secretly broader: scoped to `tools/tts_command_provider.py` (the STT
re-export path benefits because it calls the same function; no STT file edits needed).
The `utf-8-sig` test tweak is the only non-flag change, and it is a lint-policy compliance fix
on a line in the same changed file, not a behavior change.

## Risk

0.30 (bug) — surfaces: code, tests. No critical paths flagged by the triage risk tool
(install-update: none, launch: none, ui: none).

## Supersedes

- #106360 (Finn763) — got the root cause exactly right: `windows_detach_flags_without_breakaway()` on the spawn plus `windows_hide_flags()` on the timeout `taskkill`, no `BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB`, process group kept for the tree kill. This PR reuses that approach and carries co-author credit. Superseded because its tests fake `os.name` without platform markers — under AGENTS.md "Don't fake the host OS" a test that needs the interpreter to believe it is on Windows belongs on the Windows lane (`platforms("windows")`), otherwise it is green on Linux CI and invisible to the OS it exists for (the #111866 failure mode); its POSIX arm is `skipif`-ed out on win32 with an INTERNALERROR workaround, and the branch is CONFLICTING with current main with no CI run recorded on its head. This PR lands the same two-flag fix with the branch composition extracted as platform-as-data (`provider_popen_group_kwargs`) and spawn-site tests that run for real on their OS lanes.

## What does this PR do?

A Bot relay roster refresh that was in flight when the relay stopped or restarted can no longer publish a stale roster or clear a sole gateway's roster. Salvaged from #131028 (Gille / @helix4u), plus one regression test and a lint cleanup on top.

`syncRelayRosters()` only checked `disposed` before its async reads. Stopping the relay cleared timers but did not invalidate pending work, so a late `profiles.list` reply could still replace a gateway's roster or clear a sole gateway. A restart was also blocked by the previous run's `rosterBusy` flag. Each roster pass now captures a lifecycle generation; stop invalidates it and releases the busy flag; obsolete passes cannot touch the fallback cache, publish rows, mark a clear complete, or release a newer pass's busy flag.

## Related Issue

Salvages #131028. No separate issue.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Security fix
- [ ] Documentation update
- [x] Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] New skill

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/relay.ts` (Gille's commit): `rosterGeneration` counter; `isCurrent()` checkpoints after each async read and in the clear/publish loops; `stopBotRelay` bumps the generation and releases `rosterBusy`; the `finally` only releases `rosterBusy` for the current generation.
- `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/relay.test.ts` (Gille's commit): stop / stop+restart / stopped sole-peer clear regressions.
- Follow-up commit (mine): a regression for the stop/restart overlap, and `eslint --fix` for the `padding-line-between-statements` warnings the salvaged commit introduced (`origin/main` has 0 on these files).

The overlap test comes from the review on #131028 (@Enough1122): reverting only the generation guard in `finally` left all 38 tests green, but a stale run finishing after a restart then clears the new run's `rosterBusy`, so the next 60 s tick starts a concurrent roster writer.

## How to Test

1. From `apps/desktop`: `env -u NODE_ENV npx vitest run src/plugins/hermes-bots/relay.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism`
2. Mutation check: replace the `finally` guard with an unconditional `relay.rosterBusy = false` and rerun. `a stale run finishing does not free the restarted run’s busy flag` fails with `expected 6 to be 4`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `relay.test.ts` | 39 passed (38 from #131028 + 1 new) |
| `src/plugins/hermes-bots/` | 767 passed |
| New test with the `finally` guard dropped | fails, `expected 6 to be 4` |
| `tsc -p . --noEmit` | clean |
| `eslint` on the two touched files | 0 errors, 0 warnings |
| `git diff --check` | clean |

Not run: Electron/UI E2E and multi-window field attribution (same as #131028); CI owns the full workspace checks.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — N/A, JS-only change
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: NixOS (Linux), vitest

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A (platform-independent lifecycle state)
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

## Credit

- @helix4u: diagnosis, fix, and the original stop/restart tests (#131028); authorship preserved by cherry-pick.
- @Enough1122: found that the `finally` guard was unpinned and described the overlap case.
- @whyyagswhy: independent verification of the original head on Linux.

## Screenshots / Logs

No UI change.

items.body:
When the primary is rate-limited, a `fallback_providers` entry for the Desktop-managed local llama.cpp model (`provider: llamacpp`, no `base_url`) now answers from the local server instead of failing with "provider not configured" — and when that server is off, the local model name is never sent to a cloud provider.

**Root cause:** a bare `llamacpp` / `llama.cpp` / `llama-cpp` alias resolved through the generic custom branch of `resolve_provider_client` (the fallback chain's and the auxiliary tasks' chokepoint), which never looked at the managed server — it returned nothing, the primary's own endpoint, or whichever cloud provider held a key.

## Changes
- `agent/auxiliary_local_runtime.py` (new, 38 lines): `bare_llamacpp_endpoint()` — for a bare alias, the live managed endpoint read through the same ownership-checked resolver (`resolve_llamacpp_endpoint`) the main ladder uses, with the **calling profile's** config loaded at call time; a configured provider entry named like the alias still wins; explicit `api_key` beats the endpoint key.
- `resolve_provider_client` (fallback chain, init-time fallback, direct callers) and `_get_cached_client` (every aux task: compression, title, vision, …) consult it first. No running server → `(None, None)` — the main ladder's `_resolve_llamacpp_runtime` answer — never `_try_custom_endpoint` / `OPENAI_BASE_URL` / `_resolve_api_key_provider`.
- The cached aux client keys on the live endpoint (URL + key), so a server restarted on a new port/key gets a fresh client and a stopped one never serves the stale client.
- The original rung's `main_runtime is None` gate is dropped: the cached aux path always passes a normalized dict, so the rung never ran there, and a task pinned to `llamacpp` inherited a foreign main runtime's URL.
- Vision keeps the raw provider name for its final resolve so the alias isn't flattened to bare `custom` first.
- The aux "unavailable" error names the stopped local server instead of an invented `LLAMACPP_API_KEY`.
- Docs: `llamacpp` rows in the fallback-providers page (fallback table + aux provider table).
- Tests: the five resolver-stub tests (one asserted the cloud fall-through) trimmed to two invariants on a real `server.json` + live child process.

## Live repro
Isolated `HOME`/`HERMES_HOME`, real `llama-server` (PM-pinned `llamacpp-cpu` b10964, SmolLM2-135M GGUF) booted by `ensure_local_runtime(load_config())` — the same call the Desktop backend lifespan makes; primary = a named provider whose real HTTP server answers every request with 429 ("hourly limit"); `fallback_providers: [{provider: llamacpp, model: SmolLM2-135M-Instruct-Q4_K_M}]`; real `hermes chat -q` on a detached `origin/main` worktree vs this branch.

| Scenario | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Server running, no cloud key (the report) | `WARNING agent.chat_completion_helpers: Fallback to llamacpp failed: provider not configured` | `Fallback activated: laguna-free → SmolLM2-135M-Instruct-Q4_K_M (llamacpp)`, `base_url=http://127.0.0.1:18434/v1/`, reply in state.db: "Hello, welcome in five words." |
| Server running, `GEMINI_API_KEY` in `.env` (#119227) | fallback client `base_url=https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta` → `400 … unexpected model name format` | local server answers; 0 requests to Gemini in agent.log |
| Server stopped, `GEMINI_API_KEY` in `.env` | (sends to Gemini, as above) | `resolve_provider_client: llamacpp requested but no local llama.cpp server is running` + `Fallback to llamacpp failed: provider not configured`; 0 Gemini requests |
| `auxiliary.compression.provider: llamacpp`, `call_llm` across a restart 18436 → 18437, then stop | every call sent the compression request to Gemini (400), same cached client throughout | 18436 answers → cache hit (same object) → new client on 18437 answers → `AuxiliaryClientUnavailable: … no local llama.cpp server is running` |
| Vision pinned to `llamacpp`; compression pinned to `llamacpp` with a foreign (Gemini) main runtime | both → `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` | both → `http://127.0.0.1:18434/v1/` |

## Tests
| Test | origin/main | original rung (#119228 head) | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_fallback_resolution_uses_live_managed_server_or_nothing` | ✗ (Gemini client) | ✗ (server off → Gemini) | ✓ |
| `test_cached_client_follows_managed_endpoint_restart` | ✗ (Gemini client) | ✗ (cached path → Gemini) | ✓ |

`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent tests/hermes_cli/test_runtime_provider_resolution.py tests/hermes_cli/test_managed_vision_capability.py tests/hermes_cli/test_local_runtime.py`: 10567 passed, 0 failed. ruff, Windows footguns, no-tmp, subprocess-stdin, doc links, `git diff --check` clean.

Not covered live: Windows (the report's OS) and the Desktop UI itself — the managed server was booted through the backend's own `ensure_local_runtime` call, not the Electron app.

## Credit
Salvages #119228 by @albeight (commit cherry-picked with authorship; it found the missing managed-endpoint rung). The call-time `config=load_config()` and the ungated rung follow #128695 by @helix4u (co-authored).

Fixes #119227

items.body:
## Summary

Two voice-mode defects made continuous voice unusable for users who configure a low `voice.silence_threshold` (needed on quiet mics), and silently disabled streaming TTS for every macOS voice user:

1. `AudioRecorder.stop()` applied its final too-quiet discard with the hardcoded `SILENCE_RMS_THRESHOLD = 200` instead of the configured `self._silence_threshold` (wired from `voice.silence_threshold` by the CLI before each recording). With threshold 80 and a mic peaking at RMS ~160, the VAD correctly detected speech and auto-stopped — then `stop()` threw the recording away as "too quiet", so every turn after the first failed with "No speech detected".
2. `_chat_setup_turn_audio` gated streaming-TTS arming on `_import_sounddevice()`, which raises on macOS (PortAudio/CoreAudio init triggers a kTCCServiceMediaLibrary prompt — exactly why the speaker path deliberately avoids sounddevice on Darwin and routes output via tempfile → `afplay`). The bare `except: pass` swallowed the failure and streaming TTS never armed on macOS.

`stop()` now applies the same configured floor as the VAD; arming is `check_tts_requirements()` alone (the speaker side already picks its own output route per platform), and arm failures are logged at debug instead of being swallowed silently.

## Fixes

- Fixes #84046

## Root cause

- `tools/voice_mode.py:847-849` — `stop()`'s peak-RMS discard compared against the module constant `SILENCE_RMS_THRESHOLD` (200) while the VAD (`tools/voice_mode.py:659`, `:696`) used `self._silence_threshold` (config, e.g. 80); the two floors disagreed, so valid speech was recorded and then discarded.
- `hermes_cli/cli_chat_turn_mixin.py:261-266` — `_import_sounddevice()` was called as a prerequisite before `check_tts_requirements()`; on macOS it raises (TCC media-library prompt; `tools/tts_tool_speaker.py:191-198` deliberately returns False from `_device_usable()` on Darwin for this reason), and the bare `except: pass` silently left `use_streaming_tts` False.

## Tests

Red on base (`origin/main`, commit 98cceaef2b) — reproduced both defects before the fix:

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_voice_silence_threshold_stop.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_chat_turn_streaming_tts_arming.py
# base: 3 failed (arming gate: "streaming TTS must arm without sounddevice",
#        "the arm gate must not probe sounddevice", "no sounddevice probe on
#        the unarmed path") + 2 failed (threshold: peak 160 vs configured 80
#        discarded; reconfigured threshold not followed)
```

Green after the fix:

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_voice_silence_threshold_stop.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_chat_turn_streaming_tts_arming.py
# 2 files, 8 tests passed, 0 failed
```

Sibling suites covering the touched paths (all green, unchanged by the fix):

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_voice_mode.py tests/tools/test_voice_max_recording_seconds.py \
  tests/tools/test_voice_stop_phrase.py tests/hermes_cli/test_voice_wrapper.py
# 4 files, 77 passed, 0 failed (27 skipped: platform-gated linux/macos lanes + numpy-gated frames)
```

Notes on test design: the threshold tests fake captured frames as objects carrying exactly the attributes `stop()`/`_write_wav` touch (`__len__`, concatenation, `tobytes`) because numpy is absent from the test environment (`pytest.importorskip` in the older sibling tests skips them there for the same reason); they assert behavior (returned path vs `None` at a given configured threshold), never source text. The arming tests stub `_import_sounddevice` to raise the same OSError the import raises on macOS (CoreAudio TCC prompt) and assert the arm gate never calls it and the speaker thread still starts — the arm decision is data (the requirements probe), not host state, so no platform faking is needed; the macOS arm of the speaker *output policy* itself runs for real in `tests/tools/test_tts_macos_output.py` under `@pytest.mark.platforms`.

## Side effects

- **Who breaks if this is wrong?** Users with the default `silence_threshold: 200` see identical behavior (the constructor still defaults `_silence_threshold` to the same 200; the pinned test `test_stop_still_discards_below_default_threshold_without_config` guards this). macOS voice users gain streaming TTS back; Linux/Windows users are unchanged (`check_tts_requirements()` was already the real availability signal — the sounddevice probe only ever added a false negative on Darwin).
- **Fresh-install CI difference?** The tests need no numpy/sounddevice (the old sibling tests skip without them); CI runs them on every lane. The runtime change makes no new dependency demands — it removes one.
- **Does anything now behave differently for users NOT in the bug report?** A user who sets a *lower* threshold now keeps recordings the old code would have discarded — that is the fix; a user raising the threshold above 200 gets a *stricter* discard floor than before, consistent with their config and with what the VAD already did mid-recording.
- **Secretly a feature / broader than the bug?** No: both hunks are line-level corrections of the two defects in #84046. The `except: pass` → `logging.debug` change is observability for a path that was silently swallowing; it introduces no new surface.

## Self-review

- Secretly a feature? No — pure bug fix on the two reported defects.
- Secretly broader? No — `SILENCE_RMS_THRESHOLD`'s other uses (echo-guard/ambient floors in the full-duplex listener) are separate heuristics with their own calibration and are untouched. The silence-detection discard in `_should_auto_stop`/`_track_speech` already used `self._silence_threshold`.
- Tests are behavior contracts (returned WAV vs None at configured thresholds; speaker thread armed with sounddevice raising), not change-detectors, and never read source text.

## Supersedes

- #84099 (fix(voice): honor configured silence threshold on stop, by @CryptoDombili) — got the silence-threshold half exactly right: `stop()` now compares peak RMS against the configured `self._silence_threshold` and logs the effective floor, with a parameterized both-directions regression; our `voice_mode.py` hunk is the same fix and carries their Co-authored-by. Incomplete on the issue as a whole: it explicitly leaves the streaming-TTS arm gate (#84046's macOS half — `_import_sounddevice()` disabling arming via the swallowed `except`) out of scope, so macOS voice users would still lose sentence-by-sentence playback. This PR fixes both defects in #84046.

## Risk

0.30 · bug · surfaces: code, tests (per `triage risk`).

## Summary

WSL appends the entire Windows PATH (Desktop app, git, node dirs) to the Linux PATH as `/mnt/...` entries. `_build_wsl_interop_paths()` scraped **every** `/mnt/` entry into the generated systemd unit's `Environment=PATH`, so at gateway start each persisted dir forced a Plan 9 interop (9p) connection — enough heavy dirs and the 9p server connection limit is exhausted, wedging gateway startup. Interop only needs `powershell.exe`/`cmd.exe`/`explorer.exe`/`wsl.exe`, which are already covered by `which()`-resolution plus the hardcoded System32 family; the indiscriminate PATH scrape is removed.

## Fixes

- Fixes #73163

## Root cause

`hermes_cli/gateway.py:3016` (pre-fix): `candidates = [entry for entry in os.environ.get("PATH", "").split(os.pathsep) if entry.startswith("/mnt/")]` — indiscriminately persisted every Windows-derived PATH entry, including heavy Desktop-app/git/node dirs under `/mnt/d/` etc., into the gateway unit's `Environment=PATH`.

## Tests

- New `TestWslInteropPaths` in `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_service.py`:
  - `test_arbitrary_mount_entries_are_not_scraped_from_shell_path` (is_wsl patched true, PATH with `/mnt/d/heavy-app/bin` etc.): **red on base** —
    `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_service.py -k TestWslInteropPaths` failed with `assert ['/mnt/d/heav.../desktop/bin'] == []` (3 extra items scraped from PATH); **green after** the fix.
  - `test_which_resolved_tool_dirs_and_system32_set_are_included`: `which()`-resolved Windows tool dirs and the hardcoded System32 set (existence-gated, deduped) are still included; already-present entries are not duplicated.
  - `test_outside_wsl_nothing_is_added`: non-WSL hosts get nothing.
- Full touched file green after fix: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_service.py` → **109 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped**.
- Gates: `uvx ruff check hermes_cli/gateway.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_service.py` clean; `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py hermes_cli/gateway.py` clean (the one `utf-8` finding in the test file is pre-existing on base, line 2525→2595, untouched by this PR). No new `shutil.which` usage or subprocess changes, so the conditional gates do not apply.

## Side effects

- **Does anything in this change break a user whose setup isn't CI's (fresh install, local backend)?** No. The only removed behavior is the persistence of arbitrary `/mnt/` shell-PATH entries into generated units. Those entries were never needed for interop: the same function still resolves `powershell.exe`/`cmd.exe`/`explorer.exe`/`wsl.exe` via `which()` and appends the hardcoded System32 family, so `powershell.exe`/`cmd.exe` keep working in generated units.
- **Does a user lose a workflow they had before?** Only in the narrow sense that a gateway unit previously inherited e.g. `/mnt/c/Program Files/Git/cmd` in its PATH — Windows-side tools the agent invoked *by bare name from within the gateway process* would now resolve only if they are interop executables covered above, or if the user adds the dir explicitly. That inheritance is exactly the defect (9p connection-limit exhaustion at gateway start), and tools the gateway legitimately shells out to (PowerShell, cmd) are still covered by `which()` + System32.
- **Does it change what's persisted or regenerated?** Units are regenerated/diffed on every start/restart/status (`refresh_systemd_unit_if_needed`); after this fix a regeneration **drops** the scraped `/mnt/` entries from `Environment=PATH` — that is the intended repair and it applies fleet-wide on the next refresh, per the existing unit-regeneration machinery. No other persisted state changes.
- **Fresh-install / first-run behavior:** unchanged outside WSL (`is_wsl()` gate, returns `[]`); on WSL, generated units are strictly smaller-PATHed and interop still works via the same resolution paths as before (those were always appended too, and now dedupe against the caller's existing entries).

## Self-review

- Secretly a feature? No — a pure defect fix removing an overbroad PATH scrape; the function's contract (persist interop tool dirs) is preserved via the two pre-existing, more precise mechanisms.
- Secretly broader? No — single function, single call site (`generate_systemd_unit`), the dedupe/existence-gate logic and everything else in the unit-generation path is untouched.

## Risk

- Score: **0.30** (`[risk 0.30]`), kind: **bug**, surfaces: **code, tests** — no critical flags (`triage risk --issue 73163`).


## Supersedes

- **#73174** (ygd58) — got the diagnosis and the fix right: same function, same removal of the indiscriminate `/mnt/` PATH scrape, same rationale (Plan 9 round-trips per persisted dir; hardcoded System32 + `which()` cover every interop need), with its own red→green regression tests. It is superseded only because it has not been touched since 2026-08-03 and now conflicts with current `main` in both files (`hermes_cli/gateway.py` — the scrape line was reformatted to a list comprehension; `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_wsl.py` — main added `subprocess`/`Path` imports and new WSL status tests around its hunks). This PR carries the same fix rebased on current main, verified red→green there, and credits the approach via `Co-authored-by: ygd58`.

## What does this PR do?

The installer now puts `~/.local/bin` on PATH for login-bash users whose only startup file is `~/.bash_login`. A login bash reads only the first of `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`, `~/.profile`, so the `~/.profile` line the installer always wrote was hidden by an existing `~/.bash_login` and `hermes` came back "not found" in new terminals.

`~/.bash_login` is handled like `~/.bash_profile`: the guarded PATH line is appended when the file exists, and the file is never created (creating `~/.bash_profile` would shadow it).

## Related Issue

Found while closing #97401 (macOS Bash PATH), whose premise no longer held on main except for this one rare case. No public issue.

Fixes #

## Changes Made

items.body:
## Summary

`kanban_show` advertises `task_id` as optional and its description invites any agent to
(re)orient itself with a bare call — but outside a dispatcher-spawned worker there is no
default task, and the bare call was rejected with `task_id is required (or set
HERMES_KANBAN_TASK in the env)`, an env var a chat caller cannot set. Every kanban-enabled
profile that also chats hit this on its first turn (#91431). Now:

- **`kanban_show` (a read):** a bare call outside a worker returns a JSON payload
  (`{"current_task": null, "hint": "..."}`) pointing at `kanban_list` to discover task
  ids — an answer, not an error.
- **`kanban_comment` / mutation & lifecycle tools** (they need a real target, so a bare
  call stays an error): the rejection now names `kanban_list` and an explicit
  `task_id` instead of the env var. The comment handler's misleading "pulls from env
  but kept explicit here" text is gone — it never read the env.
- **Sibling case covered:** when `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` *is* present but not owned by this
  session (delegate child, cron run beside a worker), the rejection explains why the
  inherited task is not a valid default.
- **Schemas:** `task_id` descriptions now state that the env default only exists for a
  dispatcher-spawned worker, and `kanban_show`'s description says what a bare call
  returns outside one.

## Fixes #91431

## Root cause

- `tools/kanban_tools_schemas.py:6-9` — `_DESC_TASK_ID_DEFAULT` promised an env default
  unconditionally; `:43-57` — `KANBAN_SHOW_SCHEMA` marked `required: []` with an
  "orient yourself" description, inviting the bare call.
- `tools/kanban_tools.py:199-202` — `_require_task_id` rejected the bare call with the
  env-var remedy; `:637-640` — `_handle_show` called it directly, so the read path
  errored instead of answering; `:913-919` — `_handle_comment` had the same shape
  (its message even claimed an env pull that never happened).

## Tests

Red on base (all four failed with the old error / old description):
`unset PYTHONPATH && scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_kanban_tools.py -k "bare_call or task_id_descriptions"`

Green after the fix (same command), plus full files:

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_kanban_tools.py` — 48 passed
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_kanban_complete_parents_tool.py tests/tools/test_kanban_descendant_scope.py` — 5 passed
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_kanban_persisted_identity.py tests/tools/test_kanban_redaction.py` — 7 passed

New tests are behavior contracts (handler output shapes and cross-references between
schema description and stated behavior), not source-text readers: they call the real
handlers against an isolated `HERMES_HOME` board and inspect returned JSON.

## Side effects

- **Fresh install / CI:** no new deps, no config, no env vars; handlers and schemas only.
  The fresh-install surface (worker happy paths) is covered by the existing tests above,
  all green.
- **Remote backend (`hermes serve` with Desktop attached — the reporter's setup):**
  kanban tool dispatch is unchanged for dispatcher-spawned workers (env default still
  resolves); non-worker chat profiles now get a structured hint instead of an error —
  strictly less noise, no behavior removed.
- **Existing callers that match on the old error strings** (`"task_id is required (or set
  HERMES_KANBAN_TASK"`): searched the tree — no code or test matches those strings;
  the only consumer of the message was the model reading it.
- **Prompt caching:** schema strings change, which changes the tool-schema portion of the
  prompt — that happens on every release that touches any schema and is not a
  mid-conversation mutation; cached conversations continue on their old prefix.
- **Workers mid-run:** `_require_task_id`'s env-present path (delegate child / cron beside
  a worker) previously produced the same generic rejection; it now says why. No tool that
  succeeded before fails now — the only changed outcomes are error→hint (show) and
  error→better-error (comment/mutations).

## Self-review

Not secretly a feature: the bare-call hint is exactly the issue's suggested fix (option 1 +
2 combined). Not broader than the cluster: only `kanban_show`'s bare path, the
required-task rejection messages, and the schema descriptions changed; gating, ownership
enforcement, run-lifecycle guards, and every happy path are untouched. One judgment call:
`kanban_show` returns a hint payload rather than auto-running `kanban_list`, so no board
mutation or surprising fan-out happens on a read — the agent still chooses to list.

## Risk

0.30 · bug · surfaces: code, tests. Human-facing tool error text + one read handler's
bare-call path; no install/update, launch, or UI surfaces.


## Supersedes

- **#91466** (frizikk) — got a real gap right that ours missed: `_default_task_id` treated a whitespace-only or non-string `task_id` (`" "`, `12345`) as a fallback trigger instead of a value, so `kanban_show(task_id="  ")` in a worker silently resolved to the env task. Their hardening (coerce via `str().strip()`, strip the env value too) is cherry-picked onto this branch as commit `c531a45b64` with authorship preserved (Jakub Wolniewicz); their 3 regression tests ride along (`TestDefaultTaskId`). Their PR alone covered only the whitespace edge, not the issue's core unactionable-error — folded into ours rather than landed separately.
- **#91441** (Ahmett101) — right core direction: a no-arg `kanban_show` outside a worker returns the board listing so the caller can pick a task. Superseded because: (1) it makes `kanban_comment` *default to the env task* for workers — main's `kanban_comment` deliberately takes `task_id` explicitly (the "pulls from env" claim in its old error text was false), so that half changes behavior the issue did not ask for; (2) it carries ~150 lines of unrelated formatting churn across the whole file; (3) its worker `fallback`+`hint` payload shape differs from ours, and it has been untouched since 2026-08-21, conflicting with current main in both files. Our hint payload (`current_task`/`hint` → `kanban_list`) covers the same need on the read path without mutating comment semantics.
- **#114521** (patrykkopycinski) — adjacent, not competing: recognizes the `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` placeholder *pasted as a task_id value* (a different failure mode from the missing-arg one #91431 reports; their own PR says so). Clean against main and out of this PR's scope — recommend treating it as a separate follow-up PR on top of whichever fix lands here, since it touches the same `_default_task_id`/`_handle_comment` region.
