items.title: Desktop app is no longer rebuilt on updates that don't move HEAD

items.body:
When a memory provider moved out of core can't be recovered, the user is now told — in the terminal, in Desktop, or with the first reply on a messaging platform — instead of quietly running without external memory. `hermes update` asks the dependency questions once for all profiles and names the profile on every line.

**Stacked on #131266** (headless migration consent): this branch carries its commits; merge #131266 first.

Before this, the agent-start recovery (`recover_at_startup`) wrote installed / refused / failed / not-in-catalog to `agent.log` only. So did a selected provider that reports unavailable. With `security.allow_lazy_installs: false`, offline, or a declined dependency prompt, the session ran without external memory and the terminal said nothing.

## What changed
- **Startup outcomes are shown.** `recover_at_startup(name, say=…)` reports through the agent's new `_emit_startup_warning`. The CLI prints the line. Other drivers get a sticky `AgentNotice`, because Desktop shows notices as toasts but drops warn-kind `status.update`. The messaging gateway wires `notice_callback` per turn, after `__init__`, so the notice is held and sent on turn 1. A provider that reports unavailable uses the same sink.
- **`hermes update` across profiles** (`migrate_all_homes`):
  - Every line names its profile (`[profile 'work-a'] …`) and gives the exact `hermes -p <profile> plugins install <name>` command. `-p` is dropped only for the default home when no sticky profile is set, so a hint printed by an agent started for a named profile (Desktop, the gateway, `hermes -p work`) never installs into another profile.
  - Homes that share one environment get one set of dependency answers per provider (`shared_dependency_answers` in `plugins_cmd_install`). The first install asks the usual Python *and* Node questions, with the same disclosure and gate as `hermes plugins install`. Later homes reuse those answers.
  - Homes are grouped by provider and by their own unattended consent (#131266: each home's `security.allow_lazy_installs`). If you decline or an install fails, one line lists the rest of that group, instead of N clones that each fail or ask again; other groups still migrate. A default home with lazy installs off no longer marks a lazy-on profile as failed. The "answers apply to all of them" header only appears when a terminal can ask. Ctrl-C ends the migration with a message.
- **Unavailable-provider warning per profile:** it was deduped by provider name for the whole process, so a multiplexed gateway or Desktop backend told only the first profile. It is now once per (home, provider).
- **Install declined:** a first-time install refused at the consent gate said "Reinstall declined … The installed plugin and active environment are unchanged". It now says "Install declined: … Nothing was installed." A real reinstall keeps the old text.
- **Wording** (#124038): the success line no longer says `memory.<name>` settings are unchanged, since Hindsight never reads `config.yaml`. The docs now say where Hindsight reads its config, checked against the pinned vendor plugin source. The `.` doubled before "Run …" is gone.

## Validation
Live, real processes: worktree on `PYTHONPATH`, isolated `HERMES_HOME`, real catalog entry and real hindsight clone, real OpenRouter turn. Each case ran against `origin/main` first and then this branch:

| Case | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `hermes chat --oneshot`, hindsight configured, `allow_lazy_installs: false` | 0 terminal lines (agent.log only) | 1 ⚠ line with `hermes plugins install hindsight` |
| same, lazy on, consent prompt answered `n` | 0 terminal lines after the prompt | 1 ⚠ line with the error and the command |
| same, answered `y` (install succeeds) | — | ✓ line, plugin installed, then the `reports unavailable` ⚠ (no credentials) on the terminal (log-only on main) |
| real `AIAgent`, telegram shape (callbacks wired after init), 2 turns | 0 memory events | 1 warn notice, delivered on turn 1, not repeated |
| real `AIAgent`, tui shape (callbacks at construction) | 0 | 1 warn notice at init, not repeated |
| real `tui_gateway` `session.create` + `prompt.submit` | — | `notification.show` frame, `level: warn`, `kind: sticky` |
| `migrate_all_homes()` under a PTY, 3 profiles, answer `n` | 3 prompts, 3 identical unlabelled ⚠ lines | 1 prompt, 1 labelled ⚠ line + 1 line with `hermes -p work-a/work-b …` commands, no clones for the other 2 |
| same, answer `y` | — | 1 prompt, 3 labelled ✓ lines, plugin installed in all 3 homes |

Review follow-ups, live on head `2944330adc9` vs the pre-fix head, with no TTY, the real catalog entry and a real PM install:

| Case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| update, default `allow_lazy_installs: false`, work-a `true` | `RESULT []`; work-a reported "not installed … either", `PRESENT work-a False` | `RESULT ['hindsight']`, default refused with its command, `PRESENT work-a True` |
| control: default `true`, work-a `false` | — | `RESULT ['hindsight']`, default installed, work-a refused with `hermes -p work-a …` |
| default `false`, work-a + work-b `true` | — | `RESULT ['hindsight', 'hindsight']`, both lazy-on profiles installed |
| agent start in `profiles/work`, lazy off | hint `hermes plugins install hindsight` | hint `hermes -p work plugins install hindsight` |
| default home, sticky profile `work-a` | `hermes plugins install hindsight` | `hermes -p default plugins install hindsight` |
| default home, no sticky profile | `hermes plugins install hindsight` | unchanged |
| unavailable warning, 2 homes × 2 calls in one process | 1 warning | 2 warnings (one per home) |
| update under a real PTY, 3 profiles, answer `n` | — | 1 prompt, header shown, 1 ⚠ line + 1 line naming work-a/work-b with `-p` commands |

Real `~/.hermes/plugins` was the same before and after the probes.

Tests: 2 more invariant tests for the review follow-ups (a refusal in one profile does not skip a lazy-on profile; the startup hint carries `-p` for a named profile). Both fail against the pre-fix `memory_provider_migration.py` and pass here. The 95 memory/plugin/catalog/gateway-notice files: **872 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped**. Earlier: 4 new invariant tests: CLI prints the refusal; the gateway replays it once; one prompt for N homes with profile labels; a decline names the remaining profiles once. Run against `origin/main` sources they fail 4/4; on this branch they pass. Relevant agent/gateway/memory suites: 423 passed. The `tests/hermes_cli` plugin/memory files have 24 failures under the local real-HOME harness, and the same 24 fail on `origin/main`.

## Credits
Salvages and supersedes three contributor PRs:
- #119775 by @Wenfengcheng — the startup warning sink and profile-labelled update lines (both commits cherry-picked, authorship kept).
- #125067 by @Sahilvishnaliya — the honest migration wording and the docs warning (cherry-picked, authorship kept; the closing trailer was changed to a reference because #124038's broader config-source question stays open).
- #125871 by @chelsealong — one consent per update across profiles. Redone smaller as `shared_dependency_answers`: the reused answers come from the normal Python/Node prompts, so Node sidecars are still disclosed and the per-plugin gate is unchanged. This addresses the review blocker on that PR. Credited via `Co-authored-by`.

Fixes #119769. Fixes #125794. Refs #124038.

items.title: fix(memory): never lose memory silently when a provider moves out of core

items.body:
Supermemory no longer ships inside Hermes. It installs from the plugin catalog under the same name, and existing setups move over automatically with their settings unchanged. Holographic, RetainDB, ByteRover, Mem0, OpenViking and Honcho stay bundled.

**Merge order:** this PR must land after #131266 (headless consent for the migration's dependency install). The catalog entry is already on main (`plugin-catalog/supermemory.yaml` → `supermemoryai/hermes-supermemory` @ `91405dd`). The catalog plugin declares the Supermemory SDK as a Python dependency, and without #131266 the migration on current main refuses to install it when there is no TTY. See the live evidence below.

**Re-scoped:** an earlier revision of this PR also removed retaindb, byterover and holographic. That part is dropped. Only supermemory leaves core here.

## Changes
- **Removed** `plugins/memory/supermemory` (−722 LOC). `hermes_cli/memory_provider_migration.py` is untouched. It only takes effect once the bundled copy is gone, because bundled providers win in `find_provider_dir`.
- **Build:** dropped the `hermes-agent[supermemory]` extra, its exclude-newer row and the `pm/extras.py` anchor. The catalog plugin declares its SDK in its own pyproject. `uv lock` removed only `supermemory`. A recorded selection that names the extra is filtered by `pm.install._still_declared`. The `mem0` extra and its win-arm64 gate stay.
- **Prose:** CONTRIBUTING (en/es; the es copy also drops the stale hindsight entry), `plugins/AGENTS.md`, the `memory.provider` default comment and `hermes memory --help` now list supermemory as a catalog provider.
- **Tests:** deleted `test_supermemory_provider.py` and the supermemory cases in the shared suites: BOM config reads, PM SDK admission, multiplex identity scope, provider threads, plugin-family secret scope and cron `agent_context`. The other providers' cases in those suites are unchanged. No existing assertion about another provider was changed.
- **Docs:** `memory-providers.md` gives Supermemory a "Plugin catalog" note, adds `hermes plugins install supermemory` to its setup steps, and adds a "Migrating from bundled Supermemory" section modelled on the Hindsight one. memory.md, overview.md, integrations/index.md, cli-commands.md and the developer guide are corrected.
- Kept on purpose, because the catalog copy still uses them: the `SUPERMEMORY_*` env hints, the API-key redaction and `tests/_fixtures/env_filter.py`.

## Validation
Live E2E ran real processes on a fake HOME/HERMES_HOME. Only the runtime store was shared. The live-catalog cache was empty, so lookups used the in-tree catalog. There were seven homes. The default home had `memory.provider: supermemory`. Five profiles each named one of retaindb, byterover, holographic, mem0 or openviking. One profile named `vaporware`. Every home had a `memory.<name>.probe_marker` setting.

| Check | origin/main | This PR alone | This PR + #131266 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `migrate_all_homes()` (the `hermes update` hook) | `installed=[]` in 0.1s (bundled copy wins) | `installed=[]` and `⚠ … dependency install skipped (non-interactive)` | `installed=['supermemory']` in 12.3s, `✓ Memory provider 'supermemory' moved out of core …` |
| supermemory home after migration | bundled `plugins.memory.supermemory` | not present; config untouched | plugin in `<home>/plugins/supermemory`, enabled, `memory.provider` and `memory.supermemory` settings unchanged |
| retaindb / byterover / holographic / mem0 / openviking homes | bundled | bundled, nothing installed (5/5) | bundled, nothing installed, settings unchanged (5/5) |
| Loader resolves supermemory | `plugins.memory.supermemory.SupermemoryMemoryProvider` | `None` | `_hermes_user_memory.supermemory__source_<digest>.SupermemoryMemoryProvider` |
| Second `migrate_all_homes()` | — | — | `installed=[]` in 0.1s (idempotent) |
| `memory.provider: vaporware` | `⚠ … not in the plugin catalog …` | same | same; config untouched |
| First agent start, real `AIAgent()` in a fresh home with `memory.provider: supermemory` and a key in `.env` | — | — | installs from the catalog; `Memory provider 'supermemory' registered (8 tools)` and `… activated`. Run in the PM environment the plugin's deps went into, the SDK imports and `hermes memory status` shows `Plugin: installed ✓  Status: available ✓`. The probe endpoint is unreachable on purpose, so the summary reads `✗ Connection error.`. That proves the SDK client honours `base_url` from `supermemory.json`. |
| Same with `security.allow_lazy_installs: false` | — | — | `Memory provider 'supermemory' is not installed; security.allow_lazy_installs is off — run \`hermes plugins install supermemory\`.`; nothing installed; agent starts without external memory |
| Recorded PM extras `['supermemory', 'mem0', 'honcho']` | — | `_still_declared` keeps `['mem0', 'honcho']` | — |

Unit tests: 388 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped across `tests/plugins/memory`, `tests/openviking_plugin`, `tests/plugins/test_secret_scope_plugin_families.py`, `tests/agent/test_memory_{agent_context,provider}.py`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_memory_provider_migration.py`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_memory_setup_env_denylist.py` and `tests/test_project_metadata.py`. `tests/pm` plus the upgrade entrypoint suite gave 908 passed and 1 failed. That failure is `test_cold_runtime_e2e.py[python3.11]`, and it fails the same way on origin/main in this environment. `ruff`, `uv lock --check`, `git diff --check`, the tmp-literal, Windows-footgun and doc-link checks are clean. The real `~/.hermes/plugins` and `~/.hermes/profiles` were unchanged after the probes.

items.body:
Every request to a llama.cpp server fails with HTTP 400 "failed to parse grammar" because the clarify tool schema carries `maxLength: 8000`, and llama.cpp rejects bounded repetition of 2000 or more.

Closes #131278.

## What happened

The clarify tool's `choices` items schema set `maxLength` to 8000 (commit a4c31d592b9). llama.cpp's json-schema-to-grammar converter expands `maxLength`/`minLength`/`maxItems`/`minItems` into bounded repetitions and rejects anything at 2000 or more. The tool list is sent on every request, so every request to a llama.cpp server fails with "Failed to initialize samplers: failed to parse grammar", whatever the user asked. The reporter's bisect (see Credit) pinned the cutoff at 1999 working and 2000 failing.

## Change

This PR touches two files.

- `tools/clarify_tool.py`: the `choices` items schema no longer sets `maxLength`. The runtime over-limit check on choices is untouched, so the limit is still enforced.
- `tests/tools/test_schema_sanitizer.py`: two new tests, `test_clarify_schema_has_no_unbounded_repetition_keyword` (the clarify schema carries no length bound of 2000 or more) and `test_registered_tool_schemas_stay_inside_llama_cpp_repetition_limit` (no registered built-in tool ships a length or count bound of 2000 or more).

`tools/schema_sanitizer.py` is not changed. An earlier version of this PR also extended the grammar-failure recovery strip there; that was removed to keep the PR narrow.

## Credit

- @yasu224 for the bisect that isolated 1999 vs 2000 and found the cause in #131278.

## Verification

Ran on Python 3.12 at 13c84d34: `tests/tools/test_schema_sanitizer.py` and `tests/tools/test_clarify_tool.py`, 68 passed.

- Not run: the full suite, ruff, and a real llama.cpp server.
- Diff is two files: the schema line and the two new tests.

## Maintainer notes

- #124164 also edits `tools/clarify_tool.py` (reject clarify choices over the renderer cap), so one of the two PRs may need a small rebase.
- #130076 widens the classifier match for "failed to parse grammar" in `agent/error_classifier.py`. This PR does not touch that; it removes the trigger.

items.body:
Honcho memory now installs from Plastic Labs' plugin in the catalog instead of shipping inside Hermes. Homes still set to `memory.provider: honcho` get the catalog plugin installed on their next `hermes update` or agent start. Their `honcho.json` / `~/.honcho/config.json`, host blocks, peers and session mappings are read unchanged.

**Land after #131266.** Honcho declares Python deps, and on current main the unattended migration (Desktop, gateway, scripted `hermes update`) refuses the install at the dependency-consent gate. I reproduced that on this branch (table below). #131266 is what lets those deps through for migrations.

## What changed

- **Removed the bundled provider.** That's `plugins/memory/honcho/` (17 files, 7.2k lines), its tests (`tests/honcho_plugin/` plus 9 honcho-only test files) and `evals/memory/honcho_current_query.py`. The catalog entry (`plugin-catalog/honcho.yaml` → `plastic-labs/honcho` subdir `hermes-plugin-honcho` @ `f014a64`) is already on main and in the live catalog. Since bundled copies win in `find_provider_dir`, deleting this copy is what switches it on.
- **Removed the dependency wiring.** That means the `honcho` extra and its `termux` inclusion, `honcho-ai` in `[tool.uv] exclude-newer-package`, `uv.lock` (`honcho-ai` dropped, nothing else), `pm/extras.py`, `nix/packages.nix`, and the nix checks/examples (`honcho` → `exa`/`voice`). The plugin declares `honcho-ai>=2.2.0,<3` in its own pyproject, and PM installs it.
- **Untangled honcho-specific code in core:**
  - `doctor`: dropped `_memory_provider_honcho`, which reached into the plugin's `HonchoClientConfig` / client cache. Honcho now gets the same generic check as every catalog provider: load it, then `is_available()`.
  - `doctor`: dropped `_honcho_is_configured_for_doctor`, the gate for a `honcho` toolset that no longer exists.
  - `plugins/memory/__init__.py`: dropped the `honcho_command` fallback. Plugin CLI handlers resolve as `<provider>_command` only.
  - `web_server_config`: if memory-provider discovery fails, the fallback no longer offers `honcho`.
- **Telemetry:** the bounded memory-provider label was the `plugins/memory/` directory listing, so a provider that moved to the catalog collapsed into `plugin`. `honcho` would have, and `hindsight` already had. `MEMORY_PROVIDERS` now also accepts public catalog names. Any other third-party provider still reports as `plugin`.
- **Kept on purpose: host-side code the catalog plugin still relies on.** These pieces already resolve the plugin's modules through `import_provider_module` (from #119872), so they work against the catalog copy. I verified each one live below:
  - the `honcho_host_block` config storage kind; the plugin's `config_schema.py` imports it from core
  - the Desktop host-block writer
  - `hermes profile create --clone` (per-profile host block)
  - `hermes profile rename` (host-block migration, which keeps the AI peer)
  - the post-update host sync
  - the reserved `honcho` subcommand/profile name
  - `HONCHO_*` env hints and the `honcho:` config section (the plugin reads it)
- **Docs and copy:**
  - `memory-providers.md`, `honcho.md`, CLI reference, overview/integration pages, nix guide, `.env.example`, `cli-config.yaml.example`, the honcho optional skill and its generated page, `plugins/AGENTS.md`
  - `hermes memory` help text
  - tip `t200` in all 17 locales: Honcho moves from "bundled" to "via hermes plugins install"
  - links to the old in-tree README now point to the plugin's repo
- **Old-updater compat surface.** The frozen surface listed six `plugins.memory.honcho.*` names as bare (unguarded). I moved them to `guarded_only` after checking every old updater path:
  - All 1,028 historical blobs of `main.py`, `update_cmd.py`, `update_cmd_maint.py` and `profile_cmd.py` that import `plugins.memory.honcho.cli`: every call sits inside `try/except Exception` or `with suppress(Exception)`. The only unguarded call is in `cmd_honcho` (the `hermes honcho` command), which updaters never run.
  - The audit script didn't count `contextlib.suppress` as a guard; it does now (new test, red on base).
  - A full history re-audit at the recorded cutoff (`d595e636c83`) then classifies `cli::sync_honcho_profiles_quiet` as guarded.
  - The five `client::*` names are only reached through that guarded call (they're `cli.py`'s own imports). The audit doesn't carry a call-site guard into the callee, so it still lists them as bare.
  - The re-audit is history-only and would drop the tree half of the checked-in superset, so I didn't swap the whole file in. The JSON diff is just those six moves.
- **Tests that used the bundled package to exercise core seams now use small fixtures.** The host-block router tests install a `hostprov` user plugin that spells out the four names core needs from a `honcho_host_block` provider. The cwd test uses a recording provider. The seeded-branch title test keeps its core provenance assertions.

## Validation

Live E2E with imports from the worktree first on `PYTHONPATH` (`hermes_cli from: …/.worktrees/L5-honcho-removal/hermes_cli/__init__.py`), a temp `HOME`/`HERMES_HOME`, and the real catalog clone of `plastic-labs/honcho` at `f014a64`. In the positive runs I swapped PM publication for a move (`PROBE_PM_FREE`) so the shared venv was never touched. That swap also skips the consent gate #131266 lifts.

| case | result |
|---|---|
| bundled `plugins/memory/honcho` present | `False` |
| `find_provider_dir("honcho")` before | `None` |
| `migrate_home` (update path) | `honcho` — "moved out of core — installed its plugin from the catalog" |
| `find_provider_dir` after | `<home>/plugins/honcho` |
| `load_memory_provider("honcho")` | `HonchoMemoryProvider`, `is_available()` = `True` |
| config continuity | workspace=`probe-ws`, peer=`probe-user`, host=`hermes`, from the pre-existing `honcho.json` |
| install record | revision = catalog.pin = `f014a64306b` |
| declared schema via core contract | storage `honcho_host_block`, 33 fields |
| core router host-block write | `hosts.hermes.sessionStrategy = per-repo`, workspace kept |
| plugin CLI | `['honcho']` registered |
| doctor | `✓ honcho provider active` |
| `hermes profile create coder --clone` | "Honcho config cloned (peer: coder)" → host blocks `hermes`, `hermes_coder` |
| `hermes profile rename coder writer` | "Honcho host updated: hermes_coder → hermes_writer", aiPeer `coder` kept |
| `recover_at_startup` (agent-init path) | `True`, plugin installed |
| negative: `allow_lazy_installs: false` | `recover_at_startup` → `False`, nothing installed, one-liner logged |
| negative: provider not in catalog | "not installed and not in the plugin catalog", 0 install calls |
| negative: this branch without #131266, non-TTY | refused: "dependency install skipped (non-interactive)" |
| real `~/.hermes/plugins` before/after | unchanged |

Tests:
- 1,887 passed / 0 failed across 139 files: every test file that mentions honcho, plus `tests/plugins`, memory provider/migration, plugins_cmd and profiles.
- `test_web_server.py` + discovery: 203 passed.
- Audit tests: 15 passed; the new suppress test is red on base.
- `ruff`, `check_no_tmp_literals`, `check-windows-footguns --all`, `git diff --check` and `check_doc_links` all clean.

Not covered: Honcho cloud traffic (no real key), the OAuth device flow, and a nix build. PM installing `honcho-ai` into a real profile env is now covered (review follow-ups table).

## Review follow-ups (b404d549f2f)

An independent review of `58b3ea95891` found no defects in the removal itself. These commits address the findings that belong in this PR:

- **The recovery path now names the fix.** When `memory.provider: honcho` is set but the plugin isn't installed (offline, lazy installs off, or a failed migration), every place a user looks used to point somewhere useless (`hermes memory setup`, `~/.hermes/plugins/`, or "not a hermes command"). Doctor, `hermes memory status`, `hermes memory setup honcho` and `hermes honcho …` now print `hermes [-p <profile>] plugins install honcho`. This works for any catalog memory provider. The lookup reads the in-tree catalog only, so it makes no network call. `-p` is added whenever a bare command would install into a different profile: a named profile, or the default home while another profile is sticky.
- **The core host-block writer has its invariant test again.** `_write_provider_honcho` stays in core, and the deleted honcho test covered it. A new test checks the same invariant against the `hostprov` fixture: a config that exists but doesn't parse is left byte-for-byte untouched (400, `memory.provider` unchanged), and a parseable config is merged with other hosts' keys kept. The test is red when the strict read is mutated into a tolerant one.
- **zh-Hans docs** no longer point at `plugins/memory/honcho`. The memory-providers page gets the English catalog note, install row and "Upgrading from the bundled Honcho" section, plus catalog wording in tools/tools-reference. The plugin's `cli.py` link is now a `blob/` URL (also fixed in the English developer guide).

Behaviour change for release notes: `hermes doctor` used to run a Honcho-specific config and connection check. Honcho now gets the generic check like every catalog provider: the plugin loads, then `is_available()`.

| review follow-up, live (worktree imports: `hermes_cli` from `…/.worktrees/FB2-honcho-review-fixes`; `./hermes` launcher for the install and post-install runs; temp HOME; real in-tree catalog) | result |
|---|---|
| default home, not installed: doctor / memory status / memory setup honcho / `hermes honcho status` | each prints `hermes plugins install honcho` |
| `profiles/work`, not installed: doctor / memory status / `hermes -p work honcho status` | each prints `hermes -p work plugins install honcho` |
| sticky profile `work`, `hermes -p default memory status` | `hermes -p default plugins install honcho` |
| ran the exact hint doctor printed, `hermes -p work plugins install honcho --enable` (TTY, consent y) | installed in 15 s into `profiles/work/plugins/honcho`; `honcho-ai 2.5.1` in the profile's PM env; default home untouched |
| after install: doctor / memory status / `hermes honcho status` | install hint gone; `honcho configured but not available` + `✗ HONCHO_API_KEY` (no key in the probe); `hermes honcho status` runs the plugin's command |
| negative: `memory.provider: nosuch` | doctor `run: hermes memory setup`, status `Install the 'nosuch' memory plugin to ~/.hermes/plugins/`, `hermes nosuch` has no install line |
| negative: typo `hermes honcoh` | plain "not a `hermes` command", no install line |
| new tests on the pre-fix sources | 2/2 hint tests fail; the host-block test fails under the tolerant-read mutation |
| targeted suite (56 files: migration, web_server, doctor, memory_setup, parser/UX, tests/plugins/memory) | 711 passed, 0 failed, 11 skipped |
| real `~/.hermes/plugins` before/after | unchanged |

## Follow-ups for Plastic Labs (not blocking)

- **Tests.** This PR deletes about 11k lines of honcho tests, and `hermes-plugin-honcho` at `f014a64` ships none. That includes the cross-profile isolation regressions (client-singleton bleed across profiles, the per-profile OAuth loopback flow, network isolation). Porting at least the multiplex/isolation tests into `hermes-plugin-honcho/tests` with CI there should come before the next re-pin. The deleted files are recoverable from `58b3ea95891^`.
- **Dependency range.** Core pinned `honcho-ai==2.2.0`. The plugin declares `>=2.2.0,<3`, and a fresh install resolves 2.5.1.

- At `f014a64`, the compat arm in `__init__.__getattr__` imports `hermes_cli.plugin_compat.warn_once`, which core removed. It's only hit when an old private name is accessed.
- The plugin lacks core's UTF-8-BOM-tolerant reads in `cli.py` / `session_migration.py`.

## Credits

The catalog-copy resolver this relies on landed in #119872. @erosika's #116469 / #116566 (Desktop + host contract for catalog memory providers) cover more ground and are not superseded by this PR.

## Infographic

![Honcho moves to the plugin catalog](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aacbbdc/c5T0WVrKTSjpMJNa4OfhY_W8y7gbG6.png)

items.body:
Salvages the PTY liveness probe from #76768 (@webtecnica, first submitter for #76759) onto current main, plus follow-ups that end the leaked helpers and keep teardown within its time budgets.

## What was wrong
The dashboard frees a PTY session only on EOF or after the detached TTL (30 min). EOF never arrives when a helper the TUI started still holds the PTY slave: after the TUI is SIGKILLed or OOM-killed, or after it exits on SIGHUP while a helper ignores it. The registry slot stays taken until the TTL.

The helper itself is never signalled at all. `close()` signalled the process group only while the leader was alive, and looked the group up from the leader at close time.

## What changes
1. **`b3ac293084` (@webtecnica):** `reap_idle` also frees a session whose bridge reports the process dead (`PtyBridge.is_alive()`).
   - This is the liveness-probe subset of #76768.
   - Dropped from #76768: the `HERMES_PTY_*` env vars (non-secret settings belong in `config.yaml`), the 5-minute TTL and the cap changes, which are separate behaviour decisions.
   - Registry pops keep `pop(key, None)` from `5ddc5b6b0e`.
2. **`4233166702`:** `PtyBridge` records the process-group id at spawn. After the leader is gone, `close()` handles the rest of the group:
   - **Group already sent SIGHUP while the leader lived:** it only waits for the group to exit, then sends SIGKILL. The TUI gateway in that group saves its sessions on SIGHUP within a 1.0 s grace (`tui_gateway/entry.py`), and a second SIGHUP or an early SIGKILL would cut that save short.
   - **Leader already dead on entry:** it sends SIGHUP, waits, then sends SIGKILL.

   Either way it stops on ESRCH. This commit also drops the duck-typed `_bridge_alive` wrapper; the keepalive test fake now implements `is_alive()`.
3. **`44fa961273`:**
   - `close_all()` closes sessions concurrently instead of one after another, so N sessions fit inside the backend's SIGTERM → SIGKILL budget (#111912).
   - A dead remnant is closed in the background, not under the registry-wide attach lock that every new chat waits on.
   - `close()` reads and discards PTY output while it waits.
     - On macOS a child stays in exit until its pending terminal output is read, and nothing else reads it during close, so the leader wasn't reaped within 0.5 s. The existing loop then escalated to SIGTERM on the whole group, killing the gateway's SIGHUP save mid-way.
     - This also happens on main.
4. **`a9a11f1e68`:**
   - The helper grace follows `HERMES_TUI_GATEWAY_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_S` + 0.5 s, bounded to 1.5–2.0 s; the wait after SIGKILL is 0.5 s.
   - `close_all()` also awaits closes already running in the background, and the registry holds those tasks.
   - The output drain sleeps on EOF instead of busy-looping.

## Evidence
Live probe on Linux (`python:3.12-slim`), with `4233166702`'s logic: real `PtyBridge.spawn` + `PtySessionRegistry`, `sh -c "trap '' HUP; sleep N & exec sleep N"`, SIGKILL the leader, run one `reap_idle()`, then `close_all()`.

| | slots after one reap | helper processes left |
|---|---|---|
| main | 1 | 1 (survives `close_all()` too) |
| this branch | 0 | 0 |

I couldn't re-run it on the final head because the local Docker daemon was down, so the Linux CI run is the check for commits 3–4. On macOS the slot is already freed on main, because the kernel revokes the PTY when the leader dies, but the helper survives there; the bridge tests cover that case.

## Tests (each fails with only the production file reverted to its previous version)
- `test_pty_session.py`:
  - a dead attached session is reaped, and a live one past the TTL is kept;
  - `close_all()` closes the next session while another close is still parked;
  - `close_all()` waits for closes already running in the background.
- `test_pty_bridge.py`:
  - a helper that ignores SIGHUP is gone after `close()` once its leader is SIGKILLed;
  - a helper that needs 0.6 s to save on SIGHUP still finishes. This fails with the old resend-SIGHUP / 0.5 s SIGKILL. Before the output drain it also failed every run on macOS.
- `test_pty_bridge.py`, `test_pty_session.py`, `test_pty_keepalive_ws.py`: 43 passed, 2 runs.
- ruff, `check-windows-footguns --all` and `git diff --check` are clean.

## Not included
- #119551 (reaping attached PTYs whose viewer is gone) edits the same predicate. Whichever lands second adds the `is_alive()` check to `_is_reapable`.
- The systemd `KillMode` / cgroup part of #76759 needs a maintainer decision.

Refs #76759. Supersedes #76768.

A failed Codex or Anthropic model-catalog fetch no longer replaces the account's verified catalog for an hour, so account-gated rows such as GPT-6 Astra come back as soon as discovery recovers.

Salvage of #130957 (@Froraut) and the Anthropic half of #121248 (@AhmetArif0, the earliest submission for this bug), with authorship kept on both commits.

## Changes

Salvages #108143 by @Xipong (first submitter for #108141). Their commit is cherry-picked with authorship preserved, plus one test-only follow-up.

## What was wrong
`tui_gateway/event_replay.py` measured each event's JSON size when stamping it, then kept the caller's live `params` dict in the replay ring. Changing that dict afterwards changed what replay returned, and the change was never counted against the per-session/process byte budget.

Probe on main: the counted size stayed at 71 bytes while replay returned the same object, now holding 1 MB (`bytes 71 71 len 1000000 same True`).

## What changes
- **`e8ec71a580` (@Xipong):** the ring stores the frozen UTF-8 JSON bytes it already produced for sizing.
  - `events_since` copies `(seq, bytes)` pairs while holding the lock, then decodes a new dict for each event after releasing it, and puts `seq` back.
  - There's no extra serialization: main already ran `json.dumps` on every event to measure its size.
- **`72b7943a3c`:** removes test assertions on the private ring layout and on object identity. The value assertions already cover both contracts.

## Cost
Replay now decodes. For 1000 buffered events, minimum timings on a heavily loaded host:

| Payload | Main | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| ~40 B token deltas | ~0.04 ms | 1.8 ms |
| ~2 KB results | ~0.04 ms | 5.8 ms |

This is roughly 2–6 µs per event, paid only on reconnect and outside the lock. The ring is capped at 512 events / 4 MiB per session.

## Tests
- `test_tui_gateway_event_replay.py`: 15 passed. With only `event_replay.py` reverted to main, 2 fail: `'xxxx…' == 'small'` and `'caller-mutated' == 'original'`.
- `test_tui_gateway_server.py`, `test_protocol.py`, `test_multi_client_fanout.py`: 82 passed, 8 skipped.
- ruff and `git diff --check` are clean.

Fixes #108141. Supersedes #108143.

Salvages #49756 by @MaxFreedomPollard (first submitter; they also filed #49852). Their commit is cherry-picked with authorship preserved, plus follow-ups that cover the rebuild path.

## What was wrong
`_attach_built_agent` attached an agent to its session record without checking the session was still open. If `session.close` ran while `_make_agent` was building, the finished agent was attached to a dead record, which `_teardown_session` never visits again. The agent's memory provider, MCP clients and threads were never closed.

`_rebuild_session_agent`, which `tools.configure` and the Bot Chat capability refresh use, had the same window after its slow `_make_agent`.

## What changes
1. **`158b30bea7` (@MaxFreedomPollard):** while holding `_sessions_lock`, the attach checks the session is still live. If it isn't, the agent is closed and the build bails out. The race test and `test_session_db_ownership_teardown.py` are updated to match.
2. **`d060657987`:** the bail-out also sets `agent_error = AGENT_BUILD_ABANDONED`, as the replaced-session exit already did. A prompt sent to that session then reports the real cause instead of a generic error.
3. **`ea9e77a899`:** `_rebuild_session_agent` checks the session's `_closing` flag under the same lock before attaching. If the session is closing, it closes the new agent and the DB handle the rebuild opened, inside the session's profile scope, then raises. It uses `_closing` rather than membership in `_sessions` because the reset path passes records that aren't registered there.
   - The bot-capability caller already catches the `RuntimeError`.
   - A `tools.configure` call that races a close now returns an RPC error instead of reporting success for a closed session.
4. **`97e798f564`:** the race test now asserts the abandoned build registered no approval notify for the closed session. `AGENT_BUILD_ABANDONED` now names both causes (closed or replaced).

## Tests
Each new or changed test fails with only the production file reverted to main:
- `test_session_create_close_race_does_not_orphan_resources` fails with `[] == ['closed']`.
- `test_build_finishing_after_close_records_reason_and_closes_orphan` fails with `[] == ['closed']` on main, and with `None == AGENT_BUILD_ABANDONED` on commit 1 alone.
- `test_rebuild_finishing_after_close_closes_the_replacement_and_its_handle` fails with `DID NOT RAISE`.

Suite results:
- `test_tui_gateway_server.py`: 637 passed. 31 fail identically on clean main; the diff of the two failure lists is empty. They are `_make_agent` setup-readiness tests that hit this machine's real-home guard, and the file needs `ulimit -n 65536`.
- `test_session_db_ownership_teardown.py`: 10 passed; 7 fail identically on main.
- `test_none_agent_turn_guard.py` 3/3, `test_profile_rebuild_commit.py` 8/8, `test_projects_rpc.py` with no failures.

## Not in this PR
- **#75385 (@briandevans)** touches the same area for a different bug (model picks lost during the build). Its description says both can land.
- **Resume-path leak (existing on main):** `methods_session.py`'s sync resume error path pops the record without closing the agent `_init_session` built. That's a separate follow-up.
- **Rebuild on an open session:** `_rebuild_session_agent` never closes the old agent when the session stays open. Also existing on main; separate.

Fixes #49852. Supersedes #49756.

items.body:
vet402 (https://vet402.com) buys from x402 and MPP sellers with its own USDC, checks each payment on chain, and publishes whether the seller delivered. This plugin reads that record before a Hermes agent pays.

Surfaces used:
- `pre_tool_call` hook. Before `mpp_fetch` (or any tool listed in `VET402_GUARD_TOOLS`), it looks up the `url` argument. BLOCK returns `{"action": "block"}`. A WARN backed by evidence against the seller (vet402 paid and got nothing, its latest purchase failed, the answer didn't match the seller's declaration) returns `{"action": "approve"}` with a `rule_key` per method and URL, so approving one URL for the session doesn't approve another. ALLOW, a WARN only because vet402 hasn't bought there yet, an unknown URL, or an unreachable API lets the call run. `VET402_UNKNOWN=approve` sends those to the gate too.
- `vet402_check` tool, so the model can ask before deciding to pay.

It pairs with hermes-mpp. That entry's disclosure says 402s are auto-paid with no per-payment cap unless `MPP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is set. This plugin adds a per-URL check on the `mpp_fetch` path. It can't see payments made inside core HTTPX traffic, and the README says so.

Disclosure:
- Network: up to two HTTPS GETs to vet402.com per new URL (`/api/v1/resolve`, `/api/v1/resources/<id>/decision`). The only data sent is the URL about to be paid, with any user:password, query string and fragment removed. Without a key vet402 answers 10 decisions per minute per IP, and a lookup past that counts as unreachable.
- No credentials, no env vars required, no files written, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry.
- Never auto-approves. Evidence-backed WARNs go to Hermes's human-approval gate (`request_tool_approval`). With no person present that gate fails closed, and cron follows `approvals.cron_mode`.
- Standard library only, no Python dependencies. `requires_hermes` is 0.19.0, the release where the approve action got rule keys.

Checked locally at the pinned commit: `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` passes every check (security scan: safe), and `hermes plugins doctor --ci` reports 1 tool and 1 hook. I also ran the hook through Hermes's approval gate: approving one URL for the session still prompts for a different URL. I'm the owner of the plugin repository.

`tests/gateway/test_kanban_wake_acceptance.py` (and its sibling `test_completion_admission.py`) no longer hang until the 600s CI kill: their `drain()` helper can no longer busy-spin on Python 3.12+.

**Root cause:** since Python 3.12, `asyncio.gather()` over children that are all already done completes eagerly, so the helper's `while adapter._background_tasks: await asyncio.gather(...)` never yields to the loop when a task has finished but its queued `_background_tasks.discard` done-callback has not run yet — the set can never shrink and the loop spins forever.

CI evidence: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/36980998901/job/110755355858 (PR #130996, Desktop-only, no Python touched): `collected 4 items`, `...`, then `(600s exceeded; process tree SIGKILL'd)`.

### Change
Test-only. Each of the three identical drain helpers (`tests/gateway/test_kanban_wake_acceptance.py`, `tests/gateway/test_completion_admission.py`, `evals/heartbeat_idle_wire.py`) now does `await asyncio.sleep(0)` after the gather, so queued done-callbacks run before the set is checked again. No timeouts, skips or retries.

Production code is not affected: `BasePlatformAdapter.cancel_background_tasks` filters out done tasks and stops after 5 rounds. No other `while <set>: await gather(...)` loop exists in `gateway/`.

### Evidence
- **Captured hang stack** (Python 3.14.7, the CI interpreter, 16 parallel copies + 24 CPU burners, `-o faulthandler_timeout=45`): main thread at `asyncio/tasks.py:910 gather → _done_callback` ← `drain` (test line 37) ← `test_suppressed_ping_has_no_sent_receipt_but_wake_executes` (line 179). Some runs also hung in `test_notifier_retries_unaccepted_wake_without_repeating_pings` (line 144). **22 of 32 runs hung** over 2 rounds. On the local 3.11 venv: 0/48, because 3.11's gather always schedules its callbacks through the loop.
- **Deterministic forcing probe** (makes a finished task whose discard callback is still queued, then calls the module's `drain`, with a 5s SIGALRM):
  - before, 3.14.7: `test_kanban_wake_acceptance.drain: HANG`, `test_completion_admission.drain: HANG`
  - after, 3.14.7: both `OK`. 3.11: `OK` before and after.
- **Same stress after the fix:** both files, 3 rounds × 16 copies under load on 3.14.7: **48/48 passed**, 0 faulthandler timeouts.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` across all 22 `tests/gateway/test_kanban*.py`, `test_*wake*.py` and `test_completion_admission.py` files: 86 passed. `evals/heartbeat_idle_wire.py` passes on 3.11 and 3.14.
- `ruff check`, `git diff --check` and `scripts/check_no_tmp_literals.py` are clean.

Infographic skipped (test-only fix).



## Infographic

![Kanban wake test hang fixed](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aacbe2c/Q_9sKaT_wTdG5j_R5Jc29_EHUiW0mB.png)

Salvages #49020 by @srojk34 (first submitter). Their commit is cherry-picked with authorship preserved, then ported to the renamed hook file, plus two follow-ups.

## What was wrong
Deleting a session in the desktop app clears its queued prompts, session control, journals and tiles. It never cleared the session's subagent, todo, goal or background-status store entries. Those stay in memory, keyed by ids that no longer exist.

The stop paths already clear all four together (`session-tile-actions.ts`, `use-prompt-actions`).

## What changes
1. **`673ee446f7` (@srojk34):** clears subagents and todos for the stored id and the closing runtime id once `deleteSession` resolves. Ported from the old `use-session-actions.ts` to `use-session-actions/index.ts`.
2. **`dd1434ca3c`:** also clears the runtime id mapped in `runtimeIdByStoredSessionIdRef`, which can differ from the foreground runtime. This covers teknium1's runtime-id note on #49020.
3. **`bbcbc0293f`:** one loop over the distinct ids `{stored, closing runtime, mapped runtime}` now clears subagents, todos, goal (`clearSessionGoal`) and background status (`resetSessionBackground`).

All clearing runs only after the delete succeeds. A failed delete that restores the row keeps its state.

## Tests
Two tests in `use-session-actions.test.tsx`. Each uses distinct stored, foreground-runtime and mapped-runtime ids, plus an unrelated id as a control:
- **Successful delete:** only the unrelated id's subagent, todo, goal and background entries remain. This fails on main (`expected ['stored-doomed', …] to deeply equal ['runtime-other']`), and again with only commit 1 applied (the mapped runtime id survives).
- **Failed delete:** every entry survives.

Overall: vitest 16 files / 415 tests pass, `tsc --noEmit` and prettier are clean, and eslint has 0 errors. Its one warning is on a line this PR doesn't touch.

## Not in this PR
Switching gateway or profile wipes todos and session states, but not subagents, goals or background status. That's a separate follow-up.

Supersedes #49020.

Salvages #64534 by @embwl0x (first submitter for the slash-worker startup race). Their commit is cherry-picked with authorship preserved, plus follow-ups that fix a Windows regression, a startup-order regression and the tests.

## What was wrong
`tui_gateway/slash_worker.py` imported `cli` at module load. That import is heavy, and it happens before `main()` arms the parent-death watchdog, which reads `os.getppid()`. If the gateway died during that window, the worker was reparented first. The watchdog then recorded the reaper as its parent and never fired, leaving an orphaned slash worker.

## What changes
1. **`b0f099032b` (@embwl0x):** the gateway passes `--parent-pid`, and the worker arms the watchdog before importing `cli`.
2. **`e66be6a676`:** `test_slash_worker_provider.py` puts its fake `HermesCLI` on the `cli` module, which is where `main()` now reads it. #64534 had broken that test by removing the module-level name.
3. **`d1039923df`:** on Windows, keeps the observed `os.getppid()`. A venv `python.exe` is a launcher that starts the real interpreter as its child, so the worker's parent is the launcher, not the gateway. Using the gateway's pid made the watchdog kill a healthy worker on its first poll.
4. **`724b655ed4`:** drops #64534's test that only inspected a signature.
5. **`669c5711d8`:** imports `cli` after the watchdog but before `_prepare_slash_worker_runtime()` (MCP discovery). This is the order main has. Importing `cli` sets `HERMES_QUIET` and loads `~/.hermes/.env`. With #64534's order, MCP `${VAR}` interpolation in the worker would have missed `.env` secrets.
6. **`64e89c8902`:** the watchdog's parent choice moves into a pure `_watchdog_parent()` helper. Its tests pass the platform in as data instead of faking `sys.platform`.

On PID reuse (the reviewer's question on #64534): the watchdog compares the kernel's live `getppid()` against the recorded pid. A process that later takes that pid number never becomes the worker's parent, so no create-time pairing is needed.

7. **`f50f52d256`:** the import-order test removes the stub `cli` module it inserted, so it doesn't leak into other tests.

## Not included
- **#53308 (@pasevin, draining-thread join in `_SlashWorker.close()`)** is left out. 20 `slash.exec` + close cycles showed the same thread count on main and with the join (3 → 2). The join adds up to 4 s of blocking to `close()`, and needs a `getattr`/`try` guard for tests. #53499 is the same change.
- **#48656** solves a different problem (#48643).

## Tests
- Each new test fails with only `slash_worker.py` reverted to its previous version:
  - the import-order test, which records the actual `cli` import against runtime preparation;
  - the subprocess "no `cli` at import" test;
  - the 3 `_watchdog_parent` cases.
- All 38 `tests/tui_gateway` files that reference the slash worker: every slash-worker, watchdog and provider test passes. The remaining reds (`test_tui_gateway_server.py`, `test_custom_provider_session_persistence.py`) fail the same way on clean main.
- ruff, `check-windows-footguns --all` and `git diff --check` are clean.

Supersedes #64534.

Salvages #103784 by @liuhao1024 (first submitter for #103777). Their commit is cherry-picked with authorship preserved, plus two follow-ups.

## What was wrong
The profile log router routes each record by a snapshot of profile homes taken at startup. If a profile was deleted from the CLI while `serve` or the dashboard was running, the router kept writing into the deleted home, and every record printed `--- Logging error --- FileNotFoundError` to stderr. Deletes made from the dashboard were already handled by `release_profile` (#113363).

## What changes
1. **`15d7dcf06b` (@liuhao1024):** records for a routed home whose folder is gone go to the default home.
2. **`d1d778d8af`:**
   - A `named_profile_is_deleted` tombstone also counts as deleted; the CLI writes it before the rmtree.
   - On a delete, the router calls the existing `release_profile(candidate)`, which closes the stale handle and drops the home from routing.
   - The default home short-circuits these checks.
3. **`21d7cb174c`:** the liveness check runs at most every 2 s per home, and the first record for a home always checks.
   - So a write doesn't fail inside that window, a per-profile handler that can't reopen because `logs/` is gone skips the write. The router then re-checks at once, releases the home and sends the same record to the default log.

4. **`0885c7f3de`:** the handler sets an explicit `skipped_missing_dir` flag when it skips, and the router keys on that flag rather than `stream is None`.
   - On Windows, concurrent-log-handler closes the stream after every write. So every live record looked like a skipped write: the rate limit never applied, and a tombstoned home whose folder still existed got the record twice.
   - The rate-limit test now also runs with a handler that closes its stream after each write. That variant fails without this commit.

5. **`8b0bf1c7a1`:** a record skipped because `logs/` is gone now always goes to the default log. Before this, a live profile whose `logs/` had been removed by hand lost every record silently until restart. Covered by a new `logs-only` test case.

## Evidence
Live end-to-end run with a scratch `HERMES_HOME`. It creates a profile, routes logging to it, deletes the profile out of band, then emits 3 records:

| | `Logging error` on stderr | records in default log | stats per default-home emit | stats per live-profile emit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 6 | 0 / 3 | 5 | 5 |
| this branch | 0 | 3 / 3 | 5 | 5 |

The profile folder is not recreated.

## Tests
- `tests/test_hermes_logging.py`: 38 passed, 6 skipped (platform-specific).
- The new tests cover deleting via tombstone and via rmtree. Each asserts the handle is released, the record reaches the default log and nothing reaches stderr, plus one liveness check per interval.
- Each fails with only `hermes_logging.py` reverted. Mutation checks:
  - dropping the `is_dir` check fails the rmtree case;
  - dropping the tombstone check fails the tombstone case;
  - dropping the re-route fails the rmtree case.
- Related profile-delete and logging-scope files: 56 passed. 2 fail identically on clean main (the real-home guard on this machine).

## Not in this PR
- On Windows the stale handle is closed on the next routed record after the delete. A cross-process CLI delete can still race the rmtree; `release_profile_log_handlers` covers in-process deletes, and #130285 covers the gateway.
- #105285 checks `is_dir()` on every emit, including the default home, and drops deleted-profile records. The tombstone handling here covers its one extra idea.

Fixes #103777. Supersedes #103784 and #105285.

On an RTX or DGX Spark, the setup fork card no longer offers "Set up a local model". Local models come only from the app's own offer, which sets up the managed llama.cpp runtime.

## The problem

- #129646 added a "Set up a local model" row to the fork card on every Spark (`initiate-setup/scripts/host_facts.py::_from_machine`). Picking it opens a task chat whose ask is "Set up a local model."
- The task chat has no tool for the managed runtime. Only the desktop's Local Models pane drives it, through the dashboard routes in `hermes_cli/web_routers/local_models.py`. So the model improvises an install with the terminal. The reported result is an Ollama install.
- The app already has the right offer. On the RTX Spark it recommends Qwen3.8 27B on the CUDA llama.cpp build. It shows that offer three ways: the handoff signpost on the model pill, a card above the composer, and a "Run locally" row in the model menu.

| Surface | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Fork card on a Spark, no apps picked | "Install a few apps for this Spark", "Set up a local model", then the fixed rows | "Install a few apps for this Spark", a page built from the scan, then the fixed rows |
| Task chat asked for a local model | No guidance; the model installs a runtime with the terminal | Points to Run locally in the model menu, or Settings → Providers → Local Models; never installs a runtime itself |
| The app's local-setup offer | Unchanged | Unchanged |

## What changes

```diff
 def _from_machine(suggest: dict) -> list[dict]:
     kind = suggest.get("kind") or "computer"
-    if suggest.get("spark"):
-        return [{"id": "apps", "label": f"Install a few apps for this {kind}"},
-                {"id": "local_model", "label": "Set up a local model"}]
-    return [{"id": "apps", "label": f"Install a few apps for this {kind}"}] if suggest.get("fresh") else []
+    return [{"id": "apps", "label": f"Install a few apps for this {kind}"}] if suggest.get("spark") or suggest.get("fresh") else []
```

The `first-task` skill drops "Set up a local model" from its vague-ask options and from the next step after machine setup. It gains one build rule: a local model is set up by the app, so point to Run locally, and never install a model runtime or download a model by hand.

The `initiate-setup` skill gets back the line #129646 removed: asked about a local model, explain the download and hardware fit, then point to Settings → Providers → Local Models. With these changes, setup says what it said before #129646, and the app's offer is the only place a local model is recommended.

The docs pages that mirror both skills are regenerated by `website/scripts/generate-skill-docs.py`. Two bare `<machine>` placeholders from #129646 are escaped as `<machine>`. MDX reads a bare one as an unclosed tag, which fails the docs-site build on `onboarding/next`.

## Live verification

All rows ran on the RTX Spark (Windows on Arm, NVIDIA N1X) against the installed `onboarding-v1-preview #5` build (`1f817761dc`), with real host detection and a throwaway `HERMES_HOME`.

The plugin catalog no longer lists retaindb, byterover and holographic as official, Nous-maintained plugins. Nous Research does not maintain memory providers, so these entries promised something nobody will deliver. Users see no change: core still bundles all three, and the bundled copy is what `memory.provider: <name>` loads today.

## What changed

- **This PR:** deletes `plugin-catalog/{retaindb,byterover,holographic}.yaml`, which #131265 added (999506c79f3). That is the whole diff. The bundled `plugins/memory/<name>` dirs, the docs and the migration code are untouched.
- **The three NousResearch/hermes-plugin-<name> repos, already pushed:** the README banner, HANDOFF.md and repo description now say "unmaintained, looking for an owner" instead of "maintained by Nous Research". HANDOFF.md explains how to take a repo over: transfer or fork it, then send a catalog PR under the same name so `hermes update` migrates existing users. Heads: retaindb `67059ea`, byterover `1dadb18`, holographic `062762a`. Code and tags are unchanged.
- **Outreach:** a pinned "Maintainer wanted" issue in each repo (NousResearch/hermes-plugin-retaindb#1, NousResearch/hermes-plugin-byterover#1, NousResearch/hermes-plugin-holographic#1).

**For core removal PRs:** with no catalog entry, nothing can migrate these three. Core must keep bundling them until a new owner lists a catalog entry under the same name. The probe below shows the gap.

items.body:
The gateway failure-writer ownership probe no longer fails intermittently with `assert 19 == 20`. The cause: in CI it was downloading a real tirith toolchain on a background thread while it measured memory.

## What was happening

- The probe (`evals/gateway_failure_ownership/probe.py`) clears the environment down to `PATH/LANG/LC_ALL/TZ`. That also removed the harness's `HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS=1`.
- The CI PM toolchain is Python only, so tirith is not on `PATH`. In the probe's fresh home, `GatewayRunner()` → `_init_startup_checks` → `tirith_security.ensure_installed` starts a background `pm.ensure("tirith")`. That prepares the PM runtime and downloads and unpacks Python and uv from GitHub while the 20 cases run. CI logs show it happening (`uv: unpacking … Preparing the isolated Hermes runtime…`).
- The archive case asserts a **process-wide** `tracemalloc` peak under 8 MiB. When the unpacking on the `hermes-download_*` threads overlaps that window, its buffers push the peak over the bound. The case fails and the receipt reads 19/20.
- The probe's loopback fence didn't catch any of this. `hermes_bootstrap`'s happy-eyeballs `create_connection` dials with `connect_ex`, and the fence only patched `connect`. The downloads reached `github.com:443` while `blocked_external_attempts` stayed `[]`.

## Changes

- The probe sets `HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS=1`, the same hermetic switch the test harness uses.
- The fence also covers `socket.socket.connect_ex`. It returns `ENETUNREACH` and records the attempt.
- The test now asserts `blocked_external_attempts == []`. If the env scrub drops the switch again, the test fails every time instead of now and then.
- README fence note updated.

No product code changed.

## Validation (CPython 3.14.7, CI shape: no tirith on PATH)

| Run | base (`origin/main` probe) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Real run, no injection | 20/20 this time. In the background it connected to GitHub, staged `python-3.14.7` and `uv-0.12.3` into the probe home (503 MB), and recorded `blocked=0` | 20/20, no install, probe home 53 MB, `blocked=0` |
| Injected install (stand-in thread holds 9 MiB buffers, no network), probe ×5 | **5/5 fail, 19/20**, archive peak 9.78 MB, injection hit 5/5 | **5/5 pass 20/20**, peak 0.34 MB, injection hit 0 |
| Injected, `pytest tests/gateway/test_failure_writer_ownership.py::test_gateway_failure_writer_preserves_accepted_turn_identity` ×3 | **3/3 fail `assert 19 == 20`** (the CI signature) | 3/3 pass |
| Fence only, without the env switch | — | fence records the GitHub attempts, so the new assertion fails every time |
| Unloaded 2-core load runs before the fix | peaks up to 7.86 MB of the 8 MiB bound | — |
| `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_failure_writer_ownership.py tests/gateway/test_kanban_wake_acceptance.py` | — | 9 passed |

## The other flake today (kanban wake 600 s hang)

`tests/gateway/test_kanban_wake_acceptance.py` was already fixed on main by #131346 (`89937f86858`, drain helpers yield instead of busy-spinning). I re-checked it with a forcing probe: a done task whose discard callback is still queued. The pre-fix drain **hangs on 3.14.7** (and is fine on 3.11). Main's drain returns on both. None of the 4 failed CI runs since the merge contain that file. This PR doesn't change it.

## Infographic

![mission patch](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aacc166/K6Ni79FA5qazvZ8Cv7B35_rUsc1PzT.png)

## What does this PR do?

Adds `plugin-catalog/jp-corporate.yaml`, a community entry for **jp-corporate (法人照会)**. It is a lookup tool for Japanese corporations, and its data source is [gBizINFO](https://info.gbiz.go.jp/), the free corporate-information service of Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI).

What it lets an agent do:
- find a corporation by name, optionally narrowed by address, or look it up by corporate number (法人番号)
- check that a business partner's registration has not been closed
- check the corporate number on an invoice against the company name and address
- read the company's record of subsidies, government contracts, awards, certifications, financials, patents and workplace data
- list the business sites enrolled in social insurance, with insured headcount

The catalog has no plugin for Japanese public company data yet.

The plugin lives at the root of https://github.com/TakeshiTGAL/hermes-plugin-jp-corporate. It is a Python plugin that registers two read-only tools through `ctx.register_tool`:
- `jp_corp_search`: name, address or corporate-number lookup, plus checking a name or address against the official record
- `jp_corp_profile`: the detail sections of one corporation

It has no hooks, no middleware and no dependencies beyond the standard library.

Submitted by the owner of the plugin repository.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/jp-corporate.yaml`, pinned to `c6f7c9a69a7dbb2f751ae5d7ecd7e79029fc7e7e`.
- `capabilities` matches what the plugin registers at that commit: two tools, `requires_env: [GBIZINFO_API_TOKEN]`.

## Disclosure (rule 13)

- Network: sends only the names, corporate numbers and prefectures the user asks about to `api.info.gbiz.go.jp`. It contacts no other host. Redirects are not followed, so the token is never sent anywhere else.
- Credentials: one secret, `GBIZINFO_API_TOKEN`. Each user applies for their own free token from METI. Hermes stores it in `~/.hermes/.env` through the normal `requires_env` prompt. The plugin does not read any other tool's credentials.
- Local effects: no shell commands, no background processes, no files written, no telemetry. Repeated lookups within 10 minutes are answered from an in-memory cache.
- Rate: requests are spaced 0.5 s apart. Every result reports how many API requests were sent. A mistyped corporate number is caught by its check digit before any request.
- Data terms: every result that contains gBizINFO data carries the source credit that gBizINFO's terms require (source, a note that it was reformatted, and the date). The test fixtures are recorded API responses trimmed to the fields the tests read, with no personal names, and each fixture is attributed with its source page.

## How to Test

1. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` → passes.
2. Clone the repo at the pinned sha and run `hermes plugins validate --install-deps <clone>`:
   ```
   ✓ security scan — safe
   Validation passed.
   ```
   The repository's own tests run offline on recorded responses: `pytest -q` → `98 passed`.
3. `hermes plugins install jp-corporate --enable`, paste a gBizINFO token when prompted, restart, and ask:
   `法人番号 1180301018771 の会社を調べて` → トヨタ自動車株式会社, 愛知県豊田市トヨタ町１番地, status `registered`.

## Checklist

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide and the plugin-catalog README admission policy
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this entry
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS

## What does this PR do?

Adds `plugin-catalog/jp-estat.yaml`, a community entry for jp-estat, a plugin for Japanese government statistics built on the API of [e-Stat](https://www.e-stat.go.jp/) (政府統計の総合窓口). e-Stat is the portal for Japan's official government statistics, run by the Statistics Bureau of Japan and the National Statistics Center, and it has a free API.

What it lets an agent do:
- find the right statistics table by keyword, narrowed by statistic (for example `国勢調査`), survey year and area level
- see a table's areas, periods and categories by name, without knowing e-Stat's codes
- fetch values by name (`area="東京都"`, `time="2026年8月"`, `filters={"男女": "女"}`) and get them back with the unit, the survey date and a citation for the source
- get warnings that change how a number should be read: preliminary (速報) tables, index series on an older base year, raw versus seasonally adjusted month-on-month changes, and tables whose newest period is years old

The catalog has no plugin for Japanese government statistics yet.

The plugin lives at the root of https://github.com/TakeshiTGAL/hermes-plugin-estat. It is a Python plugin that registers three read-only tools through `ctx.register_tool`:
- `estat_search_tables`: keyword search over e-Stat's tables, ranked, with duplicates folded
- `estat_table_info`: the dimensions of one table and the names to use for them
- `estat_get_data`: values selected by name, with unit, notes, survey date and citation

It has no hooks, no middleware and no dependencies beyond the standard library.

Submitted by the owner of the plugin repository.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/jp-estat.yaml`, pinned to `7cf225afe7ef6f46b4dccd0e2521f137e602dd9e`.
- `capabilities` matches what the plugin registers at that commit: three tools, `requires_env: [ESTAT_APP_ID]`.

## Disclosure (rule 13)

- Network: sends only the search words, table IDs and selections the user asks for to `api.e-stat.go.jp` over HTTPS. It contacts no other host. Redirects are followed only to https://api.e-stat.go.jp. A redirect to another host or to plain HTTP is refused, so the application ID is never sent anywhere else.
- Credentials: one secret, `ESTAT_APP_ID`. Each user registers for their own free application ID on e-Stat. Hermes stores it in `~/.hermes/.env` through the normal `requires_env` prompt, and the plugin reads it from the environment on each request. The plugin does not read any other tool's credentials.
- The application ID in URLs: e-Stat requires the ID as a query parameter (`appId`), so the request URL contains it. The plugin never puts a request URL into an error, log line or tool reply. An HTTP error keeps only its status code, and network error text and e-Stat's own error messages have any URL and the ID removed. The tests check that the ID never appears in a tool reply.
- Local effects: no shell commands, no background processes, no files written, no telemetry. Two in-memory caches: table metadata (16 tables, 30 minutes) and the base years available for a statistic (1 hour).
- Unattended runs: each tool call has a 45 s budget for all its requests. Each network wait is capped at 20 s, no request starts after the budget is spent, and a failed request is retried at most once, only while the budget allows. Nothing waits for user input. A table search asks e-Stat for up to 500 table descriptions for each statistic it searches (at most three when `survey` matches several) and ranks them locally.
- Data terms: every `estat_get_data` reply that returns values carries the credit sentence that e-Stat requires of services built on its API (このサービスは、政府統計総合窓口(e-Stat)のAPI機能を使用していますが、サービスの内容は国によって保証されたものではありません。), a ready-made 出典 citation, and the extra line the terms ask for when the numbers are reworked. Replies that only ask the user to choose or narrow, and error replies, contain no values. The README shows the same credit sentence, which e-Stat's credit rule accepts anywhere users can see it. The test fixtures are real e-Stat responses trimmed to a few areas, items and periods, and `tests/fixtures/README.md` attributes each one with its source page and retrieval date.

## How to Test

1. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` → passes.
2. Clone the repo at the pinned sha and run `hermes plugins validate --install-deps <clone>`:
   ```
   ✓ security scan — safe
   Validation passed.
   ```
   The repository's own tests run offline on recorded responses: `pytest -q` → `59 passed`.
3. `hermes plugins install jp-estat --enable`, paste an e-Stat application ID when prompted, restart, and ask:
   - `令和2年国勢調査の東京都の総人口は？` → 14,047,594 人 (2020 Census, table `0003445078`).
   - `2026年8月の全国の消費者物価指数（総合）は？` → 102.2 (2025年=100, table `0004052037`).

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide and the plugin-catalog README admission policy
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this entry

## What does this PR do?

Adds a catalog entry for **memtomem**, a portable (Agent Plugins v1) package: a local memtomem
MCP server plus six memory skills. Submitted by the repository owner (`memtomem/memtomem`).

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/memtomem.yaml` — pins `memtomem/memtomem@8fc62753ef95f14848d61cd502e1bef09bfd2757`
  (the `v0.6.6` release commit), `subdir: packages/memtomem-hermes-plugin`, `version: "0.1.1"`
  (the package's `plugin.json` at that commit), `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.5"`.

## Disclosure

- **Network**: the server is launched with `uvx --python 3.12 --from 'memtomem[onnx]==0.6.6'
  memtomem-server`, so uv downloads memtomem and its dependencies from PyPI on first start, and
  Python 3.12 (about 70 MiB) if it cannot find one. With a fresh BM25-only configuration nothing
  else leaves the machine. An existing memtomem configuration (`~/.memtomem/config.json`, shared
  with the user's other agents) may enable Hugging Face model downloads, a remote embedding or LLM
  provider, Cohere reranking, or search webhooks.
- **Data read/written**: `~/.memtomem` (SQLite index and Markdown notes), plus any directory the
  user asks it to index.
- **Process**: one stdio MCP server per session; no daemon, no shell commands beyond the uvx launch.
- **Credentials**: none read. No other tool's login is touched.
- No self-updater: updates arrive only as a SHA bump here.

## How to Test

Measured with Hermes Agent 0.21.5 (`v2026.9.24`, `f97608f1`, with the `mcp` extra) on macOS, in an
isolated `HOME`/`HERMES_HOME`/`XDG_*`:

1. `hermes plugins validate --install-deps --json <pinned tree>` → `ok: true` (portable manifest,
   manifest fields, security scan `safe`; no warnings).
2. `hermes plugins install "https://github.com/memtomem/memtomem#packages/memtomem-hermes-plugin" --ref 8fc62753ef95f14848d61cd502e1bef09bfd2757 --enable`
   → rc 0; the installed tree is byte-identical to `packages/memtomem-hermes-plugin` at that
   commit (9 files); `.install-metadata.json` records `pinned: true` at that revision.
3. Runtime: the server starts through uvx (`memtomem[onnx]==0.6.6`), Hermes discovers 13
   `mcp__memtomem__*` tools, `mem_add` + `mem_search` round-trip a probe note under the isolated
   `HOME`, and the six skills load.

Not measured: Linux and Windows; installing by catalog name (this PR is what enables that).

## Checklist

- [x] Owner submission (rule 5)
- [x] Exact 40-hex SHA pin (rule 2); no self-updating code (rule 3)
- [x] `capabilities` empty — the package registers no Python tools, hooks or middleware; its tools

- [x] Disclosures above and in the package README's Network section (rule 13)

## What does this PR do?

Tells contributors and coding agents to follow `SECURITY.md` when they file security issues and PRs. Before this change, no `AGENTS.md` in the repo mentioned `SECURITY.md`, so agents only found the disclosure rules if they happened to open that file.

- **`AGENTS.md`**: adds a short "Security reports and fixes — follow `SECURITY.md`" subsection to the Contribution Rubric, which agents load automatically. It covers:
  - Vulnerabilities in scope under §3.1 that haven't been disclosed are reported through GitHub Security Advisories or security@nousresearch.com, not in a public issue or PR, and exploit details stay out of commits and PR text.
  - Hardening that §3.2 puts out of scope is filed as a regular public issue or PR.
  - Security reports name the §2 trust boundary that's crossed, with `file:line` references and a reproduction on `main`.
  - The triage sweeper leaves a public post that discloses an apparent §3.1 vulnerability for a maintainer.
- **`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml`**: adds a "Report a security vulnerability" contact link to the private advisory form. This reaches people and agents who file through the GitHub UI or API without cloning the repo.
- **`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`**: the "Security fix" checkbox now points undisclosed §3.1 vulnerabilities to Security Advisories first.

The new text restates `SECURITY.md` and adds no new policy. `blank_issues_enabled` is unchanged.

## Related Issue

None.

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [x] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `AGENTS.md`: new subsection between "Before you call it a bug" and "The Footprint Ladder" (+21 lines)
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml`: new first `contact_links` entry
- `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`: Security fix checkbox text

## How to Test

1. `python -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml'))"` parses cleanly and lists 4 contact links (checked locally).
2. After merge, the issue chooser at `/issues/new/choose` shows the security link first.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A
