items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds `plugin-catalog/jp-charts.yaml`, a community entry for jp-charts. It draws business charts as PNG images sized for a phone screen, for chat replies and for reports, with Japanese text and number conventions built in.

What it lets an agent do:
- draw a bar, line, stacked bar or 100% band chart from a list of rows, CSV, TSV copied from Excel, a Markdown table, JSON, a local `.csv`/`.tsv`/`.txt`/`.json` file, or the `{columns, rows, unit, source}` result of an e-Stat plugin
- get Japanese labels that never turn into boxes, numbers written with 万 and 億 (`1,405万`), an axis title that includes the unit, and a source line on every chart (`unit` and `source` are required)
- hand the chart to a chat: the tool result carries a `MEDIA:/path.png` line for Hermes' gateways
- trust the numbers: after drawing, the plugin reads every bar and segment length, line point, data label and axis tick back from the finished figure and compares them with the parsed values. If any of them differs, no image is returned.

Two catalog entries already show charts, inside the dashboard or the desktop app (boardstate and hermes-rich-ui, by their catalog descriptions). This one returns a PNG file instead, so the chart can go out through the chat gateways or be pasted into a document.

The plugin lives at the root of https://github.com/TakeshiTGAL/hermes-plugin-charts. It is a Python plugin that registers three tools under the `charts` toolset through `ctx.register_tool`, and one hook:
- `chart_render`: draws the chart, checks it, saves the PNG and returns `path`, `media`, `alt_text` and the check result
- `chart_validate`: the same arguments without drawing, to show how the table was read or what is wrong
- `chart_types`: when to use each chart type, the encodings it needs, data formats, presets and limits
- `transform_llm_output` hook: adds the `MEDIA:` line to a chat reply when the model forgot it (details below)

Submitted by the owner of the plugin repository.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/jp-charts.yaml`, pinned to `870b5fcb1c9ca3db00f4fe956ee8d860f20ea661`.
- `capabilities` matches what the plugin registers at that commit: three tools, one hook (`transform_llm_output`), no middleware, no `requires_env`.

## Disclosure (rule 13)

- Network: none at run time. The plugin opens no network connections and sends no telemetry. The only downloads happen at install time, when Hermes installs the Python dependencies below from PyPI.
- Credentials: none. No `requires_env`, no secrets in `config_schema`, and it does not read any other tool's credentials.
- Local reads: only when the model passes `data.path`. The path must be absolute and end in `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.txt` or `.json` (after symlinks are resolved too), and the file must be 10 MB or smaller. Any path whose resolved location has a hidden file or folder in it (a name starting with `.`) is refused, and so is everything under the Hermes home folder (config, `.env`, sessions). Parts of a file that is read come back to the model in `chart_validate`'s preview and in error messages, like any tool output.
- Local writes: PNGs go to Hermes' image cache, `<HERMES_HOME>/cache/images` (or `<HERMES_HOME>/image_cache` when an older install still uses that folder), so they are inside the folders Hermes allows for media delivery. A chart that fails its check is deleted before the error is returned. Charts that pass stay there, and the plugin does not delete them later. Outside Hermes (tests, scripts) the folder is `hermes-charts` in the system temp folder. matplotlib keeps its own font cache in its config directory.
- Output hook: `transform_llm_output` is registered and on by default (setting `auto_attach` under `plugins.entries.jp-charts.settings`). At the end of a turn on a platform that attaches files (Telegram, Slack, Discord, email, the desktop app, cron deliveries), it appends `MEDIA:` lines for charts that this session rendered and that the reply does not mention (at most 4 per turn, and only charts from the last 30 minutes, held in memory). It returns nothing, so the reply is unchanged, on `cli`, `tui`, `acp`, `sms`, `local`, `api_server`, `webhook` and `msgraph_webhook` turns, when the reply already attaches one of those charts, and when the `auto_attach` setting is `false`.
- Other plugins on the same hook: Hermes runs every `transform_llm_output` callback in the order the plugins were loaded and keeps the first non-empty text one of them returns (`agent/turn_finalizer.py`). On a turn where another plugin also rewrites the reply, only one of the two edits is kept. If the other plugin's text wins, the chart is not attached on that turn, but its path is still in the tool result. On turns where jp-charts has nothing to add it returns nothing, so other plugins' edits go through as before.
- Chat delivery not yet tested on real accounts: whether the photo actually arrives in a real Telegram, Slack or LINE chat has not been checked. What has been checked is that the hook's reply passes through Hermes' `BasePlatformAdapter.extract_media`, which returns the chart's PNG path, and that `validate_media_delivery_path` accepts it. Per Hermes' LINE adapter, LINE needs `LINE_PUBLIC_URL` to send images. The README says the same.
- Dependencies: `matplotlib>=3.8,<4` and `matplotlib-fontja>=1.0,<2` (both with upper bounds, declared in `python_dependencies`). matplotlib is imported only when a chart is drawn, so Hermes can load and list the plugin before the dependencies are installed, and a missing dependency returns an error that says how to install it.
- Font: this repository contains no font files. When no Japanese system font is installed, the plugin uses IPAexGothic (`ipaexg.ttf`), which comes inside the `matplotlib-fontja` wheel (package license `MIT AND IPA`). IPAexGothic is under the IPA Font License Agreement v1.0, and the wheel includes that license text. The plugin reads the font file by path and registers it in matplotlib's shared font list. It does not import `matplotlib_fontja` and does not change matplotlib's `rcParams`, so other tools in the same process keep their fonts.
- Other local effects: no shell commands, no background processes. While a chart is being drawn it briefly records Python warnings (process-wide) and matplotlib's log messages to catch characters no font can draw.

## How to Test

1. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` → passes.
2. Clone the repo at the pinned sha and run `hermes plugins validate --install-deps <clone>`:
   ```
   ✓ security scan — safe
   Validation passed.
   ```
   The repository's own tests run offline: `pytest -q` → `140 passed`.
3. `hermes plugins install jp-charts --yes-deps --enable`, start a new session, and ask for a horizontal bar chart of the ten most populous prefectures in the 2020 census (the same data as `tests/examples.py`, `POPULATION_TOP10`). Run against hermes-agent `0a374d1` from a `file://` install of the pinned commit, `chart_render` returned:

   Summary of the result:
   ```
   success: true, preset: mobile (1080 px wide)
   verification: ok
   checked: marks 10, labels 10, axis_ticks 3, categories 10, zero_on_axis true
   rows: 10 of 10 drawn values equal the input (東京都 14,047,594 ... 静岡県 3,633,202 人)
   ```
   With `platform="telegram"`, the hook appended `MEDIA:<HERMES_HOME>/cache/images/chart-….png` to the reply, and `extract_media` returned that path with the line removed from the text. In a terminal the reply gives the path. The README shows this chart as its first example image.

## Checklist

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide and the plugin-catalog README admission policy
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this entry
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS

## What does this PR do?

Adds `plugin-catalog/jp-egov-law.yaml`, a community entry for jp-egov-law, a plugin for Japanese law built on the API of [e-Gov 法令検索](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/), the law database run by the Digital Agency of Japan (デジタル庁). The API is public and needs no key.

What it lets an agent do:
- read one article by law name, e-Gov abbreviation (`労基法`), common short name (`個情法`), law number or law ID, with the article number written the usual ways (`第32条`, `32`, `三十二条`, `32の2`)
- read the wording in force on a past date (e-Gov keeps versions from 2017-04-01) or as a scheduled amendment will make it read
- check whether an amendment changes an article: one call with two dates returns changed true or false, a line diff and the new wording
- list a law's scheduled amendments with their enforcement dates and amending laws, and its earlier versions
- find laws by name, or by a phrase in their text

The catalog has no plugin for Japanese law yet.

The plugin lives at the root of https://github.com/TakeshiTGAL/hermes-plugin-egov-law. It is a Python plugin that registers three read-only tools through `ctx.register_tool`:
- `egov_law_article`: one article (or paragraph) of a law, today or on a given date, optionally compared with a second date
- `egov_law_search`: laws by title or abbreviation, or by a phrase in their text
- `egov_law_revisions`: the version in force now, scheduled amendments and earlier versions

It has no hooks, no middleware and no dependencies beyond the standard library.

Submitted by the owner of the plugin repository.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/jp-egov-law.yaml`, pinned to `5233802cf0b5c29b595c0f1da20abbc823e09c0d`.
- `capabilities` matches what the plugin registers at that commit: three tools, `requires_env: []`.

## Disclosure (rule 13)

- Network: sends HTTPS GET requests to `laws.e-gov.go.jp` only. A request contains what the agent looks up (a law name, law number or ID, article number, search phrase or date). Redirects are followed only to https://laws.e-gov.go.jp; a redirect to another host or to plain HTTP is refused. Python's `urllib` follows the system proxy settings such as `HTTPS_PROXY`, so with a proxy set the requests go through it.
- Credentials: none. The API needs no authentication, and the plugin reads no environment variables and no other tool's credentials.
- Limits: each request has a 15 s socket timeout and an 8 MB response cap, and requests from the process are spaced at least 1 s apart. One tool call sends at most 6 requests to e-Gov (`egov_law_article`: 6, `egov_law_revisions`: 3, `egov_law_search`: 2). The 6 are two name lookups (when a partial name matches more than 100 laws), the article, then, if the article is missing, a paragraph count (when a paragraph was asked for), the law's revision list and the article as it read the day before the current version took effect. Nothing waits for user input.
- Local effects: no files written, no database, no shell commands, no background processes, no telemetry. Name-to-law-ID answers and the law's own 附則 articles read for the transitional-rule note are kept in process memory, at most 256 entries together, and are gone when Hermes exits.
- Data terms: e-Gov's terms of use apply the Public Data License 1.0 (公共データ利用規約 第1.0版), which asks for a source credit and a note when content is edited. Every successful tool result carries `source.attribution` (`出典：e-Gov法令検索（https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/）のデータを hermes-plugin-egov-law が取得・整形（条単位の抽出等）`) and `retrieved_on`, and the `egov_law_article` description and the `source.note` in every result ask the model to show the credit with any law text it quotes. The test fixtures are recorded e-Gov API responses, and the README credits e-Gov as the source of the law data.

## How to Test

1. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` → passes.
2. Clone the repo at the pinned sha and run `hermes plugins validate --install-deps <clone>`:
   ```
   ✓ security scan — safe
   Validation passed.
   ```
   The repository's own tests: `pytest -q -m "not live"` → `75 passed, 20 deselected` (offline, on recorded responses). `pytest -q` also runs the 20 live tests against e-Gov (about 35 requests, 1 per second).
   `tests/test_amendment_titles.py` is a regression table on real e-Gov data: 45 amendments of 22 laws, each with whether the amending law's title names the law and which law it follows up, written by hand from the titles, not computed by the code under test. The offline test checks all 45 rows against recorded titles. The live test checks the rows of 4 of the laws against e-Gov now.
3. `hermes plugins install jp-egov-law --enable`, restart, and ask:
   - `労働基準法第32条の条文を見せて` → 第三十二条 of 労働基準法 (昭和二十二年法律第四十九号), whose text includes `一週間について四十時間`.
   - `労基法115条は2027年4月1日に施行される改正で変わる？` → `egov_law_article` with `law: "労基法"`, `article: "115"`, `as_of: "2027-03-31"` and `compare_with: "2027-04-01"` returns `comparison.changed: true` with the line diff. The repository's `examples/scenarios.md` (S8) records an agent asking this: that call answered whether 第百十五条 changes, and the agent also checked the revision list and 附則第百四十三条 before answering.

## Checklist

- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this entry
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS

items.body:
`/browser connect` reports success on Desktop, CLI and TUI, but the agent keeps driving the old browser. `/browser disconnect` leaves the agent in the user's browser.

## Cause

The Browser Harness daemon reads `BU_CDP_*` once, when it starts, and keeps running across calls. The connect/disconnect swap calls `cleanup_all_browsers()` before and after it changes `BROWSER_CDP_URL`. That function stops agent-browser sessions and CDP supervisors, but not harness daemons. So every `browser_exec` after the swap, named or unnamed, attaches to a daemon still pointed at the earlier browser.

- The harness driver came in with #81958 (Browser Use CLI 3.0 mode, @teknium1, salvaging #66476). The CLI has had this bug since then.
- #125995 (@teknium1, merged 2026-09-28) put `browser-harness` into the main venv. Before that, Desktop installs fell back to the built-in `browser_*` tools, where the swap worked. Now Browser Use is the default driver on Desktop too, so Desktop hits the same bug.

## Fix

`browser_exec` records each `BU_NAME` it drives. `cleanup_all_browsers()` stops those daemons with the harness's own `--reload`, which confirms the daemon's identity over IPC before it sends a signal. The next `browser_exec` starts a new daemon on whatever endpoint it resolves. The fix lives in the shared reap, so it covers CLI connect/disconnect, the `browser.manage` RPC that Desktop and TUI use, and gateway shutdown.

## Verification

Live run with real `browser-harness==0.1.13`, two real headless Chromes (A on :9400, B on :9401), and the real `browser.manage` handler. Sequence: `browser_exec` on A, `/browser connect B`, `browser_exec`, `/browser disconnect`, `browser_exec`.

| | Chrome A tabs | Chrome B tabs |
|---|---|---|
| `origin/main` | `?marker=A`, `?marker=B` | `about:blank` |
| this branch | `?marker=A` | `?marker=B` |

On this branch, the call after disconnect doesn't touch B.

On Desktop and TUI, the `/browser` subcommand picker offers `use`, because it's listed in the command registry. Neither handler knew about it, though, so choosing it just printed the usage line. `/browser use [off]` only worked in the classic CLI.

## Change

- **Backend:** `browser.manage` gets a `use` action that takes `enabled: bool`.
  - It sets the profile's `browser.backend` through `set_browser_use_mode`, a new helper in `tools/browser_use_cli.py`. The CLI `/browser use` now calls the same helper, so its config write and cache reset aren't duplicated.
  - `status` and `use` now return `browser_use`.
  - The method is now `@_profile_scoped`, so a worker session writes its own profile's config, not the launch profile's.
- **Desktop and TUI:** both accept `/browser use` and `/browser use off`, reject other arguments with `usage: /browser use [off]`, and `status` adds a line when Browser Use mode is on.
  - The current chat keeps its tools. The switch applies to new chats and the reply says so (`/new to start one`). Swapping a live agent's tools would break its prompt cache; the CLI starts a new session instead.
- **Remote backends:** `use` and `status` now work there too, since they touch the backend's own config. `connect` and `disconnect` still require a local gateway.
- **Strings:** Desktop's `/browser` description is updated in its 9 locale files. The TUI gets new `slashCmd.ops.browser.*` keys in all 16 locales; the four that overlap reuse the CLI's existing translations of the same strings. `_keys.tui.json` and the generated gateway contract are regenerated.

## Verification

Ran a real Electron Desktop from this branch with a temporary `HOME` and `HERMES_HOME`:

| typed | `browser.backend` in that profile's config | reply |
|---|---|---|
| `/browser use off` | `"off"` | Browser Use mode disabled · applies to new chats |
| `/browser use maybe` | unchanged | `usage: /browser use [off]` |
| `/browser use` | `"browser-use"` | Browser Use mode enabled · applies to new chats |
| `/browser status` | — | not connected + `Browser: Browser Use mode (…)` |

Tests:

- `test_browser_manage_use_swaps_the_profiles_browser_tools_for_new_agents` drives the real RPC.
  - The backend flips, `status` reports it, and `browser_exec` appears in or disappears from the tool definitions a new agent resolves. That proves the cached `check_fn` verdict is dropped.
  - A `profile` call writes that profile's config and leaves the launch profile's alone.
  - On `origin/main` the call returns no `result`.
- Desktop vitest: `/browser use` and `/browser use off` call `browser.manage {action: 'use', enabled}` on a remote connection and never hit `slash.exec`.
- TUI vitest: both commands added to the native-RPC routing table.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` across the browser, tui_gateway, contracts, i18n-pack and desktop-registry files: 852 passed.
- Desktop vitest: 173 passed. TUI vitest: 77 passed. `i18n:keys:check` is clean.

Follows [#131623](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/131623), which made `/browser connect` and `/browser disconnect` switch Browser Use mode's driver over to the new browser.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

The Windows MSIX package shipped one `Square44x44Logo.png` at 44 px and nothing else for the taskbar/Start slot. On any HiDPI Windows 11 machine that means the taskbar (48 px at 200 %) and every Start pin (64–256 px) are Windows **upscaling a 44 px bitmap**, and since no `altform` theme variants existed, Windows plated the icon itself. Microsoft's construction guide is explicit on both: provide `targetsize-*` bitmaps so Windows only ever scales down, and provide the default / `altform-unplated` / `altform-lightunplated` forms "even if the icon is the same".

![taskbar before/after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethernet8023/hermes-pr-assets/main/pr-131669/msix-taskbar-before-after.png)

Top row: the 48 px taskbar slot at 200 % scale, 6× nearest-neighbour so you see actual bitmaps. Before = the 44 px tile as Windows resamples it; after = the exact `targetsize-48` bitmap, dark tile on a dark theme (`altform-unplated`), light tile on a light theme (`altform-lightunplated`) — the same split macOS dark mode already gets. Bottom row: the small exact sizes in both theme forms.

The generator now emits the full qualified catalog as a table (`APPX_LOGOS` × `APPX_SCALES`, `APPX_TARGET_SIZES` × `APPX_ALTFORMS`): `<Logo>.scale-{125,150,200,400}` for all four manifest logos at Microsoft's exact pixel sizes (150 @ 125 % = 188, not 187), and `Square44x44Logo.targetsize-{16,20,24,30,32,36,40,48,60,64,72,80,96,256}` in the three theme forms — 62 files instead of 8. `before-build.mjs` stages the whole `assets/appx/` directory instead of a hardcoded list of four. No builder changes: app-builder-lib runs `makepri` and `makeappx /l` as soon as it sees a qualified asset (`winAppUtil.js::isScaledAssetsProvided`). The four `*-dark.png` logos that were generated but never staged are gone.

The design is untouched — the squircle tile is the one we want on Windows; every previously shipped output is byte-identical.

### Exposed along the way

The commit badge (dev builds only) was drawn outside the portrait's silhouette clip. At 16–30 px its anti-aliased top edge stacked coverage on the plate's own corner pixels and changed the alpha channel between build flavours — invisible before because the smallest direct render was 44 px. The badge now shares the clip, its plate is plain black, and it is left off direct renders below 32 px (`BADGE_MIN_SIZE`), where no SHA is legible anyway. Release icons are unaffected.

## Related Issue

Follow-up to #122976 (macOS 26 icon), where comparing the Windows tile against the Windows 11 guidelines surfaced this.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `scripts/generate_icons.py` — `APPX_*` catalog + `appx_targets()`/`appx_scaled()` replace the eight hand-listed appx rows in `TARGETS`/`CHECK_SIZES`; `wide` kind takes `(w, h, tile)`; badge clipped, black, `BADGE_MIN_SIZE`; docstring (99 outputs).
- `apps/desktop/scripts/before-build.mjs` — `stageMsixAssets` stages every `assets/appx/*.png`, still fails on a missing base logo.
- `apps/desktop/assets/appx/` — 58 new generated files, 4 dead `-dark.png` removed.
- `tests/scripts/test_icon_flavors.py` — new `test_msix_logos_resolve_every_slot_windows_draws` (every base has its scaled siblings at Microsoft's sizes; unplated is the dark tile, lightunplated/base the light one); flavour tests learn the `_altform-unplated` dark form and the badge-free small renders.
- `tests/scripts/test_icon_generation_exit.py` — the silhouette clip group holds the badge beside the portrait.

## How to Test

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/scripts/test_icon_flavors.py tests/scripts/test_icon_generation_exit.py tests/scripts/test_desktop_preparation.py   # 43 passed
npx vitest run tests-js/generate-icons.test.mjs
cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run --project electron electron/channel-build-version.test.ts scripts/before-pack.test.mjs
python scripts/generate_icons.py --source . --out . --check   # [ok] all 99 targets
```

On Windows the real proof is the `side-by-side.windows` lane, which runs `beforeBuild()` → `gen-msix-manifest` → real `makeappx` on the staged `build/appx`; with qualified assets present the package must now also contain `resources.pri`.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature
- [x] I've run the relevant tests and they pass (see above)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: NixOS (generator + tests); Windows 11 arm64 for the taskbar renders

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation — generator docstring; nothing user-facing
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` — N/A
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md` — N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact — Windows-only packaging change; macOS/Linux outputs byte-identical

Fixes #109101.

In the TUI, and in the web dashboard that embeds it, the agent could never save a browser login or enter a 2FA code. The terminal answered both `vault.save_login` and `vault.code` with `-32601` (method not handled). Desktop has had cards for both since vault launch.

## Change

- **Save-login card.** Two steps: the email/username is shown as you type, then the password is masked.
  - Submitting either step empty, pressing Esc, or the request timing out declines with an empty value. The tool stops waiting right away instead of sitting out its 180s timeout.
  - The pair travels as one JSON `ValueResult` and goes only to the encrypted vault.
  - Built on @liuhao1024's card from #109113.
- **Verification-code card.** Shows the site plus the backend's hint (e.g. "sent to •••42"). The code is shown as typed, like Desktop's `one-time-code` field, and is trimmed before it's sent.
- **Both cards** sit next to `VaultUnlockPrompt` in `maskedPrompt.tsx` and reuse the shared `MaskedPrompt`. A new `reveal` prop shows the typed text, so there's no second input component. The standalone `vaultSaveLoginPrompt.tsx` is removed.
- **One list for every credential prompt.** `SENSITIVE_PROMPTS` / `hasSensitivePrompt` in `overlayStore.ts` now drive Esc/Ctrl+C decline, `request.cancel` teardown, the tab-title `⚠` marker and the pet's "waiting on you" state.
  - Each of those used to be a hand-written `sudo || secret || vaultUnlock` check.
  - In #109113 the save-login card wasn't in the Esc lists, so Esc did nothing on it. A future prompt can no longer be missed by one of these.
- `dismissSensitivePrompt` is now table-driven: one notice per prompt, with no fall-through between branches.
- **i18n:** 10 new keys under `secure.vault.*`, `session.status.*` and `session.input.*`, translated in all 16 TUI locales. `_keys.tui.json` is regenerated.

## Verification

- Real ink render tests, `vaultSaveLoginPrompt.test.tsx`:
  - the identifier step shows first
  - an empty identifier declines
  - a filled identifier moves to the masked password step and submits both values
  - the code card shows the site, the hint and the typed code, and submits it
- `createGatewayEventHandler.test.ts`: `vault.save_login` and `vault.code` each open their card, set the localized status, and `request.cancel` closes the matching one. The "requests a terminal can't answer" row now checks `terminal.read` in place of `vault.code`.
- `useInputHandlers.test.ts`: dismissing either vault card replies `{ value: '' }` and prints the localized notice.
- `tsc --noEmit` is clean. Prettier and eslint are clean on the touched files.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_i18n_tui_packs.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_validate_locales.py`: 23 passed.
- Full `ui-tui` vitest: the same 23 failures as on `origin/main` (subscriptionOverlay, syntax, appChromeBlockedTimers, ink-backpressure, one palette test) and no new ones.

Credit: @liuhao1024 (#109113, cherry-picked as the first commit), @fangliquanflq (#109127) and @uzairchhapra (#109184), both added as co-authors.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

A tree:0 install checkout stops accumulating one pack per lazy fetch: `hermes update` / `hermes update --check` fold them with git's own `gc --auto`, and the checkout stops writing the commit-graph that turns one stale graph into a lazy-fetch loop.

This is the master PR for the partial-clone `.git` growth family. It salvages two PRs verbatim (authorship kept), composes them, and fixes where they disagreed; every premise below was reproduced against a real blobless clone on **git 2.50.1, 2.53.0 and 2.55.0** (2.50.1 and 2.53.0 built from the upstream tarballs).

## Related Issue

Fixes #129712
Fixes #127711
Refs #131444, #120411 (see "Not claimed")

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Premises, reproduced

| # | Claim | Result (2.50.1 / 2.53.0 / 2.55.0) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Each lazy fetch writes its own pack | `git log -p -90` on a tree:0 clone: 153 packs, all `.promisor` (2.55) |
| 2 | Nothing folds them | Post-fetch `maintenance run --auto` left 153 at 153 on 2.55; on 2.50.1/2.53.0 it folded 102 to 31, see 3 |
| 3 | A commit-graph write loops through lazy fetches (#127711) | **Only when the existing graph carries changed-path (Bloom) data**: with 30 unseen commits, `gc`, `gc --auto`, `maintenance run --task=commit-graph` and `fetch.writeCommitGraph` each did 30 lazy fetches, 30 packs, and 30 `git maintenance` children (every lazy fetch re-spawns it). Without a Bloom graph: 0, on all three gits |
| 4 | `gc.writeCommitGraph=false` stops it | gc: 31 packs → 1, 0 lazy fetches, all three gits |
| 5 | `gc --auto` folds them and keeps the marker | 104 packs → 1, `.promisor` kept, history readable under `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, all three gits |
| 6 | #127721's `gc.auto=0` is harmless | **False.** 106 packs stay 106: it turns the fold into a no-op (all three gits) |
| 7 | gc leaves an unmarked pack that crashes the next fetch (#129724's re-mark) | **Not reproduced**: marker kept on all three gits. Re-mark removed |
| 8 | A timed-out `subprocess.run(["git","gc"])` is clean | **False.** `pack-objects` keeps running after the timeout fires; the fold now runs under `bounded_probe_run` (tree-kill) |
| 9 | gc after tmp-pack cleanup helps full clones (#120422) | **Inert**: pack count unchanged after the sweep + `gc --auto` (9 → 9 on 2.50.1/2.53.0, 5 → 5 on 2.55.0; `gc.autoPackLimit` is 50), full clones keep git's own auto-gc |

## Cluster verdicts

| PR | Verdict |
|---|---|
| #129724 (@liuhao1024) | **In, picked verbatim** as the base: the fold. Our follow-up drops the re-mark (7), adds tree-kill (8) |
| #127721 (@whyyagswhy) | **In, picked verbatim** (re-authored from the placeholder `hermes-fix <fix@local>` to the `<id>+whyyagswhy` noreply). Follow-up swaps `gc.auto=0` (6) for `gc.writeCommitGraph=false` (3, 4), adds `install.ps1` (Windows has the worst reports) and an idempotent re-apply on every update check, so installs that predate the installer change converge |
| #131447 (@dskwe) | **Superseded, not picked**: sets `maintenance.auto=false` for every updater git call including full clones, which lose stock auto-gc for no reason (full clones have every tree), and overwrites `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`. The persisted keys cover the actual hazard |
| #129714 (@dskwe) | **Wrong premise, not picked**: `fetchTrackingRef` runs in the user's project repo (Start-work worktrees under `<root>/.worktrees`), not the install checkout, so it would `gc --auto` arbitrary user repos |
| #120422 (@KoNit-K) | **Inert** (9), not picked |

Closes of the superseded PRs wait for this to merge.

## Not claimed

- #131444 (Windows, git 2.53.0, 332 full-history packs): the mechanism is unreproduced here. 3 is consistent with it (commit-graph/`objects/info/packs` rewritten, only 1 pack with a marker) but I have not shown it, hence `Refs`.
- Lazy-fetch *generators* are separate lanes with their own premises and are untouched: parked-branch `git cherry` (#125529, #126693, #128335), plugin catalog dating (#122654), submodule walk on fetch (#129416), Desktop bundle-skew (#128183; #127983 already merged).
- `git maintenance register/start` is not used: it writes the user's global gitconfig and installs a launchd/systemd/schtasks job Hermes would not own.

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/gitlock.py`: `consolidate_lazy_fetch_packs` (fold, `gc --auto`, no commit-graph, tree-kill, `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH`); `disable_tree0_auto_maintenance` sets `maintenance.auto`, `gc.writeCommitGraph`, `fetch.writeCommitGraph` to `false` (idempotent, `--local`, hidden console). `gc.auto` is deliberately left alone.
- `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py`, `update_cmd_check.py`: fold during the debris cleanup that `hermes update` and `hermes update --check` already run (both explicit commands; nothing runs `--check` in the background). One shared reporter, `update_cmd_check.fold_lazy_fetch_packs`, announces a fold that will actually run and prints the hand-fold command if the fold runs out of time.
- Fold bound: 20 min, not 120 s. A killed fold restarts from scratch on every update, so the checkouts this exists for (thousands of packs, tens of GiB) would never converge, and `consolidate_lazy_fetch_packs` now returns `None` on timeout instead of a silent 0.
- `scripts/install.sh`, `scripts/install.ps1`: same three keys on fresh and existing treeless checkouts. `install.ps1` function body parse-checked and exercised under PowerShell on Linux.
- `website/docs/getting-started/updating.md`: troubleshooting entry.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gitlock.py`: salvaged mock tests replaced by four real-git invariants.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_gitlock.py` (14 passed).
2. Sabotage: restoring `gc.auto=0` fails 3 tests; removing the commit-graph guard and `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH` fails the Bloom test (11 packs instead of 1).
3. **Live (updater function, real imports, temp `HERMES_HOME`)** on a blobless clone with a Bloom graph, 30 unseen commits and ~100 lazy packs, `update_cmd_check.clear_git_debris()`:

| git | packs before → after | lazy fetches | `.promisor` | history offline | keys |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.50.1 | 102 → 1 | 0 | kept | readable | 3 set, `gc.auto` unset |
| 2.53.0 | 102 → 1 | 0 | kept | readable | 3 set, `gc.auto` unset |
| 2.55.0 | 100 → 1 | 0 | kept | readable | 3 set, `gc.auto` unset |

A second run changes nothing (1 pack).

Baseline note: `test_update_*` files fail identically on stock `main` in this environment (e.g. `test_update_target_identity` 31, `test_update_products` 12, the REAL-hermes-home guard), and `test_tag_fetch_partial_clone.py` times out at 300 s on `main` too. None are touched by this diff.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs (#129712, #127711, #131444, #120411 and keyword variants, all states)
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix (the salvaged commits are unmodified; follow-ups are separate commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` (ran `tests/hermes_cli/test_gitlock*.py`; the wider `test_update_*` set is red identically on `main`)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: NixOS (Linux), git 2.50.1 / 2.53.0 / 2.55.0; PowerShell function on Linux only, not on Windows

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (`updating.md`)
- [x] N/A `cli-config.yaml.example` (no config keys)
- [x] N/A `AGENTS.md`
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact: hidden console flags on the new git spawns, tree-kill via `bounded_probe_run`, `install.ps1` CRLF preserved; `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all` clean
- [x] N/A tool schemas

### Maintainer follow-up (review fix)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Scale measurement, real `tree:0` clone of hermes-agent (40k commits) | 750 packs / 530 MB folded in 5.8 s at 7.4 cores on NVMe. A 39 GiB pack dir on a slow disk is far past 120 s, so the bound is now 20 min |
| Live `hermes update --check`, same clone, 814 packs | printed `Folding 816 lazy-fetch packs into one (one-time; can take several minutes)...` then `(folded 815 ...)`, 589 MB → 247 MB, 1 promisor pack, objects readable with `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` |
| Live `hermes update --check`, bound forced to 1 s on 833 packs | killed mid-repack: printed the `git -C ... -c gc.writeCommitGraph=false gc --auto` hint, no leftover `pack-objects`, no tmp packs, 833 packs intact; the next normal run folded to 1, `git fsck --connectivity-only` clean |
| `test_update_debris_cleanup_folds_and_reports_a_fold_that_runs_out_of_time` | red on the previous head, green on this one. The fixture also turns off auto-maintenance, because each lazy fetch's detached gc was racing the test and folding the packs itself |
| Update suites (32 files) A/B vs previous head | identical failure set apart from the new test (all pre-existing home-guard failures from a local `.worktrees/` checkout) |

## Summary
Fixes #131523.

Preserve host-suspend credit in the cron inactivity and turn-liveness watchdogs, including suspension between the activity sample and the meter's clock reads. Awake inactivity still reaches the configured timeout.

## Prior work and credit
This carries @kohjunhao's #131524 in full via cherry-pick -x, preserving KJH's original authorship, implementation and tests. Independent review identified one remaining sampling-boundary case: fresh sleep credit was truncated against an earlier idle sample, causing premature aborts. A separate commit retains that credit until the next poll, extends both original regression tests, and qualifies the documentation's platform promise.

## Verification
- Main with source tests: 11 passed, 2 failed (original suspend cases).
- Source implementation with expanded tests: 13 passed, 2 failed (sampling-boundary cases).
- Integrated salvage, scripts/run_tests.sh tests/cron tests/agent: 11831 passed, 44 skipped, zero failed.
- Ruff and Windows-footgun scan passed; git diff --check clean.

## Scope and limitations
Clock-controlled production-path tests, not a physical suspend or live model run. Suspend exclusion depends on macOS/Linux monotonic semantics; Windows unchanged. Activity reset retains polling-scale extra grace. Separate diagnostic #127775/#127783 and provider-stream #121878/#122282 remain out of scope. No configuration, activity-generation fencing, or tool schema changes.

The correction also establishes the cron meter before the agent worker starts; a real-thread startup-boundary regression fails before that ordering change. An independent review environment saw seven baseline-equivalent relay integration failures; the worker environment full-suite result above is green.

## What does this PR do?

A turn that has already answered no longer stays "running" until another session's long tool call finishes. The shared-metrics flush, a process-wide Relay barrier, now runs on a background worker instead of the turn thread.

Salvage of #131476 (dskwe), cherry-picked so authorship is kept, plus two fixes on top. Fixes #131460. Overlaps the earlier #118298, which bounds the same call at 500 ms instead of moving it off the turn.

**Root cause.** `finish_task` and `close_session` called `relay.subscribers.flush()` on the caller's thread. `flush()` also waits for every managed tool or LLM call already in flight in any session (documented in `nemo_relay/subscribers.py`). A live thread dump of a stuck Desktop backend showed three finalizing turns parked in `finish_task → _flush_and_export → flush` while three `terminal` tools from other sessions ran. A hard stop cannot interrupt the native wait.

## Related Issue

Fixes #131460

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/observability/relay_shared_metrics.py`
  - #131476: `finish_task` and `close_session` schedule flush + export on one coalescing daemon worker per runtime. Shutdown still flushes synchronously.
  - Follow-up: the worker starts through `spawn_context_thread`. A bare `Thread` dropped the turn's contextvars, so the export read the launch profile's send/consent config instead of the finishing turn's.
  - Follow-up: the worker clears its slot under the lock schedulers check. Before, a trigger landing after the worker saw "nothing pending" but before the thread died set the flag and started no worker, so that flush waited for the next trigger.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_relay_shared_metrics_runtime.py`
  - Two invariants through the real lifecycle hooks: a task end returns while the flush barrier is parked (later ends coalesce into one extra pass), and the worker runs under the finishing turn's profile.
  - Tests that read the store right after a hook now join the worker first. #131476's own tests did not run this file, and three of its tests fail against it.
  - Replaces #131476's bare-instance, wall-clock-bound test.
- Not changed: `record_process_marks_saved` keeps its synchronous flush because it needs the saved ticket back.

## How to Test

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Real `nemo_relay` binding, another scope's managed tool running 5 s: `on_session_end` duration | 5.02 s | 0.00 s |
| Worker's profile with a context-local home override set by the finishing turn | launch home | the turn's home |
| `test_relay_shared_metrics_runtime.py`, 6 consecutive runs | n/a | 54 passed, 0 failed |
| Shared-metrics, relay and gateway metric tests (12 files) | n/a | 243 passed |

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_relay_shared_metrics_runtime.py`
2. The profile test fails without the `spawn_context_thread` change.

items.body:
With shared metrics turned on (`telemetry.shared_metrics.enabled`), every provider stream goes through NeMo Relay's managed pipeline. Relay reads the next provider chunk before it hands the current one to Hermes. Our provider callback did that read with a blocking `next()` on the stream's private event loop. As a result, each chunk sat in Relay until the provider sent the following one.

Users with metrics on see two Desktop symptoms:

- **The model looks stopped, the timer keeps going, and the queue doesn't drain.** Whatever arrived before a provider pause (thinking, tool-call arguments, a slow upstream) stays hidden. The turn is still running, so queued follow-ups keep waiting.
- **Steers stack up below the output.** Pressing Enter mid-turn redirects the request and aborts it. The abort throws away the withheld text before anyone sees it, so the user bubbles pile up with nothing between them. Reloading only shows what was actually persisted.

The fix moves the blocking provider read onto a worker thread, so Relay can hand chunk N over while chunk N+1 is still in flight. That's KoNit-K's change from #120460, cherry-picked with authorship. I rewrote its comment, which blamed starvation between concurrent streams; production gives every stream its own loop, so that can't happen.

### Repro

The repro uses the real Electron app, a real `hermes serve`, and a scripted provider that pauses after its first chunk.

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| first chunk on screen while the provider is paused | never (`U1 slow one 1s… 5s`, timer only) | ~0.7s |
| steer mid-stream, persisted turn | `user, assistant:"" , user, reply` | `user, partial reply, user, reply` |
| two steers in a row | three user bubbles stacked | partial reply between each |

I also reproduced it in isolation against `nemo_relay.llm.stream_execute` with a provider that yields once and then blocks for 3s. On main, chunk 1 reaches the consumer only at +3.01s. On this branch it arrives at +0.00s.

### Tests

- `tests/agent/test_relay_llm.py::test_managed_stream_delivers_each_chunk_before_the_provider_sends_the_next`: a single managed stream whose provider waits until its first chunk has been consumed. On main it deadlocks until the 10s guard fails. This replaces #120460's two-loop test, which covered a topology production never builds and used a 150ms wall-clock bound.
- `apps/desktop/e2e/core/relay-managed-steer.spec.ts` turns Relay managed execution on. It checks that the paused first chunk is painted, steers on top of it, queues a follow-up under the steered reply, then asserts that the queue drains, Stop goes away, and the transcript oracle holds. On main it fails at the first assertion.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` across the relay suites: 69 passed.

Supersedes #120460.

The open desktop busy/queue PRs and issues I surveyed don't cover this. They harden the renderer against a missing turn end (#118905, #128528, #129213, #119673, #124914, #66591), and those mechanisms are separate. #118901 and #70871 have similar symptoms, but the reports don't show metrics turned on, so they stay open.


Companion to #131683, which fixed the other way shared metrics stalls a turn: the end-of-turn flush waited on other sessions' in-flight tools, so an answered turn kept running. This PR fixes the in-stream half. The withheld-chunk test still fails on main with #131683 merged.

## What does this PR do?

`python scripts/release.py abandon` now force-cancels the attempt's in-progress `Stable Release` runs, so abandoning an rc stops its CI instead of leaving it building.

Before, abandon deleted the draft and wrote the marker, and the run kept going. With autopublish on, a live run can publish the draft abandon just cleared.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `scripts/releases/entrypoint.py`: `abandon` lists runs of `stable-release.yml` on the claim ref (`gh run list --branch <rc tag>`) and runs `gh run cancel <id> --force` on each one whose status is not `completed`.
- Order is: refuse if published, cancel runs, delete draft, write marker. The marker takes the attempt out of the outstanding set, so a cancel failure after it could never be retried; before it, a failure leaves the attempt outstanding and abandon can just be rerun. A published release is refused before anything is cancelled.
- `abandon_steps` prints a `Cancelled <url>` line per run. The `delete` callable is renamed `execute` since it now runs cancels too.
- `website/docs/developer-guide/stable-releases.md`: one clause on the new behaviour.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/scripts/test_release_entrypoint.py` (36 pass). Two new tests: runs cancelled with `--force` in order before the draft delete and marker, completed runs skipped; a failed cancel writes no marker. The published-refusal test now also asserts nothing is cancelled.
2. Against the base, the new force-cancel test fails (A/B with the source diff reverted).
3. `gh run list --repo NousResearch/hermes-agent --workflow stable-release.yml --branch rc.34-v0.21.5 --json databaseId,url,status --limit 100` returns the shape `_in_progress_runs` reads. I ran this read-only against the real repo; I did not run a live cancel.

## What does this PR do?

`hermes uninstall --gui --dry-run` ignored `--dry-run`. With `--yes`, or after answering `yes` at the prompt, it deleted the GUI build, the Electron user data and the workspace-root `node_modules`. The workspace root is not a GUI artifact: it holds the hoisted dependencies of the TUI and the dashboard as well.

This PR makes every dry run a real preview, stops `--gui` from deleting dependencies other frontends share, and makes `--gui` clean up a leftover desktop install record so a removed macOS app is not reinstalled by the next update.

| Path (sandboxed `HERMES_HOME`, real CLI) | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `uninstall --gui --dry-run --yes` | **Deletes** GUI artifacts + root `node_modules` | Preview only, nothing removed |
| `uninstall --gui --dry-run` in a TTY, answering `yes` | **Prompts, then deletes** | No prompt, nothing removed |
| `uninstall --gui --dry-run` without a TTY | Refused ("requires an interactive terminal") | Preview only |
| `uninstall --dry-run` without a TTY | Refused | Preview only |
| `uninstall --gui --yes` | Removes GUI artifacts **and root `node_modules`** | Removes GUI artifacts; root `node_modules` kept |
| Removal plan | Omits `desktop-installed-apps.json`, which is then deleted | Lists it |
| `uninstall --gui --yes` when only `desktop-installed-apps.json` is left | "No Hermes Chat GUI installation was found", record kept | Record previewed and removed |
| `python -W error -c 'import hermes_cli.uninstall'` | `SyntaxError: invalid escape sequence '\c'` | Imports cleanly |

## Related Issue

Fixes #128974

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

Four commits, each authored by the contributor whose work it carries:

1. **`fix(cli): honor --dry-run in uninstall --gui`** (liuhao1024, from #128981; co-authored by Yuan Li, #128977)
   - `hermes_cli/uninstall.py` `run_gui_uninstall()`: return after printing the removal plan when `--dry-run` is set, before the confirmation prompt, mirroring `run_data_uninstall()`. Covers the `--yes` path and the interactive path.
   - `hermes_cli/main.py` `cmd_uninstall()`: exempt `--dry-run` from the `--gui` TTY gate, as `--data` already does.
   - `hermes_cli/uninstall.py`: make the `_hermes_path_markers` docstring a raw string (the `git\cmd` example raised the SyntaxWarning shown in the report).
2. **`fix(cli): let uninstall dry-runs run without a TTY and list the install record`** (itsflownium, from #131147)
   - `hermes_cli/main.py`: exempt `--dry-run` from the TTY gate on plain `hermes uninstall`. `run_uninstall()` returns from `_print_uninstall_dry_run()` before any removal.
   - `hermes_cli/uninstall.py`: list `desktop-installed-apps.json` in the GUI removal plan, since `uninstall_gui()` deletes it.
   - `website/docs/user-guide/desktop.md`: document `--gui --dry-run`.
   - `tests/hermes_cli/test_gui_uninstall_retention.py`: CLI-level regression covering `--gui --dry-run` with and without `--yes`, and plain `uninstall --dry-run`.
3. **`fix(gui): keep shared workspace node_modules on uninstall --gui`** (itsflownium, from #131147)
   - `hermes_cli/gui_uninstall.py`: drop `hermes-agent/node_modules` from the GUI artifact list and correct the docstring that claimed the root only carries Electron.
   - `hermes_cli/uninstall.py`: list the shared dependencies under "Kept intact".
   - `website/docs/user-guide/desktop.md`: update the source-checkout note, which promised the root `node_modules` would be removed.
   - Regression test: a real `--gui --yes` removal keeps agent source, venv, config, `.env`, sessions and the root `node_modules`, and removes every GUI artifact.
4. **`fix(gui): detect leftover desktop install records`** (itsflownium, from #131147)
   - `hermes_cli/gui_uninstall.py` `gui_is_installed()`: count `desktop-installed-apps.json`. On macOS, `_installed_desktop_apps()` treats a recorded `Hermes.app` that has gone missing as one to reinstall, and its docstring relies on the GUI uninstall deleting the record. Before this commit, removing the app by hand and then running `hermes uninstall --gui` hit the "nothing installed" early return, kept the record, and the next `hermes update` / `hermes desktop` put the app back. No new removal targets: `uninstall_gui()` already deletes the record.
   - The retention tests now run twice, with a complete install and with the record as the only GUI artifact.

Why the root `node_modules` stays: the root `package.json` is an npm workspace (`apps/*`, `ui-tui`, `ui-tui/packages/*`, `web`, `tests-js`). Per `package-lock.json`, 14 of `ui-tui`'s 15 and 35 of `web`'s 37 direct dependencies resolve from the root `node_modules`. Electron itself resolves from `apps/desktop/node_modules/electron`, which is still removed, so the large Electron payload is still freed. Commit 3 is independent of commits 1–2 and can be dropped without affecting the dry-run fix.

### Credit

Several contributors fixed this in parallel. This PR combines the pieces:

- @liuhao1024 (#128981) and @dskwe (#128977): the `--gui` dry-run fix, TTY exemption and escape fix (commit 1).
- @itsflownium (#131147): plain-uninstall TTY exemption, accurate removal plan, root `node_modules` retention, install-record detection, docs and tests (commits 2–4).
- @helix4u: traced the macOS reinstall path and asked for commit 4 to be included.
- @JerryLiu369 (#129180, #129417) and @JoaoMarcos44 (#129027) independently reached the same TTY-gate and root `node_modules` changes; salch-cred's commit in #129501 carried the same dry-run fix.

## How to Test

1. Reproduce on `main` in a throwaway `HERMES_HOME` with a fake source-checkout GUI build (root `node_modules`, `apps/desktop/{dist,release,node_modules}`, build stamp, install record, Electron userData): `hermes uninstall --gui --dry-run --yes` deletes the GUI artifacts and the root `node_modules`.
2. On this branch, the same command, plus `--gui --dry-run` without a TTY, `--gui --dry-run` in a PTY answering `yes`, and `uninstall --dry-run` without a TTY, all exit 0 and leave every file byte-identical.
3. `hermes uninstall --gui --yes` removes the GUI artifacts, install record and userData, and keeps the agent, config, sessions, `.env` and root `node_modules`.
4. Leave only `desktop-installed-apps.json`: `hermes uninstall --gui --dry-run` lists it and keeps it; `hermes uninstall --gui --yes` removes it.
5. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_gui_uninstall_retention.py`: all 4 cases fail with `main`'s `hermes_cli/{main,uninstall,gui_uninstall}.py`; the 2 `record_only` cases fail with the commit-3 `gui_uninstall.py`; all 4 pass on this branch.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass. Ran the full suite with `scripts/run_tests.sh` in a PM-built test environment on commits 1–3: 56,063 passed, 1 failed. The failure, `tests/website/test_extract_plugins.py::test_git_dates_added_is_first_commit_updated_is_last_and_renames_keep_added`, comes from the host's git 2.43 printing `%cI` as `+00:00` instead of `Z`, and it fails identically on unmodified `main`. The full suite ran with `main` at `5c975b9`. On the current head (rebased onto `cc761dd`, plus commit 4), the focused suites (19 files, 187 passed, 0 failed) and the end-to-end run below were repeated; the full suite was not re-run for commit 4.
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Linux (kernel 6.8)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [ ] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A. The change is path-list and flag handling only, but it was exercised on Linux only; macOS/Windows run in CI. The macOS reinstall path behind commit 4 was traced in `hermes_cli/main_desktop.py` (`_installed_desktop_apps`, `_refresh_installed_desktop_apps`), not run on a Mac.
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

Focused uninstall/GUI suites on the current head (19 files): 187 passed, 0 failed, 27 platform-skipped. Commits 1–2 without commit 3: the dry-run regression test and the existing GUI/dry-run/`cmd_uninstall` suites pass (15 tests), so commit 3 can be dropped on its own. `ruff check` on the changed Python files: all checks passed. `git diff --check`: clean.

Real CLI end to end, sandboxed `HOME`/`HERMES_HOME`/XDG dirs, `hermes_cli.__file__` asserted to be this branch, run with a complete GUI install and with only the install record: `--gui --dry-run --yes`, `--gui --dry-run` without a TTY, `--gui --dry-run` in a PTY answering `yes`, and `uninstall --dry-run` without a TTY all exit 0 with every fixture file byte-identical. `--gui --yes` removes every GUI artifact (in the record-only case, the record) and keeps agent source, venv, config, `.env`, sessions and the root `node_modules`. `python -W error -c 'import hermes_cli.uninstall'` with a fresh bytecode cache exits 0.

`hermes uninstall --gui --dry-run` in a PTY, answering `yes`, on this branch:

```
Will remove:
  • …/hermes-agent/apps/desktop/dist
  • …/hermes-agent/apps/desktop/release
  • …/hermes-agent/apps/desktop/node_modules
  • …/desktop-build-stamp.json
  • …/desktop-installed-apps.json  (desktop install record)
  • …/config/Hermes  (desktop app data)

  • The Hermes agent at …/hermes-agent
  • Your config, sessions, and secrets under …

Dry run: no files or processes changed.
```

`hermes uninstall --gui --yes` with only the install record left:

```

items.body:
A partial-clone install checkout keeps git's own lazy-fetch pack fold between updates again (follow-up to #131679).

## What changed

- `hermes_cli/gitlock.py`: `_TREE0_MAINTENANCE_OFF` swaps `maintenance.auto=false` for `maintenance.commit-graph.enabled=false`. `gc.writeCommitGraph=false` and `fetch.writeCommitGraph=false` stay.
- `_restore_auto_maintenance`: an install that already has `maintenance.auto=false` from #131679 (merged 4e3fcd5) has exactly that value unset on its next `hermes update` / `hermes update --check`.
- `scripts/install.sh`, `scripts/install.ps1`: the same key swap (CRLF preserved).
- `website/docs/getting-started/updating.md`: the key list.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gitlock.py`: one invariant. Starting from `maintenance.auto=false`, a clone carrying the keys never leaves more lazy-fetch packs than a stock-config clone does.

Root cause: #127711's loop needs a commit-graph write. `maintenance.auto=false` stopped it, but it also stopped the post-fetch `gc --auto` that git ≤ 2.53 runs after every lazy fetch, and nothing calls `--check` automatically (I checked the banner prefetch and Desktop). So packs piled up until a manual update.

## Validation

Live, real `clear_git_debris()` (worktree imports), real tree:0 clone with a changed-path (Bloom) commit-graph, starting from `maintenance.auto=false`, then 100 more lazy fetches with stock git:

| git | updater fold | packs after 100 lazy fetches: main | this PR | commit-graph writes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.53.0 | 122 → 1 | 101 | **1** | 0 |
| 2.55.0 (built from tarball) | 322 → 1 | 101 | 101 | 0 |

Stock 2.55 maintenance doesn't fold lazy-fetch packs at all, with or without these keys, so on 2.55 the updater's fold remains the only one (unchanged). With only the new key set, stock `git gc --auto` still does 0 commit-graph writes on both versions. The #127711 loop (123 → 31 packs, 30 `git maintenance` children) stays closed.

| | 2.53.0 | 2.55.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/hermes_cli/test_gitlock.py`, this PR | 15 passed | 15 passed |
| same, `gitlock.py` swapped to main's | **1 failed** (`assert 5 <= 1`) | 15 passed (no stock fold to lose) |

ruff, `check_no_tmp_literals`, `check-windows-footguns --all`, `bash -n install.sh`, `check_doc_links` are all clean. `install.ps1` is a one-token change to the key list, not run on Windows.

## Earlier-cut migration (folds #131741, review point from @Godhet)

Nothing records who wrote a `maintenance.auto=false`, so it is migrated only under the fingerprint both earlier Hermes cuts left: `maintenance.auto=false` together with `fetch.writeCommitGraph=false`, and no `maintenance.commit-graph.enabled`. The first pass writes that key, so the migration runs once. An operator's own lone `maintenance.auto=false` is never touched (@ethernet8023's commit and test, cherry-picked from #131741).

The same migration removes the `gc.auto=0` that 73c17151f61 (Sep 29) persisted. 6880ffc1afa stopped writing it but never removed it, and `gc --auto` with `gc.auto=0` skips every heuristic, so **on main the update's fold is a no-op for every checkout configured Sep 29 to Oct 2**. #131741's fingerprint also required `gc.writeCommitGraph=false`, which only the Oct 2 cut wrote.

Real `clear_git_debris()`, treeless clone with 203 lazy-fetch packs; git 2.53.0 and 2.55.0 identical:

| checkout keys | main | #131741 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sep 29 cut (`maintenance.auto=false`, `gc.auto=0`, `fetch.writeCommitGraph=false`) | 203 → **203**, keys kept | 203 → **203**, keys kept | 203 → 1, both migrated |
| Oct 2 cut (+ `gc.writeCommitGraph=false`) | 203 → 1, `maintenance.auto=false` kept | 203 → 1, migrated | 203 → 1, migrated |
| operator's own lone `maintenance.auto=false` | 203 → 1, kept | 203 → 1, kept | 203 → 1, **kept** |

`tests/hermes_cli/test_gitlock.py`: 17 passed on 2.53.0 and 2.55.0. `test_a_checkout_the_first_cut_configured_folds_on_update` fails with main's and #131741's `gitlock.py` on both versions (`assert 5 == 1`). `test_an_operators_own_maintenance_auto_false_is_never_erased` fails with this PR's first commit (the unconditional unset).

## What does this PR do?

Replaces the `ci-reviewed` label gate with `.github/CODEOWNERS`, and deletes the machinery that existed to support the label.

The gate had three parts: classify which paths are sensitive, check for a label, and (in `label-rerun.yml`) wait for the CI run to finish and rerun failed jobs when the label was added. CODEOWNERS replaces all three for path-based review: GitHub requests the reviewer and enforces the approval, with no label, no classification, and no rerun.

### What moves to CODEOWNERS (`@NousResearch/hermes-agent-core`)

CI and the autofix job execute these, or they decide what users install or run. Patterns without a leading slash match at any depth.

| Group | Paths |
|---|---|
| What CI runs | `.github/` (workflows, composite actions, CODEOWNERS itself), `scripts/ci/` (the scripts the workflows call), `eslint.config.*`, `.prettierrc` |
| MCP catalog | `optional-mcps/`, `hermes_cli/mcp_catalog.py` |
| Runs at install or interpreter startup | `setup.py`, `setup.cfg`, `sitecustomize.py`, `usercustomize.py`, `*.pth` |
| Dependency manifests, pins, images | `pyproject.toml`, `package.json`, `uv.lock` (incl. `pm/uv.lock`), `*package-lock.json` (incl. `nix/node-gyp-11-4-0-package-lock.json`), `flake.lock`, `pm/lock.json`, `*Dockerfile` (3 tracked) |
| Supply-chain config | `.npmrc` (holds the 14-day `min-release-age` npm quarantine), `pm/artifact-mirror.json` (where PM fetches artifacts from) |
| Installers | `scripts/install.sh`, `scripts/install.ps1`, `scripts/install.cmd`, `scripts/gen-bootstrap-pins.py` (generates the pins the installers carry) |
| Trust model, third-party pins | `SECURITY.md`, `plugin-catalog/` (each entry pins a third-party repo by sha) |

An earlier revision of this PR left `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `flake.lock` and `package*.json` out on the assumption that the `main` ruleset's required-reviewers rule covers them. They are listed here so they request review on their own and do not depend on the ruleset.

### What this does NOT replace: content scanning

CODEOWNERS matches paths, not diff content. The supply-chain scan's content patterns (base64 decode + `exec`/`eval`, obfuscated `subprocess` commands) can fire in any `.py` file, so they cannot be owned. They used to be overridable with the label; there is no override now. The scan fails on its own again, the way it did before #68833 routed it through the label gate. The patterns are narrow by design, so a false positive should mean fixing the pattern. If you would rather keep an override for these, that is a follow-up and not something CODEOWNERS can provide.

The scan's `.pth` and install-hook path checks are dropped, since CODEOWNERS owns those paths now.

## Changes made

- Add `.github/CODEOWNERS` (every pattern matches at least one tracked file, except the `setup.cfg`, `sitecustomize.py`, `usercustomize.py` and `*.pth` guards, which match none today).
- Delete `review-labels.yml`, `scripts/ci/emit_review_status.py`, `tests/ci/test_emit_review_status.py`.
- `label-rerun.yml`: drop the `rerun-review-labels` job. The `run-e2e` rerun job stays.
- `ci.yaml`: drop the `review-labels` job, its `needs` entry, and the `ci_review`, `ci_review_files`, `mcp_catalog` detect outputs.
- `classify_changes.py`, `detect-changes/action.yml`: drop the same three outputs and their path lists.
- `required_results.py`: `review-labels` is no longer a PR-only job.
- `supply-chain-audit.yml`: scan reports and fails on its own; drop `critical_findings` plumbing and the `ci-reviewed` override.
- `lockfile-diff.yml`: the comment text now points at a core review instead of the label.

## How to test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/ci/` (22 files, 320 passed, 0 failed).
2. `actionlint` on the touched workflows reports only pre-existing findings (`if: false` at `ci.yaml:194`, two SC2034 in `lint.yml`).
3. This PR touches `.github/`, so it should itself request a `hermes-agent-core` review.

### One decision for reviewers

`plugin-catalog/` matches 354 tracked files, and community plugin PRs touch it often, so each of those PRs now waits on core review. Reverting is deleting the `/plugin-catalog/` line.

I did not run the changed workflows on Actions; CI on this PR is the first real run of the new `supply-chain-audit.yml` shape.

## What does this PR do?

Adds Sigrex to the MCP catalog and re-pins the existing `sigrex` plugin entry to v1.0.4.

- **MCP catalog entry.** Sigrex ships a remote MCP server at `https://mcp.sigrex.io` (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, Client ID Metadata Document). The entry gives users a supported sign-in path: Connect in Desktop, `hermes mcp install sigrex` in the terminal, or "connect Sigrex" in chat.
- **Why it's needed.** The `sigrex` plugin declares the same server in its `mcp.json`, but Hermes does not run OAuth for a server that comes from a portable plugin, so that entry stays unconnected (401). The catalog entry writes `auth: oauth` to `mcp_servers`, which Hermes does sign in to. A user's own `sigrex` entry takes precedence over the plugin's, and the plugin keeps providing the skill.
- **Plugin re-pin.** v1.0.4 documents the connect step for Hermes in the README, a new `after-install.md` and the bundled skill. No change to `mcp.json`, no Python, no executables.

## What does this PR do?

Restoring a Hermes window that minimize-to-tray hid no longer leaves it dead to mouse and keyboard on Windows when the restore does not come from the tray (relaunch, deep link, notification click).

## Related Issue

Fixes #127349

Overlaps #127350, which calls `focus()` only. That variant stays dead on real hardware (table below).

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/electron/minimize-to-tray.ts`: when the `restore` or `show` handler releases a window that the tray hid, it now runs `show()` then `focus()` on Windows. The call is deferred with `setImmediate`, as the hide already is. `released()` now returns whether the window was tray-hidden, so windows the tray never hid and the tray's own `restoreHidden()` path (which already releases first) are unchanged.
- `apps/desktop/electron/minimize-to-tray.test.ts`: 2 tests. An OS-driven restore of a tray-hidden window activates it (red on base), and a window the tray never hid is left alone.

Root cause: `focusWindow()` (used by `second-instance` and others) calls `restore()`, which paints the window but does not make it the OS foreground window. Electron reports `isFocused() === true` and fires `focus`, so the guarded `focus()` is skipped. Only the tray path ran `show()` + `focus()`.

## How to Test

Real Electron 40 (arm64) on Windows 11 arm64. Probe: real `minimize-to-tray.ts` + the real `focusWindow` and `ensureMainWindow`. Window options match the chat window (`titleBarStyle: 'hidden'`, `titleBarOverlay`, `focusOnNavigation: false`). Each cycle: minimize (tray hides it), restore, then a real `SendInput` click and key press. A page counter and a textarea show if the input arrived. The foreground lock timeout was set to 0 for the run, so the result is not caused by Windows foreground rules. It was restored afterwards.

| Restore path | Code | Cycles with live input |
|---|---|---|
| relaunch (`focusWindow`) | base | 0 / 3 |
| relaunch | #127350 (`focus()` in handlers) | 0 / 4 |
| relaunch | `restore()` + `focus()` forced | 0 / 3 |
| relaunch | `setSkipTaskbar(false)` first | 0 / 3 |
| relaunch | `restore()` + `show()` + `focus()` | 3 / 3 |
| relaunch | this PR | 4 / 4 |
| tray (`restore()`) | this PR | 4 / 4 |

On every dead cycle, Electron reported `focus` and `isFocused()` true, but `GetForegroundWindow()` was another app's window. The baseline click before the first minimize always worked.

Unit: `vitest run --project electron electron/minimize-to-tray.test.ts` (9 pass; the new activation test fails with the source change reverted), `tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json --noEmit`, `eslint` on both files.

## Notes for review

- Not run: a packaged build, the `mica` backdrop variant, and a restore with the foreground lock timeout at its default.
- Separate bug, not in this PR: `shouldFocusToTakeKeyboard` destructures `isFocused` from the window and throws `Object has been destroyed` (#131732 fixes it). It does not change these results: the table's last rows pass with and without it.
- `restoreHidden()` stays the only place that restores every hidden window. This change activates one window at a time, as the OS restores it.

## Checklist

Adds `plugin-catalog/agent-mail-gateway.yaml`, submitted by the repository owner.

**What it does:** a portable Agent Plugins v1 package that ships one skill, `agent-mail`. It teaches an agent how to use its own mailbox through [Agent Mail Gateway](https://github.com/dominikamann/agent-mail-gateway), a self-hosted email gateway (IMAP/SMTP behind per-agent API keys, sender/recipient allow lists, HTML-to-Markdown, calendar invites): checking and reading mail, replying in-thread, attachments, creating/moving/cancelling invites without duplicates, what each error code means, and rules for treating email content as data rather than instructions.

**Hermes surfaces used:** portable package with `plugin.json` + `skills/agent-mail/SKILL.md` only. No Python, no hooks, no middleware, no `mcp.json`.

**Pin:** `d4d857c3d6e13ef1f522971fe6b1fd7e8e7d89d5` (tag v0.1.2), `subdir: integrations/hermes/agent-mail-gateway`. `hermes plugins validate` at that commit: portable manifest ✓, manifest fields ✓, security scan: safe.

**Disclosure (rule 13):**
- The plugin itself makes no network calls, runs no commands, starts no processes and stores no credentials.
- The skill refers to tools of an MCP server the user configures separately in `mcp_servers` (their own self-hosted gateway URL and their own API key from the profile's `.env`); setup is documented in [docs/hermes.md](https://github.com/dominikamann/agent-mail-gateway/blob/main/docs/hermes.md).
- No telemetry. No self-updating code.

Duplicate and misordered replies keep coming back because the core e2e suite exercises each transition once, while the bug reports involve specific combinations of turn shape and timing. This PR forces those combinations, makes the transcript oracle stricter about ordering, and fixes the duplicate the new tests found on main.

### Fix: a tool turn that completes during the switch-back hydrate rendered its reply twice

Repro: switch away from a chat while a tool turn is still answering, then switch back. If `message.complete` arrives while the switch-back history page is still loading, the answer paints twice (sometimes frozen on its first chunk, sometimes healing at the next refresh). The new `switch-back-race` tool-turn case was red on main for this. The same mechanism shows up in four places, each matching on text that history's folded tool bubble never has:

- `appendLiveSessionProjection` stood the stale activate snapshot down only for a tool-free reply. It now stands down when the committed bubble ends in a reply covering the snapshot. A mid-turn commit ends on a tool, so a running turn still projects.
- `overlayConcurrentMessageChanges` only added and replaced rows. A page composed from the older baseline could bring back a live row the store had already retired into the committed reply. Such a row now stays retired.
- The same overlay dropped the settled live reply only when the page had a message with the same words. It now matches the reply's stored row (`final_assistant_row_id` → `sourceRowId`) first, then a folded bubble's answer text (the text after its last tool).
- When the page still carried the reply's streaming copy under the same id, the overlay replaced it in place without that check. The check now runs first and drops the stale copy.

Four `utils.test.ts` cases fail on main and pass here. The switch-back race passed 16/16 locally (`--repeat-each 4`).

### The oracle now also checks order between checkpoints

At each checkpoint, the oracle already required every stored message to render exactly once and in stored order. Its in-page sampler also failed any frame where a message appeared twice.

The sampler now also fails any frame where:
- a reply renders above its own prompt;
- two messages swap places compared with an earlier frame.

So a wrong order that corrects itself before the final check still fails. Reasoning is left out, because live and history place the thinking block differently. This applies to every spec that uses `assertTranscriptOracle`.

A steer that lands at a tool boundary is stored as its own user row, wrapped in the out-of-band marker the model sees. The oracle now compares that row by the user's own words, which is what the app shows. Rows the backend writes itself (`process_complete`, `model_switch` and the other notice kinds hydration draws as notices) are skipped, since they aren't messages.

### New scenarios: `reply-settle-paths.spec.ts`

- **An answer repeated as the final reply.** The model answers beside a housekeeping tool, then sends an empty follow-up. The backend reuses the answer as the final reply, so the same text arrives as `message.interim` and again as `message.complete`.
  - Plain: must render once.
  - With a `review.summary` row delivered before that turn's `message.complete`, the order #131626 reports. The test routes the socket and holds that one frame until the row has been delivered. It renders once on main, so this shape does not reproduce #131626. It stays as a guard.
- **A steer at every point of a tool turn:**
  - while reasoning;
  - while the narration before a tool streams;
  - while the tool runs (the steered command finishes in the background and its notification turn is checked too);
  - while the answer after it streams;
  - two steers back to back.
- **A finished two-tool turn, then reload and switch-back.**

### `switch-back-race.spec.ts`

Both orders ("reply completes first" and "switch-back hydrate resolves first") now also run with a tool turn (#128809).

### Harness

`provider.scriptPrompt(label, needle, steps)` scripts requests that carry no turn marker, such as the background review fork.

A Windows update no longer fails with `[WinError 5] Access is denied` when a running Hermes process still has the replaced Python runtime's DLLs mapped: the held tree is set aside and deleted later, and the update completes.

Reported in Discord support (Windows 11, Desktop install): `hermes update` failed twice in source preparation deleting `.previous-python-*/DLLs/libcrypto-3-x64.dll`, then again deleting a `.displaced-*` tree after a rollback. Each time the new runtime was already published (or the old one already restored); only the garbage cleanup failed, and it failed the whole update.

## Changes

- `pm/install.py::_discard_entry` owns every cleanup that runs after a publish or restore has finished: the displaced `.previous-*` entry (publish and settle arms), the restored-over `.displaced-*` tree, and the `fetch-*` archives. When the delete fails it renames the tree to `.reclaim-<uuid>` (Windows allows renaming a tree with mapped images) and logs a warning instead of raising.
  - The `.previous-<entry>` slot is free again, so the next publish of the same entry is not blocked by a still-held leftover.
  - A half-deleted tree can never be picked up by a later restore.
- `_reclaim_set_aside` deletes `.reclaim-*` trees whose hold is gone (single attempt, no retry sleep). It runs at the start of every install under the store lock, and from `hermes pm gc`.
- An interrupted restore's `.displaced-*` tree (never set aside) is still left alone by gc.
- Restore and verify failures are still fatal. Only cleanup of trees that are already garbage became best-effort. A rollback whose own cleanup is held now re-raises the error that caused the rollback, so the cleanup error no longer hides it.

Root cause: `_remove_entry` raises after ~2 s of retries, and all four post-commit cleanup sites called it as if a failed delete meant a failed install.

## Validation

| Check | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| **Live Windows** (`windows-latest`, runs 37070065756 / 37070071146, real `LoadLibraryW` of a DLL inside the live entry, reinstall over it; `wine2e/pm-held-red` vs `wine2e/pm-held-green`) | `InstallError: faketool: install failed: [WinError 5] Access is denied: …\.previous-faketool-1.0-win32-x64\DLLs\held.dll` | pass: install succeeds while the DLL stays mapped, the tree is set aside, and `hermes pm gc` removes it after `FreeLibrary` (run 37070071146) |
| `test_held_replaced_entry_does_not_fail_reinstall_and_is_reclaimed` (publish arm, two reinstalls while held, gc after release) | FAIL `PermissionError` | pass |
| `test_held_displacement_does_not_fail_restore_and_gc_spares_interrupted_one` (restore arm + gc selectivity) | FAIL `PermissionError` | pass |
| `tests/pm/test_pm_core.py`, `tests/pm/test_recovery.py` (rebased on main after #128955) | | 46 passed, 2 skipped (host-marked) |

The windows-only test runs on the PR's Windows lane. The two cross-platform tests model the hold by patching `_remove_entry`, because Linux can't hold a file the way Windows does.

## Credit

Consolidates the proposals for #124807, with authorship preserved:
- #124819 by @janviernine: best-effort `.previous-*` cleanup on both arms (earliest). Its commit is cherry-picked here.
- #128955 by @helix4u was merged to main while this PR was in CI. It added the `.displaced-*` restore arm with a `.restored` sidecar marker for gc. This PR replaces that marker with the set-aside rename, so the four cleanup sites share one mechanism. Its gc selectivity contract (an interrupted restore's displacement is never reclaimed) is kept and still tested.
- #124858 by @dskwe: the same publish-arm fix. It is superseded, and its review findings (leaked orphan, settle arm, `fetch-*` arm) are addressed here.

Review findings from @Enough1122 on #124819/#124858 (version-bump orphan unreachable by gc, restore arm still fatal, `fetch-*` arm) are all covered by this change.

Not handled: a `.displaced-*` tree that a main build since #128955 marked with `.restored` is no longer reclaimed by gc. That window is hours and only affects main-channel Windows installs that hit a held restore, so there is no compatibility code for it.

Fixes #124807
