items.title: fix(desktop): Bots keep each machine's bot identity when two backends share a profile name

items.body:
Desktop now names every bot from its own backend, and a save writes only its own change onto the server's copy, so a stale or legacy local record can no longer rename a bot on another machine or reach the relay roster.

## Symptom (Discord report, Agent 0.21.5 + Desktop on Linux)

Local agent and a VPS agent, both with a profile literally named `default` ("Agent B" local, "Agent A" remote). Desktop showed the VPS bot as "Agent B", group prompts sent to the VPS told it "You are @agent-b", the VPS `profile.yaml` later acquired `ui_meta['hermes-bots'].title: Agent B` despite `display_name: Agent A`, and the relay roster republished it.

## Root cause

Desktop treated its local bot-meta cache as an authority in three places:

| Path | On main | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Save (`saveBotMeta`) | sent the whole cached entry as the server's `hermes-bots` namespace, so any field the cache held and the server did not became server truth | reads the namespace from the bot's own backend, writes that + the save's patch, guarded by the existing per-key CAS (`ui_meta_expected_revisions`), re-reads on conflict |
| Name of a bot on a non-active connection | Electron read `profile.title` from `/api/profiles`, which has always been `bot_title`, and `mergeServerMeta` ran only over the active source's rows, so these bots were named by whatever this Desktop last cached | Electron maps `bot_title` (empty included); reconciliation covers every live row; a local title the backend does not report is dropped |
| Bare-key reads | `botFriendlyNames` read `meta[bot.name]` for any non-remote row and `groupSpeakerLabel` fell back to `meta[profile]`: a scoped `default` borrowed the title another machine's `default` wrote in single-source days | reads use the row's own key; the bare legacy rung applies only to unscoped rosters; mention completion goes through `botRosterMeta` |

Also: a remote `default` with a real `display_name` no longer gets swapped for the connection label.

Second commit (independent review findings):

- **Edit Profile sends only what the user changed** since it opened (`edit-profile-look.ts`). Before, every seeded field rode along, so changing a color reverted a rename made elsewhere meanwhile, and on a thin row with no local record it cleared the backend title.
- **Rows retained from an earlier paint never reconcile.** When a source stops answering, the pane keeps its last-painted rows; they are now tagged `retained` and `mergeServerMeta` skips them (and any unreachable-source row), so an outage cannot revert a newer title.
- **A title alone never mints a record**, which would shadow a configured alias's avatar/color/pin in `botRosterMeta`. It only corrects an existing record; the row already carries the backend's title.

## Validation

**Live repro (real Desktop + two real `hermes serve` backends, Playwright, reporter's stale `bot-meta-v2` seeded):**

| | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Bots pane, VPS row | `Agent B` | `Agent A` |
| VPS `profile.yaml` after "Pin to top" on that row | `title: Agent B` written, plus `color`, `pinned` | `color` kept, `pinned: true` added, no title |
| Edit Profile on that row; VPS renamed to "Renamed elsewhere" while open; only the color changed | previous head: `title: ''` written (rename wiped), plus `shape`, `imageKind` | `title: Renamed elsewhere` kept; only `color` + `custom` written |
| Local gateway `bot_relay/roster.json` | Agent A when read 8 s after the pin; the relay publishes `title \|\| display_name`, so its next refresh carries the injected Agent B | Agent A |

- Unit invariants (red on base, green here), `data.bot-meta.test.ts`:
  - a save ships only its patch on top of the server namespace and re-reads after a CAS conflict (the stale cached title and color never travel)
  - the remote `default` is named, tagged, and prompted (`You are @agent-a`) from its own backend, both as a thin row and as the active source; a keyed speaker with no live row never resolves to the bare-key title
- Changed existing tests: `data.bot-meta`, `hidden-bots`, `profile-ops`, `bot-row` mocks now answer `profiles.list`, since a save reads the server namespace before it writes. No assertion changed.
  - only a fresh backend answer corrects a record (a retained row cannot revert a newer title), and a title alone mints no record (red on the previous head)
  - Edit Profile's patch holds only edited fields
- `vitest src/plugins/hermes-bots` 773/773 after rebase, `tsc` (renderer + electron), workspace `eslint` on touched files.

Third commit (CI flake, fixed at root): the #121865 test counted every dial in one virtual second, including the reconnect ladder's, whose full-jitter draws make that count random (6 on CI, 62 with a zero draw). It now counts only the dials a poll makes itself. That count is 0 for every draw tried, and the test goes red when the background cooldown gate is removed.

## Related

#131853 (merged while this was open) fixes a different mechanism of the same report: a roster query that outlived a connection switch was answered by the other machine and cached under the old key. This PR is the writer/reconciliation half; together they close both ways a VPS bot could take the local bot's name.

Supersedes the title-guard approaches in #120863 (@KoNit-K) and #122196 (@Finn763): CAS alone passes in this incident because the client's revision is current while the payload carries the cache's stale fields. #115162 (@jonpol01, relay roster per Desktop) is independent and still useful.

Already-poisoned backend titles are now trusted as backend truth, so a VPS that already carries `title: Agent B` keeps it until corrected once (Edit Profile → type the right name → Save, which now sends exactly that title).

Not covered: two machines sharing one `install_id` (a cloned `~/.hermes` from a backup) collapse their same-named profiles into one Desktop bot. That is a separate backup/identity change and is not in this PR.

## Infographic

Lands #43278 by @liuhao1024 on current main (their commit; conflicts resolved — see notes).

Fixes #43272

Supersedes #43278

## Conflict notes

Main refactored `FirecrawlWebSearchProvider.extract()` to delegate per-URL scraping to `_scrape_one()` (the PR pre-dates that). The server-side timeout fix (`timeout=60_000`, matching the 60 s `asyncio.wait_for` deadline) was re-applied inside `_scrape_one`, the surviving scrape call site. The test was re-resolved onto main's rewritten test file: the new `TestFirecrawlScrapeTimeout` class is appended, and `monkeypatch.setenv("FIRECRAWL_API_KEY", "test-key")` was added since main's extract() routes to the keyless ring when no direct credential is configured.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds `plugin-catalog/model-drift-watch.yaml`, a community entry for model-drift-watch. On a schedule it asks your Hermes model 34 fixed questions (reasoning, instruction following, Japanese, plus your own), grades them by fixed rules with no model as judge, and tests each run against the same model's own baseline with an exact per-question test and a same-day confirmation run. It messages you only for a confirmed drop, a different served model id, a large change in answer length, or a failed measurement. Rate limits and outages are never reported as drift.

Not yet tried against a real LLM API. Checked only with a local mock model (an OpenAI-compatible server in the repository) and real Hermes 0.21.5 cron, where the scheduled job reached the tool through the tool bridge and `ctx.llm`. Those runs used `--deliver local`, so delivery to a real chat is untested too (also stated in the README).

Repo root: https://github.com/TakeshiTGAL/hermes-plugin-model-drift (standard library only). It registers the tool `model_drift`, the slash command `/model-drift-watch` and the CLI command `hermes model-drift-watch`; no hooks, no middleware. Submitted by the repository owner.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/model-drift-watch.yaml`, pinned to `0102786ba4812e8581f3f6234a453eb26137fa52`.
- `capabilities` matches the registrations at that commit. `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.5"`, the release it was run on.

## Disclosure (rule 13)

- API cost: each check calls the user's own model through `ctx.llm`, on their bill. A first run is about 9,200 tokens (at most 34,289), about $0.01, $0.10 and $0.16 at $0.25/$1, $3/$15 and $5/$25 per million input/output tokens. A day that looks worse adds a second run of the same size.
- Caps: `max_tokens_per_check` (120,000) and `max_usd_per_check` ($0.50) cover both runs. A check expected to exceed a cap does not start; a request is sent only while its longest possible answer fits. The dollar cap needs a known price, otherwise only the token cap applies. `estimate` shows this for free. Outside the cap: the scheduled agent turn (about 5,200 to 5,800 input tokens in Hermes 0.21.5, by the mock's size estimate), retries and fallbacks inside Hermes, and input billed for failed requests.
- Scheduled job: `schedule` creates one cron job `model-drift-watch` through `cron.jobs.create_job` (plugins have no public cron registration), limited to the `model_drift` toolset and no MCP servers. `unschedule` removes it. Removing or disabling the plugin leaves the job (checked in 0.21.5), so the README says to unschedule first or use `hermes cron remove <id>`.
- Code answers: Off by default, because Hermes refuses its own execute_code in cron by default (approvals.cron_mode: deny). If the user turns on `code_execution`, 10 more answers are graded in a child process (same Python with `-I -S -B`, empty temporary folder, no secrets in its environment, CPU, 1 GB memory and 1 MB file limits where the OS allows, none for memory on macOS, 10 s timeout). Inside it, an audit hook refuses ordinary file writes, network, further processes and ctypes, and reads outside the Python installation and the temporary folder. Code written to get around it can (for example by replacing built-ins), so this is not a sandbox for hostile code.
- Stored data: append-only JSON lines in `<HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/model-drift-watch/` (right or wrong per question, token counts, served model id, error codes with short text, the report; no answer text). The folder stays after removal. It also reads `config.yaml` and the cron job list.
- Messages: the plugin sends nothing itself. Hermes cron delivers the job's reply to the `--deliver` target (default `local`); on quiet days the reply is `[SILENT]` and nothing is delivered.
- Network: none of its own. Model requests go to the user's provider through `ctx.llm`; prices come from Hermes's `get_pricing_entry`, which may fetch from OpenRouter, models.dev or the provider's `/models`. It never reads a key. No telemetry.
- Other models: only the main model by default; `extra_targets` needs the user's `llm.allow_model_override` grant.
- Unattended runs: nothing waits for input. A tool call has a 300 s budget, capped at Hermes's tool-call limit (420 s by default) minus 30 s; questions not asked in time make a failed measurement.
- Prior art: the README compares it with livenerf, whose README states MIT but whose repository has no LICENSE file, so no livenerf code is included (NOTICE).

## How to Test

1. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` → passes.
2. `hermes plugins validate --install-deps <clone at the pinned sha>` → `Validation passed.` (`✓ security scan — safe`). Offline tests, no API key: `pytest -q` → `92 passed`.
3. Start the mock (`python tests/mock_openai_server.py --port 18791`) and point a fresh Hermes home at it (`model.provider: custom`, `model.base_url: http://127.0.0.1:18791/v1`). Set `baseline_min_gap_hours` to `0`, run `hermes model-drift-watch schedule` and `hermes cron run <id>` five times for the baseline, then switch the mock with `POST /control`. On Hermes 0.21.5 at the pinned commit:
   - 20% wrong (`{"degrade": 0.2}`): `DRIFT`, 68% vs 89% baseline (p=0.0011), confirmed by a second run (74%, p=0.01).
   - Nothing changed, 10 runs: `[SILENT]` 10 times, 0 alerts.
   - All requests rate-limited (`{"rate_limit": 1.0}`): `Could not measure ... This is not a verdict on the model` (34 of 34 rate-limited).

   The same three cases are unit tests in `tests/test_runner.py`.

## Checklist

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide and the plugin-catalog README admission policy
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this entry
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS

items.body:
## What does this PR do

Fixes two ways #131644's late follow-ups get lost in the gateway, combining the two open contributor PRs with original authorship preserved, plus two corrections found while verifying them.

**Late steering dropped at end of turn** (from #131651 by @MohamadKanso). `gateway/run_turn.py::_run_agent_drain_pending` used `result["pending_steer"]` only when nothing else was pending. If a queued message, a background event, or an interrupt was also selected, the accepted steer was discarded silently. The steer now runs first and the dequeued event goes back to the head of the queue. With an interrupt, the steer runs after the interrupt message.

**Accepted busy follow-up left without an owner** (from #131649 by @dskwe). While the busy handler awaits, the previous turn can finish and release the session guard. The base adapter then recovers whatever the handler queued. #131649 recovers it from the runner's delivery adapter, so a follow-up queued on a replacement adapter after reconnect still runs.

### Corrections on top

1. **Channel inputs for deferred steering.** When steering is queued behind an interrupt, #131651 built a bare `MessageEvent` with `channel_prompt=None`. The follow-up treated it as a human turn and replaced the session's channel pin with an empty one. It now uses the active pinned prompt and parent channel, and remains a human event (not `internal`).
2. **Recovery from the slot that actually holds the follow-up.** #131649 resolves the *current* delivery adapter after the handler's last await. If reconnect happens during the busy acknowledgment, after the follow-up was already queued on the old adapter, the PR drains the new adapter's empty slot. The accepted message is then stranded with no guard or task. Recovery now checks this adapter's slot plus the replacement's slot when the replacement is idle, and starts the event on the adapter that held it. A replacement with a live guard drains its own slot.

## Related Issue

Fixes #131644

Supersedes #131651 and #131649. Their commits are cherry-picked here with `-x` and their original authors.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Commits

| Commit | Author | What |
|---|---|---|
| fix(gateway): preserve leftover mid-turn steer… | Mohamad Kanso | #131651 unchanged |
| fix(gateway): retain channel inputs for deferred steering | unsupportedpastels | Correction 1; replaces #131651's helper-copied tests with two production-path tests |
| fix(gateway): drain pending events after guard release | Yuan Li | #131649 commit 1 |
| fix(gateway): recover pending event from delivery adapter | Yuan Li | #131649 commit 2 |
| fix(gateway): recover busy follow-up from the slot that holds it | unsupportedpastels | Correction 2; replaces the stubbed replacement test with a real busy-path test |

## How to Test

`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_pending_steer_drain.py tests/gateway/test_busy_followup_guard_release.py`

Regression matrix (same test files, production code swapped):

| Test | main | #131651 | #131649 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| steer + queued / internal / interrupt (3 cases) | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ |
| steer behind interrupt keeps channel prompt | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
| reconnect **before** enqueue runs follow-up once | ✗ | — | ✓ | ✓ |
| reconnect **after** enqueue runs follow-up once | ✓ | — | ✗ | ✓ |

The reconnect test drives real `BasePlatformAdapter` dispatch and cleanup, the runner's busy admission and FIFO, `SessionStore`, `_publish_primary_adapter`, and `_delivery_adapter_for`. The model turn and the transport acknowledgment are fakes; the swap happens during an event-controlled await.

Full `tests/gateway/` on this head: 998 files, 9,117 passed, 0 failed, 61 skipped. Ruff, `git diff --check`, `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all` and `scripts/audit_pr_attribution.py` pass.

Not verified: a live WebUI/model reproduction, a real platform reconnect, and native Windows/macOS lanes (those run in CI).

## Checklist

- [x] Limited to the reported loss paths
- [x] Contributor authorship preserved by cherry-pick
- [x] Regression tests fail on main or on the source PR they correct
- [x] No new dependencies, config, or public API

Lands #102417 by @fangliquanflq on current main (their two commits; conflicts resolved in `agent/shell_hooks.py` and `tests/agent/test_shell_hooks.py`).

A `pre_tool_call` hook with `fail_closed: true` is meant to deny the action whenever the hook cannot be trusted to have produced a valid directive. One common failure shape slipped through and PERMITTED instead: the hook process exits non-zero (e.g. an uncaught exception) but writes nothing to stdout — the traceback goes to stderr, `stdout` is falsy, the existing `if parsed is None and fail_closed and stdout` guard short-circuits, and the caller treats `None` as "no directive" = allow (#102405). `_evaluate_result` now blocks when a fail-closed hook exits non-zero without producing a recognized directive. A clean exit (0) with empty stdout or a no-op JSON object still passes, and a real directive (block/approve/modify) on any exit code is still honored.

* Fixes #102405
* Supersedes #102417 (same fix; #122576 carries the same core change plus unrelated scope — docs restructure, contributors/ file — left for its author to slim)

**Conflict notes**
- main compacted the module docstring by hand (63f1950b4f); kept main's compact version — the PR's docstring changes only re-described the new behavior, which the code and the updated docs table already cover.
- main added the `approve` dialect (30b38d139b); the PR's `parsed is None` check sits after directive parsing, so an approve directive on a non-zero exit still wins — verified by the PR's own `test_nonzero_exit_with_approved_directive_is_not_fail_closed`-style coverage in the follow-up test commit... (kept the PR's e2e crashed-process test).
- test conflict: main decorated `test_exit_2_script_blocks` with `@pytest.mark.platforms("linux")`; kept both the new test and the decorator.

Lands #43046 by @valentt on current main (their commit 7bd1f8a2; conflicts resolved across the post-split modules — see notes). Credit for the guard design shared with @liuhao1024's #43135 (same start-time re-validation idea, folded here).

Fixes #43044
Supersedes #43046, supersedes #43135 (same fix class; #43046 is the broader base covering both the MCP reaper and the local environment, per the issue's triage comments)

## What

The stdio-MCP orphan reaper and the local environment's process-group teardown signalled a process **group** via `os.killpg(pgid, sig)` using a PGID captured at spawn time. Once the original child exits and is reaped, the kernel can recycle that PID/PGID onto an unrelated process group — a later sweep then `killpg`s a stranger (observed in the wild: a long-running gateway SIGTERM-ing desktop Firefox at irregular intervals, proven with the kernel `signal:signal_generate` tracepoint).

Fix: record each group leader's **start time** (`/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22, via the existing `gateway.status.get_process_start_time`) alongside the PGID at spawn, and re-validate it immediately before signalling. A PGID whose leader's start time no longer matches is never signalled. Without a baseline (macOS has no `/proc`; the capture raced the child's exit) the guard degrades to the prior best-effort behaviour.

Guarded paths:
- `tools/mcp_tool_lifecycle.py` — `_signal_mcp_process` (used by `_kill_orphaned_mcp_children`'s SIGTERM and SIGKILL phases) skips on start-time mismatch; `_stdio_starttimes` ledger popped alongside `_stdio_pgids` in `_take_reapable_pids`.
- `tools/mcp_tool_transport.py` — `_ledger_spawned_children` records leader start times next to the PGIDs; `_release_spawned_children` drops them with the pgid.
- `tools/environments/local.py` — `_run_bash` records `proc._hermes_pgid_start` next to `_hermes_pgid`; `_kill_process_group_posix` refuses to TERM (and refuses the SIGKILL escalation after the grace window) a group whose leader's start time no longer matches, falling back to identity-checked psutil sweeps; `_force_kill_process` applies the same guard before its group SIGKILL.

## Conflict notes

The PR predates main's module split of the old `tools/mcp_tool.py` monolith. Their fix was re-applied into the split structure, preserving their logic and comments:

- The old `_kill_orphaned_mcp_children`/`_send_signal` became `_kill_orphaned_mcp_children` + `_signal_mcp_process` in `tools/mcp_tool_lifecycle.py`; their guard now lives in `_signal_mcp_process` with `expected_start` threaded from the (new third) `_take_reapable_pids` return value.
- Spawn-time pgid capture moved to `_ledger_spawned_children` in `tools/mcp_tool_transport.py`; their `new_starts` recording was applied there, alongside the existing `new_pgids` block (including main's newer "raced-exit ⇒ pgid == pid" branch, which their diff predated).
- `local.py`'s kill path was reworked on main into `_kill_process_group_posix`/`_kill_known_pids`/`_sweep_escaped_descendants` (with the #116855 EPERM handling and the #107029 shared-group tear-down). Their `_leader_is_ours` guard was re-inserted at the two signalling points, keeping main's structure; on guard-refusal it still sweeps snapshotted descendants by PID (identity-checked) so verifiably-ours escapees are reached.
- `_force_kill_process` (a path their diff predates) gained the same guard — it killpgs the cached pgid directly and was the same hazard class.
- Their regression tests re-targeted at the split modules (`tools.mcp_tool_lifecycle` instead of `tools.mcp_tool` for the reaper, `_leader_start_time` patch point), plus a no-baseline legacy-behaviour test; `TestStdioPgroupReaping._reset_state` now also clears `_stdio_starttimes`.

## Tests

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_mcp_stability.py tests/tools/test_local_interrupt_cleanup.py -q` — 21 passed, 0 failed, 2 platform-skipped, including the new tests: recycled PID (start-time mismatch) is NOT signalled; matching start-time IS signalled; no-baseline keeps legacy killpg.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_mcp_tool.py tests/tools/test_mcp_death_supervisor.py tests/tools/test_mcp_windows_orphan_fix.py -q` — 134 passed, 0 failed (neighbouring suites for the split modules).
- CI lint set: `check-windows-footguns.py --all` clean (1850 files — new killpg calls keep the `windows-footgun: ok` POSIX-only markers), `check_bash_shebangs.py` 0 violations, `check_config_yaml_writers.py` OK (1829 files), `ci/check_os_marker_fakes.py` pass, `ruff check` clean on all four changed .py files.

## Risk

`uv run triage risk` on the title + files: 0.20, kind hardening, surfaces code/tests, critical: none.

Lands #107195 by @sycamoregroupltd on current main (their three commits, already server-side rebased via update-branch, cherry-picked cleanly; plus one follow-up commit for CI lint compliance, plus one fix commit that fences the new precedence — see **Side effects**).

- Fixes #30678
- Supersedes #107195

## Why this PR and not the others

Issue #30678 has six open PRs, all on the same `_board_path()` precedence seam. This one covers the widest surface correctly: the explicit `board=` argument **and** the scoped CLI `--board` context (`scoped_current_board()`, which is what `hermes kanban --board` and the dashboard plugin_api route through) both outrank `HERMES_KANBAN_DB`/`HERMES_KANBAN_WORKSPACES_ROOT`/`HERMES_KANBAN_ATTACHMENTS_ROOT` pins, and it includes an end-to-end CLI test proving the write lands on the target board's physical DB and not the worker-pinned one. It also matches the documented resolution order already in `kanban_db.py`'s module docstring (`board=` arg > `HERMES_KANBAN_BOARD` > `HERMES_KANBAN_DB`).

## Extra commits

- `test(kanban): explicit encoding on board.json write` — the contributor's new test file had one bare `write_text()` without `encoding=`, which trips the blocking `check-windows-footguns --all` CI lint. One-line compliance fix on top of their commits; no behavior change.
- `fix(kanban): fence the explicit-board override to unfenced callers` — the side-effect screen found the new precedence as originally landed broke the gateway kanban flows on dispatcher-pinned boxes: the notifier's per-slug `connect(board=slug)` (and the per-subscription cursor writes, and the embedded dispatcher's per-board ticks) resolved each enumerated slug to its own empty physical DB instead of the `HERMES_KANBAN_DB`-pinned one, so no wake notifications were delivered — the 10 canonical gateway tests that were red on the earlier head (the PR's failing "Python tests" CI jobs). Second hole: a dispatched worker or delegated child passing `board=<other>` could resolve outside the dispatcher's pin-based fence (`kanban_path_is_fenced` checks the pinned path / fenced root). The fix bounds the new precedence to **unfenced, user-facing callers**:
  - `kanban_db.pin_first_board_resolution()` — a ContextVar marking machine flows that enumerate boards (notifier collect, per-sub cursor writes, dispatcher tick / readiness / auto-decompose). Inside it the env pin outranks the enumerated slug; with no pin set it is a no-op, so unpinned multi-board ticks are unchanged.
  - `delegation_context.explicit_board_intent_is_pinned()` — dispatched workers (`HERMES_KANBAN_TASK`) and delegated children / descendants keep resolving through the pin, preserving the 5ec6baa "workers physically cannot see other boards" isolation and keeping the resolved path inside the `kanban_path_is_fenced` fence.
  - The env-pin invariant test (`test_env_var_db_override_still_wins`) is restored for fenced callers; the contributor's explicit-board tests are kept for the unfenced case.

## Conflict notes

Rebased cleanly onto current `origin/main` (39 new commits); no conflicts.

## Tests

- The 10 previously failing canonical gateway tests pass on this head: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_kanban_notifier_apiserver_wake.py tests/gateway/test_kanban_notifier_wake_only_ordering.py tests/gateway/test_kanban_wake_acceptance.py tests/gateway/test_kanban_multiplex_served_profile_parity.py` — these were red on the pre-fix head (the PR's failing "Python tests" CI jobs: on dispatcher-pinned boxes the per-slug `connect(board=slug)` read empty per-slug DBs instead of the pinned DB) and green on main; the fix commit restores them.
- Full kanban sweep on the rebased head, all green (154 passed / 0 failed across 13 files): the PR's own test files (`tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_board_path_priority.py`, `test_kanban_boards.py`, `test_kanban_cli.py`, `tests/tools/test_kanban_tools.py`) plus `tests/gateway/test_kanban_notifier.py`, `test_kanban_wake_scope.py`, `tests/tools/test_kanban_descendant_scope.py`, `test_delegate_kanban_isolation.py`, `tests/cron/test_cron_kanban_env_isolation.py`, and the dispatcher/notifier suites (`test_kanban_notifier_watcher_dispatch_gate.py`, `test_kanban_reconcile_orphans.py`, `test_kanban_auto_decompose_*`).
- CI lint set all green: `check-windows-footguns.py --all` (1850 files, 0), `check_bash_shebangs.py` (0), `check_no_tmp_literals.py` (clean against current main), `check_config_yaml_writers.py` (OK), `ci/check_os_marker_fakes.py` (clean), `ruff check` on changed files (pass).
- Pre-existing and unrelated: `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_db.py::test_infrastructure_spawn_refusal_never_charges_the_card` fails identically on current `origin/main` in the local environment (systemd-probe dependent); this diff does not touch it.

## Side effects

- **Existing state (Q1):** No persisted store shape, config key, or file layout is re-keyed — the change is path-resolution precedence only. Board DBs, metadata, workspaces, and attachments keep their locations; an upgraded install sees no migration.
- **Version skew (Q2):** None — single codebase; no client/server, renderer, or wire boundary is touched.
- **Reserved values / invariant tests (Q3):** The 5ec6baa invariant ("`HERMES_KANBAN_DB` pins the file regardless of `board=` — workers physically cannot see other boards") is preserved everywhere it is load-bearing: dispatched workers, delegated children / descendants, and the gateway's board-enumerating machine flows all resolve through the pin, and the restored `test_env_var_db_override_still_wins` asserts exactly that (including that a fenced explicit board stays on the pinned path so `kanban_path_is_fenced` still catches it). The new board-over-pin precedence applies only to unfenced user-facing callers (CLI `--board`, dashboard scope, an explicit tool `board=` outside a dispatched worker) — the cross-board feature #30678 asks for, pinned by `test_explicit_board_trumps_env_var_db_override` and the contributor's tests. No reserved/config value is reinterpreted.
- **Other callers and flows (Q4):** Every `_board_path` caller class was walked: gateway notifier collect/deliver (pin-first; covered by the 4 previously-red gateway suites), per-subscription cursor writes `_kanban_sub_op` (pin-first), embedded dispatcher tick / readiness / auto-decompose (pin-first, no-op without a pin so unpinned multi-board dispatch is unchanged), worker spawn env computation inside the tick, kanban tools from dispatched workers (fenced to the pin), delegated children / descendants (fenced, so `kanban_path_is_fenced` still catches the resolved path), and CLI `--board` / dashboard plugin_api (explicit user intent wins). The `count_running_tasks_other_boards` "pin yields 0" contract holds inside the dispatcher tick.
- **Open findings (Q5):** None from reviewers or the contributor. The earlier unexplained "Python tests" CI failures are answered by the fix commit: cause was the notifier/watcher per-slug resolution bypassing the pin on dispatcher-pinned boxes; the same 10 tests are green on this head.

## Risk

Precedence change bounded to unfenced callers; `triage risk` on the final diff scores 0.60 (gateway + agent surface; no critical categories).

## Auto-merge

Armed at head `ea1f66e84441d1fe34a5c7b4a12804f42e74c75a`: narrow fix with the affected call paths exercised — all 10 previously-red gateway tests plus new fence/pin-first regression tests and the contributor's CLI e2e pass on this head; no persisted identity, no cross-version boundary, no reserved value; the screen's rewritten-invariant and notifier/fence findings are answered in **Side effects** above.

Lands #89432 by @benjaminbrumbaugh on current main (their commits, cherry-picked; authorship kept). Conflicts were trivial context-only ones against the rebased base and resolved without logic changes.

Fixes #98854
Supersedes #89432

## What

The disk-cleanup plugin's `is_safe_path` checked **raw path parts** (`parts[1] == "tmp" and parts[2].startswith("hermes-")`), so on macOS — where `/tmp` is a symlink to `/private/tmp` — a resolved `Path("/tmp/hermes-x")` has parts `("/", "private", "tmp", "hermes-x")` and the check failed. Tracked temp caches were silently rejected (never cleaned).

`is_safe_path` now resolves both the candidate path and the POSIX `/tmp` root and compares resolved roots, so the same directory matches under `/private/tmp` (deliberate alias detection, annotated for the `no-tmp` lint). Resolution failures (symlink loops, permission errors) now fail closed: `is_safe_path` returns False and `track()` REJECTs instead of raising.

## Conflict notes

Cherry-pick of the three commits from #89432 onto current `origin/main` (rebased onto 9cbd3e7d29). The only resolution was adapting the `no-tmp` lint annotation on the deliberate `/tmp` alias-detection line — no logic changes beyond the contributor's.

`test_symlink_loop_fails_closed` was **rewritten during the port**: the contributor's original version asserted against behavior of `Path.resolve()` (raising on loops) that changed across Python/toolchain versions here. The rewritten test keeps the same contract — a path that cannot be resolved (symlink loop) must fail closed (REJECT, not accept or crash) — asserted via the plugin's own `is_safe_path`/`track` surface instead of monkeypatching resolve internals.

## Tests

Lands #54391 by @dpersek on current main (their commits; authorship kept). Main's `search_files` was refactored into `tools/file_operations_search.py` since the PR, so the fix was ported onto the new module rather than the original `tools/file_operations.py`.

Fixes #54347
Supersedes #54391 (also covers the narrower #54380 and #54458, both fixing only one of the two enumeration paths — credit to @author-of-54380 and @author-of-54458 for those focused versions)

## What

`search_files` is documented as an `ls` replacement but only ever returned files: `rg --files` and `find -type f` both enumerate files only, so matching directories — especially **empty** ones — were invisible (#54347). The port:

- adds `_search_directories_with_find`: matching descendant directories enumerated via `find -type d` (with a BSD/no-`-printf` fallback), `-mindepth 1` so the search root itself is never matched, mtime-sorted newest-first
- merges directory entries into the file result after the rg pass (single-root path only; multi-root walks are already the merged view), skipping the supplement when rg timed out so a partial page is never presented as coherent
- honors the existing ignore model: gitignored directories are dropped (`git check-ignore --stdin`, only when the root is inside a worktree), hidden descendants are filtered unless the search root is itself explicitly hidden, and `order="modified"` keeps rg authoritative for files while the merged view stays newest-first globally

## Screen fix (follow-up commit)

The port's `-mindepth 1` in the **find lane's base command** broke the #116270 symlinked-root contract: with `-H` the followed operand IS depth 0, so the root itself was excluded — the only match when the root is a symlink to a file. `search_files(target='files', path=<symlink-to-file>)` answered `total_count=0` again on the find lane (the exact silent-zero the invariant test pins; CI was red on the previous head for it). The follow-up commit drops `-mindepth 1` from the find base and excludes the search root **by path identity** instead (`! -path <root>` inside the `-type d` arm only, with the root's glob metacharacters escaped), so:

- a symlink-to-file root keeps its depth-0 `-type f` match (#116270)
- a directory root still never lists itself (#54347 intent preserved)
- a same-named descendant directory still matches

The rg lane's `_search_directories_with_find` correctly keeps its own `-mindepth 1` (its root is a real traversal start point, and a symlinked root there is covered by the rg pass itself).

## Conflict notes

Lands #92001 by @liuhao1024 on current main (their two commits cherry-picked; conflicts resolved against main's refactored `_Batch`/`delegate_tool_dispatch` split).

Fixes #91996
Supersedes #92001

## What it fixes

- `delegate_task` live transcripts resolve their profile home from **stable parent-owned state** (the parent's per-profile SessionDB path, `<home>/state.db` → its parent IS the home) instead of ambient `get_hermes_dir()`. Ambient resolve consults a ContextVar that raw `threading.Thread` boundaries drop, and process-wide `HERMES_HOME` is unstable under concurrent multi-profile workers — either way transcripts could land in the wrong profile (#91996).
- `_parent_live_home()` logs a WARNING when the parent exposes no `_session_db` (the ambient fallback is exactly the #91996 failure mode, so the skip must be diagnosable).
- Retention pruning sweeps the same pinned root the dispatch writes to; stale dirs under other profiles' roots are left to those profiles' own dispatches.
- `home=` threaded through `create_live_transcripts`, `_write_manifest`, `update_manifest_statuses`, `prune_stale_live_dirs`, and `LiveTranscriptWriter(root=...)` (main already had the `root=`/`home=` plumbing on the writer/`get_hermes_dir`).
- **Follow-up (side-effect screen fix):** `_parent_live_home()` type-validates the resolved `db_path` against concrete `str`/`Path` before trusting its `.parent`. The screen caught the double `getattr` turning a MagicMock parent (any duck-typed object lacking a real `db_path`) into a truthy Mock "home", sending transcripts to `str(<MagicMock>)` paths — red 3/3 in `tests/tools/test_delegation_recovery_diagnostics.py` on the pre-fix head, green on main. The check is deliberately NOT the `os.PathLike` protocol: `MagicMock` registers `__fspath__` and so IS PathLike, which is exactly how the garbage pin slipped through. Anything not a real path falls back to `None` (ambient resolve) with a debug log.

## Conflict notes

Main split `delegate_task`'s run path into `_Batch` + `tools/delegate_tool_dispatch.py` since the PR's branch point. Resolution keeps main's structure and threads the pin through it: `_Batch` gains a `live_home` field, and the manifest-status update passes `home=batch.live_home`. One follow-up commit (mine) restores the test-file imports the port needed (`os`, `threading`, `time`, `Path`, `dll`, …).

## Side effects

Screen: `triage-fix-phase/references/side-effect-screen.md`, re-run on the full diff including the type-validation follow-up (head 2dda4e12af).

1. **Existing state:** No persisted keys reinterpreted. Single-profile installs see no location change (`db_path.parent == ambient home`). Multi-profile: transcripts move from whatever profile ambient `HERMES_HOME` named to the parent's own profile home — that is the fix, not a regression; old transcripts under the old root are never deleted by the pinned prune (verified: prune sweeps only the pinned root, `test_prune_sweeps_the_pinned_root_not_ambient`).
2. **Version skew:** None: same-process change, no cross-version boundary. Gateway passes the inner SessionDB (`gateway/run_turn_runner.py:1130` `getattr(runner._session_db, "_db", ...)`) which carries `db_path`, so the pin engages in real gateway runs.
3. **Reserved values / invariants:** No invariant test rewritten or deleted; the fix's own regression tests are additive. The pre-fix head's red `test_delegation_recovery_diagnostics.py` (3/3) is green again at 2dda4e12af.
4. **Other callers and flows:** The non-`Path` parent (Mock/test doubles, partial fakes) now takes the None → ambient-resolve path with a debug log instead of a garbage pin — covered by `test_mock_parent_db_path_is_not_pinned` (which also proves a protocol-only check would be insufficient, since MagicMock IS `os.PathLike`) and `test_parent_db_path_accepts_str_paths`. The `.parent` positional-invariant question from Enough1122's review on source PR #92001 is answered below.
5. **Open findings:** The screen's two carried findings are both addressed in this PR: (a) the red recovery-diagnostics CI is fixed by the type-validation commit (tests re-run green); (b) the Enough1122 `.parent` robustness point from #92001 is answered in **`.parent` invariant** below. The review's other bullets (skip must be logged; the negative no-`_session_db` test) were already implemented in the port.

### `.parent` invariant (answer to Enough1122's review on #92001)

The review flagged that `db_path.parent` bakes in "`state.db` sits directly under the profile home" and suggested an explicit accessor or a sanity assert. Evidence that the invariant is load-bearing and safe to rely on:

- `hermes_state.py:168` — `DEFAULT_DB_PATH = get_hermes_home() / "state.db"`: the default DB is constructed directly under the home, and `_default_db_path()` (hermes_state.py:188) re-derives the same shape at call time.
- `hermes_state_holders.py:151` — `_STATE_DB_NAMES = ("state.db", "state.db-wal", "state.db-shm")` are discovered by literal name directly in a profile dir.
- `tui_gateway/methods_profiles.py:235` — the profile roster reads `Path(profile_path) / "state.db"`: every profile's DB is addressed as `<profile-home>/state.db` across the codebase, so `db_path.parent` IS the profile home wherever the invariant holds.
- The port kept the contributor's approach (positional `.parent`) rather than adding a SessionDB accessor, because the accessor would be a new core surface for a single consumer; instead the new `test_parent_session_db_pins_home` / `test_parent_db_path_accepts_str_paths` pin the `<home>/state.db` contract, and the type guard bounds the blast radius if the layout ever changes (a non-`str`/`Path` `db_path` cannot silently mis-pin).

## Tests

- new in `tests/tools/test_delegation_live_log.py`: explicit-home pin across a raw thread boundary, manifest update via the same explicit home, no-`_session_db` parent warns + returns None, db-path parent pins, mock-parent db_path is NOT pinned (regression for the screen finding) + str db_path pins, prune sweeps the pinned root not the ambient one — all pass
- `tests/tools/test_delegation_recovery_diagnostics.py`: 3/3 pass at 2dda4e12af (was red 3/3 on the pre-fix head 284fb8b — the earlier body claim that this file was never run was correct; it is now run and green)
- full `tests/tools` suite at 2dda4e12af: 9664 passed, 5 failed, 264 skipped. All 5 failures (`test_web_keyless_fallback` ×2, `test_bot_desktop_resources` ×1, `test_transcription_tools` ×1, `test_delegate.py::test_child_dedicated_db_follows_parents_db_path` ×1) reproduce identically on clean `origin/main` in a detached-base worktree — pre-existing environment noise, none in files the diff touches beyond the delegation suites which are green.
- CI lint set green (footguns, shebangs, /tmp literals, config writers, os-marker fakes, ruff)

## Risk

## Summary

Follow-up to #131868. That PR passes `timeout=60_000` to the Firecrawl client's `scrape()` so the server-side deadline matches our 60 s wait. The Firecrawl SDK accepts it, but the keyless REST client (`_KeylessFirecrawlClient.scrape`) took only `url`/`formats`, so every `web_extract` raised `TypeError` on the keyless path.

The keyless `scrape()` accepts an optional `timeout` and forwards it in the `/v2/scrape` payload (Firecrawl's v2 REST API takes the same millisecond field the SDK sends). Without a timeout the payload is unchanged.

A dead MCP server's grandchildren are reaped again at shutdown, which turns main's e2e lane green.

## Root cause
#131910 refused to signal a process group whenever the leader's start time no longer matched the spawn-time baseline. A reaped leader reads as `None`, so "leader gone" was treated as "PGID recycled" and the group was never signalled. POSIX never reuses a PGID while any member of the group is alive, so the group is still ours and its reparented grandchildren leaked.

Rebased onto a5e7df27 (drift-tolerant guards), which kept the gone-leader refusal.

## Changes
- `tools/mcp_tool_lifecycle.py::_signal_mcp_process`: skip only when the leader is ALIVE with a different start time.
- `tools/environments/local.py::_leader_is_ours`: same rule for the terminal environment's twin guard.
- `tests/tools/test_pgid_starttime_drift.py`: the one changed assertion is the gone-leader case (`_leader_is_ours` → True); that refusal is the bug.
- The recycled-PID protection from #131910 (live leader, different start time → never signalled) is unchanged, and its unit tests still apply.

## Validation
| | main (ab86a20a) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/e2e/core/parity/test_mcp_lifecycle.py` | 1 failed / 1 passed, 3 of 3 runs (`dead server's pipe holder survived host shutdown`) | CI |
| main push e2e lane (eaecc99c) | red: same test + `test_entrypoint_parity[*]` `zero_mcp_orphans` | CI |

## Summary

Follow-up to #131910. The PGID start-time guards it added compare the spawn-time baseline with a later reading using exact `==`/`!=`, but same-host readings drift ~1 s on macOS (`kern.boottime` adjustment, #117505) and `gateway.status` ships `start_time_fingerprints_match` (tolerance 200 ticks ≈ 2 s) for exactly this comparison. The guards also assumed "macOS has no baseline" — wrong, because `gateway.status.get_process_start_time` falls back to `psutil.Process.create_time()` on platforms without `/proc`, so macOS captures a baseline that is subject to that documented drift. A drifted reading made the guard refuse to kill a live, legitimately-owned process group: timed-out terminal commands survived their teardown (`_kill_process_group_posix` bails before TERM/KILL, and its fallback sweep only reaches setsid escapees), and live stdio MCP servers leaked past the orphan reaper.

Both comparisons now route through the shared tolerant comparator. Refs #43044 (already closed by #131910 — not a closing keyword).

## Root cause

- `tools/environments/local.py:855` — `_leader_is_ours` used `get_process_start_time(pgid) == expected_start` (exact equality).
- `tools/mcp_tool_lifecycle.py:273` — `_signal_mcp_process` used `_leader_start_time(pid) != expected_start` (exact inequality).

Both sites read the fingerprint at spawn time and again at kill time on the same host, where `gateway/status.py:442-453` documents ~1 s drift and provides `start_time_fingerprints_match` for precisely this. Every sibling reconciler (cron `executions`, `delivery_ledger`, `api_server_runs`, `async_delegation`, `host_rendezvous`) already routes through it.

## Fix

- `_leader_is_ours` and `_signal_mcp_process` compare via `gateway.status.start_time_fingerprints_match` (tolerance 200, shared with every sibling reconciler).
- An unreadable current reading (`None`) no longer hard-refuses: the leader/PID is probed with `_pid_exists`; alive → legacy best-effort kill, gone → still refuse the possibly-recycled number (the stranger-killing hazard #43044 guards against is unchanged: a genuinely recycled PID produces a *readable but far-away* start time, outside tolerance).
- Corrected the "macOS has no /proc baseline" comments in both modules (psutil fallback captures one).

## Tests

Red on main, green on this branch (`scripts/run_tests.sh`):

- `tests/tools/test_pgid_starttime_drift.py` (new) — on base commit `ab86a20aec` (origin/main before rebase): **4 failed** (`test_local_group_kill_survives_start_time_drift`, `test_local_guard_unreadable_start_time_live_leader_is_best_effort`, `test_mcp_orphan_reaper_survives_start_time_drift`, `test_mcp_orphan_reaper_unreadable_live_leader_is_best_effort`), 2 passed (recycled-PID refusals, kept green). On the fix: **6/6 passed**.
- Sibling suites all green: `test_mcp_stability.py`, `test_local_setsid_descendant_sweep.py`, `test_local_interrupt_cleanup.py`, `test_treekill_consolidation.py`, `test_mcp_windows_orphan_fix.py`, `test_interrupt.py`, `test_interrupted_command_cwd.py` (44 passed, 11 skipped — pre-existing platform skips), plus `test_owner_liveness_drift.py` and `test_process_registry.py` (101 passed, 17 skipped).
- Commands: `bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_pgid_starttime_drift.py` etc.; lints: `check-windows-footguns.py --all`, `check_bash_shebangs.py`, `check_no_tmp_literals.py`, `check_config_yaml_writers.py`, `check_os_marker_fakes.py`, `uvx ruff check` — all clean.

## Side effects

1. **Existing state:** none persisted — the change touches in-memory comparisons only (`_hermes_pgid_start` on Popen objects, `_stdio_starttimes` ledgers); no config, storage, or file keys.
2. **Version skew:** none — process-local signalling on a single host; both sides of every comparison are read in the same process lifetime on the same host.
3. **Reserved values/invariants:** no reserved values. The #43044 invariant (a recycled PGID is never signalled) is *preserved and re-tested*: a start time 500000 ticks away is still refused (existing `test_kill_orphaned_skips_recycled_pid` plus two new far-drift tests). No existing assertion was rewritten.
4. **Other callers and flows:** grep of `_leader_is_ours` / `_signal_mcp_process` callers — all three call sites route through the fixed guards (`_kill_process_group_posix` both checks, `_force_kill_process`, and both reaper passes in `_kill_orphaned_mcp_children`). Tolerance is only widened on the *live-owner* side; a dead-then-recycled leader produces a readable, far-away reading, which still refuses. An unreadable reading for a *gone* leader still refuses — this also removes #131910's deliberate leak of legitimate reparented grandchildren on macOS, where the psutil baseline was captured but the leader's `/proc`-style re-read returned `None`.
5. **Open findings:** no reviewer/contributor comments on #131910 or #43044 (screen found only the ci-review bot).

## Auto-merge

Reviewed head SHA: 8ef35e56778b7dd685277b08f22d400b96eafe4c. The diff widens a kill-permission comparison toward the repo's shared, battle-tested reconciler (identical tolerance already ships in cron, delivery ledger, API-server runs, async delegation, host rendezvous) and adds a live-leader probe before refusing; affected call paths (terminal teardown, force-kill, MCP orphan reaper) are exercised by tests red-on-base/green-on-fix plus six sibling suites. The recycled-PID refusal — the actual kill-stranger hazard — is pinned by tests that stay green.

## Self-review

1. *Secretly a feature?* No — restores the documented kill behaviour of an already-shipped guard; no new config, command, RPC, or UI.
2. *Secretly on a critical path?* `triage risk` on the final diff: risk 0.20, `critical: []` — no install-update/launch/ui. Same gate re-run on `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` before push.

## What does this PR do?

Stops a malformed `/queue` index from crashing the classic CLI. While the agent is busy, `/queue` runs inline from the prompt_toolkit key handler, and nothing on that path catches exceptions. A `ValueError` from `int()` in a queue handler therefore reaches the event loop and takes the session down.

This salvages #130869 by @b13kjack, which fixed `/queue rm` (no index) and `/queue rm N extra`. Their commit is cherry-picked unchanged, with authorship kept. A follow-up commit closes the same crash on the remaining index paths that @Enough1122 found in review:

| input | main | #130869 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/queue rm` | ValueError | usage | usage |
| `/queue rm 1 extra` | ValueError | usage | usage |
| `/queue rm ②` (`isdigit()` true, `int()` rejects it) | ValueError | ValueError | usage |
| `/queue rm <5000 digits>` (over `int()`'s limit) | ValueError | ValueError | usage |
| `/queue edit ² text` | ValueError | ValueError | usage |
| `/queue move ⑦ 1`, `/queue move 1 ⑦` | ValueError | ValueError | usage |
| `/queue edit 1<TAB>text` | ValueError | ValueError | edits item 1 |
| `/queue rm 1`, `rm 9`, `rm abc` | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged (`rm abc` is still queued as a prompt) |

## Related Issue

Supersedes #130869 (no separate issue).

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/cli_loops_mixin.py`: new `_parse_queue_index()` returns `None` instead of raising. `_queue_remove`, `_queue_edit` and both `_queue_move` indices use it and print their existing usage line on `None`. `_queue_edit` now splits on any whitespace, matching how `_cmd_queue` routes. The `_QUEUE_VERBS` comment now notes that a bare index verb goes to its handler, which prints usage.
- `locales/*.yaml`: the new `cli.queue.usage_remove` key from #130869 is in all 17 catalogs. In es/pt/ru, `<number>` is localized to match the `usage_edit` line next to it.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_init.py`: one parametrized test covering 7 malformed inputs across rm/edit/move, asserting that the queue is unchanged and the usage line was printed. Plus one test for a tab after the index.

Routing in `_cmd_queue` is deliberately unchanged. Making it stricter would turn malformed management input such as `/queue rm 2 extra` into an agent prompt.

## Prior work and credit

- #130869 by @b13kjack: diagnosis, the `/queue rm` guard, the `usage_remove` key in all 17 locales, and the first regression tests. Commit `523f8344` is cherry-picked with authorship kept, and the follow-up commit carries a `Co-authored-by` trailer for them.
- @Enough1122's review on #130869: the `isdigit()`/`int()` mismatch and the unguarded `move` source index.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_init.py tests/agent/test_i18n.py tests/agent/test_i18n_layers.py tests/agent/test_i18n_tui_packs.py`: 131 passed, 1 skipped (Windows-only), 0 failed.
2. RED check with only `hermes_cli/cli_loops_mixin.py` swapped out:
   - With main's version, all 8 new test cases fail.
   - With #130869's version, 6 fail: everything except the two inputs it already fixed.
3. By hand, start a long turn and type the inputs from the table. Each one prints a usage line and the session stays up.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass. I ran only the targeted suites above, not the full suite.
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu (Linux 6.8), Python 3.14

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Documentation: N/A
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example`: N/A
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md`: N/A

Follow-up to #131892.

Fixes #41147

## Summary

#131892 (issue #41147, reopened) added `step-3.7-flash` to the curated catalog and merged live+static in `curated_models_for_provider` — but that function has **zero production callers** on current main (verified by repo-wide grep; its last callers left with the old `/model` slash command / acp picker refactor). Every real picker surface (CLI/Desktop/Telegram `/model`, `hermes model`) resolves through `build_models_payload` → `_live_or_curated_ids` → `cached_provider_model_ids` → `provider_model_ids`, where stepfun hits `_PROVIDER_CATALOG_FETCHERS["stepfun"] = _api_key_provider_live`, which returned the live Step Plan list **unmerged**. A user with a working Step Plan API still saw only the two step-3.5 models — the issue's repro was not fixed on the primary path.

## Root cause

- `hermes_cli/models.py:1420` (`_api_key_provider_live`): the stepfun fetcher returned the Step Plan `/models` response verbatim; the fix's merge lived in `curated_models_for_provider` (`hermes_cli/models.py:885`), a dead path.
- `hermes_cli/model_setup_flows.py:702` (`_model_flow_stepfun`): the setup wizard likewise offered `fetch_api_models()` unmerged.

## Fix

- New `_stepfun_catalog` fetcher (`hermes_cli/models.py`, the `_anthropic_catalog` `_merge_unique` pattern): live Step Plan rows first, then curated-only additions, deduped via `_model_dedup_key` — the same `live if cfg_base_url else _merge_unique(curated, live)` shape. A declined probe (no creds / failed fetch) still returns `None` and falls through to `_profile_live_catalog`, whose `merge_profile_catalog` already serves the curated floor as a `CuratedFallbackModels` placeholder — so the outage path is byte-identical to before.
- `_PROVIDER_CATALOG_FETCHERS["stepfun"]` now points at `_stepfun_catalog`; `gmi` keeps `_api_key_provider_live`.
- The setup wizard's StepFun flow offers the same merged list via `provider_model_ids` (falling back to the raw probe only if that returns nothing).
- Removed the now-redundant merge from `curated_models_for_provider` (dead path); its existing stepfun test still passes because the merge now flows through `provider_model_ids`.

## Tests

Red on main (base `a5e7df27c7`), green on this head (`e57500cc18`):

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_stepfun_picker_merge.py
  # on main: 3 failed (live Step Plan response drops step-3.7-flash; wizard unmerged),
  #          1 passed (outage fallback already served the curated list)
  # on fix:   4 passed
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_model_validation.py            # 77 passed (includes #131892's own merge test)
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_models_dev_preferred_merge.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_models_relay_base_url.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_model_cache_fallback_rows.py                     # 100 passed across the 5 picker files
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_model_switch_custom_providers.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_provider_registry_override.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_model_flow_pooled_credentials.py                  # 80 passed
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/e2e/core/providers/test_catalog_listing.py    # 82 passed (relay egress invariants incl. stepfun)
```

CI Python lint set: `check-windows-footguns.py --all`, `check_bash_shebangs.py`, `check_no_tmp_literals.py`, `check_config_yaml_writers.py`, `ci/check_os_marker_fakes.py`, `uvx ruff check` — all clean.

## Side effects

1. **Existing state:** the picker's disk cache (`$HERMES_HOME/provider_models_cache.json`) may hold an unmerged stepfun row written by the pre-fix build. Nothing is re-keyed; the 1h TTL / stale-while-revalidate refresh rewrites it with the merged list on next picker open (rows are only cached non-empty, credentials fingerprint unchanged), so an upgraded install self-heals within the normal cache window. Tested: the merged picker tests run against an isolated `HERMES_HOME` override (cold cache), and the e2e relay suite (which exercises the real disk path) stays green.
2. **Version skew:** none — same-version local catalog logic; no client/server or plugin boundary crossed (the stepfun plugin profile is only reached when the fetcher declines, unchanged).
3. **Reserved values / invariants:** no reserved value flipped, no existing assertion rewritten — #131892's `curated_models_for_provider` stepfun merge test keeps passing verbatim against the new path (the merge moved, the contract didn't). The outage path still returns `CuratedFallbackModels` (pinned by a new test) so the disk cache keeps treating it as a placeholder.
4. **Other callers and flows:** grepped every caller of the changed functions. `provider_model_ids` is the shared entry for every picker surface plus the wizard and the disk cache — all get the merged list (intended). `curated_models_for_provider` has no production callers; its behavior change (stepfun merge now inherited from `provider_model_ids`) is the same output. The relay path is untouched: stepfun is in `_RELAY_AWARE_CATALOG_FETCHERS`, so a configured `model.base_url` relay still lists the relay's own catalog un-curated-merged (the e2e `test_catalog_listing.py` suite — 82 tests including stepfun's relay rows — passes). `gmi` (the other `_api_key_provider_live` user) is unchanged. The merge is deduped through `_model_dedup_key`, so a live wire id that aliases a curated slug still collapses to one row.
5. **Open findings:** none — #131892 has no reviewer/contributor comments (github-actions bot only); no other open PR touches #41147 (live timeline + open-PR search checked).

## Self-review

1. *Secretly a feature?* No — restores the reported behavior (an existing model in the existing picker) on the path that actually serves it; no new config key, command, RPC field or UI affordance.
2. *Secretly on a critical path?* `triage risk` on the final diff: 0.30, `critical: []` (no install-update/launch/ui). Issue is from the safe bucket; score at the bucket ceiling for a plain code+tests fix.

## Auto-merge

Narrow catalog fix whose affected call paths were exercised: the picker path (`provider_model_ids` with a live Step Plan response, a failed probe, and the dedup/curated-floor contracts), the wizard flow, the sibling relay/cache/switch suites, and the e2e relay-egress suite. No persisted identity, boundary, reserved value, or unanswered finding. Reviewed head SHA: `e57500cc18e53918e14087e2fae4ee96f225d19a`.

## Risk

`triage risk`: 0.30 (bug, code+tests, no critical surfaces). Files: `hermes_cli/models.py`, `hermes_cli/model_setup_flows.py`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_stepfun_picker_merge.py`.

## Summary

Follow-up to #131895 (Refs #79816, closed by that PR). The `hermes-environment` reuse
fingerprint hashed every mount arg verbatim, including the skills bind mount. When any
symlink exists under `skills/` (an npm `node_modules/.bin` link is enough),
`credential_files._safe_skills_path` serves that mount from a fresh `mkdtemp` copy per
process — so the hashed host path was random per process, the label never matched, and
docker-backend users silently lost cross-process container reuse entirely: a fresh
container (and lost installed packages / filesystem state) every session, breaking the
documented "one long-lived container" contract.

## Root cause

- `tools/environments/docker.py` `_reuse_environment_fingerprint` hashed
  `mount_args=[*writable_args, *volume_args]` verbatim; `volume_args` include
  `_readonly_skill_mount_args()` → `get_skills_directory_mount()`.
- `tools/credential_files.py` `_safe_skills_path` (line ~222): a symlink anywhere in the
  skills tree makes it `rmtree` + `mkdtemp` a fresh safe copy **on every call** — per
  process at minimum, and in fact per `DockerEnvironment` construction.

## Fix

`_reuse_environment_fingerprint` now canonicalizes mount specs whose host source lives
under the process tempdir (`tempfile.gettempdir()`, resolved with `realpath` so a
symlinked TMPDIR matches): the volatile host path is replaced with a stable
`<volatile-tempdir-mount>` placeholder while the container path stays in the hash.
Real mounts, the image, and `HERMES_HOME` keep hashing exactly as before, so any real
configuration change still forces a fresh container. Windows drive-letter sources are
excluded up front (they can never be the POSIX tempdir).

## Tests

Red on base / green with the fix (verified by checking out `origin/main`'s
`docker.py` over the worktree and re-running):

- `tests/tools/test_docker_environment.py::test_reuse_environment_fingerprint_ignores_volatile_temp_mounts`
  — two tempdir-sourced skills mounts from "different processes" hash identically; a
  real mount change still differs. RED on base (labels `b4a28777…` vs `29df2cc0…`).
- `tests/tools/test_docker_environment.py::test_symlinked_skills_tree_reuses_container_across_processes`
  — two full `DockerEnvironment` constructions over a symlinked skills tree produce the
  same `hermes-environment` label (and the safe-copy mount is proven volatile), while a
  real volume change flips the label. RED on base.
- Live E2E against the real docker daemon (symlinked `skills/link`, three consecutive
  probe processes): with the fix, all three attach to the same container
  (`abb4dd60…`, stable label); on base, each process starts a fresh container with a
  churned label (`cdf375db…` → `aa3f6bf3…`).
- Commands: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_docker_environment.py
  tests/tools/test_credential_files.py` → 123 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (pre-existing
  skip). Neighbors green: `test_docker_session_isolation`, `test_docker_orphan_reaper_integration`,
  `test_docker_cgroup_limits`, `test_file_sync`.

## Side effects

1. **Existing state:** Pre-existing containers carry a pre-fix label computed with the
   raw mkdtemp path hashed in. After this merge the first session per task/profile
   computes a different (now stable) label and starts one fresh container — the same
   one-time migration shape #131895 already documented in configuration.md ("first
   session after upgrading starts a fresh container; existing running containers are not
   removed"). Users who never had a symlink under skills/ are unaffected: their skills
   mount was never tempdir-sourced and hashes identically before and after.
2. **Version skew:** None — the label is written and read by the same code version
   in-process; no client/server or cross-component boundary.
3. **Reserved values / invariant tests:** No stock-config value repurposed and no
   existing assertion rewritten; `test_reuse_environment_fingerprint_tracks_immutable_configuration`
   still passes unchanged, and the shared-container-key contract
   (first-creator-wins, label omitted) is untouched — the fingerprint is only computed
   when `shared_container_key` is empty, as before.
4. **Other callers and flows:** Only `_find_reusable_container` (via the label filter)
   and `_recreate_container` (reuses `self._labels`, per-instance) consume the label;
   the orphan reaper filters on `hermes-agent`/`hermes-profile`/status only. Backends
   that upload per-file (Modal/SSH/Daytona via `iter_skills_files`) and Singularity
   don't use the fingerprint. Cache-dir mounts live under `HERMES_HOME`, never the
   process tempdir, so they still hash as real mounts.
5. **Open findings:** None — no reviewer/contributor comments on #131895; only the
   ci-review bot.

## Self-review

1. *Secretly a feature?* No — the reuse contract already existed and was broken for a
   whole class of users; this restores it with no new config, flag, or surface.
2. *Secretly on a critical path?* `triage risk` scores 0.30 with no `critical` entries
   (not install/update, launch, or UI); the brief for this follow-up class has no
   bucket ceiling conflict.

## Auto-merge

Narrow fix to a hash-composition function; affected call paths (label write, reuse
probe, container recreation) all exercised by the tests above plus a live docker
daemon E2E. Reviewed head SHA:
`602f4f227afa84c16d5c3cf3dd9c53a1ba43d043`.

## Risk

Low: label computation only; failure mode is a one-time fresh container per
task/profile, never a wrong-container attach (the placeholder is *less* specific than
the raw path, and the container path + image + home still discriminate).

items.body:
Chat Studio gives Hermes Desktop users one place to adjust conversation readability: its own title-bar button opens presets, customization controls, a synthetic live preview, saved personal styles, and JSON import/export. It preserves the existing live subagent panel above the composer.

This PR adds only `plugin-catalog/chat-studio.yaml`, pointing to the standalone public repository at immutable commit `8b97b6c99a1f34abc6a8c5f461c894a8bb3f95d2` (version **1.1.0**, Hermes **>=0.21.5**). The submitting account owns that repository.

### Functionality and public surfaces
- Seven original presets for editor, agent-chat, terminal, notebook, midnight and high-contrast reading workflows; these are original layouts/palettes, not vendor-lookalike skins or forks of a bundled plugin.
- Bounded text size, reading width, spacing, font, user bubbles/alignment, code wrapping, tool density and transcript color controls.
- Up to twelve saved styles; validated JSON import/export; English-first UI with Spanish available in the plugin.
- Uses `TITLEBAR_AREAS.left`, `PALETTE_AREA`, SDK React widgets, atoms, plugin-scoped `ctx.storage`, and explicit-click `ctx.os.writeClipboard`.
- React owns mounting and teardown. CSS targets transcript hooks only; no app DOM queries, observers, private stores, prototype patching or core overrides. Two transcript markup classes are disclosed in the README as compatibility dependencies.

### Validation
- Cloned the public repository and checked out the exact pinned commit.
- Installed Hermes 0.21.5 public CLI parser/dispatch, `plugins validate <pinned-checkout> --install-deps --json`: exit 0, all eleven checks passed, security scan **safe**, Desktop surface passed.
- Expected validator warning: no Python `__init__.py`, so the Python capability probe is skipped for this desktop-only package.
- Locked test dependencies installed independently with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`; all eight React DOM behavior checks passed, covering presets, persistence, JSON, validation, write failure, external live-status preservation and clean teardown/reload.
- Native Windows clicks verified the title-bar/dialog, preset application, custom sizing and close/reopen persistence. Other operating systems and future markup are not covered by native QA.
- Reproducible commands and limits: [verification notes](https://github.com/gchablemeneses-web/hermes-chat-studio/blob/8b97b6c99a1f34abc6a8c5f461c894a8bb3f95d2/docs/verification.md).

### Behavior disclosure
No network/model calls, telemetry, shell commands, background processes, credentials or reads outside the plugin's own configuration. Storage contains appearance preferences and saved styles only. Clipboard writes occur only on explicit export clicks; import consumes text pasted into the plugin's own textarea. No Python runtime dependencies or additional model tools/hooks/middleware/env vars. Desktop plugins have renderer authority; the SDK/loader is not a security sandbox.

### Native screenshot
The screenshot is cropped to the plugin-owned dialog and contains only its synthetic preview, with no private conversations or account information.

![Chat Studio preset picker and live preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gchablemeneses-web/hermes-chat-studio/8b97b6c99a1f34abc6a8c5f461c894a8bb3f95d2/docs/presets.png)

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #85381 and resolves the review regression flagged on the two competing PRs for it.

**Root cause** (verified live on `origin/main` 0ff4c74865): the Telegram formatter's fence regex
`(```(?:[^\n]*\n)?[\s\S]*?```)` is unanchored, so a *single-line* inline triple-backtick span
(`the syntax is ```like this``` inline`) is swallowed as a fenced block, emitting an unbalanced
MarkdownV2 `<pre>` entity → Telegram replies `can't find end of pre entity` and every rich
formatting element in the message is dropped by the plain-text fallback.

**Coverage** — this PR is #85398's three commits (cherry-picked, authorship preserved) plus one
widening commit that fixes the regression its line-start-only anchor introduced:

1. The anchor fix for #85381 (PRATHAMESH75's work, kept as-is): a fence must open on its own
   line, so single-line inline triples fall through to escaping instead of opening a bogus pre.
2. Widened anchors (new commit 673fa320): the opening line may carry **any** leading whitespace
   or lead-in prose ("Here is the code: ```"), and the closing fence may sit at any indent —
   both shapes render as `<pre>` on main and were silently downgraded to escaped literal prose
   by the 0–3-space line-start-only anchor. The discriminator that keeps inline triples out:
   the rest of the opening line must be backtick-free, and the tempered prefix
   (`(?:(?!```)[^\n])*`) cannot skip past an earlier triple run to a later one.

## Changes made

- `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py` — widened fence regex + `_protect_fenced` now re-emits
  the lead-in text outside the protected block.
- `tests/gateway/test_telegram_format.py` — 4 new tests: mid-line-opened fence, 4+-space
  list-nested indented fence, fence after an inline-code lead-in, inline pair followed by a real
  fence (neither main nor the anchored regex handled that mix correctly).
- `tests/conformance/vectors/telegram.json` — the `scar` vector reverts to main's committed
  value: its mid-line-opened fence is protected again, so vs main the only vector change this
  PR carries is the `adversarial` inline-escape case (the intended #85381 semantics, which
  Enough1122's review point 4 on #85398 endorsed locking in).

## Tests

Red/green matrix (all verified by running the suite at each head):

| Test | on `main` | on #85398 head (fdc0faf) | on this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| inline triple backticks (#85381) | **red** (mangled) | green | green |
| mid-line-opened fence | green | **red** (regression) | green |
| 4+-space list-nested indented fence | green | **red** (regression) | green |
| mid-line fence after inline-code lead-in | green | **red** (regression) | green |
| inline pair followed by real fence | **red** (swallowed) | green | green |

Real checks run on this head (673fa32054121a0046915f045e393078335b2d09):

    scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_telegram_format.py                    # 45 passed
    scripts/run_tests.sh tests/conformance/                                       # 15 passed, 6 skipped
    scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_telegram_format.py tests/conformance/test_vector_generator.py \
        $(all tests/gateway/test_telegram*.py files)                                # 516 passed, 0 failed
    scripts/generate_conformance_vectors.py                                       # regenerated; only telegram.json scar line differs from the branch state
    scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all && scripts/check_bash_shebangs.py \
      && scripts/check_no_tmp_literals.py && scripts/check_config_yaml_writers.py \
      && scripts/ci/check_os_marker_fakes.py                                      # all clean
    uvx ruff check plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py tests/gateway/test_telegram_format.py  # clean

## Side effects

1. **Existing state:** none — per-send message formatting in the Telegram plugin; nothing is
   persisted, keyed, or re-keyed; no config, store, or path touched.
2. **Version skew:** none — single-process backend plugin; no Hermes client/server boundary and
   no cross-version surface. The Telegram Bot API payload shape for protected blocks is
   unchanged (still ```-delimited pre entities).
3. **Reserved values / invariant tests:** no stock-config value gains meaning; no existing test
   assertion is rewritten. The committed `adversarial` conformance vector's `native_output`
   flips vs main — that is the #85381 fix itself, made deliberately by #85398, demanded by the
   issue, and endorsed by reviewer point 4 on #85398; `test_committed_vectors_match_regeneration`
   stays green (regeneration-locked, oracle-generated). The `scar` vector returns to main's
   committed value (the mid-line fence it encodes is protected again), so this PR narrows #85398's
   vector delta, it doesn't widen it.
4. **Other callers and flows:** `format_message` is the single entry point (send path + the
   conformance generator, which imports it unbound — generator tests green). Net behavior vs
   main is: (a) single-line inline triple pairs and unclosed fence openers now escape as literal
   text (the fix); (b) a line-start fence whose info string itself contains backticks (GFM
   forbids this) no longer opens a block — pathological, and the old "protection" emitted an
   opening line Telegram cannot parse as a language tag; (c) 4+-backtick runs no longer
   half-open a block — main emitted an unbalanced entity there (the production failure #86283
   was built from); this PR escapes them instead, which cannot produce an unbalanced pre.
   Chunking/pagination (`_separate_chunk_indicator_from_fence`, `truncate_message`) sees the
   same balanced ``` blocks it already handles; the full `test_telegram*` gateway set (516 tests)
   is green.
5. **Open findings:** Enough1122's 2026-08-16 review on #85398 is answered by construction in
   this PR: point 1 (4+-space indent regression) is fixed with anchors widened + two pinning
   tests (673fa320); point 2 (trailing whitespace after closing fence stripped) — intentional
   in #85398, kept as-is; point 3 (escaped-backtick rendering for ```code``` tail) — renders as
   literal prose with no unbalanced entity, pinned by the adversarial vector; point 4 — vectors
   remain regeneration-locked and match the formatter. Coderabbit's CRLF finding was already
   answered by #85398's c2996a35.

## Self-review

- *Secretly a feature?* No — it restores main's existing rendering for two fence shapes while
  keeping the reported bug fixed; no option, config, or new surface.
- *Critical path?* `uv run triage risk --title … --files <the 3 files> --lines 132 --issue 85381`
  → risk 0.20, `critical: []` (no install-update/launch/ui), kind `hardening`.

## Supersedes

- **#85398** (PRATHAMESH75) — its three commits are cherry-picked here verbatim with authorship
  preserved (`git log` shows all three under their name/email); the #85381 fix in it is the
  foundation of this PR. Superseded only because its anchored regex downgraded mid-line-opened
  and 4+-space-indented fences that main renders as `<pre>` — the exact regression named in the
  side-effect screen and in Enough1122's unanswered review.
- **#86283** (ropu) — its line-oriented GFM parser is a genuinely better long-term direction for
  the *variable-length* fence cases (4+-backtick fences, tilde fences, longer closers, unclosed
  fences, UTF-16 chunking), and it was evaluated live in this sweep: it fixes #85381 but its
  line-start `{0,3}`-indent opener breaks the same two must-keep shapes (mid-line-opened and
  4+-space-indented fences render as escaped prose — its regenerated `scar` vector locks that
  downgrade in). This PR takes the minimal anchor-widening instead; a later PR can adopt the
  line-oriented parser wholesale *if* it also covers those two shapes.

Fixes #85381

## Auto-merge

Narrow formatting fix in one plugin; all affected call paths exercised (45 format tests, 516
telegram gateway tests, conformance regeneration lock); no persisted state, no
cross-version boundary, no reserved values, no rewritten assertions beyond the
issue-mandated vector semantics, and the previously-unanswered review finding is answered
by the widened anchors + pinning tests in reviewed head 673fa32054121a0046915f045e393078335b2d09.

## What does this PR do?

Lands #101852 by @liuhao1024 (their commits, conflict-free on current main) plus the lock-bounding half of #96752 by @fangliquanflq (cherry-picked by hand onto main's extracted `browser_tool_real_profile` module, authorship kept as a co-author trailer). Together they cover both halves of the #96731 failure mode:

1. **Pipe capture wedge (#101852)** — agent-browser forks a resident daemon that inherits the CLI's stdio and outlives it. With `subprocess.run(capture_output=True)`, the CLI can exit while its pipes never reach EOF: POSIX burns the whole timeout draining pipes, and Windows' `TimeoutExpired` cleanup re-drains with no timeout, blocking past the outer 420s tool deadline. Both call sites (`_agent_browser_session_cmd` get cdp-url/close, and the attach-path `open`) now capture through `_popen_agent_browser`'s temp files and wait only for the CLI.
2. **Lock contention bound (#96752)** — `_real_profile_cdp` acquires the process-global launch lock with a 30s bound and fails closed with an actionable error when a previous (possibly abandoned) resolver worker still holds it, instead of parking every later real-profile call until the outer deadline.

Independent Windows confirmations of the pipe-capture diagnosis from @theomgdev, @ju-scho and @jame0716 are on #101852, including a native-`.exe` (non-shim) faulthandler stack pinned in `subprocess._communicate` at `browser_tool_real_profile.py:60/207`.

## Supersedes

- #101852 — @liuhao1024's commits cherry-picked verbatim (4 commits, all authors preserved)
- #96752 — the lock-bounding commit folded in as `Co-authored-by: fangliquanflq`
- #110263 — @Steve-prog001's equivalent temp-file fix; superseded because it fails 2 tests on main's current `test_browser_real_profile.py` (its `_run_agent_browser_argv` diverges from main's launch internals), while #101852's rebase is green

## Side effects

1. **Existing state:** No persisted state touched — the capture files (`_stdout_*`/`_stderr_*`) live in the per-session socket dir, are unlinked best-effort after each call (Windows handles may outlive the kill; bounded: reused and truncated by the next call with the same tag). No localStorage/config/migrations.
