items.body:
A malformed URL authority such as `http://[::1` or `https://[not-an-ip]:80` in a WebSocket `Origin` header, a `/api/media/proxy` URL or a custom-endpoint `base_url` is now rejected cleanly (WS close 4403 `origin_mismatch`, HTTP 400). Previously it raised an unhandled `ValueError`, which surfaced as a 500.

Refs #131271

This salvages #131323. It is a hardening fix that #131323 found while working on #131271, and it does not close that issue. #131271 was already fixed on main by 03477e9ae2 (see Maintainer notes).

## What happened
`urllib.parse.urlparse` raises `ValueError` ("Invalid IPv6 URL") on bracketed authorities that don't close or don't contain an IP. Three dashboard boundaries pass user input straight to it: `_ws_host_origin_reason` (WS Origin guard), `proxy_remote_media` (`/api/media/proxy?url=`) and `_write_custom_endpoint` (custom-endpoint save). None of them caught the error. A bad header or parameter therefore escaped as an unhandled exception instead of the reject each path already uses for empty or invalid input.

## Change
- `hermes_cli/web_server_chat.py` (`_ws_host_origin_reason`): if `urlparse` raises, `parsed` is set to `None`. The existing single `origin_mismatch` return handles it, so the guard fails closed. Non-http(s) origins (`file://`, `null`) are still admitted as before.
- `hermes_cli/web_routers/files.py` (`proxy_remote_media`): `ValueError` from `urlparse` → HTTP 400 with the existing "A remote image URL is required" detail.
- `hermes_cli/web_routers/config_env.py` (`_write_custom_endpoint`): `ValueError` → HTTP 400 with the existing "base_url must include scheme and host" detail. It raises before any config mutation, so saved state is untouched.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_dashboard_auth_ws_auth.py`: `test_gated_cross_site_http_origin_still_host_checked` is now parametrized, with `http://[::1` and `https://[not-an-ip]:52133` alongside the existing `https://evil.test` row.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server.py`:
  - `test_media_proxy_rejects_disallowed_hosts_and_schemes` now asserts an exact status per row (it previously accepted `in (400, 403)`) and adds two malformed rows.
  - New `test_custom_endpoint_rejects_malformed_url_without_changing_saved_state` checks for a 400 and that `config.yaml` / `.env` are byte-identical afterwards.

## Credit
- @itsflownium wrote the fix and tests in #131323. Commit 4d79f63c4b is the net diff of their head c2f131fd90, applied with their authorship kept. The PR's interim loopback-origin exemption (3a46498eb5) and its revert (fc78c40425) are squashed out. @ehz0ah had requested changes on that exemption, and @kvnloo's later review of c2f131fd90 found no blocking issues.
- First submitter: @itsflownium (#131323, first commit 2026-10-02). No other open PR covers the malformed-authority case.
- @kshitijk4poor added two follow-up commits:
  - 5db83fb4f1 dropped the `https://[::1].evil.test` test rows. Only Python 3.14's `urlparse` raises on that input. On 3.11–3.13 the media proxy returns 403 and the custom endpoint saves it (200), so those rows failed outside 3.14. It also replaced the new 111-line `test_web_server_ws_origin.py`, which re-tested the whole login/ticket/heartbeat flow, with two parametrized rows on an existing origin test.
  - 6a4d22e254 is a review follow-up: one `origin_mismatch` return in the WS guard instead of a copied f-string. Behaviour is unchanged.

## Verification
- Tests ran in a clean archive copy (py3.12). Head: 227 passed, 1 skipped across `test_dashboard_auth_ws_auth.py`, `test_web_server.py` and `test_pty_keepalive_ws.py`. `test_pty_keepalive_ws.py` is the only other test file that references a changed symbol. Base: 224 passed, 1 skipped; the 3 new rows/tests don't exist there.
- Red on base: with the prod files reset to base, 4 of the 5 selected cases fail (media proxy, custom endpoint, and both malformed WS origin rows). The `evil.test` row passes, as expected.
- Probe (real imports, gated non-loopback bind):
  - Base: WS `http://[::1` and `https://[not-an-ip]:52133`, media `https://[not-an-ip]:80/x.png` and custom `https://[not-an-ip]:80/v1` all raise `ValueError`.
  - Head: the WS inputs → `origin_mismatch`, media/custom → HTTP 400.
  - Benign inputs are identical on base and head: `file://`, `null`, no Origin and same-host are allowed; `evil.test` and `[::1].evil.test` → `origin_mismatch`; media `evil.example.com` → 403, `file://` → 400; custom `notaurl` → 400.
- Mutation (each prod file reverted to its parent):
  - `web_server_chat.py` → 2 red; `files.py` → 1 red; `config_env.py` → 1 red.
  - 6a4d22e254 → 0 red, as expected for a pure refactor (probe output unchanged).
- `ruff` (F401/F811/F821) shows no new findings. `git diff --check` and the Windows footgun check are clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation). The single r1 finding (Low, duplicated f-string) is fixed in 6a4d22e254. Final verdict: approve.
- Gate numbers come from the pre-rebase head (b069e87a83). The branch was then rebased onto current main (c8301ea6c9) with an identical diff (5 files, +52/-14).

## Maintainer notes
- #131271 (loopback http renderer Origin rejected on a remote bind) is not changed here. That Origin came from the packaged renderer HTTP server, which 03477e9ae2 reverted before the issue was filed. Packaged windows load from `file://` again, and the guard already admits non-http(s) origins. On base, `http://127.0.0.1:53111` is still rejected on a non-loopback bind; no shipped renderer sends it anymore.
- #131498 (@creditlabsonarc-rgb, open) adds a loopback-Origin exemption for #131271. It looks unneeded on main for the same reason as the self-closed #131277. That PR is outside this salvage and is left for a separate call.
- Unconfirmed: whether CI's main test lane runs Python 3.14, which would explain why the author's run of the dropped `[::1].evil.test` rows was green.
- Sibling `urlparse` sites were checked and left alone. `web_server.py::_dashboard_public_hosts`, `dashboard_auth/prefix.py` and `dashboard_auth/routes.py` already catch `ValueError`. `web_routers/mcp.py:77` parses the server-generated `request.base_url`.

items.body:
A plugin whose `register()` walks the platform registry again (for example through i18n/YAML layering → `plugin_entries()`) now loads right away. Before, it waited out the full plugin-load deadline (10s by default) and was then abandoned. A plugin load nested inside another one now also runs inline on the outer deadline worker instead of starting a second worker.

Fixes #130575

## What happened
With a load deadline set (the default), a plugin's `register()` runs on a plugin-load deadline worker. When it walks the registry again, `PlatformRegistry._resolve` finds its own parent's deferred loader still in flight. Ownership of that loader was recorded by `threading.get_ident()`. That is the parent's thread, not the worker's, so the nested walk called `event.wait()` on its own parent's load. The parent was meanwhile joining that same worker, so both waited until `PluginLoadTimeout` abandoned the plugin. On base, the issue's probe shows two deferred plugins each timing out after 2s (4.01s total, both abandoned). Separately, calling `run_with_load_deadline` inside a load started a second worker and joined it. #130577 and #130596 both fixed the direct-nesting part. Neither fixed the registry wait path, which is the hang in the issue's stack.

## Change
- `hermes_cli/plugins_loader.py`:
  - `run_with_load_deadline` uses a ContextVar marker, copied into the deadline worker, to know it is already inside a plugin load. A nested load then runs inline on the current worker instead of starting another one (from #130577).
  - The marker holds the outermost load's list of nested `PluginContext`s. A nested inline context stays in that list only while its `fn()` runs. If the outer load times out, the outer context and any nested loads still running are abandoned. Nested loads that already finished stay enabled. This covers the gap where a nested context stayed live for late registrations from a stranded worker (idea from #130596, re-implemented without try/except).
- `gateway/platform_registry.py`:
  - In-flight ownership is now a per-registry ContextVar frozenset of load keys, set around `loader()`, instead of the `_inflight_owners` thread-id dict (removed). Deadline workers start from `copy_context()`, so a nested walk on the parent's worker takes the existing "recursively requested while loading" return. Unrelated concurrent loaders, which run in fresh contexts, still wait on the event.
  - On a plugin deadline worker (`in_plugin_load_worker()`), a resolve made while a loader is running returns before it starts a sibling deferred loader. Without this, the sibling's `_loader` blocks on `PluginManager._discovery_lock`, which the outer walk holds while it joins this worker. The outer walk resolves the siblings itself. The inline path (`plugins.load_timeout_seconds: 0`) still resolves siblings the same way main does.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins_loader.py` (new): `test_nested_plugin_load_runs_inline_on_deadline_worker`. It asserts the nested load runs on the outer worker thread. It also times the outer load out with one finished and one hung nested load, and asserts that only the outer and hung contexts are abandoned.
- `tests/gateway/test_platform_registry.py`: `test_registry_walk_from_plugin_load_worker_does_not_wait_on_parent`. It uses two deferred platforms whose loaders hold a shared RLock, like the real `_loader`, and is parametrized `(timeout, nested_sees_sibling)` = `(0.5, False)`, `(0, True)`.

## Credit
- @dskwe (Yuan Li) wrote #130577 and submitted first (commit 2c5d3b1140, 2026-10-01 23:02 +08, 27 minutes before #130596). Commits 2c5d3b1140, ae9e171f14 and 54e2f207df were cherry-picked with `-x` and authorship kept (b31ce04715, 65f7b225fb, 6f3c36622c here).
- @JerryLiu369 wrote #130596. It fixed the same direct-nesting case and added a shared abandonment scope for nested contexts, which answered a reviewer's point that #130577 left nested contexts unfenced on timeout. That idea was re-implemented in 9e84cd5247 and credited with `Co-authored-by`.
- @kshitijk4poor added these follow-up commits:
  - 0cd5eeb398: registry in-flight ownership is tracked per flow (ContextVar) instead of per thread. This is the actual fix for the hang in #130575.
  - a75c09b25e and 6a1b593931: a nested resolve on a deadline worker does not start sibling deferred loads, and this applies only on a deadline worker.
  - 9e84cd5247 and 0c0fa22415: on outer timeout, abandon nested inline contexts, but only ones still running.
  - 685e2f5070: dropped #130577's marker-visibility test, which passes even without the fix. The nested-inline test covers the behaviour and is red on base.
  - 7cb8d855e6, 668afeab1b and 2f96892c86: rename, test import hoist and comment fix.
- The contributor email map already had both authors, so there is no chore commit.

## Verification
- Tests on head (clean env):
  - `tests/gateway/test_platform_registry.py`: 27 passed.
  - `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins_loader.py`: 1 passed.
  - `test_deferred_platform_client_tools.py`: 12 passed.
  - `test_plugin_ownership_ledger.py`: 27 passed.
  - `test_startup_plugin_gating.py`: 1 passed.
  - `test_tools_disable_enable.py`: 7 passed.
- Red on base:
  - The registry-walk test fails with base `platform_registry.py` (timeout, `[] == ['reentrant']`).
  - The nested-inline test fails with base `plugins_loader.py` (the outer and nested loads run on different threads).
- Probe (the triage probe plus a sibling-under-lock check and an inline timeout-0 nested `get()` check):
  - Base: the re-entrant walk timed out on both plugins (4.01s, both abandoned). Direct nesting spawned `plugin-load:inner`. Lock-sibling took 4.02s with both abandoned.
  - Head: the re-entrant walk took 0.00s with nothing abandoned. Direct nesting stayed on `plugin-load:outer`. Lock-sibling loaded both platforms in 0.06s with nothing abandoned.
  - The benign no-re-entry load (0.00–0.01s) and inline timeout-0 nested `get()` (sees the sibling) behave the same on base and head.
- Mutation: reverting each behaviour commit's production file turns a kept test red (b31ce04715, 6f3c36622c, 0cd5eeb398, 9e84cd5247, a75c09b25e, 0c0fa22415, 6a1b593931). Reverting the rename (7cb8d855e6) and the comment-only commit (2f96892c86) stays green, as expected for changes with no behaviour effect.
- `ruff` (including F401/F811/F821) and `git diff --check` are clean. The Windows footgun scan has no findings.
- Reviewed over 3 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation):
  - r1 found the sibling-loader deadlock (High) and the over-fencing of finished nested contexts (Low). Both were fixed.
  - r2 found the nested-resolve early return firing on the inline path too (Medium). It was narrowed to deadline workers.
  - The final round approved with no findings.

## Maintainer notes
- Behaviour change: on a plugin deadline worker, a nested `platform_registry.get()` of a deferred sibling that hasn't loaded yet now returns `None` instead of loading it. The outer walk loads the sibling afterwards. This is by design, because waiting there deadlocks on the parent's `_discovery_lock`. The inline path (`load_timeout_seconds: 0`) still loads the sibling.
- Not covered, and the same as main: an EAGER (non-deferred) plugin whose `register()` calls `platform_registry.get(<deferred platform>)` on a deadline worker can still block. `_loading` is empty there, so the new guard does not fire, and the deferred `_loader` waits on `_discovery_lock` held by `discover_and_load`. This is not a regression and is outside this PR.
- Not fenced (r1 Low, skipped): a nested load that starts after the outer load has already been abandoned is not fenced by the abandonment scope.
- Overlap: #130613 (ours) also touches `gateway/platform_registry.py`. Whichever PR lands second needs a merge-tree check.
- Unconfirmed from the report: the exact i18n → `load_yaml_layer` → registry chain in the reporter's stack was not traced on base (the probe injects the registry walk directly). The reported 100% CPU at scale was not reproduced.

items.body:
The Group Chat hosted-room worker no longer fails at startup with `_DeadlockError` when the tool registry imports `tools.connectors.tool` from another thread at the same time.

Fixes #123347

## What happened
`tools/connectors/__init__.py` imported five of its submodules eagerly. A thread running `import tools.connectors` held the package's module lock while it waited for a submodule. Meanwhile another thread could hold that submodule's lock while waiting for the package. One path into the package is the hosted-room worker startup (`gateway/run_startup.py::_ensure_hosted_room_worker` → `import tui_gateway.server` → `from tools.connectors import operation`). The other is registry discovery, which imports `tools.connectors.tool` directly (`tools/registry.py:137`). When both ran at once, Python's import machinery detected the lock cycle and raised `_DeadlockError` in one of the threads.

## Change
- `tools/connectors/__init__.py`: the public surface is now exported lazily through a module-level `__getattr__` (PEP 562), so the package `__init__` no longer imports any submodule.
  - A single `_LAZY_EXPORTS` name→module map drives both `__all__` and `__getattr__`. A resolved name is cached in `globals()`.
  - `__dir__` lists the public names. Unknown names still raise `AttributeError`.
  - Attribute access, `from tools.connectors import x` and the monkeypatch of `tools.connectors.connectors_available` in `test_connector_operation_rpc.py` behave as before.
- `tests/tools/test_connectors_import_deadlock.py` (new). Both tests run in subprocesses so they start with a clean `sys.modules`:
  - `test_package_import_does_not_load_submodules`
  - `test_concurrent_package_and_submodule_import_never_deadlocks`: 3 threads import the package while 3 threads import `tools.connectors.tool`. It asserts only on `_DeadlockError`.
- `contributors/emails/crew-infra@localhost.invalid`: maps the cherry-picked commit's email to rpridal.

## Credit
- @rpridal (Rostislav Přidal) wrote the root-cause fix and its regression tests in #129507. Commit 1803f53b was cherry-picked as ba51150ffc with its authorship kept (`crew-infra <crew-infra@localhost.invalid>`, mapped to rpridal through `contributors/emails`). rpridal is also credited with `Co-authored-by: Rostislav Přidal <5829155+rpridal@users.noreply.github.com>` on fda9a9ae72.
- @Finn763 submitted first, in #123840 (2026-09-26). That PR moved the `tui_gateway.server` import onto the event loop thread. It is not taken here: the package/submodule cycle stays in place for other thread pairs, and the event loop would block on a heavy import.
- #124867 was opened for the same bug and has already been closed by its author.
- @kshitijk4poor added four follow-up commits:
  - 77a08feb9e: contributor-map entry.
  - fda9a9ae72: dropped the contributor's third test (an `__all__`/`dir()` change-detector) and kept the two invariant tests.
  - c50dfcf723: the race test now asserts only on `_DeadlockError`. The harness's own `sys.modules` purge could raise `AttributeError` under parallel load, which made the test flaky (8/160 runs red).
  - accc76d4d0: shorter docstrings, unquoted annotations, and removed a redundant `sys.path` setup in the test snippets. No behaviour change.

## Verification
- Tests on the head in a clean archive copy: 300 passed, 0 failed. This covers the new deadlock tests, the connector suites under `tests/tools/` (bridge wiring, dispatch policy, local batches, names, session scope, catalog, tool, contract, live, managed, mcp, operation, gateway client/merge/wire), `tests/tui_gateway/` connector operation e2e/rpc and MCP OAuth callback/cancel, `test_registry`, and the related `hermes_cli` and `agent` batch tests.
- The race test passed 10/10 on the head. After the c50dfcf723 fix it passed 160/160 under 8x parallel load.
- Red on base: with the base `tools/connectors/__init__.py`, both new tests fail (5/5 runs in the gate, and 30/30 runs for the race test during the fold).
- Probe (Python 3.12.7): 3 threads importing the package raced 3 threads importing `tools.connectors.tool`, 40 iterations per run, with `sys.modules` purged between iterations.
  - Base: 157 / 118 / 119 `_DeadlockError` over 3 runs.
  - Head: 0 / 0 / 0 over 3 runs, with no threads left alive. The public surface still resolves to the same objects.
  - The contributor measured 120 deadlocks before and 0 after on Python 3.14.7.
- Mutation: reverting the contributor fix turns both new tests red. The follow-up commits only change tests, docstrings or the contributor map, so no mutation applies to them.
- `ruff` F401/F811/F821, `git diff --check` and the Windows footgun check are clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- Commit author: ba51150ffc keeps the contributor's original author, `crew-infra <crew-infra@localhost.invalid>`. That email is not linked to rpridal's GitHub account, so attribution relies on the `contributors/emails` map plus the `Co-authored-by` trailer on fda9a9ae72. The alternative is to amend the author to `Rostislav Přidal <5829155+rpridal@users.noreply.github.com>` (user id from the GitHub API) before merge. Please choose one.
- The cherry-picked commit message also carries the original commit's tool `Co-Authored-By` trailer. It was left unchanged.
- Not built: #123347 also asks for an INFO log line when the hosted-room worker recovers after failing closed. That can be a separate follow-up.
- Only `tools/connectors/__init__.py` was checked. Other `tools/*/__init__.py` packages were not audited for the same eager-import pattern. `from tools.connectors import live` in `run.py` and `account.py` is a submodule import and is not affected.
- No overlap found with other open PRs on `tools/connectors/__init__.py`.

items.body:
Adds the community hermes-pii plugin to the tools catalog, pinned to version 0.1.0.dev2.

The plugin registers `pre_llm_call` and `llm_request` and uses local Presidio/spaCy to redact supported PII in Chat Completions user messages and Responses user input. System/developer prompts, tool outputs, tool-call arguments and local history are preserved.

Model provisioning is manual: install `en_core_web_sm` 3.8.0 from its GitHub release wheel in the Python environment used by Hermes before enabling the plugin, following the pinned README. The plugin no longer declares the unavailable PyPI model package or relies on `[tool.uv.sources]`. `requires_env` remains empty because no environment variable is required.

Disclosure: detection is local and models are never downloaded at runtime. Provisioning downloads the model from GitHub. Detection errors, including a missing model, fail open and send original text; this POC is not a privacy guarantee.

Validation: all 16 plugin tests pass with a preinstalled model, including offline detection and missing-model fallback; dependency compatibility and catalog structural validation pass. The installed Hermes 0.19.0 CLI does not expose `plugins validate`, so full catalog admission validation remains for CI.

items.body:
When context compaction prunes or digests an old tool result that an approval or write guard refused, the summary now says "BLOCKED, not run" and keeps the user's do-not-retry instruction. Before, it described the call as if it had run.

Fixes #131673

## What happened
Phase-1 pruning (`_demote_tool_result_at`) and the deterministic fallback digest both call `_summarize_tool_result_unguarded` in `agent/context_compressor.py`, and that function picks a per-tool one-liner. Those one-liners assume the call ran. A denied `rm -rf build` became `[terminal] ran \`rm -rf build\` -> exit -1, 1 lines output`, and a denied protected write became `[write_file] wrote to AGENTS.md (2 lines)`. The "The user has NOT consented ... Do NOT retry" text was dropped. Denial messages run past 300 chars, above the 200-char prune floor, so any long session that hit a denial could lose it this way. The same happened to pending-approval results and to the `patch` and `execute_code` refusals.

## Change
- `agent/context_compressor.py` (+26):
  - New `_summarize_refused_tool_result` runs before the per-tool summarizers inside `_summarize_tool_result_unguarded`. Both callers (prune and fallback) go through that function, so one check covers both.
  - The check works the same for any tool:
    - `status == "pending_approval"` → `awaiting the user's approval, not run`.
    - A non-empty `error` string together with either `status == "blocked"` or an error that starts with `BLOCKED` → `BLOCKED, not run`. When the error contains "NOT consented", it adds `the user did NOT consent, do not retry or reach the same outcome another way`.
    - A raw `BLOCKED: ...` string with no JSON envelope is treated as the error.
  - The output is capped below `_PRUNE_MIN_CHARS`, the same way the clarify summary is, so later prune passes keep it rather than re-summarizing it. All other results are summarized exactly as before.
- `tests/agent/test_context_compressor.py` (+72): new `TestSummarizeToolResultRefusals` with two test functions:
  - `test_denial_summary_keeps_not_run_and_no_consent` is parametrized over 7 rows built from real producers: `cli_denied`, `transport_denied`, `cli_timeout` (approval gate), `write_guard` (raw `BLOCKED:` text), `workdir_guard` (`status="blocked"`), `pending_approval`, and the negative row `kanban_block_ok`.
  - `test_prune_keeps_denial_across_passes`.

## Credit
- @EloquentBrush0x reported #131673 and wrote the fix and tests in #131674. They were also the first to submit. Their commit fd506bbccd was cherry-picked as 4b9f674e50 with authorship kept. Their contributor email was already in the map, so this stack has no map commit.
- @kshitijk4poor added these follow-up commits:
  - 69102405b3 cut the tests down to two invariant tests.
  - 236c09c8ff moved the case ids into `pytest.param` so they sit with their rows.
  - 7ba238e41e added a test for the pending-approval branch.
  - c4c635a044 makes a result count as refused only when it carries an `error`. Without this, successful `kanban_block` results and `kanban_create(initial_status="blocked")` results, which return `{"ok": true, "status": "blocked"}`, were summarized as "BLOCKED, not run". The model could then repeat a block or create that had already succeeded.
  - abd8ec65ee and d26cb78d82 add tests for the `status == "blocked"` disjunct (terminal workdir guard) and for the raw `BLOCKED:` text fallback.

## Verification
- Tests on the final head, run in a clean archive copy: `tests/agent/test_context_compressor.py` and `tests/agent/test_summarize_tool_result_type_safety.py` gave 293 passed.
- Final gate at c4c635a044, per file: `test_context_compressor.py` 283 passed, `test_compression_marker.py` 2 passed, `test_compressor_stale_tool_images.py` 6 passed, `test_ghost_skill_pruning.py` 11 passed, `test_proactive_prune_rearm_threshold.py` 5 passed, `test_summarize_tool_result_type_safety.py` 9 passed, and `tests/tools/test_computer_use.py` 86 passed with 1 skipped.
- Red on base: with the base compressor, every positive row and the prune-across-passes test fail. Only `kanban_block_ok`, the negative row, passes, which is what it should do on base.
- Probe: the real compressor fed real refusal payloads.
  - Base: all 5 refusal shapes (cli_denied, pending, write_guard, patch_guard, execute_code_blocked) come out as completed actions ("ran", "wrote to", "replace in").
  - Head: every refusal comes out as `BLOCKED, not run` with the no-consent clause, except pending, which reads `awaiting the user's approval, not run`.
  - 6 benign cases print identically on base and head: a successful kanban_block, read_file, ok and failing terminal, ok write_file, and terminal output that starts with `BLOCKED:` while `error` is null.
- Mutation: each change below was reverted on its own and the tests re-run.
  - Contributor fix reverted: 6 red.
  - Error-required follow-up reverted: 1 red (`kanban_block_ok`).
  - Pending branch removed: 1 red.
  - "NOT consented" clause removed: 5 red.
  - Length cap removed: 6 red.
  - `status == "blocked"` disjunct removed: 0 red at the final gate. abd8ec65ee added a row, and after it 1 red.
  - Raw-text fallback removed: 0 red at the final gate. d26cb78d82 added a row, and after it 1 red.
  - Target text removed: 0 red. This only affects wording.
- `ruff` (F401/F811/F821) and `git diff --check` are clean, and the Windows footgun scan is clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation). Round 1 found the kanban false positive (Medium, fixed in c4c635a044) and three test-hygiene Lows (two fixed, one docstring wording note skipped). The final gate approved with two Low test gaps, both closed in the last two commits.

## Maintainer notes
- Behaviour change: a refused or pending-approval tool result now has the same summary whatever tool produced it. `execute_code` and other tools without a `command` or `path` argument get no target in the line, for example `[execute_code] BLOCKED, not run; ...`.
- The terminal workdir-validation rejection also returns `status="blocked"`. It is summarized as `BLOCKED, not run` without the consent clause, because its text has no "NOT consented". That is accurate, since it is not a user denial.
- Cost: one extra bounded `json.loads` per summarized result. It runs only at compression time and only once per result, because the stub that replaces the result is under the prune floor.
- Not checked: `tools/osv_check.py` returns a raw `BLOCKED: Package…` string. No one traced whether it can reach a tool result unwrapped. If it does, it would also be summarized as `BLOCKED, not run`.
- #131312 (@kokhlo) fixes a different case where outcomes get lost: templated stubs that drop the failure outcome (#131244). It is not a duplicate and is not included here. It applies cleanly on top of this stack: with both applied, 298 tests passed and the probe stayed clean.
- File sizes before this change: `agent/context_compressor.py` was 5781 lines and `tests/agent/test_context_compressor.py` was 3695. This stack only adds lines (+98/-0).
- No overlap with other open PRs that touch `_summarize_tool_result*`.

items.title: Compaction no longer summarizes a denied tool call as if it ran (#131673, salvage #131674)

items.body:
Sessions whose active turn is a long run of tool calls with no text reply yet can be compressed again. Previously the whole oversized turn was kept in the protected tail, so every manual or automatic compress did nothing and logged `no_progress`.

Fixes #131412

## What happened
In `_find_tail_cut_by_tokens`, the #80449 oversized-turn split only relaxes the user anchor, and only when that anchor pulls the cut back. In a long agentic turn, the latest user message already sits inside the token-budget tail, so the split never fires. `_ensure_last_assistant_message_in_tail` then pulls the cut back to the newest assistant row that has text. When the active turn's assistant rows carry only `tool_calls`, that row is the previous turn's closer. The whole active turn rides the protected tail, the middle window collapses to almost nothing, and compression no-ops on every attempt. In the reproduction the tail was 245,901 tokens against a 30k soft ceiling, with 1,041 tokens left in the middle.

## Change
- `agent/context_compressor.py`:
  - The assistant anchor gets a bound like the one the user anchor got in #80449. When mid-turn splits are allowed, the anchored region holds `tool_calls`, and that region is over the tail soft ceiling, the walk's tool-group-aligned cut is kept instead of anchoring to the older reply. A debug log records the decision.
  - New `_tail_row_pricer(messages)` holds the per-row pricing that `_walk_tail_budget` used inline (native Anthropic budget, or the estimate that charges stale thinking only when the wire carries it, #84371). The walk and the new gate both use it, so the gate prices the region the same way the walk does. The walk's behaviour is unchanged.
  - Rolling micro-compaction (`allow_split_turn=False`) keeps the old anchoring. The multi-user anchor promise (#70250) is untouched.
- `tests/agent/test_split_turn_compaction.py`:
  - `test_assistant_anchor_cannot_retain_a_textless_oversized_turn`: the #131412 shape must cut inside the active turn, at the walk's group-aligned cut.
  - `test_assistant_anchor_still_binds`, parametrized over 3 shapes, guards the escape against over-firing. Each case must still anchor to the older closer: splitting disabled, a reasoning-heavy small turn (#84371 pricing), and an over-ceiling region of plain text with no `tool_calls`.

## Credit
- @liuhao1024 wrote the fix and both original regression tests in #131445. Commit 9259ea925c was cherry-picked as 09fab09495 with authorship kept. They were also the first and only submitter for #131412.
- @kshitijk4poor added five follow-up commits:
  - b5ebafddc2 narrows the escape gate (co-authored by @liuhao1024). As submitted, the gate measured the region with `_walk_tail_budget` from the anchored cut. That fires whenever any single region after a visible reply is over the ceiling, such as with tiny budgets or one large tool output. It dropped the last visible reply and reopened #29824: `test_reporter_repro_long_tool_run_after_visible_reply` and `test_oversized_tool_output_does_not_strand_reply` failed, matching a reviewer's finding on #131445. The gate now also requires `tool_calls` in the region and sums only `[anchor, cut)`.
  - 8e15759de5 adds `_tail_row_pricer` so the gate does not charge stale thinking that the wire never carries. Without it, a small turn with heavy `reasoning_content` tripped the gate and dropped the reply (cut 5 instead of 2).
  - ff70998595 and cec24210f9 pin exact cuts in the tests and add the plain-text row that pins the `tool_calls` sub-gate.
  - dea37b74c8 and 3b372f4669 are comment/docstring corrections.

## Verification
- Tests were run in clean archive copies of the head:
  - Final gate (at 3b372f4669), across 18 test files that reference `_walk_tail_budget`, `_find_tail_cut_by_tokens`, `_ensure_last_assistant_message_in_tail` or `_tail_row_pricer`: 442 passed, 0 failed. This includes `test_context_compressor.py` 276, `test_anthropic_preserved_thinking_replay.py` 44, `test_compressor_assistant_tail_anchor.py` 14, `test_replay_budget_accounting.py` 13, `test_estimator_parity.py` 12 and `test_split_turn_compaction.py` 10.
  - After cec24210f9, which is test-only: `test_split_turn_compaction.py` + `test_context_compressor.py` passed 287. `test_split_turn_compaction.py` alone passed 11.
- Red on base: `test_assistant_anchor_cannot_retain_a_textless_oversized_turn` fails on base and passes on head. The `test_assistant_anchor_still_binds` rows pass on base as expected, since base has no escape to over-fire. Their teeth come from the mutations below.
- Probe: a synthetic 250-message session matching the reporter's telemetry, run through the real `_find_tail_cut_by_tokens`.
  - Base: cut=5, middle 1,041 tokens, tail 245,901 tokens (wedge).
  - Head: cut=219, middle 216,315 tokens, tail 30,627 tokens.
  - Neighbouring shapes are identical on base and head: both #29824 reporter shapes keep the reply in the tail, a small active turn stays at cut=5, and a reasoning-heavy small turn stays at cut=5.
- Mutation: each change below, reverted alone, turns a test red.

  | Reverted | Test that goes red |
  |---|---|
  | contributor escape (09fab09495) | `cannot_retain_a_textless_oversized_turn` |
  | tool-region gate (b5ebafddc2) | `still_binds[_reasoning_heavy_small_turn]` |
  | `_tail_row_pricer` pricing (8e15759de5) | `still_binds[_reasoning_heavy_small_turn]` |
  | `allow_split_turn` check dropped | `still_binds[_textless_oversized_turn-False]` |
  | `tool_calls` sub-gate dropped | `still_binds[_plain_text_oversized_region]` (after cec24210f9) |

- `ruff` F401/F811/F821 is clean, `git diff --check` is clean, and the Windows footgun check found nothing in 1851 files.
- Reviewed over 3 gate rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation).

## Maintainer notes
- Behaviour change: when the escape fires, the previous turn's visible reply is no longer guaranteed to be in the tail, and it gets summarized. A real `compress()` run on the #131412 shape (with a stubbed summary) confirmed that `_ensure_compressed_keeps_last_assistant_reply` does not reinsert it, so it does not undo the reclaim. The escape only fires when the region holds tool-call bodies and is over the soft ceiling, so the #29824 shapes keep their reply.
- This touches the same function as our open #130506 (`_find_tail_cut_by_tokens`). The hunks are adjacent but disjoint: #130506 edits the user-split gate's length check, and this PR edits the assistant-anchor line. Whichever lands second rebases. #130506 alone does not fix #131412 (probe unchanged at cut=5). This PR also changes the body of `_walk_tail_budget` through the `_tail_row_pricer` extraction.
- The fix was checked on a synthetic shape, not by replaying the reporter's 878-message session with its Codex reasoning weight.
- `agent/context_compressor.py` grows from 5781 to 5806 lines.
- Possible overlap with older open #113028 ("bound oversized protected tails") and #107159 ("lean tail shed a runaway assistant message"). Neither has been diffed against this PR.
- Companion: the misleading `no_progress` failure label for this wedge is fixed separately in #131441.

items.title: Compression no longer wedges on a long tool-only turn (#131412, salvage #131445)

items.body:
Hermes processes that share one `state.db` from different PID namespaces (for example gateway and webui containers on one volume, or systemd `PrivatePIDs=`) no longer reclaim each other's live session turn leases, compression locks or flock holder records.

Refs #123081

## What happened
Lock and lease holders record `pid=<n>`, but that PID only means something inside the writer's PID namespace. Processes in a sibling namespace see a disjoint PID set, so the namespace-blind liveness probes read a live sibling's PID as gone. `_compression_lock_holder_process_is_dead` in `hermes_state.py` then reclaimed the unexpired row, and `_lock_holder_provably_dead` in `hermes_state_common.py` broke the live flock. For a turn lease this ends the sibling's in-flight turn ("another Hermes process took over this session"). For a compression lock it splits the lineage. This PR covers the session-lease half of #123081; the gateway-record half is open #123187.

## Change
- `hermes_state_pidns.py` (new, 128 lines): reads the writer's PID-namespace identity (the `/proc/self/ns/pid` inode), builds the `pidns=` holder token, and decides whether a recorded holder PID can be probed:
  - TTL-bounded rows (compression locks, turn leases), STRICT: a foreign-namespace or unstamped holder is never probed. It waits for its own expiry.
  - No-expiry flock holder records, LEGACY: a foreign-namespace record is never probed. An unstamped record keeps main's behaviour, so the #100108 orphaned-lock break still works.
  - When our own namespace lookup fails, the unstamped policy is checked first, so an unstamped flock record can still be broken and a stamped one fails closed. A failed lookup is not cached.
- `hermes_state.py`: the shared lease/lock liveness gate (used by the compression and message paths) checks `holder_pid_checkable` before probing.
- `hermes_state_common.py`: `_write_lock_holder_record` stamps `pidns`, and `_lock_holder_provably_dead` qualifies the record before probing.
- `agent/conversation_compression.py`, `agent/turn_facade_lease.py`: both structured `pid=` holder builders append the namespace token. `conversation_compression.py` stays at its base line count.
- `tests/hermes_state/test_lease_pid_namespace.py` (new): two invariant tests, with the local namespace pinned via `_LOCAL_PID_NS` so they are no longer Linux-only:
  - `test_turn_lease_of_sibling_namespace_is_not_stolen`: a sibling-namespace turn lease is not stolen, and an unstamped dead-PID TTL holder is not reclaimed before its TTL.
  - `test_flock_holder_record_qualifies_pid_namespaces`: a foreign-namespace flock record is not broken while same-namespace and unstamped dead records still are. It also covers the failed-lookup rows, recovery after a failed lookup, and that the flock record and compression-lock holder stamp our namespace.
- `tests/hermes_state/test_session_turn_lease.py`, `tests/hermes_state/test_hermes_state_compression_locks.py`: holder strings now carry the stamp, so the existing tests keep exercising the same-namespace proof path.
- `contributors/emails/32956795+aleesposito85@users.noreply.github.com`: contributor map entry.

## Credit
- @aleesposito85 wrote the fix in #131116 (opened 2026-10-02). It is the first and only PR for this bug. Commit 4b1a29f63b was cherry-picked as 074e8fa199 with authorship kept.
- @kshitijk4poor added follow-up commits:
  - 5deda1202f: trimmed the contributor's 18-test file to the two behavioural invariants.
  - 6b2f1da911, 5d669ec783, c8b074e792: condensed the module docstring, inlined a one-call parser, moved the pidns imports to module level, and replaced repeated call-site prose with pointers to the module docstring. No behaviour change.
  - ac3f6cca7e: unstamped flock records stay breakable when our own namespace lookup fails. Before this, main's #100108 cleanup was lost on those hosts.
  - fbe9bf14e8, 4c8678f5fd, e3ee4d3084: test assertions that pin the STRICT unstamped defer, the uncached failed lookup, and the writer stamps.
  - fea14db8b4: contributor-map commit.

## Verification
- Tests ran on the head in a clean archive copy:
  - `test_lease_pid_namespace.py`, `test_hermes_state_compression_locks.py`, `test_session_turn_lease.py`, `test_turn_facade_lease.py`: 37 passed.
  - `test_compress_signal_leak.py`, `test_idle_compaction_lock_and_guards.py`, `test_writer_conn_thread_safety.py`, `test_compression_concurrent_fork.py`: 58 passed.
  - `tui_gateway/test_routing_provenance_reopen.py` + `agent/test_conversation_compression_manual.py`: 27 passed. The build also ran `test_cross_process_turn_lease.py` (19 passed) and `e2e/core/compaction/test_compaction_kill9.py` (2 passed).
- Red on base: with base `hermes_state.py` and `hermes_state_common.py`, both new tests fail (`True is False`), and they pass on head.
- Probe: real imports, reader pinned to a fixed namespace, holders in a disjoint namespace.
  - Base: sibling-namespace live lease reclaim=True, unstamped lease reclaim=True, foreign-namespace flock break=True.
  - Head: those three are False (the unstamped case is the intended STRICT defer). Same-namespace dead/live holders, unstructured holders and unstamped/same-namespace dead flock records behave the same on base and head.
  - Failed-lookup rows on head: unstamped flock break=True, stamped flock break=False, stamped lease reclaim=False.
- Mutation:
  - Reverting the contributor fix fails test collection, since the module is missing.
  - The docstring and failed-lookup fix commits each turn `test_flock_holder_record_qualifies_pid_namespaces` red. The two refactor commits stay green, as expected.
  - Removing the `hermes_state.py` gate or the `hermes_state_common.py` gate turns the matching test red.
  - The final gate found that the STRICT unstamped policy, the flock-record stamp, the compression-holder stamp and the failed-lookup cache guard stayed green under mutation. The last three follow-up commits added assertions for each, and each now goes red under its mutation.
- `ruff` (F401/F811/F821) shows no new findings on touched files. `git diff --check` and the Windows footgun check are clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency) plus a final tests/probe/mutation gate.

## Maintainer notes
- Behaviour change (STRICT policy): after upgrade, an unstamped turn lease or compression lock left by a pre-upgrade process is no longer reclaimed early, even if its PID is dead. It waits out its TTL (≤300s), once. Unstamped flock records keep main's behaviour.
- Overlap: open #123187 (@Halldrix, `gateway/*`) adds a second PID-namespace resolver (`hermes_platform/host/pid_namespace.py`). Whichever PR lands second should reuse the other's resolver.
- Untested gap: removing the `pidns` token from the `agent/turn_facade_lease.py` holder string still leaves the tests green. The compression-holder and flock-record stamps are pinned.
- Not driven: a real two-container Linux run. Namespace behaviour was tested by injecting the local namespace and a fake process view.
- `agent/conversation_compression.py` is 4582 lines on main; this PR leaves the count unchanged.

items.title: Sibling PID namespaces no longer steal session leases or locks (#123081, salvage #131116)

items.body:
When PTB's dispatcher stops handing fetched updates to handlers, the Telegram adapter now marks itself degraded and hands off to the gateway supervisor for a rebuild. Before this change it logged a "healthy but deaf" warning and stayed `connected` while messages went unanswered.

Fixes #130407
Refs #131435 (this covers only the Telegram dispatch-stall part; the issue stays open for the unexplained switch of the primary provider to OpenRouter)

## What happened
The ingress watchdog from #102260 compares `_updates_received_total` (fetched by getUpdates) with `_updates_dispatched_total` (handed to a handler). When a backlog stopped making progress, `_check_ingress_dispatch_stall` only logged a warning. It never scheduled recovery or marked the adapter degraded, so `gateway_state.json` kept saying `connected`. The transport probes don't catch this either, because getUpdates is still completing round-trips. An in-place Updater restart wouldn't help, since it keeps the same wedged dispatcher. Only a supervisor rebuild clears it.

## Change
- `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py`:
  - `_check_ingress_dispatch_stall` now raises a plain `_PollingStallError` through `_schedule_polling_recovery` when there is still a backlog with no dispatch progress after `_INGRESS_DISPATCH_STALL_HEARTBEATS` heartbeats. That error skips the in-place restart and goes retryable-fatal, so the supervisor rebuilds the adapter, and the adapter is marked degraded on the way. It reports once per stall and re-arms when dispatch makes progress. The "healthy but deaf" pre-log is gone; its counts now go in the error text, the same as the sibling `_check_polling_stall`.
  - The watchdog now returns early while an unrelated recovery is in flight (`_recovery_in_flight()`). Without that check, `_schedule_polling_recovery` would drop the handoff and the latched counter would swallow the stall for good.
  - `_INGRESS_DISPATCH_STALL_HEARTBEATS` goes from 2 to 4 (360s). That is longer than `_POLLING_ERROR_TASK_STUCK_TIMEOUT` (300s), so one slow but bounded handler doesn't trigger a rebuild. PTB dispatches sequentially, and a sticker `vision_analyze` can take 120s or more.
  - The confirmed-stall fatal message now includes the redacted error text. It used to hardcode "getUpdates made no progress", which is wrong for a dispatch stall, where getUpdates is still working.
- `tests/gateway/test_telegram_ingress_delivery_gap.py`:
  - New `test_dispatch_stall_marks_degraded_and_goes_fatal`: a stall marks the adapter degraded and goes retryable-fatal naming the dispatcher, with no in-place Updater restart.
  - `test_dispatch_progress_rearms_the_report` now also covers the recovery-scheduling counts and the in-flight-recovery guard.
  - The healthy legs now assert that no handoff happens. The existing counting tests stub the handoff.
- `tests/plugins/test_telegram_update_admission.py`: the ingress admission case now loops `_INGRESS_DISPATCH_STALL_HEARTBEATS` instead of a hardcoded 3. With 3, the threshold of 4 was never reached and the case couldn't fail.

## Credit
- @JerryLiu369 wrote the fix in #130942. Two commits were cherry-picked with authorship kept:
  - 0135a67757 (from 7767ed38e4): escalate the dispatch stall to a supervisor rebuild.
  - cd0e6a1749 (from 589c8c06be): counter-reset retry fix after @Enough1122's review on #130942.
- First submitter of this bug class: @i3enl (Ben Lee) in draft #71240 (2026-07-25). It used a different detection design (`Application.running`/queue size) that predates the #102260 counters, and it now conflicts with main. No code was taken from it, and there is no `Co-authored-by` because the commit email is a local hostname.
- Follow-up commits by @kshitijk4poor:
  - 728e52d10f: dropped the no-loop `try/except RuntimeError` fallback. The only caller is the async heartbeat, which matches `_check_polling_stall`. This makes the logic of cd0e6a1749 unnecessary at head.
  - f9366d2d8e: the fatal message names the actual stall.
  - 23ccef84eb: stall budget raised from 2 to 4 heartbeats so a slow but bounded handler doesn't trip it.
  - 4b3eed8082: removed the dead `_IngressDispatchStallError` subclass and the triple announce of one stall.
  - Test commits fd1feda381, 1707ab147b, 2cb370b3be, abc2e5327e and 8b28c3ff69: folded the 8 new tests into one new test in the existing delivery-gap file, and made the healthy-leg, admission-loop and in-flight-guard assertions able to fail.

## Verification
- Tests ran at head in a clean archive copy, in separate pytest calls:
  - `test_telegram_ingress_delivery_gap.py`, `test_telegram_network_reconnect.py` and `test_telegram_polling_stall_watchdog.py`: 48 passed.
  - `test_telegram_send_path_health.py` and `test_telegram_start_polling_timeout.py`: 15 passed.
  - `tests/plugins/test_telegram_update_admission.py`, run alone: 92 passed.
  - After the last fold: delivery_gap and polling_stall_watchdog 14 passed; update_admission alone 92 passed.
- Red on base: with base `adapter.py`, 3 of the 5 delivery-gap tests fail (stall reported once, re-arm, degraded and fatal).
- Probe: real adapter imports, counters injected, heartbeats driven.
  - Base: a stalled backlog (4 and 12 heartbeats) gives `recovery_calls=[]` and a real-path `fatal=False`, so the bug fires.
  - Head: `['_PollingStallError']`, exactly once over 12 heartbeats. Real path: `fatal=True, retryable=True`, no in-place `start_polling`/`stop`.
  - Slow handler at 3 heartbeats (270s), drained queue, and a backlog that is still progressing: no recovery on base or head.
- Mutation (each behaviour commit reverted in `adapter.py`, kept tests re-run):
  - 0135a67757, cd0e6a1749, 728e52d10f and 23ccef84eb: 3 red each.
  - f9366d2d8e: 1 red.
  - 4b3eed8082: 2 red.
  - Dropping only the `_recovery_in_flight()` guard: 0 red in the final gate. 8b28c3ff69 then added an assertion, and with the guard dropped it now fails (`assert 1 == 0`).
- `ruff` and `git diff --check` are clean on touched lines. The Windows footgun scan found nothing.
- Reviewed over 3 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation), with 3 fold passes.

## Maintainer notes
- Behaviour change: a dispatch stall now causes a supervisor rebuild instead of only a warning. Updates that PTB already acknowledged but never dispatched are dropped by the rebuild. Before, they stayed stuck in the wedged queue anyway.
- Behaviour change: the stall threshold goes from 2 to 4 heartbeats (180s → 360s), so detection is slower and slow handlers get more slack. Detection is deliberately not gated on `_inflight_update_ids`, because that would hide a handler that is itself wedged.
- `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py` was already about 7411 lines on base; this PR adds a few net lines. Moving the stall watchdogs into a sibling module would be a larger refactor and is not done here.
- `tests/plugins/test_telegram_update_admission.py` must run in its own pytest process. Run in the same process as a `tests/gateway` Telegram file, it fails with "async generator raised StopIteration". This cross-file pollution happens on base too; each file passes on its own.
- The Windows-specific trigger of the PTB stall in #130407 was not reproduced. The probe injects counters, and the recovery path does not depend on the platform.
- #71240 (draft, conflicting) overlaps this PR and can be closed as superseded after merge.

When context compaction prunes a `write_file` call that was refused (stale-write guard, protected path, I/O error), its stub now reads `[write_file] a.md FAILED: <error>` instead of `[write_file] wrote to a.md (N lines)`, so the agent no longer reports a change that never landed.

Fixes #131244

## What happened
`_sum_write_file` in `agent/context_compressor.py` built its stub from the call's arguments only. It never looked at the result. A write that the stale-write guard refused (`{"error": "Refusing to overwrite ...", "stale_write_blocked": true}`), or any other `write_file` error, was compressed into the same "wrote to PATH (N lines)" stub as a successful write. After compaction the agent read that stub as fact and told the user the file had been changed. #132141 (merged) fixed the same problem for the templated stubs, including `patch`, through the shared `_result_failure_suffix`. `write_file` has its own summarizer, so it was still affected.

## Change
- `agent/context_compressor.py`: `_sum_write_file` checks `_result_failure_suffix(content)` first. When the result carries an `error` (or `success: false`), it returns `[write_file] <path> FAILED: <bounded preview>`, which matches the other marked stubs. Success payloads and non-JSON results still produce the existing "wrote to … (N lines)" stub. The change is +4 lines and adds no new helper.
- `tests/agent/test_context_compressor.py`: adds two rows to the existing `TestSummarizeToolResultOutcome` tables. A stale-write refusal row in `test_failed_call_stub_is_marked_failed` asserts the FAILED stub. A successful write row in the success table pins the unchanged "wrote to" stub.

## Credit
- @dskwe (Yuan Li) found this and was the first to submit a fix for #131244, in #131247 (06:08 UTC). Their `write_file` fix is applied as 8519e9467d with authorship kept (Yuan Li; the email is already in `contributors/emails`). It was not a plain cherry-pick. #131247 also added a `_sum_patch`, a new `_tool_result_failure_suffix` helper and a `patch` map change, and #132141 already covers all three. Bringing them in would have duplicated a helper and conflicted with the merged map line, so only the `write_file` hunk was carried over. The contributor's three tests were reduced to the table rows above.
- @kshitijk4poor added one follow-up commit, 2aedb56566. It renders the refusal through #132141's `_result_failure_suffix` instead of an inline preview, and folds the tests into the existing outcome tables.

## Verification
- `tests/agent/test_context_compressor.py`: 294 passed on head 2aedb56566 (isolated copy).
- Red on base: the new refusal row fails with the base `context_compressor.py`, which returns `[write_file] wrote to a.md (2 lines)`. The success row passes on both base and head.
- Probe: a real `_stale_write_refusal` payload plus I/O-error and `success: false` payloads.
  - Base: all three produce `[write_file] wrote to a.md (2 lines)`.
  - Head: each produces `[write_file] a.md FAILED: …`.
  - Benign payloads (`{"bytes_written": 5}`, `"error": null`, non-JSON text) give the same "wrote to" stub on base and head.
- Mutation, run against `TestSummarizeToolResultOutcome` (18 tests):
  - Reverting 8519e9467d turns the `write_file` failed row red (1 failed / 17 passed).
  - Reverting 2aedb56566 also turns that row red, because the expected format changes.
  - With both restored, 18 passed.
- `ruff` F401/F811/F821, `git diff --check` and the Windows footgun check are clean.
- Reviewed in 1 round: regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, and tests/probe/mutation. All five approved with no findings.

## Maintainer notes
- Every refusal path in `write_file_tool` that we checked puts a top-level `error` in its payload: the sensitive, binary, protected, approval, cross-profile and internal-content guards (all through `tool_error`), the stale guard, I/O errors and exceptions. All of these now produce the FAILED stub. A refusal payload without `error` would still read "wrote to", but we found no code path that produces one.
- This stub only changes text written at compaction time. The system prompt, toolsets and config are not touched.
- The contributor's `patch` half was dropped on purpose because #132141 already covers it, so #131247 is closed as salvaged here and not merged.

items.body:
On Windows and Linux, closing the last desktop window now quits the app even while a hidden helper window (Quick Entry, HUD, pet overlay) is still alive. A second launch now restores and focuses a minimized or tray-hidden window instead of doing nothing.

Fixes #130810

## What happened
On Windows and Linux the only `app.quit()` for a window close lives in `window-all-closed`. `registerChatWindow`'s `closed` handler only removed the window from `chatWindows`. Any hidden helper `BrowserWindow` blocks `window-all-closed` from firing, for example Quick Entry, which hides on blur instead of closing. When that happened the process kept running with no UI and kept holding the single-instance lock. A relaunch then went to the `second-instance` handler, which called `restore()`/`focus()` but never `show()`, so a tray-hidden window stayed invisible. Separately, `shouldFocusToTakeKeyboard` destructured `{ isFocused }` and called it without its receiver. On a real Electron `BrowserWindow` that throws `TypeError: Object has been destroyed`. This bug has been latent on main since #83998.

## Change
- `apps/desktop/electron/main-window-lifecycle.ts`:
  - New `shouldQuitOnLastChatClosed`: a single boolean expression that is true only off macOS, with no handoff in progress, no quit already in progress, and zero remaining surfaces.
  - New `activateWindow`: restore if minimized → show if hidden → focus if not focused (through `shouldFocusToTakeKeyboard`). It is a no-op for a missing or destroyed window.
- `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts`:
  - New `quitIfNoSurfaceLeft()` counts `chatWindows.size + browserWindows.size`. It runs from `registerChatWindow`'s `closed` handler and, deferred with `setImmediate`, from `spawnBrowserWindow`'s `closed` handler. The deferral is needed because the browser registry deletes its entry in a listener that is attached after the factory returns.
  - New `quitInProgress` latch. It is set in `before-quit` and cleared next to `appQuitting` when a re-entered quit is held ("Keep Running").
  - The primary window's `close` handler returns early on `event.defaultPrevented` (tray absorb, active-work guard), so a prevented close does not latch a quit.
  - The `second-instance`, tray restore and dock `activate` paths go through `ensureMainWindow(focusWindow: activateWindow)`. The `second-instance` path adds one `rememberLog('[second-instance] relaunch (deepLink=…)')` line so relaunches show up in desktop.log.
  - `handleDeepLink`'s live-window branch calls `activateWindow`. The close-preview branch keeps its unconditional `focus()` (#83998) and gains a `show()` for tray-hidden windows.
- `apps/desktop/electron/window-focus-policy.ts`: `shouldFocusToTakeKeyboard` calls `window.isFocused()` on the receiver instead of destructuring it. This fixes `activateWindow` and both `focusWindow` call sites in `main.ts` without touching the call sites.
- `apps/desktop/electron/main-window-lifecycle.test.ts`: two tests. One is a table-driven `shouldQuitOnLastChatClosed` matrix. The other drives `activateWindow` against a `class FakeWindow` whose methods read `this`, so the test fails if `isFocused` is destructured again. The 4 existing `ensureMainWindow` tests are unchanged.

## Credit
- @JerryLiu369 opened #130835, the first and only PR for #130810. It added the last-chat-window quit fallback, the `quitInProgress` gate and the show+focus restore. Both commits were cherry-picked with `-x` and authorship kept: 941845f8eb (from 14711fc196) and 62c463bbed (from ec53f082ba). @ehz0ah had approved its final head.
- @kshitijk4poor added seven follow-up commits:
  - aca8c1461e: `second-instance` now reuses `ensureMainWindow` in place of a re-implemented `decideSecondInstanceAction`. Inlined the `window-all-closed` condition again. Removed the try/catch blocks and `typeof` probes in `activateWindow`. Fixed a typo.
  - 663abd3045: trimmed the PR's 8 tests to the two invariants. Two of the dropped tests rebuilt `main.ts` state locally and then asserted it.
  - 2237854bf2: clear `quitInProgress` when a re-entered quit is held, so a later close still quits.
  - 0cb56f85a1: count open Browser pop-outs as surfaces, so closing the primary no longer kills a pop-out.
  - cc6b734cc0: route the deep-link live-window branch through `activateWindow`, and give the #83998 focus rule a single owner.
  - 2ea493de58: run the fallback when the last Browser pop-out closes after the primary is already gone.
  - fcc2129177: call `isFocused` on its receiver (the latent #83998 `TypeError`).
- The contributor email is already in `contributors/emails`, so no map commit was needed.

## Verification
- Tests (vitest, `apps/desktop`):
  - Gate run on the pre-rebase head: `main-window-lifecycle.test.ts`, `window-focus-policy.test.ts` and `session-windows.test.ts` gave 33 passed / 0 failed.
  - Re-run on the rebased head fcc2129177: 33/33.
  - On base, the two existing files gave 27/27.
  - With base `main-window-lifecycle.ts`, both kept lifecycle tests fail (`activateWindow is not a function`, `shouldQuitOnLastChatClosed is not a function`).
- Probe: real Electron 40, with `main-window-lifecycle.ts` bundled by esbuild from the tree under test.
  - Base: primary close with a hidden helper → `NO QUIT window-all-closed=false remaining=1`.
  - Head: the same scenario → `QUIT-EMITTED`, exit 0.
  - Head predicate: linux/win32 with 0 remaining → true. darwin, 1 remaining (Browser pop-out), quit in progress and handoff → false.
  - Head `activateWindow`: a hidden window ends up `visible=true`, and a null window does not throw.
- Mutation:
  - Reverting the receiver fix turns "explicit relaunch activates a minimized tray-hidden window" red.
  - Reverting 941845f8eb gives 2 red; reverting 62c463bbed gives 1 red.
  - The `main.ts` wiring commits (2237854bf2, 0cb56f85a1, 2ea493de58) have no unit-test seam. They were proven red→green with source-level probes only.
- Lint and checks: `git diff --check` is clean and the Windows footgun check is clean. ruff is N/A because only TypeScript changed. tsc was not run.
- Reviewed over 3 rounds plus a final gate (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation). The final round approved with no findings.

## Maintainer notes
- fcc2129177 also repairs a latent bug on main: since #83998, `focusWindow` and `shouldFocusToTakeKeyboard` threw `TypeError: Object has been destroyed` against a real `BrowserWindow`. Plain-object test mocks hid it. `window-focus-policy.test.ts` still uses closure mocks, but the receiver dependence is now pinned by the class-based test in `main-window-lifecycle.test.ts`.
- Not run on Windows. The probe ran on macOS with the platform passed to the predicate, so Windows-only foreground activation (`show()`/`focus()` on win32) is unverified.
- It is not proven that the reporter hit the hidden-helper path rather than a stalled `before-quit` teardown. Open #123845 (@edosulai) covers the stalled-teardown path with an `app.exit` deadline. The two are complementary, but they edit the same `app.on('before-quit')` handler, so whichever lands second needs a rebase.
- Behaviour change: on Windows/Linux, closing the last chat window quits even while helper windows are alive. Open Browser pop-outs keep the app running, and the app quits when the last one closes.
- `main.ts` is about 19.8k lines. This PR adds a net +47 there (+69/-22) and moves the decision logic into `main-window-lifecycle.ts`.
- The issue's right-click tab menu remark is a separate item and is not addressed here.

items.body:
After a rotated `/compress` (or a rotating session-hygiene compaction) in the gateway, the new session keeps the rows that were published with it, and a transient DB error no longer surfaces as "failed to persist compressed transcript" over a compression that already committed.

Refs #131756

## What happened
On rotation, `publish_compression_child()` writes the child's handoff plus any cloned foreign-tail rows (turns that landed during compression) in the same transaction that ends the parent. The gateway then rewrote that child again from the in-memory handoff with `rewrite_transcript()` → `replace_messages(active_only=False)`, at both `gateway/slash_commands_session.py` (manual `/compress`) and `gateway/run_turn.py` (hygiene). The in-memory handoff does not contain the cloned rows, so the rewrite DELETEd them. Any failure in that redundant rewrite raised a false persist error. Skipping the rewrite alone was not enough: for `/compress here N`, rotation published only head + summary and `compress_now` rejoined the kept verbatim tail in memory, so the gateway rewrite was the only thing making the tail durable. CLI/TUI/ACP never rewrite, so on those surfaces a rotated `/compress here N` already persisted only the head.

## Change
- `gateway/session_transcript.py`:
  - New `is_published_compression_child(parent, child)`. It returns True when the child row points at the parent, is a compression child, and has active messages. It looks the child up through the parent's store, because the child id is not in the routing index yet when the probe runs. Fails open (False) on any DB error so callers fall back to the old rewrite.
  - New `persist_rotated_compression_child(parent, child, messages)`: a published child is already durable; anything else gets the existing rewrite.
- `gateway/slash_commands_session.py`, `gateway/run_turn.py`: both rotation call sites call `persist_rotated_compression_child` instead of `rewrite_transcript`. One-line comment and docstring updates.
- `agent/conversation_compression.py` (`_commit_compaction`, rotation branch): when `verbatim_tail` is set, publish `rejoin_compressed_head_and_tail(compressed, verbatim_tail)` (as the in-place branch already stores it) and stamp the tail rows. The two helper imports move above the `in_place` split.
- `agent/conversation_compression_manual.py`: comment only. Stamped tail rows now also mean a rotated commit stored the tail, so `compress_now` skips its in-memory rejoin.
- `tests/gateway/test_compress_command.py`: new `test_rotated_compress_keeps_atomically_published_foreign_tail`, parametrized `main` / `fitness`. `fitness` is a multiplexed named profile backed by its own `profiles/fitness/state.db`.
- `tests/agent/test_conversation_compression_manual.py`: new `test_rotated_here_n_publishes_the_kept_exchanges`. It checks that the durable child equals `after_messages` and that the last 4 rows are the kept history.
- `contributors/emails/ned@nanobro.local`: contributor map entry.

## Credit
- @nanobro (Ned) found the destructive second rewrite and the false persist error and fixed them in #131756, which adds the published-child probe, both call-site guards and the regression test. Commit 7e023fae82 was cherry-picked as 54c6e29e26 with authorship kept. First submitter, and triage found no competing PR.
- @kshitijk4poor added follow-up commits:
  - eadb31a6aa: rotation publishes the `/compress here N` tail. Without it, skipping the rewrite lost the kept exchanges. This also fixes the latent head-only persist on CLI/TUI/ACP.
  - 0203d3bb53: the probe goes through the parent's store. Before this, under `multiplex_profiles` a named-profile child fell back to the root `state.db`, the probe returned False, and the destructive rewrite still ran.
  - bf177cdec1: one `persist_rotated_compression_child` shared by both call sites, which removes the inline duplication and a temp flag. 78a1bbc4cd: import hoist. 6e39a08185: comment wording. All three have no behaviour change.
  - a320400d5c and a81344076a: test trims. These dropped a parametrize that exercised no profile shape and a fallback test that already passed on base.
  - 9e50c227f5: contributor map.

## Verification
- Tests on the final head (clean env, no `PYTHONPATH`):
  - `test_compress_command.py`, `test_conversation_compression_manual.py`, `hermes_cli/test_partial_compress.py` and `hermes_cli/test_compress_here.py`: 42 passed.
  - `test_session_hygiene.py`, `test_hygiene_warning_lifecycle.py`, `test_session_hygiene_turnhold_adoption.py` and `test_multiplex_session_db_profile_scope.py`: 41 passed.
  - `test_compression_concurrent_sessions.py`, `hermes_cli/test_manual_compress.py`, `test_hygiene_no_commit_reason.py` and `test_codex_hygiene_compaction.py`: 24 passed.
  - Each run separately on head and base, with identical results: `test_compression_rotation_state.py` 40/40, `test_compression_persistence.py` 10/10, `test_compression_concurrent_fork.py` 48/48, `test_compression_failure_session_sync.py` 2/2.
- Red on base: `test_rotated_compress_keeps_atomically_published_foreign_tail` fails with base gateway files. `test_rotated_here_n_publishes_the_kept_exchanges` fails with base `agent/conversation_compression.py` plus the cherry-pick. Both pass on head.
- Probe: real `SessionDB` + gateway mixin, imported from each tree.
  - Base: full compress with a concurrent foreign turn leaves the child as `['[summary] compressed']`, so the cloned foreign row is deleted.
  - Head: the same case gives `['[summary] compressed', 'FOREIGN concurrent turn']`. A plain full compress is the same on both.
  - The probe's hand-built `partial-here-N` case publishes a head-only handoff and bypasses the agent, so it no longer models the real flow after eadb31a6aa. The real flow is covered by the new agent test.
- Mutation (prod files reverted per commit, then the two touched test files run):
  - 54c6e29e26 → red `[main]` + `[fitness]`.
  - eadb31a6aa → red `test_rotated_here_n_publishes_the_kept_exchanges`.
  - One-line revert of 0203d3bb53's parent-store lookup → red `[fitness]` only.
  - bf177cdec1 and 78a1bbc4cd stay green, as expected for refactors.
- `ruff` (F401/F811/F821) shows no new findings. The remaining hits are on base (`datetime` in `agent/conversation_compression.py`, `build_session_key` in `gateway/slash_commands_session.py`). `git diff --check` and the Windows footgun check are clean.
- Reviewed over 2 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation) plus a final gate. One Medium (multiplex store lookup) and four Lows were fixed in-stack.

## Maintainer notes
- The hygiene call site (`gateway/run_turn.py`) has no test of its own. It calls the same `persist_rotated_compression_child` as the tested manual `/compress` path, and the hygiene suites stay green, but the hygiene rotation flow was not live-probed.
- The multiplexed named-profile case is covered only by the `fitness` row of the gateway test.
- Behaviour change: a rotated child that is published and verified is no longer rewritten from memory. When the probe can't confirm publication (no compression child row, no active messages, or a DB error), the old rewrite still runs, unchanged.
- `is_published_compression_child` calls the private `SessionDB._is_compression_child_row`, as other gateway code in the same module family already does.
- Overlap: our merged #130523 changed the same rotation branch of `_commit_compaction`. This branch is rebased on it and the conflict is resolved.
- File sizes: `agent/conversation_compression.py` (~4.3k lines) and `gateway/run_turn.py` (~4.4k lines) were already over 2000 lines. This stack adds only a few net lines to each.

items.body:
When compaction restates a request that is still in progress, the transcript now holds one active row for it instead of two rows sharing the same `message_uid`, and the compacted window still opens on a user turn.

Refs #131104

## What happened
`ContextCompressor._reappend_inflight_user_task` appends a `[STILL IN PROGRESS]` replay of the in-flight user request after compaction. When that request was the first user row in the protected head, the original row survived as well. The durable transcript then had two active rows with the same `message_uid`, and the request rendered twice after reload (#131104, reported by @Lee-Shon on 2026-10-02). Removing the original row (the contributor fix) exposed a second problem. The summary role had already been chosen against a head that ended on that user row, so the window could open `system → assistant(tool_calls) → tool → assistant summary`. Strict-alternation chat templates reject that sequence, and native Gemini rejects a leading model `functionCall` turn.

## Change
- `agent/context_compressor.py` (`_reappend_inflight_user_task`, +40/-2):
  - When the replay has a `message_uid`, user rows other than the carrier that carry the same uid are dropped from the compacted window. This uses `message_uid_or_none` and `MESSAGE_UID`. The existing lazy `message_metadata` import is moved up so that `record_absorbed_message` is covered by it too.
  - If a row was removed and the first non-system row is no longer `user`, the standalone summary carrier moves to that position.
  - If the carrier is itself a merged tail `assistant(tool_calls)` row (`_template_visible_role(carrier) is None`), the pre-dedup list is restored for this cycle. Moving that row would split it from its tool results.
  - If an assistant carrier has no visible user turn before it after the removal, it switches to the existing `_force_user_leading` layout: carrier `role=user`, with the request merged after `_SUMMARY_END_MARKER`. The merge path records the uid as absorbed, so the uid still belongs to one row.
- `tests/agent/test_cron_inflight_prompt_reappend.py` (+52): the contributor's `test_replay_replaces_surviving_user_row_with_same_message_uid` is extended and no new test function is added. The test now checks:
  - exactly one holder per uid, counting `ABSORBED_MESSAGE_UIDS`;
  - after a real `compress()` on a head-protected uid row, the raw `compressed[1]["role"] == "user"`, strict alternation holds, and the request appears after the end marker;
  - for a merged-tail tool-call carrier, the window still opens on a user row and each `tool_calls` row is immediately followed by its tool results.

## Credit
- @dskwe (Yuan Li) wrote the uid-matched removal and its regression test in #131110. That was the first and only PR for this issue (opened 2026-10-02). Commit ff89a5cf8c was cherry-picked with authorship kept (`-x 581719d1da`). Their contributor-map entry was already on main.
- @Lee-Shon reported #131104.
- @kshitijk4poor added follow-up commits after review:
  - b6e18ac0dd: when the removal leaves no user turn before the carrier, use the user-leading layout. Carries `Co-authored-by: Yuan Li`.
  - b5039e6a3e: move the carrier to the window opening so a leading tool-call row cannot be first (Gemini).
  - 69769365d0: do not move a merged tail tool-call carrier, so its tool pairing stays intact.
  - 2af1339013 and 0b37f4ca4c: behaviour-neutral refactors (`!= "user"`, `message_uid_or_none` / `MESSAGE_UID`).
  - 991506dc5e: the test uses `ABSORBED_MESSAGE_UIDS` and `_template_visible_role` instead of copies.

## Verification
- Tests were run on the head in a clean archive copy:
  - `test_cron_inflight_prompt_reappend.py`, `test_context_engine_message_uid.py`, `test_context_compressor_zero_user_provenance.py` and `test_summary_role_template_alternation.py`: 55 passed.
  - `test_context_compressor.py`: 276 passed.
- Red on base: the kept test fails with base `context_compressor.py`, and it also fails with the contributor-only prod file (before the follow-ups). It passes on head.
- Probe: real `compress()` on the head-protected in-flight shape.
  - Base: `DUP_UIDS={'U1': 2}`.
  - Head: `DUP_UIDS={}`, first non-system role `user`, Gemini's first content is `user`, alternation OK.
  - Three benign shapes (completed turn, newer user in the tail, legacy row without a uid) give the same output on base and head.
  - Merged-tail tool-call carrier shapes give row-for-row the same output as base, with pairing intact.
- Mutation: reverting any one of the four behaviour commits (ff89a5cf8c, b6e18ac0dd, b5039e6a3e, 69769365d0) turns the kept test red. The three refactor/test-only commits are behaviour-neutral.
- `ruff` (F401/F811/F821), `git diff --check` and the Windows footgun check are clean.
- Reviewed over 4 rounds (regression, reuse, quality, efficiency, tests/probe/mutation). Rounds 2 and 3 found the leading-tool-call (Gemini) and split-pairing issues, which are fixed above. Round 4 approved with no findings.

## Maintainer notes
- Trade-off: when the summary is merged into a tail `assistant(tool_calls)` row, the dedup is skipped for that compaction. The output is identical to base for that shape: the duplicate uid remains, tool pairing is intact, and the window opens on a user row. The duplicate is cleaned up on a later compaction, once the carrier is a standalone row.
- Unverified rare shape: a merged carrier that is an assistant *text* row (no tool_calls) at the same time as a removed head row. In that case the move-and-flip would make that row `role=user`, putting the prior assistant narration, still framed as `[PRIOR CONTEXT — for reference …]`, into a user row. Three real-compress sweeps (budgets 60–3000, protect_first_n 2/3/4) never produced that shape. Every merged carrier was the tool-call row, which the restore branch covers. Calling the function directly on that shape keeps alternation and pairing valid.
- Gemini: the leading model `functionCall` turn is fixed for the standalone carrier (b5039e6a3e). The Gemini 400 itself is based on the documented turn-order rule; no live API call was made.
- Scope: the second half of #131104 is not addressed here. That half is the model echoing the `[PRIOR CONTEXT — for reference only; not a new message]` frame of a merged carrier, i.e. the "re-delivers the previous reply" behaviour. On the DB side it is already correct (old row inactive, carrier active), so this PR uses `Refs`. It is recommended to track it separately with the merged-carrier frame work.
- Not changed: `agent/conversation_compression.py` `_ensure_compressed_has_user_turn` copies a user row while keeping its `message_uid`, which is the same class of bug. It is not reached when a real user row is present or when the merged replay is recognised.
- `agent/context_compressor.py` is about 5.8k lines; this PR adds 40.
- No overlap with other open compaction PRs: #130672 and #130523 do not touch `_reappend_inflight_user_task`.
