items.body:
Renaming a session to a title held by an abandoned empty session (ended, no messages, visible, not archived) now works, and so does creating a session with that title through `POST /api/sessions`: the ghost gives the title up in the same transaction, so the user no longer hits "Title 'X' is already in use by session <id>" for a session they can't see.

Refs #81888. That issue is a session-management UX umbrella (dual state.db, ghost clutter, profile grouping). This PR fixes only the title-blocking part.

## Changes
- `hermes_state_titles.py::_set_session_title`: the conflict lookup now also computes `_EMPTY_SESSION_WHERE`, the same predicate `count_empty_sessions` / `delete_empty_sessions` use (ended, `message_count = 0`, no rows in `messages`, not archived). If the conflicting holder matches it and isn't hidden, its `title`/`title_source` are cleared inside the existing CAS write transaction. This is the same mechanism the retired archived Bot Chat branch already uses.
- The full `idx_sessions_title_unique` index is unchanged. There is no schema or index migration.
- The conflict block now lives in `SessionTitlesMixin._resolve_title_conflict(conn, session_id, title)` (moved verbatim) and `gateway/platforms/api_server.py::_handle_create_session` calls it on the same connection instead of its own `SELECT ... WHERE title = ?`, so create-with-title and rename follow one rule. On conflict the inserted row is still deleted and the response is still 400 `invalid_title`.
- Test: `TestSessionTitle::test_title_conflict_yields_only_to_ended_empty_visible_holder`, parametrized over 4 holder states. Only the ended visible ghost yields; a live empty session, a hidden one, and a real one each keep the title. After the rename, the old ghost can still be appended to. The existing `test_create_session_respects_browser_source_and_model_lock` is extended: create-with-title over a ghost → 201, over a live holder → 400 with no stray row.

## Credit
@AbhijatSaxena's commit `a28e084278` is cherry-picked with `-x`, authorship kept. A mapping commit adds their email to `contributors/emails/`. The contributor's `hermes_state_schema.py` hunk was dropped on conflict because main had since rewritten `_ensure_unique_title_index` (#132258). The follow-up commit then replaces the PR's `message_count > 0` filter.

## Validation
| Check | origin/main base | PR as submitted | head |
|---|---|---|---|
| Probe: rename real session to an ended ghost's title | `ValueError: already in use` | `IntegrityError: UNIQUE constraint failed` (conflict check skipped, full index still fires) | succeeds; ghost title cleared; `resolve_session_by_title` returns the real session |
| Probe: ghost gets its first message after losing the title | — | partial index: `IntegrityError` on `append_message` | append ok |
| New test (4 cases) | 1 failed / 3 passed | 3 failed (IntegrityError) / 1 passed | 4 passed |
| `tests/hermes_state/` + 41 files touching title APIs (`-n 8`) | 74 failed / 2631 passed | — | 73 failed / 2636 passed; no failure exists only on head (all reds are present on base: SQLite 3.46 WAL/repair env, plus 1 tui flake that passed on head) |

Independent review (2 rounds: correctness, tests/probe/mutation, reuse, quality, efficiency) approved. Round 2 probe, API create: ghost → 201 (base 400); live, with-message, hidden ghost, live hidden Bot Chat → 400 with no new row (same as base); no holder → 201.

Mutations on head, each caught by a kept test:
- Revert the api_server change: the extended create test goes red.
- Revert to base titles: `[ghost]` goes red.
- Drop the `not hidden` guard: `[hidden]` goes red.
- Replace `_EMPTY_SESSION_WHERE` with `message_count = 0`: `[live-empty]` goes red.

`ruff`, `git diff --check` and `check-windows-footguns.py` all pass.

## Maintainer notes
- **Why the PR's partial index was not kept.** `UNIQUE(title) WHERE message_count > 0` permits a ghost and a real session to share a title. When the ghost later receives a message, `append_message` increments its `message_count`, moves the row into the index, and raises `IntegrityError` mid-write, so a message write fails. Two empty sessions that share a title fail the same way. The PR as submitted also kept the full index for existing DBs (`DROP` + `CREATE` sat inside the old guarded repair path), so the rename crashed with `IntegrityError` rather than succeeding.
- **Why "ended" is required.** An early version freed the title of any empty row. In this suite that stole titles from live sessions whose `/title` lands before the first turn (CLI pending title, `/title` in the gateway, instant auto-title collisions), which broke 5 existing tests. `_EMPTY_SESSION_WHERE` already defines "empty ghost" for the empty-session sweep, so reusing it keeps the two definitions consistent.
- **Behaviour change:** an ended empty visible session silently loses its user title when someone else claims it. That session has no content and does not appear in `min_messages=1` listings.
- **API create follows the rename rules.** `POST /api/sessions` with `title: "Bot Chat"` over an archived hidden Bot Chat now succeeds and retires the old row's name (was 400), matching what rename already does (`test_deliberately_archived_canonical_chat_releases_name_for_replacement`).
- **Error wording:** the API's 400 now carries the DB's message, `Title 'X' is already in use by session Y` (was `Title already in use by session Y`). Desktop matches `/already in use/i` and `hermes peer` checks for "title", so both still match.
- Open question: the empty-session sweep (`prune_empty_ghost_sessions`) only removes untitled TUI ghosts; whether it should also cover titled or Desktop ghosts is left for a follow-up.

items.body:
Follow-up to the merged qdrant entry (#127847) — the pin moves to `b2475f7` / **0.1.7**, and the entry becomes true of what it pins.

## Why this is one PR and not two

Three admission rules bind this diff and all three are unsatisfied at the current pin, so splitting the version bump from the feature would put a known-false entry through review first:

- **Rule 13** — the merged entry discloses no reads outside the plugin's own data, which is exactly what the new `md_search` tool does.
- **Rule 14** — `requires_hermes` must be truthful and never newer than the current release.
- **Claim accuracy at the pin** — "Registers 5 tools" and "(ONNX, no torch)" are both false of 0.1.5: that release still shipped `sentence-transformers` as a hard dependency, so a default install pulled ~1.2 GB of torch.

## Rule 13 — what `md_search` actually does

- **Reads outside the plugin's own data:** `~/.hermes/skills`, the Obsidian vault at `~/Documents/hermes_default`, the hermes-agent website docs, plus any path set in the `md_docs_roots` config key. Content is indexed locally and never sent anywhere.
- **A separate collection:** `hermes_md_docs`, with its own multilingual model (`paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2`, from `huggingface.co` on first use). It carries no session scope and is never queried against memory vectors.
- **State on disk:** FTS5 index and ingest state in `<HERMES_HOME>/state/md-search/`, outside the plugin directory.
- **Per-process model copies:** the plugin registers no MCP server, but it is loaded in-process into every Hermes process that embeds, so each pays its own model copy — 211 MB for one process, ~194–197 MB marginal per additional concurrent one (5 concurrent = 1,071 MB resident, measured).

## Rule 14

`requires_hermes` `>=0.21.4` → `>=0.21.5`, the current release and the version the suite runs against.

## Claim accuracy

- **"Registers 5 tools" → 7:** `qdrant_forget` (point-targeted deletion, dry-run by default, no delete-all) and `md_search`. `capabilities.provides_tools` mirrors all 7 manifest tools.
- **"(ONNX, no torch)" → measured:** 0.1.7 moves `sentence-transformers` to an optional `gpu` extra; a clean runtime-only resolve is **206 MB with zero torch/nvidia/triton**, against ~1.2 GB when it was a hard dependency.
- **`known_issues` gains the installer's surprise:** `md_search` reports "no markdown index yet" until `scripts/md_ingest.py` is run once. Nothing does that for you.

## What is preserved

Every disclosure line teknium1 wrote at the merge of #127847 is kept **verbatim** — including the `storage.googleapis.com/qdrant-fastembed` fallback and the `or qdrant.json` wording on the API key. The diff is one file.

## Verified at the pinned SHA (`b2475f7`, detached checkout)

- `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` — passes; structural validator `OK: 1 file(s) valid`; self-updater grep empty
- 210 tests pass / 8 skipped · ruff 0 findings · mutation check 18/18 · docs-honesty gate clean
- Every entry claim re-derived from the **remote** tree at the pin (declared version, the 7 tool schemas, manifest tool list, `sentence-transformers` under `optional-dependencies`, no torch in runtime deps)

Scope: one file, 8 insertions / 5 deletions.

— k

Anonymous guest Portal users get free managed Perplexity fast search again. That was the point of #130121 (@rewbs).

**Who / when / why:** #130121 opened it to every Nous identity. Our salvage, #130660 (commit `cee3000c24`, kshitijk4poor, 2026-10-01), added a `fast_search_entitled()` gate that left out the anonymous tier, because we treated #122404 / #122967 as precedent. The author says that removed the main purpose of the change. As merged, guests still use the keyless ring and never send a request to the gateway.

**Change**
- `tools/managed_tool_gateway.py`: `resolve_free_search_gateway()` decides on identity alone again, as @rewbs wrote it. The token reader still applies `nous.guest: false`, expiry refresh and dead-guest replacement.
- `tools/tool_backend_helpers.py`: removes `fast_search_entitled()` and `fast_search_unavailable_message()`. Nothing else uses them.
- `plugins/web/perplexity/provider.py`: the stored-`nous` refusal says there is no usable Nous identity.
- Docs: the autodetect row says a Nous identity, guests included.
- Tests: the anonymous identity is back in the autodetect and rescue cases. The tests that pinned the guest exclusion are removed.

- Follow-up commit, from the review and simplify pass: removes the gate's leftovers. `_account_info` is folded back into `managed_nous_tools_enabled`, and the `managed=` parameter on the Perplexity `_managed_gateway` is gone. It also moves test coverage for the tier rules we kept to the entitlement copy that uses them, so a guest whose lookup failed, or whose tier arrives as `"ANONYMOUS"`, still gets "needs a Nous account".

**Unchanged:** the case- and whitespace-insensitive `is_anonymous_tier`, the account tier on error snapshots, one route walk per dispatch, and the paid entitlement gate on every other vendor and on the billed managed-Firecrawl fallback.

**Validation**
| | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| anonymous guest, nothing configured: `POST /perplexity/search` with the guest bearer and `search_type: "fast"` | no request (keyless ring) | yes |
| guest whose fast-search call fails: keyless rescue, no `/v2/search` | red | green |

Live against production with a real minted anonymous guest: `POST https://perplexity-gateway.nousresearch.com/search` returns 200 with `search_type: "fast"`. On origin/main the same guest never calls the gateway (details in the comment below).

`scripts/run_tests.sh` across 12 web, nous and tools-config files: 276 passed. Full `tests/tools/`: every failure also fails on origin/main (matched by test ID). Mutation checks: adding the anonymous exclusion back to the resolver, dropping the tier normalization, and dropping the tier on error snapshots each turn the guard tests red. On macOS, `test_web_keyless_fallback.py` exits non-zero after all 22 tests pass. That comes from a `home_io_guard` INTERNALERROR, and it happens on origin/main too.

Scripted single-prompt CLI runs (`hermes -z`, `hermes chat -q` off a TTY, `-Q`, `--oneshot`) now report shared-metrics entrypoint `one_shot` instead of `interactive`, and `hermes -z` actually writes its `task_run.finished` / `session.count` rows, so fleet telemetry can tell humans chatting in the CLI apart from scripts.

## Infographic

![one-shot entrypoint](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aacec69/tgK97cUHZAE3m2dMD1VuP_flkt2j0i.png)

## Changes

- **New closed entrypoint `one_shot`**: added to `TASK_ENTRYPOINTS` and to the v3 package schema's `task_entrypoint` enum. `execution_surface` stays `cli`. It reaches every metric that carries `entrypoint`: `task_run.started`, `task_run.finished`, `session.count`.
- **Where it is declared**: `relay_shared_metrics._with_launch_entrypoint`, at the point the `hermes.task_run` scope opens. It only touches cli-surface tasks that carry the `HERMES_SINGLE_QUERY_SESSION` marker. The one-shot paths already set that marker (`cli_single_query.py` for `chat -q`/`-Q`/`--oneshot`/`--stream-json`, `oneshot.py` for `-z`), and the session source (`oneshot`) and `cache_ttl: auto` (#118337) already read it. No second detector was added.
- **Hermes-internal one-shot spawners** (audited):
  - kanban worker (`kanban_db_dispatch`: `chat -q` + `HERMES_SESSION_SOURCE=kanban`) → `background`
  - A2A forward (`a2a/adapter.py`: `chat -q … -Q --source a2a`) → `background`
  - Bot Chat delivery turns (`tools/bot_mode_dm`, `tui_gateway/methods_bot_relay`, the cron Bot Chat delivery: `chat -c "Bot Chat" -Q`) → `one_shot`. I did not label these `background`, because a relayed turn's author can be a person on another connection.
  - delegation uses in-process children (`parent_session_id`) and stays `delegated`. That rule still wins inside a finite run.
  - cron runs in-process as `scheduled_task` and is unchanged.
- **Why `background`**: it already exists in `TASK_ENTRYPOINTS`, and the code treats it as unattended (`_UNATTENDED_ENTRYPOINTS`, not engaged). That matches "a Hermes dispatcher spawned this and nobody is at the keyboard". `delegated` would be wrong because there is no parent task.
- **`hermes -z` exit flush**: `-z` leaves through `os._exit`, which skips the atexit hook that closes the metrics session. Before this change only `task_run.started` survived, and the store was left with a hot `-journal`. `_ONESHOT_CLEANUPS` now calls the new `relay_shared_metrics.shutdown_runtimes()`.
- Docs: `relay-shared-metrics.md` gains the entrypoint vocabulary table, including what `one_shot` and `background` mean.
- The relay smoke drives `chat --query … --quiet` (a one-shot run), so its three expected `entrypoint` values move from `interactive` to `one_shot`.

## How each entrypoint-keyed derivation treats the new values

| Derived set | `one_shot` | `background` (kanban/A2A children) |
|---|---|---|
| `shared_metrics_engagement._ENGAGED_ENTRYPOINTS` | added → same as before (counted as engagement, like `interactive`) | not engaged (was engaged while mislabelled `interactive`) |
| `shared_metrics_model.attended()` (task cost, session tool usage, friction) | attended → same as before | unattended (was attended) |
| session summary `!= "delegated"` | counted → same | counted → same |
| milestones (`first_scheduled_task` only keys on entrypoint) | unchanged | unchanged |

`one_shot` keeps today's treatment on purpose. Inside the process, a person typing `hermes -z` looks the same as a script looping it, so the label lets the rollup split the two instead of the client guessing. Kanban workers and A2A forwards are Hermes machinery, not a person, so dropping them from engagement and attended-only rows is the correct consequence of `background`. All of their `task_run.*`, `session.count` and model/tool rows are still recorded.

Consent copy: unchanged. This adds no new data category, only a new value in an existing closed dimension.

## Live repro (real `hermes` processes, OpenRouter `google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite`, rows read from each run's `metrics.sqlite3`)

| Run | origin/main `3c9847f5e86` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `hermes -z "Reply with exactly: pong"` | `task_run.started {entrypoint: interactive, surface: cli}` only; **no `task_run.finished`, no `session.count`**, hot `metrics.sqlite3-journal` left behind | `task_run.started {entrypoint: one_shot, cli}`, `task_run.finished {end_reason: completed, entrypoint: one_shot, outcome: success}`, `session.count {entrypoint: one_shot, surface: cli, turn_count_bucket: 1}` |
| `hermes chat -Q -q "…"` | `task_run.started/finished` and `session.count` with `entrypoint: interactive` | same rows with `entrypoint: one_shot` |
| `HERMES_SESSION_SOURCE=kanban hermes chat -q "…"` (non-TTY, the worker's env stamp) | `interactive` | `task_run.*` + `session.count` with `entrypoint: background` |
| interactive PTY `hermes`, 2 turns, `/exit` | `task_run.started` ×2, `task_run.finished` ×2, `session.count {entrypoint: interactive, turn_count_bucket: 2, model_call_count_bucket: 2}` | identical |

Relay smoke (`scripts/smoke_nemo_relay_shared_metrics.py`, stripped env, fake provider): passes. Its packaged `task_run.*` rows carry `one_shot` and validate against the v3 schema.

## Root cause

`_SURFACE_ENTRYPOINTS` maps the `cli` surface straight to `interactive`, and no production caller declares an `entrypoint`. Separately, the `-z` hard exit skipped the atexit flush that writes the terminal rows.

## Tests

- `test_finite_cli_runs_report_their_own_entrypoint` checks: REPL → `interactive`; marker → `one_shot`; marker + kanban source → `background`; a delegated child inside a finite run → `delegated`; a Desktop task → `interactive`. It covers `task_run.started/finished` and `session.count`.
- `test_oneshot_hard_exit_cleanup_records_the_session_summary`: the `-z` pre-exit cleanup writes `session.count {one_shot}`.
- Both tests fail when the touched source files are swapped back to `origin/main` copies. The second test also fails with only `hermes_cli/main.py` reverted.
- Existing assertions: none weakened. The only edited expectations are the smoke's three `entrypoint` values, which changed because the smoke runs a one-shot `chat --query --quiet`. The schema/contract parity test (`set(enum) == TASK_ENTRYPOINTS`) now covers `one_shot`. Rows from before this change (`interactive`) are still in the enum and still validate.

TUI and Desktop `/save` (the tui_gateway `session.save` RPC) now write the stored session like CLI and messaging `/save json` do: turns that in-place compaction archived are kept, rows removed by undo/rewind stay out, and `sessions.max_export_messages` applies.

Refs #130339

## Changes
- `hermes_cli/session_export.py`: new `load_save_snapshot(db, session_id, fmt)`, extracted from the CLI and messaging `/save` call sites. It runs the cap check, the export projection and the undone-row filter. CLI (`cli_session_mixin.py`) and messaging (`gateway/slash_commands_session.py`, one `asyncio.to_thread` hop) now call it, so all three surfaces share one code path.
- `tui_gateway/methods_session.py` `session.save`:
  - Reads the session's own profile `state.db` under that profile's config, so a secondary profile's `max_export_messages` is the one that applies.
  - Reads the row the live agent writes to (`_submit_row_target_key`), so a compression rotation doesn't export the stale parent.
  - Writes the canonical export shape.
  - Refuses an oversized session with RPC error `4131` and the same message as the CLI.
  - Falls back to the in-memory history (old shape) only when no stored row exists or the read fails. The handler has no net line growth.
- `tui_gateway/compute_host.py`: turn-isolated sessions already ran this same handler on the host. The host now forwards the handler's error `code` in `control.error` (only when one is set, so codeless frames are unchanged), and the parent passes it through for `session.save`, so the refusal arrives as `4131` and not the generic `5011`.
- When a session has no stored row, the in-memory fallback now writes the same importable shape (`id`, `model`, `started_at`, `system_prompt`, `messages`) instead of the legacy keys.
- `session.save` runs on the RPC worker pool (`_LONG_HANDLERS`): a save at the default 20k-row cap took 0.77 s, which would otherwise block the reader thread.
- `tui_gateway/server.py`: `session.save` moves to `_LONG_HANDLERS` (the RPC pool). A save at the default cap is a full read plus render, about 0.8 s for 20k rows, and that should not stall the reader thread.
- Docs: `user-guide/sessions.md` now says the `/save json` and `max_export_messages` text covers TUI and Desktop, and documents `4131`.

## Validation
Independent review: 2 rounds (correctness, tests/probe/mutation, reuse, quality, efficiency); round 2 approved with no findings.

| Check | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `test_save_json_restores_compacted_history_as_archived[tui / tui-compute-host / tui-profile]` | red | green |
| Live probe: compacted store, a rewound row → TUI `session.save` | 2 rows, 0/5 archived answers, no `timings` | 13 rows, 5/5 archived answers, undone row absent, `timings` present |
| Live probe: `max_export_messages: 5` (launch profile / secondary profile) | file written / file written | RPC error `4131` / `4131` |
| No stored row (in-memory fallback) | legacy keys, not importable ("session id is required") | `{id, model, started_at, system_prompt, messages}`, imports; same `id` as the DB path |
| Mutations (prod file reverted per commit) | n/a | DB export → 3 red; fallback shape → 1 red; profile scope removed → 1 red; `session.save` dropped from the RPC pool → 1 red |
| `test_tui_gateway_server.py` (own process, ×2 per tree) | 669 passed | 669 passed |
| save/export, compute-host (7 files), protocol + export formats | — | 28 / 36 (2 skipped) / 82 passed, 0 failed |

`ruff`, `git diff --check`, and `check-windows-footguns.py --all` are clean.

## Maintainer notes
- The TUI/Desktop JSON file changes shape. It used to be `{model, session_id, session_start, system_prompt, messages}`; it is now the canonical session export that CLI `/save json` writes since #132211 (`id`, `started_at`, `title`, `system_prompt`, every stored row with `active`/`compacted` flags, `timings`). The dashboard import accepts it. The RPC result (`{file}`) is unchanged.
- #117292 (TUI/Desktop `/save md|html [filename] [redact]`) is orthogonal in behaviour, but both PRs rewrite the same handler body, so whichever lands second needs a rebase. On top of this branch it would pass `fmt` to `load_save_snapshot` and apply `redact_session_data` after it, the same as the CLI.
- #125242 (save under the session's profile) already landed on main via a salvage. This branch keeps that behaviour, and the profile tests pass.
- #61338 (title in `/save` JSON): the DB export already carries the session's stored `title`, so TUI/Desktop snapshots now include it. That PR's generate-a-title-when-missing fallback is not covered here.

items.body:
Auxiliary model calls (titles, compression, vision, ...) now report their real outcome in shared metrics. Failures carry the classifier's `error_class`, Hermes' own aborts count as `cancelled` instead of `failed`, and title generations that finish beside the turn get counted.

Fleet data (Sep 28 - Oct 2): 12,756 of ~46k aux route rows were `failed`, and every one had `error_class=unknown`. Primary calls in the same window fail 0.6-1.1% and are classified.

## Root cause
Three bugs in how aux calls are recorded:
1. **No error class.** The aux logical scope only carried `outcome/model/provider`, and the contract projection hard-coded `unknown` for every non-success (`shared_metrics_contract._auxiliary_model_call_dimensions`).
2. **Aborts counted as failures.** `_relay_aux_call_scope` recorded every `BaseException` leaving `call_llm` as `failed`, including Ctrl+C or `/stop` during compression (`AuxiliaryExplicitCancellation`), `InterruptedError` from interrupted aux streams, `KeyboardInterrupt`, and `CancelledError`.
3. **Title generations dropped.** Title generation runs beside the turn. When it finished, the turn's own scopes were above its logical scope, so `pop_relay_scope_if_top` skipped it. The turn-close drain then closed it as an orphan with no route, so no row was written. Because this mostly drops successful titles, the failure share looked worse than it is.

## Changes
- New `agent/auxiliary_call_outcome.py` (kept out of the 8k-line `auxiliary_client.py` facade):
  - classifies an aux error with `agent.error_classifier.classify_api_error`. An HTTP-200 body carrying a provider `error` object (aggregators relay upstream failures this way) is classified from that object.
  - defines what counts as a Hermes abort: any non-`Exception` BaseException, or `InterruptedError`.
- `auxiliary_client`:
  - the terminal error's class rides on `complete_logical_call`.
  - each failed attempt (transport errors in `_relay_sync/async_completion`, invalid-shape responses in `_validate_llm_response`) is noted, so a recovered success reports the last error it recovered from, the same as primary calls.
  - aborts close as `cancelled`.
  - the invalid-response `RuntimeError` keeps its message and type, so the recovery ladder routes it exactly as before.
- `relay_llm`:
  - `complete_logical_call` / `_complete_logical` take `error_class`.
  - MoA aggregator streams (`ManagedLlmStream`) classify the same way.
  - a scope that can't be popped yet hands its real output to the runtime.
- `relay_runtime`: `RelayRuntime.defer_scope_output`. The orphan drain closes a deferred scope with its stored result instead of `{"outcome":"cancelled","hermes.orphan_drain":true}`.
- Contract projection reads the optional `error_class`. `cancelled` → `none`, and `failed` with no class → `unknown`, as the doc already specified. Older rows without the field still project the same way. No new vocabulary and no schema change, because `error_class` is already a `model_route` dimension.
- Docs: `relay-shared-metrics.md` now describes aux semantics.

TTFT: left as `unknown` for aux rows. Most aux calls aren't streamed, and the only cheap signal (the aux "first progress" hook) can't tell a first chunk from a whole response. Faking a bucket would mislead.

## Live repro
Real `hermes chat -q` processes, OpenRouter, isolated `HERMES_HOME`. Rows come from each run's own `counter_aggregates`. Base = detached `origin/main` 3c9847f5e; fix = this branch. Primary rows were identical in every pair and are left out of the table.

| Scenario | origin/main aux row | this branch aux row |
|---|---|---|
| Title generation, healthy model (`gemini-3.5-flash-lite`) | *(no aux row)* | `auxiliary success none` ×1 |
| Title generation pointed at `openai/hermes-no-such-model-zz` | *(no aux row)* | `auxiliary failed model_not_found` ×1 |
| Compression pointed at `deepseek/hermes-no-such-model-zz` (2 preflight compressions) | `auxiliary failed unknown` ×2 | `auxiliary failed model_not_found` ×2 |
| Ctrl+C (SIGINT) 6 s into an in-flight compression call (`deepseek-v4.1-flash`) | `auxiliary failed unknown` ×1 | `auxiliary cancelled none` ×1 |
| Healthy compression (2 calls) | — | `auxiliary success none` ×2 |

For the Ctrl+C run, the log shows `Interrupt requested (hard): explicit stop requested` → `Turn ended: reason=interrupted_by_user`.

## Tests
`tests/agent/test_auxiliary_relay.py`. All new tests run through a real Relay turn and a real `SharedMetricsSubscriber`/`SharedMetricsStore`:
- `test_auxiliary_model_routes_carry_classified_error_class`: a 404 failure records `failed/model_not_found`; a 429 followed by success records `success/rate_limit`. On base: `failed/unknown`, `success/none`.
- `test_aborted_auxiliary_call_is_cancelled_not_failed[explicit-cancel, InterruptedError, KeyboardInterrupt]` records `cancelled/none`. On base: `failed/unknown`.
- `test_auxiliary_call_finishing_under_the_turns_live_scope_is_counted` records `success/none`. On base: no row.
- Updated the existing exact-dict expectations so the outputs carry `error_class`. A fallback that recovers from an unclassifiable invalid shape now reports `success/unknown` (the recovered error) instead of `none`. Each test keeps its original invariant: one logical call, one terminal route.

Gates: `ruff check` on touched files, `check-windows-footguns.py --all`, `check_no_tmp_literals.py`, `git diff --check`, `scripts/run_tests.sh` on the relay/aux/shared-metrics/error-classifier files. The 8 failures in that run fail the same way on origin/main: they come from the worktree-under-`~/.hermes` guard and the local env.

## Infographic
![aux-call-telemetry](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aacecbc/ZfDZSaPNTMV8xax6Mx7D2_kXk1GEJH.png)

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Killing a `use_pty=True` background process hung forever when one of its descendants `setsid()`s and keeps the PTY slave open. This PR fixes that hang.

`kill_process` → `_move_to_finished` → `_release_finished_handles` called `session._pty.close()`. ptyprocess wraps the master in an `io.BufferedRWPair`, and the PTY reader thread sits in `read1()` holding that object's buffer lock. That read only ends (EIO) once every holder of the slave side is gone, and a detached descendant outlives the kill. So `close()` waited until the escapee exited, which for a long-lived one is forever.

How things get stuck (details in the issue):
- The `process` kill tool call never returns, so its turn hangs. A stop abandons the call, but the worker thread stays blocked.
- The process session never completes: no completion event, no notification.
- After the finished-TTL, `_prune_if_needed` repeats the same blocking close while holding `ProcessRegistry._lock`, which wedges every registry user.
- With `telemetry.shared_metrics` enabled on a build without #131683, every finished turn in the process waited on this tool call through `subscribers.flush()`. Sessions stayed "running" forever, and stop and the turn watchdog could not clear them.

### The fixes

- **No close under a live reader:** on POSIX, `_release_finished_handles` leaves the PTY close to the reader while it is alive and isn't the calling thread. The reader's own teardown (`_finish_reader` → `_finish_exited` → `_move_to_finished` → `_release_finished_handles`, on the reader thread) closes the PTY once its read ends, so the master FD is still released. It's held only until the reader's read ends, the same trade-off #114597 makes for Windows pipes. pywinpty reads don't block, so on Windows the PTY closes on the finish path exactly as on `main`.
- **Killed output stays frozen:** while the reader outlives a kill, it keeps draining the PTY but no longer appends to or streams into the killed session. The reader admits each chunk with `ProcessSession.append_output_if_running()`, which checks `exited` and appends under the same session lock the kill holds while it snapshots the output and sets `exited`. So a chunk is either in the kill's receipt or dropped, including one the reader had already read when the kill ran. Only the kill sets `exited` on a PTY session while its reader is alive, so a normal exit's final output is unaffected. The pipe reader is unchanged.

### Not in this PR: reaping the escapee on a dashboard / serve backend

The issue's second half is that a supervised `hermes dashboard` / `hermes serve` backend gives its background processes no systemd scope, so the kill can't reach a `setsid()` escapee. An earlier revision of this PR scoped them. Review showed that this moved them out of the backend's service cgroup, so they survived a backend restart. Nothing in dashboard/serve startup recovers the process checkpoint, though, so they kept running while process list/poll/kill could not find them, and the next spawn dropped their checkpoint record. On `main` they die with the backend.

Recovering them in serve would make serve a second owner of the profile's `processes.json`, which conflicts with #106742 making the gateway the only session runtime (the gateway and managed workers adopt from that checkpoint). So that part is removed and dashboard/serve behaves as on `main`. The escapee cleanup belongs with the serve-to-gateway cutover, where the gateway already has per-process scopes and startup recovery.

Without a scope the kill still returns promptly, and the PTY is released when the escapee exits.

## Related Issue

Part of #132358 (the kill hang; the dashboard/serve escapee cleanup is left to the #106742 follow-up).

Related:
- #130889 / #114597: the Windows `stdout` pipe variant of the same buffer-lock wait. That change leaves the PTY path alone, and this one does not touch the pipe path. Both edit `_release_finished_handles`, in separate branches.
- #106742: gateway as the single session runtime; see above.
- #132385: `systemd-run --scope` can expand the command line (`$$` → `$`). On this host (systemd 255) it reproduced only with `--expand-environment=yes`, not with the defaults. Not touched by this PR.
- #131683 (merged): moved the shared-metrics flush off the turn path, which removes the cross-session freeze but not this hang.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Changes Made

- `tools/process_registry.py`:
  - `_release_finished_handles()` skips `_pty.close()` on POSIX while the session's reader thread is alive and isn't the calling thread.
  - `_pty_reader_loop()` admits output only while the session is running, atomically with the kill (`append_output_if_running()`, `_ingest_output(..., unless_exited=True)`).
- `tests/tools/test_process_registry_pty_kill.py` (new), real PTY and real processes, no systemd scope:
  - `test_kill_returns_while_escaped_descendant_holds_the_pty`: the escapee stays silent past the 5 s kill deadline, so nothing but the fix lets the kill return. The kill must return `killed` within 5 s, and the reader must exit and close the PTY once the escapee does.
  - `test_output_after_the_kill_is_not_added_to_the_killed_session`: the escapee prints after the kill. The reader drains it, but it must reach neither the session buffer nor the live stream.
  - `test_chunk_read_before_the_kill_is_not_added_after_it`: pauses the reader between reading a chunk and buffering it, runs the real kill, then resumes. The chunk must be in neither the kill's receipt, the session buffer nor the live stream.
  - The spawn helper terminates the PTY child it spawned if its readiness check fails; the kill tests do the same on failure.

## How to Test

1. `bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_process_registry_pty_kill.py`
2. Against `main` `b412ee9206` with only the new test file copied in: 3 of 3 fail.
3. With this PR: 3/3 pass (three consecutive runs).
4. Mutation checks on this head:
   - Removing the reader-close guard (closing under the live reader again) fails only the hang test.
   - Restoring a separate `exited` check before the append fails only the in-flight chunk test.
   - Dropping the check entirely fails the in-flight chunk test and the late-output test.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass. Not run locally: focused suites only, listed below. CI ran the full suite on the earlier heads.
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu, Linux 6.8, Python 3.14.7

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility). The reader-close guard is POSIX-only, so Windows closes the PTY exactly as on `main`. The PTY tests are POSIX-only and skip elsewhere.
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

- **New test file on this head:** 3 passed, 0 skipped.
- **Focused suites on this head** (`run_tests.sh`): the new file, every `test_process_registry*.py`, `test_terminal_tool_pty_fallback.py`, `test_pty_query_responder.py`, `test_kanban_gateway_restart_handoff.py` and four `test_web_server_*` files. Result: **172 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped.**
- **Not in that list:** `test_persist_on_release.py::test_agent_close_owned_loop_skips_persisted_sessions` fails locally on this branch and on `main` alike. Its real-home guard trips because my worktree's git dir sits under `~/.hermes`.
- **CI on earlier heads:** green on `235635a` (full suite passing in both shards) and on `080b109`.
- **Ruff:** clean on the changed files.

## What does this PR do?

Bumps the Prompt Studio community entry from 1.8.0 to 1.9.0. I am the owner and only maintainer of https://github.com/bwoliveira/prompt-studio.

- Pinned to the full commit SHA of release [v1.9.0](https://github.com/bwoliveira/prompt-studio/releases/tag/v1.9.0) (`ecead76f0b2ff4f46c09341c871e234eb1692a1a`), not the annotated tag object.
- Adopted range: [51bd933...ecead76](https://github.com/bwoliveira/prompt-studio/compare/51bd9330d4841de13624d3315cb4bec66434b71d...ecead76f0b2ff4f46c09341c871e234eb1692a1a); full notes in the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/bwoliveira/prompt-studio/blob/v1.9.0/CHANGELOG.md#190).

items.body:
## What was wrong

Register a second gateway and the sidebar profile rail switches to fleet mode, which drops the default ↔ all home pill. Once the fleet passes 13 profiles the rail condenses into a menu, and that menu is the only pointer route left to a default. It listed the default of every *at-rest* gateway (the remote's, or "This device") but left out the *active* gateway's own default. On the usual setup that means the local default disappears while the remote default stays listed. The trigger also showed "Profiles" instead of the profile you were on. ⌘1 / mod+d was the only way back.

The behavior is the same in both directions: if a remote is active, its default goes missing and This device's shows up.

## Fix

- `profile-switcher.tsx`: in fleet mode the condensed menu puts the active gateway's default first. The row and the trigger use the home glyph, and the row routes on the active connection the same way the home pill does. Non-fleet keeps its pill, so the non-fleet menu is unchanged.
- Hover prewarm on current-source picks (rail squares, both profile menus) went through the bare name, which resolves on the legacy door. Hovering a remote gateway's `default` therefore warmed This device's default. This is the P2 review on #100098. `prewarmProfilePick` warms the same `(connection, profile)` the click dials (`profilePickConnectionId`), which fixes the hover for named rows on a remote source too.

## Proof

- Vitest, red on `main` and green here:
  - `profile-rail-fleet.test.tsx` covers the active default row: listed, checked, home glyph, trigger label, and `selectProfile('default')`, with both local and remote active.
  - `profile.test.ts` checks that the hover warm and the click dial the same pair.
- New core E2E `fleet-condensed-default.spec.ts`, running in the required `E2E Desktop core` lane. It uses a real app, a real local backend, and a real second `hermes serve` registered as a remote connection. It asserts the active default is in the menu, then switches to the remote and asserts it again. Run locally: on `main` it fails with `Expected substring: "default"`, `Received string: "Profiles"`. On this branch it passes (~10 s).

## Keeping it fixed

- Layout matrix in `profile-rail-fleet.test.tsx`. It covers a single gateway and a fleet, the expanded strip and the condensed menu, local or remote active, starting from a named profile or the all view, and asserts the active default is one click away in every case. This runs on every desktop PR. On `main` the four fleet + condensed cases fail and the other eight pass, so a future layout that drops the default fails CI.
- `scripts/ci/classify_changes.py`: the core E2E lane starts on a PR only when the PR touches the paths it guards. A change to `profile-switcher.tsx` or `fleet-*` would have met the new E2E only after merge to main. Both paths are now in the lane, and `test_classify_changes.py` has a row for them. `store/profile.ts` stays out on purpose: it's a hot file, and its prewarm contract is covered by vitest.

Supersedes #100098, #124000, #132241, which were three passes at the same prepend. This PR adds the prewarm routing from the #100098 review, the home-connection route, and the E2E. Authors are credited as co-authors.

Fixes #106017
Fixes #131632

items.body:
Background terminal commands run inside a systemd scope now run exactly as written — `$$`, `${VAR}` and `${arr[@]}` are no longer rewritten by `systemd-run` before the shell sees them.

Fixes #132385

## What happened

Supervised gateways run background processes in a transient scope (`systemd-run --user --scope …`, from #70716). On systemd builds where `--expand-environment` defaults to `yes` (systemd 254+, e.g. Fedora's 259), `systemd-run` expands `$`-references itself in scope mode, so `bash -c 'echo $$'` printed `$` and `${arr[@]}` became an empty string with a stderr warning. `tools/process_registry.py::_systemd_scope_argv` never passed `--expand-environment=no`.

## Change

- `tools/process_registry.py::_systemd_scope_argv` adds `--expand-environment=no` (after `--quiet`) while `_SYSTEMD_RUN_NO_EXPAND` is set.
- `_systemd_run_user_scope_available` (the existing cached probe) retries once without the flag when systemd-run rejects it (stderr names `expand-environment`, i.e. systemd < 254 getopt rejection) and clears `_SYSTEMD_RUN_NO_EXPAND`, so older systemd keeps its cgroup isolation instead of losing the scope. No extra subprocess on systemd ≥ 254; at most one extra probe on older systemd, once per process.
- Every scope spawn goes through this builder: background pipe/PTY spawns (`_scope_argv`) and restart-safe cron/kanban children (`restart_safe_gateway_child_argv`). `hermes_cli/update_abort_recovery.py` builds its own argv but passes a fixed Python argv with no shell string, so it is unaffected.
- `tests/tools/test_process_registry.py`: one parametrized test (`systemd>=254` / `systemd<254`) pinning the flag in the spawn argv, the unchanged command tail after `--`, and the probe fallback.

## Credit

Diagnosed by @teknium1 in #132385; @kokhlo confirmed the code path in the thread. No code was taken from either.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Live, Fedora 44 / systemd 259, real `_build_systemd_scope_argv(['bash','-c','X=(a b); echo "pid=$$ arr=${X[@]}"'])` — main | `pid=$ arr=` + `Invalid environment variable name evaluates to an empty string: X[@]` |
| Same — this branch | `pid=2109 arr=a b` |
| Live, Debian 12 / systemd 252 — this branch | probe drops the flag, scope available, `pid=2149 arr=a b` (isolation kept) |
| Live, Ubuntu noble / systemd 255.4 — main | does not expand (distro build); the flag is accepted there, so harmless |
| New test on main / branch (Linux) | red ×2 / green ×2 |
| Mutations (drop flag / no retry / no flag clear) | each turns a test row red |
| `test_process_registry`, `cron/test_restart_safe_worker`, `test_kanban_gateway_restart_handoff`, `test_process_registry_windows_live` (macOS) | 129 passed, 31 skipped (Linux-gated) |

Independent review: correctness, tests/probe/mutation, reuse, quality and efficiency passes — no findings.

## Maintainer notes

- Alternative gate considered: parse `systemd-run --version` (≥ 254) in the probe. Not used — it adds a subprocess per probe; option-rejection detection costs nothing on new systemd.
- The flag is never re-enabled within a process (a live systemd upgrade under a running gateway keeps the old behaviour until restart — same as main).
- #132247 (held) adds a foreground scope through the same `_systemd_scope_argv`; on rebase the two return-list additions combine (`*no_expand` after `--quiet`, `*limit` at the end) and the foreground path is covered with no further change.

items.body:
A manual or event-triggered `cronjob run` that runs longer than the stale allowance is no longer force-released by the in-flight sweep, so a second copy of the same job can no longer start while the first is still running.

Fixes #132223

## What happened

Direct runs (`tools/cronjob_tools.py::_run_claimed_job`) registered in-flight with the `_FUTURE_PENDING` sentinel and never attached a real Future (since #80807), while `sweep_stale_inflight` force-releases pending-sentinel registrations past the age allowance (since #86319). A healthy long direct run therefore got swept, and the next tick or a second `run` was admitted. Separately, an older dispatch's late cleanup could release or overwrite a newer run's registration for the same job, because release and future-attach were keyed by job id only.

## Change

- `tools/cronjob_tools.py`: the direct run registers with an already-running `Future` and completes it on every exit path.
- `cron/scheduler.py`: every registration carries an owner token (`_running_registration_owners`); `release_running_job(…, owner=)` and the ticker's late future-attach act only on the registration they own; the sweep clears the owner with the rest of the registration.
- `tests/cron/test_registration_ownership.py` (new): a live direct run survives the stale sweep; a parametrized case (direct, ticker, direct-error, submit-error, setup-error) shows a late cleanup never removes a successor's registration.
- Our follow-up: module-level `Future` import.

## Credit

@cdb-lumen (#132236) — commit `2e19852916` cherry-picked with authorship kept (`-x dd834c874f`). External review on #132236 by @ehz0ah. Attribution map in `8492ad7856`.

## Verification

| Check | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Live: real `_execute_job_now` (no_agent script) → `sweep_stale_inflight` → second concurrent run | registration is `PENDING-sentinel`; sweep releases it (`forced_release reason=age future=pending`); second run `claimed: True` | registration is a `Future`; sweep releases nothing; second run refused (`Job is already being fired`) |
| Sequential third run (neighbour) | runs; no leftover map entries | same |
| `test_registration_ownership.py` | 6 red | 6 green |
| Mutations | reverting the commit, the scheduler half, the tools half, the owner fence, the attach guard or the running Future each turns tests red | |
| 15 cron/tools/gateway test files referencing the touched symbols | — | 315 passed, 6 skipped |

Independent review: correctness, tests/probe/mutation, reuse, quality and efficiency passes approved; one import-placement nit fixed (`8180d3e848`).

## Maintainer notes

- By design a genuinely hung direct run (non-done Future) is no longer age-swept — the same treatment ticker pool runs already get; `_wedged_inflight_keys` still reports it to the restart drain.
- Untested defensive hunks: the outer-`finally` release passing `owner=` (only reachable when setup fails between register and the inner try) and the sweep's owner pop (otherwise overwritten by the next register).
- Other open PRs touching `_run_claimed_job` (#107564, #104118, #105144, #122647, #116316, #124254) or `sweep_stale_inflight` (#126599, #86969) may need a rebase.

items.body:
Cron jobs run by the restart-safe external worker now fire the profile's config `hooks:` (shell hooks and `hooks.outbound` webhooks), the same as jobs run in-process.

Fixes #131764

## What happened

The external cron worker (`cron/scheduler.py::_run_external_worker_payload`, added in #101940) discovered plugins (since `411c0405b6`) but never registered config hooks, so `hooks:` and `hooks.outbound` silently did nothing for worker-run jobs while plugin hooks still fired — which hid the gap.

## Change

- `cron/scheduler.py::_run_external_worker_payload`: after plugin discovery and inside the payload's home override and secret scope, call the gateway's own `GatewayStartupMixin._register_config_hooks` (the helper the gateway uses per profile at startup). Registration happens once per worker process; both registries are keyed per home and idempotent.
- `tests/cron/test_external_worker_config_hooks.py` (new): a multiplexed payload registers the owning profile's shell hook and a `secret_env` outbound webhook under that profile's home key.

## Credit

@liuhao1024 (#131831, draft) — commit `7c3dc30b57` cherry-picked with authorship kept (`-x d1971c698a`). Our follow-up `018d9130a1` reuses the gateway helper instead of a copied registration sequence and moves registration inside the secret scope: in the original ordering, an outbound webhook with `secret_env` raised `UnscopedSecretError` on a multiplexed gateway and was silently dropped.

@drafie found the same gap first in #119421 (shell hooks only).

## Verification

| Live probe — real `_run_external_worker_payload`, 2 payloads per worker | on_session_start callbacks | outbound callbacks | hook fires |
|---|---|---|---|
| main (single-profile and multiplexed) | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| #131831 alone, multiplexed | 1 | **0** | 2 |
| this branch (single-profile and multiplexed) | 1 | 1 | 2 |
| profile without `hooks:` (neighbour), main and branch | 0 | 0 | — |

- New test: red on main (shell hook not registered) and red with only the contributor commit (outbound webhook missing); green on the branch.
- 13 related test files (cron worker, outbound webhooks, shell hooks, gateway profile/hook scope, plugins, scheduler): 324 passed, 17 skipped.
- Import cost of the lazy `gateway.run_startup` import in the one-shot worker: 2–3 ms (does not import `gateway.run`).

Independent review: correctness, tests/probe/mutation, reuse, quality and efficiency passes approved.

## Maintainer notes

- Cron calls a private static method on a gateway mixin. Kept deliberately for this fix; a later cleanup could move it to one public `register_config_hooks()` shared with `cli.py` and `hermes_cli/main.py`, which hand-write the same sequence.
- `tui_gateway/server.py` re-registers shell hooks per session but not outbound webhooks — separate, out of scope here.
- #124847, #124855 and #128324 also touch `_run_external_worker_payload`.

items.body:
Desktop now shows, selects and sends OpenAI Ultrafast as its own speed tier instead of collapsing it into "Fast" — and a new chat that asks for Ultrafast gets Ultrafast, not Priority.

Refs #132275

## What happened

Since #128307 the Desktop counted `ultrafast` as Fast (`isFastTier`), so the model pill said "Fast", the profile default lost the distinction, and New Chat sent `fast: true`, which the backend maps to Priority. `session.create` had no way to carry an exact tier (`service_tier` was rejected as an extra input), and the model inventory never reported which models offer Ultrafast.

## Change

- `hermes_cli/inventory.py`: each model row reports `ultrafast` when the model and route offer it (one capability resolve per model).
- `tui_gateway/contracts/sessions.py` + `methods_session_model_guard.py::create_overrides`: `session.create` accepts an exact `service_tier` that wins over the legacy `fast` flag; an unknown tier word returns 4002. `agent/fast_mode.py::parse_exact_service_tier` is the strict parse. Generated contracts regenerated.
- Desktop: the exact tier rides through presets, drafts, the menu and the pill label; Settings and the model menu get a Standard / Fast / Ultrafast select on models that offer Ultrafast (other models keep the Fast switch). Labels in en/de/es/fr/ru/zh/ar/zh-hant.
- Desktop ↔ older backends: `service_tier` is sent only for Ultrafast (`fast` already expresses Priority/Standard). If a pre-Ultrafast backend rejects the field, `createGatewaySession` drops it once and resends with `fast` kept — same matcher as the existing `cwd_explicit` fallback — so the chat opens on Priority instead of failing.
- Config words Desktop doesn't know (`flex`, `scale`, `auto`, …) seed the composer as Standard instead of being forwarded raw (which would hit 4002). Settings and the composer share one parse (`lib/model-status-label.ts::composerServiceTier`).
- `methods_session.py` shrinks (2624 → 2610 lines): the create-override parse moved to `methods_session_model_guard.py`.

## Credit

@Froraut (#130990) — `2065f68e7f` (feature) and `90478d050c` cherry-picked with authorship kept; `2a72fa0446` re-applied with `--author` from the PR's merge commit (its PR-side hunks only). Our follow-ups: the module split, test trim, the older-backend retry, the config-word normalisation, and the review folds.

## Verification

| Check | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Inventory caps, `gpt-6-astra-900k` | `fast: true`, no `ultrafast` | `fast: true, ultrafast: true` |
| `session.create` with `service_tier: "ultrafast"` | rejected (`Extra inputs are not permitted`) | accepted; tier sent `ultrafast` |
| Legacy `{fast: true}` | `priority` | `priority` (unchanged) |
| Desktop pill for an Ultrafast selection | "GPT-5.5 · Fast" | "GPT-5.5 · Ultrafast" |
| New Desktop → old backend, Ultrafast pick | — | one rejected send, resend without `service_tier` → Priority |
| Daybreak / `gpt-5.6-cyber` fast capability and CLI `/fast` | available | available (unchanged) |
| Inventory rewrite equivalence (21 models × 8 routes) | — | 0 differences vs the two-resolve form |

- Python: 41–96 passed per review round across `test_openai_ultrafast`, inventory, fast-mode, TUI session-scope and codex transport files; `test_tui_gateway_server.py` 669 passed.
- Desktop vitest: 589 passed across settings, composer, session-actions, model menu, presets and status-label files.
- Mutations: the feature commit, the Daybreak revert, the older-backend retry, the ultrafast-only send, and the config-word normalisation each turn a test red.
- Independent review: three rounds (correctness, tests/probe/mutation, reuse, quality, efficiency). Round 1 found the older-backend and raw-config-word regressions; both are fixed and re-reviewed.

## Maintainer notes

- Partial for #132275: Auto and Cold are still CLI/config-only — Settings shows a saved `auto`/`cold` as Standard and turning Fast on overwrites it.
- The contributor's rule removing speed controls from Daybreak and `gpt-5.6-cyber` aliases was dropped on maintainer decision; those models keep Priority as on main.
- `2a72fa0446` (rollback-state eviction) and `90478d050c` (stamp release) are memory hygiene with no observable behaviour a test can pin.
- `create_overrides` still returns 4002 for an unknown tier word from a non-Desktop client — intentional strictness for the new field.
- Overlaps: #129251 (Daybreak, same author) must rebase onto `create_overrides` in `methods_session_model_guard.py`; #107951 edits the moved `_create_overrides`; #116369 / #122111 touch fast gating in `hermes_cli/models.py`.

items.body:
Cron crash and dispatch-failure notices now go out with the firing profile's home channel and bot token, instead of the default profile's — or not at all on a multiplexed gateway.

Fixes #131585

## What happened

`run_one_job` sent the pre-handoff dispatch-failure notice (`_deliver_crash_failure`) before any profile secret scope was installed (since `ecc5c263ec`), and `_run_one_job_body` installed its scope only after `claim_dispatch` / `mark_execution_running`, so a crash in either also notified unscoped. On a single-profile process that read the default profile's credentials; under multiplex `get_secret` fails closed, so the notice raised `UnscopedSecretError` and never went out.

## Change

- `cron/scheduler.py::run_one_job`: the dispatch-failure notice runs inside the fire secret scope (contributor commit).
- `cron/scheduler.py::_run_one_job_body`: the scope is installed at the top of the body, before `claim_dispatch`, so every early crash-notice exit is scoped; the existing function-level `finally` still resets it.
- `_fire_secret_scope()` context manager next to `_install_fire_secret_scope`, used at the new site and in `_launch_external_cron_worker`.
- `tests/cron/test_restart_safe_worker.py`: the contributor's test, parametrized for the handoff and claim-dispatch stages.

## Credit

@skyeyesec333 (#130431) — commit `0e72052688` cherry-picked with authorship kept (`-x 5e0735b172`; one trivial import conflict resolved in favour of main). Attribution map in `f0ae667ae4`. Our follow-ups `f954477f1d` (earlier body install — the case #130431's description mentions) and `7f5539e1d8` (context manager).

## Verification

| Live probe — two profiles, fake delivery recording `get_secret` at send time | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| single-profile, handoff failure / claim-dispatch crash | sent with `DEFAULT-111 / DEFAULT-TOKEN` | sent with `WORKER-222 / WORKER-TOKEN` |
| multiplexed, both stages | `UnscopedSecretError` ("could not read this profile's TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL"), no notice | `WORKER-222 / WORKER-TOKEN` |
| scope left installed after the fire | no | no |

- Kept test: `[handoff]` red on main; `[claim_dispatch]` red on main and with the contributor commit alone; both green here.
- Mutations: reverting either behaviour commit alone turns its row red.
- `test_restart_safe_worker`, `test_scheduler`, `test_cron_failure_deliver`, `test_run_one_job`, `test_cron_multiplex_desktop_ticker_scope`: 172 passed, 4 skipped.

Independent review: correctness, tests/probe/mutation, reuse, quality and efficiency passes approved; the quality pass's two cleanups are folded in.

## Maintainer notes

- Work moved inside the scope (`claim_dispatch`, `mark_execution_running`) reads no secrets; scope install is fail-open, so an install error can't block the claim.
- Overlaps: #128063 touches `_install_fire_secret_scope`; #120360, #120391, #82901, #124756, #128324, #126012 touch nearby `run_one_job` code.

items.body:
`hermes gateway setup` → Discord now checks the pasted bot token with Discord and does the Developer Portal busywork for you: a bad token is re-asked instead of saved, a missing Message Content Intent gets a direct link and a re-check, the invite link is printed, and the bot's owner (you) is allowlisted without Developer Mode. The `.env` template finally has a Discord section.

Prompted by the Linus Tech Tips segment on Hermes (youtube.com/watch?v=gvzRPEW5eEc): "everyone that I know that runs Hermes agent runs it through Discord", yet the `.env` template had no Discord section ("you just append it to the bottom"), and between the Developer Portal, creating the server and configuring permissions, three people did not finish setup in a day.

## Changes
- **Token checked live**: the wizard reads `GET /applications/@me` with the token. A 401 says "Discord rejected that token", re-prompts, and saves nothing (3 tries). Offline/5xx: the token is saved with the manual intent reminder, as before.
- **Intents**: Message Content Intent off → warning that Discord will refuse the connection (Hermes always requests it, close 4014), link to `discord.com/developers/applications/<app id>/bot`, Enter to re-check (or `skip`). Server Members Intent off → optional note, and a note again if the user allowlists by username.
- **Invite link**: printed with `client_id`, `scope=bot applications.commands`, `integration_type=0` (guild install) and `permissions=309241171008` (the documented Recommended set + Connect/Speak). The wording changes when `approximate_guild_count == 0` ("The bot isn't in any server yet").
- **Allowlist adds the owner** (existing entries are kept): "Allow yourself (@name) to talk to the bot?" uses the application owner, or accepted team members for team-owned apps. Others can still be added by ID or username.
- **`.env.example` Discord section** (copied to `~/.hermes/.env` by `install.sh`): token, allowed users/roles, home channel, the intent warning and an invite URL template.
- **Docs**: a shortcut tip before Step 1; Step 3 and Troubleshooting now say a disabled Message Content Intent keeps the bot offline (it was described as blank messages); the wizard's checks described in Step 8, and the Full permissions row.
- **Salvage #83296** (@GottZ, authorship kept): Recommended invite integer gains Create Public Threads (`309238025280`), so `/thread` and auto-threading stop failing with `50001 Missing Access`; plus the parent-channel troubleshooting note.
- The wizard moves out of the 7k-line `adapter.py` into `plugins/platforms/discord/onboarding.py`, unchanged where not listed above.

## Validation
| | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Paste `abc.def.ghi` as the token | saved to `.env` as `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN='abc.def.ghi'` | `✗ Discord rejected that token…`, re-prompted |
| Paste the real token | saved, no feedback | `✓ Token works: this is the bot "Hermes-TestingBot"`, `✓ Message Content Intent is on` |
| Invite link | none, build it by hand | printed with the app's client_id |
| Allowlist | Developer Mode → Copy User ID by hand; Enter left it empty | "Allow yourself (@teknium)?" Enter → `DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS=<owner id>` |
| Reconfigure with `DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS=999` already set | kept | kept and extended: `999,<owner id>` |
| Token pasted inside curly quotes | stripped with a warning | stripped with the same warning, then checked: `✓ Token works` |

**Live repro:** PTY run of the real wizard (dispatched via `gateway_setup_wizard._configure_platform`, the `hermes gateway setup` path) against the real Discord API with a real bot, isolated `HOME`/`HERMES_HOME`, on a detached `origin/main` worktree and on this branch; outcomes in the table above. Not covered live: the intent-OFF branch (it would mean flipping the toggle on a real bot). It ran in-process to check the message and link.

Tests: one new invariant test against the Discord stand-in server (real HTTP). It records every `.env` write and checks four things: a rejected token is never written, a curly-quoted paste is sanitized before the check, the owner is added to an existing allowlist, and the invite has the app's client_id and the permission integer. It fails on the previous PR head with `UnicodeEncodeError`. Existing wizard tests run the offline path. The 60 Discord/setup/gateway test files pass (557).

## Allowed users: one visible box per ID (Desktop + dashboard)

Every platform's allowlist used to be one empty input with a `«redacted:…»` placeholder, so a saved list looked like a hidden secret and could only be replaced as a whole.

- The backend marks allowlist rows `is_list` and returns their plain value. These are IDs, not secrets. Password fields still only return the redacted preview.
- **Desktop and dashboard** show each entry in its own plain text box with an × to remove it. "+ Add another" (or Enter) adds a box. Pasting `111,222` splits it into two boxes.
- The value is saved in the same comma-separated format the gateway already reads. Removing every entry and saving clears the key.
- The Desktop help text for allowlist fields now says "one per box" in all 9 locales.

| Live check (real `serve` / `dashboard` backend, sandbox `.env`) | Result |
|---|---|
| Desktop opens Discord with `DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS=111…,222…` | two `type=text` boxes showing both IDs |
| remove 111, + add 333, Save | `.env` has `DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS=222…,333…`; boxes refresh from the server |
| remove both, Save | key cleared from `.env` |
| Dashboard Configure → same three steps | same `.env` results |

Tests: `test_allowlist_value_is_readable_but_secrets_stay_redacted` (API) and two Desktop vitest cases (boxes and save, emptying clears). The vitest cases fail on main's `index.tsx`.

## Infographic
![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aacf0c1/2Uaby28nlbZkVXz7OFOcr_bk9qwSP3.png)

## Not in this PR
Desktop's Discord card still shows one hint line ("Invite the bot to your server with the right scopes"). `check_bot_token()` can back a Desktop "Check bot" button that shows the invite link, the intent state and an "Allow me" action; that UI change needs a design pass with screenshots first.

items.body:
One-shot runs (`hermes -z`) now close their Relay session, so exported Relay telemetry gets a session end and `on_session_finalize` fires, on success and on failure.

## Changes
- `hermes_cli/oneshot.py::_run_agent` records the session id at turn entry. Compression can rotate `agent.session_id` mid-turn without opening a second Relay root.
- `_close_agent` calls `hermes_cli.lifecycle.finalize_session` for that id after the background-completion linger and before memory/agent teardown. This is the same chokepoint the interactive CLI and TUI already use.
- `hooks.md`: `on_session_finalize` now lists the one-shot exit.

Root cause: `run_conversation` ends the turn but keeps the Relay root resumable, and the one-shot exit is `os._exit`, which skips the atexit finalizer every other CLI path relies on. `finalize_session` is the only caller of `SESSION_COORDINATOR.finalize_conversation`, and one-shot never reached it.

## Validation
**Live repro**, a real `hermes -z` on OpenRouter `google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite` with a real `on_session_finalize` plugin in an isolated `HERMES_HOME`. The plugin also checks whether the Relay root is still registered after the close.

| Run | origin/main 7e19f41 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `hermes -z "pong"` (rc 0) | no `on_session_finalize`, root never closed | fires once, `reason=shutdown`, `relay_root_open_after_close=false` |
| `hermes -z` with an invalid model (rc 2) | n/a | fires once, root closed |
| Control: `hermes chat -Q -q` | fires, root closed | unchanged |

- `test_oneshot_closes_its_relay_root_before_agent_teardown[success|failure]`: red with `oneshot.py` swapped back to origin/main, green here. It pins the entry id over a compression-rotated one and the finalize → memory → `agent.close()` order.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_tui_resume_flow.py`, `test_oneshot_surrogate.py`, `test_relay_shared_metrics_runtime.py`: 67 passed, 0 failed. Run with a fake HOME because of the known `.worktrees/manifest.json` guard.
- ruff, windows-footguns, no-tmp-literals, `git diff --check`, doc links: clean.
- Billed: 3 flash-lite calls, well under $0.01 (estimate, not checked against the invoice).

Same class as #132357, which flushes the shared-metrics session past `os._exit`. This one closes the Relay root itself.

Fixes #79471. Salvages #79563 by @lesterlxt (this mechanism: entry-id capture, finalize in `_run_agent`'s teardown, failures covered; commit authorship kept) and credits #79533 by @thatssoheil, the first fix for the issue (co-author). #79533 changed `run_oneshot`'s return type and skipped finalization on failed runs; the cleanup-path placement is not used here.

## Infographic
![one-shot runs close their session](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aacf0ec/Bjr0Z1dhOPzMFslqELTiJ_sTGycrM2.png)

Follow-up to the catalogued plugin (owner-submitted pin bump, catalog rules 4 and 5).

Pin: 3d691dadfdd515083237337c4a9747389a18ca4a -> f848f777145d69b7f417d6cc86a48821bd85bc77
Version: 1.0.6 -> 1.0.10
Release: https://github.com/soyelmismo/hermes-antigravity-subscription/releases/tag/v1.0.10

Commits adopted in range (`v1.0.6..v1.0.10`):

• `f848f77` test(debug): pin authentication in the prompt-dump dispatch tests
• `d8af07e` release: v1.0.10
• `3df003c` fix(prompt): give the persistent-worker delta the same latest-request instruction
• `3986677` release: v1.0.9
• `8d28625` fix(stream): defer blocking close() work off a running event loop
• `a056b65` docs only (release skill limit)
• `f44ee04` release: v1.0.8
• `596e5af` test(stderr): make the drainer tests pass on Windows
• `c611d6f` release: v1.0.7
• `6a20cca` fix(prompt): answer feedback on prior work instead of continuing the old task
• `3796e70` fix(process): drain agy stderr continuously so a full pipe cannot block the child
• `acf28cd` fix(usage): single-flight agy /usage refresh and cover the stale-cache path
• `fba4622` fix(process): strip SSH session vars when the credential lives in the keyring
• `ba145f7` feat: subscription usage and quota tracking via agy /usage (soyelmismo/hermes-antigravity-subscription#19)
• `c7c57a6`, `a2309c8`, `c08caa0` docs only (AGENTS.md, release skill)

v1.0.7 was tagged but never pinned: its Windows CI run failed on two test-only defects, fixed in `596e5af`. v1.0.8 was the first tag with green Linux and Windows CI; v1.0.9 and v1.0.10 add a stream lifecycle fix and a prompt fix on top.

### Root Cause / Motivation

1. **Keyring users failed auth under inherited SSH vars** (soyelmismo/hermes-antigravity-subscription#18). agy 1.2.16 switches to file-based token storage when it sees `SSH_CONNECTION`, `SSH_CLIENT` or `SSH_TTY` (`Using file-based token storage because SSH session detected`). A local session whose credential lives in the OS keyring then failed with `You are not logged into Antigravity`, while `is_authenticated()` reported success. `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` does not trigger the switch (verified by toggling each variable).
2. **Unread stderr pipe could block agy** (soyelmismo/hermes-antigravity-subscription#17). The persistent worker was spawned with `stderr=PIPE` and the pipe was never read. Past the pipe buffer (64 KiB with 4 KiB pages, 1 MiB with 64 KiB pages), agy blocked in `write()`. Measured with a mock worker writing 3 MB to stderr: blocked for more than 120 s without draining, finished in 0.3 s with it. The request timeout did not recover the turn.
3. **No quota visibility.** `/usage`, the status bar and the desktop quota view showed nothing for this provider.

### Changes in v1.0.10

1. **`usage.py`, `__init__.py`**
   - `fetch_account_usage()` returns an `AccountUsageSnapshot` with weekly and 5h windows per model group, read from `agy -p "/usage" --output-format json` in a private temp HOME. agy reports `num_turns: 0` for this call, so it consumes no tokens.
   - 8 s subprocess timeout, inside the 10 s `PLUGIN_USAGE_HOOK_DEADLINE_S` bound in `agent/account_usage.py`. 60 s cache. Refresh is single-flight: concurrent callers share one subprocess. An unforced failure serves the previous snapshot.
2. **`process.py` `build_child_env()`**
   - On POSIX, when no token file exists, drops `SSH_CONNECTION`, `SSH_CLIENT` and `SSH_TTY` from the child env. Keeps `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`. With a token file present, the env is unchanged. The parent `os.environ` is never modified.
3. **`process.py`, `client.py`, `stream.py`**
   - A daemon thread per agy child drains stderr and keeps the last 64 KiB. The oneshot error message reads that tail instead of `proc.stderr.read()`.
4. **`prompt.py`**
   - The latest-request instruction tells the model to address feedback on prior work instead of continuing the earlier task, and to ask one short question when intent is ambiguous.
5. **`stream.py` `close()`**
   - Hermes' `_aggregate_chat_stream_async` calls the synchronous `close()` on the event loop thread. Terminating agy (`terminate()`, `wait(2)`, `killpg`) could stall the loop for about 2 s. When a loop is running on the calling thread, `close()` now runs that body on a short-lived daemon thread; outside a loop it stays synchronous. The worker lock is still released only after the worker is terminated.
6. **`prompt.py` `_format_delta_prompt()`**
   - After a finished turn, a new user message on the persistent worker goes through the delta path, which closed with a weaker instruction than the full prompt, so the model continued the earlier task instead of answering. Both paths now build the closing section from one function, `_latest_user_request_section`. Verified live: a prime-number task followed by an unrelated one-word question was answered directly on the delta path.
   - New opt-in `ANTIGRAVITY_DEBUG_PROMPT_DIR` writes each prompt sent to agy (0700 dir, 0600 files) with its branch (`delta`, `full`, `retry`, `oneshot`). Unset means no extra I/O.

No new dependencies, no new tools, hooks or env vars. `capabilities:` unchanged. The catalog description adds the `/usage` quota read to the existing disclosure.

### Validation

• Plugin repo CI: 236 passed on ubuntu-latest, 235 passed and 1 skipped on windows-latest, against `HERMES_REF v2026.9.21`.
• `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/antigravity-subscription-directsdk.yaml` passed (1 file valid).
• `hermes plugins validate /root/.hermes/plugins/antigravity-subscription-directsdk` passed (safe, declared capabilities match).
• Manifest version 1.0.10 matches git tag `v1.0.10` and the catalog entry.
