items.body:
## Root cause

#131740 (reopened) reports Desktop turns that logged `Turn ended: reason=text_response(finish_reason=stop)` but never emitted the `tui turn finished` bookend; the liveness watchdog fired ~600 s later naming `API call #N completed` as the last activity, and the abort hit a turn whose loop had already finished.

#132140 (merged 21d59f18e7) moved the bookend/idle release ahead of the post-turn memory trim on the gateway side. The residual stall sits **inside `run_conversation`**, and the watchdog window pins it exactly:

- `Turn ended` is logged mid-way through `finalize_turn` (`agent/turn_finalizer.py`, `_log_turn_exit`), and the whole tail of `finalize_turn` plus `export_current_turn_boundary` / `_close_durable_failed_turn` runs after it with the watchdog still armed.
- The watchdog is disarmed only when `conversation_loop.run_conversation` returns — the facade's inner `finally` (`agent/turn_facade.py`) calls `lease.stop_refresher()` before any relay teardown or gateway-side work, so **everything in `tui_gateway/prompt_turn.py`'s `finally` (trim, TTS sentinel, scope resets, bookend, marker retirement) runs after the watchdog disarmed**. A 600 s watchdog fire therefore proves the wedge was between the `Turn ended` log and `run_conversation` returning.
- With the reporter's config (Windows, default Desktop, no plugins named), every step in that window is in-memory, bounded (30 s plugin-hook cap in `hermes_cli/plugins_dispatch.py`, 10 s relay `_SCOPE_OP_TIMEOUT`), or gated off (`trim_memory` is a no-op on Windows — the glibc probe returns before `gc.collect`; telemetry/relay observers default off; no memory provider). No single step can be convicted from the logs — nothing in the window stamps the activity clock or captures stacks, which is why the maintainer asked for a watchdog sample that localizes the frame.

The issue's "watchdog should treat a turn whose loop already returned as finished" half is **not** a safe skip: the watchdog firing on this wedge is the only thing that freed the reporter's sessions (a single desktop backend has no other process to TTL-reclaim the lease). Skipping would trade a 600 s recovery for an indefinite hang.

## Fix

Two small, fail-open changes that keep the watchdog's authority unchanged:

- **`agent/turn_finalizer.py`** — `_log_turn_exit` stamps the activity clock (`_touch_activity("turn end logged")`) at the `Turn ended` line. A stall in the post-loop tail is now measured — and surfaced — from when the loop actually finished, and the watchdog's `last activity` names the finalizer instead of a stale `API call #N completed`. The stamp is guarded (`getattr`/`try`), so a test double without the activity seam never breaks the finalizer.
- **`agent/turn_liveness.py`** — when the watchdog surfaces a stall (once per activity generation, the existing rate limit), it dumps every thread's stack to errors.log with the turn thread marked (`sys._current_frames()`, 40-thread cap; in-tree precedent: `tools/delegate_tool_child_run.py` diagnostics). The next occurrence produces the wedged frame directly in errors.log, with no py-spy/faulthandler setup from the reporter.

Refs #131740 — this is the guard + diagnostics half. The unknown blocking step in the finalizer tail is not fixed by this PR; the stack dump exists to convict it.

## Coverage

| #131740 requirement | Status |
|---|---|
| Bookend + `session["running"]=False` + marker retirement must always run regardless of post-turn work | Met by #132140 (merged), not this PR |
| The residual 600 s stall inside `run_conversation` after `Turn ended` | Not met — root cause not convicted from available evidence; this PR adds the stack dump that will pin it on the next occurrence |
| Watchdog stall surface mislabels a finished loop as `API call #N completed` | Met — the activity clock is stamped at turn end |
| Watchdog aborts a turn ~10 min after its loop ended with a misleading message | Partially met — the watchdog still fires (correctly: it is the only recovery), but now measures from the loop's end and its surface names `turn end logged`; the message wording itself is unchanged |
| Watchdog should skip turns whose loop already returned | Deliberately not done — see Root cause; skipping would remove the only recovery path |
| Trim lock bounded (`mem_trim` suggestion 2) | Ruled out for this reporter: `trim_memory` is a no-op on Windows (glibc probe returns before `gc.collect`) |

## Tests

Red on base, green on head (proved by swapping `git show origin/main:agent/{turn_finalizer,turn_liveness}.py` in the worktree):

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_turn_end_stall_diagnostics.py
# base: 2 failed (activity stamp missing; stall dump missing), 1 passed
# head: 3 passed
```

Neighbouring suites on head (54 + 63 + 32 tests, 0 failed):

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_turn_liveness_watchdog.py tests/agent/test_turn_liveness.py \
  tests/agent/test_turn_finalizer_cleanup_guard.py tests/agent/test_turn_finalizer_final_response_persistence.py \
  tests/agent/test_turn_finalizer_interrupt_alternation.py tests/agent/test_turn_finalizer_iteration_limit_exit.py
# 6 files, 54 passed, 0 failed
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_compress_context_progress_timeout.py tests/agent/test_codex_app_server_event_bridge.py tests/agent/test_session_activity_persist.py
# 3 files, 63 passed, 0 failed
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_diagnostic_turn_end_to_end.py tests/tui_gateway/test_prompt_accept_logging.py \
  tests/tui_gateway/test_turn_finished_failure_cause.py tests/tui_gateway/test_closed_session_turn_lease.py \
  tests/tui_gateway/test_compute_host_borrowed_lease.py
# 5 files, 32 passed, 0 failed
```

Gates: `uvx ruff check` clean on all three files; `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --all`, `check_bash_shebangs.py`, `check_no_tmp_literals.py`, `check_config_yaml_writers.py`, `scripts/ci/check_os_marker_fakes.py` all pass. Post-rebase rerun of the new + watchdog suites green before push.

## Side effects

1. **Existing state**: nothing persisted or re-keyed; the stamp writes the existing in-memory activity clock (and the already rate-limited SessionDB activity projection, which already consumes `_touch_activity` every loop tick — no new store or key).
2. **Version skew**: none — both sides ship in the same backend process; no wire/RPC contract touched.
3. **Reserved values / invariant tests**: no config value, default, or assertion flipped. The watchdog's abort authority (generation revalidation under the shared lock) is untouched — the stamp goes through the same `_touch_activity` path the loop already uses, so an in-flight abort claim is invalidated by real progress exactly as before.
4. **Other callers and flows**: the stamp also fires on interrupted turns' `_log_turn_exit` — measured there it is harmless (the facade's finally disarms the watchdog as it unwinds, and a wedged unwind now gets a truthful clock). Cron/kanban turns already stamp `_touch_activity` per tick; one extra stamp per turn is noise. The stack dump runs on the watchdog's scheduler worker at stall time only, bounded and fail-open (`try/except` → debug log); it cannot delay or break the abort itself (dump precedes the existing `_surface_stall` log line; `_tick` order unchanged). CLI/gateway/messaging surfaces all inherit the same two seams with no behavioural change beyond diagnostics.
5. **Open findings**: none on this cluster. kshitijk4poor's reopen comment asks for a watchdog sample on a build including 21d59f18e7 — the stack dump added here is exactly that sample machinery; the reporter's next stall will carry the frame.

## Self-review

1. *Secretly a feature?* No — the stamp is a one-line clock write at an existing log seam; the dump is an error-log diagnostic behind an existing rate limit. Both serve the reported bug's diagnosability and the mislabeled-activity defect directly.
2. *Secretly on a critical path?* `uv run triage risk` on the final diff scores 0.80 with `critical: ['ui']` — the `ui` surface comes from the issue's desktop labels, not the diff (no `apps/desktop` or UI file is touched; files are `agent/turn_finalizer.py`, `agent/turn_liveness.py`, one test file). The touched runtime surface is the agent loop's finalization tail and the watchdog, both exercised by the suites above. Held for review regardless (below).

## Auto-merge: armed (rebase)

Backend diagnostics only: one activity stamp at `Turn ended` and a thread-stack dump when the watchdog fires. No UI, install/update, wire contract or config change; `classify_automerge` reads SAFE. Reviewed head `00a3fcb3eeb28a7539d3ff8be1b64e9145dbe9e6`.

items.body:
Duplicate skill names now resolve the same way everywhere — the skills list, the prompt index, slash commands, `skill_view`, `-s` preload and cron agree on which copy a name loads, and only advertise names that actually load.

Fixes #64392

## What happened

When two directories (local, `skills.create_dir`, `external_dirs`, project) held a skill with the same name, each surface picked differently. The list showed one row, the prompt index showed two, the slash command registered the first copy found, `skill_view` refused the name as ambiguous, and `-s`/cron reported it as unknown or skipped it. A local copy that collided with an external one at the same path could not be loaded by any name. `skill_view` and the prompt builder also used two different directory orders (`_skill_search_dirs` omitted `create_dir`), and the docs stated three different precedences.

## Change

- One resolver in `agent/skill_utils.py`: `get_skill_search_roots` is the single directory order (project > local > `create_dir` > `external_dirs`); `resolve_skill_catalog` / `pick_skill_candidate` / `skill_candidate_rank` decide which copy owns a name, and every surface reads that decision.
- Across directories, the higher tier wins and a one-time warning names the shadowed copy (silent when it's a symlink or byte-identical copy). Within one tier, two different skills with the same name are still refused — kept from the existing ambiguity protection — and both are listed under their exact paths (`a/one`, `b/two`), which load.
- Slash commands register only names that resolve to one copy; ambiguous ones are reachable as `/skill a/one`.
- `-s` preload (CLI, oneshot, TUI) and cron say `Ambiguous skill name X: use one of <paths>` instead of "Unknown skill(s)" / "not found".
- `skills.disabled` matches a skill's name, or the exact path a duplicate is listed under, on every surface; disabling a path never hides an unrelated skill in another tier.
- `hermes skills list` labels each row's real source (project / local / create_dir / external) instead of "local" for everything.
- Prompt index snapshot version 3 → 4 (row identity now includes the load path).
- Docs (`website/docs/user-guide/features/skills.md`): one stated precedence plus a "Duplicate skill names" section.

## Credit

- @yu-xin-c (#64462) — `7011493903`, rebuilt from `ef3d8ba385e` with authorship kept: list and prompt index only advertise names `skill_view` loads. The basis of this design.
- @TalOrbach (#55634, the first submitter of the local-wins precedence) — `15c6c79506`, rebuilt from `aba7772261f` with authorship kept: `skill_view` applies cross-directory precedence instead of refusing. Attribution map in `6a7884db25`.
- Our follow-ups: slash/preload/cron surfaces, the shared directory order, disabled-path handling, docs, tests, and the review folds.

## Verification

| Fixture | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `dup-demo` in `a/one` and `b/two` (same tier) | list 1 row, index 2 rows, `/dup-demo` loads `a/one`, `skill_view` "Ambiguous", `-s` "Unknown skill(s)" | every surface shows `a/one`, `b/two`; bare `dup-demo` → "Ambiguous … use one of a/one, b/two" everywhere |
| `xdup` local + `productivity/xdup` external | not loadable by any name; `-s` missing; cron skips | local copy loads by `xdup` and `productivity/xdup` on every surface, cron included |
| `skills.disabled: [a/one]` | — | only that copy hidden/refused everywhere; `b/two` and an unrelated `other` at external `a/one` stay loadable |
| `skills.disabled: [dup-demo]` | — | both copies hidden/refused |
| unrelated skills (`extonly`, `misc/xbare2`, …) | — | unchanged except the source label |

- Tests: about 3,870 across the 76 files that touch skills, prompt building, preload, cron, plugins and org skills — no failures beyond those that also fail on main (4) and xdist-only flakes that pass serially.
- Changed assertions (intentional, from the new precedence): the cross-directory refusal test is now `test_higher_tier_wins_cross_directory_collision` (6 parametrized rows); the same-tier refusal test is kept and also checks the "use one of" paths; the org-collision test now shows the org copy under its path name. Two new tests (one end-to-end across every surface).
- Mutations: reverting any behaviour commit turns a test red.
- `resolve_skill_catalog` costs about 7 ms for 300 skills and only runs on a catalog/prompt cache miss; files are hashed only for colliding names, and the decision is memoized.
- Independent review: three rounds (correctness, tests/probe/mutation, reuse, quality, efficiency); findings — disabled-by-path being ignored, then over-matching across tiers — fixed and re-reviewed.

## Maintainer notes

- User-visible: a same-tier ambiguous name no longer gets a bare slash command (`/dup-demo` → `/skill a/one`); a local copy that used to be shadowed into unloadability now loads; external skills are labelled "external".
- Two different skills with the same name in two `external_dirs` (same tier) are listed and loaded only by path.
- Follow-ups not in this PR: the CLI/TUI partial-preload warning is covered through the shared formatter's oneshot test only; a collision log line prints twice on partial preload; `_scan_skill_md` could read catalog entries directly (would change slash-command description truncation).
- Overlapping open PRs: #64453 and #132310 (superseded — partial fixes of the same issue); #112180, #100719, #115126 (same-root dedupe / categorized names — covered by the path rows and same-root rank here); #117727 and #103796 (alternative opt-in policies — made unnecessary by a fixed precedence); #108454 (prompt-size attribution, orthogonal).

Skill Sync (`hermes sync`) is removed from core, along with the org-shared skill mirror it fed. It only ever worked against a Nous Portal sync plane that was never made publicly available, so no install has used it.

## Changes
- Deleted `hermes sync`, `tools/skills_sync_client.py`, `skills_sync_client_org.py`, `skills_sync_client_wire.py` and their test file.
- Deleted the personal and org pull ticks from gateway housekeeping, classic CLI startup and `hermes serve` maintenance, plus the debounced push after `skill_manage` writes.
- Deleted the per-skill `sync` usage flag (`set_sync` / `is_sync_enabled`).
- Deleted the `skills/_org/<org_id>/` mirror: `.active_org` index gating, the `[org-shared]` and name-collision labels in the skills index, the org provenance header and `org_provenance` field on `skill_view`, the org delete guard, and the auto-propose `org_sharing` note on `skill_manage`.
- Docs: dropped the Skill Sync mentions in `curator.md` and `multi-profile-gateways.md`.

No new hooks or plugin surface. An earlier version of this PR moved sync into a private plugin behind a new `on_maintenance_tick` hook; with no users, the feature is simply removed instead. The code stays in the private NousResearch/hermes-skill-sync repo if it comes back.

## Validation
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `hermes sync status` (real CLI, temp home) | rc=2, "'sync' is not a `hermes` command" |
| `hermes skills list` (real CLI, temp home) | local skill listed, unchanged |
| Real `hermes chat` turn (OpenRouter, gemini-2.5-flash) loading a local skill | `skill_view` returned the skill content (no `org_provenance` field), model followed it |
| Prompt builder, skill utils/usage/manager/batch, skills tool, multiplex cache scope, housekeeping profile scope, serve and CLI maintenance tests | 244 passed |
| ruff, no-`/tmp`, Windows footguns, doc links | clean |

## Infographic
![Skill Sync removed from core](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aacfbe5/rJj5vwfCcMMeT1MUxqM4L_MlJPfVXS.png)

items.body:
Home Assistant (gateway platform + `homeassistant` toolset) leaves core for the official catalog plugin **`homeassistant`** ([NousResearch/hermes-homeassistant](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-homeassistant) @ `ba30cb0` (2.0.1)), and every profile that used it gets the plugin installed automatically — same names, config keys and env vars, no reconfiguration.

## Infographic

![Home Assistant leaves core](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aacf1af/8hlIRE2-s2N9YsrzBnb-g_xGkxQhIE.png)

## Changes

- **Removed from core:** `plugins/platforms/homeassistant/`, `tools/homeassistant_tool.py`, their tests (moved to the plugin repo), the `homeassistant` / `hermes-homeassistant` toolsets, `Platform.HOMEASSISTANT`, the `HASS_TOKEN` env-enable row, the `homeassistant` pip extra (+ `uv.lock`), the locale key, and every hardcoded HA entry (webhook/cron delivery lists, dump, setup summary, `hermes tools` row and HASS_TOKEN auto-enable, dashboard platform card + env keys, ACP/parallel-safe tool lists, v3 metrics schema enums, local-env blocklist rows).
- **Migration — `hermes_cli/left_core_migration.py`:** a generic "left core" table (`LEFT_CORE`: catalog plugin + read-only "this home uses it" predicate) reusing the memory-provider migration's helpers (install command, consent, labels, grouped dependency answers). Home Assistant is the first row. Runs from `hermes update` for every profile home sharing the venv (`source_build.py`), and lazily once per process at agent start (`_load_tools`, before the tool snapshot) and gateway start (before the runner loads platform config). Installs go through `dashboard_install_plugin(catalog_name=…)` at the reviewed pin; unattended dependency consent only for these core-shipped rows. Every outcome (installed / failed / not in catalog / lazy installs off) reaches terminal, Desktop and chat; a gateway-start outcome is queued for that home's first agent.
- **Predicate ("had it enabled")** — what made core run HA for a home: `HASS_TOKEN` in its `.env` (it enabled both adapter and tools), the platform on in its gateway config as the gateway loader merges it (legacy `gateway.json`, `gateway.platforms` / `platforms` / `gateway.homeassistant` blocks; last explicit `enabled` wins; a stored token without any `enabled` counts), or `homeassistant` / `hermes-homeassistant` selected in `platform_toolsets` / `toolsets`. At startup a `HASS_TOKEN` from the process environment (systemd/Docker) also counts. An already-installed plugin dir (enabled or not) is never reinstalled, but still gets the one-time toolset-scope conversion.
- **New generic `PlatformEntry` seams** (HA is the consumer; the plugin feature-detects them so it still loads on older cores): `trusted_inbound` (allowlist/pairing bypass for an event-bus platform; replaces the HA name check in `authz_mixin`), `display_tier` (built-in display defaults; replaces the HA row in `display_config`), `shared_env_prefixes` (profile-clone "shared with tools" ownership rule; replaces the HA rows in `profile_channels`). Cron delivery uses the existing `cron_deliver_env_var` seam (`HASS_HOME_CHANNEL`).
- **Catalog:** `plugin-catalog/homeassistant.yaml` lands separately in #132476 — official, NousResearch, `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.5"` (this checkout's `base_version`; a floor of the not-yet-cut next release would make the loader refuse the plugin on every main build until the cut).
- **Docs:** `user-guide/messaging/homeassistant.md` (+ zh-Hans) rewritten as install-from-catalog with the migration note; every other mention fixed; seams documented in `adding-platform-adapters.md`; `plugins/AGENTS.md` records the left-core table.

Behaviour change worth knowing: like every plugin tool, the `ha_*` tools now sit behind Tool Search (`tool_search`/`tool_call`) when it is on, instead of being in the direct tool array.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| (1) Fixture home with HA on **origin/main** | platform registered; `ha_list_entities/get_state/list_services/call_service` in tool list; `ha_list_entities` → 2 entities from a local fake HA |
| (2a) Same home on this branch, before migration | platform not registered, no HA tools |
| (2b) Update path `migrate_all_homes()` | `[profile 'default'] ✓ Home Assistant moved out of core — installed the 'homeassistant' plugin from the catalog …`; plugin enabled; platform back (`trusted_inbound: True`, `display_tier: minimal`), same 4 tool names, `ha_list_entities` → fake HA |
| (2c) Lazy path, real `hermes gateway run` | `WARNING hermes_cli.left_core_migration: ✓ Home Assistant moved out of core …` → `✓ homeassistant connected`; fake HA log: `WS auth ok=True`, `WS subscribe_events event_type=state_changed` |
| (2d) Lazy path, `AIAgent(platform="telegram")` | plugin installed during init; sticky `success` chat notice queued; `tool_call ha_list_entities` → fake HA; second agent: 0 notices |
| (3) Control home without HA | `recover_at_startup` → `[]`, no notices; update path prints nothing |
| (4) Profiles A (HA) / B (none) + default (none) | only `[profile 'hapa']` migrated; B and default have no plugins |
| `ha_*` platform tool selection | `homeassistant` on for platform `homeassistant`, `cron`, `cli` with and without `platform_toolsets: {homeassistant: [hermes-homeassistant]}` |
| Terminal child env (main vs branch) | `HASS_TOKEN`/`HASS_URL` invisible to `terminal` children on both (installed plugin's manifest secrets) |
| Plugin repo | 60 passed / 2 skipped against this branch; `hermes plugins validate` → `Validation passed` (no collisions, safe, no core override) |
| `validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/homeassistant.yaml` | `OK: 1 file(s) valid` |
| Unit tests | `test_left_core_migration.py` (predicate matrix, install/fail/miss/present, two-profile grouping, lazy opt-out, gateway→agent notice hand-off), `test_platform_entry_plugin_seams.py`, profile-clone `shared_env_prefixes` test with a real user plugin; all pass |
| Touched-dir suites (`scripts/run_tests.sh`, fake HOME) | gateway 9122✓ / 1✗, tools 9729✓ / 3✗, agent+cron+acp+plugins+security+scripts+root 15969✓ / 12✗, hermes_cli 14007✓ / 91✗. Every failure is environmental and reproduces on origin/main in the same fake HOME or is a missing toolchain (`uv`, `fal_client`, `parallel-web`, dev-shell toolchain, home-I/O guard); the 8 hermes_cli and 10 plugin-file stragglers from the loaded run pass when re-run alone (165✓ / 13✓) |

Catalog note for the probes: the production docs site only carries the new entry after this merges, so the live probes served `plugin-catalog.json` built from this branch by `website/scripts/extract-plugins.py` (what the docs deploy publishes) on 127.0.0.1 and pointed `LIVE_CATALOG_URL` at it. Until the deploy, a migrating user sees the "not in the plugin catalog yet" notice and the lazy path retries on the next start. The fake HA is a ~50-line aiohttp REST+WebSocket stub (no real Home Assistant available).

Desktop: untouched. Its messaging-source list, icon and setup hint are cosmetic tables keyed by platform name (already missing most plugin platforms); the plugin keeps the `homeassistant` name, so they still apply.

Credit: the moved code's authors are credited via Co-authored-by trailers on the plugin repo's initial commit (Teknium, kshitijk4poor, ethernet, 0xbyt4, xxxigm, Jay Stothard, tachyon-r, dippwho, charliekerfoot, Jeeves Assistant, Dusk1e).


## Independent review follow-ups
- `HASS_TOKEN` stays stripped from child processes even when the plugin is not installed (each left-core row lists env core keeps stripping). Live: leaked on the previous head, stripped now.
- HA tools stay off on platforms where core had them off (explicit saved toolset lists without HA, acp, webhook); probe across 5 configs x 8 platforms matches main exactly.
- Every profile a multiplex gateway serves is migrated in its own scope before its adapters start. Live: secondary-only HA profile got the plugin and its adapter connected in the same start.
- A user plugin cannot set `trusted_inbound` on a platform core ships; `hermes plugins validate` prints the flag.
- Plugin 2.0.1 (`ba30cb0`) stays inactive on a core that still bundles HA (no shadow warnings), and carries the ported multiplex endpoint-scope tests.

Land order: this PR → #132476 (catalog entry; its pinned-source validation needs core's `ha_*` tools gone) → manual `deploy-site.yml` dispatch so the live catalog lists `homeassistant`. Until the redeploy, migrating users see a retryable "not in the catalog yet" notice.

Product trade-off kept: `ha_*` are plugin tools now, so they sit behind Tool Search (one extra round trip on first use) and lose the parallel-safe flag.

## Second review follow-ups (F1 / F3 / F4 at `f645a96`)
Each reproduced red on `f645a96` with a real-filesystem probe (fake HOME, real imports, no mocks), then fixed with one invariant test proven red on `f645a96`.

| Finding | Fix | Before (f645a96) | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1: in-use detection missed configs the gateway loader enabled | `f8e1d19a526` — `platform_configured_on()` reuses `load_legacy_gateway_json` + `read_yaml_layers` + `merge_platform_sections` (new `also=` so the `gateway.<platform>` shorthand counts before the plugin registers) + `PlatformConfig.from_dict` | gateway.json enable, `gateway.homeassistant`, nested+top-level merge → `in_use=False`, 0 notices; `gateway.homeassistant.enabled: false` over a nested enable → in use | all 4 in use with a notice; config.yaml `enabled: false` over gateway.json and shorthand disable over nested stay not-in-use |
| F3: preinstalled plugin skipped the toolset-scope conversion | `f0273f6650a` — conversion is separate from install: runs once per home and row, plugin present or not, completion recorded as `_left_core_scoped` in the same config.yaml write | real plugin 2.0.1 installed with `hermes plugins install --ref ba30cb0`, `telegram: [web]`: HA on for telegram / acp / webhook | off for all three, on for cli; after the user enables HA on telegram via the tools-save path, update + startup re-runs keep it on |
| F4: channel-less clone kept HA identity while the plugin is absent | `caa3bccf34d` — `LEFT_CORE` rows declare `enable_env` + `channel_env_prefixes`; `profile_channels` folds them into platform ids, the shared-prefix rule, the enable gate and the credential inventory, plugin installed or not | real `hermes profile create s5ha2-* --clone/--clone-all --no-alias`: HASS_TOKEN/HASS_URL kept (flat, shorthand, env-only, clone-all), `gateway.homeassistant` block kept | stripped in all four; tool-only source (`enabled: false`) keeps HASS_* as a tool key; real-plugin control strips; model key kept; source untouched |

Plugin unchanged (`ba30cb0`); `hermes plugins validate` passes against this branch. Touched-dir suites (`tests/hermes_cli tests/gateway`, fake HOME): 23170 passed / 92 failed; the same 92 fail with this round's three source files swapped back (missing `uv`, home-I/O guard on the fake-home test store), and the one extra row (`test_update_check_clean`, a 30 s load timeout) passes alone.

items.body:
Adds `homeassistant` to the plugin catalog: the Home Assistant gateway platform and the `ha_*` tools as a standalone official plugin (NousResearch/hermes-homeassistant @ f272c96).

- `plugin-catalog/homeassistant.yaml` only. Catalog-entry PRs must touch nothing else (`pinned-source-validate`), so this is split out of #132469.
- The plugin keeps every name core used: platform `homeassistant`, toolset `homeassistant`, tools `ha_list_entities` / `ha_get_state` / `ha_list_services` / `ha_call_service`, env `HASS_TOKEN` / `HASS_URL`.
- #132469 removes the bundled copy from core and migrates every profile that used Home Assistant onto this entry (on `hermes update`, and lazily at agent/gateway start).

`scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` → OK. `hermes plugins validate` on the pinned plugin is clean.

## Infographic

![Home Assistant joins the plugin catalog](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aacf288/pQk2WqFfTW6ic7AjG_REQ_65UR5vzs.png)

## What does this PR do?
Adds the community mistral-vibe model-provider plugin to the plugin catalog, pinned to the exact commit SHA of v1.1.0 (c0d7bc8d11306e18499c84dd94cc3581de550e55).

Submitted by the plugin's author. The plugin provides direct Mistral Vibe subscription access:

Browser PKCE login (hermes auth add mistral-vibe) with a dedicated credential pool — never MISTRAL_API_KEY, no internal model substitution
Account-visible catalog discovery via read-only GET /v1/models, filtered on capabilities.completion_chat
Relay-verified reasoning_effort for GLM models (v1.1.0): top-level wire field, per-model vocabularies verified live, nearest-weaker clamping, fail-closed on unverified models — without it, hybrid reasoning models silently run at the relay's deepest default effort
Security posture: fixed origins, no redirects/env proxies/SDK retries, guarded client, offline test suite (30 tests, socket-blocked, TDD)
No Python dependencies, no self-updater. It's the standalone-provider route the maintainers pointed to when declining in-tree integration (#63060).

## Type of Change

 ✨ New feature (catalog entry only; no Hermes code changes)
Changes Made
plugin-catalog/mistral-vibe.yaml: the new entry. Capabilities match what the plugin registers at the pinned commit.
contributors/emails/46002544+nebneo@users.noreply.github.com: maps the commit author email to nebneo for the Contributor Attribution Check.
How to Test
python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/ — passes (405 files valid)
Clone https://github.com/nebneo/hermes-mistral-vibe at the pinned SHA and run hermes plugins validate . — all checks pass, security scan safe, SHA reachable from main
hermes plugins install mistral-vibe --enable on a clean HERMES_HOME, then hermes auth add mistral-vibe → hermes model shows the provider

## Checklist

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide (third-party integrations ship as standalone plugins)
- [x] Commit message follows Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched existing PRs; this isn't a duplicate
- [x] This PR contains only the catalog entry and the contributor email mapping
- [x] Tested on Linux (Ubuntu, kernel 7.0)
- [x] Documentation: the README at the pinned SHA documents install, auth, and limitations

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Launcher publication resolved its interpreter through `store_root()`, which returns an inherited `HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR` before anything else. A process started with that variable aimed at an e2e fixture home under `cache/scratch` (or any other short-lived store) that reached `stage_launcher` rewrote the real install's `.hermes/bin/hermes` and `hermes-acp` to exec the fixture's Python. Idle pruning later deleted that tree, and after the next reboot the gateway unit exited 127 forever.

Publication now binds the tree's own recorded store. The inherited runtime directory is used only when the tree records no store of its own. That keeps the environments that legitimately keep their whole store beside `HERMES_HOME` working (the desktop source-backend contract, the documented dev setup). Execution-side resolution still honors the override.

`HERMES_HOME` alone was not the trigger: a fixture home under `~/.hermes` still resolves `get_default_hermes_root()` to `~/.hermes`, so only the runtime override could point publication at the fixture's store.

## Related Issue

Fixes #131745
Salvages #131994

## Changes Made

- `pm/environments.py`: `store_root(..., honor_runtime_override=False)` resolves the tree's store without the inherited override (from 686f6c61's branch).
- `hermes_cli/_launchers.py`: `resolve_store_python(..., publication=True)` prefers the tree's own store and falls back to the override only when the tree records none. `stage_launcher`, `expose_cli` and the `_launchers.py` CLI entry use it.
- `hermes_cli/gateway.py`: the service-launcher publication gate asks the same question as `stage_launcher`.
- Tests in `tests/hermes_cli/test_source_launcher_publication.py`:
  - `stage_launcher` and `_prepare_service_launcher` bind the tree store under a foreign `HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR` (686f6c61)
  - runtime selection still honors the override (686f6c61)
  - the issue's exact `cache/scratch/hermes-e2e-*/hermes-home/tools` layout through `ensure_install_launchers` (adapted from #131994)
  - a tree with no store still publishes from the runtime store

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_launch_completion.py`: the `resolve_store_python` stubs accept keywords. On the cherry-picked commit alone, 6 of these tests raised `TypeError`.

## How to Test

`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_source_launcher_publication.py tests/hermes_cli/test_launcher_runtime_selection.py tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_service.py`: 138 passed, 13 skipped.

RED, new tests over each production state:

| prod code | failing new tests |
|---|---|
| main | 3 (scratch layout, `stage_launcher` foreign store, service launcher) |
| #131994 | the same 3 (a foreign store outside `cache/scratch` still rebinds) |
| 686f6c61's commit alone | 1 (no-own-store fallback) |
| this branch | 0 |

The desktop contract fixture `apps/desktop/electron/fixtures/source-backend.py` (`HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR` beside `HERMES_HOME`) passes on main and on this branch, and fails `assert launchers` on 686f6c61's commit alone.

## Prior work and credit

- #131994 (@liuhao1024): refused publication when the store sat under `cache/scratch` and the repo did not. That catches the reported layout but not the cause: a foreign store anywhere else (for example a `/tmp` e2e home) still rebound the launchers, and the gateway gate still honored the override. Its fixture layout became a regression test here.
- @686f6c61's `fix/131745-launcher-scratch` (77370d46, comment on #131745): diagnosed the inherited `HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR` and added the publication-only resolution plus tests. Cherry-picked with authorship kept. The follow-up adds the no-own-store fallback, because ignoring the override outright broke the desktop source-backend contract.
- @Christopher-Schulze's branch (39251006/d7ddd2e): a path-ownership scratch refusal plus 686f6c61's commit. Not used: the merged `gateway.py` passes `honor_runtime_override` to a `resolve_store_python` that lacks the keyword, so 8 tests fail with `TypeError`.

## Not in scope

- `venv_sync.publish_launchers` keeps its existing gate. It can now only produce a louder "publication failed" in a mixed environment, never a foreign-bound launcher.
- Self-healing an already-corrupted launcher (the issue's suggestions 2 and 3) is a separate change.

items.body:
## Why

Under the host multiplexer, WhatsApp runs only for the profile that launched the gateway. A secondary profile with `WHATSAPP_ENABLED=true` and its own paired phone is skipped with one INFO line (`gateway/run_adapters.py`, the `Platform.RELAY, Platform.WHATSAPP` shared-ingress skip from febd2af391).

That skip assumed a secondary has no WhatsApp credential of its own. It does: the session directory is `get_hermes_dir("platforms/whatsapp/session")`, which is relative to each profile's home, so every profile already has its own paired session. What actually collides is the bridge port (3000 for every profile) and `connect()`, which adopts any healthy bridge on that port or kills whatever node process holds it. Under multiplex, that would be the default profile's bridge.

## Changed

This is #122758 rebased onto current `main`, plus one follow-up commit.

- **#122758 (cherry-picked, authorship kept):** the WhatsApp credential is the profile's own `creds.json`, checked in that profile's scope. An unpaired secondary is reported once as `whatsapp_unpaired` with `hermes -p <name> whatsapp`. A paired secondary gets its own adapter on its own port. The port is an explicit `platforms.whatsapp.extra.bridge_port`, or else allocated from 3001..3999 and recorded in `platforms/whatsapp/bridge_port`. A secondary never port-scans or kills anything; it adopts or reaps only a bridge that its own pidfile identifies by pid and kernel start time. Out-of-process sends read the same record. Relay stays shared ingress.
  - Conflicts with `main` resolved: kept main's `pm.ensure("node")` preamble in `connect()` and main's `utf-8-sig` pidfile read (moved into the shared `_read_bridge_pidfile`), and kept the `gateway.standalone` note for Relay in the multi-profile docs.
- **Follow-up:**
  - Allocation skips ports that another profile's record already claims. Before, a sibling whose bridge was down left its port unbound, a newly paired profile took it, and the second of the two to start hit a non-retryable `whatsapp_bridge_conflict` on every restart (reported by @Enough1122 on #122758).
  - A non-numeric record now names the record file and says to delete it, instead of surfacing `int()`'s "invalid literal" message.
  - The secondary `connect()` tests stub `find_node_executable`. Since main added the Node preamble, they returned before reaching the secondary path wherever Node isn't on `PATH`.
  - **Adoption is bound to the port.** Before, a secondary treated a bound port as `ours` whenever its pidfile named a live bridge, even if that bridge listened somewhere else. Case: a crash leaves the old bridge alive, then `bridge_port` is pointed at a port another profile's bridge holds. The secondary probed and adopted the foreign bridge, because script hash and read-receipt config don't tell phones apart. `bridge.pid` now records the spawn port on line 3, and `ours` requires pid, start time and port to match. Pidfiles without a port fail closed for secondaries. The default path still reads only lines 1–2.
  - **One port resolution for launch and send.** A profile that recorded a port as a secondary and later launched its own gateway started its bridge on 3000, while `whatsapp send` read the record. The launch adapter now resolves its port the same way standalone send does: explicit config, then the record, then 3000. Profiles without a record are unchanged.
  - `gateway/AGENTS.md` no longer lists the WhatsApp bridge as default-only shared ingress.

## Tests

- `tests/gateway/test_whatsapp_multiplex.py::test_allocation_skips_ports_recorded_by_siblings` (new). Run against each version of `bridge_ownership.py`:
  - salvage: passes
  - #122758: fails (only this test)
  - `main`: helper absent, so this allocator-specific test cannot run there. Separately, the paired-secondary startup test fails behaviorally on main (`connected == 1`, expected 2).
- `test_live_old_bridge_does_not_authorize_a_different_port` and `test_launch_startup_and_standalone_send_agree_after_role_change` (new) fail without the follow-up and pass with it. `test_ownership_verdicts` now also covers wrong-port and port-less pidfiles.
- Independent reviewer probe, real processes and listeners. Before: `verdict: ours`, adopted the foreign bridge (`CONNECT_TO_FOREIGN True`), launch port 3000 vs send port 3003. After: ownership refused, no HTTP probe sent, launch and send both use 3003.
- WhatsApp multiplex, adapter-registry, shared-ingress, send-media, pidfile, stale-bridge and connect suites: 89 passed, 3 skipped.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/ tests/tools/ tests/plugins/platforms/ tests/hermes_cli/`, compared with `main`: main: 33,236 passed, 18 failed, 542 skipped; salvage (head `fd97ca89fa2`): 33,248 passed, 18 failed, 542 skipped. No salvage-only failed test IDs in the captured logs (19 shared IDs across initial attempts/retries). These broad runs are not fully green.

Not verified live: there is no second paired phone on the test host. #122758's boot-level proof (fake `HOME`, dummy port-3000 holder survives, alpha gets 3001, unpaired beta reported once) covers the startup path.

## Not in scope

- `hermes -p X whatsapp send` for a secondary that has never started still falls back to port 3000, the default profile's bridge (unchanged from `main`).
- Bridge session identity in `/health`: #115603. That is a stronger identity check, and it would also cover the default path. This PR binds secondary adoption to pid, start time and port without changing `bridge.js`. The two compose.

## Prior work and credit

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

A launch of a source checkout under another data root (a test's temporary `HERMES_HOME`, a per-task home, a CI service home) rebinds the checkout's shared `.hermes/bin` launchers to that root's store Python. Once the root is deleted, every `hermes` on the host fails with `cannot execute: No such file or directory`. The same launch also downloads a full tool store (~0.5 GB) into the temporary root and runs the checkout's update tail (product rebuilds, stamp rewrite) against the shared tree.

**Root cause.** Dependency state and the store are scoped to whichever data root `HERMES_HOME` selects (`installs_root()`, and `store_root()` falling back to `get_default_hermes_root()/"tools"` for source stamps, which never carry `runtimeDir`). The checkout, its launchers and its stamp exist only once. So a non-owning root treats the checkout as its own fresh install, and `prepare_launch()` republishes the launchers whenever the store Python differs from `sys.executable` (`venv_sync.py`, `if not current or not same: publish_launchers(root)`).

Two layers:

1. **Launcher guard** (@Finn763, #123887, cherry-picked unchanged). `ensure_install_launchers()` keeps an existing checkout launcher that execs a *live* interpreter outside the launching root's store. Missing launchers, dead interpreters and same-store repins still publish. An install laid out as `<home>/hermes-agent` with `<home>/tools` republishes when the active root owns the checkout, which heals checkouts that were already rebound.
2. **Ownership** (@Froraut, from #128579). `pm.environments.owning_home_root()` finds the root that installed the checkout among the roots holding `facts.json` for it (the root the checkout sits in, and the platform default root). A borrower's own sync writes `facts.json` too, so that alone cannot decide. The owner is the one whose `tools/` holds the live interpreter the checkout's `hermes` launcher execs. A borrower cannot rebind that launcher: the guard keeps a live foreign launcher, `prepare_launch()` never publishes for a borrower, and the layout-based heal path in `ensure_install_launchers()` (`<home>/hermes-agent` with `<home>/tools`) now also requires the active root to own the checkout, so `HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR=<home>/tools` on a borrower cannot reach it. With no live launcher, the root the checkout sits in wins.
   - `store_root()` resolves an unstamped store to that owner's `tools/`, so a borrowing root downloads no tool store.
   - `prepare_launch()` syncs only the borrowing root's own dependency generation. It never arms or runs the tail, never publishes launchers, and never touches the owner's markers.
   - Owners, their profiles, fresh installs and custom roots that own their tree keep today's behaviour. `HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR` and a stamped `runtimeDir` still win.

The guard still matters when no owner can be discovered, for example a checkout outside any root that holds state for it.

## Related Issue

Fixes #123238
Salvages #123887
Salvages #128579 (in part; its macOS update-panel commits stay on that PR)

## Prior work and credit

- #123887 by @Finn763: the launcher guard, plus review fixes for the dead `.exe` shadow, the `own is None` keep and the distlib CRLF shebang. All three commits are cherry-picked with authorship. @bmetcalf21's review suggestions are in `81c8bf7`.
- #128579 by @Froraut: the borrowed-home ownership commit and its Windows test fix, cherry-picked. Its two macOS update-panel commits (elapsed clock, "Applying code changes" stage) are unrelated to this issue and are left out. #128579 stays open for them.
- @bmetcalf21 reported #123238 with the root-cause analysis. @artyficialmind, @adrax0509 and @get6 supplied the CI-runner, tool-store/OOM and lock data points. @Enough1122 and @whyyagswhy reviewed.

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/_launchers.py`: `_launcher_python()`, `_kept_shared_launcher()` and the guard in `ensure_install_launchers()` (#123887).
- `pm/environments.py`: `owning_home_root()`, `_unstamped_store()` (#128579).
- `hermes_cli/venv_sync.py`: `_prepare_borrowed_launch()`; `_sync_source_dependencies(borrowed_from=...)` keeps the owner's markers (#128579).
- `contributors/emails/finn@example.com`: maps the first #123887 commit's author email to Finn763, which the attribution gate requires.
- `pm/environments.py` follow-ups: `_launcher_bound_root()` picks the owner by the checkout launcher's interpreter, with the parent root as fallback. Without them, a borrower's own first sync wrote `facts.json` and became the "owner" on the next launch, in both layouts: a custom-root checkout launched from the default root, and a default-root checkout kept in `install.sh --dir <dir>` launched with `HERMES_HOME=<dir>`.
- `hermes_cli/_launchers.py` follow-up: the heal path that skips the guard for an `<home>/hermes-agent` + `<home>/tools` layout now also requires `owning_home_root()` to report the active root as the owner. Without it, an explicit `sync` from a borrower with `HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR=<home>/tools` rebound the shared launchers.
- `hermes_cli/_launchers.py` follow-up: `_launcher_python()` lexes a POSIX wrapper's interpreter with `shlex` (first token only). The writer quotes with `shlex.join`, so an owner path with an apostrophe read back truncated, the live launcher looked dead and was republished to the borrower.
- Tests trimmed to the invariant contracts AGENTS.md asks for. The guard tests now carry `platforms("any")`, and the dead-`.exe` regression runs under `platforms("windows")`, so the Windows lane exercises them.

## How to Test

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_hermes_home_shared_launchers.py tests/hermes_cli/test_borrowed_home_launch.py
```

- On main, `test_temp_home_prepare_launch_relaunches_without_rebinding` fails: a temp-home launch rewrites the shared launcher bytes. `test_borrowed_home_launch.py` fails to import because `owning_home_root` does not exist yet.
- Reverting only `_launchers.py` fails the rebinding test. Reverting only `venv_sync.py` fails `test_a_borrowing_launch_syncs_its_own_dependencies_and_nothing_of_the_checkout`. Reverting only the store fallback fails that test and `test_a_borrowers_own_dependency_state_never_makes_it_the_owner`. Reverting only the launcher-based owner check, or only the owner condition on the heal path, fails `test_a_borrower_holding_the_checkout_never_becomes_its_owner`.
- Related suites (`tests/pm/` plus the launcher, venv-sync, update-launch, runtime-path and gateway-service files; 129 files) give 1141 passed, 10 failed and 8 setup errors. Those 18 ids are identical on unmodified main (network and tool-bootstrap tests in this environment).
- `ruff` is clean, `check-windows-footguns.py --all` is clean, and `audit_pr_attribution.py` reports all emails mapped.

## Not in scope

- @get6's per-task homes whose `installs` symlink back to the owner count as the owner and still take the per-home update lock. A lock keyed to install state would serialize them, but that lock is shared with Desktop update detection. Follow-up.
- #131745 (launcher bound to an e2e scratch store) is fixed on main by #132512 (`2c79189`, `a4648c5`): publication prefers the tree's own store over an inherited `HERMES_RUNTIME_DIR`. This PR rebases onto it cleanly and composes with it: the unstamped store fallback here is what that own-store lookup resolves to, so a borrowing launch publishes nothing of its own and the checkout keeps the owner's interpreter.

## Infographic

![borrowed-homes-safe-launchers](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aacf90c/gJtopYWUGypUNBoLVf0jK_N71Dn5aY.png)

## What changed between the pins (v0.1.0 → v0.2.0)

From the repo's commit log (`git log v0.1.0..v0.2.0`, no CHANGELOG file in the repo):

- Requires `gonogo-eval>=0.3,<0.4` — gonogo 0.3 semantics (grouped pairing, non-degenerate paired interval); 0.2 is not compatible. This is a dependency-range bump, not a code vendoring change.

- `gonogo_compare` reports the trial unit (cases or groups) and requires explicit stable ids on raw rows; a saved plugin report with generated ids is refused for comparison (`metadata.ids_source`).
- Strict input validation: `passed` must be a JSON boolean (`bool("false")` is `True`); scores must be finite; target/level are validated when present rather than silently defaulted; mixed missing/present confidence is rejected; all JSON output is emitted with `allow_nan=False`.
- Decision payload separates `n_passed` (cases) from `n_trials_passed` (trials) so grouped runs are not misread.
- README: ecosystem map (one loop, four repos) with the gonogo README as the root; catalog mirror file kept next to the code it pins.

Manifest surface unchanged from the pinned v0.1.0 entry: same 3 tools (`gonogo_decide`, `gonogo_report`, `gonogo_compare`), 0 hooks, `requires_env: []`. The catalog entry changes only `sha:` and `version:`.

items.body:
Desktop now runs new and resumed sessions on the gateway you picked, so choosing This device in the quick-selector no longer sends the next chat to Home server (#132235).

Salvage of #132237 by @unsupportedpastels: their eight commits are cherry-picked onto current `main` with authorship intact, plus one follow-up commit from us.

## Changes

From #132237 (@unsupportedpastels):
- A pinned new-chat route (from a gateway-group `+`) is cleared when a gateway switch commits, so the next chat runs on the source you switched to. A newer draft is not re-homed by a late switch.
- Project-tree session rows carry their registry source, so opening one routes to its owner.
- Resuming a session while This device is the active registry secondary keeps This device as the owner instead of falling back to the primary.
- A failed RPC is never replayed on a different gateway than the one it was sent to.
- The primary socket reconnects to its own recorded route instead of the foreground route. A reconnect lookup that a connection apply replaced is dropped (Nandoca95's review).

Follow-up (ours, from dokterdok's review of #132237):
- `useGatewayRequest` primary recovery only publishes, clears or dials while the primary still owns the foreground (it checks the gateway activation epoch). Before this, a late profile-less lookup could write its answer over the newer source's descriptor, or a failed lookup could clear it, so REST and filesystem helpers went to the old backend.
- Both primary reconnect paths re-check ownership after the WebSocket ticket mint as well as after the route lookup. An apply that landed during the mint, with its own socket already dropped, could otherwise re-dial the gateway the user had just left (independent review finding).
- Doc fix: the owner-stamp helper now names the `local`-as-secondary exception that `stampProjectSessions` handles.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Vitest: gateway hooks, connection/project stores, session actions (39 files) | 719/719 pass |
| The 6 production files swapped back to `main` | 15 of the new regression tests fail |
| Our recovery tests against the #132237 head | descriptor test fails both cases (stale descriptor published / cleared); post-mint tests fail (boot dials the old primary URL, request recovery dials the primary). All pass with the fixes |
| `npm run check:lint` (typecheck + eslint) | clean |

**Live repro:** a real Desktop build (Electron under Playwright, headless ozone) with two real gateways: the app's own local backend and a second `hermes serve --isolated` registered as "Home server". Both run a real model (OpenRouter `google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite`). Evidence is read from each gateway's own `state.db`.

| Scenario | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| On Home server, click the Home group's `+` (All profiles, grouped by gateway & profile), quick-select **This device**, send | lands in **Home's** state.db; the status bar flips back to Home server | lands in **This device's** state.db; the status bar stays on This device |
| Back to Home server, New session, send | Home | Home |
| Control: Home as primary, chat on This device, resume it from the sidebar, send a follow-up | same local session | same local session |

The other mechanisms (project-tree tags, untagged resume, cross-gateway replay, reconnect and recovery races) are timing- or topology-specific and are covered by the regression tests above, not driven live.

Root cause: several new-chat, resume, replay and reconnect paths resolved their target from a stale pinned route, an untagged row, or the current foreground, not from the session's owner.

Closes #132235. Supersedes #132237.

## Infographic

![Sessions follow your gateway](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aacf8b6/qywB9kJkxFh1Z2JjmreiC_vN1ogHsM.png)

items.body:
## Why

Two profiles that run separate gateways on one host both default to WhatsApp `bridge_port` 3000, each with its own profile-scoped session directory. The second profile to start probes the port and finds the first profile's bridge. `/health` never said which session a bridge serves, so `_reuse_running_bridge` either:

- **adopts** it, when the script hash and read-receipt setting match. Profile B then answers as profile A's phone.
- **kills** it, when the bridge is starting, reconnecting or waiting on a QR code (`status: disconnected`). `_kill_port_process` checks only that the listener is a `node` process.

#132518 gave multiplexed secondaries their own ports and pid/start-time/port ownership. The launch-profile path still adopts or clears port 3000 without knowing whose bridge holds it, and that #132518 body names #115603 as the missing identity check.

## Changed

This is #115603 cherry-picked onto current `main` with authorship kept, plus three follow-up commits.

- **#115603 (@victor-kyriazakos):** bridge `/health` reports `session`, its absolute session directory (`path.resolve`, no symlink resolution, to match Python's `os.path.abspath`). The adapter normalizes `session_path` once at construction and checks `session` before the status and hash checks. A bridge serving another session is never adopted and never killed; `connect()` fails non-retryably with `whatsapp_bridge_foreign_session`, naming the port, the other session and `platforms.whatsapp.extra.bridge_port`.
  - Conflicts with `main` resolved: kept #132518's `standalone_bridge_port()` resolution in `__init__` and its secondary-aware reaping in `connect()`. The foreign-session fatal sits ahead of both.
- **Follow-up:**
  - Dropped the separate "no `session` -> restart" branch. A bridge without the field runs an older `bridge.js`, so its `scriptHash` already marks it stale.
  - Inlined `sessionIdentity()` as `path.resolve()` and dropped its node test. That test only exercised `path.resolve`, and no CI lane runs `scripts/whatsapp-bridge/*.test.mjs`.
  - Folded the four adapter cells into one parametrized invariant, per the AGENTS.md salvage bar. The existing read-receipt test now reports its own session, so it still restarts for the read-receipt reason rather than for a missing field.
  - Docs: moved the separate-gateway guidance into the existing "Multiple profiles" section instead of keeping a second multi-profile section.
- **Ownership gaps found in review:**
  - A port holder that does not answer `/health` within 2s, whether it stalls on the headers or on the JSON body, no longer falls through to `_kill_port_process`. `_probe_bridge_health` used to swallow a body-read timeout as an unparseable 200; timeouts now propagate from both phases. This profile's own stale bridge is still reaped by its pidfile. If a listener remains after that, `connect()` leaves it running and fails with the retryable `whatsapp_bridge_unresponsive`.
  - The listener check uses `_port_listener_pids()`, which is netstat on Windows and lsof/ss elsewhere, the same scan `_kill_port_process` uses. If listeners cannot be listed, nothing is killed.
  - `_standalone_send` (`hermes send --to whatsapp:<chat_id>`, cron delivery) now reads `/health` before every send, not only for mentions. It sends nothing through a bridge that reports another profile's session or whose `/health` is not a 200. A 200 without `session` (older `bridge.js`, before the gateway restarts it) is still used.
  - Docs: corrected the nonexistent `hermes whatsapp send` (also in #132518's paragraph) to `hermes send --to whatsapp:<chat_id>`.
  - The adapter and standalone sends resolve the session dir with one helper, `_session_dir()`.

## Tests

- `tests/gateway/test_whatsapp_stale_bridge.py::test_bridge_is_adopted_or_left_running_by_its_session[own-session-adopted | other-session-connected | other-session-starting | health-headers-timeout | health-body-timeout | health-body-timeout-windows]`
- `tests/tools/test_whatsapp_send_message_media.py::test_standalone_send_posts_only_through_this_profiles_bridge[own-session | other-profile-session | pre-session-bridge | health-503]`
  - `main` adapter: every foreign/unanswered cell fails, and the own-session cells pass.
  - Mutations: with the status check moved ahead of the session check, `other-session-starting` fails. With the foreign fatal disabled, both `other-session-*` cells fail. With the timeout guard removed, the timeout cells fail. With the body-read timeout swallowed again, both `health-body-timeout*` cells fail. With the guard using the POSIX-only scan, `health-body-timeout-windows` fails. With the standalone session check removed, `other-profile-session` fails, and with non-200 `/health` allowed, `health-503` fails.
  - The existing standalone tests now also assert that `/health` is checked first, on the same port.
  - The PR's own suite passes on the #115603 head (8/8).
- Real-process repro: a `node` listener stands in for profile A's bridge, and profile B's adapter is built through the real `__init__` and runs the real `connect()`, including `_kill_port_process`. Only dependency install, the session lock and B's own spawn are stubbed.

  | A's bridge | `main` | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | connected | B adopts A's bridge and starts polling it | not adopted, A alive, `whatsapp_bridge_foreign_session` |
  | disconnected | B kills A's bridge | not killed, A alive, `whatsapp_bridge_foreign_session` |
  | `/health` headers after 3s | B kills A's bridge | not killed, A alive, `whatsapp_bridge_unresponsive` |
  | headers at once, `/health` body after 3s | B kills A's bridge | not killed, A alive, `whatsapp_bridge_unresponsive` |

  A second probe ran the real `_standalone_send` from profile B against a local HTTP sink that reports profile A's session. On `main` it posts `/send` and reports success; on this branch it reads `/health` only and returns the foreign-session error without posting.
- All WhatsApp gateway/tool suites plus the multiplex adapter-registry and shared-ingress suites: 224 passed, 3 skipped (Windows-only), on the rebased head.
- Full suite, run before the rebase on base `c225c4a04e8`: 56,590 passed, 7 failed, 745 skipped. Six failures (`test_cold_runtime_e2e` ×2, `test_fresh_source_install` ×3, the `test_extract_plugins` git-dates test on git 2.43) fail identically on that base. `test_bot_relay_windows_paths::test_local_delivery_resolves_sibling_hermes` failed only because a git-ignored `.hermes/bin/hermes` launcher sat in the test checkout; it passes with that launcher moved aside. `test_lazy_secrets_dispatch::test_update_check_clean` (a real `hermes update --check` subprocess with a time limit) timed out twice and then passed. The full suite was not rerun after rebasing onto `24b9f0f8c5d`; that rebase touched no WhatsApp files.
- `ruff check` and `git diff --check` are clean.

## Not in scope

- Native Windows was not run; the Windows listener path is covered by the `health-body-timeout-windows` cell only.
- A 200 `/health` without `session` comes from a pre-upgrade `bridge.js`. Standalone sends still use it, so until the other profile's gateway restarts its bridge after the upgrade, such a bridge can still deliver for the wrong profile. Refusing it would break every standalone send between upgrading and that restart.
- #126824 / #126840 (an adopted bridge keeps its spawn-time policy) and #83395 / #83432 (bridge API authentication) touch `_reuse_running_bridge` but are separate defects. They compose with this change.

## Prior work and credit

- #115603 by @victor-kyriazakos: diagnosis, `/health` session handshake, check ordering, path normalization, tests and docs. Cherry-picked with authorship kept; co-author on the follow-up.
- @whyyagswhy independently verified #115603's head.
- #84122 by @SWOOPPMAIN removes port-based kills, which covers the kill half for unrelated listeners (#78365) but not adoption. Its principle (no kill on port ownership alone) shaped the unanswered-`/health` handling here, but no code was taken from it, and the PR stays open for #78365.

Salvages #115603
Fixes #65426

## Infographic

![one-bridge-per-session](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aacfa5e/ntqOt8s_v5FKSH-DHpDKP_smO1p82p.png)

items.body:
Loading a bundled skill (or hitting one of three tool errors) no longer puts a bare chat-role tag into the conversation, so OpenRouter stops rejecting the request — and every later turn of that session — with a 403.

Refs #132504

## What happened

Three bundled skills (an autonomous-ai-agents delegation skill, hermes-agent-skill-authoring, unreal-mcp) and the optional system-atlas skill (`SKILL.md` and `assets/data.example.mjs`) wrote their name placeholders as a bare chat-role tag. `skill_view` returns that text as-is, and OpenRouter's gateway rejects a request containing one with HTTP 403 `role_tag_injection` ("prompt injection patterns detected"). The text stays in history, so every later request in the session fails too, and the cross-provider retry hits the same 403. Three tool-error strings returned to the model as tool results used the same placeholder: the tool_call bridge "not a known tool name" hint, and the malformed connector-name error in `model_tools.py` and in the connector gateway. On main, Hermes' own skill scanner also logs a "may indicate prompt injection" warning when system-atlas loads.

## Change

- one `skills/autonomous-ai-agents/` delegation skill's `SKILL.md`, `skills/software-development/hermes-agent-skill-authoring/SKILL.md`, `optional-skills/creative/unreal-mcp/SKILL.md`: the role-tag placeholder becomes `{tool}`, the brace form already used in `hermes-agent/references/native-mcp.md` (contributor commit).
- `optional-skills/creative/system-atlas/SKILL.md` + `assets/data.example.mjs`: `docs/{system}/atlas/`.
- `tools/tool_search_validation.py::not_deferrable_error` (message and docstring), `tools/connectors/gateway/merge.py::partition_calls`, `model_tools.py` (malformed connector name): the role-tag placeholder becomes `{tool}`. Callers and tests match only the unchanged parts of these messages.
- `tests/skills/test_bundled_skill_doc_placeholders.py` (new; 2 tests):
  - scans every file under `skills/`, `optional-skills/` and `plugins/` (`.hub` excluded; 1485 files) for an open or close tool/system/assistant role tag. It decodes files the same way `skill_view`'s `_read_skill_text` does, so nothing `skill_view` can serve is skipped.
  - runs the same pattern over the rendered `not_deferrable_error` and `partition_calls` error messages.
  - The pattern is built from fragments, so the source never contains the token.
- `website/docs/user-guide/skills/...`: regenerated with `website/scripts/generate-skill-docs.py` for the 4 changed skills (the docs-site-checks step fails on generator drift).

Doc meaning is unchanged: `mcp__<server>__{tool}`, `terminal(command="{tool} ...")`, `mcp_unreal_engine_{tool}` and `docs/{system}/atlas/` still read as placeholders. Comments, docstrings, debug-log labels and the injection-detector patterns elsewhere never reach the provider and are left alone. The axolotl/unsloth chat-template docs use pipe-delimited special tokens and `tool_call` tags, which the pattern does not match.

## Credit

@strzhao (赵桂雄) — DRAFT #132534, first submitter. Their two commits are cherry-picked with authorship kept:
- `99b0eff8e5`: braces the 3 SKILL.md placeholders and adds the guard test (`-x c080bc17`).
- `1b998e022c`: widens the guard to all bundled markdown and moves it to `tests/skills/` (`-x 52d2e4e3`).

Issue reported by @RealPLU. Attribution map in `75f2b839a7`.

Our follow-ups:
- `241bece12d`: the system-atlas siblings and the 3 tool-error strings.
- `a7bf122567`, `3675072843`, `62568a8aba`: widen the guard to the whole role-tag family and every servable file, decoded like `skill_view`.
- `6200aabc32`: pins the tool-error strings.
- `c624c18eb1`: website regen.

## Verification

| Live probe — real `skill_view` / error producers on a temp `HERMES_HOME` | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `skill_view` delegation skill / hermes-agent-skill-authoring / unreal-mcp / system-atlas | role tag present (1 each) | clean |
| `skill_view(system-atlas, assets/data.example.mjs)` | role tag present | clean |
| `not_deferrable_error`, `partition_calls` malformed-name error, `model_tools` malformed-name string | role tag present (1 each) | clean |
| Hermes skill security warning for system-atlas | logged | none |
| Unrelated neighbours (`skill_view(systematic-debugging)`, known-tool branch of `not_deferrable_error`) | — | byte-identical to main |

- Red on main: the scan test fails with main's skill trees and lists all 5 offending files. The error-string test fails when either `tool_search_validation.py` or `connectors/gateway/merge.py` is reverted.
- Mutations: reverting `99b0eff8e5` or `241bece12d` turns the scan test red. Before `6200aabc32`, reverting the `.py` half of `241bece12d` stayed green, and the review flagged that. Now it turns the error-string test red. The `model_tools.py` string has no cheap pure caller, so it is covered by review only.
- Tests:
  - `test_bundled_skill_doc_placeholders`: 2 passed.
  - With `test_connectors_gateway_{merge,client,wire}`: 60 passed.
  - `test_connector_bridge_wiring` + `test_schema_sanitizer`: 72 passed.
  - First review round, with `website/` present: `test_skill_docs_contract` + `tests/website/test_generate_skill_docs` + `test_tool_search` (with the placeholder test): 58 passed.
- Scan cost: 1485 files in about 0.26s.

Independent review: 2 rounds. Round 1 covered correctness and tests/probe/mutation. Its two Low test findings (the error strings had no test; the scan was limited by file suffix) are fixed. Round 2 covered reuse, quality and efficiency; all approved, and the one quality cleanup (decode like `skill_view`) is fixed.

## Maintainer notes

- **The website/docs-site CI must pass before merge.** The build's test archive excluded `website/`, so `test_skill_docs_contract` and the docs-site-checks / `check_doc_links` steps were not run on the final head. Round 1 of review ran `test_skill_docs_contract` with `website/` present on the regen commit and it passed. Later commits are test-only.
- `Refs`, not `Fixes`: this covers the bundled-content half of #132504. Two parts are not built here:
  - **Error classification.** The OpenRouter guardrail 403 ("prompt injection patterns detected" / `role_tag_injection`) is still classified as the generic "request blocked" in `agent/error_classifier.py::_status_403`. It should map to `content_policy_blocked` and skip the cross-provider retry.
  - **Other text sources.** User-authored skills, user files and transcripts re-imported via `session_search` can still carry the tag. Escaping it on the send path would be a separate change.
- The hub index cache (`skills/.hub/index-cache/`) is untracked. Existing installs keep the old text there until the cache is rebuilt.
- Overlaps (conflict by file only; not checked line by line):
  - #125130 edits the same unreal-mcp line (trivial rebase).
  - `tools/tool_search_validation.py` is also touched by #123411, #122717 (+`model_tools.py`), #110452, #131399 and #122730.
  - Other open PRs on the delegation-skill and skill-authoring SKILL.md files are listed in #132534.

items.body:
On Windows, a multiplexed gateway keeps running when a profile's own-gateway probe stalls on its named pipe. Before this change the watchdog hard-killed it with exit 75.

Fixes #132547

## What happened

Every 30 s, `reconcile_served_profiles` checks whether a not-yet-served profile still runs its own gateway. It calls `live_gateway_pid_for_home` inline on the gateway event loop. On Windows that check can end in `query_gateway_control` reading from a named pipe. A pipe handle has no read timeout, unlike the POSIX socket, which already used `settimeout`. When the peer never answered (including the self-dial case where the pipe belongs to this same process), the read blocked the loop thread. `shutdown_watchdog` then stopped getting liveness ticks and killed the multiplexer with exit 75.

## Change

- `gateway/run_profile_reconcile.py`: the own-gateway probe runs on the housekeeping pool through `asyncio.wait_for` with a 5 s limit (`_OWN_GATEWAY_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECS`) (contributor commit). If the probe times out, the profile is skipped for that cycle and the next scan probes it again. The log says `Own-gateway probe for profile '…' timed out; not serving it this cycle`, not "still runs its own gateway", and the profile is not recorded as blocked. That warning is logged once per stall. Repeats while the same peer stays wedged go to DEBUG (`_profile_probe_timeout_warned`).
- `gateway/control_socket.py::_query_windows_pipe`: the pipe exchange runs through the existing `agent.deadline.run_bounded_sync`. This bounds Windows `query_gateway_control` verbs at their `timeout` (2 s default), and they return `None` on a stall, which matches POSIX.
- `hermes_cli/web_server_cron.py::_forward_cron_fire_to_gateway` and `hermes_cli/web_routers/messaging.py::update_messaging_platform`: these two dashboard coroutines made the same probe inline. They now use `asyncio.to_thread`, the same pattern as the sibling `/api/gateway/start|stop` routes.
- Tests:
  - `tests/gateway/test_multiplex_hot_serve.py`: the contributor's stalled-probe test, extended to cover the timeout log, the not-warned state and the once-per-stall dedupe.
  - `tests/gateway/test_control_socket.py`: a new test for the bounded pipe query. It fakes the pipe handle through `open`, not `sys.platform`.
  - `tests/hermes_cli/test_cron_fire_dashboard.py`: `test_fire_endpoint_default_port` gains a loop-liveness check, with httpx stubbed so no socket is dialled.

## Credit

@liuhao1024 (#132593, a draft): commit `c037bfa679` was cherry-picked with authorship kept (`-x 84209e2f1a`). That commit moves the reconcile probe off the loop and adds the regression test. Their contributor email mapping was already on main, so no map commit was needed. The issue was reported by @spec288. @aron-intframe and @vanscodex traced the root cause in the issue thread to the probe dialling its own pipe from its own loop thread.

Our follow-ups:
- `cbbd5c8136`: bounds the Windows pipe query at its own timeout.
- `c139834fa0`: moves the two dashboard coroutines' probes off the loop.
- `cb815aa7d3`: reports a timed-out probe as a timeout, not a live gateway.
- `be5cb7d677`: warns once per stall.
- `272b6247c3` and `6c7db1a369`: dashboard loop-liveness test, and the httpx stub in that test.

## Verification

| Live probe | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Real reconcile, `live_gateway_pid_for_home` blocking 3 s, 0.1 s ticker | 2 ticks during reconcile, max gap 3.11 s (loop starved) | 32 ticks, max gap 0.10 s |
| `query_gateway_control` on Windows path, silent pipe peer, `timeout=0.5` | returned after 6.01 s (full peer stall) | `None` after 0.51 s |
| Same, answering peer / no pipe / POSIX with no socket | `{'pid': 4242}` / `None` / `None`, instant | unchanged |
| Stalled probe over 3 passes, log levels | n/a | `WARNING, DEBUG, DEBUG`; profile not added, not in the warned set |

- Kept tests (2 new test functions):
  - `test_stalled_own_gateway_probe_never_wedges_the_loop_or_serves` is red on main and green here. Each fold step also failed first: the timed-out message assertion was red on the contributor's head, and the single-WARNING assertion was red before `be5cb7d677`.
  - `test_windows_pipe_query_is_bounded_when_the_peer_never_answers` is red on main (10.0 s against a 2.0 s limit) and green here.
- Mutations:
  - Reverting `c037bfa679` turns the reconcile test red. So do two mutants that keep the constant: an inline probe, and treating a timeout as "free".
  - Reverting `cbbd5c8136` turns the pipe test red.
  - Reverting the cron half of `c139834fa0` turns the extended `test_fire_endpoint_default_port` red (loop blocked for 3.0 s, limit 1.0 s).
- `test_multiplex_hot_serve`, `test_profile_signature_during_connect`, `test_cron_fire_dashboard`, `test_control_socket`: 52 passed, 1 skipped (a Linux-only marker). The wider r1 run also covered the dashboard messaging/cron-profile, status and Windows-live suites. Their only failure, `test_collect_fleet_versions_falls_back_to_state_file`, fails the same way on main.
- Lint: ruff clean on touched files, `git diff --check` clean, Windows-footguns scan clean.

Independent review:
- Round 1: the correctness and tests/probe/mutation passes approved. They found two Low issues: the timeout was logged as "still runs its own gateway", and the dashboard `to_thread` commit had no test. Both are folded in.
- Round 2: the correctness, reuse, quality and efficiency passes approved. They found two Low issues: the timeout WARNING was not deduplicated, and the test dialled a real port 9. Both are folded in.

## Maintainer notes

- Not in this PR: answering `identify` in-process when the probed record is this process (`record.pid == os.getpid()`), as proposed in the issue thread. With this stack a self-dial costs at most one bounded read on a worker thread, not the event loop. The short-circuit would be a cheap optional follow-up.
- Behaviour change:
  - A stalled Windows pipe now costs one skipped reconcile cycle for that profile, which is retried on the next scan. Before, it stalled the event loop.
  - Windows `query_gateway_control` verbs (all routed through `_query_windows_pipe`) now return `None` after `timeout`. Before, they could block indefinitely.
  - `run_bounded_sync` logs a WARNING on each Windows pipe timeout, while POSIX timeouts stay silent.
- Each stalled pipe read leaves one daemon thread until the peer answers or exits. This happens at most once per `host_gateway` cache miss while the peer stays wedged. Before, the caller blocked forever.
- `update_messaging_platform`'s `to_thread` wrap has no dedicated test. The cron half of the same commit is the one pinned.
- Still on the loop, but now capped at 2 s by the pipe bound:
  - `_restart_gateway_after` / `_spawn_gateway_restart` in 4 dashboard routes. Moving them to `to_thread` is a possible follow-up.
  - The startup-only paths `start_gateway`, `_claim_host_gateway_role` and the dashboard lifespan orphan reap.
- Overlaps:
  - #125511 moves the `profiles/` scan in `reconcile_served_profiles` off the loop, which is the same function, so expect a textual conflict.
  - #126577 and #127302 touch `live_gateway_pid_for_home` internals, but not the callers changed here.
